Tuanbo Lake has about 50 square kilometres of open water, and its wetland is on China's list of wetland nature reserves and is a Tianjin bird reserve; hot-spring hotels line the shore.

rows.name: Ruins of Tianfei Palace (Dazhigu Mazu Temple)
rows.summary: The site of a temple to the sea goddess Mazu founded in the Yuan dynasty beside the Hai River, the oldest temple site in Tianjin's urban area and the 'East Temple' to the Tianhou Palace's 'West Temple'. The temple was burned in 1900, abandoned in the 1950s and its hall demolished in the 1970s. Excavations from 1997 uncovered the foundations of a Ming–Qing hall about 14 m wide and Yuan-dynasty foundations, which are shown in the site museum that opened in 2002.

rows.name: Samaranch Memorial Museum
rows.summary: A museum on the west shore of Tuanbo Lake dedicated to Juan Antonio Samaranch, who led the International Olympic Committee for 21 years, opened in 2013 with the authorisation of the Samaranch family and the IOC. It holds about 16,000 items from his books, souvenirs and personal belongings, including the passports that record his visits to China, and sits in grounds with an Olympic sculpture park. It was rated a national second-grade museum in 2024.

rows.name: Sanchakou Confluence (Grand Canal)
rows.summary: The spot in the city centre where the Ziya River and the Grand Canal's South and North canals meet to form the Hai River, where Tianjin began as a canal and grain-shipping hub. The Tianjin section of the Grand Canal is part of the canal's UNESCO World Heritage listing, and the confluence is overlooked by the Tianjin Eye, Wanghailou Church and the Temple of Great Compassion. A monument of 1986 to the Luan River water diversion to Tianjin stands at the present confluence.

rows.name: Shi Family Grand Courtyard (Yangliuqing Museum)
rows.summary: The mansion of the Qing-dynasty merchant Shi Yuanshi, one of Tianjin's 'eight great families', begun in 1875 and now the Yangliuqing Museum, on the South Canal in the old canal town of Yangliuqing. Its courtyards are noted for brick, wood and stone carving and include a private theatre, one of the better-preserved closed residential theatres in China. Displays cover Yangliuqing New Year prints, brick carving, paper-cuts, kites and wedding and merchant customs.

rows.name: Shuigao Manor
rows.summary: An agricultural leisure park of about 1,500 mu (roughly 100 hectares) in Xinkou town, in the Dongdian modern-agriculture zone south-west of Yangliuqing. It has five zones, covering farming scenery, a Ziya River theme, fruit picking, a greenhouse display and a rural hot-spring area, with fishing, dining and accommodation. It suits families looking for a rural day out.

rows.name: Site of the Peiyang University (Beiyang Daxuetang)
rows.summary: The surviving buildings of China's first government-run modern university, founded in 1895 and moved in 1903 to the former Xigu arsenal beside the North Canal. What remains on the campus of today's Hebei University of Technology is the Tuancheng courtyard of about 1930, the red-brick South Building of 1933, now the university's history museum, and the North Building of 1936, now a teaching block.

rows.name: Siyuan Hall, Nankai University
rows.summary: Siyuan Hall is a three-storey red-brick science building with a six-column porch, finished in 1923 with money from the Rockefeller Foundation and the Yuan family, and is the only early main building of Nankai University's Balitai campus still standing. Japanese bombing set it on fire in 1937, it was repaired after 1945, and it is now used by the university's medical school.

rows.name: Taku Forts (Dagukou Forts)
rows.summary: Coastal forts at the mouth of the Hai River, rebuilt and extended several times under the Qing, which were the main battleground of the Dagu battles of 1858, 1859 and 1860 in the Second Opium War and saw fighting again in 1900. Most of the forts were demolished under the Boxer Protocol; the restored Wei fort on the south bank, opened to visitors in 1997, survives beside a memorial park. A museum in a rust-coloured steel building has galleries on the forts, the wars fought here and the 1901 protocol, and a 3D cinema.

rows.name: Tasly Health City
rows.summary: The campus of the pharmaceutical group Tasly in Beichen District, open to visitors as an industrial-tourism site on about 53 hectares. Visitors can see a production workshop and exhibitions on traditional Chinese medicine culture, and the site also runs study programmes for young people.

rows.name: Temple of Great Compassion (Dabei Yuan)
rows.summary: Tianjin's largest surviving Buddhist monastery, a working Chan temple founded in the mid-17th century, expanded in 1669 and extended with a large eastern compound in the 1940s. Its halls hold a Ming-dynasty bronze Shakyamuni, a hall of three Burmese jade Buddhas completed in 2000, and hundreds of older statues in stone, wood and bronze. A memorial hall to the monk Hongyi stands in the grounds.

rows.name: Tianhou Palace (Tianjin Mazu Temple)
rows.summary: Tianhou Palace, popularly called Niangniang Gong, is a temple to the sea goddess Mazu on the west bank of the Sancha Estuary, begun in the Yuan dynasty, formally ordered by the court in 1326 and largely rebuilt in 1985. Its halls run east to west from an opera stage and flagpoles through the gate, archway and main hall to a scripture pavilion, and today they house the Tianjin Folk Museum, with displays on canal transport, marriage customs, commerce and folk art.

rows.name: Tianjin Eye
rows.summary: A Ferris wheel about 120 m tall built into Yongle Bridge beside the Sanchakou confluence, with 48 enclosed capsules. A full turn takes about half an hour, and all the capsules were replaced in 2023. It is lit in the evening, and Jingang Bridge just to the south is the usual place to photograph it with the confluence in view.

rows.name: Tianjin Fantawild Adventure
rows.summary: A theme park in the Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-city run by the Chinese chain Fantawild, opened in July 2014. Its attractions combine science-fiction and animation themes with 3D and 4D screen technology, and include areas based on the Boonie Bears cartoon. The park stages seasonal events such as a summer water-splash festival and fireworks, and it suits families with children.

rows.name: Tianjin Happy Valley
rows.summary: A theme park by Dongli Lake run by the tourism group OCT, with indoor and outdoor rides and daily parades and shows. It is laid out in themed zones that include Viking Harbour, Christmas Village and Flying Caribbean, and it holds seasonal events and opens in the evening at busy times.

rows.name: Tianjin Jinxiang Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A wildlife park in the Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-city, reopened in 2024 on the site of the former Yili Fairy-tale Park. A walking zone has twelve themed areas with more than a hundred species, among them giant pandas, giraffes and zebras. A separate drive-through zone is toured by sightseeing train or a safari-style vehicle along a 2.1 km route past lions, wolves and antelope.

rows.name: Tianjin North Railway Station
rows.summary: A railway station opened in 1903 as Xinkaihe station, built on the initiative of Yuan Shikai, then governor-general of Zhili. The wooden station building and a steel footbridge across the platforms, both from 1903, survive in their early twentieth-century form, and the station is often used as a film location. It is still a working station, with regional trains to Jizhou.

rows.name: Tianjin Polar Ocean Park (Haichang Polar Ocean World)
rows.summary: An aquarium and marine-animal park in a whale-shaped building in the Xiangluowan business district, on the south bank of the Hai River facing Tanggu's commercial centre. Its exhibits include polar animals, an undersea tunnel, a beluga area and a jellyfish hall, and the park puts on regular animal shows. It suits families with young children.

rows.name: Tianjin Port Culture and Tourism Area
rows.summary: A port-themed tourism zone of about 23 square kilometres in the Dongjiang area, linking Dongjiang Bay beach, the Tianjin International Cruise Home Port, a warehouse-style wine showroom and several container terminals. It was accepted as a national 4A scenic area in October 2023, when it introduced a sea route of about 40 minutes past the terminals, from which the port can be seen at work. Dongjiang Bay is a large man-made beach on the Bohai coast.

rows.name: Tianjin Tropical Plant Garden
rows.summary: A greenhouse botanical garden beside the Caozhuang flower market in Xiqing District, opened in 2003, with an indoor collection of tropical and subtropical plants that includes palms and dragon trees. It closed in November 2023 to be converted into an aerospace-biology science park, and no reopening has been announced.

rows.name: Tianjin Water Park
rows.summary: Tianjin Water Park opened in 1951 on a marshy pool called Qinglongtan and is described as the largest comprehensive park in central Tianjin, laid out around lakes and islands linked by bridges. Its garden-within-a-garden sights include the Kobe Garden, a Japanese-style garden finished in 1989, and a Suzhou-style bonsai garden, and the park hosts large public events and festivals.

rows.name: Tianta Lake and Tianjin TV Tower
rows.summary: The Tianjin Radio and Television Tower, completed in 1991, stands 415.2 metres tall in the middle of Tianta Lake in south-west Tianjin, with a parabolic shaft and a saucer-shaped pod near the top built to hold an observation hall and a revolving restaurant. The landscaped lake around it has a main plaza facing the east gate of Tianjin Water Park, and the tower is one of the 'Ten Views of Tianjin', 'Clouds Swirling Round the Tower'.

rows.name: Tianzun Pavilion (Taiyi Temple)
rows.summary: Tianzun Ge, also called Taiyi Temple, is a Daoist pavilion built in the Kangxi reign of the Qing dynasty in Fengtai town and counted among Tianjin's three Daoist pavilions. The 17.4-metre timber pavilion has three storeys, with eight columns running from the ground to the roof, and stands behind a two-storey gate; its levels were dedicated to the Heavenly Honoured One, the Queen Mother of the West and the Ziwei deity. Conservation work on the buildings and courtyard was accepted as complete in 2023.

rows.name: Yangliuqing Manor
rows.summary: A leisure and holiday park of about 800 mu (roughly 53 hectares) in the north of Yangliuqing town, with wooded grounds and lakes, a hotel and conference facilities, fishing and fruit picking. It was upgraded in April 2024 with a series of rides branded Jack Park, and it suits families and groups on a day out from the city.

rows.name: Zhang Garden
rows.summary: Zhang Garden is a European-style mansion built in 1915–16 for Zhang Biao, a former Qing army commander, in what was then the Japanese concession. Sun Yat-sen stayed here for 27 days in December 1924 and the last emperor Puyi lived here from 1925; after 1949 the house served as the seat of the Tianjin Military Control Commission and the city's Party committee, which gives the site its official national-list name. Part of it has been open as a memorial museum since 2018, and the museum reopened in January 2026 after a refit.

rows.name: Jiulongshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 2,126 ha in the Chuanfangyu area of Jizhou, in the hills north of Tianjin, made a national forest park in 1997. It takes its name from nine ridges that run together like dragons and has woodland walks, limestone caves and viewpoints looking towards the Great Wall and Cuiping Lake. It is one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Ancient Lotus Pond
rows.summary: A walled garden of ponds, bridges, pavilions and towers in the centre of Baoding, begun in the 13th century as a private garden and rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. In the Qing it became the site of the Lotus Pond Academy and was used by the Qianlong, Jiaqing and Guangxu emperors as a travelling palace. It gave its name to Baoding's Lianchi District and now operates as the Lianchi Academy Museum, with many inscribed steles.

rows.name: Baishi Mountain
rows.summary: Baishi Mountain is the northern end of the Taihang range, a block of pale marble and dolomite in Laiyuan County whose jagged peaks poke out of low cloud on overcast days. Walkways run along its cliffs, including two glass-floored skywalks opened in 2014 and 2015, and stretches of old Great Wall lie around the foothills. It forms part of the Fangshan UNESCO Global Geopark, which also takes in Shidu and Yesanpo.

rows.name: Baiyang Lake
rows.summary: Baiyang Lake is the largest freshwater lake in northern China, a patchwork of shallow lakes, channels, reed beds and lotus ponds within the Xiong'an New Area. The usual visit is by boat from the main tourist wharf, where clean-energy 'water bus' boats link the garden and island sites, drifting through the reeds and lotus to lake-island villages where local restaurants cook fish and other lake produce. The lake sheltered guerrillas fighting the Japanese occupation during the war and is the setting of well-known Chinese stories such as Little Soldier Zhang Ga.

rows.name: Baoding Banquet Food Museum
rows.summary: A large food-hall and restaurant complex in Baoding's high-tech zone, opened in September 2023 and registered as a museum of Zhili (Qing-era provincial) cuisine, with a small collection of historic cookery books and tableware. The ground floor is a street of snack stalls selling local favourites such as donkey-meat sandwiches, and the upper floors have banquet halls modelled on the old provincial guild halls of Baoding, plus a dinner-theatre show. It suits visitors who want to try Baoding food in one place rather than see a historic site.

rows.name: Baoding Bell Tower
rows.summary: A two-storey, double-eaved tower on a brick platform in Baoding's old city, whose present form dates from the Ming dynasty (Xuande era, 1426–35) and which has been repaired several times since. It houses a large iron bell cast in 1181 under the Jin dynasty and decorated with bands of Buddha figures and inscriptions. It stands a short walk from Daci Pavilion, so the two are usually seen together.

rows.name: Baoding Military Academy
rows.name_zh: 保定陆军军官学校旧址
rows.summary: Memorial hall and surviving grounds of the Baoding Military Academy, which trained thousands of officers between 1912 and 1923 and served as a model for the Whampoa Academy set up in Guangzhou in 1924. Most of the original campus is gone: a firing range, a reviewing stand and a moat survive, and the former parade ground is now a public square. A memorial hall opened in 1995 and covers the academy's history.

rows.name: Beiyue Temple
rows.summary: A walled temple compound in the old town of Quyang, built for worship of the spirit of the Northern Peak; emperors sacrificed to the Northern Peak from here until 1660, when the rite moved to Mount Heng at Hunyuan in Shanxi. Its main building, the Yuan-dynasty Dening Hall, is described as the largest surviving Yuan timber hall and has wall paintings of heavenly figures traditionally attributed to the Tang painter Wu Daozi. The grounds also hold a stele gallery of over a hundred inscribed stones and a small exhibition hall on the temple's history.

rows.name: Buli Work-Study School for France
rows.name_zh: 布里留法工艺学校旧址
rows.summary: The site of a school founded in 1917 to prepare young Chinese for work and study in France, one of the places where the work-study movement began. The surviving single-storey classrooms, workshop and offices stand in a courtyard behind a gate that mixes a Gothic-style brick tower with a traditional Chinese arch. Visitors also see an exhibition room on Li Shizeng, one of the school's founders, and a locust tree planted by Cai Hesen, who was at the school in 1918 before leaving for France in 1919.

rows.name: Ciyun Pavilion
rows.summary: Ciyun Pavilion is a two-storey pavilion in Dingxing county town, originally called the Dabei (Great Compassion) Pavilion; the surviving building dates from a rebuilding in 1306, under the Yuan dynasty. It is square in plan, three bays by three, with a hip-and-gable roof and a height of 13.3 m, and became a national heritage unit in 1996.

rows.name: Daci Pavilion
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Baoding's old city whose main hall, a three-storey pavilion on a stone platform, is the tallest surviving historic building in the city. It was founded under the Yuan dynasty and rebuilt in the Qing after a fire in the Qianlong reign, and is flanked by bell and drum towers with a Guandi temple behind. Inside the main hall stands a gilded wooden thousand-armed Guanyin, and the temple has been in religious use again since 2006.

rows.name: Dajidian Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old village on the western side of Baoding that has been restored as a cultural-tourism area. It keeps an opera tower protected as a municipal heritage site since 1993, nine restored stone tablets and a stream crossed by six bridges. State-media reports of 2021 and 2022 describe it as re-themed as a music and culture town, with an artists' creative park, craft, food and creative-goods outlets, performances, a water-and-light show on the river and an annual music festival.

rows.name: Daodejing Pillar at Longxing Daoist Temple
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty octagonal stone pillar about 6 metres high, raised in 738 and carved with the Daodejing together with Emperor Xuanzong's commentary. It stands in the built-up part of Yi County town under a protective pavilion built in 2001, and is all that remains of the Longxing Daoist temple apart from three steles. Some scholars attribute the calligraphy to the Tang calligrapher Su Lingzhi.

rows.name: Ding Kiln Site
rows.summary: The main production site of Ding ware, the white porcelain of one of the Song dynasty's 'Five Great Kilns', on the edge of Jianci village. Excavations from 1985 uncovered kilns of the Tang, Five Dynasties, Song and Jin periods, workshops, clay-washing pools and glaze pits, and more than ten thousand porcelain and kiln-furniture specimens. Much of the site is open ground with heaps of porcelain shards, an exhibition hall shows Ding ware from the Tang to the Song, and a larger archaeological park and museum have been announced.

rows.name: Dingzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: One of the best-preserved Confucian temples in Hebei, founded in the Dazhong era of the Tang dynasty (mid-9th century) on the site of a Buddhist temple and enlarged under the Song, Ming and Qing. Three adjoining courtyards hold the Lingxing Gate, the Dacheng Hall for Confucius and his disciples, a lecture hall and a Wenchang pavilion, with a shrine to local filial and chaste figures in a courtyard to the south. It is a quiet site with old steles, and two old locust trees in the grounds are traditionally said to have been planted by Su Dongpo, who served as governor of Dingzhou.

rows.name: Dingzhou Examination Hall
rows.summary: The Dingzhou Examination Hall, begun in 1738 and enlarged in 1834, is described as the most complete surviving imperial examination compound in northern China. It has a long screen wall where results were posted, the Kuige hall of examination cells where candidates sat, and the two-storey Lansheng Tower where examiners lived and worked. Old locust trees in the grounds are traditionally said to have been planted by the Qianlong Emperor.

rows.name: Dingzhou Han Tomb and Stone Carving Museum
rows.summary: The Dingzhou Han Tomb and Stone Carving Museum is a heritage compound in the old part of Dingzhou that brings together three protected sites: a Han-dynasty tomb of the Zhongshan kingdom, stone carvings from the Beizhuangzi Han tomb and the city's collection of inscribed steles. Dingzhou was the capital of the Han kingdom of Zhongshan, and finds from its royal tombs, including a silver-thread jade burial suit, are shown at the Dingzhou Museum.

rows.name: Dingzhou Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque on Zhongshan Road in the old town, facing west, with buildings dating from the Yuan to the Qing dynasties. Its brick-vaulted rear sanctuary, the Houyao Hall, is a surviving Yuan-period structure built without beams, and a Yuan stele records a repair of the mosque in the Zhizheng era (1341–68). The prayer hall and gate are in the Ming–Qing Chinese style, with lecture halls on either side of the compound.

rows.name: Fangshun Bridge
rows.summary: A bridge in Fangshunqiao village in Mancheng District that the heritage list dates to the Ming and Qing dynasties, protected nationally since 2013. It crosses a watercourse running through the village. Visitors should expect a village bridge rather than a developed attraction.

rows.name: Flower Pagoda of Qinghua Temple
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda, eight-sided and about 13 metres high, standing alone on the lower slope of Longgong Hill north of Beiluoping village; the rest of Qinghua Temple has disappeared. Its upper part is covered by 120 small Buddha niches arranged in eight tiers, which gives it the name 'flower pagoda'. It is a quiet stop for those interested in Liao-period architecture and has been nationally protected since 2001.

rows.name: Former Residence of Yan Yangchu
rows.summary: Part of the compound where the educator Yan Yangchu (James Yen) lived from 1926 to 1936 while his Mass Education Movement ran a rural literacy and reconstruction experiment in Ding County. Only the living quarters of the west courtyard survive, a north hall, two side wings and a south range, all with grey-tiled gable roofs. The experiment ended in 1936 as Japanese forces advanced, and the site stands a short walk from Dingzhou Museum, which displays finds from the town's two Song-dynasty pagoda crypts.

rows.name: Former Yude Middle School
rows.summary: A late-Qing brick-and-timber courtyard that housed Yude Middle School, founded in 1907, and now serves as the memorial hall of the Work-Study in France movement. In 1917–20 the school ran preparatory classes for young Chinese heading to France to work and study, whose students included Li Weihan, Li Fuchun and Liu Shaoqi, later senior Communist Party figures. The hall's exhibition covers the movement through documents, photographs and reconstructed scenes.

rows.name: Gaobeidian Green Building Technology Industrial Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 绿建科技工业旅游景区
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism area in Gaobeidian's economic zone, run by Aorun Shunda, a maker of energy-saving windows and green-building systems, and earlier listed as its doors-and-windows industrial-tourism area. The city tourism bureau describes a visiting route through a green-building technology innovation centre, a history hall, the China Door and Window Museum, an ultra-low-energy building test centre and the production base; the museum's halls were described in 2017 as covering carved stone windows, timber doors and windows, and modern types. State media also describe automated production lines and a climate-simulation test chamber on the company campus, so it suits visitors interested in building technology or industry.

rows.name: Geyuan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the old town of Laiyuan whose Manjusri Hall, traditionally dated to 966, is counted among the 'eight great Liao structures' and is the earliest of them. It is a timber hall with deep eaves and fewer interior columns than usual, window lattices from the Liao to the Qing dynasties, and wall paintings that survive mostly under later mud plaster. In the courtyard hangs an iron bell cast in 1114, weighing about two tonnes and bearing over 1,200 Chinese characters.

rows.name: Guangyuan Garden
rows.summary: The surviving main building of a residence put up around 1917 by Cao Kun, the Zhili-clique military leader then based in Baoding, which combined a Western-style hall with Chinese courtyard planning. Most of the original compound was demolished in the 20th and early 21st centuries, leaving one brick hall with a hip roof and carved stone doorway. It has been restored and houses the Baoding local-chronicles museum (opened 2015), with rooms on local history, the War of Resistance and the Republican period.

rows.name: Huai Army Hall
rows.summary: Built in 1888 at the request of Li Hongzhang, then Viceroy of Zhili, as a memorial shrine and headquarters for his Huai Army, this compound mixes Huizhou-style halls from Anhui in its south-east, northern courtyards in its north-east and a landscaped garden in the west. Part of the central axis became a shrine to Li Hongzhang himself in 1902. Its old theatre building survives, and the compound is run as the Baoding Huai Army Hall Museum.

rows.name: Huangfu Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A brick pagoda with closely stacked eaves standing in farmland beside Huangfusi village, mainly of Jin-dynasty date with possible later work. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013. It is a roadside stop for anyone exploring the old pagodas around Laishui rather than a destination in its own right.

rows.name: Jade Emperor Hall of Dadao Temple, Dingzhou
rows.summary: Dadao Guan, a Daoist temple founded under the Yuan dynasty, once had a full axial layout but only its Jade Emperor Hall survives, in the built-up area of Dingzhou. The hall, which the national heritage list dates to the Ming, is described by the city as showing typical Yuan-period construction, and inside is a large mural of the gods paying homage, made in the Wanli era with raised, gilded lines.

rows.name: Jin-Cha-Ji Border Region Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 晋察冀边区革命纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial museum at Chengnanzhuang that first opened in 1974 in the former headquarters of the Jin-Cha-Ji Military Region and was enlarged and renamed in 2005. Its photographs and objects cover the Jin-Cha-Ji border region during the War of Resistance against Japan and the civil war, and the preserved headquarters are three rows of 21 adobe houses, including rooms used by Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Ren Bishi, an operations office, a telephone room and a meeting room. Chengnanzhuang is also where the Communist Party issued its 1948 May Day slogans.

rows.name: Jinmen Floodgates
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty flood-relief sluice on the right bank of the Yongding River, made up of fifteen stone bays spread over about 100 metres. A sluice of this name was first built in 1701 nearby; the relief weir was moved to this site in 1738 and rebuilt as the present sluice in 1909, and steles beside it record later repairs and carry imperial inscriptions. The structure is fenced off in a remote spot and was half hidden by vegetation until volunteers cleared part of it in June 2026, so it suits only heritage and waterworks enthusiasts.

rows.name: Jinshan Temple Relic Pagoda
rows.summary: A stone relic pagoda of the Yuan dynasty with closely stacked eaves, standing on a wooded hillside near Donglongquan village in the mountains north of Laishui. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013. It suits visitors touring the old pagodas of Laishui County by car.

rows.name: Kaishan Temple
rows.summary: A small Buddhist temple in Xincheng town whose timber main hall was built under the Liao dynasty in the mid-11th century. The five-bay hall has a hipped roof, deep eaves and large brackets, and only four columns stand inside because of its column-reducing frame, while the halls in front are Ming and Qing. Floodwater reached the compound in August 2023.

rows.name: Liaodi Pagoda
rows.summary: The Liaodi Pagoda, in the former Kaiyuan Temple precinct of Dingzhou, is an octagonal, eleven-storey brick tower about 84 m tall and is regarded as the tallest surviving historic brick pagoda in China. It was built between 1001 and 1055 under the Northern Song to house Buddhist relics brought from India, and doubled as a lookout against the Khitan Liao to the north, hence the name meaning 'enemy-spotting pagoda'. The ground-floor corridor keeps Song-dynasty murals.

rows.name: Liulingzui Distillery Site, Xushui
rows.summary: Liulingzui is a liquor distillery in Xushui whose old works preserve a distillery site of the Jin and Yuan dynasties: two rows of 16 fermentation pits that archaeologists say have been in continuous use ever since, and an underground 'wine sea' of Ming and Qing wooden and wicker storage vats. The site became a national heritage unit in 2006 and national industrial heritage in 2020, and suits anyone curious about how Chinese baijiu is made and aged.

rows.name: Longyan Temple Pagoda, Laishui
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty pagoda on the east bank of the Qingshui River, just west of Zhongshuidong village and known locally as the Shuidong Pagoda. Tradition says it was built to hold back mountain floods. It is one of several Liao-period pagodas around Laishui and was added to the national heritage list in 2019.

rows.name: Mancheng Han Tombs
rows.summary: Two rock-cut tombs on Lingshan hill belonging to Liu Sheng, Prince Jing of Zhongshan, and his wife Dou Wan, dated to the end of the 2nd century BC and found by military engineers in 1968. Each tomb has a long entrance passage, side chambers, a central hall and a rear chamber, with drainage and anti-theft features cut into the rock. The finds included two gold-thread jade burial suits and the Changxin Palace lamp, which are now in the Hebei Museum, with replicas shown on site, and the tombs are counted among the major Chinese archaeological discoveries of the 20th century.

rows.name: Mount Langya
rows.summary: A scenic mountain area in the Taihang range in the west of Yi County, known for the story of the 'Five Heroes of Mount Langya'. In the official account, five Eighth Route Army soldiers covering a withdrawal in September 1941 retreated to the summit ridge, Qipantuo, and went over a cliff rather than be captured. An exhibition hall about them stands near the entrance, and a memorial tower on Qipantuo marks the place.

rows.name: Nanyang Site, Xiong'an
rows.summary: Nanyang Site is a Warring States site in the Xiong'an New Area where archaeologists have found two city sites with south and west gates, connecting roads and tombs, along with finds in the style of the Yan culture. Part of the dig has been kept beside the research station, which has a small exhibition room of pottery, eave tiles and metal objects, and Xinhua reports the site open to schools and the public, with an archaeological park planned.

rows.name: Qinghe Circuit Office
rows.summary: The office of the Qinghe circuit intendant, an official in charge of rivers and lakes in southern Zhili, set up in 1726; the present compound of gates, three halls on a central axis, staff courtyards and a Huizhou-style flower hall dates from the 1830s–40s. After 1911 it was used as a warlord's residence, offices, a clinic and housing before restoration. Since the end of 2021 it has housed the Baoding Water Conservancy Museum, Hebei's first museum devoted to water, with displays of traditional water-lifting tools and local water-management history.

rows.name: Qishan Ski Resort
rows.summary: A ski resort on the hillside south of Laiyuan town, with ski runs and lifts. The same site holds China's national ski-jumping training and research base, which was built for the national ski-jumping and Nordic combined teams. Skiing runs through the winter, and the county also presents the resort as a summer retreat.

rows.name: Ranzhuang Tunnel Warfare Site
rows.summary: A village in Qingyuan District where, during the war against Japan, residents dug a network of tunnels under the houses and streets to hide in and fight from, and which later became the setting of the film Tunnel Warfare. The network had four main lines and 24 branches, about 16 km in all, of which about 3 km survives. A memorial hall founded in 1959 shows photographs, models and wartime objects, and the village keeps its 1930s–40s look with tunnel entrances, defensive works and slogans.

rows.name: Shengtayuan Pagoda
rows.summary: Shengtayuan Pagoda is an octagonal, thirteen-tier brick-and-stone pagoda, 24 m high, begun in 1103 under the Liao dynasty and repaired several times from the Ming dynasty up to 1985–86. It stands on Jingke Hill, now Jingke Park, south-west of Yi County town, and is popularly known as the Jing Ke Pagoda.

rows.name: Shuangta'an Twin Pagodas
rows.summary: Shuangta'an Twin Pagodas are two dense-eaved brick pagodas, the east and west pagodas, standing north-west of Tainingsi village in Yi County and listed as a national heritage unit in 2013. The national register dates them between the Jin and Ming dynasties, and they lie in Xiling township, named after the Western Qing Tombs.

rows.name: Song–Liao Border Tunnels, Xiong County
rows.summary: The Song–Liao border tunnels are a network of brick-vaulted underground passages dug in the early Northern Song as a defence against the Liao, with traces known across Xiong, Bazhou, Wen'an, Yongqing and Gu'an over roughly 65 km from east to west. The part open to visitors is a restored section in a park in Xiong County town, where passages and chambers (a command platform above, then lookout, council, armoury, 'maze' and rest rooms below) can be entered, and some passages are only about 0.6 m high. The park has been open since 2009.

rows.name: Sutra Inscriptions at Bahui Temple
rows.summary: Sui-dynasty Buddhist inscriptions carved in a stone niche on the summit of a hill near Xiyangping village, south of Quyang. Five complete sutras are cut into the rock, including the Lotus Sutra's chapter on Guanyin and a sutra on Maitreya. The hilltop is also a temple site, and the hill is climbed at the Double Ninth festival, when a temple fair is held at its foot.

rows.name: Taihang Water Town
rows.summary: A purpose-built tourist town in Angezhuang township, Yi County, laid out in Ming-and-Qing style with stone-paved lanes and grey-roofed, white-walled buildings beside a lake on the Yishui River. It has shops, snack stalls and guesthouses, a campsite and seasonal festivals, and it has operated since about 2017, so it is a modern development rather than a historic village. It suits families and short breaks from Beijing, Baoding or Xiong'an, and is easy to combine with nearby Yishui Lake.

rows.name: Tanpu Gorge
rows.summary: Tanpu Gorge is a scenic area in the Taihang mountains of western Tang County, formerly known as Dashiyu, built around rocky valleys with a series of pools and waterfalls. The pools and falls are the main sights, so it suits a half-day outing for those who like walking among rock and water.

rows.name: Tianshengqiao Waterfalls
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in western Fuping County, known for a single gully of nine waterfalls stepping down the valley, the highest of which, on Yaotai mountain, drops 112.5 metres. The area is also a national geopark, and its name means 'natural bridge'.

rows.name: Tiger Mountain Scenic Area, Quyang
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of more than 20 square kilometres in the Taihang foothills at Quyang's northern edge, named after a tiger-shaped rock near the summit. A stream valley with springs and waterfalls runs through it, and an old gold mine with its tunnel and miners' quarters is open as a sight. The main peak, Sanjianliang, rises to a little over 1,100 metres.

rows.name: Tomb of Prince Yi, Laishui
rows.summary: The tomb of Yinxiang, thirteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor, who was made Prince Yi under the Yongzheng Emperor, was built in 1730 beside Dongyingfang village in Laishui County. The burial vault was looted in the 1930s and the tomb itself is gone, but a stele inscribed in Manchu and Chinese, a bridge, carved stone archways and ornamental columns survive above ground.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhang Rou
rows.summary: The family cemetery of Zhang Rou (1189–1268), a general who served the Jin and then the Yuan dynasty, laid out in 1269 on about 17 hectares in the countryside near Gangtou village. Above ground it has four square stepped earth mounds, three further tombs without mounds, two stone stelae and a few stone figures and animals, and the stele at the tomb of his son Zhang Honglüe is unusually tall. It is an open-air site in farmland rather than a developed attraction.

rows.name: Viceroy of Zhili's Office, Baoding
rows.summary: The only complete provincial-level Qing government compound to survive in China, built in 1729 and used by successive viceroys of Zhili, the province around Beijing, until the end of the Qing. Five courtyards run along a central axis from the main gate through the ceremonial gate, main hall and second hall to the residential quarters. Seventy-four men held the post here over 99 terms, among them Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang, and the compound is now the Zhili Governor-General's Office Museum.

rows.name: Wang's Manor, Yaoshan
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty manor of the Wang family, begun in 1647 by Wang Xigun, a Han banner general who entered China proper with the Manchu army and was granted land here. The estate was expanded to about 50 courtyard houses by 1746, and the surviving south garden has gates, courtyards and halls such as Renhe Hall, with brick, wood and stone carving on the screen wall, gateways and eaves. It is a rare surviving manor-style complex in Hebei.

rows.name: Wangdu Han Tombs
rows.summary: Two Eastern Han brick tombs about 30 metres apart on the east side of Wangdu town, whose chambers hold over 100 square metres of wall paintings showing officials, attendants and heavenly signs. Tomb 1, excavated in 1952, was begun in 132 and is thought to be that of Sun Cheng, Marquis of Fuyang, while its grave goods are held by the Palace Museum in Beijing. A small museum was built next to the tombs around 2010, and the murals were digitally recorded in 2020 for conservation.

rows.name: Western Qing Tombs
rows.summary: The Western Qing Tombs are one of the Qing dynasty's imperial burial grounds, set among wooded hills in Yi County, with the tombs of four emperors (Yongzheng, Jiaqing, Daoguang and Guangxu) and of their empresses, concubines and princes. Tailing, the Yongzheng Emperor's tomb, is the earliest and largest, reached along a long stone spirit way with memorial archways, stone bridges and rows of stone statues, while the underground burial chamber of Chongling, the Guangxu Emperor's tomb, was opened to visitors in 1980. The complex is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties', inscribed in 2000.

rows.name: Wofo Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: The Wofo Temple Cliff Carvings are Northern Song figures cut into a limestone cliff face about 6 m high, facing west, at the Wofo Temple Reservoir in Baihe township, Tang County. They have been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Wuhou Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-period brick pagoda of five storeys and about 22.5 metres, hexagonal rather than the more usual octagon, standing among the houses of Nanwuhou village. The base and eaves carry brick carvings of people, animals and flowers, and some of the glazed tile fittings survive. The ground-floor doorway has been bricked up, so the pagoda is seen from the outside.

rows.name: Wuren Bridge
rows.summary: Wuren Bridge is a five-arch stone bridge over the Ci River, begun in 1599 and finished in 1600 in the Ming dynasty; it is also known as Guifei Bridge, or Noble Consort Bridge. It stands at Wurenqiao town in Anguo and has been a national heritage unit since 2006, making it a short stop for anyone interested in historic stone bridges.

rows.name: Xiahuliang Bridge
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty bridge in Xiahuliang village on the northern side of Zhuozhou, protected as a national heritage unit since 2013. It stands beside the G107 road and is a short roadside stop rather than a destination in its own right. It can be combined with the much longer Yongji Bridge about 2 km to the south.

rows.name: Xigang Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda with closely stacked eaves in the north-west of Laishui town, the easiest of the county's old pagodas to reach. It became a provincial heritage unit in 1982 and a national one in 2006. Laishui County has several pagodas on the national list, ranging from the Liao to the Yuan dynasty.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple Pagoda, Jiecun
rows.summary: Xingguo Temple Pagoda is a Tang-dynasty stone pagoda in Jiecun village, Boye County, listed as a national heritage unit in 2006. It stands in a quiet village on the plain and suits visitors tracing early Buddhist architecture around Baoding.

rows.name: Xingwen Pagoda
rows.summary: A five-tier octagonal pagoda of solid brick, built to imitate timber construction and about 21.5 metres high, in the east of Laiyuan town beside the springs that feed the Laishui River. County sources date it to 744 from an inscribed tablet and describe it as a feng shui pagoda paid for by craftsmen of a coin-casting workshop, while the national list dates the surviving structure to the Liao dynasty. Taishan Palace beside it hosts the town's biggest temple fair on the 18th day of the fourth lunar month.

rows.name: Xiong'an Suburban Park
rows.summary: Xiong'an Suburban Park is a large planted-woodland park on the northern edge of the Xiong'an New Area, opened in 2021 and covering about 26,000 mu (roughly 17 square kilometres). It has fourteen themed gardens, one for each of Hebei's eleven prefecture-level cities plus Xiong'an, Dingzhou and Xinji, along with a forest animal park and family areas, and suits a relaxed day outdoors.

rows.name: Xiude Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A tall octagonal brick pagoda about 32 metres high on the south-west side of Quyang town, the only part of Xiude Temple still standing. The present tower dates from 1019, although an inscription in its underground chamber traces a relic pagoda on the spot back to 601. Its second storey is covered in small niches, a style known as a 'flower pagoda', and some of the Buddhist statues found at the temple site are shown at the Beiyue Temple exhibition hall nearby.

rows.name: Yaowang Temple, Anguo
rows.summary: The Medicine King Temple in Anguo, long known as northern China's herb-trading town, honours Pi Tong, a Han-dynasty general venerated as the god of medicine. Its origins are traced to the Eastern Han, and the present complex of about 3,200 square metres was laid out in the Yongle era (1403–24) around Pi Tong's tomb and extended in the Qing, with an archway, tomb pavilion, main hall, bell and drum towers and a hall of famous physicians. Temple fairs are traditionally held in spring and winter, peaking on the 28th day of the fourth lunar month and the 15th day of the tenth.

rows.name: Yesanpo National Park
rows.summary: Yesanpo is a mountain-and-river scenic area in Laishui County, where the Taihang and Yan ranges meet along the Juma River. Its best-known part is Baili Gorge, a series of narrow karst canyons with walkways and stairs, and the area also takes in river rafting, the Baicaopan forest reserve and a section of Great Wall at Longmen Gorge. It was badly damaged by the flooding of July–August 2023 and has since reopened.

rows.name: Yicihui Stone Pillar
rows.summary: The Yicihui Stone Pillar is a 7 m limestone pillar of the Northern Qi dynasty on a small mound in Shizhu village, set up as a memorial to the defeat of the Ge Rong uprising against the Northern Wei, at a mass grave of rebels where an earlier wooden post had stood. An octagonal shaft carries more than 4,000 characters of inscription explaining why it was raised, topped by a small three-bay stone house with carved eaves and Buddha figures, and a protective pavilion has stood over it since not long after 1956.

rows.name: Yishui Lake
rows.summary: A mountain reservoir south-west of Yi County, ringed by steep hills and usually seen from the water, with a waterside plank walkway along the cliffs of Laozi Peak. The lake takes its name from the Yi River, which features in the story of the assassin Jing Ke setting out for the state of Qin, and it pairs easily with nearby Taihang Water Town.

rows.name: Yong'an Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty pagoda on the edge of Tazhao village, the only part left of Yong'an Temple, whose other buildings were pulled down in 1952. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013. It is a quiet stop for visitors interested in Liao architecture, with no temple around it any more.

rows.name: Yongji Bridge, Zhuozhou
rows.summary: A long stone-arch bridge across the Juma River on the northern edge of Zhuozhou. The nine-arch main span was built in 1760 next to an earlier bridge begun in 1574, and long approach causeways with small culverts bring the whole structure to over 600 metres; its balustrades are carved with vases and lotus leaves. The bridge was repaired between 2008 and 2012 and now forms part of a riverside scenic area.

rows.name: Yugu Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave and spring in the Yesanpo area of Laishui County, which the Baoding government describes as a geological attraction and summer retreat. A spring, the Yugu Spring, lies beside the cave. It is one of the visitor districts of Yesanpo, alongside Baili Gorge, Longmen Tianguan and Baicaopan.

rows.name: Yunhua Valley
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Taihang range in Fuping County, built around a forested valley with streams and rock formations. It is one of several scenic areas in Fuping, alongside Tianshengqiao Waterfalls and the Jin-Cha-Ji memorial. It suits a nature-focused day out for visitors already in the Fuping area.

rows.name: Zhuozhou Twin Pagodas
rows.summary: The Zhuozhou Twin Pagodas are two octagonal Liao-dynasty brick pagodas, built to imitate timber construction, standing a few hundred metres apart in the northern part of the old town: Zhidu Temple Pagoda to the south, about 44 m high, and Yunju Temple Pagoda to the north, about 56 m. Both have been national heritage units since 2001.

rows.name: Zijingguan Pass
rows.summary: Zijingguan is one of the Great Wall's main passes, on the Juma River in Yi County, and with Juyongguan and Daomaguan it formed the 'Inner Three Passes' guarding the approaches to the capital region. It was fought over more than 140 times, and the Oirat Mongols broke through in 1449 after the Tumu Crisis; stretches of Ming wall and gates survive around Zijingguan village.

rows.name: Botou Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque founded in 1404 under the Ming and enlarged in the Chongzhen era (1628–44), with more than twenty timber buildings in Chinese rather than domed style, split into a main mosque and a separate women's mosque. A two-storey call-to-prayer tower about 20 m high stands at the front, followed by a middle courtyard and the main prayer hall with its upswept eaves. Chinese sources describe it as the earliest and largest surviving mosque in Hebei.

rows.name: Dan Bridge
rows.summary: A five-arch stone bridge begun in the late Ming, 69 m long and nearly 10 m wide, across an old course of the Hutuo River at Danqiao village; its arches differ in span, and the city describes it as a leading example of the Chinese multi-arch open-spandrel bridge. It was given its first large-scale repair in 2013–14 on a 'repair as before' basis, and the village around it has since been landscaped as a small scenic area.

rows.name: Dengying Bridge
rows.summary: A three-arch stone bridge, also called Dulin Bridge, built in 1594 and repaired in 1907 across an old course of the Hutuo River in the middle of Dulin town. Two small arches rise above the piers between the three main arches, the piers have triangular cutwaters, and the balustrade posts and panels carry carved monkeys, lions, qilin and story scenes. A stele of 1594 recording its construction stands beside it.

rows.name: Guangming Theatre, Hejian
rows.summary: A brick-and-timber theatre of 1934, funded by five local families and modelled on the Dawutai theatre in Tianjin in a mixed Chinese and Western style, with a four-storey front, a relief 'Guangming' plaque and Baroque-style gables. Inside, a two-level auditorium with side boxes holds over a thousand people and faces a front and a rear stage. During the War of Resistance a number of important meetings of the Jizhong administrative office were held here.

rows.name: Haifengzhen Ruins and Site Museum
rows.summary: The site of Haifengzhen, a salt-trading port town of the Jin and Yuan dynasties, spread over about 228 hectares of farmland east of Huanghua and excavated since 2000. A site museum opened in 2019 shows finds in three sections, on the salt town, its trade and its place as the 'northern starting point of the Maritime Silk Road'; they include porcelain from kilns as far apart as Ding and Longquan. Walking paths and protective fencing have been laid around the unexcavated ground.

rows.name: Han Tombs in Xian County
rows.summary: A group of Han-dynasty burials east of Xian County town, the best known being the tomb of Liu De, Prince Xian of Hejian, a son of Emperor Jing remembered for reviving Confucian scholarship, with the tombs of later Han princes of Hejian nearby. The burial mound survives, and the county museum in Xian town devotes a gallery, 'Great Han Confucian Legacy', to the Hejian kingdom.

rows.name: Hejian Prefectural Government Office
rows.summary: The seat of Hejian prefecture, first set up in 1108 under the Northern Song and rebuilt on its original site in 2010–13 after standing in ruins for decades. The compound has more than 60 buildings and about 300 rooms in three rows along an axis, with the main hall, offices, residence, prison office and temples, and seven exhibition sections covering local history, official culture, intangible heritage and clean-governance culture. It suits a short visit together with the nearby Guangming Theatre.

rows.name: Iron Buddha Temple, Dongguang
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in a park on the southern edge of Dongguang town, built around a seated cast-iron Shakyamuni in the main hall that the county gives as over 8 m high and 48 tonnes, and that the city government describes as the largest seated iron Buddha in China. The temple began as Puzhao Temple in the early Northern Song and holds 33 Buddha images in all; its gate plaque was written by the calligrapher and Buddhist leader Zhao Puchu. The park also has a lake, a Taoist temple on a mound called Erlanggang, a Mount Tai shrine and memorial halls to the Yuan dramatist Ma Zhiyuan and the Peking-opera performer Xun Huisheng, both linked to Dongguang.

rows.name: Iron Lion of Cangzhou
rows.summary: Cast in 953 under the Later Zhou, this hollow iron lion carries a lotus-shaped basin on its back and is among the oldest and largest surviving iron castings in China; accounts of its weight range from about 32 to 50 tonnes. It stands under a protective roof inside Jiuzhou, the old walled city of Cangzhou, where stretches of the Song-period earth wall can still be traced, and the Iron Lion and Old City Site Park around it has an exhibition hall, a folk-culture hall and the site of an iron-coin storehouse. A replica poured in 2010 and completed in 2011, about a third larger, stands in Lion City Park in Cangzhou itself.

rows.name: Jiedi Flood-Diversion Sluice
rows.summary: A flood-control complex where the South Canal meets the Jiedi relief channel, one of the Hebei parts of the Grand Canal protected as a national monument. A diversion sluice has stood here since 1490; the present eight-bay sluice dates from 1933, and the provincial heritage bureau says its German Siemens hoists still work. Stone pavilions beside it shelter an imperial stele of 1771 carrying a poem by the Qianlong Emperor on the works, and a Qing notice of 1872 setting out eight rules for maintaining the canal and relief-channel embankments, in a garden laid out as the Imperial Stele Garden.

rows.name: Juguan Ancient Tribute Jujube Garden
rows.summary: An orchard of about 1,000 mu (roughly 66 hectares) of winter jujube trees at Juguan village that supplied fruit to the Ming and Qing courts. It holds 198 trees put at more than 600 years old and 1,067 more than a century old, and the Huanghua museum says it is the only plant population in China protected as a national cultural relic. The fruit ripens in autumn, and a wooden fence marking the protected boundary and a rebuilt guard house were added in 2018–19.

rows.name: Machang Battery
rows.summary: A late-Qing earth fort beside the Grand Canal, begun in 1871 when Li Hongzhang moved two battalions of the Huai Army here to guard the canal; the camp had 14 batteries on the two banks. What survives is a circular central battery of three stacked tiers with a hidden passage, a crescent-shaped battery beside it, earth platforms of the other batteries and stretches of the camp wall.

rows.name: Nandagang Wetland
rows.summary: A coastal marsh on the west shore of the Bohai Sea, about 90 per cent covered by reed beds, with open water, meadow and salt-tolerant plants. Experts have recorded 268 bird species here, including red-crowned and white cranes, swans, spoonbills and oriental storks, and there are observation platforms for watching them. The best times are the spring and autumn migrations, and the wetland was added in 2024 to the UNESCO World Heritage listing for the Yellow Sea and Bohai Gulf migratory bird habitats.

rows.name: Tomb of Ji Xiaolan
rows.summary: The shared grave of Ji Yun (1724–1805), better known as Ji Xiaolan, the Qing scholar who was chief editor of the Siku Quanshu, and his wife; it is an earth mound with a stele granted by the Jiaqing Emperor. Beside it the county opened the China Grand Canal Ji Xiaolan Cultural Park in 2023, with a tomb garden, an exhibition hall on his life and two themed gardens, Yuewei and Siku.

rows.name: Wuqiao Acrobatics World
rows.summary: A performance park opened in 1993 in Wuqiao, the county known as the home of Chinese acrobatics, covering about 36 hectares. Its main attraction is the Jianghu Culture City, a walled street recreating the market scenes of early 20th-century Wuqiao, where performers stage stunts, hard-qigong feats and magic; the park also has an acrobatics museum, theatres, a 'comic zoo' and a circus amusement area. It is a commercial attraction, so expect staged entertainment rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Xiejiaba Dam
rows.summary: A rammed-earth flood dam on the east bank of the South Canal at Lianzhen, built in the late Qing from layers of lime-soil bound with glutinous-rice mortar. It is 218 m long, 3.6 m thick and 5 m high, one of only two such dams left on the Hebei stretch of the canal, and the only World Heritage point on the Cangzhou section. A water-engineering exhibition hall opened nearby in 2021, and conservation repairs on the dam began in 2024.

rows.name: Anyuan Temple
rows.summary: A Qing temple of 1764 on a hill east of the Wulie River, built for the Dashidawa, an Oirat Mongol group resettled at Rehe, and modelled on the Gurzha Temple beside the Ili River in Xinjiang, which gave it the nickname Yili Temple. The main building, the Pudu Hall, is about 27 m high and has a roof of black glazed tiles, said to guard against the fire that destroyed the original. The temple was restored in the 1980s and again in 2011.

rows.name: Bancheng Liquor Museum Park, Chengde County
rows.summary: A distillery-based tourist park run by the Bancheng liquor company in Xiabancheng, the seat of Chengde County. It combines liquor-culture displays, viewing of the brewing process and hands-on experiences, and its museum holds more than 2,000 exhibits, including a 1:4 enlarged replica of a Jin-dynasty still excavated in 1975. It has also been named a national study-tour base and is used for school groups.

rows.name: China Horse Town (Mazhen), Fengning
rows.summary: A modern resort town on the Bashang plateau in northern Fengning, themed on horse culture and built around staged performances. By day it stages a dancing-horse show and a live drama, 'Zhao Zilong, God of War', in a Shangdu-themed set that visitors can walk through, and evenings bring bonfire gatherings and fire shows. It suits families and groups on a grassland trip who want shows and activities rather than open landscape.

rows.name: City God Temple, Chengde
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty temple to the city god in the old Erdao Pailou quarter of Chengde, a short way west of the Mountain Resort, listed as a national heritage site in 2006. The quarter's 2021–2035 conservation plan calls for repairs to the temple and encourages cultural displays and folk-custom activities in its heritage buildings. It is run as a small A-level tourist site and suits visitors with spare time in the old town rather than as a main stop.

rows.name: Dingsheng Cultural Industry Park
rows.summary: A modern cultural-tourism complex at the foot of Yuanbao Hill in Shuangluan District, built around an evening outdoor drama and an old-style shopping street. The show, 'Dingsheng Dynasty: the Kangxi Ceremony', uses the hillside as its backdrop, with hundreds of performers and several horses staging scenes of the Mulan hunt, court ritual and southern China, and local media report more than 2,700 performances and over 4.3 million visitors. Yuanbao Street below has craft stalls, snacks and costumed street performances, and the park suits families and groups who want an evening show.

rows.name: Dong Cunrui Martyrs' Cemetery and Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial park in the town of Longhua for Dong Cunrui, a People's Liberation Army soldier who died in May 1948 detonating an explosive charge at a Nationalist bunker during the fighting at Longhua, and who was later widely publicised as a model soldier. Laid out from 1954 on about 9 ha, it has a memorial arch, a granite monument, a statue of Dong, his tomb, inscription corridors and a memorial hall rebuilt in 2008, with the site of his death about 200 m outside the park. It is a national patriotic education base and was listed among China's classic red-tourism scenic areas in 2004.

rows.name: Great Khan's Palace, Fengning
rows.summary: A modern themed complex on the Bashang grassland in northern Fengning that sets out to recreate a Mongol-Yuan court, with palace-style halls and yurt-style buildings laid out across the plain. Chengde officials describe it as an immersive recreation of Mongol-Yuan history, and visitors can ride horses and try traditional archery. It is a new-built attraction rather than a historic palace, and suits families and groups touring the grassland.

rows.name: Guandi Temple, Fengshan
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty temple to Guan Yu, the god of war and loyalty, in the old town of Fengshan, the former county seat of Fengning, listed as a national heritage site in 2013. The compound has an ornamental archway, a main hall and an opera stage protected as part of the same group, and repairs have been phased since 2020; the temple fair is on Chengde's list of intangible heritage. It suits visitors interested in old market-town architecture.

rows.name: Imperial Steles and Cliff Inscription of the Mulan Hunting Ground
rows.name_zh: 木兰围场御制碑、摩崖石刻
rows.pinyin: Mùlán Wéichǎng Yùzhì Bēi, Móyá Shíkè
rows.summary: Seven Qing imperial steles (six by the Qianlong Emperor and one by the Jiaqing Emperor) and a cliff inscription recording a tiger killed in the 1752 hunt, all tied to the Mulan autumn hunt in the imperial hunting ground centred on today's Weichang County. Some are carved in Manchu, Chinese, Mongolian and Tibetan, and many were damaged in the 20th century and have been pieced together and re-erected in recent decades. One pair stands at Miaogong village, where the Qianlong stele "Composed on Entering the Pass" and the Jiaqing "Record of Mulan" face each other across the Yixun River.

rows.name: Panlong Lake, Kuancheng
rows.summary: A large lake in the hills of Kuancheng Manchu Autonomous County where the Great Wall runs down into the water, so that stretches of wall can be seen under the surface in clear conditions. Boats run along the cliff-lined shore to see this 'underwater Great Wall', and the lake also has kayaks and motorboats and is one of the national rowing team's training bases. It suits a half-day outing on the water, and local routes link it with the Xifengkou Great Wall.

rows.name: Pule Temple
rows.summary: A Qing temple built in 1766–67 on a rise east of the Wulie River, with a Chinese-style front half and a Tibetan-style rear half. The rear is dominated by the Xuguang Pavilion, a round double-eaved hall about 23 m high standing on a three-tier terrace, with a large wooden mandala and a bronze double-figure Samvara inside. Unlike most of its neighbours it never had resident monks and was run by the Imperial Household Department.

rows.name: Puning Temple
rows.summary: A Qing imperial temple built in 1755–59 after the Qing campaign against the Dzungar Mongols, nicknamed the Big Buddha Temple. Its front half follows a Chinese seven-hall plan, while the rear half is a Tibetan-style mandala modelled on Samye Monastery in Tibet, centred on the Mahayana Hall, which holds a gilded wooden Guanyin with a thousand arms and eyes that stands more than 20 m high. It is still a working Buddhist temple, and the adjoining Puyou Temple, built in 1760 as a monastic college and now displaying carved wooden arhat statues, is reached through a door inside it.

rows.name: Puren Temple
rows.summary: Built in 1713 at the request of Mongol princes who came to celebrate the Kangxi Emperor's 60th birthday, this is the earliest of the Eight Outer Temples and the only surviving temple at Chengde from Kangxi's reign. It follows the Chinese seven-hall plan, with a gate, a Hall of Heavenly Kings, a main hall and a rear hall, while its sister temple Pushan, to the north, survives only as foundations.

rows.name: Putuo Zongcheng Temple
rows.summary: A vast Qing imperial temple built in 1767–71 on a mountain slope and modelled on the Potala Palace in Lhasa, which earned it the nickname Little Potala; it is the largest of the Eight Outer Temples. Its core is the Great Red Terrace, a red block about 25 m high, with the Wanfa Guiyi Hall, roofed in gilded copper tiles, at its centre. The stele pavilion near the entrance carries inscriptions recording the return of the Torghut Mongols and their submission to the Qing.

rows.name: Qicai Forest, Fengning
rows.summary: A forest holiday park on the Bashang plateau in northern Fengning, built on state forest-farm land around a lake, white-birch woods and wooden boardwalks. Visitors ride a sightseeing miniature train through the trees, walk boardwalks over wetland and visit an animal farm and pet park. County and city officials present it as a summer outing for families, and it is usually combined with nearby China Horse Town.

rows.name: Qingchui Peak National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the hills east of Chengde's centre, named for Qingchui Peak, a tall hammer-shaped rock pillar (also called Bangchui Mountain, 'club mountain') above the Wulie River. A cable car and footpaths climb the slope to viewing platforms over the city and the river, and local media describe the red rock walls as Danxia-type and a favourite for autumn colour. The peak is mentioned in the Shuijing zhu, a 6th-century geography, and the Mountain Resort's garden is described as borrowing it as a distant view.

rows.name: Rehe Chinese Herbal Flower Town
rows.summary: A herb-growing farm and ecological study park on terraced hillsides in Xiayingzi village, Jingoutun town, in the Yan Mountains of Luanping County. It grows over 120 kinds of medicinal plants, with skullcap on about 100 hectares, and has walking trails, a medicinal-plant exhibition hall, a study classroom and a hands-on herb centre; the herbs flower from early summer. Hebei named it a provincial biodiversity experience site in 2026, and it receives school study groups as well as day-trippers.

rows.name: Saihanba National Forest Park
rows.summary: A planted-forest park on the high Saihanba plateau in northern Weichang County, once part of the Qing dynasty's Mulan imperial hunting ground. Farming and logging had stripped the land bare before a state forest farm began replanting it in 1962 with a founding team of 369 people; today there are larch and spruce plantations, lakes, grassland, forest walks and an exhibition hall at the farm's headquarters town. The planters won the UN Environment Programme's Champions of the Earth award in 2017, and a 2023 report put the part of the farm open to visitors at about 1.35 per cent of its area.

rows.name: Shanzhuang Laojiu Liquor Culture Park, Pingquan
rows.summary: A working distillery estate on the edge of Pingquan city that is open as a tourist site, centred on the China Royal Liquor Culture Plaza. Its buildings are modelled on ancient wine vessels (the office block on a four-ram bronze zun, the museum on a winged cup), and it has a liquor museum with more than 500 wine vessels, a technology museum, cellars over 300 years old and a production viewing area. The museum says the Kangxi Emperor gave the 'Shanzhuang Laojiu' name after a banquet at the Mountain Resort in 1703, and the park suits visitors curious about baijiu, the Chinese grain spirit.

rows.name: Shuangta Mountain
rows.summary: Two tall rock pillars rise side by side beside the Luan River on the western edge of Chengde city, in Shuangluan District. Local media describe a Danxia-type landscape of rock peaks and woods, with a cable car between the peaks, stone steps and footpaths, and a feeding platform for a troop of monkeys. It suits a short climb or ropeway outing from the city.

rows.name: Shuxiang Temple, Chengde
rows.summary: A Qing temple built in 1774–75 on the slope north of the Mountain Resort, dedicated to Manjusri and modelled on the Shuxiang Temple at Mount Wutai in Shanxi. It is a Chinese-style temple with a rockery garden meant to evoke Wutai, and its Baoxiang Pavilion is described as housing a wooden Manjusri on a lion about 11.6 m high. The Qing court used it as a favourite family temple, with Manchu lamas in residence.

rows.name: Tangjiawan Scenic Area, Chengde County
rows.summary: A resort area in Cangzi township, Chengde County, built around red Danxia sandstone peaks, Tianmen Lake and a hot spring. Local media count more than 20 Danxia peaks and ridges, with hiking routes through Qingliang Valley and Tianmen Mountain, a children's play area, a lodge and a fluoride spring, and the area was upgraded in 2026 with new lawns, photo spots and costumed actors. It suits families and short stays from Chengde and nearby cities.

rows.name: Xinglong Karst Cave
rows.summary: A show cave in the Yan Mountains of Xinglong County, in Taojiatai village in the foothills south of Wuling Mountain. Local state media report three chambers covering more than 4,000 square metres with eight side passages and some 59 kinds of formation, including stalactites, stalagmites, columns and a soda straw about 4.35 m long, and a summer temperature of around 10 degrees Celsius. It suits a cool short stop on a Xinglong County trip, alongside Wuling Mountain Nature Reserve further north.

rows.name: Xinglong Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill-country scenic area in the Yan Mountains of Xinglong County, with steep rock peaks, dense forest, streams and cliff-side plank walkways, plus a vertical lift up one cliff face. Local media describe a gently graded path network that older visitors and children can manage, named rock features such as Wanfo Cliff, and sea-of-cloud views. It sits beside Shishangzhuang, a village known for its poets, and local media say its forest was protected from felling for about 250 years under a feng shui ban.

rows.name: Xumi Fushou Temple
rows.summary: A Qing temple built in 1780 as a residence for the 6th Panchen Lama, who came to Chengde for the Qianlong Emperor's 70th birthday, and modelled on Tashilunpo Monastery in Shigatse. Its main block is the Great Red Terrace, whose central Miaogao Zhuangyan Hall has a roof of gilded copper tiles with eight gilded dragons, and a seven-storey glazed-tile pagoda stands at the rear. It lies next to Putuo Zongcheng Temple, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Yudaokou Grassland and Forest Scenic Area
rows.name_zh: 御道口草原森林风景区
rows.summary: A large state-farm landscape on the Bashang plateau in northern Weichang County, once part of the Qing imperial Mulan hunting ground, where the Kangxi Emperor drilled troops at the mouth of the Ruyi River. It lies at roughly 1,230–1,820 m and combines open grassland, birch and planted forest and many lakes, among them Moon Lake, Sun Lake and Taoshan Lake, and it borders the Saihanba forest area. It suits a summer day of driving and walking through open country rather than a visit to a single sight.

rows.name: Book of Songs Culture Park, Jize
rows.summary: A landscaped culture park in Jize county town named for the Book of Songs, the ancient poetry anthology whose surviving text is the version annotated by Mao Heng and Mao Chang, scholars that the Jize gazetteer counts as locals. The county government promotes it as a local leisure spot, and its media reported costume-style 'national style' shows and an intangible-heritage acrobatics programme there over the October 2026 holiday. It suits a short stop in Jize rather than a trip of its own.

rows.name: Changshou Village Scenic Area, Wu'an
rows.summary: A mountain village in Huoshui township, in the Taihang Mountains of western Wu'an, run as a scenic area for rest and health holidays, with guesthouses in converted village houses. It suits a quiet countryside weekend rather than a sightseeing checklist.

rows.name: Chaoyanggou, Wu'an
rows.summary: A wooded valley scenic area in the Taihang Mountains of north-west Wu'an, themed on the Henan opera Chaoyanggou, a 1958 play about an urban student who settles in a mountain village, and on rural 'educated youth' culture. Its museum, open since 2003, has nine exhibition areas, including one on the opera's author Yang Lanchun and others set out as a production team, a village school and the homes of characters from the play. It suits visitors interested in the opera or in rural-themed heritage, with mountain scenery around the village.

rows.name: Chengtang Temple Gate, She County
rows.summary: The surviving gate hall of Chengtang Temple in Jingdian village, built in 1164 under the Jin dynasty and repaired in 1555. It is three bays wide, with a single-eave hanging-gable roof edged in glazed tiles, an open timber roof frame and bracket sets with double lower ang under the front and rear eaves. Inscriptions on the octagonal stone pillars include one describing local damage from an earthquake in the Kangxi reign, and about a dozen stelae stand with it.

rows.name: Cishan Site
rows.summary: The type site of the Cishan culture, an early Neolithic farming culture, found in 1972 during irrigation work on the north bank of the Nanming river; its earliest layers have been dated to about 8,000 years ago. Excavations since 1976 uncovered house foundations, ash pits and grain-storage pits, with millet, the bones of domestic animals, mainly dogs and pigs and probably chickens, and more than 5,000 pottery, stone and bone objects. The visit centres on the Cishan Culture Museum beside the site, which also has a study centre and a small park.

rows.name: Cixian Northern Dynasties Tombs
rows.summary: A cluster of 134 burial mounds of Eastern Wei and Northern Qi rulers, nobles and officials, spread over the countryside south and south-west of Cixian town; 19 have been excavated, among them the tombs of Gao Run, of a Rouran princess and of the Wanzhang village tomb numbered 106. The finds are shown at the Northern Dynasties Archaeology Museum in Cixian, which holds about 3,000 objects, mostly from these tombs, including pottery figurines, porcelain, murals, tomb inscriptions and gold and silver ware. Two stone steles of the period still stand above ground among the mounds.

rows.name: Cizhou Kiln Site
rows.summary: The kilns around Pengcheng and Guantai made the white-slipped, black-painted stoneware known as Cizhou ware, from the late Northern Dynasties into the Republican period, and the site has been a national heritage unit since 1996. At Pengcheng, in Fengfeng Mining District, two kiln-site museums can be visited: Futian, with ten old kilns, five workshops, wells and clay-processing pits, and Yandian, with a Republican-era kiln, cave workshops, an excavated Yuan-dynasty kiln and demonstrations of the traditional firing process. It suits those interested in ceramics.

rows.name: Congtai Liquor Garden
rows.summary: A visitor park at the Congtai liquor distillery in Feixiang's economic development zone, built around a museum in Warring States and Han style with some 13,800 m² of floor space. The museum was set up in 2015 and has six sections on the origins of Chinese baijiu, the long history of brewing around Handan and the growth of the Zhenyuanzeng distillery, the present company's predecessor. It is a corporate attraction that mainly suits visitors curious about baijiu.

rows.name: Congtai Park
rows.summary: A city park in the middle of Handan, first planned in 1939 to protect the Wuling Congtai, a terraced tower traditionally linked to King Wuling of Zhao in the Warring States period. The three-storey tower, about 26 m high, dates from the Qing dynasty and has been restored since; it stands beside a lake in grounds of roughly 25 hectares that also hold a plum garden and a shrine to seven sages, with a stele carved with a poem written by Guo Moruo in 1961 outside the main gate. It is a convenient stop for anyone interested in Handan's history as the Zhao state's capital.

rows.name: Daming Ancient City
rows.summary: The walled county town of Daming, rebuilt in 1401 on the north bank of the Wei River after floods destroyed the Song-era city to the north-east, with walls about 4.5 km round and four gates. The north gate has a tower, and inside the walls are four main streets, eight lesser streets and some seventy lanes, which the county has been developing for tourism. Daming is best known to Chinese readers from the novel Water Margin, where it features in nineteen chapters, and is also known for its straw weaving and traditional snacks.

rows.name: Daming Stone Carving Museum
rows.summary: A museum of more than a hundred stone steles, epitaphs and carvings collected around Daming, housed in a hall on the eastern edge of the town. Its best-known piece is the Wuliji Stele, which the museum describes as the largest ancient stele in China, shown with the epitaph of He Hongjing, a stele carved with Zhu Xi's calligraphy and Ming-dynasty memorial inscriptions. It suits visitors interested in Chinese calligraphy and inscriptions.

rows.name: Dongshan Culture and Arts Park, Wu'an
rows.summary: A landscaped park on the east side of Wu'an, laid out in 2003 on about 500 mu (roughly 33 ha) with pavilions, bridges and ponds, and divided into seven zones that include geology, plants and folk-culture areas. Its main draw is the Wu'an Museum, opened in 2019 inside converted park buildings, whose seven halls include ancient history, the local ironmaking industry, intangible heritage and the revolutionary period. It suits a relaxed half-day out that mixes a municipal museum with general park leisure.

rows.name: East Taihang Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area on the eastern side of the Taihang range in north-west Wu'an, with a planned area of about 26 square kilometres and a highest point of 1,428 m at North Peak. Its landscape of red cliffs and gorges is classed as Zhangshiyan landform, and the area has a via ferrata (cliff-climbing) route on the rock face. It suits a day out from Wu'an or Handan for views and walking.

rows.name: Eighth Route Army 129th Division Headquarters
rows.name_zh: 八路军一二九师司令部旧址
rows.summary: Chi'an village in Henandian township was the headquarters of the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division under Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping during the war against Japan, and it is now a memorial complex. The headquarters consists of three northern-style courtyards, including the former Liu and Deng residence, and the complex also has an exhibition hall on the division's history and General's Ridge, a hillside where the ashes of Liu Bocheng, Xu Xiangqian and other senior officers of the division are interred. It is a red-tourism site, and the courtyards, hall and ridge together take about half a day.

rows.name: Fahuadong Grottoes, Wu'an
rows.summary: A small Song-dynasty cave temple in a hollow of Fahua Hill, north-east of Qingyansi village in the hills west of Wu'an, cut in 982 and added to in the Ming and Qing periods. Three caves lie side by side: the main central cave, about 7 m deep, carries more than 500 relief figures, mostly arhats, with a thousand-armed Guanyin on one wall, and the right-hand cave is a natural cave. Official descriptions note that the figures combine Central Plains Buddhist style with Tantric Tibetan Buddhist elements and mix Buddhist and Daoist features.

rows.name: Grain Painting Town, Guantao
rows.summary: A rural tourist village on the west side of Guantao, developed since 2014 from a poor village into a showcase 'beautiful village' planned over 3.7 square kilometres and organised as four adjoining village communities. Its streets of grey-roofed, white-walled houses have cafés, grain-painting workshops, a small cinema and restaurants, and more than 20 hands-on craft workshops cover grain painting, gourds, black pottery and cloth painting. It also has over 20 themed guesthouses and a hot-spring bathing facility, and suits families and short rural breaks rather than history.

rows.name: Gu Wudang Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Taihang range north-west of Wu'an, whose main summit, the Golden Peak, rises above 1,400 m. It has a cable car, plank walkways and a high footbridge, and since September 2023 it has also run night climbs to see the lit-up summit and the sunrise. A temple stele is said to record the mountain as Wudang Mountain from the Tang dynasty at the latest, which the scenic area cites to claim that its name is older than that of Hubei's better-known Wudang Mountain.

rows.name: Guangfu Ancient City
rows.summary: A walled Ming-dynasty prefectural city on a peninsula in the Yongnian wetland, with a moat outside walls about 4.5 km round that were rebuilt in brick from 1542. It is the home town of Yang Luchan and Wu Yuxiang, founders of the Yang and Wu styles of tai chi, and their former residences are among the sights, along with Ming and Qing courtyard houses. The old streets follow a grid of four main streets and eight smaller ones.

rows.name: Handan Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped park on the western edge of Handan, laid out for the 2020 Hebei Garden Expo on land that had held foundries, steel-slag works and construction-waste dumps. It has gardens for 13 Hebei cities, lakes lit up in the evening, industrial tanks left by a stone-crushing plant converted into a climbing wall, a petting zoo with peacocks and alpacas, and a children's play area. It suits families and relaxed outings rather than historic sightseeing.

rows.name: Hanwang Jiuzhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Taihang foothills south of She County town, in the Qingzhang River area, themed in part on the Han general Han Xin, with a 'Han King Valley', re-created 'Qin' and 'Han' stockade settings, hiking routes to summit viewpoints and mountain camping. In autumn colourful rice-paddy art is laid out across the valley below, and a new walking route to the summit, themed on Han Xin mustering troops, opened in spring 2026.
