It makes a half-day stop in a county that also has Nüwa Palace and the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division sites.

rows.name: Holy Mother Temple, Jiujiang
rows.summary: A small temple compound on the slope above Guantao village, in the hills north-west of Wu'an, dedicated to the Holy Mother (Shengmu). Its buildings date from the Yuan to the Qing dynasties, and it has been a national protected site since 2013. It is a quiet rural temple that suits a short stop for those interested in village temples of the Taihang foothills.

rows.name: Hongji Bridge
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty stone arch bridge over the Fuyang River at Dongqiao village, with a single main arch spanning 31.88 m and open spandrels, similar in form to the Zhaozhou Bridge. The deck is 48.9 m long and 6.82 m wide, the arch is made of 18 parallel rings bound with iron cramps, and the arch faces and balustrades are carved with dragons, a phoenix, a flying horse, lions and monkeys. An inscription on the central balustrade is dated to the tenth year of the Wanli reign (1582).

rows.name: Huangliangmeng Lüxian Temple
rows.summary: A Daoist temple complex north of Handan built around the Tang-dynasty tale of the Yellow Millet Dream, in which the scholar Lu Sheng naps on a pillow at an inn while millet steams and lives a whole career in his dream, only to wake before the meal is cooked. The main axis runs through a lotus pond, an octagonal pavilion and bell and drum towers to halls for the immortals Zhongli and Lü Dongbin and to a hall with a reclining figure of Lu Sheng, and more than thirty stone tablets record repairs, visitors' inscriptions and poems. Most surviving buildings date from the Ming and Qing periods.

rows.name: Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Border Region Government Site
rows.name_zh: 晋冀鲁豫边区政府旧址
rows.summary: The courtyards in Tanyin village, Suobao township, where the Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Border Region Government worked between 1942 and 1945, during the war against Japan. Eight courtyards make up the site, among them the government offices with a main hall and an opera stage, the high court, two canteens, a granary yard and the homes of officials including the chairman Yang Xiufeng, and all except Yang's residence, rebuilt in 2002, are said to keep their original form. It lies a short way south of the Nuwa Palace temple complex, so the two can be combined.

rows.name: Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Central Bureau and Military Region Site, Yetao
rows.name_zh: 中共晋冀鲁豫中央局和军区旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Jìnjìlǔyù Zhōngyāngjú Hé Jūnqū Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The courtyards in Yetao village that housed the Communist Party's Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu (Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan) Central Bureau and the region's military headquarters from 1946 to 1948, during the civil war. The listed buildings include the Central Bureau and military command courtyards, the former residences of Liu Bocheng, Deng Xiaoping, Li Da and Bo Yibo, and the meeting sites of the North China finance, southern-campaign and land conferences. The site now operates as the Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Border Region Revolutionary Memorial Museum, with six exhibition halls.

rows.name: Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery and museum in southern Handan, inaugurated in October 1950 with the reburial of General Zuo Quan and other soldiers of the Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu border region, and described as the first martyrs' cemetery built after the founding of the People's Republic. Zuo Quan's tomb, with an inscription by Zhou Enlai, stands in the grounds, and the cemetery is noted for the many inscriptions by senior Communist leaders. The site now also operates as the Jin-Ji-Lu-Yu Revolutionary Memorial Museum, whose collection runs to more than 21,000 items.

rows.name: Jingniang Lake
rows.summary: A mountain reservoir in the Taihang foothills of north-west Wu'an, formally the Koushang Reservoir (built 1966–69) and better known by the name of the folk tale in which the future Song founder Zhao Kuangyin rescues a kidnapped girl, Zhao Jingniang, and escorts her home. The scenic area has boat trips on the lake and through the narrow Jingniang Gorge, a shrine to Jingniang and steep cliffs around the water. The reservoir was listed as a national water-conservancy scenic area in 2005 and suits a day out in the hills.

rows.name: Main Hall of Changle Dragon King Temple
rows.summary: A Yuan-dynasty hall for worshipping the dragon king, standing about 50 m south-west of Changle village in Suobao town and counted among the few timber-framed Yuan buildings left in Hebei. It is three bays wide (10.10 m), two bays deep (12.15 m) and 6.55 m high. It is a small village temple rather than a developed attraction, and worth a stop for those interested in early timber architecture, for example when visiting nearby Nuwa Palace.

rows.name: Mother of Grace Cathedral, Daming
rows.summary: A Gothic-style Catholic church built by French missionaries between 1918 and 1921 and still the cathedral of the Diocese of Daming, so it remains a place of worship rather than a museum. The cruciform building has a tower with a four-faced clock, an arched interior carried on fourteen stone columns, over a hundred coloured-glass windows and a large organ at the north end. It stands on East Street inside the old walled town, so it can be combined with a walk round the ancient city.

rows.name: Nüwa Palace
rows.summary: A temple complex dedicated to the mythical goddess Nüwa, who is said to have mended the sky and made humankind, with halls and pavilions built out along the cliff face of Fenghuang (Phoenix) Mountain, the present buildings dating from the Ming and Qing periods. Beside it, Buddhist sutras of more than 130,000 characters were carved into the rock under the Northern Qi in the sixth century. Nüwa rituals held here are on China's national intangible heritage list, and the temple sees extra pilgrims around Tomb Sweeping Day.

rows.name: Qianfodong Grottoes, Quli
rows.summary: A single Ming-dynasty cave temple cut into a mountainside in the uplands of Shexian, about 4 km north-west of Quli village. The rectangular cave, about 34 square metres, holds a seated main Buddha around 3 m high flanked by twelve seated Bodhisattvas of the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra, and two columns running up to the ceiling, each carved with 16 rows of small Buddhas. Heritage authorities describe it as the only cave in Hebei to carve these twelve Bodhisattvas.

rows.name: Qibugou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain valley scenic area in the Taihang foothills of Huoshui township, north-west of Wu'an, near Qibugou village. Its attractions are scenic rather than historic: steep rock walls, a small mountain lake and waterfalls, and in spring 2026 state media reported a rose-planted section of the canyon with pools. It suits a half-day outing from Wu'an or Handan for walkers.

rows.name: Qingquan Temple, Shexian
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on a hillside south of Shigang village, south-east of Shexian town, said to have been founded in the Northern Qi dynasty during the Tiantong era (565–569) and named after a spring to the east of the temple. The buildings standing today date mainly from the Ming and Qing dynasties, and the temple became a national protected site in 2019. It is a quiet stop for visitors exploring Shexian's old temples.

rows.name: Shuiyusi Grottoes
rows.summary: A small cave temple in the hills about 4 km east of the northern Xiangtangshan caves, known locally as Little Xiangtang because it is smaller than the northern and southern groups. Its carvings range in date from the Northern Dynasties to the Ming, and it is usually counted as the third part of the Xiangtangshan cave complex. It is best taken as an add-on to a visit to the northern caves.

rows.name: Site of Damingfu Old City
rows.summary: The site of Daming Prefecture, which the Northern Song made its northern capital in 1042, centred on the villages of Dajie, Yuying and Shuangtai north-east of today's Daming. A flood in 1401 buried the city under silt, so most foundations lie 1–5 m underground and only four stretches of rammed-earth wall show above ground. A site museum opened in 2024 and shows the city through a model, multimedia displays, and archaeological finds and reconstructions.

rows.name: Taihang Wuzhi Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area south of Shexian town, named for five peaks that resemble the fingers of the Buddha's hand, the highest reaching 1,283 m. The attractions listed for it include a plaza, a cliffside plank walkway, a glass bridge, Wukong Valley, a ski slope and a statue of the monkey king Sun Wukong, which ties the peaks to the Journey to the West story of the monkey pinned beneath a mountain. It suits a half-day trip from Shexian for hiking and views.

rows.name: Tianbaozhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill-country scenic area around Huatuo village in Taoquan township, in the far west of Ci County, developed from 2017 by a county-owned coal company after its mine closed; villagers replanted the slopes with more than a million saplings. The county promotes it for autumn colour, and a 2022 provincial report listed seasonal projects there including a summer water-play area and a winter snow-and-ice carnival. Huatuo was the site of an Eighth Route Army arsenal in 1938–43 and has a museum on it.

rows.name: Tianqing Temple, Wu'an
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple among the houses of Cuilu village, whose main hall, built in the Ming dynasty, is the protected building. It has been a national protected site since 2013 and is quick to see.

rows.name: West Eight Sluices on the Fuyang River
rows.summary: Eight Ming-dynasty sluices on the Fuyang River west of the old city of Yongnian, strung out along the north bank between Xidaci and Tianbu villages and named from west to east Guangren, Puhui, Bianmin, Jimin, Guangji, Runmin, Huimin and Fumin. Five of them, the second, fourth, sixth, seventh and eighth, were reported still in use, while the first, third and fifth have been abandoned. It is a piece of waterworks rather than a developed attraction, so it mainly suits those interested in historic hydraulic engineering.

rows.name: Wu'an Sarira Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal, 13-storey brick pagoda built in 1091 under the Northern Song, the only surviving part of the former Miaojue Temple in Wu'an's old town. It is 41.66 m tall, with brick brackets copying timber ones under the eaves of every level, and the interior has chambers with brick imitation brackets and caissons on the first, second, third, fifth and ninth storeys. It was repaired in 1610 and 1906 and is one of the few Song brick pagodas still standing in southern Hebei.

rows.name: Xiangtangshan Caves
rows.summary: A group of Buddhist cave temples cut into the limestone of Mount Gu and Mount Fu, begun under the Eastern Wei and carved chiefly under the Northern Qi (550–577), whose capital stood at nearby Ye. The northern group is the main stop, with large caves built around central pillars, such as the Big Buddha Cave, and Buddhist sutras carved into the rock; the southern group, about 12 km away, has smaller caves with carved sutras and a site museum beside it. Many heads and reliefs were chiselled off in the early twentieth century and are now in museums abroad, so some figures on site are later replacements.

rows.name: Ye City Site
rows.summary: Ye was the capital of Cao Cao's Wei state and later of the Later Zhao, Ran Wei, Former Yan, Eastern Wei and Northern Qi, until it was burned in 580. Little stands above ground: in a small park at Santai village the Jinfeng Terrace of Cao Cao's Three Terraces still rises about 12 m and a corner of the Bronze Bird Terrace survives, while the Ye Museum about 2 km to the north-east, whose main building is modelled on a gate of the Eastern Wei and Northern Qi city, displays finds including Buddhist statues unearthed in 2012. This is the Hebei part of a site that continues across the provincial border into Henan.

rows.name: Yuquan Temple, Shexian
rows.summary: A village temple in Shangwen, north-west of Shexian town, whose main hall dates from the Jin and Yuan dynasties. The hall has been a national protected building since 2013 and makes a short stop for visitors interested in early temple architecture.

rows.name: Zhao Royal City, Handan
rows.summary: The remains of Handan, capital of the state of Zhao from 386 to 228 BC, in the south-west of the modern city, of which the visitable part is the Zhao Royal City, the palace quarter. It consists of three joined walled enclosures (west, east and north) with stretches of rammed-earth wall and large palace platforms, the biggest being the Dragon Terrace in the western enclosure. Since 2022 it has been presented as a national archaeological site park, with a site museum whose design echoes the terrace and a neighbouring Zhao-culture park, while the much larger commoners' city lies mostly buried under modern Handan.

rows.name: Zhaowang Impression City
rows.summary: A corporate culture-and-tourism park in Guangping, run by a food and liquor producer and themed on the Warring States state of Zhao. Its four zones include a culture hall whose main building is styled as the palace of King Wuling of Zhao, a working production area that visitors can view, and cultural activities on Zhao and liquor themes. State media reported horse-riding parades, a war-drum show and costumed role-play there during the 2026 Spring Festival and May Day holidays.

rows.name: Zhaoyuan Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped park in north-west Handan, opened in 2004 and built in the style of the Warring States Zhao kingdom, with lakes, lotus ponds and a series of themed garden zones. Inside are earthen remains that local archaeologists link to Zhao-period metalworking, including a platform about 9 m high known as the arrow-casting furnace, and a Han tomb, and one garden presents idioms that originated in Handan. It is a local green space that suits a short walk when in the city.

rows.name: Zhifang Yuhuang Pavilion
rows.summary: A Ming-period brick pavilion named for the Jade Emperor, standing in West Zhifang village on the north bank of the Fuyang River and also called the Beamless Pavilion because its brick structure has no timber beams. A repair tablet beneath it indicates that it was first built in the Longqing or Wanli reigns (1567–1620) and rebuilt in 1896. It is about 450 m from the southern Xiangtangshan caves, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Zhushan Inscription
rows.summary: A 15-character seal-script inscription carved on a sloping rock face at the top of Zhu Hill, about 1 km north of Wuzhuang village, whose text records ministers of the state of Zhao offering a toast in the 22nd year of its reign. Official accounts now date it to 158 BC, under the Western Han kingdom of Zhao, although it was once classed as fourth-century Later Zhao. The hill has been laid out as a cultural park and botanical garden around it, and rubbings of the inscription are held by museums in Britain, France and Japan.

rows.name: Anji Bridge, Hengshui
rows.summary: A seven-arch stone bridge over the Fuyang River in Hengshui's old town, 116 m long, with 58 posts along each side topped by carved stone lions, some of them restored. The present bridge dates from 1766 and was built on the remains of Ming bridges; its central arch was blown up by Japanese troops in 1937 and later rebuilt in concrete, which the recent restoration kept as a record of the war, with a plaque explaining it. The bridge reopened to pedestrians in 2022 after more than two years of repairs.

rows.name: Baoyun Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda about 35 m tall, standing in the grounds of Baoyun Temple at Jiucheng village on the south-western edge of Hengshui. Its lowest two levels show Tang-style detailing and the upper levels Song features, and heritage experts date it to the early Northern Song; it has been nationally protected since 2006. After repairs the pagoda and its temple grounds reopened to visitors in 2014, and many locals visit on the 15th and 16th days of the first lunar month.

rows.name: Dongzi Xue Village, Gucheng
rows.summary: A cultural-tourism village at Dongxue village, Fangzhuang town, where local tradition says the Western Han Confucian scholar Dong Zhongshu taught behind a lowered curtain, giving the village its old name Xiawei. It was developed in recent years for study tours, with four themed parts: the Dongxue garden on Confucian learning, a ten-li 'long street' on local customs, farm fields for field-work lessons and the Siyuan River for nature study. It is a modern themed village built around that tradition rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Hengshui Lake
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A freshwater lake and wetland reserve on the south side of Hengshui, with about 75 sq km of water plus marsh, mudflats, meadow and woodland; it is described as the second-largest freshwater lake on the North China Plain after Baiyangdian. More than 330 bird species have been recorded, with swans and geese wintering and autumn migration peaking in mid to late November, so it is best known for birdwatching and for cycling round the shore. The developed visitor area is on the north shore, in a former garden-expo park that now holds the Hengshui Ecology Museum.

rows.name: Hengshui Laobaigan Distillery
rows.summary: A visitor area built around the working plant of Hengshui Laobaigan, a baijiu (Chinese grain spirit) maker whose traditional brewing method is a national intangible heritage item. The plant's earthen-jar fermentation workshop holds 47,666 jars under about 61,000 sq m of floor space and was certified by Guinness World Records in 2021 as the largest of its kind, and a museum in the complex explains jar fermentation and the history of liquor-making. It is a corporate attraction best suited to visitors interested in baijiu or industrial tourism.

rows.name: Jingzhou Pagoda
rows.summary: A thirteen-storey octagonal pagoda of brick and stone, 63.85 m tall, rising above the town of Jingxian. The present structure was rebuilt in 1079 in Song style; iron plaques record earlier repairs under the Northern Qi and Sui, and the first pagoda may date from the Northern Wei. It has been a national heritage site since 1996 and is counted among Hebei's 'four ancient treasures' with the Cangzhou iron lion, Zhaozhou Bridge and the bronze Bodhisattva of Longxing Temple.

rows.name: Jizhou Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: The surviving walls and moat of old Jizhou, a city that dates back to 201 BC, when it was founded under the name Xindu, on the south-western shore of Hengshui Lake. About 3 km of rammed-earth wall, up to roughly 9 m high, and some 2 km of moat still stand above ground, and the area is laid out as a ruins park with railings and signs. It is an earthwork site rather than a museum, so it suits history-minded visitors and pairs well with the nearby lake and the Jizhou Museum in town.

rows.name: Qinglin Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A tall octagonal brick pagoda in pavilion style, built in the early Northern Song and about 35 m high, in Raoyangdian town in western Gucheng County. A repair project was completed in 2013, and it has been a nationally protected site since 2006. It is a short stop for pagoda enthusiasts rather than a full excursion.

rows.name: Taicheng First Rural Party Branch Memorial
rows.summary: A memorial museum in Taicheng village, Anping County, devoted to the Taicheng special branch of the Chinese Communist Party, which party history and state media present as the first rural branch, founded in August 1923 by Gong Zhongtao under Li Dazhao's guidance. Its displays also cover the first county party committee in Hebei, set up in Anping in August 1924, and Anping's wartime role as a command centre of the central Hebei base area. The exhibition was fully refreshed for the branch's centenary in 2023, and the site is used for school and party-study visits.

rows.name: Wuqiang New Year Picture Museum
rows.summary: A museum in Wuqiang, long known for woodblock New Year pictures (nianhua), which describes itself as the first museum in China devoted to the craft and was approved in 1985. Its collection includes more than 10,000 historic woodblocks and printed pictures from the Ming and Qing dynasties onwards, and hands-on woodblock printing is offered to visitors. A good fit for anyone interested in folk art and festival customs.

rows.name: Yingyi Granary, Shenzhou
rows.summary: A courtyard-style Qing granary in the middle of Shenzhou, dating from 1898, with an administrative courtyard to the east and a storage courtyard to the west; its 51 rooms could hold about 1,500 tonnes of grain. Local heritage officials describe it as the only fully preserved Qing granary found north of the Yellow River. After repairs it reopened in 2019 as the Shenzhou Granary Museum, with five themed exhibitions on grain, food and storage customs.

rows.name: Zhouwo Music Town
rows.summary: A village-based visitor area at Zhouwo in Wuqiang County, a place that began making Western wind and string instruments more than 30 years ago and has turned village homes into music-themed shops, workshops, cafés and guesthouses since 2012. There is a world musical-instruments museum with well over a thousand instruments, and villagers play saxophone and other instruments for visitors. It is a small, informal place that suits visitors interested in music or in how a Hebei village reinvented itself.

rows.name: CITIC Guoan First City, Xianghe
rows.summary: A large leisure complex developed by the CITIC Guoan group in Xianghe, built on the model of Ming and Qing Beijing with a walled-city layout and palace-and-garden-style buildings, covering about 3,320 mu (roughly 2.2 square kilometres). It has a lotus garden and an old temple, Da'an Temple, inside its grounds, hosts seasonal events such as a lotus festival and Spring Festival fairs, and since April 2025 has run an immersive Ming-themed park called Daming Fantasy with costumed performers around the site. It is a modern commercial development rather than historic buildings, and suits Beijing-area day-trippers.

rows.name: China Redwood City, Dacheng
rows.summary: A large market complex of traditional-style halls and courtyards in Dacheng County, which state media call north China's largest hub for making and trading redwood (hongmu, meaning rosewood and other hardwood) furniture. The county government gives its site as 730 mu (about 49 hectares) with more than a thousand traders selling classical-style furniture and carvings, and a large weekly redwood market is held there on Tuesdays. It grew out of the county's long-running redwood and antiques market, which moved to a new redwood-culture district in 2014, and is a shopping and trade venue rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Daxinge Stone Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty stone pagoda in Daxinge village, Yongqing, standing in the grounds of the White Pagoda (Baita) Temple. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 1982 and as a national one in 2013, and Yongqing's tourism bureau named the temple among the county's sights in 2024. It is a short stop for pagoda enthusiasts.

rows.name: Golden Key Furniture Mall, Xianghe
rows.summary: A large furniture mall opened in 2003 in Xianghe's furniture-trading district, with about 180,000 square metres of floor space on four floors: general and brand-name furniture, European-style pieces and a redwood hall. State media list it among Xianghe's tourism brands and call Xianghe's furniture city north China's biggest furniture distribution hub, but it is a showroom complex rather than a sight in the usual sense. Visit only if you want to browse furniture.

rows.name: Mengdongfang Future World
rows.summary: An indoor space-themed activity park in Yanjiao, the commuter town of Sanhe on Beijing's eastern edge, inside the Tianyang City development. Exhibits and activities aimed at families and school groups have included astronaut-training equipment, a space medical centre, a genetics centre and spacesuit photos. It is a commercial attraction that suits children and visitors staying in the Beijing area.

rows.name: Yannanchun Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: A liquor-culture visitor park attached to the Yannanchun distillery in Yongqing's industrial area, built around a museum that traces Chinese liquor-making and local history under a Song–Liao theme, with several hundred objects. The grounds include a Song–Liao-style pedestrian street and a peony garden of nearly 10,000 plants that holds a festival each spring, and visitors can taste the distillery's baijiu (Chinese grain spirit). A corporate attraction suited to visitors with an interest in baijiu.

rows.name: Banchangyu Brick Kiln Sites
rows.summary: Remains of Ming kilns beside Banchangyu village, where bricks were fired for the Great Wall. A survey has recorded 136 kiln sites, mostly brick kilns, over about 160,000 square metres, and the group joined the national list in 2013. It is a low-key archaeological site close to the Banchangyu stretch of the Great Wall.

rows.name: Beidaihe Historic Villas
rows.summary: A seafront resort district of villas built from the 1890s for foreign residents and wealthy Chinese, after the Qing government named Beidaihe a summer resort for people of all nations in 1898. Twenty buildings are on the national list, among them the five-villa Wufenglou group and a church, out of roughly 110 old villas that survived to 2013. Many are now hotels, restaurants or offices, so most are best seen from the street while walking the seafront between Lianfeng Hill and Pigeon Nest Park.

rows.name: Biluota Sea Bar Park
rows.summary: A seafront leisure park on the easternmost stretch of Beidaihe's beach, opened in 2013 and laid out like a small peninsula between Jinshanzui and Pigeon Nest Park. It is built around a conch-shaped tower and is aimed at evenings more than daytime sightseeing, with bars, a seaside stage and live shows, including electronic-music sets by resident DJs. It is a modern leisure development, not a historic site.

rows.name: Bingtangyu Great Wall Canyon
rows.name_zh: 冰塘峪长城风情大峡谷
rows.summary: A mountain canyon scenic area in the hills north-west of Qinhuangdao, named for the Great Wall remains on the ridges above the valley. It suits walkers and families on a day trip from the coast.

rows.name: Changli Sand-Sliding Centre
rows.name_zh: 昌黎县旅游滑沙活动中心
rows.pinyin: Chānglí Xiàn Lǚyóu Huáshā Huódòng Zhōngxīn
rows.summary: A sand-sliding centre on the Changli Golden Coast, where visitors slide down sand dunes close to the beach. It is a small leisure venue rather than a sightseeing stop, set on a coast known for its long beaches and dunes.

rows.name: Changshou Mountain
rows.summary: A small rocky hill north of Shanhaiguan, laid out as a scenic area with footpaths up its slopes. It is mainly a local day-walk rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Dharani Sutra Pillar, Lulong
rows.name_zh: 大佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经幢
rows.summary: A Jin-dynasty stone sutra pillar in the old town of Lulong, about 10 metres tall and built in six tiers. Pillars of this kind carry Buddhist dharani texts, and this one was listed nationally in 2006 after provincial protection from 1982. The Yongping city wall is about 250 m to the west, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Former Yaohua Glass Factory
rows.summary: The surviving core of the Yaohua glass factory, founded in 1922 and described as China's first large mechanised glassworks: a two-storey Gothic power house, a pump house and a water tower. The power house is now the main hall of the Qinhuangdao Glass Museum, which opened in 2012 as the country's first state-run museum on glass. Its displays cover ancient glass, the Chinese glass industry and glassmaking today.

rows.name: Huaxia Manor Winery
rows.summary: A wine estate on the northern edge of Changli, one of China's wine-growing counties, with vineyards and a winery that visitors can see and where they can taste wine. It is a commercial tourist estate, so it suits a short stop rather than a full day.

rows.name: Jiaoshan Great Wall
rows.summary: A mountain section of the Ming Great Wall running up from Shanhaiguan to the flat summit of Jiaoshan, with the Hanmen Pass and Qixian Temple on the way. The lower wall was restored in the 1980s and part of it can be climbed for views of the town and the sea, while higher up it is left in its original, crumbling state. At the foot of the hill, the Shanhaiguan China Great Wall Museum holds more than 5,000 relics and has four permanent exhibition halls.

rows.name: Jifa Agricultural Dream Kingdom
rows.summary: A family-oriented farm and leisure park in Beidaihe that mixes agricultural exhibits with play areas. In summer it also stages evening light shows along the Dai River, including a lantern festival with lanterns made in Zigong and drone displays. It is a modern commercial attraction aimed at families with children.

rows.name: Ledao Ocean Kingdom
rows.summary: An ocean-themed park on the coast south of Shanhaiguan, with staged shows by dolphins, sea lions and beluga whales, a large wave pool and water slides, and a beach for sand and water play. It is a day out for families rather than a historic stop.

rows.name: Lianfeng Mountain Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill park behind the western end of Beidaihe's seafront, with two low peaks covered in pines and cypresses, rock formations, caves, pavilions and winding paths. Its temples include the Ming-dynasty Guanyin Temple, and a viewing pavilion near the summit looks over the resort and the sea. It makes a shaded walk of an hour or two away from the beach.

rows.name: Nandaihe International Entertainment Centre
rows.summary: A seaside leisure complex at Nandaihe, south-west of Beidaihe, with a funfair that includes a Ferris wheel and a dome-screen cinema. Its Chinese Lotus Garden, about 40 hectares with some 300 lotus varieties, holds a lotus festival in summer. It is a modern commercial attraction for families rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Pigeon Nest Park
rows.summary: A small headland park at the north-eastern end of the Beidaihe seafront, known for watching the sunrise over the Bohai Sea from the rock at its tip. Beidaihe is a major bird-migration stopover, so the park is also a birdwatching spot in spring and autumn. Visitors walk the beach and the headland paths, and an hour or two is enough to see it.

rows.name: Qin Emperor's Immortality Quest Park
rows.summary: A 19-hectare park on the Bohai shore at Nanshan, opened in 2002, built in ancient style around a Ming stele of 1477 said to mark where the First Qin Emperor sent men to sea in search of the elixir of life. It combines a garden on the quest theme with a Warring States garden, both laid out with ancient-style buildings and sculptures.

rows.name: Qin Travelling Palace Site, Beidaihe
rows.summary: Foundations of a Qin-dynasty palace at Jinshanzui on the Beidaihe shore, excavated from 1986 to 1991 over about 15,800 square metres and made up of four building groups and fourteen units. It is identified as a travelling palace used on the Qin emperors' eastern tours, which supports the story behind the name Qinhuangdao, 'Qin Emperor Island'. A site museum opened in 2019 shows the foundations and finds in an exhibition on the Qin tours and the excavation.

rows.name: Qinhuangdao Port Historic Quarter
rows.name_zh: 秦皇岛港口近代建筑群
rows.summary: The old West Port of Qinhuangdao, where the harbour opened to trade in 1898 and the Kailuan mining company built its offices, power plant, staff housing, wharves and railway. Nine of its buildings and sites are on the national list, and the former Kailuan staff club is now the Qinhuangdao Port Museum. Parts of the old port have been opened as an industrial-tourism area, so it works as an industrial-heritage walk beside the working port.

rows.name: Qinhuangdao Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A large safari-style wildlife park on the Beidaihe coast, opened in 1995, where animals including tigers, lions and bears are kept in zoned areas set in coastal woodland. Visitors tour it in their own vehicle or by park bus, with some areas open on foot. A giant panda house with two pandas opened in January 2026, and the park suits families for about half a day.

rows.name: Xin'ao Underwater World
rows.summary: An aquarium on Qinhuangdao's seafront, with marine animals to view and staged shows by dolphins and sea lions. It is a commercial attraction aimed at families.

rows.name: Yongping Prefecture City Wall
rows.summary: Surviving parts of the wall of Ming-dynasty Yongping Prefecture, first built in brick and stone in 1372, including the west gate (Wangjing Gate) with its barbican, the small west gate and the small south gate. Restoration of the west wall began in 2014. Lulong was the prefectural seat, and the wall is the main reminder of that role.

rows.name: Yuanying Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 13-storey octagonal pagoda of brick and timber with closely spaced eaves, built in the Jin dynasty and rebuilt several times since, standing in the north-west of Changli town and about 36 metres high. Changli County Museum, opened beside it in 2024, tells the story of the tower and its repairs with displays indoors and outdoors.

rows.name: Yudao Ocean Resort
rows.summary: A large commercial seaside resort on the Golden Coast in the Beidaihe New Area, centred on a water park, a Ferris wheel and a myth-themed show quarter with mechanical-beast attractions. Performances run through the day and into the night, and the resort also has hot-spring pools. It is a modern family resort rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Yutian Qilihai Resort
rows.summary: A family holiday resort beside the Qilihai lagoon on the Golden Coast, built around a themed resort town. It offers family attractions by day and stages shows and drone displays in the evenings. It is a modern commercial resort aimed mainly at families.

rows.name: Zuoyou Valley
rows.summary: A rural leisure and holiday park in the Yanshan foothills of Lulong County, laid out with orchards and farmland for countryside sightseeing and family holidays. It is one of the scenic areas Qinhuangdao has added in recent years, so it suits a relaxed half-day rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Zushan
rows.summary: Zushan, called the 'ancestor of the Yanshan', is a large mountain scenic area in the Yanshan range north of Qinhuangdao; its highest peak, Tiannü Peak, rises to 1,428 m. Visitors come for the rocky peaks, gorges and streams, and a cable car serves the higher parts.

rows.name: Anji Bridge (Zhaozhou Bridge)
rows.summary: A single-span stone arch bridge over the Xiao River at Zhao County, usually dated to about 605 in the Sui dynasty and credited to the craftsman Li Chun. Its shallow arch has two small arches set into each shoulder, and it is generally described as the world's oldest stone bridge of this open-spandrel type; the parapets are carved with dragons and animal masks. The bridge was heavily rebuilt in 1952–56, which changed its appearance, and it now stands in a park that includes an exhibition on ancient bridges.

rows.name: Baodu Zhai
rows.summary: A steep-sided mountain on the western edge of Luquan whose cliff-ringed summit, 580 m above sea level, holds about 660 mu (44 hectares) of level ground. The main sights are on the summit plateau, among them the South Heaven Gate, a Five Hundred Arhats hall, the Jinque Palace, caves and a ring wall known locally as the Great Wall, and local tradition ties the mountain to the Han general Han Xin. Visitors can climb a stepped path of about 3 km with roughly 3,000 steps, or take the cable car.

rows.name: Chengling Pagoda, Linji Temple
rows.summary: A nine-tier, eight-sided brick pagoda about 30 m high beside Linji Temple in the old town of Zhengding, built to hold the relics of Linji Yixuan (died 867), founder of the Linji school of Chan Buddhism, known in Japan as Rinzai. The tower is in Jin-dynasty style, was repaired on an imperial order of 1183 and again in the 1980s with help from Japanese Zen communities, and delegations from Japan's Rinzai and Obaku schools have visited since 1980. The temple, founded in the sixth century, is an active monastery.

rows.name: Daguan Stele (Emperor Huizong's School Rules)
rows.summary: A Northern Song stone stele of the Daguan era (1107–1110) carrying a school-rules edict, the 'eight virtues and eight punishments', written by Emperor Huizong; several copies survive across China and this one is a national heritage unit. It stands in Zhao County town on Shita Road, a short walk from the Dharani Pillar. It is mainly of interest to people who follow Song-dynasty inscriptions.

rows.name: Fenglongshan Grottoes
rows.summary: A small group of Buddhist rock-cut caves on Fenglong Mountain, on the Yuanshi–Luquan border; the heritage listing dates the carving from the Northern and Southern Dynasties to the Ming, and a 1994 field survey placed one cave between the Northern Qi and the Sui. The mountain is better known for the Fenglong Academy, which Chinese sources trace back to the Han and where two Han-dynasty stelae stand in a pavilion.

rows.name: Former People's Bank of China Headquarters, Shijiazhuang
rows.name_zh: 中国人民银行总行旧址
rows.summary: A three-storey grey-brick building put up in 1940–41 and known as the 'Little Grey Building'. The People's Bank of China was founded here on 1 December 1948 and issued the first series of renminbi notes the same day. Since 2009 it has housed a memorial museum on the bank's founding and the Hebei Coin Museum, with recreated offices of the early bank and displays of Hebei's historical currency.

rows.name: Fuxi Terrace
rows.summary: A three-tiered, irregularly octagonal rammed-earth terrace about 9 m high on the plain at Xinle, traditionally linked with the mythical ancestor Fuxi, with remains from the Neolithic to the Han dynasty in the ground around it. A temple complex along its north–south axis (gate, Liuzuo Hall, Longshi Hall and the rear sleeping hall) is known locally as the Ancestor Temple, and the annual Fuxi sacrifice held here on the 17th to 19th of the third lunar month is on China's national intangible-heritage list. The surrounding area has been developed with a cultural market and leisure spaces.

rows.name: Guanghui Temple Hua Pagoda
rows.summary: A four-storey, eight-sided brick pagoda, the main surviving building of Guanghui Temple in the old town of Zhengding. Its top storey is a cone-shaped body covered in modelled figures of warriors, lions, elephants, Buddhas and bodhisattvas, in the manner of a flower bouquet, which gives this rare 'flower pagoda' type its name. The temple was founded in the Tang, the tower is mainly of Song–Jin date, and it was restored in 1994–99.

rows.name: Guoyu Hot Spring Resort Town
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort hotel and leisure complex in Gaocheng District, fed by a spring that the district government says is drawn from a depth of 3,254 m. The district government described three hot-spring gardens with more than fifty pools, a children's water area, steam rooms, a traditional-medicine hall and a small street of shops and restaurants. It is a modern commercial resort rather than a heritage site, aimed at hot-spring stays.

rows.name: Heishan Grand Canyon
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A forested gorge scenic area of about 17 km² in the north-west of the Taihang range, close to the Shanxi border, with a main summit of 1,910 m and an average altitude of about 1,300 m. Its sixty or so listed sights include a waterfall zone, Fusheng Temple and old woodland with wild kiwi trees more than a century old. It is a cool place to walk in summer.

rows.name: Jingxing Kiln Site (Nanhengkou)
rows.summary: The Jingxing kilns, founded in the Sui dynasty and at their height in the Song and Jin, were scattered through the mountains of Jingxing County, and the Nanhengkou site is the largest and best preserved of those found. Visitors can look inside a bun-shaped 'mantou' kiln, where the fire chamber and kiln bed survive, and see village walls built from discarded firing saggars. Since 2016 the village has also been developed as a 'Ceramic Water Town', with a ceramics street, working pottery studios where visitors can try making ware, and guesthouses.

rows.name: Jingxing Old Post Road (Qinhuang Ancient Road)
rows.summary: A surviving stretch of the old trunk road through the Jingxing pass, the only one of the Taihang range's eight historic passes that carts could use, linking the North China plain with Shanxi. At Baishiling and the Dongtianmen pass the road is cut into bare rock, with cart ruts more than 30 cm deep, a stone gateway whose upper pavilions were rebuilt in the Ming and Qing, and a section paved with hexagonal stones between the East and West gates. It is also called the Qinhuang (First Emperor) road, and a stone beyond the west gate commemorates the general Han Xin, whose 'back to the river' victory near here is a famous episode of the Chu–Han war.

rows.name: Jingxing Old Town Wall (Tianchang)
rows.summary: Tianchang is the old county town of Jingxing, which became the county seat in 1075 and remained so until 1958, and its Ming and Qing town wall is a national heritage unit. Parts of the wall survive, together with a city-god temple, a Confucian temple hall and the Jieshan Academy, all listed at provincial level, in a town named one of China's historic and cultural towns in 2008. The Jingxing kiln villages lie a few kilometres to the east.

rows.name: Jinxiu Daming Chuan (Shuqiao Tourist Area)
rows.summary: A leisure and camping resort built from late 2018 on a reclaimed river flat beside the Wuyuezhai exit of the Xifu Expressway at Zhaitou in Lingshou County, known for its 'tree bridge' riverside park. It has a large visitor centre, car parks and a dining area, about 150 camping and lodging units including RVs, tree houses, tents and star-gazing cabins, a children's park, a pet park and, in winter, a snow field with lantern displays. It is a modern purpose-built destination for family and group outings, not a historic or natural sight.

rows.name: Junlebao Dairy Industrial Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 君乐宝乳业工业旅游区
rows.summary: A dairy industrial-tourism area run by the Junlebao dairy company in Luquan District, with a dairy-processing zone and a ranch zone; the company began offering industrial tourism in 2012. At the ranch, visitors see a cattle-science hall, a milking hall, a grazing area, a feeding area and a visitor centre with a milk-culture display. It is a modern company attraction aimed at families and school groups, and its subject is dairy farming rather than local history.

rows.name: Kaihua Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-tier, eight-sided pagoda of solid brick, about 25 m high, standing on a carved stone base in the old town of Yuanshi. It is all that is left of Kaihua Temple: the tower dates from the Jin dynasty and was rebuilt in the Chenghua era of the Ming (1464–87), and it still carries brick reliefs, donors' inscriptions and shell marks from the fighting for the town. It makes a brief stop for anyone interested in Jin and Ming brick architecture.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple, Zhengding
rows.summary: The surviving part of a temple founded in 540 in the old town of Zhengding, with the square nine-tier Xumi Pagoda, about 42.5 m high and begun in 636, facing a two-storey bell tower across the former courtyard. Local heritage authorities describe the bell tower as the only Tang-dynasty bell tower still standing, and the carved stone columns of the gate tower, dated to 692, were re-erected in 2008. An excavation south of the temple, showing seven periods of layered remains, can be seen through a glass wall.

rows.name: Liang Ancestral Hall, Zhengding
rows.summary: A late-Ming ancestral hall of the Liang family, one of Zhengding's leading official families, on Yanzhao South Street in the old town. The family rose with Liang Menglong, a Ming minister of war and later of personnel, and the hall and its gateway are one of only two surviving buildings of the family's former estates. The five-bay hall with a flush-gable roof was taken down and rebuilt in 1997–98, and its interior is no longer used for the family tablets.

rows.name: Lingshou Stone Archway
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty memorial archway of 1641 in Lingshou county town, known as the 'Three Generations of the Central Pivot' arch. It is carved wholly from stone to imitate timber, about 12 m high and 8 m wide, in a four-column, five-roof design with dozens of carved lions. Its inscriptions record imperial honours for three generations of the Fu family, centred on Fu Yongchun, a Ming vice-minister of war who later headed the Ministry of Personnel.

rows.name: Lingxiao Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey, eight-sided pagoda about 41 m high, the main surviving building of the former Tianning Temple in the old town of Zhengding. The lower storeys are brick and the upper ones timber, with a timber central pillar running up the inside, a structure that is uncommon among China's surviving pagodas. A crypt found beneath it in 1982 showed that it was begun in the Tang dynasty between 756 and 779, and it was rebuilt in 1045 and again in 1141.

rows.name: Longxing Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple founded in 586 under the Sui dynasty and enlarged by order of the first Northern Song emperor, laid out along a long north–south axis and counted among the earliest, largest and best-preserved temple complexes in China. Its highlights are the Mani Hall of 1052, cross-shaped in plan with a gabled porch on each side and a hanging-sculpture Guanyin inside, the revolving sutra cabinet, and the Great Compassion Pavilion with its very large bronze thousand-armed Guanyin of the Song period. The architect Liang Sicheng surveyed the complex in 1933 and rated it the finest temple outside Beijing.

rows.name: Manshan Huaxi Valley
rows.summary: A mountain-valley leisure and holiday resort on the south side of the Wuyuezhai massif, developed from 2011 around two former mountain hamlets. The Lingshou county government describes a valley about 12.5 km long and 20 km² in area, rising from about 800 m to over 2,000 m, with a stream along its floor, a mountain flower garden, a lake in the gorge and an elevated 'glass rafting' course. It has lodging, dining and recreation facilities, and suits families wanting a cool summer weekend rather than a hard hike.

rows.name: Mount Cangyan
rows.summary: A wooded gorge in the Taihang foothills where the Fuqing Temple complex is built into the cliffs, with its Bridge-Tower Hall carried on a stone arch spanning a narrow cleft high above the valley floor. The temple is traditionally said to date from the Sui dynasty and to have been the retreat of Princess Nanyang, a daughter of Emperor Yang; the present buildings are Ming and Qing, and the temple is a national heritage unit. The setting was used in the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (2000), and a stepped path climbs from the temple towards the summit.

rows.name: North China Military Region Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery and park of about 21 ha in Shijiazhuang, opened in 1954 to commemorate people who died in the revolutionary wars in North China. Its graves include those of the Canadian doctor Norman Bethune and the Indian doctor Dwarkanath Kotnis, who both worked with the Communist-led armies, and its grounds hold a monument, bronze statues of named martyrs, a memorial hall on the North China revolutionary war and a memorial hall for the Bethune–India medical team. It is a state-designated patriotic-education and red-tourism site.

rows.name: Oriental Giant Turtle Garden
rows.summary: A family leisure park on the east bank of the Ye River in Pingshan County, built by a local entrepreneur whose business began with soft-shelled turtle farming. Its sights include a giant turtle-shaped landmark, a long gallery walkway, a landscaped garden themed on Chinese history, an aquarium and water-play areas, with the turtle-farming side of the business also on show. It suits families with children and school study groups rather than heritage travellers.

rows.name: Pagoda of Bailin Temple
rows.summary: The memorial pagoda of the Tang Chan master Zhaozhou Congshen, rebuilt in 1330 under the Yuan dynasty and standing in the front courtyard of Bailin Chan Temple in Zhao County. It is an octagonal brick pagoda with seven tiers of closely stacked eaves above a carved Sumeru-style base showing musicians, guardian figures, animals and peonies, and 136 iron wind bells hang from its eaves. The temple around it was rebuilt in the 1990s and is an active Chan monastery, and the Zhaozhou Bridge is about 3 km to the south-south-west.

rows.name: Pilu Temple, Shijiazhuang
rows.summary: A small temple on the north-western edge of Shijiazhuang, founded in the Tang dynasty and rebuilt several times; its two main old halls, the Shijia Hall and the Pilu Hall, are of the Ming period. The walls of the Pilu Hall carry more than 120 square metres of Ming 'water-and-land' ritual murals, with 122 groups and over 500 figures: Buddhist figures on the north wall, Daoist ones on the east and west walls, and Confucian and everyday scenes on the south wall. The paintings date from a rebuilding between 1495 and 1535, and Chinese specialists name them, with those of Beijing's Fahai Temple, as the best-known Ming temple murals.

rows.name: Qipanshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area of about 20 km² in the Taihang foothills of western Zanhuang County, divided into four sub-areas (Apricot Valley, Qipanshan, Camel Peak and Eight Immortals Ridge) with more than 110 named sights, among them dozens of peaks, cliffs and caves. The highest point, Sixianggong Zhai, is 1,342.3 m, and the long apricot valley blossoms around the end of March, with wild peach and rhododendron following in spring and summer. Its summers are cool, with a hottest-month average of about 22 °C.

rows.name: Qiushan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested hill-and-valley scenic area of about 8 km² in the Taihang foothills of Lingshou County, bounded by reservoirs on three sides, with more than 95 per cent plant cover, small waterfalls, lakes and stone outcrops. The official description names a stretch of old wall called Tianlei Great Wall, the Qinghu and Cuihu lakes and an old battlefield site among its sights, and gives a summer temperature on the hill of about 20 °C. It suits a cool day out from Shijiazhuang for people who prefer quiet woodland to developed attractions.

rows.name: Rongguo Mansion, Zhengding
rows.summary: A full-size replica of the Rong family mansion from the novel Dream of the Red Chamber, built in Zhengding between 1984 and 1986 as the set for the 1987 television adaptation and kept open afterwards as an attraction. The courtyard houses, with 212 rooms in three axes of five courtyards each, are furnished in Ming and Qing style, and Ningrong Street beside them is a 200 m street of 51 shop-fronts built in Qing style. It is a film set rather than a historic building, and suits fans of the novel or the series.

rows.name: Shuiquanxi Nature Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain-stream scenic area of about 47 km² in the Taihang hills of Lingshou County, with forest covering about 90 per cent of the ground and more than 100 named spots, among them Qingshi Gorge, Wolong Rock, the Fairy and Rainbow waterfalls and a cave called the Immortals' Cave. The largest waterfall drops over 100 m, and the streams and shade make it a cool place in the warmer months. It suits walkers and families who want water and woodland rather than temples or towns.

rows.name: Stele of the Prince of Qinghe (Li Baochen Stele)
rows.name_zh: 大唐清河郡王纪功载政之颂碑
rows.pinyin: Dàtáng Qīnghé Jùnwáng Jìgōng Zàizhèng Zhī Sòng Bēi
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty stone stele set on a tortoise base under a top of interlaced dragons and sheltered by a stele pavilion in the old town of Zhengding. Erected in 766 by imperial order, its 1,007 surviving characters, in regular and running script, praise the record of Li Baochen, military governor of the Chengde circuit. It is also known as the wind-moving stele.

rows.name: Stone Pagoda of Zhiping Temple
rows.summary: The surviving remains of Zhiping Temple, a temple founded in the Sui dynasty and largely destroyed in the war against Japan: a four-storey octagonal stone pagoda dated to 749, two small stone pagodas and a dharani pillar, all of the Tang period. The group stands at the northern edge of Jiayingsi village in the Zanhuang countryside. It is a small rural monument for people interested in early stone architecture, not a developed attraction.

rows.name: Tenglongshan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 8 square kilometres in Wangpo township, in the north-west of Pingshan County, known for woodland hung with vines. The city government describes streams, pools and small waterfalls among the rocks, and the ridge also keeps the remains of blockhouses from the war against Japan. It suits a half-day walk in the hills.

rows.name: Tiangui Mountain
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of steep peaks, caves and springs in the Taihang hills of Pingshan County, with a large Taoist temple complex, Qinglong Guan, that is said locally to have begun as a late-Ming imperial lodge. On one cliff is a carving of the Chinese character gui ('return'), 97.71 m high and 49.1 m wide, cut in 1997 to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule. Other sights include a cave and exhibition hall linked to the White-Haired Girl story and a Taoist martial-arts square.

rows.name: Tianhu Dharani Pillar
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty Buddhist sutra pillar dated by its inscription to 727, standing in the grounds of the former East Chan Temple in Tianhu village, on the site of the Tang town of Tianhu. The octagonal stone shaft is carved with a dharani sutra and rises from a stepped base, with tiers of carved beasts, arhats and Buddhas above it, and Chinese sources count it among the earliest surviving sutra pillars in China. Its upper tiers were knocked down in a theft in December 2010 and the stolen piece was recovered within two days.

rows.name: Tianshan Sea World
rows.summary: A commercial leisure complex in Shijiazhuang's Yuhua District, opened in 1999, that combines shopping and entertainment with a water park. A 2018 upgrade added water attractions such as a lazy river and slides, and since 2023 the winter water-play area has been a children's play park. It is a modern mall-and-leisure venue rather than a historic sight, and it suits families wanting an indoor day out in the city.

rows.name: Tuoliang Scenic Area
rows.summary: A high Taihang mountain area of 158 km² with a summit of 2,281 m, one of the five highest peaks in Hebei, and about 98% forest cover. More than 200 sights are listed, among them a gorge of small waterfalls (Baipu Gorge), stepped cascades and the sub-alpine Yunding meadow, which is in flower in summer. It is also a national forest park and nature reserve, and its summer average of about 19°C is why it is promoted as a cool retreat.

rows.name: Wanshou Temple Pagoda Forest
rows.summary: A group of twelve brick tomb pagodas for the abbots of Wanshou Chan Temple, also called Linshan Temple, on the western foot of Donglin Mountain at Sanji in Pingshan County. They range in date from the Five Dynasties to the Qing, and the inscriptions on seven of them can still be read. It is a quiet add-on to a visit to the Zhongshan site about 3 km to the south.

rows.name: Wuwushui Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst valley scenic area of about 11.5 km² in western Pingshan County, where a spring breaks out high on the hillside and feeds waterfalls with drops of 93 m and 45 m; in winter the water is used for an ice-fall display. The area also holds a late Palaeolithic cave site, Shuilian Cave, and a small hydroelectric station built in 1947–48 to supply power to Xibaipo, then the seat of the Communist Party's central leadership. It suits visitors who want mountain scenery and some red-tourism history in one outing.

rows.name: Wuyuezhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area and national forest park in the north-west corner of Lingshou County, named for five peaks standing side by side; the main summit is close to 2,000 m, with deep gorges, larch and birch woods and an alpine meadow near the top. The best-known sight is the waterfall called the First Waterfall of Yan and Zhao, a drop of about 108 m billed as the largest mountain waterfall in northern China. Routes range from a short gorge-and-waterfall loop to a full-day circuit to the main peak, and the area is known for its cool summers.

rows.name: Xibaipo (Former CPC Central Committee Site)
rows.summary: The village where the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party and the headquarters of the People's Liberation Army were based between 1947 and March 1949, and from which the Liaoshen, Huaihai and Pingjin campaigns of the civil war were directed. The site holds the residences and offices of leaders including Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Liu Shaoqi, the hall where the Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee met in March 1949, the military operations room, and a large memorial museum with exhibitions on the period. The original village was flooded by the Gangnan Reservoir in 1959, so the buildings are reconstructions on higher ground, rebuilt from 1970.

rows.name: Xiyuan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort hotel in Wentang township, Pingshan County, with a four-star hotel of about 460 rooms and a bathing and water-play complex called Xiyuan Xiangshuiwan. It has indoor water slides and a children's play area, landscaped outdoor pools fed by cold, warm and hot waterfalls, herbal baths, and a cave-themed water zone. It suits families and groups who want a hot-spring stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Yongtong Bridge
rows.summary: A single-span stone arch bridge on the west side of Zhao County town, known locally as the Small Stone Bridge and built on the same open-spandrel plan as the Anji Bridge a few kilometres to the south. It is admired for the relief carvings on its parapets, arch faces and piers, and a local saying credits the big bridge with engineering and the small one with ornament. Its date is debated: stones found beneath it in 1986 point to about 765 in the Tang, while older accounts give the Jin dynasty, and a small park has been laid out around it.

rows.name: Youju Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: The only surviving building of Youju Temple, which was founded in the Northern Qi dynasty in the 6th century and destroyed in the Qing period: a seven-tier square brick pagoda of the Tang dynasty, about 23 m high, with tightly stacked eaves. The national heritage record notes three Northern Qi Buddha figures kept inside it. It stands in a hill village in the Taihang foothills and is a remote rural monument rather than a developed attraction.

rows.name: Yujiashan Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty seated Maitreya, 8 m high and carved in 1056 on a hill about 2 km west of Nanye village, which the national heritage authority calls the largest single Song stone image in Hebei. It is sheltered by the Maitreya Pavilion, a two-storey brick vaulted hall rebuilt in 1574. On a cliff to the south are 42 small seated Buddhas and a water-moon Guanyin with an inscription dated 1072.

rows.name: Zhangshiyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national scenic area and geopark on the western edge of Zanhuang County, where the Taihang range breaks into three stacked tiers of red sandstone cliffs, each about 100–150 m high and running for tens of kilometres. The Zhangshiyan landform is named after this place, and Chinese sources rank it with the Danxia and Zhangjiajie landforms as China's three main sandstone landforms. The area has five zones, including Jiunü Peak, the Echo Wall (a huge amphitheatre-shaped cliff valley that returns clear echoes), the Dongling Bei ice-fall valley and a flower-valley zone, with cable car, rafting and camping facilities.

rows.name: Zhaozhou Dharani Pillar
rows.summary: A seven-tier octagonal stone sutra pillar built in 1038 under the Northern Song, 16.44 m high, on the site of the former Kaiyuan Temple in the middle of Zhao County town. Its tiers are carved with the dharani sutra, Buddhist scenes, guardian figures and miniature buildings, and Chinese sources describe it as the tallest surviving pillar of its kind in China. Lightning damaged the middle tiers in 1983, it was repaired by 1990, and it now stands in a protective pool ringed by a stone balustrade.

rows.name: Zhengding City Wall
rows.summary: The brick wall of the old prefectural city of Zhengding, which reached its present form in a Ming rebuild finished in 1576; each of its four gates had three layers of defence, the main gate, a barbican and a crescent outer wall. Much of it was pulled down from 1958, but the south gate group, the Changle Gate, and the adjoining stretches have been restored since 2014, and visitors can walk on top of the wall. The old town's temples and streets lie to the north.

rows.name: Zhengding County Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county Confucian temple in Zhengding old town, whose main hall, the Dacheng Hall, is regarded as the oldest surviving Confucian temple hall in China. The county gazetteer gives a Ming date of 1374, but its five bays, hip-and-gable roof and heavy bracket sets point to the late Tang or Five Dynasties. The site also keeps a screen wall, a Pan Pool, a gate hall and side halls, and the separate prefectural Confucian temple stands nearby.

rows.name: Zhengding Prefectural Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The surviving gate hall and flanking side rooms of the Confucian temple of Zhengding Prefecture, founded in 1070. The five-bay gate hall dates from the Yuan dynasty and is described by the county government as the only Yuan-period building left in Zhengding. The gate hall and side rooms have been repaired, and the site opened to the public on 30 December 2019 together with the east city gate, the City God temple and the Zhengding Museum.

rows.name: Zhengfeng Mine Industrial Buildings (Duanjialou)
rows.summary: The head office and staff housing of the Zhengfeng coal-mining company, built from 1913 to a German-led design after the mine was reorganised in 1912 with investment from the Beiyang general Duan Qirui; the complex is known locally as Duanjialou. Visitors can see the general manager's office building with its banquet hall and period fittings, the smaller residences, and part of a tunnel that runs beneath the site. Chinese state media describe it as one of the better-preserved groups of modern industrial buildings in north China.

rows.name: Zhongshan Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The remains of Lingshou, the later capital of Zhongshan, a Warring States kingdom founded by the Xianyu, a northern Di people, which lies mostly in Sanji township in Pingshan County. Excavations from 1974 uncovered the kingdom's royal tombs, among them that of King Cuo, and more than 19,000 objects including inscribed bronzes. The part open to visitors is the tomb of King Cuo with the Zhongshan Royal Tombs Exhibition Hall, a cultural experience hall and an archaeology centre, while many of the best finds, such as the inlaid bronze plan of the necropolis, are shown at the Hebei Museum in Shijiazhuang.

rows.name: Ziyun Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 5 km² in the Taihang hills of Pingshan County, with a main peak of 1,128 m, more than twenty natural limestone caves hung with stalactites, stone-built farmhouses and red autumn foliage on the slopes. It has also been developed with red-tourism and ethnic-culture displays and is a pilot forest-wellness base. It suits a quiet half-day in the hills.

rows.name: Baiyangyu Great Wall
rows.summary: A stretch of Ming Great Wall about 4.5 km long along the ridges at Baiyangyu pass, with 21 towers, of which the Qian'an city government counts six as fairly complete. State media describe about 1.5 km of it as the 'marble Great Wall', with its base and tower foundations laid in marble and the wall standing up to 10 m high.

rows.name: Bodhi Island
rows.summary: The wooded island of the three that make up Tangshan International Tourist Island, in the Bohai Sea off Laoting County; state media describe it as an island of old trees, in contrast to the sandy Yuetuo Island. It lies within the Bodhi Islands provincial nature reserve, a migratory-bird stopover for which the Ministry of Ecology and Environment reports 379 bird species a year. A visitor centre and a culture hall stand by its harbour plaza at the north-east end.

rows.name: Caofeidian Wetland
rows.summary: Part of a coastal wetland on the Bohai shore of Caofeidian District, made up of reed beds, marshes, fish ponds, shallow reservoirs and tidal flats; the provincial-level wetland and bird reserve covers about 110 square kilometres and lies on the East Asian–Australasian migratory route. Around Cao Fei Lake, visitors can take boat trips, fish, walk a reed-maze trail with a lookout tower and watch birds, with waterbirds most numerous in April and May. More than 300 bird species have been recorded.

rows.name: Doma Park, Caofeidian
rows.summary: A fishing-themed leisure park inside the Caofeidian wetland resort, where visitors catch fish, crabs and clams by traditional methods and by newer ones. Attractions include robot fishing, an underwater-camera fishing system and a water-borne 'space-time express' train, according to the park's publicity as reported by state media. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Eastern Qing Tombs
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: The burial ground of five Qing emperors (Shunzhi, Kangxi, Qianlong, Xianfeng and Tongzhi), 15 empresses and 136 imperial concubines, spread over about 80 square kilometres of hills around Changrui Mountain. Visitors walk the stone-lined spirit ways, with their archways, bridges and carved figures, to the halls of several tombs, among them Xiaoling (Shunzhi), Jingling (Kangxi), Yuling (Qianlong) and Empress Dowager Cixi's Ding Dongling; the underground chambers of Yuling and Cixi's tomb can be visited. Chinese official sources describe it as the largest and most complete surviving Qing imperial tomb complex, and it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.

rows.name: Fenghuang Mountain, Qianxi
rows.summary: A limestone mountain about 400 m high in Xinji town, southern Qianxi, named for its resemblance to a phoenix with spread wings, with secondary forest and a Buddhist temple, Putuo Chan Temple, at its foot. The main event is a traditional temple fair on the 19th day of the second lunar month, with opera, folk dance and other folk arts, and the park also runs high-mountain rafting and a tree-house area.

rows.name: Hetou Old Street
rows.summary: A shopping, food and entertainment street built in old-street style on both banks of the Tangjin Canal, on the line of the 1881 coal canal that gave Hetou its name. It first opened in January 2023 and has run as a regular attraction since early 2024; evenings are the main draw, with street and stage performances, a floating market selling local snacks, lantern-lit bridges, costumed actors and the outdoor shows Tang Wang Dong Zheng and Da Tang Cao Fei. It was named a national tourism and leisure street in December 2023 and a national night-time culture and tourism cluster in January 2024.

rows.name: Huaxiang Guoxiang Rural Park, Qianxi
rows.summary: A rural-tourism zone in Qianxi built around flower and fruit farming, with oil-peony and kiwi-fruit farms and organic grain fields, approved as a national 'rural complex' pilot (the only one in Hebei when state media reported on it in 2020). Pear-blossom, peony and harvest festivals have been held in season, and the surrounding villages run farmhouse restaurants.

rows.name: Jingjue Temple, Yutian
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the countryside of Yutian County, traditionally said to date back to the Tang dynasty but mostly rebuilt in 1842–55 under the Qing. Its buildings run along a central axis, from an archway and a brick-vaulted 'beamless' gate hall through a stele pavilion, bell and drum towers and the main halls, over a site of about 1.85 hectares with roughly a hundred statues and eight steles. The mix of Ming and Qing styles and the late-Qing calligraphy on its plaques and steles are the main interest.

rows.name: Jingzhong Mountain, Qianxi
rows.summary: A temple mountain about 610 m high in Qianxi, where Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian shrines stand in three clusters at the foot, middle and summit, joined by a stairway of 1,872 steps through pines more than 200 years old. The Shunzhi and Kangxi emperors visited six times between them, and Kangxi wrote the inscription 'Famous Mountain Under Heaven' for it; large temple fairs are held on the 18th day of the fourth lunar month and the 15th of the tenth.

rows.name: Lanyuewan Seaside Area, Caofeidian
rows.summary: A seaside leisure area on the Bohai shore of Caofeidian New City, built around a sandy bay with about 12.8 km of shoreline and a 13.14 km coastal walking trail. Beach camping, seafood meals, kite events and open-air film shows are on offer.

rows.name: Li Dazhao Memorial Hall and Former Residence
rows.summary: Li Dazhao, an early leader of the Chinese Communist Party, was born in 1889 in Dahetuo village, where the three-courtyard farmhouse he grew up in is a nationally protected site. The memorial hall in Laoting town, on a site of about 9 hectares, holds some 35,000 objects, with a white-marble statue of Li in its tribute hall. The memorial hall is a first-class national museum and one of the 100 national red-tourism classic scenic areas.

rows.name: Longjingguan Great Wall and Rafting Area
rows.summary: A river-rafting scenic area at Longjingguan, a Ming Great Wall pass at the foot of Qi Mountain in Han'erzhuang, northern Qianxi. The county government describes a rafting course of about 9.8 km on the Sa River, taking around two hours, with a tunnel section about 1 km long adapted from Ming-era soldiers' caves and an armoury under the mountain. The pass and the wall on the hills above form the backdrop.

rows.name: Luanzhou Ancient City
rows.summary: A reconstruction of the old walled town of Luanzhou in Ming-Qing style, opened in 2012, with a rebuilt city gate, bell and drum towers, a reception pavilion and the old county yamen from the 'Yang Sanjie' opera story. Inside are commercial streets, folk-custom and temple-fair quarters and the Luanzhou Shadow Puppet Museum, in a region known for shadow puppetry and pingju opera. It is a new development rather than a surviving old town, so it suits a relaxed stroll and a meal.

rows.name: Panjiayu Massacre Site and Memorial Hall
rows.summary: Panjiayu was a village used as a base by the Eastern Hebei anti-Japanese resistance, and on 25 January 1941 Japanese and puppet-government troops surrounded it and killed more than 1,200 villagers, described as the first large-scale atrocity under the Japanese 'Three Alls' policy. A memorial hall and museum stand at the site, with an ancestral hall put up by the villagers for the victims. It was named a national patriotic education base in 2001 and listed as a nationally protected site in 2006.

rows.name: Qinglong Mountain, Luanzhou
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area in the north-west of Luanzhou, a spur of the Yan Mountains, with Buddhist and Taoist temples and walking routes through pine and cypress woods. It is promoted for spring blossom and autumn colour.

rows.name: Qingshanguan Great Wall
rows.summary: A Great Wall pass in the mountains of north-eastern Qianxi, reckoned the best-preserved part of the county's Ming wall, with a surviving lift-type water gate, a 72-arch tower, the round 'Moon City' and a 'prison tower'. Below the wall stands a fort more than 400 years old, whose former offices, barracks, temples, teahouses and inns are now partly restored as restaurants and guesthouses. Climbing the wall is steep in places.

rows.name: Qixin Cement Industry Museum, Tangshan
rows.name_zh: 唐山启新水泥工业博物馆
rows.summary: A museum without walls on the site of the Qixin Cement Works, founded in 1889 as China's first cement works, with 24 old buildings kept, among them silos, a freight platform and red-brick walls. Rotary kilns 4 and 5 date from the early 1910s and are described by state media as the oldest surviving in China, and kilns 6 and 7 ran from 1922 to 1998. The site is also the Qixin 1889 creative park, with cafés, craft shops, a 3D cinema and art exhibitions in the old halls.

rows.name: Shangheyuan Tourist Area, Zunhua
rows.summary: A leisure and rural-tourism area in Xingwangzhai town, west of Zunhua, centred on Lianxiang Town, a street of buildings built in old-street style that is hung with red lanterns for the New Year. Local government and state-media reports show seasonal events there, among them garden parties with stage shows, costumed performers and bonfire evenings, and visitors in Han-style dress. It suits families and groups wanting an easy half-day outing rather than historic buildings.

rows.name: Shanyekou Scenic Area, Qian'an
rows.summary: A scenic area of about 14 square kilometres in the hills west of Qian'an, opened in 2011 and known for its stream-cut valley, a mountaintop lake and coloured conglomerate pebbles and boulders from very ancient rock. It is part of Qian'an National Geopark and has a geology gallery and exhibition hall. A few dozen farmhouse restaurants and guesthouses serve visitors in the village at its entrance.

rows.name: Tangshan Earthquake Ruins Memorial Park
rows.name_zh: 唐山地震遗址纪念公园
rows.summary: A memorial park built around the ruined steel-casting workshop of the former Tangshan Locomotive and Rolling Stock Works, left standing as evidence of the 7.8-magnitude earthquake of 28 July 1976 that flattened the city. A long black wall beside the ruins is engraved with the names of more than 240,000 people who died, and the China Tangshan Earthquake Museum next door covers the quake, the rescue and the rebuilding with objects from old Tangshan and a shaking simulation. The ruined workshop is one of three earthquake sites in the national-level listing; the others, a former college library and a former school, are elsewhere in the city.

rows.name: Tangshan Nanhu and Kailuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Two linked parks in the middle of Tangshan: Nanhu, a lake park of nine lakes and five islands laid out on ground that sank after a century of coal mining, and the Kailuan National Mining Park beside it. The mining park has the Kailuan Museum, the zero-kilometre marker of China's first standard-gauge railway, a railway museum with a full-size replica of the 'Dragon' locomotive and an old mine shaft toured in miner's gear; its nationally protected core is the 1878 mine shaft, the railway's starting point and the Dadao road-rail underpass. Nanhu is for walking and cycling round the water, with a light-and-water show in the evening.

rows.name: Tangshan Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: The municipal science and technology museum, in a large modern building in central Tangshan on the south side of Xinhua Road, just west of its crossing with Weiguo Road. Its science educators perform live experiment shows, such as the 'elephant toothpaste' demonstration staged at Hebei's 2024 Science Popularisation Day event, and the museum is one of Tangshan's designated parent-and-child activity bases, so it suits visitors travelling with young children.

rows.name: Tiangong Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A thirteen-tier octagonal pagoda of brick and stone from the Liao dynasty, about 24 m high on a 5 m platform, completed in 1062 and the only part left of the former Tiangong Temple. Dragon-carved corner columns, lotus-petal bands and eaves hung with bells decorate the body. The 1976 earthquake shook off the finial and cracked the tower, and repairs in 1986–89 uncovered two chambers holding statues and scriptures.

rows.name: Yuetuo (Moon) Island
rows.summary: A crescent-shaped sandy island in the Bohai Sea off Laoting County, one of the three islands of Tangshan International Tourist Island (with Bodhi and Xiangyun islands), which state media call a national demonstration base for island development. State media describe it as having white sand and clear water, and nickname it the 'little Holland hanging in the Bohai'.

rows.name: Assembly Hall of the Boxer Movement
rows.summary: A traditional northern-style house of five rooms in Shaliuzhai village, where Zhao Sanduo and other leaders of the Yihequan ('Boxer') movement are recorded as meeting to plan the 1898 uprising. Restored from 1986, it holds an exhibition on Zhao Sanduo and the movement, and his own house stands 60 m away with period furniture, weapons and farm tools. A separate memorial museum in Wei County town covers the wider Boxer movement.

rows.name: Bian Que Temple
rows.summary: A large temple complex at the foot of Que Mountain in Shentou village, dedicated to the physician Bian Que; tradition dates it to the Warring States period, though the present buildings are Ming and Qing rebuilds. It is known for its ancient cypresses, more than 100 steles from the Song to the Qing, halls to Bian Que and the Three Pure Ones, a tomb mound and a Han-dynasty stone beast. It is a national education base for traditional Chinese medicine culture, and a Bian Que Culture Festival is held in Neiqiu, most recently in September 2026.

rows.name: Delong Steel Culture Park
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism park inside the working Xingtai plant of Delong Steel, a private steelmaker, in Xindu District. Xingtai Daily reported in October 2026 that it is the first national AAAA scenic area in China built on a steelworks that is still producing, with sculptures made from scrap steel and a disused railway turned into an industrial-culture wall. It is a factory tour rather than a heritage site, so it suits visitors curious about modern heavy industry.

rows.name: Jiulong Gorge
rows.summary: A sandstone gorge area in the Taihang Mountains of Xindu District, named for its nine gorges and nine valleys and planned to cover about 64 square km, with 1,800-metre Wangmao Mountain as its main peak. Its sights include waterfalls and pools, a peach-blossom valley, red-leaf slopes in autumn, Guanyin Cave and a stretch of Ming Great Wall. It is a day trip for walkers who want canyon scenery west of Xingtai.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple, Xingtai
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the north-east corner of Xingtai's old city, known as the East Temple, which takes its name from the Kaiyuan era (713–741) of the Tang dynasty and became an imperial temple under the Yuan. The old western compound keeps Ming and Qing halls, a Tang pillar with sixteen faces carved with a Buddhist dharani text, a second dharani pillar of 915 and a Jin-dynasty iron bell cast in 1184, while a large new temple built after 2006 stands to the east. It pairs well with Qingfeng Tower, Tianning Temple and the Xingtai Museum a few hundred metres away.

rows.name: Kongshan Baiyun Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave in the Taihang foothills of Lincheng, formed in the Cambrian period and found in 1988 by quarrymen, which opened to visitors in 1990. The route passes through five halls named the Human World, Heaven, Labyrinth, Underworld and Dragon Palace, where the temperature stays around 17 degrees Celsius all year.
