The scenic area looks across the sand to Shapotou in Ningxia.

rows.name: Aolunsumu City Ruins
rows.summary: Aolunsumu, also written Olon Süme, is a ruined walled city in the steppe of Damao Banner, identified since the 1930s as a possible northern capital of the Ongud, a Turkic-speaking people allied to the Mongol rulers and prominent under the Yuan dynasty. Low banks mark a rectangular enclosure with many building platforms inside it. Nestorian Christian objects found in Damao, such as a gilt-bronze cross, show the religious mix of the Ongud, and the site suits visitors interested in medieval Inner Asian history.

rows.name: Badekar Monastery (Wudangzhao)
rows.summary: Badekar Monastery, known in Chinese as Wudangzhao, is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery in the hills of Shiguai District, founded in the early 18th century and enlarged from 1749. It is the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Inner Mongolia: six main halls, three residences of reincarnate lamas and a mausoleum for their remains are scattered over the slopes of Jihuluntu mountain, with more than ninety earthen lamas' lodgings among them. It suits visitors interested in Tibetan Buddhist architecture and can be seen in a day from Baotou.

rows.name: Bailing Naadam Park
rows.summary: Bailing Naadam Park is a purpose-built festival ground on the edge of Bailingmiao, with an oval racecourse, a main grandstand for about 11,000 people, six stables holding 360 horses and a sales area for local goods. It hosts the Damao Banner's summer Naadam, whose programme includes the traditional wrestling, archery and horse racing; the 34th festival opened here on 19 July 2024 and the 35th on 31 July 2025. It suits visitors timing a trip to the festival, whose dates change each year.

rows.name: Baogang Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: The tour area is run by the Baotou Iron and Steel (Baogang) group at its works in Kundulun District, one of the three large steel complexes begun in the 1950s. Its route takes in an exhibition on the story of building Baogang, a steam-locomotive display, a culture hall and plaza at Blast Furnace 1, which tapped its first iron on 26 September 1959 with Premier Zhou Enlai at the opening ceremony twenty days later, and, by arrangement, views of working production lines. It was named a National Industrial Tourism Demonstration Base in 2022 and suits visitors interested in heavy industry and the history of Baotou.

rows.name: Chilechuan Scenic Area, Tumed Right Banner
rows.summary: Chilechuan Scenic Area is a group of sights in Tumed Right Banner, covering about 16 square kilometres between the Daqing Mountains and the Yellow River. Its anchor is the Chilechuan Museum in Salaqi, a branch of the Inner Mongolia Museum with galleries on regional history, local revolutionary history and folk culture; the area also takes in Jiufeng Mountain, an orchard-picking and village-life area at Dayantan, a liquor-making culture park and a leather and fur market. It suits visitors who want a museum visit combined with outings from Baotou or Hohhot.

rows.name: Chunkunshan
rows.summary: Chunkunshan is a mountain area of about 30 square kilometres in Guyang County, the highest range in Baotou, with a main peak of 2,340 metres. Its upper slopes are gently rounded and carry extensive alpine meadow, while the steeper flanks have rock outcrops, birch stands and caves; named sights include Hongqi Peak, a herb garden and a cave gully. It suits hikers and day visitors from Baotou.

rows.name: Huawu Renjian Garden Park
rows.summary: Huawu Renjian is a commercial leisure park in the hills of the Xiguitu new district of Shiguai District, modelled on a park of the same name near Chengdu. It combines urban-farming plots and a children's creative farm with a castle-style play area, a lawn wedding venue, a winery and a French-style small town. It is a modern attraction built for families and day-trippers from Baotou rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Jimusitai Scenic Area
rows.summary: Jimusitai, which Chinese sources render as Huaguoshan or 'Flower-and-Fruit Mountain', is a group of rocky hills with weathered stone formations in Damao Banner. Walking trails of about 4 km run through the 'stone forest' and past old elm trees to the Bayanbaogeda obo, a stone-cairn shrine, and horse riding, archery and horse shows are among the activities on offer. It suits visitors who want hill scenery and Mongolian culture on a trip from Bailingmiao.

rows.name: Kundulun Zhao (Faxi Temple)
rows.summary: Kundulun Zhao, given the name Faxi Temple under the Qing, is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery in the foothills on the northern edge of Baotou's Kundulun District. Its small Yellow Temple dates from 1729, and the complex became the banner temple of the Urad Middle Banner, once with more than twenty halls, white stupas and dozens of lamas' houses. The Yellow Temple pairs a Tibetan-style prayer hall with a Chinese-style hipped-roof sanctuary behind it, and the monastery suits visitors interested in Mongol Buddhist architecture who want a short trip from the city.

rows.name: Machi Ancient City and Zhaowan Tombs
rows.summary: Machi is the site of Jiuyuan, a frontier city founded by the state of Zhao in the Warring States period and kept as the seat of Jiuyuan Commandery under the Qin and of Wuyuan Commandery under the Han. It is laid out in two joined enclosures, a north and a south city, and the rammed-earth wall of the south city, more than 2,000 years old, can still be climbed. The Zhaowan Han tombs nearby have yielded roof tiles inscribed 'Chanyu tianjiang', linked to the Xiongnu ruler Huhanye's visit to the Han court in 33 BC.

rows.name: Meidaizhao Monastery
rows.summary: Meidaizhao is a walled monastery in Tumed Right Banner that began as a fortified town built by the Tumed Mongol leader Altan Khan in the 16th century and later became a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist temple. Earth walls faced with stone, about 5 metres high, enclose halls of the Ming period, and the murals, about 1,650 square metres in all, include scenes from the Buddha's life and a group of Mongol donor figures. It suits visitors interested in Mongol history and Buddhist art.

rows.name: Meilegen Scenic Area
rows.summary: Meilegen is a mountain valley on the south side of the Wula Mountains in Jiuyuan District, with a Gelug-school lamasery at its mouth and a stream, cypress woods and waterfalls further up; one waterfall drops about 60 metres. The lamasery, Meilegen Zhao (Guangfa Temple), was a centre of the Mongolian-language Buddhist chanting tradition of the Urad Mongols, and the valley was historically a route through the Yin Mountains. It suits hikers and visitors interested in Mongolian Buddhist heritage who want a half-day outing from Baotou.

rows.name: Nanhai Wetland
rows.summary: Nanhai Wetland lies on the north bank of the Yellow River at the southern edge of Baotou's Donghe District, a lake and floodplain wetland that formed after the river shifted south. About 2,990 hectares in all, it takes in a provincial wetland nature reserve and Baotou Yellow River National Wetland Park, with Nanhai Lake and Erhaizi lake fringed by reeds and open woodland and grass. Lakeside paths, viewpoints and a sand beach make it an easy half-day outing from the city.

rows.name: Northern Weapon City
rows.summary: Northern Weapon City is an open-air display of retired weapons set in a landscaped park with lakes in Baotou's Qingshan District, planned and set up by the Beizhong Group (Northern Heavy Industries), part of China North Industries Group. It shows more than 40 pieces, including artillery, armoured vehicles, aircraft, missiles and steam locomotives, among them the first anti-aircraft gun, missile and jet fighter developed in China. It is listed as a National Industrial Tourism Demonstration Base under the name Northern Heavy Industries Industrial Tourism Zone and suits visitors interested in military and industrial history.

rows.name: Qin Great Wall, Guyang
rows.summary: This stretch of the Great Wall was built under the First Emperor of Qin more than 2,200 years ago and runs for about 120 km through the hills of Guyang County, north of Baotou, as a defence against the Xiongnu. A Qin Great Wall National Cultural Park in the county, with a visitor centre, a frontier post-station building, a lecture hall and a walking trail along the wall, was under construction in 2024 and was receiving visitors by 2025. It suits visitors interested in early imperial China and the northern frontier.

rows.name: Saihan Tala Urban Grassland
rows.summary: Saihan Tala is a large area of native grassland in the middle of Baotou, protected by a city regulation since 2007 and covering about 10,680 mu (roughly 7 square kilometres) as of 2020. Cattle and sheep graze on it, and deer and more than 30 species of wild animals live in the park. It suits visitors who want to walk or sit on open grassland without leaving the city.

rows.name: Shihua Grassland (Poetry and Painting Grassland)
rows.summary: Shihua Grassland is a purpose-built tourist camp on open steppe in Damao Banner, made up of arcs of white ger-style buildings around landscaped plazas. In 2022 Baotou named it one of the first seven night-time culture and tourism consumption zones in the city, and in 2024 it was a branch venue of the banner's Naadam festival. It is a modern commercial development rather than a traditional encampment, suited to visitors who want an organised grassland outing near Bailingmiao.

rows.name: Silu Mengjun Grassland Tourism Area
rows.summary: Silu Mengjun is a purpose-built tourist complex on the grassland near Xilamuren town in Damao Banner, laid out as a compound of ger-style buildings around central plazas. In 2022 Baotou named it one of the first seven night-time culture and tourism consumption zones in the city, and in 2024 it was a branch venue of the banner's Naadam festival. It is a modern commercial development, suited to visitors who want an organised grassland outing with an evening programme.

rows.name: Hetao Agricultural Culture Expo Park
rows.summary: The Hetao Agricultural Culture Expo Park is a farming-themed attraction in Wuyuan County, built by a local agricultural company within the Baliqiao farm-tourism complex. Its Hetao Farming Museum shows more than 6,000 farm tools from the Stone Age to the present day, and the grounds include a 476-metre model of the Yellow River, a solar-terms square and greenhouses. It is used for school study tours and suits families with children.

rows.name: Hetao Liquor Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: The Hetao Liquor Industrial Tourism Area is a factory-visit attraction at the Hetao liquor company's distillery in Shanba, the Hanggin Rear Banner seat. The Hetao brand grew out of a distillery founded there in 1952, is listed as a China Time-honoured Brand, and is best known for its baijiu. It suits visitors interested in how local spirits are made.

rows.name: Nalin Lake
rows.summary: Nalin Lake is a reed-fringed lake and wetland on the Nalintaohai farm in Dengkou County, at the western edge of the Hetao plain. It is run as an ecotourism area, and Bayannur's official food-themed tourism route lists the fish meals served beside it. It suits a short lakeside stop rather than a full day.

rows.name: Sanshenggong Water Conservancy Scenic Area
rows.summary: Sanshenggong is a large barrage on the Yellow River, built between 1959 and 1961, that feeds the Hetao irrigation district. The scenic area covers the barrage and about 55 km of river channel, with sandbars and more than 30,000 mu of wetland, and it straddles Dengkou County in Bayannur, Hanggin Banner in Ordos and Alxa Left Banner. A lake park lies beside the east end of the barrage, on the Hanggin Banner bank.

rows.name: Ulan Buh Sand Sea Lake
rows.summary: The Ulan Buh Sand Sea Lake tourist area lies at the eastern end of the Ulan Buh Desert in Hanggin Rear Banner, where dunes meet a lake, with the Yin Mountains to the north and the Yellow River to the south. It offers sandboarding, rides by camel or dune buggy, desert camping and evening bonfires, and has hosted events such as a desert Naadam. It has been developed as a tourism area since 2015.

rows.name: Ulansuhai Nur (Wuliangsuhai)
rows.summary: Wuliangsuhai, or Ulansuhai Nur, is a shallow freshwater lake on the north bank of the Yellow River in Urad Front Banner, formed from an old river channel and fed mainly by drainage from the Hetao irrigation district. Reed beds cover much of it, and it is a stopover for more than 120 species of bird, among them whooper swans and spot-billed pelicans, as well as an important freshwater fishery. The ecotourism area is in Erdenburag sumu on the lake's south-western side.

rows.name: Wuyuan Anti-Japanese War Memorial Park
rows.summary: The Wuyuan Anti-Japanese War Memorial Park commemorates the Wuyuan campaign of early 1940, in which Chinese forces under Fu Zuoyi retook Wuyuan, Linhe and Shanba from Japanese forces after about two months of fighting. The park holds the Inner Mongolia Anti-Japanese War Memorial Hall and a street laid out for urban-fighting displays. It suits visitors interested in the war in northern China and in Bayannur's local history.

rows.name: Xinhure Ancient City
rows.summary: Xinhure is the ruin of a large walled town of the Yuan and Ming periods on the grassland of Urad Middle Banner, a roughly square enclosure about a kilometre across. Lines of earth wall can still be traced round the enclosure, and the interior is now farmland. It suits visitors interested in frontier towns of the Mongol era who are happy to see an unmarked site.

rows.name: Yinshan Rock Paintings
rows.summary: The Yinshan rock paintings are engraved images on cliffs and boulders along the Langshan range, spread over Dengkou County and the Urad banners of Bayannur. Surveys in 1976–80 counted more than 10,000 images of animals, hunters, riders, chariots and dancers, with later inscriptions in Turkic, Uyghur, Tangut and Mongolian, dating from the Neolithic to recent centuries. Bayannur's official archaeology route takes visitors to the Gel Aobao Gou and Molehetu Gou panels in Dengkou.

rows.name: Aohan Hot Spring Resort
rows.time_needed: Half a day or an overnight stay
rows.summary: A hot-spring health resort at Reshuitang village in the hills of south-west Aohan Banner, about 695 m above sea level beside planted pine woods. The spring comes out at about 68°C and is rich in radon, and the wellness complex includes a Mongolian and Chinese medicine hospital. It suits a spa stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Arshihaty Granite Forest
rows.summary: A park area of the Hexigten Global Geopark in the north of Hexigten Banner, where granite columns and crags 5 to 30 metres high stand along a mountain ridge at about 1,700 metres above sea level. The rock is notable for its strong horizontal jointing, and sections of the forest have names such as Moon Castle, Sworn Brothers and Eagle with Folded Wings. The name comes from a Mongolian word meaning steep rocks.

rows.name: Baoshan and Hansumu Tombs
rows.summary: Baoshan is an early Liao cemetery of Khitan nobles on a gentle slope, enclosed by earth walls about 200 m long on the east and west sides, with gates and barbicans on the east and south, and the tombs lie in three rows in the middle and northern part. Tomb 1 is dated to 923, the earliest dated tomb of a Khitan aristocrat known, and its chambers hold about 150 square metres of murals painted in three tiers, excavated in 1993. The listing also covers the Hansumu tombs, the cemetery of the Yelü Yuzhi family, a separate group in the same banner where stone figures lie scattered over the ground.

rows.name: Chaganhaote Ruins (White City)
rows.summary: Chaganhaote, or the White City, is the ruined capital that scholars identify with Ligdan Khan, the last Great Khan of the Mongols, and it is among the best-preserved earthen city sites in Inner Mongolia. Rammed-earth walls up to five metres high and palace foundations survive at the south foot of Mount Abaga, with a walled inner city 255 metres square inside an outer wall; the whole complex, with the East and West White Cities and a ritual site on the mountain, covers 690,000 square metres. Finds from the palace area include glazed dragon-scale bricks and tiles and white granite column bases.

rows.name: Chengzishan Site
rows.summary: Chengzishan is a hilltop site of the Lower Xiajiadian culture, about 4,000 years old, whose central area on the summit covers about 150,000 square metres. A low stone wall about 1.3 km long and 0.5 to 1 metre high encloses six zones with nine gates, and archaeologists found 232 circular stone rings, taken to be altars, and 80 square courtyards inside it, as well as a boar's head carved from the rock at the south-west corner. It is one of eight national heritage sites in Aohan Banner, which is known for its prehistoric archaeology.

rows.name: Chifeng Museum
rows.summary: Chifeng's main history museum stands on the bank of the Xibo River in the city's new district; its present building opened in 2010, and it is now part of the Chifeng Museum Institute. Four permanent exhibitions cover the prehistoric Hongshan culture, Bronze Age finds from the Xiajiadian cultures, the Liao dynasty, and the Yuan to Qing periods. The collection holds more than 80,000 items, including 133 first-class national relics.

rows.name: Chifeng North Great Mosque
rows.summary: Founded in 1739 and rebuilt between 1742 and 1747, this is regarded as the largest and oldest mosque in the Chifeng area, and it was listed nationally in 2013. It follows a Chinese courtyard plan on a central axis, with a gate, side halls and a prayer hall, and a two-storey hexagonal minaret pavilion about 30 metres high rising behind the prayer hall. Carved brick, stone and wood decoration includes Arabic inscriptions and geometric and plant patterns.

rows.name: Daguangdingzi Wind Culture Resort
rows.summary: A wind-themed leisure resort on high grassland in Hexigten Banner, set among wind turbines. It combines an amusement park, a windmill-themed park, a ski area and flower fields, and hosts a music festival and a kite festival. It suits families and groups looking for rides and events rather than quiet scenery.

rows.name: Dali Lake
rows.summary: A saline lake without an outlet on the Hexigten Banner steppe, dammed by lava flows, with the Hunshandak sand dunes on its southern side and a group of extinct volcanoes to the north-west. Swans, geese, gulls and cranes use it in summer, and it forms part of the Hexigten Global Geopark. The lake freezes from about mid-November to early April.

rows.name: Daoxugou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Daoxugou is a forested valley scenic area inside the Heilihe National Nature Reserve in the far west of Ningcheng County, covering about 1,180 hectares. Its sights include a granite 'stone-sea' forest and glacial features such as ice potholes, boulders left by glaciers and stone rivers, together with lakes, a waterwheel park, a yurt-style park and walking trails through the woods. It suits walkers and photographers who are prepared for a long drive into the mountains.

rows.name: Erdaojingzi Site and Museum
rows.summary: Erdaojingzi is a settlement of the Lower Xiajiadian culture, about 4,000 years old, found in 2009 during construction of the Chifeng–Chaoyang expressway and named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of that year. The expressway was routed through a tunnel beneath the site so that the excavated houses, courtyards, storage pits, roads and walls could be kept where they were. An air-supported membrane building now covers the dig as the site museum, opened in 2018, where visitors see the ancient structures in place and watch 4D films about the site.

rows.name: Falun Temple
rows.summary: Falun Temple is a Tibetan Buddhist temple built in 1745 in a mixed Mongol and Han style, and served as the banner temple of the Harqin Mongol princes. Its surviving buildings include the Hall of Heavenly Kings, bell and drum towers, the Zhantan Hall, the main hall, two Arhat halls and side halls, which make it a useful place to see Qing-period temple architecture in the Harqin area.

rows.name: Fanzong Temple
rows.summary: Fanzong Temple is a Gelug Tibetan Buddhist monastery that served as the banner temple of the Ongniud princes; it was moved to its present hillside site in 1743, and the Qianlong emperor gave it its name. Its halls climb the slope in three courtyards, from the Hall of Heavenly Kings through the two-storey main sutra hall to the Maitreya hall, with painted and carved decoration on the roofs and beams. Damaged in the Cultural Revolution, it has been restored since 1987 and was registered as a place of worship in 1995.

rows.name: Fuhui Temple
rows.summary: Fuhui Temple was the banner temple of Harqin and the family temple of the princes, built in the Kangxi period of the Qing dynasty. It has subsidiary temples beside a main axis of gate, Hall of Heavenly Kings, sutra hall and main hall, and about 450 lamas lived there at its height. It stands in Damiao village about a kilometre from the Harqin princes' palace and is managed together with the museum there.

rows.name: Han Kuangsi Family Cemetery
rows.summary: The cemetery of Han Kuangsi, a Liao-dynasty official, and his family lies on the south slope of Baiyinhan Mountain in Bairin Left Banner. It has two groups of graves: the north gully, where Han's own tomb is ringed by a stone-built cemetery wall, and the west gully, with more than twenty graves; rows of building foundations and scattered Liao bricks and tiles can be made out on the ground to the south-east.

rows.name: Heicheng Han City Site
rows.summary: Heicheng is the site of a walled city of the Han dynasty beside Heicheng village in Youbeiping town, identified in Chinese sources as Pinggang, the Western Han seat of Youbeiping commandery. Banks of the old earthen walls still mark out large rectangular enclosures, which have been fenced off from the surrounding fields as a protected area. The site suits visitors with a particular interest in the Han dynasty in this region.

rows.name: Hongshan Sites
rows.summary: Hongshan, a reddish hill on the north-east edge of Chifeng that gave the city its name, is the type site of the Hongshan culture (about 4700 to 2900 BC), first recorded there in 1908 by the Japanese archaeologist Torii Ryūzō. The protected group takes in Hongshan-culture settlement remains and later Xiajiadian-culture ritual sites and stone-coffin graves on and around the hill. The Hongshan Culture Museum at the foot of the hill, opened in 2019, shows the finds in a permanent exhibition of seven sections with models and multimedia.

rows.name: Huifu Temple
rows.summary: Huifu Temple is a Gelug Tibetan Buddhist temple in the middle of Daban, built in 1706 under Prince Urgun of the Bairin Right Banner and Princess Rongxian, a daughter of the Kangxi emperor. Its three courtyards run from the Hall of Heavenly Kings through the main hall to the sutra hall, with murals and woodblock prints inside, and the temple has been in worship use again since 1995. Large temple fairs are held there several times a year, including on the fifteenth day of the fourth and sixth lunar months.

rows.name: Ka La Qin Palace
rows.summary: The palace was the seat of the Harqin princes under the Qing dynasty, begun in 1679 and enlarged in 1783 to the standard of a prince's mansion. It covers about 40,000 square metres in three parallel axes and now houses the Harqin Banner Museum, whose collection is mostly Qing and Republican-period furniture, porcelain, Tibetan Buddhist objects and Mongol household items. Gungsangnorbu, the last prince and a reformer, was born here in 1872.

rows.name: Liao Imperial Tombs and Qingzhou White Pagoda
rows.summary: This national heritage listing covers the burial grounds of the Liao emperors and the towns that served them, spread across Bairin Left and Bairin Right Banners. At Qingzhou, a seven-storey octagonal brick and timber pagoda built in 1047–49 for the mother of Emperor Xingzong rises about 73 metres above the plain, covered in relief carvings that include 56 guardian kings. At Zuzhou, in Bairin Left Banner, rammed-earth walls with four gates and corner towers still stand beside Zuling, the tomb of the dynasty's founder Abaoji and his empress Shulü Ping, completed in 927.

rows.name: Liao Middle Capital (Zhongjing) Site
rows.summary: Zhongjing was the Middle Capital of the Liao dynasty, walled in 1007 and laid out in three nested enclosures on the model of the Northern Song capital Kaifeng. Little remains above ground apart from stretches of wall and three Liao pagodas, the tallest of them the Daming Pagoda, a 13-storey octagonal brick tower about 80 metres high. The Liao Zhongjing Museum beside it has a model of the city layout and an exhibition on its history.

rows.name: Liao Shangjing Site
rows.summary: Shangjing, founded in 918, was the first capital of the Khitan-built Liao dynasty, and its ruins beside the Shali River form a national archaeological site park. The northern imperial city still has rammed-earth walls several metres high, which visitors can follow on a boardwalk through the horseshoe-shaped barbican of the west gate, and the remains of a large Buddhist temple stand on a rise inside the walls. The Liao Shangjing Museum beside the site shows tomb murals, epitaphs, clay arhat figures from the temple and a model of the city.

rows.name: Lingyue Temple
rows.summary: Lingyue Temple stands in the middle of Jinshan town and was built in the Kangxi reign as the family temple of the emperor's fifth daughter, Princess Heshuo Duanjing, and her husband. The symmetrical Qing layout runs from a gate with bell and drum towers through front, middle and main halls to a sutra store, with decorated eaves and a century-old silk tree in the courtyard. It once had more than 100 halls and about 500 resident lamas, and worshippers come on the first and fifteenth of the lunar month and at Buddhist festivals.

rows.name: Longquan Temple, Jinshan
rows.summary: Longquan Temple is a small hillside temple about 3 km north-west of Jinshan, built in three terraces below Lion Rock beside a spring that gives it its name, Dragon Spring. The compound has a gate, front hall, side halls and a rear main hall, with a reclining stone lion in the courtyard and old pines and cypresses. Two stone tablets stand before the side halls: one of 1341 records the temple's building in 1317 under the Yuan, and one of 1917 records its repair by the Harqin prince.

rows.name: Meilingu Ski Resort
rows.summary: A ski resort in the mountains of Harqin Banner with eight runs, three for beginners and five for intermediate and advanced skiers, and a 194-room hotel. It was a venue for the alpine skiing and snowboard events of the 14th National Winter Games in 2024 and hosted the opening snowboard parallel giant slalom races of the 2024–25 FIS World Cup in late 2024, on a run certified by the International Ski Federation. It suits skiers and snowboarders, from beginners upwards.

rows.name: Mushixia Wartime Fortifications Site
rows.name_zh: 侵华日军木石匣工事旧址
rows.summary: Fortifications built by the Japanese army in 1941–43 survive beside the Mushixia river at Silibeng village in Tongxing town, at the eastern foot of the Huanggangliang range. An exhibition hall at the site displays objects (some of them replicas), photographs and reconstructed scenes covering the occupation period and the revolutionary history of Hexigten Banner from 1921 to 1949, and visitors can also see the remains of the works themselves. It is a local-history stop of about an hour for visitors interested in the region's twentieth-century history.

rows.name: Wu'anzhou Site and White Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda stands on a rise at the west edge of Baitazi village and is the standing monument of the Wu'anzhou site, a town of the Liao, Jin and Yuan periods that was listed nationally in 2013. The pagoda is octagonal with closely spaced eaves and a hollow interior, and dates from the early Liao. It was repaired from 2020 to 2022 after cracks and a lean put it at risk of collapse.

rows.name: Yingchang
rows.summary: Yingchang was a walled city built from 1270 for the Khongirad Mongols, who supplied empresses to the Yuan court, and its lords held the title Prince of Lu. The last Yuan emperor, Toghon Temür, withdrew here in 1369 after losing Dadu and died here in 1370; Ming forces took the city in 1370 and it fell out of use in the following decades. The earthen walls, about 650 m from north to south and 600 m from east to west and up to 3 m high, still enclose the grassland, with gates in the east, south and west walls.

rows.name: Yulong Sand Lake
rows.summary: A lake among dunes at the western edge of the Horqin Sandy Land in Ongniud Banner, with grassland, wetland, rock outcrops and pine stands nearby. It is named after the Hongshan-culture jade dragon unearthed in the area in 1971 and known as China's first dragon. Activities include sightseeing around the lake and off-road driving on the dunes.

rows.name: Zhang Yingrui Family Cemetery
rows.summary: Zhang Yingrui was a Yuan-dynasty official who served the Khongirad princes, and his family cemetery lies at Guogongfu village in Wutonghua town. The buildings above ground are gone, but a 4.3 m stele naming him Duke of Ji, a title granted in 1335, survives complete beside a broken second stele, and the grounds hold two civil and two military officials in stone with pairs of stone lions, qilin and other beasts. The inscription is a rare surviving Yuan stele and is used as a source for the history of the Khongirad tribe.

rows.name: Zhenji Temple Grottoes (Zhaomiao)
rows.summary: The Zhenji Temple grottoes are three Liao-dynasty caves cut into a cliff face in a valley in the hills south of Lindong, with a Qing-dynasty lamasery, Shanfu Temple, built against them; locally the place is called Zhaomiao. The central cave, whose lintel is inscribed "Zhenji Zhi Si", holds a reclining Buddha with mourning disciples and over a hundred small Buddha figures on its walls, the south cave has a Buddha flanked by Manjushri on a lion and Samantabhadra on an elephant, and the north cave has two chambers with relief figures. The Zhaomiao scenic area around them covers about 60 square kilometres of rock outcrops and temple buildings in the Qiguoshan National Geopark.

rows.name: Zimeng Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir in the hills of Ningcheng County, known as Dahushi Reservoir until it was renamed Zimeng Lake in 2010, with a water surface of about 600 hectares. The south shore has boat rides and water activities, and the north shore has a children's play castle, a rainbow slide, a water-play park, barbecue and camping areas, evening light shows, an exhibition hall and a folk museum. It suits families after a day of water play.

rows.name: Aolunbukan Forest Culture Tourism Area
rows.summary: Aolunbukan is a forest tourism area of about 292 square kilometres in the Greater Khingan hills near Bailang town, Arxan, with primeval forest, volcanic lava terrain, wetland and streams. An upgrade in 2026 added ten staged scenes along its trails, rafting on its natural river and UTV routes through forest and lava field. It suits visitors adding half a day to an Arxan trip.

rows.name: Arxan Port Scenic Area
rows.summary: The scenic area is built around Arxan Port, a road port of entry in the forested Greater Khingan hills west of Arxan. The port became a class I port in 2012, was closed from the end of 2019 and reopened on 3 April 2023. It suits visitors to Arxan with half a day to spare.

rows.name: Arxan–Chaihe Scenic Area
rows.summary: The scenic area covers about 1,031 square kilometres and spans Arxan in Hinggan League and Chaihe town in Zalantun, Hulunbuir. The Arxan part is centred on the Arxan National Forest Park, with forest, the crater lake of Tianchi (Heavenly Lake), the Yimin River and the Shitang Forest, in a town whose name comes from the Mongolian for 'hot holy water' because of its mineral springs. The Chaihe part lies north in Hulunbuir, around the Chaihe and Chuoer rivers.

rows.name: Chaersen Reservoir
rows.summary: Chaersen Reservoir is a large reservoir on the Tao'er River, a tributary of the Nen, 1.7 km north of Chaersen town in Horqin Right Front Banner. Work began in 1973, stopped in 1980, restarted in 1987 and had its main works finished in 1990, for flood control and irrigation with some power generation, and the reservoir can hold about 1.25 billion cubic metres. It was named a national water-conservancy scenic area in 2005 and suits visitors who want open water an easy trip from Ulanhot.

rows.name: Former Office of the CPC Inner Mongolia Working Committee
rows.name_zh: 中国共产党内蒙古工作委员会办公旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng Nèiměnggǔ Gōngzuò Wěiyuánhuì Bàngōng Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The offices used by the CPC Inner Mongolia Working Committee in 1947 stand in the centre of Ulanhot and are now an exhibition site. A telegram gallery displays 31 telegrams sent from the party centre, together with radio sets and coded messages, and visitors can try a simulated telegram send-and-receive. The site is managed with the May First Site by the Inner Mongolia National Liberation Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Genghis Khan Temple, Ulanhot
rows.summary: The Genghis Khan Temple stands on Hanshan hill in the north of Ulanhot and was built in the early 1940s, finishing in 1944, with donations from Mongol communities. The hall is shaped like the character shan (山) with a round dome over a square body, and houses a gilded bronze seated statue of Genghis Khan, 2.8 m high, with Yuan-period weapons and costume in the side halls and murals of his life on the walls. The temple was damaged in the Cultural Revolution, restored from 1983 and completed in its present form in 1987.

rows.name: Haishen Shengquan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in the centre of Arxan, built over the town's mineral springs, with spa pools, a rehabilitation hospital and the China Hot Spring Museum, which opened in 2004. Arxan takes its name from the Mongolian for 'hot holy water', and the town's springs range from cold to very hot. It suits visitors who want to soak after hiking in the forest park.

rows.name: Hangali Lake Resort
rows.summary: Hangali Lake is a lake just north of Bayan Huxu in Horqin Right Middle Banner, with a leisure resort on its eastern shore. It is one of the stops on the banner's tourist circuit, with the maple forest and the Tushiyetu prince's palace. It suits visitors who want a short lakeside stop in the banner.

rows.name: Inner Mongolia Autonomous Government Founding Conference Site
rows.name_zh: 内蒙古自治政府成立大会会址
rows.pinyin: Nèiměnggǔ Zìzhì Zhèngfǔ Chénglì Dàhuì Huìzhǐ
rows.summary: This two-storey blue-brick hall with a swallow-tail roof was built in 1935 as the auditorium of the Manchukuo army's Xing'an military academy. The Inner Mongolia People's Congress met here from 23 April to 1 May 1947 and elected the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Government, with Ulanhu as chairman. The building was fully repaired in 2007 and shows 159 exhibits, and the Inner Mongolia National Liberation Memorial Hall manages it.

rows.name: Inner Mongolia National Liberation Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 内蒙古民族解放纪念馆
rows.summary: The memorial hall in Ulanhot, the city where the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Government was founded in 1947, was built to mark the autonomous region's 60th anniversary and opened in August 2007. It also manages the May First Site, the Inner Mongolia Working Committee office and the Ulanhu office, which together are known as the 'one hall, three sites'. It suits visitors interested in modern Inner Mongolian history and can be combined with the other sites in the city.

rows.name: Japanese Military Fortification Remains at Arxan
rows.name_zh: 侵华日军阿尔山要塞遗址
rows.summary: The site is a group of Japanese military works of 1935–44 around Arxan, listed together as a national monument, including the town's railway station and the bunkers at the ends of the North and South Xing'an tunnels. Arxan station, first named Wenquan (Hot Spring) station, was built in 1935–37 for the military railway line and is still used by passenger trains. The station is the part easiest to visit, in the centre of the town.

rows.name: Tianjiao Tianjun Eco-tourism Resort
rows.summary: Tianjiao Tianjun is an eco-tourism resort on the hill of Tianjun at the northern edge of Ulanhot, close to an expressway interchange. The hill, bared by stone quarrying, was replanted by the local government and opened as a scenic area. It has terraced planting, visitor buildings and a viewing platform, and suits residents and passing visitors who want a short outing from the city.

rows.name: Ulan Maodu Grassland
rows.summary: Ulan Maodu is a rolling hill grassland in the north-west of Horqin Right Front Banner, crossed by the winding Jiuqu River. Visitors eat Mongolian food in gers, and the grassland hosts riding, costume and music events, including the Hinggan League Naadam in August 2023, which drew more than 220,000 visitors. It suits visitors who want open grassland in Hinggan.

rows.name: Wujiaofeng Maple Forest
rows.summary: The scenic area is a large stand of painted maples (wujiaofeng) scattered through open woodland on the Daichintala grassland in Horqin Right Middle Banner. The leaves turn red, purple and orange in early October, and the banner runs a maple tourism season with a camping ground, guesthouses and cultural events. It suits visitors in the first half of October, and is usually visited together with the Tushiyetu palace and Hangali Lake.

rows.name: Zhongying Film Production Base
rows.summary: Zhongying Film Production Base is a film-set complex of streets and buildings next to the Tushiyetu prince's palace in Horqin Right Middle Banner, open to visitors as a tourist site. The palace, the seat of the Qing prince of the banner, stands a few hundred metres away and is a separate attraction. Visitors travelling the banner's circuit of maple forest, palace and lake can fit the film base in as a short stop.

rows.name: Aowei Horse Culture Eco-tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 奥威马文化生态旅游区
rows.summary: Aowei is a horse-culture park of about 1,542 mu (roughly 100 hectares), set up in 2014 at Qiganqi village in Shengle town, with a racecourse for up to 20,000 spectators, stables and a riding ground. Visitors can feed, groom and ride horses, take riding lessons and watch staged horse shows and parades, and the park also has a children's playground, a boating lake and a horse museum. It suits families and school groups wanting hands-on time with horses within a day trip of Hohhot.

rows.name: Daheihe Military Culture Park
rows.summary: Daheihe Military Culture Park is a themed leisure park on the Daheihe river in Saihan District, on the south-eastern side of Hohhot. It has a flower-field zone and serves as an events ground: its winter ice-and-snow festival has an ice castle, ice-sculpture lanterns and a food market, and the park was the main venue for the opening of Inner Mongolia's 2026 Spring Festival tourism programme and for parts of the Zhaojun Culture Festival. It suits local families and visitors in Hohhot during the festival seasons.

rows.name: Daqingshan Anti-Japanese Guerrilla Base Site, Wuchuan
rows.name_zh: 大青山抗日游击根据地旧址旅游区
rows.pinyin: Dàqīngshān Kàngrì Yóujī Gēnjùdì Jiùzhǐ Lǚyóuqū
rows.summary: The Daqing Mountains around Deshenggou village in Wuchuan County were the core of the Daqingshan anti-Japanese guerrilla base, set up in 1938 by an Eighth Route Army force that marched north from Shanxi. The tourism area includes the old command-post site in Deshenggou village at about 2,000 m and an exhibition hall on the base's history, with farmstays in nearby villages. Chinese historical accounts record more than 500 engagements with Japanese and puppet forces in the area between 1938 and 1942.

rows.name: Daqingshan Taiwei Sports and Leisure Resort
rows.name_zh: 大青山太伟运动休闲度假区
rows.summary: Daqingshan Taiwei Sports and Leisure Resort is a resort in the foothills of the Daqing Mountains in Baoheshao town, on the north-eastern edge of Hohhot. The city's culture and tourism bureau lists it as one of Hohhot's three ski areas, alongside Mazongshan and Northern Lights. It suits winter visitors who want to ski within a short drive of the city.

rows.name: Daqingshan Wildlife Park
rows.summary: Daqingshan Wildlife Park is a zoo of about 12,300 mu (roughly 8 square kilometres) on the northern edge of Hohhot, set against the Daqing Mountains and open since 2006. It holds around 100 species in themed animal areas. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Dashengkui Museum Cluster
rows.summary: The Dashengkui Museum Cluster is a group of small museums in courtyard buildings in the style of Qing-dynasty houses, in the old town of Hohhot. It is themed on Dashengkui, the Shanxi merchant house that traded with the Mongolian plateau and Russia until it collapsed in 1929. The district government describes seven themed halls with reconstructed street scenes of the Dashengkui shop, a money-shop and a tea house, and displays of camel-caravan account books and merchants' contracts; the Inner Mongolia Morin Khuur Art Museum is in the north section.

rows.name: Dayao Site
rows.summary: Dayao is a Palaeolithic stone-tool workshop on the south hill above Dayao village, found in 1973, where people quarried flint and made tools from roughly 500,000 to 10,000 years ago; it gave its name to the Dayao culture. The site spreads over more than 2 sq km of gullies and slopes, with scattered stone flakes on the ground, a protection monument and an excavated earth section 16 m deep at the Sidaogou locality. It is run as the Dayao Site Park by the Hohhot Museum Academy and suits visitors interested in early tool-making.

rows.name: Dazhao Temple
rows.summary: Dazhao is the oldest Gelug (Yellow Hat) temple in Hohhot, begun in 1579 by the Tümed Mongol leader Altan Khan in his newly founded city of Guihua. This Tibetan Buddhist monastery is also called the Silver Buddha Temple after its silver statue of Sakyamuni, which the Third Dalai Lama consecrated during his visit in 1586. The temple has a Chinese-style layout with a main hall combining Chinese and Tibetan styles, and holds Buddhist festivals through the year.

rows.name: Five Pagoda Temple, Hohhot
rows.summary: The Five Pagoda Temple, formally the Diamond Throne Relic Pagoda, is a Qing-dynasty brick pagoda about 16 m tall, begun in the Yongzheng reign (from 1727), with five small pagodas on a square base. The base is carved with the Diamond Sutra in three scripts and the upper part with more than a thousand small gilded Buddha figures, and a stone-carved star chart labelled in Mongolian stands against the north wall of the compound. The compound is now run as the Five Pagoda Temple Museum.

rows.name: Former Residence of Ulanhu
rows.summary: Ulanhu's former residence is a courtyard of about 20 rooms in Tabusai village, where Ulanhu, the founding chairman of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, was born and spent his youth. Most of the original buildings were burned in 1939 and the house was rebuilt in 1991; it now presents a farmyard with main rooms, side wings, a mill and a granary, together with exhibition rooms and a bust of Ulanhu in the yard. It is run together with the Ulanhu Memorial Hall in Hohhot.

rows.name: Grassland Gate Cultural Tourism Area, Wuchuan
rows.summary: A cultural-tourism complex built from 2020 in the town of Wuchuan by Yangufang, an oat-food company. Its themed halls cover the tea road, grassland life, ethnic culture, dairy foods and oats, and it also has a Russian-style hall, a food street built in Northern Wei style, restaurants and an evening tourism zone. It is a modern commercial development rather than a historic site, and suits visitors passing through Wuchuan on the road north to the Xilamuren and Gegentala grasslands.

rows.name: Great Mosque of Hohhot
rows.summary: The Great Mosque of Hohhot, founded in 1693 by Hui Muslims, is regarded as the oldest and largest mosque in Inner Mongolia and is an active place of worship. Its black-brick halls follow traditional Chinese building styles with Islamic decoration around two courtyards, with a prayer hall, two lecture halls, a washing room and a moon-viewing tower added in 1939. The mosque holds a handwritten Arabic Quran in 30 volumes and seven stone tablets from the Qing dynasty and later.

rows.name: Haohanshan Ming Great Wall National Cultural Park
rows.name_zh: 好汉山明长城国家文化公园
rows.pinyin: Hǎohànshān Míng Chángchéng Guójiā Wénhuà Gōngyuán
rows.summary: This is a section of the Ming-dynasty Great Wall at Haohan Mountain in Beibao township, in the far south of Qingshuihe County, where a Great Wall national cultural park began trial operation in October 2024. In 1989 the Great Wall scholar Luo Zhewen judged the Qingshuihe walls, with their watchtowers and beacon towers, to rival Badaling in construction, and the park adds a Great Wall inn, a dome-screen flight cinema and a tea-and-horse-market experience area. It suits visitors interested in Ming frontier defences.

rows.name: Hasuhai Lake
rows.summary: Hasuhai is a shallow natural lake in Tumed Left Banner, with a water surface of roughly 30 sq km and a depth of about 2 m, ringed by reed beds that attract wild ducks, geese and other waterbirds. A road circles the lake, and the scenic area on its north shore adds lakeside pavilions and tourist facilities. It is a local spot for lakeside walks and birdwatching, listed by the region as the Chilechuan Grassland Cultural Tourism Area (Hasuhai).

rows.name: Hohhot Sculpture Art Museum
rows.summary: Opened on 14 October 2023, the Hohhot Sculpture Art Museum is a grass-roofed building of 25,000 sq m on a 7.35-hectare site in eastern Hohhot, with a main sculpture hall, thematic galleries, artists' studios, a cafe and a gift shop. It opened with the first Hohhot International Sculpture Exhibition, which showed 58 invited works and 100 selected entries, and also has a gallery of Inner Mongolia-themed works. The adjoining Hohhot International Sculpture Park in the Silk Road Park to the south has 46 pieces, and the city presents both as part of a cultural axis with the Inner Mongolia Museum and Art Museum.

rows.name: Huanghe Maiyegu Eco-leisure Area
rows.summary: Huanghe Maiyegu is an eco-leisure area at Dongyingzi village in the Hekou tourist resort area of Tuoketuo County, on the Yellow River plain. Picking activities were part of the county's Yellow River opening festival in March 2024, and in March 2023 the Inner Mongolia culture and tourism department named it among the first 19 intangible-heritage tourism experience bases in the region, which host craft and performance activities. It suits families on a day trip from Hohhot.

rows.name: Inner Mongolia Museum
rows.summary: The Inner Mongolia Museum is the region's main museum, and it opened a new building of about 147,000 square metres in Hohhot on a trial basis on 20 June 2025. Its permanent exhibitions cover fossils and prehistoric life, the history of the region's peoples from the Palaeolithic to the Qing dynasty, the Great Wall zone, the region's national intangible heritage, its modern history and its ecology. The collection runs to more than 150,000 items, including dinosaur fossils and artefacts of the region's historic northern peoples.

rows.name: Inner Mongolia Museum of Natural History
rows.summary: The Inner Mongolia Museum of Natural History is the autonomous region's first large general natural-history museum, in a modern building that opened to the public in 2018. Its five permanent halls cover the region's forests, grasslands, waters and deserts, wildlife, fossils, geology and minerals, and farming and herding, and include a dinosaur hall, with an outdoor mineral park beside the building. It suits families and anyone interested in the region's natural history.

rows.name: Inner Mongolia Racecourse
rows.summary: The Inner Mongolia Racecourse, first built in 1956, is a 32-hectare equestrian ground in northern Hohhot with a grandstand 275 m long, an obstacle-riding arena, a stunt-show ground and a standard speed-racing track. It hosts the Inner Mongolia International Equestrian Festival and other horse events, and has a Horse Culture Art Gallery. The district government also lists trick-riding displays by the regional equestrian team, including mounted vaulting, archery and sabre cutting.

rows.name: Lamadong Zhao (Guanghua Temple)
rows.summary: Lamadong Zhao, named Guanghua Temple by the Qing court in 1784, is a Gelug-school Buddhist temple built against the south slope of the Daqing Mountains, below the cave where its founding lama meditated. It is counted among Hohhot's eight small zhao and consists of a front temple at the foot of the slope and a rear temple on the hillside joined to the cave. The cliff beside the cave carries Mongolian, Tibetan and Sanskrit inscriptions and about a dozen Buddha figures in relief, the carvings that give the site its national listing.

rows.name: Laoniupo Red Culture Area, Qingshuihe
rows.name_zh: 老牛坡红色文化旅游区
rows.summary: Laoniupo is a red-tourism area at the foot of the Ming Great Wall in Beibao township, in the far south of Qingshuihe County where it meets Pianguan County and Pinglu District in Shanxi. It presents the area's wartime role as a route linking Yan'an with the Daqingshan guerrilla base, through a memorial plaza for local martyrs, a Great Wall exhibition hall and wartime sites in Beibao village. The Beibao section of the Ming Great Wall runs through the same village.

rows.name: Laoniuwan Yellow River Grand Canyon
rows.summary: Laoniuwan is a gorge where the Yellow River leaves Inner Mongolia for Shanxi and the Ming-dynasty Great Wall comes down to meet the water. On the Qingshuihe bank the village has stone-built cave dwellings and a Qing-dynasty opera stage dating from 1852, and a viewing platform looks across to Wanghe Tower, a Ming watchtower on the Shanxi side. Boat trips run on the river, and the area became Hohhot's first national 5A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Little Grass Seed Park
rows.summary: Little Grass Seed Park is a visitor and study attraction inside the Mengcao Seed Industry Centre, run by the grassland-restoration company Mengcao in Shenggaiying village, north-east of central Hohhot. The centre keeps a bank of native plant seeds and grows native grasses in field plots, and it hosts school study visits in which children collect seeds and learn how grass roots hold soil. It suits families and school groups interested in grassland plants and ecological restoration.

rows.name: Mazongshan Ski Resort
rows.summary: Mazongshan Ski Resort is a ski area in the hills east of Hohhot, one of the three ski areas listed by the city's culture and tourism bureau. It has a lift serving its intermediate runs and offers night skiing in winter, and in warmer months it has dry-slope skiing and other leisure activities, with guesthouses on site. It has operated since 2022 and suits skiers and families who want snow near the city.

rows.name: Mengcao Grass Expo Park
rows.summary: Mengcao Grass Expo Park is a plant-themed park run by the grassland-ecology company Mengcao in the Horinger New Area, showing native grassland plants. It has a native-plant hall, a youth plant-ecology education zone, a wildflower valley, a drought-resistant plant institute and a seed-processing centre. It suits families and school groups interested in grassland plants and ecological restoration.

rows.name: Mengliang Ethnic Folk Park
rows.summary: A commercial ethnic-crafts centre on the western side of Hohhot. Visitors can watch handicrafts such as hand-painted shawls and leather paintings being made, and buy Mongolian costume and headwear, silver and horn crafts, knives and dairy products. It suits visitors who want to see Mongolian craft products and souvenirs in one place.

rows.name: Mengniu Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: Mengniu Industrial Tourism Area is a dairy-industry visit at the Mengniu company's base in Horinger's dairy development zone, open to visitors since 2007 and named a national industrial tourism demonstration base in November 2022. The route passes exhibition corridors on the company's history, research and product quality, an indoor display of grassland with cows and alfalfa, and the automated production lines; the visit was relaunched with updated displays in July 2026. It suits families and school groups interested in how milk is produced; the plant is an operating factory.

rows.name: Moni Mountain Intangible Heritage Town
rows.summary: Moni Mountain is a village-scale heritage tourism town on a hillside in the Daqing Mountains foothills north-west of Hohhot, where more than 80 intangible heritage items are shown and taught through master workshops, an art centre, a museum and practice bases. Its founder's family craft, Mongolian leather art, is a national intangible heritage item. It was named a national preferred project for combining heritage and tourism in 2022 and one of the region's first intangible-heritage tourism experience bases in 2023, and in June 2025 it hosted the region's main intangible-heritage event for Cultural and Natural Heritage Day.

rows.name: Nanshan Scenic Area, Horinger
rows.summary: A landscaped hill park of about 5 sq km on the southern edge of Horinger, laid out from 2000 with themes drawn from the culture of Shengle, an early capital of the Northern Wei dynasty. Its gardens include a calligraphy park, a zodiac garden, a lake and an altar of giant stone coins among about a hundred pavilions, and a peony garden is planted for the spring flowering. It is mainly a local leisure park, suited to a half-day outing from Hohhot.

rows.name: Residence of Gurun Princess Kejing
rows.summary: The Residence of Gurun Princess Kejing was built for the Kangxi Emperor's sixth daughter, who married a Khalkha Mongol prince and lived in Guihua, as old Hohhot was called. Four courtyards on a central axis survive, from the screen wall and gate through the main hall and sleeping hall to the rear rooms, and a permanent display recreates how the residence looked and was used. After housing a teacher-training school in the early 20th century, it opened as a museum around 1990.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Hohhot
rows.summary: Sacred Heart Cathedral, built in 1922–24, is the seat of the Catholic Archdiocese of Suiyuan and an active church. It is a red-brick building in a mix of Romanesque and Gothic Revival styles, with round-arched windows, a cross-shaped plan and a single 30 m bell tower; a second tower was planned but never built. It was used as a warehouse during the Cultural Revolution and returned to the church after 1980, and the bishop's residence beside it is now the Catholic seminary of Inner Mongolia.

rows.name: Saiwai Taoyuan Eco-tourism Area
rows.summary: Saiwai Taoyuan is a farm-based leisure area in Xindianzi town, in the south-east of Horinger County, which the county government describes as a green organic-farming tourism area. Its facilities include crop-growing areas using farm technology, an orchard and flower area, restaurants, leisure activities and cave-dwelling guesthouses, with wellness and retirement-living projects. It suits families and groups looking for a farm outing or an overnight stay.

rows.name: Shenquan Eco-Tourism Area, Togtoh
rows.summary: A leisure park of about 4 sq km astride the Yellow River at Haojiayao village, with a classical Chinese-style garden, lakes and birds on the east bank and a sand-dune amusement area on the Kubuqi Desert edge on the west bank. County media list activities such as sand-sliding, zip-lines, camel rides and a staged horse show. The surrounding village of Haojiayao is known for its vineyards and has a separate Yellow River viewing platform.

rows.name: South Lake Wetland Park, Hohhot
rows.summary: Nanhu (South Lake) Wetland Park is a landscape park in the south of Hohhot, laid out by the city government from 2005 and opened to the public in 2007, with wetland, fishing and grassland areas. Woodland, reed beds and ponds are crossed by paths, and the main gate is on the park's northern side.

rows.name: Suiyuan General's Yamen Museum
rows.summary: The Suiyuan General's Yamen was the office of the Qing general who commanded the Manchu banner garrison of Suiyuan, the walled 'new city' built beside Guihua (old Hohhot) between 1735 and 1739. Founded in 1737, its three courtyard routes now hold a restored display of the general's office, a Republic-era section and galleries on the history of Suiyuan and Hohhot. About 700 m of the Qing city wall survives at the former city's north-east corner, a few hundred metres from the yamen.

rows.name: Tuchengzi Archaeological Park (Shengle Ancient City)
rows.summary: Tuchengzi is regarded as the largest ancient city site on the north bank of the Yellow River's great bend, a walled city used from the Spring and Autumn period to the Yuan dynasty and identified with Shengle, the first capital of the Northern Wei. Its four walled sections, about 1.45 by 2.3 km in all, survive as earthen walls from 0.5 to 10 m high around farmland, which can be viewed from a lookout platform. The museum at the entrance shows the finds and has a reconstruction of the Eastern Han painted tomb found at Xindianzi, whose original chamber is not open to visitors.

rows.name: Ulanhu Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The Ulanhu Memorial Hall stands in Ulanhu Park in Hohhot and opened in December 1992 as a museum on the life of Ulanhu, the first chairman of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. The complex has a main exhibition hall, a memorial square, a statue platform, a flagpole, a stele pavilion and a memorial archway, with about 650 objects, photographs, documents and reconstructed scenes on display. His birthplace in Tabusai, about 43 km to the south-west, is run as part of the same museum.

rows.name: Wanbu Huayanjing Pagoda (White Pagoda)
rows.summary: The Wanbu Huayanjing Pagoda, known locally as the White Pagoda after its original whitewash, is a seven-storey octagonal brick tower from the Liao dynasty that stood in the walled city of Fengzhou, which was destroyed in the late Yuan period. Its inner galleries hold six surviving Jin-dynasty stone tablets and several hundred hand-written inscriptions left by visitors from the twelfth century onwards, in scripts including Chinese, Khitan, Jurchen and Mongolian. An exhibition hall stands beside the tower, and in 2020 visitors could no longer climb inside.

rows.name: Wusutu Apricot Valley
rows.summary: Wusutu Apricot Valley is a village-edge garden park at East Wusutu, at the foot of the Daqing Mountains on the north-western edge of Hohhot. It was laid out around old apricot trees, with pavilions and winding paths, and has added fruit picking, animal-contact areas, children's play activities and camping and barbecue spots. It is known for its apricot blossom in spring and suits families on a short outing from the city.

rows.name: Wusutu Zhao Monastery
rows.summary: Wusutu Zhao is a group of Tibetan Buddhist (Gelug) temples on the lower slope of the Daqing Mountains at the north-western edge of Hohhot, the largest temple complex outside the old city. The main temple, Qingyuan Temple, dates from the Wanli reign of the Ming dynasty, and the other temples, including Guangshou, Changshou, Luohan and Faxi, were added around it between 1690 and 1725, each walled in red and set against the hillside. Remains of the Zhao-state Great Wall lie behind the temples.

rows.name: Xilitu Zhao
rows.summary: Xilitu Zhao, also called Yanshou Temple (a name given by the Kangxi Emperor), is a Gelug Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Hohhot's old town, founded in the late 16th century. It covers about 13,000 sq m, and its large main sutra hall combines Han and Tibetan architecture. From 1708 its Xilitu Living Buddha usually held the senior monastic post in Qing-dynasty Guihua, and the temple remains an active place of worship.

rows.name: Yili Grassland Dairy Culture Tourist Area
rows.name_zh: 伊利草原乳文化旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Yīlì Cǎoyuán Rǔ Wénhuà Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: A visitor complex run by the Yili dairy group in Hohhot's dairy industrial park, built around the Yili Grassland Dairy Culture Museum, which covers the history of dairy-making among northern pastoral peoples and early dairy equipment. Visitors can walk the viewing routes through the group's milk-powder and liquid-milk plants and see feeding and milking at its model dairy farm, and a pet-interaction park opened on the site in September 2025. It is a corporate showcase, suited to families and to anyone curious about the dairy industry.

rows.name: Zhaojun Tomb
rows.summary: A 33 m rammed-earth mound on the south bank of the Dahei River is the traditional tomb of Wang Zhaojun, the Han-dynasty woman who married a Xiongnu ruler; her actual burial place is not recorded. A processional path of about 400 m lined with stone figures leads from the Zhaojun Museum to the mound, which has pavilions on its upper terrace and summit. The museum's halls cover Han-Xiongnu marriage alliances and include one called the Chanyu's Great Tent, and the mound has been restored several times since the 1960s.

rows.name: Aoluguya Reindeer Tribe
rows.summary: This scenic area beside Genhe presents the culture of the Aoluguya Ewenki, the only group in China that herds reindeer, who moved out of the forest into a settled township in 2003. Visitors walk a boardwalk into a forest enclosure to feed and photograph reindeer, see the conical tents known as chuoluozi and birch-bark craft workshops, and visit a museum devoted to reindeer culture; in winter there are reindeer-sleigh rides. It suits travellers interested in Ewenki culture and the Greater Khingan forest.

rows.name: Barag Mongol Tribe Tourist Area
rows.summary: A folk-custom park and ger camp on the Hulunbuir grassland, named after the Barag Mongols, whom the Qing court settled in Hulunbuir in the 1730s. The daily staged shows include a horse show with lasso-catching, wrestling and riding stunts using a herd of more than 300 horses, and evenings bring a bonfire party; visitors can also stay overnight in gers. It suits families and groups on a day trip along the Hailar–Manzhouli road who want a staged introduction to Mongolian customs.

rows.name: Bayanwula City Ruins
rows.summary: The ramparts of a large square walled town of the Yuan period stand in open steppe in the south of the Ewenki Autonomous Banner. A fainter outer enclosure surrounds the main walls, and traces of buildings can be made out inside.

rows.name: Busuli Military Culture Area
rows.name_zh: 布苏里北疆军事文化旅游区
rows.summary: A former military logistics reserve base in the Greater Khingan forest of the Oroqen Autonomous Banner, now presented as a military-themed visitor area. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism's rural tourism route page describes it as one of the largest military-experience sites in northern China. It is visited on the same Oroqen route as the Tuoba Xianbei park and Alihe National Forest Park.

rows.name: China Daur Ethnic Park
rows.summary: A newly built park beside Nirji, the seat of Morin Dawa Daur Autonomous Banner, themed on the history, culture and customs of the Daur people, one of China's recognised ethnic minorities. It has an intangible-heritage exhibition area, a stage for Daur song and dance, Daur-style family restaurants and a lakeside landing stage that doubles as a camping ground. Morin Dawa is known in China for the Daur hockey game, beikou, which visitors can try.

rows.name: Chinese Eastern Railway Buildings, Zalantun
rows.name_zh: 扎兰屯中东铁路建筑群
rows.summary: Zalantun grew around a station of the Russian-built Chinese Eastern Railway, and the town keeps a large group of buildings from that period, protected as part of the national-level Chinese Eastern Railway complex. The listed buildings include the station area, a water tower, a suspension bridge, a railway club, and the former railway meeting hall and forest-police headquarters, built in 1903 and 1909, which now house branches of the Inner Mongolia Chinese Eastern Railway Museum. Other listed parts of the same complex are at Bugt, where an open-air museum covers the railway tunnel, loop line and locomotive depot, and in Manzhouli.

rows.name: Ergun National Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 额尔古纳国家湿地公园
rows.summary: A river-wetland park in the Shangkuli area north-east of Ergun city, opened to visitors in 2018 and covering about 120 sq km, of which roughly 10 sq km is open to the public. A sightseeing road and footpaths link eight viewpoints among birch and willow woods, grassland and rivers, and the Bird Island–Handagai point has an elevated lookout over the whole wetland. Extras include a deer enclosure, animal feeding and rafting.

rows.name: Ergun Wetland Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hilltop viewing area on the edge of Ergun city, overlooking the winding channels of the wetland along the Genhe River and the town's blue and pink roofs. It is popular with photographers and is one of several wetland sites around Ergun, alongside the larger national wetland park to the north-east.

rows.name: Ergun White Birch Forest
rows.summary: A single-species stand of native white birch north of Ergun city, laid out with an elevated timber walkway and four themed zones for sightseeing and photography. The tourism department's description groups them as a sky walkway, a fairy-tale forest, a romance area and a photography zone. It suits a short stop on a day out from Ergun.

rows.name: Gaxian Cave and Tuoba Xianbei Park
rows.summary: Gaxian Cave is a granite cave in the forests of the northern Greater Khingan range whose west wall carries a 201-character inscription cut in 443 on the orders of the Northern Wei emperor Tuoba Tao, recording a prayer at the Tuoba Xianbei ancestral home; archaeologists identified it in 1980. The Tuoba Xianbei History and Culture Park around it adds an altar, a museum and other buildings, together with an Oroqen village display. Scholars still debate whether the cave marks the Tuoba's true place of origin.

rows.name: Genheyuan National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park around the upper Genhe River in the Greater Khingan forest, where forest, marsh, river and lake habitats are interlaced across about 590 sq km, of which roughly 200 sq km is wetland. East Asian waterfowl breed here, and the river it protects feeds the Ergun River. Visitor facilities include forest walks, an RV and log-cabin camp, and in summer rafting and wild-berry picking.

rows.name: Haotetaohai City Ruins
rows.summary: The earthen ramparts of a rectangular walled town of the Liao period stand on open grassland at the edge of a village in Chen Barag Banner. The enclosure is several hundred metres across, and faint outlines of buildings can be made out inside it.

rows.name: Heishantou City Ruins
rows.summary: The earthen ramparts of a walled town of the Jin and Yuan periods survive on a terrace in the grassland near Heishantou, a large enclosure with a smaller walled compound at its centre. The walls are now low banks and part of the interior is ploughed. The Inner Mongolia culture and tourism department identifies the town as the fief of Jochi Khasar, a younger brother of Genghis Khan.

rows.name: Hohnuur Scenic Area
rows.summary: A ger-camp resort on the shore of Hohnuur, a lake in the Chen Barag grassland, with about 4 sq km of steppe and 12 sq km of water inside the scenic area. A yurt-style visitor centre forms the core of a cluster of gers where visitors can eat, stay overnight and try horse riding, archery and Mongolian wrestling. It suits a short stop or an overnight stay on the Hailar–Manzhouli road.

rows.name: Honghuaerji Mongolian Pine National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 红花尔基樟子松国家森林公园
rows.summary: A forest park of about 67 sq km on the southern edge of the Hulunbuir sands, protecting a large continuous belt of Mongolian pine, an evergreen conifer suited to sandy soil. Rivers, lakes and marshy grassland lie among the pines, and the park borders the Ewenki and Barag steppes. It is a forest-and-grassland stop for travellers in the south of Hulunbuir.

rows.name: Hulun Lake
rows.summary: Hulun Lake, also called Dalai Lake, is the largest lake in Inner Mongolia and one of the largest freshwater lakes in China, covering about 2,300 sq km at the western end of the Hulunbuir grassland. Its shores are low and open, fringed with reed beds and wetland that form a protected nature reserve, and the lake is frozen from early November until early May. The lake is shared by Xin Barag Right Banner, Xin Barag Left Banner and Zhalainur District.

rows.name: Jinlongshan Ski Resort, Zalantun
rows.summary: A ski and leisure resort in the hills north-west of Zalantun, with 18 pistes graded from beginner to advanced, a U-shaped snowboard halfpipe and an aerials course used by national ski teams for training. It was a venue for snow events at the 2024 National Winter Games and is listed among China's first national ski-tourism resorts. Winter extras include snowmobiles and snow tubing; in summer the hill is used for hiking and camping, and a hot-spring hotel provides accommodation.

rows.name: Manzhouli National Gate and Matryoshka Square
rows.name_zh: 满洲里中俄边境旅游区
rows.summary: Manzhouli is China's largest land port, and this 5A-rated zone takes in two of its best-known sights. The first is the monumental 'national gate' at the port, the fifth gate on the site, built in 2008 with models of the four earlier ones beside it. The second is Matryoshka Square in the town, a theme square built around giant nesting dolls, the largest of which houses a hotel and a performance hall.

rows.name: Moerdaoga National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 莫尔道嘎国家森林公园
rows.summary: Moerdaoga was the first national forest park in the Inner Mongolia part of the Greater Khingan range, covering cold-temperate forest of larch and birch that turns orange and yellow in autumn. The town of Moerdaoga lies inside the park, which has about 14 sights linked by a tourist loop of more than 100 km, including a small forest sightseeing train and White Deer Island. The local government gives May to October as the best season.

rows.name: World Anti-Fascist War Memorial Park, Hailar
rows.name_zh: 世界反法西斯战争海拉尔纪念园
rows.summary: The park occupies Beishan hill on the northern edge of Hailar, where the Japanese Kwantung Army built a large underground fortress between 1934 and 1937. Visitors can enter part of the concrete tunnels and rooms beneath the hill, which held command posts, quarters and stores, and an exhibition hall covers the fortress's construction, including the testimony of a labourer who escaped, and the Soviet attack on it in August 1945. The Hailar works were among the largest fortifications the Kwantung Army built in north-east China.

rows.name: Wulan Mountain, Ergun
rows.summary: A hill scenic area of 4.7 sq km on open grassland in Heishantou town, with viewing platforms on the hill. It has a tent camp and an RV camp, and activities such as a zip line, a swing and a grass-sledging slope. It suits a half-day stop on the northern Hulunbuir tourist route.

rows.name: Zhalainur Mammoth Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park in the new town of Zhalainur District, centred on a large group of mammoth sculptures set among lakes and paths. It refers to the mammoth fossils and other Ice Age animal remains found in the local coalfield, which scientists named the Zhalainur fauna. The Zhalainur Museum on the same street displays the area's mammoth fossils, ancient human skulls and Palaeolithic stone tools, with further halls on coal mining and the Hulun Lake wetlands.

rows.name: Alzhai Grottoes
rows.summary: The Alzhai Grottoes are a Buddhist cave temple on a hill in the steppe of Otog Banner, known in Chinese as Baiyanyao, 'Hundred-Eye Caves', and nicknamed the 'Dunhuang of the grassland'. Specialists trace the carving back to the Northern Wei, while the national heritage list dates the site from the Western Xia to the Ming; about 600 m² of murals survive, mostly Tibetan Buddhist (tantric) subjects but also secular scenes, with inscriptions in Mongolian, Sanskrit, Tibetan and Chinese. It was added to the national heritage list in 2003.

rows.name: Bulonghu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Bulonghu is a hot-spring and lake resort on the grassland of Otog Banner, beside the Bulong reservoir where the Dusitu River makes a wide bend. The Ordos government's English site describes a grassland lake resort combining recreation, hot springs, conference reception, catering, accommodation and water entertainment. It is a leisure resort rather than a sightseeing destination.

rows.name: Chengchuan City Ruins
rows.summary: Chengchuan City Ruins are the remains of a walled city north-east of Chengchuan town, which the Otog Front Banner government identifies as Jianing in Youzhou, a prefecture set up in 738 to settle Turkic and Sogdian groups from the Six Hu Prefectures. Under the Western Xia it was the seat of a military commission guarding Silk Road post stations, and a Mongol army captured and burned it in 1227. The earthen walls of a rectangular enclosure about 800 m across still mark the city's outline.

rows.name: Chengchuan Red Culture Tourism Area
rows.summary: Chengchuan in Otog Front Banner was part of a Communist-led base area in the 1940s, and the tourist area gathers its memorial sites: the Yan'an Nationalities Institute Chengchuan Memorial, a memorial to Yang Zao and Han Chun, whom the Ordos government calls international communist fighters, and the Wang Zhen Well memorial park. The well was dug in 1944 under the Eighth Route Army commander Wang Zhen during wartime land reclamation, and a branch of the institute was based in Chengchuan from 1945. The area also runs training and study programmes.

rows.name: Dashatou Desert Tourism Area
rows.summary: Dashatou is a desert sports and leisure resort in the Mu Us sandy land in Otog Front Banner. Its roughly 9,600 mu (about 6 sq km) include dunes up to 50 m high, and it runs desert sports, conferences and cultural events, among them a fireworks music festival and a desert car-and-motorbike challenge in July 2025. It is a commercial resort aimed at weekend visitors and event crowds.

rows.name: Donglian Animation City
rows.summary: Donglian Animation City is a themed leisure and education complex in Hantai town, Dongsheng District, built around animated stories on moral education. Alongside animation entertainment it offers youth study tours, outdoor training and red-culture education programmes. It is a modern commercial attraction aimed at school groups and families, not a heritage site.

rows.name: Engebei Ecological Tourism Area
rows.summary: Engebei is an ecological demonstration area of about 300,000 mu (about 200 sq km) at the eastern end of the Kubuqi Desert, reclaimed from drifting sand through years of planting and development. Its attractions include the Inner Mongolia Engebei Desert Museum, viewing of desert birds and animals and of sand-binding plants, and ecological farming. It suits visitors interested in desert control and day trips from Baotou.

rows.name: Ganlinwusu Lake Area
rows.summary: Ganlinwusu is a lake-and-wetland tourist area in the Mu Us sandy land in southern Uxin Banner, where autumn brings large flocks of migrating birds to its lakes. Uxin Banner's tourism bureau presents it with the Wengongmanha National Desert Park for desert off-roading, grassland sightseeing and wetland leisure, and it has hosted open-water swimming events.

rows.name: Jiuchenggong Resort
rows.summary: Jiuchenggong is a large resort of about 6 sq km in Hantai town, Dongsheng District, themed around Manhan culture, the blend of Mongolian and Han folk traditions of the Ordos area. In winter it runs a ski field and ice-and-snow activities, and in the warmer months it offers a glass bridge, glass rafting, a jungle adventure course, go-karts, horse riding and archery. Cave-dwelling courtyards provide lodging, and it suits families and groups on a day or overnight break from the city.

rows.name: Jungar Yellow River Grand Canyon
rows.summary: In the south-east of Jungar Banner the Yellow River runs through a deep canyon along the Shanxi border, with villages, forts and river views strung along its bank. The Ordos government lists Cuijiazhai, a village registered as a traditional village in 2014 with a history of more than 170 years, the Wanjiazhai water-control project, the Taiji Bay river bend and more than 50 sights including old forts, village walls and a riverside plank path. Via ferrata routes and a glass viewing platform have been added, and Cuijiazhai stages a traditional wedding performance.

rows.name: Kangbashi Tourist Area
rows.summary: Kangbashi is the new urban district where the Ordos city government sits, and its core is rated as a tourist area made up of squares, themed parks and a city lake. The Ordos government counts 28 sights, among them seven themed squares, five themed parks, three museums, an ancient site and seven cultural buildings. The Ordos Museum, Ordos Bronze Museum and Ordos Revolution History Museum stand together on Wenhua West Road and are registered museums open all year.

rows.name: Kangzhen Grassland Silk Road Cultural Town
rows.name_zh: 康镇草原丝路文化景区
rows.summary: Kangzhen is a cultural-tourism town of about 3,500 mu in Kangbashi, built in the manner of buildings from regions along the grassland Silk Road. Its courtyards and streets imitate Mongolian, Beijing, Jin-merchant, Guanzhong and north-western styles, with food and folk displays. It is a modern theme town rather than a historic one, and stages festival events such as opera performances, fairs and winter ice-lantern shows.

rows.name: Malanhua Grassland
rows.summary: Malanhua is a grassland resort in Otog Front Banner with a large performance stage, a racecourse, a Mongolian tribe-style village, a hotel named for the 38th parallel and a ceremonial oboo square. The indoor stage seats 1,200 people for shows, and the resort is aimed at tour groups and families.

rows.name: Ordos Cashmere Industrial Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 鄂尔多斯羊绒工业旅游区
rows.summary: This industrial-tourism area in Dongsheng District is the Ordos cashmere brand's production base, about 2,800 mu in size, with east and west plants, an office zone, living quarters and a research centre that houses the national cashmere products engineering research centre. A marketing and display centre of 3,000 sq m shows the brand's full range of garments. It is a company-run site, so check whether tours are running before planning a visit.

rows.name: Ordos Cultural Industry Park
rows.summary: The Ordos Cultural Industry Park is a development of 11.9 sq km near Altan Xire, the Ejin Horo Banner seat, built around film and television production, cultural exhibition and cultural tourism. It stages live shows, and the Inner Mongolia Museum has an Ejin Horo branch here. It suits visitors interested in film and culture; it is a modern development, not a historic site.

rows.name: Ordos Grassland Tourism Area
rows.summary: This ger resort on the dry steppe of Hanggin Banner is arranged around two Mongolian golden tents and a camp of about 400 gers. It offers lodging and dining for up to 1,500 guests and Mongolian-culture activities, and suits groups and families on a grassland stay.

rows.name: Ordos Racing Town
