rows.summary: The town is built around the Ordos International Circuit, a track certified by the FIA at grade 2 that opened in 2010 and has hosted 79 national and regional events, including CTCC circuit-racing and CDGP drifting championship rounds and the long-running 'Warm City' (Nuancheng) race weekends. Other attractions are a kart track, a racing-themed hotel and the Taifaxiang Museum, a private collection of mineral crystals and ornamental stones. It suits motorsport fans and families looking for a short stop in Kangbashi.

rows.name: Ordos Wildlife Park
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Ordos Wildlife Park covers about 12 km² of hills in Dongsheng district and opened in July 2012. It has four display zones with 25 venues and outdoor areas for birds, kangaroos, bears, tigers and leopards, mountain animals and wolves, as well as a petting area and a separate marine hall. Giant pandas Qiqiao and Qixi are among the animals on show, and the park suits families.

rows.name: Qixinghu (Seven Star Lakes), Kubuqi Desert
rows.summary: Qixinghu, 'Seven Star Lakes', is a lake-and-dune resort area in the heart of the Kubuqi Desert in Hanggin Banner, developed by the Elion Resources Group; its seven lakes are laid out like the Big Dipper. A desert hotel, a desert science museum and a desert botanical house stand beside the main lake. The area was designated Kubuqi National Desert Park in 2014, and suits visitors who want to stay in the desert.

rows.name: Salawusu Site
rows.summary: Salawusu is a Palaeolithic site along a 39 km canyon of the Salawusu River in the Mu Us Sandy Land, where Émile Licent found fossils in 1922 and excavated with Pierre Teilhard de Chardin in 1923; a human tooth from the finds became the emblem of 'Hetao Man'. The fossils and stone tools belong to the Late Palaeolithic, and in June 2025 the site was listed among the national archaeological parks approved by the National Cultural Heritage Administration. Visitors see fossils and animal bones in the Salawusu Site Museum, enter a protective shelter over part of the site and walk the valley boardwalks, and the tourism area also takes in the Batuwan red-culture town, which presents local revolutionary history.

rows.name: Shartemtu Temple
rows.summary: Shartemtu is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery on the steppe of Hanggin Banner, also called Putiji'du Temple, first built in the early Ming and enlarged in 1862. Its halls were pulled down in 1958 and the temple has been rebuilt since 1989, with a Kalachakra stupa added in 2005. A small temple museum holds more than 300 Buddhist statues, thangkas and other items collected by the lama Jamyang Tubdan.

rows.name: Shuijinghu Lake Resort
rows.summary: Shuijinghu is a lakeside leisure-farming resort in the north of Jungar Banner. It has an eco-agriculture garden, a copy of an old Beijing courtyard house, angling on the lake, a fountain with music and bonfire evenings, and a hotel that can host more than 200 guests. It is a modern commercial resort for weekend breaks rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Subohan Grassland Resort
rows.summary: Subohan is a grassland leisure resort in Subuerga town, Ejin Horo Banner, built around Mongolian herding life: guests stay in gers, ride horses, eat Mongolian meals and watch staged shows. The Ordos government describes the grassland as a historic gathering and review ground of the seven banners of the Ordos league and as the site of the largest Ming and Qing post station in Ordos. It suits families and groups on a short stay away from the city.

rows.name: Uxin Zouma Culture Resort
rows.summary: This resort in Suldesumu, Uxin Banner, was begun in 2006 on saline-alkali land that has since been restored as a wetland grassland within the Mu Us sandy land. It combines grassland sightseeing and folk-culture experiences with horse events: Uxin is the home of zouma, the walking-horse contest, which is on the national intangible cultural heritage list and judges horses on a smooth, even gait. The area hosts banner-level festivals such as the fourth Uxin tourism Naadam in August 2025.

rows.name: Wanjiahui Happy World
rows.summary: Wanjiahui Happy World is a large indoor leisure complex in Dongsheng District, with about 330,000 sq m of floor space. It combines a water park of about 90,000 sq m, an indoor snow and ice park, a European-style amusement park, a themed hotel of 1,500 rooms and areas for food and shopping, so it can be visited in any season. It is a modern commercial development rather than a heritage site, and suits families with children.

rows.name: Wantong Ecological Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 蒙根花万通生态旅游区
rows.summary: A farm-based tourism area in Bainijing town, Dalad Banner, developed from the Wantong modern agriculture and livestock park. Its demonstration areas cover crop growing, greenhouse and soilless cultivation, livestock breeding and farm-technology training, and an exhibition hall serves school labour-education visits. It suits families and school groups interested in modern farming rather than historic or scenic sights.

rows.name: Xiangshawan
rows.summary: Xiangshawan is a desert resort at the eastern end of the Kubuqi Desert in Dalad Banner, known for dunes whose sand makes a humming sound when it slides. Visitors can slide down the dunes, ride camels, cross the sand by cable car or off-road vehicle, play at a desert water park and stay at resort 'islands' with hotels and tented camps, and Mongolian song-and-dance shows are staged. It is a heavily developed, family-oriented attraction that suits a day trip from Baotou or Ordos.

rows.name: Yihe Ecological and Cultural Expo Park
rows.summary: Yihe is a walled park in Ejin Horo Banner on the western edge of Kangbashi, begun in 2011 and built in Mongolian, Tibetan and Han styles, with 999 prayer wheels set in its circular outer wall. Its courtyards hold the Inner Mongolia Buddhist Culture Museum, a temple hall named Erdeni Zhao, the residence of the Ulan Living Buddha and a culture experience centre. The park runs tea-tasting, incense-making, handicraft and meditation activities and is popular with families.

rows.name: Yinkentala Desert Oasis
rows.summary: Yinkentala is a desert-and-grassland tourist park in Dalad Banner, on the south side of the Yellow River. The Ordos government lists activities including sand sledding, desert off-roading, camel rides, a desert ropeway, horse displays and an oboo ceremony, with Mongolian-style meals. It is a commercial leisure park for day trips from Baotou or Ordos.

rows.name: Yousongwang, the Pine King of Jungar
rows.summary: Yousongwang, the 'Pine King', is a Chinese pine standing in Narisong town in the south of Jungar Banner. The Ordos government gives its age as nearly a thousand years, dates its sprouting to the Xining era of the Northern Song (1068–1077) and calls it the oldest known Chinese pine in China. Temple fairs are held beside it on the 13th day of the fifth lunar month and the 15th of the seventh.

rows.name: Zhaizigedan Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic stone-walled settlement on a hilltop above the Yellow River in Jungar Banner, dating to about 5,000 years ago, between the Yangshao and Longshan cultures. An oval stone wall encloses the hilltop, with the base of a stepped platform in the middle that archaeologists read as an altar, and steep ground protects the hill on three sides. It was found in 1998 during surveys for the Wanjiazhai water project and listed nationally in 2013, and it suits visitors with a particular interest in prehistory.

rows.name: Zhunge'er Zhao (Baotang Temple)
rows.summary: Zhunge'er Zhao, formally Baotang Temple, is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery founded in 1623 and enlarged in the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns. The Ordos government describes it as the largest and best-preserved Gelug temple complex surviving in Ordos. The surrounding tourist area adds a lake with boating, a vegetarian dining hall and guest courtyards, and large religious gatherings are held here in the first, fourth and seventh lunar months.

rows.name: Baogutu Desert
rows.summary: Baogutu Desert is a stretch of dunes in Baiyintala sumu, Naiman Banner, run as a scenic area with camel rides, off-road vehicle runs over the dunes and sand sliding. It has a self-drive campsite with capsule-style rooms and regularly hosts desert off-road car races. It suits visitors who want a short desert outing in the south of Tongliao.

rows.name: Caogan Desert
rows.summary: Caogan Desert is a village-run scenic area of dunes, grass and small lakes in Sandu sumu, Horqin Left Rear Banner, set up in 2014 and covering about 9 square kilometres. It has ger-style restaurants, log cabins, container and caravan lodgings and a caravan campsite, with dune vehicle rides, a virtual-reality hall, archery tag and beach football. It suits families and self-drive groups who want an overnight stay in the desert.

rows.name: Daqinggou Nature Reserve
rows.summary: Daqinggou is a national nature reserve in the middle of the Horqin sandy land, where two spring-fed valleys, Daqinggou and Xiaoqinggou, hold broadleaf forest and streams among the dunes. A boardwalk of more than 4 km follows the valley floor, and other sights include a small lake, a lotus lake and a museum of Horqin Mongol customs, geology and specimens. Approved in 1980 and made a reserve in 1988, it suits visitors who want shade, water and woodland in a sandy region.

rows.name: Hamin Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: Hamin Archaeological Site Park protects a Neolithic village of semi-subterranean houses, dated to about 5,500 to 5,000 years ago, found in the Horqin sandy ground in 2010 after looters disturbed it. A protective hall keeps part of the excavated house floors in place, and the museum beside it, reopened in July 2024 after a refit with AR displays, shows 188 pottery, stone, jade, bone and shell pieces, while a reconstructed settlement shows how the villagers lived. It suits visitors interested in prehistoric China and can be seen in half a day from Tongliao.

rows.name: Kailu Pagoda (White Pagoda)
rows.summary: Kailu Pagoda, known locally as the White Pagoda, is a brick stupa of the Yuan dynasty standing in Baita Park in Kailu town. It has a square base, a bowl-shaped body, a spire of thirteen tiers and a bronze finial, and it was repaired in 1962 and 1993. The Kailu County Museum, which also looks after the Mai Xin memorial hall, stands in the same park.

rows.name: Mengjiaduan Wetland
rows.summary: Mengjiaduan is a large irrigation reservoir on the right bank of the West Liao River in northern Naiman Banner, built in 1958, whose upper and lower basins together hold about 108 million cubic metres. It is a national wetland park, which passed the National Forestry and Grassland Administration's pilot-stage acceptance in 2020; several rare migratory birds roost there, and the visitor area includes a fishing village and an ecological education display. It suits birdwatchers and visitors who want a day beside open water away from the towns.

rows.name: Mongol King Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: Mongol King Industrial Tourism Area is an industrial-tourism site named after the Mongol King baijiu brand, in the south of Tongliao. Tongliao's tourism bureau has backed its upgrade as one of the city's industrial-tourism sites since 2024, and the brand's baijiu won silver at the 2020 China tourism-commodities competition. It suits visitors interested in local liquor and company-run industrial tourism, and it can be fitted into a stay in the city.

rows.name: Naiman Mongolian Prince's Mansion
rows.summary: Naiman Prince's Mansion is a large Qing-period complex of grey-brick halls and courtyards in Daqintala, begun in 1863 as the residence of the Naiman Banner's Mongol prince. It is one of the better-preserved Qing official-style compounds in Inner Mongolia and now houses a museum with 46 exhibition halls, showing local history and restored period interiors of a banner prince's household. It suits visitors interested in Qing-era Mongol banner life and architecture.

rows.name: Nanbaoligaotu Site
rows.summary: Nanbaoligaotu is a late Neolithic settlement and cemetery in Jarud Banner, dated to about 4,500 to 5,000 years ago. Excavation covered more than 10,000 square metres and found 18 house sites, over 400 graves and more than 1,500 objects; the site museum, built in 2017, shows 566 pieces, among them a human-shaped pottery jar, jade ornaments and a bone headdress that the museum counts among the earliest in China. It suits visitors interested in prehistoric China, and the museum has an outdoor simulated-dig area.

rows.name: Palace of Sengge Rinchen
rows.summary: The Palace of Sengge Rinchen was built from 1740 as the palace of the ruling prince of the Horqin banner, and is best known as the seat of Sengge Rinchen (1811–1865), a Mongol prince and general who served the Qing court in the Second Opium War and against the Taiping and Nian rebellions. Part of the original palace survives, including its five-bay main hall, and the Horqin Folk Customs and History Culture Park, about 10 hectares with 85 halls, has been built around it in Qing style. It suits visitors interested in Qing-period Mongol banner life and architecture.

rows.name: Shouyin Temple
rows.summary: Shouyin Temple, also called Maidar Gegen Temple, is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist temple in the south-west of Hure Banner. Its main hall is a two-storey building in a Tibetan-Chinese style with three roofs, a three-bay porch on four carved stone columns and wooden tiger and elephant heads on the brackets, and its murals include a depiction of the eighteen hells. It joined the national list in 2013 and is a stop on a Tongliao heritage trail of Qing-style buildings.

rows.name: Three Great Temples of Kulun
rows.summary: The Three Great Temples of Kulun are three Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist temples side by side in Kulun town: Xingyuan Temple, begun in 1649, Xiangjiao Temple, built in 1670, and Fuyuan Temple, built in 1742. Under the Qing, Kulun was the only banner in Inner Mongolia ruled jointly by its lamas and the state, and Xingyuan, the largest of the three, was the seat of the head lama. About 59,000 square metres of historic buildings survive, and the group is a stop on a Tongliao heritage trail of Qing-period buildings that also takes in Naiman Prince's Mansion.

rows.name: Xiaozhuang Garden (Darhan Prince's Mansion)
rows.summary: Xiaozhuang Garden is a reconstruction of the Darhan Prince's mansion, the family home of Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang, who grew up in Horqin and married into the Qing court. The mansion was rebuilt on its old site in 2008 and opened to visitors in 2012; a hall added in 2019 presents local intangible heritage such as horse-head fiddle playing and Mongolian embroidery. The buildings are modern, and the visit suits those interested in Qing-Mongol history and the Horqin village setting.

rows.name: Yinshawan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Yinshawan is a dune scenic area in Hure Banner, Tongliao, used for desert driving and off-road sport. It has hosted off-road car and motorcycle races over the dunes, among them a winter car challenge in January 2025 on a natural course of about 20 km. It suits visitors interested in dunes and motor sport.

rows.name: Zhurihe Grassland
rows.summary: Zhurihe is a grassland scenic area on the Zhurihe ranch in the north-west of Horqin Left Middle Banner, built around a racecourse with a reviewing stand. It is the main venue of the 8.18 Jerim horse-racing festival, whose 24th edition was held there in August 2023, and a speed-horse race meeting was run there in June 2024. It suits visitors interested in Mongolian horse culture and open grassland.

rows.name: Chaer Lake (Friendship Reservoir)
rows.summary: Chaer Lake is the Friendship Reservoir on the Dongyang River, begun in 1958 and finished in 1973, in Xinghe County on the border with Hebei. The reservoir holds 116 million cubic metres, and the resort area of about 4,400 hectares around it has boating, horse riding, a caravan camp and farmland and wetland scenery, with skating and skiing in winter. It suits visitors who want a day beside open water within reach of Jining.

rows.name: Daihai International Ski Resort
rows.summary: A ski resort on the north-facing slope of Wofo Mountain above Lake Dai, with 12 runs for beginner, intermediate and advanced skiers, a top station at 2,100 m, a vertical drop of 397 m, snowmaking, lifts and a snow-play area, and a resort with a hotel and hot-spring bathing. It hosted events including cross-country skiing and biathlon at the 14th National Winter Games in February 2024. It suits skiers and families from Jining and Hohhot.

rows.name: Gegentala Grassland
rows.summary: Gegentala is a grassland tourist centre on the northern foothills of the Daqing Mountains in Siziwang Banner, the main landing site for China's Shenzhou spacecraft. The regional tourism Naadam has been held here in late July every year since 1989, and an oboo-offering festival takes place on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. The centre promotes itself as one of the autonomous region's five main grassland tourist areas, and it suits visitors who want an easy grassland stop north of Hohhot.

rows.name: Hongshiya Ecological Park
rows.summary: Hongshiya is a privately developed grassland resort in Hongzhao township, Zhuozi County, on the northern side of the Daqing Mountains. It combines alpine meadow ranchland of about 100,000 mu (about 6,700 hectares) with a hot-spring spa drawing on a geothermal well of more than 2,300 m, a water park, a glass footbridge 380 m long between two cliffs, a Buddhist temple and a museum of the anti-Japanese war in the Daqing Mountains. It suits families and day-trippers from Hohhot.

rows.name: Hongzhao Jiulongwan
rows.summary: Jiulongwan is a forested mountain valley in Hongzhao township, Zhuozi County, inside the Daqingshan nature reserve and covering about 100 square kilometres of birch woods, cliffs, streams and meadow. It is named for its nine winding ridges, which look like dragons from the air, and visitors can ride a cable car or an off-road vehicle through it or try a glass walkway, cliff swing and zip line. It suits a summer or autumn day trip from Hohhot.

rows.name: Huitengxile Huanghuagou Grassland
rows.summary: Huanghuagou is the main visitor area of the Huitengxile alpine meadow in Chahar Right Middle Banner, at an average height of about 2,100 m. The meadow covers about 600 square kilometres, with lakes among volcanic rock, and the visitor area has a 16 km route served by a small train, cable car, sightseeing buses and animal carts, plus boardwalks, glass walkways, a ger resort and a staged show based on an oboo offering and Naadam. It suits a summer day out from Jining or Hohhot.

rows.name: Jining Campaign Memorial Park
rows.summary: The memorial park covers about 13 hectares on Quanshan North Street in Jining and is built around the Jining Campaign Memorial Hall, which opened in October 2010. The hall's displays follow the fighting around Jining in 1946, with more than 1,200 objects, photographs and artworks, a sound-and-light panorama and a 5D cinema. The grounds also hold Victory Square, a generals' garden, a monument to the people's heroes and the site of the campaign command post.

rows.name: Jining Campaign Site (Old Flour Mill)
rows.summary: The Jining Campaign Site is a four-storey concrete building of 1940 in the Qiaoxi district of Jining, put up by the Japanese army as a flour mill. It stands 21.4 m high and its walls still carry dense bullet marks from the fighting of 1946, when Jining was contested by Communist and Nationalist forces. It is the first national-level protected site in the Jining district and suits visitors interested in the 1946 campaign, who can pair it with the memorial park.

rows.name: Kelimeng City Site
rows.summary: Kelimeng is the site of a walled town occupied from the Han dynasty to the Northern and Southern Dynasties, in Chahar Right Rear Banner. Its earth walls form a fenced rectangular enclosure on open grassland, with an inner walled compound and the line of a gate in the south wall, and a track crosses the site. It suits visitors with an interest in the early history of the region.

rows.name: Lake Dai (Daihai)
rows.summary: Lake Dai (Daihai) is a saline inland lake in a fault basin in Liangcheng County, the third largest inland lake in Inner Mongolia. The resort area on its shore has a hot spring with a surface temperature of 38 degrees Celsius, boating and activity facilities, and hotel accommodation. It suits visitors who want a lakeside day or an overnight stay within reach of Jining and Hohhot.

rows.name: Linhu Gusai Resort
rows.summary: Linhu Gusai is a mountain resort planned across about 21 square kilometres in Dayushu township, Zhuozi County, themed on the Linhu, a people of the northern frontier in the Warring States period, and on local revolutionary history. Four giant pandas arrived there in September 2019 with the support of the China Conservation and Research Centre for the Giant Panda and were on show at the Qingming holiday in 2024; the resort also has leisure and accommodation facilities and was named a regional-level tourist resort in 2021. It suits families and visitors looking for a resort stay east of Hohhot.

rows.name: Mingxinggou Resort
rows.summary: Mingxinggou is a resort in a mountain valley in Dayushu township, in the south-west of Zhuozi County, planned across about 17 square kilometres in eight zones. Its guest rooms are cave-style dwellings (45 rooms sleeping about 90), and there is a restaurant seating 300 and a stream of more than 300 m running past the entrance. It suits visitors who want a quiet overnight stay in the hills, and it borders the Linhu Gusai resort.

rows.name: Riguang Grassland and Dahewan Resort
rows.summary: A year-round resort in the hills north of Jining, built around the Riguang Volcano and Dahewan ski area and hot-spring wellness facilities. In winter the ski area offers runs for different levels and snow play, and in summer the grassland is used for cool-weather stays, with guesthouse villages nearby. It suits visitors from Jining and further afield who want a winter or summer break close to the city.

rows.name: Shajing Zongguanfu City Site
rows.summary: The Shajing city site is the ruin of the Yuan-dynasty seat of the Shajing zongguanfu, an administrative unit set up in 1316 in the lands of the Ongud people, north of the Jingzhou circuit. The outline of the walls and of the street grid inside, a square roughly 750 m across, survives as low earthworks that show clearly in aerial imagery, and the site is fenced in open grassland. It suits visitors with a special interest in Yuan history in the region.

rows.name: Siziwang Banner Prince's Mansion
rows.summary: The Siziwang Banner Prince's Mansion was the seat of the Qing-era prince of the Sizi Buluo banner, built in 1905 for the 13th prince, Lawangnaerbu. A brick-and-timber complex with tiled roofs, red columns and painted beams, it has a front hall for the prince's official business, a rear hall where the prince's family lived and two small prayer halls for monks, and the family temple stands beside it. It suits visitors with an interest in Mongol princely history who are already at the Gegentala grassland.

rows.name: Sumushan Forest Park
rows.summary: Sumushan is a forested range south of Xinghe where Inner Mongolia, Hebei and Shanxi meet, rising to Huangshiya at 2,334.7 m, the highest point in Ulanqab. The scenic area has a 12 km wooden boardwalk through pine woods, the Bingling ravine, rock formations, a cave where monks once meditated and the film set used for the television series Dasheng Kui. It suits walkers and visitors who want cool mountain air within day-trip distance of Xinghe.

rows.name: Contemporary China Calligraphy Art Museum
rows.summary: A large art museum in Haibowan, built from 2010 in a city that the China Calligraphers Association named a calligraphy city in 2008. The square building has a glass dome carrying a design taken from the sun-god rock engraving of Zhuozi Mountain, about 38 exhibition halls and room to show more than 6,000 works at once. It suits visitors interested in calligraphy and Chinese painting.

rows.name: Jinshawan (Golden Sand Bay)
rows.summary: Jinshawan is a desert recreation area north of Wuhai, set in a hollow between two facing sand hills, the eastern one rising to 156 m. Visitors slide down the dunes, ride camels and take dune-buggy rides, and the area lies close to Wuhai airport. It suits visitors who want a short desert outing from the city.

rows.name: Menggenhua Eco-Leisure Park
rows.summary: Menggenhua is a leisure park beside Wuhai airport that combines an indoor hot-spring and water-park complex with an amusement park, greenhouses and a peony garden. It also has a hotel and villas for overnight stays and suits families looking for an indoor day out.

rows.name: Rock Paintings of Zhuozi Mountain (Zhaoshaogou)
rows.summary: The Zhuozi Mountain rock paintings, a national protected site spread across Wuhai and Ordos, are best seen at Zhaoshaogou, where more than a hundred Neolithic engravings, mostly human faces including the well-known sun-god face, cover a gentle limestone slope. The slope is fenced and a protective hall designed by Tsinghua University architects has been built over it; other panels lie on cliffs in gullies of the same mountain, partly across the boundary in Ordos. It suits visitors interested in prehistoric art.

rows.name: Sunshine Tianyu International Winery
rows.summary: Sunshine Tianyu is a vineyard and winery visitor estate in Saihanwusu, Hainan District, south of Wuhai, that began receiving visitors in early 2015. It presents wine culture through sightseeing, farm experiences, resort and conference facilities, with Mongolian cultural elements built into the design, across about 750 mu of visitor area. It suits visitors with an interest in wine and farm stays.

rows.name: Wuhai Lake
rows.summary: Wuhai Lake is the reservoir of the Haibowan water control project on the Yellow River, completed in 2013, and its 118 square kilometres of water lie between the Ulan Buh Desert and the city. Visitors can take boat trips from the No. 1 pier, ride a small sightseeing train and try more than twenty water and desert activities, from speedboats and flyboards to desert buggies and camel rides, while reed beds on the south and west shores attract many water birds. It suits visitors who want a desert-edge lake right beside a city.

rows.name: Beizi Temple (Chongshan Temple)
rows.summary: Beizi Temple is a Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Chinese–Tibetan style, founded in 1743 below Erdun Aobao hill and given the name Chongshan Temple by the Qianlong emperor. Five of its original seven main halls survive, in four courtyards, and in the early 19th century the monastery housed about 1,500 lamas. Xilinhot was itself once called Beizimiao, after the temple.

rows.name: Bulin Spring, Ulagai
rows.summary: Bulin Spring is a grassland scenic area built around eight springs that flow all year at about 5 °C, with the remains of Bulin Temple, founded in 1672, about 1.5 km away; the temple site was conserved from 2010. The area also has an octagonal pavilion, a Genghis Khan statue, a ger camp, a boardwalk, an oboo and a bonfire square, and more than ten films, including Wolf Totem, have been shot here. It suits visitors who want a night in a ger camp on the grassland.

rows.name: China Horse Capital Core Area
rows.summary: A sports and culture complex of about 15 square kilometres on the southern edge of Xilinhot, developed from 2013 around Xilingol's title as China's horse capital, which the China Horse Industry Association gave the league in 2010. It has indoor and outdoor racecourses with stands, an equestrian club and riding school, stables, a horse-culture museum and a theatre for horse shows, and it has hosted national equestrian competitions. It suits visitors interested in horses and racing rather than historic sites.

rows.name: Duolun Lake
rows.summary: Duolun Lake is a reservoir on the upper Luan River, created by the Xishanwan hydropower scheme completed in 1999, with a surface of about 20,000 mu among hills, sand and grassland. The resort area is made up of seven linked lakes with islands and peninsulas and has a hotel, a visitor centre, a fishing village, lakeside piers and a riding trail, and a road cycling race has been held around the lake each year since 2007. It suits visitors who want a lakeside stay or day out in the Duolun area.

rows.name: Erenhot National Gate Scenic Area
rows.summary: The scenic area is built around the National Gate, a monumental gateway at Erenhot's port of entry on the northern edge of the city. Visitors can see ger-building craft works, cultural products and study-tour programmes, and alpacas from Sunid Left Banner joined the attractions in 2024. It suits travellers who want to see the port of entry on the Trans-Mongolian railway route.

rows.name: Erenhot National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 二连浩特国家地质公园
rows.summary: The geopark lies on the north-eastern edge of Erenhot, in the Iren Dabasu area, which is known for Cretaceous dinosaur fossils. Its dinosaur museum has large moving models of the animals. It suits families and anyone passing through Erenhot with a few hours to spare.

rows.name: Huizong Temple
rows.summary: Huizong Temple, called the Blue Temple in Mongolian, is a Gelug-school monastery built between 1691 and 1712 after the Kangxi emperor held an assembly of Mongol princes at Duolun Nor in 1691. Its main hall was burned in 1945 and has since been rebuilt, and the grounds cover about 18 hectares. It suits visitors interested in Qing relations with the Mongols and in Buddhist architecture.

rows.name: Imperial Horse Park, Taipusi (Yumayuan)
rows.summary: Yumayuan is a horse-culture and riding centre on the grassland of Taipusi Banner, with a collection of horses of more than twenty breeds, among them Akhal-Teke, Friesian, Dutch warmblood and English thoroughbred. It has stables, a racing track, a barrel-racing ground, indoor and outdoor training areas, a horse hospital and a museum of imperial horse culture, and visitors can watch and ride the horses and join study programmes. It suits families and groups on a grassland trip.

rows.name: Mongol Khan City
rows.summary: Mongol Khan City is a ger resort camp in the grassland of West Ujimqin Banner, with buildings modelled on the khan's city of Genghis Khan's enthronement and more than 150 gers for dining and overnight stays. It stages Mongolian song and dance, a small Naadam-style show and evening bonfire gatherings, and in 2023 it was named one of the region's first intangible-heritage tourism experience bases. It suits groups and families who want to stay in a ger on the grassland.

rows.name: Shangdu (Xanadu)
rows.summary: Shangdu, known in the West as Xanadu, was the summer capital of Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty, founded in 1256 beside the Luan River in the grassland north of the Great Wall, and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012. The remains include the palace enclosure, imperial city, outer city, temples, tombs and the Tiefangang canal, with earthen walls and palace foundations still visible on open ground; the World Heritage property also takes in the Zhenzishan tomb group. A site museum, the Xilingol Cultural Heritage Museum, stands about 5 km south of the ruins.

rows.name: Shanxi Guild Hall, Duolun
rows.summary: The Shanxi Guild Hall is a Qing-period complex built from 1745 by Shanxi merchants trading in Duolun Nor, with lodgings, an entertainment area, a business meeting area and a temple to Guan Yu; about half of the original buildings remain. A restoration in 2008 added a museum on the Shanxi merchants who traded with Mongolia, and the hall keeps a large bronze bell, an iron incense burner and carved brick and wood. It is one of the best-preserved Qing buildings in the town and suits visitors interested in trade history.

rows.name: Starry Sky Cultural Tourism Camp
rows.summary: The camp occupies 1,300 mu of grassland in Zhengxiangbai Banner, just north of the National Astronomical Observatory's Mingantu observing station. It has a science area with an astronomy exhibition hall, a science square and a lecture hall, and a living area with folk-style lodging and dining, and it runs stargazing and study programmes on astronomy, spaceflight and weather. It suits families and school groups with an interest in astronomy.

rows.name: Ulagai Jiuquwan (Nine-Bend Bay)
rows.summary: Jiuquwan is a stretch of the Ulagai River in the far east of Xilingol where the river winds in tight loops through wetland and grassland. The scenic area covers about 3,500 hectares and has been developed since 2015, with a large visitor centre; visitors can ride in a traditional ox cart, watch Mongolian song and dance and take cross-country trips over the grassland. It suits visitors who want river and wetland scenery on the grassland of north-eastern Inner Mongolia.

rows.name: Ulagai Wolf Valley
rows.summary: Wolf Valley is a themed grassland attraction on the Hesige Ula ranch in the Ulagai Management Area, and was one of the main filming locations for the film Wolf Totem. Visitors cross the grassland on a small tourist train, stay in colourfully painted lodging houses, join evening tours of the valley and see steppe wolves at close range. It suits families and groups who want a themed stop on a grassland trip rather than open landscape.

rows.name: Wulan Wutai (Red Wutai)
rows.summary: Wulan Wutai is a scenic area of Mongolian Buddhist culture in the grassland of West Ujimqin Banner; its name means Red Wutai in Mongolian. The banner government built a large oboo, a Genghis Khan square, a Wutai temple and sixteen pagodas here in 2006, and an oboo-worship day with Buddhist rites, wrestling and horse racing is held on the 13th day of the fifth lunar month. It suits visitors interested in Mongolian religious customs and grassland scenery.

rows.name: Ajitai Health and Leisure Park
rows.summary: A health and leisure park in Otog Front Banner, on the south-western edge of Ordos close to the Mu Us sandy lands, built around Mongolian-medicine wellness and grassland leisure. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base.

rows.name: Mongolian Origin (Mengwu Shiwei) Cultural Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 蒙古之源·蒙兀室韦文化旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Ménggǔ Zhī Yuán · Méngwù Shìwéi Wénhuà Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: A cultural tourism area at Mengwu Shiwei on the Ergun River, presenting the early history of the Mongols with rebuilt obo cairns and commemorative squares, with a Mongolian-medicine element added by its operator. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base.

rows.name: Ansteel Museum and Early Steelworks Buildings
rows.name_zh: 鞍钢博物馆（鞍山钢铁厂早期建筑）
rows.summary: The Ansteel Group Museum fills the former No. 2 sintering shop of the Anshan steelworks, a 1950s building designed with Soviet help and one of eight early buildings listed together as a national heritage unit that runs from the Japanese-run works of the 1920s and 1930s to the Soviet-assisted rebuilding of the 1950s. Eleven themed galleries and a steel-themed park cover the works' history, and the old shop keeps its sintering machine and overhead crane beside Anshan's No. 1 blast furnace of 1919, shut down in 2005. The other listed buildings include offices, workshops and former housing in and around the working plant and are mostly in other use.

rows.name: Jade Buddha Palace
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple complex on the west slope of Jade Buddha Hill in Anshan, opened in 1996 and built around a hall about 33 m high that houses a statue carved from a single block of Xiuyan jade weighing 260.76 tonnes, with Shakyamuni on the front and Guanyin crossing the sea on the back. Its buildings include a Heavenly Kings hall, bell and drum towers and a jade-belt bridge, and the complex was enlarged and reopened in 2006. In 2015 the site was approved as a place of Buddhist worship and renamed Jade Buddha Temple, so it is a working temple as well as a sight.

rows.name: Jianing Happy Valley
rows.summary: A leisure-farm resort of 340 mu (about 23 ha) in Yujiagou village near Tanggangzi, combining fishing, fruit picking, a zoo, a children's play area, a water park, sand and grass sliding, horse riding and live-action team shooting games. The provincial tourism page also lists hot-spring bathing, a swimming pool, an aerial cableway and a rapids ride, with garden features such as a Great Wall, a waterfall cave and zodiac figures. It is a commercial attraction for family and group outings.

rows.name: Jinta Pagoda, Haicheng
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda, 31.5 m high, on a hillside above Yangjiaoyu village, octagonal with 13 close-set storeys of eaves and named Jinta (Golden Pagoda) for its pale yellow colour. Its two-tier base is carved with musicians, dancers and guardian figures at the corners, and each face of the body has a niche with a seated Buddha, attendants and flying apsaras. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 1963 and as a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Longquan Lake Resort, Xiuyan
rows.summary: A lake-and-hills leisure resort in Qianying, Xiuyan Manchu Autonomous County, begun in 2000 and covering nearly 10,000 mu, about 6.5 sq km. The provincial tourism page says a stream rises in a mountain-top lake, which it calls rare in north-east China, and that buildings step down the valley in the outline of a dragon. The resort has since added culture and arts activities, lodging, dining, shopping, and wellness and retirement services, so it is mainly a leisure destination.

rows.name: Qianshan National Park
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 44 sq km, among the first national scenic areas named in 1982, with granite peaks, old pines and valleys where Buddhist and Daoist temples stand side by side. The listed old buildings are the 'five great Chan monasteries' (Longquan, Xiangyan, Da'an, Zuyue and Zhonghui) and the Daoist Wuliang Temple, mostly Ming and Qing in date. Stone steps climb to viewpoints such as Xianren Tai (708.5 m, the highest point visitors can reach), and Maitreya Peak, a natural outcrop shaped like a seated Buddha, is known as the Great Buddha of Qianshan.

rows.name: Qianshan Old Courtyard Resort
rows.summary: A leisure resort in the village of Hanjiayu, in the Qianshan hills, laid out around courtyard-style buildings and gardens in a traditional manner. The provincial tourism page lists guesthouses, a petting zoo, a children's adventure park without powered rides, a winter snow-and-ice area, restaurants and a summer tent camp with 30 tents. It suits families and short breaks rather than sightseeing, and lies next to the Qianshan scenic area rather than inside it.

rows.name: Qingliangshan Scenic Area, Xiuyan
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 30 sq km in the north-east of Xiuyan Manchu Autonomous County, with steep peaks, deep valleys, primary forest, streams, an underground lake and hot springs, according to the provincial tourism page. Its main peak, Maokuishan (also called Zuofoshan), reaches about 1,141 m, the highest point in Anshan prefecture. The page lists sightseeing, rock climbing and hill walking among the activities.

rows.name: Shanshui Manor Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring leisure resort at Gushouyu, in the Yuanbao hills at the foot of Qianshan. The provincial tourism page describes a rural-style resort where visitors can travel, stay, dine, shop and be entertained, in a hilly setting it calls a natural bonsai landscape. It is a modern commercial resort aimed at short breaks from Anshan rather than a historic or scenic sight.

rows.name: Shitouji Qianshan Grand View Garden
rows.summary: A themed garden based on Dream of the Red Chamber (also called The Story of the Stone, Shitouji in Chinese), built at the foot of Qianshan in Anshan's high-tech zone and opened in 2023. More than 20 groups of buildings follow the novel's descriptions, among them the Yihong Courtyard, Xiaoxiang Lodge and Longcui Convent, and the Xiaoxiang group holds an art museum for the actress Chen Xiaoxu, a native of Anshan who played Lin Daiyu in the 1987 television series. The garden is lit at night and stages performances based on the novel.

rows.name: Tanggangzi Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring spa district about 12 km south of Anshan, used for bathing since the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-05 and developed as a spa by the South Manchuria Railway Company from 1920, and in that era counted as one of the 'three great hot springs of Manchuria'. The provincial tourism page describes a 64-hectare resort with a medical and rehabilitation zone, hotels, a swimming hall, a sports centre and garden sights such as a lotus lake and a ginkgo square. Today it works as a modern health and leisure resort.

rows.name: Tianyuan Agricultural Park, Haicheng
rows.summary: A commercial agri-tourism resort of 300 mu (20 ha) at Beigeng village in Gengzhuang town, built around a hot-spring water park with about 12,000 sq m indoors and 4,600 sq m outdoors. The provincial tourism page also lists a winter snow-and-ice play area, a tropical plant garden with some 300 species of rare plants, a fishing pond, a children's play area and a 45,000 sq m agricultural showcase growing more than 600 crop varieties. It is aimed at family days out and group events rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Wolongshan Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: A hill fortress of the late Goguryeo period, in the Sui and Tang era, which the provincial heritage page calls the largest and reasonably well preserved of several such forts in Xiuyan county; it was formerly known as Niangniang Cheng. The inner wall runs about 2.8 km along the ridges in dressed wedge-shaped stones, with surviving stretches 3 to 5 m high, traces of bastions and a beacon platform, and an east gate beside a wall about 8 m high, while a lower outer wall of about 2.3 km closes the south-east. Roof tiles with lotus patterns, pottery and iron arrowheads have been found inside, and the ground within the walls is mostly wooded.

rows.name: Xianghe Holiday Manor
rows.summary: A family leisure resort of about 22 ha in Qianshan District, south-west of Anshan, built around an indoor children's play park modelled on a candy town and a flower valley with more than a hundred species of flowers. The provincial tourism page also lists mini golf, an archery hall, a go-kart club, children's off-road karts and bumper boats, and two hotels, villas and log cabins for overnight stays. It is aimed at families with children and short breaks rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Ximucheng Dolmen
rows.summary: A Bronze Age dolmen about 3,000 years old: six granite slabs form a chamber 2.8 m high under a capstone of about 6 m by 5 m, standing on a high terrace at the foot of a hill. The provincial heritage bureau counts it among the larger, finer and best-preserved dolmens found on the Liaodong peninsula, and says a smaller twin below it was blown up in 1952 during road building, which gave the pair the local name Gusao Stones (the sister-in-law stones). Most Chinese archaeologists read such dolmens as tombs, though an altar is another suggested use.

rows.name: Yinta Pagoda, Haicheng
rows.summary: A white brick pagoda of nine close-set storeys of eaves on a hexagonal plan, about 15.6 m high, begun in the Liao or Jin period and rebuilt in the Ming, on a hillside north of West Tazigou village. Its base has a carved brick balustrade with cormorants, tigers, lotus leaves and fish, and each face of the body has a Buddha niche with attendants and flying figures. The temple that once stood beneath it, the Miaode or Silver Pagoda Temple, was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and the pagoda was repaired in 1953 and 2009.

rows.name: Yutangquan Hot Spring Water World
rows.summary: An indoor water park and hot-spring resort in the Tanggangzi new town, under an all-glass roof, with more than a hundred Southeast Asian plant species growing inside. The provincial tourism page lists a wave pool and more than 20 rides and slides, including an 'Amazon' rafting river. It is a modern commercial attraction for families and groups, not a historic bathing place.

rows.name: Benxi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: Benxi Grand Canyon is a gorge in Nanfen District, inside a national geological park, that has been developed as a thrill-oriented adventure park. Its core attractions are a high-level glass suspension bridge and a forest slide, with newer rides such as a "flying wing", an aerial walk, a cliff swing and a water slide. It suits visitors who want activities rather than a quiet walk, and anyone uneasy about heights may prefer to skip the glass bridge.

rows.name: Benxi Water Caves
rows.summary: The Benxi Water Caves are a karst cave system with an underground river, about 5.8 km long, of which roughly 2.8 km has been opened to visitors. Visitors travel through the lit cave by boat past stalactites and stalagmites, in air that stays around 12°C all year. In winter, rime often forms around the cave mouth.

rows.name: Benxihu Industrial Heritage Complex
rows.summary: This group of mining, ironmaking and company buildings in Xihu District comes from the Benxihu Coal and Iron Company, which Japanese interests began developing in 1905 and which became part of the Benxi Iron and Steel works after 1949. The listed parts include the first ironworks site, which closed in 2008, the cooling-tower area of a power plant, the company's former headquarters and office buildings (the "Little Red Building" and "Big White Building"), the Central Incline of the mine with a burial mound for victims of the 1942 mine explosion, the Caitun mine shaft and Benxihu station. The former ironworks site now serves as a provincial overseas-Chinese cultural exchange base and has hosted visiting groups.

rows.name: Dabinggou Forest Park
rows.summary: Dabinggou is a forested valley in Nanfen District, with tree cover of about 97 percent and groundwater that stays near 4°C all year. It is known for ice waterfalls in summer, which the provincial tourism page calls rare at such a low altitude in a temperate zone. The park also has a stand of Siebold's magnolia (tiannü mulan) and maples that turn red in autumn.

rows.name: Dashi Lake and Laobiangou
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Dashihu is a two-part mountain scenic area in Benxi Manchu Autonomous County, made up of the Dashi Lake section and the Laobiangou valley, and noted for its autumn maples. The lake section is divided into Wulong Lake, Bingling Gorge, Xiangshui Lake and Mulan Valley zones, while Laobiangou has a river valley, a boulder slope and Wanxiang Valley; the provincial page also describes it as a national geological park. Several sites of fighting by anti-Japanese guerrilla forces lie in Laobiangou.

rows.name: Dayahe Rafting and Longxi Valley
rows.summary: Dayahe is a river and valley leisure area in Huanren Manchu Autonomous County, at the foot of Huaping Mountain, an area nicknamed the "little Guilin of the north". It has two parts: a 6.6 km rafting run on a river that alternately narrows and widens, and Longxi Valley, where about 85 percent of the ground is forested and maples grow among waterfalls and a dragon pool. Restaurants, accommodation and entertainment are on site.

rows.name: Fenglin Valley Forest Park
rows.summary: Fenglin Valley is a forest park in Huanren Manchu Autonomous County, known for the red maples of autumn; forest covers nearly 99 percent of the park and its highest peak, Bamianwei, reaches 1,305 m. The provincial tourism page gives a summer average temperature of about 20°C. The park also contains remains of an anti-Japanese guerrilla base, including a stone barracks and a hidden mountain camp at Wohu Peak.

rows.name: Green Stone Valley (Tangchigou)
rows.summary: Green Stone Valley is a forested valley in Benxi Manchu Autonomous County, named for the moss-covered boulders that fill the valley and give the rocks a jade-green look. Waterfalls large and small run through it, and the provincial tourism page calls it a rare moss-viewing area, with tree cover of about 90 percent.

rows.name: Guanmenshan Forest Park
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Guanmenshan is a forested valley in Benxi Manchu Autonomous County, named for two facing peaks that look like a gate, and is known above all for its autumn maples. The park is divided into five zones, including Longmen Gorge and Mingcui Valley, and the provincial tourism page counts 108 sights. Remains of camps used by anti-Japanese guerrilla forces, including barracks and hidden storerooms, are scattered through the park.

rows.name: Guanshan Lake
rows.summary: Guanshan Lake is a reservoir in forested hills in Benxi Manchu Autonomous County, developed as a national water-conservancy scenic area and known for its autumn colour. The provincial tourism page lists about 40 sights in four zones, built around boat cruises on the lake, a summit climb, a spring-fed valley and a lakeshore circuit. Activities include kayaking, small lake rafts, a campfire barbecue ground and an RV camp.

rows.name: Qingyunshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Qingyunshan is a hill scenic area on the southern edge of Benxi city, in Mingshan District, where visitors climb up for views out over the city. Official tourism pages record events there in 2024 and 2025: a spring garden fair with a night lantern show, lantern-floating wishes, intangible-heritage displays and hanfu (traditional dress) activities; a Mid-Autumn moon-viewing fair; a hill-running race in May 2025; and a martial-arts event on its Sifangtai platform in October 2025. It suits a short outing from the city, and because the events run on a seasonal calendar, check what is on before planning around one.

rows.name: Tieshashan
rows.summary: Tieshashan, also called Jiuding Tieshashan ("nine-peak" Tieshashan), is a Daoist mountain in Benxi Manchu Autonomous County that is regarded as the birthplace of the Longmen school of Daoism in north-east China. Five main peaks, which look like nine when seen from different sides, belong to the Changbai mountain range, and the best-known of its many caves is Babao Yunguang Cave. Old inscriptions are cut into the rock across the mountain, and the Sanqing Temple on the mountain was founded in 1744.

rows.name: Wangtian Cave
rows.summary: Wangtian Cave is a karst cave in Huanren Manchu Autonomous County that the provincial tourism page dates to about 200,000 years ago. Explored passages total nearly 10 km, of which about 2.1 km is open to visitors, and the cave has corridor-like, hall-like and maze-like sections. Its best-known feature is a maze of about 1.1 km of passages, alongside small rimstone terraces and thin, translucent "stone flags".

rows.name: Wunü Mountain
rows.summary: Wunü Mountain is a flat-topped massif with steep cliffs above the Hun River, crowned by the ruins of a Goguryeo hill fortress that is generally identified as the first capital of the Goguryeo kingdom (founded in 37 BC). The fortress belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage listing for the Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom (2004), and the scenic area of about 10.8 square kilometres combines its stone walls, gates and building foundations with a slot gorge, lookouts over Huanlong Lake and the Wunü Mountain Museum. It was rated a 5A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Xiaoshi Yizhuang
rows.summary: Xiaoshi Yizhuang is a rural tourism village at Tongjiangyu in Xiaoshi town, about 1 km from the Benxi Water Caves, developed around folk-custom experiences, local food, countryside stays and cultural shows. It has been named a provincial night-time culture and tourism consumption zone, so evening events are part of the offer. It is a modern tourism development rather than a historic village, and suits visitors who want a meal stop or a base next to the water cave.

rows.name: Balengguan Pagoda
rows.summary: Balengguan Pagoda is a Liao-period octagonal brick pagoda of thirteen tiers of dense eaves, about 34 m high, standing on a hilltop with the Daling River to its south. Across the river lie the ruins of the Liao city of Jianzhou. It has been a provincial heritage unit since 1979 and a national one since 2013.

rows.name: Chaoyang Bird Fossil National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 朝阳鸟化石国家地质公园
rows.pinyin: Cháoyáng Niǎo Huàshí Guójiā Dìzhì Gōngyuán
rows.summary: The geopark in Longcheng District centres on the Liaoning Chaoyang Palaeontological Fossil Museum, which reopened in April 2025 after an upgrade. Xinhua reported that the museum now shows 2,025 fossils, up from 435, in a main hall on the Jehol Biota and four themed halls covering dinosaurs, the origin of birds, flowering plants and mammals. The provincial tourism page also lists a geological corridor, a fossil excavation site on the original find location and a petrified-wood forest.

rows.name: Chaoyang North Tower
rows.summary: Chaoyang North Tower is a 42.6 m square brick pagoda with thirteen tiers of dense eaves, built up over several dynasties on the palace site of the Yan-state capital Longcheng, which is why it is nicknamed the 'Five Ages Pagoda'. Its walls carry relief carvings of seated Buddhas, bodhisattvas and flying apsaras, and the adjoining North Tower Museum displays finds from the pagoda's underground and upper chambers. Xinhua reported that in 2026 the tower was opened for climbing, with limited numbers, on some festival days.

rows.name: Chaoyang South Pagoda
rows.summary: Chaoyang South Pagoda is a square brick pagoda of thirteen eaves from the Liao period, standing at the south end of Murong Street as the counterpart to the North Tower. Inscribed bricks and a stone chamber found during repairs point to a first building probably in 984, with repairs in 1076 and around 1156 to 1161; the chamber held Buddhist relics, a stone casket and a gilded silver coffin. The tower's plain body is marked by rows of square sockets where decorations were probably once attached.

rows.name: Daxuan Mountain, Beipiao
rows.summary: Daxuan Mountain, the name the provincial culture department now gives to the Dahei Shan scenic area, is a forested mountain in the north-west of Beipiao with rocky peaks and, by the department's figure, forest cover above 93%. The official description lists a 2.2 km sightseeing cable car, a 4.5 km step-free path and a 5 km timber boardwalk on the upper slopes, and more than a hundred sights, among them one called 'May ice'. It suits walkers and families wanting a half day in the hills.

rows.name: Dongpingfang Pagoda
rows.summary: Dongpingfang Pagoda is a Liao-period brick pagoda on a hilltop above the Daling River, six-sided and originally nine tiers of dense eaves, of which eight survive. The solid tower is about 19 m high. It is one of several Liao pagodas strung along the river valley west of Chaoyang, and it stands in Dongpingfang village in Dapingfang town.

rows.name: Dongshanzui Site
rows.summary: Dongshanzui is a ritual site of the late Hongshan culture, more than 5,000 years old, on a terrace above the west bank of the Daling River; it has a square stone-walled platform with standing stones and a small round altar paved with pebbles. Excavated in 1979 and 1982, it produced painted pottery, two small clay figurines of pregnant women and jades such as a double-dragon-head pendant. Since 2017 there has been a visitor path, a protective fence and a 600 m² exhibition hall showing finds, a site model and digital displays.

rows.name: First Bend of the Daling River
rows.summary: The Daling River makes a sharp S-shaped bend between hills in Kazuo county, and this scenic area links viewpoints along the river through four townships. Downstream, high in a cliff above the river, lies Gezidong ('Pigeon Cave'), a limestone rock shelter used by Palaeolithic people some 70,000 to 80,000 years ago, excavated in 1973 and 1975 and listed as a national heritage unit in 2019.

rows.name: Fossil Valley, Chaoyang
rows.summary: Fossil Valley is a commercially run, fossil-themed attraction in Longcheng District on the north-west side of Chaoyang, covering about 1.7 hectares in three parts: an interactive 'legendary fossil' experience park, the Chaoyang Jurassic Palaeontological Fossil Museum (a privately owned museum, formerly the Jizantang museum) and a fossil-culture creative area. It suits families and school groups who want a hands-on introduction to the area's fossils. The separate Chaoyang Bird Fossil National Geopark lies about 2 km to the west-north-west.

rows.name: Huanghuatan Pagoda
rows.summary: Huanghuatan Pagoda is a Liao-period octagonal brick pagoda of thirteen tiers of dense eaves standing on an earth mound with the Daling River to its south, facing the site of the Liao city of New Jianzhou. It rests on a base platform and a two-stage Sumeru-style plinth, its spire has collapsed, and about 32 m of it survives.

rows.name: Laohugou Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: Laohugou ('Tiger Gully') is a wooded valley scenic area in Dawangzhangzi township, south-west of Lingyuan, a township nicknamed the 'seventy-li apricot valley' and rich in Jehol Biota fossils. A palaeontological fossil museum in Gongjiashaoguo village, where the scenic area lies, opened in December 2025. It is a small, recently developed area that suits a short outing from Lingyuan.

rows.name: Longfeng Mountain, Kazuo
rows.summary: Longfeng ('Dragon and Phoenix') Mountain is a hill scenic area east of Kazuo county town, with rock outcrops, old cypresses, an old temple, caves and springs. Named features on the official page include an entrance-gate area, a pool-and-stream system, a misty forest, a primitive-tribe theme area and Longquan Valley, and the area is promoted around dragon and blessing-prayer themes.

rows.name: Longyuan Tourism Area, Kazuo
rows.summary: The Longyuan tourism area is a lakeside leisure district at the edge of Kazuo county town, built around Longyuan Lake. The provincial tourism department lists a city-planning exhibition hall, a health-and-leisure centre, the Tiancheng Taoist temple, an ethnic-folk museum, the Lizhou Pagoda, the Baiyin'aili ethnic village and a purple-clay pottery culture park among its sights, and describes it as shared between visitors and residents.

rows.name: Niuheliang
rows.summary: Niuheliang is a Hongshan-culture ritual and burial complex spread over ridges where Lingyuan meets Jianping, with a platform known as the Goddess Temple, a three-ring altar and clusters of stone-mound tombs. The national archaeological site park, which covers about 8 km², has a site museum with jades and painted pottery, plus protective halls built over the excavated Goddess Temple (Locality 1) and over the altar and cairns (Locality 2), so the remains can be seen where they were found. The site museum dates the complex to roughly 5,800 to 5,000 years ago.

rows.name: Phoenix Mountain, Chaoyang
rows.summary: Phoenix Mountain is a wooded ridge on the eastern edge of Chaoyang that rises to about 660 m, was known as Dragon Mountain in earlier times, and carries a group of old temples and pagodas on its slopes. The provincial tourism department lists three pagodas and four temples (Yanshou, Tianqing, Yunjie and Huayan); the landmark among them is the Liao-period Yunjie Temple Pagoda, a square brick tower of thirteen eaves some 37 m high whose body and base are carved with Buddhas, bodhisattvas, arhats and flying apsaras. It makes a half-day outing from the city that combines a hill walk with the temples.

rows.name: Qianfodong Scenic Area, Chaoyang County
rows.summary: Qianfodong ('Thousand Buddha Caves') is a hill scenic area in Nanshuangmiao township, south of Chaoyang, with odd-shaped rock formations, a Buddhist site that the provincial culture department traces back a thousand years and the remains of what it calls a Sui–Tang 'general-review platform'. It is split into history-and-culture, ecological-leisure and adventure zones, with a zip line, a rainbow bridge across a gorge, a revolutionary-themed film and television base and more than thirty named sights.

rows.name: Qingfeng Pagoda
rows.summary: Qingfeng Pagoda is a square thirteen-tier brick pagoda of the Liao period on the summit of West Pagoda Hill at Wushijiazi village in Xiyingzi township, hollow inside, with a porch on its south face and the spire lost. The provincial culture department calls its porch form unusual and rates it among the finer Liao pagodas of the Chaoyang area.

rows.name: Taiji Mass Grave Site, Beipiao
rows.summary: The Taiji mass grave site is a memorial on a hillside south of Taiji town in Beipiao, where miners who died at the local coal mine under Japanese occupation were buried; Chinese state media say tens of thousands of labourers died in the Beipiao coalfield after 1931 from overwork, hunger and disease. A memorial hall opened on the site in 1969, and a 2015 People's Daily Online report says it keeps the remains of more than 31,000 people in two large rooms and twelve others, with a new memorial building begun in 2014. It became a provincial patriotic-education base in 2005 and a national heritage unit in 2019.

rows.name: Tombs of the Princes of Kharachin Right Banner
rows.name_zh: 喀喇沁右翼旗蒙古王陵
rows.summary: This is the burial ground of the Qing-era princes (zasag) of the Kharachin Right Banner, a Mongol banner, set in a pine grove at the foot of Longdan Mountain in Sanjia township. The eastern garden, about 130 m square, has a front hall, a stone archway with a plaque in Emperor Kangxi's calligraphy, a main hall, an offering hall with portraits of thirteen princes and thirteen princely tombs; the last prince buried there was Gungsangnorbu, who died in 1931, and the western garden of relatives' graves has not survived. The provincial heritage page calls it the most representative Qing-era Mongol princely tomb complex.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Shuangta Temple
rows.summary: Two small octagonal brick pagodas stand side by side on a hillside beneath a rock overhang in a gully north-west of Zhengzhangzi village, in Mutouchengzi town. The west pagoda has three tiers and is about 13 m high, the east pagoda has a single eave and is about 11 m high, and both are Liao in origin, the east one possibly Liao-Jin. The provincial culture department says each carries both Liao and Qing features, reflecting the rise and fall of Buddhism at the site.

rows.name: Youshun Temple
rows.summary: Youshun Temple is a Tibetan Buddhist (Gelug) monastery built between 1698 and 1707 under the Kangxi emperor, laid out along a north-west to south-east axis of about 233 m, with a memorial archway, gate, Hall of Heavenly Kings, sutra hall and a main hall about 21 m high, flanked by monks' quarters, a Guandi hall and an opera stage. The Chaoyang Buddhist Culture Museum is based in the temple. It stands in the old town close to the two pagodas, and Xinhua wrote in 2026 that the bells and drums of Youshun and the neighbouring Guandi temple still ring out each day.

rows.name: Yulonggu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Yulonggu is a hot-spring and water-play resort with a Mongolian theme on the south-western side of Kazuo, with hot-spring pools, a large wave pool and a drifting river that runs partly underground. It also has some twenty amusement rides, meeting rooms and restaurants, and suits families and groups after a leisure day or an overnight stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Anbo Hot Spring Tourist Area
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Anbo is a hot-spring area in the hills of northern Pulandian District, and the listed scenic area spreads across five of the district's subdistricts. It includes a hot-spring villa, a ski resort, a water park, hill scenic spots such as Laomaoshan and Jiguanshan, and a Manchu folk park. The Weibashan fortress and the Shipenggou dolmen, both national heritage sites, lie within the area and have their own entries.

rows.name: Baiyushan Hill, Lüshun
rows.summary: Baiyushan is a hill in the old town of Lüshun that looks down on the naval harbour and the town. On its summit stands Baiyushan Tower, which the Japanese military built in 1907–09 as a memorial to its dead of the Russo-Japanese War and which was renamed after 1945, together with a naval weapons museum. A path of 499 steps, two roads and a cable car lead up.

rows.name: Bangchuidao Guesthouse Scenic Area
rows.summary: This coastal scenic area on the eastern stretch of Dalian's Binhai Road takes its name from a small club-shaped islet about 600 m offshore. Its core is the Bangchuidao Guesthouse, which the provincial tourism department and the national environment ministry describe as one of the first four state guesthouses of the People's Republic, set in woodland beside a sand beach with a lotus lake and a tree-lined avenue. The beach, about 1.2 km long, is the main draw for visitors.

rows.name: Bingyu Valley
rows.summary: Bingyu Valley is a mountain gorge in the Xianrendong area of Zhuanghe, known for forested peaks of quartzite, deep side valleys and clear streams and pools, and promoted as the 'Guilin of southern Liaoning'. It adjoins Xianrendong National Forest Park, which the provincial tourism department describes as rich in wildlife and plants. It suits a day trip into the mountains.

rows.name: Dahei Mountain
rows.summary: A 663-metre mountain and forest park in Jinzhou, with Buddhist and Taoist temples and rock canyons, and azaleas that bloom on the slopes in mid-April. Along the ridges runs Beisha Fortress, a ruined Goguryeo hill fort of about 5 km, whose west gate, Guanmenzhai, stands at the canyon entrance. The fortress is a national heritage site and one of the scenic area's main sights.

rows.name: Dalian Forest Zoo
rows.summary: Dalian Forest Zoo covers 7.2 square kilometres of Baiyun Hill in the south of the city and opened in 1997, with a free-range area added in 2000. It keeps more than 200 species and over 2,000 animals, with a panda house, hippos, golden snub-nosed monkeys, Siberian tigers, flamingos and cranes among its exhibits. It suits families.

rows.name: Dalian Laohutan Ocean Park
rows.summary: Laohutan Ocean Park is a marine-themed park on about 4 km of winding coastline in Dalian, with a core area of 118 hectares. Its main venues are the Polar Aquarium, a coral hall, a bird garden, a sea-mammal hall and a show theatre with staged animal performances, and it also has a cable car across the bay, a Jurassic-themed children's play island and 180- and 360-degree film attractions. It is a commercial park aimed mainly at families.

rows.name: Dalian Martial Arts Culture Museum
rows.summary: A museum of Chinese martial arts, with exhibits on the history of the martial arts in China and in Dalian over the past century. The collection centres on cold weapons from the Ming dynasty to modern times, along with boxing manuals and other martial-arts papers. A sunken ring-shaped theatre hosts demonstrations and staged shows.

rows.name: Dalian Modern Museum
rows.summary: Dalian's city museum stands beside Xinghai Square and opened in 2002. Its permanent exhibition, 'Modern Dalian', covers the city's history from 1840 to 1949 in seven sections, from naval defence and the 1894–95 war through Russian and Japanese rule to the establishment of people's government in 1949. Other halls hold changing exhibitions of art and antiquities borrowed from Chinese and foreign museums.

rows.name: Dalian Natural History Museum
rows.summary: The museum, on the Heishijiao shore, covers geology, palaeontology, zoology and botany in 12 halls, among them earth sciences, dinosaurs, marine life, north-eastern forest animals, wetlands, biodiversity and western Liaoning fossils. It holds about 200,000 specimens, and its grounds include a 270,000-square-metre area of sea. Its predecessor dates from 1907 and the present building opened in 1998.

rows.name: Dalian Sun Asia Ocean World
rows.summary: This commercial aquarium park in Xinghai Park by Xinghai Bay has four venues: Ocean World with a 118 m underwater tunnel, Polar World with Antarctic penguins and a spotted-seal bay, Coral World, and a zone of sea, land and air animals. Dolphin, sea-lion and beluga shows are staged in the park. It suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Delisi Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: A Goguryeo-period stone hill fortress on Longtan Mountain, with a wall of about 2.5 km round the ridge, east and west gates, and a stone-lined pool inside that gives the mountain its name. Rebuilt temples, including Deli Temple, stand within the walls. The ground was also fought over in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904.

rows.name: Dongjiguan Mountain
rows.summary: Dongjiguan ('East Cockscomb') Mountain, on the north-eastern edge of Lüshun, was a main battlefield of the Russo-Japanese War of 1904–05, when Japanese forces took the Russian fort on its north side in December 1904. The scenic area keeps the East Cockscomb North Fort, Erlongshan Fort and the Wangtai Battery, which the provincial tourism department calls an open-air history museum. Visitors walk through the preserved fortifications.

rows.name: Former Dalny City Hall
rows.summary: Built in 1900 as the administrative office of Dalny, the port city the Russians began planning on the site of today's Dalian, this two-storey Russian-designed building with a basement later became Japan's Manchuria Resources Museum, then the north-eastern local gazetteer museum, and from 1959 the Dalian Natural History Museum. The museum moved to a new building in 1998, and the old hall is no longer open to the public. Its long front, with dormer windows and a tall central roof, stands at the end of a street of old Russian-built houses.

rows.name: Former Kwantung Army Headquarters
rows.summary: This two-storey European-style building was put up by Russia in 1903, served from 1906 as the army department of Japan's Kwantung Government-General, and from 1919 housed the Kwantung Army headquarters, where the Mukden Incident of September 1931 was planned; the headquarters moved to Shenyang on 19 September that year. It later became an army hospital, was used by Soviet and then Chinese forces, and opened as a museum site in 2004, joining the Lüshun Museum in 2007. It was being restored in 2025.

rows.name: Former Kwantung Prefectural Office
rows.summary: Russia built this two-storey European-style building in 1900 as Lüshun's municipal hotel; after the Russo-Japanese War it housed Japan's Kwantung Government-General and later the Kwantung Agency and the Kwantung Prefectural Office, which moved to Dalian in 1937. It then served as a teachers' school, a Soviet building and, from 1955, a People's Liberation Army club and the quarters of its ski team, and it has stood largely vacant since the late 1990s. It was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013, and restoration work was reported under way in 2025.

rows.name: Guan Xiangying Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum at the birthplace of Guan Xiangying (1902–46), a Chinese Communist leader who served as a political commissar in the Red Army and the Eighth Route Army. The site has his restored family home, a Manchu-style courtyard and a main hall with about 2,000 sq m of galleries, including scenes of the Long March. The museum was first built in 1964, and its displays were renewed in 2022.

rows.name: Haiwang Jiudao (Nine Islands of Haiwang)
rows.summary: Haiwang Jiudao is a group of nine islands and dozens of reefs in the Yellow Sea off Wangjia town, Zhuanghe, including Dawangjia, Xiaowangjia and Shoulong Islands. The land area is 9.64 square kilometres and the sea area 380 square kilometres, and the islands are a national island forest park and a provincial-level tourism resort. The provincial tourism department recommends them as a summer retreat, with a mild semi-humid monsoon climate.

rows.name: Hengshan Beipuduo Theme Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 横山北普陀主题文化公园
rows.summary: This Buddhist-themed culture park of about 45 hectares in wooded hills was begun in 2003 and rated 4A in 2014. The provincial tourism department describes pavilions, halls, streams and ponds that combine traditional architecture, garden design and calligraphy, with spring flowers and autumn foliage. The park includes Hengshan Temple, a Buddhist temple.

rows.name: Jiangjunshi Seaside Resort
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A leisure resort at Bohai village on the Bohai coast of Wafangdian, centred on a hotel with villas, a hot-spring club and conference rooms. Activities include fishing, picking, a ski slope, a riding ground, a sailing base and a yacht marina. It suits families and groups looking for a weekend resort rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Jinshitan (Golden Pebble Beach)
rows.summary: Jinshitan is a coastal resort area in Jinzhou district, approved by the State Council as a national tourist resort in 1992. It is known for sea-eroded sedimentary rock formations several hundred million years old, now protected in a national coastal geological park, along with the Golden Coast beach and Jinshi Garden. Other attractions include the Discovery Kingdom theme park, a wax museum and a life-science museum.

rows.name: Laotieshan Lighthouse
rows.summary: A white iron lighthouse completed in 1893 by the Qing maritime customs service, standing on the Laotieshan headland at the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, where the Yellow Sea meets the Bohai Sea. It is still a working navigation light, and its French-made Fresnel lens turns on a mercury float. The station is run by the maritime authority, and the tower can be seen from the headland.

rows.name: Lüshun Museum
rows.summary: Founded in 1915 under Japanese administration and housed since 1918 in an eclectic Renaissance-style building, the Lüshun Museum is a national first-grade museum whose collections include archaeology of the Dalian area, relics from Xinjiang, ceramics, snuff bottles, coins and a gallery of mummies gathered on early twentieth-century expeditions to Central Asia. The building is nationally listed as the former Kwantung Museum, and the Sino-Soviet Friendship Tower stands in the cherry-planted square in front of it. Temporary exhibitions change through the year.

rows.name: Lüshun Russo-Japanese Prison
rows.name_zh: 旅顺日俄监狱旧址博物馆
rows.summary: Built by Russia from 1902 and enlarged by Japan from 1907, this former prison in Lüshun held mainly activists from Manchuria and Korea until 1945, and it opened as a museum in 1971. Inside a perimeter wall about 725 m long, visitors see the brick cell blocks, an interrogation room, an execution room and the former prison workshops. Two exhibition rooms cover the Korean independence activist An Jung-geun, who was held here in 1909–10 after killing the Japanese statesman Itō Hirobumi at Harbin station and was executed in March 1910.

rows.name: Lüshun Submarine Museum
rows.summary: The museum stands on the seafront below Huangjin (Golden) Hill in Lüshun and shows a retired Type 033 submarine alongside more than 60 other retired naval, land and air equipment items. It also has two '6D' ride theatres that simulate a submarine cruise, and the site includes the Huangjin Hill bathing beach. The museum and its partner areas cover about 6 hectares.

rows.name: Minghu Hot Spring and Ski Resort
rows.name_zh: 铭湖国际温泉滑雪度假区
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A resort of more than 4,000 mu (about 270 hectares) in the hills of Paotai subdistrict, combining a hot-spring hotel, a ski area and a farm-style ranch. The hot-spring water comes from a well about 2,600 m deep, and the ski area has five slopes plus a tubing run. It suits winter family trips more than sightseeing.

rows.name: Modern Buildings on Zhongshan Square in Dalian
rows.name_zh: 大连中山广场近代建筑群
rows.summary: Zhongshan Square is a round plaza 213 m across, with ten streets radiating from it, at the centre of old Dalian; the Russians laid it out around 1899 as Nikolayevskaya Square, and most of the buildings around it date from 1908 to 1936, when Japan administered the leased territory. The ring of Gothic- and Renaissance-style buildings is now mostly banks, plus the Dalian Hotel in the former Yamato Hotel, so most visitors walk round the outside. The national listing covers the former Dalian civil administration office, the former Bank of Chōsen branch and the Yamato Hotel, with a fourth building elsewhere in the city.

rows.name: Pingdao Sea Cucumber Town
rows.summary: A tourist island off the Yellow Sea coast of Pulandian District, themed on local sea-cucumber farming, for which the provincial tourism department lists 12 protection zones. Its landmark is a sea-cucumber sculpture carved from a single block of Xiuyan jade, and at low tide visitors can gather shellfish and fish along the beaches around the island. It suits families and anyone curious about the local seafood industry.

rows.name: Qicai Nanshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Qicai Nanshan is a rural tourism park of about one square kilometre at Xiaonan village in Lüshun, opened in 2010. According to the provincial tourism department it has five parts: a 'space plants' garden, a butterfly garden, the Songshushan fort (a Russo-Japanese War site), a countryside play area and a folk village, plus a village history hall and children's play areas. It mainly suits families with children.

rows.name: Shipenggou Dolmen
rows.summary: A Bronze Age stone burial chamber on a low hill east of Shipengtun hamlet, one of six dolmens that once stood here. It is formed by three upright slabs on the east, west and north sides under a thick capstone, about 25 sq m in plan, and is well preserved; the five smaller ones survive only as traces. It is one of the larger dolmens on the Liaodong Peninsula.

rows.name: Shiwai Jiantang Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring scenic area of about 3.8 sq km in wooded hills at Jiantang, in Anbo subdistrict of Pulandian District. The provincial tourism department describes a spring that flows naturally at about 57°C, set among forest and countryside. It suits visitors who want hot-spring bathing in a rural setting.

rows.name: Sino-Soviet Friendship Memorial Tower
rows.summary: The 22.2 m tower was built in 1955–57 in the square in front of the Lüshun Museum, around the time Soviet forces withdrew from Lüshun and the port was returned to China in May 1955. Reliefs on its base show Tiananmen and the Kremlin, the Anshan blast furnaces, Lüshun scenery with a Soviet army victory tower, and a combine harvest at a Sino-Soviet state farm, and a gilded peace dove tops the shaft. It has been a national heritage unit since 1961.

rows.name: Site of the Kwantung Governor-General's Office
rows.summary: This group of Russian-period buildings at 45 Gangwan Street in old Lüshun, dated 1899 in the official list, is listed as the site of the Japanese Kwantung governor-general's offices. Photographs taken in 2013 show yellow-rendered two-storey buildings with pedimented gables and an arched passage opening on a cobbled courtyard behind iron gates. The site was taken over by the People's Liberation Army after 1949 and was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: South Armory
rows.summary: The South Armory was an ammunition depot built in 1884, according to the official heritage list, during the construction of the Qing government's naval port at Lüshun, on the coast east of Huangjin Hill. It was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.
