Xinhua reported in 2025 that it and three other relics outside army compounds were being handed to the district government for a patriotic and national-defence education base.

rows.name: Tianmenshan National Forest Park, Zhuanghe
rows.summary: Tianmenshan National Forest Park lies in the mountains of northern Zhuanghe and borders Gaizhou, Yingkou and Xiuyan. The provincial tourism department lists 36 peaks above 800 m, the highest being Douyunfeng at 926 m, with cliffs, caves and gorges. Its main activity is rafting on the Tianmen Gorge, a course of about 10 km with a 91 m drop that takes two to three hours.

rows.name: Wanzhong Tomb
rows.summary: Wanzhong Tomb is the communal grave of people killed in Lüshun (Port Arthur) in the days after Japanese forces took the town in November 1894. The first burial dates from 1895, a tablet bearing the tomb's name was set up in 1896, and the site was rebuilt in 1948 and again in 1994, when a memorial hall, a sacrificial plaza and a memorial stele were added. Today it consists of the tomb chamber, a sacrificial hall and gate, and the memorial hall, and it has been a national heritage unit since 2006.

rows.name: Weibashan Fortress and Qingquan Temple
rows.summary: Weibashan, also called Wugu City, is a Goguryeo-period hill fortress whose stone wall follows the ridge around the mountain for about 3 km. In its eastern part stands Qingquan Temple, a Qing-style complex of three courtyards holding 72 painted clay figures, among them the Jade Emperor, Laozi, the Buddha, Confucius and famous physicians, all kept behind glass. The fortress and temple are listed among the sights of the Anbo scenic area.

rows.name: Xianyuwan Beach Resort
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A seaside resort on the west coast of Wafangdian, with about 11 km of shoreline of which 6.4 km is bathing beach, backed by woodland and a forest park. The resort has a visitor centre, a seaside temple, a pine maze, a hot-spring hotel and silica-sand bathing. It was named a national marine park in 2016 and a 4A tourist resort in 2017.

rows.name: Xiaoshuikou Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded coastal park of about 1.2 sq km at the eastern tip of Xiaochangshan Island in the Changshan Islands. A boardwalk of about 550 m runs along the rocky shore, with a glass-floored section of over 30 m, and woodland covers more than 80 per cent of the park. Local tourism officials describe it as the only 4A scenic area on the islands.

rows.name: Xijiao National Forest Park, Dalian
rows.summary: A large forest park of about 70 sq km on the north-western edge of Dalian, with some 85 per cent tree cover. Its main areas are West Mountain Lake with a nine-island wetland, Tangli Lake, which has hosted trail-running and archery events, Hongqi Valley with a golf course, and Changqing Lake, known for cherries. It serves as one of Dalian's main green spaces.

rows.name: Yingchengzi Han Tombs
rows.summary: The provincial heritage department describes this as the largest Han-dynasty cemetery found in north-east China, with nearly 300 tombs excavated since the 1930s. The Dalian Han Tombs Museum, opened in October 2010, shows excavated tomb structures and finds; the painted tomb dug in 1931 is known for a mural of the tomb owner ascending to immortality. The cemetery is spread across three villages along the railway line, so the museum is the place to visit.

rows.name: Yinggeshi Botanical Garden
rows.summary: This privately run botanical garden of about 100 hectares in the hills of Dalian's high-tech zone was begun in 2003 and opened in April 2014. The provincial tourism department says it has collected 3,021 plant species in 126 families, and it is known for successive flowerings from spring to autumn, including tulips, cherry and peach blossom, peonies, hydrangeas and chrysanthemums.

rows.name: Ziyun Huaxi Lavender Estate
rows.summary: A flower and herb farm of about 1,100 mu (roughly 73 hectares) in the hills of Xiangying subdistrict, planted mainly with lavender, verbena, sage and roses, plus fruit orchards and plum trees. It is run as a romance-themed leisure park, with RV camping, lodging, picking and activities such as small-bore shooting. Its lavender and other blue-purple flower fields are the main draw.

rows.name: Dalishu Agricultural Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 大梨树生态农业观光旅游区
rows.summary: The Dalishu tourism area is a rural-tourism complex in and around Dalishu village, south-west of Fengcheng, which the provincial tourism department counts among the first national agricultural-tourism demonstration sites. It is laid out as four zones, for leisure-farming experiences, health and culture, ethnic-village sightseeing and visitor services, and it includes picking gardens and a film-set town. It is a modern leisure attraction for families and groups, not a historic village.

rows.name: Dalu Island
rows.summary: Dalu Island lies at the mouth of the Yalu, about 4 km long, with a fishing and tourism village and a bathing beach. The sea to the south is one of the sites of the 1894 naval battle of the Sino-Japanese War, and the island has a tomb and statue of the Chinese naval officer Deng Shichang, a British-style lighthouse, a sea-goddess temple, a stele to the Ming general Mao Wenlong and the ruins of a Danish church. Visitors come by boat and can combine the memorials with the beach.

rows.name: Hekou Broken Bridge, Kuandian
rows.summary: The Hekou Broken Bridge is the surviving part of a road bridge across the Yalu built in 1942, originally about 700 m long with 23 spans. It was damaged by air attack in November 1950 during the Korean War and repaired, then cut in the middle by bombing in November 1951; nine spans remain on the Chinese side and five on the Korean side, with three piers standing in the river between them. It sits in the Hekou scenic area, which also runs river boat trips and takes in Changhe Island, and visitors can look across the water to Sakju County in North Korea.

rows.name: Hushan Great Wall
rows.summary: Hushan Great Wall is a restored stretch of Ming-era wall, about 1.2 km long, that climbs Hushan hill (146 m) beside the Yalu where the Ai River joins it. Surveys in the late 1980s and early 1990s identified the ruins here as the eastern end of the Ming wall in Liaoning, and the wall has been restored in stages since 1992, with a rebuilt entrance gate and a series of towers. From the top there are views over the river to the North Korean bank.

rows.name: Memorial of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
rows.summary: This national first-grade museum on Yinghua Mountain in Dandong is devoted to the Korean War, which China calls the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, and to the campaign in China to support it. The complex has an exhibition building with halls on the war, the home-front campaign, Sino-Korean ties and those who died, a panorama hall with a large painting of the 1950 Chongchon River battle, a 53 m memorial tower and an outdoor park of displayed weapons, with views toward Sinuiju across the river. It reopened in 2020 after a refit that began in 2014 and holds more than 20,000 relics, according to the provincial tourism page.

rows.name: Phoenix Mountain, Fengcheng
rows.summary: Phoenix Mountain is a rocky mountain area south-east of Fengcheng, divided into West Mountain, East Mountain and Ancient City sections, with cliff-side boardwalks, a glass-floored walkway, a glass suspension bridge and several temples. The Ancient City section holds the Goguryeo-period Fenghuangshan Mountain City, also called Wugu City, begun in the early fifth century, where stretches of wall and the remains of its gates survive. Several routes run along cliff faces, so it suits confident walkers.

rows.name: Tianhuashan Forest Park
rows.summary: Tianhuashan is a provincial scenic area and forest park in the mountains of Guanshui town in northern Kuandian County, made a provincial forest park in January 2001. The provincial tourism page lists Bailongjian, Tianhuafeng, Yulongjian, Qinglongjian and Foguangding among its walking areas and picks out Bailongjian, Tongtian Gorge, Tiantai and Maogong Peak as its main sights. It is a gorge-and-peak landscape for walking, well away from the Dandong riverfront sights.

rows.name: Tianqiaogou
rows.summary: Tianqiaogou is a forest park in the mountains of northern Kuandian County, close to the boundaries with Huanren and Benxi counties, and is best known for its autumn maple colour. The provincial tourism page describes it as covering more than 4,000 ha and as one of China's well-known maple-viewing parks. Autumn is the season to go.

rows.name: Yalu River Broken Bridge
rows.summary: The Broken Bridge is what remains of the first bridge built across the Yalu, a 12-span steel railway bridge that Japan began in 1909 to link Korea with the Eurasian rail network and that later carried road traffic. United States aircraft bombed it in November 1950 during the Korean War; the Korean-side spans were later dismantled, and the four surviving Chinese spans have been a walkway since 1993, ending mid-river at a viewing platform beside the old swing-span mechanism. The Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge stands just upstream, and the city of Sinuiju faces the walkway across the water.

rows.name: Yalu River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Yalu River Scenic Area is a national-level scenic and historic area that follows the river from the Hun River mouth, at the Liaoning–Jilin boundary, down to the sea; the provincial tourism department lists six sections: Jiangkou, Daqiao (the bridges at Dandong), Hushan, Taipingwan, Shuifeng and Lüjiang. Most visitors meet it in Dandong, where the riverfront looks across to the North Korean city of Sinuiju and the Broken Bridge and the Hushan Great Wall, both national heritage units with entries of their own, are the best-known stops. The pin marks the central riverfront park by the bridges rather than a single gate.

rows.name: Zhangdao Island
rows.summary: Zhangdao, also called Xiaoludao (Little Deer Island), is a small island village in the Yellow Sea off Beijingzi town in Donggang. According to the provincial tourism department it is one main island with six smaller mounds, which separate into six islets at high tide and join into one island at low tide. The village lives mainly from tourism, fishing and aquaculture and has more than 110 hotels and farm guesthouses, so it suits a seaside day trip or a short stay.

rows.name: Fushun Lei Feng Memorial Hall
rows.summary: Opened in 1965 near the former barracks of Lei Feng's army unit, this memorial park commemorates the soldier Lei Feng (1940–1962), who became the subject of a long-running national 'Learn from Lei Feng' campaign. The grounds of about 10 ha hold an exhibition hall on his life, a 13.4 m granite monument, his tomb, statues and a court of stone tablets, and the tomb and monument together are a national heritage unit. The displays present the official Chinese account of his life and of the campaign.

rows.name: Fushun War Criminals Management Centre
rows.summary: Built by the Japanese authorities in 1936 as a prison, the site was turned in 1950 into a detention and re-education centre for Japanese war-crimes suspects, officials of the Manchukuo regime including the last Qing emperor Puyi, and captured Nationalist officers. The preserved prison now houses an exhibition on the detention of the Japanese prisoners, a separate display on Puyi's years there, and the original cells and facilities, all presenting the Chinese account of the period. The Japanese prisoners were released between 1956 and 1964, and the other detainees were amnestied between 1959 and 1975.

rows.name: Hemu National Forest Park
rows.summary: Hemu is a long, narrow forest park in the Longgang foothills of Xinbin Manchu Autonomous County, about 7.5 km from end to end and covering some 20,300 mu (about 1,350 ha). The Fushun tourism bureau describes it as holding the country's oldest planted larch forest, and it has a visitor centre, a bagua-pattern maze, log cabins and a hotel used for retreats and conferences. It suits visitors looking for forest walks and a short stay.

rows.name: Hetu Ala
rows.summary: Hetu Ala was the first capital of Nurhaci, the Jurchen leader who began building the city in 1603 and proclaimed himself khan here in 1616, founding the Later Jin state, the forerunner of the Qing dynasty. The hill-and-river site keeps the line of its walls and several historic sites, among them the Khan's Great Yamen, the Khan's well, the Zhengbai Banner office, the former home of Nurhaci's father Taksi, a qipao museum and the Manchu Museum. The capital moved to Liaoyang in the early 1620s, and the old city was renamed Xingjing in 1634.

rows.name: Kuangzigou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Kuangzigou is a forested river-valley scenic area in Qingyuan Manchu Autonomous County, with forest cover given as 95 percent by the local tourism bureaus. A stream runs through the valley past a string of waterfalls, four numbered 'pot' pools, a suspension bridge and birch woods, and the area is promoted for summer cool and autumn colour.

rows.name: Nantianmen Scenic Area
rows.summary: Nantianmen is a mountain-and-water leisure resort in Qingyuan Manchu Autonomous County with a planned area of about 10 sq km. Its attractions include a high-level glass water slide, a children's park, a high-level swing, a rainbow slide, a jungle-crossing course, a glass suspension bridge, bamboo rafts and boats and plank walkways. It is a commercial leisure park that suits families and groups looking for a day of activities.

rows.name: Pingdingshan Massacre Memorial Hall
rows.summary: Pingdingshan was a village beside Fushun's coal workings where, on 16 September 1932, Japanese troops killed villagers in reprisal for an attack by an anti-Japanese volunteer army the night before; the memorial gives a toll of more than 3,000. Excavations in 1970 uncovered a pit of remains, and a hall built over it now displays the remains of more than 800 people under glass. The grounds also hold a four-hall exhibition on the massacre and its aftermath, a 19.32 m memorial column and a court of 60 stone tablets carrying survivors' testimony.

rows.name: Red River Gorge Rafting
rows.summary: Red River Gorge is a 12.8 km river-rafting run through a forested, U-shaped valley in Qingyuan Manchu Autonomous County, known locally as the 'Little Three Gorges of the north-east' and promoted with the slogan 'the first rafting in the north'. The trip takes about two and a half hours, with calm and fast stretches, and the service areas at the start and finish have changing rooms, showers, a dining hall, a landing stage and parking. Rafting is a summer activity: the 2025 season was formally launched on 22 June.

rows.name: Sankuaishi National Forest Park
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Sankuaishi is a mountain forest park in Fushun County, named for three huge boulders that stand together on a high summit; its main peak reaches 1,131 m. The Fushun tourism bureau gives its area as 108.7 sq km, with forest covering about 92 percent of it. It was a base area during the war against Japan and the civil war, and sites of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army survive there, so it is promoted for red tourism as well as scenery.

rows.name: Shenxian Valley Eco-Resort
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Shenxian Valley ('Ginseng Immortal Valley') is a forest leisure resort of about 1,360 ha in the mountains of Xinbin Manchu Autonomous County, developed over several years from the mid-2010s. It has lakes, wooded valleys, wooden lodges on the water, a high-level glass rafting ride and other adventure activities, with snowmobiles and horse-drawn sleds in winter, and it is run as a commercial resort. The tourism bureaus repeat a local tradition that the area was once an imperial ginseng ground and hunting preserve of Nurhaci.

rows.name: Tiannüshan Forest Park
rows.summary: Tiannüshan is a forested mountain park in Fushun County whose main peak rises to 780 m, covering about 1,380 mu (some 92 ha). It has more than twenty named sights, including the Tongtian path, Nantianmen ('South Heaven Gate'), the Fox Spirit Cave, Zhuanxin Lake and the Phoenix Terrace. The Fushun tourism bureau highlights the tiannü magnolia in summer, azaleas in spring and red maples in autumn.

rows.name: Yongling Tomb, Xinbin
rows.summary: Yongling is the burial ground of Nurhaci's forebears: his father Taksi, grandfather Giocangga, great-grandfather Fuman and the earlier ancestor Mengtemu, together with two of his uncles. Laid out from 1598 and renamed Yongling in 1659, it is entered through a Manchu-style gate with a wooden-fence door, passes four stele pavilions with inscriptions in Manchu, Mongolian and Chinese, and ends at a square courtyard with a main hall and a circular wall around the graves. It is the senior but smaller of the three Qing imperial tombs of the Shenyang–Xinbin area, and with Fuling and Zhaoling it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2004 as part of the Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties.

rows.name: Yuanshuailin, Zhang Zuolin's Mausoleum
rows.summary: Yuanshuailin ('Marshal's Grove') is a mausoleum begun in 1929 by Zhang Xueliang for his father, the warlord Zhang Zuolin, who was killed in 1928. Work stopped after the Mukden Incident of 1931 and Zhang Zuolin was buried instead at Yimafang near Jinzhou in 1937, so the tomb here has always been empty. The southern halls were lost to the Dahuofang Reservoir, begun in 1954, but the circular wall and burial mound survive on the higher ground, together with stone sculptures that Zhang Xueliang bought in the western outskirts of Beijing.

rows.name: Baodi Spa Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort town in Dongliang town, south-west of Fuxin, whose spring water is drawn from a well about 1,888 m deep at 82 °C and described by the provincial tourism page as a sodium bicarbonate spring. The leisure area has a hotel, restaurants, a water park and indoor and outdoor soaking pools, and a separate wellness and retirement section offers medical, research and education services for longer stays. It is a modern commercial resort for relaxing breaks rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Chahai Neolithic Site and Museum
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement about 8,000 years old (radiocarbon-dated), excavated in seven seasons between 1986 and 1994 over nearly 7,800 sq m, which revealed house foundations, storage pits, a ritual pit and a dragon-shaped arrangement of stones about 20 m long. The site museum, opened in 1992 about 50 m south of the dig, is built to resemble six half-sunken houses, with red walls textured like bark; its permanent exhibition covers the Chahai culture, and an outdoor area shows the excavated house foundations and the stone dragon. The provincial heritage page calls Chahai an early forerunner of the Hongshan culture and the origin of the zigzag-patterned pottery of the West Liao River valley.

rows.name: Deligeer Grassland Scenic Area, Zhangwu
rows.summary: A lakeshore leisure area of about 800 mu (53 ha) on Deligeer Lake in Zhangwu county, where the provincial tourism page says lake, island, wetland, grassland and sand lie side by side. The listed facilities are a visitor centre, a camping area, guesthouses, a racecourse, an island attraction called Bixin Island, a rainbow slide, a petting zoo, a youth activity base and peony and lotus gardens. It is a commercial site aimed at family and group outings.

rows.name: Dongtashan Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda standing on a wooded hillside in Hongmaozi town, Fuxin Mongol Autonomous County, octagonal with close-set storeys of eaves and niches, imitation timber brackets and relief carving on its body. The provincial heritage page dates it to the reign of Emperor Shengzong of the Liao, and notes that the finial is long gone.

rows.name: Fuxin Miners' Mass Graves Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 阜新万人坑死难矿工纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial and museum on the site of the mass graves of miners who died in the Fuxin coalfield while it was run by Japanese-controlled companies, from the 1930s to 1945; official figures put the number buried in the city's graves at about 70,000. Halls built over excavated pits show remains in place, one for miners and one for labourers held at a nearby camp who took part in a 1942 uprising, and exhibitions cover the history of the mines; the site spans about 57 ha. The memorial opened in 1968, was repaired and reopened in 2015, and is a national heritage unit.

rows.name: Haitangshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain of old pines and rock outcrops in Daban town, Fuxin Mongol Autonomous County, protected as a national nature reserve and forest park, with a main peak of 715.4 m. Its best-known sight is a set of Qing-dynasty Buddhist figures carved into the cliffs, which the provincial tourism page calls fine examples of Qing Buddhist sculpture. The mountain was historically an area where the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism spread, and Puan Temple, founded in 1683, stands in it.

rows.name: Huangjiagou Resort, Fuxin
rows.summary: A four-season leisure resort in Sihe town, Xihe District, which the provincial tourism page describes as set among a hill, two rivers, nine lakes and about 1,000 mu (67 ha) of pine woods. A water park in summer and a ski field in winter are the main attractions, with hot-spring guesthouses and rural tourism among the resort's five sections, and flower viewing and fruit picking in spring and autumn. The resort area has been named a national key village for rural tourism.

rows.name: Ruiying Temple
rows.summary: A working Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Fosi town, Fuxin Mongol Autonomous County, founded in 1669 and named by the Kangxi emperor in 1703, and long the seat of the Chagan Diancheqi line of incarnate lamas. The provincial tourism page calls it the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery of north-east China and the eastern Mongol lands; in the Qing period it had colleges for philosophy, medicine, tantra and astronomy and influenced Mongolian medicine and calendar-making. The halls were badly damaged and the monks dispersed during the Cultural Revolution; restoration began in 1984, and the temple is a provincial heritage unit, with smaller temples on the hilltops around the main halls.

rows.name: Tayingzi Pagoda
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty brick pagoda 32 m high, octagonal with 13 close-set storeys of eaves, standing near the middle of the old Yizhou city site at Tayingzi village, and also called the Baoyan Temple Pagoda. The provincial heritage page calls it the best preserved of the three Liao brick pagodas still standing in this district, with a three-tier base carved with lions, musicians and guardian figures and seated Buddhas in round niches on the first storey. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013, and the walls of the old city around it are a provincial heritage site.

rows.name: Wulanmutu Mountain
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 30 sq km in Bajiazi town, Fuxin Mongol Autonomous County, whose main peak, at 831.4 m, is the highest in Fuxin prefecture. The provincial tourism page highlights rock formations, dense woodland, temples built into the cliffs and a large wild stand of Amur tree lilac, and notes that the mountain had a different name in the Liao period and was settled in Hongshan-culture times. It also mentions herbs, deposits of maifan stone and local folk customs among the area's resources.

rows.name: Baitayu Pagoda
rows.summary: Baitayu Pagoda is a Liao-dynasty brick pagoda with eight sides and thirteen tiers of close-set eaves, standing on a hillock south of Jiulong Mountain. A stone inscription found in its crypt in 1972 records that it was begun in 1092 as a relic pagoda of Kongtongshan Wuji Monastery. It was once counted among Xingcheng's eight scenic views as the 'Nine Dragons Smoke Pagoda' and has been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Huanle Longwan Hot Spring Water Park
rows.summary: Huanle Longwan is a water park on the Xingcheng seafront with wave pools, slides, a drifting river, a children's water zone and hot-spring bathing pools, plus restaurants and rest pavilions. It is a modern leisure development rather than a historic site, aimed mainly at families.

rows.name: Hulu Ancient Town
rows.summary: Hulu Ancient Town is a leisure and farm-tourism complex on the northern edge of Huludao, begun in 2001 and themed on gourd culture (hulu, as in the city's name) and the folk customs of north-east China (Guandong). It offers folk-custom performances, fruit picking, study-tour programmes, a folk museum, restaurants and lodging, and skiing and skating in winter, in newly built old-style buildings rather than historic ones. It suits families and groups rather than visitors looking for heritage sites.

rows.name: Jiangnüshi Site
rows.summary: Jiangnüshi is a coastal complex of Qin and early Western Han palace remains on the Zhimao Bay shore, found in 1982 and excavated from 1984 to 2002; it was the first Qin-era travelling palace found outside the Guanzhong region. Its core, the Jieshi Palace site, is a large terraced platform of rammed earth close to the shore, facing three sea-eroded rocks offshore known as the Jiang Nü Tomb, which legend links to Meng Jiangnü and which scholars identify as the 'Jieshi' (Stone Gate) of ancient texts. On the ground there are low earth platforms and foundation lines rather than standing buildings.

rows.name: Jiumenkou Great Wall
rows.summary: Jiumenkou is a stretch of Ming Great Wall that crosses a seasonal river on a stone gateway-bridge about 110 m long and 10 m high, with nine arched openings that carried heavy double wooden doors, shut at low water and opened to let floods through. The river bed is paved with square stone slabs, which gave the pass its old name Yipianshi ('One Slab of Stone'), and watchtowers and wall run up the hills on either side as part of the eastern end of the Ming Jizhen defences. The site straddles the Liaoning–Hebei border; the Liaoning side lies in Suizhong County.

rows.name: Juehua Island
rows.summary: Juehua Island, renamed in 2009 from Juhua (Chrysanthemum) Island, is the largest island in Liaodong Bay, with about 13 km² of land, 27 km of coastline and a high point of 198 m. The tourism department lists the Dalonggong Temple (a Liao-period foundation, rebuilt in 2002), an octagonal well, the remains of a Ming-era camp, a bodhi culture park, an east-coast park and bathing beaches. In Ming times it was a grain depot for the Liaodong army, and Nurhaci's forces attacked it in 1626.

rows.name: Lingshan Scenic Area, Lianshan
rows.summary: Lingshan is a hilly forest area in Lianshan District with crags, odd-shaped rocks, caves and cliffs, and an old temple complex that is a provincial heritage site. Named features include the Nantianmen (South Heaven Gate), a group of twelve-zodiac rocks, an eagle-beak rock and a camel-shaped peak. The department describes it as one of Liaoning's ten best forest parks and a provincial ecotourism demonstration area.

rows.name: Longtan Grand Canyon, Jianchang
rows.summary: Longtan Grand Canyon is a wooded gorge in the hills of western Jianchang County, close to the Hebei border, with cliffs, pools, waterfalls, caves and oddly shaped rocks; the tourism department also describes it as a national geopark. Facilities include a glass-floored suspension bridge, a dry slide, boat rides and a small forest train, so the scenery comes with adventure-park attractions.

rows.name: Longwan Beach, Huludao
rows.summary: Longwan Beach is a seafront resort strip on Liaodong Bay in Longgang District, with a sand beach more than 2 km long, a marble-paved central plaza flanked by European-style hotels, a coastal boardwalk, and shopping and amusement areas. The scenic area covers 6.9 km² and is split into a bathing beach, a commercial street zone, a boardwalk-and-green-space zone and a visitor-service zone.

rows.name: Moshigou Pagoda
rows.summary: Moshigou Pagoda is a Liao-period brick pagoda 17.4 m high, with eight sides, nine tiers of close-set eaves and a hollow interior, standing on a hill beside Moshigou hamlet in Hongyazi Manchu township. Each face of the tower is about 2 m wide; its base is badly damaged and only the upper part of the stepped Sumeru-style pedestal survives. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Shaguotun Cave Site
rows.summary: Shaguotun is a small cave on a wooded hillside that the Swedish scholar Johan Gunnar Andersson and the Canadian scholar Davidson Black dug in June 1921, in what is regarded as the first formal archaeological excavation in China. It yielded prehistoric painted pottery and jade; the material was first compared with Yangshao and later Hongshan finds before being assigned to the Xiaoheyan culture. What can be seen on the spot is the cave mouth and a protection marker on the slope.

rows.name: Shaguotun Stone Pagoda
rows.summary: This small stone pagoda was built in 1206 under the Jin dynasty and is about 5 m high, hexagonal, with five tiers of close-set eaves and a solid core. It stands at the east edge of Shaguotun village in Nanpiao District and has been a national heritage unit since 2013. The Shaguotun cave site, where the first formal archaeological excavation in China took place in 1921, lies about 2 km to the south-east.

rows.name: Shengshui Temple, Huludao
rows.summary: Shengshui Temple is a Qing-dynasty complex built in 1720 on the south slope of Zhenlianhua Mountain, combining Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist halls in one walled compound of about a hectare. The central axis runs from the Tianyuan Palace gate hall through the Biyun Palace and a bell and drum tower to the main hall, with side courtyards that include a beamless hall and a nine-bay hall. It has been a national heritage unit since 2006.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Miaofeng Temple
rows.summary: Two Liao-dynasty brick pagodas stand about 50 m apart on Miaofeng Ridge, the only surviving parts of Miaofeng Temple, which was destroyed in the late Ming or early Qing. The eastern pagoda is 19 m high, octagonal with nine tiers and hollow, on a base 2.4 m high; the western one is 10 m high, hexagonal with five tiers, and matches it in structure and carving. They were built in the Qiantong era (1101–1114) and have been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Xingcheng Old Town
rows.summary: Xingcheng Old Town is the former Ming garrison city of Ningyuan, founded in 1428 and enclosed by a roughly square circuit of brick-faced walls about 3 km round, with a gate in each side; it is counted among the best-preserved Ming city walls in China. At the crossing of the main streets stands a drum tower built in 1454 and repaired in 1777, and two carved stone memorial arches put up by the Zu brothers in 1631 and 1638 stand on Yanhui Street, along with a Confucian temple dating from 1428. The Ming general Yuan Chonghuan defended the town against a Manchu army in 1626, in the Battle of Ningyuan.

rows.name: Xingcheng Seaside Scenic Area
rows.summary: Xingcheng Seaside is a 14 km sandy seafront on Liaodong Bay, divided into the Xinghai, Gangkou and Bingjia bays, with a gently shelving beach and no offshore reefs. A boardwalk of about 1.7 km runs along the shore between the rocky Longhuitou headland and Bingjia Bay, linking wooden and rope bridges, pavilions and plazas. It is a summer holiday and sanatorium resort.

rows.name: Yintai Shuixing Ocean Park, Dongdaihe
rows.summary: Yintai Shuixing (Water Planet) Ocean Park is a beachfront leisure development in the Dongdaihe New Area, rated a 4A scenic area in 2017, with 4.6 km of sandy coastline. The tourism department describes a seaside holiday zone with caravan and car camping, a culture plaza with creative markets and stage shows, and a sea-themed amusement area with a marina and a slide park. It is a modern resort rather than a historic site, aimed at summer beach holidays.

rows.name: Zhongqiansuo Garrison Town
rows.summary: Zhongqiansuo is a Ming garrison town, one of the 'thousand-household battalions' under the Guangning Qiantun Garrison, founded in 1428 and later repaired under the Qianlong emperor. The walled area is roughly square, about 528 m by 521 m, with gates on the east, west and south sides, each fronted by a barbican, and walls 7–8 m high that survive largely as built. The original buildings inside have mostly gone, and the enclosure is now filled by a small modern town.

rows.name: Banji Pagoda
rows.summary: A small Liao-dynasty brick pagoda of 1058 at the foot of Pangu hill, about 0.5 km north of the Xiaoling River. About 11 m high, it is a 'flower pagoda', a seven-tier octagonal solid tower whose upper part is covered with niches holding Buddha figures; the provincial heritage page counts it among the few Liao flower pagodas that survive in China and the only Liao pagoda in Linghai. A small vaulted brick-and-stone hall stands 2 m to its east.

rows.name: Beiputuo Mountain, Jinzhou
rows.summary: A hill park of about 26 sq km on the north-western edge of Jinzhou, made up of six peaks and nine sights, with a Buddhist temple that holds Spring Festival prayer events. The provincial tourism page calls it western Liaoning's foremost 'cave-heaven' and says the site has a history of more than 1,400 years; the hills are wooded, with peach blossom in spring and red leaves in autumn.

rows.name: Beizhen Temple
rows.summary: The state temple to the spirit of Yiwulü Mountain, the northern one of China's five guardian mountains, founded in 594 and rebuilt under the Ming dynasty from 1370. Its halls climb a hillside along a 240 m axis, from a stone arch and gate through the main hall to the rear sleeping hall, with bell and drum towers, stele pavilions and 56 steles of the Yuan, Ming and Qing periods. The provincial heritage department calls it the best-preserved large temple of the five guardian mountains, and the foundations of a Qianlong-era travelling palace lie to its east.

rows.name: Bijia Mountain
rows.summary: A small island of about 1 sq km in Liaodong Bay that a natural sand-and-gravel causeway about 1.6 km long links to the mainland; the tides expose it twice a day and cover it again. On the island is a group of old buildings, including Sanqing Pavilion, an all-stone pavilion built without timber or nails that houses Confucian, Daoist and Buddhist figures. The causeway can only be walked at low tide, so check tide times before going.

rows.name: Dachaoyang Hot Spring Resort, Beizhen
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort and hotel complex at the foot of Yiwulü Mountain about 6.5 km west of Beizhen town, developed by a Liaoning company and next to the Yiwulü nature reserve. It has spa pools, a three-star hotel, conference facilities and a museum of the history and folk culture of the Yiwulü area. It is a modern commercial resort, useful as a base for visiting the mountain.

rows.name: Daluhua, Yiwulü Mountain
rows.summary: A scenic area in Baojia township on the middle-southern part of the Yiwulü range, a national geopark known for steep rock pinnacles, with a main peak of about 630 m. The name means 'big reed flowers': according to the provincial tourism page, reeds cover the hillsides here and their plumes drift in autumn. It is one of several separate scenic areas on the range, alongside the main Beizhen section and Qingyan Temple.

rows.name: Dongfang Huadicheng Wetland Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 东方华地城湿地温泉旅游度假区
rows.pinyin: Dōngfāng Huádìchéng Shīdì Wēnquán Lǚyóu Dùjiàqū
rows.summary: A resort of about 28,000 mu (roughly 1,900 ha) on the wetlands at the mouth of the Daling River on the Bohai coast, including about 10,000 mu of reed beds. It offers boat trips among the reeds, a hot-spring spa fed by a well about 1,368 m deep, villa and cabin accommodation and a winter snow-and-ice attraction. The provincial page also lists farm-experience activities and a youth nature-education base, so it is a modern commercial resort rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Fengguo Temple
rows.summary: A Liao-dynasty temple founded in 1020 in the old town of Yixian, whose main hall, nine bays wide and raised on a 3 m platform, is one of the largest surviving timber Buddhist halls in China. Inside sit seven Liao-period Buddhas of the past, each over 8 m high with its base and attended by bodhisattvas, with painted flying figures on the roof beams. The gates, an arch and a smaller hall are Qing-dynasty additions, and the main hall has been on China's tentative list for World Heritage status since 2013, together with the wooden pagoda at Yingxian.

rows.name: Guangji Temple Complex and Jinzhou Museum
rows.name_zh: 广济寺古建筑群（锦州市博物馆）
rows.summary: A walled group of old temple buildings in the middle of Jinzhou, centred on a 13-tier brick pagoda begun under the Liao dynasty in 1057 and a Buddhist temple rebuilt in the Qing dynasty, with a Mazu temple, a Guanyin pavilion and a shrine to soldiers killed in the 1894 Sino-Japanese War. Jinzhou Museum shares the site, with permanent displays on the city's history, western Liaoning fossils, local customs and Buddhist art, and exhibitions on Mazu worship and the 1894 land war in the old halls. The pagoda, about 71 m high after its 1996 restoration, stands in Guta Park in the middle of the city.

rows.name: Guangning City, Beizhen (Drum Tower and Li Chengliang Arch)
rows.name_zh: 广宁城（鼓楼与李成梁石坊）
rows.pinyin: Guǎngníng Chéng (Gǔlóu Yǔ Lǐ Chéngliáng Shífāng)
rows.summary: Guangning was the Ming-dynasty garrison city of Beizhen, and two of its landmarks stand on the main north–south street: the Drum Tower of 1563, a two-storey tower on a brick-and-stone base pierced by a gateway, and the stone memorial arch of 1580 to the Ming frontier commander Li Chengliang, about 9 m high. A stair of 39 steps leads up to the platform of the Drum Tower, which the provincial heritage department describes as one of Beizhen's tourist sights. Most of the 7 km city wall was pulled down in the 1960s and 1970s and a ring road follows its line, but a 378 m stretch of brick wall and a 1,250 m stretch of rammed-earth wall are preserved.

rows.name: Guangsheng Temple Pagoda, Yixian
rows.summary: A 13-tier octagonal brick pagoda at the south-west corner of Yixian's old town, with seated Buddhas, bodhisattvas, flying figures and guardians carved in brick on every face. The temple that stood beside it disappeared in the 20th century; a carved stone pillar found next to the pagoda in 1980 gave it its present name and a date of 1107, although some scholars think it was begun later in the Liao dynasty and finished under the Jin. After repairs in 2012 it is about 50 m high.

rows.name: Jinzhou Oriental Happy Kingdom Water World
rows.name_zh: 锦州东方欢乐王国水世界
rows.summary: A seaside water park on the Bohai coast next to the Bijia Mountain scenic area, with more than ten water rides, a wave pool, a seawater cascade pool, an infinity pool facing the Bijia causeway and a sand beach. In summer it also stages evening fireworks, music events on the beach and other shows. It is a modern commercial attraction that suits families in summer rather than a sight of historical interest.

rows.name: Jinzhou World Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: The main site of the 2013 Jinzhou World Garden Expo, a landscaped park of about 7 sq km on the Bohai coast, of which 3.3 sq km is land and 3.7 sq km water. The provincial tourism page describes hills, woods, islands, flower beds, buildings and bridges arranged to give a seaside-garden feel. The park stages seasonal events, such as a lantern fair at Chinese New Year in 2025, and the grounds are large enough that a short visit covers only part of them.

rows.name: Liaoshen Campaign Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum and memorial park about the Liaoshen Campaign, the autumn 1948 campaign of the Chinese Civil War in which the People's Liberation Army took Jinzhou, Changchun and Shenyang from Nationalist forces. The main hall, opened in 1988, has an introductory hall and galleries on the course of the fighting, civilian support and the dead, plus a panorama hall depicting the assault on Jinzhou. The grounds also hold a memorial tower and an arcade engraved with the names of PLA soldiers who died in the north-east.

rows.name: Liaoxi Jiuhua Mountain, Linghai
rows.summary: A privately developed theme park of about 3.5 sq km on a wooded hill at the edge of Linghai's town centre, built from 2013 and rated 4A in 2015, which became a social-media hit in 2023 as a 'compressed pack' of China's famous sights. Its attractions include the Buddhist Cihai Temple, a Tibetan-style 'Little Potala' building, terracotta-warrior figures and statues of historical figures, a lotus lake with a music fountain and water-screen show, a night market and amusement rides. It is a modern commercial park rather than a historic site, and suits families and visitors who like photogenic themed scenery.

rows.name: Qingyan Temple, Beizhen
rows.summary: A temple complex in three courtyards, upper, middle and lower, set on steep ground at the southern end of the Yiwulü range in Changxingdian town, within a scenic area of about 13 sq km that the provincial tourism page also describes as a national geopark. The page lists 'eight scenes and twelve wonders' and notes pear blossom in spring, waterfalls in summer, red leaves in autumn and rime ice in winter.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Chongxing Temple
rows.summary: Two octagonal, 13-storey solid brick pagodas stand 43 m apart in the north-east of Beizhen's old town, 44.46 m and 42.63 m high, with Buddha niches, guardian figures and flying figures carved in brick. Their style dates them to the late Liao dynasty, and they were repaired under the Yuan, Ming and Qing, with the east pagoda overhauled again in 1998. A Ming and Qing temple behind them gives them their name, and the provincial heritage page notes that Liao twin pagodas standing together are rare.

rows.name: Wanfotang Grottoes
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple cut into a cliff on the north bank of the Daling River, begun in 499 under the Northern Wei dynasty and among the oldest grottoes in north-east China. Sixteen caves and nearly 500 carvings survive in a west and an east group, including a 3 m cross-legged Maitreya in West Cave 6 and the Yuan Jing inscription, a well-known piece of Northern Wei calligraphy. A Ming-dynasty pagoda stands above the east group, and the site lies between Fu hill and the river.

rows.name: Yanjing Temple Scenic Area
rows.summary: A wooded hill park in Wendilou town north of Jinzhou, set between two peaks of about 436 m and 459 m and protected as a city-level nature reserve. Its sights include the Ancient Buddha Cave, the Twin Dragon Well, the Sansheng Hall and bell and drum towers, in woodland that the provincial tourism page calls primeval.

rows.name: Yiwulü Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain range some 45 km long on the western edge of Beizhen, revered since ancient times as the guardian mountain of the north and, under the Liao dynasty, an imperial hunting ground; its highest peak, Wanghai Peak, is about 870 m. The Beizhen scenic area has forest walks, an old stand of black pine and temples such as the Guanyin Pavilion. Other parts of the range, such as Daluhua and Qingyan Temple, are separate scenic areas with their own entries.

rows.name: Dongjing City Site, Liaoyang
rows.summary: Dongjing was the capital of the Later Jin state under Nurhaci in the early 1620s, built on the east bank of the Taizi River with a diamond-shaped wall and eight gates until the court moved to Shenyang in 1625. The city was then dismantled, so little original fabric survives: the main thing to see is the Tianyou Gate, now with a gate tower and a length of brick-faced wall on its surviving base and a paved square in front, while the Octagonal Hall and the Khan's palace are known only as foundations. It gives context for the Manchu rulers' early years and for the nearby Dongjing Mausoleums.

rows.name: Dongjing Mausoleums
rows.summary: The Dongjing Mausoleums were built on Yanglu hill from 1624 to hold Nurhaci's relatives, moved from Hetu Ala, and three walled compounds survive: those of his brother Shurhaci, with a stele pavilion, of his brother Murhaci and nephew Darcha, with three stone steles, and of his eldest son Cuyen, with a gateway and walls about 4 m high. The earliest ancestors were later moved back to Xinbin and Nurhaci's wives to Shenyang, so this is a small site rather than a grand imperial tomb. It is a short stop for readers of early Manchu history.

rows.name: Ginseng Valley Forest Park
rows.summary: Ginseng Valley (Renshengu) Forest Park is a hill park in Anping Township, in the north of Gongchangling District, Liaoyang, set among rocky peaks and cliff faces. A hiking trail about 2.6 km long, built in 2023 from local stone, rammed earth and timber, links two hills, and official reports list more than 30 named sights along it, among them Eight Hundred Arhats Peak, a plank path along the natural rock wall, a seated Guan Yu stone figure and a platform called Dianjiangtai (the 'general-mustering platform'). The summit area looks out over Gongchangling's urban district, and the park suits a half-day of walking.

rows.name: Guangyou Temple and White Pagoda, Liaoyang
rows.summary: The White Pagoda is an eight-sided brick pagoda with thirteen tiers of eaves, 70.4 m high, which the provincial heritage department calls the tallest ancient pagoda in Liaoning and which is usually dated to the middle or late Liao period. It stands in Baita Park beside the rebuilt Guangyou Temple, which tradition dates to the Eastern Han; the temple was burned down in 1900 and rebuilt in 2002–04 in Liao-influenced style around a large main hall and a gilded camphor-wood seated Buddha. The pagoda and temple were once one complex, and Baita District is named after the pagoda.

rows.name: Liaoyang Lei Feng Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The memorial hall in Gongchangling District covers the months from August 1959 to January 1960 that Lei Feng, a young soldier whose name is used in China's long-running 'learn from Lei Feng' campaigns, spent working here before he joined the army. Its central hall, exhibition hall and theatre show his life through diary entries, photographs and objects and present him as a worker; the provincial tourism page says more than twenty well-known diary entries were written here. It is a separate museum from the Lei Feng memorial in Fushun, and it was named a national patriotic-education demonstration base in 2014.

rows.name: Liaoyang Museum
rows.summary: Liaoyang Museum is a local-history museum in a Chinese-style building that opened in 2009, with two permanent exhibitions: one on ancient Liaoyang and one of highlights from the collection. Most of its 6,000-plus objects come from local excavations, with the emphasis on Han, Liao–Jin and Ming–Qing material, and it has been a national second-grade museum since 2024. It gives an overview of the history of the old Liaoyang area.

rows.name: Longshi Scenic Area, Liaoyang
rows.summary: Longshi Scenic Area, in Hongwei district south-east of central Liaoyang, has two parts: the wooded Longding Mountain and the Shidonggou area. The provincial tourism page gives its forest cover as 90% and highlights a zoo inside the area, a draw for children. It is a local hill-walking and day-out destination rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Taizi River Scenic Belt, Liaoyang
rows.name_zh: 太子河历史文化风光带
rows.summary: This 4A listing covers the Taizi River as it runs through Liaoyang, where the provincial tourism page describes a riverside garden belt about 9 km long between the Yanshui and Xiangping bridges, laid out by the city for residents. It also names sights along the river, including the Yanzhou fortress, Dongjing city and the Dongjing Mausoleums (which have entries of their own), Shenwo Lake and Tanghe Lake. By tradition the river is named after Prince Dan of Yan, who is said to have hidden along it.

rows.name: Tanghe International Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 汤河国际温泉旅游度假区
rows.summary: Tanghe International Hot Spring Resort is a hot-spring resort area at Tanghe town in Gongchangling District, which the provincial tourism department describes as the province's first provincial-level hot-spring resort zone. It combines hot-spring bathing, a winter ice-and-snow programme, mountain scenery and rural tourism, and the page describes the water as weakly alkaline and radon-bearing. It suits a leisure break rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Tong'erbao Fur Shopping Area
rows.name_zh: 佟二堡皮草购物旅游区
rows.summary: Tong'erbao is a fur and leather market town in Dengta, listed as a shopping tourism area. The provincial tourism page says the area sells fur coats, leather clothing and bags at a range of prices, with the Haining Leather City, Hong Kong Times Square and Wangding malls among the larger complexes, and that most visitors are winter shoppers from the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, Inner Mongolia and the three north-eastern provinces. It is a shopping destination rather than a sight.

rows.name: Yanzhou Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: Yanzhou, once called Baiyan City, is a Goguryeo mountain fortress begun in 403 on Shicheng Hill above the Taizi River, which the Tang army took in 645. Walls of dressed blue-grey stone, with nine bastions on the north and west sides and a cliff on the south, enclose a site roughly 480 m by 440 m with a gate site, a reservoir, a well and a stone lookout platform at the highest point. Archaeologists worked here from 2009 to 2017, and the provincial heritage department calls it a representative late Goguryeo fortress in Liaoning.

rows.name: Beilü Tianyuan Great Tang Cultural Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 北旅田园大唐文化旅游区
rows.summary: Beilü Tianyuan, also called Heifengguan Ancient Town, is a leisure complex in Xinli town, Dawa District, themed on Tang-dynasty culture, with a town in Tang style that has market streets, a 'granary' zone and costumed street performances. The tourism department also lists a hot-spring resort, a 'minus five degrees' snow village, Tang-style guesthouses and rice-field viewing areas, and since 2025 the town has also had a Journey to the West theme, licensed from the 1986 CCTV series. It is a modern attraction, not a historic town.

rows.name: Former Kwantung Army Panshan Railway Guard Detachment Site
rows.name_zh: 侵华日本关东军护路守备队盘山分队旧址
rows.pinyin: Qīnhuá Rìběn Guāndōngjūn Hùlù Shǒubèiduì Pánshān Fēnduì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: This red-brick, blockhouse-style building was put up by the Japanese Kwantung Army in April 1932 as the headquarters and barracks of the Panshan detachment of its railway guard corps, in front of the old Panshan railway station. It has a parapet and a lookout on its upper level and round blockhouses at the south-east and north-west corners, and covers 198 m² on a 450 m² plot. It was listed as a Liaoning provincial heritage site in 2008 and as a national one in 2019.

rows.name: Guangsha Art Street, Panjin
rows.summary: Guangsha Art Street is a modern arts and leisure street at the centre of the Liaohe International Art Zone in Panjin's Xinglongtai District. The tourism department describes galleries and painters' studios, creative-product shops, cafes and restaurants, two chain hotels and a library and cultural centre, with more than 100 resident artists from China and abroad.

rows.name: Jinbo Beach, Panjin
rows.summary: Jinbo Beach is a 1.6 km sandy beach on the Liaodong Bay coast in Panjin's Liaobin coastal development zone, promoted as the northernmost beach in China. The tourism department lists it as a 4A area offering food, lodging, entertainment and photo spots as well as bathing, and it lies beside the Liaohe estuary wetlands.

rows.name: Liaohe Stele Forest
rows.summary: Liaohe Stele Forest Park is an oval island of land and water of about 167 ha in the middle of Panjin, laid out from 1985 around a collection of carved stone steles and antique-style halls. About 100 ha of it is land and 67 ha water, and the park faces the Liao River across an embankment. The steles are described as covering calligraphy from every dynasty.

rows.name: Panjin Specialty Products Museum Park
rows.summary: The Panjin Specialty Products Museum Park combines four museums devoted to local products (rice, river crab, barbecue and reed weaving), in buildings that mix Chinese and foreign, old and modern styles. Rice and river crab are the delta's best-known farm products, and the park is a commercial attraction in Panshan County.

rows.name: Tianzhuangtai Site of the First Sino-Japanese War
rows.summary: Tianzhuangtai was a river port on the lower Liao River where, from 7 to 9 March 1895, Qing and Japanese forces fought the last and largest land battle of the First Sino-Japanese War; the Qing side lost, and the Treaty of Shimonoseki followed in April. A memorial site of about one hectare, built in 2002 and known locally as the 'Qing soldiers' graves', commemorates the Qing soldiers killed there, and a memorial hall for the final battle stands on the site. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Weihai Dingxiang Reed Sea Resort, Panjin
rows.name_zh: 盘锦苇海●鼎翔生态旅游度假区
rows.pinyin: Pánjǐn Wěihǎi Dǐngxiáng Shēngtài Lǚyóu Dùjiàqū
rows.summary: This 72 km² wetland resort on the western edge of Panjin, where the Liao and Raoyang rivers meet, has three areas: the Taiping River scenic belt, a 'reed sea and crab flat' reached by boat through the reed beds, and a bird park with an observation gallery. Visitors can watch, angle for and handle crabs on the crab flat, and the tourism department says more than 200 bird species rest and breed there.

rows.name: Zhongyao Colourful Manor
rows.summary: Zhongyao Colourful Manor is an agri-tourism park in Dawa District built around local farm produce, with a shopping street themed on Panjin's history, a modern-agriculture exhibition, an animal ranch park, fishing and herding experiences, a tomato theme park, defence-education and farm study programmes, and a water park. Since 2025 it has also had a '1955 State Farm' section of recreated period shops with costumed performers. It is a commercial leisure development for families and school groups.

rows.name: 9.18 Historical Museum
rows.summary: A museum in north-eastern Shenyang documenting the Mukden Incident of 18 September 1931, when Japanese forces attacked Shenyang, through photographs, objects and audio-visual displays. The present complex, opened on 18 September 1999, grew out of an earlier memorial from 1991 built around the Broken Calendar monument and an underground hall. In the grounds stands a bronze monument put up in 1999 by Japanese orphans left in China after the war, to thank their Chinese foster parents.

rows.name: BMW Brilliance Tiexi Plant
rows.summary: A car factory in Tiexi district, run by BMW Brilliance and opened in 2012, which in February 2017 became the first car plant in China to receive a national 4A tourist rating. Visitors can watch cars being built, with robots working on the production line. It is a working factory, so it mainly suits people interested in car manufacturing.

rows.name: Beidaying Barracks Site
rows.summary: Beidaying ('North Barracks') was a Chinese army camp built in 1907 about 5 km north of the old city of Shenyang, and the first place attacked by the Japanese Kwantung Army on the night of 18 September 1931, the start of the Mukden Incident. Three of its single-storey barracks were identified in 2011, and an exhibition hall built on the site opened in December 2021. It uses photographs, objects, reconstructed scenes and a panoramic sand-table model to set out the events of 1931 and what followed.

rows.name: CPC Manchuria Provincial Committee Site
rows.summary: From 1927 until the Japanese takeover of Shenyang in 1931, this single-storey grey-brick house in the old Beishichang district was the headquarters of the Communist Party's Manchuria Provincial Committee, its organisation for Northeast China. The six-room house is now a memorial hall, with a history exhibition of more than 300 objects and a recreated scene in two of the rooms. Nearby stands a reconstruction of the former residence of Liu Shaoqi, who led the committee in 1929–30.

rows.name: Former Liaoning Main Station (Old North Station)
rows.summary: A station building completed in 1930 and opened in 1931, designed by the architect Yang Tingbao, which served as Shenyang North Station until a new station replaced it in 1988. Its symmetrical façade has a central arched hall flanked by three-storey wings, mixing classical and Chinese features, with a rectangular square in front. The railway still uses it for offices, but it was restored in 2017 with some exhibits upstairs, and a steam locomotive and a carriage have been placed beside it.

rows.name: Fuling Mausoleum (Dongling Park)
rows.summary: The tomb of Nurhaci, founder of the Later Jin state that preceded the Qing dynasty, and his wife Empress Xiaocigao, begun in 1629 on a wooded hillside and added to the UNESCO-listed Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in 2004. Stone animals line the way from the red gate to a flight of 108 steps, a stele pavilion and the walled square city with the sacrificial hall, and the burial mound lies behind it. The grounds have been a public park since 1929 and are ringed by old pine forest, which makes this a good companion to Zhaoling.

rows.name: Hot Go Park
rows.summary: A large resort of about five square kilometres in the Shenyang–Fushun (Shenfu) Reform and Innovation Demonstration Zone, between the two cities. It has five land theme parks, a water park, a shopping area by Dolphin Lake and a castle-themed hotel, with more than 300 rides and attractions, and it mainly suits families.

rows.name: Hoten Camp (Allied POW Camp Site)
rows.name_zh: 沈阳二战盟军战俘营旧址
rows.summary: Between 1942 and 1945 the Japanese army held more than 2,000 Allied prisoners of war at Mukden, now Shenyang, latterly in this purpose-built camp on the east side of the city; they came from the United States, Britain, Australia, the Netherlands, Canada and other countries, and were put to work in a nearby machinery factory. An exhibition hall on the site shows photographs, documents and personal items, including a numbered prisoner tag classed as a first-class national relic and a sculpture titled Friendship.

rows.name: Industrial Museum of China
rows.summary: A museum in Tiexi, Shenyang's old heavy-industry district, built in and around the former casting workshop of the Shenyang Foundry, a hall of 1956 where giant ladles and furnaces still stand. Its halls cover the history of Chinese industry, machine tools, cars and the Tiexi district, with a collection of more than 20,000 items. It suits anyone interested in industrial heritage, and the old foundry was named a national industrial heritage site in 2018.

rows.name: Liaoning Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: The provincial science and technology museum, in the cluster of new cultural buildings in Hunnan district beside the Liaoning Provincial Museum. It has four permanent exhibition halls, a children's science playground and a science cinema with an IMAX giant screen. It is mainly for families and school groups.

rows.name: Marshal Zhang's Mansion
rows.summary: The former residence and offices of the Northeast warlord Zhang Zuolin and his son Zhang Xueliang, begun in 1914 in the old city of Shenyang. The compound has a traditional three-courtyard house, the three-storey Western-style 'Big Green Building' of 1922, a group of red-brick buildings in the west courtyard and the former home of Zhao Yidi. Several buildings are now open as a museum, the Zhang Xueliang Former Residence Exhibition Hall, and visitors walk through connected courtyards with carved beams and painted rafters.

rows.name: Old North Market (Laobeishi)
rows.summary: A pedestrian quarter on the site of the Beishichang market, a trading and street-entertainment district founded in 1921, which was redeveloped in the style of its earlier buildings, with the work completed on 1 October 2020. It now has shops, eateries and evening performances around Huangsi Temple, a Tibetan Buddhist temple built in the 1630s, and it keeps traditions such as Beishi wrestling, a national intangible cultural heritage item. It suits an evening stroll and a meal.

rows.name: Qipanshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill-and-lake recreation area in north-eastern Shenyang, on a spur of the Changbai mountains and named for a boulder on Mount Qipan that is said to be a chessboard on which two of the Eight Immortals once played. The peaks of Qipan, Hui and Dayang stand around Lake Xiu and the Pu River, within the 190-square-kilometre Qipanshan tourism zone, which also holds the Shenyang Botanical Garden and the Forest Zoo, listed separately.

rows.name: Rice Dream Space
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park in the rice-growing countryside of Shenbei district, north of Shenyang, whose main feature is rice-field art: coloured rice varieties are planted to form large pictures that can be viewed from an observation platform. The scenic area covers about 100 hectares and also has farming-science displays and family leisure areas. It mostly suits families and photographers when the rice is growing.

rows.name: Royal Ocean Park
rows.summary: An ocean-themed leisure park of about 60 hectares in the Shenyang–Fushun (Shenfu) Reform and Innovation Demonstration Zone, between the two cities, laid out as six themed worlds. They include a polar-themed aquarium area and an indoor beach water park with a wave pool, and the park mainly suits families with children.

rows.name: SAC Aviation Expo Park
rows.summary: An aviation museum run by the Shenyang Aircraft Corporation (AVIC Shenyang), on Lingbei Street beside the company's factory, which tells the story of the firm and the fighter aircraft it has built. The main hall of about 4,600 square metres has eight exhibition sections with some 1,950 historical photographs and 1,200 objects, and fighters made by the company, including J-5, J-6 and J-8 types, are displayed outdoors on the square. It suits aviation enthusiasts.

rows.name: Sacred Heart of Jesus Cathedral, Shenyang
rows.summary: The Catholic cathedral of Shenyang, a brick Gothic Revival church with two towers about 40 m high and a large rose window above the entrance. The first church here dates from the 1870s; it was burnt down in 1900 during the Boxer Rebellion and rebuilt in 1909–12 to a design by the French priest Henri Lamasse, paid for with Boxer indemnity money. It remains an active church, and a sunken plaza was laid out in front of it in 2000–01.

rows.name: Sannong Expo Park, Xinmin
rows.summary: An agriculture-themed cultural park of about 33 hectares in Daliutun town, north of Xinmin, begun in 1997 and designated a national agri-tourism demonstration site. It has more than thirty exhibition halls on history, folk customs, opera and local figures as well as farming, with ornamental gardens and lakes, and it serves as a study base for Shenyang's school pupils, so it mainly suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Shenyang Aisin-Gioro Royal Museum
rows.name_zh: 沈阳爱新觉罗皇家博物院
rows.summary: A Manchu-themed museum and liquor-making complex of about 80,000 square metres at Banlashan village in Faku county, north of Shenyang, run by the Aisin-Gioro Zujiafang liquor company. It presents the history, customs and traditional liquor-making of the Manchu people, with the original distillery in the northern part, and the operator says the distillery dates back to the Liao dynasty and supplied the Qing court.

rows.name: Shenyang Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A 246-hectare garden in the Qipanshan area on the north-eastern edge of Shenyang, founded in 1959 and the site of the 2006 China Shenyang International Horticultural Exposition, which is why it is also called the Shenyang Expo Garden. Wooded hills hold about 100 display gardens in the styles of Chinese and foreign regions, a rose garden and a science hall, and the 125-metre Lily Tower, shaped like an opening white lily, is the garden's landmark.

rows.name: Shenyang Fantawild Adventure
rows.summary: A theme park in Shenbei New District, on about 50 hectares, run by the Chinese theme-park chain Fantawild and opened in 2011. It is known for science-fiction and interactive attractions, with more than a dozen themed zones and roller coasters among its rides, along with live performances and seasonal events. It mainly suits families with children.

rows.name: Shenyang Forest Zoo
rows.summary: A zoo in the forested Qipanshan hills on the eastern edge of Shenyang, which moved here from the old city-centre zoo and opened in 1999 as the Shenyang Forest Wild Animal Zoo. Its animals include Amur tigers, elephants, rhinoceroses, ring-tailed lemurs and giant pandas, which have lived here since 2017. It is a half-day outing mainly for families.

rows.name: Shenyang Guaipo (Strange Slope)
rows.summary: A scenic area in Shenbei New District best known for the Strange Slope, a short stretch of road about 80 m long where cars left in neutral appear to roll uphill by themselves. The effect was noticed in 1990 and gives walkers the odd sense that going downhill is hard work and going uphill is easy. The wider scenic area also has a tiger park and a glass viewing bridge.

rows.name: Shenyang Korean War Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.name_zh: 沈阳抗美援朝烈士陵园
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery east of Beiling Park, built in 1951 for soldiers of the Chinese People's Volunteers who died in the Korean War. It holds the graves of 123 Volunteers, including named heroes such as Huang Jiguang and Qiu Shaoyun, a wall inscribed with the names of 197,653 Volunteers who died in the war, and a memorial hall displaying photographs and personal objects. Since 2014 the remains of Volunteers returned from South Korea have been reburied here, 981 of them by April 2025.

rows.name: Shenyang Railway Museum
rows.summary: A railway museum on an 80,000-square-metre site in Sujiatun district, with some 800 pieces of railway equipment, including dozens of locomotives, and more than 1,500 historical photographs. Steam locomotives on show include a US-built engine of 1907, a German-built 'forest railway' locomotive of 1914 and a Japanese-built locomotive of 1934, and a green-carriage 'time train' recreates an old platform scene. A railway-themed square outside has sculptures and a small sightseeing train.

rows.name: Shenyang Science Palace
rows.summary: A science education centre in south-eastern Shenyang (Shenhe district) that opened in June 2000. It has a science exhibition hall, a safety-education experience hall and a special-effects cinema, and sends a mobile science bus to schools and villages. It is mainly of interest to families with school-age children.

rows.name: Shenyang Station and Former Mukden Railway Buildings
rows.summary: Shenyang's main railway station still uses the red-brick east building that the South Manchuria Railway opened in 1910 as Mukden Station, with white mouldings and three green metal domes, designed by two pupils of the Japanese architect Tatsuno Kingo. It is part of the national listing for the Chinese Eastern Railway buildings, which also covers the former Fengtian Railway Office of 1911 (now a hotel near the station) and the former South Manchuria Railway headquarters buildings on Taiyuan North Street, now offices that are best seen from the street.

rows.name: Shenyang War Crimes Tribunal Site (1956)
rows.name_zh: 审判日本战犯特别军事法庭旧址
rows.pinyin: Shěnpàn Rìběn Zhànfàn Tèbié Jūnshì Fǎtíng Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A two-storey Chinese-style building with a golden glazed-tile roof, where in 1956 a special military tribunal of the Supreme People's Court tried Japanese war criminals; trials were held at Shenyang and at Taiyuan, with 45 defendants in all. It is now a memorial hall with the courtroom restored to its 1956 appearance, along with exhibits such as the judges' chairs, trial records and defendants' written statements. The hall opened to the public in 2014 and stands on a residential street.

rows.name: Tawan Sarira Pagoda (Wugou Jingguang Pagoda)
rows.summary: A 13-tier octagonal brick pagoda more than 30 m high, built in 1044 in the Liao dynasty and repaired in the 1640s, with a Buddha niche on each face; it was the pagoda in 'Evening Glow at Tawan', one of the old Eight Views of Shenyang. Repairs in 1985 showed the tower to be hollow, with a crypt of well-preserved painted walls and a large hoard of relics. A small museum of finds from Shenyang's pagodas stands to its north.

rows.name: Xibe Ancestral Temple (Taiping Temple)
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist (Gelug) temple founded in 1707 as the family temple of the Xibe people stationed in Mukden, and the place where Xibe soldiers and their families gathered in 1764 before the move west to Ili, which the Xibe still mark as the Westward Migration Festival. The halls standing today are a rebuilding finished in 2004, with a front hall, middle hall, main hall, meditation hall and monks' quarters. It stands among the shops and stages of the Old North Market, close to Huangsi Temple.

rows.name: Xinle Site Museum
rows.summary: A museum on the site of a Neolithic village of the Xinle culture, found in 1973 on a terrace of the old Hun River course in the north of Shenyang and dated to more than 7,000 years ago. The north section has a reconstructed village of half-sunken houses with scenes of daily life, and the south hall displays finds such as stone tools, pottery, jade and carved wood. A bird-shaped wood carving from the site was the model for the Sun Bird sculpture that has become an emblem of Shenyang.

rows.name: Yong'an Stone Bridge
rows.summary: A stone arch bridge 37 m long, built in 1641 in the Chongde reign of Hong Taiji, which spans an old course of the Pu River at Yong'an village on the north-western edge of Shenyang. A stele at the bridge head carries an inscription in Manchu, Chinese and Mongolian recording that the emperor ordered the bridge built in the sixth year of Chongde. It is a small rural monument that suits people following early Qing sites around the city.

rows.name: Zhao Mausoleum (Beiling Park)
rows.summary: The tomb of Hong Taiji, the first Qing emperor, and Empress Xiaoduanwen, built between 1643 and 1651 and part of the UNESCO-listed Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties. A sacred way of about 1.2 km, lined with stone animals, leads to a stele pavilion, a walled square city with the sacrificial hall and, behind it, the burial mound. The tomb stands in the 330-hectare Beiling Park, a public park since the late 1920s with lakes, pine woods and flower gardens.

rows.name: Zhongshan Square Historic Buildings, Shenyang
rows.summary: A round civic square laid out in 1913 in the Japanese-run railway zone of old Mukden, surrounded by bank, hotel and office buildings put up by Japanese architects, mostly in the 1920s and 1930s. The listed group includes the former Yamato Hotel (now the Liaoning Hotel), the former Yokohama Specie Bank branch (now a bank), and the former Chosen Bank, Mitsui, Oriental Development Company and police headquarters buildings, which are mostly in office use and best seen from the square. A large statue of Mao Zedong dating from 1969 stands in the centre of the square.

rows.name: Chengzishan Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: A large stone-walled mountain fortress on Chengzishan in Liangquan town, which the provincial heritage department dates to the early Tang dynasty and describes as a major city of the late Goguryeo kingdom; the national list gives Tang to Liao–Jin. It covers about 167 ha and still has roughly 4.4 km of wall around the mountain section, three gate sites, a water gate, a reservoir, a command platform and a winding path of about 1.7 km. The site is also a provincial forest park and 4A scenic area, with more than 30 peaks, the highest 760 m, old pines and rock formations.

rows.name: Chongshou Temple Pagoda, Kaiyuan
rows.summary: An octagonal, 13-tier solid brick pagoda about 46 m high, standing in the grounds of the Chongshou Chan temple in Kaiyuan's old town, begun in the late Liao dynasty and finished in the early Jin. Each face has an arched niche holding a brick Buddha, with flying figures and canopies carved above, and the pagoda was restored in the early 2010s. The provincial heritage department counts it among the oldest surviving Liao pagodas in the north-east, and it is surrounded by old houses near the line of the old west wall.

rows.name: Lotus Lake Wetland, Tieling
rows.summary: An urban wetland park of about 1,040 ha around Lotus Lake in Tieling's Fanhe New District, made up of constructed wetlands, a lake with a bird island, a lotus-variety garden, a hill and a children's park. The Liao River Museum in the park presents the history, culture and ecology of the river, and the lotus bloom and birdlife are the main draw in summer.

rows.name: Tiemei Steam Locomotive Museum, Diaobingshan
rows.summary: A railway museum and tourist site on the Tiefa coal railway at Xiaoming town in Diaobingshan, where a depot keeps 21 steam locomotives of several types that the provincial tourism page describes as still able to run. An exhibition park traces the development of the steam locomotive with texts, photographs, objects and models. The page says more than 160 films and TV series have been shot here, so it suits railway enthusiasts and photographers.

rows.name: Yingang Academy
rows.summary: A Qing-period academy founded in 1658 by Hao Yu, a scholar exiled to Tieling, which later became a modern school; the compound has a gate, a two-courtyard layout with a lecture hall and a shrine to Hao Yu at the rear. Zhou Enlai studied here for about half a year from 1910 at the age of 12, and since 1979 the compound has housed a memorial museum with displays on the academy's history and on Zhou Enlai's youth.

rows.name: Baishawan Golden Coast
rows.summary: Baishawan is a 14.7 km stretch of sandy Liaodong Bay coast in Guizhou town, Gaizhou, with a coastal road running along it and a reputation as a summer retreat. The provincial page says the scenic area combines the seashore with woodland, island views, orchards and vineyards, and names local relics including a sea-viewing tower and Han-dynasty tombs, as well as the local peaches. It suits summer beach trips rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Chishan Scenic Area, Wanfu
rows.summary: Chishan ('Red Mountain') is a mountain national forest park in Wanfu town, south-east of Gaizhou, lying between Buyun Mountain to the east and the Yushi Reservoir to the north. The provincial page describes it as a well-known Liaodong mountain since the Sui and Tang dynasties and as a resort combining leisure, sport, sightseeing and prayer. The Yingkou government describes it as known for odd peaks, caves, clear springs and old temples, with sights that include Longtan Temple, a glass-floored walkway and the White Dragon Pool.

rows.name: Former Russian Consulate, Yingkou
rows.summary: Built in 1900 after Russian forces occupied Yingkou, this single-storey brick, stone and timber building was first the Russian civil administration office and later a consulate, until consular status ended in 1920. It has a domed pavilion at its north end, an arched west door and cast-iron canopies and railings showing Art Nouveau influence, and is described as the only well-preserved foreign consulate building left in Yingkou. After restoration it reopened in December 2024 as a public reading room, the first in an old building in the city.

rows.name: Former Xiongyue Agricultural Experiment Station and Arboretum
rows.name_zh: 满铁农事试验场熊岳城分场旧址
rows.pinyin: Mǎntiě Nóngshì Shìyànchǎng Xióngyuèchéng Fēnchǎng Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Founded in 1909 as a South Manchuria Railway Company tree nursery beside Xiongyue station, the site became an agricultural experiment station in 1913 and was among the earliest modern agricultural research institutions in northern China. What survives is a group of four early twentieth-century buildings (an office with weather station, a laboratory, a silkworm house and an insect-rearing house) and an arboretum begun in 1915, which the provincial heritage office calls the first modern arboretum on the Chinese mainland. Yingkou's tourism pages present the arboretum as a tree garden with northern and southern sections.

rows.name: Gaolicheng Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: Gaolicheng, also known as Qingshiling Mountain Fortress, is a Goguryeo-period hill fortress with a wall circuit of about 6.5 km on the hills north-east of Gaizhou, identified with Jian'an, a fortress fought over in the Tang–Goguryeo wars of the seventh century. Its walls are of stone in places and rammed earth in others, the rammed-earth sections standing up to 19 m, and they enclose a basin with a small central hill, gate and corner-tower foundations, a large reservoir and terraces bearing the largest Goguryeo-period buildings known in China. Archaeologists from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Liaoning provincial archaeology institute have excavated parts of it since 2015.

rows.name: Hongxigu Hot Spring Resort
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Hongxigu is a hot-spring and leisure resort in Shuangtai town, Gaizhou, close to the Bayuquan district of Yingkou, with a planned area of about 12 sq km. The provincial page lists a hot-spring centre, a holiday hotel, banquet and performance venues, a hot-spring water park, a mountain ski area, a football training base and the Silabao hot-spring town. It is a modern commercial resort for spa and holiday stays rather than a sightseeing site.

rows.name: Jinniushan Site
rows.summary: Jinniushan is a low, isolated hill of about 69 m in Yong'an town, where excavations from the 1970s found Palaeolithic stone tools and fossils of 42 mammal species. In 1984 a Peking University team found more than 50 bones of one adult woman, roughly 260,000 years old and named 'Jinniushan Man'; the Yingkou government calls the cave the earliest Palaeolithic site found in north-east China. An exhibition hall opened on the hill in 1992, and the Dashiqiao Jinniushan Museum, set up in 2005, is in Xitian village, the same village as the hill.

rows.name: Moon Lake Park
rows.summary: Moon Lake Park is a 91-hectare park around a seawater lake where two rivers reach the sea, in the south of the Yingkou Economic and Technological Development Zone at Bayuquan. About 53 ha is land and 38 ha water, and the provincial page says it has an ocean-culture theme with spaces for recreation, dining, fitness and exhibitions. It suits a short stroll or an evening by the water rather than a full excursion.

rows.name: Shipengshan Dolmen
rows.summary: Shipengshan Dolmen is a Bronze Age stone chamber more than 3,000 years old, standing on a low mound in farmland near the village of Dashipeng. About 3.1 m high, it consists of a capstone weighing over 60 tonnes resting on three wall slabs above a paved floor, and the Liaoning heritage office describes it as the largest, best-made and best-preserved dolmen in China and north-east Asia. Excavated dolmens of this kind have proved to be tombs, and an engraved human face survives on the capstone.

rows.name: Tuanshan National Marine Park
rows.summary: Tuanshan is a stretch of Liaodong Bay shoreline on the western seafront of Yingkou's Beihai New Area in Gaizhou, developed as a coastal leisure and holiday area with sightseeing, entertainment and fitness facilities.
