Liaoning's tourism department includes its sea-eroded rock formations on its 2025 summer coastal route. According to the provincial page it was named one of Liaoning's ten best seaside and island destinations in 2015, rated a 4A scenic area in 2017 and listed among China's 'remarkable landforms'.

rows.name: Wang'er Mountain
rows.summary: Wang'er Shan ('Mountain of Watching for the Son') is a small lone hill of about 82 m beside Xiongyue town, topped by a Tibetan-style brick pagoda of the late Ming or early Qing and named for a legend of a mother waiting for her son's return. The provincial page calls it the only sea-eroded red-rock (Danxia) landform in the north-east, and says an annual Mother's Day event, which it describes as China's first organised one, has been held here since 1995, with the 28th in 2023.

rows.name: Xipaotai Fort
rows.summary: Xipaotai ('West Fort') is a coastal artillery fort built in the 1880s at the mouth of the Liao River, made up of three earthen batteries, a moat, a rammed-earth wall and gates; Liaoning's heritage office calls it the largest well-preserved earth-built structure in north-east China. Japanese forces attacked it in March 1895 during the Sino-Japanese War, and Russian troops occupied Yingkou in 1900. A replica of a 210 mm Krupp gun stands on the main battery, and an exhibition hall shows cannon, shot and soldiers' belongings recovered from the site.

rows.name: Xuanzhen Temple, Gaizhou
rows.summary: Xuanzhen Temple, known locally as Shangdi Temple, is a Daoist temple in the old town of Gaizhou, founded in 1382 and dedicated to Xuanwu, the Daoist god of the north; of the original complex only the main hall, the gate and a few ancillary buildings remain. The hall, five bays wide with a single-eaved hip roof, keeps Jin–Yuan-style bracket sets, painted beams and an ink inscription on the ridge purlin dated 1382. It became a national heritage unit in 1988, and the hall was taken down and rebuilt in a restoration completed in 1992.

rows.name: Chagan Haote Tourist Resort
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area in the north-west of Baicheng's Taobei district, close to the Inner Mongolia border, built around Tuanjie Lake (also called Hasar Lake), a reservoir dating from the 1970s. It has a Mongolian-themed camp of yurts with a Genghis Khan statue and a performance stage, a beach and waterfront plaza, and a small ice-and-snow park used in winter, and a snow-sculpture festival was held here in December 2023. The grounds also hold the remains of an airfield built by the Japanese Kwantung Army from 1936, a provincial-level heritage site with the remains of its hangars and some surviving brick buildings.

rows.name: Momoge Wetland
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Momoge National Nature Reserve in Zhenlai County, where the Nen and Tao'er rivers meet on the Songnen Plain: a 1,440 sq km mosaic of river channels, reed marsh, sedge meadow and saline-alkali flats whose seablite meadows turn red in autumn. It has been a Ramsar wetland of international importance since 2013 and is a major stopover for the Siberian crane; in 2025 the first arrived on 12 March and the last left on 11 May, and more than 1,900 had been counted by late October. Red-crowned cranes and Oriental storks also breed in the reserve, which has been a 4A tourist area since 2005.

rows.name: Nenjiang Bay, Da'an
rows.summary: A riverside park of about 3.5 sq km on a bend of the Nen River, on the north-eastern edge of Da'an, laid out around a lake and reed wetland with bridges, a quay and walking paths. Local government pages record the Liao-dynasty emperors holding their spring camps (chunabo) on this stretch of the river, fishing through the ice, and the sights include the Laokanzi wharf, the Liao Emperor's Fish-Viewing Platform and the Huayi Tongfeng courtyard. It is a national wetland park and forest park, was named a 5A scenic area in December 2024, and ran a winter snow programme in the 2024–25 season.

rows.name: Xianghai Wetland
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Xianghai National Nature Reserve in Tongyu County, a wetland of reed marsh, lakes, sand dunes and old elm woodland on the Horqin grassland, added to the Ramsar list of wetlands of international importance in 1992. It is known as a home of the red-crowned crane, and local government pages record six crane species; the sights include a bird garden, Crane Island and the Lanhai Pavilion viewing tower over the elm forest. The provincial tourism bureau promotes it as a self-drive destination, with homestays near the reserve.

rows.name: Changbai Mountain Huamei Resort
rows.summary: A holiday resort of about 25 km² in the forest of Manjiang town, Fusong county, run as Luneng Shengdi before it took the Huamei Shengdi name. It has hotels, a ski area of about 32 ha on gentle slopes, a camping and RV site with an evening bonfire square, a glass net bridge, go-karts, a deer-feeding park and a children's castle. It suits families and groups who want a forest base on the west side of Changbai Mountain rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Chen Yun Former Residence Memorial, Linjiang
rows.summary: A single-storey building in the Linjiang Forestry Bureau compound beside the Yalu, where the Communist leader Chen Yun lived and worked from November 1946 to June 1947 and which was also the headquarters of the Northeast Democratic Allied Army in the Civil War campaign known as the Four Defences of Linjiang. Two exhibition rooms hold photographs, documents and some of Chen Yun's work and daily items, covering his time in Linjiang and the course of the campaign. The State Council listed it in 2006 as the Site of the Headquarters of the Four Defences of Linjiang Campaign.

rows.name: Four Defences of Linjiang Campaign Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall at the foot of Maoer Hill in Linjiang, built in 2005 by enlarging a 1992 martyrs' hall inside the cemetery that was laid out in 1947 for those killed in the Four Defences of Linjiang campaign of the Civil War. Eight exhibition halls with more than 1,000 objects cover the planning before the campaign, how it was fought and the civilian support for the army. The same grounds hold a memorial monument and 438 graves.

rows.name: Lingguang Pagoda
rows.summary: A five-storey hollow brick pagoda about 13 m tall, square in plan and facing south, which survives from the Bohai kingdom (698–926) that ruled this region. It stands in Tashan Park, a hill park above Changbai town with several viewing areas and a martyrs' cemetery, and from the top the Yalu and the North Korean side are in view. The State Council listed it as a national heritage unit in 1988.

rows.name: Lushuihe National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the Lushuihe, a 63 km tributary of the Second Songhua River that runs between wooded hills and cliffs in Fusong county. State media report that the river stays above freezing through the winter, so rafting trips in the cold months pass trees coated in rime. People's Daily describes the surrounding Lushuihe forest area as holding what is left of China's Korean pine mother-tree forest, about 12,000 hectares.

rows.name: Neyin Ancient City
rows.summary: A fortress-style attraction in forest at the head of the Toudao Songhua River, presented as a Jurchen tribal fortress; it is a modern reconstruction that the Chinan district authorities began building in 2014, not an excavated site. Inside it stands the Lingying Palace, a Daoist temple completed in 2016 and dedicated to the Changbai Mountain deity. It is a short stop for visitors already in the Manjiang area.

rows.name: Qiannian Yacheng (Thousand-Year Cliff City)
rows.summary: A themed attraction on the Yalu bank in Changbai town, built in the style of Bohai-period architecture, with a market area and a village section in the style of the local ethnic Korean (Chaoxian) community. It has a glass corridor bridge and a cliffside walkway with views of the river and the North Korean bank, and costumed staff stage short period dramas. It suits a short stop alongside the Lingguang Pagoda.

rows.name: Shiren Xueleishan Miners' Memorial
rows.name_zh: 石人血泪山死难矿工纪念地
rows.summary: Shiren Xueleishan, the 'Hill of Blood and Tears', is a memorial on a low hill beside the former Shiren coal-mining area in Dashiren town. Mine workers who died under the harsh conditions of the Japanese occupation of north-east China (from 1938) were buried on this hillside, and a memorial hall opened in 1964 shows archive material and recreated scenes in six galleries. The grounds also hold a monument and seven sites on the hill linked to the deaths, including mass graves.

rows.name: Songhua River Ecological Tourism Area, Jingyu
rows.name_zh: 松花江生态旅游风景区
rows.summary: A scenic area on the upper Songhua River in Huayuankou township, Jingyu county, built around sightseeing boat trips on the river; a 500-passenger new-energy cruise boat, the Tianhe 1, was launched at its Songjiang pier in September 2024. Xinhua reported nearly 700,000 visitors in the first two years after boat services began. It suits visitors who want a river and forest outing on the western side of Changbai Mountain.

rows.name: Wangtian'e Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley in the Changbai Mountain foothills of Changbai county, known as Shiwudaogou, with old trees, waterfalls, springs and rock walls and pillars beside the stream. Xinhua's photo feature on the valley highlights the winter ice-falls, where the stream freezes into half-ice, half-flowing curtains on the rock. It suits walkers and winter photographers who are happy to travel into the hills.

rows.name: Beihu National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A large urban wetland park on the northern edge of Changchun, with lakes, reed beds and boardwalks and more than 200 bird species recorded. The grounds also hold Wanshou Temple and the Youguo Pagoda, and lotus flowers are a summer feature.

rows.name: Changchun Agricultural Expo Park
rows.summary: A leisure park in the Jingyue district south-east of Changchun, built around exhibition halls and greenhouses first used for agricultural expositions. It stages the Jilin (Changchun) Winter Agricultural Expo, whose 16th edition ran there in February 2026, and has indoor greenhouse gardens, a World Agricultural Scenery Garden and, in winter, ice sculptures and a light-and-projection show. It suits families after an indoor garden visit rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Changchun Confucius Cultural Park
rows.summary: A cultural park built around the Changchun Confucian Temple, founded in 1872, rebuilt from 2002 and enlarged in 2012, the year the park opened. The three-courtyard compound has a Dacheng Hall, bell and drum towers, a pool and archways, and today it also runs as the Changchun Confucian Temple Museum, with exhibitions, traditional ceremonies and lectures.

rows.name: Changchun Daotai Yamen (Local Chronicles Museum)
rows.summary: A regional government compound built in 1909 in the last years of the Qing dynasty and the earliest surviving official building in Changchun, with colonnaded halls in a Western-influenced style. Puyi took his oath as chief executive of Manchukuo in its main hall on 9 March 1932. It reopened in December 2018 as the Changchun Local Chronicles Museum, with an exhibition on the city's history in the main hall and a recreation of Puyi's office and living room in a side hall; it was previously the city's urban-construction exhibition hall.

rows.name: Changchun Film Studio Former Site Museum
rows.summary: The old Changchun Film Studio complex, whose first buildings date from the 1930s Manchukuo Film Association; from 1945 it was the studio that state media call the cradle of new China's cinema. It is now a museum in the restored studio buildings, showing film props, scripts and reconstructed sets, the Third Studio, one of the earliest special-effects stages still standing, and a film-processing workshop kept as an exhibit. Costumed performers stage short film-themed scenes in the buildings.

rows.name: Changchun Movie Wonderland
rows.summary: A film-themed amusement park run by the Changchun Film Studio group, established in 2005 in the Jingyue district on the south-eastern edge of the city. Its grounds of about 33 hectares are laid out in four sections, with special-effects cinemas including dome and 4D theatres, film-dubbing and sound-effects experiences and film-themed live performances. It suits families and groups looking for a theme-park day, and the city tourism bureau lists it among the attractions that add ice-and-snow programmes in winter.

rows.name: Changchun World Sculpture Park
rows.summary: A landscaped sculpture park on the southern side of Changchun, laid out around lakes and opened in 2003, with works by sculptors from many countries set among the grounds. Several museum buildings stand inside, including a sculpture museum and a collection of Makonde wood carvings from East Africa. It makes an easy half-day outdoors, and in recent winters the park has also put on an ice-and-snow event.

rows.name: Changchun Zoological and Botanical Park
rows.summary: A municipal zoo and botanical park in the south of central Changchun, built in 1938 and opened to the public in 1987, with animal exhibition areas, a bird house and a planted hill with trees from the Changbai Mountain area. It now features a Journey to the West-themed area, where performers in costume stage shows on themed stages, and lantern displays are added in winter.

rows.name: China FAW Museum
rows.summary: A museum of China's car industry inside the original First Automobile Works plant in west Changchun, where the first Jiefang truck came off the line in 1956. It opened to the public in July 2026 in a red-brick toolshop built from 1953, one of the early factory buildings on the national heritage list, and shows about 150 vehicles, including Jiefang and Hongqi models, with more than a thousand historical items and recreated scenes from the plant's early years.

rows.name: Dehui Museum and Chinese Eastern Railway Buildings
rows.name_zh: 德惠中东铁路建筑群（德惠市博物馆）
rows.pinyin: Déhuì Zhōngdōng Tiělù Jiànzhùqún (Déhuì Shì Bówùguǎn)
rows.summary: Russia built the Chinese Eastern Railway through Dehui in the 1890s and early 1900s, and several buildings from the 1903 station area still stand around today's Dehui railway station. The easiest place to see them is Dehui Museum, which opened in December 2022 in the former Russian émigré school, known locally as the White Building; downstairs is an exhibition on Dehui's history and upstairs one on the railway and its buildings. The national listing also takes in the 1903 station buildings, the Songhua River railway bridge, an Orthodox church in Dehui and a former Russian railway club in Changchun's Kuancheng district.

rows.name: Former Central Bank of Manchukuo
rows.name_zh: 伪满洲国中央银行旧址
rows.summary: The Manchukuo-era headquarters of the Central Bank of Manchukuo on People's Square, built between 1934 and 1938 with ten Greek-style columns across the front, three basement levels and four storeys above ground. Still used by the People's Bank of China and commercial banks, it opened to visitors in September 2025 with a special exhibition on the building's history in the banking hall of a working branch. Marble floors, a revolving door and a glass canopy can be seen inside.

rows.name: Guandong Culture Park, Changchun
rows.summary: A garden-style hot-spring resort on the north-western edge of Changchun, built from 2010 on the site of abandoned brick kilns, with lakes, planted gardens and buildings in the Guandong (north-east Chinese) style. It has hot-spring pools and themed lodging in courtyard-style buildings, and folk events such as traditional wedding re-enactments have been held in the grounds.

rows.name: Guoxin Nanshan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring hotel and spa resort set in wooded hills in Shuangyang district, south-east of Changchun. The city tourism bureau describes a bicarbonate-sodium spring coming out at around 60°C, with more than 70 pools, indoor halls, a children's hall, a traditional-medicine hall and villa lodgings across the site. It also operates a ski area in winter.

rows.name: Jilin Liquor Culture Museum
rows.summary: A privately run museum in the south of Changchun devoted to alcohol, showing about 6,000 bottled drinks from the 1960s to the present. They range from local Jilin brands such as Yushuqian, Taonanxiang and Taoerhe to national names such as Moutai and Wuliangye, so it suits a short stop.

rows.name: Jilin Natural History Museum
rows.summary: A natural-history museum run by Northeast Normal University on its Jingyue campus, holding tens of thousands of specimens, mostly from Jilin's own environments. Its permanent displays include rare animals, fossils, minerals, insects and a butterfly hall.

rows.name: Jingyuetan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A large forest park around the Jingyuetan reservoir on the south-eastern edge of Changchun, begun in the 1930s as a man-made forest and now one of the city's main outdoor spaces. Visitors come for lakeside and forest walks; in winter the park hosts skiing and a snow-sculpture area, and the Vasaloppet China cross-country ski festival has been held here every year since 2003.

rows.name: Kaisa Forest Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort with a hotel, set in woodland beside Jingyuetan forest park on the south-eastern edge of Changchun. Its pools have included lemon, lavender and herbal baths, and it has also been promoted with a water park and a children's forest play area.

rows.name: Lianhuashan Ski Resort Town
rows.name_zh: 莲花山冰雪旅游度假小镇
rows.summary: A ski resort in the hills east of Changchun, with day and evening skiing in winter; the city tourism bureau groups it with Miaoxiangshan as better suited to skiers beyond the beginner stage. The area also has a summer amusement park, Baturu Park, which closed for the 2026 season on 8 October and is expected to reopen in spring 2027.

rows.name: Liao Pagoda, Nong'an
rows.summary: A 13-storey octagonal brick pagoda of the Liao dynasty, about 44 m high, standing in the middle of Nong'an town. It began as Longan Pagoda beside the Huanglongfu temple and was used to hold the remains of monks; it was repaired in 1953 and again from 1985, when its original form was restored, and bronze and silver Buddhist objects found inside in 1953 are now in the Jilin Provincial Museum. Nong'an occupies the site of Huanglongfu, a Liao and Jin regional centre, and the pagoda is the town's main landmark from that period.

rows.name: Liao-Jin Era Culture Park, Nong'an
rows.summary: A 300-hectare rural leisure park in Qiangang township, Nong'an county, themed on the Liao and Jin dynasties that once ruled this area. It combines Liao-Jin folk-culture tourism, farm and orchard experiences with fruit picking, youth study tours and national-defence education, and the city tourism bureau lists it as a national study-tour base. It is a modern attraction rather than a historic site, and suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Lotus Island Film and TV City
rows.summary: A film-and-television leisure park on the southern outskirts of Changchun, with period-style street and building sets that visitors use for costume photography; the city tourism bureau suggests Republic-era-style shoots. It also holds seasonal events, among them an Ice and Snow Lantern Festival that ran from December 2025 to March 2026.

rows.name: Miaoxiangshan Resort
rows.summary: A ski resort in the hills of Jiutai district, east of Changchun, one of the ski areas the city tourism bureau promotes. The bureau describes its slopes as better suited to skiers who have moved past the beginner stage, with day and evening sessions in the winter season.

rows.name: Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo
rows.summary: The former residence of Puyi, the last Qing emperor, during his years as head of the Japanese-backed state of Manchukuo (1932–1945), now run as a museum. The main buildings are the Qinmin Building, where state ceremonies were held, the Jixi Building with the private rooms of Puyi and his family, and Tongde Hall, built in 1937–38 as a temporary palace that Puyi never moved into; a separate hall covers the occupation of north-east China. The national heritage unit also covers ten other former Manchukuo ministry and Kwantung Army buildings around the city, five of them on Xinmin Street, which are not part of the museum.

rows.name: Qingquanhu Resort
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure resort in Kuancheng district, part of the Changchun New Area, centred on a lake of about half a square kilometre. It offers boat rides, a hot-air balloon, a sand-beach play area, fishing, camping, a fruit-picking garden, a small animal area with camels, ostriches, raccoons and yaks, and a children's play area. Accommodation includes farmhouse-style courtyards, wooden cabins and converted railway carriages.

rows.name: Shenlufeng Resort, Shuangyang
rows.summary: A mountain resort in Shuangyang district built around the area's sika-deer tradition, with rides and attractions that include a glass skywalk, a high-level swing, a zip line, a cave and a children's play area. On the hillside there is a deer enclosure where visitors can feed the animals and have their photograph taken with them. Shuangyang calls itself the hometown of sika deer, with deer farming going back more than 300 years.

rows.name: Tiandingshan Resort Town
rows.summary: A ski resort and holiday town in the hills east of Changchun, with runs aimed mainly at beginners. Guesthouses and small restaurants serving north-eastern dishes stand beside the slopes, and in winter the Changchun Ice and Snow New World park, with ice sculptures and long slides, operates a street away.

rows.name: Tianyi Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in wooded hills near Xinlicheng Reservoir, south of Changchun. The provincial tourism department describes spring water coming out at 58°C, with an indoor bathing hall and four outdoor areas, including a forest zone, an island and a winter bathing area, and farmhouse-style single-storey rooms for overnight stays.

rows.name: Yulong Hot Spring Resort, Shuangyang
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Shuangyang district, south-east of Changchun, with about 50 pools set in planted subtropical-style gardens, plus a hotel with villas, restaurants and sports facilities. The pools include herbal, flower-scented and play pools, and the restaurants serve dishes made with deer products, reflecting Shuangyang's long tradition of sika-deer farming.

rows.name: Ashihada Cliff Inscriptions
rows.summary: Two inscribed rock faces on a riverside cliff above the Songhua River, carved in 1421 and 1432 to record visits by Liu Qing, the Ming commander sent to build ships here for expeditions down the Songhua and Amur rivers. The Jilin city government describes them as the only Ming rock inscriptions found in the province. Each is sheltered by a small pavilion, and the Jilin Ming and Qing Shipyard Site Museum beside them explains the shipyard that stood here.

rows.name: Beidahu Ski Resort
rows.summary: A downhill ski resort on Beidahu mountain in Yongji county, built in 1993 and extended since, with dozens of runs on a mountain whose main peak, Nanlou, rises to about 1,405 m and gives a vertical drop of about 870 m. It staged skiing events at the 2007 Asian Winter Games, and its 2025–26 season opened in late October 2025. It also promotes summer and cable-car sightseeing, and suits skiers and active families.

rows.name: Beishan Park
rows.summary: A hillside city park in the west of Jilin, laid out in 1924 around a group of Qing-period temples, among them the Guandi Temple of 1701, the Yaowang (Medicine King) Temple of 1738 and the Jade Emperor Pavilion of 1776, with a granite arch bridge of 1935 spanning the valley between the two peaks. Its temple fairs were added to China's national intangible heritage list in 2011, and the rear hill has a martyrs' cemetery and a four-season cross-country ski centre. It is a popular place for local walks and views over the city.

rows.name: Dongtuanshan Site
rows.summary: Dongtuanshan is an archaeological site on the east bank of the Songhua River in Jilin city, linked to the Buyeo (Fuyu) kingdom that ruled the area from the Western Han period. It has a small fortified hill, about 50 m high with three surviving wall lines, and beside it an oval lowland town whose wall ran for about 1,050 m; finds range from the Bronze Age to the Ming and Qing dynasties. An exhibition hall opened on the site in October 2024, with photographs, finds and a sand-table model, and the village below now has a pottery gallery and a café.

rows.name: Family Cemetery of Wanyan Xiyin
rows.summary: A Jin-dynasty family cemetery in a wooded valley south-east of Shulan, the burial place of Wanyan Xiyin, a founding minister of the Jurchen Jin state credited with devising the Jurchen script, and of his relatives. Five burial areas hold seven groups of stone figures, tigers, sheep and pillars in front of the tombs, with tombstones that name the family members buried there. It is run as a site park, and the provincial tourism office suggests about three hours.

rows.name: Forest Slow Valley Resort
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area of about 1,000 ha in forested hills near Huadian, opened in phases from June 2023 around a reservoir, with cycling round the lake, water barbecues, fishing and camping. In winter it offers snow-play areas and ice fishing. It is a new resort aimed at short family breaks rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Former Jihai Railway Terminus (Jilin West Station)
rows.summary: A Gothic-style station building of 1928–29 with a stone-walled hall and a clock tower about 29 m high, built as the terminus of the Jihai Railway, which People's Daily's Jilin channel calls the first railway in the north-east built by Chinese themselves. The old station, now called Jilin West Station, still handles freight only and has had no passenger trains since 2011. After restoration the building opened to the public on 1 September 2024, with an exhibition on the railway, a recreated station waiting hall and booking office, and a café.

rows.name: Former Jilin Machine Bureau
rows.summary: The surviving north gate and three arms-store buildings, built in 1928, of an arsenal set up in 1881–82 under the Qing self-strengthening programme, the only large arms works in the north-east at the time. The old works on the north bank of the Songhua now house the Jilin Art Centre and, since 1 May 2024, the 1881 Jilin Machine Manufacturing Bureau exhibition hall, a stop on the city's heritage routes. A café and a library were added in 2025.

rows.name: Former Jilin University Teaching Buildings (Stone Buildings)
rows.summary: Three granite teaching buildings completed in 1931 for Jilin Provincial University, designed by Liang Sicheng with colleagues from Northeastern University as his first work after returning from the United States, with Chinese-style ridged roofs and ridge-end ornaments on solid stone walls. They are still in use as part of Northeast Electric Power University, and an exhibition on their history opened on the second floor of the east building around the start of 2024. The Jilin tourism bureau promotes the group mainly as a photo stop.

rows.name: Hongshi National Forest Park
rows.summary: A large forest park of about 28,600 ha across Huadian and Jingyu county, set up in 2005 and opened in 2007 around a former logging area that is now protected natural forest. The Jilin tourism bureau lists forest walks, a red-leaf garden, a birch-covered ridge, rafting on the Bailu River and a camp associated with the Communist-led guerrillas under Yang Jingyu. It suits visitors who want woodland and autumn colour away from the city.

rows.name: Hongshilazi Anti-Japanese Base
rows.name_zh: 红石砬子抗日根据地遗址
rows.summary: The site of what Chinese accounts call the first anti-Japanese base area set up by the Communist Party in the north-east, in forested hills near Panshi, where the local party committee and Yang Jingyu's South Manchuria guerrilla force ran a hospital, a printing shop and other facilities in 1932–33. Archaeological surveys since 2021 have recorded more than 3,300 remains, including semi-underground dwellings and log houses, and the site now has restored remains, a viewing circuit, protective sheds and interpretation signs. The Panshi Anti-Japanese Struggle Memorial Hall in the city, in a building completed in 2022, displays objects and the history of the base.

rows.name: Jilin City Museum
rows.summary: The city's main museum, with permanent exhibitions on the history of Jilin city, the 1976 meteorite shower and local intangible heritage, art galleries, and a collection of more than 25,000 objects. Its best-known exhibit is the 1,770 kg 'Jilin 1' stone from the 1976 shower, usually cited as the largest single stony meteorite ever recovered. It was rated a national first-class museum in 2024.

rows.name: Jilin Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty Confucian temple in the old centre of Jilin, first built in 1736 and moved to its present site in the early 1900s, one of the earliest the Qing built in the north-east. Its halls follow the usual axial plan from a screen wall and the Lingxing Gate through to the Dacheng Hall, which is eleven bays wide, and the complex now houses the Jilin Confucian Temple Museum. It is a popular place for photographs, including in traditional dress.

rows.name: Jilin Labour Memorial Hall (Fengman Mass Grave Site)
rows.summary: A memorial hall at Fengman, beside the hydroelectric complex on the Songhua River, built over three long trenches in which labourers who died while the Fengman dam was being built in 1937–43 were buried, when the region was under Japanese control. An exhibition room was set up on the site in 1963, opened to the public in 1964 and named the Jilin Labour Memorial Hall in 1997, with a memorial stele in front. The exhibitions record the labourers who built the dam.

rows.name: Lafa Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park around Lafa Mountain, a rocky peak of 886 m that rises from a flat plain north of Jiaohe, known for its nine-peaked outline and its many natural caves. The largest, the Eight-Treasure Cloud-Light Cave, is about 60 m long and has three openings facing east, west and south, and visitors climb by footpath to the summit. Sunrise and sea-of-cloud viewing has become popular since a viewing programme was introduced in 2023, and the park opened for winter visits for the first time in December 2024.

rows.name: Laoheigou Massacre Site
rows.summary: A memorial site in the hills of Shulan commemorating the Laoheigou killings of 29 May to 6 June 1935, when Japanese troops attacked villages in the area and Chinese sources record about a thousand civilians killed. A memorial stele erected in 1995 stands at the site with two smaller steles carved with a diagram and a summary of the events, and a memorial hall opened in 1997 in the township. The site was added to the national list of anti-war memorial sites in 2015.

rows.name: Longtan Mountain Fortress
rows.summary: A hill fortress attributed to the Goguryeo or Buyeo peoples on Longtan Mountain, now a public park on the north-eastern edge of Jilin, whose rammed-earth wall runs for about 2.4 km along the ridge and was reused by later states into the Ming period. Visitors can see the stone-lined Longtan reservoir at the north-west corner, a circular pit called the Dry Prison that was probably a granary or store, and the Nantianmen summit with views over the city. The park also holds Longfeng Temple, a temple group first built in 1754.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Jilin
rows.summary: A Gothic Revival Catholic church on the north bank of the Songhua River beside Jilin Bridge, completed in 1926 after French priests of the Paris Foreign Missions Society began building in 1917, with a cruciform brick-and-stone plan and a 45 m bell tower. It was the seat of the Jilin diocese until 1994, was occupied and damaged after 1966, and has been used for services again since repairs in the 1980s. State media noted in 2024 that sunlight through its stained glass draws photographers.

rows.name: Shengdequan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring and leisure complex in farmland west of Jilin, in Soudengzhan town, offering hot-spring bathing, a garden of fossil tree trunks and dishes made with its own vegetables. It is a commercial resort suited to a half-day outing from the city.

rows.name: Shengxin Winery Estate
rows.summary: A wine-themed leisure estate in the hills south-east of Jilin, built around the story of the Chuang Guandong settlers who moved to the north-east, with Huizhou-style buildings, a red-wine hot spring and campfire evenings. The estate's own wines can be tasted on site, and some of the old-style buildings are used as guesthouses. It is a commercial attraction best suited to a short outing, often combined with Zhuque Mountain.

rows.name: Shennong Manor
rows.summary: An agri-tourism estate in rice-growing farmland north-west of Jilin, built around a hot-spring bathhouse and with farming-culture displays, gardens and a rice-field art viewing area. It suits families and travellers who want a rural day out with a soak.

rows.name: Songhua Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir of about 550 km², the largest lake in Jilin province, created by the Fengman dam on the Second Songhua River, begun in 1937, and a national-level scenic area since 1988. The scenic area near the dam offers boat and speedboat trips, walking and cycling in the surrounding forest, and the Wuhu Island leisure area with an amusement park and a water park. Freshwater fish from the lake is the local speciality.

rows.name: Songhua Lake Resort
rows.summary: A ski and mountain resort on Daqingshan, south-west of the Fengman dam on Songhua Lake. It was developed and run as the Vanke Songhua Lake Resort until China Travel Service (Hong Kong) bought its owner and operator in 2025, and it now trades as Zhonglü Songhua Lake Resort. It is a national-level ski tourism destination, and its summer season, which opens in late April, offers sunrise and cloud-sea viewing, mountain flower fields and mountain biking.

rows.name: Wulajie Qing Mansions (Wula Three Mansions)
rows.summary: Three Qing-period official mansions, Houfu, Safu and Kuifu, in the Manchu town of Wulajie on the Songhua River, where the Qing office that gathered tribute goods for the imperial court was based; the listing also includes a mosque in the town. After restoration in 2024 the three mansions opened as museums with period-style displays, and the Jilin tourism bureau lists Manchu-culture exhibits, an archery demonstration and period-dress photography. Houfu belonged to one of the tribute office's chiefs and Kuifu to Wang Kuifu, a late-Qing official.

rows.name: Xituanshan Site
rows.summary: A low granite hill on the western edge of Jilin where Bronze Age stone-slab cist graves were excavated in 1948–50, giving its name to the Xituanshan culture of the Songhua valley. The site reopened in October 2024 after restoration, with an exhibition hall on Xituanshan culture showing stone tools, pottery, bronze knives and replicas, while the graves themselves are no longer on view.

rows.name: Zhuoyuan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort set in farmland at Yilaxi town in Yongji county, west of Jilin, offering herbal hot-spring baths, private spring guesthouses and farmhouse meals, according to Yongji county tourism material of 2025. It is a commercial leisure stop for a relaxed half day.

rows.name: Zhuque Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain park on the south-eastern edge of Jilin, one of the four hills that local tradition places around the city, with Zhuque, the Vermilion Bird, standing for the south. Visitors come mainly to hike and for the autumn colours, and the park has staged evening light-show tours in the autumn holiday season. The Ashihada cliff inscriptions and the Shengxin winery estate are close by.

rows.name: Liaoyuan Miners' Mass Grave
rows.summary: A burial ground and site museum for coal miners who died at the Xi'an (now Liaoyuan) mines during Japan's occupation of north-east China in 1931–45. Many thousands of miners were buried on this hillside from about 1940 and a furnace for burning the dead was added in 1943; the pits were excavated in 1963, and halls built over parts of the burial ground now show the remains laid out in rows, alongside mining equipment. A monument stands in the wooded grounds, and the site is both a national heritage unit and a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Liaoyuan WWII Allied POW Camp Site
rows.name_zh: 辽源二战盟军战俘营旧址
rows.summary: A former Japanese Army prisoner-of-war camp, the second branch of the Mukden camp, where 34 Allied prisoners were held between December 1944 and August 1945: five lieutenant-generals, four major-generals, seven colonial governors and 18 orderlies, American, British and Dutch among them. They included US General Jonathan Wainwright and British General Arthur Percival, who were both present at the Japanese surrender ceremony on the USS Missouri on 2 September 1945. The site is now an exhibition centre with more than 400 objects, the foundations of barracks and the remains of a guard tower, and it reopened after a refit in 2026.

rows.name: Tianyu Tourist Resort
rows.summary: A countryside leisure resort in Dongliao County, built in recent years as a German-themed village, with a castle-style building, a landscaped stream, flower beds, lawns, windmill-style villas and a fruit-picking garden. People's Daily Online describes it as a mixed leisure complex with dining and lodging, outdoor activities, family events and wedding services. It is a modern attraction rather than a historic one, and suits families and couples looking for a day out from Liaoyuan.

rows.name: Yuedong Liaoyuan Happy Carnival
rows.summary: A family amusement complex in Liaoyuan's Xi'an district, described by the provincial tourism bureau as an immersive children's leisure park of about 30,000 sq m with a fairy-tale theme that mixes technology and outdoor play. It is a modern commercial park rather than a historic or natural site, and suits parents with young children.

rows.name: Siping Campaign Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum in Hero Square in central Siping about the four battles fought for the city between March 1946 and March 1948, when Communist-led and Nationalist forces fought over this railway junction during the Chinese Civil War. Founded in 1958, it covers the course of the fighting, the support given from the rear areas and the people killed, through photographs, documents and objects. It suits visitors interested in the history of the civil war in north-east China.

rows.name: Yehe Nara City
rows.summary: A Manchu-style walled complex rebuilt in 1994–95 on a hill beside Zhuanshan Lake, in the homeland of the Yehe tribe, from whose Nara clan Empress Dowager Cixi's family descended. Inside are an old-style post station, a council hall, a princess's tower and exhibition halls on Yehe history, Cixi, Nurhaci and the Manchu poet Nalan Xingde, as well as a Manchu costume hall. It is a reconstruction, not the original town: the two original Yehe cities, destroyed by Nurhaci in 1619, survive only as earth walls elsewhere in the valley, mostly in farmland.

rows.name: Yimashu Forest Park
rows.summary: A provincial forest park on the sandy edge of the Horqin grassland near Shuangliao, planted largely with pines that foresters first trialled on the sands some forty years ago. Local pages list a forest-bathing area, a small zoo and botanical garden, a play zone with zip lines and sand motorbikes, and farmhouse restaurants and picking gardens. It is described as the back garden of Shuangliao's residents, so it suits a short local visit rather than a long trip.

rows.name: Yitong Manchu Museum
rows.summary: A county museum of Manchu history and folk culture in Yitong Manchu Autonomous County, recognised as the Yitong branch of the China Ethnic Museum. Its galleries cover the origins of the Manchus, production, daily life, culture, ritual and belief, and Yitong past and present, using photographs, models and audiovisual displays alongside a collection of about 5,000 items. It is a compact museum, best as a short stop for anyone interested in Manchu customs.

rows.name: Chagan Lake
rows.summary: Chagan Lake is a shallow freshwater lake of several hundred square kilometres in the north-west of Qian Gorlos Mongol Autonomous County, the largest natural lake in Jilin province and described by state media as one of China's ten largest freshwater lakes. Its headline is the winter fishing: from mid- or late December to about February, fishers cut holes through ice 70 cm to 1 m thick, draw a net more than a kilometre long beneath it and haul it out with horses turning a capstan, a method on China's national intangible heritage list since 2008. A fishing and hunting culture museum stands by the lake, and in the warmer months the area is promoted for spring outings, summer lotus and autumn birdwatching.

rows.name: Great Jin Deshengtuo Stele
rows.summary: A bluestone stele 3.2 m tall, put up in 1185 by the Jin emperor Shizong to mark Deshengtuo, where his grandfather Wanyan Aguda swore in his troops before marching on the Liao city of Ningjiangzhou. The front carries a six-character seal-script title and Chinese text and the back Jurchen script, and it is described as the best-preserved Jurchen-language stele in north-east China. It stands under a stele pavilion in open countryside near Desheng town.

rows.name: Prince Zhong Stele (Kuli Stele)
rows.pinyin: Qīng Zhuīfēng Héshuò Zhōng Qīnwáng Bēi
rows.summary: A Manchu and Mongolian stone stele recording the posthumous titles given to Jaisang, a Khorchin Mongol noble, and his wife Boli, the parents of Empress Xiaozhuangwen and maternal grandparents of the Shunzhi emperor. The stele was broken during the Cultural Revolution and repaired in 1983, and it is now shown in the exhibition hall of the Xiaozhuang ancestral tomb site in Changshan town. The State Council listed it as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: Songyuan Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: The Songyuan Planning Exhibition Hall is a municipal exhibition in Ningjiang district on the city's development and urban planning. Its displays include interactive holographic projections, relief murals with historical themes and figure scenes of local customs. It is a modern civic exhibition rather than a historic site, and the district promotes it as a family stop alongside nearby villages.

rows.name: Baijifeng Forest Park, Tonghua
rows.summary: A national forest park in the mountains south-east of Tonghua, centred on Baijifeng ('White Chicken Peak', 1,318 m), the highest peak in the city's surroundings. Its named rock features include the pale outcrops known as the 'chicken waists', and the paths pass the sites of several small temples dating from the late Ming and early Qing. It is also marketed as a forest-health resort.

rows.name: China Mountain Wine Museum, Tonghua County
rows.summary: A wine park in Kuaidamao, the seat of Tonghua County, run by the Tongtian wine company and centred on the China Mountain Wine Museum, which covers wines made from wild mountain grapes, a speciality of the Tonghua area. A passage from the exhibition halls leads down to an underground cellar. It suits visitors interested in how Tonghua's mountain-grape wines are made.

rows.name: City Living Room Riverside Park, Meihekou
rows.summary: A landscaped riverside promenade along the Huifa River through central Meihekou, laid out as an urban wetland park with plazas, flights of steps down to the water and landscape bridges. A lotus-growing demonstration area comes into flower from the end of June and draws visitors and photographers from nearby towns. It is a place for an easy walk by the river rather than a destination in itself.

rows.name: Daquanyuan Distillery and Baoquanyong Brewery
rows.name_zh: 大泉源酒业宝泉涌酒坊
rows.summary: A working liquor distillery in Daquanyuan township whose Qing-dynasty Baoquanyong brewery is a national heritage unit. The visit takes in the old brewery's surviving features (a well, a steaming stove, fermentation pits and a group of large storage vessels known as 'liquor seas'), a company history museum, a stele garden and a traditional brewing workshop beside the modern production hall. It suits visitors interested in how Chinese grain liquor was made.

rows.name: Donggou Tombs and Gwanggaeto Stele, Ji'an
rows.summary: The largest group of Goguryeo tombs, spread along the valley of the Tonggou River around Ji'an and part of the town's UNESCO-listed Goguryeo sites and its 5A scenic area. Its two best-known monuments are the 6.39 m Gwanggaeto Stele, erected in 414 and carved with Chinese characters, and the General's Tomb, a stepped granite pyramid that is the best preserved of Ji'an's royal tombs. More than ten thousand tombs were counted in the valley in the 1960s, mostly earth mounds and stone cairns, and some have wall paintings.

rows.name: Guonei City, Ji'an
rows.summary: The lowland capital of the Goguryeo kingdom for about four centuries until 427, now in the middle of Ji'an town and part of the UNESCO-listed Goguryeo sites and of Ji'an's 5A scenic area. A stretch of the stone west wall can be walked, with remains of corner towers, and the Goguryeo Ruins Park inside the old walls shows two excavated palace foundations. The Ji'an Museum, which is devoted to Goguryeo finds, and the town's morning market are close by.

rows.name: Hailong Lake Park, Meihekou
rows.summary: A man-made lake park on the south-eastern edge of Meihekou, opened to the public in 2018 and covering about 109 ha, of which roughly 47 ha is water. Paths run past lakeside plazas, a wetland with stepped weirs, three islands, a sand beach and a children's playground, and there is a shopping street of new buildings in Huizhou (Anhui) style. It suits families and locals out for a stroll, and camping areas are provided.

rows.name: Jiguanshan Forest Park, Meihekou
rows.summary: A mountain forest park of about 15 km² in the Changbai Mountains foothills in the south-west of Meihekou, named for a peak shaped like a rooster's comb. The main peak, Jiguanlazi, is 969 m high and the highest point in Meihekou, and the park is known locally for azaleas in spring, autumn colour, seas of cloud and winter rime. It has an artificial lake, a suspension bridge, forest chalets and hiking paths, and holds a mountain-climbing festival each May.

rows.name: Longwan Crater Lakes, Huinan
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A group of volcanic crater lakes (maar lakes) in the Longgang mountains of Huinan County, protected as a national forest park and nature reserve. The best-known stops are Sanjiaolong, a triangular lake formed by an eruption about 200,000 years ago, and Dalongwan, the largest lake in the park, with boat trips on the lakes and the Diaoshuihu waterfall nearby. Forest paths run around the lakes.

rows.name: Luotong Mountain Fortress, Liuhe
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the north-east of Liuhe County, built around Luotong Mountain Fortress, a large stone-walled hill fort of the Goguryeo period that was reused under the Jin dynasty and is a national heritage unit. A route through the fortress passes the west gate site, a barracks site, a drill ground with a commander's platform, an old well and a reservoir, while the surrounding area has karst caves, old elm trees and a Taoist temple, the Sanqing Palace. A red-history exhibition hall stands at the south gate.

rows.name: Northeast Bureau Meihekou Conference Site
rows.name_zh: 中共中央东北局梅河口会议会址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Zhōngyāng Dōngběijú Méihékǒu Huìyì Huìzhǐ
rows.summary: A two-storey red-brick building put up in 1936 as a railway staff dormitory, where the Northeast Bureau of the Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee held a series of meetings in March and April 1946. The meetings reviewed the military situation in north-east China and set out the plan to take Changchun first and Siping afterwards. The building is still used by the railway as offices; a small upper-floor room, under 30 square metres, is laid out as an exhibition room.

rows.name: Qidaogou Victims' Memorial, Tonghua County
rows.name_zh: 七道沟死难同胞纪念地
rows.summary: A memorial site at the former Qidaogou iron mine in Tonghua County, where miners who died while the mine was worked under Japanese control between 1938 and 1945 were buried. A stone monument 7 m high was put up on the burial ground in 1964, and the site also includes remains of the military barracks, the mine workings and a labourers' house. It is on Jilin's red-tourism list and on China's national heritage list.

rows.name: Qingyun Cliff Inscription, Meihekou
rows.summary: A Jin-dynasty inscription cut into a rock face near Qingyun village in Xiaoyang township, described in Meihekou's tourism handbook as one of only a few surviving texts in Jurchen script. No visitor facilities are listed for it, so it mainly suits those with a specific interest in the Jurchen and Jin period.

rows.name: Tonghua Winery Underground Cellar
rows.name_zh: 通化葡萄酒厂地下贮酒窖
rows.summary: The underground storage cellar of the Tonghua Winery, a works founded in 1937 that has made wine from the wild mountain grapes Tonghua is known for. About 4.5 m below ground, the cellar covers more than 10,000 square metres and holds 772 large oak barrels, and the national heritage list dates it to 1937–1983. Visitors walk through its passages among the barrels.

rows.name: Tongjia River Resort, Tonghua
rows.summary: A riverside leisure park on the south side of Tonghua, laid out as an urban park around a performance island with a theatre that seats 3,000. It has a children's play area, a boat pier, a 2.7 km forest boardwalk with three viewing platforms, a camping area and a small sightseeing train, and it is lit up in the evening. It suits families on a relaxed half-day out rather than visitors looking for a major sight.

rows.name: Wandu Mountain City, Ji'an
rows.summary: A Goguryeo mountain fortress above Ji'an, built as a military refuge for the lowland capital and used as a capital itself for a time; it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site and of Ji'an's 5A scenic area. A visitor path climbs through the stone walls, which run for almost 7 km with seven gate sites, to a lookout platform, palace foundations and the remains of a lotus pond. The walls look down on hundreds of Goguryeo tombs of different types at the foot of the mountain.

rows.name: Wunüfeng National Forest Park, Ji'an
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain forest park north of Ji'an, named for a line of steep peaks said to resemble five women in green veils. It covers about 69 km² with 26 larger peaks, 17 of them above 1,000 m, and is known locally for its rock formations, forest and deep valleys. It is one of the ten 'sights of Tonghua' named on a Jilin provincial government website.

rows.name: Yalu River Border Gate, Ji'an
rows.summary: A scenic area on the Yalu River at Ji'an, built around the border gate of the road crossing and the 1939 railway bridge, with the North Korean town of Manpo on the opposite bank. Visitors can see the gate, the bridge and the river from the Chinese side, and the railway bridge was one of the routes used by Chinese troops entering Korea in 1950. The provincial tourism bureau describes it as the only border-gate scenic area in China with both a rail and a road crossing.

rows.name: Yang Jingyu Martyrs' Cemetery, Tonghua
rows.summary: A memorial park on a hillside beside the Hun River in Tonghua, laid out in the 1950s around the grave of Yang Jingyu, a commander of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, who is shown in a bronze statue at the centre of the grounds. The Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army Memorial Hall beside the cemetery uses photographs, objects, paintings and reconstructed scenes to tell the story of the guerrilla forces that fought the Japanese occupation in the north-east. It is on Jilin's red-tourism list and is designated a national patriotic-education demonstration base.

rows.name: Zhenguo No. 1 Manor
rows.summary: A large estate on the shore of Yingebu Reservoir in the hills west of Tonghua, covering about 13 km² of forest, water and farmland and run by the Zhenguo pharmaceutical company. It combines holiday accommodation and dining with a forest-ginseng growing base, boat trips to the ginseng plots, a traditional-medicine clinic and bonfire evenings.

rows.name: Zhibei Village, Meihekou
rows.summary: A leisure village built in 2021–22 on the southern edge of Meihekou in the style of a 1970s north-eastern Chinese village, with 91 buildings holding shops, a tea house, restaurants, a guesthouse, a folk museum and an intangible-heritage hall. It is a new development rather than a historic village, and is mainly somewhere to eat, shop and take photographs, with a flower-field park next door. The first phase opened on 31 December 2021.

rows.name: Zi'an Mountain Fortress, Tonghua
rows.summary: The ruins of a large hilltop fortress on a flat-topped hill where the Hani River meets the Hun River, on Tonghua's north-eastern edge. Parts of the low stone wall survive along with gate sites, wells and a reservoir, and two earth bases outside the main gate are thought to be the footings of a Han-style gate tower. It was used from the Han period into the Goguryeo era, and conservation and display works have been carried out on the site since 2012.

rows.name: Ancient Tombs at Longtou Mountain
rows.summary: A cemetery of the Bohai kingdom on the east side of Longtou Mountain in Toudao town, where more than ten tombs in three burial zones have been found since 1980. The first to be found, the tomb of Princess Zhenxiao, has the best-preserved Bohai wall paintings known, and a copy of its murals and stele is shown in the Yanbian Museum in Yanji. Helong presents the tombs and the Xigucheng city site together as the Bohai Zhongjing national archaeological site park, with a tomb museum among its stops, but no opening of the museum had been reported by October 2026, so check whether it is open before going.

rows.name: Baihuagu Korean Folk Village
rows.name_zh: 长白山百花谷朝鲜族古村落
rows.summary: Baihuagu is a village of traditional-style ethnic Korean (Chaoxian) houses built in the late 2010s on the road to Changbai Mountain, in Songjiang town, Antu county. It has a folk museum on ethnic Korean migration to China and everyday life, an exhibition hall on intangible cultural heritage, a hall where visitors can try making kimchi and pounding rice cake, a costume hall and guesthouses. Folk song-and-dance performances are staged for visitors.

rows.name: Baliancheng, Bohai Eastern Capital Site
rows.summary: Baliancheng is the site of Dongjing Longyuanfu, the 'Eastern Capital' of the Bohai kingdom, founded around 785 and abandoned about 928. It had a roughly square outer wall about 2.9 km round with a moat, and a rectangular inner city of about 1 km circumference; excavations in 2004–2009 uncovered two large buildings on the central axis and the south gates. It is described as a national archaeological site park, but little of the interior can be seen beyond those foundations, and the surroundings are farmland.

rows.name: Bohai Zhongjing Site (Xigucheng)
rows.summary: Xigucheng is the site of Zhongjing, the 'Middle Capital' of the Bohai kingdom (698–926), a city built around 742 in what is now Helong. The walled city measured about 630 m by 730 m, with a smaller inner city holding palace foundations, and excavations in 2000–2002 confirmed that the ruins are Zhongjing. It forms part of the Bohai Zhongjing national archaeological site park together with the Longtoushan tombs 6 km away.

rows.name: Changbai Mountain Canyon Floating Stone Forest
rows.summary: A canyon about 5 km long and up to 40 m deep, cut into volcanic ground near the north side of Changbai Mountain, where weathering has left some 30 formations of pumice, a porous volcanic rock light enough to float. A boardwalk and path follow the canyon floor past underground streams and springs to the Bingshui (ice-water) spring, a 3.2 km walk of about an hour and a half, and an eight-storey tower looks out over the forest and the mountain's peaks. The canyon is also visited in winter, when it is covered in snow and walked on foot.

rows.name: Changbai Mountain History and Culture Park
rows.summary: A themed cultural park beside the road to Changbai Mountain in Sihe village, Songjiang town, laid out as 'four gardens and one zone' and presenting Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist themes. It has a Buddhist temple (Tai'an Temple), a Nine-Dragon Wall, a bronze gate on Chan and Daoist themes, an ecological garden with a wooden boardwalk and flower fields, and a hotel whose roof terrace faces Changbai Mountain. It is a modern park rather than a historic temple site.

rows.name: Changbai Mountain Temple Site (Baomacheng)
rows.summary: The Changbai Mountain Temple site, long known locally as Baomacheng, is the remains of a Jin-dynasty (1115–1234) imperial temple on a raised terrace in the forest north-west of Erdaobaihe, where the court made sacrifices to Changbai Mountain. Excavated from 2014, it was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2017 as the first state mountain-worship site found outside the Central Plains, and it has been on the national list of archaeological site parks in preparation since December 2022. A site museum was due to open at the end of September 2026, but building work was still under way on 30 September.

rows.name: Daguandong Culture Park
rows.summary: Daguandong Culture Park is a forest park in Dongqing village, Antu county, founded in 2013 and themed on Manchu customs and the 'Guandong' frontier culture of north-east China. Its walking route of under 5 km passes a Manchu courtyard house, displays of traditional kang beds, crafts and shamanic culture, a deer park and a forest boardwalk, and it includes a memorial hall for the Dasha River ambush, an action by the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army. Most visitors come with tour groups on Changbai Mountain itineraries.

rows.name: Daxitaihe Scenic Area
rows.summary: Daxitaihe is a forest and river-valley scenic area run from the Huangsongpu forestry station of the Changbai Mountain forestry group, on the way to the north gate of Changbai Mountain. It was rated 4A in 2014 and has been managed with the Changbai Mountain tourism company since 2018. Antu county's tourism pages list a night-time forest light show among its 2025 night-tour routes and winter activities such as skiing, all-terrain vehicles and horse-drawn sleighs in 2024, and forestry families in Huangsongpu run guesthouses for visitors.

rows.name: Erdaobaihe
rows.summary: Erdaobaihe is the gateway town on the north side of Changbai Mountain and an important base for visitors going up from this side; its centre was approved as a 4A scenic area in January 2019. The town has a network of riverside walking and cycling paths, parks and plazas, and a sculpture park among stands of the tall local pines known as 'beauty pines', with hotels, restaurants and shops serving the mountain.

rows.name: Fangchuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Fangchuan is a small village on the lower Tumen River at the eastern tip of Hunchun, close to where the borders of China, Russia and North Korea meet. From the viewing tower, the Longhu Pavilion, visitors can see the river, the Russia–North Korea railway bridge, the Russian settlement of Khasan and, across the river to the south-west, the North Korean city of Rason. The scenic area also holds the Tuzi marker, a granite boundary stone set up in 1886 and now a nationally protected monument, as well as a folk-culture area of the village's ethnic Korean community and a lotus lake.

rows.name: Former Yanji Border Affairs Bureau
rows.name_zh: 延吉边务督办公署旧址
rows.summary: A Qing government office building of the frontier affairs commission that was set up in Yanji in 1907 and headed by the commissioner Wu Luzhen; it is nicknamed the 'garrison tower' and the 'daoyin building'. After conservation work it reopened to visitors with an exhibition on Wu Luzhen's work on the frontier, which opened on 18 June 2025.

rows.name: Hancongling Scenic Area
rows.summary: Hancongling is a forested ridge in Dunhua's forestry district where units of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army under commanders including Yang Jingyu, Wei Zhengmin, Wang Detai and Chen Hanzhang fought and lived during the Anti-Japanese War. Xinhua describes the camp remains as among the best preserved and most militarily distinctive of the army's camps in Northeast China, and the state forest farm there runs a red-education base with study groups. The 4A listing calls it a red-tourism and sightseeing area, and Chinese state media also note its autumn leaves and a forest road popular with cyclists.

rows.name: Haoji Cultural Tourism Resort
rows.summary: Haoji Cultural Tourism Resort is a 720,000 m² complex of antique-style buildings in Wangqing County, built around the Haoji soy sauce factory. Visitors can see traditional soy sauce brewing in wooden fermentation barrels, a method listed as provincial intangible cultural heritage, and a soy sauce culture exhibition hall; the complex also has a performance hall, restaurants and a study-trip programme, and period-costume photography studios operate in the grounds.

rows.name: Hongshifeng Scenic Area
rows.summary: Hongshifeng is a forested area at the Hongshi forestry station east of Erdaobaihe, with old forest and unusual rock outcrops. Since 2020 the Changbai Mountain tourism company has run it as an outdoor-activity area. Its activities include a clifftop café, rafting and a railway-track crossing challenge in summer, cliff-top walks and an off-piste snow park in winter, and autumn colour in October.

rows.name: Laobaishan Primeval Forest Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest tourism area developed by a state forestry company on former logging land in the Huangnihe district of Dunhua. Reports from 2021 and 2022 describe summer flower fields and walks, a winter 'snow village' with snow tubing and snowmobiles, and displays on the region's loggers' (mubang) culture, with guesthouses and restaurants run by forestry families.

rows.name: Liangtian Baishi Holiday Park
rows.summary: Liangtian Baishi is a leisure and holiday park on the bank of the Hailan River in Dongshengyong town, Longjing, planned as the main tourism area of the Yanji–Longjing–Tumen new district and receiving visitors since 2022. It offers camping lawns and rented tents, a flower-field train, a smart farm growing vegetables without soil, a riverside restaurant and a hotel opened in 2024. It suits families and groups looking for a day out or a night under canvas rather than historic sights.

rows.name: Liudingshan Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: Liudingshan is a large cultural tourism area on the southern edge of Dunhua, laid out around a lake. Its centrepiece is the Zhengjue Buddhist temple, whose halls climb the hillside in 20 terraces to a culture and art museum at the top with views over the town, and there is also a park on the Qing founding ancestors with a museum and a shrine hall. The grounds hold the Liudingshan tombs, a Bohai-period (698–926) cemetery of more than 80 stone-chamber and earth-mound tombs that has been a national heritage unit since 1961.

rows.name: Mengdumei Folk Resort and Ski Area
rows.name_zh: 梦都美民俗旅游度假村
rows.summary: Mengdumei is a holiday resort in Chunxing village, Yilan town, on the north side of Yanji, whose main draw is its ski area. Alpine ski competitions were held there in the 2024–25 season, and the slopes were open day and night over the 2026 Spring Festival.

rows.name: Mojie Scenic Area
rows.summary: Mojie ('Demon Realm') is a forest and wetland scenic area of about 88 ha near Erdaobaihe, on the north slope of Changbai Mountain. It is laid out with a wetland reserve, a wildlife-viewing area, streams and small waterfalls, forest walks, a photography zone and a rafting area. The name comes from the mist over the river and the fallen trees standing in the water, which photographers prize in winter when hoar frost coats the branches.

rows.name: Piyanshan Cultural Tourism Scenic Area
rows.summary: Piyanshan is a hill beside Longjing from which visitors look over the Hailan River valley and the prefecture's largest apple-pear orchard, which flowers in spring. The scenic area lies next to the orchard and to the Piyanshan hot-spring village, and the Jilin tourism department suggests mid-April to mid-May for the blossom.

rows.name: Piyanshan Hot Spring Village
rows.summary: Piyanshan Hot Spring Village is a hot-spring resort built in traditional Korean style, with white walls, dark roof tiles, timber galleries and stone-paved lanes, next to Piyan Mountain near Longjing. The resort says its water is drawn from about 2,500 m underground at around 51 °C and feeds 66 indoor and outdoor pools, and it also has a hotel, a restaurant serving Korean dishes and live shows in the afternoons. It is marketed as China's first hot-spring folk village.

rows.name: Qinglong Fishery Park
rows.summary: Qinglong Fishery Park is a spring-fed cold-water fish farm turned leisure resort at Qinglong village, Toudao town, in Helong. Salmon-family fish, including the large taimen, swim in viewing pools of about 17,000 sq m filled with underground spring water at a constant 8 °C. The resort also has a camping area, a glass suspension bridge, a water park and a lure-fishing base, and serves spring-fish meals.

rows.name: Xueshan Feihu (Snow Mountain Lake)
rows.summary: Xueshan Feihu, also called Snow Mountain Lake, is a reservoir on the upper Second Songhua River in Liangjiang town, surrounded by forest and cliffs, with many small peninsulas and rock formations the county names Banana Rock and Sun Rock. The county tourism pages say the lake was a filming location for the television drama Flying Fox of Snow Mountain, and the remains of an ancient Bohai-kingdom hillfort are among its best-known sights. It suits a quiet half day by the water in a forested setting.

rows.name: Yaguang Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A reservoir and wetland park in the hills of Dashitou town, Dunhua, about 6.2 km from north to south and 5.5 km from east to west and covering 2,291 ha of forest, lake, hills, wetland and grassland. A boardwalk about 10 km long runs through the wetland, and a 135 ha meadow is covered in irises in June. The park held its formal opening on 23 June 2025 and has viewing pavilions and a camping area; the lake is also visited for sunrise and sunset.

rows.name: Yanbian Museum
rows.summary: Yanbian Museum is the main museum of Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture, a national second-class museum with about 15,000 items, in a new building opened in 2012 on a site of more than 20,000 m² on Changbai West Road. Its core displays cover finds from the prefecture, the folk customs of the ethnic Korean (Chaoxian) community and the history of the community's revolutionary struggle, and they include a copy of the mural and stele from the Bohai Princess Zhenxiao's tomb. The folk-customs exhibition received an excellence award in a national top-ten museum exhibitions selection in 2013.

rows.name: Yanji Maoershan Dinosaur Culture Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 延吉帽儿山恐龙文化旅游区
rows.summary: This tourist area of about 1.8 km² on the southern side of Yanji combines dinosaur-themed attractions, the woodland of Maoershan hill and a folk and commercial quarter. The Yanji Dinosaur Museum shows fossils and science displays in two zones, and the Dinosaur Kingdom beside it is a theme park with rides, a water park and holiday shows. The China Korean Folk Park has about 40 Korean-style buildings recreating household scenes, where visitors can try on traditional dress.

rows.name: Yuncuigu Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 云翠谷温泉旅游度假村
rows.summary: A hot-spring holiday resort in the hills east of Siping, run by a leisure company, with hot-spring pools and forest walks. It is the Yuncuigu forest-wellness base, one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Xianrenqiao Forest Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Xianrenqiao town in Fusong county, run by the Jilin Forest Industry group; it grew out of a forestry-system hot-spring hospital founded in 1969. Visitors bathe in the spring pools and use the resort's forest-wellness facilities. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Changbai Mountain Valley, Linjiang
rows.summary: A forest park and holiday area near Huashan town in Linjiang, known for a hilltop meadow where cattle and sheep graze and for autumn foliage in its maple-lined valley. It was named among the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020.

rows.name: Baiquan Valley Forest Area
rows.summary: A forest tourism area at the Cuifeng forest farm of the Jiagedaqi forestry bureau, on the southern slopes of the Yilehuli Mountains. The bureau has developed it as a forest-health base with a self-drive campsite, forest 'star-room' cabins, a radon-spring bath, hot-spring log huts and a boardwalk trail, and offers riding, camping, fishing and forest-bathing activities. The prefecture's own description also mentions ancient rock paintings, a picking garden and old-growth forest.

rows.name: Beiji Village
rows.summary: A village on the south bank of the Heilongjiang River in the far north of the province, with a scenic area of about 16 sq km rated 5A in 2015. Visitors come for the 'Divine Land's North Pole' stone beside the river, the northernmost post office and sentry post, a sandbar park and the river view; the city promotes it for long midsummer days, aurora watching and deep winter cold. The settlement began in 1860 as Mohe village and was a station on the gold road to the Mohe mines in the 1880s.

rows.name: Huma Museum
rows.summary: The county museum of Huma, on the Heilongjiang River, which opened in April 2016. Its stone tools, rock paintings, potsherds and iron and copper cauldrons tell the history of the area; it joined the 4A list in October 2025.

rows.name: Jiagedaqi Cold-Temperate Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A botanical garden of forest and lakeside planting just south of Jiagedaqi, with Mongolian pine and white birch around a stream and a lake. The district's media describe it as a 4A attraction with spring flowers and autumn fruit.

rows.name: Longjiang First Bend
rows.summary: A sharp bend of the Heilongjiang River in the Tuqiang forestry bureau's area, where the river turns back on itself below the Hongqiling hills and is seen from viewpoints at the top of a hill reached by stairs. There are two ways up: a newer, gentler path and an older, steeper one that gives a fuller view of the bend.

rows.name: Luding Mountain, Huma
rows.summary: A steep hill beside Huma town on the Heilongjiang River, named after Jin Yong's novel 'The Deer and the Cauldron'. Faulting and volcanic activity have left fault scarps and sheer rock faces, and the summit looks over the meanders of the Huma River, the plain and the town; a winter martial-arts culture week is held here.

rows.name: Twenty-Second Post Station and Old Post Road
rows.summary: A scenic area at the 22nd station of the old Mo'ergen-Mohe post road, which the Qing court opened in 1685 to carry military dispatches and reopened in 1888 as the 'gold road' to the Mohe mines. The site has post-station statues, log-cabin station houses, stables, a 'northernmost post office', an educated-youth culture park, a rafting stop and a car-camping ground, and the site of the old station is among the stops nearby. The road's national listing covers its stations in Huma, Tahe and Mohe counties and in Nenjiang.

rows.name: Amuta Mongolian Folk Island
rows.summary: A Mongolian-themed tourist area on the Amuta peninsula, a long spit running into one of the lakes of the Lianhuan Lake system in Dorbod Mongol Autonomous County. Its centre is a shrine to Hasar, a brother of Genghis Khan, which holds a flame brought to the site in his memory; yurts, an obo cairn group and horse-riding and archery grounds make up the rest, with Mongol and fish dishes on offer. It was built by the Daqing media group and rated 4A in 2015.

rows.name: Beiguo Hot Spring Resort, Lindian
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort on the south-western edge of Lindian town, themed on cold-region hot-spring culture, with, by the county's count, 83 pools in indoor, water-play, forest and herbal-bath zones, a 'Guandong'-style old street and a hotel. Its water comes from the Lindian geothermal field, which the county promotes as one of the largest medium- and low-temperature geothermal fields in China.

rows.name: Daqing Inaugural Oil Well (Songji-3 Well)
rows.summary: The well that found the Daqing oilfield: it first flowed commercial oil on 26 September 1959 and was shut down in 1988 when its casing was found to be broken beyond repair. On the plot, still run by the oilfield company, stand a memorial stone of 1989, the well's preserved wellhead 'Christmas tree' and a long relief wall titled 'Daqing Starts from Here'.

rows.name: Daqing Museum
rows.summary: Daqing's city museum, which grew out of an exhibition hall founded in 1964 and has stood in its present building in the Daqing High-tech Zone since 2008. It is best known for Quaternary-period fossils from north-east China, among them mammoth and woolly rhinoceros, shown in permanent exhibitions on the Quaternary environment and mammals of north-east China and on early human cultures around Daqing. It was ranked a national first-grade museum in 2017.

rows.name: Daqing Oil Pavilion
rows.summary: A museum on Century Avenue at Dongfeng Road in Saertu, Daqing's central district, housed in the former Petroleum Pavilion of Expo 2010 Shanghai, which was moved to Daqing and opened there in September 2012. Its exhibitions cover the development of the Daqing oilfield and the growth of the city around it. Heilongjiang's provincial tourism department recommends it as the place in Daqing to learn about the past and present of oil and the culture and spirit the industry gave the city.

rows.name: Daqing Racing Town
rows.summary: A motorsport complex on the northern edge of Saertu district, with a 3.16 km circuit built to the FIA grade-3 standard and opened in 2024 (a grandstand for 3,000), plus an off-road course, drift area, drag strip, go-karting and motorcycle stunt track. It also has a used-car market, a large graffiti-art zone and a camping ground, and holds races and festivals through the year.

rows.name: Feilong Four Seasons Hot Spring, Lindian
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at the southern edge of Lindian, recognisable by its Russian-style domed buildings beside the expressway toll gate. Its indoor halls hold more than 20 pools, including spa, swimming and fish-therapy pools, and there are 22 open-air pools; a military-culture museum opened in the grounds in 2017.

rows.name: Heminghu Wetland Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the edge of Heming Lake wetland in Lindian County, with indoor and outdoor pools. The grounds include bamboo-raft and boat rides and bird-watching on the reed marsh, a wetland museum and, in winter, an ice-and-snow park with an ice-lake zoo and sliding runs.

rows.name: Iron Man Wang Jinxi Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum on the life of Wang Jinxi, the oil driller nicknamed 'Iron Man' who led a drilling team to Daqing in 1960, in a building whose plan and profile spell out the characters for 'worker'. The galleries on the second and third floors hold more than 200 photographs and 300 objects with scene reconstructions, and the grounds have a 6.5 m granite statue of him and a Soviet-built drilling rig of the type his team used. The present building opened in September 2006 and the museum is a national first-grade museum.

rows.name: Iron Man's First Well (Well Sa-55)
rows.summary: Well Sa-55, the first well drilled by the team of Wang Jinxi, nicknamed 'Iron Man', after it reached Daqing in March 1960; the crew began drilling in April and finished the hole in five days and four hours. The well kept producing until 2017, and the site keeps the unloading pit, mud pit, oil pit, watchman's hut and dugout of the crew's first weeks, with a Soviet-type Bu-40 rig of the same model as theirs beside it. The oilfield company runs it as an education base.

rows.name: Lianhuan Lake Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the shore of Lianhuan Lake, a large shallow lake system in Dorbod Mongol Autonomous County, open since 2010. It has indoor and outdoor pools in landscaped grounds, herbal baths and a Mongolian-medicine bath, with ice-and-snow activities in winter; the county tourism office says the water comes from about 1,800 m underground at around 48 °C.

rows.name: Yili Dairy Plant, Dorbod
rows.name_zh: 杜尔伯特伊利乳业工业园
rows.summary: A visitor route through a plant of the Yili dairy group in the Delige'er development zone beside Dorbod's county seat, on a site of about 20 hectares. The indoor route covers company exhibits, a product hall and an explanation of milk-powder production, with windows over the workshop floor, and the outdoor route passes the milk-reception square and the warehouse. It is a 4A industrial-tourism site and was the first stop on the county's 2024 rural-tourism route listed by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism.

rows.name: Acheng Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque in central Acheng, west of Qingzhen Square, whose compound dates from the late Qing dynasty. The complex is laid out in a raised 'convex' plan with a prayer hall and ancillary buildings, about 2,800 square metres of floor space in all, and its architecture blends Islamic features with Chinese building traditions. It became a provincial heritage site in 1986 and a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Baiyupao Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park of about 3.3 square kilometres in Juyuan town, Daowai District, mostly reed marsh and open water north-east of Harbin. It is home to more than 80 kinds of waterbirds and land birds and about 20 wild fish species, and visitors tour the reeds in sculling boats, fish, or visit an education hall on wetland ecology. A lotus pond of about 2,000 square metres flowers from late July for roughly a month.

rows.name: Dadingzi Mountain Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A modern hot-spring resort beside the Songhua River in Hulan district, built around a large indoor spa hall with an 800 sq m pool and many types of hot-spring bath. Water is drawn from a mineral spring about 1,620 m underground, and the outdoor baths look out over the river and the hill that gives the resort its name.

rows.name: Dragon Tower
rows.summary: A 336 m steel lattice tower for television and radio, opened in 2000, which is among the tallest lattice towers in the world. It has observation levels and a revolving restaurant, and its base has held science and wax-figure exhibits, according to a 2017 China Daily profile. It is also the Heilongjiang provincial radio and television tower.

rows.name: Erlongshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lake-and-hill scenic area around the Erlong reservoir in Binxian County, east of Harbin; the dam was built between 1958 and 1974, and the lake gives the area its name.
