Activities include skiing and grass-skiing, zip-lining and climbing, with dozens of hotels and holiday villages in the area. In winter the frozen lake hosts a snow-play zone and an ice-fishing festival, and a small art museum stands inside the area.

rows.name: Feihe Harbin Smart Industrial Park
rows.name_zh: 飞鹤（哈尔滨）智能产业园
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism park built around a plant of Feihe, a Heilongjiang infant-formula and dairy company, in Shuangcheng district south of Harbin. It offers factory sightseeing and study visits. The provincial tourism department approved it as a 4A scenic area in October 2025.

rows.name: Former Front Command Post of the Northeast Democratic Allied Army, Shuangcheng
rows.name_zh: 东北民主联军前线指挥部旧址
rows.pinyin: Dōngběi Mínzhǔ Liánjūn Qiánxiàn Zhǐhuībù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A courtyard compound in the town of Shuangcheng, built in 1917 as a private residence, which served from 1946 to 1948 as the front command post of the Northeast Democratic Allied Army, later the Fourth Field Army. It is now the Fourth Field Army Memorial Hall, a revolutionary-history museum with a themed square, an open-air weapons display and a main hall in two courtyard buildings. The command post was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: Harbin Beer Museum
rows.summary: A three-storey museum at the Budweiser Harbin brewery in Pingfang District, telling the story of Harbin Beer, which dates from 1900 and is billed as China's earliest beer brand. The ground floor covers the brewery's history, the second floor is an interactive experience area and the top floor is a 'beer college', with guides on each level. It opened in 2014 and appears in the official A-level list as the Centenary Harbin Beer Cultural Tourism Area.

rows.name: Harbin Confucius Temple
rows.summary: A Qing-style temple complex built in 1926–29, described as the largest Confucian temple in north-east China, laid out along a central axis from a pool and the Lingxing Gate to the Dacheng Hall and the Chongsheng Shrine. It was later used as a library and a store, and now houses the Heilongjiang Museum of Nationalities, which also holds traditional-culture events at the temple. Only part of the original grounds survives.

rows.name: Harbin Jewish Heritage Sites
rows.name_zh: 哈尔滨犹太人活动旧址群
rows.summary: Fourteen buildings in Harbin's Daoli and Nangang districts record the Jewish community that settled in the city from the early 1900s and was one of the largest in the Far East until it dwindled in the 1950s. Visitors can see inside the 1921 New Synagogue, now the Harbin Museum of Jewish History and Culture, and the 1909 Old Synagogue, a concert hall since 2014 with a bookshop on the third floor; the former Jewish Middle School beside the Old Synagogue is now a music school. The other listed buildings, mostly banks, shops and houses around Central Street, are in other use and are best seen from outside.

rows.name: Harbin Northern Forest Zoo
rows.name_zh: 哈尔滨北方森林动物园
rows.summary: A forest zoo in the hills of Acheng district that opened on 28 September 2004 to replace Harbin's old city zoo. The district government counts 23 exhibition halls and five large free-range zones, including ones for lions and tigers, large herbivores and wolves, with more than 240 species on show, among them Siberian tigers, white lions and red-crowned cranes. It has a small forest train and suits families.

rows.name: Harbin Polarland
rows.summary: A polar-themed animal park in Songbei district beside Sun Island, which trades as Harbin Polarland and was formerly known as the Harbin Polar Museum. It combines exhibits of polar and Arctic animals such as penguins and polar bears with staged shows featuring beluga whales, sea lions and walruses, according to a 2017 China Daily listing. It suits families.

rows.name: Heilongjiang Provincial Museum (Former Moscow Market)
rows.summary: A Baroque-style building put up as the Moscow Market, a commercial building of Harbin's Russian era, and used as a museum since the early 1920s. It is now Heilongjiang's provincial museum, whose collections the museum puts at more than 600,000 items covering the province's history and natural history. The national heritage listing covers the building itself.

rows.name: Heilongjiang Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: A ship-shaped science museum on the north bank of the Songhua River, opened in August 2003, with about 13,000 square metres of permanent galleries, a domed-screen cinema and a 4D cinema. Exhibits cover mechanics, space, life and environment and information technology, and there is a children's floor. In 2025 the ground-floor galleries were refitted with new themed zones on ice and snow, aviation, deep space and the oceans.

rows.name: Huazishan Geological Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain park in Tonghe County, named after its plough-blade-shaped peaks (huazi means ploughshare), with the Dahuazi, Erhuazi and Sanhuazi summits and a highest point of 680.7 m. A walking route of about 3 km passes some 38 sights, among them a rock field, a waterfall and a footbridge. A base of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army also lay on the mountain, and its remains are a county-level protected site.

rows.name: Jiguanshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested hill area in Mulan County, north-east of Harbin, made up of a geopark, a forest park and the remains of a base of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army. Its best-known geological feature is the 'Thousand-metre Gallery', a long cliff and rock landscape that from the air looks like a dragon winding through the hills. It was listed as a 4A scenic area in the province's 2023 list.

rows.name: Jinlongshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills south-east of Harbin, approved in 2007, whose main peak, Jinlong Mountain, reaches 826 m. The park is divided into six zones, including Lingyin Mountain with its temple and a wooden boardwalk of 'eighteen bends' up the slope, and it is known locally for autumn colour, with a red-leaf festival held each autumn. The official A-level list names it the Jinlongshan International Tourism Resort.

rows.name: Maple Leaf Town Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Harbin's northern Songbei district with thermal bathing pools. It is a commercial leisure resort rather than a historic or natural site, suited to a relaxing half-day.

rows.name: Meilidao Hot Spring Water Park
rows.summary: A hot-spring and water-park resort at Liaodian in Acheng district. It is a commercial leisure complex rather than a historic or natural site.

rows.name: Northeast Martyrs' Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A three-storey neoclassical building put up in 1928–31 as a library and later used as the Harbin police headquarters under the Japanese-controlled state of Manchukuo, which has been a memorial hall since 1948. Its main exhibition covers the anti-Japanese resistance and the civil-war period in north-east China and, according to a 2021 official case study, includes more than 600 photographs and 400 objects, alongside displays on the building's use by the police. A historic tram car stands in the square outside.

rows.name: Phoenix Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 50,000 ha in the mountains of southern Wuchang, run by the Shanhetun Forestry Bureau and also designated a national geological park. It has two main visitor areas, the Grand Canyon and the Alpine Garden (also called the Sky Garden), with boardwalks and trails; the main peak is about 1,700 m. The high ground stays cool in summer, and the park also runs a separate winter ice-and-snow season.

rows.name: Pingshan Forest Tourism Area
rows.summary: A forest recreation area in the hills of Acheng district, centred on a semi-wild deer park where more than a thousand sika and red deer roam and visitors can feed them, according to the district government. Nearly 10 km of forest boardwalk runs through the park, and the area also offers boating on the Xiquanyan reservoir in summer and skiing in winter, with hotels on site.

rows.name: Poseidon Resort
rows.summary: A Greek-myth-themed resort in the Harbin New Area north of the Songhua, opened in stages from 2017. It has an indoor beach water park, an aquarium called Undersea World with a glass tunnel, and a shark-themed hotel; the second phase, opened in 2019, also added a dolphin-show arena. The resort covers about 1,600 mu (around 107 hectares).

rows.name: Provence Lavender Manor
rows.summary: A flower park of about 1,200 mu (around 80 hectares) on rolling hills in Xiangyang town, Xiangfang District, planted with lavender, salvia, verbena and some 70 kinds of ornamental flowers. It has a glamping area with tents and barbecue facilities, and is run as a lavender-themed park for families. The flowers peak in summer, so it suits a summer day out from the city.

rows.name: Shangjing Huiningfu, Jin Dynasty Capital
rows.summary: The first capital of the Jurchen-led Jin dynasty, used from 1115 until the court moved to Yanjing (Beijing) in 1153. Two adjoining walled cities in an L shape, with the palace enclosure inside the southern one, survive as earth walls with bastions, gate remains and palace foundations, about 11 km round. The Jin Shangjing History Museum stands beside the ruins, close to the memorial park at Emperor Taizu's first burial site and Baosheng Temple.

rows.name: Siberian Tiger Park
rows.summary: A tiger park and breeding centre on the north bank of the Songhua River, covering about 80 hectares and open to visitors since 1996. Siberian tigers are watched from a vehicle in the open-range zone and on foot from walkways and a viewing platform, alongside white tigers, white lions, leopards and other big cats. The operator describes it as a breeding base for Siberian tigers and a source of animals for the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park.

rows.name: Songfengshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain south-east of Harbin, whose main peak, Chimney Peak, is 627 m, long used as a Daoist retreat. The Taiyi Daoism founder Xiao Baozhen set up a cave hermitage here in 1143, and the Haiyun Temple, rebuilt on the old temple site in the Qing dynasty, still has resident Daoists and holds temple fairs. Rock formations, carved stones and old Daoist tombs lie along the paths, and the scenic area was rated 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Sun Island Scenic Area
rows.summary: A river island and wetland on the north bank of the Songhua opposite central Harbin, where Russian residents built summer villas in the early twentieth century. Its main area, Sun Island Park, has lakes, flower gardens and a Japanese-style garden, with art museums and, in winter, an international snow-sculpture expo; the planned scenic area covers about 38 sq km. The Harbin Ice and Snow World, a separate winter venue, lies just to the west and has its own entry.

rows.name: Sunac Park, Harbin
rows.summary: A large theme park in Songbei district, part of the Sunac tourism and residential development. It has rides and live shows, including a parade and a mythology-themed show street, and is aimed at families.

rows.name: Unit 731 Museum and Former Headquarters
rows.name_zh: 侵华日军第七三一部队罪证陈列馆
rows.pinyin: Qīnhuá Rìjūn Dìqīsānyī Bùduì Zuìzhèng Chénlièguǎn
rows.summary: The site of Unit 731, an Imperial Japanese Army unit that developed biological weapons and carried out human experiments, whose base here dates from 1936 and whose buildings were mostly blown up in August 1945. The museum complex has a large exhibition building opened in 2015, with documents, photographs and objects, and the preserved former headquarters grounds a few hundred metres away. Since 2012 the site has been on China's national tentative list for World Heritage nominations.

rows.name: Volga Manor
rows.summary: A Russian-themed estate of about 60 hectares on the Ashi River in Xiangfang District, built by a private company over more than twenty years. Its main sights are a full-size reconstruction of Harbin's St Nicholas Cathedral, rebuilt in 2007, the Petrov Art Palace, with Russian paintings, murals and sculpture, and copies of other lost Harbin buildings such as a sailing-ship-shaped restaurant from Sun Island. It is a themed attraction rather than a historic site, and suits visitors who want a Russian-style day out.

rows.name: Xianglushan Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the southern hills of Binxian County, named after its main peak, which is shaped like an incense burner and rises to 790 m. Sights include the Ice Lake, Butterfly Valley and Lovers' Peak, and there are hotels and a ski area at the foot of the mountain. The park has received visitors since 1999.

rows.name: Yabuli Ski Resort
rows.name_zh: 亚布力滑雪旅游度假区
rows.summary: A ski resort in the Zhangguangcai range, laid out across three linked peaks of 1,374 m, 1,258 m and 1,000 m, and also a national winter-sports training base. Skiing is the main draw in winter, while summer attractions include a hot spring, a water park, a mountain-bike park and a 20 km wooden hiking trail. It was among the first 12 national ski tourism resorts publicised by the culture and sports ministries in January 2022.

rows.name: Yagou Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Two line-engraved figures cut into neighbouring rock faces at the south foot of Shiren (Stone Man) Hill, east of Acheng: a man in a helmet and a narrow-sleeved robe holding a short sword, about 1.85 m tall, and a woman beside him whose figure is worn. They date from the early Jin dynasty and are described as the only surviving Jin-era figure carvings, and who they portray is disputed, with Emperor Taizu and his wife, memorial portraits and tomb guardians all suggested. The site was made a national heritage unit in 1988.

rows.name: Yingjie Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hot-spring and leisure resort in a wooded valley at Youlian village, Binxian County, with a hot-spring complex of 54 indoor and outdoor pools, an indoor water park and a winter snow-play and ski area. Other sights include a Mongolian-style park, a glass walkway and a wooden boardwalk up the 722 m Hutou Cliff. Several TV dramas, including later seasons of the series Country Love, were filmed in the village.

rows.name: Yiyuan Street No. 1 Mansion (Revolutionary Leaders Memorial Hall)
rows.summary: A French classical-revival mansion built in 1919–23 for a Russian timber merchant and later used by Japanese intelligence during the Manchukuo period. Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Liu Shaoqi stayed here on visits to Heilongjiang, and it is now a memorial hall about those visits, run together with the Northeast Martyrs' Memorial Hall. It has a four-storey main house and a three-storey annex joined by an arched balcony.

rows.name: Baoquanling Modern Agriculture Eco-Park
rows.name_zh: 宝泉岭现代农业生态园
rows.summary: A farm-tourism park of the Baoquanling branch of the Beidahuang agricultural group, built around solar greenhouses where visitors pick fruit such as cherries, strawberries and dragon fruit. In summer, flower fields and a lawn camping area open, and school groups come for farming-science visits. It suits families and study groups.

rows.name: Hegang National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills north of Hegang, run by the city forestry bureau and made up of the Xilinhe folk-culture park, the Shilihe ecological scenic area and the Tongzigou stand of old-growth Korean pine. The Xilinhe park combines woodland scenery with folk song and dance performances and about 7 km of raft drifting on the river.

rows.name: Mingshan Scenic Area, Luobei
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area at Mingshan town on the Heilongjiang (Amur) River, centred on the wooded Mingshan Island and a riverside park along the shore. The island holds the Heilongjiang River Basin Museum, a second-grade national museum opened in 2009 with natural-history, history and ethnic-folk halls and more than 4,000 objects, including fossils and displays on the peoples who live along the river. The park looks across the river to the Russian bank.

rows.name: Qingyuan Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir-lake scenic area in the Heli River valley west of Hegang, laid out with ten zones in a Nordic style across a core area of 147 hectares inside a wider area of 1,600 hectares. The zones include fishing, flower viewing, lotus ponds, a wetland walk, a wedding-themed area, a children's water-play area and an agricultural sightseeing area. It is run by the city water bureau and also serves as a water-conservation education site.

rows.name: Songhe West Lake Park
rows.summary: A lake park of about 300 hectares, 60 of them water, in wooded foothills of the Lesser Khingan west of Hegang, enclosed by hills on three sides and centred on the lake and Feilai Peak. It has a sandy beach, non-powered play rides, a forest adventure course, fishing, children's play areas and a conference centre for about 200 people. It was upgraded to a 4A scenic area in the 2025 review.

rows.name: Taipinggou Scenic Area, Luobei
rows.summary: A scenic area in the Lesser Khingan foothills on the Heilongjiang River, known for the Longjiang Three Gorges (Longmen, Jinlong and Jinman gorges), which visitors see from boats, and the 5 km Xinglong Canyon, about 400 m deep, with forest walkways and a steel lookout tower. Huangjin Ancient Town, built around the late-Qing gold-mining history of Taipinggou, has a gold-panning experience, a performance square and period-style shops and tea houses.

rows.name: Yueyahu Northern Ethnic Park, Suibin
rows.summary: A lakeside park of about 84 hectares on the Heilongjiang River plain, part of the 570-hectare Yueyahu (Crescent Lake) National Wetland Park. It has three zones: a history zone with reconstructions of the Jin-era walled town of Aolimi and the Tongren culture site, an ethnic-customs zone with houses, costume and displays for the Daur, Oroqen, Hezhe (Nanai) and other northern peoples, and a lakeside leisure zone. The wetland park also has an exhibition hall with bird specimens.

rows.name: Aihui History Museum
rows.summary: A museum on the site of New Aihui, a Qing-era walled town dating from the 1680s that served as the seat of the Heilongjiang General and is now a national heritage unit. Its displays include a reconstructed scene of the signing of the 1858 Treaty of Aigun, a panorama painting of the 1900 events at Blagoveshchensk (Hailanpao), archaeological finds and ethnic artefacts from the Heilongjiang basin, and local Qing-period weapons. The grounds hold a rebuilt Kuixing Pavilion and a heritage stele marking the old town.

rows.name: Chaoyangshan Base of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
rows.name_zh: 朝阳山东北抗联第三路军密营遗址
rows.pinyin: Cháoyángshān Dōngběi Kànglián Dìsān Lùjūn Mìyíng Yízhǐ
rows.summary: A wooded hill area where the Third Route Army of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (an armed force that fought the Japanese occupation) had its headquarters and where the CPC North Manchuria Provincial Committee was based; the Third Route Army was set up here on 30 May 1939. Visitors can see the Dahengshan headquarters ridge, where machine-gun positions survive, a bullet-scarred boulder known as the Merit Stone, a memorial cemetery and a museum, with a themed park and homestay accommodation added in recent years.

rows.name: China–Russia Ethnic Folk Park
rows.summary: A purpose-built cultural park of about 35 ha on the western outskirts of Heihe, laid out in eight themed zones. They cover Oroqen folk displays, an 'Eight Banners' maze, a film and television set, a folk-style town, flower fields, outdoor activities, a water park and a star-gazing campsite, so it suits families and groups looking for a leisure stop.

rows.name: Former Heilongjiang Provincial Committee and Government Sites, Bei'an
rows.name_zh: 中共黑龙江省工作委员会和省政府旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Hēilóngjiāng Shěng Gōngzuò Wěiyuánhuì Hé Shěng Zhèngfǔ Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Two former administrative buildings in Bei'an where the Chinese Communist Party's Heilongjiang committee and the provincial government were based from November 1945 until the provincial seat moved to Qiqihar in May 1949. The committee building, a grey two-storey block of about 1944 built as a Manchukuo-era county office, has reconstructed offices of the committee's secretary and department heads; the government building, put up in 1937 as the Manchukuo provincial office, has nine reconstructed offices and the meeting room where Oroqen representatives negotiated their resettlement.

rows.name: Oroqen Divine Spring Altar Site
rows.summary: A Qing-period ritual site of the Oroqen, a people of forest hunters, set beside a 'divine spring' in the forests of Xunke County and covering about 1.5 hectares. It has been a national heritage unit since 2013. It is a remote forest site, so it suits only travellers with a particular interest in Oroqen culture.

rows.name: Qinghua Military Industry Site Museum
rows.summary: A small-arms museum inside the former Qinghua Tool Factory, a state arms plant in Bei'an, which describes itself as the only firearms-themed museum in China. It has four areas (a history exhibition, a transition hall, the preserved factory site and a light-weapons hall) and, as of 2022, 5,621 items including 539 firearms and 149 machine tools.

rows.name: Shankou Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir of about 84 sq km on the upper Nemor River, completed in 1999 and ringed by forested hills with many small islands. Boat trips pass granite crags such as Bajie Rock and Turtle Island, and the lake sits inside a nature reserve that is an important stop for waterbirds. Frost on the trees and ice scenes also draw winter visitors.

rows.name: Shengshan Fortress, Sunwu
rows.summary: Remains of a fortified zone built by the Japanese Kwantung Army over about seven years from the early 1930s to face the Soviet border, covering some 138 sq km. Surviving works include an underground command post, barracks and tunnels, an artillery position and depots; there is a site museum, and the area is also a national forest park.

rows.name: Wudalianchi Volcanic Field
rows.summary: A volcanic landscape of 14 cones, the last of which erupted in 1719–21, spread over about 1,060 sq km at the foot of the Lesser Khingan range. Lava dammed a river to make five linked lakes, and the area also has fields of lava rock and cold mineral springs; it has been a UNESCO Global Geopark since 2004. Cones such as Laoheishan and the geopark museum are the main stops, and the spring water is a local draw.

rows.name: Xinsheng Oroqen Folk Village
rows.summary: A folk-culture visitor area in Xinsheng, an Oroqen township; the Oroqen are a traditionally hunting people of the Khingan forests. It has the Lingshangren Museum on Oroqen life, a herbal-medicine museum, a re-created 'primitive tribe' camp and the Cierbin River, and visitors can try horse riding, shooting and archery, dried-meat tasting and birch-bark or roe-deer-skin crafts. The township also stages the Gulunmuta fire-god festival, a national intangible cultural heritage item.

rows.name: Aoqiwan Hezhe Tourist Area
rows.summary: A Hezhe cultural area on the Songhua River bank at Aoqi, the Hezhe village in the suburbs of Jiamusi. Xinhua reports that visitors make fish-skin pictures, try on fish-skin clothing and eat river fish, and that Aoqi town drew more than 300,000 visitors between 2024 and mid-2025. The Hezhe festival Wuribong, held every four years, was staged in Jiamusi's suburbs in 2025, and a ski slope on the same riverbank is used in winter.

rows.name: Daliangzihe National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 大亮子河国家森林公园
rows.summary: A forest park in the hills of Tangyuan county, set up in 1992, with a trail through the woods to the site of the secret camp of the Sixth Army of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army. Only the stone foundations of the original log buildings survive, and beside them stand full-size replica log cabins that form a memorial museum, with the army's headquarters, uniform workshop and cadre school re-created (Xinhua, October 2026).

rows.name: Fujin National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland on the south-west side of Fujin that has been restored over many years and is now a summer gathering place for waterbirds, with a lotus pond. It is a designated national wildlife-protection education base and suits birdwatchers and anyone crossing the Sanjiang Plain.

rows.name: Fujin Rice Paddy Park
rows.summary: A rice-farming park on the Sanjiang Plain beside the Harbin–Tongjiang expressway, known for giant rice-field pictures: in 2026 the designs covered 120,000 square metres, planted with black rice, ordinary green rice and ornamental varieties and viewed from an observation tower. Visitors can also try transplanting rice in a demonstration field, see rice being milled and visit a small exhibition on rice growing, and the park has added camping and caravan areas (Xinhua, September 2026). The pictures are at their clearest in summer.

rows.name: Heixiazi Island Bear Park
rows.summary: A large wildlife park on Heixiazi Island where more than 110 black bears, together with roe deer, deer and wild boar, are kept in semi-wild enclosures across 130 hectares of wetland and woodland; China Daily (2024) calls it the country's largest black-bear zoo. Visitors tour it by vehicle on a winding route and watch the bears swim, dig and climb trees. The island's Chinese name means 'black bear island'.

rows.name: Heixiazi Island Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Chinese part of Heixiazi Island, a low wetland island where the Amur and Ussuri rivers meet opposite the Russian city of Khabarovsk. The main sight is the Dongji Pagoda, a nine-storey, 79 m Han–Tang-style tower on a circular plaza 171 m across, completed in 2016, with views north over the Amur and east towards Khabarovsk. Visitors also come for the wetland park, boundary marker 259 and the nearby 'first guard post of the east', the area being billed as China's eastern extremity.

rows.name: Huanan Forest Steam Train and Forestry Yard Village
rows.summary: A narrow-gauge forest railway of the Huanan forestry bureau, described locally as a century old, on which steam locomotives carry sightseeing trains to the Sengong Dayuan folk village. The village re-creates a 1960s–70s logging community, with an old co-op shop, a photo studio and a school, and there is a campsite beside the station and evening performances in summer. The 2026 season began on 1 May, and weekends and holidays are the busiest times.

rows.name: Jiejinkou Hezhe Resort, Tongjiang
rows.name_zh: 街津口赫哲旅游度假区
rows.summary: A Hezhe settlement area on the Amur in Tongjiang, centred on Jiejinkou Hezhe Township. The Hezhe are one of China's smallest ethnic groups, traditionally river fishers, and their sung epic Yimakan is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage in need of urgent safeguarding; Tongjiang promotes Hezhe-style villages, murals and crafts. The township lies below the wooded Jiejinshan, a national forest park.

rows.name: Qixing Tourist Town, Qixing Farm
rows.summary: A farm-based tourist complex at Qixing Farm, a large state-run rice farm of the Beidahuang Group in the Jiansanjiang district of the Sanjiang Plain. The draw is large-scale rice farming: Xinhua photographs from July 2026 show big rice-field pictures planted on the farm, and a 2025 Xinhua report describes drones carrying rice seedlings across its paddies.

rows.name: Sanjiangkou Confluence Park, Tongjiang
rows.summary: A riverside wetland park where the Songhua River joins the Amur (Heilongjiang), a confluence that Xinhua describes as a stretch where the dark water of the Amur and the yellow water of the Songhua run side by side before mixing. The park is also the northern starting point of the Tongsan highway, which runs more than 5,000 km south to Sanya on Hainan, and its wetland is home to more than 200 bird species according to Xinhua. It suits a short stop for the river view.

rows.name: Xinghuo Rice Village, Huachuan
rows.summary: A Korean-minority farming village on the Sanjiang Plain that became a visitor attraction in 2025, built around its rice paddies, with rice-field pictures, a Xinghuo Tower, a re-created village co-op shop and about ten other sights, and a snow park in winter. China Daily reports that the first collective farm of the People's Republic was founded in the village on 19 February 1951. Xinhua counted more than 1.1 million visitors by early 2026, and the village restaurants serve Korean-minority dishes.

rows.name: Beidahuang Calligraphy Garden, Mishan
rows.summary: A calligraphy garden beside the General's Lake reservoir north of Mishan, laid out over about 16 hectares as a garden of corridors, platforms and stone tablets. According to the city government it holds more than 2,400 carved stone tablets bearing the writing of about 1,600 people, from revolutionary figures and writers to contemporary calligraphers. The reservoir, formerly the Youth Reservoir, was built from 1958 under General Wang Zhen during the opening up of the Great Northern Wilderness.

rows.name: Dangbi Lake Khanka Resort
rows.name_zh: 当壁镇兴凯湖旅游度假区
rows.summary: A state-farm lakeside resort district on the western end of Lake Khanka, beside the Mishan border port, with a sandy shore, a lakeside deer park, a Russian-style park, a picking garden and a water park. Its history sights are memorials to the opening up of the Great Northern Wilderness, including a hall holding General Wang Zhen's tools and photographs, and the Bailing River bridge, kept as a relic of the old border crossing. The resort has been developed since the 1980s and is aimed at summer holidaymakers.

rows.name: Dongfanghong Wetland, Hulin
rows.summary: A lake and wetland tourist area in the Dongfanghong forestry area of Hulin, run from the forestry bureau and rated 4A. The provincial review of October 2025 lists it under the name Dongfanghong Nanchahu Scenic Area.

rows.name: Guokuishan Mountain Fort
rows.summary: The remains of a hill fort on the summit of Guokuishan in Yong'an town, Jidong county, mainly of the Bohai-kingdom period (the national list gives the Tang era). A dry-stone wall about 1.3 km long with 13 bastions runs along the edge of the summit, enclosing a well, a horse-watering pit and house foundations, and an old path on the east side leads to the fort's only gate. The county holds walking festivals at the foot of the hill, with a stage and entrance gate set up for them.

rows.name: Hutou Scenic Area and Fortress Museum
rows.summary: A scenic area on the Ussuri River at Hutou, built around the remains of the Hutou fortress, one of a chain of fortifications that the Japanese Kwantung Army built along the north-eastern frontier in the 1930s and that Soviet forces attacked in August 1945. It has the fortress museum with relics and exhibits, wartime remains such as a military wharf, a large bronze tiger statue on the river bank, a Guandi temple and riverside wetland, looking across the river to the Russian city of Dalnerechensk. The fortress is part of a national heritage unit of the north-eastern fortifications.

rows.name: Jixi Japanese Crimes Exhibition Hall and Didao Mass Grave
rows.name_zh: 侵华日军鸡西罪证陈列馆
rows.summary: A museum in Didao district recording the 1933–45 Japanese occupation of the Jixi coalfield and the miners who died under it. It began in 1966 as a local exhibition and held an opening ceremony in September 2015 together with the unveiling of a memorial to the miners buried in the mass grave; its fourth hall holds a provincially listed furnace that was used to cremate bodies, alongside a bone-sorting vat found during repairs in 2015. The national listing is the Jixi Mass Grave Site, in a valley about 1.5 km from the hall, where a memorial monument and plaza stand inside a fenced protected area.

rows.name: Qilinshan Scenic Area, Jidong
rows.summary: Rock peaks and a lake in Xingnong town, Jidong county, named for a ridge whose north and south peaks are said to look like the head and tail of a qilin, the mythical beast. A hill path leads to a viewing platform at about 555 m, and around the 26.8-hectare lake there are play features such as coloured slides, a water-curtain bridge, high-level rafting and a 'Dream Island' play area, plus a horse show in summer (county government, 2025–26). It is also a provincial geopark and suits families on a day trip from Jixi.

rows.name: Tiexi Forest Park, Mishan
rows.summary: A forest, lake and wetland area in the hills west of Mishan, covering about 80 square kilometres by the Jixi city government's figure. It has reservoirs, a lotus pond crossed by a zigzag boardwalk, an island with villas, a crane-breeding base and Korean and Mongol-style folk parks, and a seasonal water park. It suits a half-day nature stop in summer.

rows.name: Xinkailiu, Lake Khanka
rows.summary: A lakeside scenic area on the sand ridge between Big and Small Lake Khanka, with a viewing platform, a bird-watching platform, a boat landing and a long sandy beach. The area includes the Xinkailiu site, a Neolithic fishing settlement about 6,000 years old that was excavated in 1972 and yielded 32 graves, 10 fish pits and net-patterned pottery, as well as a carved bone eagle's head that has become a symbol of the culture. A fishing-ritual performance is staged on the frozen lake in winter.

rows.name: Chaihe Jiuzhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A valley scenic area at the Hongsheng forest farm of the Chaihe forestry bureau, in Weihushan National Forest Park, where two clear mountain streams, the Golden Stream and Silver Stream valleys, drop over a group of cascades known as the Nine-Tier Springs. Around them are stone peaks, old pines and primeval forest, and the area is promoted as the 'little Jiuzhaigou of the north', after the famous valley in Sichuan.

rows.name: Dongning Fortress
rows.summary: The Dongning fortress group was built from 1934 by the Japanese Kwantung Army, with forced Chinese labour, along the frontier south-east of Mudanjiang, and saw heavy fighting in August 1945. The visit centres on the Xunshan underground fortress, with a museum at its foot whose five permanent exhibitions cover the fortress itself, the Japanese occupation, local anti-Japanese resistance, the 1945 fighting and later peace and friendship exchanges. A garden commemorating Anti-Japanese United Army fighters and an ordnance display are in the same grounds, and the site is part of the national protected unit 'Fortifications of the Japanese Invasion Troops'.

rows.name: Heibao Bear Park
rows.summary: A bear park of about 10 hectares inside Sandaoguan National Forest Park, north-west of Mudanjiang, that keeps and breeds captive bears for visitors to view. Its official A-level name also includes 'Water World'.

rows.name: Hengdaohezi Russian Town
rows.name_zh: 横道河子俄罗斯风情小镇
rows.summary: A railway town founded in 1897 when the Russian-built Chinese Eastern Railway came through, with more than 250 Russian-style buildings, six of them national heritage buildings. The highlights are the fan-shaped locomotive roundhouse, whose 15 doors now front a railway museum, the Russian Orthodox Church of the Presentation of the Virgin, the former locomotive-crew apartment block and the old street of Russian-style stone and timber houses; together these form the Hengdaohezi parts of the national Chinese Eastern Railway Buildings unit. UNESCO's 2018 Asia-Pacific heritage awards gave the town an honourable mention, and it has become popular with photographers, especially in snow.

rows.name: Hengdaohezi Siberian Tiger Park
rows.summary: A tiger park that grew out of a feline breeding centre set up at Hengdaohezi in 1986 and renamed the Northeast Tiger Park about ten years later; it keeps captive-bred Siberian tigers. Visitors ride in armoured sightseeing vehicles through a series of protective gates into the tiger enclosures and watch through the windows as the animals walk, climb and play-fight. Keepers say the tigers are livelier in cold weather, so winter is a good time to go.

rows.name: Jingpo Lake
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A long, narrow lake in the Zhangguangcai and Laoye mountains, formed when lava from volcanic eruptions dammed the Mudan River; its water area is about 90 sq km and the scenic district is also a UNESCO Global Geopark. Most visitors head for the northern end, around Diaoshuilou Falls, and take a boat out along the lake. The wider scenic district also takes in the Underground Forest crater park and the Bohai Shangjing site, which have their own entries on this map.

rows.name: Luolemishan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest tourism area at Hongqi forest farm, run by the Fangzheng forestry bureau and listed in the province's 2025 review as the Yuanyang Peak Scenic Area, with a walk up Yuanyang Peak past rock formations and a waterfall; the area reaches 1,357 m. The best-known sight is the Magpie Bridge, a glass-floored footbridge 214 m long between two summits about 290 m above the valley, and there are also a 527 m glass walkway, a forest slide, a glass-bottomed rafting course and a jungle rail car. The wider area of about 3,000 hectares includes a rafting zone on the Xiangshui River and a forest wellness centre.

rows.name: Northeast Old Flight School Site, Mudanjiang
rows.name_zh: 人民空军东北老航校旧址
rows.summary: The site of the first flying school set up by the Chinese Communist Party, founded in 1946 and based at Mudanjiang's airfield for part of 1946 and again from 1948 to 1949; its first flights took place here in 1946. The remains are a runway, a control tower, hangars and aircraft shelters, and two old hangars now hold exhibition halls on the school's history. The site is on an active Air Force base.

rows.name: Peony Group Smart Science and Technology Museum, Ning'an
rows.name_zh: 牡丹集团宁安智慧科技馆
rows.summary: A science and technology museum run by the Peony Group in Bohai town, about 2 km from Xinglong Temple and the Shangjing site, with digital and interactive displays aimed mainly at families and school groups. It was added to the 4A list in 2024.

rows.name: Sandaoguan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 8,000 hectares on the north-western edge of Mudanjiang, at roughly 300 to 740 m above sea level, with dense forest, rocky cliffs and streams. Two areas are open to visitors, Wuxi ('Mist Stream') Valley and Xiaohuangshan ('little Huangshan'), and the park is promoted as a summer escape from the city. The separately listed Heibao Bear Park lies inside the park.

rows.name: Shangjing Longquanfu
rows.name_zh: 渤海国上京龙泉府遗址
rows.summary: Shangjing was the main capital of the Bohai kingdom, a Tang-era state in north-east Asia, laid out on the plan of the Tang capital Chang'an with outer, inner and palace cities, until the Khitan destroyed the kingdom in 926. The palace-city site is now a national archaeological park with a scale model of the palace city, at one-twentieth size, and models of six individual halls, and a site museum nearby shows finds and research in four galleries. Xinglong Temple, a Qing-dynasty temple built on the old Bohai temple ground, keeps Bohai stone carvings including a stone lantern and a large stone Buddha.

rows.name: Suifenhe Love Valley
rows.summary: A love-themed park opened in October 2020 on the northern edge of Suifenhe, in a valley between Tianchang and Jiudi mountains around the Tianchang Lake reservoir. It has a birch-wood boardwalk, a giant rotating ring sculpture, a 100 m footbridge made of 16 red heart-shaped frames and a long stepped path up to a viewpoint. The name plays on the park's position, 131° E and 44° N, and its 520 m altitude, which read as 'one life, one world' and 'I love you'.

rows.name: Taipinggou Primeval Forest Scenic Area
rows.summary: A stand of about 297 hectares of primeval Korean pine at the Taipinggou forest farm, part of Xuexiang National Forest Park, which the provincial tourism department describes as the best-preserved forest tourism resource in north-east China. It was named one of 'China's most beautiful forests' in 2019, and one thousand-year-old pine in it carries the title 'China's most beautiful red pine'. Visitors can follow a stream trail through the forest and try an adventure course through the treetops.

rows.name: Volcanic Crater National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the eastern slope of the middle Zhangguangcai Range, north-west of Jingpo Lake, where ten volcanic craters of different sizes, with steep inner walls, are mostly filled with primeval forest; it is also called the Underground Forest. The park has a lava tunnel with lava stalactites and an open-air ice cave in which ice can be seen all year. It counts as one of the three parts of the Jingpo Lake scenic district, with the lake itself and the Bohai Shangjing site.

rows.name: Weihushan Film and TV City
rows.summary: A film and television set built in 1998 near Hengdaohezi, with about 107 buildings laid out as the world of the novel Tracks in the Snowy Forest, including Forest Sea Town, the thatched village of Jiapigou and Weihu Hall; People's Daily's Heilongjiang channel (2021) counts more than 600 films and series shot here. In 2021 an exhibition on the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army and staged immersive shows were added. It is a themed set rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Yilong Water Park
rows.summary: A water park on the Hailang River in Xin'an Korean township, south-west of Hailin, with a children's water area, water slides, a wave pool and a cable ride across the river, plus fishing, barbecue and camping areas. It first opened in 1997 and is mainly a summer attraction for families.

rows.name: Zhongxing Korean Folk Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 中兴朝鲜民族文化风情园
rows.summary: Zhongxing, an ethnic Korean village in Hainan Korean township, has been turned into a folk-culture tourist area, with Korean-style buildings, a tall drum-shaped building with a view over the village, costume photography, Korean-style restaurants and homestays among the rice fields. A folk-custom park started in 2014 by a returning villager includes a small folk museum, and a group of small exhibition halls includes a New Year picture hall and a 3D experience hall. It suits visitors interested in Korean-Chinese village life and food.

rows.name: Ang'angxi Sites and Site Museum
rows.summary: The Ang'angxi sites are a group of Neolithic fishing-and-hunting settlements on the Nen River plain, which gave their name to the Ang'angxi culture first dug by the archaeologist Liang Siyong in 1930. The site museum, built in 2002 beside the Tengjiagang site, shows stone, bone and jade tools and other finds from the group, more than 3,000 objects in all. The sites themselves lie on sand dunes outside the town, so the museum is the part to visit.

rows.name: Bukui Mosque
rows.summary: Described by Xinhua as the largest and oldest mosque in Heilongjiang, Bukui Mosque is still used for worship in the old centre of Qiqihar. It grew from two separate mosques: an East Mosque built in 1684, seven years before the city was founded, and a West Mosque built in 1852 by followers of the Jahriyya order who had come from Gansu; the two were merged in 1958. The compound covers about 6,400 square metres and includes a pagoda-style minaret.

rows.name: China First Heavy Industries Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: China First Heavy Industries is a heavy-machinery maker in the industrial town of Fularji, one of the three Soviet-aided projects of China's first Five-Year Plan sited there in the 1950s. Visits take in production workshops and the company's exhibition hall on its history and equipment, and a neighbouring steelworks, Jianlong Beiman Special Steel, has an exhibition hall of its own on the same circuit. It suits visitors interested in heavy industry rather than a general sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Former Heilongjiang Military Governor's Office
rows.summary: The former headquarters of Heilongjiang's military governors in the early Republic of China, built over an earlier Qing residence in Qiqihar's old walled quarter. A two-storey brick-and-timber building and a group of single-storey halls survive from the complex, which later housed the provincial government until 1954. It stands beside the Qiqihar Museum, whose main exhibition covers the history of the Nen River region and Qiqihar.

rows.name: Hala New Village
rows.summary: A village of about 60 hectares on the grassland at the edge of Qiqihar, marketed as the first Daur village in China; the Daur are an ethnic minority of the Nen River valley. Its attractions include an intangible-heritage experience hall, Morgen Square, traditional houses, the Hala ancient-city site, a grassland with an obo shrine and horse riding, and a street of village guesthouses. Daur music and the lurige dance are shown here, and the village hosts the annual Kumul festival.

rows.name: Hecheng Happy World
rows.summary: An amusement park inside Hecheng Park in the south of Qiqihar, with some 30 rides, among them a Ferris wheel, pirate ship, carousel and bumper cars, plus an indoor children's play area and a hotel. In winter the park switches to an outdoor ice-and-snow programme. It is aimed at families and local day trips.

rows.name: Jiangqiao Resistance Memorial Site
rows.summary: A memorial park and museum at Jiangqiao on the Nen River, where Heilongjiang provincial troops under Ma Zhanshan fought Japanese forces at the railway bridge in November 1931. The museum, opened in 2008, shows photographs and objects from the campaign, a display recreating the wooden railway bridge and a sand-table model, and the grounds beside the river have a statue of Ma Zhanshan. It also displays finds from the Ang'angxi culture.

rows.name: Longsha Park
rows.summary: A large urban park of about 64 hectares in the centre of Qiqihar, with Laodong Lake and Wangjiang Tower, a lakeside pavilion first built in 1908. The former Heilongjiang Provincial Library building, put up in 1930 and now a nationally protected monument, stands in the grounds, along with other historic buildings such as a former Russian consulate. In winter the park hosts ice sculptures.

rows.name: Longsha Zoo and Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A zoo and botanical garden on the northern edge of Qiqihar, with more than 200 species and about 3,000 animals from five continents, along with plants of the 47th parallel. It has a tiger-viewing corridor behind strengthened glass, a primate rainforest house, a small train through themed animal zones, stage shows, and animal feeding and parades in season, and it suits families.

rows.name: Longteng Eco Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 龙腾生态温泉度假庄园
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Fuyu county on the edge of the Longanqiao wetland, across the Wuyuer River from the Zhalong reserve. It offers hot-spring bathing, wooden, water-side and hot-spring villas, fruit picking and speciality farming, and has five lakes in its wetland park. It suits families and groups wanting a spa stay near Zhalong.

rows.name: Mingyue Island
rows.summary: A wooded island in the Nen River just north-west of Qiqihar, laid out as a park from 1981 and named Mingyue ("Bright Moon") in 1984. It has a Buddhist temple first built in 1925, the Heilongjiang General's Mansion complex with a multimedia show on the history of old Bukui (Qiqihar), a 500 m poetry corridor and flower gardens, and a small tourist train that restarted in June 2024 after about 11 years. Visitors reach it by boat or, when the water is too low, by a floating bridge.

rows.name: Nianzishan Tourism Area
rows.summary: A district-wide tourism area in the low hills at the eastern foot of the Greater Khingan range, west of Qiqihar, rather than a single park. Its sights are spread over the district: a ski resort, a military-industry culture park showing arms production and a firing range, a 12 km stretch of the Yalu River for rafting, Shexian Cave where Palaeolithic stone tools were found, and a section of the Jin-dynasty frontier earthwork. Chongshan Park above the town, begun in 1982, has a liberation monument and viewpoint pavilions, and the district promotes flowers in spring, rafting in summer, fruit picking in autumn and skiing in winter.

rows.name: Shuishi Forest Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort set in a forest park near Shuishiying in Ang'angxi district, covering about 2.5 square kilometres. It combines natural hot springs, a water park, non-powered rides, rooms and restaurants with fruit picking and Mongolian-style barbecue. It suits families and groups wanting a day or overnight stay, and it ran a night-time light-and-shadow festival in autumn 2025.

rows.name: Taihu National Wetland Park, Tailai
rows.summary: A national wetland park on the eastern edge of Tailai county town, developed from 2002, with a lake, reed beds and a lotus pond. Visitors can walk the lakeside boardwalk, take a boat or battery car, visit the lake island and the Guangming Temple, or use the water park. It is a leisure park next to the town rather than a remote nature site.

rows.name: Tazicheng Walled City Site
rows.summary: Tazicheng is the walled city of the Liao and Jin dynasties, once the seat of Taizhou prefecture, whose square circuit of about 4.5 km still shows in the landscape even though most of the wall and its gate-forts have worn down. A village now fills the interior, and the county has added a site museum and a Liao-Jin square, with the gate sites, moat, wall remains and a generals' platform to see on a walk. Four granite and marble column bases from lost buildings are recorded inside the city, and Liao-Jin tombs lie outside it.

rows.name: Zhalong Nature Reserve
rows.summary: A vast freshwater reed marsh on the Wuyuer River plain, known as a breeding ground for red-crowned cranes and listed as a wetland of international importance (Ramsar) in 1992. The tourist area, about 4.7 square kilometres of the much larger reserve, has a viewing platform for scheduled flight displays by trained, captive-bred cranes, plus boat trips through the reeds and walking trails. The displays continue through the winter, and the area was upgraded to a 5A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Wusihun River National Forest Park, Boli
rows.name_zh: 乌斯浑河国家森林公园
rows.summary: A forest park in the hills south-west of Boli town, Qitaihe, which held its opening events in mid-August 2026 as the county's first 4A scenic area after a four-year upgrade. The park has forest streams, old pines and a rafting run, and the local report also mentions the area's revolutionary history.

rows.name: Anbanghe National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A river-and-marsh wetland park of about 290 ha in north-eastern Jixian County, one of China's first national wetland parks and used for nature education. A small county museum inside the park is open seasonally, from early May to early October.

rows.name: Beidahuang Agricultural Machinery Park
rows.summary: A 35-hectare agricultural science park at Youyi, in the Beidahuang farming region, built around an exposition centre of farm machinery. The grounds also have a forest botanical garden, a landscaped avenue and a Beidahuang culture square, and the park is aimed at school groups and visitors interested in modern farming.

rows.name: Qingshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain park of about 28,500 ha in Lingdong district, south of Shuangyashan, with 82% tree cover, rocky peaks and many streams. It has a visitor centre, two Buddhist temples (the Jiufeng Chan Temple and the Pudu Temple), a hill with stone Buddhas and the Xingyue ('Star-Moon') Lake with a bathing beach.

rows.name: Qixingshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the northern slope of the Wanda Mountains where Jixian, Lingdong district and Huanan County meet, named for seven rock crags; the highest, at 852.7 m, is billed as the first peak of the Sanjiang Plain. In the 1930s the area was one of the largest bases of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, with camps, an arsenal and a school; a memorial and carved stones mark the mid-slope, a red-tourism hall stands at the foot, and the park also has a film set for a television drama about the army.

rows.name: Shengjie Cradle Mountain Resort
rows.summary: A ski and outdoor-sports resort on the Lishu forest farm in Baoqing County, where the city government says snow lies for about 130 days a year. The ski area has 12 runs from beginner to advanced with a vertical drop of 365 m, and the county government describes the resort as the province's second national-level ski-tourism resort.

rows.name: Sipai Hezhe Folk Park
rows.summary: A folk park beside the G331 road at Sipai Hezhe Ethnic Township on the Ussuri River, built on about 10 ha with seven main zones. A boat-shaped hall on the Hezhe 'Ussuri Boat Song' and a tent-shaped intangible-heritage centre show clothing, fishing tools and ritual objects, and the visitor centre holds a 44 m fish-skin picture, 'Hezhe Panorama', made from nearly 22,000 salmon skins. A Hezhe river-lantern festival is held in mid-July.

rows.name: Xiaonanshan Site and Raohe Museum
rows.summary: A saddle-shaped hill beside the Ussuri River at Raohe, where excavations between 2015 and 2021 found Neolithic and Bronze Age remains and burials and more than 200 jade objects, dated to about 9,000 years ago; it was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2019. The finds are shown at the Raohe County Museum at the foot of the hill, which has digital displays on jade-working, and the county also runs a jade-culture plaza and an outdoor video display of the excavation results, and plans a national archaeological site park.

rows.name: Yanwodao Wetland Tourist Area
rows.summary: A wetland tourist area at the Yanwo Island marsh in northern Baoqing County, beside the 853 state farm in the Beidahuang land-reclamation region. It has an ecology museum, a long zigzag covered walkway, a water park with a boat pier and an exhibition hall on the 'Beidahuang spirit', and a landscape stone carved with the name 'Yanwodao' in the calligraphy of Dong Biwu. The city government also mentions a Jurchen-era site more than 800 years old inside the area.

rows.name: Suiling Forestry Bureau Ecological and Cultural Area
rows.name_zh: 绥棱林业局生态文化旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Suílíng Línyèjú Shēngtài Wénhuà Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: The cultural park at the seat of the Suiling forestry bureau, in the south-western foothills of the Lesser Khingan range, built around a steam-powered forest railway. The 'Anti-Japanese United Army' steam train, refitted in 2026, runs past the Plant Kingdom garden, the Dingsheng Garden square, a log-style station and the Suiling Forest Region Museum, which traces the area's logging history. The park also has black-pottery and dough-figure workshops.

rows.name: Huilongwan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 6.4 sq km set up in 1993 on a bend of the Tangwang River in Meixi, enclosed by the river on three sides; local legend makes it the birthplace of a black dragon, which gives the name. Alongside the forest walks, the park hosts a large holiday and recuperation centre built for model workers, whose first phase was finished in 2015.

rows.name: Jiayin Dinosaur National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 嘉荫恐龙国家地质公园
rows.summary: A geopark on Longgushan (Dragon Bone Hill) near the Heilongjiang river, where fossils of the duck-billed dinosaur found in 1902 were among the earliest dinosaur discoveries in China. It has the Jiayin Shenzhou Dinosaur Museum, whose centrepiece is a mother-and-baby hadrosaur skeleton, plus the original excavation site, a Dinosaur Tower, a garden of statues of 24 palaeontologists and dinosaur-themed attractions for children.

rows.name: Jinxiu Shanshui Park
rows.summary: A landscaped city park in the urban area of Yichun, laid out with walking paths and planted trees. It is a place for a short walk rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Jiufengshan Yangxin Valley
rows.summary: A forest health resort and small animal park in a mountain-ringed valley in Jinlin district, Yichun. It combines forest walks, flower fields, farm picking and forest-food products, and visitors can feed and approach animals such as deer and squirrels. The valley is one of Yichun's provincial demonstration bases for traditional Chinese medicine health tourism.

rows.name: Maolangou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested stream valley in Xiangyang township, Jiayin County, close to Maolangou village and listed as a national forest park. Visitors walk along the stream through dense woodland, crossing on stepping stones.

rows.name: Tangwang River Stone Forest
rows.summary: A forest and granite scenic area of about 190 sq km on the Tangwang River in the Lesser Khingan mountains, rated 5A in 2013. More than 100 granite peaks rise out of the woods in what is called a 'granite forest', among streams and old mixed forest. It is the core of a national forest park that is also a granite geopark.

rows.name: Taoyuan Lake, Taoshan
rows.summary: A forest lake near Taoshan town in Tieli, with outdoor hot-spring pools, a hotel, a forest trail and winter activities on the snow and ice. The hot springs are promoted for soaking in the snow, so winter is its best-known season, and the resort is among China's first national forest wellness bases.

rows.name: Toulong Mountain
rows.summary: A small hill on the southern slope of the Lesser Khingan range, named for two caves facing each other beside a waterfall; its 'nine peaks and eighteen sights' include Mandarin Duck Tree, Immortal Maiden Cave and Crouching Tiger Peak. Timber lodges at the foot offer dining, entertainment and rooms, and the site stages a winter outdoor drama about the anti-Japanese united army and performances of Khingan logging songs. It joined the 4A list in 2024.

rows.name: Wuying National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park at Wuying in the Lesser Khingan range, in the part of Yichun known as the 'home of the Korean pine', also promoted as the Wuying Red Pine Sea scenic area. Boardwalks run through old Korean pine forest, which is at its most colourful in autumn. The park was among the third batch of national AAAA-rated tourist areas in 2002.

rows.name: Xiling Forest Eco-Resort
rows.name_zh: 西岭森林生态旅游度假区
rows.summary: A forest tourism and holiday area at the former Xiling forest farm in Wucui district, with homestay and hotel accommodation, a hot-spring hotel and forest-wellness programmes among woodland. On nearby Guokui Mountain a memorial marks the former site of the Communist Party's North Manchuria Provincial Committee. It is somewhere to stay for a few days rather than a sight to visit for an hour.

rows.name: Xinqing National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A 4,490-hectare wetland park of peat bog and marsh near Xinqing town in Fenglin County, set up in 2007 and accepted as a national wetland park in 2013. It is a breeding ground of the hooded crane (white-headed crane), with about 150 returning each spring from late March or early April, so spring is the time to go.

rows.name: Xishui National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Xishui forest area of the Shangganling forestry bureau, in the Lesser Khingan mountains of Youhao district. It has a visitor centre, themed hiking routes through the forest and forest-wellness activities such as forest meditation, and is popular for autumn colour. It works as a short half-day trip from Yichun city.

rows.name: Shuangqiaozi Forest Area, Suiyang
rows.summary: A forest tourism area run by the Suiyang forestry bureau of the Longjiang Forest Industry group, in the Laoyeling hills of Dongning. It has woodland walks, wetland and relics of old logging camps, and in 2026 became a study base for Mudanjiang schools. It was named among the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020.

rows.name: 1933 Old Millfun
rows.summary: The former abattoir of the Shanghai Municipal Council, a reinforced-concrete complex completed in 1933 and described as the largest slaughterhouse in Shanghai at the time. Restored and reopened in 2007 as a creative complex, its curved stairways, thick walls and bridged walkways now hold shops, cafés, restaurants and event spaces open to the public.

rows.name: Bicester Village Shanghai
rows.summary: An outlet shopping village beside Shanghai Disney Resort, opened in 2016 as Shanghai Village, with about 200 boutiques selling discounted fashion and lifestyle brands. Its low-rise buildings in a 1920s Art Deco style curve around Xingyuan (Star Wish) Lake, where short boat rides run in fine weather, and cafés and restaurants line the lakeside. It suits shoppers and makes an easy add-on to a Disney visit.

rows.name: Bihai Jinsha (Sunny Beach)
rows.summary: A seaside leisure area on Hangzhou Bay, one of Shanghai's few beaches, where a sea wall encloses a sheltered stretch of water behind an artificial beach of sand brought from Hainan. The city's visitor site lists about 60,000 square metres of swimming area, used mainly from June to September, with seafood and barbecue restaurants and water sports such as windsurfing and kayaking, and it suits a family day by the sea.

rows.name: Caojing Shuike Scenic Area
rows.summary: A water-village scenic area in Caojing town centred on Shuiku village, where 41 rivers and canals and more than 70 islands and peninsulas make up about 40 per cent of the village's area. Visitors take boat trips, kayak or paddleboard, walk the reed marshes and woods of Caojing Country Park and eat river food in the village, and it suits a slow day in the countryside.

rows.name: Century Park
rows.summary: A park of about 140 hectares of lakes, lawns and woodland at the end of Century Avenue in Pudong, designed by the British consultancy LUC, opened in 2000 and described as the largest naturalistic park inside Shanghai's Inner Ring Road. It is laid out in seven areas, including a lakeside area, a bird-protection zone and an 'exotic' garden area, with small sights such as a flower clock and a music fountain, boating and bicycles for hire, and makes a quiet break next to the science museum.

rows.name: Changfeng Park and Changfeng Ocean World
rows.summary: A large landscaped park in Putuo, opened in 1959 around the artificial Yinchu Lake and Tiebi Hill. Its northern half reopened in October 2026 after nearly two years of renovation, with several gates and stretches of boundary wall removed and the old 'Path of the Brave' adventure trail rebuilt on Black Pine Hill. Changfeng Ocean World, an aquarium opened in 1999 beneath the lake's west shore, shows rays, penguins and other marine life.

rows.name: Changxing Island Country Park
rows.summary: One of Shanghai's first seven country parks, opened in 2016 on Changxing Island in the Yangtze estuary beside the Qingcaosha Reservoir; its first phase covers 5.58 km². It is a farmland landscape of orange groves, rose and flower fields, orchards and a lotus garden, with kayaking and paddleboarding on Huaxi Lake in summer and a former farm barracks converted into the 'Qianwei 1966' area.

rows.name: Chen Yun Memorial Hall and Liantang Ancient Town
rows.summary: A memorial complex opened in 2000 in Liantang, the home town of the senior Chinese Communist Party leader Chen Yun (1905–1995), and renamed Chen Yun Memorial Hall in 2013. It brings together a bronze statue square, exhibition halls on his life, a hall of his personal relics, his restored former residence and a corridor of stelae carved with his handwriting, and the scenic area also takes in the canal-side streets of Liantang's old town.

rows.name: China Maritime Museum
rows.summary: China's national maritime museum, opened in 2010 beside Dishui Lake in Lingang, in a building whose central roof is shaped like a white sail. Six halls cover navigation history, ships, ports, maritime safety, seafarers and naval history, and the central hall holds a full-size replica of a Ming-dynasty Fujian-type sailing ship modelled on those of Zheng He's fleets. It suits anyone interested in ships and China's seafaring past.

rows.name: Dongping National Forest Park
rows.summary: A 3.55 km² planted forest on reclaimed land in northern Chongming, begun as a state forest farm in 1959 and opened to visitors in 1989. Paths run through dawn redwoods around Shuishan Lake to themed gardens of bamboo, maples, osmanthus, plum and cherry and a wisteria walk about a kilometre long, and there is an RV and camping area with barbecue grounds.

rows.name: Dongtan Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park opened in 2010 at the eastern tip of Chongming Island, beside the Chongming Dongtan bird reserve, which became part of a UNESCO World Heritage site for migratory-bird habitats in 2024. Its wetlands lie on a major migration route for waterbirds, and summer nature programmes cover insects, Chinese alligators and stargazing.

rows.name: Early Buildings of Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Xuhui Campus)
rows.name_zh: 上海交通大学早期建筑
rows.summary: The historic core of the university's Xuhui campus, where Nanyang Public School was founded in 1896, with a group of teaching and administration buildings from 1899 to the 1950s. They include Zhongyuan of 1899, the Old Library of 1919 with its Corinthian columns, the 1925 gymnasium, the 1933 administration hall and New Shangyuan of 1954.

rows.name: Fangta Park (Square Pagoda)
rows.summary: A park laid out from 1978 by the architect Feng Jizhong around the Square Pagoda, a nine-storey brick-and-timber pagoda built under the Northern Song in the late 11th century and the only survivor of the Xingshengjiao Temple. Around it stand a carved brick screen wall of 1370 from the old prefectural City God Temple, the Tianfei Palace moved here from Henan Road in the late 1970s, a Ming hall, and Feng's bamboo-and-thatch pavilion He Lou Xuan, whose restoration won a UNESCO Asia-Pacific heritage award in 2024.

rows.name: Fengjing Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town on Shanghai's south-western border with Zhejiang, founded in the Yuan dynasty, whose old streets of Ming- and Qing-style houses are crossed by dozens of bridges, the oldest being the Yuan-era Zhihe Bridge. Small museums remember local figures such as the painter Cheng Shifa and the cartoonist Ding Cong, and the town is the home of Jinshan peasant painting; the Legoland Shanghai resort, opened in 2025, is nearby.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Socialist Youth League of China (Yuyangli)
rows.name_zh: 中国社会主义青年团中央机关旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngguó Shèhuìzhǔyì Qīngniántuán Zhōngyāng Jīguān Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A shikumen lane house at No. 6 New Yuyangli, off Middle Huaihai Road, where the Shanghai Socialist Youth League was founded in August 1920 and where the league's central office and a Foreign Languages School teaching Russian were based until 1921. The Comintern envoy Voitinsky also lodged here, and the house, with its rooms restored to their 1920–21 arrangement, forms part of a memorial hall opened in 2004.

rows.name: Former Hujiang University Buildings
rows.summary: The former campus of Hujiang University (University of Shanghai), a Baptist missionary college founded in 1906 and closed in 1952, with a campus plan drawn up in 1919 by the American architect Henry Murphy's firm. About 35 of its roughly 60 pre-1949 buildings survive, many in red-brick Collegiate Gothic style, including Yates Hall of 1909, and they are now used by the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology on its riverside Jungong Road campus.

rows.name: Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen
rows.summary: The two-storey grey house on Xiangshan Road (formerly Rue Molière) in the old French Concession where Sun Yat-sen lived with Soong Ching-ling from 1918 to 1924, after four overseas Chinese in Canada bought it for him; Soong stayed on until 1937. The ground-floor reception and dining rooms and the upstairs study and bedrooms are shown as a period home, and a neighbouring exhibition presents Sun's life with documents and objects.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhang Wentian
rows.summary: The birthplace and childhood home of Zhang Wentian, born here in 1900, an early leader of the Chinese Communist Party who served as its general secretary and later as a vice-minister of foreign affairs. The single-storey farmhouse round a three-sided courtyard was built by his family in the late Qing dynasty, and an exhibition room on his life has been open since 1990.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhou Enlai (Zhou Gongguan)
rows.summary: A 1920s Spanish-style garden house at 73 Sinan Road that served in 1946–47 as the Shanghai office of the Chinese Communist Party delegation during its negotiations with the Nationalist government, with Zhou Enlai, Deng Yingchao and Dong Biwu living and working here. Restored as a memorial from 1979, it shows the rooms as they were used at the time, with a bronze statue of Zhou in the courtyard next door, and it reopened in July 2024 after renovation.

rows.name: Fuquanshan Site
rows.summary: A 7.5-metre man-made mound in Chonggu town, raised by people of the Neolithic Liangzhu culture as a high-status cemetery on top of an older Songze settlement and nicknamed the 'Eastern Pyramid'. Excavations since 1982 have recovered more than 2,800 objects, including jade cong, ivory sceptres and a burial with evidence of human sacrifice, and the mound is open to visitors as a heritage site.

rows.name: Gaojiazhuang Eco-Park
rows.summary: An eco-farm leisure park in Gangxi town on Chongming Island, with a lake, gardens, pick-your-own orchards and farm-style accommodation. Boating, cycling and fishing are the usual activities, and it suits families looking for a rural day out.

rows.name: Gongqing Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park beside the Huangpu in north-east Yangpu, planted from the 1950s by volunteer youth on dredged-up riverbank land and opened as a park in 1986. The northern part has woods, lawns and a lake with an amusement area, barbecue grounds and horse riding, while the southern Wanzhu Garden shows dozens of bamboo species among Jiangnan-style buildings.

rows.name: Guangfulin Culture Park
rows.summary: A culture park opened in 2018 on the Guangfulin archaeological site, where excavations since 1999 have uncovered remains from the late Neolithic to the Eastern Zhou, including those of the Guangfulin culture, named in 2006. The site's archaeological museum (opened 2020), shaped like half-buried pots, and the partly water-set Guangfulin Cultural Museum present the finds, while the rest of the park is a newly built complex of temples, halls and lakeside buildings in traditional style.

rows.name: Gucun Park
rows.summary: A large park in Gucun, Baoshan, opened in 2009, with woods, lawns, lakes and themed gardens. It is best known for its cherry trees: the Shanghai Cherry Blossom Festival has been held here every spring since 2011.

rows.name: Guyi Garden
rows.summary: One of Shanghai's five classical gardens, begun in the Ming dynasty's Jiajing era and renamed Guyi Yuan after a new owner bought and enlarged it in 1746, with bamboo planted throughout. Its sights include the Yiye Hall, a lotus pond with a Song-dynasty pagoda, a Tang sutra pillar brought here in the 1950s, and a pavilion built in 1933 with one corner left missing to mark the loss of north-east China in 1931. The garden is also linked with the origins of Nanxiang xiaolongbao soup dumplings.

rows.name: Happy Valley Shanghai
rows.summary: An amusement park of the Happy Valley chain, opened in 2009 in the Sheshan resort area and covering about 65 hectares, according to the city's visitor site. Its seven themed zones hold roller coasters, among them a 60-metre floorless drop coaster and a 1,200-metre wooden coaster, a 30-metre shoot-the-chute water ride and stage shows, and it suits families and thrill-ride fans.

rows.name: Holy Trinity Church
rows.summary: A red-brick Gothic Revival church on Jiujiang Road, designed by Sir George Gilbert Scott and consecrated in 1869, which served Shanghai's English-speaking Anglicans and was known locally as the Red Church. After decades of other uses, including as a cinema during the Cultural Revolution, it was restored and reopened for worship in December 2022 as a church of China's national Protestant bodies.

rows.name: Huating Seawall (Fengxian Section)
rows.summary: A stone sea wall begun in 1726 under the Yongzheng emperor to protect old Huating county from the tides of Hangzhou Bay, built with interlocking 'fish-scale' courses of dressed stone and later strengthened and encased in earth. About 4.5 km of it was uncovered in 1996 when Fengzhe Road, which runs on top of it, was lowered, and the exposed blocks, some carved with builders' names and blessings, can be seen along the roadside in Zhelin town.

rows.name: Jiading Old Town (Zhouqiao)
rows.summary: The historic core of Jiading, a county town since 1217, where canals and old streets around the Zhouqiao bridge lead to the Southern Song Fahua Pagoda, the Ming garden Qiuxia Pu and Huilongtan Park. The scenic area also takes in the Jiading Confucian Temple, founded in 1219 and described by the city as one of China's well-preserved county-level Confucian temples, which reopened in September 2024 after restoration.

rows.name: Jiangnan Sanmin Culture Village
rows.summary: A folk-culture park in central Chongming built around the traditional customs of the Jiangnan region and Chongming's local crafts. Its halls include a Chinese Dragon Palace with a 36-metre dragon made from about 5,000 carved boards, museums of Chongming homespun cloth, carved boards and longevity customs, and a street of small halls showing old household objects.

rows.name: Jin Mao Tower 88th-Floor Observation Deck
rows.summary: The observation deck on the 88th floor of the 420-metre Jin Mao Tower, a pagoda-inspired Lujiazui skyscraper completed in 1999, about 340 metres above the street. Besides views of the Bund and the taller towers next door, it looks straight down into the Grand Hyatt hotel's atrium, which rises through the building's upper floors, and an open-air skywalk runs round the outside of the tower at this level.

rows.name: Jinshan City Beach
rows.summary: A man-made beach on the north shore of Hangzhou Bay, opened in 2006 between two older seaside bathing grounds, with about 160,000 square metres of sand, a swimming area and a 1.5 km seaside promenade. Swimming is open from late June to early September; at other times visitors come for the sand, boat rides, horse riding, go-karts and beach sports, and it suits a family day by the sea.

rows.name: Jinshanzui Fishing Village
rows.summary: A working fishing village on the north shore of Hangzhou Bay, said to be the only village in Shanghai that still sends boats out to sea. Visitors walk Jinshanzui Old Street and eat seafood at the restaurants of its seafood street and food court, and it suits a relaxed seaside lunch combined with Jinshan City Beach.

rows.name: Jinze Ancient Town
rows.summary: A small canal town in western Qingpu near the Jiangsu and Zhejiang borders, once known for its many temples and bridges, of which 21 old bridges survive. The Puji and Wan'an bridges, both from the Southern Song dynasty, are regarded as the oldest stone arch bridges in Shanghai, and Yihao Temple beside the old streets was founded in 1260.

rows.name: Langxia Country Park
rows.summary: A country park among farmland and villages in Langxia town, southern Jinshan, opened in 2015, where white-walled, black-tiled houses in local style line the lanes and events such as half marathons and cycling races are held through the year. It takes in Shantang Old Street, a village street whose bridge crosses into Zhejiang, and farmhouse restaurants and guesthouses in Zhonghua village, and suits a day out in the countryside.

rows.name: Lianyi Loquat Park
rows.summary: A farm park on the edge of Qingpu New City named after its large loquat orchard, where the fruit can be picked during a season of about three weeks in early summer. Greenhouses grow tropical fruit such as wax apples, dragon fruit and mangoes for picking, and a farm restaurant reached through the orchard, wooden cabins and an RV campsite make it a family weekend spot.

rows.name: Longhua Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A large memorial park beside Longhua Temple that takes in the former Songhu Garrison Command of the Nationalist government, where Communists and left-wing activists were imprisoned and executed between 1927 and 1937, among them 24 people shot on 7 February 1931, including five writers of the League of Left-Wing Writers. The listed memorial site in its north-east corner keeps the 1920 gatehouse, the men's and women's cell blocks and the execution ground, and a memorial hall opened in 1997 presents this history.

rows.name: Longhua Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal seven-storey brick-and-wood pagoda whose main structure was built in 977 under the Wuyue king Qian Chu, in the early Northern Song, standing across Longhua Road from Longhua Temple. Later additions were removed in the 1950s and the pagoda was restored to its Song form; it is not open to climb, and is usually seen together with a visit to the temple.

rows.name: Madame Tussauds Shanghai
rows.summary: A branch of the Madame Tussauds wax museum chain on the tenth floor of the New World department store at the People's Square end of Nanjing Road, opened in 2006. Its figures of Chinese and international film and music stars, athletes, scientists and world leaders are arranged in themed zones, and it suits families and fans of Chinese pop culture.

rows.name: Marble Hall (China Welfare Institute Children's Palace)
rows.summary: A mansion completed in 1924 for the British Jewish businessman Sir Elly Kadoorie, nicknamed the Marble Hall for the Italian marble on its walls, floors and staircases. Since 1953 it has housed the China Welfare Institute Children's Palace, founded by Soong Ching Ling, so visitors see the building from outside on Yan'an West Road.

rows.name: Minhang Cultural Park
rows.summary: A landscaped city park in Qibao, Minhang, opened in stages from 2013, with lawns, a lake and wetland, magnolia and camphor groves and an orchard. It also contains the Minhang Museum, opened in 2019, whose permanent galleries include one on the Maqiao culture of about 3,900 to 3,200 years ago, first identified at Maqiao in the same district, and the Powerlong Museum of art, opened in 2017.

rows.name: Moller Villa
rows.summary: A Scandinavian-style villa enlarged from an older house for the Swedish-born shipping owner Eric Moller and finished in the mid-1930s, with steep brown-tiled gables, spires and turrets behind a walled garden. Since 2002 it has been run as the Hengshan Moller Villa hotel, so non-guests see it from the street and the hotel lobby.

rows.name: Moon Lake Sculpture Park
rows.summary: A sculpture park in the Sheshan resort area, laid out around the artificial Moon Lake with shores themed on the four seasons. Sculptures by artists from China and abroad stand in the lawns and woods, and the park suits an unhurried walk combined with a visit to the Sheshan hills nearby.

rows.name: Nanxiang Old Town
rows.summary: An old market town known as the home of xiaolongbao soup dumplings, whose restored old streets centre on the Twin Pagodas, a pair of small Five Dynasties–Northern Song brick pagodas imitating timber buildings that face each other across a street. In front of them are two ancient wells excavated during the street renovation that began in 2008, and nearby is Liuyun Chan Temple, still widely called Yunxiang Temple, rebuilt in 1998–2004 on the site of the old Nanxiang Temple.

rows.name: North Bund International Cruise Terminal
