rows.summary: Winged lions (bixie), qilin, steles on stone tortoises and fluted columns that once lined the spirit ways to the tombs of Southern Dynasties emperors and princes of the 5th and 6th centuries, still standing in the open at sites scattered across Nanjing's eastern and southern suburbs, mostly in Qixia and Jiangning districts. The densest group is at Ganjiaxiang in Qixia District, where the carvings from the tombs of three Liang-dynasty princes, Xiao Xiu, Xiao Dan and Xiao Hui, stand within a few hundred metres of each other, Xiao Xiu's ensemble beside the gate of a primary school and the other two in a small park. The winged lion is Nanjing's city emblem, modelled on the one at the tomb of Xiao Jing about a kilometre to the south-west.

rows.name: Taiping Murals on Tangzi Street
rows.summary: A late-Qing courtyard house on Tangzi Street, just inside Hanzhongmen, which the Taiping rebels took over after capturing Nanjing in 1853 and used as an office and later a minor prince's residence, painting its walls and wooden partitions. Eighteen paintings survive in the main and rear halls, landscapes, birds, flowers and animals in a bold folk style with no human figures, one of them a watchtower guarding the Yangtze with warships below. The house serves as the Taiping mural art museum, which also shows copies of Taiping murals from Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui.

rows.name: Tangshan Zhiqing Lake Resort
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort in the Tangshan spa area east of Nanjing, developed over more than a decade, combining hotels, outdoor hot springs and a wildlife park. Dozens of pools, among them waterfall pools, mineral-salt and stone-slab baths and fish pools, are spread over a wooded hillside facing the lake. Its wildlife world has giant pandas, elephants, giraffes, zebras, primates and parrots and a drive-through section, and with a children's play centre and a water park the resort is aimed at families and short stays.

rows.name: Tianshengqiao, Lishui
rows.summary: A natural-looking stone bridge over the Yanzhi River, a canal that the Ming founder Zhu Yuanzhang had a large labour force cut through a ridge in Lishui in 1393–1395, to link the Qinhuai River with the Taihu waterways for grain transport. Instead of cutting through the whole hill, the workers left a band of rock in place and chiselled the channel beneath it, giving the 'heaven-made bridge' its name; a second such bridge further north collapsed in 1571. The bridge, high above the water in the steep-sided cutting, is the centre of a scenic area along the canal and one of the New Forty-Eight Views of Jinling.

rows.name: Tomb of the King of Boni
rows.summary: The tomb of Maharaja Karna (Abdul Majid Hassan), ruler of Boni, a state on Borneo sometimes considered a forerunner of modern Brunei, who came to the Ming court in Nanjing in 1408 and died there that autumn at the age of 28. The Yongle Emperor had him buried with honours south of the city, and a spirit way lined with stone warriors, grooms, horses, tigers and rams leads to the grave mound; a small exhibition room was added in the early 2000s. Forgotten after the Ming, the tomb was rediscovered in 1958 and is one of only two tombs of foreign rulers in China.

rows.name: Two Mausoleums of the Southern Tang
rows.summary: The underground tombs of the first two rulers of the Southern Tang, a 10th-century kingdom based in Nanjing, at the southern foot of Zutang Hill: the Qinling of the founder Li Bian and the Shunling of his son Li Jing. Excavated from 1950, both are built of brick and stone in imitation of timber halls, with front, middle and rear chambers flanked by side rooms, and visitors can walk through them and see a small exhibition hall. The third and last ruler, the poet Li Yu, died in captivity in Luoyang and is not buried here.

rows.name: University of Nanking Campus
rows.summary: The former campus of the University of Nanking, a university sponsored by American churches, laid out in the 1910s on a north–south axis in the manner of an American campus, with buildings that pair Chinese hip roofs and grey-brick walls with Western structures and materials. Its landmark is the tower-topped North Building of 1919, and around it stand the chapel of 1918, now the university auditorium, and the 1936 library by Yang Tingbao, now Nanjing University's history museum. Since 1952 it has been part of Nanjing University's Gulou campus.

rows.name: Xuanwu Lake
rows.summary: A lake of about 10 km round just north of the old city, bounded on the west and south by the Ming city wall and looking east to Purple Mountain, which has been an imperial park and pleasure ground since the Six Dynasties. Five islands, Huanzhou, Yingzhou, Lingzhou, Liangzhou and Cuizhou, are linked by causeways and bridges and planted with willows, cherry trees and lotus; in the Ming dynasty the empire's household registers were archived on Liangzhou. It became a public park after Xuanwu Gate (then Fengrun Gate) was opened in the wall in 1909 for the Nanyang Industrial Exposition.

rows.name: Yangliu Village Historic Buildings
rows.summary: A village of Qing-dynasty mansions at Hushu in southern Jiangning, built mainly in the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns between Machang Hill and Yangliu Lake; of its 36 original compounds, 17 were still fairly complete when surveyed in 1982. They are deep multi-courtyard houses behind high walls, with tall gate towers carved in brick with figures, flowers and animals and unpainted carved beams inside. The best-preserved group, three linked halls at the west end of the village built by the Zhu family in the Qianlong era, has been restored to house the Jiangning folk-custom museum and an intangible-heritage exhibition.

rows.name: Yangshan Quarry
rows.summary: An ancient stone quarry in the hills near Tangshan where, from 1405, the Yongle Emperor had a vast memorial stele cut for his father's tomb, the Ming Xiaoling, using a huge labour force. The three parts, the tortoise base, the tablet and its crowning head, were never moved because they were far too heavy, and they still lie where they were carved, partly freed from the bedrock; a much smaller stele was set up at the tomb instead. The quarry is the centre of a 4A scenic area branded the Ming Culture Village.

rows.name: Yangtze River Crossing Victory Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum on the Yangtze waterfront where the Qinhuai River enters it, about the April 1949 campaign in which the People's Liberation Army crossed the Yangtze and took Nanjing, then the Nationalist capital. Its galleries tell the story through photographs, documents, objects and reconstructed scenes, and the Jingdian, a small steam launch that ferried troops across the river, is displayed in the forecourt. The Yangtze Crossing Victory Monument of 1979 stands about 1.7 km to the north-east on Rehe Road Square.

rows.name: Youzi Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded range of low hills in eastern Gaochun, whose name ('the wanderer's mountain') comes from a tradition, recorded in a Song-dynasty gazetteer, that Confucius passed this way on his journey to the state of Chu. The scenic area combines forest walks with a hall honouring Confucius and a martyrs' cemetery, while the nearby old village of Qiqiao has been home to descendants of Confucius since the Southern Song.

rows.name: Yuejiang Tower
rows.summary: A seven-storey tower in Ming style on Lion Hill in north-western Nanjing, completed in 2001 to realise a building that the Hongwu Emperor ordered in 1374 but never finished, and which was known for six centuries only through essays such as Song Lian's 'Record of Yuejiang Tower'. From the top there are views north over the Yangtze and south over the city, and inside are murals including scenes of Zheng He's voyages. Lion Hill, inside the Ming city wall near Yijiang Gate, also has old caves said to have hidden troops.

rows.name: Yuhuatai (Rain Flower Terrace)
rows.summary: A ridge of low hills just south of Zhonghua Gate, named after a legend that flowers rained from the sky when the monk Yunguang preached here in 503. From 1927 to 1949 it was an execution ground where many Communists and other prisoners were killed, and Japanese war criminals were executed here after the war; since 1950 it has been a memorial park with a martyrs' monument on the main hill, a large sculpture group and a memorial hall. The wider scenic area also holds the tomb of the Ming scholar Fang Xiaoru, the Gaozuo Temple, a museum of the coloured 'rain-flower' pebbles and a spring once ranked second south of the Yangtze.

rows.name: Yunyougu Scenic Area
rows.summary: A leisure park in the hills of Tangquan, at the western edge of Pukou District, that combines countryside scenery with a farm-themed amusement park. It has fairground rides such as a Ferris wheel, a carousel and go-karts, as well as a glass footbridge. It suits families with children on a day out from Nanjing.

rows.name: Zhan Garden
rows.summary: Regarded as the oldest surviving private garden in Nanjing, it was begun in the Ming dynasty by a descendant of the founding general Xu Da in the grounds of the family mansion, and named after an inscription by the Qianlong Emperor, who stayed here. Restored in the 1960s under the architect Liu Dunzhen, its western part has rockeries, covered walkways and a main hall surrounded by water on three sides. The eastern part houses the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom History Museum, recalling the garden's use by Taiping leaders after they took the city in 1853.

rows.name: Dasheng No. 3 Cotton Mill
rows.summary: Zhang Jian opened his third Dasheng cotton mill here in 1921, at Sanchang near the Yangtze east of Haimen. Its clock tower, head office and raw-cotton warehouse survive, were restored between 2021 and 2023, and the tower again strikes the hours. They now form part of a heritage walk with the old Qinglong ferry port on the Yangtze, and together with the first mill at Tangzha in Nantong they make up the national heritage site of the Dasheng Cotton Mills.

rows.name: Dieshiqiao Home Textile Market
rows.summary: Diesiqiao in Sanxing town is a vast wholesale market district for bedding, curtains and other home textiles, built up over some forty years and described by provincial media as the world's largest home-textile cluster, with more than 2,500 firms. The tourist area pairs the market halls, where visitors can buy direct from traders, with an exhibition hall on the trade, and a local brand opened a bedding museum in the same town in 2025.

rows.name: Hai'an Museum and Han's Mansion
rows.summary: Hai'an Museum is spread over a modern main building and Han's Mansion (Han Gongguan), the 1906 family residence of Han Guojun, a late-Qing official who governed Jiangsu in 1913 and again in 1922–25 and in old age refused to serve the Japanese-backed regime. The mansion is a compound of late-Qing-style halls and courtyards, and the main building holds the museum's displays on local history and archaeology.

rows.name: Haohe River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Haohe is Nantong's old city moat, dug by the 10th century and still ringing the historic centre in a gourd-shaped loop about 10 km long that widens from 10 m to more than 200 m. Its banks link Tianning Temple, the Song-era city-wall remains at Beijige, the Ming Wenfeng Pagoda, Nantong Museum and the old Sijie and Xinanying lanes, with parks and smaller museums in between. Boat trips run day and night, and an evening show of lights and live performance along the boat route was added in 2026.

rows.name: Langshan (Wolf Hill)
rows.summary: Langshan is a low hill on the Yangtze shore south of Nantong, the highest of five small hills grouped as a scenic area and counted among China's eight lesser Buddhist mountains. Guangjiao Temple, founded in 669 by the monk Sengjia and dedicated to the bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta (Dashizhi), spreads its halls from the foot to the summit, which is crowned by the Song-dynasty Zhiyun Pagoda. Old ginkgos, cliff inscriptions and the tomb of the Tang poet Luo Binwang line the climb, and a Catholic pilgrimage church stands on the hill's north side.

rows.name: Nantong Forest Safari Park
rows.summary: A large wildlife park on Nantong's northern outskirts covering about 2 km², which the city says holds nearly 20,000 animals of some 300 species. Two giant pandas from Chengdu have lived here since 2019, and visitors can tour the grounds on foot, by bike or by boat. It forms part of the Sendi resort, which adds a water park, an indoor snow and ocean park opened in 2026 and a hotel, and the zoo has offered night tours in summer.

rows.name: Nantong Museum
rows.summary: Founded in 1905 by the industrialist and educator Zhang Jian, Nantong Museum is regarded as the first public museum set up by a Chinese founder, laid out as a garden with exhibition halls among lawns, ponds and trees. Its early South, Central and North halls, the oldest from 1906, still stand beside a new main building of 2005 by the architect Wu Liangyong, and the collections cover local history, art and natural history. The grounds also take in Haonan Villa, Zhang Jian's 1910s house, which mixes Western columns and fireplaces with a Chinese courtyard garden and now tells his life story.

rows.name: Qingdun Neolithic Site
rows.summary: Villagers digging a canal in 1973 found this settlement of about 5,000 years ago, and three seasons of excavation in the late 1970s followed; the city calls it the best-preserved Neolithic site in the eastern Jianghuai plain. Finds include a pottery axe with its handle and a carved deer antler with markings likened to the eight trigrams, and the Qingdun Site Museum just north of the site uses objects, photos and video to show daily life of the time.

rows.name: Red 14th Army Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This memorial hall in a park on the east side of Rugao covers the 14th Red Army, formed in 1930 from Communist guerrilla bands in the Nantong, Haimen, Rugao and Taixing countryside and formally founded at a rally south-west of Rugao that April. Its commander He Kun was killed within weeks, and Nationalist forces had broken up the base by 1931; the exhibits follow the army's short history.

rows.name: Rugao Bonsai Park (Penjing Daguan)
rows.summary: Rugao calls itself China's capital of flowers and bonsai, and its Rugao school, known for trees shaped with a 'cloud head, rain feet and beauty's waist', is counted among the country's seven main schools of penjing. This scenic area on the city's southern side shows the craft at scale, with displays built around the Jiangsu Bonsai Museum, and bonsai traders line nearby streets.

rows.name: Seyuan Garden
rows.summary: Seyuan is a large wooded park in Nantong's southern suburbs, counted by the city as one of its biggest botanical gardens and the burial place of Zhang Jian (1853–1926), the scholar-industrialist who built the Dasheng cotton mills and Nantong Museum. The tomb was wrecked during the Cultural Revolution and rebuilt in 1983, with his bronze statue put back in 1985, when the grounds took the name Seyuan after his art name Se'an. Each spring the park holds a tulip festival; the 2026 edition planted 130,000 tulips of 23 varieties.

rows.name: Shuihui Garden
rows.summary: Shuihui Garden in Rugao was begun by the Mao family in the late Ming and became the home of the scholar Mao Xiang (Mao Pijiang) and the courtesan Dong Xiaowan, whose romance made it famous. Built around water in an Anhui-influenced style, it centres on the Shuiming Lou, a two-storey boat-like pavilion by the Xibo Pond added in the Qianlong era. The wider scenic area also holds a garden of Rugao-style bonsai, including a cypress said to be 1,000 years old, and the Rugao Longevity Museum.

rows.name: Tianning Temple, Nantong
rows.summary: Founded in the Tang dynasty as Baoen Guangxiao Temple and given its present name in 1457, Tianning Temple is the old heart of Nantong: the 10th-century city was laid out on an axis running from the temple to Langshan. Its Song-style main hall and the Guangxiao Pagoda, an octagonal brick-and-timber tower of five storeys first built in the Tang and rebuilt in the Song, stand with four old ginkgos and two Ming wells. In the late Qing Zhang Jian turned the eastern part of the grounds into a school, today's Nantong High School.

rows.name: Tonghai Land Reclamation Company Site
rows.summary: Zhang Jian founded the Tonghai Land Reclamation Company here in 1901 to turn coastal salt flats into cotton farms for his Dasheng mills; it is regarded as China's first agricultural joint-stock company. The company compound was rebuilt on its old site from 2021 in late-Qing and Republican style, with a main hall, a farm-affairs hall, wing rooms and a grain-drying yard, and exhibitions of photos, film and objects tell the company's story.

rows.name: Wonderful Farm
rows.summary: A farm-themed leisure park of about 53 hectares on Nantong's northern edge, opened in October 2021 and rated 4A in December 2024. Its seven themed sections build farming into family entertainment, with sightseeing fields, hands-on farm work, nature lessons and folk-craft activities, and there is a hot-spring hotel, guesthouses and restaurants. It suits families with young children and sits next door to Nantong Forest Safari Park.

rows.name: Zhouji Green Expo Park
rows.summary: A botanical park in Nantong's Tongzhou district that the city says holds more than 8,000 plant species gathered from around the world. It was the first scenic area in Tongzhou to be rated 4A and is mainly visited for its seasonal flowers and autumn colour.

rows.name: China Poplar Museum, Siyang
rows.summary: A museum in Siyang county devoted to the poplar. The county began planting poplars introduced from Italy in 1972 and, with large plantations, promotes itself as China's 'hometown of poplars'; the museum stands on the southern side of the county town.

rows.name: Dragon King Temple Palace, Zaohe
rows.summary: A temple to the Dragon King beside the Grand Canal and Luoma Lake in Zaohe town, first built in the Kangxi reign and rebuilt in 1727 and 1813, where the Qianlong Emperor lodged on five of his six southern tours; it is popularly called the Qianlong Palace. Three courtyards on a central axis lead past a stage and the imperial stele pavilion to the double-eaved Dragon King Hall and the Hall of Yu the Great. The site, which includes the remains of the imperial wharf, is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Hongze Lake Wetland, Sihong
rows.summary: A wetland scenic area in the shallows of north-western Hongze Lake, China's fourth-largest freshwater lake, forming part of the Sihong Hongze Lake Wetland National Nature Reserve. Boats thread through a maze of reed channels where waterbirds gather, and there is a wetland science museum, a dawn-redwood forest and a VR ride on the legend of Sizhou, the city the lake swallowed.

rows.name: Lakeside Park, Suqian
rows.summary: A public park on the southern shore of Luoma Lake, in Suqian's Hubin new district and the Luoma Lake tourist resort. By 2025 it had been upgraded together with neighbouring lakeside gardens into an open shoreline park more than 10 km long, and it is a place for a lakeside walk rather than a sight in its own right.

rows.name: Santai Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on low wooded hills on the northern edge of Suqian city. Seasonal flower fields of verbena, cosmos and spider flowers, a mist-spraying boardwalk, a petting area for small animals and guesthouses make it a popular family outing.

rows.name: Shennong Era Agricultural Park, Yanghe
rows.summary: A modern agricultural theme park near Yanghe town, named after Shennong, the legendary inventor of farming. Eight themed pavilions show vegetables, flowers, fruit trees and plant factories grown with modern farming technology, and there is a petting area with small animals and family activities such as cooking and crafts.

rows.name: Shuanggou Distillery, Sihong
rows.summary: A visitor area at the Shuanggou distillery in Shuanggou town, home of Shuanggou Daqu, a strong-aroma baijiu. The route takes in the historic brewing core, a museum on the site of a Song and Yuan-dynasty distillery, the large modern production halls and packaging centre, and a re-created Ming-style hand-brewing scene where visitors can try mixing the fermented grain.

rows.name: Xiang Yu's Hometown
rows.summary: A park in southern Suqian on the traditional birthplace of Xiang Yu, the Chu warlord who fought Liu Bang for control of China after the fall of the Qin and died in 202 BC. A locust tree said to have been planted by Xiang Yu stands among halls and gardens such as the Xiang residence and the Six Arts Garden, which present his life and Western Chu culture. Daily performances include Chu dances, guqin music and re-enactments of the Battle of Julu and the Feast at Hongmen.

rows.name: Xuefeng Park, Suqian
rows.summary: A memorial park of about 21 hectares in Suqian city, opened in 2007 in memory of Peng Xuefeng, a New Fourth Army commander killed in 1944, and others who fought in the War of Resistance against Japan. At its centre the Peng Xuefeng Memorial Hall displays about 400 photographs and more than 100 objects such as mortars, machine guns and a sword, with an exhibition upstairs on clean government in the wartime base area.

rows.name: Yanghe Distillery
rows.summary: The home of Yanghe, one of China's largest baijiu makers, in Yanghe town south-east of Suqian, where a visitor route runs through the working distillery. Stops include the Meirenquan spring, a hand-made production area, the old brewing site, a group of Ming and Qing fermentation pits and the underground cellar dug between 1960 and 1975, now a national heritage site.

rows.name: Baimajian Eco-Park
rows.summary: A park of about 1.5 km² in the wooded hills on Suzhou's western edge, west of Fengqiao in the High-tech District, which the city calls the district's 'green lung'; legend makes the valley a horse farm of the King of Wu. Its centre is Longchi (Dragon Pond), a valley lake with a long boardwalk along the water, a waterfall and a shallow stream for paddling, and hiking paths continue across the hills.

rows.name: Beisi Pagoda (Bao'en Temple)
rows.summary: The pagoda of Bao'en Temple in the north of Suzhou's old city, a nine-storey, eight-sided brick-and-timber tower about 76 m high with wooden eaves and balconies on every floor. The temple is said to have been founded by Sun Quan of Wu in the 3rd century, and the present pagoda was rebuilt in 1153, under the Southern Song; its spire was damaged in the earthquake of 1918. The temple grounds also hold the Hall of Seven Buddhas and a small plum garden.

rows.name: Caiyi Hall, Weng Family Residence
rows.summary: The main hall of the Weng family residence in Changshu's old town, a late-Ming building whose beams and pillars carry painted decoration regarded as a leading example of Suzhou-style colour painting. The house was bought in 1833 by the Qing official Weng Xincun, and his son Weng Tonghe, later a senior official at the Qing court, grew up here. The residence is now the Weng Tonghe Memorial Museum.

rows.name: Canglang Pavilion
rows.summary: The oldest of Suzhou's surviving classical gardens, laid out in the mid-1040s by the Song poet Su Shunqin on the site of a Five Dynasties garden and named after a line in the Songs of Chu about the clear and muddy waters of the Canglang. The garden centres on a wooded earth-and-rock hill, with halls and covered walks around it and a gallery along the canal outside that 'borrows' the water into the view. It also has a hall of stone-carved portraits of famous people linked with Suzhou and a great variety of patterned lattice windows, and is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Caoxieshan Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement near Yangcheng Lake, first inhabited about 6,000 years ago, whose deep layers record the Majiabang, Songze and Liangzhu cultures in one continuous sequence. Digs uncovered carbonised rice, early textile fragments and a Liangzhu grave with jade cong, and in 1992–1995 Chinese and Japanese archaeologists found paddy fields with irrigation channels from about 6,000 years ago. An archaeological park opened here in 2022 with displays of finds, reconstructed prehistoric paddies and excavated remains.

rows.name: Carved Building (Chunzai Lou)
rows.summary: A mansion in Dongshan town on the Dongshan peninsula, formally named Chunzai Lou, built in 1924 by craftsmen of the Xiangshan building tradition and covered with intricate carved decoration. It shows off the Xiangshan builders' techniques, now on China's national list of intangible heritage, and has served as a set for many films and television series, among them the Hollywood production Pavilion of Women. It is one of the named sights of the Lake Tai scenic area on Dongshan.

rows.name: China Embroidery Art Museum, Zhenhu
rows.summary: A museum of embroidery in Zhenhu, a lakeside subdistrict west of Suzhou known for Su embroidery, where more than 8,000 local people work as embroiderers. Its galleries cover China's four famous regional embroidery styles, the work of master embroiderers, the history of the craft and Zhenhu's own embroidery, and it holds special exhibitions, has embroiderers demonstrating their work and lets visitors try stitching.

rows.name: Chuihong Bridge Ruins
rows.summary: The surviving end sections of the Chuihong Bridge, which crossed the Wusong River outside the east gate of old Wujiang. First built of timber in 1048, it was rebuilt in 1324 as a long multi-arch stone bridge with a pavilion at its centre, and stood until it collapsed on 2 May 1967. Its remaining arches were excavated and restored in 1983 and 2005 and stand in the Chuihong Ruins Park, laid out in 1995.

rows.name: Couple's Retreat Garden
rows.summary: A garden on the east edge of the Pingjiang historic district, surrounded by canals on three sides, rebuilt in the late 19th century by the retired official Shen Bingcheng, who withdrew here with his wife; 'ou' means a pair, hence the name. Unusually, two gardens flank the central residence: the eastern one, the finer, is built around a rugged yellow-stone rockery surviving from an 18th-century garden on the site, while the western one uses Taihu rocks. It is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Dayangshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park covering Yangshan, a wooded range of hills on the north-western edge of Suzhou whose main peak, Jianque Peak (338 m), is the second-highest around the city. The listed scenic area has two parts with separate entrances: a botanical garden at the foot of the hills, which stages seasonal flower shows, and Wenshu Temple, a Buddhist temple on the hillside.

rows.name: Dongmiao Bridge
rows.summary: A bridge from the Southern Song dynasty (1127–1279) over the Henggu waterway in Dongmiaoqiao village, Qidu, near the southern shore of Lake Tai in Wujiang district. It was listed as a national monument in 2013 and is a quiet rural detour rather than a sight in its own right.

rows.name: Dongshan Ming Residences (Mingshan Hall)
rows.summary: Three old mansions on the Dongshan peninsula of Lake Tai listed together as a national monument: Huaiyin Hall and Mingshan Hall in Yangwan village, and Ningde Hall in Wengxiang, home of the late-Ming physician Wu Youxing. Mingshan Hall, a late-Ming or early-Qing house with a great hall, flower hall, study and Buddhist chapel, is known for the brick-carved gateway and screen walls in front of its main hall, and opened to visitors after repairs in 2014. Ningde Hall keeps a rich set of Suzhou-style painted decoration inside.

rows.name: Fangta Pagoda (Chongjiao Xingfu Temple Pagoda)
rows.summary: Changshu's 'Square Pagoda' is the surviving pagoda of Chongjiao Xingfu Temple, begun in 1130 and rebuilt in 1272. It is square in plan, with nine storeys of brick and projecting wooden eaves that give it a gently curved outline, and has wooden stairs inside; its ground-floor gallery was destroyed by bombing during the war against Japan. It stands in Fangta Park, a garden laid out on the former temple site at the eastern end of the old town.

rows.name: Former Residence of Liu Yazi
rows.summary: A Qing mansion in Lili old town, Cifu Hall, built for Zhou Yuanli, a Minister of Works under the Qianlong Emperor; the poet and political activist Liu Yazi (1887–1958) rented two of its six ranges from 1922. Liu led the Southern Society, a literary group that backed Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary alliance against the Qing, and later took part in Kuomintang and China Democratic League politics. The house is now the Liu Yazi Memorial Hall, with exhibitions on his life and family and manuscripts of Southern Society members.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhao Yongxian (Yushan Guqin Museum)
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty house in Changshu's old town that belonged to the Ming official Zhao Yongxian (1535–1596) and his son Zhao Qimei, both noted book collectors. The surviving central range keeps its gatehouse, front hall and rear hall, with fine wood carving and Suzhou-style painted beams, together with the Maiwang Library, once one of the best-known private libraries of the lower Yangtze. It now houses a museum of the Yushan school of guqin, the seven-string zither tradition named after Changshu's hill.

rows.name: Garden of Cultivation
rows.summary: A scholar's garden of the Ming dynasty hidden in a lane near Changmen gate, built in 1541 by Yuan Zugeng and later owned by Wen Zhenmeng, great-grandson of the painter Wen Zhengming, and by the scholar-official Jiang Cai, whose son gave it its present name. It keeps much of its late-Ming layout: a broad pond with halls and a large waterside pavilion on the north bank, a rocky hill with cliffs and paths on the south, and the small Ruyu Pavilion, itself a Ming structure, on the east shore. It was little known before it was added to the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site in 2000.

rows.name: Grand Canal at Pingwang (Wujiang Canal Culture Area)
rows.summary: The old town of Pingwang in southern Wujiang, where the Ditang canal from Huzhou joins the Grand Canal at Yingdou Lake, rated a 4A scenic area in 2023. Its small core, about 0.2 km², keeps the linear layout of a canal-side market town, and a walkway lined with canal-history steles leads from the lakeshore into the old lanes. It is a quiet stop for travellers following the canal between Suzhou and Zhejiang.

rows.name: Guangfu Scenic Area (Xiangxuehai & Situ Temple)
rows.summary: A group of sights around Guangfu, a town in the hills by Lake Tai west of Suzhou, managed as one scenic area with its visitor centre beside Situ Temple. The Xiangxuehai plum groves on the hillsides have long been ranked among China's classic places for plum blossom, admired by the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors and planted with more than 20 varieties; Situ Temple is known for four ancient cypresses nicknamed Pure, Rare, Ancient and Strange. The plum season in February and March is the main time to go.

rows.name: Hanshan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Fengqiao, about 5 km west of Suzhou's old city, facing the old canal; tradition dates it to 502–519 and names it after the legendary monk-poet Hanshan, said to have been its abbot in the Tang. It owes its fame to Zhang Ji's Tang poem 'A Night Mooring by Maple Bridge', in which the temple's midnight bell reaches a traveller's boat. Destroyed in 1860 during the Taiping war, it was later rebuilt and today has a bell tower and a large bronze bell cast in 2007.

rows.name: Jiachen Lane Brick Pagoda
rows.summary: A miniature five-storey, eight-sided brick pagoda that imitates a timber pagoda in the details of its eaves, brackets, doors and windows. Long thought to be Song, since it appears on the city map of 1229, it has bricks that tests date to the late Tang or Five Dynasties; it is the last of the small brick pagodas once recorded in the old city. Hemmed in by houses until 1993, it now stands in a small courtyard of its own.

rows.name: Jingsi Garden
rows.summary: A large private garden in classical Suzhou style, built over ten years from 1993 by a local entrepreneur in the countryside of Wujiang. Its centrepiece is the Qingyun Peak, a tall Lingbi rock from Anhui pierced by many holes, set among ponds and pavilions. It is a modern creation rather than a historic garden.

rows.name: Jinji Lake
rows.summary: The lake at the centre of Suzhou Industrial Park, the modern district east of the old city, turned from a shallow marshy lake into a ring of waterfront parks and promenades under a landscape plan of 2003. Around it stand the Suzhou Culture and Arts Centre, the International Expo Centre and towers such as the Gate of the Orient, while the late-Qing Ligongdi causeway is lined with restaurants and a rebuilt Ferris wheel on the east shore reopened in 2025 as the Suzhou Eye. A footpath runs right round the lake.

rows.name: Jinxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town among the lakes of south-west Kunshan, called Chenmu from 1512 until 1992 after the 'water tomb' of a Song imperial consort, Consort Chen, on an islet in Wubao Lake beside the town. Old stone bridges, among them a ten-arch bridge, and a covered bridge cross its waterways, and the town calls itself a 'home of folk museums' for its many small museums of private collections. It lies a few kilometres from Zhouzhuang and is easily combined with it.

rows.name: Jiyang Lake Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A large lake park on the southern side of central Zhangjiagang, with lakeside paths, gardens and lawns around the water. A small amusement park, Happy World, occupies one corner of the grounds. It suits a stroll or a family outing for visitors staying in the city.

rows.name: Jusha Pagoda, Meili
rows.summary: A brick pagoda in the small town of Meili, north-east of Changshu, first built in the Southern Song dynasty between 1131 and 1162. It is octagonal, seven storeys tall and ringed with wooden eaves; a typhoon toppled its top in 1911 and left it leaning, and it was straightened in 1993 and restored to its Song form in 1997. Jusha Garden, a small park laid out around the pagoda at that time, makes up the listed scenic area.

rows.name: Lake Tai Scenic Area, Wuzhong (Dongshan, Qionglong & Wangshan)
rows.summary: A 5A scenic area on the eastern shore of Lake Tai in Suzhou's Wuzhong district, made up of three separate parts: the Dongshan peninsula, Qionglong Mountain and the Wangshan valley. On Dongshan it takes in Luxiang, a lakeside village with a Ming stone-paved street, three memorial arches and the hall of the Ming grand secretary Wang Ao, as well as Sanshan Island and the Qi Garden, built on the shore in 1933 to mark the Kangxi Emperor's landing there in 1699. Qionglong, the highest hill around Suzhou, is where tradition says Sun Tzu wrote The Art of War, and Wangshan is a rural valley of farm-stay villages with Baohua Temple.

rows.name: Lili Ancient Town
rows.summary: A well-preserved canal town in the south-east of Wujiang near the borders with Shanghai and Zhejiang, laid out as one canal with a street along each bank. Both banks are lined with two-storey Ming and Qing buildings whose shopfronts and halls run on without a break along the water. Among them is the house the poet Liu Yazi rented from 1922, once a Qing minister's mansion and now a memorial museum.

rows.name: Lingering Garden
rows.summary: One of Suzhou's largest classical gardens, begun in 1593 by the official Xu Taishi outside Changmen gate, rebuilt by Liu Shu in 1794–1798 and given its present form and name by Sheng Kang in 1873–1876. Four sections — a central pond with its hill and pavilions, halls and courtyards packed closely to the east, and further sections to the west and north — are linked by long covered walkways set with stone calligraphy tablets. Its best-known feature is the Cloud-Capped Peak, a tall Taihu rock said to come from the Song emperor Huizong's collection; it is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Lion Grove Garden
rows.summary: A garden founded in 1342 by disciples of the Chan monk Tianru as part of a Buddhist monastery, named after its Taihu rocks, which are said to look like lions. Its centre is a huge labyrinth of rockery, with paths, tunnels and caves that climb and twist so that visitors can see each other but take a long way round to meet; halls and a pavilion in the lake surround it. In 1917 it was bought by Bei Runsheng, a great-uncle of the architect I. M. Pei, and it is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Luzhi Ancient Town & Baosheng Temple
rows.summary: A canal town east of Suzhou whose old quarter keeps Ming- and Qing-style houses along its waterways and many old stone bridges, a few from the Song and Ming dynasties; in 2003 it was named one of China's first historic and cultural towns. Its centrepiece is Baosheng Temple, founded in 503, where the surviving clay arhats of an original set of eighteen are kept in a hall built for them around 1930; tradition credits them to the Tang sculptor Yang Huizhi, while the national listing dates them to the Northern Song. The temple grounds also hold the tomb of the Tang poet Lu Guimeng, who lived here in retirement.

rows.name: Master of the Nets Garden
rows.summary: A small residential garden first laid out in the Southern Song as an official's library retreat and rebuilt in the Qianlong era by Song Zongyuan, who renamed it after the fisherman, the 'master of the nets', as a symbol of the simple life. Halls, galleries, a rockery and a pavilion are fitted closely around a central pond, with the family residence to the east and a quiet inner courtyard to the west. That courtyard, Dianchun Yi, was the model for the Ming Xuan court built at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York; the garden is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty
rows.summary: A very small garden on Jingde Road almost entirely taken up by an artificial mountain of Taihu rock, built in 1807 by the rockery master Ge Yuliang, with a winding path through it and a pool around its foot. The rockery is often ranked the finest of its kind in Suzhou, and the site was once the home of the Ming grand secretary Shen Shixing; the garden took its present name in 1847. It is part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Mudu Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old canal town at the foot of Lingyan Hill on Suzhou's western edge, named a national historic and cultural town in 2005, which the Qianlong Emperor visited six times and which fills half of the 18th-century scroll Prosperous Suzhou. Its main sights are restored private gardens and houses: the Yan Family Garden, rebuilt by Xiangshan craftsmen after 1902 and the birthplace of Yen Chia-kan, later president of the Republic of China on Taiwan, the Old Pine Garden and Hongyin Shanfang, a residence associated with Qianlong's visits.

rows.name: Old Campus of Soochow University
rows.summary: The original campus of Soochow University, founded by American Methodist missionaries in 1900, which now forms the southern half of Soochow University's main campus in the east of the old city. Western-style brick buildings of the 1900s to 1930s stand around a large lawn, led by Lin Hall (1903) with its clock tower, the university's landmark, and Sun Hall (1912), with a row of staff villas beside the old gate.

rows.name: Pan Family Mansion (Ligeng Hall)
rows.summary: A large Qing merchant mansion just east of Pingjiang Road, built in 1787 by Pan Linzhao, a merchant from Huizhou, and known by the name of its main hall, Ligeng Tang. Restored in stages from 2001, it reopened in 2014 as a cultural venue with a bookshop, teahouse and exhibitions, and since 2022 it has also housed the Suzhou Urban Construction Museum. Several finely carved brick gateways survive among its courtyards.

rows.name: Pan Gate & Ruiguang Pagoda
rows.summary: The only original gate left from Suzhou's city wall, a combined land and water gate at the south-west corner of the old city where the moat meets the Grand Canal; the present gate was built in 1351 under the Yuan, with a square barbican added in 1356, and it is a component of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site. The scenic area also takes in Wumen Bridge, a tall single-arch stone bridge over the moat rebuilt in 1872, and Ruiguang Pagoda, a seven-storey octagonal pagoda whose brick body dates from the early 11th century. Relics of the Five Dynasties and early Song were found inside the pagoda in 1978.

rows.name: Pingjiang Road Historic District
rows.summary: A historic quarter in the north-east of Suzhou's old city, laid out along Pingjiang Road and the Pingjiang canal, which have run side by side for some 800 years and already appear on the city map of 1229. Lanes of whitewashed houses, humped stone bridges and side canals branch off the main street, which is lined with bookshops, teahouses and small venues for Suzhou storytelling and ballad singing. The district is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site and holds the Couple's Retreat Garden, the Kunqu Opera Museum in the Quanjin Guild Hall and the Pan family mansion.

rows.name: Precious Belt Bridge
rows.summary: A long, low stone bridge of 53 arches that carries the old towpath of the Grand Canal across the mouth of Tantai Lake, south-east of Suzhou. First built between 816 and 819 under the Tang, when the prefect Wang Zhongshu is said to have paid for it with his jewelled belt, it dates in its present form from a Ming rebuilding of 1446 and repairs of 1873; its three central arches are raised to let larger boats through. It is the longest old multi-arch stone bridge in Jiangsu.

rows.name: Prince Zhong's Mansion (Suzhou Museum)
rows.summary: The residence and offices that the Taiping commander Li Xiucheng, the Loyal Prince (Zhong Wang), built from 1860 out of existing mansions and gardens next to the Humble Administrator's Garden; it was still unfinished when Qing forces under Li Hongzhang retook Suzhou in 1863, and later served as the Jiangsu governor's office and a guild hall. Its three lines of halls keep a theatre with an old stage and many painted beams from the Taiping period. Since 1960 it has been the home of the Suzhou Museum, whose new galleries by I. M. Pei opened beside it in 2006.

rows.name: Qiandeng Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old canal town south of Kunshan, threaded by a stone-slab street. Its landmark is the Qinfeng Pagoda, a slender seven-storey brick-and-timber pagoda whose founding is traditionally dated to 503, restored to its Song appearance in 1994 and closed to climbers since 2007. The town was the birthplace of the Ming–Qing scholar Gu Yanwu, whose five-courtyard family house, shrine and tomb form one site, and the home of Gu Jian, credited with founding Kunqu opera, who has a memorial hall here.

rows.name: Quanjin Guild Hall (China Kunqu Opera Museum)
rows.summary: A guild hall built by Shanxi merchants trading in Suzhou, first founded outside Changmen gate in 1765 and rebuilt on its present site off Pingjiang Road in 1879 after the original was burnt in 1860. Its central courtyard holds a richly carved and gilded two-storey opera stage under a domed ceiling, and the hall now houses the China Kunqu Opera Museum, with displays on the history, scripts, costumes and instruments of Kunqu, which UNESCO recognised as intangible heritage in 2001. Kunqu performances are staged here regularly, and the hall is a component of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Retreat & Reflection Garden
rows.summary: A late-Qing garden in Tongli built in 1885–1887 for Ren Lansheng, an official dismissed from his post in Anhui, and designed by the painter Yuan Long; its name comes from a line in the Zuo Zhuan about reflecting on one's faults in retirement. Unusually it is laid out along an east–west axis, with the family residence to the east and the main garden to the west, where halls, galleries and a boat-shaped pavilion sit low around a pond so that they seem to float on the water. It is one of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

rows.name: Shajiabang & Yushan–Shanghu Scenic Area
rows.name_zh: 沙家浜·虞山尚湖旅游区
rows.summary: A two-part 5A scenic area in Changshu, a county-level city north-east of Suzhou. Shajiabang, on the reed marshes beside Yangcheng Lake, is the setting of the revolutionary opera Shajiabang, one of the 'model operas' of the Cultural Revolution about local resistance to the Japanese occupation, and has a revolutionary history memorial hall, the Hongshi folk-culture village, the old Hengjing street and a reed-marsh wetland park. Yushan, a long wooded hill that reaches into Changshu's old town, is a national forest park with old temples and tombs, and Shanghu Lake lies at its south-western foot.

rows.name: Shangfang Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill on the shore of Shihu Lake on Suzhou's southern edge, protected as a national forest park and known for remains linked to the ancient states of Wu and Yue. Its twenty-odd sights include the Lengqie Pagoda on the summit, Zhiping Temple, stretches of old wall attributed to Wu and Yue, a beacon platform, the Shihu Thatched Hall and an imperial path laid for the Qianlong Emperor.

rows.name: Shantang Street
rows.summary: A canal street in north-west Suzhou that follows the Shantang canal, dug in 825 under the poet and prefect Bai Juyi to link Changmen gate with Tiger Hill; street and canal run for 'seven li' (about 3.8 km), the source of its nickname. Its eastern section is lined with restored old houses, guild halls and small museums, with stone bridges over the canal. Burnt in 1860 and rebuilt, the street so pleased the Qianlong Emperor that he had a copy, Suzhou Street, built at the Summer Palace in Beijing.

rows.name: Shaxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town on the Qipu River in the middle of Taicang, named a national historic and cultural town of China in 2005. Its long old street runs beside the river, lined with Qing-era houses with carved doors and windows and stone steps down to the water, and old stone arch bridges of the Ming and Qing cross the river.

rows.name: Shijian Hall
rows.summary: A Qing merchant compound in Zhenze old town, the ancestral property of the town's Xu family, which combined trade and family life on one site. From the canal it runs back through a riverside rice warehouse and a row of shops, across Baota Street itself, which passes through the compound, to the main hall and two-storey family quarters. A tiny garden of galleries, rockery and a half-pavilion lies on its east side.

rows.name: Siben Bridge
rows.summary: A bridge from the Southern Song dynasty (1127–1279), also called Sifen Bridge, in Lianxing village (formerly Liaobang village of Tongli), about 1.5 km west of Tongli old town. It was listed as a national monument in 2013 and makes a short detour from Tongli.

rows.name: Suzhou Amusement Land Forest World
rows.summary: A forest-themed amusement park at the foot of Dayang Mountain in Suzhou's western New District, opened after the original Suzhou Amusement Land of 1997 closed in 2017. It is laid out in six themed zones with more than 20 rides, among them a flying theatre and a vertical-drop roller coaster, plus shows and parades, and the same operator runs a summer water park and a children's park, Candy World, next to it. It suits families with children rather than sightseers.

rows.name: Suzhou Bay Golden Lakeshore
rows.summary: A waterfront leisure area of about 200 hectares on the shore of East Lake Tai in Suzhou Bay, the new lakeside district of Wujiang, made up of the East Lake Tai Ecological Park, the Suzhou Bay Plaza Park, a lakeside viewing platform, a restaurant quarter and a yacht club. Paths and cycle tracks follow the water past lawns and wetland planting, and the Suzhou Bay Cultural Centre with its grand theatre, designed by Christian de Portzamparc, stands on the same shore. It is a place for a walk, a bike ride or the sunset over the lake rather than a historic sight.

rows.name: Suzhou Confucian Temple (Stone Inscription Museum)
rows.summary: Suzhou's Confucian temple and prefectural school, founded in 1035 by the statesman Fan Zhongyan, who joined temple and school in a pattern later copied across China; it now houses the Suzhou Stone Inscription Museum. Its most important exhibits are four Southern Song steles: the Pingjiang Map of 1229, a detailed plan of the city with its walls, canals and bridges and the oldest surviving city plan in China, together with a star chart, a map of the Song empire and a chart of royal succession carved in 1247. The Ming Dacheng Hall of 1474 and a Ming stone gateway survive among buildings mostly rebuilt in 1864.

rows.name: Suzhou Imperial Kiln Gold Brick Museum
rows.summary: A museum in Suzhou's Xiangcheng district beside the old Lumu imperial kilns, which in the Ming and Qing dynasties fired the fine clay floor tiles known as 'gold bricks' for the Forbidden City and the Summer Palace. Designed by the architect Liu Jiakun and opened in 2016, it pairs a modern exhibition building with a park around the surviving kiln remains.

rows.name: Suzhou Lake Tai National Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 苏州太湖国家湿地公园
rows.summary: A national wetland park of about 230 hectares on the shore of Lake Tai at Zhenhu, in Suzhou's High-tech District, made by turning former fish ponds back into lakeside wetland. Boardwalks and bridges lead through reed beds, ponds and small islands, one of them home to sika deer, and boat trips run through the wetland; more than 170 species of wild birds have been recorded here.

rows.name: Taicang Modern Agricultural Park (Rose Manor)
rows.summary: A large modern farming park of about 8,000 mu (533 hectares) in northern Taicang, run as a showcase for agricultural technology and ecology. Its signature section is Rose Manor, a rose-themed garden that the city is developing into a leisure destination with study tours, accommodation and wedding venues. It suits families and garden lovers rather than visitors looking for historic sights.

rows.name: Tianchi Mountain & Huashan (Jijian Temple)
rows.summary: Two wooded hills west of Suzhou, Tianchi Mountain and Huashan, which with the neighbouring Baixiangwan valley form one scenic area inside the Dongwu National Forest Park. On Tianchi Mountain stands Jijian Temple, founded in 1357, whose Yuan-dynasty stone hall and two flanking stone shrines are carved to imitate timber buildings and set against the cliff, with Yuan Buddha figures in their niches. The area suits a half-day hill walk combined with the temple.

rows.name: Tianfei Palace, Liuhe
rows.summary: A temple to Tianfei (Mazu), goddess of seafarers, in Liuhe, the old port of Liujiagang near the mouth of the Liu River, from which Zheng He's fleets set out on their voyages to South-east Asia and the Indian Ocean between 1405 and 1433. In 1431 Zheng He and Wang Jinghong set into its wall a stele recording the voyages and crediting the goddess's protection; the stele was later lost and has since been re-created. The surviving buildings of the temple date from the Qing dynasty.

rows.name: Tianping Mountain
rows.summary: A low hill on Suzhou's western outskirts, long linked with the Song statesman Fan Zhongyan, whose ancestors are buried here and who is honoured in a memorial hall. It is known for three things: its oddly shaped rocks, its springs and its red maples, which draw crowds in autumn.

rows.name: Tiger Hill & Yunyan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A small hill on the north-west edge of Suzhou where King Helü of Wu is said to have been buried in the 5th century BC, and a celebrated beauty spot for well over a thousand years. Its summit is crowned by the Yunyan Temple Pagoda, a seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda completed in 961 that leans visibly, while below it lie the Sword Pond and the broad Thousand-Person Rock, both tied to legends of the king's tomb. Buddhist scriptures in a stone casket were found inside the pagoda during repairs in 1957.

rows.name: Tinglin Park, Kunshan
rows.summary: Kunshan's main city park, laid out in 1906 as Ma'anshan Park around Yufeng Hill (Ma'anshan) in the north-west of the city and renamed in 1936 after the scholar Gu Yanwu, known as Master Tinglin. Near the east gate are three small museums: one on Kunqu opera, which takes its name from Kunshan, one on Gu Yanwu and one on Kunshan stone, a prized ornamental rock that comes from this hill. The park also grows the qionghua viburnum and twin-flowered lotus that, with Kun stone, are called Kunshan's three treasures.

rows.name: Tongli Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town of more than a thousand years on the edge of Wujiang, crossed by waterways and old stone bridges and named in 2003 among the first ten historic and cultural towns of China. Its best-known sight is the Retreat and Reflection Garden of 1885–1887, part of the Classical Gardens of Suzhou World Heritage Site; in the old town too is Gengle Hall, a house founded in the 1440s and rebuilt under the Qing, with a lotus pond, old pines and osmanthus in its garden. Luoxing Islet in the lake holds Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian shrines.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas (Luohan Temple)
rows.summary: A matching pair of seven-storey, eight-sided brick pagodas built in 982 under the Northern Song by Wang Wenhan and his brothers, the main survivors of the Luohan (later Dinghui) Temple. Their iron finials are unusually long for the size of the pagodas and are the earliest large iron finials known in China. Just north of the pagodas, the stone columns, column bases and carved fragments of the temple's main hall, burnt in 1860, are laid out as a ruin.

rows.name: Wanfo Stone Pagoda, Zhenhu
rows.summary: A stone pagoda first built in the Song dynasty and rebuilt under the Yuan, standing at Wanfo Temple in Zhenhu on the eastern shore of Lake Tai. The temple is about 2 km from the China Embroidery Art Museum, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Xiancan Temple (Silk Patrons' Shrine), Shengze
rows.summary: A shrine to the patron deities of silk, the Yellow Emperor, Shennong and Leizu, built in 1840 by the silk merchants of Shengze, with a main hall, an opera stage and a meeting hall that also housed the silk trade guild. Every May around the Xiaoman solar term it hosts a silkworm-blessing ceremony and performances of traditional Xiaoman opera as part of a local festival.

rows.name: Xiangshan Scenic Area, Zhangjiagang
rows.summary: Zhangjiagang's highest hill, at 136.6 m, a wooded ridge in Jingang (formerly Nansha town) west of the city centre, laid out as a scenic area of about 4.4 km² with plum groves, the Peach Blossom Brook valley, a lake and Buddhist halls. On the summit stands the Plum Blossom Hall, whose name board is attributed to Su Dongpo; it was rebuilt in the late Ming by the elder brother of the travel writer Xu Xiake, who stayed here on three visits and wrote poems about the hall.

rows.name: Xishan Island
rows.summary: The largest island in Lake Tai, a hilly landscape of orchards and villages joined to the mainland by the Taihu Bridge, with Piaomiao Peak as its high point. The scenic area takes in Linwu Cave, counted in Taoist tradition as the ninth of the ten great grotto-heavens, the rocky lakeside headland of Shigong Hill, Mingyue Bay and Baoshan Temple. The island grows loquats, bayberries, plums, oranges and peaches, so spring and early summer bring fruit-picking.

rows.name: Xuanmiao Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple in the heart of Suzhou's old city, founded in 276 and facing the busy Guanqian Street shopping street. Its main hall, the Hall of the Three Pure Ones, is a broad double-eaved timber hall rebuilt in 1179 under the Southern Song and still standing. Inside are a Song copy of a stone portrait of Laozi after the Tang painter Wu Daozi, with calligraphy by Yan Zhenqing, and around the hall a carved stone balustrade of the Five Dynasties.

rows.name: Xuanyuan Temple, Dongshan
rows.summary: A temple at the west end of Yangwan, an uncommercialised village of old houses on the Dongshan peninsula, first built to honour Wu Zixu, the minister of the ancient state of Wu, and rededicated to the Yellow Emperor in the Republican era, which gave it its present name. The temple was rebuilt in the Southern Song and repaired again in the mid-17th century, and its main hall, dated to 1338 under the Yuan dynasty, is a three-bay timber building with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof.

rows.name: Yan Garden, Changshu
rows.summary: A small classical garden in Changshu's old town, laid out in 1780 by Jiang Yuanshu, a former prefect of Taiwan. Its highlight is the Swallow Valley, a rockery of yellow Yushan stone with a gorge, caves and a bridge, built after 1829 by the rockery master Ge Yuliang; it is one of only two of his rockeries that survive largely intact, the other being at the Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty in Suzhou. Halls, a lotus pond and a second rockery of Lake Tai stone fill the rest of the compact site.

rows.name: Yang Family Mansions, Tianzhuang Old Street
rows.summary: Qing-dynasty mansions of the Yang family, a local gentry family, on Tianzhuang Old Street in Fenghuang town, a canal-side street of white-walled, black-tiled houses. The Bangyan Mansion and the Yang Filial Memorial are among the Yang buildings open to visitors along the street, the core of one of China's historic and cultural towns.

rows.name: Yanzi Shrine, Changshu
rows.summary: A shrine to Yan Yan (Ziyou), the disciple of Confucius who came from the southern state of Wu and was honoured as the 'Master of the South'. It has stood on the east side of Changshu's Confucian temple since 1486 and was restored in 1872; its square main hall keeps the form of Song and Yuan buildings. Restoration of the Confucian temple complex around it began in 2008.

rows.name: Yonglian Village Scenic Area
rows.summary: Yonglian is a village in Nanfeng town whose rolling mill, set up by the village committee in 1984, grew into the Yonggang steel group. Its tourist area has two parts: Yonglian Town, with an exhibition hall on the village's history, and the Jiangnan Farming Culture Park, a farm-themed leisure park opened in 2010 with rides, play areas and a water park. It suits families and visitors curious about the industrialised villages of the Yangtze delta.

rows.name: Yuan-Dynasty Stone Arch Bridges of Taicang
rows.summary: Five stone arch bridges built under the Yuan dynasty between 1329 and 1334, close in date and style and listed together. Three of them — Gao Bridge (1334), Zhou Bridge (1329) and Zhoujing Bridge (1330) — still cross the Zhihe canal through Taicang's old town beside Xinhua Road; the three-arched Zhou and Zhoujing bridges are the largest, Gao Bridge a single arch. The other two, Jingting and Jinji bridges, stand in Xinfeng village on the southern outskirts.

rows.name: Zhang Pu Residence
rows.summary: A late-Ming house on Ximen Street in Taicang's old town, built in the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns (1621–1644) by Zhang Fuzhi, uncle of the writer Zhang Pu (1602–1641), who led the Restoration Society (Fushe), an influential late-Ming association of scholars. Three courtyards of five-bay, two-storey halls are joined by upper-floor galleries into a typical Jiangnan 'running-horse' house, and the society's members met here.

rows.name: Zhenze Ancient Town & Ciyun Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A former silk town in the south-west of Wujiang on the Zhejiang border, a national historic and cultural town whose old quarter centres on Baota Street. Its landmark is the pagoda of Ciyun Temple on that street, a six-sided, five-storey brick-and-timber tower, mostly Ming in date, which alone survived when the temple was burnt in the wars of the 1850s; the temple has since been partly restored. Nearby is Shijian Hall, a merchant family's compound that combines a rice warehouse on the water, shops, living quarters and a small garden.

rows.name: Zijin Nunnery
rows.summary: A small Buddhist temple in the hills of the Dongshan peninsula, its present halls built in the Ming and Qing, whose main hall is filled with painted clay figures of Buddhas, Guanyin, guardian kings and celestial beings. Its sixteen arhats, each shown with a different pose and expression, are recorded as the work of the Southern Song sculptor Lei Chao and his wife. It is one of the named sights of the Lake Tai scenic area on Dongshan.

rows.name: Daohe Historic Quarter
rows.summary: Just outside Taizhou's old north gate, the Daohe quarter is the city's main surviving block of old houses, lining the Daohe and Caohe rivers with Hanxi Street on one bank and five parallel lanes on the other. It grew up from 1372, when the Ming court resettled migrants from Suzhou and other southern prefectures here, and prospered as a landing for grain and salt boats, leaving Ming and Qing houses, an old pawnshop and a Ming bridge.

rows.name: Fengcheng River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Fengcheng River is the old moat that rings Taizhou's historic centre, landscaped with waterside parks and walks and plied by sightseeing boats. Along it stand the Wanghai Tower, the Taoyuan garden and the Mei Lanfang Memorial, a garden museum on the site of the opera star's ancestral home that he visited in 1956, and a new leisure hub has been added on Changdao and Maple Leaf islands.

rows.name: Guluotang Old Street Quarter
rows.summary: Guluotang is a restored and partly rebuilt old-street quarter along North Street in the centre of Jiangyan. Its southern half gathers the historic sights, among them the Wang clan ancestral hall and a memorial hall to the Qing Go master Huang Longshi, while the northern half is given over to shops, cafés and an evening market.

rows.name: Huangqiao Campaign Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 新四军黄桥战役纪念馆
rows.summary: In October 1940 the Communist-led New Fourth Army under Chen Yi and Su Yu defeated the Nationalist 89th Army of Jiangsu governor Han Deqin around Huangqiao, a clash within the wartime alliance that secured the Communists a base in central Jiangsu. The memorial hall in the town tells the story of the campaign; the battle's former command post in the old town is the protected heritage site, and a martyrs' memorial tower stands nearby.

rows.name: Kou'an Carved Mansion
rows.summary: The Diaohualou ('carved building') is a merchant's mansion of the Qing and early Republican periods in the old town of Kou'an near the Yangtze, with two-storey main buildings and side wings around a square courtyard richly decorated with wood, brick and stone carving. It is the centrepiece of a small old-town scenic area and has been a Jiangsu provincial heritage site since 2002.

rows.name: Lizhong Water Forest
rows.summary: The Lizhong Water Forest is a man-made wetland forest begun in the early 1980s, when villagers planted pond cypress and dawn redwood on raised plots in waste marshland north-west of Xinghua. The trees now stand with their roots in water, and herons and other water birds nest among them; in 2014 it became Xinghua's first scenic area rated 4A.

rows.name: PLA Navy Birthplace Memorial Hall
rows.summary: On 23 April 1949, at Baimamiao, then the headquarters of the Third Field Army's eastern command for the Yangtze crossing, the East China Military Region Navy was formed under Zhang Aiping, a date the PLA later adopted as the navy's founding day. The protected site is a former landlord's manor with a two-storey Qing building where Su Yu, Zhang Zhen and Zhang Aiping worked, and beside it a memorial hall opened in 1999, its newer main building shaped like a ship's bow, displays retired fighters and bombers, a helicopter, torpedoes, naval guns and missiles.

rows.name: Qinhu Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Qinhu was Jiangsu's first national wetland park and China's second, a lake and marshland in the Lixiahe lowlands where wetland covers most of the park and hundreds of wild plant and animal species have been recorded, Père David's deer among them. Boats link the visitor hall with a wetland science museum and a bird museum across the lake, and each Qingming festival around a thousand boats crowd the water for the Qintong Boat Festival, a national intangible heritage.

rows.name: Qintong Ancient Town
rows.summary: Qintong is a Ming- and Qing-era water town at the meeting of the Jiangxing and Taidong rivers, listed as one of China's historic and cultural towns in 2005. Its lanes keep old houses such as the Ming-dynasty Lüshu Courtyard and the Zhu family house, a Qing pharmacy and fire-brigade hall, and an old camellia famed locally for its thousands of blooms. The town hosts the Qintong Boat Festival on nearby Qinhu Lake at Qingming.

rows.name: Qiuxue Lake Eco-Park
rows.summary: A large eco-park of lakes, wetlands and farmland on the north-eastern edge of Taizhou's main urban area, combining modern farming with waterside walks and leisure attractions. A children's amusement park, Fairy-tale Forest, stands beside it, and the area suits a half-day family outing.

rows.name: Rishe Garden (Qiao Garden)
rows.summary: Built in 1574 for the Ming official Chen Yingfang and later called Qiao Garden after a Qing salt commissioner who owned it, Rishe Garden is regarded as the oldest surviving classical garden in northern Jiangsu. Restored in 1990 after a Qing painting of the garden, it packs a central hall, pavilions on a rockery crowned by three stone 'swords', a stream and an old cypress said to date from the Ming into a small space; the opera star Mei Lanfang stayed in one of its pavilions in 1956.

rows.name: Shagou Ancient Town
rows.summary: Shagou is an old water town in the far north-west of Xinghua, where five counties meet, long a market centre for the fish and rice of the Lixiahe plain and named a China Historic and Cultural Town in 2010. Its lanes keep a Ming stone-slab street at the old fish market, the Ming-dynasty Hong Bridge, Qing houses and a clan hall, and an old wharf.

rows.name: Shangchizhai Pharmacy
rows.summary: Shangchizhai was founded in the Kangxi–Yongzheng period by Fang Shichuan of Yangzhou and named after a line in Sima Qian's biography of the physician Bian Que; its shop buildings date from the Qing and Republican periods. It stands in the Jindongmen historic quarter, Xinghua's old trading street east of the walled town, among other listed houses including the former home of the painter Zheng Banqiao.

rows.name: Taizhou City God Temple
rows.summary: Taizhou's City God Temple was founded in the Tang, rebuilt in 1439 and restored in 1853, and is now used as a Taoist temple. Its south-facing compound keeps a gate, a judgement hall, the main hall and the side halls of the 24 underworld bureaus, along with smaller shrines to the gods of fortune and the land.

rows.name: Tianmushan Site
rows.summary: The Tianmushan site is the remains of a walled settlement of the Western Zhou, flourishing about 3,100 years ago where the New Tongyang Canal meets the Jiangqin River on Jiangyan's northern edge. A site museum beside the remains displays the finds.

rows.name: Xinghua Duotian Raised Fields
rows.summary: Duotian are small island fields, each ringed by water, that farmers in the low-lying Lixiahe marshes have worked for more than 600 years. The system was named a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization in 2014 and a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Xuezheng Examination Hall
rows.summary: From the Kangxi era until the abolition of the imperial examinations, candidates from the counties of Yangzhou prefecture sat the licentiate examination (yuanshi), set by the Jiangsu education commissioner, in this hall; it is the only fairly complete compound of its kind left in Jiangsu. Only the gate and second hall had survived, and the rest was rebuilt in 2005–06 from an old gazetteer plan, opening in 2008 as the Taizhou Imperial Examination Museum with displays on how the examinations worked.

rows.name: Zheng Banqiao and Fan Zhongyan Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This memorial museum in Xinghua's old town honours two men tied to the city: the painter and calligrapher Zheng Banqiao (Zheng Xie, 1693–1766), born in Xinghua and one of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou, known for his ink orchids, bamboo and rocks, and the Song statesman Fan Zhongyan, who served as Xinghua's magistrate in the 1020s and led the building of sea dykes along this coast. It shares its grounds with the Xinghua Museum and the Li Garden, a small Qing garden with a boat-shaped hall, and Zheng's former home survives nearby in the Jindongmen quarter.

rows.name: CCTV Wuxi Film and TV Base (Three Kingdoms & Water Margin Cities)
rows.summary: A film and television base built by China Central Television on the shore of Lake Tai from 1987, whose 5A part is made up of Three Kingdoms City and Water Margin City, full-scale sets of palaces, naval camps and old streets built for the 1990s television series of Romance of the Three Kingdoms and Water Margin. The sets are still used by film crews, and the base stages more than 20 shows a day, including horseback battle stunts and special-effects demonstrations, as well as boat trips on the lake.

rows.name: China Yixing Ceramics Museum
rows.summary: One of China's earliest specialist ceramics museums, at the foot of Xianhe Hill in Dingshu, Yixing's pottery town, and since 2013 also designated the China Zisha Museum. Its displays run from Neolithic pottery, Han glazed wares and Jin celadon through Song and Yuan Jun-style pottery to Ming and Qing purple-clay (zisha) teapots and modern work, with a gallery for the master potter Gu Jingzhou and studios where visitors can try making pottery.

rows.name: Chinese Decorative Stone Park
rows.summary: A museum and garden of ornamental stones at the northern entrance of the China Wu Culture Expo Park in Hongshan, founded as the first stone garden of the View Stone Association of China. Eight themed galleries show more than a thousand pieces, from oddly shaped and patterned stones to mineral crystals and fossils, and the prize exhibit is a fossil of Daxiatitan, a giant long-necked dinosaur from the Lanzhou Basin in Gansu.

rows.name: Chong'an Temple Quarter
rows.summary: The historic core of central Wuxi, named after a temple said to have been founded on the calligrapher Wang Xizhi's donated house in the 4th century and lost in the early 20th century; today it is a pedestrian shopping and food quarter around Erquan Square, known for old Wuxi restaurants and xiaolongbao. It takes in Chengzhong Park, laid out in 1905 as one of China's first public parks, and the 1914 clock-tower building of the old county library. In its south corner is the former residence of the blind street musician Abing (Hua Yanjun), composer of the erhu piece 'The Moon Reflected on Erquan', who was born and died here; it is now a memorial hall showing his erhu, pipa and modest living rooms.

rows.name: Dangkou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town in Ehu, east of Wuxi near the Suzhou border, that grew up from the early Ming dynasty as the home of the Hua clan, with Ming and Qing houses along the Beicang River; restoration began in 2009 and it is now run as a scenic area. Its main monument is the Hua Family Old Charitable Estate, begun in the 1740s and the first such clan estate in Wuxi, which used rents from its land to support widows, orphans and a clan school; four halls survive, the main ones built of nanmu wood.

rows.name: Dayao Road Kiln Sites (Wuxi Kiln Ruins Museum)
rows.summary: A line of old brick and tile kilns along Dayao Road on the east bank of the old Grand Canal, where kilns fired building bricks from the Ming dynasty onwards and are recorded as having made 'gold bricks' for the imperial palace; dozens of the kilns still stand along the street. A former factory on the street is now the Wuxi Kiln Ruins Museum, with Wuxi city-wall, floor and tomb bricks, replicas of bricks and tiles from across China, a cut-away kiln and hands-on brick-making.

rows.name: Donglin Academy
rows.summary: A Confucian academy in central Wuxi founded in 1111, where the Song scholar Yang Shi taught, and revived in the early 1600s by Gu Xiancheng and Gao Panlong, whose circle of scholar-officials criticised court politics and became known as the Donglin faction. Destroyed in 1626 and rebuilt under the Qing, it keeps a stone memorial archway, the Lize and Yiyong lecture halls and the Daonan Shrine to Yang Shi, with Gu's well-known couplet about caring for 'the affairs of family, state and world'.

rows.name: Former Jiangyin Fortress Headquarters
rows.summary: A Chinese-Western house built in 1917 by the Jiangyin industrialist Wu Tinglu, with a brick screen wall and garden in front of two Chinese-style halls and a two-storey Western-style villa at the back. Occupied by the Japanese army from 1937, it became the headquarters of the Nationalist Jiangyin Fortress in 1947, whose garrison went over to the People's Liberation Army in April 1949 during the Yangtze crossing campaign. It remained in military use until 2003 and opened in 2007 as an exhibition hall on Jiangyin's history and notable people.

rows.name: Former Maoxin Flour Mill
rows.summary: Wuxi's first flour mill, started in 1902 by the industrialist brothers Rong Zongjing and Rong Desheng beside the Grand Canal, the first factory of the Rong family's industrial business. Bombed in 1937, the mill was rebuilt in 1946–48 to designs by the architect Tong Jun, and after it closed in 2003 the mill buildings were turned into the Wuxi China National Industry and Commerce Museum, part of the Wuxi Museum group, on the history of the city's private industry.

rows.name: Former Residence of Qin Bangxian (Bo Gu)
rows.summary: A late-Qing courtyard house on Chongning Road where Qin Bangxian, better known as Bo Gu, lived with his parents from 1916 to 1921; born in Wuxi in 1907, he was General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party from 1931 until the Zunyi Conference of January 1935. The house, which belonged to his uncle's family and has a main range of seven courtyards, was restored in 2004 and is now a memorial hall about his life.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xu Xiake
rows.summary: The family home of Xu Xiake (1587–1641), the late-Ming traveller and geographer whose diaries of more than 30 years of journeys across China are a classic of Chinese travel writing, in the Jiangyin township now named after him. The three-courtyard house, rebuilt in the Qing dynasty, keeps a podocarpus said to have been planted by Xu himself, and the nearby rebuilt Qingshan Hall holds 76 stone tablets carved with Yuan and Ming calligraphy he collected from 88 writers, including Song Lian, Wen Zhengming and Zhu Yunming.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xue Fucheng
rows.summary: The mansion that the late-Qing diplomat and reformer Xue Fucheng, envoy to Britain, France, Italy and Belgium, had built in Wuxi's old city between 1890 and 1894, known by its imperial name plaque as the Qinshidi, the 'Imperial Envoy's Residence'. Covering more than 2 hectares, it is one of the largest surviving late-19th-century official residences in Jiangsu, laid out on three parallel axes with a screen wall, reception halls, a two-storey 'turntable' building, a theatre stage, granaries, a library tower and a rear garden.

rows.name: Grand Buddha at Ling Shan
rows.summary: A Buddhist complex on the north shore of Lake Tai, centred on an 88 m bronze standing Buddha, including its lotus base, consecrated in 1997 and assembled from about 2,000 cast panels weighing 725 tonnes in all. An axis leads from the gate past the Nine Dragons Bathing the Buddha, a timed fountain show in which a 7.2 m gilded statue of the infant Buddha rises from an opening lotus, to the Grand Buddha. Beside it the Lingshan Brahma Palace, opened in 2009 with richly carved halls and a domed hall, is the permanent venue of the World Buddhist Forum.

rows.name: Helü City Ruins and Museum
rows.summary: A museum opened in 2014 beside the remains of Helü City, a walled settlement on the Wuxi–Changzhou border that archaeologists identified in 2008 as a capital of the Spring and Autumn state of Wu under King Helü in the late 6th century BC, although the location of his capital is still debated. Built into the face of a former quarry by Lake Tai, it shows finds from the site, with a 3D cinema and multimedia displays on the excavations and on King Helü; only parts of the earthen ramparts can still be traced in the countryside nearby.

rows.name: Hongshan Site Museum (China Wu Culture Museum)
rows.summary: A site museum in Wuxi's Hongshan area built over a cemetery of tombs of Yue-state nobles, whose excavation was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2004. Its galleries centre on the great Qiuchengdun tomb, shown in place, with the celadon, low-fired glazed ceramics and finely carved jades found in the graves, which shed light on the burial rites and music of the Wu and Yue states.

rows.name: Hongshan Taibo Scenic Area
rows.summary: The burial place on Hongshan hill traditionally held to be that of Taibo, the legendary founder of the Wu state, laid out with Wu Culture Square in front and the tomb area behind. Its 20-odd sights include Ming and Qing structures such as the Yangzhi Pavilion and the Imperial Stele Pavilion, and since 2006 it has hosted the annual Taibo memorial ceremony and Wu Culture Festival on 10 April.

rows.name: Huishan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A cluster of ancestral halls and their gardens, 108 of them dating from the Tang dynasty to the Republican era, along two old streets at the eastern foot of Mount Hui, combined with neighbouring Xihui Park into one scenic area that also takes in Huishan Temple, Jichang Garden and the hilltop Longguang Pagoda. Halls honour figures such as Fan Zhongyan, Lu Zhi and Ni Zan, two carved stone dharani pillars of 876 and 1070 stand inside the temple's front gate, and the Second Spring under Heaven, ranked the second-best water for tea in the Tang dynasty, gave its name to Abing's erhu piece 'The Moon Reflected on Erquan'. Shops along the streets sell Huishan painted clay figurines.

rows.name: Jiangsu Education Commissioner's Office, Jiangyin
rows.summary: The site of the provincial education commissioner's office, unusually based in Jiangyin rather than in a provincial capital: the commissioner for Suzhou and Songjiang moved here in 1614, and from 1725 until the examinations ended in 1906 the Jiangsu commissioner, responsible for eight prefectures and three departments, was based here. Only the five-bay ceremonial gate survives, together with inscribed steles including one in the Qianlong emperor's hand and a set of poem tablets, and the site is now a cultural park with statues of former commissioners and the old rear garden, renamed Zhongshan Park.

rows.name: Jiangyin Riverside Fortress Scenic Area
rows.summary: Riverside parks on Huangshan hill and Ebizui (Goose Beak) Point just north of central Jiangyin, where the Yangtze narrows to little more than a kilometre and has been fortified since the late Ming. Gun batteries from the Ming–Qing, late-Qing and Republican periods survive on the hilltops, a stone at Ebizui marks the spot as the river's 'tail' and the sea's 'head', and the paths give close views of passing ships and the Jiangyin Yangtze River Bridge.

rows.name: Jichang Garden
