rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty garden at the foot of Mount Hui, begun in the Zhengde era (1506–1521) by the official Qin Jin on the site of two monks' lodges and given its present name by his descendant Qin Yao after 1591. It is laid out around a long pond with Mount Hui and the Longguang Pagoda on Xishan 'borrowed' as a backdrop, and a rocky ravine, the Bayinjian, carries water from the Second Spring through an artificial hill. The Kangxi and Qianlong emperors each visited on their southern tours, and Qianlong had it copied as the Garden of Harmonious Interests in Beijing's Summer Palace.

rows.name: Li Garden (Liyuan)
rows.summary: A lakeside garden on the north shore of Lihu Lake, created between 1927 and 1936 by the Wang family of Qingqi village and joined in 1952 with the neighbouring Yuzhuang garden of 1930 to form a public park. Water covers much of its 8.2 hectares, with rockeries, a long waterside corridor, a lake pavilion and four pavilions planted for the four seasons, and its name recalls the legend that the Yue minister Fan Li went boating here with Xi Shi.

rows.name: Longbeishan Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill park of about 5.5 km² on the southern edge of Yixing's city centre. Its landmark is the Wenfeng Pagoda, from which there are views over the city's lakes towards Lake Tai, and the park also holds memorial halls to notable people from Yixing in history, science and the arts.

rows.name: Nanchan Temple, Wuxi
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple near the old Grand Canal just south of central Wuxi, first founded in the Southern Dynasties and restored in 1995, whose seven-storey octagonal Miaoguang Pagoda was named by the Song emperor Huizong in 1104 and rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. The pagoda has been counted among the Eight Views of Wuxi since the Ming, and the streets around the temple now form a pedestrian quarter of shops and restaurants.

rows.name: Qianshu Dragon Kiln (Yixing Kiln Sites)
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty 'dragon kiln' in Dingshu, a long, sloping, wood-fired tunnel kiln running up a hillside, which is still fired today and is the part of the Yixing Kiln Sites that visitors can see; the national listing groups it with five other old kiln sites around Yixing. Firings are held as public events at festivals such as the Dragon Boat Festival, and in 2025 the kiln was added to China's list of national industrial heritage.

rows.name: Qingming Bridge Historic District
rows.summary: A stretch of the old Grand Canal south of Wuxi's former city wall, lined with old waterside houses along Nanchang Street and Nanxiatang and crossed by the humpbacked Qingming Bridge, first built in the Ming dynasty and last rebuilt in 1869. Restored from 2007 and reopened in 2011, the district is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site; alongside its shops and creative businesses are museums in old industrial buildings, including the China Silk Industry Museum in the former Yongtai silk mill, and the remains of the brick kilns along Dayao Road.

rows.name: Shanjuan Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave in Luoyan Hill near Zhangzhu, the first of Yixing's 'three wonders' among its caves, with upper, middle and lower chambers full of stalactites and a water cave where boats follow an underground river. The scenic area is tied to the Butterfly Lovers legend of Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, with a Tang inscription marking 'Zhu Yingtai's study', and nearby at the foot of Guoshan stands the Guoshan Stele, a cylindrical stone carved in seal script in 276 to record the sacrifices to heaven and earth held there for the Wu ruler Sun Hao.

rows.name: Shiyuan Garden, Jiangyin
rows.summary: A small private garden in Jiangyin's old town, laid out in the mid-19th century by Chen Shijin, a lover of painting and calligraphy, beside the family house, around a pond with rockeries and a waterside pavilion. Its rockery holds inscribed stones including calligraphy by Dong Qichang and Liang Tongshu and the 'Goose Exchange Stele' attributed to Wang Xizhi, brought from the Confucian Temple. Damaged in the Cultural Revolution, it was rebuilt with city funds in 2008.

rows.name: Taibo Temple, Meicun
rows.summary: A temple beside the Bodu River in Meicun on the spot where Taibo, the eldest son of the Zhou king who gave up his claim to the throne and founded the Wu state, is said to have lived; a temple was first raised here in 154 AD. The present Ming and Qing buildings are entered over a stone bridge and through a granite archway and the Lingxing Gate, and the temple fair held for Taibo's birthday on the ninth day of the first lunar month is on China's national intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Taozu Shengjing Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area in the bamboo-covered hills of Huxu, south-west of Yixing, developed around Muli Cave, a karst cave whose route includes a stretch by boat. It is named after Fan Li, honoured in local tradition as the ancestor of pottery, and adds bamboo walks, a pottery workshop and sights themed on the legend of Fan Li and Xi Shi.

rows.name: Tuanjiu Lake Scenic Area
rows.summary: A small round lake on the western edge of Yixing's city centre, one of the three 'jiu' lakes that give the city its waterside setting. The scenic area rings it with promenades and parks, among them the Yi Garden (Yiyuan), laid out in Jiangnan garden style with bridges and pavilions, the south-shore promenade, Jiubin Park and a wetland park.

rows.name: Wuxi Film City (National Digital Film Industry Park)
rows.summary: A film-industry park on Lihu Avenue in southern Wuxi, built on the site of the Xuelang steel-rolling mill that closed in 2009, whose old factory sheds were converted into about 15 sound stages used by film and television crews. For visitors it adds a digital-cinema science museum, a waxworks museum and a film-themed street, and it mostly draws local families with children.

rows.name: Wuxi Museum
rows.summary: The city's main museum, opened in 2008 in a large steel-framed building beside Taihu Square, which merged the old Wuxi Museum with the city's revolutionary and science museums. Its collection of nearly 40,000 objects is strongest in Ming and Qing painting and calligraphy, and the displays also cover local history, Yixing purple-clay teapots, Huishan clay figurines and Wuxi's industry, with a bronze sword of King Liao of Wu among the highlights.

rows.name: Wuxi Plum Garden
rows.summary: A hillside garden west of Wuxi begun in 1912 by the industrialist Rong Desheng, who planted some 3,000 plum trees around his family villa; it is one of the best-known places in the Jiangnan region to see plum blossom in late winter and early spring. Paths climb past pavilions, a nanmu-wood hall and the three-storey Nianqu Pagoda, built by the Rong brothers in 1930 in memory of their mother, to the 1930s Kaiyuan Temple; Rong Yiren gave the garden to the state in 1955 and it was later extended onto neighbouring Hengshan hill.

rows.name: Wuxi Zoo and Taihu Amusement Park
rows.name_zh: 无锡动物园·太湖欢乐园
rows.summary: A combined zoo and amusement park on the slopes of Mount Hui in western Wuxi, opened in 2010 when the city zoo moved here from Xihui Park, where it had been since 1956. The zoo is divided into areas by region and animal group, with giant pandas, giraffes, rhinos, chimpanzees, red pandas and lemurs among its animals, and the amusement park section has fairground rides and staged children's shows. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Xiaolou Lane
rows.summary: A historic lane quarter in central Wuxi that was for centuries the home of the Tan and Qin families, two of the city's leading scholar-gentry clans, whose members included many successful examination candidates from the Song dynasty onwards. Most of the surviving houses date from the late Qing and Republican periods, and the block was restored and partly rebuilt from 2008 as a pedestrian heritage street.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal brick pagoda in Xingguo Park in the south-west of Jiangyin's old town, first built in the Taiping Xingguo era of the Northern Song (976–984) and raised from seven to nine storeys during a Ming repair. A fire in 1817 burned away its wooden eaves and finial, leaving the brush-shaped brick shaft that locals call the Wenbi ('writing brush') Pagoda, and in 1925 a shell fired from the Huangshan forts during a warlord war damaged its top storeys; it was strengthened in 1985 and 2005.

rows.name: Xu Ancestral Hall, Fuxi
rows.summary: The clan temple of the Xu family of Fuxi, built in 1490 for the family of the Ming official Xu Pu and also known as the Grand Tutor Xu Family Temple. Of its five courtyards, the second and third halls are original, and the main hall's nanmu beams and pillars still carry brightly coloured Suzhou-style painted decoration of scrolling flowers, brocade patterns and cranes; the gate and an opera stage are recent rebuilds.

rows.name: Yangshan Peach Blossom Land
rows.summary: The peach-growing country around Yangshan town in western Wuxi, known across China for its juicy honey peaches, with orchards that blossom in spring and are picked in summer. Around the town are the Peach Culture Square, pick-your-own orchards, farm-stays and guesthouses, a geology exhibition hall on the ancient volcano of Yangshan hill, the Anyang Academy and the Chaoyang Chan Temple.

rows.name: Yixing Bamboo Sea
rows.summary: A forest park of bamboo-covered hills in the far south of Yixing, where Jiangsu meets Zhejiang and Anhui, long known as a 'sea of bamboo'. Its visitor area of about 1,000 hectares is crossed by paths through the groves, and a cable car climbs into the hills along the Zhejiang border.

rows.name: Yuantouzhu
rows.summary: A rocky headland on the north shore of Lake Tai shaped like a turtle's head, developed from 1916 by Wuxi businessmen with lakeside villas and gardens and now a large park of wooded hills, pavilions, rock inscriptions and wide lake views. It is best known for its cherry trees, first planted by the Changchun Bridge causeway in 1936 and greatly extended with trees planted by Japanese visitors since 1988, which draw big crowds when they bloom in spring. Boats run from the park's pier to Taihu Xiandao, a group of small islands built up with Taoist-style buildings since the 1990s.

rows.name: Yunhu Lake Scenic Area, Yixing
rows.summary: A scenic area around Yunhu Lake, the former Hengshan Reservoir in the hills of Xizhu in south-western Yixing, combining lakeside walks and a wetland park with a tea-culture zone that includes the Yangxian Tea Culture Museum. On the lake shore stands Dajue Temple, a large Buddhist complex rebuilt here from 2004 and recognised as the ancestral temple of the Taiwan-based Fo Guang Shan order.

rows.name: Zhaosi Hall
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty hall in Shuofang, built as the house of the official Cao Cha, who passed the imperial examinations in 1528, and turned into the Cao family's ancestral temple in 1748. Known as the Fragrant Nanmu Hall, it is five bays wide and built entirely of fine nanmu timber, and is described as the oldest and most complete Ming nanmu building in Jiangsu.

rows.name: Zhouwang Temple (Yixing Stele Museum)
rows.summary: A memorial temple in the old centre of Yixing to Zhou Chu, a local general of the third century remembered in the folk tale of how he rid the district of a tiger, a river dragon and finally his own bad ways. First built in 962 and rebuilt many times, it keeps a Ming main hall of 1566 with stone pillars and a rebuilt opera stage, and its large collection of inscribed steles from the Tang to the Qing, including Su Dongpo's 'Ode to Chu' inscription, has made it the Yixing Stele Museum.

rows.name: Aishan Scenic Area, Pizhou
rows.summary: A hill scenic area of about 15 km² in Tiefu, northern Pizhou, that mixes woodland scenery with restored historic sites. Black locust and Chinese tallow woods and red autumn maples cover the slopes, and peach orchards ring the hill.

rows.name: Baolian Temple, Pantao Hill
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple complex on Pantao Hill in the Xuzhou Economic and Technological Development Zone, east of the city, centred on Baolian Temple, rebuilt from 2009 on the site of an older monastery that had fallen into ruin by the mid-20th century. Besides the main halls and a multi-storey pavilion it has a temple to the Queen Mother of the West, and a traditional temple fair on the third day of the third lunar month draws large local crowds.

rows.name: Dadong Mountain
rows.summary: At 361 m the highest hill in the Xuzhou area, rising on the southern edge of Jiawang district centre and managed as a wooded scenic area. Paths and a brightly painted 'rainbow' walkway climb slopes planted with large pomegranate orchards, where fruit can be picked in autumn, and Zhuyu Temple within the scenic area is known for its vegetarian noodles and buns.

rows.name: Dashahe Wetland Park, Feng County
rows.summary: A wetland park along the Dasha River in Feng County, in the far north-west of Jiangsu, where long riverside sandbanks, reed beds and ponds are laid out with birdwatching platforms and waterside paths. Rated a national 4A scenic area at the start of 2024, it is aimed mainly at families, with nature classes, a children's camp and seasonal themes running from birdwatching in spring and lotus in summer to water-caltrop picking in autumn and reed scenery in winter.

rows.name: Dugong Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir east of Jiawang's district centre, built in 1958 and now a lakeside scenic area with waterside paths. It is mostly a local day-trip spot, busiest when its peach trees blossom in spring.

rows.name: Fengminghai Park, Jiawang
rows.summary: A park on the eastern side of Jiawang, the former coal-mining district north-east of Xuzhou, which the district promotes as one of its scenic areas alongside Pan'an Lake and Dadong Mountain. It includes a horse-riding club with Mongolian-style yurts, which has staged riding displays, camel rides and bonfire evenings on public holidays.

rows.name: Guishan Han Tombs
rows.summary: The joint tomb of Liu Zhu, sixth king of Chu in the Western Han dynasty, and his queen, cut side by side into the west face of Guishan hill on Xuzhou's north-western edge and identified in 1985 from the king's silver seal. Two narrow passages about 56 m long, with finely smoothed walls, lead to fifteen rock-hewn rooms including bedchambers, a kitchen, a well, a carriage room and a toilet, which visitors can walk through; a museum opened at the site in 1993.

rows.name: Huaihai Campaign Martyrs Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park on the southern side of central Xuzhou honouring soldiers of the People's Liberation Army killed in the Huaihai Campaign of November 1948 to January 1949, one of the decisive campaigns of the Chinese Civil War. Its centrepiece is a 38.15 m obelisk completed in 1965 and inscribed in Mao Zedong's calligraphy, and the grounds also hold the Huaihai Campaign Memorial Hall, whose exhibitions cover the campaign.

rows.name: Hubu Hill Historic Buildings
rows.summary: A low hill in the heart of Xuzhou named after the Ming Ministry of Revenue branch office that moved up here when the Yellow River flooded the city in 1624, after which wealthy families crowded its slopes with courtyard houses. Thirteen fairly complete compounds of the Ming to Republican eras survive, among them the Yu and Zhai family mansions, now the Xuzhou Folk Custom Museum, and houses linked to the scholar-officials Cui Tao and Li Pan, while Ximatai, a terrace linked by tradition to Xiang Yu, stands on the hill. The surrounding Huilongwo streets, with shops, teahouses and restaurants, were named a national tourism and leisure block in 2024.

rows.name: Liu Bang's Hometown Cultural Area, Feng County
rows.summary: A Han-dynasty theme park in Feng County, which the ancient histories give as the birthplace of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty. Tall modern gate towers in Han style mark the entrance, and inside are a 42.6 m bronze statue of Liu Bang with an immersive hall on early Han history at its foot, a ceremonial altar and a mound honoured as the tomb of the emperor's ancestors. It suits families and visitors interested in early Han history, and holiday fairs have brought Han costume, pitch-pot, archery, drumming and dragon dances.

rows.name: Maling Mountain
rows.summary: A range of low red-sandstone hills south of Xinyi city, with Danxia-type cliffs and rock formations, caves, small lakes and pine woods, which local tradition identifies as the site of the Warring States Battle of Maling and where the Qianlong Emperor stayed on his southern tours. At its western foot lies the Huating site, a Neolithic cemetery of about 5,500 to 4,500 years ago whose finds, including fine jades, mix the northern Dawenkou culture with elements of the Liangzhu culture from the south; it is presented through a site museum and a reconstructed 'Huating tribe' area. Trails, a zip line and campsites make it a popular weekend escape.

rows.name: Pan'an Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park in Jiawang district made from what was the largest and most damaged area of subsided ground over old coal mines around Xuzhou, flooded and landscaped since the late 2000s into lakes, reed beds and stands of pond cypress. Visitors take rowing boats across the water and birdwatchers come for species such as the reed parrotbill, while the 'Xuzhou Night' street opened on the shore in 2023 for evening food and shows, and neighbouring Mazhuang village is known for its embroidered sachets.

rows.name: Pengzu Park
rows.summary: A large wooded city park on the southern side of central Xuzhou dedicated to Peng Zu, the legendary sage said to have lived some 800 years, whom tradition makes lord of the ancient state of Dapeng at Xuzhou. Paths wind over low hills and round ponds to a statue of Peng Zu, his memorial shrine and a pavilion, and the park's cherry trees draw crowds in spring.

rows.name: Ruins of the Ancient City of Xiapi
rows.summary: The buried remains of Xiapi at Gupi in northern Suining County, a walled city for well over a thousand years and the place where the warlord Lü Bu was captured and put to death at the end of the 2nd century, an episode retold in Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Excavations since 2014 found walls of the Eastern Han, Western Jin, Song–Jin and Ming–Qing periods stacked one above another, before an earthquake in 1668 led to floods that left the city under a lake. Little stands above ground: an archaeological park was approved in 2023 and is still being developed, while the town has a local history museum and a new Three Kingdoms-style market street.

rows.name: Shuiyue Temple, Suining
rows.summary: A large Buddhist temple in Suining County, built in recent years on the site of the county's former Dizang Temple inside the Baitang River wetland park. Its halls follow a traditional monastery layout but in a deliberately modern architectural style, and paths through the surrounding wetland make it a quiet half-day outing.

rows.name: Xuzhou Amusement Park
rows.summary: A theme-park complex west of Yunlong Lake made up of a water park and two themed ride parks, with a resort hotel and a shopping street attached. It is a family day out rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Xuzhou Han Culture Scenic Area (Shizishan)
rows.summary: A park in Xuzhou's eastern suburbs built around Shizishan, where a Western Han king of Chu was buried in the 2nd century BC in a tomb cut 117 m into the hillside; visitors walk through its passages and a dozen rock-hewn chambers, found in 1991 and excavated in 1994–95. Nearby, the Han Terracotta Army Museum shows the four pits found in 1984 that held more than 2,300 painted pottery figures, and two further cavalry pits are displayed under water in a gallery opened in 2006. Tomb and pits belong to the national heritage unit of the Han Chu king tombs; many of the finds, including a gold-threaded jade suit, are in the Xuzhou Museum.

rows.name: Xuzhou Han Stone Relief Art Museum
rows.summary: A museum on the eastern shore of Yunlong Lake devoted to the carved stone panels that lined Eastern Han tombs, shrines and gate towers around Xuzhou. The reliefs show scenes of daily life, historical tales and the world of immortals and mythical beasts, and the museum is run as a branch of the Xuzhou Museum.

rows.name: Xuzhou Museum
rows.summary: Xuzhou's main history museum, a national first-class museum at the northern foot of Yunlong Mountain, best known for finds from the rock-cut tombs of the Western Han kings of Chu, among them a jade burial suit sewn with gold thread. Its grounds take in the excavated Han-dynasty quarry where stone was cut from the hillside, part of the national heritage unit of the Chu king tombs, and the surviving main hall of a palace built for the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour of 1757.

rows.name: Yaowan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town on the Grand Canal where it meets Luoma Lake, in the south-west of Xinyi, with some 1,300 years of history; it grew into a busy trading port in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Stone-paved lanes keep a large group of Ming and Qing buildings, among them merchant guild halls and old banking houses, and in the evenings the town stages shows including the molten-iron 'fire flower' display, with lantern-lit boat trips along the water.

rows.name: Yunlong Lake
rows.summary: A lake on the south-western edge of central Xuzhou, enlarged from low-lying ground into a reservoir and now the heart of a 5A scenic area, framed by green hills on three sides with Yunlong Mountain to the east. Paths, causeways, old-style bridges and pavilions run round the water, with peach blossom and willows in spring, lotus in summer, red maples in autumn and plum blossom in winter, and the Han Stone Relief Art Museum stands on the eastern shore.

rows.name: Anfeng Ancient Town
rows.summary: Anfeng grew rich as the leading salt-producing town of the old Huainan salt fields, drawing Huizhou salt merchants who built along a long street beside the Chuanchang canal, and it was named a China Historical and Cultural Town in 2007. The preserved stretch of the old street, about 500 m long, keeps houses such as the Huizhou-style Bao family mansion of 1850 and the Wu clan hall, while a salt office, an opera stage and a salt wharf have been rebuilt nearby. The town was also known for its teahouses, which doubled as venues for Yangzhou-style storytelling.

rows.name: Caofangzi (Grass House) Park
rows.summary: A rural theme park of about 350 mu in Zhouhuo village, the home village of children's author Cao Wenxuan, winner of the 2016 Hans Christian Andersen Award, planned around the site of the original straw-roofed houses behind his novel Caofangzi (The Grass House). A re-creation of the novel's Youmadi primary school and play areas spread across the Lixiahe farmland, with stage shows, outdoor activities and school study programmes. It mainly suits families and readers of the book.

rows.name: China Water Margin Park & Shi Nai'an Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A themed park in Baiju town built around the Shi Nai'an Memorial Hall, which presents Baiju as the home town of Shi Nai'an, the writer traditionally credited with the classic novel Water Margin (the claim is shared with neighbouring Xinghua). The memorial hall shows more than 100 editions of the novel and material on Shi's life, and the wider park around it is themed on the novel. It suits readers of the novel more than general sightseers.

rows.name: Dafeng Dream Maze
rows.summary: A hedge-maze park in the countryside of Caoyan town that Guinness World Records lists as the largest permanent hedge maze, measured at 35,596.74 m² in June 2018, with about 9.5 km of paths. The main maze is laid out in the shape of a milu deer, with smaller heart-shaped, circular and children's mazes, an observation tower and bridges for seeing the pattern. It mainly suits families and groups.

rows.name: Dafeng Milu (Père David's Deer) Park
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Dafeng Milu National Nature Reserve on the Yellow Sea coast, where Père David's deer (milu), which had died out in China, were brought back in 1986 with 39 animals from British zoos; the reserve now holds the world's largest wild population of the species. Sightseeing buggies take visitors through woods, reed beds and grassland to see the deer herds, passing an arch made of thousands of shed antlers. The reserve is part of the Yellow Sea-Bohai Gulf migratory bird World Heritage Site and a Ramsar wetland.

rows.name: Dafeng Port Ocean World
rows.summary: An ocean-themed family attraction in the marine-industry park near Dafeng Port, with aquarium halls, marine science exhibits, a tropical plant house and a children's play area. It is a modern built attraction rather than a natural site, best for families with children.

rows.name: Dayangwan Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A large park on the northern edge of Yancheng where the old and new channels of the Yangwan river loop around islands and inlets, laid out with lawns, flower meadows and waterside paths. Visitors can ride painted boats or steer small self-drive boats along the water, and a staged show on the city's past, 'Yandu Wangshi', has been put on here.

rows.name: Dazong Lake
rows.summary: A shallow lake of about 28 km² on the border with Xinghua, long admired for its autumn views, whose northern, Yancheng shore is developed as a lakeside resort with a national wetland park. The scenic area has reed and water landscapes, a cherry-tree avenue about a kilometre long, a 25 m statue of Guanyin standing in the water and a water park. Next door, Dongjin Water Town is a newly built canal town of Song- and Republican-style buildings on nine islands linked by 24 bridges, with light and fountain shows.

rows.name: Dutch Flower Sea
rows.summary: A large flower park in Xinfeng town, named in memory of the Dutch water engineer who planned the area's irrigation in 1919, where tulips are grown over thousands of mu and a tulip festival has been held every spring since 2013. Tulips flower from March to May, followed by summer flowers and an autumn lily season, around a small town of European-style buildings. The park is popular for wedding photography and also has a theatre complex, Only Love: Theatre Fantasy City, created by director Wang Chaoge.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Reformed New Fourth Army (Taishan Temple)
rows.summary: After the Wannan Incident of January 1941, when Chiang Kai-shek ordered the New Fourth Army disbanded, the Communist leadership re-established the army's headquarters here in Taishan (Dongyue) Temple, a Ming-dynasty temple rebuilt in 1582. Liu Shaoqi and Chen Yi led the northern Jiangsu base area from the temple, and the Central China Bureau of the Communist Party was founded here in May 1941. The temple, wrecked in 1945, was restored to its old four-courtyard form in 1984 and opened to visitors in 1986.

rows.name: Huai Opera Town, Jianhu
rows.summary: A waterside village quarter of about 350 mu on the edge of the Jiulongkou wetland, renovated and extended in old style as a showcase for Huai opera and Jianhu acrobatics, both national intangible heritage. Old lanes and new buildings in matching style hold opera performances, street acrobatics, an art space, a bookshop and stalls selling local snacks such as lotus-root starch balls and fish balls. It is easily combined with a visit to Jiulongkou.

rows.name: Jinsha Lake, Funing
rows.summary: A lake and wetland resort on the southern edge of Funing town, developed from 2010 around about 10,000 mu of water with reed-fringed islands, and listed as a national water conservancy scenic area. Its freshwater sand beach and bathing area draws summer crowds, while egrets, kingfishers and other birds use the quieter islands.

rows.name: Jiulongkou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lake and marsh area in the Lixiahe lowlands where nine natural rivers meet around a small island, giving the name 'Nine Dragons' Mouth'. The scenic area covers reed beds, lotus and water-chestnut ponds and waterways, rich in water birds, and includes Longzhu (Dragon Pearl) Island; the Huai Opera Town, rated separately, lies next door.

rows.name: Longgang Peach Blossom Land
rows.summary: An orchard park in Longgang, an old market town west of Yancheng named after the 15-li sand ridge to its north said to resemble a lying dragon. Peach and pear orchards planted from 1959 on the sandy soil cover a core area of about 1,900 mu, best in March when the blossom is out, and the park adds riverside walks, a chestnut avenue, sand play areas, fruit picking and a wartime air-raid shelter.

rows.name: Majiadang Wetland
rows.summary: Majiadang is a broad expanse of reed marsh, fish ponds and waterways in south-western Funing, counted as the first of the 64 marshes of the Lixiahe lowlands, with villages built along the water. The scenic area, rated 4A in 2023, centres on Maliang Lake, with a newly built old-style 'Maliang Ancient Town' and a small amusement park, and takes in the waterside village of Mugou.

rows.name: Meihuawan Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park on the north-western edge of Dafeng themed on plum blossom, laid out around lakes off a branch of the Doulonggang River with groves of plum, cherry and crabapple among camphor, osmanthus and magnolia trees. It also has Chinese-style garden buildings, a plum culture hall, an angling centre and a water play area, and egrets and other birds nest in the trees; late winter and early spring, when the plums flower, is the time to go.

rows.name: New Fourth Army Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum opened in 1986 on Jianjun East Road about the New Fourth Army, the Communist-led army that fought the Japanese in central China and had its headquarters re-established in Yancheng in 1941 after the Wannan Incident. Its galleries draw on a collection of more than 10,000 wartime relics, documents and artworks, and the memorial also looks after the former headquarters at Taishan Temple across town. It is listed among China's national memorial sites of the War of Resistance against Japan.

rows.name: Shanghai Sent-Down Youth Memorial Hall, Dafeng
rows.summary: A museum on Haifeng Farm, one of the state farms run by Shanghai inside Dafeng, recording the tens of thousands of young Shanghai people sent to reclaim the Yellow Sea mudflats in the 1960s and 1970s. It occupies the former Yuanhua farm headquarters, a brick hall from the early 1950s, and displays hoes, straw sandals, call-up notices, photographs and wax figures, with recreated thatched living quarters. It is part of a cluster of sent-down-youth exhibition halls on the same site.

rows.name: Sheyang Andersen Fairy Tale Park
rows.summary: A modern theme park on the edge of Sheyang county town built around Hans Christian Andersen's stories, with four themed zones based on The Little Match Girl, Thumbelina, The Emperor's New Clothes and The Ugly Duckling, rides, themed halls, a castle and a water park. It forms one complex with the neighbouring Qianhe Lake park, a hotel and a shopping street, and is aimed at families with young children.

rows.name: Tiaozini Wetland
rows.summary: A vast tidal mudflat on the Yellow Sea coast, part of the Migratory Bird Sanctuaries along the Coast of Yellow Sea-Bohai Gulf of China World Heritage Site since 2019 and a key stopover on the East Asian–Australasian Flyway. The flats are cut by branching tidal creeks and turn red with seepweed in autumn, and at high tide tens of thousands of shorebirds crowd onto the '720' roost, 720 mu of former fish ponds turned into a fixed high-tide refuge in 2020; rarities include the spoon-billed sandpiper and Nordmann's greenshank. Only a small area of about 5 km² is open to visitors, with spring and autumn migration the best seasons.

rows.name: Xixi Tianxianyuan Scenic Area & Haichunxuan Pagoda
rows.summary: Xixi, on the western edge of Dongtai, was a salt-making centre from the Han dynasty and is linked with the folk legend of Dong Yong and the Seventh Fairy, a national intangible heritage item. The scenic area combines the Dong Yong and Seventh Fairy culture park, a rebuilt old town of Xixi and the garden of Taishan Temple, where the Haichunxuan Pagoda, a multi-eaved brick pagoda listed as Tang-dynasty and a national heritage site since 2013, still stands. The area has also staged shows based on the fairy legend and on Fan Zhongyan, who served as a salt official at Xixi.

rows.name: Xixin Temple
rows.summary: A large Buddhist temple near the Sheyang River, founded in the late Ming dynasty as a small shrine (Zhenlong Temple, later Xixin An), later destroyed and rebuilt from 1993. The new complex follows a traditional Chinese temple plan, with a Mahavira Hall, a Hall of Heavenly Kings, a Great Compassion pavilion, a ten-thousand-Buddha pagoda, a hall of 500 arhats, a jade Buddha hall and a Buddhist relics exhibition. It is an active temple with large crowds on festival days.

rows.name: Yancheng Museum
rows.summary: Yancheng's city museum, founded in 1961, moved in 2021 into a new group of buildings in traditional style on Jianjun West Road in the old centre. Its galleries cover the area's history, coastal ecology, urban development and folk traditions through more than 2,000 objects, and the building also houses an intangible-heritage performance centre. The former New Fourth Army headquarters at Taishan Temple is next door.

rows.name: Yancheng Red-crowned Crane Wetland (Yancheng National Nature Reserve)
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Jiangsu Yancheng Wetland Rare Birds National Nature Reserve, set up in 1983, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1992 and part of the Yellow Sea-Bohai Gulf migratory bird World Heritage Site since 2019. Several hundred wild red-crowned cranes winter on the coastal marshes from late October to March, while the visitor zone has a red-crowned crane museum, a crane breeding and feeding centre with captive cranes of several species, a water-bird lake and viewing pavilions among the reeds.

rows.name: Yancheng Sea Salt Historic and Cultural Zone (China Sea Salt Museum)
rows.summary: Yancheng, literally 'salt city', tells the story of its salt trade in this zone beside the Chuanchang River, an old salt-transport canal. The China Sea Salt Museum, opened in 2008, uses relics, models, sculptures and wax figures to show how sea salt was boiled from brine and later sun-dried; next to it, Salt Town Water Street is an old-style canal street with a Salt Yamen, a salt god's temple, a salt merchants' guild hall and Huai opera on a theatre boat, linked to the large Yandu Park. Evening boat trips run on the Chuanchang River.

rows.name: Yanfu Region Anti-Japanese Martyrs' Memorial Tower
rows.name_zh: 盐阜区抗日阵亡将士纪念塔
rows.pinyin: Yánfù Qū Kàngrì Zhènwáng Jiàngshì Jìniàntǎ
rows.summary: A memorial tower about 20 m high built in 1943 at Lupu to honour New Fourth Army soldiers and cadres killed in the Yanfu (Yancheng–Funing) anti-Japanese base area; local people supplied the bricks and labour, and a cast-iron statue of a soldier stands on top. Shelled in 1947 during the civil war, it was restored in 1959 with inscriptions by Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yi, Huang Kecheng and Zhang Aiping. Around it are marble tablets carved with the names of the dead, martyrs' tombs and a small exhibition room.

rows.name: Yellow Sea Coastal National Forest Park
rows.summary: A large planted forest on reclaimed coastal land near the Yellow Sea, begun in 1965 as the Dongtai state forest farm and made a national forest park in 2015. The mainly broadleaf plantation woodland shelters a rich wildlife, with 628 plant and 342 bird species recorded, and the park lies a short drive from the Tiaozini mudflats, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Crane Mosque
rows.summary: One of the oldest mosques in China, founded in 1275 by Puhaddin, an Arab missionary said to descend from the Prophet Muhammad, and rebuilt in 1390 and again in 1523. It is traditionally counted with mosques in Guangzhou, Quanzhou and Hangzhou as one of China's four great coastal mosques, and its name comes from a layout said to resemble a crane. It is still the main place of worship for Yangzhou's Muslims.

rows.name: Daming Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the Shugang hills, founded in the Daming era (457–464) that gave it its name, where the monk Jianzhen taught before his voyages to Japan, which he finally reached in 753 after five failed attempts. Its sights include the Jianzhen Memorial Hall, designed by Liang Sicheng after the main hall of Tōshōdai-ji and completed in 1973, Pingshan Hall, built in 1048 by the Song writer Ouyang Xiu, the nine-storey Qiling Pagoda, rebuilt in 1995, and a spring in the West Garden once ranked fifth in China for making tea.

rows.name: Dongguan Street
rows.summary: A 1,122 m flagstone street that ran from the Great East Gate of Yangzhou's old city to Dongguan by the canal, once one of the city's busiest trading streets. It keeps long-established shops such as the Simei pickle shop and the Xie Fuchun cosmetics shop, and along it or just off it are Ge Garden, Yipu, Wang Xiaoyuan and the rebuilt Xiaolinglong Shanguan garden. It was named one of China's famous historic streets in 2010, and the restoration of its houses and gardens won a UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award of Excellence for heritage conservation in 2023.

rows.name: Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum to the Qing painters known as the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou, opened in 1993 in the former Xifang Temple, where one of them, Jin Nong, lodged from the age of 70 until his death in 1763. The temple's Ming-dynasty main hall of nanmu timber is the protected monument, and the halls show calligraphy and paintings by the group, statues of the painters and a reconstruction of Jin Nong's lodging.

rows.name: Gaoyou Pawnshop (Tongxing Pawnshop)
rows.summary: A pawnshop outside Gaoyou's old north gate, opened in the early to mid Qing and said by local tradition to have belonged to the minister Heshen; it traded until 1927, reopened briefly and closed for good during the war against Japan. The compound of five rows of buildings covers about 3,300 m² and is one of the better-preserved large pawnshops of the period, with its storage building and recreated scenes showing how pawning worked.

rows.name: Ge Garden
rows.summary: A salt merchant's garden rebuilt in 1818 by Huang Zhiyun on the site of an older Ming garden and named after its bamboo, whose clustered leaves resemble the character 个 (ge). It is best known for its four-season rockeries, which use bamboo with rock, grey Taihu stone, Huangshan stone and Xuan stone to evoke spring, summer, autumn and winter. The garden is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Han Guangling Tomb Museum (Hanling Yuan)
rows.summary: A museum on the Shugang hills built around the tomb of Liu Xu, the first Prince of Guangling in the Western Han, and the tomb of his consort, both excavated at Tianshan in Gaoyou from 1979 and later moved here. They are large timber tombs of the rare huangchang ticou type, in which the coffin chamber is enclosed by walls of stacked timber, and the reassembled chambers are the centrepiece of the museum.

rows.name: He Garden
rows.summary: A large late-Qing residence and garden, also called Jixiao Shanzhuang, built from 1862 to 1875 by He Zhidao, a former circuit intendant in Hubei, who added the older Pianshi Shanfang garden in 1883. A two-storey covered walkway links the halls of the house with the garden, and buildings with Western details stand among classical rockeries and ponds; the rockery of Pianshi Shanfang is attributed to the painter Shitao. In China it is often called 'the foremost garden of the late Qing'.

rows.name: Jia Salt Merchant Residence & Erfen Mingyue Lou
rows.summary: The house and garden of the late-Qing Zhenjiang salt merchant Jia Yuan, a residence of linked halls and courtyards with the Erfen Mingyue Lou garden, named after the Tang poet Xu Ning's line giving Yangzhou two of the world's three shares of moonlight. Since 2023 it has been the core of Guangling Youyan, a restored block of about a hectare that also takes in a former salt-trade guild hall and an old school, with workshops for Yangzhou crafts such as silk velvet flowers, embroidery and woodblock printing.

rows.name: Longqiuzhuang Neolithic Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement dated to about 7,000–5,000 years ago, found in the 1970s and excavated in 1993–95, when 402 burials and a house site were uncovered; it gave its name to the Longqiuzhuang culture of the Jianghuai region east of the Grand Canal. The site is now a park that combines displays on that culture with wetland scenery.

rows.name: Lu Salt Merchant Residence (China Huaiyang Cuisine Museum)
rows.summary: Built in 1897 for the Jiangxi salt merchant Lu Shaoxu, this is the largest surviving salt merchant's house in Yangzhou, with more than 130 rooms on over a hectare: a nine-courtyard residence in front and the Yi Garden, with a stone boat, pavilion and pond, behind. Four of its halls burned in 1981 and were rebuilt in 2005–06, and the house now holds the China Huaiyang Cuisine Museum, with displays on the regional cuisine and a restaurant serving banquets. It is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Memorial of the Last Battle of the War of Resistance, Gaoyou
rows.name_zh: 抗日战争最后一役文化园
rows.pinyin: Kàngrì Zhànzhēng Zuìhòu Yī Yì Wénhuàyuán
rows.summary: In December 1945, more than four months after Japan announced its surrender, the New Fourth Army's Central China Field Army under Su Yu attacked Gaoyou, whose Japanese and collaborationist garrison had refused to surrender to it; the town fell on 26 December and the Japanese garrison surrendered in the auditorium of its headquarters. That building at 70 Xihe Lane is preserved as the site of the surrender, with a memorial hall and a victory square, and Chinese official histories call the action the last battle of the War of Resistance Against Japan. According to Chinese state media, 892 Japanese soldiers were taken prisoner.

rows.name: Nashan Geopark
rows.summary: Nashan, a 146 m hill in the countryside of Yizheng, is an extinct shield volcano whose interior was exposed by quarrying from the 1980s. The geopark, opened in 2016, shows basalt columns with five different forms of columnar jointing, along with volcanic bombs and scoria, and has a geology museum with immersive displays; tea is grown on the slopes.

rows.name: Phoenix Island Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A wetland park on the islands among the rivers north-east of Yangzhou, laid out around water, islands, woodland and birds. Inside are a petting area with capybaras, alpacas, rabbits and call ducks and a walk-through bird park, so it mainly suits families and anyone wanting greenery outside the city.

rows.name: Sanwan Park & China Grand Canal Museum
rows.summary: In 1597 Yangzhou's prefect Guo Guangfu replaced a straight stretch of the canal, nearly 200 m long, with a 1.8 km course of three bends to raise the water level and slow the current; after 2014 factories and wharves were cleared from its banks, which reopened in 2017 as a wetland park. Its centrepiece is the China Grand Canal Museum, opened in June 2021 in a ship-shaped building designed by Zhang Jinqiu, with the Dayun Pagoda beside it. The galleries cover the whole canal, from a 25.7 m section of riverbed lifted from the Zhouqiao site on the Bian canal to a restored Qing passenger boat and a recreated canal-town street.

rows.name: Song Jiacheng Archaeological Park (Yangzhou City Ruins)
rows.summary: The Jiacheng was a walled enclosure the Southern Song built between Yangzhou's main city and the fortress on the Shugang hills; its earthen walls, about 2.6 km round and still 1–3 m above the surrounding ground, are ringed by water and now form a park with paths and the excavated north gate. It is one of the visible parts of the Yangzhou City Ruins, the overlapping Sui, Tang and Song cities protected as one national site, whose other display points include the West Gate ruins museum of the Song city on Siwangting Road and the Tang City Ruins Museum on the Shugang, built over the site of the Sui emperor's Jiangdu palace.

rows.name: Tomb of Emperor Yang of Sui
rows.summary: The tombs of Emperor Yang of Sui, who was killed in a mutiny at his Jiangdu palace in Yangzhou in 618, and of his empress Xiao, found on a building site at Caozhuang in 2012 and identified the next year by an epitaph naming 'the late Emperor Yang of Sui'. Finds included a complete thirteen-ring gold-and-jade belt of imperial rank and two of the emperor's teeth. A site park and museum opened in 2024: the tombs are covered by a hall shaped after the truncated-pyramid mounds of Sui and Tang imperial tombs, and galleries explain the excavation and Sui history.

rows.name: Tomb of Puhaddin
rows.summary: The walled cemetery of Puhaddin, an Arab missionary said to be a 16th-generation descendant of the Prophet Muhammad, who came to Yangzhou in the late Southern Song and died in 1275. His square tomb chamber combines an Arab-style domed interior with a Chinese tiled roof, and around it are other Muslim graves, a pavilion with four Yuan-dynasty Arabic tombstones, a small mosque and a garden. It is on China's list of sites for a future Maritime Silk Road World Heritage nomination.

rows.name: Wang Xiaoyuan Residence
rows.summary: A salt merchant's house in the Dongquanmen lanes, built in the late Qing by the Huizhou merchant Wang Zhuming and enlarged by his eldest son in the early Republic, and one of the most complete merchant residences of that period in Yangzhou. Its name, 'Wang's Little Garden', refers to its small but carefully made gardens set among the halls; the house was restored in 2017 and 2019 and is open to visitors.

rows.name: Wenyou Terrace, Gaoyou
rows.summary: A group of halls in the north of Gaoyou that began in 976 as a temple to the god of Mount Tai. Its name, 'Terrace of Literary Outings', recalls a gathering in 1084 when Su Dongpo, passing through, met the Gaoyou poet Qin Guan and the scholars Sun Jue and Wang Gong here to drink and talk about literature. The core of the site is a provincial heritage unit and one of the traditional Eight Views of Gaoyou.

rows.name: Wu Daotai Mansion (Wu Family Residence)
rows.summary: A large mansion begun in 1888 for Wu Yinsun, a Qing official who had served as circuit intendant at Ningbo, and laid out after the intendant's office there. Its surviving buildings include a Western-style house and the Cehai Lou library, modelled on Ningbo's Tianyi Pavilion, which once held some 200,000 volumes; the family garden and ancestral hall have gone. After 1949 the compound was used by a hospital, and part of it is shown to visitors as the Wu Daotai Mansion.

rows.name: Xiaopangu Garden
rows.summary: A compact garden and house in the lanes of south-east Yangzhou, laid out in the late 18th century and rebuilt after 1904 by Zhou Fu, Viceroy of Liangjiang, with the residence on the west and the garden on the east over about 5,700 m². Its name, 'Little Winding Valley', comes from the rockery and its twisting paths, which are the garden's main feature; it is regarded as a typical Qing-dynasty Yangzhou garden.

rows.name: Yangzhou Museum & China Block Printing Museum
rows.summary: Yangzhou's main museum shares a modern building beside Mingyue Lake with the China Block Printing Museum, so the pair is known locally as the 'Double Museum'; both opened here in 2005. The galleries trace the city's history from the Neolithic to the late Qing, with special emphasis on woodblock printing and shipbuilding. The best-known piece is a Yuan-dynasty blue-glazed vase with a white dragon, one of only three known.

rows.name: Yipu Garden
rows.summary: A compact house and garden on Dongguan Street, built in 1910 for the banker Li Hesheng, with a five-courtyard residence on the west and the garden on the east, separated by a fire lane. Unusually for Yangzhou, the garden lies beside rather than behind the house: rockwork is built against the boundary wall, with a five-sided half-pavilion over a pool, and a flower hall leads to a rear garden enclosed by a two-level corridor and rockwork. The house was restored in 2007–08.

rows.name: Yucheng Postal Stop
rows.summary: The largest relay station on the Ming–Qing Grand Canal, founded in 1375 beside the canal at Gaoyou to keep post horses and boats and lodge officials; it burned in 1557, was rebuilt in 1568 and was repaired several times under the Qing. The restored complex includes the Huanghua Hall where officials were received, the Zhujie Hall with Ming beams and columns, and a three-storey drum tower, and it houses a museum of China's postal relay system. It is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Zhuyuwan Scenic Area (Yangzhou Zoo)
rows.summary: A peninsula park in Wantou, north-east of Yangzhou, that combines gardens, woodland and water with the city zoo. Its best-known animals are two giant pandas, and there are also tigers, giraffes, gibbons, meerkats and capybaras as well as an aquarium hall, so it is mainly a family outing.

rows.name: Jinshan, Jiaoshan and Beigushan
rows.pinyin: Jīn Shān · Jiāo Shān · Běigù Shān
rows.summary: Zhenjiang's three classic Yangtze hills are managed as one scenic area but are separate parks several kilometres apart. Jinshan, a former island joined to the south bank by silt in the late Qing, is covered by Jinshan Temple, the setting of the Legend of the White Snake, and topped by the Cishou Pagoda, while Jiaoshan, reached by a short ferry, holds Dinghui Temple and the Jiaoshan Stele Museum, whose more than 400 inscribed stones include fragments of the 'Eulogy on Burying a Crane' cliff inscription. On Beigushan stand Ganlu Temple, linked in legend to Liu Bei's marriage, and its iron pagoda, whose base and lower storeys date from the Song dynasty.

rows.name: Mi Fu Calligraphy Park
rows.summary: A park in the Changshan hills of Dantu District devoted to Mi Fu, the Song-dynasty calligrapher and painter who spent much of his life in Zhenjiang. It has a gallery of model calligraphy engraved in stone, a Mi Fu academy and a hall on Chinese characters, and is popular for school study trips.

rows.name: Mount Baohua and Longchang Temple
rows.summary: Mount Baohua, a forested hill just east of Nanjing, is a national forest park whose main sight is Longchang Temple, founded in 502 and regarded as the ancestral seat of the Vinaya (monastic discipline) school of Chinese Buddhism. Its protected buildings are a copper hall and two brick 'beamless' halls built in 1605, and the temple also keeps its ordination platform and ginkgo trees about 400 years old.

rows.name: Mount Mao (Maoshan)
rows.summary: A low range on the Jurong–Jintan border, rising to 372.5 metres at Damao Peak, revered as the birthplace of the Shangqing school of Taoism and called by Taoists the 'eighth grotto-heaven and first blessed land'. The two main halls of the Maoshan Taoist Temple are the Jiuxiao Wanfu Palace on the summit and the Yuanfu Wanning Palace below Jijin Peak, where a 33-metre copper statue of Laozi has stood in the open since 1997. Other temples rebuilt since the 2000s are spread across the scenic area.

rows.name: Nanshan Scenic Area, Zhenjiang
rows.summary: A belt of low wooded hills on the southern edge of Zhenjiang, rising to 185 metres at Jiuhua Shan and protected as a scenic area of about 15.6 square kilometres, known as the city's 'mountain forest'. It is divided into the Zhulin, Zhaoyin and Wenyuan sections, with old Buddhist temples, springs and walking trails close to the city.

rows.name: Southern Dynasties Tomb Sculptures, Danyang
rows.summary: Danyang holds the mausoleums of emperors of the Southern Qi and Liang dynasties, both of the Xiao clan, and about a dozen groups of 5th- and 6th-century stone guardians still stand in the fields east and north-east of the town. Most groups are pairs of winged beasts, qilin and tianlu at the imperial tombs, and at Sanchengxiang, where several mausoleums lie close together, the tomb of Xiao Shunzhi also keeps its carved columns and stele bases. The groups have been fenced since 2019, after one was damaged by illegal rubbing.

rows.name: Xijindu Ancient Street
rows.summary: A stepped lane climbing Yuntai Hill in western Zhenjiang to the old Xijin ferry crossing on the Yangtze, where poets such as Li Bai, Wang Anshi and Su Shi waited for boats. Its stone steps pass Qing-era houses and shops, Guanyin Cave and the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda, a Tibetan-style stupa of the late Yuan or early Ming built over the street so that people walk beneath it, and the slope above holds buildings of the former British concession. The pagoda's restoration in 2000 won a UNESCO Asia-Pacific heritage conservation award in 2001.

rows.name: Zhenjiang Museum (Former British Consulate)
rows.summary: Zhenjiang's city museum has occupied the former British consulate since 1958: five colonial-style verandah buildings of 1889–90 on the slope above Xijindu, rebuilt after the first consulate was burned in riots in 1888. Its collection of nearly 30,000 objects is strongest in bronzes of the Wu state, Six Dynasties celadon, Tang gold and silver, Song silks and paintings of the local Jingjiang school.

rows.name: Zhenjiang Vinegar Culture Museum
rows.summary: A museum opened in 2010 by the Hengshun Group, maker of the well-known Zhenjiang vinegar, beside its works in Dantu District. It traces the history of vinegar-making through a history hall, a reconstructed old vinegar workshop, a traditional sauce yard and a hall on modern production.

rows.name: 1954 Constitution Drafting Site
rows.name_zh: 五四宪法历史资料陈列馆
rows.summary: A 1930s villa on the southern slope of Geling hill above West Lake's north shore, where Mao Zedong and a drafting group worked from December 1953 to March 1954 on the first draft of the constitution of the People's Republic, adopted in 1954. Since 2016 it has been an exhibition hall, with the single-storey wing set out as the offices and meeting room used by the drafters and the two-storey building telling the story of the constitution from drafting to adoption.

rows.name: Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City
rows.summary: The remains of the walled capital of the Neolithic Liangzhu culture (about 3300–2300 BC), which with its outer dams and the Yaoshan altar was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019. The site park lays out the raised palace platform of Mojiaoshan, the earthen city walls and the Fanshan elite cemetery, while the finds themselves are shown at the Liangzhu Museum.

rows.name: Baochu Pagoda
rows.summary: A slender seven-storey solid pagoda about 45 m tall on top of Baoshi Hill, the landmark of West Lake's northern skyline. First built in the 10th century, according to tradition to pray for the safe return of Qian Chu, the last king of Wuyue, from the Song court, it was rebuilt many times, most recently in the 20th century, and has no stair inside; paths and steps lead up to it from all sides of the hill.

rows.name: Cangqian Granary
rows.summary: A group of four storehouses beside the Yuhang Tang River at Cangqian, including two old timber granaries with a board dated 1859, where local grain keepers in 1953 created what was promoted as China's first insect-free granary. It became the model for a national campaign for granaries free of insects, mould, rats and sparrows, and a small exhibition on that history opened on the site in 2009.

rows.name: Chaoshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A low hill on the plain north-east of Hangzhou, famous for centuries for its plum trees and made popular by poets and artists in the late Qing and early Republican years. Around the Damingtang hall at its foot are the Song Plum Pavilion and the tomb and memorial hall of Wu Changshuo, first president of the Xiling Seal Society, and paths climb past the Miaoxi and Yuxi temples to a 'stone forest' of rocks on the summit.

rows.name: China National Silk Museum
rows.summary: A national museum of silk and textiles south of West Lake at the foot of Yuhuang Hill, opened in 1992 and rebuilt and enlarged in 2015–16. Its galleries trace Chinese silk and dress from Neolithic finds to the 20th century, with a weaving workshop, displays on sericulture and silk crafts (on UNESCO's intangible heritage list since 2009) and a textile conservation gallery, and it has held a Chinese costume festival every year since 2018.

rows.name: Daciyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rocky mountain in south-west Jiande nicknamed the 'little Jiuhua of western Zhejiang', whose cliffs, caves and trees are read together as the face of a giant natural standing Buddha. Its main temple hall, dedicated to Ksitigarbha, is built into a cave in the cliff with half of it overhanging the drop, which has earned it the name 'hanging temple of Jiangnan', and cliff walkways and incense corridors lead around the rock.

rows.name: Daming Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Qingliangfeng town on the far western edge of Lin'an, on the border with Anhui, whose cliffs and rock pinnacles are often compared to Huangshan. Besides a gorge with waterfalls, a lake and upland meadows, it now offers a cliff swing, mountain go-karts, a long slide and guided stream walks.

rows.name: Dream Town, Cangqian
rows.summary: A start-up and internet-business district opened in 2015 in the core of Cangqian, Yuhang, laid out as a scenic area from the start. Its Internet Village, Angel Village and start-up market sit along Cangqian's old street, renovated as an Entrepreneurship Street in 2016, close to the old Cangqian granary and Zhang Taiyan's former residence.

rows.name: Fantian Temple Dharani Pillars
rows.summary: A pair of octagonal stone dharani pillars, each 15.76 m tall, put up in 965 by the Wuyue king Qian Chu in front of the vanished Fantian Temple at the eastern foot of Phoenix Hill. The two identical pillars stand a little over ten metres apart, their eight-sided shafts finely carved.

rows.name: Feilai Feng Grottoes
rows.summary: Hundreds of Buddhist figures carved between the 10th and 14th centuries into the caves and cliffs of Feilai Feng, a limestone hill across a stream from Lingyin Temple. Most date from the Song, and the largest niche shows a laughing Maitreya surrounded by the Eighteen Arhats, while the Yuan carvings made under the Tibetan Buddhist monk Yang Lianzhenjia are counted among the largest surviving groups of Yuan-dynasty sculpture in China.

rows.name: Former Hangchow University (Zhijiang Campus)
rows.summary: The hillside campus above the Qiantang River of Hangchow University, a Presbyterian missionary college whose roots go back to a boys' school founded in Ningbo in 1845 and which was closed in 1952. Its 22 protected buildings, among them a red-brick clock tower and the Duke Hall chapel of 1917–19, have been used by Zhejiang University since 1961 and now house its law school.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhang Taiyan
rows.summary: The birthplace and family home of Zhang Taiyan (Zhang Binglin, 1869–1936), the philologist and anti-Qing revolutionary, on the north bank of the Yuhang Tang River at Cangqian. The narrow house runs back through four sections, three built before the Taiping war and the last in the early Republic, and is now the Zhang Taiyan Memorial Hall, with its halls, bedroom, study and kitchen around small courtyards and an exhibition in the rear building.

rows.name: Former Site of Qiushi Academy
rows.summary: The two surviving halls of Puci Temple on Daxue Road, where Qiushi Academy, one of China's first colleges on a Western model and the forerunner of Zhejiang University, opened in 1897. The site served as the Zhejiang University campus until 1956; most of it is now housing and shops, and only the main and side halls of the temple remain.

rows.name: Former Zhejiang Xingye Bank Building
rows.summary: A three-storey neoclassical bank building of 1923 at Yangbatou on Zhongshan Middle Road, put up in its home city by the Zhejiang Xingye Bank (the National Commercial Bank), one of the "Three Southern Banks" of Republican-era finance, to a design by the architect Shen Liyuan. It still works as a branch of ICBC, and its decorated facade faces Zhongshan Road, which follows the line of the imperial avenue of Southern Song Hangzhou.

rows.name: Fuchun Taoyuan
rows.summary: A scenic area at Shanglian village in Xukou town, in the hills of south-western Fuyang. Its centrepiece is Jiuxiao Biyun Cave, a limestone cave promoted for the size of its single main hall, and beside it the Yanling reservoir, the largest in Fuyang, is toured by bamboo raft; a small amusement park and a rafting run are also part of the area.

rows.name: Gaoting Hill
rows.summary: A chain of wooded hills about 9 km long on the north-eastern edge of urban Hangzhou, rising to 361 m at Gaoting peak; the western end is Banshan National Forest Park and the eastern end the Gaoting Shan scenic area. The hills are known for peach blossom in spring and once held several Buddhist temples, and their legends are painted in a mural in the Wangchen Pavilion on Banshan.

rows.name: Gongchen Pagoda
rows.summary: A five-storey square brick pagoda about 25 m tall on Gongchen Hill in the centre of Lin'an, built in 915 by Qian Liu, founder of the Wuyue kingdom, who was born at the foot of the hill. Its timber eaves have long gone, leaving a brick shell with doorways and niches on every face, and the site of the Gongchen Temple founded at the same time is part of the same listing.

rows.name: Grand Canal in Hangzhou & Gongchen Bridge
rows.summary: The southern end of the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal, part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site since 2014, runs through northern Hangzhou, and its landmark is Gongchen Bridge, a three-arch stone bridge 92 m long first built in 1631 and rebuilt in 1885. Around the bridge are the canal-side streets of the Qiaoxi historic quarter and the Grand Canal Museum on Canal Culture Square. Further south along the canal stands Fuyi Granary, built in 1880–84 to store tribute grain and now Hangzhou's only surviving canal granary.

rows.name: Hangzhou Confucian Temple & Forest of Steles
rows.summary: The former prefectural Confucian temple and school of Hangzhou on Fuxue Lane, of which only the Qing-dynasty Dacheng Hall survives, with a stele museum laid out around a water garden beside it. Its stones include the Southern Song Imperial Academy classics, portraits of Confucius and his 72 disciples, calligraphy by masters such as Zhao Mengfu and star maps from Wuyue royal tombs, and it is regarded as the largest stone-inscription museum in Zhejiang.

rows.name: Hangzhou Orient Culture Park
rows.summary: A large culture park opened in 2000 on the southern slopes of Yangqi Hill in Yiqiao, Xiaoshan, laid out on the eight trigrams and built around the three teachings of Confucianism, Buddhism and Daoism. It has a Guanyin square, a rebuilt Yangqi Chan Temple, a Daoist area and a Confucian temple, linked by a painted corridor over 2.7 km long, plus a resort area and gardens.

rows.name: Hangzhou Paradise
rows.summary: An amusement park opened in 1999 by the Songcheng group in the Xianghu resort area of Xiaoshan, with a suspended roller coaster, a log flume, a bungee jump and dozens of other rides, plus parades and stage shows. It suits families and ride fans.

rows.name: Hangzhou Polar Ocean Park
rows.name_zh: 杭州长乔极地海洋公园
rows.summary: A marine theme park opened in 2008 in the Xianghu area of Xiaoshan, with themed halls of polar and ocean animals including beluga whales, dolphins, penguins, polar bears, Arctic wolves, seals and sea lions. It suits families, and a separate Changqiao children's park lies next door.

rows.name: Hangzhou Safari Park
rows.summary: A large safari park opened in 2002 in Yinhu, Fuyang, with about 200 species, among them giant pandas, crested ibises, white tigers, white rhinos and golden snub-nosed monkeys. Animals are seen from walking trails and from vehicles in a drive-through section, and the park also stages animal shows; it suits families with children.

rows.name: Historic Buildings of the Zhejiang Library
rows.summary: The early buildings of the Zhejiang Library, founded in 1900 as one of China's first provincial public libraries. On Gushan island in West Lake stand the two-storey Western-style White Building of 1911–12, among China's earliest purpose-built public library buildings, the Red Building of 1906, built as a state guesthouse for a visiting German crown prince, and the 1936 Qingbai Villa, which now house its ancient-books department. On Daxue Road the neoclassical library of 1931, with a front of 16 Doric pilasters and a name board written by Cai Yuanpei, is still used as a reading room.

rows.name: Hu Qing Yu Tang & Hu Xueyan's Former Residence
rows.summary: A traditional Chinese medicine pharmacy founded in 1874 by the merchant-banker Hu Xueyan, whose Jiangnan-style courtyard building on Dajing Lane still sells medicines and houses a museum of Chinese medicine with demonstrations of traditional preparation. The listing also covers Hu Xueyan's former residence on Yuanbao Street nearby, a mansion and garden built in 1872–75 and restored in 2001.

rows.name: Huang Gongwang's Retreat
rows.summary: A bamboo-filled side valley at Miaoshanwu near Fuyang, by local tradition where the Yuan painter Huang Gongwang lived in his last years and painted 'Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains' (around 1350), whose two surviving parts are now in the Zhejiang Provincial Museum and the National Palace Museum in Taipei. Paths lead past a memorial hall to his life and work, a boat landing, an archway at the site of his hut, a spring and the South Tower presented as his studio.

rows.name: Jiande Aviation Town
rows.summary: A general-aviation town built around Qiandaohu General Airport near Shouchang in south-west Jiande, with a 1,200 m runway, flight schools and aviation companies. Visitors come for skydiving from about 3,000 m, low-level helicopter sightseeing flights and tethered hot-air balloon rides, and the town also has aviation-themed hotels and a hot-spring centre.

rows.name: Jiangnan Old Villages (Shen'ao and Dipu)
rows.summary: Five neighbouring villages in Jiangnan town, Tonglu (Shen'ao, Huanxi, Dipu, Xufan and Qingyuan), developed together as one rural scenic area of old houses, ancestral halls and farmland. Shen'ao, a national historic and cultural village since 2007, keeps a complex of old houses and halls protected by the province, while Dipu, home to the Shentu and Jiang clans, has ancestral halls, a memorial arch and Huizhou-style houses from the Ming to the Republic, with flower fields on its northern edge.

rows.name: Jingshan & Jingshan Temple
rows.summary: Jingshan Temple, on the summit area of Mount Jing in north-western Yuhang, was founded in 745 and in the Southern Song ranked first among the 'Five Mountains', the leading Chan Buddhist monasteries. It is honoured in Japan as one of the ancestral temples of Zen and in China as one of the birthplaces of tea culture. The present buildings were rebuilt on the old site from 1994, and the scenic area also takes in the old Jingshan path and the bell tower with a Southern Song imperial stele and a Ming bell.

rows.name: Laohuling Dam Site Park
rows.summary: A small site park at one of the high dams of the Liangzhu water-control system, built about 5,000 years ago in the hills north-west of the Liangzhu ancient city and part of the same World Heritage Site. Opened in 2022, it shows a cut through the 140 m-long earth dam under a glass shelter, where the bundles of grass-wrapped mud used to strengthen it can be seen, with a small visitor centre beside it.

rows.name: Leifeng Pagoda
rows.summary: A pagoda on Sunset Hill on the south shore of West Lake, rebuilt in 2002 over the ruins of the brick tower that the Wuyue king Qian Chu completed in the 970s and that collapsed in 1924. The new steel-framed tower, reached by escalators and served by lifts, preserves the base of the original inside, and the pagoda is famous as the prison of the White Lady in the Legend of the White Snake.

rows.name: Liangzhu Museum
rows.summary: The museum of the Neolithic Liangzhu culture, set in a park at Liangzhu in a building by David Chipperfield of four long stone-clad blocks around courtyards, opened in 2008. Its three galleries show more than 1,000 jades, pottery and lacquer pieces from the Liangzhu sites and explain the walled city a few kilometres to the west that is now a World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Lingqi Caves
rows.summary: One of the first show caves developed in Zhejiang, in the hills of Hangtou town south-west of Jiande city, made up of three limestone caves and a small stone forest. Lingquan Cave is known for its underground water, which visitors can tour by rowing boat, Qingfeng Cave for its cool draughts and Aiyun Cave for its mists, and all are lit with coloured light shows. The site was a filming location for the 1986 television series Journey to the West.

rows.name: Liuhe Pagoda
rows.summary: The Six Harmonies Pagoda on Yuelun Hill above the Qiantang River, first built in 970 by the Wuyue kingdom to calm the river's tidal bore and long used as a beacon for boats. The present brick core dates from the Southern Song rebuilding of the 1160s and its timber outer eaves from the Qing, so the octagonal tower shows thirteen roofs outside but has seven storeys within, linked by internal stairs to the top.

rows.name: Longmen Ancient Town
rows.summary: A clan town at the foot of Longmen Mountain on the south side of the Fuchun River, where more than 90 per cent of the 7,000 residents are surnamed Sun and claim descent from Sun Quan, ruler of the Three Kingdoms state of Wu. Its lanes and long market street are lined with more than 40 Ming and Qing halls of the Sun clan, centred on two ancestral temples, as well as houses, brick memorial archways, a pagoda and footbridges, and the townspeople still live in them.

rows.name: Longwu Tea Town
rows.summary: A tea-growing district in the hills of Zhuantang, south-west Hangzhou, where tea gardens cover the slopes around the villages; Hangzhou media describe it as the largest producing area of West Lake Longjing tea. It was developed as one of Zhejiang's first 'characteristic towns', combining tea growing with tea houses, tea culture and rural leisure.

rows.name: Mahakala Carving at Baocheng Temple
rows.summary: A small temple on the south-eastern slope of Wu Hill, founded under the Wuyue kingdom, whose cliff niches hold a carving of Mahakala dated 1322, the only dated Mahakala image in China. The fierce protector deity of Tibetan Buddhism, worshipped by the Yuan court as a god of war, is flanked by Manjushri and Samantabhadra, with a Chinese inscription beside the niche.

rows.name: Mount Tianmu
rows.summary: A forested mountain in western Lin'an, about 80 km west of Hangzhou, whose West Tianmu peak (1,506 m) and its slopes have been a national nature reserve since 1986 and a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1996. It is known for giant Japanese cedars, one of them named 'Giant Tree King' by the Qianlong Emperor, old ginkgos, waterfalls and temples, among them Chanyuan Temple at the foot of the mountain.

rows.name: Nanfeng and Beifeng Pagodas, Meicheng
rows.pinyin: Méichéng Nánfēng Tǎ hé Běifēng Tǎ
rows.summary: Two seven-storey brick pagodas on hilltops facing each other across the river at Meicheng, where the Xin'an River meets the Lan. The South Peak pagoda, first built in the Sui or Tang and rebuilt in the Ming, is octagonal and about 35 m tall, and the pair, known as the 'twin pagodas above the clouds', was one of the Eight Views of Yanling.

rows.name: Nanshan Cliff Carvings, Pingyao
rows.summary: A row of Buddhist figures and one Taoist figure cut into an old quarry face on Nanshan hill at Pingyao, most of them seated Amitabha Buddhas from the Yuan dynasty, the largest almost 10 m tall. Inscriptions of 1328 and 1341 name monks of a nearby temple as the patrons, and the plainer, more human-looking figures differ in style from the Yuan carvings at Feilai Feng; nine badly damaged Ming figures stand at the eastern end.

rows.name: Phoenix Mosque
rows.summary: One of the four great old mosques of China's south-east coast, on Zhongshan Middle Road in central Hangzhou, first built in the Tang or Song and rebuilt in 1281 with funds from Ala al-Din, a Persian Muslim settler. Its brick prayer hall without beams is roofed by three domes painted inside, an unusual blend of Islamic and Jiangnan building, and a Ming carved board of 1451 with Qur'an text stands against its rear wall. The front buildings were cut back for road widening in 1928, and the gate with its moon-viewing tower was rebuilt in 2009.

rows.name: Qiandao Lake Stone Forest
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A karst landscape of about 20 km² in Shilin town, south of Qiandao Lake, where limestone pinnacles and ridges stand in maze-like clusters among the hills. It is made up of three areas, Lanyuping, Daimaoling and Xishanping, where visitors walk among the stone peaks, springs and gullies, and a glass walkway, a via ferrata and a canyon swing have been added.

rows.name: Qiantang River Bridge
rows.summary: A double-deck road and rail bridge across the Qiantang River, designed by the engineer Mao Yisheng and built between 1934 and 1937 as the first such bridge designed and built in China. Less than three months after it opened it was blown up by the Chinese side to slow the Japanese advance, and it was fully repaired only in 1953; it still carries trains on the lower deck and road traffic above, and a memorial hall near its northern approach tells its story.

rows.name: Qinghefang Historic District
rows.summary: Described as the only fairly intact old street quarter left in Hangzhou, Qinghefang lies at the foot of Wu Hill and is named after the mansion of the Southern Song general Zhang Jun, Prince of Qinghe. Its spine is Hefang Street, a pedestrian street of old-style shopfronts and stalls, with side lanes such as Dajing Lane leading to the Hu Qing Yu Tang pharmacy and Hu Xueyan's mansion.

rows.name: Qingshan Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake of about 20 km² on the eastern edge of Lin'an, built in 1964 for flood control on the Nantiaoxi river and now part of a national forest park. On its northern arm grows a 'water forest' of pond cypresses and redwoods planted in the water in 1977, and a 42 km greenway for cycling and walking circles the lake.

rows.name: Songcheng Theme Park
rows.summary: A theme park opened in 1996 on the south-western edge of Hangzhou, built as a Song-dynasty town with streets in old style, about 20 small theatres and staged street performances. Its main draw is The Romance of the Song Dynasty, an hour-long stage spectacle running since 1997 that retells episodes of Hangzhou's history and legend such as the White Snake story, and the park suits families and fans of big shows rather than visitors looking for historic buildings.

rows.name: Southern Hills Carvings (Ciyunling, Yanxia Cave, Tianlong Temple)
rows.summary: Three groups of 10th-century Buddhist carvings from the Wuyue kingdom in the hills south of West Lake, listed together with Feilai Feng. At Ciyunling a niche of 942 holds seven figures around Amitabha, flanked by bodhisattvas and guardian kings, and nearby at Tianlong Temple three niches of 965 show Maitreya, Amitabha and a Water-Moon Guanyin; in Yanxia Cave, 3 km to the west, sixteen Wuyue arhats line the cave with Song bodhisattvas at its mouth.

rows.name: Southern Song Capital Lin'an & Deshou Palace Museum
rows.summary: Remains of Lin'an, capital of the Southern Song from 1138 to 1276, lie buried beneath central Hangzhou, the palace area on Phoenix Hill more than 3 m down, with an imperial street that ran north through the city. The main place to see them is the Deshou Palace Site Museum, opened in 2022 over the excavated palace where the emperors Gaozong and Xiaozong lived after abdicating, with a reconstructed hall and digital displays over the foundations. Nearby, the Imperial Ancestral Temple site is a public park with column bases on show, and site displays along Zhongshan Road show excavated sections of the Imperial Street.

rows.name: Southern Song Guan Kiln Museum
rows.summary: A ceramics museum opened in 1992 over the Jiaotanxia kiln site at the southern foot of Yuhuang Hill, where the Southern Song court made its official 'Guan' ware. The excavated kiln remains, including a dragon kiln, are shown in place beside the galleries, and since 2020 the museum has been run as a branch of the Hangzhou West Lake Museum.

rows.name: Stone Pagoda of Puqing Temple
rows.summary: A small granite pagoda of six sides and seven storeys, about 7 m tall, carved in the early 1320s under the Yuan dynasty and the only thing left of Puqing Temple. Its niches hold 28 small seated Buddhas, and the top storey is inscribed with wishes for the emperor's long life, good harvests and peace in the realm.

rows.name: Sutra Pillar of Longxing Temple
rows.summary: An octagonal stone sutra pillar about 5 m tall, carved in 837 under the Tang dynasty and the oldest surviving structure in central Hangzhou. Its shaft is inscribed with the Usnisa Vijaya Dharani Sutra and its base carved with strongmen, and since the temple around it was demolished in 1959 it has stood alone under a protective pavilion and glass on Yan'an Road.

rows.name: Taihu Source
rows.summary: A wooded gorge about 5 km long in Taihuyuan town, northern Lin'an, with cliffs, waterfalls and clear streams, promoted as one of the sources of the Lake Tai river system. It is a summer retreat from Hangzhou's heat, and the town's villages, among them Baisha, have more than 500 homestays and farm guesthouses.

rows.name: Tangxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town on the Grand Canal north of Hangzhou, often spelt Tangqi, which grew into one of the richest market towns of the Jiangnan region in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Its landmark is Guangji Bridge, a seven-arch stone bridge over the canal rebuilt in 1489, and the old town keeps a Qianlong-era imperial stele, an ancient well and the riverside Shuibei street. The area is also known for its loquats and local pastries.

rows.name: Tianzidi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area of about 6 km² at Luoshan village in Baijiang town, in the hills of western Tonglu towards Qiandao Lake, now run as the Tianzidi mountain park. A covered moving walkway carries visitors up the slope to a karst cave, an aerial playground, a raft slide down the Zilong gorge and a dinosaur park, with more amusement rides added in 2025, so it suits families with children.

rows.name: Tomb of Qian Liu (Wuyue Royal Mausoleums)
rows.summary: The tomb of Qian Liu (852–932), founder of the Wuyue kingdom that ruled Hangzhou and the lower Yangtze in the tenth century, on the southern slope of Taimiao Hill in Lin'an: an earth mound 9 m high and about 50 m square in a memorial park with a spirit way, gate towers, an archway and the Qian Wang Shrine. Robbers reached the burial chamber in 2019; some of the objects recovered by police in 2020, among them gold-and-jade belt plaques and fine celadon, are now in the Lin'an Wuyue Culture Museum.

rows.name: Tomb of Yu Qian
rows.summary: The tomb of Yu Qian (1398–1457), the Ming minister of war who led the defence of Beijing after the emperor was captured by the Mongols in the Tumu crisis, and who was executed when that emperor regained the throne.
