Rebuilt in 1982, the horseshoe-shaped mound at the foot of Santai Hill is approached through a stone gateway and a spirit way lined with six pairs of stone figures, and the neighbouring Yu Qian Shrine has an exhibition on his life.

rows.name: Wenlan Pavilion
rows.summary: One of the seven imperial libraries built to hold the Qianlong Emperor's great manuscript collection, the Siku Quanshu, completed in 1783 and the only one of the three southern libraries still standing. Rebuilt in 1880 after the Taiping war, it is a small walled garden with a rockery, a pond with a tall standing stone and the two-storey library hall, now part of the Gushan branch of the Zhejiang Provincial Museum.

rows.name: Wenyuan Shicheng, Jiangjia
rows.summary: A new town built in the mid-2010s at Jiangjia on Qiandao Lake as a recreation of Shicheng, the old seat of Sui'an county that was drowned when the Xin'an River reservoir filled in 1959. Its streets of new traditional-style buildings are lined with rebuilt memorial arches and hold a Shicheng museum, craft workshops, old-brand shops, bars and homestays. It is the centre of Jiangjia's 'Leshui' lakeside resort town, which the 4A listing names with it.

rows.name: West Lake Expo Museum
rows.summary: The industry hall of the first West Lake Exposition, held in 1929, and the only one of the fair's purpose-built halls to survive. Behind a classical-style front it has a wide-span timber-trussed interior, and since 2003 it has housed a museum on the 1929 exposition and its later revivals, built up largely from donated objects.

rows.name: Xiajiang Village
rows.summary: A mountain village in Fengshuling town, Chun'an, with white-walled houses along a clear stream, once one of the poorest in the area. From the 2000s it was the rural contact point of five successive Zhejiang Party secretaries, Xi Jinping among them, and it is now presented as a model of rural revitalisation, with dozens of homestays, orchards and a covered bridge. It was a filming location for the 2020 film 'My People, My Homeland' and was named one of UN Tourism's Best Tourism Villages in 2024.

rows.name: Xianghu Lake and Kuahuqiao Site Museum
rows.summary: A lake in Xiaoshan south of the Qiantang River, first dammed as an irrigation reservoir in 1112 and later largely filled in by brickworks, which was dredged and landscaped in stages between 2006 and 2016 as a lakeside park and resort area. On its south shore the Kuahuqiao Site Museum, opened in 2009, presents a Neolithic village of about 8,000 to 7,000 years ago, including a pine dugout canoe that is the oldest yet found in China, kept in a hall over the excavation.

rows.name: Xiling Seal Engravers' Society
rows.summary: The hillside home on Gushan of a society of seal carvers founded in 1904 by a group of engravers, with the master carver Wu Changshuo as its first president, and nicknamed "the foremost society under heaven". Its grounds keep an Eastern Han stele and a collection of inscriptions by noted artists carved on stones and rock faces, and the society's seal-engraving craft is on China's national list of intangible heritage.

rows.name: Xinye Village
rows.summary: A clan village of the Ye family in south-west Jiande, founded in the early 13th century at the foot of Yuhua Hill. It keeps 16 ancestral halls, a pagoda, a temple and more than 200 old houses built between the Ming dynasty and the Republican era, among them the Xishan ancestral hall, the Youxu hall and the Tuanyun Pagoda, and the villagers still hold ancestral rites each spring at the Shangsi festival.

rows.name: Xishan Bridge
rows.summary: A single-span stone bridge in Zizhou village, dated by an inscription to 1265 in the Southern Song dynasty and still used by villagers. Its arch is built of long stone slabs set in five straight sections, giving a polygonal span of about 11 m.

rows.name: Xixi National Wetland Park
rows.summary: An urban wetland of about 11.5 km² on the western edge of Hangzhou, a maze of six main watercourses, ponds and fish ponds among thousands of old persimmon trees, long admired by poets and painters. Opened in 2005 as China's first national wetland park, it mixes protected marsh, where more than 80 bird species have been recorded, with water-village houses, humped bridges and pavilions.

rows.name: Yan Ziling's Fishing Terrace
rows.summary: A riverside hill on the Fuchun River south of Tonglu, honouring Yan Guang (Yan Ziling), a first-century scholar who refused office from his old schoolfellow Emperor Guangwu of Han and retired here to fish. Visitors arrive by boat to see a stone memorial archway, a garden of inscribed steles with poems and essays about the place, and the Shrine of Mr Yan, first founded by Fan Zhongyan in the Northern Song.

rows.name: Yanzhou Ancient City (Meicheng)
rows.summary: The old prefectural town of Meicheng, where the Xin'an and Lan rivers meet to form the Fuchun, which for about 1,200 years was the seat of Muzhou and later Yanzhou prefecture. Most of its walls, rebuilt in 1361, were pulled down in 1938, but a riverside stretch of about 380 m survives with two southern gates, and the lanes behind keep old houses, memorial archways and the Yuquan Temple alongside gates rebuilt or reopened in 2013–14.

rows.name: Yaolin Wonderland
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in Yaolin town, in the hills north-west of Tonglu, whose first hall opened to visitors in 1980; its winding halls are filled with stalactites, stalagmites and flowstone. The caves are now lit with coloured light installations and an artificial snowfall effect, and the Chuiyun Tongtian River cave lies in the same town.

rows.name: Yue Fei Temple and Tomb
rows.summary: The temple and tomb of Yue Fei, the Song general who fought the Jurchen Jin and was executed in 1142 through court intrigue, first built here in 1221 after his rehabilitation and long a symbol of loyalty to the nation. The complex at the foot of Qixia Ridge has the temple hall with his statue, a separate Temple of Loyalty, and the tombs of Yue Fei and his son behind a spirit way of stone figures; it was badly damaged in 1966 and restored in 1979.

rows.name: Yuhuangshan South Fund Town
rows.summary: A finance district for private investment funds at the southern foot of Yuhuang Hill, between West Lake and the Qiantang River, which began promoting itself as a tourist area in 2015. For visitors its interest lies in the landscaped parks and old sites inside it, among them the Baguatian ('Eight Trigrams Field') heritage park, the Jiangyangfan ecological park and Baita Park, with the Southern Song Guan Kiln Museum, the Tianlong Temple carvings and the Zhakou White Pagoda close by.

rows.name: Zhakou White Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal stone pagoda about 14 m tall, carved to imitate a timber building down to its brackets and window bars, and dated on its style to the Wuyue kingdom or the early Northern Song. Its storeys carry reliefs of Buddhas and bodhisattvas and sutra texts, now much weathered, and it stands in Baita Park by the Qiantang River, where it once marked the point at which the Grand Canal met the river.

rows.name: Zhejiang Art Museum
rows.summary: The provincial art museum, opened in 2009 on Nanshan Road beside West Lake, in a building of 32,000 m² with 14 exhibition halls. It focuses on modern and contemporary art, especially artists from or active in Zhejiang, alongside changing national and international exhibitions and holdings of older, folk and decorative art.

rows.name: Zhexi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A long valley system in the Qingliangfeng Nature Reserve of western Lin'an, where a headwater of the Qiantang River runs fast through steep-sided gorges in the outlying ranges of the Huangshan mountains. The developed stretch, the 18 km Longjing Gorge, has waterfalls, river pools and the narrow Jianmen Pass; a higher stretch of the valley is the only source of Changhua bloodstone, a red-mottled stone prized for carving seals.

rows.name: Zhongyi Bridge
rows.summary: A small single-arch stone bridge over the Xixi River in Liuxia, built in 1218 under the Southern Song and the only original Song bridge left in urban Hangzhou. About 15 m long, with steps at each end and a deck of long bluestone slabs, it still serves as a footbridge.

rows.name: Anji Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The square earthen enclosure of an ancient walled town at Gucheng village, north of Anji, occupied from the Spring and Autumn period to the Southern Dynasties and identified with Guzhang, where the Qin later based its Zhang commandery; its rammed-earth walls still rise above the fields. Large mound tombs of Yue nobles on nearby Longshan hill belong to the same protected site, and the area is now open as the Anji Ancient City National Archaeological Site Park, with a site museum on the excavations.

rows.name: Anji Old City Wall (Ancheng)
rows.summary: The stone-faced walls of the former Anji prefectural and county town at Ancheng, north of present-day Anji, described as the most complete prefecture- and county-level city walls left in Zhejiang. Begun as an earthen rampart in 1356 and faced with stone a year later, the peach-shaped circuit survives almost whole with its west, south and north gates, and still encloses a village.

rows.name: Chaoyin Bridge
rows.summary: A three-arch stone bridge of 1539, rebuilt in 1605, across the Zha Stream just inside the old south gate of Huzhou, named after the Chaoyin ferry it replaced. A small extra arch at its western end carries the riverside lane underneath, which earned it the local name 'bridge within a bridge', and pairs of stone lions guard both ends.

rows.name: China Alligator Village, Changxing
rows.summary: A breeding and conservation centre for the Chinese alligator, a small endangered crocodilian found only in China, set among ponds, woods and bamboo in the countryside of western Changxing. Visitors see the alligators in breeding ponds and enclosures, with displays on the species and the work to return it to the wild.

rows.name: China Bamboo Expo Park
rows.summary: A bamboo garden on the south-western edge of Anji town, in a county known as China's 'home of bamboo', planted with more than 300 kinds of bamboo gathered from across China and abroad. It contains the China Bamboo Museum, whose halls cover the plant's history, cultivation, crafts and place in art, and paths lead through the groves past bamboo-themed scenes.

rows.name: Daochang Hill Prayer Inscription
rows.summary: A Yuan-dynasty rock inscription on Daochang Hill on the southern edge of Huzhou, recording prayers for a good harvest by the darughachi, the Mongol overseer of the prefecture, and one of very few dated Yuan carvings of its kind in Zhejiang. It lies in a hollow east of Wanshou Temple; the hill, long counted among Huzhou's beauty spots, is crowned by the seven-storey Duobao Pagoda, first built in the Northern Song and restored in 1987–88.

rows.name: Deqing Proto-porcelain Kiln Sites
rows.summary: The low hills around Longsheng and Longshan villages, north-east of Deqing's county town, hold kiln sites that fired proto-porcelain from the Shang to the Warring States period, an early centre of Chinese porcelain-making named one of China's six major archaeological discoveries of 2010. The kilns themselves are excavated earthworks, but the Porcelain Origins Museum, Deqing's county museum, opened at Longsheng in December 2025 as the centrepiece of a cultural heritage park and displays the finds.

rows.name: Digang Village
rows.summary: A water village in Hefu town south-east of Huzhou, set among the fish ponds and mulberry dykes of the Taihu plain, with old houses and family halls along its canals, more than 30 old stone bridges, a temple and covered streets running beside the water. It was named a Chinese Historic and Cultural Village in 2014.

rows.name: Dusong Pass and the Old Post Road
rows.summary: A stone gateway on the Dusong ridge, on the old road between Hangzhou and Xuancheng, built in the Jianyan era (1127–30) to guard the approaches to the Southern Song capital at Lin'an, today's Hangzhou. The arched gate passage with a small walled courtyard survives, together with about 1.5 km of cobbled post road and four old bridges running south from Guanshang village into Hangzhou's Yuhang district, still used as a village path.

rows.name: Feiying Pagoda and the Gucheng Scenic Area
rows.summary: Huzhou's 'pagoda within a pagoda': a stone relic pagoda of 884–894 enclosed from the Northern Song in an outer brick-and-timber pagoda, rebuilt after a lightning fire in the Southern Song and restored in the 1980s. It stands in Feiying Park in the old city, one of five sights of the Gucheng scenic area with Lotus Villa, the garden of the Yuan painter Zhao Mengfu rebuilt in 1986, the China Huzhou Writing Brush Museum and the former home of the revolutionary Chen Qimei.

rows.name: Golden Lakeshore, Taihu Lake Resort
rows.summary: A stretch of the southern shore of Taihu Lake in Huzhou's Taihu tourist resort, running east from Moon Plaza and the ring-shaped 'Moon Hotel' that has become a city landmark. The shore faces a wide expanse of open water and is a favourite spot for sunset and evening walks, when the hotel is lit up.

rows.name: Golden Spike Ancient World, Meishan
rows.summary: At Meishan in north-western Changxing a quarried limestone face, Section D, was chosen in 2001 as the global reference point, the 'golden spike', for the boundary between the Permian and Triassic periods about 250 million years ago, the time of the largest mass extinction in Earth's history; a second golden spike, for the base of the Changhsingian stage, was fixed in the same section in 2005. The scenic area in the geological reserve shows the exposed rock beds and has a geology museum with fossils and displays on the history of life.

rows.name: Hello Kitty Park, Anji
rows.summary: China's first Hello Kitty theme park, built on the eastern edge of Anji town by a Chinese company under licence from Sanrio and opened in 2015. Six themed zones of rides, shows and character buildings are aimed at families with young children rather than at sightseers.

rows.name: Huzhou Silk Town (Xishanyang)
rows.summary: A new silk-industry and leisure district in Huzhou's eastern new town, built around Xishanyang, a lake and wetland park that is the main attraction for visitors. Footpaths circle the water past modern buildings for silk fashion and trade, a nod to Huzhou's claim to be the origin of silk.

rows.name: Jiangnan Tianchi
rows.summary: The upper reservoir of the Tianhuangping pumped-storage power station, a lake held on a mountain top in southern Anji, with the power plant itself hidden in caverns deep inside the mountain. An 18 km hairpin road climbs to it through bamboo forest, and the lake gives wide views over the hills of southern Anji.

rows.name: Lingzhi Pagoda (Yong'an Temple Pagoda)
rows.summary: A solid nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda at the foot of Longtou hill on the east bank of the West Tiao stream, facing the old Anji county town across the water; tradition dates it to the Wuyue kingdom, and inscriptions record repairs in 1047 and 1260. During restoration in 1993–94 a Northern Song relic chamber near the top yielded a silver-gilt miniature stupa, bronze mirrors, glass vessels and coins.

rows.name: Mount Mogan
rows.summary: A bamboo-covered hill resort in western Deqing, about 60 km from Hangzhou, where foreign missionaries and merchants built summer villas from the 1890s and Chinese officials, businessmen and cultural figures followed in the 1920s and 1930s. Dozens of the villas are protected as a heritage group, among them Huang Fu's Baiyun Shanguan, scene of Nationalist–Communist talks in 1937, and Songyuelu, where the 1948 gold-yuan currency reform was decided; paths lead through the bamboo to Sword Pond and its waterfall and to viewpoints over the plain.

rows.name: Nanxun Ancient Town
rows.summary: A canal town that grew rich on the raw-silk trade from the Ming dynasty onward, where late-Qing silk magnates built houses and gardens mixing Chinese and Western styles. The scenic area takes in Little Lotus Villa, the Liu family garden and ancestral temple around a lotus pond; the Jiaye Library, built in 1920–24 for Liu Chenggan's collection of old books; the Zhang Shiming residence, with French tiles, coloured glass and a Western-style ballroom; the former home of the Nationalist elder Zhang Jingjiang; and the Baijian Lou riverside houses.

rows.name: New Fourth Army Jiangsu–Zhejiang Military Region Sites
rows.summary: In 1944–45 the Communist-led New Fourth Army made the hill villages around Huaikan, in north-western Changxing, the base of its Jiangsu–Zhejiang Military Region, which was formally set up at Wentang village in February 1945 with Su Yu as commander. Fifteen former command and support sites are protected as a group, and a memorial hall on the site of the First Column headquarters presents the history of the base.

rows.name: Pangong Bridge
rows.summary: A three-arch stone bridge over the Fangsheng canal outside Huzhou's old north-eastern gate, named after the Ming hydraulic engineer Pan Jixun, who paid for the first bridge here in 1585–90. The present arches come from an 1839 rebuilding that replaced the original five-span beam bridge to let floodwater through, and an inscription on the bridge records the donors.

rows.name: Qianshanyang Site
rows.summary: A late Neolithic village site on the east bank of the former Qianshanyang lake, south-east of Huzhou, where excavations in the 1950s found fragments of silk fabric, silk thread and ribbon some 4,700 years old, among the oldest silk textiles known; in 2014 its remains were defined as a distinct Qianshanyang culture. The excavations have been filled in, so there is little to see at the site itself; it lies in Lu, an old canal village restored for rural tourism since 2020, which has several small exhibition halls and runs silk-heritage activities.

rows.name: Shouchang Bridge
rows.summary: A single-arch stone bridge over the Shangzhu river at Wayao hamlet in Erdu, built in 1265–74 under the Southern Song by a local man, Yao Zhi, and the best-preserved old bridge in Deqing. Its balustrades rest on Sumeru-style bases between lotus-capped posts; it heads the Deqing ancient bridges group, whose other listed Song-to-Ming bridges are scattered across the county.

rows.name: Shuikou Tea Culture Area (Guzhu Mountain)
rows.summary: Guzhu Mountain in Shuikou township grew Zisun ('purple shoot') tea, sent to the Tang court as tribute from 770, when a tribute-tea workshop was set up here, and Lu Yu, author of the Classic of Tea, studied tea on these hills. Officials who supervised the tribute, among them Yuan Gao and Du Mu, left inscriptions on the cliffs that survive in three groups. The scenic area centres on the rebuilt Great Tang Tribute Tea Institute, a hillside complex of Tang-style halls with tea-ceremony demonstrations, and also takes in Shousheng Temple and the tea village of Guzhu.

rows.name: Taihu Lougang Waterways (Yigao)
rows.summary: The lougang are hundreds of small channels and larger waterways cut from the Spring and Autumn period onward through the southern shore of Taihu Lake, which with cross-dykes and polder fields drained the land and regulated the lake; the network is best preserved in Wuxing and was listed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in 2016. Visits centre on Yigao, an old village strung along its channel near the lake, with stone bridges, a Lougang culture exhibition hall, cafés and guesthouses.

rows.name: Taihu Tuying Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park on the south-western shore of Taihu Lake in Changxing's Tuying resort area, described as the last natural lakeside wetland on this stretch of shore, with fish ponds, winding channels, reed beds and more than 20 small islands. Boat trips run through the channels, and the reeds turn white with flower in early winter.

rows.name: Three Bridges of Shuanglin
rows.summary: Three stone arch bridges, Wankui, Huacheng and Wanyuan, span the Shuanglin canal within about 350 m of each other on the north side of Shuanglin, an old silk town in Nanxun district. Each has three arches on thin piers; Huacheng, in the middle, began as a Yuan-dynasty wooden bridge rebuilt in stone in the Ming, and the tallest, Wanyuan, dates from a rebuilding finished in 1840.

rows.name: Jialebi Fantasy Park, Anji
rows.summary: A family amusement park in the Lingfeng resort area south-west of Anji town, listed as Tianyuan Jialebi and now run as Qihuan ('Fantasy') Jialebi together with a resort hotel, orchards and white-tea gardens. Nearly 40 rides and a boating pier are joined by a pet-animal park, outdoor and farm-kitchen cooking, and tea picking and tea making, so it mainly suits families with young children.

rows.name: Tomb of Chen Qimei (Chen Yingshi)
rows.summary: The tomb of Chen Qimei (1878–1916), courtesy name Yingshi, a Huzhou-born revolutionary of the Tongmenghui who took Shanghai for the republicans in 1911 and was a close ally of Sun Yat-sen, on the eastern slope of Xian Hill on the southern edge of the city. Built in 1918 and enlarged in 1934, it has a granite memorial archway with an inscription in Sun Yat-sen's hand, a 100 m tomb path and a terrace with Sun's eulogy carved in stone; it was wrecked in the Cultural Revolution and rebuilt in the 1980s.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhao Mengfu
rows.summary: The joint tomb of Zhao Mengfu (1254–1322), the leading painter and calligrapher of the Yuan dynasty, and his wife Guan Daosheng, herself a noted painter, on a hillside at Dongheng village in Luoshe, northern Deqing. The original mound had long gone, but excavation in 1992 found the stone burial chamber and a spirit way, and the restored tomb of 1993 is lined with stone horses and civil officials carved from Taihu stone.

rows.name: Xiagucheng Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The rammed-earth ramparts of Gucheng, regarded as the forerunner of Huzhou: the Chu lord Chunshen made it the seat of Gucheng county in the late Warring States, and under the Qin it was the seat of Wucheng county until the town moved north to the present city site. Inner and outer walls, 6–9 m high in places, still enclose fields and ponds below Jingai Hill beside the East Tiao river, and a granite wall in the inner city is carved with the site's history.

rows.name: Xianshan Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake and national wetland park at the western tip of Changxing county, close to where Zhejiang, Jiangsu and Anhui meet. A causeway crosses the lake beside Xianshan, a small hill that local legend links to the Silla prince-monk later revered as the bodhisattva Dizang, and the reed beds and shallows draw large numbers of wintering water birds.

rows.name: Xiazhu Lake Wetland
rows.summary: A natural lake-and-marsh landscape of about 10 km² in eastern Deqing, a maze of some 600 low islets, reed beds, bamboo groves and fish ponds threaded by channels. It is toured mainly by boat; egrets and herons gather in summer and wild ducks in winter, and the shrine of Fangfeng, a legendary local chieftain, stands near the north-western shore.

rows.name: Yu Village (Yucun), Anji
rows.summary: A village in the bamboo hills of Tianhuangping town that closed its limestone quarries and cement works in the early 2000s and turned to forestry and rural tourism. In August 2005 Xi Jinping, then Communist Party secretary of Zhejiang, first set out here the idea that 'clear waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver'; the village meeting room where he spoke is preserved as a provincial heritage site, and UN Tourism has named Yucun one of its Best Tourism Villages.

rows.name: Yuanxiang Town (Butterfly Valley)
rows.summary: A rural leisure park opened in 2018 at Zhao village in the Xisaishan hills west of Huzhou, built around a large indoor butterfly house where visitors watch butterflies breed, emerge and fly. Plum and peach orchards, tea gardens, a hillside boardwalk, a small farm and children's play areas fill the rest of the valley, and it suits families with young children.

rows.name: Yucun, Moganshan
rows.summary: The village at the eastern foot of Mount Mogan where Huang Fu, a Republican-era statesman who retired to the mountain in 1928, founded a library, a school and a silkworm-egg farm in the 1930s; he is buried here. Its main street keeps Republican-era buildings, among them the old library of 1932, and a square on the site of the old bus station, and is now lined with cafés, a gallery, small shops and guesthouses.

rows.name: Zhebei Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A forested river gorge in the hills of south-western Anji, near Baofu, where a walking trail follows a clear mountain stream past boulders, pools and a string of waterfalls. Its shade and running water make it a summer escape from the heat of the plains.

rows.name: Zhejiang Museum of Natural History, Anji Branch
rows.name_zh: 浙江自然博物院安吉馆
rows.summary: The second site of the provincial natural history museum, opened in December 2018 on a hillside north-west of Anji town in a group of eight buildings designed by David Chipperfield Architects. Six themed halls, among them geology, dinosaur, ocean and ecology halls, are joined by temporary exhibitions, a 4D cinema and a hands-on discovery centre, and the displays lean towards interactive learning for families.

rows.name: Zhongnan Baicaoyuan Eco-Park
rows.summary: A hillside eco-park on the north-western edge of Anji town, laid out as a series of themed gardens (cherry, plum, Japanese maple, purple bamboo, white tea, roses, osmanthus and medicinal herbs) among streams and ponds. A small sightseeing train runs through its European Pasture section, where children can meet farm animals, and the park also has models of prehistoric animals and a campsite, so it suits family outings.

rows.name: Anguo Temple Sutra Pillars
rows.summary: Three octagonal stone pillars inscribed with a Buddhist dharani sutra, carved in 842, 844 and 865, are the chief survivors of Anguo Temple, founded in 713, which declined after 1894 and was cleared in 1978. Between 5.8 and 7 m tall, they rise in tiers of lotus, cloud and coiled-dragon carving with niches of seated Buddhas, and are among the oldest standing structures in Haining.

rows.name: Chen Gelao Mansion
rows.summary: The mansion of the Chen clan of Haining, greatly enlarged by Chen Yuanlong (1652–1736), a minister under the Kangxi Emperor who became a grand secretary under Yongzheng; 'gelao', a name for grand secretaries, gives the house its name. Qing buildings survive on the eastern axis, among them the ancestral hall, the family's sleeping quarters, a study and a flower hall, while the central halls were rebuilt in 2002–03. The house keeps a set of calligraphy steles, a nine-dragon plaque granted by the Yongzheng Emperor and a Ming-era podocarp tree.

rows.name: East Lake, Pinghu
rows.summary: A lake on the edge of central Pinghu whose shores and islands form a 4A scenic area. Its landmark is the Li Shutong Memorial Hall, a white lotus-shaped building of 2004 set partly over the water in Shutong Park on Daying Island, with seven galleries on Li Shutong (1880–1942), the painter, musician and teacher of Pinghu descent who became the Buddhist monk Hongyi. Baoben Temple and its pagoda stand on the south shore.

rows.name: Former Residence of Shen Junru
rows.summary: The Jiaxing family house of Shen Junru (1875–1963), a lawyer and politician who was one of the 'Seven Gentlemen' arrested in 1936 for campaigning for resistance to Japan, later led the China Democratic League and was the first President of the Supreme People's Court from 1949. The courtyard house, built in the early 19th century and his home in 1908–19, was restored and opened as a memorial in 1998. A seated statue stands in the main hall, and the rear two-storey building holds an exhibition on his life and belongings.

rows.name: Gefeisong Chocolate Town
rows.summary: A chocolate factory and themed visitor park in Dayun town, opened in 2014 by the Gefeisong chocolate company. A glass-walled gallery about 150 m long lets visitors watch chocolate being made from mixing to packing, and the park adds a chocolate-making workshop, Swiss-style streets and buildings, a wedding venue and gardens, which makes it mainly a family outing.

rows.name: Huili Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the southern slope of Xishan (Ziwei Hill) in central Haining, founded in the Eastern Jin period in about 373–375 and given its present name in 1009. Most buildings are recent rebuilds, but the Mahavira Hall dates from 1922, and in front of the temple stand two octagonal stone sutra pillars of 874, about 5 m tall, carved with coiled dragons and flying apsaras.

rows.name: Jiashan Library and Museum
rows.summary: A civic cultural complex in Jiashan town, opened in 2019, that pairs the five-storey county library with the four-storey Jiashan Museum in buildings whose kiln-like form recalls the county's brick and tile making. The museum presents local history from prehistoric times and holds temporary exhibitions, and the library has a large children's picture-book hall; it suits a rainy-day visit combined with Xitang or Dayun.

rows.name: Jiaxing Catholic Church and Vincent Abbey
rows.summary: A brick church in simplified Gothic style with twin bell towers 37 m high, built in 1917–30 to the design of the Italian Vincentian priest Angelo-Joseph Asinelli and for long the tallest building in Jiaxing. Its roof and fittings were wrecked during the Cultural Revolution, and the church was restored in 2020–21, when the ground around it was opened up as a public lawn beside the Zicheng site park. The same listing covers Vincent Abbey, the Vincentians' seminary built in 1902–03 with arcaded wings, about 2 km to the north-east on Guangming Street.

rows.name: Luojiajiao Site Park
rows.summary: An early Majiabang-culture settlement of about 12 ha beside the old course of the Grand Canal at Shimen, where excavations in 1979–80 found four Neolithic layers and 794 objects, with charred reeds dated to about 7,000 years ago. Since 2018 it has been a provincial archaeological site park of about 20 ha on the theme of Neolithic rice farming, with a display hall that opened around 2021.

rows.name: Majiabang Site and Museum
rows.summary: The site, found in 1959 where three streams meet south-west of Jiaxing, gave its name to the Majiabang culture, the Neolithic farming culture of the plain north of Hangzhou Bay; the settlement here dates from about 6000 to 5500 years ago and yielded over thirty burials, a house and pottery, stone, jade and bone objects. The site has been laid out as an archaeological park, opened in 2021, and the adjoining Majiabang Culture Museum, a branch of Jiaxing Museum, displays finds from the excavations.

rows.name: Meihuazhou
rows.summary: A rural water-village scenic area in Fengqiao town, south-east of Jiaxing, named for the way its streams split the land into five petal-shaped islands like a plum blossom. Old stone bridges link the islands, among them the paired Sanbu Liangpan Bridges, a provincial heritage site, and Xianghua Bridge in front of Shifo (Stone Buddha) Temple, and the area also has two ancient ginkgo trees, the Feng family's old house, orchards and play areas aimed at families.

rows.name: Mo's Manor
rows.summary: A late-Qing merchant family house in the old centre of Pinghu, built in 1897–1900 and home to three generations of the Mo family. Its seventy-odd rooms are arranged in east, central and west groups on a plot of about 4,850 m², and the house, run as an exhibition hall, has been used as a set for several television dramas.

rows.name: Nanbei Lake
rows.summary: A lagoon of about 1.2 km² near Ganpu on the Hangzhou Bay coast, divided into a south and a north lake by an old causeway and enclosed by wooded hills on three sides, with the sea to the south. Paths and a waterside greenway follow the shore, and trails climb Yingkeding, the highest hill in Jiaxing, a traditional spot for watching the sun and moon rise together over the bay around the first day of the tenth lunar month.

rows.name: Qi Garden
rows.summary: A private garden in the centre of Haiyan laid out in 1871 by the merchant Feng Zuanzhai, who reused the rocks of two ruined Ming gardens; the garden historian Chen Congzhou ranked it first among the gardens of Zhejiang. About a hectare of old trees, three rockeries and two ponds crossed by zigzag bridges is set off by just four small pavilions and halls. At the front, one storeyed hall of the family house of 1870 survives behind a carved brick gateway.

rows.name: South Lake (Nanhu), Jiaxing
rows.summary: Jiaxing's best-known lake, about half a square kilometre on the south side of the old city, has a garden island reached by boat whose Yanyu (Misty Rain) Tower, last rebuilt in 1918, so pleased the Qianlong Emperor that he had a copy built at his summer resort in Chengde. In early August 1921 the First National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party, after leaving Shanghai, held its final session on a pleasure boat on this lake, and a replica of the boat built in 1959 is moored at the island as the commemorated site. The South Lake Revolutionary Memorial Hall, in a building opened on the south shore in 2011, presents the party's founding.

rows.name: Tomb of Wu Zhen and Plum Blossom Hermitage
rows.summary: The tomb of Wu Zhen (1280–1354), one of the Four Masters of Yuan painting, best known for landscapes, bamboo and pictures of fishermen, lies on a spot he chose himself in his home town of Weitang. The low mound on an octagonal stone base is flanked by the Plum Blossom Hermitage, built in the Wanli reign to guard it, and by corridors of steles carved with his bamboo and fisherman designs. A memorial hall opened in 2000 presents his life and work.

rows.name: Wangdian Soviet-Style Granaries
rows.summary: A group of fourteen cylindrical concrete grain silos with six-sided tiled roofs, built in the 1950s with Soviet advice beside the Changshui canal in Wangdian town to store grain for the local rice mill. Each silo is 12 m across and 8.15 m high, set in three staggered rows; left idle after the mill was restructured in 2002, the compound was tidied up in the late 2010s and one of its side buildings became a collectors' market in 2023.

rows.name: Xiangjiadang Lake
rows.summary: A lake of about 2,000 mu (1.3 km²) on the north-eastern edge of Jiaxing, whose shoreline park forms the 4A scenic area. A greenway of about 13 km links the lake with the city, and around the shore are a sandy beach called Moon Bay, a wetland park, a forest park and a farm park, with seasonal festivals through the year.

rows.name: Xitang Water Town
rows.summary: A canal town about 10 km north of Jiashan, on the old border between the Wu and Yue states, whose preserved centre of Ming and Qing houses is threaded by nine waterways crossed by 27 stone bridges. Its signature is nearly a kilometre of tiled covered walkways running along the canal-side streets, with narrow alleys such as Shipi Lane between the houses. Xitang was in the first national list of historic towns in 2003, appears in the film Mission: Impossible III and has hosted a yearly Hanfu (traditional dress) festival since 2013.

rows.name: Yanguan Tide-Watching Area
rows.summary: Yanguan, the old county seat of Haining on the north bank of the Qiantang River, is the classic place to watch the river's tidal bore, which arrives here as a single long wave, with the largest tides around the 18th day of the eighth lunar month. A stone seawall of interlocking 'fish-scale' blocks, built in the Qing dynasty, runs along the riverside tide-watching park, overlooked by the seven-storey Zhan'ao Pagoda of 1612. In the old town behind are the Sea God Temple, built on imperial order in 1729, and the childhood home of the scholar Wang Guowei.

rows.name: Yunlanwan Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort built in the 2010s in Dayun town, part of the Dayun provincial tourist resort area, using water drawn from more than 2,000 m underground. Its spa centre is designed in the shape of two half-open lotus flowers, and the resort adds a hotel, seasonal flower fields and, in summer, a children's water-play park; it suits a relaxed half-day or an overnight stay.

rows.name: Zhapu Forts
rows.summary: Two Qing coastal batteries at Zhapu on the north shore of Hangzhou Bay, part of the Qing coastal defences and a reminder of the First Opium War, when British forces captured Zhapu in 1842. Tianfei Palace Fort, at the south end of Tangshan Park, keeps a fan-shaped row of four gun shelters with three iron cannon, one made by the Jiangnan Arsenal in 1884. Nanwan Fort, on the western end of Jiulong Mountain to the south-east, has two shelters and a breech-loading gun made in 1888.

rows.name: Zicheng Citadel Site Park
rows.summary: The inner citadel of old Jiaxing, founded in 231, held the offices of the county and later the prefecture for centuries and served as the Taiping Prince Ting's headquarters; after 1912 it became barracks and then a hospital. Its gate tower, of Yuan origin and rebuilt in 1908, survives with short stretches of wall and is described as the only old gate tower left on a city wall in Zhejiang. Since 2021 the site has been an archaeological park entered through a memorial arch, with a path set with 18 bronze strips recording dates from 231 to the present.

rows.name: Baitan Residences, Dongyang
rows.summary: Two large Qing-dynasty family compounds in Baitan village, Weishan town, east of Dongyang. Fuyu Hall, built from the Jiaqing to the Xianfeng reigns (about 1800–1860), spreads over more than a hectare on two parallel axes, while Wuben Hall, built from the early 19th century to the early Republic, is a row of linked halls; both are decorated with wood carving, stone carving and wall paintings.

rows.name: Bamian Hall, Huangshan Village (Yiwu)
rows.summary: A large mansion built in the Qianlong and Jiaqing eras (late 18th to early 19th century) by the merchant Chen Zicai in Huangshan village, Shangxi town, west of Yiwu, about 70 m long and 40 m wide. It is known for its brick, stone and above all wood carving.

rows.name: Chen Ancestral Hall, Xiabaishi
rows.summary: A Chen clan hall of 1693 in Xiabaishi village, Zhiying town, Yongkang, which keeps its original structure despite later repairs. Its three halls, each five bays wide and rising in steps, enclose an opera stage, side pavilions, two pools and a tea pavilion, and the beams carry painted decoration and shallow relief carving.

rows.name: China Woodcarving Culture Expo City, Dongyang
rows.summary: A vast trade complex in Dongyang, a city known for its woodcarving tradition, where some 3,000 manufacturers sell carved woodwork, rosewood (hongmu) furniture and bamboo crafts from about 8,000 shops. Alongside the market halls are the China Woodcarving Museum, a wood-art hall and a woodcarving theme park, and more than 70 master craftsmen have studios here. It suits shoppers and anyone curious about Dongyang woodcarving, a nationally listed intangible-heritage craft.

rows.name: Da'an Temple Pagoda, Yiwu
rows.summary: A six-sided, five-storey brick pagoda beside Xiuhu Lake in central Yiwu, built in the 12th century for a temple that has since vanished and the oldest brick-and-timber structure in the city. Its timber eaves, balconies and spire are lost, but brick imitations of timber columns and brackets survive, as do bricks inscribed with the names of its donors; it stands about 23 m high.

rows.name: Falong Temple Dharani Pillar, Jinhua
rows.summary: An octagonal stone pillar of 857, all that remains of Falong Temple, also called Jinqian Temple, south of the river in Jinhua. About 6.3 m stands above ground, inscribed with a Buddhist dharani sutra and carved with guardian figures, a railing motif, bird-bodied kalavinkas and heavenly musicians.

rows.name: Fang Clan Ancestral Hall, Tangxia
rows.summary: The main ancestral hall of the Fang clan in Tangxia village, Houzhai subdistrict, north-west of central Yiwu, founded in the Ming Jiajing era and rebuilt in 1898. Facing south, it has three halls linked by two side galleries and covers about 2,000 m².

rows.name: Fangyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national scenic area of red Danxia rock east of Yongkang, where flat-topped Fangyan rises sheer from the plain and the classic way up is a steep stepped path of cut stone and timber known as the Flying Bridge. On top is a temple to Hu Ze, a Northern Song official worshipped locally as Hu Gong, whose temple fairs feature folk performances; nearby are the Five Peaks, where the Southern Song thinker Chen Liang taught and the Wufeng Academy grew up. During the war against Japan the Zhejiang provincial government was based here.

rows.name: Former Residence of Chen Wangdao
rows.summary: The birthplace of the scholar Chen Wangdao (1891–1977), later president of Fudan University, in Fenshuitang village north-west of Yiwu. In 1920 he made the first Chinese translation of the Communist Manifesto here, working from a Japanese edition, and the house is visited as a site associated with the early history of the Chinese Communist Party. Built by his father in 1909, it is a typical central-Zhejiang brick-and-timber courtyard house of about 430 m².

rows.name: Guyue Bridge
rows.summary: A single-span stone bridge of 1213 at Yazhijie village in Chi'an town, south of Yiwu, dated by an inscription on its beam. Its arch is built of five straight segments, each made of six long stone ribs joined by transverse locking stones, and it is the earliest surviving bridge of this ribbed, polygonal-arch type in China. It is 31.2 m long with a 15 m span.

rows.name: Houwu Village
rows.summary: An old village in Qiancang town, Yongkang, on the border with Jinyun County, whose history goes back to the early 13th century. Its village layout, historic setting and a number of old halls and houses are well preserved, and it was named a National Historic and Cultural Village in 2007.

rows.name: Huayuan Village, Dongyang
rows.summary: A village about 16 km south of Dongyang city, founded in 1342, that has twice absorbed its neighbours since 2004 and now covers 12 km² with more than 65,000 residents, most of them migrant workers. Promoted nationally as a model of rural development, it was the first single village in Zhejiang to be rated a 4A scenic area and is also listed as a provincial folk-culture village. It suits travellers curious about rural development in eastern China.

rows.name: Jinlin Fingered Citron Culture Park, Jinhua
rows.summary: A farm park in Chisong town, Jindong district, devoted to the fingered citron or Buddha's hand, a fragrant citrus grown on the southern slopes of Jinhua's northern hills for nearly a thousand years. It combines citron plantations with displays and science education on the fruit, sales of farm produce and rural sightseeing. It suits families looking for a rural outing near Jinhua.

rows.name: Jiqing Hall, Shefeng
rows.summary: A branch ancestral hall in Shefeng village, Yongchang subdistrict, Lanxi, probably founded in the Southern Song; the present building dates from the late Ming and was repaired in the Kangxi and Qianlong eras. It faces east, is four halls deep and flanked by two Qing memorial arches to chaste widows, and is noted for its fine carving and good state, despite years of use as a rice mill.

rows.name: Kong Family Temple, Juxi
rows.summary: A family temple of descendants of Confucius in Juxi village, Panfeng township, Pan'an, where Kong Duangong, of the 48th generation, settled after following the Song court south in the late 1120s; Emperor Lizong ordered the temple built in 1254. The present Qing rebuilding, of about 836 m² with a gatehouse, opera stage, halls and small courtyards, looks like a typical central-Zhejiang clan hall, and Kong Duangong's tomb is also in the village.

rows.name: Light of Jinhua Cultural Plaza
rows.summary: A civic culture complex completed in 2019 on Yanweizhou, the point where Jinhua's rivers meet, in the new Duohu business district. Its four linked buildings house the Jinhua City Exhibition Hall and the Jinhua Science and Technology Museum, whose four galleries cover life and evolution, discovery, design and the earth and universe; a hall of local intangible heritage opened inside in 2024. It stands beside the China Wu Opera House and suits families and anyone curious about the city.

rows.name: Liudong Mountain Underground River, Lanxi
rows.summary: A provincial scenic area on a low hill of karst caves between Jinhua and Lanxi, opened to visitors in 1985 and named after its six caves. Its main sight is the Underground River, a 2.5 km cave route that begins with an 800 m boat ride along an underground stream, at a steady 18°C all year, and continues on foot past stalactites, stalagmites and flowstone. A few minutes away is Qixia Garden, a Qing house that was the ancestral home of Zhao Yidi (Edith Zhao), the lifelong companion of the general Zhang Xueliang, with an exhibition on the couple.

rows.name: Longde Temple Pagoda, Pujiang
rows.summary: A seven-storey, six-sided brick pagoda of 1016 on Longfeng Hill in Tashan Park, Pujiang county town; the temple that gave it its name has gone. Fires and lightning destroyed its timber eaves, top and spire, leaving a brick shell about 36 m high whose body is original Northern Song work.

rows.name: Lu Family Residences, Dongyang
rows.summary: A large complex of Ming and Qing mansions and halls on the east side of Dongyang, built by the Lu clan, who settled here in the Southern Song and prospered after a family member passed the highest imperial examination in the early 15th century. The buildings, covering about 2.5 hectares, are grouped around the clan's main ancestral hall and three branch compounds, of which the Suyong Hall complex is the centrepiece, and are rich in the wood carving Dongyang is known for. The scenic area also takes in a street of intangible-heritage workshops and Luzhai Old Street, about 500 m of shops selling carving and old building parts.

rows.name: Main Hall of Tianning Temple, Jinhua
rows.summary: The only surviving building of Tianning Temple in central Jinhua, founded in the early 11th century: a square, three-bay hall with a hip-and-gable roof, rebuilt in 1318. Dating of the timbers during repairs in 1978 showed that the Yuan rebuilding reused some Song-dynasty pillars, and a bell of 1128 and a Qing stone carving of Guanyin after Wu Daozi are kept inside.

rows.name: Mashangqiao Flower Hall, Dongyang
rows.summary: The house of the local merchant Lü Fujin in Mashangqiao village, Huxi town, south-east of Dongyang near Hengdian, built between 1820 and 1830 and also called Yijing Hall. Four courtyards deep, with a gatehouse, screen wall, main hall and two rear halls flanked by side wings, it is filled with carving and is regarded as a model of Dongyang woodcarving applied to a family home.

rows.name: Ming and Qing Residences Expo City, Hengdian
rows.summary: A park of about 60 hectares run by Hengdian World Studios that combines old buildings with film sets. Its Taohuayuan section gathers more than 120 Ming, Qing and Republican-era houses moved here from Zhejiang, Anhui and Jiangxi, with carved timber, brick and stone, ancestral halls, a theatre and a copy of Tunxi Old Street. The Qinhuai River section recreates old Nanjing around a Confucius Temple and examination hall and includes a scaled-down copy of the Yuanmingyuan.

rows.name: Niutou Mountain National Forest Park, Wuyi
rows.summary: A national forest park in the mountains of western Wuyi County around Niutou Mountain, which at about 1,560 m is billed as the highest peak in Jinhua prefecture. Its forested valleys and streams are visited for walking, sightseeing and as a cool retreat in summer.

rows.name: Qijia Hall, Yafan
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty hall in Yafan Er village, Yafan town, south-east of Jinhua city, square in plan with a screen wall, courtyard, front and rear halls and side wings. Its layout is complete and its timber frame is plain and well built.

rows.name: Shangshan Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: The site in Huangzhai town, Pujiang, that gave its name to the Shangshan culture, a group of early Neolithic settlements in the Jinhua–Quzhou basin about 10,000 years old. Excavations since 2001 have found pottery tempered with rice husks, grinding stones and remains of some of the world's earliest cultivated rice. It has been an archaeological park since 2016, with a display hall, a research centre and surrounding rice fields, and was named a national archaeological park in 2025.

rows.name: Shangzu Ancestral Hall, Lanxi
rows.summary: The main ancestral hall of the Xu clan, also called Xiaolun Hall, in Xiamengtang village, Yongchang subdistrict, Lanxi, probably built in the late Ming or early Qing. Its three halls and side wings, with a free-standing middle hall, form a square plan of about 1,700 m²; the building, which housed the village school until the 1990s, was restored in 2008 and is complete.

rows.name: Shide Hall, Sanquan
rows.summary: An ancestral hall, also known as Jiangshi Hall, in Sanquan village, Huangdian town, north-west of Lanxi city, founded in the Southern Song with its three halls rebuilt in the Ming and Qing. The first hall is a carved brick gateway in the form of a memorial arch from the Ming Jiajing era (16th century); the rear hall was added around 1900.

rows.name: Shuanglong Scenic Area (Double Dragon Cave)
rows.summary: A national scenic area on the southern slopes of Mount Jinhua, about 8 km north of the city, rated 5A in 2024. Its best-known sight is the Double Dragon Cave: visitors lie flat in a boat to pass under a low rock from the outer cave, with old inscriptions, into the inner cave, whose rock folds are said to look like two dragons; nearby Binghu Cave has a large underground waterfall. The area also includes other karst caves and the Huang Daxian Ancestral Temple, the home temple of the Taoist immortal Huang Daxian, whose cult has spread overseas.

rows.name: Siping Village
rows.summary: An old village in Tangxi town, in the west of Jinhua's Wucheng district, settled in the late Yuan or early Ming, with an intact village layout and many complete halls and houses in the Huizhou style. Its brick carving is especially rich, earning it the nickname of China's most beautiful brick-carving village, and it was named a National Historic and Cultural Village in 2010.

rows.name: Tongzhou Bridge, Lanxi
rows.summary: An 84 m covered bridge over the Meixi stream at Juren village, Meijiang town, in north-eastern Lanxi, on the old road between Pujiang and the Lan River. Its five-arch stone base carries a timber gallery of 21 bays with a shrine pavilion at the centre and pavilions at each end, the form it took when it was rebuilt in 1886–88. The writer Cao Juren, who grew up nearby, is said to have first met his wife on the bridge.

rows.name: Wulong Gorge, Pan'an
rows.summary: A gorge on the upper Jiaxi stream at Louxiazhai village, Jianshan town, in north-eastern Pan'an, where the stream cuts down through a raised plateau in a series of pools, waterfalls and small lakes. The scenic area, rated 4A in 2017, is divided into five sections named after dragons, and also takes in the old houses of Louxiazhai and the Daxingguo remains on Chenglishan.

rows.name: Wuzhou Ancient City and Shiwang Palace, Jinhua
rows.summary: Jinhua's old inner city, first walled around 903, now a restored historic district of lanes with snack stalls and shops, a stretch of rebuilt red-sandstone city wall and the rebuilt Confucian temple, with the Jinhua Museum on its eastern edge. At its heart is the Shiwang Palace, an old government compound that the Taiping general Li Shixian, the Shi Wang, made his headquarters in 1861–63; it is the most complete surviving Taiping building complex and keeps more than a hundred wall paintings. On the southern edge, the Bayong Tower, a riverside pavilion first built in 494 and rebuilt in the Qing, was celebrated in a poem by Li Qingzhao.

rows.name: Xianhua Mountain, Pujiang
rows.summary: A national scenic area in the north of Pujiang County whose summit, above 600 m, is a cluster of sheer volcanic rock pinnacles; the highest, Shaonü Peak, reaches 720.8 m. Legend says a daughter of the Yellow Emperor became an immortal here, and the early-Ming scholar Song Lian praised it as one of the most beautiful places on earth. With 24 named peaks, over a hundred viewpoints and dense forest, it is a popular summer retreat.

rows.name: Xijiang Ancestral Hall, Lanxi
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty clan hall in Xijiang village, Shuiting She Ethnic Township, Lanxi, four halls deep with side wings and covering about 2,000 m². Plainly decorated but built of massive timbers, it is one of the largest and highest-ranking folk ancestral halls in Zhejiang, and the architectural historian Luo Zhewen called it China's largest and most significant family temple of its kind.

rows.name: Xu Ancestral Hall, Shinantang
rows.summary: A Xu clan hall founded in the Ming Wanli era beside the Wuyi River at Shinantang village, Yafan town, south of Jinhua, on the site of the old Yongqing ferry. Enlarged and rebuilt several times in the Ming and Qing, it faces south and has three halls five bays wide around two courtyards, covering about 1,000 m².

rows.name: Yaduan Village
rows.summary: A Chen-clan village in Chi'an town, south of Yiwu, enclosed by hills on three sides with the Yaxi stream in front. Its Qing-dynasty core, known as the 'seven buildings and five halls', was built over three generations of the Chen family and includes the clan ancestral hall, Rong'an Hall with its side wings and several other courtyard houses, covering about half a hectare.

rows.name: Yanfu Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in a hill hollow at Taocun village, Taoxi town, in southern Wuyi County, founded in the 10th century. Its main hall, rebuilt in 1317 and given a lower second roof in the Ming, is the oldest Yuan-dynasty timber building in Zhejiang, with unusual long-beaked bracket sets that the architectural historians Liang Sicheng and Lin Huiyin studied in 1933. The other halls are Qing, and the complex was restored in 2014–16.

rows.name: Ye Family Flower Hall, Shijiazhuang
rows.summary: A two-storey house completed in 1915 by the ham merchant Ye Zhangchao in Shijiazhuang hamlet, Weishan town, north-east of Dongyang. Its three-bay hall under a double-eaved roof is covered in intricate Dongyang wood carving, which earned it the nickname 'the finest hall in Wuzhou'.

rows.name: Yiwu International Trade City
rows.summary: Described by the World Bank in 2005 as the world's largest wholesale market for small commodities, it is a chain of huge linked halls with more than 75,000 booths selling toys, jewellery, hardware, kitchenware, stationery, clothing accessories and much more, mainly to traders from around the world. It grew out of a street market legalised in 1982; its first district here opened in 2002, and District 2 houses a museum of the commodity trade's history. Even a quick look takes hours, and many visitors come simply to see the scale of global trade in everyday goods.

rows.name: Yuqing Hall, Dudu
rows.summary: An early-Ming ancestral hall of the Hongwu era (late 14th century) in Dudu village, Nüfu subdistrict, Lanxi. It faces west, has three halls and a connecting passage covering about 860 m², and keeps a pair of Ming stone lions in front.

rows.name: Yushan Ancient Tea Market, Pan'an
rows.summary: A tea-trading compound below Chachang Hill at Matang village, Yushan town, Pan'an, founded in the Song and rebuilt in 1781, with a tea-market temple, a local patrol office and the market buildings themselves. Combining tea production, trade and worship in one place, it is described as the only surviving ancient tea market in China, and the 'Gan Chachang' tea-market fair held here is listed as national intangible heritage.

rows.name: Yuyuan Village
rows.summary: An old village in Yuyuan township, south-west Wuyi County, founded in the Southern Song by the Yu family; tradition says the Ming strategist Liu Bowen laid it out to match the stars, and it is promoted as the 'Taiji star village'. It keeps 53 buildings from the Song to the Qing with more than 1,000 rooms, decorated with wood carving, murals and pebble work, and was among the first National Historic and Cultural Villages named in 2003.

rows.name: Zhengyimen (First Family South of the Yangtze)
rows.summary: The home of the Zheng clan of Zhengzhai, Pujiang, which lived as one undivided household sharing a single kitchen for fifteen generations, from 1127 until a fire in 1459, and was honoured as a model of family virtue. Around the clan ancestral hall, rebuilt in 1797, stand more than 50 structures from the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, including the Xiaogan Spring, a stele pavilion, the Dongming Academy, bridges and lesser halls; the site is promoted as the 'First Family South of the Yangtze'.

rows.name: Zhiyan Village
rows.summary: A village in Huangdian town, northern Lanxi, founded in the Southern Song, that keeps 66 Ming and Qing buildings, mostly Ming, over about 2.5 hectares. They include ancestral halls such as Yande Hall and Xiaosi Hall and many family houses, and Xinye, another well-known old village just across the border in Jiande, is less than 4 km away.

rows.name: Zhu Family Buildings, Chi'an
rows.summary: A cluster of Zhu family buildings in Chi'an town, south-west of Yiwu, spanning several centuries: the Ming-dynasty Jianxu Hall, the Qing Liufang Hall, an official's mansion of the Guangxu era and side wings added in the Republican period. The Qing Neo-Confucian scholar Zhu Yixin and his brother lived in the mansion.

rows.name: Zhuge Village
rows.summary: A village in western Lanxi, founded in the Yuan, whose residents, mostly surnamed Zhuge, claim descent from Zhuge Liang, the third-century chancellor of Shu Han. Its lanes are laid out like the eight trigrams around a central pond, with eight lanes radiating out and eight low hills ringing the village, and it keeps more than 200 buildings from the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, including ancestral halls and houses built with wealth from the herbal-medicine trade. The protected site also covers the old houses of Changle village, about 2 km away.

rows.name: Ziweishan Residences, Dongyang
rows.summary: Late-Ming mansions in Ziweishan village, Huashui town, south-west of Dongyang, built by Xu Honggang, Minister of War at Nanjing, and his two brothers on three parallel axes. The third brother's mansion has gone, but the gatehouse and Yiyan Hall of the minister's house and the Kaitai Hall, rear hall and side rooms of the second house survive, a rare group of late-Ming buildings in Dongyang.

rows.name: Baishanzu
rows.summary: At 1,856.7 m, Baishanzu is the second-highest peak in Zhejiang and the core of a nature reserve of about 109 km² in Qingyuan county, within the area proposed for the Qianjiangyuan–Baishanzu National Park. Its old forests shelter the Baishanzu fir, a conifer found only on this mountain and listed as critically endangered. The cool climate makes the villages around the reserve a popular summer retreat.

rows.name: Baoxi and Xitou Village
rows.summary: A mountain township in western Longquan whose village of Xitou has made celadon for centuries and was named one of UN Tourism's Best Tourism Villages in 2024. Seven old wood-fired kilns are still in use, the largest a long dragon kiln climbing a hillside, and firings draw visitors to watch the kilns opened. Nearby, a cluster of 18 bamboo buildings designed by architects from nine countries includes an exhibition hall of excavated and contemporary celadon.

rows.name: China Celadon Town and Piyun Celadon Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 中国青瓷小镇·披云青瓷文化园
rows.pinyin: Zhōngguó Qīngcí Xiǎozhèn · Pīyún Qīngcí Wénhuàyuán
rows.summary: Shangyang town is where modern Longquan celadon began: the state-owned Longquan Porcelain Factory was set up here in 1954, gathering leading craftsmen to revive the ware. The old factory has been turned into an intangible-heritage cultural centre with an interactive museum, and around the town visitors can watch the whole making process or try making pieces of their own.

rows.name: Dayao Longquan Kiln Sites
rows.summary: The heartland of Longquan celadon, where 126 kiln sites lie in a 5.2 km² protected area around Dayao village. Kilns began here in the Five Dynasties, and from the Southern Song to the early Ming the area is described as China's largest porcelain-making centre, whose jade-green wares travelled across Asia, Africa and Europe. A national archaeological site park of 9.74 km² opened here in October 2018, and the listing also covers the Shangyang kiln sites over the hill in Qingyuan and the Yuankou kilns.

rows.name: Dongxi Rock Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 2.5 km² area of Danxia-type sedimentary rock in Laozhu She Ethnic Town, named after two great rocks that face each other from east and west. Paths link gorges, caves and outcrops such as Breeze Gorge, Sword-Split Rock, General Rock and the Seven Goddesses. The area lies in a She ethnic district, and She songs, dances and wedding ceremonies have been staged here on holidays and at the Sanyuesan festival.

rows.name: Dushan Stone Archway
rows.summary: A granite memorial archway of three bays and five roofs at the south-east edge of Dushan village, built in 1569 by the county magistrate Chi Yude for Ye Yifan, an official of the Ministry of Works born in the village. The 11.7 m-wide gateway imitates timber construction, with an inscription praising repeated imperial favour on its central lintel and carvings of lions, dragons, phoenixes and auspicious beasts.

rows.name: Former Site of Zhejiang University Longquan Branch
rows.name_zh: 浙江大学龙泉分校旧址
rows.summary: When Zhejiang University moved inland during the war with Japan, it opened a branch in 1939 in the Zeng family mansion at Fangye on the edge of Longquan so that students from the south-east could keep studying; it became the Longquan Branch in 1940. The mansion, a Jiangnan courtyard house behind a Baroque-style brick façade, was restored from 2023, and its ground floor now holds an exhibition on the university's wartime migration and the branch, with upper floors opening as their displays are finished.

rows.name: Guyan Huaxiang (Ancient Weir Painting Village)
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area on the Ou River about 25 km south-west of Lishui, taking in the old river port of Dagangtou, Yantou village by the 6th-century Tongji Weir, and the Baoding celadon kiln sites. Painters borrowing the plein-air approach of France's Barbizon school have worked here since the 1980s, giving rise to the "Lishui Barbizon" school, and the area keeps an old street, pavilions, river landings and groves of old camphor trees, with boats crossing between the banks.

rows.name: Haochuan Site
rows.summary: A late Neolithic cemetery of about 4,300 to 3,700 years ago on a low hilltop in Haochuan village, where 80 graves were excavated, the richer burials at the centre and poorer ones on the slopes. Its jade, pottery and lacquer finds, related to but distinct from the Liangzhu culture, define the Haochuan culture and are shown in a dedicated gallery of Suichang County Museum, while an archaeological park with walkways is being developed at the site.

rows.name: Heyang Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village of the Zhu clan in Xinjian town, founded in the Five Dynasties period and replanned in the Yuan, whose lanes and water channels still follow that plan. It keeps more than 1,500 rooms in buildings from the Ming and Qing dynasties and the Republican era, among them some 30 complete old houses and more than ten ancestral halls, entered through the Yuan-period Bashi Gate honouring eight local imperial-examination graduates. Bashimen Street has been revived with craft shops, and the teahouse by the gate has been a stage for dujiao taichang, a local art in which one performer plays a whole band's music.

rows.name: Jinzi Peak (Qingyuan National Forest Park)
rows.summary: A forested mountain area a few kilometres north-west of Qingyuan town, centred on Jinzi Peak and run as a state-owned scenic area. In cold spells in winter its upper slopes are coated with rime ice.

rows.name: Lingjiu Temple Stone Pagodas
rows.summary: Four small stone stupas about 4 m high, carved in 1216 and 1218 under the Southern Song for Lingjiu Temple in Lishui's eastern outskirts, surviving from a set of seven that stood for the Seven Buddhas. Moved to Yunhe in the 1950s and brought back in the 1980s, they now stand at the south-west foot of Wanxiang Hill in the city centre.

rows.name: Longquan Mountain (Fengyang Mountain)
rows.summary: A mountain resort area on Fengyang Mountain inside the Fengyangshan–Baishanzu National Nature Reserve, crowned by Huangmao Peak, at 1,929 m the highest point in Zhejiang. With an average annual temperature of about 12 °C it is busiest in summer, and its upland meadows, winter rime ice and seas of cloud are the main sights.

rows.name: Nanjian Rock Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 6 km² mountain area in south-west Suichang county with craggy peaks, odd-shaped rocks, streams and mountain views. Its slopes hold about 133 hectares of terraced fields built up by generations of villagers, whose layered lines are the main sight.

rows.name: Nanming Mountain Cliff Inscriptions
rows.summary: Fifty-eight inscriptions carved on the rocks of Nanming Mountain, now a park on the southern edge of Lishui city, grouped at the Stone Beam, Gaoyang Cave and Yunge Cliff. They range from the Jin dynasty to the Republic and include a note by the prefect Guan Jinghui dated 1093, a record left by the scientist Shen Kuo on his tour of Zhejiang's farm irrigation, and two large characters attributed to the Taoist Ge Hong.

rows.name: Qianfo Mountain, Suichang
rows.summary: A privately run mountain park in Shilian town in western Suichang, named for rock formations said to resemble a thousand Buddhas. A path follows a wooded gorge with waterfalls, pools and streams up to a small Buddhist temple.

rows.name: Qingtian Stone Carving Cultural Area
rows.name_zh: 青田中国石雕文化旅游区
rows.summary: Qingtian's showcase for its soft, many-coloured local stone, carved for at least 1,500 years into seals, figures and landscapes and listed as national intangible heritage in 2006. Its centrepiece is the Qingtian Stone Carving Museum, whose oldest piece is a Songze-culture pendant of Qingtian stone, and the craft can be watched in nearby Shankou town, its traditional home, where more than 1,000 workshops carve and sell work.

rows.name: Rulong Bridge
rows.summary: A timber-arch covered bridge in Yueshan village, rebuilt in 1625 according to an inscription on its ridge beam, which makes it the oldest known timber-arch covered bridge in China with a precisely dated rebuilding. Its single woven-timber arch spans 19.5 m and carries a nine-bay gallery 28.2 m long. It is the best known of the 25 Chuzhou covered bridges that share its national listing across Lishui, and the woven-arch building technique is on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.

rows.name: Ruoliao Primeval Forest
rows.summary: A privately developed forest area in Anmin township in south-west Songyang, opened up for visitors from 2000, with forest cover put at about 95 per cent. It rises to Ruoliaoxian, at 1,502 m the highest peak in Songyang county, and forms part of the Ruoliao–Andaihou provincial scenic area.

rows.name: Shimen Cave, Qingtian
rows.summary: A scenic area at Gaoshi on the Ou River that Tang-dynasty Taoists counted among the 36 lesser grotto-heavens. Its cliffs at Qigu Hill and the Moon Cave carry about 80 inscriptions and 25 carved steles from the 5th century to the 20th, including works attributed to Xie Lingyun, Shen Kuo, Ruan Yuan and Guo Moruo. Local legend holds that the young Liu Ji (Liu Bowen), the Ming founder's strategist, studied here.

rows.name: Shisi Temple
rows.summary: A temple complex in the Daji basin whose oldest buildings date from the Yuan dynasty, with additions of the late Ming and early Qing. Within an enclosure of about 66 by 57 m stand the gate, bell tower, main hall, Sanqing Hall, a shrine to the local goddess Ma Xian and the Mei clan ancestral hall. A huge old Japanese cedar stands at the gate.

rows.name: Songyin River
rows.summary: The Songyin is a 119 km tributary of the Ou River that rises in the hills of Suichang and flows east across the Songyang basin, past Songyang town, to join the main stream at the Tongji Weir in Liandu. Its reach through Songyang is listed as a scenic area, based on the south bank at Songyang town.

rows.name: Suichang Gold Mine National Mine Park
rows.name_zh: 遂昌金矿国家矿山公园
rows.summary: A former polluted gold-mining district east of Suichang town that was cleaned up and opened to visitors as a national mine park in 2007. It has a gold museum, a protected area of old mine workings and an exhibition of mining technology, linked by a sightseeing tram, and suits visitors curious about industrial history.

rows.name: Tongji Weir
rows.summary: An irrigation system begun in 505 at Yantou village, where a curved weir diverts the Songyin River onto the Bihu plain; the timber dam was rebuilt in stone in 1205, and the surviving 275 m arch weir is described as the world's earliest arch dam. A 22.5 km main canal and hundreds of smaller channels still water about 2,000 hectares, and the system was named a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in 2014. Beside the sluice gate a temple holds 18 old steles, and Yantou keeps a Wenchang Pavilion and stone archway of the Qing period.

rows.name: Window of She Culture, Dajun
rows.summary: A village scenic area at Dajun in Jingning, the only She autonomous county in China, set up to present the culture of the She people. It has a She exhibition hall, and has offered staged She wedding and welcome ceremonies, song-and-dance performances and rafting on the river.

rows.name: Wu Wenjian Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall in Yueshan village founded in 1522, laid out as gate tower, main hall and rear hall around courtyards; the national listing dates the surviving buildings to the Qing dynasty. Its timber frame shows ruyi-pattern bracket sets, a reduced-column structure and carved column bases, and Rulong Bridge and two other old covered bridges stand in the same village.

rows.name: Xiandu Scenic Area
rows.summary: A valley of rock peaks along the Lianxi stretch of the Haoxi River north-east of Jinyun town, named "capital of immortals" by the Tang emperor Xuanzong; its emblem is Dinghu Peak, a 170.8 m stone pillar shaped like a bamboo shoot, from which the Yellow Emperor is said to have ascended to heaven. Riverside paths link Dinghu Peak, Little Red Cliff, the Xiandu Taoist temple, Niweng Cave and Zhutan Hill, and the cliffs and caves along the way, most densely around Niweng Cave, carry 123 inscriptions from the Tang to modern times, including work by Li Yangbing, Zhao Bian and Shen Kuo. Ceremonies honouring the Yellow Emperor are held here at Qingming and the Double Ninth festival.

rows.name: Xiyang Hall (Temple of Wu Sangong)
rows.summary: A temple beside the Songyuan River in Xiyang village dedicated to Wu Sangong, revered locally as the founder of shiitake mushroom growing; it was first built in 1265 and rebuilt in 1875. Along its axis stand a screen wall, gate, front hall, opera stage, courtyard and main hall, with bell and drum towers in the side wings, and Lanxi Bridge, a timber-arch covered bridge of 1794, crosses the river in the same village.

rows.name: Yanqing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A six-sided, seven-storey brick pagoda with timber eaves, built between 999 and 1002 to hold relics brought back by the monk Xingda, and the only surviving part of Yanqing Temple. It stands 37.2 m tall, and because its structure shows no trace of later rebuilding it is regarded as one of the most completely preserved Song-dynasty pagodas south of the Yangtze.

rows.name: Yunhe Rice Terraces
rows.summary: Rice terraces climbing from about 200 m to over 1,400 m above sea level in Chongtou town, begun in the Tang dynasty and greatly extended in the Yuan and Ming when silver mining brought settlers; in 2024 they became China's first terraced-landscape 5A scenic area. A cableway 3.9 km long rises some 800 m over the fields, and at their foot Kenggen village keeps stone houses said to have been built by miners. The visitor centre houses the World Terraces Museum, and the ploughing festival held here at Grain in Ear is on the national intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Yunhe Silver Mine Site
rows.summary: Remains of the Ming-dynasty silver mines whose working helped prompt the founding of Yunhe county in 1452, centred on Huangjiashe, a village at about 980 m reached through the Yunhe terraces. The village's silver-mine exhibition hall shows miners' tools, ore and local silver jewellery around a stele of 1458 recording the imperial silver bureau set up here, and old adits survive on the hill south of the village.

rows.name: Yunzhong Daji Scenic Area
rows.summary: A high mountain basin in north-west Jingning, more than 1,000 m above sea level, where villages and terraced fields are ringed by steep peaks. Its sights include Snow Daji, a waterfall of about 100 m, the old Shisi Temple with a huge Japanese cedar at its gate, and Huguan Bridge, a timber covered bridge of 1781. Cool summers have made Daji a busy homestay retreat in July and August.

rows.name: Zhan Bao Jinshi Archway
rows.summary: A bluestone memorial archway on Xiama Street in eastern Songyang town, raised for Zhan Bao, who passed the highest imperial examination in 1496, and inscribed "brothers both jinshi" on one face and "father and son both successful" on the other. The 8.5 m-high gateway of three bays and five roofs imitates timber construction, with bracket sets and reliefs of lions with a ball, cranes, qilin, figures and flowers.

rows.name: Zhulong Town
rows.summary: A mountain town on the upper Wuxi River in north-west Longquan that lay at the heart of the Communist base area in south-west Zhejiang in the 1930s and is promoted as "Zhejiang's little Jinggangshan". Riverside Red Army Street in Zhuxi village is lined with restored timber houses now used as guesthouses, teahouses and shops, and the restored seat of the Southwest Zhejiang Special Committee stands in nearby Xijing village. Zhulong is also a national historic and cultural town, visited for its river scenery, camping and spring cherry blossom.

rows.name: Ala de Hai Water Park, Xiangshan
rows.summary: A large water park in the Damuwan new town on the coast south-east of Xiangshan's county town, with water slides and pools, which also stages summer events. It is a summer outing for families and groups.

rows.name: Ancient Opera Stages of Ninghai
rows.summary: Ninghai County keeps more than 120 old opera stages in temples and clan halls, and ten of them, mostly from the Qing dynasty and the Republican period, are protected together as one national monument. The best known, in the Hu clan hall at Aohu village (built in 1797 and enlarged in 1854), has three linked caisson ceilings spiralling over the stage and its corridors, and the others are similarly painted and carved. Together they show how village opera was staged in eastern Zhejiang.

rows.name: Baiyunzhuang (Baiyun Manor), Ningbo
rows.summary: A small walled estate in western Ningbo, built from 1611 as the tomb manor of the Wan family, which in the late 1660s and 1670s became the home of the Yongshang Zhengren Academy, where the philosopher Huang Zongxi taught the Wan brothers and other students and the Eastern Zhejiang school of historical scholarship took shape. The buildings, largely rebuilt in 1934 and restored from the 1980s, house exhibitions on the Wan family, the academy and Huang Zongxi, with Wan family tombs beside them.

rows.name: Baoguo Temple
rows.summary: A hillside temple north-west of Ningbo whose main hall, built in 1013, is one of the few Northern Song timber buildings surviving south of the Yangtze. The hall predates the Song building manual Yingzao Fashi by 90 years yet matches it closely, with melon-ribbed pillars and three caisson ceilings, while the outer eaves were added in 1684. There are no monks now: the halls form an architecture museum explaining how the building was made.

rows.name: China Fishing Village, Shipu
rows.summary: A seaside resort area on Huangcheng beach, a few kilometres north of Shipu town on the southern Xiangshan coast, themed on the fishing-village culture of the area. Its sandy beach is used for swimming in summer, and it suits a half-day by the sea combined with Shipu's old town.

rows.name: China Port Museum
rows.summary: A large museum of China's ports and maritime trade at Chunxiao on the Beilun coast, opened in 2014 in a building designed by Cheng Taining that is shaped to suggest a conch shell and a sail. Its galleries trace port history and sea-borne trade, with hands-on halls on port science and the ocean, and it is also the Ningbo base of the national underwater cultural heritage programme; it was rated a national first-grade museum in 2020.

rows.name: Cicheng Ancient Town
rows.summary: The walled seat of the old Cixi County until 1954, Cicheng was spared later redevelopment and keeps lanes of Ming and Qing mansions, guildhalls, memorial arches and wells. Highlights include one of the best-preserved Confucian temples in eastern Zhejiang and family mansions such as Jiadi Shijia and Buzhengfang, and the town's restoration received a UNESCO Asia-Pacific heritage award (honourable mention) in 2009. It is a pleasant half-day of lanes, courtyards and small museums.

rows.name: Danshan Chishui Scenic Area, Yuyao
rows.summary: A stream-valley scenic area by Shilin village in Dalan town, high in the Siming Mountains of southern Yuyao, where a walking route follows the water past pools, small waterfalls and rock formations. Shilin is a mountain village some 600 years old known for its 'diaohong' persimmons, grown here for more than 400 years, which hang red on the trees in autumn.

rows.name: Dapeng Mountain
rows.summary: A 422 m hill near the coast north of Ningbo, renamed after the legend that the Qin-dynasty court sorcerer Xu Fu set sail from here for the islands of the immortals. The Youngor Group has developed it as a resort, with a Xu Fu culture park and Foji Temple in the forest park on the hill, a children's amusement park and lodgings. It suits a family day out or a hillside walk from Ningbo.

rows.name: Erling Pagoda
rows.summary: A stone pagoda about 10 m tall on the ridge of Erling Hill, a snake-shaped peninsula on the south-east side of Dongqian Lake, built in the Zhenghe era (1111–1118) of the Northern Song. Carved in imitation of a timber pavilion-style tower, it is a rare Northern Song stone building in Zhejiang, and with Erling Temple below it forms one of the lake's traditional Ten Views, 'Evening Glow at Erling'.

rows.name: Fantawild Oriental Heritage, Ningbo
rows.summary: A large theme park of the Fantawild chain in the Hangzhou Bay new area on the coast north of Cixi, whose rides and shows are themed on Chinese history and legend and make heavy use of screen and special-effects technology. It suits families and theme-park fans and takes most of a day.

rows.name: Fenghua Museum
rows.summary: The district museum of Fenghua, opened in 2020 in a converted former power-plant building on Dacheng Road in the town centre.
