Its permanent galleries cover Fenghua's history, Chiang Kai-shek and Chiang Ching-kuo and their ties with Fenghua, and local gazetteers and old books, and the history gallery won a national exhibition award for 2021.

rows.name: Former Sites of the Eastern Zhejiang Anti-Japanese Base Area, Liangnong
rows.summary: A group of old houses at Hengkantou village near Liangnong, in the northern Siming Mountains, that served in 1942–1945 as the command centre of the Communist-led anti-Japanese base area in eastern Zhejiang. They held the regional Party committee, the administrative office, the headquarters and political department of the New Fourth Army's Eastern Zhejiang column, its bank and newspaper and a branch of the Lu Xun Academy, and are now open as exhibition sites. The Eastern Zhejiang Revolutionary Base Memorial Hall stands opposite, and the village receives many school study groups.

rows.name: Guangji Bridge, Nandu
rows.summary: A covered bridge over the Xian River at Nandu village, on the old post road from Ningbo to Taizhou, whose stone piers date from a rebuilding of 1286 and carry a timber deck under a long tiled gallery; it is described as the only surviving Yuan-dynasty gallery bridge in Zhejiang. Each pier is a splayed frame of slender stone posts rather than solid masonry, one post is inscribed with the date and the name of the mason, and tea and stele pavilions stand at the ends.

rows.name: Haipi Island Water Park, Hangzhou Bay
rows.summary: A large water park in the Hangzhou Bay new area on the coast north of Cixi, with slides, pools and a wave pool in indoor and outdoor sections. It is mainly a summer outing for families and groups.

rows.name: Haitian Yizhou Sea Platform
rows.summary: A service and sightseeing platform built on piers in the sea beside the middle of the Hangzhou Bay Bridge, opened to visitors in 2010. A 145.6 m observation tower has a 360-degree gallery near the top, and the platform holds a bridge exhibition hall, cafés and a hotel. It is a stop for views of the bridge and the open bay on a drive between Ningbo and Shanghai.

rows.name: Hemudu Site and Museum
rows.summary: The type site of the Hemudu culture, a Neolithic rice-growing culture of about 5000–3000 BC, found in 1973 on the north bank of the Yao River; its waterlogged layers preserved timber pile-houses joined with mortise and tenon, cultivated rice, black pottery and carved ivory. The site museum, raised on stilts like the excavated houses, shows the finds, and an outdoor area reconstructs the village. In February 2026 a larger archaeological site park with wetlands and hands-on displays of early farming and building opened for trial operation beside it.

rows.name: Hua'ao Barracks Site
rows.summary: Dry-stone army camps built from 1646 on remote Hua'ao Island by the Ming loyalist commanders Zhang Huangyan and Zhang Mingzhen during their resistance to the Qing, the best preserved of their island bases. The two main camps at Gaotu'ao and Zhijishan keep walls, gates, rows of barrack rooms and tunnels, and a memorial hall to Zhang Huangyan opened at Gaotu'ao in 2007. The island also has a stone forest of columnar volcanic rock and traditional salt pans.

rows.name: Huangxian Forest Park, Fenghua
rows.summary: A coastal forest park around Huangxian village in Qiucun, south-eastern Fenghua, covering about 10,000 mu (some 670 hectares) of wooded hills above the shore of Xiangshan Bay, promoted as the 'Huangxian Great Wall on the Sea'. The village is linked by local tradition with the Northern Song poet Lin Bu and with Xia Huanggong, a scholar of the late Qin.

rows.name: Jiufeng Mountain, Beilun
rows.summary: A forested range of hills in Daqi, Beilun district, with 26 peaks, two lakes and valleys of streams, pools, rock formations and waterfalls, and walking routes popular with Ningbo hikers; the Ruiyan Temple valley lies on its eastern side. Its old plum garden of more than 6,000 trees blooms in late winter, and in 2025 the scenic area added an evening tour with light displays and performances.

rows.name: Jiulong Lake, Zhenhai
rows.summary: A reservoir lake in the hills of Jiulonghu town, northern Zhenhai, completed in 1988 and later switched from drinking-water supply to landscape and recreation use. The tourist area combines the lake shore with side valleys of small waterfalls, pools and named rocks, and the lakeside has become a provincial tourism resort with hotels and family attractions.

rows.name: Liangzhu Culture Park
rows.summary: A park in Gaoqiao, on the western edge of Ningbo, devoted to the legend of Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, the 'Butterfly Lovers', and built on the site of a temple and a Jin-dynasty tomb traditionally said to be Liang Shanbo's. Opened in 1999 and reopened in 2012 after expansion, it tells the story in scenes along garden paths, with pavilions, the Liang Shanbo temple, a rebuilt joint tomb of the lovers and a sculpture of the pair turned into butterflies. It has nothing to do with the Neolithic Liangzhu culture near Hangzhou.

rows.name: Lin Residence, Zijin Street
rows.summary: A Qing mansion rebuilt by the brothers Lin Zhongsong and Lin Zhonghua after they passed the provincial examinations in the Tongzhi era (1862–1874), known for its carving: about 170 brick carvings and some 50 in wood and bamboo survive. A 6 m gate tower with relief scenes, carved screen walls and a rockery like the one at Tianyi Ge fill a compound of about 3,500 m².

rows.name: Lvye Villa, Cicheng
rows.summary: A rural leisure resort in the hills of Wuxing village on the north-western edge of Cicheng, where visitors try farm work, walk in the countryside and eat farmhouse food, and whose cherry trees draw crowds when they flower in spring. An adjoining amusement area, Lvye Happy Valley, adds rides, and the old county town of Cicheng is close by.

rows.name: Mashan Leisure Area, Dongqian Lake
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area of about 100 hectares on the south-eastern shore of Dongqian Lake, centred on the Mashan wetland, where boardwalks run through reed beds and waterside trees that draw many birds. Around it are tent and camper-van campsites and the Erlingshan hot-spring resort, and the Southern Song Stone Sculpture Park lies within the area.

rows.name: Minghe Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town at the foot of Wulei Mountain in Guanhaiwei, south-eastern Cixi, with about 1,200 years of history, whose lanes, waterways and stone bridges are lined with large houses of merchants, many of whom grew rich in the herbal-medicine trade in the Ming and Qing. It is a provincial historic and cultural town, and Du Lake, Baiyang Lake, Wulei Temple and Jinxian Temple lie close by.

rows.name: Ningbo Banking Guild Hall
rows.summary: The guildhall of Ningbo's native banks (qianzhuang), built from 1925 for their meetings and money-market dealings; Ningbo bankers had pioneered a book-transfer clearing system in the 19th century. Its three courtyards combine traditional timber halls with a Western-style brick front and red tiled roofs, and the rear council hall lies behind a garden with a domed pavilion. In 1994 it became the home of the Ningbo money museum.

rows.name: Ningbo Museum
rows.summary: The city's history museum, opened in 2008 and designed by Wang Shu, who in 2012 became the first Chinese citizen to win the Pritzker Prize. Its sloping walls are faced with Ming and Qing bricks and tiles collected in the region and with concrete cast in bamboo formwork, and the galleries cover Ningbo's history and folk customs. It is now part of the Ningbo Museum group, which also runs the Ningbobang Museum.

rows.name: Ningbo Ocean World
rows.summary: A city aquarium beside Ningbo Children's Park in Yinzhou district, with walk-through viewing tunnels beneath its tanks and galleries and gardens styled on places such as ancient Egypt and Cambodia. It suits families with young children and makes an easy indoor stop in the city.

rows.name: Ningbo Science Exploration Center
rows.summary: A large hands-on science museum in the Ningbo Cultural Plaza of the Eastern New Town, open since 2014. Galleries on the ocean, the environment and the universe fill the second floor, with safety-education halls and an 18 m dome cinema above. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Ningbo Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A large zoo on hilly ground with lakes at the north-east edge of the Dongqian Lake resort area, opened in 2004 as Youngor Zoo and renamed Ningbo Wildlife Park in 2021. Animal enclosures are spread around the lakes and woods, making it a family day out.

rows.name: Ningbobang Museum
rows.summary: A museum about the 'Ningbo bang', the network of Ningbo-born merchants prominent in shipping, banking and trade in Shanghai and later overseas, opened in 2009 in a building by the architect He Jingtang laid out along a water street. Its four galleries trace how the merchants left home, the businesses they built and their ties with their home region.

rows.name: Ninghai Forest Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in the wooded hills of north-western Ninghai County, built around the Nanxi spring, whose water reaches about 49°C and contains more than 20 dissolved minerals. The surrounding forest is a national forest park, and the resort suits a relaxing half-day or an overnight stay away from the city.

rows.name: Old Bund, Ningbo
rows.summary: A riverside quarter on the north bank of the Yong River at Ningbo's Sanjiangkou, where the foreign settlement grew up after Ningbo was opened as a treaty port in 1844, two decades before Shanghai's Bund took shape. Some 54 listed historic buildings remain, among them the former British consulate, the Zhejiang customs house, the old post office and the Catholic church, in cobbled streets now lined with bars, restaurants and shops. It is busiest in the evening, when the waterfront is lit up.

rows.name: Qiantong Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old clan town in the hills of south-west Ninghai, founded when the Tong family settled here in 1233; about eight in ten residents still bear the surname. Lanes of Ming and Qing houses are laced with small channels fed by the Baixi and Lianghuang streams, and the Tong ancestral hall dates from 1385. It makes an unhurried half-day of old courtyards, stone bridges and village life.

rows.name: Qing'an Guildhall
rows.summary: A temple to the sea goddess Mazu that doubled as the guildhall of Ningbo's northern-route shipowners, completed in 1853 on the east bank of the river at Sanjiangkou and since 2014 part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site. It is unusual for having two opera stages, and is richly decorated with carved stone dragon columns, brick reliefs and red-and-gold lacquered woodcarving. The halls house the East Zhejiang Maritime Folk Museum, with models of Chinese ships through the ages.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Ningbo
rows.summary: A Gothic Revival cathedral built in 1872 under the French bishop of the Zhejiang vicariate, whose single bell tower, added in 1899, is a landmark of the riverside at Sanjiangkou. Gutted by fire in 2014, it was restored with its original style of roof tiles and reopened in 2016, and it remains an active Catholic church. It stands at the north end of Xinjiang Bridge, a short walk from the Old Bund.

rows.name: Shanglin Lake Yue Kilns
rows.summary: Nearly 200 kiln sites around Shanglin Lake and its neighbouring lakes made Yue ware celadon from the Eastern Han to the Southern Song, and the Housi'ao kiln, excavated in 2015–2017, is thought to have produced the 'secret-colour' celadon found at Famen Temple. The national archaeological park built since 2015 displays a dragon kiln at Hehuaxin, untouched shard heaps at Zhuyuanshan and workshop remains at Housi'ao, and the Shanglin Lake Yue Kiln Museum stands by the lake. It suits anyone interested in Chinese ceramics.

rows.name: Shipu Fishing Port Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old quarter of Shipu, a fishing port at the southern end of the Xiangshan peninsula, set at the foot of a hill facing the harbour, with stone-paved lanes lined with old shops, houses and a temple; Shipu is a nationally listed historic and cultural town. A second section reopened in 2025 with plazas, boutique hotels, restaurants, exhibitions and music bars, and the lanes look out over the working harbour and the sea.

rows.name: Songlanshan Coast
rows.summary: A stretch of rocky headlands and small sandy bays on the open coast east of Xiangshan town, including East Beach, South Beach and Baisha Bay. In summer it is a busy seaside resort with a bathing beach and a sunrise pavilion, and the Zhejiang Ocean Sports Centre on its shore was the sailing venue of the Hangzhou Asian Games. It suits a beach day or a coastal walk.

rows.name: Southern Song Stone Sculpture Park, Dongqian Lake
rows.summary: A park on the south-eastern shore of Dongqian Lake built around the tomb path of Shi Jian, a posthumously ennobled member of the Shi clan that gave the Southern Song several chancellors, whose avenue of paired stone officials, generals, horses, tigers and sheep between memorial gateways is described as the best-preserved Southern Song tomb path in China. More than 200 stone figures, mostly Southern Song but some from the Ming and Qing, have been gathered here from sites around the lake, with an indoor museum on the carvings and their history. Other Shi family tomb paths still stand in place in the hills around the lake.

rows.name: Stone Archways of Miaogouhou and Hengsheng
rows.summary: Two small two-pillar stone archways from the Southern Song or Yuan dynasty that once marked the spirit paths of tombs, carved in imitation of timber with brackets and tiled hip-and-gable roofs, and counted among the oldest stone archways in China. The Miaogouhou arch, 6.16 m high, stands on a hillside near Hanling village by Dongqian Lake; the Hengsheng arch, found in 1999, is about 14 km to the north in Wuxiang.

rows.name: Tashan Neolithic Site
rows.summary: A hillside settlement and cemetery in Xiangshan's county town, occupied from about 4000 to 500 BC, where excavations in 1990, 1993 and 2007–2008 found more than 60 Neolithic burials with pottery and jade. The finds show the Hemudu and Majiabang cultures meeting on the Xiangshan coast. The site itself is covered by a public park, and artefacts from it are displayed in the Xiangshan County Museum in the same town.

rows.name: Tashan Weir
rows.summary: A stone weir across the Yin River built in 833 under the county magistrate Wang Yuanwei, which kept tidal salt water out and diverted fresh water to irrigate the plain and supply the city of Mingzhou, today's Ningbo. The 113.7 m dam of dressed stone blocks is still in use, and in 2015 it was named a World Heritage Irrigation Structure. A temple to Wang stands on the hill beside it.

rows.name: Temple of King Ashoka
rows.summary: A Buddhist monastery at the foot of Mount Mao east of Ningbo, traditionally founded in the Western Jin and named by Emperor Wu of Liang, and known for a relic said to come from the Buddha's skull. The monk Jianzhen stayed here in 744 between attempts to reach Japan; the temple was fifth of the Five Mountains under the Southern Song and is regarded as an ancestral temple of Japan's Rinzai school. Most of its halls were rebuilt in the Qing dynasty, and it remains an active monastery.

rows.name: Tiangong Manor, Yinzhou
rows.summary: A rural tourism park of about 1,600 mu (some 107 hectares) run by Wandi village in Xiaying, on the southern edge of Ningbo city, combining farm fields and orchards with hands-on farm activities, children's study programmes, leisure facilities and halls showing local intangible-heritage crafts and the village's development. It receives large numbers of school study groups and suits families wanting a countryside day out close to the city.

rows.name: Tianluoshan Site
rows.summary: A Hemudu-culture village site at Xiang'ao village in Sanqishi, inhabited about 7,000 to 5,500 years ago, found in 2001 and excavated from 2004, whose waterlogged layers kept timber pile-house remains, the layout of a village, rice, food remains and what are thought to be the roots of cultivated tea plants. A shelter hall built over the excavation in 2007 lets visitors look down on the dig and its finds.

rows.name: Tianning Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A square, multi-eaved brick pagoda about 12 m tall, dated by its inscribed bricks to the 860s, which is the only part of Tianning Temple (founded in 851) still standing. It is the oldest Tang brick pagoda in Zhejiang, kept in a small green on Zhongshan West Road after a proposal to remove it when the road was widened in 1995 was dropped.

rows.name: Tiantong Temple
rows.summary: A large Chan monastery in the forested Taibai Mountains east of Ningbo, traditionally founded in the Western Jin, ranked third of the Five Mountains under the Southern Song and regarded as the cradle of Japan's Sōtō Zen school. Its oldest surviving hall dates from 1631, and an avenue of more than 200 old ginkgo trees turns gold in late autumn. It remains an active monastery.

rows.name: Tianxia Yuyuan Jade Park, Yuyao
rows.summary: A jade-themed culture park at the foot of Jiulong Hill in Dayin town, eastern Yuyao, laid out on a hillside around a lake with a Buddhist temple, terraces, gateways and gardens, and centred on a giant stack of jade boulders. It suits a short visit for those interested in Chinese jade.

rows.name: Tianyi Ge and Moon Lake
rows.summary: Tianyi Ge, built in 1561–1566 by the official Fan Qin, is the oldest surviving private library in China, a two-storey book tower with a fire-pond in front and a rockery garden. The museum around it adds the Fan family residence, a forest of steles and the Qin clan hall, and the library's layout was copied for the imperial libraries built to hold the Siku Quanshu. Next door, Moon Lake, dug in the Tang, is a park of islands, bridges and restored historic houses in the heart of the city.

rows.name: Tongji Bridge, Yuyao
rows.summary: A tall three-arch stone bridge across the Yao River in the centre of Yuyao, first built in timber in 1047, rebuilt in stone in 1332 and given its present form in 1729–1731. Its steep central arch let sea-going boats pass beneath under sail, and it is nicknamed the 'First Bridge of Eastern Zhejiang'. At its north end stands the Shunjiang Tower, an old city-gate tower, and the bridge lies in the protected historic quarter around Fuqian Road.

rows.name: Wang Yangming's Former Residence
rows.summary: The birthplace in central Yuyao of Wang Shouren, better known as Wang Yangming (1472–1529), the Ming philosopher who brought the Confucian 'learning of the mind' to its fullest form. Along its axis stand a gatehouse, a sedan-chair hall, a carved brick gate tower, the Shoushan Hall and the two-storey Ruiyun Tower where he was born, rebuilt in 1996, and the house has been a memorial museum since 2007. The protected unit also covers his tomb, on the slopes of Xianxia hill in Lanting, Shaoxing, built in 1529 and reached by a stepped path of more than 100 steps.

rows.name: Wulongtan (Five Dragon Pools), Ningbo
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Longguan township, in the Siming foothills of south-western Haishu district, developed from 2000 around a stream that drops through a chain of five pools and waterfalls, each named after a dragon. A path climbs past rock inscriptions, cliffs and the pools to Yinglin Lake higher up, and a small Guandi and Dragon King temple, rebuilt many times, stands by the entrance.

rows.name: Wushan Grottoes, Ninghai
rows.summary: An old stone quarry in low coastal hills at Changjie, eastern Ninghai, where stone was cut from the Sui and Tang onward, most intensively under the Song and Yuan, leaving more than 800 man-made caverns in some 30 groups. Some caverns are linked by passages or open to the sky through shafts, others are flooded into clear green pools, and paths and stairs lead through them to a pavilion on the hilltop. Opened to visitors after 2004, it stays cool even in summer.

rows.name: Xiangshan Global Studios
rows.summary: A film and television studio complex in Xinqiao, Xiangshan County, begun in 2003 for the wuxia series The Return of the Condor Heroes and open to visitors since 2005. Its period backlots include a Song-style martial-arts town, a Spring and Autumn and Warring States town, a Tang city and a Republican-era street, among sets used for many historical dramas. It suits film and TV fans and families.

rows.name: Xikou–Tengtou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Xikou, a town on the Shan stream below the Siming hills, is the home town of Chiang Kai-shek, and its protected Chiang family buildings include Fenghao House, the family residence he enlarged in the late 1920s, the salt shop where he was born in 1887, the house where his son Chiang Ching-kuo lived from 1937 and his mother's tomb. Above the town, Xuedou Mountain has waterfalls, cliffs, Chiang's Miaogaotai villa and Xuedou Temple, a Chan monastery founded in the Jin and linked with the cult of the Maitreya Buddha, with a giant bronze Maitreya statue. The scenic area also takes in Tengtou, an ecological model village about 10 km east of Xikou with gardens, orchards and a collection of old carved stone windows.

rows.name: Yongfeng Warehouse Site
rows.summary: The site of a large state warehouse used from the Southern Song to the Ming, best known as the Yongfeng storehouse of the Yuan dynasty, excavated in 2001–2002 beside the Drum Tower. Finds included ceramics from kilns across China and Persian blue-glazed pottery, evidence of Ningbo's overseas trade. The excavation was backfilled, and a park opened in 2009 shows a full-size replica of the foundations from boardwalks.

rows.name: Zhaobao Mountain
rows.summary: A hill guarding the mouth of the Yong River, fortified from the Ming to the 1940s against Japanese pirates and British, French and Japanese forces, and the core of the Zhenhaikou coastal defence monuments. Paths lead to the Ming Weiyuan fort on the summit (1560), the Moon fort of 1883, old steles and the round Anyuan battery of 1887, with the Aozhu Pagoda on the hill and a coastal defence museum, opened in 1997, at its foot. Further monuments of the same group, including Qing batteries and a lookout on Jinji Hill, lie across the river in Beilun.

rows.name: Dachen Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village with a history of more than 600 years in Dachen township, Jiangshan, its houses, mostly from the Qing dynasty, built close against the surrounding hills. The village keeps the ancestral hall of the Wang clan, and in 2019 Dachen was named in the first national list of key villages for rural tourism.

rows.name: Guanxi Shijia Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: A Ming ancestral hall of the Wanli era (1573–1620) in Yangjia village in the north of Longyou, two courtyards deep with a stage. Its gatehouse has an imposing double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, a stone tablet set in the east wall records when and how it was built, and its brick-framed gable walls are typical of Ming building in Longyou.

rows.name: Gutianshan National Nature Reserve
rows.summary: A national nature reserve of about 81 km² in the mountains of western Kaihua on the Jiangxi border, set up in 1975 and upgraded in 2001 to protect subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest. Its wildlife includes Elliot's pheasant and the black muntjac, and the highest point, Shi'ershan, reaches 1,258 m. Part of the reserve is open to visitors as a scenic area, and the whole reserve lies within the Qianjiangyuan national park area at the source of the Qiantang River.

rows.name: Huzhen Sarira Pagoda
rows.summary: A six-sided, seven-storey brick pagoda about 27 m tall, built solid in imitation of a timber tower, on Xiajie street in Huzhen town. It was first built in 1058 in the Northern Song and was repaired in the Ming and again in 1903.

rows.name: Lan Clan Ancestral Hall, Beier
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Lan clan, a family of the She ethnic minority, in Beier village, Hangbu town, built in 1628 at the end of the Ming dynasty. Covering about 650 m² and finely crafted, it is regarded as the best-preserved She ancestral hall in Zhejiang.

rows.name: Longyou Caves
rows.summary: A group of 24 huge man-made caverns cut into the sandstone of Fenghuang Hill beside the Qu River, found in 1992 when farmers drained five village ponds and discovered that they were flooded caverns. Nobody knows who dug them, when or why: their walls, ceilings and pillars are covered in neat bands of chisel marks, there is no record of their making, and pottery found in the silt dates from the Han dynasty. Several caverns can be walked through, with tall chambers supported by stone pillars left in place.

rows.name: Longyou Folk Residence Garden
rows.summary: An open-air museum of old architecture on Jiming Hill on the southern edge of Longyou town, where Ming and Qing buildings from around the county that could not be protected where they stood have been dismantled and rebuilt since 1991. Among them are the Gaogang Qifeng hall with its double-eaved gatehouse, a Ming stone pavilion, the Wu family hall with an unusual earthquake-resistant bracket frame, the Wang family house and the Lingshan flower hall, grouped around the Ming Jiming Pagoda, which stands on its original site.

rows.name: Longyou Rosewood Town
rows.summary: A modern 'characteristic town' of about 3.5 km² in Huzhen, Longyou, built around the rosewood (hongmu) furniture industry, with traditional-style buildings, furniture workshops, a timber trading area and a rosewood cultural and creative park. Visitors come to see furniture being made and to shop, and the town has staged evening events such as bonfire parties and music festivals.

rows.name: Meishudi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested hill scenic area of about 8 km² in eastern Changshan, known for its old trees, wide bamboo forests and the Jiulong Waterfall, which drops down a sheer cliff. Walkers can climb Baijuhua Peak, the highest point in Changshan county, and the villages offer family inns serving local tea, wild greens and 'Guanyin tofu', a jelly made from leaves.

rows.name: Mount Fugai
rows.summary: A forested mountain on the Zhejiang–Fujian border just south of Nianbadu, an outlier of the Xianxia range whose 1,146 m summit lies on the Fujian side. On the Jiangshan side a scenic area has been laid out with walking trails, and Jiangshan promotes it together with Mount Jianglang and Nianbadu old town.

rows.name: Mount Jianglang & Nianbadu
rows.summary: Mount Jianglang is a row of three sheer red-rock pillars, Langfeng, Yafeng and Lingfeng, each more than 300 m tall, with the summit of Langfeng at 816.8 m; it is part of the China Danxia World Heritage Site, and paths climb between the peaks, including the narrow 'strip of sky' passage between Yafeng and Lingfeng, only 3.5 m wide at its narrowest. The same 5A area takes in Nianbadu, about 30 km to the south near the Fujian border, a former garrison town on the Xianxia road whose old street of Ming to Republican-era houses and temples is known for the many surnames and dialects of its residents.

rows.name: Qicai Changhong Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area covering Changhong township in the forested north-west of Kaihua, on the Jiangxi border next to Wuyuan, with woodland over more than 85% of its land. Its two main sights are Taihuishan, a hillside village nicknamed the 'Potala Palace of Jiangnan', and Gaotiankeng, an old upland village at about 680 m whose dark skies have made it a stargazing spot with a dark-sky park, an astronomy museum and viewing platforms. It suits walkers, photographers and anyone wanting a quiet night under the stars.

rows.name: Quzhou Ancient City & City Walls
rows.summary: The historic core of Quzhou, a 3.2 km² cultural tourism zone opened in 2016 around Shuiting Gate, where the Ming–Qing city wall stands beside the Qu River, and the 'three streets and seven alleys' of old lanes lined with restored buildings, craft workshops and food stalls. Six old gates survive along with stretches of the wall that earned the city the name 'Iron Quzhou' in past sieges, and a gate tower over Shuiting Gate and a bell tower on its Ming stone base have been rebuilt. Near the gate on Xiaying Street stands the Zhou Xuanling Wang Temple, a shrine to a filial son first built in the Southern Song and rebuilt in the Ming.

rows.name: Root Palace Buddhist Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.summary: A cultural park on the edge of Kaihua county town created by the root-carving artist Xu Guqing, where garden courtyards and buildings display thousands of root carvings and bonsai made from tree roots, a craft practised in Kaihua since the Tang dynasty. Its centrepiece is the 'Root Palace Buddhist Kingdom', with large Buddhist figures and a set of 500 arhats carved from roots, and the zone counts more than 20,000 root carvings across over 40 sights. It suits anyone interested in Chinese folk crafts.

rows.name: Sanhuai Hall, Rudamen
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Wang clan in Rudamen, part of Tianchi village in Hengshan town, a Ming–Qing building five courtyards deep with a stage and side rooms, covering about 1,500 m². Tianchi village keeps 86 old buildings, most of them from the Ming and Qing, and its lotus fields, farmed for some 800 years, flower from June to September.

rows.name: Sanmenyuan Ye Family Residences
rows.summary: Three surviving mansions of the Ye family in Sanmenyuan village, Shifo township, built in 1846 against Hushan hill above a stream, with courtyards, a garden and a pond. Their brick gatehouses carry 23 finely carved panels of scenes from Wu opera, the regional opera of central Zhejiang, valued as a rare well-preserved record of local theatre.

rows.name: Sanqingkou Porcelain Workshops
rows.summary: A porcelain-making village in a small valley in Xiakou town, where the Huang family set up kilns in the Qianlong era of the Qing dynasty, using local kaolin, water-powered pounding mills and wood from the hills, and shipped blue-and-white wares along the Xianxia road. Workshops, water-driven mills, kilns, a kiln-god temple, houses and the clan hall survive, including a 35 m dragon kiln built on the slope in 1962 that stopped in 1997 and was relit in 2023. An old single-arch stone bridge, the Wenchang Bridge, crosses the stream in the village.

rows.name: Sanqu Stone Forest
rows.summary: A karst landscape on Sanqu Mountain in Huibu town, Changshan, where limestone formed from a reef about 440 million years ago (late Ordovician) has weathered into clusters of rock pinnacles, mazes, arches and fissures. Paths lead past a sinkhole about 40 m deep, vine-hung gorges and caves, and the rock holds fossils of corals and other reef animals. It is one of the highlights of the Changshan Geopark, which was designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in April 2026.

rows.name: Shaoyi Hall & Hengshan Pagoda
rows.summary: Two Ming monuments in Hengshan town in northern Longyou, listed together. Shaoyi Hall in Gaoshan village is a brick-and-timber hall of the early Ming Hongwu era, of which the front two of its four courtyards survive. Hengshan Pagoda in Hengshan village is an octagonal, seven-storey hollow brick pagoda of the 1530s, some 30 m tall, restored in 2006–07.

rows.name: Taoyuan Qili Scenic Area
rows.summary: A large mountain and rural scenic area of about 60 km² in Qili township, Kecheng, at an average altitude of 650 m and almost entirely forested. It takes in the Daguping range, with 15 peaks above 1,000 m, waterfalls such as Yanghua and Feilaishi, the Zhiling stone forest and old villages including Yangwu, Shangcun, Junliang and Zhiling. Being several degrees cooler than the city, it is popular in summer for walking and village homestays.

rows.name: Temple of Southern Confucianism
rows.summary: The family temple of the southern branch of Confucius's descendants, who followed the Song court south after the fall of Kaifeng in 1127 and were given a home in Quzhou; the temple has stood on its present site since 1520 and took its current form in a rebuilding of 1821–23. Its halls are laid out on three parallel axes, with the Dacheng Hall on the central one, the rebuilt Kong family mansion to the west and a garden behind. A memorial ceremony for Confucius is held here every year and is listed as national intangible cultural heritage.

rows.name: Wenchang Palace, Nianbadu
rows.summary: A temple to Wenchang, the god of literature, in Xunli, the core of Nianbadu old town, built in 1909–1911 with three courtyards and a three-storey main hall under a double-eaved roof with painted ceilings. It is one of the main buildings of Nianbadu, a former garrison town on the Xianxia road near the Fujian border whose old street of Ming to Republican-era houses runs along the Feng stream.

rows.name: Wu Ancestral Hall, Chetang
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty ancestral hall of the Wu clan in Chetang village, Yunxi township, built in the Jiajing reign in the early 1530s. It is laid out as a square with halls on all four sides of the courtyard, and the front hall contains a theatre stage.

rows.name: Xianxia Pass
rows.summary: A fortified pass on the ancient Xianxia road over the Xianxia range, for centuries an important overland route between the Qiantang and Min river basins of Zhejiang and Fujian. Four stone gateways and about 5 km of stone-paved road survive; tradition says the road was opened by Huang Chao's rebel army in the late Tang. The pass was defended against the Qing by Southern Ming forces, and Chinese troops held the area against a Japanese advance in 1942.

rows.name: Xianyan Cave Inscriptions
rows.summary: A red-sandstone cave with a mouth about 25 m wide and a depth of about 22 m, south of Hongxing village in Zhangtan, whose walls carry more than 50 carved inscriptions left by officials and scholars from the late 8th to the late 19th century, most of them from the Southern Song. The most valued, on the west wall, dates from 1121 and records the government troops sent against the Fang La rebellion. A temple that stood outside the cave was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution.

rows.name: Yang Ancestral Halls, Nanwu
rows.summary: Two ancestral halls of the Yang clan in Nanwu village, Fenglin town: the inner hall in the village centre dates from the late Ming or early Qing, and the slightly later outer hall at the village entrance adds side wings. Both are three courtyards deep in the local Jiangshan style, each with an old well outside, and the village's temple fair is listed as Quzhou intangible heritage.

rows.name: Yaowang Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area in southern Qujiang, part of the Ziweishan National Forest Park, promoted for its clean air and themed on traditional Chinese medicine, from which it takes its name ('Medicine King Mountain'). Its sights include the Mawei Waterfall, which drops 88 m, as well as a glass skywalk and a fibreglass slide.

rows.name: Anchang Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old canal town in northern Keqiao, named in the late Tang and listed among China's historic and cultural towns in 2005, with cobbled lanes and black-awning boats on its waterways. It is known for cured foods, with sausages, soy-sauce duck and dried fish hung under the eaves before the Lunar New Year, when the town holds a folk festival, and for the Renchang soy sauce works, founded in 1892 and still using traditional methods.

rows.name: Ancient Towpath, Keqiao
rows.summary: A stone towpath along the Eastern Zhejiang Canal from which boats were hauled by men on foot, first worn along the banks after the canal was dug in the Western Jin and rebuilt in stone in the Hongzhi reign of the Ming (1488–1505). The protected 7.5 km stretch runs from Banqiao in Qianqing to Shangxie bridge in Keqiao, partly along the bank and partly as a causeway out in the water, with bridges at intervals to let boats through, which earned it the name 'white jade dyke'.

rows.name: Angsang Lake Causeway
rows.summary: A stone causeway about 3.5 km long that winds north–south across Angsang Lake on the northern edge of Shaoxing, built in the late Ming and finished after 1642 so that boats could shelter from wind and waves, while also linking the two shores. Its S-shaped bank of dressed stone, paved with large slabs, is broken by five stone beam bridges and has a small stone roadside pavilion carrying Qing inscriptions on its repair. The northern 1.5 km still has water on both sides, while the southern part has had water on one side only since land was reclaimed in the 1970s.

rows.name: Bazi Bridge
rows.summary: A stone beam bridge in the eastern part of Shaoxing's old city, rebuilt in 1256, whose stepped approaches split at both ends so that the bridge is shaped like the character 八 ('eight'); it is the only known early example of this form among China's simple beam bridges. It heads the protected group of Shaoxing's ancient bridges, which also includes eleven other stone bridges from the Yuan to the Republic in Yuecheng and Keqiao, among them the Guangning, Guangxiang, Tishan and Xiegong bridges in the old city.

rows.name: Cao'e Temple
rows.summary: A temple on the west bank of the Cao'e River honouring Cao E, an Eastern Han girl who drowned in the river trying to save her father and became a model of filial piety; she was reburied here with a memorial stele in 151, and a shrine grew up around her grave. The present buildings, set out on three parallel axes with an opera stage, date from a rebuilding of 1931–36 after a fire in 1929 and are known for the dense carving of their columns, beams, brackets and doors. The temple also keeps a Song copy of the Cao E stele from 1093 and more than 30 couplets and plaques by noted calligraphers.

rows.name: Chongren Old Town
rows.summary: A village-town in western Shengzhou, settled before the Three Kingdoms, which became the home of the Qiu clan after they moved here in the 1040s and keeps more than 200 buildings from the early Ming to the Republic, among them 154 old courtyard gates (taimen), 14 tea and road pavilions and 51 old wells. Highlights are the Yushan ancestral hall of 1791, the largest in the town, the mid-Qing Wulian Taimen, a group of linked courtyards with fine woodcarving, a former pawnshop and the Republican-era town office and courthouse.

rows.name: Chuanyan Nineteen Peaks
rows.summary: A scenic area of red sandstone cliffs in Jingling town, south-west Xinchang, named after a row of nineteen peaks that rise above the meeting of several mountain streams. Paths climb to the peaks and run through Qianzhang Gorge (Qianzhang Yougu), a narrow ravine walked on a mostly level path, and the area also hosts events such as a motorcycle and music festival.

rows.name: Chunhui Middle School Old Campus, Baima Lake
rows.summary: A private secondary school on the shore of Baima Lake, paid for by the merchant Chen Chunlan and opened in 1922 under the educator Jing Hengyi, where writers and artists such as Zhu Ziqing, Xia Mianzun, Feng Zikai and Zhu Guangqian taught in the 1920s; it pioneered co-education among Zhejiang's secondary schools. Its early buildings, joined by covered corridors, are still used by the school, while the teachers' houses along the lake outside the north gate, including Feng Zikai's Xiao Yangliu Wu, Xia Mianzun's Ping Wu and Li Shutong's Wanqing Shanfang, have been restored.

rows.name: Dafo Temple, Xinchang
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the Shicheng hills on the edge of Xinchang town, founded in 345, whose great hall encloses a seated stone Maitreya carved into the cliff of Xianji Rock and completed in 516 after the work of three successive monks. Nearby, the Thousand Buddha Cliff (Qianfoyan) carries rows of small Buddha figures from the same Southern Dynasties period, and the grounds also hold a reclining Buddha hall, cliff inscriptions and a petrified forest.

rows.name: Dali Silk World, Xinchang
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism site at the works of Dali Silk, a silk textile and garment maker in Xinchang, which the company began developing around the theme of silk in 2007. Visitors see how silk is produced and learn about silk culture, and it suits travellers with an interest in textiles or a short stop in Xinchang.

rows.name: Dashan Pagoda
rows.summary: A hexagonal, seven-storey brick pagoda 40.5 m tall in the centre of Shaoxing, named after Dashan Temple, founded in 504, in which it once stood. It burned with the temple in 1197 and was rebuilt in 1228, then repaired in 1403, 1669 and 1957; the wooden eaves and the stairs inside are gone, leaving a hollow brick shell with doorways and niches on every level.

rows.name: Datong School and Xu Xilin's Former Residence
rows.summary: A school opened in 1905 in a former Qing granary by Xu Xilin and Tao Chengzhang of the anti-Qing Guangfuhui to train members of secret societies for an armed rising; after Xu left for Anhui it was run by Qiu Jin, who was arrested here on 13 July 1907 after Xu's failed Anqing uprising. Its halls and classrooms, restored from 1981, display documents and relics of these events. The protected site also covers Xu Xilin's birthplace, a Qing house of three halls with a library in Dongpu old town, about 7 km north-west.

rows.name: Daxianglin and Doushuaitian
rows.summary: A Buddhist-themed scenic area in Hutang, Keqiao, at the western end of the Kuaiji hills, known for more than 400 mu (about 27 hectares) of sweet osmanthus trees, among them one over 1,000 years old that is billed as the 'King of Chinese Osmanthus'. Higher up stand Longhua Temple and the Doushuaitian (Tushita) palace, a hall built around a giant seated Maitreya Buddha. The trees flower in autumn, when the area is at its busiest.

rows.name: East Huacheng Temple Pagoda, Fengqiao
rows.summary: A brick pagoda built in 1092 on the Ziwei hill ridge just south-east of Fengqiao, named after the East Huacheng Temple that once stood in front of it and also called the Yuanyou Pagoda after the reign in which it was built. Originally seven storeys of brick and timber, it now stands four storeys high as a bare brick shell on a stone base, with brick brackets and some bricks stamped with pagoda designs or the date of construction.

rows.name: East Lake, Shaoxing
rows.summary: A small lake on the eastern edge of Shaoxing that fills an old quarry: from the Han dynasty onwards masons cut away half of a hill of grey stone, leaving sheer cliffs and deep pools, which the late-Qing local scholar Tao Junxuan enclosed with a long dyke and laid out as a garden. Small boats take visitors under stone bridges and into the cliff caves, such as Xiantao and Taogong caves, past pavilions along the shore, and the Tao She hall on the west side commemorates the 1911 revolutionary Tao Chengzhang.

rows.name: Fenghuangshan Kiln Sites
rows.summary: A group of kilns on the hill slopes behind Dashan village in Shangpu, Shangyu, which fired early celadon for daily use and for burials during only fifty or sixty years, from the late Three Kingdoms to the end of the Western Jin in the third and early fourth centuries. Excavated dragon kilns are displayed under timber shelters with boardwalks in the Fenghuangshan archaeological site park. About 2 km away is the Eastern Han Xiaoxiantan kiln site, whose finds show that mature porcelain was already being made in Zhejiang at that time, though there is little to see there.

rows.name: Former Residence of Cai Yuanpei
rows.summary: The birthplace of Cai Yuanpei (1868–1940), the educator who was president of Peking University and founder of the Academia Sinica, and earlier a leader of the anti-Qing Guangfuhui. It is a traditional Shaoxing taimen house bought by his grandfather in the Daoguang reign, whose gatehouse and main hall keep Ming-style features, with a two-storey rear building added later, in the Jishan (Shusheng Guli) historic quarter.

rows.name: Fuzhi Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain of the Siming range where Shangyu, Shengzhou and Yuyao meet, rising to about 860 m as the highest point in Shangyu; its name, 'the upturned wine cup', comes from a line by the fifth-century poet Xie Lingyun, who wrote of drinking and composing poems on the mountain, then turning his cup over. On its slopes in Lingnan township more than 20,000 small terraced fields, farmed for centuries, spill down past the old village of Dongcheng, and a dozen 'stone rivers' of tumbled boulders, regarded as relics of Ice Age glaciation, streak the hillside. The terraces turn yellow with rapeseed flowers in spring, when the township holds a flower festival.

rows.name: Jianchu Land-Purchase Inscription
rows.summary: A cliff inscription cut in AD 76 on the eastern slope of Tiao hill in Fusheng, recording in 20 characters that six brothers bought this hillside together as a burial ground, with the words 'Da Ji' ('great fortune') above. It is the oldest known cliff inscription in Zhejiang and the largest surviving land deed for a tomb in China, with a colophon of 1823 by the Qing scholar Wu Rongguang carved beside it, and the rock now sits inside a small railed shelter.

rows.name: Keyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area of about 6.9 km² west of Shaoxing made up of three parts: the rocks of Ke hill, a stretch of Jian Lake and Luzhen, a water-town quarter. Its centrepiece is the Tiangong Great Buddha, a seated Maitreya 11.3 m high carved in the Song dynasty inside a great curved rock face, with Puzhao Temple behind it and inscriptions from the Ming and Qing dynasties on the Yungu rock, Qixing Rock and other cliffs.

rows.name: Lu Xun Native Place & Shen Garden
rows.summary: The block on Lu Xun Middle Road where the writer Lu Xun (Zhou Shuren) was born in 1881 and grew up until 1898, now a historic quarter taking in his ancestral home, the family's New Taimen house with the Baicao Garden behind it, the Sanwei Study across the canal where he went to school, and the Shaoxing Lu Xun Memorial Hall, first opened in 1953. About 500 m east along the same road is Shen Garden, linked to the Song poet Lu You and his first wife Tang Wan, which was rebuilt from 1984 on a plan of the old garden and keeps a gourd-shaped pond, a well and an earth mound from the Song.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Yu the Great
rows.summary: The traditional burial place of Yu the Great, the legendary tamer of floods and founder of the Xia dynasty, at the foot of Kuaiji Mountain south-east of Shaoxing. The site has three parts: the tomb, marked by a stele pavilion inscribed 'Da Yu Ling' beside Yu Pool; the Yu Temple, first built in the early Liang dynasty and laid out as a palace-style complex; and the sacrificial hall, rebuilt in 2007–08. The temple grounds also hold the Goulou stele with its puzzling tadpole-like script and the Bianshi, a conical stone with a hole through it.

rows.name: Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)
rows.summary: The garden at the foot of Lanzhu hill where, in 353, the calligrapher Wang Xizhi and more than forty friends held a spring gathering, floating cups of wine down a winding stream and writing poems, for which he wrote the Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Poems, the most celebrated work of Chinese running script. The present site was rebuilt in 1548 and restored to its Ming and Qing layout from 1979, with the Goose Pond, the Lanting stele, the Liushang pavilion beside the winding stream, the Wang Xizhi memorial hall and a stele carved with inscriptions by both the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors. A calligraphy museum and stone copies of the Preface by later masters complete the visit.

rows.name: Oriental Neverland (Kuwan Town)
rows.summary: An amusement-park complex in Keqiao, listed together with the surrounding 'Kuwan Town' leisure development, made up of the indoor Mountain Kingdom, the outdoor Coldplay Kingdom (Kuwan Wangguo) with several roller coasters including an inverted coaster, and a water park. It suits families and thrill-ride fans looking for a day of rides rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qiaobo Ice and Snow World
rows.summary: An indoor ski centre beside the Keyan scenic area in Keqiao, founded by the former speed-skating world champion Ye Qiaobo, where a refrigerated hall with artificial snow allows skiing and snowboarding all year round. Its two broad, gentle trails suit beginners and children, and the complex also has an exhibition on skiing and the Winter Olympics, an ice rink and a hotel.

rows.name: Qingteng Studio (Xu Wei's Former Residence)
rows.summary: The birthplace and study of Xu Wei (1521–1593), the Ming painter, calligrapher, poet and playwright whose free ink painting gave rise to the Qingteng school, named after one of his art names; the late Ming painter Chen Hongshou later lived here too. The protected unit also covers Xu Wei's tomb, a square stone-built mound restored in 1989 at the foot of Jiangpo hill in Lanting subdistrict, next to the Yinshan royal tomb.

rows.name: Qiu Jin's Former Residence
rows.summary: The family home of the revolutionary and writer Qiu Jin at Hechangtang, on the south-west foot of Pagoda Hill, where she spent her girlhood and lived again from her return from Japan in 1906 until her execution in 1907. The brick-and-timber house of five successive halls, once part of a Ming official's villa, was acquired by her grandfather in 1890. The protected site also includes the Qiu Jin Martyr Memorial at Xuantingkou on Jiefang North Road, completed in 1930–33 at the place where she was executed.

rows.name: Shunwang Temple
rows.summary: A temple on Shunwang hill in Wangtan town, southern Keqiao, dedicated to the legendary sage-king Shun, who by local tradition took refuge here from the unrest stirred up by Yao's son Danzhu. The present buildings were rebuilt in the Xianfeng reign and again in 1862, and on about 1,760 m² they include a gate, an opera stage with double eaves and a coffered ceiling, front and rear halls and side wings.

rows.name: Si Family Houses, Sizhai
rows.summary: Fourteen large houses from the Qing and Republican periods in Sizhai, a hill village in Dongbaihu town where the Si clan has lived since the Tang. The largest is the Sishengju, known as the 'Thousand-Pillar House', a Jiaqing-era mansion covering 6,850 m², alongside the Faxiangju of the same period (3,257 m²) and the Huaguogong villa of the Daoguang reign.

rows.name: Wang Clan Ancestral Halls, Huatang
rows.summary: Two ancestral halls in Huatang village, Jinting town, the seat of a Wang clan descended from the fourth-century calligrapher Wang Xizhi. The great hall, begun in 1512 for Wang Qiong, a 36th-generation descendant, and his wife, covers about 1,800 m², and a newer hall stands beside it. Wang Xizhi's reputed tomb, with a stone pavilion and a memorial archway, lies in the Wang Xizhi former residence area in the same town.

rows.name: Wuxie Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill scenic area in Wuxie town, in the north-west of Zhuji, named after a chain of five waterfalls, counted from the first to the fifth, that step down a forested gorge. The area is listed as a national scenic area and a national forest park.

rows.name: Xi Shi's Hometown (Xishi Guli)
rows.summary: A tourist area of about 1.44 km² on both banks of the Huan River at the foot of Zhuluo hill in Zhuji, built by the city from 2003 around the legendary home of Xi Shi, one of the Four Beauties of ancient China. Its core is the Xishi Temple, completed in 1990 using more than 12,000 carved beams, brackets, windows and other parts salvaged from old houses across Zhuji, and around it are a hall of famous women, a shrine to Fan Li, a folk museum and a shopping street built in old style.

rows.name: Yinshan Royal Tomb of Yue
rows.summary: The tomb of a king of the Spring and Autumn state of Yue, possibly Yunchang, father of King Goujian, cut into the top of Yin hill and ringed by a moat; excavated in 1996–98 after tomb robbers struck, it was the first Yue royal tomb found in China. A museum hall built over the open pit shows the timber burial chamber, 34.8 m long with a rare triangular cross-section formed by more than 100 leaning beams, and a lacquered coffin about 6 m long hollowed from a single log.

rows.name: Changyu Dongtian Quarry Caves
rows.summary: A hill near Xinhe in Wenling honeycombed with man-made caverns left by some 1,500 years of quarrying stone slabs, now a national mine park and, with nearby Fangshan, a national scenic area. Linked halls, pillars and pools such as the Shuangmen, Guanxi, Shuiyun and Lingxiao caves can be explored on foot, and one cavern holds a giant carved stone bowl. It forms part of the Yandangshan Global Geopark, listed in 2005.

rows.name: Dachen Islands
rows.summary: A group of 29 islands and islets about 52 km off Taizhou, with Upper and Lower Dachen the two inhabited main islands, wooded hills that form a provincial forest park, sea-worn rocks, beaches and fishing harbours. The islands were held by the Republic of China until February 1955, when, after the loss of nearby Yijiangshan, its troops and the whole civilian population were evacuated to Taiwan under US Navy escort; Chiang Ching-kuo's former residence and old command posts and tunnels survive from that period. On Upper Dachen the Wushatou area has a cliffside walkway about 2.5 km long with a short glass skywalk.

rows.name: Fangshan, Wenling
rows.summary: A flat-topped mountain of volcanic rhyolite in Daxi town, western Wenling, on the border with Yueqing, ringed by sheer cliffs but open on top, where lakes and ponds dot the summit plateau and wild azaleas flower in spring; the Taizhou government describes it as the largest Mesozoic rhyolite volcanic platform in Asia. The Wenling side is divided into the Fangshan, Nansongyan and Shifeng areas, and the mountain forms the eastern section of the Yandangshan Global Geopark, listed in 2005, and, with Changyu Dongtian, a national scenic area since 2006.

rows.name: Former Enze Hospital
rows.summary: Three two-storey Western-style buildings joined by covered bridges on the slope of Beigu Mountain in Linhai, the remains of the first Western-medicine hospital in Taizhou, opened by the British Anglican mission in 1901. In 1942 its doctors treated injured crewmen of a B-25 bomber from the Doolittle Raid that had come down off the Sanmen coast, including pilot Ted Lawson, whose leg was amputated here, before they were escorted west; Lawson told the story in his memoir Thirty Seconds over Tokyo. Restored by Taizhou Hospital, the buildings now house its history museum, with exhibitions on the hospital's founding and the rescue of the American airmen.

rows.name: Guoqing Temple
rows.summary: The temple at the southern foot of Tiantai Mountain where the Tiantai school of Buddhism began, founded in 598 under the Sui dynasty in fulfilment of the last wish of the school's founder Zhiyi and rebuilt under the Yongzheng Emperor in the 1730s. The Japanese monk Saichō studied here in 804–805 before founding the Tendai school, and the temple is still honoured as an ancestral seat of Tendai, with memorial steles set up by Japanese Buddhists. Its halls hold a 13-tonne Ming bronze Shakyamuni and Yuan-dynasty nanmu figures of the eighteen arhats, and outside the gate stands the hollow, roofless Sui Pagoda, one of the oldest brick pagodas in China.

rows.name: Hou'an Village
rows.summary: A village of farm-stay guesthouses in Jietou town, western Tiantai, beside the Shifeng stream below a long wall of cliffs known as the 'Ten-li Iron-Armoured Dragon'. Villagers quarried stone slabs here until the quarries were shut in 2008 because of the dust that had made many workers ill; the village then turned to rural tourism, with dozens of family guesthouses and restaurants and seasonal events such as peach-picking and lotus festivals. The Tang poet-recluse Hanshan is said to have lived for decades in the Hanyan cave in front of the village.

rows.name: Huangyan Museum
rows.summary: The district museum of Huangyan, founded in 1984, with more than 8,000 objects ranging from Western Zhou proto-celadon and Tang and Song celadon to Buddhist relics of the Song dynasty. Its best-known holding is the silk clothing excavated from the Southern Song tomb of Zhao Boyun, hailed in China as 'the crown of Song dress'.

rows.name: Jiangxia Tidal Power Station
rows.summary: China's first two-way tidal power station, built across the Jiangxia inlet at the northern end of Yueqing Bay, where the tidal range reaches 8.39 m; its first turbine began generating in May 1980 and the plant now has about 4.1 MW installed. A rock-fill barrage 670 m long holds back the tide, with a sluice, powerhouse and substation beside it, and the whole complex was listed as a national heritage site in 2019. It is a working plant, seen from outside: a local road crosses the barrage beside the sluices and powerhouse.

rows.name: Jinqing Great Bridge
rows.summary: A five-arch stone bridge 64 m long over the Jinqing waterway below Piyun Hill in Xinhe town, built in the early Jiaqing reign (around 1800) when an older flat bridge was rebuilt with arches. Its stepped deck rises between small platforms set with carved roundels of lotus, waterbirds, flowers and birds, the balustrades carry 28 posts on each side topped with lotus and lion carvings, and a square pavilion stands at each end. A modern road bridge built nearby in 1986 took over its traffic.

rows.name: Jinshan Pagodas, Linhai
rows.summary: A group of old brick pagodas on and around Jinshan, the small twin-peaked hill in the south-east corner of Linhai's walled town, long the landmark of the former prefectural city. The tallest is the Qianfo ('Thousand Buddha') Pagoda in Longxing Temple at the western foot of the hill, a seven-storey hexagonal pagoda of 1299 about 28.7 m high whose upper storeys are faced with moulded Buddha-image bricks. The protected group also includes the Great East Pagoda on the eastern summit, rebuilt in 1865, and the Nanshandian Pagoda on the south-west slope, while Longxing Temple itself is honoured as one of the sources of Japanese Tendai Buddhism.

rows.name: Jiufeng Park
rows.summary: A wooded hillside park on the eastern edge of Huangyan, named after the nine peaks that enclose its valley, opened in 1959 on the site of a Song-era monastery and a Qing academy and now covering about 106 hectares. Its oldest monument is the Ruilong Ganying Pagoda, a seven-storey, octagonal brick-and-timber pagoda 35.2 m tall from the 10th century, and paths lead on past springs, pools, waterfalls and pavilions towards the peaks. Local people come to walk and to fill bottles with spring water.

rows.name: Kanmen Tide Station
rows.summary: The first tide-gauge station in China to be sited, designed and built by Chinese surveyors, set up in 1929–1930 in a rocky cove at Kanmen on the south-east coast of Yuhuan and still recording tides today. Its readings fixed the 'Kanmen zero' datum, from which heights in Zhejiang and many other provinces were measured from 1936. The historic features are small: the tide well of 1932 in a natural gully with its hut above, the three-walled Huilan sluice that calms the inflow, and a benchmark carved into the bedrock.

rows.name: Lin Yingqi Memorial Arch
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty memorial archway (paifang) in Fuying subdistrict north-east of Xianju town, honouring Lin Yingqi (1506–1583), a native of the area who passed the imperial jinshi examination in 1535 and served as a county magistrate and prefectural official. Known locally as the Panlong Fufeng arch, it became a provincial protected monument in 2017 and a national one in 2019.

rows.name: Linghu Lake Park
rows.summary: A lake park in Linhai's newer eastern district, about 5 km east of the walled old town, laid out around a broad lake with an island, willow-lined causeways and waterside paths. It is a city park used by residents for walking and cycling rather than a sight in its own right, and suits a relaxed stroll after visiting the old town.

rows.name: Nanfeng Pagoda
rows.summary: A hexagonal, seven-storey brick pagoda 23.8 m tall on Nanfeng Hill on the south side of Xianju town, built in 1032–1033 under the Northern Song and repaired in the Ming dynasty. Its brickwork imitates timber construction, with balconies, eaves and bracket sets on every storey, and the hollow core has footholds cut into the inner walls for climbing. The protected unit also includes the Song-dynasty Fuyinshan Pagoda elsewhere in the county.

rows.name: Qi Jiguang Memorial Temple, Jiaojiang
rows.summary: A temple complex in Jiaojiang's old quarter, the former Haimen garrison town, that combines the garrison's City God temple with a shrine to the Ming general Qi Jiguang, who was stationed here in the mid-16th century to fight the wokou pirates. First built in the early Ming and rebuilt in the late Qing, it is laid out along an axis of screen wall, bridge, front hall, opera stage, pond, viewing pavilion and main hall. Since 1987 it has housed the Qi Jiguang Memorial Hall with an exhibition on his campaigns against the pirates.

rows.name: Rouchuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area in Yutou township in the forested hills of western Huangyan (Rouchuan is the township's old name), following the Rouji stream, a tributary of the Yongning River, for about 20 km through the valleys. Along it are old bridges, temples and the Shatan old street, whose buildings include the township offices and clinic of the 1980s, together with campsites and pick-your-own orchards.

rows.name: Shenxian Oxygen Bar Town
rows.summary: A tourism district of about 3.8 km² spanning 20 villages in Baita town, at the approach to Shenxianju, developed as one of Zhejiang's provincial 'characteristic towns' around the area's clean mountain air and its closeness to the 5A scenic area. Its villages, set among fields and streams, are lined with homestays and hotels. It works mainly as a base for visiting Shenxianju rather than as a sight in itself.

rows.name: Shenxianju
rows.summary: A 5A mountain scenic area in western Xianju county and the core of Xianju National Park, known for sheer cliffs, rock pillars and peaks of volcanic rhyolite that are often wrapped in cloud. Cable cars and escalators lift visitors to a cliff-hugging walkway, glass-floored viewing platforms and the Ruyi Bridge, a curving steel-and-glass footbridge opened in 2020 about 140 m above a valley. The area also hosts international high-altitude slackline events.

rows.name: Shepan Island
rows.summary: An island in Sanmen Bay, joined to the mainland on its Ninghai side by land reclamation in 2008, known as the 'Island of a Thousand Caves' for the roughly 1,300 caverns left by quarrying its red Shepan stone from the Song dynasty onwards. At Gaolou Rock two linked caverns together reach the size of two basketball courts, with clear pools about 10 m deep, and Huangnidong village keeps 55 houses built of the local stone. The island also has shrimp ponds and seafood restaurants.

rows.name: Taizhou Ocean World
rows.summary: An aquarium beside Taizhou Civic Square in Jiaojiang, opened in 2005 in a five-storey building that is toured from the top floor downwards. Its galleries cover a tropical rainforest, coral-reef life and an underwater tunnel, alongside some amusement facilities, and it is aimed mainly at families with children.

rows.name: Taozhu Fortress Town
rows.summary: A Ming coastal fort town near the East China Sea in south-east Linhai, built in 1443 as one of the garrison posts raised against wokou pirates; Qi Jiguang wiped out a pirate band here in 1560. Its walls, about 1.4 km round and 4.5 m high, survive with three gates and their barbicans, and inside the lanes keep mostly Qing-dynasty houses, an ancestral hall and a Guandi temple in a town that is still lived in and busy on market days. Nearby, the rice fields of Taojiang Shisanzhu, cut into islets by the river, and the volcanic rock landscape of the Linhai geopark make a pleasant side trip.

rows.name: Tiantai Mountain
rows.summary: The forested granite range north of Tiantai town that gave its name to the Tiantai school of Buddhism, a 5A scenic area whose two main parts are Guoqing Temple at its foot (separate card) and the Shiliang area high on the mountain. At Shiliang two streams meet and plunge more than 30 m in three cascades beneath a natural stone beam about 7 m long, with the Middle and Lower Fangguang temples beside it and rock inscriptions from the Song onwards, including one attributed to Mi Fu. Huading, the main peak, has a national forest park, the Huading temple founded in 936, tea gardens and old cloud-brocade azaleas that flower in May.

rows.name: Tiantai Mountain Great Waterfall and Qiongtai Valley
rows.name_zh: 天台山大瀑布（琼台仙谷）
rows.summary: A scenic area on the western slope of Tongbai Mountain, about 7 km north-west of Tiantai town, that joins the Tiantai Mountain Great Waterfall to Qiongtai Valley, a gorge of oddly shaped cliffs and rocks with plank walkways. According to the Taizhou government the waterfall drops 325 m in a long series of tiers and is up to 90 m wide; it can be viewed from a path of about 2.5 km along the top or from sightseeing lifts. The Taoist Tongbai Palace, regarded as the ancestral temple of the Southern school of Taoism, is close by.

rows.name: Walled City of Taizhou Fu
rows.summary: Linhai's old walled town, seat of Taizhou prefecture from 591 until 1993, is now a 5A scenic area of 3.12 km² taking in the city wall, Ziyang Street, East Lake and Jinshan Hill. The wall follows the Ling River and climbs the ridge of Beigu Mountain; the Ming general Qi Jiguang raised it and added two-storey hollow watchtowers against pirate raids, and its river-facing bastions were given rounded fronts to withstand floods. Inside, the 1,080 m flagstone Ziyang Street is lined with old shops, small museums and craft workshops, and about 28,000 people still live in the old town.

rows.name: Xianju Ancient Yue Rock Carvings
rows.summary: Rock carvings attributed to the ancient Yue people of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, found at seven sites in the hills of Xianju county, with more than 220 motifs over about 1,400 m² of rock. The carved designs include snakes, birds, bird-headed fish, horses, suns, human figures, knives, rakes and grid patterns, with snake and rake shapes at almost every site. This card is placed at the Songlong Hill site west of Zhaojiayang village in Fuying, the nearest to the county town; others lie at Zhongyangkeng in Guangdu and Xitang in Shangzhang.

rows.name: Xinhe Lock Bridges
rows.summary: Four old stone sluice-bridges on the canals around Xinhe town in eastern Wenling, the Zhongzha, Maci, Beizha and Xialu sluices, which served both as river crossings and as water gates. Each has two or three spans of stone beams resting on corbelled piers with cutwaters, and the plain Maci sluice is thought to survive from the Song or Yuan, the others from the Ming and Qing.

rows.name: Xuanmen Bay Agricultural Sightseeing Park
rows.summary: A large agri-tourism park of nearly 10,000 mu (about 670 hectares) on the western edge of Qinggang town, Yuhuan, beside the Xuanmen Bay wetland and looking across Yueqing Bay to the Yandang mountains. It is divided into orchards, including a garden of pomelo varieties, a farming-culture area, a water garden, fishing ponds, a bird garden and a fishing-village area. It suits families and anyone curious about local fruit such as the Yuhuan pomelo.

rows.name: Xuanmen Bay National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park of 31.48 km² in northern Yuhuan, where Yuhuan island meets the Chumen peninsula, made up of tidal flats, open water, freshwater marsh, islets and wooded hills. A stopover on the East Asian–Australasian Flyway, it had recorded 320 bird species by September 2026, among them black-faced spoonbills, spoon-billed sandpipers and wintering Saunders's gulls, and it was named a provincial bird-watching site in 2023. Visitors can take boats on the lake, ride a small sightseeing train and visit the wetland science centre, and the Xuanmen Bay agricultural park lies next door.

rows.name: Yijiangshan Islands Battle Site
rows.summary: Two small, steep islands about 30 km off Jiaojiang where the People's Liberation Army took the islands from Republic of China forces on 18 January 1955, its first combined operation of land, sea and air forces; the loss led the ROC to evacuate the nearby Dachen Islands the following month. More than 150 bunkers, gun positions, trenches, barracks and landing stages survive along some 8 km of trenches, and a visitor centre with a battle history exhibition, a memorial and a weapons display were added between 2008 and 2015. The protected unit also includes the battle's memorial tower on the mainland in Jiaojiang.

rows.name: Yong'an River Greenway
rows.summary: A riverside route for cycling and walking along the Yong'an River, the 'mother river' of Xianju, which crosses the county's farmland basin from west to east. Along the river visitors can cycle the banks or take bamboo-raft trips, including a rafting stretch of about 5 km near the county town, with views of fields, woods and the hills framing the valley.

rows.name: Bagua and Hexi Bridges
rows.summary: Two Southern Song stone beam bridges in Taoshan town, western Rui'an. Bagua Bridge in Taofeng village, built in the Chunxi reign (1174–89), crosses the Tao stream on five spans 25.4 m long, its polished deck slabs carved with patterns to stop slipping; Hexi Bridge, at the western end of Huayuandi village, is a similar five-span bridge 24.5 m long.

rows.name: Bao Ancestral Hall, Yuyan
rows.summary: A large clan hall of the Bao family on a hillside in Yuyan village, Sixi town, founded in the Chenghua reign (1465–87) and rebuilt in 1847. Laid out on an axis that climbs the slope, it has an archway, outer gate, half-moon pond, gate hall, front hall, main hall and sacrificial hall over about 3,400 m², and it is part of the Sixi covered-bridge culture park.

rows.name: Caowanshan Site Museum
rows.summary: A Neolithic hilltop settlement on Caowan Hill in Tengqiao town, more than 4,000 years old and belonging to the Haochuan culture, with a living area of stone footings and a cemetery of 35 graves. A site museum opened for trial visits in early 2025, showing replicas of the finds, such as a jade-inlaid handle and a pottery steamer, with interactive displays on the area's early farmers.

rows.name: Chixi Five-Span Bridge
rows.summary: A five-span stone beam bridge, 24.6 m long and only 1.7 m wide, crossing the stream at Guoxi village in Chixi town. When it was first built is unknown; the present bridge dates from a rebuilding in 1267, late in the Southern Song.

rows.name: East Pagoda, Yueqing
rows.summary: A seven-storey hexagonal brick pagoda about 18 m tall on Donggao Hill in Yuecheng, central Yueqing, moved here in the Xining reign (1068–77) after lightning destroyed an earlier tower, with further building in the 1170s. Its eaves are corbelled out in brick over bracket sets, many of its bricks carry donors' inscriptions, and the hill around it is now Dongta Park.

rows.name: Fanshan Alum Mine
rows.summary: The old alum works of Fanshan, a town long known for producing potash and soda alum; the listed remains date from the Qing dynasty to 1994. On the north slope of Jilong Hill at Fudewan village survive five calcining furnaces, a tall water-boiling furnace and workshops, together with miners' stone houses, an old street of hillside homes from the late Qing and early Republic, and temples; Fudewan is now a listed historic village with craft workshops and guesthouses.

rows.name: Five Buddha Pagodas of Qizhen Temple
rows.summary: A row of small hexagonal Song-dynasty stone pagodas from Qizhen Temple in Luoyang village near Aojiang, carved to imitate timber buildings with single eaves. Five were made and four survive, all without their finials; they first stood before the temple's release pond and were later moved and reassembled on their present site.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Red 13th Army
rows.summary: The Hu family ancestral hall of 1728 in Wuxia village, Wuchi township, northern Yongjia, where southern Zhejiang Red Army guerrillas set up the headquarters of the 13th Army of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army, which stayed from May 1930 to autumn 1932. The timber courtyard hall is preserved, with a newer museum on the army's history beside it and a memorial monument on the slope opposite.

rows.name: Former Liji Medical School
rows.summary: The former Liji Medical School in central Rui'an, founded in 1885 by the reformers Chen Qiu, Chen Jieshi and Chen Baoshan as a new-style school of Chinese medicine run on Western educational lines, which trained some 300 doctors and published its own journal from 1896. The courtyard complex pairs a Western-style five-bay main building with Chinese timber wings and a herb garden, and now houses the Liji Medical School Museum.

rows.name: Furong Village
rows.summary: A Chen clan village in Yantou town on the middle Nanxi River, said to have been founded at the end of the Tang dynasty and laid out to a 'seven stars and eight dippers' plan, with lamp platforms as the stars and wells as the dippers. Nearly 50 old buildings survive within the village wall and gates, including the Chen ancestral hall, Furong Academy, Furong Pavilion and large houses such as the Sima Residence.

rows.name: Hu Family Compound, Xuexi
rows.summary: A walled family mansion in Xuexi township, Taishun, built over some 40 years from 1832 to 1874 by Hu Dongwei, whose forebears had moved here from Qingyuan in the Ming dynasty. Behind a stone gateway, the front, lower and upper halls line a central axis, with finely carved beams, brackets and corbels showing dragons, phoenixes, flowers and figures.

rows.name: Hufa Temple Bridge and Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song stone bridge and a small brick pagoda beside it in Hufasi village, Wangli town. The three-span beam bridge, 10.3 m long, carries an inscription dating it to 1088, while the 4.2 m pagoda, with carved water-and-cloud patterns and a two-tier pedestal, is said to be the last of nine that stood before the temple.

rows.name: Impression Nantang
rows.summary: A riverside leisure and shopping district in central Wenzhou along the Nantang River, combining Nantang Street, lined with restaurants and shops, with Bailuzhou Park, a culture village and waterside gardens. It is busiest in the evening, with a night market, a light show in Bailuzhou Park and lit-up river views, and suits a relaxed walk and dinner.

rows.name: Jiangxin Islet
rows.summary: A long islet in the Ou River opposite central Wenzhou and long the city's emblem, with Jiangxin Temple, founded in 1137 when monks filled the channel between two islets, the East and West Pagodas, a shrine to the Song loyalist Wen Tianxiang, and buildings recalling the poets Xie Lingyun and Meng Haoran. At the foot of the East Pagoda stands the former British Consulate, a verandahed three-storey building of 1894 from the treaty-port era, which now houses a museum on Wenzhou's opening as a port. Gardens and lakes fill the rest of the island.

rows.name: Jinzhao and Xiantai Archways
rows.summary: Two Ming timber memorial archways in the Nanxi valley. The Jinzhao Arch in Shangcun village by Yantou, a six-post gateway with three roofs, 7.63 m tall, was raised in 1565 when Jin Zhao passed the highest imperial examination; the Xiantai Arch in Huatan village, Shatou, about 12 km to the south-east, is a four-post arch of 1505 built by the Wenzhou prefect and the Yongjia county magistrate in memory of Zhu Liangyi, a native of Huatan.

rows.name: Liu Bowen's Hometown (Baizhangji Falls and Liu Ji Temple)
rows.summary: Wencheng County's 5A scenic area, named for the home region of Liu Ji (Liu Bowen), the strategist who helped found the Ming dynasty, combines two sites about 10 km apart. Baizhangji is a three-tier waterfall in a deep V-shaped ravine whose top fall drops 207 m in a single leap; in Nantian to the north-west, the Liu Ji Temple is a Ming timber hall complex of the Tianshun reign (1457–64) hung with commemorative plaques, and Liu Ji's tomb lies at the foot of Xiashan nearby.

rows.name: Middle Yandang Mountain
rows.summary: A national scenic area in the hills south-west of Yueqing, described as the 'toe' of the Yandang range and centred on Yuzeng Peak, a pale rock dome named for its resemblance to an ancient steamer pot. Trails link the peak with three lakes, Baishi, Zhongqian and Longshan, and with the waterfalls of the Xiji gorge, amid farmland villages. It is a separate area from the main Yandang Mountains 5A scenic area about 35 km to the north-east.

rows.name: Nange Archways
rows.summary: Five Ming-dynasty archways standing along the pebble-paved lane of Nange village, Xianxi town, raised between 1439 and 1544 to mark the examination honours and official ranks of the local Zhang clan. Each is about 8 m high, with square stone main posts, round timber side posts, dragon-head ridge ornaments and large red name boards with gilded characters.

rows.name: Nanji Islands
rows.summary: An archipelago of 52 islands in the East China Sea off Pingyang, protected since 1990 as one of China's first national marine nature reserves and part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves since 1998, known for the variety of its shellfish and seaweeds. The main island, Nanji, has the Dasha'ao beach, sea-eroded headlands at Sanpanwei and cliff inscriptions at Guoxing'ao, a cove named after Koxinga, who used the island as a base in the 17th century.

rows.name: Nanxi River Ancestral Halls
rows.summary: A protected group of Ming and Qing clan halls spread across villages of the Nanxi River valley in Yongjia. One of them, the Yongjia Commandery Hall in Shangcun, Bilian town, began as the Liu clan hall of the forebears of the Ming statesman Liu Ji and has an imperial-edict pavilion, gatehouse, opera stage, galleries and main hall arranged around courtyards. The others include Xiaosi Hall at Shatou and the main halls of the Zheng, Xie, Ye, Shao, Ji and Chen clans in other villages.

rows.name: Nanxi River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national scenic area along the Nanxi River, a clear, shallow tributary of the Ou that winds south through Yongjia County in 36 bends and 72 shoals, with pebble beaches, volcanic cliffs, waterfalls and the old clan villages of its middle reaches. Its eight sections include Daruoyan, where Taogong Cave, a huge natural cavern, was the retreat of the Daoist scholar Tao Hongjing. The river is on China's tentative list for World Heritage and forms the western part of the Yandangshan Global Geopark.

rows.name: Pagoda of Guo'an Temple
rows.summary: A solid stone pagoda built in 1090–1093 at Huang'ao in Yaoxi, Longwan District, nine storeys high on a hexagonal plan and shaped like a timber pavilion tower. Its top has been lost, and about 17 m of the tower survives.

rows.name: Puzhuang Fortress
rows.summary: A Ming coastal fortress near the Zhejiang–Fujian border, begun in 1384 against Japanese pirate raids and still a lived-in walled town, now called Pucheng. Its stone-faced walls, curved on the hill side and straight towards the sea, have three gates with square barbicans, and the street plan inside is unchanged since the Ming, with the City God temple, a Mazu temple and Ming-era houses. The national listing also covers the smaller Baiwan fort at Chixi and the Zhuangshi fort.

rows.name: Sanyang Wetland
rows.summary: A large wetland park on the south-eastern edge of central Wenzhou, where a dense grid of rivers breaks the land into 161 small islets, traditionally farmed with orchards of Ougan, the local citrus.
