Paths and bridges link gardens, a banyan grove, a bird island, the Wufuyuan area and the Nan Huaijin Academy, and 142 bird species have been recorded here. It was rated 4A in December 2023 and is an easy half-day outing from the city.

rows.name: Shengjingshan Stone Halls
rows.summary: A complex of stone-built temple halls on Shengjing Mountain in Mayu town, Rui'an, described as the oldest and largest of its kind in southern Zhejiang: it was founded in 1260, and the present halls date from the Wanli reign (1573–1620) to the late Qing. Inside is the 'holy well' that gives the mountain its name, a shallow spring said never to dry up or overflow, and the Baochang and Tongji temples stand nearby.

rows.name: Shishui Stepping Stones
rows.summary: A stepping-stone crossing of 1795, rebuilt in 1820, across the river at Xidong village in Shiyang town, southern Taishun: 233 stones over 144 m, each step having a higher block of white granite and a lower one of bluestone so that two people can pass. Seen from a distance the line of stones looks like a keyboard, which gives it the local name 'piano bridge'.

rows.name: Shunxi Old Mansions
rows.summary: Shunxi town, deep in the hills of the South Yandang area in western Pingyang, keeps the Chen clan ancestral hall and ten large Chen family mansions, most built in the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns (1736–1820). The large timber courtyard houses were built for branches of one clan living side by side, and their layout reflects traditional ideas of lineage and fengshui.

rows.name: South Yandang Mountain
rows.summary: A national scenic area in western Pingyang with five sections of rocky peaks, caves, clear streams and waterfalls, long paired with the northern Yandang Mountains. The core Dongxidong section packs Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist temples among its cliffs and caves, and rows of Ming and Qing houses survive in the villages; the Shunxi section to the west holds the Chen family mansions.

rows.name: Stone Pagoda of Guanyin Temple, Rui'an
rows.summary: A hexagonal stone pagoda of 1068, originally called the Thousand Buddha Pagoda, at the southern foot of Wansong Hill in Zhouhu village, Longshan, on the eastern edge of central Rui'an. Carved in the form of a timber pavilion-style tower, it once had seven storeys, of which six survive to a height of 7.8 m.

rows.name: Stone Pagodas of Zhenru Temple
rows.summary: Four hexagonal stone pagodas in front of Zhenru Temple in Chongshi village, Panshi town, the survivors of seven that once stood here; only one is complete, the other three having lost their tops. The temple was founded in 888 and rebuilt in 1298, and the pagodas belong to that Yuan-dynasty rebuilding.

rows.name: Su Buqing's Hometown, Tengjiao
rows.summary: A cultural tourism area in Tengjiao town, Pingyang, built around the hometown of the mathematician Su Buqing (1902–2003), a founder of differential geometry in China and later president of Fudan University. It takes in his late-Qing timber family house, a museum on his life, a hands-on mathematics hall and maths park, the old Tingzi street and a stele garden honouring Chinese chess champions, as Tengjiao is known for the game. It was rated 4A in December 2023.

rows.name: Taishun Covered Bridge Culture Park (Xidong and Beijian Bridges)
rows.summary: A heritage park in Sixi town built around Xidong Bridge (1745) and Beijian Bridge (1803), two timber covered bridges with woven-beam arches that stand close together over the streams of Xiaqiao village. The park also takes in old buildings such as Zhang Shiyi's former residence and the Bao ancestral hall, and showcases Taishun's puppet theatre. The two bridges head the national listing of 15 Taishun covered bridges scattered across the county; three of them were swept away by floods in 2016 and rebuilt in 2017, reusing as much of their original timber as possible.

rows.name: Taishun Tulou
rows.summary: Six fortified earth buildings in Taishun County, built in the Fujian earth-building tradition between the Qing dynasty and the Republic. The listed buildings include Shangjiaoyang Tulou near Luoyang, a square two-storey block of rammed earth on a stone base, with timber rooms around a central courtyard and a defensive ditch, built in the late Qing by the Zeng clan, who came from the Quanzhou area of Fujian; around it the village's semicircular 'water-castle' houses ring the clan temple.

rows.name: Tieding Liuliu Park
rows.summary: A rural theme park near Dajing in northern Yueqing, built around the growing of tiepi shihu (Dendrobium officinale), a medicinal orchid long associated with the Yandang area. It has three parts: a slide park with many indoor and outdoor slides, including a 1,620 m rail slide and a 61.8 m slide tower, a dendrobium culture park and a farming park. It suits families combining it with a visit to the Yandang Mountains.

rows.name: Tongling Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in western Wencheng, with forest over about 98% of its area and rare wildlife such as Cabot's tragopan. Its best-known sight is Tongling Gorge, an S-shaped ravine of about 500 m where swirling water has drilled deep potholes into the rock; the park also has Xiaoyaochi, a pool at about 1,000 m near a sunrise viewpoint, and Tonglingzhai, a cliff-top stronghold of a late-Yuan rebel leader. A pavilion built in 1997 commemorates Red Army soldiers killed in an ambush here in 1936.

rows.name: Wanyao Ancient Village
rows.summary: An old pottery village in a wooded valley above Yulong Lake in Qiaodun, founded in the early Ming, which preserves its old hand-worked bowl kilns and workshops. Old houses in early Qing style, with more than 300 rooms in all, climb the hillside, with an old temple, an opera stage, water-powered mills and a few stilt houses, and a three-tier waterfall drops into deep pools nearby. It was among the first villages named Chinese Traditional Villages in 2012.

rows.name: Wencheng Forest Oxygen Town
rows.summary: A mountain resort area in western Wencheng, where Wencheng, Jingning and Taishun counties meet, made up of the Tianshengshan area in Xikeng She Ethnic Town and the Tonglingshan town area, with core areas above 1,000 m and forest covering about 96% of the land. Its facilities have included Swan Castle (Tian'ebao), an indoor ski hall, and Anfu Temple, a Buddhist temple of the Medicine Buddha, and the Tongling Mountain and Longqiyuan scenic areas lie within its bounds. It was rated 4A in 2018.

rows.name: Wenzhou Amusement Park
rows.summary: Wenzhou's first theme park, open for about two decades in Chashan south of the city, with a European-style zone, a cartoon zone, an adventure valley and a dinosaur zone, plus rides such as a suspended roller coaster added in 2008. The Wenzhou Polar Ocean World aquarium next door opened in 2019, and a third phase opened in May 2025 with a circus arena staging acrobatics and horseback acts and a mermaid-themed family hotel. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Wuyanling National Nature Reserve
rows.summary: A national nature reserve of 18,861.5 ha in north-western Taishun, set up mainly to protect Cabot's tragopan, a pheasant found only in China, and one of the best-preserved subtropical evergreen broadleaf forests in eastern China. Only a small part is open to visitors: trails follow two streams past waterfalls and pools such as Baiyun Falls and Longjing Pool, and a paved path climbs to Baiyunjian (1,611 m), the highest peak in Wenzhou.

rows.name: Xiandieyan and Banping Island
rows.summary: Two coastal sights in the Dongtou islands off the mouth of the Ou River. Banping ('half-screen') Island has a sheer east-facing sea cliff about 1.2 km long and 120 m high, said in local legend to be one half of a mountain whose other half lies in Taiwan, and a sandy beach at Dashalong on its north-west side; Xiandieyan, south-east of the Dongtou district centre, is a headland of stacked, wave-worn rocks. The cliffs show different shapes when seen from boats circling the island.

rows.name: Yandang Mountains
rows.summary: The main area of the North Yandang range in Yueqing, a 5A scenic area and Global Geopark of about 450 km², formed by volcanic eruptions more than 100 million years ago and eroded into cliffs, pinnacles, caves and waterfalls. Its 'three wonders' are the rock silhouettes of Lingfeng by night, the rope-crossing act between the cliffs at Lingyan and the Dalongqiu waterfall, and Lingyan also has Lingyan Temple and the Xiaolongqiu falls. Inside Longbi (Dragon's Nose) Cave in the Lingyan area, 94 cliff inscriptions from the Tang dynasty to modern times include one by the Song scholar Shen Kuo.

rows.name: Yongchang Fort
rows.summary: A fortified village built in 1558 by the local Wang family against Japanese pirates, after two of their kinsmen were killed fighting the raiders, and described as the only surviving privately built walled town in Zhejiang. The rectangular fort keeps its north wall, most of the east wall and the east gate with its barbican and gun gallery, and a moat and two canals run through a village of old houses that includes the Wang ancestral hall.

rows.name: Yucang Mountain
rows.summary: A granite mountain north-west of Cangnan's county town, rising to 921.5 m and protected as a national forest park since 1991. It is known for its 'stone sea' of rounded boulders in odd shapes, its sunrises and seas of cloud, and a handful of small upland lakes, and Fayun Temple, founded in the 1260s and rebuilt in 1983, stands at about 770 m.

rows.name: Yuhai Library
rows.summary: A private library built in 1888 by the late-Qing scholar Sun Yirang and his father Sun Yiyan, counted among Zhejiang's four great private libraries and named after the Song scholar Wang Yinglin's encyclopedia Yuhai. The complex of about 8,000 m² joins the two-storey timber library, ringed by water on three sides, with the Baijin Taozhai and Sun Yirang's former residence; its surviving rare books have been moved to the Rui'an Museum for safekeeping.

rows.name: Yuliao Beach
rows.summary: A coastal scenic area near the southern end of Zhejiang's coast in Cangnan, centred on Yuliao beach, a broad sandy bay about 2 km long, with a smaller crescent beach at Wuchengao. Rock formations along the shore, such as the 'music stone' that rings when struck, and offshore islets frame the bay, which is used for sea bathing in summer.

rows.name: Zeya Scenic Area and Siliandui Paper Mills
rows.summary: A large mountain scenic area west of Wenzhou, nicknamed the 'West Yandang', with eight sections of waterfalls, pools and gorges such as the Qipujian (Seven Waterfalls) ravine and Jinkeng Gorge. Zeya was long a 'paper mountain' of bamboo-paper makers, and at Siliandui four water-powered trip-hammer mills, first built in the early Ming, stand along a 230 m channel on the Longxi stream as a protected relic of traditional papermaking. The first section opened to visitors in 1990 as the papermaking trade declined.

rows.name: Fayu Temple
rows.summary: The 'rear temple' and second-largest of Mount Putuo's three great temples, founded in 1580 as the Haichao Hermitage and renamed after the Kangxi Emperor granted the plaque 'Tianhua Fayu' ('heavenly flowers, Dharma rain') in 1699. Its halls climb the hillside below Foding Shan in six tiers, and the Guanyin Hall, also called the Nine Dragon Hall, is the most richly decorated.

rows.name: Huaniao Island & Lighthouse
rows.summary: The northernmost island of the Zhoushan archipelago, a small island whose blue-and-white painted village houses have earned it the nickname 'Santorini of the East', with clear-water bays, a sandy beach at South Bay and seasonal 'blue tears' of glowing plankton along the shore. On its north-western headland stands Huaniao Lighthouse, designed by the Scottish engineer David Marr Henderson and completed in 1870 to guide ships between the Yangtze mouth and the Pacific: a 16.5 m white-and-black tower with a copper dome, radio masts, service buildings and a fog signal, still in service. Visitor numbers on the island are capped each day.

rows.name: Nandong Art Valley
rows.summary: A village in a small valley ringed by hills in Xinjian, Ganlan town, in the north of Zhoushan Island, once poor and remote and since redeveloped for rural tourism with an arts theme. Visitors come for its rural scenery, homestays and an old green steam train kept as a photo spot, and it is a stop on a national boutique rural tourism route together with the Ma'ao Museum.

rows.name: Nansha Beach, Zhujiajian
rows.summary: Nansha is one of the five linked sandy beaches, about 6 km in all, that line the east coast of Zhujiajian Island, just south of Mount Putuo across a narrow strait. It is the venue of the Zhoushan International Sand Sculpture Festival, held on the beach each year since around 2000; outside festival time it is an open sandy beach, and the island's coast is also popular for surfing.

rows.name: Puji Temple
rows.summary: The 'front temple' and principal Guanyin shrine of Mount Putuo, which grew out of the shrine founded for a Guanyin image that the Japanese monk Egaku left on the island, and took its present name from a plaque given by the Kangxi Emperor. Its halls, largely rebuilt in 1731–34, cover about 37,000 m², and the main Yuantong Hall holds a Vairocana Guanyin surrounded by the bodhisattva's 32 manifestations. Beside it stands the Duobao Pagoda, a three-tier stone pagoda paid for by a Yuan prince in 1333–34 and the oldest surviving structure on the island.

rows.name: Shengsi Five Fishing Villages
rows.summary: A string of five fishing villages in Wulong township on the east side of Sijiao, the main island of the Shengsi archipelago: Tian'ao, Huangsha, Bianjiao'ao, Huicheng and Shiwuzhi'ao. Bianjiao'ao's houses were painted in bright colours by teachers and students of the China Academy of Art, Huangsha has a village art museum and history hall, and fishermen's paintings, sea-view homestays and seafood are found throughout. It suits a slow day or two of island village life.

rows.name: Shenjiamen Fishing Port Town
rows.summary: Shenjiamen, on the south-east shore of Zhoushan Island, grew up around one of China's largest fishing harbours, sheltered by Lujiazhi Island and long the centre of the Zhoushan fishery. The 4A area takes in the harbour waterfront and the Zhoushan International Seafood Trade Center, where visitors can learn about the fishing industry and buy fresh seafood, and the seafront is known for its open-air seafood restaurants in the evening.

rows.name: Taohua Island
rows.summary: A hilly island of about 44 km² south of Zhoushan Island, known across the Chinese-speaking world as the Peach Blossom Island of Louis Cha (Jin Yong)'s martial-arts novels, and used as a filming location for television adaptations of them. The scenic area spreads over six sections, among them the Tawan golden sands, Anqi Peak with Shengyan Monastery near the summit, and Taohua Valley, with beaches, rock formations, the seven-storey Jilin Pagoda and a bronze statue of Jin Yong set up in 2001.

rows.name: Baiyun Forest Park, Lishui
rows.summary: A forested hill park right beside the city of Lishui in the Xianxia–Kuocang mountain belt, used by locals for walking and as a green backdrop to the city. It was named one of the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020.

rows.name: Lingjiu Mountain Forest Base, Quzhou
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in Jiuhua township, Kecheng, covering roughly 4,960 hectares of forest by the 2020 listing. The base has four visitor education venues: a forest science hall, a nature-sketching base, a farming-culture garden and an outdoor training camp, and old mountain trails host an annual trail race. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Baimatan Rafting Area
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area in Shuihou town below the western side of Mount Tianzhu, run mainly for rafting. Bamboo-raft and inflatable-boat trips float down the river valley in summer, and a water-splashing rafting festival has been held there in July.

rows.name: Baiya Fortress
rows.summary: A mountain-top stronghold on Baiya Shan in Zhifeng township, first built at the end of the Yuan dynasty and enlarged in the late Ming and late Qing. A stone wall about 4 km round, with five gate towers, encloses surviving buildings such as a Guandi temple and a Kuixing pavilion. In 1932 the Red Army's 27th Army was formed here, and in 2024 the fortress drew new visitors as a model for scenes in the video game Black Myth: Wukong.

rows.name: Dabie Mountains Rainbow Waterfall
rows.summary: A waterfall at Monkey Cliff in Huangwei village, northern Yuexi county, where a stream rising on Baima Peak, the highest summit of the Dabie Mountains, drops nearly 100 metres. Its spray throws up a rainbow on most sunny mornings, which earned the falls a place on China's first national list of weather and climate landscapes; a glass viewing platform faces the falls and boardwalks follow the stream.

rows.name: Duxiu Mountain
rows.summary: A hill in Huangdun town, Huaining county, from which Chen Duxiu, a founder of the Chinese Communist Party, took his pen name. The scenic area is themed on him: a boardwalk circles the hill past four small pavilions with displays on the stages of his life, and outdoor activity grounds are used by school study groups. Family attractions such as a glass water slide, go-karts and lakeside camping have since been added by the Guanyin Cave reservoir at its foot.

rows.name: Duxiu Park and Tomb of Chen Duxiu
rows.summary: A memorial park in the northern outskirts of Anqing built around the tomb of Chen Duxiu, a leader of the New Culture Movement, founder of the magazine New Youth and a founder and early leader of the Chinese Communist Party, who died in 1942. His remains were brought here in 1947, and the grave was rebuilt in 1979 and again from 1998. The park adds a bronze statue, a stone gateway, inscriptions from New Youth and an exhibition hall on his life.

rows.name: Fayun Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty brick pagoda in Qianfota village, Xiangchang town, the main survivor of the Fayun Temple that once stood here. Square in plan and seven storeys high, it has arched openings on each face of the upper storeys and niches with brick-carved Buddha figures, which give it its local name, Qianfo Ta (Thousand-Buddha Pagoda).

rows.name: Feiqi Zhai
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area around the peak of Feiqi Zhai in Lianyun township, west of Yuexi county town in the Dabie Mountains. It is best known for wild azaleas that bloom down its cliffs in spring, one of the sights of Yuexi's annual azalea festival in April and May.

rows.name: Five Thousand Years Culture Park
rows.summary: A modern cultural theme park on the hills at Taihu county town, built to showcase Chinese history and folk art rather than an old site. Its set pieces include a 35-metre statue of Laozi, a 490-metre stone dragon carved with the 47,035 characters of the Kangxi Dictionary, a hillside relief of the Along the River During the Qingming Festival scroll and a hall of more than 27,000 root carvings.

rows.name: Huating Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir in the hills north of Taihu county town, formed by the Hualiangting Dam, which was begun in 1958 and largely completed in 1976; it is now a national scenic area. Boats run out to islands and coves such as Moon Bay, and Xifeng Cave, a cliff-side site with an old temple, has views over the water.

rows.name: Kongcheng Old Street
rows.summary: An old market street in Kongcheng town that grew in the Ming and Qing dynasties as a river port between the Chaohu Lake region and the Yangtze. About 3 km long and paved with granite slabs, it winds in an S-shape past grey-brick shops and houses with upturned eaves, the old Tongxiang Academy and the Ni family mansion, built by a late-Qing prefect who retired here; the central sections were restored and partly rebuilt from 2009.

rows.name: Linghu Park
rows.summary: Linghu (Water Chestnut Lake) and the gardens around it form a large public park in the centre of Anqing, with pavilions, bridges and lawns along the water. The Huangmei Pavilion in the park hosts performances of Huangmei opera, the regional opera closely tied to Anqing.

rows.name: Miaodao Mountain
rows.summary: A national forest park high in the Dabie Mountains of western Yuexi county, at the end of the G318 'Cloud Road' drive that also serves Mingtang Mountain and Tianxia Gorge. It is known for its ancient purple willows, locally said to be a thousand years old, set in deep mountain forest.

rows.name: Mingtang Mountain
rows.summary: A three-peaked mountain of the Dabie range in Hetu town, western Yuexi, whose main summit reaches 1,563 m; legend says it is named after the ritual hall (mingtang) set up here when Emperor Wu of Han honoured nearby Mount Tianzhu. A cable car climbs to the summit area, where a glass walkway, glass bridge and glass viewing platforms ring the main peak, and a long slide runs back down. High-altitude azaleas flower in late April and May, and the Huluhe gorge below has a chain of four waterfalls.

rows.name: Mount Tianzhu
rows.summary: A granite mountain in Qianshan whose main summit, Tianzhu Peak (1,489 m), stands like a pillar above more than 50 lesser peaks; its old name, Wan Shan, gave Anhui its one-character abbreviation. Emperor Wu of Han honoured it as the 'Southern Peak' in 106 BC, and it is now part of a UNESCO Global Geopark. Cable cars and stepped trails lead to the summit area, the 450-metre boulder-cave passage of Shenmi Gu (Mysterious Valley) and the high mountain lake of Liandan Hu.

rows.name: Nanguan Mosque, Anqing
rows.summary: A mosque in the southern part of Anqing's old city, near the Yangtze riverfront, whose Qing-dynasty buildings were listed as a national heritage site in 2013. It is one of a cluster of historic sites in the old city, with the Catholic cathedral, Shitaishi Mansion and Zhenfeng Pagoda all within about 1.5 km.

rows.name: Qingyun Gorge
rows.summary: A river valley in Huangwei town in the Dabie Mountains of northern Yuexi county, developed as a scenic area whose main attraction is summer rafting. It lies about 6 km south of the Dabie Mountains Rainbow Waterfall, so the two can be visited on the same trip.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Anqing
rows.summary: A Catholic church in Anqing's old city, built by French Jesuits between 1866 and 1872, which in 1929 became the cathedral of the new Apostolic Vicariate of Anqing, then run by Spanish Jesuits. Worship stopped in 1957, and the church was repaired and reopened for services in 1983.

rows.name: Shangu Liuquan Cliff Inscriptions
rows.summary: A stream gully at the southern foot of Mount Tianzhu, beside Sanzu Temple, whose boulders and rock walls carry several hundred inscriptions from the Tang dynasty to the Republican era, most of them along a stretch of under 300 metres. They include poems, travel notes and names left by visitors such as Wang Anshi, Su Shi and Huang Tingjian, in every main script style. The gully, also called Shiniu Gudong (Stone Ox Ancient Cave), was landscaped as a culture park in 2009–2010.

rows.name: Shilian Cave National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills on the western edge of Susong county town, named after Shilian (Stone Lotus) Cave. Paths across its four hill areas, Hexi Shan, Fuyu Shan, Yangjiao Jian and Luohan Jian, lead to caves, pools, pavilions and Buddhist temples, among them Lingyin Temple and Dongshan Temple.

rows.name: Shitaishi Mansion
rows.summary: A large brick-and-timber courtyard house in Anqing's old city, begun in the Wanli reign of the Ming as an official's home and rebuilt in the Qing dynasty. Its name, 'Mansion of Generations of Historians', refers to the Zhao family, who bought it in 1864 and produced four successive generations of Hanlin Academy scholars; the Buddhist leader Zhao Puchu was born here. Two parallel lines of halls and courtyards, restored in a three-year project completed in 2003, lead back to a small garden.

rows.name: Tianlong Pass
rows.summary: A narrow, steep-sided gorge in Shuihou village on the western flank of Mount Tianzhu, named for its winding course, likened to a dragon flying up to heaven. It lies beside a pass that in the Ming and Qing was the main way from the Yangtze lowlands into the Dabie Mountains, known locally as the 'First Pass of the Southern Sky'.

rows.name: Tianxia Gorge
rows.summary: A gorge in Hetu town, western Yuexi, on the southern slope of the watershed between the Yangtze and Huai rivers, with nine waterfalls of more than 30 metres along its streams. From late March to May a kilometre-long belt of wild azaleas flowers along a ridge above 600 metres, drawing big spring crowds, and the scenic area has a glass walkway.

rows.name: Tianxian Gorge
rows.summary: A mountain gorge in Tianzhu village, Shuihou town, close to the main Mount Tianzhu scenic area, opened in 2018 as a leisure area of streams, pools and highland village scenery. When it opened its attractions included a 1.6 km glass water slide, a flower valley and fountains.

rows.name: Tianyuewan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring and wellness resort in Yuexi county town, built around a hot-spring park with a cluster of hotels. It also has a sports and culture centre, a traditional Chinese medicine clinic and a branch of the Anhui Provincial Library, and is used by workers' unions in Anhui and Shanghai for rest-and-recuperation stays. It suits a soak after walking in the Dabie Mountains.

rows.name: Tianzhu Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A steep valley on the south-eastern side of Mount Tianzhu, next to the main peak area, where a stream drops more than 200 metres through a chain of waterfalls; the highest, Tongtian Falls, falls about 100 metres. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Tongcheng Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The former county Confucian temple in the centre of Tongcheng, a town famed for the Tongcheng school of Qing-dynasty prose writers. Founded in the Yuan dynasty and moved to this site in the early Ming, it was rebuilt by local gentry in 1864–1866 after war damage that left only the Lingxing Gate standing. Its symmetrical courtyards, with a screen wall, a semicircular pond and bridge and the Dacheng Hall, now house the Tongcheng Museum.

rows.name: Wanguang Garden and Taiping Pagoda
rows.summary: A landscaped museum park in Meicheng, the centre of Qianshan, home to the Qianshan Museum and to memorial exhibitions on the novelist Zhang Henshui and on Cheng Changgeng, one of the founders of Peking opera. Its centrepiece is the Taiping Pagoda, a seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda rebuilt after a fire in 1154 and set inside and out with niches of brick-carved Buddhas.

rows.name: Wulong Creek, Dalong Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded stream valley on the south-eastern side of Dalong Mountain National Forest Park, in the hills just north of Anqing city. About 4 km of looped walking trails run through the forest past the old Yuanzhao Temple, and the scenic area has added a glass bridge and a coloured toboggan slide; the forest farm has held an orange-season festival in autumn.

rows.name: Xizi Lake
rows.summary: A natural lake and wetland scenic area in Xizihu town, south-east Tongcheng, covering about 71 km², more than half of it water. Along with lakeside wetland walks it offers fishing, a resort hotel, a camping ground, boat and jet-ski rides, go-karts and other family amusements. In winter large flocks of migratory birds, including spoonbills and swan geese, gather on the shores.

rows.name: Xuejiagang Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement and cemetery on a narrow mound near where the Qian and Wan rivers meet, south-east of Qianshan city, which gave its name to the Xuejiagang culture of the middle and lower Yangtze. Six excavations since 1979 have uncovered more than a hundred graves and some 3,000 objects, mainly stone tools, pottery and jade. The site is now presented to visitors as an archaeological site park.

rows.name: Yezhai Cemetery of Soldiers Killed in the War of Resistance
rows.name_zh: 野寨抗日阵亡将士公墓
rows.summary: A cemetery and memorial built in 1942–1943 at Yezhai, at the foot of Mount Tianzhu, for 985 soldiers of the Nationalist army's 176th Division killed fighting Japanese forces, paid for by people of 13 counties in Anhui and Hubei. Its communal grave, memorial hall, pavilion and memorial tower stand inside the campus of Yezhai Middle School, which was founded alongside the cemetery as a memorial school. A memorial garden with large reliefs of the division's war was added beside the graves in 2023.

rows.name: Zhenfeng Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda in the grounds of Yingjiang Temple on the Yangtze riverfront in Anqing, built in the late Ming dynasty around 1570. Standing at a bend of the river, it once served as a beacon for boats, and its storeys are set with hundreds of small brick-carved Buddha images. The temple around it is an active Chan (Zen) Buddhist monastery.

rows.name: Bengbu Museum
rows.summary: Bengbu's city museum, a national first-grade museum, which moved in 2015 into a large new building on the west side of Citizens' Square whose design evokes Yu the Great cutting through the mountains to channel the Huai. Its galleries cover the region's prehistory, the history and culture of the Huai River and the city's modern growth. Star pieces include a Neolithic clay human head with facial markings from the Shuangdun site and a Yuan-dynasty blue-and-white jar from the tomb of Tang He.

rows.name: Gaixia Site
rows.summary: An earth-walled settlement on the south bank of the Tuo River, known locally as Bawang Cheng (the Hegemon-King's City); excavations since 2007 have dated its walls to about 4,600 years ago, in the Dawenkou culture, and the county presents it as the oldest walled town found in Anhui. Tradition places here the Battle of Gaixia, where Xiang Yu heard the 'songs of Chu on all four sides' and parted from his consort Yu, and the archaeological park has spots linked to these stories alongside an intangible-heritage centre.

rows.name: Guo River First Bridge, Huaiyuan
rows.summary: A granite stone-arch road bridge across the Guo River at the foot of Gui Shan on the western edge of Huaiyuan town, begun in 1959 and, after a pause in construction, opened to traffic at the end of 1964, when it was the longest bridge on the Bengbu–Fuyang road. Its four main arches of 50 metres made it Anhui's first long-span stone-arch road bridge; it was listed as a national heritage site in 2019 and is best seen from the riverbank or on a walk across.

rows.name: Hequan Farm
rows.summary: A farm-based leisure park on the western outskirts of Bengbu, founded in 2001, that mixes seasonal flower fields and fruit picking with restaurants, a hotel and guesthouses, children's rides and a row of workshops where sesame oil, vinegar and dendrobium liquor are made in front of visitors. It also stages folk performances such as Huagudeng (flower-drum lantern) dance and seasonal events like music festivals and a farmers' market, and suits families looking for a day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Longzi Lake
rows.summary: A long, shallow lake on the eastern side of Bengbu, ringed by low hills and now enclosed by the growing city. Landscaped parks with lawns, wetlands and a long footbridge line both shores, and the scenic area also takes in Cao Shan, with the Bengbu Revolutionary Martyrs' Cemetery and the early-Ming tomb of Tang He.

rows.name: Old Bengbu Huai River Railway Bridge
rows.summary: A steel truss railway bridge across the Huai River at Bengbu, completed in May 1911 for the Tianjin–Pukou Railway; its opening turned Bengbu from a small market town into a railway city. Blown up in 1938 and again in 1949 and repaired each time, it was lengthened in 1987–1988 and still carries the Beijing–Shanghai line, now beside a twin bridge built in 2002. A monument at its southern end remembers six army railway divers who died while the crossing was being restored in 1949–1950.

rows.name: Shuangdun Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement of more than 7,000 years ago in Xiaobengbu town north of the Huai River, type site of the Shuangdun culture, whose pottery bears over 600 incised signs showing animals, plants and daily life. The same park holds two earth mounds over 9 metres high, the 'twin mounds' of its name, one of which was found in 2006–2008 to be the tomb of Bai, ruler of the Spring and Autumn state of Zhongli. Opened as a national archaeological site park in June 2025, it has a museum with finds from both sites and an excavation area under a protective shed.

rows.name: Yuhui Village Site
rows.summary: A Longshan-culture site of 4,400–4,100 years ago at the southern foot of Mount Tu, on the east bank of the Huai River, named after the tradition that Yu the Great gathered the lords at Tushan. Excavations from 2007 uncovered a large raised platform first read as a ritual altar; work in 2020 showed it to be part of the wall of a town of at least 18 hectares, which archaeologists describe as the largest Longshan walled town yet found in the middle Huai valley.

rows.name: Zhanggong Mountain Park
rows.summary: A city park of about 110 hectares in western Bengbu, made up of Zhanggong Shan, a 71-metre hill, and the lake beside it. The seven-storey Wanghuai Pagoda, built on the summit in 1986 and a city landmark, looks out towards the Huai River, while lakeside galleries, a classical garden-within-a-garden and a pearl-mussel sculpture at the south entrance fill the rest of the grounds.

rows.name: Ancient Tunnels of Bozhou (Cao Cao's Troop Tunnel)
rows.summary: A network of underground passages beneath the old city of Bozhou, the home town of Cao Cao, begun in the late Eastern Han but surviving mostly from the Song dynasty; the tunnels radiate from the old crossroads of Dayushou and are built partly of earth and timber but mostly of brick. A section open to visitors is presented as 'Cao Cao's Underground Troop Tunnel', with low brick passages running several metres below the streets.

rows.name: Bozhou Museum
rows.summary: The city museum of Bozhou, founded in 1959 and now a national second-grade museum, in a Han-style building among trees. Its permanent exhibition, 'Through Five Thousand Years', follows the city's history from early cultures on the Guo River and the Shang capital of Bo through the age of Laozi and Zhuangzi and the Han–Wei era of Cao Cao and Hua Tuo to the merchant town of later centuries. It stands beside Cao Cao Park, around which some of the excavated tombs of Cao Cao's clan lie.

rows.name: Cao Clan Tombs
rows.summary: The burial ground of Cao Cao's family on the southern side of Bozhou, a scatter of Eastern Han tombs that includes those of his father Cao Song and his grandfather Cao Teng. Most were excavated in the 1970s after earlier looting and yielded jade burial suits sewn with silver and copper thread, jade pigs and hundreds of bricks inscribed in several scripts, including early cursive; Cao Teng's tomb had stone chambers with carved reliefs and paintings. A few excavated brick-and-stone chambers with carved doorways can be entered, while other tombs remain unexcavated mounds.

rows.name: Gujing Gongjiu Brewing Site and Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The historic core of the Gujing Gongjiu distillery in Gujing town, where a Song-dynasty well, a Ming well and a set of fermentation pits in use since at least 1515, the date on a boundary brick found among them, are protected with the excavated remains of a Ming–Qing brewery. Around them the company's liquor culture park centres on a museum built in 1995, whose prizes include a Qing palace wine jar and samples of all 368 liquors entered in China's last national liquor competition in 1989, opposite a garden with a corridor of inscribed steles. The local liquor was sent as tribute to the Ming court, and the brand traces its method to a recipe Cao Cao presented to the Han emperor in 196.

rows.name: Huaxilou (Shanxi–Shaanxi Guild Hall)
rows.summary: A guild hall and temple to the war god Guan Yu built in the Qing dynasty by medicine merchants from Shanxi and Shaanxi trading in Bozhou, on Xianning Street in the old northern quarter. Its popular name, 'flower opera tower', comes from the opera stage facing the main hall, covered in painted wood carvings of Three Kingdoms stories; the gateway is faced with intricate brick carving and flanked by a pair of tall iron flagpoles.

rows.name: Linyongcheng Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the south-western edge of Bozhou laid out around a reservoir, also known as Yaodu Linhai, the 'forest sea of the medicine capital', after the city's role as a centre of the herbal-medicine trade. Besides woodland walks it has a botanical garden, family attractions and a virtual-reality 'metaverse' hall.

rows.name: Mengcheng Museum
rows.summary: The county museum of Mengcheng, home county of the philosopher Zhuangzi, opened in 2014 and now a national third-grade museum. Its main gallery presents the Neolithic village excavated at Yuchisi, 20 km north-east of the town, including the large pottery zun jars for which the site is known, some incised with early symbols; other galleries cover ancient Mengcheng, the local tradition of couplet writing and local role models.

rows.name: Nanjing Lane Qianzhuang (Old Bank)
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty qianzhuang, a traditional private bank and money-changer, on Nanjing Lane in the old northern quarter of Bozhou, a few minutes' walk from Huaxilou. Its grey-brick courtyard buildings, a national heritage site since 2013, can be visited.

rows.name: Tianjing Palace
rows.summary: A Taoist temple at Zhengdian village on the northern outskirts of Guoyang, on the spot that local tradition, recorded in Yuan- and Ming-dynasty steles, names as the birthplace of Laozi, the founder of Taoism. Long ruined, the temple site has been excavated and the temple rebuilt, and the cycle of Laozi legends told around it is listed as national intangible cultural heritage.

rows.name: Wanfo Pagoda, Mengcheng
rows.summary: A thirteen-storey octagonal brick pagoda built in 1102, in the Northern Song dynasty, for the Xinghua Temple, which has since disappeared. Its walls are set with thousands of small Buddha images moulded in brick, which give the 'Ten Thousand Buddha Pagoda' its name.

rows.name: Xuege Pagoda
rows.summary: An eight-sided, seven-storey brick pagoda built between 1772 and 1812, in the Qing dynasty, in imitation of a timber tower. Originally called Wenfeng Pagoda, it stands on Xuege Road in central Bozhou.

rows.name: Baisui Palace
rows.summary: A ridge-top monastery above Jiuhua Street that grew from a Ming hermitage where the monk Wuxia (Haiyu) lived in the Wanli era and died aged 110; his body did not decay and, gilded, is still enshrined in the temple, and in 1630 the Chongzhen Emperor honoured him as a 'Bodhisattva of the Manifested Body'. Gate, halls, monks' cells and guest rooms are combined in one five-storey block against the rock, giving it the look of a castle from below; damaged by fire in 1717 and in the Taiping war, it was refurbished in 1982.

rows.name: Baiyashan Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey, six-sided brick pagoda on the eastern foot of Baiya Hill in central Chizhou, built in 1538 under the prefect Lu Gang with money raised by the city's river-trade brokers, who gave it its name. About 34 m tall, it has arched doors, windows and niches on every storey and a spiral stair inside; damaged by lightning in the late Qing and by Japanese shelling, it was repaired in 1982 and 2001 and listed nationally in 2019 together with the city's other Ming pagoda, Qingxi Pagoda.

rows.name: Dawang Cave
rows.summary: A 10 km² karst scenic area in Paifang town on the south bank of the Yangtze, Chizhou's first 4A site, built around the Dawang Cave, whose name was written by the calligrapher and Buddhist leader Zhao Puchu. Besides the cave it takes in a natural stone bridge, the Linyu Gorge, Dawang Lake and a cable car over the countryside.

rows.name: Dayuan Cultural Park
rows.summary: A Buddhist-themed park at Kecun, the northern foot of Mount Jiuhua, built around a 99-metre bronze statue of Ksitigarbha, the bodhisattva of the mountain; the height stands for Jiuhua's 99 peaks and the 99 years of Kim Gyo-gak, the monk revered as his incarnation. Halls, pavilions, bridges and towers in a modern blend of Tang and Huizhou styles surround the statue.

rows.name: Guaitan Rafting
rows.summary: A whitewater rafting run of about 4.5 km on a mountain river, taking around an hour and a half through three sets of rapids, six river bends and five clear pools between forested hills. The wider Guaitan scenic area at Diaoyutai in Hengdu town also has a valley of oddly shaped boulders, a wildlife specimen hall and forest walks, and in spring some 20 kinds of azalea flower along the banks.

rows.name: Guniujiang Longmen Scenic Area (Shitai side)
rows.summary: The Shitai-county side of Guniujiang, a 6,700-hectare forest that has been a national nature reserve since 1988, Anhui's first forest-ecosystem reserve of that rank; its main summit, Guniu Dagang (1,727.6 m), is the third-highest peak in southern Anhui. Two areas are open to visitors: Longmen, with trails past Longmen Pool, a four-tier waterfall and old trees to Yanjia, an old village with a wall of Red Army slogans, and Shuanglong Valley, richest in the reserve's wildlife. A 2025–2026 upgrade added a hillside escalator, a natural-history hall and a 1.9 km twin-track glass water slide.

rows.name: Huacheng Temple
rows.summary: The oldest and leading temple of Mount Jiuhua, in the middle of Jiuhua Street: tradition dates it to 401, and the Silla monk Kim Gyo-gak lived here in the 8th century, after which it was dedicated to Ksitigarbha and called the head of all the mountain's temples. Rebuilt in 1391, 1435 and 1681, it climbs in steps along a north–south axis through the Lingguan, Heavenly Kings and main halls to a Ming-dynasty sutra library. It was declared a national key Buddhist temple in 1983.

rows.name: Hualong Cave
rows.summary: A Palaeolithic cave site on the southern slope of Meiyuan Hill where excavations since 2006 have recovered human fossils about 300,000 years old, including the skull known as 'Dongzhi Man', together with stone tools and the bones of giant pandas, stegodons and other animals. The excavated cave is now protected under a 680 m² Chinese-style shelter, with sculptures of ancient animals and a bronze hunting scene on the lawns outside; a site museum 1.2 km away, built to look like a cave inside, explains the finds in four galleries.

rows.name: Jiuhua Shenlong Valley
rows.summary: A wooded gorge about 3 km long on the southern side of Mount Jiuhua, cut by streams from Pusatou and Loutai hills and known locally as 'nine drops and eighteen bends'. A path follows the stream past a chain of waterfalls, deep pools and boulders with names such as Shenlong Falls and Bathing Immortal Pool.

rows.name: Jiuhua Tianchi
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in south-eastern Guichi, developed from 2007 around the Siling Reservoir, a lake high in the hills known as the 'heavenly pool'. A trail of about 4 km climbs through the boulder-filled Glacier Stone Valley, named after ancient glaciation, to Longchi Falls and the lake, where boats cross the water; rafting and a zip line across a gorge are also on offer. At the entrance, Nuoxian Town, a street of new Huizhou-style buildings opened in 2024, stages evening shows built on local Nuo masked opera, with street processions, molten-iron 'fireworks' and aerial acts.

rows.name: Jiuziyan
rows.summary: A rocky mountain area on the eastern side of the Jiuhua range that gave Mount Jiuhua its old name, Jiuzi ('Nine Sons') Mountain, and is regarded as the cradle of Buddhism there: among its relics is the spot where Kim Gyo-gak, later venerated as Ksitigarbha, first practised. Paths and a cable car lead up through pines, oddly shaped rocks, waterfalls and steep peaks.

rows.name: Jiyang Cao Ancestral Hall (Qingyang Museum)
rows.summary: Two Ming–Qing clan halls that were taken down in villages near Lingyang and rebuilt in Qingyang town between 1991 and 1995, where they house the county museum: the Cao ancestral hall, with its gate tower, Minglun Hall and rear shrine, and the Chen clan's Xiaosi Hall. With them stands a four-pillar Qing stone archway honouring the filial piety of one Chen Liangtai.

rows.name: Li Ancestral Hall, Shangzhang
rows.summary: A Huizhou-style clan temple in Shangzhang village whose present buildings date from a rebuilding of 1781–1799, with a front hall, the Xulun ancestral hall and a two-storey rear shrine set one behind another. It is known for its carving: a pair of carved stone drums at the gate, the clan's family instructions cut into a screen wall, balustrades carved with scenes from opera, and richly carved and painted woodwork in the rear shrine.

rows.name: Lianfeng Yunhai
rows.summary: A scenic area on Lianhua (Lotus) Peak (1,048 m) at the northern foot of the Jiuhua range, named for the seas of cloud often seen from the summit; the peak's shape also earns it the name Brush-Rest Mountain. Paths lead past rock caves, the stone-built Jingxin Temple of 1480 and the gate of a Taiping-era hill fort, and the scenic area has a hotel and a folk museum showing Qingyang farmers' paintings and farm tools.

rows.name: Penglai Cave
rows.summary: A large limestone cave more than 3,000 m long near Ducun, the home village of the late-Tang poet Du Xunhe, formed on four levels: upper, middle and lower caves and an underground river. Its best-known formations are a white 'gauze curtain', fine 'heavenly threads', a wall like a landscape painting and a 'thousand-Buddha hill'; the cave reopened in March 2025 after a lighting upgrade that added projected light shows to several formations.

rows.name: Qingxi Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda, originally named Miaoyin Pagoda, built between 1601 and 1612 under a succession of Chizhou prefects where the old course of the Qingxi River meets the Yangtze, on the north-eastern side of the city. About 56 m tall, it has arched doors, windows and Buddha niches (now empty) on every storey and stairs inside the walls; its finial was destroyed by lightning in 1642, Japanese shelling during the war left dozens of scars that can still be seen, and it was repaired in 1982, 2002 and from 2019.

rows.name: Qishan Hill and Pingtian Lake
rows.summary: A 40 km² scenic area on the eastern edge of Chizhou that joins Qishan, a hill whose rocks carry cliff inscriptions left by visitors from the Tang dynasty to the Republic, among them a line attributed to the Song general Yue Fei, with Pingtian Lake and the wetland park on its southern shore. The lake, named after a line in Li Bai's 'Songs of Qiupu', is listed as a nationally important wetland, and its shores are laid out with paths and viewing points such as the Lotus Terrace.

rows.name: Qiupu River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A stretch of the Qiupu River near Shitai, the 'river of poems' where Li Bai stayed on five occasions and wrote his seventeen 'Songs of Qiupu'. The scenic area combines a 4 km raft run through 14 rapids, Qiupu Fishing Village, a farm-stay with a Li Bai exhibition hall and hot-spring baths, and Baizhangya, a gorge fitted with rope bridges, wire walks and other outdoor-adventure courses.

rows.name: Shrine of Living Buddha
rows.summary: The hall on Shenguang Ridge above Jiuhua Street that houses the remains of Kim Gyo-gak, the Silla prince-monk who died in 794 and was venerated as Ksitigarbha; his body was placed in a stone stupa, around which the hall was later built. Inside the iron-tiled, pagoda-like hall a seven-storey octagonal wooden pagoda enshrines the stupa, surrounded by statues of Ksitigarbha and the Ten Kings of Hell. Unusually, the hall faces north, towards Kim's homeland in Korea.

rows.name: Taiping Shanfang
rows.summary: A village school building in Suo village on the south side of Mount Jiuhua, first a hall of the Chen clan and turned into a school in 1771; it is one of the best-preserved old school buildings in Anhui. A gate hall, main hall and rear building with side rooms enclose small courtyards; the front halls date from the late Ming or early Qing and the rear building from the early Ming.

rows.name: Xianyu Mountain and the Jugen Pass Ancient Hui Road
rows.pinyin: Xiānyù Shān Jǔgēn Guān Gǔ Huī Dào
rows.summary: A mountain area in Xianyu town on the western arm of the Huangshan range, rising to 1,376 m, whose centrepiece is the Jugen Pass Ancient Hui Road: a 7.5 km stone-paved trade route of Tang origin by which Huizhou merchants carried tea and scholars' supplies, lined with old rest pavilions, inscribed steles and a stone-slab bridge of 1802. At the pass stands a stone wall and gateway built by Zeng Guofan's Hunan Army during the Taiping war. The scenic area also takes in Dashan, a village known for its selenium-rich farmland and long-lived residents, a stream gorge and a long dry toboggan run.

rows.name: Xinghua Village (Apricot Blossom Village)
rows.summary: A landscaped park on the western edge of Chizhou on the site that local tradition links to the 'apricot blossom village' of 'Qingming', the poem Du Mu wrote while prefect of Chizhou in the Tang dynasty; a Qing gazetteer of the village was included in the imperial Siku Quanshu collection. Apricot groves, streams and small bridges surround pavilions and halls named after poets, a poetry-reciting terrace and a wine shop.

rows.name: Xiushan Gate Museum
rows.summary: A private museum of traditional Chinese building crafts, opened in 2006 in the gate tower and walls of Xiushan Gate, the west gate of old Chizhou, which took its present name in 1235 in memory of Xiao Tong, the Liang-dynasty Crown Prince Zhaoming. Its halls are fitted out with carved wooden doors and windows, brackets, stone drums and lions, brick carvings and inscribed boards gathered from old buildings, alongside porcelain, paintings and embroidery.

rows.name: Yulong Cave
rows.summary: A limestone cave in Qidu town named for the way it winds under the hill like a coiled dragon; its mouth, about 8 m wide and 5 m high and shaped like a crocodile's open jaws, is hung with stalactites above a clear pool that never dries. Inside, the air stays at an even temperature all year, and since a 2025 upgrade visitors ride track-guided dragon boats along the underground water past projected light shows.

rows.name: Zhiyuan Temple
rows.summary: One of the four great monasteries of Mount Jiuhua, a few minutes' walk from Huacheng Temple on Jiuhua Street, founded in the Jiajing era of the Ming as a small hermitage and named after the Jetavana grove where the Buddha taught. Most of the present halls are Qing, from the gate hall with its guardian figures and the Heavenly Kings Hall to the double-eaved main hall roofed in yellow glazed tiles, which houses gilded bronze statues of three Buddhas.

rows.name: Zuishanye (Huangya Gorge and Ciyun Cave)
rows.summary: A scenic area in Yuanxi village just outside Shitai town with two parts. Huangya Grand Canyon is a wooded gorge of small dams, green pools and stepped falls fitted with a zip line over 300 m long, a glass bridge and a 'shouting fountain'; Ciyun Cave, opened in 2018, is a karst cave of stalagmites, stalactites, columns and flowstone curtains.

rows.name: Banta Battle Site and Wandong Revolutionary Memorial Hall
rows.summary: Banta, a market town in northern Lai'an County, was the centre of the anti-Japanese base area that the Communist-led New Fourth Army set up east of the Tianjin–Pukou railway from August 1939, and gives its name to the Banta Defence, a battle fought over the town during the war. The battle site is protected as national heritage, and the town has a martyrs' cemetery and the Wandong (Eastern Anhui) Revolutionary Memorial Hall, a state museum.

rows.name: Chishan Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park in south-eastern Lai'an County on the border with Nanjing's Luhe District, named for the pond cypresses (Taxodium) that grow in its lake and form a flooded forest. The trees and open water are a gathering place for water birds, and the park was rated 4A in 2023.

rows.name: Huangfu Mountain
rows.summary: A range of forested hills in Nanqiao District, west of Chuzhou, protected as a national forest park, with a provincial nature reserve named after it in the same hills. Rated 4A in 2023, it is a place for woodland walks rather than sights.

rows.name: Jiushan Cave
rows.summary: A large limestone cave in the Jiushan hills of Yinjian town in southern Fengyang County, inside the Jiushan National Forest Park and rated 4A in 2020. Old accounts say it could shelter several thousand people, and in the Southern Song the general Wang Weizhong built stone walls around it as a stronghold against the Jin, whose stockade site is a protected relic.

rows.name: Langxiang Maze Valley
rows.summary: A karst scenic area in Fengyang County where narrow, winding passages cut through limestone form a natural maze, some so tight that visitors have to turn sideways or stoop to get through. Boardwalks link the maze with a cave and a Buddhist temple in the same hills, and it has been rated 4A since 2007.

rows.name: Longgang Ancient Town
rows.summary: Longgang, now part of Tongcheng town in northern Tianchang, is an old market town where the Eighth Branch of the Communist-led Anti-Japanese Military and Political University (Kangda) ran its school from the autumn of 1941 to the spring of 1944. The former school buildings in the town are protected as provincial heritage, and a memorial hall presents the school's history.

rows.name: Ming Imperial Mausoleum (Huangling), Fengyang
rows.summary: The tomb that Zhu Yuanzhang, founder of the Ming dynasty, built between 1366 and 1379 for his parents, about 7 km south of Fengyang town, in the county where he grew up in a poor family. Its spirit way is lined with 28 pairs of stone figures carved by 1369, among them qilin, lions, tigers, rams, horses with grooms, civil and military officials and eunuchs, and the Great Ming Imperial Tomb Stele near the mound is a key source on Zhu's family. The statues and stele were damaged in the Cultural Revolution and re-erected during restoration from 1982.

rows.name: Ming Zhongdu Imperial City
rows.summary: The remains of the 'Central Capital' that Zhu Yuanzhang began building at his birthplace in Fengyang in 1369 and abandoned in 1375; its planning served as the model for the later palaces of Nanjing and Beijing. Much was pulled down for bricks and farmland between 1950 and 1975, and what survives is part of the imperial-city wall with its gates, among them the Wu (Noon) Gate, and the base of the drum tower; most other structures are reconstructions from the 1990s onwards.

rows.name: Mount Langya
rows.summary: A range of wooded hills on the south-western edge of Chuzhou, rising to 321 m, made famous by the Song writer Ouyang Xiu, who governed Chuzhou in the 1040s and wrote 'The Old Toper's Pavilion' about the Zuiweng Pavilion in its valley (the present pavilion is Qing). Up the valley is Langya Temple, founded in the 760s, whose Beamless Hall, a Ming brick-vaulted hall with no timber beams, is national heritage, as are more than 400 cliff and stele inscriptions, seven of them Tang, around the temple and the Zuiweng and Fengle pavilions. Lake Shenxiu, the Huifeng Pavilion and old paths make it a half-day walk.

rows.name: Taiping Bridge, Chihe
rows.summary: A multi-arched stone bridge across the Chi River at the western end of Chihe town, built in 1375 by the Dingyuan magistrate on the official road linking Nanjing, Fengyang and Beijing, and the only Ming stone arch bridge left in northern Anhui. As first built it had 13 arches over 142 m; three central arches blown up in 1938 to slow the Japanese advance were later patched, and since 1985 the bridge has carried only pedestrians, with a full restoration completed in 2014. Its original stone lions and inscribed steles are lost.

rows.name: Wu Jingzi Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum to Wu Jingzi (1701–1754), the Quanjiao-born author of The Scholars, often seen as China's foremost satirical novel, on Zoumagang on the northern edge of Quanjiao town, facing the site of his family home across the Xiang River. Opened in 1986 in Ming and Qing style and enlarged since 2019, it holds Wu family heirlooms, scholars' writings on Wu and works of calligraphy and painting, and his cenotaph stands in the grounds. His rebuilt family home, opened in 2015, is across the river.

rows.name: Xiaogang Village
rows.summary: The village in Xiaoxihe town, Fengyang, where on the night of 24 November 1978 eighteen farmers secretly signed a pledge to divide the collective fields into household plots, a step later held up as the start of China's rural reforms. The 1979 grain harvest equalled the village's total for 1966–1970; the site of the pledge is protected as national heritage, and the Da Baogan (household contract) Memorial Museum tells the story. In 2024 UN Tourism named Xiaogang one of its Best Tourism Villages.

rows.name: Bali River Scenic Area
rows.summary: Bali River is a lakeside park in Balihe town, Yingshang County, built by local farmers from 1992 on a flood-prone marsh near where the Ying River meets the Huai, and opened in 1996 as a 'farmers' park'. Its sections include a bird garden, a 'World Scenery' area of concrete miniatures of foreign landmarks such as the Arc de Triomphe, Chinese-style gardens and pavilions, and flower islands, set in a 15.8 km² area that is mostly water. In 2013 it became northern Anhui's first 5A scenic area.

rows.name: Digou Ecological Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area in Digou town, Yingshang County, made up of an ecological park that keeps peacocks, water birds, swans, parrots and monkeys among collections of rare plants, the Buddhist Zhuyin Temple and a culture square. It is mainly a day out for local families.

rows.name: Fengbaigang Lotus Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural lotus and wetland park near the seat of Dicheng town in southern Funan County, close to the Huai River. Its centrepiece is a lotus garden of about 400 mu (27 ha) crossed by boardwalks, pavilions and arched bridges, best when the lotuses flower in summer, with farm-style restaurants nearby.

rows.name: Fuyang Ecological Park
rows.summary: A large leisure park on the north-western edge of Fuyang that mixes farm-style sightseeing with family entertainment. Its sections include a culture garden on Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi, two Song writers linked with old Yingzhou (Fuyang), a tropical plant house, a pick-your-own orchard, a dinosaur park, a zoo and a children's amusement area with a Ferris wheel.

rows.name: Jinzhongzi Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The visitor park of the Jinzhongzi (Golden Seed) baijiu company in southern Fuyang, whose distillery grew from the Fuyang County liquor works founded in 1949. It presents the company's brewing heritage, including fermentation pits the company dates to the Ming dynasty, alongside landscaped grounds, and suits visitors curious about Chinese liquor.

rows.name: Linquan Magic City
rows.summary: A tourism complex on the west bank of the Liu'an River in western Linquan, themed on the 'Investiture of the Gods' legends of the Shang–Zhou period. It groups a Nezha-themed water park, a large zoo, a 'Fengshen' fantasy valley, a craft street, a theatre and a hotel. The zoo stages animal shows, such as sea lion and bird performances, and offers animal feeding.

rows.name: Ming-Qing Garden, Yingshang
rows.summary: A compound of Ming- and Qing-style courtyard buildings, including houses, a temple and an opera stage, beside the riverside park in Yingshang county town, a short walk from Guanzhong Old Street. Although it lies about 9 km north of the Bali River park, it is promoted as one of that scenic area's five sections, and local tourism material calls it the largest group of buildings in this style in northern Anhui.

rows.name: Taihe Global Carnival Amusement Park
rows.summary: An amusement park beside the Shaying River at Taihe, about 500 m west of the river's third bridge, whose rides include the 'Eye of Taihe' Ferris wheel, a roller coaster, a log flume and a water-play area. It is aimed at local families.

rows.name: Yingzhou West Lake
rows.summary: Yingzhou West Lake was a celebrated lake of Song-dynasty Yingzhou, today's Fuyang, praised by Ouyang Xiu and by Su Shi, who compared it with Hangzhou's West Lake, until Yellow River floods silted it up. The present lake was recreated from the 1980s about 4 km south-west of the old site and is now a national wetland park; its first phase, the South Lake area, combines wetland scenery with a historical and cultural zone devoted to Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi.

rows.name: You Family Garden and Wulihu Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 尤家花园·五里湖湿地公园
rows.summary: A private garden begun in the late Qing beside Wuli Lake on the western edge of Yingshang town, together with the wetland park around the lake. The garden, ringed by water, is laid out in the Suzhou manner with rockeries, small bridges, pavilions, shaped pines and potted landscapes, and is nicknamed the 'Yu Garden of northern Anhui'; the wetland park adds lakeside paths for walking.

rows.name: Anhui Art Museum
rows.summary: Anhui's provincial art museum, opened in May 2022 on the north shore of Chao Lake in Hefei's Binhu New District, beside the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign Memorial Museum. The five-storey white steel-framed building of 50,000 m² has galleries of up to 2,000 m², a spiral staircase and a 70-metre suspension walkway, and shows changing exhibitions.

rows.name: Anhui Museum
rows.summary: Anhui's provincial museum, whose main Shushan building opened in 2011 in Hefei's government district; its collection numbers about 220,000 objects. Highlights include the great Zhuke ding from the tomb of a Chu king at Shou County, the bells of the Marquis of Cai and the E Jun Qi bronze tallies, and a full-size relocated Huizhou house showing the region's wood, stone and brick carving.

rows.name: Anhui Museum Luyang Branch (Old Exhibition Building)
rows.summary: The original Anhui Provincial Museum on Anqing Road in central Hefei, an exhibition building of 11,580 m² begun in 1954 and completed in 1956, the year the museum was formally founded. Since the main museum moved to its new Shushan building in 2011, the listed building has served as the museum's Luyang branch for exhibitions.

rows.name: Bantang Tulip Highland
rows.summary: A hillside flower park in the Chaohu Economic Development Zone near the Bantang hot springs, east of Chaohu city. Its slopes are planted with tulip fields, which are at their best in April, so it is mainly worth a visit in spring.

rows.name: Bao Gong Hometown Cultural Park
rows.summary: A culture park opened in 2023 in Baogong town, Feidong County, where Bao Zheng, the Song official remembered as Judge Bao, was born and grew up. Laid out in Song style, it presents his life through three staged drama shows, a mystery game, a holographic theatre and craft activities. It includes the Huayuan Well, by tradition the well of the Bao family garden.

rows.name: Baogong Park
rows.summary: A park along the Bao River in central Hefei dedicated to Bao Zheng (999–1062), the upright Song-dynasty official known to generations of opera and television audiences as Judge Bao. It contains the Bao Gong Shrine, a memorial temple with his statue, his four guards and the three bronze guillotines of the Judge Bao stories, his tomb complex rebuilt in 1987 to Song building rules, the Qingfeng Pavilion and the Fuzhuang garden.

rows.name: Changlin Old Street
rows.summary: The old street of Changlinhe, a town near the north shore of Chao Lake in Feidong County, lined with traditional houses and shops. Its Qing buildings include the provincially listed Wu family residence, a three-courtyard house in central-Anhui style, and the Liujiafan old houses and the Zhenhu Pagoda of 1892 stand a few kilometres to the south by the lake.

rows.name: Dawei Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A farming town on the south-eastern outskirts of Hefei developed for farm tourism, where city residents come to pick seasonal fruit and vegetables and to fish. It makes an easy half-day outing from the city, best in the fruit-picking seasons.

rows.name: Former Residence of Feng Yuxiang
rows.summary: The house in Zhuke village, Xiage town, where the Republican-era general Feng Yuxiang (1882–1948), known in the West as the 'Christian General', stayed on visits to his ancestral home in 1936–37. The compound of five buildings with 22 rooms over 4,690 m² includes his study, bedroom, guards' room, reception hall and garden.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Hongzhang
rows.summary: Part of the family mansion of Li Hongzhang (1823–1901), the late-Qing statesman who founded the Huai Army and the Beiyang Fleet and was for decades the face of the Qing court in foreign affairs, on the Huaihe Road pedestrian street in central Hefei. Restored and opened in 1999, the 2,000 m² compound in late-Qing Jianghuai style runs from the gate through front and middle halls to a two-storey rear building, with displays on his life and calligraphy and rooms furnished in Qing style.

rows.name: Former Residence of Liu Mingchuan
rows.summary: The moated, fortified manor of Liu Mingchuan (1836–1896), the Huai Army general who became the first governor of Taiwan under the Qing, 2 km north of Daqian Mountain in Feixi County. Built from 1868, it was his home after he left Taiwan in 1891; more than 40 buildings survive, restored and partly rebuilt in 2014–15, and the manor opened as a memorial museum.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhang Zhizhong
rows.summary: The birthplace home of Zhang Zhizhong (1890–1969), a Nationalist general who in 1949 stayed on the mainland and later held senior posts in the People's Republic, at Hongjiatuan in Huanglu town on the north shore of Chao Lake. He also founded the Huanglu Normal School in the town in 1933.

rows.name: Golden Peacock Hot Spring Resort, Tangchi
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort with accommodation in Tangchi, a spa town in western Lujiang County and one of the two hot-spring areas around Chao Lake. It suits a relaxing overnight stay.

rows.name: Guanting Forest Park
rows.summary: A large planted forest park on the Yangtze–Huai watershed at Guanting town in Feixi County, centred on Fengxiang Lake. A landmark on its eastern side marks the divide, where rain runs south-east to the Yangtze or north-west to the Huai, and a viewing platform in the middle of the forest looks over groves of red maple, cherry, plum, magnolia and crabapple, a rose garden and more than ten lotus ponds around the lake.

rows.name: Hechai 1972 Creative Park
rows.summary: A creative and leisure quarter opened in 2019 in the former Hefei Diesel Engine Factory, which started work in 1972 and whose site was later used as a prison until 2018. Watchtowers, domed workshops, a chimney and red-brick buildings have been kept and now house the Hefei Home Appliance Story Museum, a contemporary art museum, cafés and shops.

rows.name: Hefei Binhu National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 合肥滨湖国家森林公园
rows.summary: A 10.7 km² wetland forest park on the north shore of Chao Lake near the mouth of the Nanfei River, opened in two phases in 2012 and 2013 and made a national forest park in 2013. Paths lead through plantations of poplar, dawn redwood and privet and around 2.6 km² of ponds and wetland, making it a good place to walk or cycle on the edge of the Binhu New District.

rows.name: Hefei Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A 70-hectare botanical garden on the south-eastern shore of Dongpu Reservoir in Hefei's Shushan District, established in 1987 on the site of a former horticultural farm. It holds more than 2,000 plant species in nine themed gardens, among them plum, osmanthus, bamboo, magnolia, pomegranate, water and bonsai gardens.

rows.name: Hefei Sunac Land
rows.summary: A large theme park in Hefei's Binhu New District, built as Wanda's Hefei park and now run by Sunac, with themed zones, rides and live shows. Rides include Soaring with Dragon, an Intamin launched roller coaster opened in 2016 that reaches 125 km/h, and the park suits families and thrill-ride fans, with a shopping mall next door.

rows.name: Hefei Wildlife Park
rows.summary: Hefei's main zoo, a wildlife park on Wangjiang West Road at the foot of Dashu Mountain on the western edge of the city. It suits families and can be combined with a walk up neighbouring Dashu Mountain forest park.

rows.name: Huiyuan Garden
rows.summary: A theme park of gardens opened in September 2001 in Hefei's economic development zone, with about 45 sights; pavilions and gardens represent each of Anhui's cities, such as the Hefei and Lu'an gardens. It gives a quick overview of the province's regional architecture without leaving the city.

rows.name: Mushan Island
rows.summary: A wooded volcanic islet of 0.86 km² in the middle of Chao Lake, 3.5 km off Zhongmiao on the north shore. On its summit stands the Wenfeng Pagoda, a seven-storey, 51-metre octagonal pagoda of dressed stone begun in 1631 and finished in 1878 at Li Hongzhang's initiative, which holds 802 brick-carved Buddhas and 25 inscribed plaques. A shrine on the hillside and a sheltered harbour on the south shore add to a half-day trip with wide lake views.

rows.name: Sanhe Ancient Town
rows.summary: A river town where the Fengle, Hangbu and Xiaonan rivers meet near Chao Lake, scene of the Taiping army's 1858 victory over the Xiang Army at the Battle of Sanhe. Its 4.7 km² scenic area mixes a few older buildings, such as the Liu Tongxing shop-residence and the house where the physicist Chen-Ning Yang's family took refuge in 1937, with much new construction in traditional style along waterways and wide streets. It is known for its rice wine and makes an easy day trip from Hefei.

rows.name: Sanshigang Eco-Agricultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A rural township of orchards and farmland on Hefei's north-western edge, developed for farm tourism with seasonal activities such as blossom viewing and fruit picking. The Three Kingdoms Xincheng Site Park lies within the township.

rows.name: Three Kingdoms Xincheng Site Park
rows.summary: The ruins of Hefei's Xincheng ('New City'), a fortress the Wei general Man Chong built in 233 west of old Hefei to hold off the state of Wu, which besieged it several times without taking it. Excavations in 2004–05 uncovered three gates, a drill platform, a weapon-casting kiln and a cart road, and the park shows these with partly rebuilt walls and gates, a restored moat and exhibition halls in Han style. It suits visitors interested in the Three Kingdoms period.

rows.name: Xiangyuan Flower World
rows.summary: A modern flower-themed resort park built around Tanchong Lake at Shangpai town in Feixi County, south-west of Hefei. Themed gardens and seasonal flower fields are combined with children's play areas, boating and camping, and in early May it has hosted the Hefei Rose Season. It suits a family outing.

rows.name: Xiaojingzhuang Village
rows.summary: A small village in Shannan town, Feixi County, whose 32-household production team secretly divided its farmland among households on 5 September 1978, during a severe drought, an early case of the household contract system that spread through China's rural reforms. A memorial stone at the village entrance marks it as a birthplace of household contracting, a title more often given to Xiaogang village, which followed three months later.

rows.name: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign Memorial Museum
rows.summary: A memorial museum opened in 2012 on the north shore of Chao Lake about the People's Liberation Army's April 1949 crossing of the Yangtze, which ended with the capture of Nanjing. The complex runs from Liberation Square through the 44-metre-high main hall, built leaning forward at 49 degrees, past a group statue of the General Front Committee to Victory Square and a 99-metre victory tower. The rating also covers the neighbouring Anhui Celebrities Hall.

rows.name: Yaogang Headquarters of the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign
rows.summary: A group of late-Qing courtyard houses in Yaogang, Feidong County, where the Communist General Front Committee under Deng Xiaoping and Chen Yi directed the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign in April 1949 before moving to Nanjing at the end of the month. Five restored buildings, including the committee's headquarters, secretariat and staff office and the office of the East China Bureau, show the leaders' rooms and campaign material, and a memorial museum stands alongside.

rows.name: Yefu Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill north-east of Lujiang town, protected as a national forest park and named, by legend, after the swordsmith Ou Yezi, who is said to have forged swords here. Its two Buddhist temples frame the walk: Shiji Temple at the foot of the mountain and Fuhu Temple on the summit.

rows.name: Zipeng Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A range of low wooded hills in Feixi County south-west of Hefei, protected as a national forest park and laced with walking trails. Its main sight is Xilu Temple, a large Buddhist temple on the mountain.

rows.name: Ziwei Cave
rows.summary: A limestone cave in the hills on the northern edge of Chaohu city, also called Shuangjing ('Twin Wells') Cave after its two shaft-like openings, about 3 km long with a main passage of some 1.5 km along an underground river. The scenic area also contains Wangqiao Cave, whose walls carry more than 620 carved Buddhist figures, almost all of them now headless.

rows.name: Huaihai Campaign General Front Committee Site (Wenchang Palace)
rows.summary: Wenchang Palace in Linhuan, a temple to the god of literature founded under the Tang and later used as an academy and a school, became the forward headquarters of the Communist Central Plains Field Army on 10 November 1948, during the Huaihai Campaign. The General Front Committee of Liu Bocheng, Chen Yi, Deng Xiaoping, Su Yu and Tan Zhenlin, set up on 16 November to direct the campaign, was based here until it moved to Xiaolijia village, about 5 km to the east, on 23 November. Opened as a memorial hall in 1988, its grey-brick courtyards hold six rooms, among them the committee's meeting room and the commanders' bedrooms restored to their 1948 state, with the rest given to displays on the campaign.

rows.name: Linhuan Ancient City Walls
rows.summary: Linhuan, the ancient town of Zhi, is still ringed by rammed-earth walls first raised by the state of Song in the late Warring States period, nearly square in plan and shaded by tall trees. Used until the Yuan and little altered since, the walls are being repaired section by section, starting with the north. Inside, the town is known for its old teahouses serving 'stick tea' brewed from tea stalks and local spring water, often to the sound of Huaibei drum-song storytelling.

rows.name: Liuzi Grand Canal Site
rows.summary: Liuzi village lies on the Tongji Canal section of the Sui–Tang Grand Canal, and excavations here in 1999 and 2012–13 confirmed the canal's route and uncovered Tang boats, Song stone bridge piers and pottery from more than 20 kilns. It is a component of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site, and the excavated bridge remains, under a large protective hall, opened to the public in May 2025 as the Liuzi Canal Bridge Site Museum. Many of the finds are shown at the Huaibei Museum.

rows.name: Nanhu Park
rows.summary: Nanhu (South Lake) is a lake and wetland park in Huaibei's Lieshan district, created on land that subsided above coal workings and part of the chain of reclaimed lakes that now runs through the city. Paths and 45 decorative bridges link 22 viewpoints around the water, which draws water birds. A monument to the first borehole of the Huaibei coalfield stands in the lake as a reminder of the city's mining past.

rows.name: Sijiliuyuan Pomegranate Park
rows.summary: Sijiliuyuan is a rural scenic area in the hills of Lieshan district, built around more than 1,000 mu of pomegranate orchards surviving from the Ming and Qing, in an area where pomegranates have been grown since at least the Song and Yuan. It links the old orchards, the China Pomegranate Museum with more than 500 exhibits, and the Longji Tianlu scenic mountain road, with a ski slope opened in the winter of 2024–25, camping and children's play areas. Autumn, when the fruit is picked and a pomegranate festival is held, is the best time to come.

rows.name: Suixi Ancient Town
rows.summary: Suixi Ancient Town is a leisure district in Suixi county town, home of the Kouzi liquor brand, that joins Qianlong Lake park to an old-style shopping quarter. The lake area of about 2,550 mu has four boat piers and the Huili Pavilion lookout, and the 283 m South Street links it to a canal-side street lined with liquor workshops, silversmiths and long-established shops. It suits an evening stroll and local food.

rows.name: Xiangshan Park
rows.summary: Xiangshan Park covers the southern slopes of Xiangshan, a hill on the northern edge of central Huaibei that was one of the eight views of old Suzhou prefecture. Among its 18 sights are Xiantong Temple, founded under the Jin dynasty (265–420) and with Qing buildings and 22 steles from the Song to the Qing, along with springs, caves, Yinma Pool and the Zouming Terrace. During the Huaihai Campaign of 1948 the Communist commander Su Yu held a meeting of senior officers at the temple.

rows.name: Anfengtang Reservoir (Quebei)
rows.summary: Anfengtang, known in antiquity as Quebei, is an irrigation reservoir in southern Shou County that tradition attributes to Sunshu Ao, chief minister of the state of Chu in the Spring and Autumn period, although some scholars argue it is no older than the Han. Still in use, it was rebuilt in 1978 and holds about 67 million m³ of water. A memorial hall to Sunshu Ao stands in Anfengtang town.

rows.name: Anhui Chu Culture Museum (Shou County Museum)
rows.summary: Shou County's museum, founded in 1958, reopened in 2022 in a new 15,000 m² building as the Anhui Chu Culture Museum, inside the Shouchun City National Archaeological Site Park on the site of the capital the state of Chu moved to in 241 BC. Displays include Chu bronzes, a pile of 158 Chu gold coins, a bronze sword of a king of Yue and a recreated chariot-pit excavation. Visitors enter along a 40-metre glass walkway over a layer of Warring States roof-tile rubble found during building work.

rows.name: Bagong Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A range of some 40 low peaks between Huainan and Shou County, named after the 'Eight Gentlemen' of the Western Han prince Liu An, who compiled the Huainanzi here and, by legend, invented tofu; the Battle of Fei River of 383 was fought below them. The scenic area on the Huainan side, a national forest park and national geopark, has a geological museum on the area's ancient fossils, including the 'Huainan worm', the White Pagoda Temple, the Huainan King's Palace, an immortals' terrace and a stone forest.

rows.name: Datong Wanrenkeng Memorial Hall (Huainan Japanese Occupation Sites)
