rows.summary: A memorial hall in Huainan's Datong coal-mining district built at the Wanrenkeng ('ten-thousand-person pits'), three trenches on the northern foot of Shungeng Mountain that hold the remains of more than 10,000 miners and resistance fighters who died under the Japanese occupation of the Datong mines. Together with eight nearby sites built in 1938–41, including blockhouses, water dungeons, a miners' temple and the Japanese headquarters and ammunition depot, it was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and as a national war memorial site in 2014. The memorial site covers about 31,000 m², with some 2,400 m² of exhibition rooms.

rows.name: Jiaogang Lake Film and Television Base
rows.summary: A large outdoor film set beside Jiaogang Lake, built as a backlot of walled mansions, farm courtyards, an old railway station and locomotive, trenches, an old hospital, a people's commune hall and dormitories for 'sent-down' youth. Parts of the CCTV drama Six Sisters were filmed here, and on holidays the base stages short live shows in its streets during the day and fire performances in the evening.

rows.name: Jiaogang Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A lake of about 40 km² on the north side of the Huai River in Huainan's Maoji district, cut off from the river by embankments in the 1950s and now a national wetland park and water-conservancy scenic area. Visitors boat through reed beds and lotus ponds, fish, and watch birds such as common cranes, and lakeside restaurants serve local salted duck eggs and wine-lees fish.

rows.name: Longhu Park, Huainan
rows.summary: Huainan's oldest public park, laid out around a lake in Tianjia'an District from 1957 and opened in 1980. Rebuilt in 2008, it has quiet garden areas, a waterfront, boating on the lake, a small animal and plant garden, children's rides and a food area, and is a pleasant stop for an hour or two in the city.

rows.name: Shangyao National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 30 wooded hills and 10.4 km² in Huainan's Datong District, near Shangyao town, one of the centres of the Tang-dynasty Shouzhou kilns. Paths lead to the Buddhist Dongshan Temple, a Ksitigarbha hall, a release pond and the exhibition hall of a New Fourth Army memorial forest.

rows.name: Shou County Confucius Temple
rows.summary: The Confucian temple of Shou County stands on West Street inside the walled old town, a complex of Ming and Qing buildings that includes the Dacheng Hall and a Kuixing Pavilion, with old ginkgo trees in its courtyards. Until the new Anhui Chu Culture Museum opened in 2022, the county museum occupied buildings just south of the temple.

rows.name: Shou County Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque in Qingzhensi ('Mosque') Lane inside the walled old town of Shou County, whose surviving buildings date from the Ming and Qing dynasties. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 together with the town's Confucius Temple and is open to visitors.

rows.name: Shou County Old Town and City Wall
rows.summary: Shou County's old town, the Shouchun of history and the last capital of the state of Chu, is still ringed by its city wall, rebuilt in the Southern Song with bricks stamped 'Jiankang' that can still be seen. All four gates, Binyang (east), Tongfei (south), Dinghu (west) and Jinghuai (north), keep their barbican enclosures, and the wall held back the Huai River floods of 1991 while the town sheltered refugees. Inside are the Confucius Temple, a Ming–Qing mosque and Bao'en Temple, and the low Bagong hills rise just north of the town.

rows.name: Bao Ancestral Hall, Fancun
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Bao clan in Fancun village, Shangfeng township, completed in 1787 in the Qianlong era of the Qing. It survives intact and was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Bei'an Covered Bridge and Wu Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: Bei'an village in eastern Shexian has two national heritage sites side by side: a mid-Qing covered bridge of three stone arches, 33 m long, roofed over with an eleven-bay gallery with benches, window openings and a small shrine, and the Wu clan's Zhide Hall. The ancestral hall, founded in 1622, rebuilt in the late Qianlong era and enlarged in 1826, is three halls deep.

rows.name: Changqing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey square brick-and-timber pagoda 23.1 m high, built in 1119 in the Northern Song at the foot of Xigan Hill on the south bank of the Lian River, facing the old town of Shexian; it is regarded as the oldest surviving pagoda in old Huizhou. The temple it was named after has gone, but the pagoda, standing in front of the present Taiping Xingguo Temple, keeps its Song form, with a gallery round the base, stone lotus thrones in its arched doorways and painted Buddhas on its walls.

rows.name: Changxi Village
rows.summary: An old village in south-eastern Shexian, founded in the Tang and home to the Wu clan since the Southern Song, which in Ming and Qing times was known as the first village of southern She and was filled with buildings paid for by its merchants. Two of its ancestral halls are national heritage: the Taihu Hall, whose main and rear halls were completed in 1579 and 1599, faces a large square where opera is staged at festivals, and the Yuangong branch hall of the Jiaqing era (1796–1820) stands behind a square pond and a wooden gateway.

rows.name: Cheng Ancestral Hall, Xingcun
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Cheng clan in Xingcun village, Gantang town, on the north side of the Huangshan range, first built in the Ming and rebuilt in the late Qing. Its entrance hall, main hall and rear shrine hall run 58.6 m deep and 22.3 m wide over about 1,300 m².

rows.name: Chengkan Village
rows.summary: A village of the Luo clan in a basin ringed by hills beside the Zhongchuan stream, laid out on feng shui principles, with more than 120 Ming and Qing houses along three streets and 99 lanes; 49 of its buildings, including houses, ancestral halls, shops, watchtowers and bridges, are national heritage. Its centrepiece is the Luo Dongshu Ancestral Hall, begun in the Jiajing era and completed in the Wanli era on a plan modelled on a Confucian temple, with the Baolun Pavilion at the rear. Chengkan is a core part of the Ancient Huizhou Culture Tourism Zone.

rows.name: Choushu Memorial Archways
rows.summary: Four stone memorial archways at the entrance to Choushu, a village of the Wang clan of merchants in Zhengcun town, built between 1628 and the 1770s. They honour a father and son who both held office, three generations of a family, and two widows' chastity.

rows.name: Daguling Gorge
rows.summary: A deep wooded gorge on the Dagu stream in Meixi township, in the mountains of Yi county, where a path climbs through bamboo forest past clear pools such as the Fairy Pool, a 'water-curtain cave' behind a falling spring and the three-tiered Sandie waterfall. Steep boardwalks lead on to a pavilion on the ridge at about 1,200 m, where visitors beat a drum that echoes round the valley.

rows.name: Dengfeng Bridge
rows.summary: A nine-arch stone bridge 148 m long across the Heng River at the northern foot of Mount Qiyun, on the old walking route up the Taoist mountain. First built in 1587 at the urging of the Huizhou prefect Gu Zhixian and rebuilt in its present form in 1791, it has a stone gateway at each end, of which the southern one is original.

rows.name: East Huangshan Resort (Huangshan Tea Farm)
rows.summary: A resort area on the Huangshan Tea Farm at Tanjiaqiao, a state farm that has been run by Shanghai since 1965 and to which large numbers of young people from Shanghai were sent to work in the 1960s and 1970s. Since 2003 Shanghai's Bright Food group has turned the farm into a tourist area with hotels and tea gardens, and its 'educated youth town' recreates Shanghai lanes and shikumen-style houses, with themes drawn from the farm's sent-down past, Shanghai culture and tea.

rows.name: Emerald Valley
rows.summary: A wooded valley in Shancha village below the eastern side of Huangshan, whose stream runs through a chain of clear green pools and small waterfalls. Also called Lovers' Valley after a group of 36 young Shanghai hikers who were stranded here in 1986, it was a filming location for 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon' and hosts the Huangshan Qixi (Chinese Valentine's Day) festival each summer.

rows.name: Former New Fourth Army Headquarters, Yansi
rows.summary: The Jin family compound at 22 Yinshan Road in Yansi, used as headquarters by the Communist-led New Fourth Army in the spring of 1938, when guerrilla units from eight southern provinces gathered here to be reorganised before moving to the front against Japan; the commanders Ye Ting and Xiang Ying lived in two of its three houses. A memorial museum stands across the lane from the compound, and the site also takes in the Ming Hongqiao covered bridge, beside which the army's code office worked, and the Ming Wenfeng Pagoda and Fengshan platform, where troops drilled and were reviewed.

rows.name: Former Seat of the Anhui–Zhejiang–Jiangxi Provincial Committee, Shiwukeng
rows.name_zh: 中共皖浙赣省委驻地旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Wǎn Zhè Gàn Shěngwěi Zhùdì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A three-storey house in Shiwukeng village, Wangcun town, in the hills of south-western Xiuning, which housed the Chinese Communist Party's Anhui–Zhejiang–Jiangxi provincial committee from its founding in April 1936 until it left in January 1937. The building was repaired in 2014 and listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Furong Valley
rows.summary: A forested gorge on the northern side of Huangshan, where a stream runs through bamboo groves past a chain of green pools and waterfalls. Alongside the natural scenery the valley has been fitted out with family attractions, including a 500 m glass water slide, a 2,170 m mountain coaster, a 400 m zip line and a 'sky mirror' viewing platform looking towards the Huangshan peaks.

rows.name: Guchengyan
rows.summary: A wooded rise beside the Heng River on the eastern edge of Wan'an town, with a Ming pagoda of the early Jiajing era (1520s), where since 1999 old buildings from around Xiuning county that could not be preserved where they stood have been moved and rebuilt. It now holds four stone memorial archways, six Ming and Qing houses, two ancestral halls and two other buildings, among them the Gulin double-chastity archway of 1730 and the hall of the Huang clan.

rows.name: Guniujiang: Guanyintang (Qimen side)
rows.summary: The Qimen entrance to Guniujiang, a forested range on the border of Qimen and Shitai counties that continues the Huangshan mountains westwards, rising to 1,727.6 m and protected as a nature reserve since 1982, now a national nature reserve of about 67 km². Of the five scenic areas usually listed for the range, Guanyintang is the only one in Qimen; the other four are reached from Shitai county in Chizhou.

rows.name: Hong Ancestral Hall (Jingben Hall), Yecun
rows.summary: The Jingben Hall, a branch ancestral hall of the Hong clan in Yecun village, Sanyang, founded in 1554 and repaired in 1807 and 1897. Five bays wide and three halls deep, it is entered through a carved brick gate tower and keeps a series of honorific boards in its two-storey rear shrine hall.

rows.name: Hong Ancestral Hall, Sanyang
rows.summary: A large Ming and Qing ancestral hall of the Hong clan, a lineage of merchants, in Sanyang town in the hills of north-eastern Shexian. It is three halls deep and was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Hong Family Mansion, Qimen
rows.summary: A Huizhou mansion on East Street in Qishan, the Qimen county town, begun in 1844, whose four linked halls cover more than 1,200 m². In 1860, during the war against the Taiping rebels, the Qing commander Zeng Guofan made it his headquarters, and Taiping troops who took Qimen in 1862 left writing on a wall of its Chengze Hall.

rows.name: Hongkeng Archways and Hong Family Temple
rows.name_zh: 洪坑牌坊群及洪氏家庙
rows.pinyin: Hóngkēng Páifāng Qún jí Hóngshì Jiāmiào
rows.summary: Four surviving stone memorial archways, of an original seven, in Hongkeng village, Yansi town: two record the Hong clan's examination successes, among them the Shike archway erected in 1498, which lists 21 graduates down to the top scholar of 1809, and two honour widows' chastity. Beside them stands the Ming family temple of the Hong clan, a branch hall founded by Hong Yuan, a minister of works in Nanjing.

rows.name: Huashan Mysterious Grottoes
rows.summary: A group of 36 large man-made caverns cut into the hills on the south bank of the Jian (Xin'an) River on the eastern edge of Tunxi, unrecorded in any historical source until they were found by chance in 2000. Stalactites inside are more than 1,700 years old, so the caves were dug no later than the Jin dynasty, but who made them and why is still unknown; some are held up by rows of stone pillars like underground halls, while others wind back to green pools.

rows.name: Huizhou Ancient City (Shexian)
rows.summary: The old town of Shexian (Huicheng), seat of Huizhou prefecture from the Song to the Qing, and the core of the Ancient Huizhou Culture Tourism Zone, whose other parts are Tangyue, Tangmo, Chengkan and the Qiankou Ming houses. At its centre stands the Xu Guo Archway of 1584, an eight-legged stone memorial arch covered in carving, built for the grand secretary Xu Guo, close to the gate towers of the old prefectural yamen. Nearby Doushan Street, a flagstone lane about 500 m long, is lined with the high walls and gateways of Qing merchants' and officials' mansions.

rows.name: Jinshi Hall, Huangcun
rows.summary: A Ming hall, also called the Huang family hall, built in 1532 by the Huang clan of Huangcun in Shangshan town to honour Huang Fu, who passed the palace examination in 1529. About 790 m² in area, it runs four sections deep through a gate tower, gatehouse, sacrificial hall and two-storey rear hall.

rows.name: Lixi Village
rows.summary: An old village in Likou town in northern Qimen, founded in the Southern Tang among tea hills on the Shunxi stream, which rises on the Guniujiang mountains. A bamboo grove, an old bridge and a grove of old trees with an ancient camphor mark the village entrance; the Heyi Hall and the village's other Ming and Qing buildings are protected at provincial level, and a gorge, the Lixi Grand Canyon, lies nearby.

rows.name: Liyang in Lane
rows.summary: A leisure quarter on the old Liyang street across the Heng River from Tunxi Old Street, redeveloped between 2007 and 2013 around the original street plan and about ten restored Huizhou houses, with new buildings around them. It is filled with bookshops, guesthouses, bars and craft workshops, and in 2022 it was named one of China's first national tourist and leisure quarters.

rows.name: Mount Qiyun
rows.summary: One of China's four sacred mountains of Taoism, a range of red sandstone (Danxia) cliffs and peaks rising to 585 m west of Huangshan city, where Taoist worship goes back to 758–760 and flourished in the Ming around the cult of Zhenwu, the Perfected Warrior. Paths lead past caves, cliff-side temples and shrines, and the mountain holds 305 cliff inscriptions and 232 stone tablets from the Northern Song onwards, the largest a tablet 7.6 m high below the Yuxu Palace inscribed by the Ming painter Tang Yin.

rows.name: Nanping Village
rows.summary: A village of the Ye clan at the foot of a hill west of the Yi county town, founded in the Northern Song, that keeps more than 300 Ming and Qing buildings, eight of them ancestral halls. Seven of its buildings are national heritage, including the Ye clan's Xuzhi Hall, the Ming Kuiguang branch hall, the Cheng clan hall, the Yinan Villa and the Bingling Pavilion.

rows.name: Nine Dragon Waterfall
rows.summary: A waterfall described as the largest at Huangshan, which drops 360 m in nine stages over a 600 m course from the cliffs of Xianglu Peak into a U-shaped valley on the eastern side of the mountain, forming nine cascades and nine pools. The last and largest fall is 120 m high and more than 20 m wide, and its Xixi stream valley is a place to paddle in summer.

rows.name: Old Opera Stages of Qimen
rows.summary: A group of eleven opera stages built into clan ancestral halls in the villages of Xin'an township and Shanli town in western Qimen, dating from the late Ming to 1927. The oldest, in the Chen clan's Huiyuan Hall at Kengkou (1587), collapsed in a fire in 2013 and has been rebuilt on its site, while the Dundian Hall stage at neighbouring Pancun dates from the 1860s.

rows.name: Pan Ancestral Hall, Dafu
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Pan clan in Dafu village, Bei'an town, built in 1585 in the late Ming and preserved intact. It is three halls deep and noted for its imposing scale and for fine wood and brick carving.

rows.name: Pingshan Village
rows.summary: A village of the Shu clan on the Jiyang stream north-east of the Yi county town, settled at the end of the Tang, that keeps more than 200 Ming and Qing houses. Its two linked clan halls, the Qing Shu Guangyu Hall in front and the Ming Shu Qingyu Hall behind, are entered through a rare seven-eaved gate tower said to have been permitted by the Chongzhen emperor to honour a loyal official of the clan.

rows.name: Qiankou Ming Houses
rows.summary: An open-air museum of Ming-dynasty Huizhou architecture on a hillside at Qiankou, where about ten fine buildings that could not be kept safely in their home villages were taken down and re-erected from 1984 onwards. Houses, ancestral halls, a roadside pavilion and a stone archway are laid out like a traditional village, and the site is one of the five parts of the Ancient Huizhou Culture Tourism Zone.

rows.name: Sanhuai Hall, Xitou
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Wang clan in Xitou village, Haiyang town, founded by Wang Jingtian in 1602 in the late Ming. It was once three halls deep and eleven bays wide, but its rear hall was pulled down in the 1950s; the two surviving halls, about 900 m², are joined by a large open courtyard with smaller courtyards in the side wings.

rows.name: Shuyuan Memorial Archways
rows.summary: Three stone memorial archways at the entrance to Shuyuan village, Qiankou town: the Zanxian archway of the Jiajing era (1522–1566) honouring Bao Zhen, a 'centenarian' archway of 1742 for a woman who lived from 1644 to 1744, and a chastity archway of 1775. They are one of several archway groups in the countryside between Qiankou and Shexian, with those at Tangyue and Choushu.

rows.name: Taiping Bridge, Shexian
rows.summary: A 16-arch stone bridge 268 m long across the Lian River outside the west gate of the old Huizhou prefectural town, described as the largest old stone bridge in Anhui. Built in stone in the Hongzhi era (1488–1505) on the site of a 1234 pontoon bridge and rebuilt several times under the Qing, it lost its stone deck in a 1969 flood and was given a concrete one. The Taibai Pavilion and the Xin'an stele garden stand at its western end.

rows.name: Taiping Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake formed in 1970 by damming the Qingyi River, winding between forested hills in Huangshan district over about 88 km²; it was Anhui's first national wetland park. Boat trips run on the lake, and the lakeside resort area has a water park with motorboats, kart boats and kayaks.

rows.name: Tangmo Village and Tangan Garden
rows.summary: A village in Qiankou town threaded by the Tangan stream, with old trees, small bridges, pavilions and archways, and one of the five parts of the Ancient Huizhou Culture Tourism Zone. Its Tangan Garden, made in the early Qing by a wealthy merchant as a miniature of Hangzhou's West Lake for his mother, has a pavilion in the lake set with marble tablets of calligraphy by 18 masters of the Song to the Qing, among them Su Shi, Mi Fu and Dong Qichang, and nearby stand the octagonal Shadi pavilion, the Tongbao Hanlin archway and the Gaoyang covered bridge.

rows.name: Tangyue Memorial Archways
rows.summary: Seven stone memorial archways, built between 1420 and 1820, stand in a line on the approach to Tangyue, the home village of the Bao clan, merchants in Ming and Qing times, honouring filial piety, widows' chastity, charity and high office. Beside them are the Bao clan's Dunben Hall and the Qingyi Hall, an ancestral hall for the clan's women, and the village keeps a dozen listed old buildings. The large Bao Family Garden, destroyed in the Taiping war and rebuilt in 2002, is visited with the archways as one part of the Ancient Huizhou Culture Tourism Zone.

rows.name: Three Houses of the Cheng Family
rows.summary: Three Ming-dynasty houses of the Cheng family at Nos. 6, 7 and 28 Baishu Dongli Lane in Tunxi, the oldest begun at the end of the Yuan or start of the Ming. Each is a closed two-storey brick-and-timber house of two halls around a light well, with wood, brick and stone carving typical of Ming Huizhou homes; the older houses around them were cleared in 2007, and they now stand amid a new shopping street in old style.

rows.name: Tong'an Hall, Xiuning
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty Huizhou merchant's house at 152 Qining Street in Haiyang, the county town of Xiuning, preserved intact with five halls set one behind another. It covers about 1,300 m² and is known for the quality of its brick and wood carving.

rows.name: Wu Ancestral Halls, Shitan
rows.summary: Two ancestral halls of the Wu clan in Shitan, a hillside village of Xiakeng town in eastern Shexian: the Xulun Hall, a Ming hall rebuilt in the Qing with five bays, three halls and a 'hundred-beam' hall, and the Qing-dynasty Chunhui branch hall. Both are known for delicate carving, and the village is popular with photographers for its seas of cloud and summer flower fields.

rows.name: Xiangyuan Keemun Tea Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 祥源祁红产业文化博览园
rows.summary: A tea park devoted to Keemun (Qimen) black tea on the eastern edge of the Qimen county town, built by the Xiangyuan group in new Huizhou-style buildings. It combines a Keemun tea museum of seven halls, a demonstration factory whose production lines can be watched from walkways, a centre where visitors can try hand-making the tea, and a garden of tea varieties; the park is a stop on the county's 'red and black' tea route launched in 2024.

rows.name: Xieyuda Tea Culture Museum
rows.summary: The museum of Xieyuda, a producer of Huangshan Maofeng green tea that takes its name from the Shanghai tea house of the 19th-century Huizhou merchant Xie Zheng'an, set in the company's tea expo park at Qiankou. Its displays trace the history of Huangshan Maofeng and of Huizhou's tea merchants, and the surrounding park has tea gardens of nearly 2,000 mu (about 130 hectares) and a rainbow slide.

rows.name: Xin'an River Scenic Gallery
rows.summary: A stretch of the Xin'an River of roughly 50 km through southern Shexian, between steep green hills dotted with Huizhou villages and old wharves, usually seen on boat trips from Shendu. Stops along the way include thousand-year-old camphor trees and the river villages of Jiusha and Miantan, and the banks are bright with rapeseed and azaleas in spring and with coloured leaves in autumn.

rows.name: Xin'an Riverside, Tunxi
rows.summary: A stretch of the Xin'an River on the eastern side of Tunxi whose banks, once lined with wharves, have been landscaped as riverside parks for walking. Boat trips run on the river, including evening cruises to see the waterfront and the lit-up bridges.

rows.name: Xiongcun Village and Zhushan Academy
rows.summary: A village of the Cao clan on the Jian River in southern Shexian, listed as a national historic and cultural village in 2014. Its main sight is the Zhushan Academy, founded beside the river in 1755, with an octagonal pavilion, a Wenchang pavilion and halls over about 2,000 m², and the village also keeps a group of five stone archways, several old houses and the Taohua embankment along the river.

rows.name: Xixinan Village
rows.summary: An old village on the Fengle River, founded in 860, that was home to the Wu clan of salt merchants, who filled it with houses, gardens and halls; most were lost in fighting in 1856, but more than 100 Ming and Qing buildings remain along three old streets and three channelled streams. Its national heritage sites are the Laowu Pavilion, a mid-Ming two-storey house whose upper hall was the main living floor, and the Lürao Pavilion, a square roadside pavilion by a pond rebuilt in 1456, and beside the village a wetland grove of Chinese wingnut trees stretches for about 4 km.

rows.name: Xu Ancestral Hall (Dunmu Hall), Jincun
rows.summary: The Dunmu Hall, ancestral hall of the Xu clan in Jincun village, Xucun town, built in 1536 in the Ming dynasty. It is three halls deep, and its beams and columns carry extensive Huizhou painted decoration in the 'wrapped brocade' style; the front two halls were restored in 2014.

rows.name: Xucun Old Village
rows.summary: A large old village of the Xu clan in north-western Shexian, where close to 200 Ming and Qing buildings, among them memorial archways, pavilions, a covered bridge, ancestral halls and houses, line an old street about 1.5 km long. Fifteen of them form a national heritage group, including the Gaoyang covered bridge, the Wuma archway and the Dabangbo ancestral hall, the last two restored in 2008–09.

rows.name: Yuliang Dam and Old Street
rows.summary: An ancient stone weir about 140 m long across the Lian River just south-east of Shexian town, first built in the Tang and rebuilt in 1605 from massive blocks locked together with stone dowels. It raised the river for boats, making Yuliang the main point from which Ming and Qing Huizhou merchants set out by water for Zhejiang and Jiangsu. Beside it runs Yuliang Street, a cobbled street of old houses and shops with lanes down to the wharves, where the Ming–Qing house of the salt-merchant family of the Qing seal carver Ba Weizu, the largest old residence in the village, was restored and opened as a museum.

rows.name: Zheng Ancestral Hall, Zhengcun
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Zheng clan in Zhengcun town, founded in the Chenghua era (around 1466) in memory of the late-Yuan recluse and Neo-Confucian scholar Zheng Yu. Covering 1,867 m² behind a richly carved four-pillar gateway, it is regarded as the largest ancestral hall in Shexian.

rows.name: Zhenhai Bridge
rows.summary: A seven-arch stone bridge, 133 m long, across the Heng River at the western end of Tunxi Old Street, near where the Shuai and Heng rivers meet to form the Xin'an, linking the old town with Liyang on the far bank. Recorded by 1491 and rebuilt in 1699, it was swept away by a flash flood in July 2020; its stones were salvaged and the restored bridge reopened in December 2021.

rows.name: Zhou Ancestral Hall, Changxi
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Zhou clan, also called Liushun Hall, in the hamlet of Zhoubangtou on the edge of Changxi in south-eastern Shexian. Built in the Daoguang era (1821–1850), it is five bays wide and three halls deep, with an entrance hall, a sacrificial hall and a rear shrine hall.

rows.name: Anhui Dream Ocean World
rows.summary: Anhui Dream Ocean World is a commercial indoor aquarium of about 10,000 m² in the Zhedong trade centre in central Lu'an, opened by private investors as a marine-life exhibition and science-education venue. It suits families with children looking for a couple of hours indoors.

rows.name: Baimajian (Main Peak of the Dabie Mountains)
rows.summary: Baimajian, at 1,777 m the highest summit of the Dabie Mountains, rises in the far south-west of Huoshan County inside the Dabie Mountains nature reserve. The 4A Dabie Main Peak scenic area, a unit of the Dabie Mountains (Lu'an) National Geopark, also takes in the Longjing gorge, the Siwangbao lookout and Biehu Lake.

rows.name: Dabieshan Fengqing Valley
rows.summary: Fengqing Valley is a forested valley scenic area in Hongshan village, next to the Dabieshan Grottoes, with a narrow rock cleft, waterfalls dropping into a lake, a stream with sandy banks, bamboo groves and a stand of nanmu trees. Local curiosities include coffins wedged in cliff crevices, old cave dwellings and the ruins of Taiping stockade, and an opera stage puts on Lu opera and local folk songs. It makes a summer outing for walkers from Lu'an.

rows.name: Dabieshan Grottoes Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Dabieshan Grottoes are natural rock shelters and caves, not carved shrines, in a wooded scenic area with a 15 km² core in Hongshan village, part of the Dabie Mountains (Lu'an) National Geopark. The best known, Changyan Cave, was shaped by water, weathering and rockfall; other curiosities are coffins set in cliff niches, old cave dwellings and the ruins of earthen hill forts. The Tianfo Chan Temple, a late-Yuan foundation once called Jiulong Tang whose ruins remain on the summit of Hongshanzhai, has been rebuilt with a gate hall, a Heavenly Kings hall and a main hall.

rows.name: Dawan Village
rows.summary: Dawan is a tea-growing mountain village in Huashi township whose 2.5 km² scenic area combines tea gardens, farm guesthouses and a group of twelve ancient sandalwood trees with sites of the revolutionary period. Preserved buildings include the former office of the Communist Party's Anhui Provincial Work Committee and the former local soviet government and clinic. A folk museum displays Dabie farming tools, household goods and costume, and the village runs a rafting route.

rows.name: Dongshisun Scenic Area
rows.summary: Dongshisun is a hill scenic area south of Maotanchang town whose slopes are built of stacked slabs of metamorphic rock, rising to just over 760 m. Its namesake is a free-standing rock pillar about 38 m tall, left where two faults meet and the surrounding rock collapsed. Paths lead past waterfalls, quartz-strewn slopes, pavilions and a small temple.

rows.name: Dushan Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: Dushan is a market town in the Dabie foothills where a Communist-led uprising broke out in 1929, in the years when the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet base was being formed. Along its old street, now branded 'Soviet City', a group of buildings including the uprising's headquarters is preserved and presented as a museum complex. Together with separate sites in Jinzhai County farther west, it forms part of the national heritage listing for the former Hubei–Henan–Anhui revolutionary base area.

rows.name: Foziling Reservoir
rows.summary: Foziling Reservoir on the upper East Pi River was built between 1952 and 1954 as the first large water-conservancy and hydropower project of the People's Republic, and is officially called the 'first dam of New China'. Its 74.4 m reinforced-concrete multiple-arch dam, designed by the hydraulic engineer Wang Huzhen, was the first of its kind in China and is now a national heritage site. The scenic area around the lake includes hill outlines known as the 'Reclining Buddha' and 'Sleeping Beauty', a resort and rafting on the East Pi River.

rows.name: Hengpaitou Headworks
rows.summary: Hengpaitou, on the Pi River at Subu town, is the head of the Pi River main canal of the Pishihang irrigation district, a large scheme serving farmland in Anhui and Henan. The scenic area takes in the canal head on the river and the tree-lined canal that runs about 20 km north to Lu'an, with water views and pleasure boats. Subu, an old market town known for its food, lies next to it.

rows.name: Huoshan Grand Canyon Rafting
rows.summary: The Huoshan Grand Canyon is a rafting and adventure area on the Kongque River, where an 8 km run drops 160 m in total, with a largest single drop of 19 m, over smooth patterned rock beds between bamboo-covered slopes. Other attractions are the Baiyunxia waterfalls, the Feiyun glass suspension bridge, 188 m long and 108 m above the valley, and a slide through bamboo forest. Rafting runs in the summer season only.

rows.name: Jinzhai Red Army Square
rows.summary: Red Army Square in Jinzhai county town is a memorial park on the county's revolutionary history, laid out around a monument tower to revolutionary martyrs. It brings together the Jinzhai County Revolution Museum, a Red Army martyrs' cemetery, a Red Army memorial hall and a monument to General Hong Xuezhi. Jinzhai is known in China as a 'county of generals' for the many army generals born here.

rows.name: Jiugongzhai
rows.summary: Jiugongzhai is a wooded hill in Shibanchong township, counted among the eight traditional sights of Lu'an and long associated with Buddhism. Legend says Emperor Wu of Liang built a temple here with materials supplied by nine elders from the villages below, which gave the hill its name ('Stockade of the Nine Elders'). Paths climb past Buddhist statue plazas, Gaofeng Temple, boulders such as Chessboard Rock and a waterfall.

rows.name: Li Family Manor
rows.summary: The Li Family Manor, also called Lijiawei, is a moated landlord's estate begun in 1856 by the Li clan, who by the late Qing held land across western Anhui and neighbouring Henan. Built over ten years in the moated-compound style of the Jianghuai region, it once had more than 430 rooms; only the western compound survives, restored in two phases from 2008, and a third phase of repairs was contracted in 2025. It is officially described as one of China's four great landlord manors.

rows.name: Linhuaigang Flood Control Project
rows.summary: Linhuaigang is a flood-control scheme on the Huai River, described by the Lu'an government as the largest water-control project on the river, with a main dam, auxiliary dams, a diversion channel, a ship lock and sluices stretching some 78 km across the river plain north of Huoqiu. The scenic area built around it includes the main dam and a 49-bay sluice, an exhibition hall and a monument square on Huai River control, as well as wetlands and an old course of the river.

rows.name: Liuwan Qingxia Gorge Park
rows.summary: Liuwan Qingxia is a commercial leisure complex built around a wooded gorge in Luoerling town, rated 4A in 2025 and themed partly on the area's anti-Japanese war history. It combines a film-set town in Republican-era style, a children's activity zone, a gorge walk and a viewpoint at Longtou Rock with rides such as a glass water slide, a dry slide through bamboo, zip lines and boat trips, plus a staged show, 'Legend of the Dabie Mountains'. It suits families and groups looking for activities rather than quiet scenery.

rows.name: Longjin Xidi Gorge
rows.summary: Longjin Xidi is a gorge scenic area about 8.5 km long in the hills of Quanjun township, developed by a private tourism company across the river from Xijiuhua Shan in Henan. A trail follows the valley past three pools, six waterfalls and named rocks and peaks, and a small sightseeing train runs through bamboo forest. A hotel and an outdoor-activity base stand near the entrance.

rows.name: Meishan Reservoir
rows.summary: Meishan Reservoir on the upper Shi River is one of the large reservoirs built to control the Huai River, supplying flood control, power and water for 3.83 million mu of farmland in Anhui and Henan. The old town of Jinjiazhai, which gave Jinzhai County its name, lies beneath the lake, and the present county town sits beside the dam. A national water-conservancy scenic area since 2004, the lake can be toured by passenger boat from a pier that opened in 2026.

rows.name: Nanyue Shan
rows.summary: Nanyue Shan is a 405 m hill rising 2.5 km south of Huoshan county town, steep on its southern face and gently sloping to the north. Over the centuries it has been known by several names, among them Tianzhu Shan, Huo Shan, Hengshan and 'Little Nanyue' (Little Southern Peak), and together with Foziling Reservoir it forms a provincial scenic area.

rows.name: Tiantangzhai
rows.summary: Tiantangzhai, at 1,729 m the second-highest peak of the Dabie Mountains, stands on the Anhui–Hubei border on the watershed between the Huai and Yangtze rivers. The Anhui side is a national forest park of about 120 km², with peaks such as Baima Peak, forest cover of over 95 per cent and more than ten waterfalls along its stream valleys. A site linked to the Communist army's 1947 advance into the Dabie Mountains is also marked in the area.

rows.name: Tongluozhai
rows.summary: Tongluozhai is a steep, isolated peak of 1,096 m in the heart of the Dabie Mountains, within a 92 km² scenic area of pine-clad crags and oddly shaped rocks. Below it the Tongluo gorge runs for about 7 km past sheer cliffs, deep pools and waterfalls, with traces of an old plank road and of temples and houses. Its name ('Bronze Gong Stockade') comes from a legend that Emperor Wu of Han dreamed of the moon turning into a gong and falling onto the mountain.

rows.name: Wanfo Lake
rows.summary: Wanfo Lake is the scenic name of Longhekou Reservoir, built by around 100,000 labourers mobilised from across Shucheng County from 1958 and largely finished in 1970 as a flood-control and irrigation source for the Pishihang irrigation district. The lake covers about 50 km² of a 135 km² scenic area, with wooded islands such as Zhouyu Island, the long earth dam, a reservoir memorial hall and the Longhe Pagoda. Boat trips between the islands and lakeside resorts make it a popular weekend escape from Hefei.

rows.name: Wanfo Mountain
rows.summary: Wanfo Mountain is a forested range in south-western Shucheng County, a national forest park and geopark of about 50 km² whose main peak, Laofoding, reaches 1,539 m. Trails climb past dozens of named peaks and rock formations, and the Jiutan valley holds a string of pools and waterfalls. Lesser sights include a small temple near the summit, a cave linked by legend to the monk Kim Gyo-gak before he went to Jiuhua Shan, and the site of a Red Army hospital.

rows.name: Wanxi Grand Rift Valley
rows.summary: The Wanxi Grand Rift is a deep V-shaped cleft through a wooded hill in Taipingqiao village, part of the Dabie Mountains (Lu'an) National Geopark. Visitors scramble up the gorge floor between mossy cliff walls, using hands and feet to squeeze through three points so narrow that only one person can pass sideways. A rock shelter in the gorge is linked by local tradition with the late-Ming rebel leader Zhang Xianzhong, who is said to have camped his troops here.

rows.name: Wanxi Museum
rows.summary: The Wanxi Museum is Lu'an's city museum, founded in 1980, whose present Hui-style building opened in 2011 and partly reopened in August 2025 after a refit. The main exhibition, renamed 'Into Lu'an', traces the region's history through bronzes, ceramics, burial customs and the revolutionary period, with a section on Gao Yao, the legendary judge associated with Lu'an. Smaller galleries are devoted to Lu opera and local folk customs.

rows.name: Xianghongdian Reservoir
rows.summary: Xianghongdian Reservoir on the West Pi River was built between 1956 and 1958 behind an 87.5 m concrete gravity-arch dam for flood control, irrigation and power, and is a main source of the Pishihang irrigation district. The long, winding lake between steep wooded hills is navigable for more than 20 km and is promoted locally as western Anhui's 'Little Guilin'; the dam and the lake views are the main sights.

rows.name: Yanzihe Grand Canyon
rows.summary: Yanzihe Grand Canyon is a forested gorge about 5.8 km long in Yanzihe town, adjoining the Tiantangzhai area and part of the Dabie Mountains geopark. A walking route follows the stream past pools, cliffs and waterfalls, with a suspension bridge and a sinkhole-like basin promoted as 'Tiankeng Fairyland'. A glass water slide nearly 2.1 km long, with a drop of 133 m, runs down the valley.

rows.name: Youran Lanxi Resort
rows.summary: Youran Lanxi is a large resort complex in Sanshipu town built by the Xingmao property group, laid out round a lake with new Chinese-style buildings, gardens, a big fountain square and stone-inscription galleries. Its themed zones are loosely based on the 'five rites' associated with Gao Yao, the legendary judge linked with Lu'an. It has hotels, a children's play area and shopping and bar streets.

rows.name: Youran Nanshan Resort
rows.summary: Youran Nanshan is a sports and leisure resort in Zhongdian town built by a property developer, with Mediterranean-style buildings, hotels and inns. Its facilities include an 18-hole golf course in the hills and indoor halls for basketball, tennis, swimming, table tennis and badminton. It suits visitors wanting a sporty stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Baochan Mountain
rows.summary: Baochan Mountain, a wooded hill north-east of Hanshan county town, was once called Hua Shan and took its present name from the Tang monk Huibao, who built a hermitage at its foot and was buried here. In 1054 the statesman and writer Wang Anshi explored one of its caves and wrote the celebrated essay 'A Record of a Trip to Baochan Mountain', which made the hill widely known.

rows.name: Caishi Rock
rows.summary: Caishi Rock is the cliff-bound foot of Cuiluo Hill where it juts into the Yangtze on the south-western edge of Ma'anshan, counted first of the river's three famous rocks and long a strategic crossing, where Song forces led by Yu Yunwen defeated an invading Jin army in 1161. Legend says the poet Li Bai drowned here trying to embrace the moon's reflection, and the hill is dotted with memorials to him, among them the Qing-dynasty Taibai Tower, a national heritage site, a Li Bai memorial museum and his cenotaph. Other sights include Sanyuan Cave, the Lin Sanzhi art museum and viewpoints over the river.

rows.name: Daqingshan Wildlife World
rows.summary: Daqingshan Wildlife World is a commercial zoo and theme park of more than 2,000 mu in Taibai town, rated 4A in 2023, keeping over 3,000 animals of more than 200 species. Besides the animal exhibits it has a circus arena with staged shows, an outdoor-sports area, jungle adventure trails, an ice-and-snow hall and children's rides. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Dehuatang Chinese Antique Bed Museum
rows.summary: The Dehuatang museum in Ma'anshan's Yushan district is a private museum of traditional Chinese beds, displaying carved wooden beds, most of them from the Qing dynasty and the Republican era, with other old furniture in period room settings. It suits visitors interested in Chinese furniture and woodcarving and makes a short city stop.

rows.name: Jilong Mountain and Banyue Lake
rows.summary: Jilong Mountain is a forested hill of about 240 m in western He County, an outlier of the Dabie range with some 20,000 mu of woodland. Known as 'Little Jiuhua north of the Yangtze' and as the 42nd of the Taoist blessed places, it has a Taoist Sanqing Hall, the Sanhe altar, a 'Southern Gate of Heaven', a limestone cave and the Buddhist Fenglin Chan Temple. The rated scenic area also takes in Banyue Lake.

rows.name: Lingjiatan Site
rows.summary: Lingjiatan, on the north bank of the Yuxi River, was a large late-Neolithic settlement of about 3800–3300 BC with double moats, a ritual altar platform and a cemetery rich in jade. Now a national archaeological park, it has a site museum opened in May 2025 that shows about 1,100 objects, among them jade human figures, a jade eagle bearing an eight-pointed star, an engraved jade plaque and an 88 kg jade pig found on top of the so-called 'king's tomb', 07M23. Lingjiatan ranks with the Hongshan and Liangzhu cultures as one of the three great jade-working centres of prehistoric China.

rows.name: Putang National Holiday Park
rows.summary: Putang is an area of about 20 km² of wooded hills on Ma'anshan's eastern edge, now run as the Putang National Holiday Park, with 49 peaks, 53 small valleys and eight reservoirs. Its forests and bamboo groves hold tea gardens and old trees, among them a ginkgo more than 800 years old and an evergreen holly whose crown spreads over 200 m².

rows.name: Taihu Mountain
rows.summary: Taihu Mountain in southern Hanshan County is a wooded upland made up of the Taihushan National Forest Park, about 1,800 ha with 95% forest cover, and a deer park. A Buddhist centre since the Northern Song, it keeps a temple complex of long standing and is nicknamed 'Little Jiuhua north of the Yangtze'.

rows.name: Tomb of Li Bai
rows.summary: The Tang poet Li Bai, who died in Dangtu in 762, was reburied in 817 at the western foot of Qingshan (Green Hill), where his grave mound lies in a memorial garden with the Taibai Shrine. The shrine and some of the old inscriptions were destroyed in a Japanese air raid in 1938, and the tomb and shrine were restored from 1979. The tomb is the core of the Daqingshan Li Bai Culture Tourism Area, which also takes in the surrounding hills and rural-tourism villages such as Taohua.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhu Ran
rows.summary: This is the family burial ground of Zhu Ran (182–249), a general of the Eastern Wu state in the Three Kingdoms period, whose brick tomb, found in 1984, was the highest-ranking Wu burial excavated up to 2013. The brick chambers of his tomb and of a neighbouring family tomb can be seen in the site museum of the Three Kingdoms Zhu Ran Cultural Park. The tombs yielded more than 140 objects, over half of them painted lacquerware made in the Chengdu area, which fill a gap in surviving painting from the period.

rows.name: Xiangquan Hot Springs
rows.summary: Xiangquan is a small hot-spring town in He County whose warm spring has been used for bathing for centuries; legend says the Liang-dynasty crown prince Xiao Tong was cured of a skin complaint here. On the old street a public open-air spring pool is still used by local people, while a resort nearby has more than 50 landscaped pools, and Xiangquan Lake hosts dragon-boat races. Mutton noodles are the town's best-known dish.

rows.name: Caiwa Huaihai Campaign Headquarters Site
rows.summary: The village of Caiwa in Xiao county, headquarters of the East China Field Army during the Huaihai campaign of 1948–49, one of the decisive battles of the Chinese Civil War. The preserved buildings where the campaign's General Front Committee met are shown together with a memorial hall, and the only photograph of all five committee members together, Deng Xiaoping, Liu Bocheng, Chen Yi, Su Yu and Tan Zhenlin, was taken here.

rows.name: Dangshan Pear Tree King Scenic Area
rows.summary: Old pear orchards around Liangli village in Dangshan, the county that calls itself China's pear capital and the home of the Dangshan Su pear, centred on an ancient tree known as the 'Pear Tree King'. The orchards are busiest during the pear-blossom festival in late March and early April, when opera is staged among the trees, and at the pear-picking festival in early September. Farm-stays, a pear-wine workshop and an exhibition hall on northern Anhui farming life have been added nearby.

rows.name: Grand Canal, Sixian Section
rows.pinyin: Suí Táng Dà Yùnhé Sìxiàn Duàn
rows.summary: The only stretch of the Sui–Tang Grand Canal in Anhui that still carries water: 28 km of the Tongji Canal, dug in 605 to join the Yellow River to the Huai, winds through Si county, and the 5.8 km section north-east of the county town is part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site inscribed in 2014. A walk along the old towpath follows banks that keep much of their original profile, and the Sui–Tang Grand Canal Museum, opened in 2019 on the north bank at Shilijing, tells the canal's story with models, maps and local finds such as a stone water-guardian beast dug up nearby.

rows.name: Huangcangyu National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded valley in the low limestone hills of Xiao county, named 'the valley where the emperor hid' after the tradition that Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty, sheltered here before his rise. Old trees, springs and caves such as Huangcang Cave and Sanxian Cave are linked by paths, with the Ruiyun Temple in the valley, and the area is known locally for its mushroom-stewed chicken.

rows.name: Lingbi Modern Agriculture Expo Park
rows.summary: A showcase farm park at the core of the Lingbi Sanhe provincial modern-agriculture demonstration zone, built around four large glasshouses: an agricultural science hall, an 'urban forest' hall, a desert-plant hall and a hall of city gardens and vegetable plots. It suits families and school groups interested in plants and farming.

rows.name: Lingbi Stone Culture Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park on the south-western side of Lingbi town, by the old Bian river, devoted to Lingbi stone, the ringing, intricately shaped limestone counted among China's four famous ornamental stones and used since antiquity for chime stones. Huizhou-style halls and pavilions in a classical-garden layout are set among display stones, and the main building, Bianyang Tower, houses the Lingbi Museum. A large stone market and 'stone town' next door sell rocks to collectors.

rows.name: New Bian River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A landscaped riverside park along the New Bian River, a canal dug in the late 1960s for flood relief and irrigation, roughly parallel to the long-silted Bian canal of the Sui and Tang, where it passes the north of Suzhou city. At its head stand the Bian River Museum and the 'Yuanhang' (Setting Sail) sculpture; the north bank has 13 plazas on battles fought in the region, from the Dazexiang uprising and Gaixia to the Huaihai campaign, and the south bank 12 plazas on local customs and notable people.

rows.name: Suzhou Museum (Anhui)
rows.summary: The city museum of Suzhou in northern Anhui, opened in 2010 in a Han-style building on a raised platform and rated a national first-grade museum in 2020. Its upper floors trace the area's history with more than 700 objects, from early settlements and the Qin–Han period to the Sui–Tang canal, the Ming and Qing and modern times, while a ground-floor folk-art hall covers local opera, the Yongqiao circus tradition, crafts, painting and Lingbi stones.

rows.name: Datong Ancient Town
rows.summary: Datong, on the Yangtze south-west of Tongling, was one of Anhui's main river ports, and the sandbank of Heyuezhou across the narrow Que River was from the 1860s to the 1930s a salt market and steamer landing nicknamed 'Little Shanghai', with three streets and thirteen lanes. Heyuezhou's streets burned in 1938 and floods and the decline of river trade later emptied it, leaving abandoned lanes, while Lanxi Old Street on the Datong side keeps its flagstones and old shopfronts and is busy with visitors and snack stalls on holidays. Datong is a national historic and cultural town.

rows.name: Fenghuang Mountain
rows.summary: A group of low hills in Shun'an town, south-east of Tongling, known for Fengdan medicinal peony and named in 2000 'China's home of the medicinal peony'. Its peony garden holds more than 200 ornamental tree-peony varieties and more than 100 herbaceous peonies, including the four classic named cultivars; other sights are the Dishui Cliff and the 'Lovesick Tree'. The ancient copper-mine site at Jinniudong is nearby.

rows.name: Fushan Mountain
rows.summary: An extinct volcano of the early Cretaceous on the shore of Baidang Lake in northern Zongyang, which seems to float on the water and is called 'the foremost literary mountain' for the poets who came here, from Meng Jiao and Bai Juyi in the Tang to Fan Zhongyan, Wang Anshi and Wang Yangming. Its caves and rock walls carry hundreds of inscriptions from the Tang to the Republic, protected as national heritage, among temples, pagodas and pavilions, and the scholar Fang Yizhi is buried on the mountain. It is a national geopark and national forest park.

rows.name: Jinniudong Ancient Copper Mine
rows.summary: Tongling has been called China's 'ancient copper capital', and the Dagongshan–Fenghuangshan mines straddling the Nanling–Tongling border were worked from the Western Zhou to the Song. The visitable part is Jinniudong, a low hill near Fenghuang Mountain where excavations exposed ancient shafts and galleries with mining tools and pottery from the Spring and Autumn period to the Western Han; it was the second ancient copper mine in China opened to visitors, after Tonglüshan in Hubei, and has a small site museum.

rows.name: Liqiao Water Town
rows.summary: A village in Xilian town, north-east of Tongling, redeveloped into a 'water town' resort around its old street, where Ming and Qing buildings have been restored as small museums, a crafts street and boutique inns. The scenic area also includes the Manyuan garden and the old Liqiao street, and is lit up for night visits. It is a newly developed resort around an old village and suits an evening stroll or an overnight stay.

rows.name: Qishan Hanwu Cultural Park
rows.summary: A public hillside park on Qishan in Zongyang county town, themed on Emperor Wu of the Han, who by local tradition shot a flood dragon in the Yangtze at Zongyang on a southern tour and wrote the 'Song of Shengtang and Zongyang'; Zongyang became a county in 106 BC. The Hanwu Pavilion stands in the park.

rows.name: Tianjing Lake Park
rows.summary: A lake park of over 1,200 mu in the centre of Tongling, named after the 'heavenly well' on a small island in the lake. The 4A scenic area combines the lake with a copper-culture garden, a Jiangnan-style garden, a lakeside square and the North Lake, and makes a pleasant walk in the city.

rows.name: Tongling Museum
rows.summary: The city museum of Tongling, long known as China's 'ancient copper capital', is devoted to bronze and copper culture. Since 2020 it has also run a digital copper museum, with a hall of digital displays and a children's interactive area showing models and images of Chinese bronzes held in other museums at home and abroad. It stands beside the West Lake Wetland Park.

rows.name: West Lake Wetland Park, Tongling
rows.summary: An urban wetland park laid out around West Lake in the Xihu new district on Tongling's north-eastern side, with lakes, planted woodland and paths for walking. The city museum stands on its eastern shore, so the two make an easy pair.

rows.name: Wutong Flower Valley
rows.summary: A countryside flower park in Zhongming town on Tongling's eastern border with Nanling and Fanchang, covering 15.4 km² of hills and farmland. It has a peony garden, a large field of Fengdan medicinal peony, a green-plum orchard, tulip beds, Wutong Lake with Rose Island and the Big and Little Jinshan hills, and is best in spring.

rows.name: Yongquan Resort
rows.summary: A farm-stay resort in the Yeshan forest park in Zhongming town, eastern Tongling, built in Huizhou garden style, with guest houses and villas, a food street of local snacks in Jiangnan-style buildings and a collection of Huizhou carvings. Its Siji Lanshan area adds an orchid garden and karst stone-forest scenery, and the resort suits a weekend stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Dapu Rural World
rows.summary: An agricultural tourism park at Dapu in Xuzhen town, northern Nanling County, that mixes flower fields and farm displays with family amusements. Attractions include an indoor wave pool, a glass bridge between islands, water slides, a rose maze and a small train, as well as a tropical plant house and a medicinal-plant garden used for study tours; rape and rose fields flower in spring and fireworks are put on during holidays. It suits families on a day out from Wuhu rather than sightseers.

rows.name: Fanchang Kiln Archaeological Park
rows.summary: A kiln site of the Five Dynasties and Northern Song on the northern slopes of Ruomaojian and Zhuizishan hills, just south of Fanchang town, which specialised in bluish-white qingbai porcelain fired one piece to a saggar. Two excavated dragon kilns climbing the hillside, with mounds of waste saggars and sherds below, are shown in situ in a protective hall with an exhibition of finds. The site opened as an archaeological park on the May Day holiday of 2026, with pottery workshops, a Song-style tea house and costumed performances, and a site museum has been under construction since 2025.

rows.name: Fantawild Resort, Wuhu
rows.summary: A cluster of Fantawild theme parks in Jiujiang District on Wuhu's north-eastern side, run by the Huaqiang Fantawild group. The city government lists three parks: Fantawild Oriental Heritage (opened 2015), with more than 20 zones built around Chinese legends such as Nüwa mending the sky and the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl, plus a wooden roller coaster; Fantawild Dreamland (2010), with animation-themed attractions and fairground rides; and a water park. It suits families who want a full day of rides; Wuhu was also home to the chain's first large park, Fantawild Adventure, which opened in 2007 and closed in 2020.

rows.name: Former British Consulate, Wuhu
rows.summary: After the 1876 Chefoo Convention opened Wuhu as a treaty port, Britain built its consulate on Fanluo Hill above the Yangtze: the hilltop office of 1877 is a two-storey colonial building with arcaded verandahs on three sides, grey brick banded with red and a hipped iron roof. Two smaller red-brick buildings on the hillside, an assistants' block of the early 1900s and a customs administration office of 1912, are listed with it. Used as city government offices until 2010, the three buildings were being restored in 2026, and the city plans to use them for an exhibition on Wuhu's treaty-port history.

rows.name: Former Residence of Dai Anlan
rows.summary: The family home of Dai Anlan (1904–1942), a Nationalist army major general who commanded the 200th Division in the battles of Kunlun Pass and Toungoo and died of wounds in May 1942 while withdrawing from Burma. The house, in Lianxi, Hongxiang town, in south-western Wuwei, is a grey-brick building of two courtyards and three bays, repaired and fitted with displays of his cap, holster, medals, documents and personal belongings. Dai's tomb is on Zheshan hill in central Wuhu.

rows.name: Guangji Temple, Wuhu
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the south-western slope of Zheshan hill in central Wuhu, founded in the 890s and long called 'Little Jiuhua' because pilgrims bound for Mount Jiuhua stopped here first to venerate a gold seal of the bodhisattva Dizang said to date from 757. Its oldest structure is the Zheta Pagoda behind the halls, a five-storey hexagonal brick pagoda of 1065, 28 m high, with a seated Dizang inside; most halls are recent rebuilds stepped up the slope in imitation of Jiuhua. 'The Zheta Pagoda in clearing mist' is counted first among Wuhu's traditional scenic views.

rows.name: Huangjin Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song pagoda, dated in the county heritage register to 998, that stands beside the West River in Fenghe village on the edge of Wuwei's main town. It is one of the stops on Wuwei's heritage routes together with the Mi Fu Memorial Shrine, and lightning protection was fitted in 2024.

rows.name: Jiuzi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A newly built old-style town in Jiujiang District, developed by the Xinhualian group around the theme of the Huizhou merchants and put up by craftsmen in hand-worked Huizhou style. The Biandan River splits it in two: the west side holds buildings presenting merchant guild halls (Chaozhou, Huizhou and Hunan), the houses of notable families, an academy and a money shop, while the east side is given over to hotels, snack stalls, inns and bars. It is a modern resort town rather than a historic one and suits an evening stroll.

rows.name: Jiuzi Scenic Area (Mirror Lake)
rows.summary: Wuhu's central lakeside district, made up of Jiuzi Square, Mirror Lake Park and the Zhongshan Road pedestrian street; Jiuzi is the city's ancient name. Mirror Lake (Jinghu), formed by the Large and Small Mirror lakes, was Wuhu's first open public park, and the pedestrian street is busiest in the evening when it is lit up. It makes an easy stroll combined with Zheshan and the riverfront.

rows.name: Maren Qifeng
rows.summary: A forested range of limestone peaks rising to 316 m in Suncun town, where Fanchang meets Nanling and Tongling, protected as a national forest park and national geopark. Besides cliffs and rock formations, it has built attractions such as the 'Flying Dragon' glass bridge, a glass walkway on a cliff face and a cable car, and more recent additions include themed trails through a nanmu forest and, in winter, an artificial-snow park with snow slides. It suits a day of walking and rides.

rows.name: Old Wuhu Customs House
rows.summary: Wuhu's customs office, opened in 1877 after the Chefoo Convention made the city a treaty port, moved in 1919 into this building on the Yangtze waterfront, now inside Binjiang Park. The two-storey brick building faces the river, with a four-storey clock tower carrying clock faces on three sides and granite bands on its exposed-brick walls. Restored in 2023 and then fitted out for display, it opened to the public in April 2025.

rows.name: Renzidong Palaeolithic Site
rows.summary: A fossil-bearing cave site on the southern slope of Laili Hill in Suncun town, Fanchang, discovered in 1998 and dated to the early Pleistocene, about 2.2–2.56 million years ago. Eleven seasons of excavation have produced fossils of about a hundred vertebrate species, among them sabre-toothed cats and a mastodon, and over 200 stone and bone pieces that the excavators read as human-made, which would make this one of the oldest traces of humans in Eurasia, a claim some archaeologists dispute. The site is being laid out as an archaeological park with a renovated exhibition hall and life-size reconstructions of the animals.

rows.name: Shanshuijian Red Tourism Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area in Hongmiao town, north-western Wuwei, built around the former headquarters of the Communist-led New Fourth Army's 7th Division, which fought in the Wanjiang region along the Yangtze during the war against Japan. It takes in the headquarters site at Sanshuijian, the 7th Division Memorial Hall and the Wanjiang Revolutionary Martyrs' Cemetery in Haiyun village, set among hills, flower fields and blueberry farms that also draw weekend visitors.

rows.name: St. Joseph Cathedral, Wuhu
rows.summary: A large Romanesque-style Catholic church on Heer Hill above the Yangtze in central Wuhu, built by French Jesuits: the first church was burned shortly before completion in the Wuhu riot of 1891, and the present building was finished in 1895 with the indemnity money. Its west front has twin bell towers 29 m high, and it became Anhui's first cathedral in 1921. Reopened in 1983 after use for other purposes during the Cultural Revolution, it faces Jihe Square, laid out in 2000.

rows.name: Taoxin Shuiyun Water Country
rows.summary: A water-country landscape around Taoxin town in Wanzhi District, between the Qingyi and Qing'an rivers, where an old grid of waterways is lined with large lotus fields. Both a 4A scenic area and a national water-conservancy scenic area, it holds a lotus festival each June (the sixth was in 2023), and its routes link Xianghu Island and Lianhuawan, the old village of Housha and fruit-picking farms. It is best in summer, when the lotus is in flower.

rows.name: Wang Jiaxiang Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial garden built in 1986 on Shizi Hill in central Wuhu, in the grounds of the former St James Middle School, an Anglican mission school where the Communist leader Wang Jiaxiang (1906–1974) studied in 1924–25. It has a bronze statue, a memorial stele and an exhibition on his life told through documents, photographs and objects. The school's early 20th-century red-brick buildings, among them the 1910 St James Hall with its clock tower, are protected as national heritage but stand in a working school.

rows.name: Yugeng Hill Cultural Park
rows.summary: A small hill beside the Catholic cathedral in central Wuhu whose mission buildings were turned in 2013 into a cultural and creative park with a wine theme. Its core is the former St Aloysius (Neisi) technical school, built by Spanish Jesuits in 1934–35: a large block stepping down the hill, five storeys on the lower side and two at the top, with strong vertical lines and Huizhou-style stepped gables. Beside it on the summit is the former British consul's residence of 1887–89, which the Catholic mission bought for offices in 1934.

rows.name: Zhenshui Guanxiang Water Village
rows.summary: Guanxiang is an old village in Liulang town, Wanzhi District, ringed by ponds planted with lotus and water lilies; the Tao family genealogy records 13 imperial officials from the village after the Song, whose private lanes gave it the name 'Officials' Lanes'. Rated 4A in 2020, the scenic area centres on the village and its water street and also takes in the Yiranxiang oil-pressing culture park, where traditional wooden presses are shown, a mushroom garden and farm stays. It suits a relaxed half day in the Wuhu countryside, with local 'eight water vegetables' dishes.

rows.name: Zheshan Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill park in the middle of Wuhu covering the two summits of Zheshan, named for its reddish-brown rock; the higher peak is 84.8 m and has long been the place to look out over the city and the Yangtze. Paths lead to garden spots such as Cuiming Garden and Shutian Pavilion, the Zhongshan Hall and the tombs of the educator Liu Xiping and of General Dai Anlan, and there is a small zoo with children's rides. Guangji Temple on the south-western slope belongs to the same 4A scenic area.

rows.name: China Xuan Paper Culture Park
rows.summary: Jing County is the home of Xuan paper, the absorbent paper prized for Chinese calligraphy and painting, whose hand-making craft is on the UNESCO intangible heritage list. This 4-hectare park at Wuxi includes the China Xuan Paper Museum, a traditional workshop where the old hand process is demonstrated, a room where old-style books are printed on the paper, and craft areas where visitors can try making paper, ink, brushes and inkstones.

rows.name: Chinese Alligator Scenic Area
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Anhui Chinese Alligator National Nature Reserve's breeding base on the southern edge of Xuancheng, opened to tourists in 1987 as 'China Alligator Lake' and renamed in 2016. Visitors see captive Chinese alligators, a critically endangered species found in the wild only along the lower Yangtze, in outdoor pools and a winter alligator house, and an education hall explains the breeding and release programme that helped Anhui's wild population pass 1,600 in a 2024 survey.

rows.name: Enlong World Wooden House Village
rows.summary: A resort and leisure park opened in 2001 on a 150-hectare site in the Qinglongwan forest area, built around clusters of timber holiday villas. Its grounds include a large ginkgo grove, orchards, a water park and a folk-culture park with model houses of several ethnic minorities. It is aimed at families and groups wanting a countryside stay rather than at heritage.

rows.name: Former New Fourth Army Headquarters, Yunling
rows.summary: From July 1938 to January 1941 the Communist-led New Fourth Army had its headquarters at Yunling, 25 km west of Jing county town, with its offices spread across 13 hamlets in a valley. Visitors see the command post in two former landlord houses at Luoli village where Ye Ting and Xiang Ying lived, the assembly hall in the Chen ancestral hall, the arms-repair workshop in a Guandi temple with a carved opera stage, and the memorial museum opened in 1985.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wang Jiaxiang
rows.summary: A late-Qing house in Hou'an village, Taohuatan town, where Wang Jiaxiang, a Communist Party leader and the People's Republic's first ambassador to the Soviet Union, was born in 1906 and lived during his primary-school years. A memorial hall of 2,630 m² was built beside it in 2006 for the centenary of his birth.

rows.name: Guangjiao Temple Twin Pagodas
rows.summary: Two seven-storey brick pagodas, about 17 m tall and imitating timber construction, were built in 1096 under the Northern Song and stand 26.9 m apart at the south-eastern foot of Jingting Mountain. They are all that survived when Guangjiao Temple, founded in 849 by the Chan master Huangbo Xiyun, was destroyed during the war with Japan; the temple halls were rebuilt in 2004–2006. The painter Shitao lived here as a monk in the Kangxi era.

rows.name: Guantang Lake Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A privately developed eco-tourism and leisure area on the shore of Guantang Lake in the north of Xuancheng's economic development zone, formerly called the Guantang Lake Eco-Sightseeing Garden. The city government describes lakeside gardens and farm-style sightseeing, an intangible-heritage museum, water-based amusements, restaurants and lodging. It suits a relaxed half day rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Guantianxia Scenic Area (Shifo Mountain and Tianzi Lake)
rows.summary: This scenic area in Yaocun township, Langxi County, joins Shifo (Stone Buddha) Mountain, a 353 m hill long known as a Buddhist mountain, with Tianzi Lake, a 3.5 km² reservoir on its eastern side. Temples are built on the rocks of the summit among oddly shaped boulders, including a 32-tonne rocking stone, a cable car crosses the area and the lake is used for boating. A temple fair is held on the mountain each year on the 30th day of the seventh lunar month.

rows.name: Huangtian Village
rows.summary: Huangtian, in Langqiao town south of Jing county town, is a village of the Zhu clan founded in the Song whose Qing-dynasty houses survive in unusual numbers: 57 sites with 110 buildings. The best known is the Yangchuanwu, or 'foreign ship house' (Duchengtang), alongside halls such as Sishentang and Juxingtang, lanes with open and covered water channels, and the Fengzi River running past the village.

rows.name: Huizhou–Hangzhou Ancient Trail
rows.summary: The Huizhou–Hangzhou Ancient Trail is a stone-paved mountain path, begun in the Tang, along which Huizhou merchants carried goods towards Hangzhou, and it is now a popular hiking route. The classic section runs about 16 km from Fuling town in Jixi to Qingliangfeng in Zhejiang's Lin'an district, through the Qingliangfeng nature reserve and past the Jiangnan Diyiguan pass, old tea pavilions and stone bridges. The national listing also covers a section of the old eastern Huizhou road in Langxi County.

rows.name: Jiangcun Village
rows.summary: Jiangcun is a village of the Jiang clan in Baidi town, Jingde County, founded in the Sui–Tang period and at its height in the Qing, and listed as a national historic and cultural village in 2005. Its surviving Ming and Qing buildings include the Jiang ancestral hall, a filial-piety shrine, the Father-and-Son Jinshi memorial archway, several family halls and an old street, as well as the former homes of the mathematician Jiang Zehan and of Jiang Dongxiu, the wife of the scholar Hu Shi.

rows.name: Jingde Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Jingde's Confucian temple in the county town was founded under the Northern Song and repaired through the Yuan, Ming, Qing and Republican periods. The south-facing complex keeps its Pan pool and bridge, the Ji gate, shrines to famous officials and local worthies, side halls, the main Dacheng Hall and a Wenchang pagoda.

rows.name: Jingting Mountain
rows.summary: Jingting Mountain is a range of low wooded hills on Xuancheng's northern edge, rising to 324 m at Cuiyun Peak, and is known as the 'poetry mountain' of the south. Xie Tiao wrote of it in the fifth century, and Li Bai climbed it seven times and left some 45 poems about it; Bai Juyi, Du Mu, Su Shi and many others followed. Paths lead from the forest-park entrance past tea gardens to viewpoints over the city.

rows.name: Longchuan Village
rows.summary: Longchuan is a Hu-clan village on the Dengyuan River 11 km east of Jixi county town, where the Ming general and official Hu Zongxian was born in 1512. Its Hu Clan Ancestral Hall, founded in the Song, rebuilt with funds raised by Hu Zongxian in the Jiajing era and restored in 1898, is known for more than 600 carved wooden panels. On the canal street stands the Yishi Shangshu stone archway of 1562, honouring two Hu ministers, and Hu Bingheng's residence is listed with it.

rows.name: Longquan Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in the Shuidong area, south-east of Xuancheng, more than 2 km long, with halls such as the Milky Way Hall and White Dragon Palace and an underground river. Old inscriptions left on the walls by Southern Song and late Ming visitors survive inside, the air stays around 18°C all year, and the rebuilt Longquan Temple faces the cave exit.

rows.name: Qinglongwan Eco-Tourism Resort
rows.summary: Qinglongwan is the resort area around Qinglong Lake, the reservoir of the Gangkouwan dam west of Ningguo, where about 34 km² of water and 38 islands lie among forested hills. Boat services run on the lake, and the wider area takes in the Tang-founded Baiyun Temple on a summit and the Banqiao reserve, which keeps a large stand of natural evergreen chinquapin forest. It suits boating, lakeside walks and a quiet overnight stay.

rows.name: Qingqing Farm Estate
rows.summary: A farm park of about 100 hectares in Xinhang town, run by a local company that grows kiwifruit and raises free-range chickens. Visitors come for seasonal fruit picking in the orchards, lotus ponds and plum trees, and farm meals. It lies about ten minutes by road from Taiji Cave and is often combined with it.

rows.name: Shangzhuang Village
rows.summary: Shangzhuang, in western Jixi County, is the home village of Hu Shi, the scholar and diplomat who was a leading figure of the New Culture Movement. The listed group of seven buildings includes his former residence, built by his father Hu Chuan in 1897, his family school, Hu Chuan's own house and the former house of the ink-maker Hu Kaiwen, and the village is open to visitors as a scenic area.

rows.name: Shuidong Old Town
rows.summary: Shuidong is a market town 29 km south-east of Xuancheng that grew rich in the Ming and Qing on river trade along the Shuiyang River and on its candied jujubes, and was named a national historic and cultural town in 2008. Its old streets keep Ming-era bluestone paving, the Dafudi mansion, the eighteen-step 'Shiba Ta' well, Ningdong Temple and a Catholic church, and several films and TV series have been shot there.

rows.name: Shuimo Tingxi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Tingxi, south-east Jing County, made up of the Danankeng, Majialing and Taoling sections across a planned 40 km² with about 80 per cent forest cover. Visitors come for forested gorges, streams and pools, tea gardens and terraced fields, an old arched stone bridge and the winding Taoling mountain road, and for cool air in summer.

rows.name: Shuixi Twin Pagodas
rows.summary: Two Song-dynasty brick pagodas stand on the south-eastern slope of Baiyun Hill at Shuixi, 2 km west of Jing county town on the far side of the Qingyi River. The Daguan Pagoda of 1108 is 45 m tall, square in its lower storeys and octagonal above, while the slender square Xiaofang Pagoda of 1161 rises 21.3 m.

rows.name: Taiji Cave
rows.summary: Taiji Cave is a limestone cave system in Shilong Mountain, 38 km north-east of Guangde near where Anhui, Jiangsu and Zhejiang meet; it is about 5.4 km long and was opened to visitors in 1986. The route passes through some 19 chambers of stalactites and flowstone on dry and water-filled levels, including a boat ride on the underground river, and Song- and Ming-era inscriptions survive in and around the cave. A cable car runs on the mountain outside.

rows.name: Taohuatan (Peach Blossom Pool)
rows.summary: Taohuatan is a deep pool on the river 40 km west of Jing county town, famous from Li Bai's poem 'To Wang Lun', written when his friend saw him off here. On the east bank the Ming-built Tage Pavilion marks the old ferry where Wang Lun is said to have sung farewell, with old lanes behind it; across the water are the Huaixian Pavilion, Wang Lun's tomb and other sites, and downstream stands the octagonal Wenchang Pavilion of the Qianlong era.

rows.name: Tianshou Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey hexagonal brick-and-timber pagoda, 42.8 m tall, on Yingchun Street in the centre of Guangde and the only survivor of Tianshou Temple. First built in 979 and rebuilt in 1100–1105 after a fire, it was repaired many times; its present eaves and floors date from a 1984–86 restoration, and further repairs finished in 2017. An old well and a Ming-dynasty ginkgo stand beside it.

rows.name: Wannan Incident Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery opened in 1991 at the southern foot of Shuixi Hill, on the western edge of Jing county town, for the New Fourth Army soldiers killed in the Wannan (South Anhui) Incident of January 1941. The army's headquarters column of about 9,000, leaving Yunling, was surrounded and attacked by Nationalist government forces at Maolin in Jing County. The 15-hectare site centres on a monument inscribed by Deng Xiaoping, with an exhibition hall on the incident and a tomb of unknown soldiers.

rows.name: Xialin Jiutian Waterfalls
rows.summary: A forested valley of about 11 km² at Xialin village in Zhongxi town, where the Huangshan and Tianmu ranges meet, known for its many waterfalls. Trails follow the Wolong and Feilong gorges past pools and falls such as Dalong Pool and the three-tiered Guanyin Falls, which drop more than 30 m, and a 1.5 km rafting run descends Wolong Gorge in the warm season.

rows.name: Xianren Pagoda
rows.summary: Xianren (Immortal) Pagoda, also called Dangyang Pagoda, is a seven-storey hexagonal brick pagoda built in 1143 under the Southern Song and repaired in the Qing. More than 26 m tall, it stands on a cliff at the mouth of a valley south of Zheting village in Xianxia town, south-east Ningguo. It makes a short stop rather than a destination in itself.

rows.name: Xuanjiu Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The visitor park of the Xuanjiu baijiu distillery in Xuancheng's economic development zone, presenting the local liquor and how it is made. The company traces its craft to Ji Sou, a Tang-dynasty brewer of Xuancheng whose death Li Bai mourned in a short poem, while the modern distillery grew from four private workshops merged in 1951. It suits visitors interested in Chinese liquor and factory visits.

rows.name: Zhaji Village
rows.summary: Zhaji, 60 km west of Jing county town, has been home to the Zha clan since the Sui dynasty and stretches for about 1.5 km along three streams. More than 140 old structures survive, among them the Yuan-dynasty De Gong Hall, Ming and Qing ancestral halls such as the Baogong and Erjia halls, old village gates, pagodas and dozens of stone bridges. It is a national historic and cultural village and a popular base for art students who come to sketch.

rows.name: Zhang Ancestral Hall, Jingxian
rows.summary: A clan hall of the Zhang family in Houshan village, Dingjiaqiao town, first built in the Hongzhi era of the Ming and rebuilt in 1880. The complex combines the ancestral hall with a clan schoolhouse, with about 1,300 m² of floor space.

rows.name: Zhangshan Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area of about 15 km² at the southern entrance to the Qingliangfeng national nature reserve, 22 km south-east of Jixi county town where the Tianmu and Huangshan ranges meet. Trails follow the Zhang River past pools and waterfalls below Baizhangyan, a sheer rock face about 460 m high, and a crag said to resemble Mao Zedong's profile, which gives the canyon the nickname 'Great Man Valley'. A stretch of the old Huizhou–Hangzhou trail also passes through.

rows.name: Zhuwang Village
rows.summary: Zhuwang is a traditional village in Caijiaqiao town, Jingde County, with a history of about 1,300 years and 47 well-preserved Ming and Qing buildings.
