It is known for the 'nine wells and thirteen bridges' along its stream and for the old Fushan Academy, and it has been opened as a scenic area while villagers still live and trade there.

rows.name: Doushahe Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: A hot-spring and holiday resort in the Dabie Mountains of Huoshan County, at the northern foot of Baimajian, the range's highest peak, near the source of the Pi River. It has hot-spring pools fed by a borehole and a water park, and its hot-spring centre was named in 2020 as one of the first national forest-wellness bases.

rows.name: West Huangshan Selenium-rich Resort
rows.summary: A tea-growing and resort estate in Shitai County, in the hills of southern Anhui, run by a local tea company around its resort hotel. Visitors stay and walk among the tea and forest grounds. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: West Tea Valley Theme Park, Jinzhai
rows.summary: A tea-valley theme park in Jinzhai County, in the Dabie Mountains of western Anhui, developed by a local agricultural company. The grounds combine tea terraces and valley scenery for walking and day visits. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Huazu Temple (Hua Tuo Memorial)
rows.summary: A temple-museum to Hua Tuo, the Han-dynasty physician born in Bozhou, on Yong'an Street in the old city. Its halls, Wuqinxi (five-animals exercise) stage, small herb garden and stele corridor are described in tourist listings; it forms the core of the Hua Tuo hometown culture-tourism base listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base.

rows.name: Yashan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Nanling County, southern Wuhu, known for its flower fields and stone forest. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base.

rows.name: 68 Nautical Miles Scenic Area
rows.summary: A coastal scenic area at Dong'ao village on Pingtan Island, named for the 68 nautical miles (about 126 km) of sea that separate Pingtan, the closest point of mainland China to Taiwan Island, from Hsinchu on the other side of the strait. It takes in Houyan Island and two neighbouring islets, known for rugged rocks and huge boulders, with a sandy beach beside them.

rows.name: Baijigou Waterfalls
rows.summary: A gorge just over 1 km long in Wutong town, western Yongtai, named for the scores of waterfalls large and small that pour into it, with walkways cut along the cliffs through a sinkhole-like canyon. The Dazhang River flows past its mouth, and rides such as a coloured slide, a zip line and a glass bridge have been added.

rows.name: Black Pagoda (Wuta)
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal granite pagoda at the eastern foot of Wushan Hill, begun in 941 by Wang Yanxi, ruler of the Min kingdom, and left at seven of its nine planned storeys when he was assassinated in 944. Weathering has darkened the stone, hence its popular name, and dark shale panels carved with Buddhas and donors' names are set into every storey. It is one of the few stone pagodas left from the Five Dynasties period and now stands among modern apartment blocks.

rows.name: Chen Taiwei Palace
rows.summary: A village temple at Qianxi in Zhongfang town that began in 909 as the ancestral hall of Chen Su, who had come to Fujian with Wang Shenzhi's army, and later became a shrine to him and to a descendant honoured for fighting the Mongols. The main hall, built without iron nails, has dense bracket sets rising to a square coffered ceiling and is counted with Fuzhou's Hualin Temple among Fujian's three great Song-era timber buildings. A Ming-dynasty gateway and opera stage stand in front.

rows.name: Fuzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The city's temple to Confucius, on a site that has held Fuzhou's government school since the Tang and its Confucian temple since the Song, rebuilt after a fire in 1851–52 and restored in the 2000s after decades as a school, a shopping arcade and a children's palace. Its axis runs from a stone lattice gate and a semicircular pond to the Dacheng Hall, a seven-bay hall with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof and unusually massive stone columns.

rows.name: Fuzhou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 860 hectares in the hills on Fuzhou's northern edge, founded in 1960 as the city arboretum, also run as Fuzhou Botanical Garden and the first national forest park in Fujian. Paths wind through tree collections, glasshouses and themed gardens and along the Bayi Reservoir, beside which stands a huge old banyan known locally as the 'king of banyans'.

rows.name: Gui'an Xintiandi Resort
rows.summary: A large resort and residential development built from 2011 by a property group in the Gui'an hot-spring area of Lianjiang county and rated 4A in 2014. It combines hot-spring hotels with the Gui'an Water World water park and an amusement park, and suits families wanting a resort break near Fuzhou.

rows.name: Gushan (Drum Mountain)
rows.summary: A forested mountain on Fuzhou's eastern edge, rising to 919 m, whose slopes hold Yongquan Temple, founded in 783, and more than 300 inscriptions carved into the rock from the Song dynasty onwards, among them calligraphy by Cai Xiang and Zhu Xi. Two Northern Song pottery pagodas stand in front of the temple, and paths link it with viewpoints and scenic spots such as Heshui Rock.

rows.name: Haitan Strait Underwater Sites
rows.summary: The Haitan Strait between Pingtan Island and the mainland holds shipwrecks and lost cargo from the Five Dynasties to the Qing, among them the Wanjiao No. 1 wreck, whose excavation is described as the first large-scale underwater excavation China carried out entirely on its own. The wrecks cannot be visited, but finds from these waters are the subject of the China Underwater Archaeology exhibition hall in the Pingtan Ocean Science and Technology Culture Centre, which opened for trial visits in May 2024.

rows.name: Hualin Temple
rows.summary: A small temple compound at the foot of Pingshan Hill whose main hall, built in 964 when Fuzhou was ruled by the Wuyue kingdom, is regarded as the oldest surviving timber building south of the Yangtze. Its tiers of bracket sets and single-eave hip-and-gable roof preserve early Song carpentry, a style thought to have influenced Japanese temple building in the Kamakura period. The gate and side halls around it were added when the hall was restored in the 1980s.

rows.name: Jiutouma Residences
rows.summary: A walled Qing-dynasty residential complex in Qiyang village, Heshang town, built by Chen Lihuan and his son from the Jiaqing era until about 1872 and named after nine large boulders scattered through it. Inside a 120 m square of 6 m walls stand 22 timber houses in five rows, each row with gates aligned so that all could be opened for weddings and funerals, and carved beams, doors and stone column bases throughout.

rows.name: Keqiutou Site Museum
rows.summary: A group of Neolithic to Shang-period settlement sites in northern Pingtan Island, about 7,500 to 3,000 years old, studied as possible early links in the spread of Austronesian-speaking peoples to Taiwan and across the Pacific. Shell-impressed pottery, stone adzes and shell-midden finds are shown in the Keqiutou Site Museum at Shangpan village, Suping, which became a branch of the China Archaeology Museum in 2025, and the 2023 excavations were named among China's top ten archaeological discoveries of that year.

rows.name: Lin Zexu Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The ancestral shrine of Lin Zexu, the Qing commissioner who forced foreign merchants to hand over their opium and destroyed it at Humen in 1839, an act that led to the First Opium War. Built in 1905 at the foot of Wushan Hill, its halls and courtyards now house the Fuzhou Lin Zexu Memorial Hall, with an exhibition on his life.

rows.name: Lingji Palace Stele
rows.summary: A Ming imperial stele 6.2 m tall on a tortoise base inside Lingji Palace at Qingpu village, a temple to the Southern Tang princes Xu Zhizheng and Xu Zhi'e said to date from 945. Its text, written out by the scholar Xie Jin, records the temple's rebuilding, and it stands under a square, 16-pillar double-eaved pavilion built in 1417; local tradition holds that Zheng He brought the stone from Nanjing.

rows.name: Longjiang Bridge, Fuqing
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty stone beam bridge at Haikou, built between 1113 and 1124 by monks of Taiping Temple, that spans 476 m across the Longjiang estuary on 39 boat-shaped piers. Its deck is made of stone beams about 9.5 m long, and a pair of small solid stone pagodas stands at the bridgehead.

rows.name: Luoxing Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal stone pagoda on Luoxing Hill above the Min River at Mawei, rebuilt in the 1620s on the site of a Song-dynasty tower and long used as a landmark by ships. Foreign sailors named the anchorage below it the Pagoda Anchorage, scene of the 1884 Battle of Fuzhou, in which the pagoda was damaged. The hill, once an island in the river, is now joined to the shore.

rows.name: Luoyuan Bay Ocean World
rows.summary: A marine park in the Luoyuan Bay waterfront new town, built by a property group as part of a large resort and residential development and opened in 2015. Besides its aquarium halls and staged shows, an animal park with land animals and a camping and picnic area were added in 2026; it suits families.

rows.name: Mawei Shipyard Heritage Area (Foochow Arsenal)
rows.summary: The site of the Foochow Arsenal, the Qing navy yard and naval school founded at Mawei in 1866 with French engineers, which built steam transports and gunboats and trained many of the officers of the late-Qing Beiyang Fleet. Surviving workshops and the Chuanzheng Culture Museum tell its story, and one old machine shop now hosts an immersive staged show. A short walk away, the Mawei naval battle memorial hall, the Zhaozhong shrine and the martyrs' cemetery on Maxian Hill recall the Chinese sailors killed when a French squadron destroyed the Fujian fleet here on 23 August 1884.

rows.name: Mingshan Shi Cave Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple on Gaogai Mountain in Dayang town, founded in 888 and given its name by the Min king in the late 920s, with timber halls built into a series of rock caves. Much Song and Yuan work survives, including an original Song patriarch hall, a small bluestone shrine holding a seated Guanyin, reliefs of Buddhist tales such as the prince who gave his body to a starving tigress, and old rock inscriptions.

rows.name: Minjiang Estuary National Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 闽江河口国家湿地公园
rows.summary: A 282-hectare wetland park of tidal flats and restored fish ponds at the mouth of the Min River in north-east Changle, part of an estuary wetland that joined China's World Heritage tentative list in 2022 and became a Ramsar site in 2023. Boardwalks, bird hides and a wetland museum serve birdwatchers: tundra swans and swan geese winter here from October to February, and the rare Chinese crested tern visits in the warmer months.

rows.name: Minyue Water Town
rows.summary: A modern themed water town on the Min River at Zhuqi in Minhou, whose first phase opened in 2021 and which was rated 4A in 2024. Canals are lined with shops and restaurants built in old-street style, with an opera stage, pavilions and immersive staged shows.

rows.name: Oulebao Ocean World, Yongtai
rows.summary: A marine theme park in Geling town with aquarium halls of sea and polar animals, several theatres for staged marine-animal shows, and a water park next door. It is aimed at families on a day out from Fuzhou.

rows.name: Qingyun Mountain
rows.summary: A national key scenic area of deep gorges cut into volcanic rock in Linglu township, south of Yongtai town, made up of sections such as the Yuntian stone corridor, Baima Gorge, Shuilian Palace and Qinglong Waterfall, each with trails past cascades, pools and cliffs. The separately run Yunding scenic area occupies the plateau at the top of the same mountain.

rows.name: Ruiyan Mountain and Maitreya Statue
rows.summary: A hill at Haikou town east of Fuqing whose eastern foot holds a laughing, pot-bellied Maitreya Buddha about 9 m tall, carved into the rock between 1341 and 1368 and described as the largest Yuan-dynasty Maitreya in China. The pavilion that once sheltered it is long gone, leaving ten stone pillars and three steles, and a temple with a main hall and bell and drum towers stands on a hillside carved with some 170 inscriptions, among them some by the Ming general Qi Jiguang.

rows.name: Sanfang Qixiang
rows.summary: Fuzhou's best-preserved old quarter, a grid of three lanes and seven alleys either side of pedestrianised Nanhou Street that keeps the walled-ward street plan laid out when the city walls were built in the late Tang. Behind high walls stand Ming-to-Republican courtyard houses of scholar-official families, several of them open to visitors, among them the translator Yan Fu's home on Langguan Alley and a mansion with Fuzhou's only waterside opera stage. The smaller Zhuzifang block, just east across Bayiqi Road, shares the national heritage listing.

rows.name: Shangxiahang Historic District
rows.summary: Two parallel streets near the Min River in Taijiang district, Shanghang and Xiahang, that grew from riverside landing places into Fuzhou's main trading quarter after the city was opened as a treaty port in the 1840s. Tea, timber, paper and dried-goods merchants built warehouses and family shrines here, and traders from across Fujian set up guild halls. Many of these buildings survive in the restored district, some reused as teahouses and shops.

rows.name: Shengshou Pagoda
rows.summary: A 27.4 m seven-storey octagonal stone pagoda imitating timber construction, built between 1096 and 1117 on Taping Hill in what is now Zheng He Park, Changle. Its base and walls are carved with flying musicians, guardian figures and some 200 small seated Buddhas, and in the early Ming it served as a lookout and landmark for Zheng He's fleets, which assembled at Changle before sailing.

rows.name: Shizhu Mountain
rows.summary: A Taoist holy mountain west of Fuqing known for its long-standing custom of dream-seeking, in which pilgrims sleep overnight in a cave shrine hoping for a dream that answers their prayers. Temple halls, towers and a pagoda climb the wooded slopes, and a lake with small islands lies at the foot of the mountain.

rows.name: Tannan Bay and Haitan Ancient City
rows.summary: A combined scenic area in south-east Pingtan made up of Tannan Bay, a sweep of fine white sand with more than 25 km of sandy shore running south to Jiangjun Hill, and Haitan Ancient City, a commercial complex of shops and restaurants built in the style of an old walled town. The bay is known for 'blue tears', glowing plankton that can light up the surf on some nights, and part of it is a protected area for Chinese horseshoe crabs.

rows.name: Tanshishan Site Museum
rows.summary: A Neolithic to Bronze Age settlement mound on the north bank of the lower Min River, about 5,500 to 2,700 years old, that gave its name to the Tanshishan culture, the first archaeological culture identified in Fujian. A provincial site museum shows its pottery, stone and bone finds, and a hall built over the 1996 excavation displays restored graves, ditches and pottery kilns in place.

rows.name: Tingjiang Fort
rows.summary: The remains of a Qing-dynasty gun battery at Nanban village in Tingjiang town, on the Min River downstream of Mawei, part of the defences along the river route to Fuzhou. It was added to the national heritage list in 2013 and is a minor site, best combined with the shipyard and naval battle memorials at Mawei.

rows.name: Tomb of Lin Zexu
rows.summary: The family tomb at the foot of Jinshi Hill, on Fuzhou's northern outskirts, where Lin Zexu, the official remembered for destroying opium at Humen in 1839, lies with his parents, wife, brother and sister-in-law. The grave is built of rammed lime and earth on four terraces, and Lin's descendants still gather here to pay their respects.

rows.name: Tombs of Qing Soldiers Who Served in Taiwan, Min'an
rows.summary: A hillside cemetery on Hutou Hill at Min'an, the old garrison town on the lower Min River, where 135 men of the Qing navy's Min'an garrison are buried, each under a headstone giving his name and home town. They died in 1874, when the Qing government sent forces to Taiwan under Shen Baozhen after the Japanese expedition there that followed the Mudan Incident, and their remains were brought back to Min'an for burial. The national listing also covers similar tomb groups at Dongshan in Zhangzhou and Qinyu in Fuding.

rows.name: Wushan and Yushan Hills
rows.summary: Two small hills in the old city centre that, with Pingshan, make up Fuzhou's traditional 'Three Hills', their rocks covered with inscriptions carved from the Tang dynasty to modern times. Wushan's prize is the seal-script 'Prajna Terrace' inscription by the Tang calligrapher Li Yangbing, alongside carvings by Song figures such as Cheng Shimeng and Zhu Xi; Yushan, about 1 km east, adds the White Pagoda, a shrine to the general Qi Jiguang and more inscriptions. Both are landscaped hill parks with paths and lookouts over the city.

rows.name: Xianying Palace Clay Sculptures
rows.summary: A Mazu temple in Xianqi village, Zhanggang, founded in 1138 and buried by drifting sand in the late Qing, then found again in 1992 when villagers dug house foundations. More than 50 painted clay figures of Mazu, sea deities and local gods, mostly Ming and Qing, were excavated, and the old temple is kept as found beneath a new temple built above it in 1993, reached by steps from the bell tower.

rows.name: Xishan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in the Gui'an hot-spring area of Lianjiang county, with a hotel, thermal pools and leisure facilities. Together with neighbouring Gui'an Xintiandi it is one of two 4A-rated resorts in the area and suits a relaxing overnight stay near Fuzhou.

rows.name: Yongtai Fortified Manors (Zhuangzhai)
rows.summary: Five Qing-dynasty fortified family compounds, known locally as zhuangzhai, in Yongtai's mountain villages, each a large timber-built residence covering roughly 3,000 to 10,000 m². The listed group is Renhe Zhuang in Tong'an, Shengping Zhuang in Dayang, Jishan Tang in Xiaba, Shao'an Zhuang in Dongyang and Zhongpu Zhai in Changqing, picked from more than 150 surviving compounds across the county.

rows.name: Yunding Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain-top scenic area on the summit plateau of Qingyun Mountain in Linglu township, most of it above 1,100 m, opened in 2010. Meadows ring a small lake in an old volcanic crater, and there are terraced fields, a canyon trail past a chain of waterfalls and a walkway hung on the cliffs.

rows.name: Caigai Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: A large late-Qing Hakka ancestral hall in Miaoshang village, Miaoqian town, dedicated to Jiang Caigai, a 14th-generation ancestor of the local Jiang clan. It has two main parts, the front Sixin Hall and the rear Juhuan Hall, and stands about 3.5 km from the Zhixi ancestral halls, so the two are easily seen together.

rows.name: Central Red Communication Line Sites
rows.summary: Relay stations on the secret route that in the early 1930s linked the Communist Party's underground headquarters in Shanghai with the Central Soviet Area, running via Hong Kong, Shantou and Dabu into western Fujian and on to Ruijin. The listed Fujian buildings are village houses, shops and ancestral halls in Yongding and Changting, among them the Chunsheng ancestral hall in Tufang, Changting, where the West Fujian party committee and soviet government moved in 1931, and the Bogong'ao station near Yongding town, the first stop after the route crossed from Guangdong. A memorial hall in Jinsha town, Yongding, tells the story with maps, objects and reconstructed scenes.

rows.name: Changting Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: Six buildings in Changting's old town used by the Communist movement in 1929–33, when Changting was a key part of the Central Soviet Area. They include the Central Red Hospital in the former Gospel Hospital, founded by a British mission in 1904, the Fujian Provincial Soviet Government in the old Tingzhou prefectural examination hall, the Fourth Red Army headquarters at Xingeng Villa, where Mao Zedong and Zhu De stayed, and the provincial party committee in a former church.

rows.name: Former Minxi Workers' and Peasants' Bank
rows.summary: The building on Xiajing Lane in central Longyan where the West Fujian (Minxi) Soviet Government opened the Minxi Workers' and Peasants' Bank in September 1930 to counter the Nationalist economic blockade of the base area. It was the first financial institution set up in any of Fujian's revolutionary base areas and one of the earliest banks of the Central Soviet Area. It now stands in the restored Central Soviet Area Financial Street, a historic quarter of old buildings, exhibitions, shops and cafés.

rows.name: Guantian Li Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: The ancestral temple of Li Huode, regarded as the first of the Li clan to settle in Fujian, built in 1836 in Guantian village, Rentian town, and restored in 1909 and 1984. It is a large Hakka complex laid out like the character 回, with the entrance and main halls in the centre ringed by two-storey wings of more than a hundred rooms.

rows.name: Guanzhai Mountain
rows.summary: A cluster of sheer cliffs and rock pillars rising straight out of the plain just east of Liancheng town, named after a boulder said to resemble the head of the xiezhi, a mythical horned beast. The scenic area is split into several zones, including the main summit, Wulao Peak (661 m), Shimen Lake and the Zhu'an and Qishi stockades, and it was shortlisted as a national geopark in 2009. Liancheng's airport and railway station are both named after it.

rows.name: Gutian Congress Site
rows.summary: The Liao clan ancestral hall in Gutian town, built in 1848 and later used as a school, where the Fourth Red Army held its ninth party congress on 28–29 December 1929 and adopted a resolution drafted by Mao Zedong that set the principle of party control over the army. The restored hall shows the meeting room and the offices used by Mao, Zhu De and Chen Yi. The 5A tourist area around it also takes in the Gutian Congress Memorial Hall, a museum opened in 1974, and nearby houses that served as the army's headquarters and political department.

rows.name: Liangye Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain near Wuping county town, protected as a national nature reserve, with gorges, cliffs, deep pools and a chain of waterfalls. Fairy Lake lies between the upper and lower falls near Yuncha village, and the reserve's broadleaf forest shelters a wide range of birds, animals and plants.

rows.name: Linjiang Lou
rows.summary: A late-Qing brick and timber house on the north bank of the Ting River in Shanghang town, built as a paper merchant's warehouse and villa, with arched stone verandas on its ground and top floors. Mao Zedong stayed here for more than 20 days in autumn 1929, recovering from malaria after the Red Army took Shanghang, and wrote his poem 'Double Ninth' (to the tune 'Caisangzi') during the stay.

rows.name: Long March Starting Point of the Red Ninth Corps
rows.summary: Guanshou Hall, an early-Qing ancestral hall in Zhongwu village, Nanshan town, served in September 1934 as the headquarters of the Red Army's Ninth Corps, which with the 24th Division and local forces covered the main Red Army's withdrawal after the Nationalist attack on Songmaoling. On 30 September 1934 the corps held a rally in front of the hall and set off on the Long March.

rows.name: Longkong Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in Longkang village, Yanshi town, with passages on three levels, large chambers full of stalactites and other formations, and an underground river. A trail of about 2 km leads through the cave, and at its end visitors can take a wooden boat along the river to the exit.

rows.name: Mao Zedong's Caixi Investigation Sites
rows.name_zh: 毛泽东才溪乡调查旧址
rows.pinyin: Máo Zédōng Cáixī Xiāng Diàochá Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Buildings in Xiacai village, Caixi town, linked with Mao Zedong's third visit to Caixi in 1933, when he carried out a social survey of the township and wrote it up as 'The Caixi Township Investigation'. The group is made up of the former Caixi district soviet office, the district trade union hall known as Lenin Hall, the Glory Pavilion and the Lenin Platform.

rows.name: Meihuashan South China Tiger Park
rows.summary: A breeding and rewilding centre for the South China tiger, a critically endangered subspecies found only in China, on the southern slopes of the Meihuashan National Nature Reserve near Gutian. The Meihuashan South China Tiger Breeding Research Institute has run the programme since 1998, and visitors can watch the tigers in large grassy, wooded enclosures.

rows.name: Peitian Ancient Village
rows.summary: A Hakka village of the Wu clan in Xuanhe, Liancheng, founded in the late Yuan and early Ming, whose present buildings date from the Ming and Qing, many of them rebuilt in the late Qing. It sits in a small basin with a stream curving round its eastern side, and its lanes are lined with large family mansions, ancestral halls, private academies, memorial arches and temples. It was named a Chinese Historical and Cultural Village in 2005.

rows.name: Qianlu Lake Wetland
rows.summary: A wetland of hill ponds, small lakes and marshes among wooded valleys in Chengxiang town, just outside Wuping county town, forming part of the Zhongshan River National Wetland Park. Its name, 'lake of a thousand egrets', refers to the many egrets that live here and to the scattering of small lakes.

rows.name: Shiyan Cave and Junqing Temple
rows.summary: A limestone cave whose mouth looks like the open jaws of a lion, joined to Junqing Temple, the founding temple of Dingguang Buddha, the deified monk Zheng Ziyan from Tong'an whom Hakka communities honour as their protector. A statue of Dingguang sits inside the cave among stalactites, and the temple, founded in the early Song and granted its name by the court in 1011, is still an active place of worship. The Dingguang cult spread from here across the Hakka areas of Fujian, Guangdong and Jiangxi and to Taiwan and South-East Asia.

rows.name: Sibao Woodblock Printing Buildings
rows.summary: Sibao, in the hills of northern Liancheng, was one of China's four main centres of woodblock printing in the Ming and Qing dynasties, and many of its family printing and bookselling workshops survive in the villages of Wuge, Zhongnan, Siqiao and Tiancha. Most are courtyard houses built of fire-resistant brick, and old carved printing blocks and tools such as cutting frames, knives and ink vats are kept in the area.

rows.name: Tianzi Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Dongxi village just outside Yongding town, with a large number of open-air thermal pools set in gardens styled after South-East Asia and a children's water play area. It is an easy stop for visitors staying in Yongding town on the way to or from the tulou.

rows.name: Tingjiang National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A river wetland park on the Ting River at Sanzhou, in a part of Changting that was once among the worst-eroded red-soil areas of southern China, its bare hills nicknamed the 'Flaming Mountain'. Decades of soil-conservation work have reforested the slopes, and the park now has ponds and lotus beds where 424 vascular plant species and 180 wild vertebrate species have been recorded. The neighbouring village of Sanzhou is a listed historic village.

rows.name: Tingzhou City Wall
rows.summary: The wall of the old Tingzhou prefectural city was first built of rammed earth in 769, faced with brick and stone in 1371 and partly rebuilt in modern times, and long stretches survive along the Ting River. At both ends it climbs the ridge of Wolong Hill, so that half the hill lies inside the town, and gates and towers such as Chaotian Gate and Sanyuan Pavilion stand at the edge of Changting's old streets.

rows.name: Xibei Tianhou Palace
rows.summary: A temple to the sea goddess Mazu in Xibei village, Gaobei town, begun in 1542 and completed in 1662 by the local Lin clan, many of whose members had emigrated to South-East Asia. Its centrepiece is a seven-storey tower-like hall known locally as the Wenta, with Mazu on the ground floor and Guandi, Wenchang, Kuixing and Cangjie on the floors above; the complex also has a gateway and an opera stage facing the main hall.

rows.name: Zhixi Ancestral Halls
rows.summary: Zhixi village in Miaoqian town is packed with Qing-dynasty Hakka ancestral halls, most of them combined halls and family homes built on the 'nine halls and eighteen courtyards' plan and fronted by finely made gatehouses. The listed group includes the Chengchuan, Cuichou and Yang Hui halls and the Huang and Yang family temples, and Zhixi was among the first villages named Chinese Traditional Villages.

rows.name: Beiyuan Imperial Tea Works Site
rows.summary: The site of the imperial tea works at Beiyuan, which sent tribute tea to the court from the 10th century until the early Ming dynasty and is best known for the pressed 'dragon and phoenix' tea cakes of the Song. Its main sight is a cliff inscription about 3.5 m high on a hilltop among tea gardens, in which the Fujian fiscal commissioner Ke Shi recorded the works' location, founding, boundaries and buildings in the 1040s. The walls, well and drains found by a 1995 excavation are being re-exposed under a conservation plan approved in 2025, which provides for an archaeological park with a visitor centre.

rows.name: Chengcun Han City Site (Minyue King City)
rows.summary: On the hills south-west of Chengcun village lie the ruins of an early Han-dynasty walled city, regarded as the largest and best-preserved of its period in southern China and often attributed to the Minyue kingdom that the Han conquered in 110 BC. Excavations since 1980 have exposed walls, gates, a water gate, palace and temple platforms, roads and wells over some 48 hectares, and the Minyue King City Museum beside the site displays the finds. The site is part of the Mount Wuyi World Heritage property, and Chengcun itself is a historic village with Ming and Qing houses.

rows.name: China Baojiu Culture Park, Pucheng
rows.summary: A visitor park opened in 2015 by a Pucheng drinks maker and also called 'Impression Xiaomi', in the Ronghuashan industrial zone north of Pucheng, built around baojiu, a traditional local rice wine. One of Fujian's first 'tourist factories', it combines a look at production with Hui-style buildings and Suzhou-style gardens, tastings, dining and shopping, and has a guesthouse on site.

rows.name: Da'anyuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Da'anyuan lies in Da'an village, Yangzhuang township, in the north of Wuyishan city on the north-western edge of the Wuyishan national nature reserve. The scenic area takes in forested valleys with clear streams and waterfalls, including a canyon below Huanggang Mountain and a stretch of an old tea road.

rows.name: Dongyue Temple, Jian'ou
rows.summary: A temple to the god of the Eastern Peak (Mount Tai) outside the old east gate of Jian'ou, facing the Jian River with Baihe Hill behind it. Rebuilt in 1672 and repaired many times since, the complex covers about 2.7 hectares, with a gate, front hall, opera stage and halls to the Eastern Peak god, the Empress (Niangniang), Guanyin and the Medicine Buddha. The main hall is five bays wide under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof.

rows.name: Heping Ancient Town
rows.summary: Heping, in the south-west of Shaowu, grew up in the Tang and Song and flourished in the Ming and Qing as a rare walled market town, and is now a national historic and cultural town. Gate towers survive at the east and north gates with stretches of wall, and a flagstone main street about 600 m long runs past nearly 200 Ming and Qing buildings, among them the Heping Academy, a scholar-official's mansion and the county assistant magistrate's office. The Ming Jukui Pagoda also stands in the village.

rows.name: Jian'ou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The former Confucian temple of Jianning prefecture, moved to this site in 1405 and rebuilt in its present form between 1869 and 1879. Its axis runs from a screen wall through the Lingxing Gate, the crescent pool and the Ji Gate to the double-eaved Dacheng Hall, flanked by side galleries. It keeps a Ming stele engraving of Confucius after Wu Daozi and a stele of the Kangxi emperor; the Jian'ou Museum, long housed here, moved to a new building in 2023.

rows.name: Jianzhou Ancient City, Jian'ou
rows.summary: Jian'ou was the seat of old Jianzhou, whose first character supplied the 'Jian' in Fujian's name. The scenic area centres on the Tiejinglan–Zizhi Street historic block, restored with nearly 50,000 salvaged old bricks, tiles and paving stones and reopened in 2023, including the Wanshou Palace with its restored opera stage. Workshops along the lanes show local crafts such as rubbings and Song-style whisked tea, among dozens of old-name shops.

rows.name: Jinkeng Red Tourism Area
rows.summary: Jinkeng is a township in the hills of western Shaowu, close to the Jiangxi border, that lay within the Communist Min–Gan (Fujian–Jiangxi) soviet area of 1933–35. The red-tourism area presents the former offices of the Min–Gan provincial Party committee and the East Army headquarters, the site of a battle at Huangtu Pass, Red Army slogans and a bullet-scarred wall, alongside the village's Qing-dynasty buildings, among them the Wenchang Palace, used as a temporary headquarters by the Red Army's Third Army Corps, and a Rulinlang mansion.

rows.name: Main Hall of Baoshan Temple, Shunchang
rows.summary: On the summit of Baoshan, at 1,304 m the highest peak in north-western Shunchang, stands a temple whose main hall was built in 1363, at the end of the Yuan dynasty, entirely of stone carved to imitate timber framing. The five-bay hall bears its dated founding inscription under the ridge and more than a dozen later Yuan, Ming and Qing inscriptions; the gate, front hall and side buildings were rebuilt in the Qing.

rows.name: Main Hall of Baoyan Temple, Shaowu
rows.summary: The only surviving building of Baoyan Temple, a Tang foundation in the centre of Shaowu that took this name in 1023. The hall was rebuilt in 1533 and is five bays square, about 11.6 m high under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, with its date written in ink on the main beam. In October 1932, when Red Army forces held Shaowu, the county soviet government had its office here; the hall was restored in 2009.

rows.name: Meikou Old Wharf, Songxi
rows.summary: Meikou is a village on the Songxi River in Zhengdun town whose old landing, dated by the county to the Song dynasty, was a river port on the trade routes that carried tea north. The scenic area takes in the old wharf and ferry crossing, lanes of old houses including the Wu and Lu family compounds, a river-transport exhibition hall and a grove of old camphor trees, and stages folk performances and festivals.

rows.name: Min–Gan Ancient Post Road, Wuyishan
rows.summary: A paved mountain road across the Fujian–Jiangxi border, first built in the Tang and Five Dynasties period, that climbs from Lingyang village in Langu township to the pass at Guanding on the provincial boundary. The protected section runs for about 2 km and is 1.8–2.3 m wide, with three stone arch bridges, two road pavilions, the ruins of the Qiuling post station, cliff inscriptions and a well along the way.

rows.name: Shizhen Bay White Tea Town, Zhenghe
rows.summary: Shizhen is a village almost encircled by water just west of Zhenghe town, which served as the county's river landing and goods depot in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Its old houses keep the look of a traditional northern Fujian village, with white tea planted around them, and the scenic area adds the old wharf, the Xingxi Academy and white-tea gardens that present Zhenghe's tea culture. The county itself takes its name from the Zhenghe reign era of the Song emperor Huizong, said to have been granted for its tea.

rows.name: Tiancheng Gorge
rows.summary: A privately run scenic area in the Jiangshi nature reserve, Xiaojiafang town, in the far south-west of Shaowu, counted as part of the Taining UNESCO Global Geopark. Its Danxia cliffs, forest and streams are kept close to their natural state, and visitors explore them on foot and by bamboo raft.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhu Xi
rows.summary: The grave of Zhu Xi (1130–1200), the Southern Song philosopher whose commentaries on the Confucian classics shaped Neo-Confucianism and the imperial examinations for six centuries. He was buried in 1200 at the foot of Jiufeng Mountain in Houtang, Huangkeng; the pebble-built tomb has a headstone re-erected in 1717, and a pavilion rebuilt in 1987 shelters an 1848 stele marking the spirit way.

rows.name: Wuyi Huahua World
rows.summary: A rural leisure park of about 40 hectares in Kaoting village on the edge of Jianyang, which began in 2011 as a family farm. It now combines fruit and vegetable picking, a theme park, a petting area, a campground and guesthouses. Its Yanzhan tourist factory, with seven Song-style buildings and three traditional dragon kilns, shows how Jian-ware tea bowls are made.

rows.name: Wuyi Tea Expo Park
rows.summary: This 7.8-hectare park in the Sangu resort area beside the Wuyi Mountains scenic area is devoted to Wuyi tea. A landscaped garden recalls famous writers on Wuyi tea, and the tea museum covers the history, legends and processing of Wuyi rock tea, with tea-art demonstrations. The park also holds the seating area for an open-air evening show staged against the landscape.

rows.name: Xiangjiang Tea Garden, Wuyishan
rows.summary: A tea company's visitor estate in Wuyishan's eco-enterprise park, rated a 4A scenic area in 2016 and listed by the province as a 'tourist factory' and a study-tour base. Set in a Jiangnan-style garden, it runs tea-making and tea-art sessions in which visitors try processing Wuyi rock tea by hand and taste the results.

rows.name: Xiyuan Canyon
rows.summary: Xiyuan Canyon is the core scenic area of the Mangdangshan national nature reserve, in Shangyang village on the western side of Nanping's Yanping district. A path follows the stream up a forested gorge, the 'canyon gallery', past the Zhongyan waterfall to Longde Temple and the Xiyuan Hermitage.

rows.name: Yangkou Red Tourism Town
rows.summary: Yangkou, on the Futun stream 12 km from Shunchang county town, was long a river port and market for north-western Fujian and in the 1930s was counted among the province's four best-known towns. In August 1933 the Red Army's East Army under Peng Dehuai held the town for 39 days and set up a soviet government, and the red-tourism town presents restored sites from that time, among them Peng Dehuai's office, the East Army political department and the soviet government office, together with a Red Army bridge and an exhibition hall on the town's revolutionary history.

rows.name: Yunfeng Temple, Pucheng
rows.summary: A temple in a fold of the hills about 2 km north-west of Cao village, Shuibeijie town, founded in the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty. Its main hall, rebuilt in 1482, is a compact Ming timber building about 11.6 m high under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, and keeps steles recording the temple's history; a Heavenly Kings hall also survives.

rows.name: Yunling Mountain
rows.summary: A privately run mountain scenic area beside National Road 316 in Longdou village, Shuibei town, north-west of Shaowu city. Its forested valleys are known for a 5.2 km canyon rafting run that starts from the 1,370 m Yunling Mountain and drops 216 m.

rows.name: Zhangshantou Red Army Cemetery
rows.summary: Across about 19 hectares of low hills east of Zhangshantou hamlet lie more than 1,300 graves of Red Army soldiers and cadres from 22 counties of Fujian, Zhejiang and Jiangxi who died here between 1928 and 1935. Many were wounded men who died at a nearby Red Army hospital; others were executed in internal purges. The graves are simple earth mounds faced with brick or stone, and a stone marker carved 'Red Army grave' with a star is dated 1931.

rows.name: Zhiqing Bridge, Jian'ou
rows.summary: A timber covered bridge at the water-mouth of Huang village in Dikou town, first built in the Hongzhi reign of the Ming dynasty (1488–1505) and heavily repaired in 1706 and 1787. It spans about 30 m on stacked, cantilevered timber beams, and its gallery holds three shrines with traces of painted decoration and Ming inscriptions.

rows.name: Ziyou Town Car Theme Park, Wuyishan
rows.name_zh: 自遊小镇汽车主题乐园
rows.summary: A privately run, car-themed leisure park near the Wuyishan resort area, rated a 4A scenic area in 2015 and aimed at self-drive visitors. It combines car-culture attractions with a campground for camper vans and tents and hotel accommodation.

rows.name: Baiheling Ancient Road
rows.summary: A stone-stepped official road built in 1225–27 under Ding Daquan, then registrar of Ningde county, as part of the overland route between Fuzhou and Wenzhou; it climbs from the old west gate of Ningde over the hills towards Luoyuan. About 4.9 km survives in four sections of bluestone steps 2–3 m wide, passing a dozen rock inscriptions, eight inscribed tablets, two old bridges and the sites of pass gates and beacon towers.

rows.name: Baishuiyang and Yuanyang Stream
rows.summary: A crescent-shaped scenic area of about 66 km² in Pingnan county, built around volcanic-rock gorges and the Baishuiyang 'shallow-water square', a flat bedrock riverbed across which the stream spreads in an even sheet that visitors can wade through. Its 36 km of streams also take in Yuanyang (Mandarin Duck) Stream, named after the ducks it is known for, and summer activities include kayaking, water games and rock climbing. It is part of the Ningde UNESCO Global Geopark.

rows.name: Baiyun Mountain, Fu'an
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 67 km² north-west of Fu'an and part of the Ningde UNESCO Global Geopark, known for its volcanic-rock mountain scenery. Its valleys hold granite canyons, deeply incised meandering streams and clusters of potholes worn into the stream beds, and the Jiulong Cave section is one of the main sights.

rows.name: Baofeng Silver Mine Site
rows.summary: Remains of a state silver mine worked from the 1080s until it was finally closed in 1510, at its height among the largest silver mines of Song China, around Shengyinlou Mountain in south-western Zhouning. More than 220 adits, about 40 smelting and miners' living sites, rock inscriptions and stone grinding wheels are spread over the hills, and the tunnels still show the marks of fire-setting used to crack the rock. It was named a provincial mine park in 2019, and an exhibition on the old mine has opened in the restored Baofeng official residence in Qinxi village, once the miners' settlement.

rows.name: Cuiping Lake
rows.summary: The reservoir of the Gutian River hydropower scheme, formed when the dam's sluices closed in June 1959, drowning the old county town of Gutian, which had been the county seat for more than a thousand years, and displacing more than 36,000 people. Its long arms wind between wooded hills and islands, and boat trips run on the lake.

rows.name: Fengqi Wu Family Mansion
rows.summary: The largest old house in Zherong county and the only building in the hamlet of Fengqi in Zhayang township, so that the house and the village are one: a Wu family mansion of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns (1736–1820) whose walled core, outbuildings and terraces cover some 14,000 m². The main house is laid out symmetrically, two courtyards and three halls deep and three ranges wide, and finished in plain timber and brick.

rows.name: Guanyinting Fort
rows.summary: A Buddhist shrine on the old post road at Banling, a She ethnic village in Shuimen township, first built in 1369, restored in 1791 and enclosed by a wall in 1863 against the Golden Coin Society uprising, which turned it into a small fort whose gate examination candidates bound for the capital passed through. Inside are a front hall and a rear main hall in timber; six stone columns carved with Chan sayings survive, and an 89 m stretch of the old post road runs past. She people from Fuding, Fu'an and Pingyang in Zhejiang gather here to sing at the Lantern and Double Ninth festivals.

rows.name: Huang Ancestral Hall, Fu'an
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Huang clan in Huangcuo Lane, Yangxia village, now on the edge of Fu'an city, founded in the late Song and rebuilt in 1694 on a plot of about 2,500 m². Behind a semicircular pond and screen wall it has front and rear halls five bays wide, with interior columns left out to make lofty open halls, a covered pavilion between them, and an opera stage with an archway-like facade flanked by two-storey galleries.

rows.name: Huotong (Huang Ju) Irrigation System
rows.summary: An irrigation system on both banks of the Huotong Stream at Huotong town, begun by the Sui official Huang Ju around 618 and still watering farmland today. On the right bank the Longyao canal runs along the hillside into Shiqiao village, where it once drove a cascade of water-powered rice pounders and still feeds ponds named after the sun, moon and stars; on the left bank the Pipa Cave channel ran through tunnels cut by heating the rock with fire and cracking it with water. It was listed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in 2017.

rows.name: Jiulongji Waterfalls and Carp Stream
rows.summary: This 4A area joins two places near Zhouning town that together form a 13.5 km² national scenic area within the Ningde UNESCO Global Geopark. Jiulongji is a staircase of nine waterfalls dropping some 300 m over about 1 km through a gorge in volcanic rock. In the old village of Puyuan, settled by the Zheng clan in the early 13th century, villagers have long protected the carp in the stream that runs through it, a custom now on Fujian's provincial intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Jixia Village
rows.summary: An old village in a mountain basin in Gantang township, Pingnan, where two streams meet below rows of timber houses built along the water; it is the ancestral home of the Qing general Gan Guobao and a national historic and cultural village. Its Ming street plan of three lanes along the slope and two up it survives, and the Longji Xiangong temple, dating back at least to 1550, has a double-eaved pyramidal roof and Qing paintings on its ceiling and wall panels. Restored houses now hold cafés and homestays, some run by newcomers, and the village keeps a midsummer festival of welcoming the immortal.

rows.name: Lingong Zhongping Wang Ancestral Temple
rows.summary: The ancestral temple of Lin Gong (Lin Zugen), a Song-dynasty healer from Fu'an who was deified after ridding the district of wild animals and epidemics, in Shanyang village, Makeng township. Built from 1513, it keeps a Ming gate tower, bell and drum towers and a hip-and-gable main hall with carved altar tables, plus a Qing pavilion of 1805 above the gate; the side halls were rebuilt in 2007. Lin Gong worship has spread from here across eastern Fujian and to Taiwan and Singapore.

rows.name: Linshui Palace, Gutian
rows.summary: The founding temple of Chen Jinggu, Lady Linshui, a protective goddess of women, children and childbirth worshipped across Fujian, Taiwan and South-East Asia, in Daqiao town, Gutian. Founded around 792 and rebuilt after a fire in 1876–79, the hillside complex has a five-bay main hall with an opera stage and worship pavilion under carved octagonal ceilings in front, and side halls for her attendants and her mother. It is the centre of the Chen Jinggu cult, a national intangible heritage item, and receives pilgrims from more than 4,000 branch temples.

rows.name: Mount Taimu
rows.summary: A granite mountain rising above the sea south of Fuding, long the sanctuary of the local goddess Taimu Niangniang and, from the Tang dynasty on, a centre of Buddhism with many temples on and around it. It is known for weathered granite peaks and pinnacles, caves among fallen boulders such as Seven Stars Cave, frequent mist and views over the coast and its islands. It is part of the Ningde UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2010.

rows.name: Niulanggang Coast
rows.summary: A seaside scenic area on the Fuding coast south-east of Mount Taimu, with a flat, clean sandy beach backed by green hills and sea-worn rocks given names such as Mandarin Duck Reef, the Weaving Maid's Cave and a narrow sea cleft. It was rated 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Shifeng Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at the foot of Lion Peak in Baizhuyang village, Xibing town, founded in 892 and moved down from the summit in the Yongle reign of the Ming. Its main hall, rebuilt in 1612, is one of the few well-preserved Ming timber temple halls in Fujian, with a double-eaved roof, 24 stone columns and a painted octagonal coffered ceiling, and the Heavenly Kings Hall of 1876 is known for its painted plaster decoration. In 1933–34 the local Communist organisation used the temple as the base of the 'Red Belt' peasant movement in Fu'an and Xiapu.

rows.name: Wan'an Bridge
rows.summary: Pingnan's Wan'an Bridge, 98.2 m long and described as the longest timber-arch covered bridge in China, is the best known of the covered bridges of north-eastern Fujian listed together as a national heritage unit. First recorded in 1090 and rebuilt many times, it crosses the stream at Changqiao on five stone piers carrying a 37-bay gallery; most of it burned down in August 2022, and the bridge seen today is a reconstruction, reusing the surviving timbers, that was accepted in October 2024. The listing also covers the Qiancheng and Baixiang bridges in Pingnan, the Luanfeng, Yangmeizhou and Chanxi bridges in Shouning, Dongyuan Bridge in Zherong, Tiandi Bridge in Gutian and Yuqing Bridge in Wuyishan.

rows.name: Yuanyang Meadow
rows.summary: An upland grassland on the hills of Dongyuan township, Zherong, promoted as 'the Hulunbuir of the south' for its rolling open meadows, and rated 4A in 2022. Trails link viewpoints such as the sky walkway and the Turtle Stone platform, and since 2024 a cross-country race has been run across the meadows each August.

rows.name: Bao'en Temple Pagoda, Putian
rows.summary: A three-storey octagonal stone pagoda, 13 m tall, on the central axis of Bao'en Temple on Dongyan Hill in Putian, between the Mahavira Hall and the Guanyin Hall. Built in the Shaosheng years of the Northern Song (1094–98), it came through a major earthquake in 1604 undamaged and was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Jiuli Lake
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Zhongshan town, Xianyou, named after the legend of nine immortals who rode carp up to heaven. It is known for its lake, caves, rocks and above all the upper five of the Nine Cascades waterfalls, and the Ming traveller Xu Xiake, who came in 1620, ranked it with the Wuyi Mountains and Yuhua Cave as one of Fujian's three wonders. The area is also known for its tradition of dream divination, and an old trail restored in 2023–24 links it with Jiulonggu Forest Park downstream.

rows.name: Jiulonggu National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 1,090 hectares in Xinan village, Changtai town, with forest cover of over 95 per cent. It adjoins Jiuli Lake: of the nine cascades that Xu Xiake described in 1620, the lower four lie here, among them the General, Flying Phoenix and Chessboard falls, and a restored stretch of the old Xiake trail links the two scenic areas.

rows.name: Longhua Twin Pagodas
rows.summary: A pair of old pagodas beside Longhua Temple in Dengta village, Longhua town, a few kilometres south-west of Xianyou county town; the national listing dates them to the Song and Qing dynasties. They became a provincial heritage site in 2001 and a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Meizhou Mazu Temple
rows.summary: Meizhou Island, off the coast of Putian, is revered as the birthplace of Mazu, the sea goddess whose worship spread along the Chinese coast, to Taiwan and across South-East Asia. The ancestral temple on Woniu Hill, first built in 987, was almost entirely destroyed in the Cultural Revolution and has been rebuilt and greatly enlarged since the 1980s with donations from worshippers in China and abroad, especially from Taiwan. The whole island is a 5A scenic area devoted to Mazu culture, with a beach beyond the temple.

rows.name: Mulan Weir
rows.summary: An irrigation weir across the Mulan River below Mulan Hill, completed in 1083 by Li Hong after two earlier attempts, the first led by a woman named Qian Siniang in 1064, were swept away. The 219 m barrage of interlocking granite blocks has 32 sluice openings between its piers, blocks the tide coming up from Xinghua Bay and feeds a network of canals; in 2014 it was among the first World Heritage Irrigation Structures. A park and memorial hall stand beside it.

rows.name: Ninghai Bridge
rows.summary: An old bridge across the mouth of the Mulan River at Qiaodou village, Huangshi, dated by the national listing to the Yuan dynasty and more than 700 years old; 'Sunrise at Ninghai' is one of Putian's traditional twenty-four views. For decades it carried road traffic on a concrete deck laid over the old structure until it was declared unsafe, and work began in 2012 on a new bridge about 100 m downstream to take the traffic off it.

rows.name: Pinghai Tianhou Palace
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty temple to Mazu in Pinghai village, on the coast of Xiuyu District south-east of Putian. Pinghai was from 1388 the seat of the Pinghai Guard, one of the Ming dynasty's main coastal-defence garrisons in Fujian, and the temple became a provincial heritage site in 1996 and a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Putian Arts and Crafts City
rows.summary: A trade and exhibition complex for Putian's craft industries, above all woodcarving and classical hardwood furniture, which with oil painting and gold and silver jewellery are among the city's traditional mainstays. It was the venue of the 2025 Cross-Strait (Putian) Crafts Fair, and its showrooms suit visitors interested in carving and furniture.

rows.name: Ruiyun Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in Dayang township, in the hills of northern Hanjiang District, whose peaks rise to over 1,000 m and are known for oddly shaped rocks, among them formations named the Heavenly Dog and the Sleeping Lion of the East. The scenic area includes the Fengwei waterfall and Yongxing Cave Temple, a provincial heritage site, and its forest shelters rare protected plants such as the Chinese yew.

rows.name: Shijia Wenfo Pagoda, Guanghua Temple
rows.summary: A five-storey octagonal stone pagoda about 30.6 m tall on the east side of Guanghua Temple, at the foot of Phoenix Hill in southern Putian; its earliest inscription shows it was standing by 1165. Built to imitate a timber tower, it has stone bracketed eaves, seated Buddhas in niches and reliefs of lions, guardian figures and phoenixes, with stairs inside up to the top storey. Guanghua Temple, founded in the 6th century, was one of the four great Buddhist monasteries of Fujian.

rows.name: Shouxi Park
rows.summary: Shouxi Park follows the Shouxi, as the Yanshou stream, the largest tributary of the Mulan River, is called where it flows through central Putian. Developed since 2011 as the city's green heart, it is laid out around lychee groves, waterways, old bridges and village houses, in eight themed zones that include 'Fishing Boats on the Shouxi', one of Putian's traditional twenty-four views.

rows.name: Tianzhong Wanshou Pagoda
rows.summary: A solid granite pagoda of the casket-stupa (baoqieyin) type on Tadou Hill in Fengting town, built in 1059 and also known as the Green Conch Pagoda. On a base 7.8 m square, its three-tier plinth is carved with dragons, the plum, orchid, bamboo and chrysanthemum, and figures of Buddhas and guardian warriors, and its top has banana-leaf corner ornaments and a five-ring finial.

rows.name: Wuchen Pagoda
rows.summary: A five-storey octagonal stone pagoda in Fengding village, Xiyuan township, high in the hills of north-western Xianyou. First built in 865 and rebuilt early in the Song dynasty, it imitates a timber pavilion-style tower, is hollow inside and stands 15.56 m tall. It is next to the old Jiuzuo Temple, about 2 km from the Xianshuiyang scenic area.

rows.name: Xianshuiyang
rows.summary: At about 870 m in Fengshan village, Xiyuan township, a mountain stream spreads ankle-deep for more than 600 m over a single, almost flat bed of brown rock. In summer it is a popular place to wade and splash, and the scenic area, rated 4A in 2026, has added a lakeside boardwalk, water games, artificial snow in winter and evening fire-and-light shows. Seven traditional villages lie around it, and the Jiuzuo Temple and Wuchen Pagoda are about 2 km away.

rows.name: Xianyou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Founded in the Tang and moved to this site in 1002, Xianyou's Confucian temple was rebuilt after storm damage in 1678 and 1780 and restored again in 2006–09. Its axis runs from the main gate past the crescent pool and bridge and the Ji Gate to the double-eaved Dacheng Hall, which has carved stone dragon columns, an octagonal caisson ceiling and copies of Qing emperors' plaques. The Minglun Hall, a separate courtyard for study, lies to the east.

rows.name: Yuanmiao Temple
rows.summary: Yuanmiao Guan in the old centre of Putian is a Taoist temple founded in 628 and rebuilt in 1015, whose Hall of the Three Purities is one of the rare Song-dynasty timber halls in southern China. The seven-bay hall rests on 20 stone columns under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, with Song-style bracket sets and lotus column bases. Qing halls to the Eastern and Western Peaks and other gods stand alongside, with steles including one in the calligraphy of Emperor Huizong.

rows.name: Zhenhai Seawall
rows.summary: A stone seawall along the shore of Huangshi town east of Putian, first built in the Tang dynasty's Yuanhe era (806–820) on the initiative of the Fujian regional commissioner Pei Ciyuan. In 1387 its stones were taken to build the Pinghai and Puxi garrison forts; it was rebuilt in 1826–27 and extended in 1964, and the surviving wall is about 3.5 km long and 3.7 m high.

rows.name: Anping Bridge
rows.summary: A granite beam bridge more than 2 km long across a tidal inlet between Anhai and Shuitou, completed in 1151 after 13 years' work and regarded as the longest ancient stone bridge surviving in China; its length gave it its other name, the Five-Li Bridge. Paved with stone slabs up to 11 m long laid on hundreds of stone piers, it has rest pavilions with Song guardian statues, small pagodas and a white hexagonal pagoda at its eastern end, and its surroundings have been laid out as a park. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Anxi Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A county Confucian temple founded in 1001 and rebuilt in 1686, set against Feng Hill in the centre of Anxi town and covering about 1.3 hectares. Its axis runs from a semicircular pool through the Lingxing and Ji gates to the Dacheng Hall, whose double-eaved roof rests on four finely carved stone dragon columns at the front, with the Chongsheng Hall behind and the Minglun Hall outside the east wall.

rows.name: Anxi Tulou (Xiping)
rows.summary: Three earthen fortified houses in the tea country of Xiping in south-western Anxi, separate from the better-known Fujian tulou of Yongding and Nanjing about 90 km to the south-west. Yingbao Lou, begun in 1372, is a two-storey rammed-earth block of 72 rooms behind a stone-arched gate and a square pond; Jusi Lou, of late-Ming origin, has massive river-cobble outer walls around a three-storey square building about 10 m high; and Taishan Lou dates from 1892.

rows.name: Banpu Old Houses
rows.summary: A hamlet of 13 large red-brick houses and two wells built by the Hong clan of Wengshan from the Qianlong reign of the Qing onwards, covering more than 6,000 m² in Liangshan village, Yingdu town. The group includes a house laid out on a chessboard plan, several ancestral and family halls and a house with an arrow tower.

rows.name: Baogai Mountain
rows.summary: A granite hill about 209 m high on the eastern edge of Shishi, the highest in the city, crowned by Wanshou Pagoda, popularly the Gusao (Sisters-in-Law) Pagoda: a hollow five-storey octagonal stone pagoda about 22 m high, built in the Shaoxing era (1131–1162) as a landmark for ships, with stairs inside its walls. A niche on its top storey holds a relief of two women said to be the sisters-in-law of the legend, and the pagoda is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site. Huxiu Temple, founded in the Tang, stands at the eastern foot of the hill.

rows.name: Beixi Wenyuan Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A rural eco-tourism area in Beixi village, Hushan town, set in a wooded valley with streams and waterfalls. It makes an easy half-day outing from Yongchun town.

rows.name: Cai Family Old Residences
rows.summary: A village of Qing-dynasty mansions in Zhangli, Guanqiao town, built from 1865 to 1911 by Cai Qichang, who had returned from the Philippines, and his son Cai Zishen. Spread over more than 3 hectares with nearly 400 rooms, the red-walled, red-tiled houses with swallowtail ridges are a showcase of southern Fujian residential architecture.

rows.name: Cao'an
rows.summary: A small granite shrine in Luoshan, Jinjiang, long regarded as the only intact Manichaean temple in the world, with a relief of Mani as the 'Buddha of Light' carved into the rock face behind it in 1339. The seated figure, about 1.5 m high in a round niche, has a beard and a halo of 18 rays, and was later venerated as a Buddhist image. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: China Museum for Fujian-Taiwan Kinship
rows.summary: A large state museum opened in 2006 on the historical ties between Fujian and Taiwan, in a red-brick and white-stone building whose four long flights of steps climb to a roof terrace over the city. Its main galleries trace migration, family lineages, trade, culture and shared folk religion across the strait, and a further hall presents folk customs through the four seasons.

rows.name: Chongfu Temple, Quanzhou
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple founded around 960 in the north-east of Quanzhou's old city, whose national listing is for the Yinggeng Pagoda: a seven-storey octagonal stone pagoda about 11 m high from the early Song, older than the rebuilt stone pagodas of Kaiyuan Temple and regarded as the oldest in the city. The pagoda leans slightly, which is said to have given it its name. The temple's other treasures are a huge cauldron said to cook for a thousand people and a great Song bell.

rows.name: Chongwu Ancient City
rows.summary: A granite-walled coastal garrison town built from 1387 to defend the coast against wokou pirates, regarded as the most complete stone sea-wall town surviving in China. Its walls, about 2.5 km round and 7 m high with some 1,300 crenellations, watchtowers and four gates, were restored in the 1980s and enclose old stone houses, temples and ancestral halls.

rows.name: Cizao Kiln Sites (Jinjiaoyi Hill)
rows.summary: The remains of Song–Yuan dragon kilns on Jinjiaoyi Hill in Cizao town, among more than two dozen kiln sites along the Meixi River that made pottery for export to Japan and South-East Asia from the 6th to the early 20th century. Excavations in 2002 uncovered kilns, workshops and waste heaps with hundreds of restorable pieces, and a museum of ancient Quanzhou export ceramics stands at the site, which is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Deji Gate Site
rows.summary: The excavated foundations of Deji Gate, the southern gate of Song–Yuan Quanzhou through which goods passed to and from the riverside port, lie open beside Tianhou Temple. First built in 1230 and destroyed by fire in 1948, the site was dug in 2000 and shows city-wall footings from the Song to the Qing, inner and outer moats, a stone bridge and the walls of the barbican. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Dharani Pillar of Taoyuan Palace
rows.summary: A Northern Song stone pillar carved with Buddhist dharani texts, standing in Taoyuan Palace, a village temple in Taoyuan, Fengzhou town. It was among the first sites protected by Fujian province in 1961 and joined the national list in 2019.

rows.name: Ding Family Ancestral Hall, Chendai
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Ding clan of Chendai, a Hui community whose forebears were Arabs who settled here in the early Ming. Founded in the Yongle era, burnt in 1560 and rebuilt in 1600, the hall is laid out like the character 回 around a central hall, and since 1985 it has housed an exhibition on the history of the Hui in Chendai.

rows.name: Fuxing Hall, Hushan
rows.summary: A southern Fujian-style family house completed in 1947 in Tangxi village, Hushan town, five bays wide and two courtyards deep with flanking side wings. Built of brick, stone and timber with about 1,570 m² of floor space, it borrows Western decorative details and has been on the national list since 2019.

rows.name: Jingsheng Villa
rows.summary: A four-storey villa completed in 1948 in Longxue village, Baogai town, that blends a European verandah house with southern Fujian building traditions. Five bays wide with verandas on all sides, it is built of brick, stone, timber and concrete and has been on the national list since 2019.

rows.name: Jiuri Mountain Inscriptions
rows.summary: A low hill at Fengzhou in Nan'an whose eastern and western peaks carry more than 70 cliff inscriptions from the Northern Song to the Qing, most of them Song. Several record the ceremonies at which Song officials prayed here each year for favourable winds for overseas shipping, and a stone Buddha was carved on the western peak in 965. As the Jiuri Mountain Wind-Praying Inscriptions it is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Jiuxian Mountain, Dehua
rows.summary: A mountain of about 1,650 m in northern Dehua, on the meeting point of Chishui, Shangyong and Daming townships, with a scenic area of about 35 km² known for rime ice on its trees in winter. A Song–Yuan stone Maitreya statue, protected by the province, and a weather station stand on the mountain.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple (Quanzhou)
rows.summary: Quanzhou's principal Buddhist temple, founded in 686 on West Street in the old city and covering some 7.8 hectares, is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site. Its twin five-storey granite pagodas, rebuilt in stone between 1228 and 1250 and 48 m and 44 m tall, are the tallest pair of stone pagodas in China, and the Ming main hall rests on 86 stone columns with carved flying musicians on its brackets. The grounds also hold Hindu carvings left by South Indian traders, an ordination platform and a memorial hall to the monk Hongyi.

rows.name: Kuixing Rock Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A Southern Song relief of the 'Three Sages of Huayan' — Shakyamuni flanked by the bodhisattvas Manjushri and Samantabhadra — carved on a rock face at the Kuixing Rock temple in Taochang, Shigu town, on the edge of Yongchun town. Protected by the province since 2001, it was added to the national list in 2019.

rows.name: Laozi Statue (Laojun Rock)
rows.summary: A seated figure of the philosopher Laozi carved from a single natural granite boulder at the foot of Mount Qingyuan's western peak, over 5 m high and about 7 m wide and made no later than the Song dynasty. Regarded as the largest Song Taoist stone statue in China, it shows the sage with a flowing beard, one arm resting on a low table and the other hand on his knee. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Li Family Residences, Guanshan
rows.summary: Three houses built between 1890 and 1936 in Guanshan village, Meishan township, by Li Gongcang, an overseas Chinese from Indonesia, and his eldest son Li Chengqi. They comprise a Western-influenced 'fanzai' house and two red-brick courtyard houses named after their builders, with about 1,400 m² of floor space in all.

rows.name: Lin Family Residence, Nan'an
rows.summary: Four side-by-side buildings — an ancestral hall, living quarters and a study — that the overseas Chinese builder Lin Lu designed for his home village of Manshanhong and completed in 1908. The red-brick courtyard houses follow southern Fujian tradition but have Western-style corner towers and imported cement floor tiles, and face a stone forecourt, a pond and a waterside pavilion.

rows.name: Lingshan Islamic Cemetery
rows.summary: Two tombs on the southern slope of Ling Hill, revered by Chinese Muslims as the graves of two early missionaries whom Ming sources say came to Quanzhou in the Tang dynasty, lie under a stone pavilion rebuilt in 1962. In the stone gallery behind are an Arabic inscription of 1322 and a stele recording that the admiral Zheng He came to burn incense here in 1417 before one of his voyages. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Liusheng Pagoda and Old Quanzhou Port Sites
rows.summary: An octagonal five-storey granite pagoda 36 m high on the southern shore of Quanzhou Bay at Shihu, first built in 1111 and rebuilt in 1285 as a landmark for ships, its storeys carved with guardian figures and bodhisattvas. About 1 km away is Shihu Dock, an old wharf said to date from the Tang. Both belong to a national heritage group of old port buildings that also includes Wanshou Pagoda on Baogai Mountain and Zhenwu Temple with the Song docks at Fashi in Quanzhou city, all components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Longshan Temple, Anhai
rows.summary: A Guanyin temple in Anhai town traditionally dated to 618, whose main image is a thousand-armed Guanyin that legend says was carved from a single camphor tree. The halls were rebuilt in 1831 with stone columns and carved bluestone panels at the gate, and hold calligraphy by the Ming master Zhang Ruitu and the monk Hongyi. Emigrants carried its cult abroad, and many temples trace their origin to it, including the Longshan temples of Bangka (Taipei), Lukang and Singapore.

rows.name: Luoyang Bridge
rows.summary: A stone beam bridge across the tidal mouth of the Luoyang River, built in 1053–1059 under the prefect Cai Xiang, whose builders strengthened its foundations by cultivating oysters on the stones. It now runs about 730 m by way of a mid-river islet, lined with Song guardian figures, small stone pagodas and inscribed stelae, and a memorial temple to Cai Xiang stands near its southern end. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Mount Qingyuan
rows.summary: A granite hill range on the northern edge of Quanzhou, protected as a national scenic area and scattered with shrines, hundreds of cliff inscriptions and Song–Yuan stone statues. Besides the famous Laozi statue at its western foot (separate card), carved figures on its slopes include a Buddha in a stone shrine of 1364 at Mituo Rock and a rare group of three Tibetan-style Buddhas carved in 1292 at Bixiao Rock. The stupa of the monk Hongyi also stands on the mountain.

rows.name: Nantian Temple Stone Buddhas
rows.summary: A hillside Buddhist temple on Daifeng Hill in Dongshi town, Jinjiang, known for its stone Buddha statues and cliff inscriptions of the Song and Ming dynasties. Protected by the province since 1985, the carvings were added to the national list in 2013.

rows.name: Niumulin Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain eco-tourism area in Xiayang town in the far west of Yongchun, described by the county as one of the best-preserved native forests in Fujian, with several waterfalls along its paths. It has been a 4A scenic area since 2003 and makes a full-day trip from Yongchun town.

rows.name: Qingjing Mosque
rows.summary: Founded in 1009 on Tumen Street in the old city, Qingjing is regarded as the oldest surviving mosque in China built in the Arab style, and it is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site. A tall gateway of dark diabase and white granite with pointed arches and a moon-watching platform on top leads to the roofless stone walls and columns of the original prayer hall. Beside them stand a smaller prayer hall of Ming foundation and a pavilion sheltering Yuan and Ming stelae on the mosque's restorations.

rows.name: Qingshan Palace, Hui'an
rows.summary: A folk-religion temple in Qingshan village, Shanxia town, Hui'an, dedicated to Qingshan Ling'an Zunwang, a mountain deity worshipped across the three old counties of Quanzhou. Its buildings date from the Ming and Qing dynasties, and it has been on the national heritage list since 2013.

rows.name: Qingshuiyan Temple
rows.summary: A mountain temple in Penglai town, Anxi, where the Northern Song monk Qingshui Zushi practised, and the mother temple of his cult, which spread with emigrants to Taiwan and South-East Asia. A pilgrims' stairway climbs to the main Penglai ancestral hall, and the grounds include a sacred spring, an ancient camphor tree, a square pond and a tree whose branches are said all to point north.

rows.name: Quanzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The prefectural Confucian temple and school of Quanzhou, on this site since the late 10th century and rebuilt in 1137, is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site. Its Dacheng Hall stands under a double-eaved, yellow-tiled hipped roof carried on carved dragon columns, with the school's Minglun Hall alongside. The side halls hold exhibitions on Quanzhou's history, the temple itself and the city's tradition of learning, and three Ming memorial shrines survive around the square.

rows.name: Quanzhou Museum
rows.summary: The city museum, opened in 2005 in a large building in southern Fujian style at the foot of Mount Qingyuan, north of West Lake Park. Its permanent galleries cover Quanzhou's history and notable people and the culture of the Minnan region, including Nanyin music, local opera and puppetry, drawn from a collection of more than 10,000 objects.

rows.name: Quanzhou Oulebao Ocean Kingdom
rows.summary: A seaside theme-park complex at Zhangban on the northern shore of Quanzhou Bay, made up of three parks: a water park, an ocean park with marine-life exhibits and staged shows, and a fairy-tale park with rides. Rated 4A in 2023 and also a provincial tourist resort, it suits families with children.

rows.name: Qudougong Kiln Site (Dehua Kilns)
rows.summary: The excavated remains of a Song–Yuan kiln on the southern slope of Pozhai Hill at Dehua, the porcelain-making town of inland Quanzhou: a dragon kiln divided into chambers, a step towards the later stepped kiln. Found in 1953 and dug in 1976, it forms the Dehua Kilns component of the Quanzhou World Heritage site with the Weilin–Neiban kilns, and a display hall beside it shows more than 600 pieces from Dehua's old kilns.

rows.name: Shiniu Mountain
rows.summary: A granite mountain in Shuikou town, north-eastern Dehua, named after a great rock on it that looks like a bull, and protected as a national forest park and national geopark. Its main peak rises to 1,782 m, and it is known for steep peaks, oddly shaped rocks and caves, the Daixian twin waterfalls with a total drop of 314 m, and the Shihu Temple, a folk-Taoist shrine.

rows.name: Stone Buddha of Xizi Temple
rows.summary: Song-dynasty stone Buddha carvings on Zhuowang Hill in Yanfeng village, Jinjing town, on the south-eastern coast of Jinjiang, kept at the hillside Xizi Temple. Protected by the province since 1985, they were added to the national list in 2013.

rows.name: Tianhou Temple, Quanzhou
rows.summary: A temple to the sea goddess Mazu founded in 1196 near the old southern gate and river port, and regarded as one of the oldest and highest-ranking Mazu temples in China; many Mazu temples in Taiwan and South-East Asia trace their origin to it. Along its axis stand a gateway with a stage, a main hall with a richly decorated double-eaved roof and a Ming rear hall. It is one of the components of the Quanzhou World Heritage site.

rows.name: Tomb of Koxinga (Zheng Chenggong)
rows.summary: The hillside family tomb of Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga), the Ming loyalist commander who defeated the Dutch East India Company on Taiwan at the siege of Fort Zeelandia in 1662 and died suddenly the same year. His remains were brought back to his home district and the tomb was built in 1699, holding him with his son and his father in nine chambers in three rows, fronted by a pair of carved stone columns and a stone lion. Items found in his coffin are shown at the Zheng Chenggong Memorial Hall in nearby Shijing.

rows.name: Tukeng Village
rows.summary: A former harbour village on the southern shore of Meizhou Bay in Houlong town, whose merchants prospered in the Ming and Qing from seaborne trade and from pawnshops, pharmacies, cloth shops and timber yards. Its red-brick mansions stand closely side by side along a grid of four main lanes and five cross lanes, and it is listed as a Famous Historic and Cultural Village of China.

rows.name: Wudianshi Historic Quarter
rows.summary: A restored historic quarter in central Jinjiang, said to be named after five shops opened here by the Cai clan in the Tang dynasty, with more than 130 Ming, Qing and early modern buildings: red-brick houses, Western-influenced 'fanzai' houses, ancestral halls and temples. Next to a modern shopping centre, it now holds museums and exhibition halls, studios, cafés and teahouses among the old houses.

rows.name: Wulin Traditional Village
rows.summary: A 600-year-old home village of emigrants to the Philippines and South-East Asia in Xintang, Jinjiang, with 132 historic buildings: red-brick southern Fujian mansions next to Gothic and Roman-style villas and hybrid 'fanzai' houses that returning emigrants built mainly in the 1930s. Restored from 2018 and opened as a scenic area, it has cafés and restaurants in the old houses and folk performances during festivals.

rows.name: Wutayan Stone Pagodas
rows.summary: Song-dynasty stone pagodas at Wutayan ('Five Pagodas Rock'), a hillside temple on Longshui Hill near Zhukou village, Guanqiao town, Nan'an. Protected by the province since 1996, they were added to the national list in 2013.

rows.name: Xiheshan Tieguanyin Culture Park
rows.summary: A tea-themed leisure park on the edge of Anxi town built around Tieguanyin, the oolong tea for which Anxi is famous, and rated 4A in 2022. It combines tea gardens and a tea exhibition hall with flower fields, a lake, glass tea houses and children's play areas, and suits families and tea lovers.

rows.name: Yang Amiao Residence
rows.summary: The house of Yang Amiao, a late-Qing overseas Chinese, built over 18 years from 1894 to 1911 in Tingdian on the southern side of the Jin River. It is a large red-brick residence in the southern Fujian style laid out around five courtyards, with a square pavilion under a rolled roof added in front of the eastern flower hall.

rows.name: Yingliang Stone Natural History Museum
rows.name_zh: 英良石材自然历史博物馆
rows.summary: A museum founded by a local stone merchant near Shuitou, the stone-trading town of Nan'an, in a modern building conceived like a book of stone pages.
