Its collection of more than 100,000 items runs from meteorites, minerals and gem crystals to fossils, the best known being 'Baby Yingliang', an oviraptorosaur embryo curled inside its egg, and a laboratory lets visitors watch fossils being prepared.

rows.name: Yongchun Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county Confucian temple of Yongchun, founded in the 1040s and rebuilt in 1785, on Taocheng Road in the county town. Facing south over some 3,000 m², it has a screen wall, the Lingxing Gate, a semicircular pool, the Ji Gate, side halls and a Dacheng Hall with a double-eaved roof, encircling verandas and four carved stone dragon columns at the front.

rows.name: Yuanhe 1916 Creative Industry Park
rows.summary: A creative park in former factory buildings on Xinmen Street at the western edge of Quanzhou's old city, centred on the Yuanhe Tang candied-fruit works founded in 1916 and later joined by neighbouring flour, television and jute mills. Old workshops, a barley store and a red-brick chimney more than 20 m tall have been kept and now house design and craft studios, shops and cafés, with exhibitions on the site's industrial past.

rows.name: Yunlonggu Gorge
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area in Foling village, Guobao township, on the southern slopes of the Daiyun Mountains near Jiuxian Mountain, named after its long winding valley and a small temple, Yunlong Palace. Rated 4A in 2023, it is built around a frog mascot, with walking trails and boardwalks through the wooded valley, gorge rafting, a children's playground, a petting area and a campsite, and suits families.

rows.name: Zhongxiandi Mansion, Shijing
rows.summary: A large Qing-dynasty courtyard mansion on Yanping East Road in Shijing town, Nan'an, built for the family of Zheng Yunjin and known locally as the 'Ninety-Nine Rooms'. It is a protected example of southern Fujian residential architecture, on the national list since 2013.

rows.name: Anzhen Fort
rows.summary: A huge fortified earthen house in Huainan town, Yong'an, built in 1885–99 by the local gentleman Chi Zhanrui and his son to protect their family from bandits, which it did through three sieges. Behind outer walls of stone and rammed earth 9 m high and 4 m thick, pierced by nearly 200 firing holes, more than 360 rooms are arranged in three courtyards rising 4 m up the slope, and the halls keep a wealth of murals and wood carving. It is regarded as the largest surviving earthen fort in the Sanming area.

rows.name: Central Soviet Area Anti-Encirclement Memorial Park, Jianning
rows.name_zh: 中央苏区反“围剿”纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park in the north of Jianning town on the county's role in the Red Army's campaigns against the Nationalist government's encirclement offensives of 1930–34; Red Army units took Jianning on 31 May 1931 in the last battle of the second campaign. It contains the former headquarters of the leading organs of the First Front Red Army, used in 1931–33, and the former residence of Zhou Enlai as head of its General Political Department, together with an exhibition hall on the campaigns and a bronze sculpture group nearly 100 m long.

rows.name: Dajin Lake and Taining Geopark
rows.summary: Taining's 5A scenic area covers the Taining UNESCO Global Geopark, about 490 km² of mainly Danxia red-sandstone landscape, part of which is inscribed in the China Danxia World Heritage Site. Its centrepiece is Dajin Lake, a reservoir filled from 1980 whose winding arms run between red cliffs, rock towers and gorges and are toured by boat, with shoreline sights such as Ganlu Temple. Other zones include the Shangqing Stream, the old county town and Jinnao Mountain.

rows.name: Datian Earthen Forts
rows.summary: Five fortified earthen houses (tubao) in Datian county make up this national heritage group: Pipa Fort in Jianshe town, Fanglian Fort in Junxi town, Anliang Fort in Taoyuan town, and Tai'an Fort and Guangchong Hall in Xiaohua village, Taihua town, built between the Qianlong reign (1736–95) and 1857. They were built as defensible family homes, with rammed-earth outer walls enclosing halls and living quarters, a building type typical of the hills of central Fujian. Two more forts, Guangyu and Shaohui in Guangping town, are provincial-level monuments.

rows.name: Daxianfeng 'Tea Beauty' Scenic Area
rows.summary: A tea-themed scenic area around Daxian Peak in Pingshan township, Datian, whose terraced tea gardens have been named among China's 30 most beautiful and whose cherry trees blossom in late winter. Datian grows about 70 per cent of China's 'Oriental Beauty' (meiren) tea, and monks at the Chongsheng Rock temple on Daxian Peak, founded in 1164, are recorded as growing tea around it. The mountain is also a provincial nature reserve.

rows.name: Dishuiyan Red Army Field Hospital Site
rows.summary: A karst cave about 2.5 km from Mingxi town where the Red Army ran a field hospital from 1931 to 1934, treating more than 250 of its own wounded and some 540 wounded prisoners; the cave had water and gave cover from air attack. A memorial stone marks the 'Former Site of the Red Army Field Hospital', and the area has been developed as a red-tourism scenic area, rated 4A in 2022.

rows.name: Gexikao National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park at Louyuan in Xinkou town, south-west of Sanming, protecting a natural forest of Castanopsis kawakamii (gexikao), a tall evergreen of the beech family listed as near-threatened. The surrounding nature reserve holds about 700 hectares of it, and paths lead through the old trees of a park that is also run as a forest-wellness base.

rows.name: Guifeng Village
rows.summary: A hillside village in Yangzhong town, north-eastern Youxi, where 39 Ming and Qing buildings with yellow walls and dark tiles are stacked up three slopes around a valley; it is a national historic and cultural village, described as one of the best-preserved old villages in Fujian. It once stood on the road between Youxi and Fuzhou, and old houses such as the Stone Lion House and Louping Hall survive along with stone paths, ancient trees and inscribed tablets. Today it has homestays and tea houses and holds festivals such as an autumn crop-drying festival.

rows.name: Guxi Xinghe Resort
rows.summary: A leisure resort in the hills of Tangchuan township, eastern Youxi, at about 870 m above sea level, developed since 2016 in what had been an empty mountain valley. It has hotels and homestays, including a hotel in the shape of an earthen tulou, farm fields, children's play areas and a park devoted to the local goddess Ma Xian, and holds seasonal events such as a rape-flower festival and a summer firefly season.

rows.name: Jinnao Mountain (Minjiang Source Eco-tourism Area)
rows.summary: The eco-tourism area of Jinnao Mountain in south-eastern Jianning, inside the Minjiang Source national nature reserve; the range's main peak, Baishiding, reaches 1,858 m, and its spur Yanfeng Mountain is taken as the true source of the Min River. The forests hold ancient ginkgo and Japanese cedar, village cattle graze on the upland meadows in summer, and a cable car climbs towards the summit area.

rows.name: Jiufu Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in Xicheng town, south-west of Youxi town, lying within the Jiufushan provincial nature reserve. An eco-tourism zone with a gate, visitor centre and other facilities was built in the reserve's experimental zone from 2013 and rated 4A in 2019. It is also a provincial forest-wellness base whose streams and shady forest draw visitors in summer.

rows.name: Jiulongtan, Taining
rows.summary: A Danxia gorge north of Taining town where visitors drift on bamboo rafts between red cliffs and deep green pools. In the evening the 'Dream of Jiulongtan' night tour lights the gorge with projections, installations and a light show. It lies on the road to Shangqing, in the core of the Taining heritage and geopark landscape along with the Shangqing Stream and Zhuangyuan Rock.

rows.name: Mingqing Garden, Taining
rows.summary: A museum park on the Jinxi River just east of Taining town, made up of dozens of old Ming- and Qing-style buildings collected from elsewhere; the first phase has nine buildings on different themes and a large collection of carved woodwork. Since 2022 one hall, the Baifu Guan, has displayed more than 100 Ming and Qing objects decorated with the character fu (good fortune), such as chests, plaques and steelyards.

rows.name: Ruiyun Mountain
rows.summary: A small hill scenic area of about 3 km² in Chenda town on the northern edge of Sanming city, combining forest with temple buildings and old rock inscriptions. Its sights include Tianma Rock and Ruiyun Cave, and groves of the rare Sichuan cycad and of ubame oak.

rows.name: Sansteel Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: Industrial tours inside the works of Fujian Sansteel, the steel producer in the Liexi area of Sanming. The route links the 1958 Industrial Memory Park and Memory Hall, on the city's industrial past, a safety-education hall and three viewing areas in the working plant, where visitors follow steelmaking from molten iron through to the rolling mills. In 2026 it was named among Fujian's first priority projects for industrial tourism.

rows.name: Shangshu Di, Taining
rows.summary: A Ming mansion on Shangshu Street in Taining's old town, built in the late Wanli and Tianqi reigns (early 1600s) for Li Chunye, Minister of War: five houses side by side, each with three courtyards, on a plot about 80 m by 50 m. Next to it the Shide Tang, six parallel houses of the Chen family from the early to middle Ming, and several Qing houses and an ancestral hall complete a group often described as one of the most intact sets of Ming town houses in southern China.

rows.name: Shaxian Snack Culture City
rows.summary: A food-themed quarter built from the late 2000s at the foot of Taojin Mountain on the north-west side of Shaxian town, laid out in the style of the mansions of the area's wealthy Ming and Qing families. It is the showcase for Shaxian snacks, the cheap eateries serving wontons (bianrou) and other local dishes that Shaxian people run in thousands of towns across China, and is lined with restaurants and shops.

rows.name: Shibi Hakka Ancestral Land
rows.summary: Shibi in Ninghua county is revered as the cradle of the Hakka people, the place where Hakka forebears settled before spreading south and overseas. The scenic area centres on the Shibi Hakka Ancestral Hall, said to be the largest of its kind and treated as the common ancestral temple of some 120 Hakka surnames; a World Hakka ancestor-worship ceremony has been held here each autumn since 1995.

rows.name: Shuimei Earthen Forts
rows.summary: Three fortified earthen houses built by the Zhang family of Shuimei village, Shaxian, between the Daoguang and Tongzhi reigns (1821–74): Shuangji, Shuangxing and the largest, Shuangyuan, which covers about 6,000 m² and climbs the hillside in tiers. Their high, thick walls with a walkway, corner towers and firing holes enclose halls with painted wood carving, and a few Zhang households still live in Shuangyuan. Together they are described as the largest group of earthen forts in Shaxian and the only cluster of forts built side by side in Sanming.

rows.name: Shuiwei Red Army Village
rows.summary: A mountain village in Kefang township on the Fujian–Jiangxi border which was a rear base of the Red Army and seat of the Jianning county Soviet government in the early 1930s. Restored former sites include the headquarters of the Fujian–Jiangxi guerrilla column, a Red Army hospital, an arsenal, a Soviet-area bank and the Soviet government office, and the village now caters mainly for study groups, with homestays in a converted school.

rows.name: Taoyuan Cave and Linyin Stone Forest
rows.summary: A Danxia landscape scenic area of about 29 km² north-east of Yong'an city, made up of Taoyuan Cave, Baizhang Rock and three other zones; its best-known sight is Yixiantian, a cleft 90 m high and 127 m long that narrows to 0.4 m and is climbed by 206 steps. Rebels of Deng Maoqi's Ming-dynasty uprising held a stockade here, and three gates and stretches of wall remain. The listing also covers the Linyin Stone Forest, a 1.2 km² field of rock pillars about 13 km north-west of the city.

rows.name: Tian'e Cave, Ninghua
rows.summary: A group of limestone caves east of Ninghua town, the core of a 143 km² national geopark of karst landscapes. Tian'e (Swan) Cave is dense with stalactites, stalagmites and flowstone, and visitors take a boat along the Shenfeng underground river, where pillars of rock rise from the water. The caves stay at about 18 °C all year.

rows.name: Tianfang Yuetan Hot Springs
rows.summary: A hot-spring and forest-wellness resort at Gaolai near Songkou in eastern Qingliu, in what the county describes as Fujian's densest belt of hot springs. Its pools are fed by natural springs, and visitors can cook eggs in the hot water; the resort is also a provincial water-conservancy scenic area and a holiday base for workers' rest-and-recuperation trips.

rows.name: Wanshouyan Site
rows.summary: A small, isolated limestone hill at Yanqian, west of Sanming, whose caves hold the oldest known traces of people in Fujian: stone tools from Lingfeng Cave have been dated to about 185,000 years ago, and Chuanfan Cave preserves a stone-paved floor and drainage channel some 30,000–20,000 years old. Saved from quarrying in 2000, the site has had a museum since 2006, the only museum of a Palaeolithic site in Fujian, and opened as a national archaeological site park in 2019. The surrounding Wanshouyan culture-and-tourism town adds parkland, a children's play area themed on early cave life and a library branch in a converted steelworks building.

rows.name: Xiatianxia Scenic Area
rows.summary: A martial-arts (wuxia) themed adventure area in Tangchuan township, eastern Youxi, which opened in 2015 as the county's first A-rated attraction. A plank walkway winds along the cliffs, and the main thrills are a two-level glass suspension bridge and a lift up the cliff built in the shape of a sword.

rows.name: Yong'an Wartime Provincial Capital Sites
rows.summary: From 1938 to 1945 Yong'an was Fujian's wartime provincial capital, and twelve buildings used by the provincial government and its offices form this heritage group, listed among the national memorial sites of the War of Resistance against Japan in 2015. Most are old houses in and around Jishan village, about 4 km from the city centre, which held the provincial courts and health and education offices and, at Fuxing Fort, the Kuomintang's Taiwan party branch; the government itself worked from the Confucian temple in the city. Jishan was also where Fujian's music college was founded in 1940, soon one of the country's three national conservatories of the time.

rows.name: Yuhua Cave
rows.summary: A limestone cave often described as the largest in Fujian, at the foot of Tianjie Mountain south-east of Jiangle town, with about 6 km of passages through six chambers and three underground streams thick with stalactites and stalagmites. The traveller Xu Xiake explored it in 1628 and compared it favourably with Zhanggong Cave in Yixing, and 17 inscriptions from the Song to the Republican period survive at the entrances and inside.

rows.name: Zhengshun Temple
rows.summary: A temple to the local deity Xie You in the Liexi area of central Sanming, founded in 1233 and regarded as the oldest and best-preserved timber building in the city. The seven-bay main hall is mostly Ming, but its spindle-shaped pillars, column bases and steps survive from the Song, and the gateway carries a 'Zhengshun' plaque said to be in the hand of Emperor Xiaozong. It housed the Sanming Museum from 1986 to 2012 and has held exhibitions again since 2016.

rows.name: Zhu Xi Cultural Park
rows.summary: A park at the birthplace of the Neo-Confucian philosopher Zhu Xi, born here in 1130, on Gongshan hill on the south side of Youxi town. At its heart is the Nanxi Academy, founded in 1241 on the site of the house lent to his father where he was born, with the square half-mu pond named after one of his best-known poems; new Song-style buildings around it hold a Zhu Xi museum and further academy halls, and a second phase is being added.

rows.name: Aoyuan and the Tomb of Tan Kah Kee
rows.summary: A walled memorial garden on the Jimei waterfront holding the tomb of Tan Kah Kee (1874–1961), the Singapore-based businessman and philanthropist who founded the Jimei schools and Xiamen University; he began building the tomb in 1955 and was buried here in 1961. A long gallery of carved stone panels leads to the Jimei Liberation Monument, and behind it the turtle-shaped tomb is ringed with stone reliefs showing scenes from his life.

rows.name: Beichen Mountain
rows.summary: A hill park of about 12 km² in Wuxian town, Tong'an, best known for the Twelve Dragon Pools, a chain of waterfalls and clear pools of different sizes running down a valley from near the top of the hill. It also has cultural spots such as the Hundred Dragon Garden.

rows.name: Early Buildings of Jimei School Village and Xiamen University
rows.name_zh: 集美学村和厦门大学早期建筑
rows.pinyin: Jíměi Xuécūn hé Xiàmén Dàxué Zǎoqī Jiànzhù
rows.summary: Thirty-one school and university buildings put up between the 1920s and the 1950s with money from Tan Kah Kee, in the 'Jiageng style' that combines Western and Chinese elements. They stand in Jimei School Village, the campus town he began in 1913 on the mainland shore facing Xiamen Island, among them the Nanxun and Daonan buildings, and on Xiamen University's main campus by the sea in Siming District.

rows.name: Fantawild Dreamland Xiamen
rows.summary: A theme park in Tong'an District opened in 2013 by the Huaqiang Fantawild group, covering about 40 hectares. Most of its main attractions are large indoor rides and shows using 4D film and other special effects, many on themes from Chinese stories and culture, and it suits a full day out with children.

rows.name: Huihe Stone Culture Park
rows.summary: A park in Huli District devoted to stone carving, with a stone-culture gallery, a stone carving museum, a treasure gallery and a hall of 'stone shadow carving', a southern Fujian craft listed as intangible heritage, plus space for workshops and folk performances. It runs study trips and family activities around stone carving and suits anyone curious about southern Fujian's stone-carving tradition.

rows.name: Hulishan Fort
rows.summary: A coastal fort on the south-eastern tip of Xiamen Island, completed in 1896 in a mix of European and Chinese styles, with granite ramparts, underground passages, barracks, magazines, lookout posts and a moat. Its main exhibit is a late-19th-century 280 mm Krupp breech-loading coastal gun, about 13 m long, the survivor of the fort's original pair; appraisals by the National Cultural Heritage Administration and the Krupp archive identified it as the largest surviving 19th-century coastal gun. The fort looks out across the water towards Kinmen.

rows.name: Laoyuanzi Folk Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 老院子民俗文化风情园
rows.summary: A commercial culture park opened in 2015 near Xiamen North Railway Station, with a folk-culture area built in southern Fujian style. Its centrepiece is 'Minnan Legend', a live-action show on southern Fujian history and folk life in which a 3,000-seat moving grandstand carries the audience between outdoor sets, with motorboat stunts, high diving and water effects ending with a statue of the sea goddess Mazu rising from the water.

rows.name: Qingjiao and Baijiao Ciji Palaces
rows.summary: Twin founding temples of Baosheng Dadi, the deified Song-dynasty physician Wu Tao, about 3 km apart on either side of the Xiamen–Zhangzhou boundary: the 'east palace' in Qingjiao village, Haicang District, Xiamen, and the 'west palace' in Baijiao village, Jiaomei town, Longhai District, Zhangzhou. Both were founded in the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song and rebuilt in the Qing with some Song stonework surviving, and they are known for their carved stone dragon columns in southern Fujian style. They are the mother temples of Baosheng Dadi worship in southern Fujian, Taiwan and South-East Asia.

rows.name: Riyue Valley Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at the foot of Tianzhu Mountain in Haicang, with indoor and outdoor thermal pools in gardens styled after South-East Asia, leisure facilities and a hotel. The resort describes its water as a mild, neutral silicate spring.

rows.name: Site of the Xiamen Prison Break
rows.summary: The former Siming county jail on Siming South Road, where on 25 May 1930 an armed Communist team led by Tao Zhu broke in and freed more than 40 imprisoned party members and supporters without loss. Three Republican-era cell blocks and an interrogation room survive inside a brick perimeter wall, and the site is now a small memorial museum with an exhibition on the break-out, replica instruments of torture and restored cells. The event inspired Gao Yunlan's novel 'Annals of a Provincial Town' (Xiaocheng Chunqiu).

rows.name: Tianzhu Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: Forested hills in Dongfu, Haicang, on Xiamen's western mainland edge, with lakes and valleys, a bamboo garden of more than 200 kinds of bamboo and around 60 cultural spots, including small Buddhist and Taoist temples such as Longmen Temple and Zhenji Temple. Tianzhu Lake, at its eastern end, mirrors the temples and ridges around it.

rows.name: Xiamen Botanical Gardens
rows.summary: A large botanical garden founded in 1960 on Wanshi Hill, close to central Xiamen, covering 4.91 km² and holding more than 9,000 plant species. It is laid out in 16 themed sections, among them a rainforest area, cactus, succulent, palm and bamboo gardens and a large bougainvillea collection, and several old temples such as Wanshilian Temple stand within the grounds.

rows.name: Xiamen Chengyi Nature Exploration Museum
rows.summary: An indoor family museum in Jimei, opened as the Chengyi Discovery Center with exhibits on space, aviation and navigation, which reopened on 3 July 2026 after a refit as a natural-history centre. Its four new halls, covering 7,260 m², use fossils, dioramas and hands-on displays to tell the story of life on Earth, with material from the National Museum of Natural History, the Hezheng Paleozoological Museum in Gansu and the Yingliang Stone Natural History Museum.

rows.name: Xiamen Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: The site of the 6th China International Garden and Flower Expo in 2007, built on Xinglin Bay in Jimei by cutting channels through the bay's central islands to form nine islands joined by 16 bridges. About half of its roughly 10 km² is water, and the islands are laid out as gardens in many different styles, now used for flower shows, recreation and outdoor learning.

rows.name: Xiamen Lingling International Circus City
rows.summary: A circus-themed resort in Xinglin, Jimei, with a large circus theatre seating about 10,000, an 'animal kingdom' zoo area, a hotel and play areas for children. The theatre stages a resident circus show with acrobats from many countries alongside performing-animal acts.

rows.name: Baitang Bay
rows.summary: Baitang Bay, on the coast of Longjiao She Ethnic Township facing Xiamen across the water, has a 3.2-km crescent of sandy beach and the ancient volcanic crater at Niutou Shan, whose rows of basalt columns are nicknamed the 'terracotta warriors of the sea'. The resort area adds a visitor centre, an infinity pool by the sea, a volcano science hall, a container hotel, camping and caravan sites and flower fields.

rows.name: Former Tianyi Remittance Bureau
rows.summary: The Tianyi bureau was founded in 1880 by Guo Youpin, an Overseas Chinese merchant in the Philippines, in his home village of Liuchuan to carry letters and money ('qiaopi') between emigrants and their families. By 1911 it had 28 branches in China and South-East Asia, and it handled a large share of southern Fujian's remittances before closing in 1928. The surviving buildings include the Wannan Lou of 1911 and a two-storey Chinese–Western office block of 1921.

rows.name: Gaofeng Valley
rows.summary: Gaofeng Valley is a mountain tea-garden resort near Guanfeng village in Xiazhai town, western Pinghe, run by a Zhangzhou state-owned group around some 1,000 mu (about 67 hectares) of tea gardens. Visitors come for walks through the tea gardens and wooded valley, tea-culture activities and on-site lodging.

rows.name: Guanshe She Village
rows.summary: Guanshe is a She ethnic village in the hills of Xinxu town, Hua'an County, promoted as 'Colourful Guanshe' for its brightly painted houses. It opened as a scenic area in 2019 and puts on She cultural events for visitors, such as displays of She wedding customs at holiday times.

rows.name: Hua'an Tulou (Dadi Cluster)
rows.summary: The Hua'an tulou tourist area centres on the Dadi cluster in Xiandu town: three large earthen houses, Eryi Lou, Nanyang Lou and Dongyang Lou, built by the Jiang family in the Qing dynasty and inscribed in 2008 as part of the Fujian Tulou World Heritage Site. Eryi Lou, built in 1770, has a four-storey outer ring around a single-storey inner ring, and each family's vertical section has its own staircase instead of shared open galleries. The cluster lies some 80 km north-east of the better-known Nanjing and Yongding tulou.

rows.name: Jiangdong Bridge
rows.summary: Also known as the Hudu ('Tiger Crossing') Bridge, this crossing of the North Jiulong River began as a pontoon bridge in 1190, became a timber bridge on stone piers in 1210 and was rebuilt in stone after a fire in 1237. Bombing during the Second Sino-Japanese War left only five of the old piers, which were given a reinforced-concrete deck in 1969. Two spans still carry original stone beams about 23 m long, which the historian of science Joseph Needham judged to have no equal elsewhere.

rows.name: Jintang Bay
rows.summary: Jintang Bay is a seaside hot-spring resort at Chendai town on the coast of Yunxiao County, built around a natural seawater hot spring with a high mineral content. Its seawater hot-spring park is the main draw for visitors.

rows.name: Lin Ancestral Hall (Bigan Temple), Zhangzhou
rows.summary: Built jointly by the Lin clans of Zhangzhou's seven counties, this ancestral hall on Zhencheng Lane is also called the Bigan Temple, because the Lins honour the ancient Shang-dynasty noble Bigan as their founding ancestor. Its surviving main hall and east corridor are Ming: the three-bay timber hall, under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, keeps building features of the Song and Yuan periods.

rows.name: Lin Family Charitable Estate
rows.summary: This charitable estate was built in 1819–21 by Lin Pinghou, a native of the old Longxi County who made his fortune in Taiwan and founded the Lin Ben Yuan family of Banqiao, to support his clansmen at home. The courtyard complex has 99 rooms over about 2,500 m², and a stele of twelve polished black stone slabs set into the wall records how the estate was founded, funded and run.

rows.name: Lukai Eco-Manor
rows.summary: Lukai Eco-Manor is a farm resort at Zhouzai village in the Shuangdi Overseas Chinese Farm, a state farm founded in 1960 to resettle Chinese returnees from Indonesia, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries. It combines leisure farming with study visits for school groups and suits families looking for a countryside day out near Zhangzhou.

rows.name: Malan Bay
rows.summary: Malan Bay is a broad sandy bay in Kangmei town on the east coast of Dongshan Island, run as a public beach resort area. It makes an easy add-on to the Wind-Moved Rock and old town at Tongling, a few kilometres to the north.

rows.name: Nanshan Palace, Hua'an
rows.summary: Nanshan Palace, on the eastern slope of Nanshan at Qinling village just south of Hua'an town, is a folk temple to the deities Shengzu Daxian and Dutong Sheren, founded in 1275 and rebuilt in 1505. Its main hall, dating from the late Ming or early Qing, is a three-bay timber building with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, an encircling gallery and an octagonal spiral coffered ceiling.

rows.name: Pinghe City God Temple, Jiufeng
rows.summary: This Qing-dynasty City God temple stands in Jiufeng, which was the seat of Pinghe County from its founding in 1518 until 1949 and is now listed as a national historic and cultural town. A visit can be combined with Jiufeng's old streets and the tulou in the surrounding villages of western Pinghe.

rows.name: Sanping Temple
rows.summary: Sanping Temple, in the hills of Wenfeng town in eastern Pinghe, grew from the retreat where the Tang Chan monk Yizhong (781–872), revered as the Sanping Patriarch, preached from the 820s. Its present buildings are Qing, and it keeps an edict plaque from Emperor Xuanzong of Tang granting him the title Guangji Dashi, a stone image of the patriarch and a camphor-wood statue of him with movable limbs. Worship of the patriarch spread with emigrants to Taiwan and South-East Asia and is listed as national intangible cultural heritage.

rows.name: Shili Lanshan
rows.summary: Shili Lanshan is a hillside leisure park in the Mayangxi Eco-Tourism Zone of Changtai, on the boundary with Xiamen, with flower fields, walking trails and a campsite that looks out over the lights of Xiamen after dark. It suits an easy half-day outing from Xiamen or Zhangzhou.

rows.name: Southeast Flower Capital Expo Park
rows.summary: This flower park at Xiban village in Zhangpu's Guanxun town is the showground of Zhangzhou's annual flower expo, held here since 1999 and long known as the Cross-Strait Flower Expo; in 2025 it took place as the Southeast Modern Agriculture Expo and Flower Expo. The roads leading to it run through a long corridor of nurseries in one of the area's main flower-growing districts, and the park itself displays flowers, potted plants and nursery trees.

rows.name: Tianfu 'Crossing to Taiwan' Stone Carving Park
rows.name_zh: 天福“唐山过台湾”石雕园
rows.pinyin: Tiānfú Tángshān Guò Táiwān Shídiāo Yuán
rows.summary: Opened in 2003 beside the Tianfu service area on the coastal expressway, this sculpture park was paid for by Li Ruihe, the Taiwan-born founder of the Tianfu tea group, whose ancestors sailed to Taiwan from Zhangpu. About a hundred groups of stone carvings tell the story of the migrants who crossed the strait from southern Fujian to Taiwan ('Tangshan' was their old name for the mainland they left) and of their descendants who later returned to invest, and a second section shows Fujian and Taiwan folk customs.

rows.name: Tianfu Tea Museum
rows.summary: Built by the Tianfu tea group as a non-profit cultural project, this museum complex at the company's tea estate covers about 130 mu (8.7 ha). Its galleries trace some 3,000 years of Chinese tea culture and tea customs in other countries, alongside a hall on the company's history and a hall of calligraphy and painting.

rows.name: Tianzhushan Happy World
rows.summary: This theme park and resort inside the Tianzhu Mountain National Forest Park in Changtai was developed from 2011 and opened in 2017–18. Its centrepiece is an ocean park with a large aquarium tank, alongside an animal park with some 200 species, and staged dolphin and sea-lion shows are put on in its theatre.

rows.name: Wind-Moved Rock and Guandi Temple, Dongshan
rows.summary: On the seaside rocks by the east gate of Tongshan, the stone-walled town built in 1387 to guard the coast against pirates, the Wind-Moved Rock is a huge boulder resting on a tiny base that seems to rock in the wind. The scenic area also takes in the old town's walls and gate and the Dongshan Guandi Temple, founded in 1387 and rebuilt in 1680, from which many of Taiwan's Guandi temples trace their incense. The Ming calligrapher and loyalist Huang Daozhou was born in the town.

rows.name: Wugengliao Backyard Blast Furnaces
rows.summary: Eight cylindrical red-brick blast furnaces, each about 5 m tall, stand in a north–south row at Wugengliao in Shangtian village, the remains of an ironworks set up during the 1958 Great Leap Forward steel campaign. At its height the site had 24 furnaces, but poor-quality iron and difficult transport ended production in April 1960 and most were later demolished.

rows.name: Xianzitan Rock Carvings
rows.summary: Xianzitan, the 'Pool of the Immortals' Writing', at Tainei village near Shajian in southern Hua'an, is named after the ancient carved marks on its cliff face, rock art that the national heritage listing dates to between the Neolithic and the Zhou dynasty. The carvings were among the first sites to be protected by Fujian province, in 1961, and in 2015 the China Rock Art Association put Xianzitan, the only site from Fujian, on its first list of certified rock-art sites.

rows.name: Yundongyan
rows.summary: Yundongyan ('Cloud Cave Rock') is a hill of small caves and boulders on the eastern edge of Zhangzhou city whose rocks carry more than 200 inscriptions from the Five Dynasties to the Qing, among them the characters 'Xishan Diyi' ('first among streams and hills') attributed to the Song philosopher Zhu Xi, who lectured here. It is a provincial-level scenic area with paths climbing past the carved rock faces.

rows.name: Zeng Family 'Fanzai Lou', Dongmei
rows.summary: Completed in 1911 for the Zeng family of Dongmei, this compound of 13 buildings and 99 rooms mixes Chinese and Western styles: a front row of traditional southern Fujian houses, a central block in 'Nanyang Gothic' style and a rear row of red-brick arcaded buildings. It covers more than 5,300 m², laid out in five columns and three rows.

rows.name: Zhangpu Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Zhangpu's Confucian temple was founded in the Song dynasty and rebuilt in 1369, at the start of the Ming; only its Dacheng Hall survives. The hall, five bays wide and five deep, has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, a front gallery and elaborate bracket sets under the eaves.

rows.name: Zhangzhou Coastal Volcano National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 漳州滨海火山国家地质公园
rows.pinyin: Zhāngzhōu Bīnhǎi Huǒshān Guójiā Dìzhì Gōngyuán
rows.summary: This national geopark protects the volcanic coast of southern Zhangzhou, shaped by eruptions millions of years ago; this scenic area covers its Zhangpu section between Qianting and Fotan. Columnar-jointed basalt, old craters, clusters of gas vents and lava formations line the shore and the offshore islets, notably Linjin Islet. The geopark's ancient crater at Niutou Shan, across the boundary in Longhai, is visited from Baitang Bay.

rows.name: Zhangzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Founded in 1139 and rebuilt in 1482, Zhangzhou's prefectural Confucian temple keeps its ceremonial gate, Dacheng Gate, side halls, terrace and Dacheng Hall in a south-facing compound of about 2,600 m². The five-bay main hall, under a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, shows features of early southern Fujian (Minnan) timber architecture.

rows.name: Zhangzhou Stone Memorial Arches
rows.summary: Four carved stone memorial archways stand in Zhangzhou's old town: two from the Ming Wanli reign (1605 and 1619) at Shuangmending on Hong Kong Road, honouring the officials Lin Shizhang and Jiang Mengyu, and two from the Qing Kangxi reign on Xinhua East Road, raised for the generals Lan Li (1707) and Xu Feng (1722). Each is a three-bay, five-roofed structure on twelve columns, 11–12.5 m tall, built of alternating grey-blue and white stone and regarded as fine examples of southern Fujian stone carving.

rows.name: Zhaojiabao and Yi'anbao Fortified Villages
rows.summary: Zhaojiabao is a walled village built from 1600 by Zhao Fan, a Ming official descended from the Southern Song imperial prince Zhao Ruohe, and enlarged by his son in 1634; its layout and features such as the Bianpai Bridge are said to imitate the Song capital Bianjing (Kaifeng), and Zhao descendants still live inside. Nearby Yi'anbao is a stone-walled fort town built in 1687 by the Qing official Huang Xingzhen, with gate towers, a walkway along the 6.7-m walls and rows of houses with swallowtail roof ridges.

rows.name: Zhenhai Wei Garrison Town
rows.summary: Zhenhai Wei was a Ming coastal garrison town founded in 1387; abandoned during the early Qing coastal evacuation, it was restored in 1681 as a garrison fort. About 2.7 km of its oval wall of rough stone blocks survives, 4–7 m high, with gates of granite slabs, and inside are three old streets, a Ming stone memorial arch, a City God temple and Ming stone arhat figures.

rows.name: Zhishan Red Building (Former Headquarters of the East Route Red Army)
rows.summary: This three-storey Western-style brick building on the southern slope of Zhishan hill was built as the American trustees' house of the Xunyuan Middle School, a Reformed Church in America school that moved here from Gulangyu in 1925. After the Red Army's East Route Army took Zhangzhou on 20 April 1932, Mao Zedong stayed in the building for more than 20 days. It opened as a revolutionary memorial hall in 1957 and is now a museum on the Red Army's capture of Zhangzhou.

rows.name: Kuangshan Ecological Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest scenic area around Mount Kuang in Fuling town, Pucheng County, in the north of Fujian, where the Kuangshan National Forest Park protects a large stand of natural forest. The first phase of its development was named in 2020 as one of the first national forest-wellness bases.

rows.name: Pien Tze Huang Industry Expo Park
rows.name_zh: 漳州片仔癀产业博览园
rows.summary: A visitor site of Zhangzhou Pien Tze Huang Pharmaceutical, the maker of a famous traditional Chinese medicine brand dating from the Ming dynasty. The company also runs a museum in Zhangzhou's old city, and the expo park was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base.

rows.name: Caoshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Mount Cao is where the Tang monk Benji taught, and he is counted as the second patriarch of the Caodong school of Chan Buddhism, which spread to Japan as Soto Zen. A cultural-creative street in the scenic area shows Yihuang opera, summer-cloth weaving and other local crafts. The provincial culture department lists it among Fuzhou's wellness destinations.

rows.name: China Lotus Scenic Area, Yaoxi
rows.summary: Yaoxi village in Yiqian town is one of the main lotus-growing areas of Guangchang, a county known as China's home of the white lotus. Its lotus fields were certified by Guinness World Records in July 2016 as the world's largest lotus pond. The flowers are at their best in midsummer.

rows.name: Dajue Stream Tourist Zone
rows.summary: Dajue Stream Tourist Zone is a 7.3 km countryside corridor along a stream in Zixi County, built by the county in 2018. It strings together grape-picking gardens, a bread plaza, guesthouses, a food village, a paragliding base, a pet park, a farming-culture park and seasonal flower fields. It suits visitors who want a gentle rural stop alongside Mount Dajue.

rows.name: Dasima Memorial Archway
rows.summary: Dasima Archway is a six-column, three-bay memorial archway put up in 1574 to honour Tan Lun, a Ming minister of war who fought the wokou pirates. It is carved in relief and inscribed with the title Dasima and with Tan Lun's name and office. It is a national heritage unit and a quick stop for anyone in Yihuang.

rows.name: Foling International Park
rows.summary: Foling International Park is a landscaped park on wooded hills beside a reservoir south of Xiaogang, the district town of Dongxiang. It was laid out around Buddhist, traditional and local-culture themes within a natural setting, and was listed as a 4A scenic area in 2018. The district promotes it as a leisure and wellness destination.

rows.name: Fourth Counter-Encirclement Campaign Sites, Hougong
rows.name_zh: 中央苏区第四次反“围剿”战役遗址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngyāng Sūqū Dìsì Cì Fǎn Wéijiǎo Zhànyì Yízhǐ
rows.summary: Hougong is a village in Zuofang town, Jinxi County, where the Red First Front Army had its headquarters in 1933, during the fourth of the Nationalist government's encirclement campaigns against the Central Soviet Area. The preserved compound includes the headquarters building, the health department and the former quarters of Zhu De, Zhou Enlai and Wang Jiaxiang, with exhibitions inside and a memorial hall to the Jinxi campaign. It is one of two parts of a national heritage listing, the other being the Dengxian Bridge battle site in Gugang township, Le'an County.

rows.name: Ganzhu Old Street (Xuyuan Shouzhen), Guangchang
rows.summary: Ganzhu Old Street is the historic street of Ganzhu, a small town in Guangchang county, and the centre of the Xuyuan Shouzhen scenic area. Eleven old buildings in the Ganzhu district have been restored as part of the Long March National Cultural Park, and seven red-history exhibition halls, among them the former headquarters of the Red Army's 9th Army Corps and an ancestral hall, are linked by a sketching base and walking trails. At holiday periods the street stages themed street performances and folk-music shows.

rows.name: Huwan Book-Printing Quarter
rows.summary: Huwan was a major commercial woodblock-printing centre in the Ming and Qing periods, and 14 historic buildings of its book trade are protected as one national heritage unit. They include block-printing workshops, a trading house, a silk shop, a granary and the Xu clan ancestral hall. Wander the old streets to see how a book town was laid out.

rows.name: Jinzhu Waterfalls
rows.summary: Jinzhu Waterfalls is a forested valley of waterfalls in Jinzhu She ethnic township in the southern mountains of Le'an County, and was named one of Jiangxi's hundred scenic spots. Summers are cool, heavy snow can linger in winter, and the township keeps She customs. Preserved revolution-era sites in the area include former residences of Red Army leaders.

rows.name: Jiupu Gorge
rows.summary: Jiupu Gorge, meaning Nine Waterfalls Gorge, is a forested mountain valley of streams and waterfalls in Zhaoxie town in the south of Le'an County, listed as a 4A scenic area in 2020. River rafting is one of the summer activities offered in the valley. A larger resort project around the gorge was under construction in 2023.

rows.name: Kuibi Lianhui Residence, Yiqian
rows.summary: Kuibi Lianhui is a Qing-dynasty residence and the largest surviving old house in Yiqian village, entered through a gatehouse inscribed with its name. Lotus carving runs through the house, from the timber pillars standing on round wooden bases like lotus seats to a stone second gate with three bands of lotus motifs. It is one of more than fifty Ming and Qing buildings in a village known for its white lotus.

rows.name: Lichuan Old Town
rows.summary: Lichuan Old Town is the historic centre of Lichuan, a river town in the south-east of Fuzhou (Jiangxi), with a network of narrow lanes of old houses and shops beside the water. Its Old Street and Xianshi Street are protected as historic districts, and the streets host performances at festivals such as the Lunar New Year. It is a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Lingu Peak
rows.summary: Lingu Peak is a wooded hill of a little over 300 m on the eastern outskirts of Fuzhou (Jiangxi), laid out with footpaths and listed as a 4A scenic area in 2018. A local legend ties it to the poet Xie Lingyun, who governed Linchuan, and a Taoist hermitage he founded here. At the Lunar New Year, residents climb it to pray for blessings.

rows.name: Liukeng Village
rows.summary: Liukeng is a large village of Ming and Qing houses and ancestral halls between a lake and the Niutian river in Le'an County, founded under the Southern Tang in the 10th century and home mostly to the Dong clan. It is nicknamed the First Village of the Ages, has been a national heritage unit since 2001, and was in the first group of national historic and cultural villages in 2003. Old camphor trees line the river downstream.

rows.name: Longtu Xueshi and Cishi Chuanfang Gateways
rows.name_zh: 龙图学士和刺史传芳牌楼门
rows.pinyin: Lóngtú Xuéshì Hé Cìshǐ Chuánfāng Páilóumén
rows.summary: Two memorial gateways stand side by side, separated by a narrow lane, in Shuikou village in Le'an County. The Longtu Xueshi gateway was first built in 1368, rebuilt in 1473 and put up by the Peng family in memory of their ancestor Peng Yanzhao, while the Cishi Chuanfang gateway dates from the Yuan period and was rebuilt in 1751 for another ancestor, Peng Gan. It is a national heritage unit and a short stop for anyone interested in timber architecture.

rows.name: Magu Mountain
rows.summary: Magu Mountain is a wooded mountain area west of Nancheng that Taoist tradition counts as the 28th of the 36 lesser cave-heavens, linked with the immortal Magu. In 771 the Tang calligrapher Yan Zhenqing, then prefect of Fuzhou, visited and wrote the Record of the Immortal Altar of Magu Mountain, one of the best-known works of his regular script. The mountain is a 4A scenic area that Fuzhou promotes for wellness stays.

rows.name: Min-Gan Provincial Committee Site, Hufang
rows.summary: In May 1933 the Min-Gan Provincial Committee of the Communist Party and its revolutionary committee were set up in the Gong family house at Hufang, and in June the Min-Gan military district was established in the Wu clan ancestral hall. The offices moved to Lichuan town in July 1933. Both buildings are protected as one national heritage unit.

rows.name: Mount Dajue
rows.summary: Mount Dajue is a forested mountain and canyon area of about 204 sq km on the western side of the Wuyi range in Zixi County, Fuzhou (Jiangxi). A cableway climbs the mountain, Dajue Temple sits inside a large granite cave, and a rafting run threads through the canyon. A cliff-side electric train about 11.8 km long was added in 2024, and a resort town at the foot of the mountain serves as the base.

rows.name: Qiawan Ancient Village
rows.summary: Qiawan is a river village on the Canglang River in Nanfeng County whose core is Makou Street, the old river-port street, with more than twenty well-preserved Ming and Qing buildings, among them ancestral halls and old houses, and about a dozen small temples. The best-known building is the Hu clan ancestral hall, built between 1608 and 1623, with three halls, two courtyards and 256 pillars. The village is on China's list of traditional villages and is promoted as a boat-shaped ancient town.

rows.name: Sanweng Garden
rows.summary: Sanweng Garden is a riverside park in the urban area of Fuzhou (Jiangxi), laid out on both banks of the Fenggang River as seven themed gardens: an amusement park, azalea, Yuming, aquatic-flower, cherry, perennial-flower and rose gardens. It is a place for seasonal blossom and an easy walk, and local day-trip routes pair it with the city's memorials to Wang Anshi and Tang Xianzu. It was listed as a 4A scenic area in 2018.

rows.name: Shiwuli Stone House, Yiqian
rows.summary: Shiwuli is a Qing house of 1716 in Yiqian old village, built entirely of polished stone. Two identical buildings are joined and divided into upper, middle and lower halls, with 27 rooms and seven skylight courtyards in all, on a plan 21 m wide and 38.6 m deep. It is a national heritage unit and sits a few minutes' walk from the Kuibi Lianhui residence.

rows.name: Tangyin Old Town
rows.summary: Tangyin is a market town founded in 1031 that grew rich on summer cloth woven from ramie in the Ming and Qing periods. Five of its buildings are national heritage units: the Cheng'en archway, the Bafujun ancestral temple, Yingen Pagoda, the Luo family compound and a Guanmaoting house, and a local history exhibition hall tells the town's story. Around 70 Ming and Qing buildings survive, including houses, ancestral halls, archways, a pagoda and bridges.

rows.name: Tomb of Tan Lun
rows.summary: The tomb of Tan Lun, the Ming minister of war who fought the wokou pirates, was built in 1579 and covers about 3,000 sq m in Lianqian village, near Erdu town. It is laid out in five parts: a gate, a sacrificial way, an archway, a spirit way and the burial mound. It is a national heritage unit, and the Yihuang County Museum, also called the Tan Lun Memorial Hall, is in the same village.

rows.name: Tongsheng Jiuqu Dongli Scenic Area
rows.summary: Tongsheng Jiuqu Dongli is a privately funded leisure and holiday area on the shore of Liaoyuan Reservoir in Rifeng town, Lichuan County. It joins lake and hill scenery to buildings in traditional style, and is planned around leisure, culture and entertainment, sport and wellness. It is a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Wannian Bridge
rows.summary: Wannian Bridge is a stone arch bridge over the Xu River at Nancheng, begun in 1635 and finished in 1647. It is 411 m long and 10 m high, with 23 arches carried on 24 piers. Juxing Pagoda stands on Wugang hill at the bridge head, so walk across and climb the hill to see the two together.

rows.name: Wenchang Li
rows.summary: Wenchang Li is a Ming–Qing-style historic district on the east bank of the Fu River in Fuzhou's old town, a provincially protected quarter with 11 listed buildings and 9 historic buildings among its lanes, shops and food stalls. It is a popular evening destination, with street events and a live-action show, Xun Meng Mudan Ting, based on The Peony Pavilion by Tang Xianzu, the playwright from Fuzhou.

rows.name: Xian'gai Mountain Agricultural Park
rows.summary: Xian'gai Mountain Agricultural Park is a hillside leisure park south of Fuzhou (Jiangxi) that combines farming, sightseeing, traditional Chinese medicine and wellness-retirement facilities across more than 200 projects. Visitors come for walks among the farm gardens, a grass-sledding slope and cultural activities. It suits families and groups after a relaxed countryside outing.

rows.name: Yelang Valley
rows.summary: Yelang Valley, meaning Wild Wolf Valley, is a commercial outdoor-themed park in Caoping village, built around a wolf theme and offering wolf-culture experiences. It also has a guesthouse and a motorhome campsite. It is part of the Zhenxiang Countryside belt.

rows.name: Yulong Wanshou Palace
rows.summary: Yulong Wanshou Palace is a temple complex of Ming origin, rebuilt in the Qing, laid out along an east-facing axis of forecourt, gate, opera tower, front hall, Jingyang Shrine and pavilion. The axis is 94.5 m long and the site covers 4,205 sq m, with wing buildings, a Fire God temple and a Taoist priest's lodge at the sides. It is one of the Wanshou Palaces found across Jiangxi and has been a national monument since 2013.

rows.name: Yulongwan Resort
rows.name_zh: 资溪御龙湾国际旅游度假区
rows.summary: Yulongwan International Resort is a leisure resort in Yongsheng village, Matoushan town, in the north of Zixi County, rated a 4A scenic area in 2018. Its facilities were listed at that time as a beach area, a leisure corridor, camping tents, a children's playground and a walking trail. Zixi's tourism officials promote it, with Mount Dajue, as a place for fresh air and rest.

rows.name: Zeng Gong Cultural Park
rows.summary: Zeng Gong Cultural Park on the southern edge of Nanfeng is built around the memory of Zeng Gong, the Northern Song prose writer counted among the Eight Great Prose Masters of the Tang and Song. It holds the Zeng Gong Memorial Museum, opened in 2019 with six galleries, together with the Zeng Wending ancestral hall, a reading rock, an ink pond and cliff inscriptions. Come for the museum and the garden setting.

rows.name: Zhenxiang Countryside
rows.summary: Zhenxiang Countryside is a belt of villages in Wushi town in the south of Zixi County, promoted as one valley and four households: Yelang Valley plus the villages of Changxing, Chenfang, Caoping and Xinyue. Xinyue is a She village that stages folk performances, Chenfang has a restored opera stage and clan hall, and Caoping has rebuilt commune-era buildings with an exhibition on the sent-down youth of that period. The area is a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Zhuqiao Ancient Village
rows.summary: Zhuqiao is a Jiangxi village founded in the late Yuan or early Ming that keeps the layout of Ming and Qing Gan-style houses, ancestral halls and memorial archways. It is one of Jinxi's national historic and cultural villages, and foreign guests were taken there during the 2024 Tang Xianzu international theatre month. It is a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Anjishan Forest Park, Longnan
rows.summary: Anjishan is a provincial forest park in Chenglong town, west-south-west of Longnan, with dense woodland and a stretch of river. Visitors walk forest paths and take boat trips on the water.

rows.name: Baguanao
rows.summary: A high-mountain scenic area in Gaotian town, in the north-east of Shicheng county, promoted by the county as a high-altitude azalea viewing spot. Rice terraces above 1,000 m, planted with the local tribute rice, lie in the same town.

rows.name: China (Quannan) Climbing Town
rows.summary: A sports-tourism complex in Chengxiang town, on the north-western side of Quannan, built around rock climbing, with a 15 m competition wall, four zones and eleven activity areas, plus a national training base for young climbers. Quannan is the home county of the speed-climbing world champion Zhong Qixin, and the town hosts national climbing events.

rows.name: China Gannan Navel Orange Industrial Park
rows.summary: A 5,400-mu (about 360-hectare) agricultural park in Anxi town, developed by the drinks company Nongfu Spring around a 5,000-mu navel orange demonstration orchard. It also has a 6,000 m² orange-culture exhibition hall and a glasshouse seedling nursery, and in 2018 it became Xinfeng county's first national 4A scenic area. It suits visitors interested in how Gannan navel oranges are grown and processed.

rows.name: Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army School Site, Ruijin
rows.name_zh: 瑞金中央工农红军学校旧址
rows.pinyin: Ruìjīn Zhōngyāng Gōngnóng Hóngjūn Xuéxiào Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Five adjoining Yang-clan ancestral halls in Shangyang, in Ruijin's old town, housed the Red Army's officer school in the early 1930s, one hall for each department: general affairs, political work, school affairs, instruction and the club. The brick-and-timber halls were built between 1608 and 1921 and cover about 6,100 square metres. The school ran six courses and trained more than 11,500 cadres under principals who included Liu Bocheng and Ye Jianying, before it was reorganised into the Red Army University and other schools in October 1933.

rows.name: Cuiweifeng
rows.summary: A cluster of red-sandstone Danxia peaks and cliffs on the north-western edge of Ningdu town, with a path to the summit at Lingxiao Pavilion and a glass walkway on the mountainside. At the end of the Ming dynasty a group of scholars known as the Nine Masters of Yitang lived on the peak and ran a school there. The area closed in November 2022 for a large-scale upgrade and reopened on 1 October 2025.

rows.name: Dabaoguang Pagoda
rows.summary: A white-marble memorial pagoda of the Tang dynasty, 4.5 m tall, standing inside the Daijue Hall of Baohua Temple in Tiancun town and also known as the Jade Stone Pagoda. It marks the tomb of the Chan monk Zhizang, who died in 817; the pagoda was destroyed in the suppression of Buddhism in 845, rebuilt in 853 and rebuilt again in 874. It stands on a three-tier Sumeru base, its body holds a small chamber flanked by inscriptions, and it is topped by a four-sided roof and finial, with a Northern Song stele recording its history in front of the hall.

rows.name: Dongsheng Wei
rows.summary: A large square Hakka walled house built from 1842 in the Qing dynasty and extended three times over 25 years, listed as a national heritage unit in 2013. It faces west and is laid out as a rectangle within a rectangle, with 199 rooms, nine courtyards and 18 halls (locally called nine wells, eighteen halls), and with its outbuildings and outer gate it covers about 30,000 m².

rows.name: Fushou Ditch
rows.summary: Fushou Ditch is the Song-dynasty drainage network of Ganzhou's old city, begun in the Northern Song under the local prefect Liu Yi and about 12.6 km long, with sections still used as drains today. Its two main channels, Fu and Shou, are named for the way their routes trace those characters in seal script, and the system works with ponds, silt wells, coin-shaped drain covers and one-way water windows at the river outlets. The Fushougou Museum on Houde Road shows a length of the channel that is still in use.

rows.name: Gan River Source Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in Ganjiangyuan town, in the far south of Shicheng county, named for the headwaters of the Gan River that Shicheng counts as the river's source. The surrounding hills are protected as the Jiangxi Ganjiangyuan National Nature Reserve, and the scenic area was rated 4A in February 2026.

rows.name: Ganzhou City Wall
rows.summary: The best-preserved stretches of Ganzhou's Song-dynasty city wall run beside the Zhang and Gong rivers on the old city's two river sides, about 3.7 km in all, with brick and stone facing over a rammed-earth core roughly 7 m high. Gates such as Yongjin and Jianchun, bastions and crossbow platforms survive along the walk, and many wall bricks are stamped with reign dates from the Song to the Qing. State media describe it as the largest and best-preserved Song-dynasty city wall in China.

rows.name: Ganzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple founded in 1050 as the school of Gan County, on the site of an earlier Taoist temple. Most of the present buildings date from 1778 and stand in three parallel groups covering about one hectare, with the central axis running from the Dacheng Gate through side halls and shrines to the Dacheng Hall, and the Kuixing Pavilion and a scripture library on the east side.

rows.name: Ganzhou Pagodas
rows.time_needed: Under 1 hour for the Ganzhou pagoda
rows.summary: Five hexagonal pagodas of similar style, built mostly in the Northern Song, are protected together as one national site. They are Ciyun Temple Pagoda in Ganzhou city, Dasheng Temple Pagoda in Xinfeng, Wuwei Temple Pagoda in Anyuan, Baofu Monastery Pagoda in Shicheng and Jiayou Temple Pagoda in Dayu. The pin is on Ciyun Pagoda, the one in Ganzhou's old city.

rows.name: Guanxi Walled Houses
rows.summary: Guanxi Xinwei is a Hakka walled mansion begun in 1798 and completed in 1827 by Xu Mingjun, a near-square block 83 m by 95 m inside 10 m-high walls, with watchtowers at the four corners and 27 gun loops in the walls. The scenic area around it takes in five more houses of the Guanxi group: Xichang, Pengao, Tianxin, Zhenxia and the Dashufang study. Inside, visitors see stone lions, carved window lattices, door-stones and an opera stage.

rows.name: Gushan Scenic Area, Xinfeng
rows.summary: A wooded hill park on the south-western edge of Xinfeng town, laid out as a forest park and topped by the Xinfeng Pavilion (Xinfeng Ge). It was rated a national 4A scenic area in June 2020.

rows.name: Hakka Culture City, Ganxian
rows.summary: A Hakka-culture complex in the south of Meilin, the seat of Ganxian district, laid out as a group of Hakka-style buildings for ceremonies, exhibitions, trade and leisure, and home to the Jiangxi Hakka Museum. Its long cherry-blossom walkway is the main draw in spring, and the Gannan Hakka Culture Tourism Festival opened here in March 2026.

rows.name: Hanxianyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A red-sandstone Danxia hill and gorge area in the south of Huichang county, named after the legend that Han Zhongli, one of the Eight Immortals, attained immortality here. Stone carvings of the Eight Immortals stand at the entrance, and the trail climbs through narrow rock clefts past inscriptions cut over several centuries to a small cave linked with him, then drops to a slit-like gorge. Boats on Hanxian Lake give a view of the whole cliff face.

rows.name: Hongxinggu Study Campus, Xingguo
rows.summary: A study and training campus of about 900 mu (60 hectares) on the north-western outskirts of Xingguo town, built by the Jiangxi expressway group and opened in 2023. It is designed to house about 5,000 students at once and receive up to 20,000 visitors a day, and runs study courses built around the county's revolutionary history. It forms part of Xingguo's red-tourism offer alongside the Generals' Park and other sites.

rows.name: Huangpi Site of the Central Bureau's First Enlarged Conference
rows.name_zh: 黄陂中共苏区中央局第一次扩大会议旧址
rows.pinyin: Huángpí Zhōnggòng Sūqū Zhōngyāngjú Dìyī Cì Kuòdà Huìyì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A former village building in Shantang village, Huangpi town, north-west of Ningdu, where the Soviet-area Central Bureau of the Communist Party held its first enlarged conference in 1931, during the Jiangxi Soviet period. It was listed as a provincial site in 2018 and added to the national list in 2019, in the eighth batch.

rows.name: Huichang Theatre Town
rows.time_needed: Half a day, longer for an evening performance
rows.summary: A theatre quarter of about 128 mu (roughly 8.5 hectares) in Huichang town, developed with the director Stan Lai, whose father came from Huichang, and opened in January 2024. Old buildings were converted into theatres, including an ancestral hall made into a garden theatre, a former printing works and street houses, and they stand around a 300-year-old tree beside the Huichang Museum, which has a gallery on Lai's work. Seasons of plays and street performances by Chinese and foreign companies are staged here, so what is on depends on the dates.

rows.name: Jiangnan Song City
rows.summary: A historic-quarter tourist area of about 50 ha in the northern part of Ganzhou's old city, whose landmarks are Yugutai, the hilltop pavilion on the highest point of the urban area, and Bajing Terrace at the meeting of the Zhang and Gong rivers. The main street is a pedestrian street of Song-style timber buildings, entered through the Junmen gate tower and a plaza with statues of four Song-era figures linked to the city, and an outer zone takes in the Fushou Ditch museum and the Wei family compound. The street and gate tower are modern reconstructions, while the Song-dynasty city wall passes below Yugutai.

rows.name: Jingtang Site of the Central Branch Bureau and Government Office
rows.name_zh: 井塘中共中央分局、中央政府办事处旧址
rows.pinyin: Jǐngtáng Zhōnggòng Zhōngyāng Fēnjú Zhōngyāng Zhèngfǔ Bànshìchù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A large brick-and-timber courtyard hall in Jingtang village, Huanglin township, used from late 1934 by the Central Branch Bureau of the Communist Party and the Central Government Office, the bodies that stayed in the Soviet area after the main Red Army set out on the Long March. Xiang Ying, secretary of the Branch Bureau, had his room at the front of the building. It was added to the national list in 2019.

rows.name: Jiuqu Resort, Dingnan
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A holiday resort on the Jiuqu river at Tianjiu town, Dingnan county, set in bamboo woods with a waterfall, boat rides on its lake and a street presenting Hakka intangible heritage. It is a national 4A scenic area and was named one of Jiangxi's summer-retreat destinations in 2023.

rows.name: Long March Departure Sites, Yudu
rows.summary: In October 1934 more than 86,000 Red Army troops gathered around Yudu and crossed the Yudu (Gong) River at night at several crossing points, the start of the Long March. The national heritage listing covers eight sites in and around the town: the east-gate ferry crossing used by the central leadership, other units' crossing points, and the headquarters and lodgings used before the departure, including those of the Central Military Commission, the First and Fifth Army Corps and the Gannan provincial Soviet government. A memorial park on the riverbank at the east-gate crossing has the Central Red Army Long March Departure Memorial Hall and a monument.

rows.name: Luohan Rock, Ruijin
rows.summary: A red-sandstone (Danxia) scenic area around the Chenshi Reservoir in Rentian town, north-east of Ruijin, where cliffs and oddly shaped rock stacks rise beside a lake. It forms one of the two districts of the Ruijin National Scenic Area, the other being the Yeping–Shazhouba revolutionary sites. The provincial tourism department promotes the wildflowers of spring and summer, and Chenshi is another name for the rock.

rows.name: Luotian Rock Inscriptions
rows.summary: A red-sandstone (Danxia) outcrop on the south bank of the Gong River just south of Yudu town, with temple buildings set against the cliff and some seventy inscriptions cut into the rock faces between the Northern Song and the Republic. The earliest dates from 1051, and the carvers include the Song scholar Zhou Dunyi, who left a poem here in 1063, as well as Yue Fei, Wen Tianxiang and Wang Yangming.

rows.name: Mei Pass
rows.summary: A mountain pass on the Meiling ridge between Jiangxi and Guangdong, on the old trade road that the Tang chancellor Zhang Jiuling had cut through the Dayu range in 716, about 5 m wide and 8 km long with a paved surface. The Ming-dynasty gate tower is inscribed Southern Guangdong's Mighty Pass on its north face and First Pass of Lingnan on its south face, and the Jiangxi side of the pass and the old road were listed as a national heritage unit in 2006. Plum trees were planted along the route, which gave the pass its name, and the road can be walked.

rows.name: Nan Wudang Mountain
rows.summary: A national scenic area of 13.5 sq km in Wudang town, near the Guangdong border, where 99 red-rock peaks rise from the valley beside National Road 105 to a main summit of 864 m. A stepped path climbs onto the elephant-shaped rock masses, and a suspended walkway, glass walkways, a glass bridge and a viewing platform run among the peaks. The name Wudang comes from a couplet that the Ming philosopher Wang Yangming wrote after climbing it.

rows.name: Nankang Furniture Town
rows.summary: A purpose-built furniture-industry town in Jingba town, planned over 5 km² with a 2 km² core around a lake of more than 300 mu. It has a furniture-culture museum, a rosewood exhibition hall, Hakka walled-house-style buildings and folk performances, and lets visitors watch furniture production lines. It was named a national industrial-tourism demonstration base in 2023.

rows.name: Ningdu Conference Site, Xiaoyuan
rows.summary: The Zeng family ancestral hall of Xiaoyuan village, built in the Kangxi reign of the Qing and known as the Bangshan Weng hall, where the Soviet-area Central Bureau of the Communist Party held a plenary meeting in early October 1932, known as the Ningdu Conference. The village, in Dongshanba town, has been developed for red tourism, with the hall and a village history hall used as teaching sites and a lotus pond in front.

rows.name: Ningdu Uprising Headquarters Site
rows.summary: A two-storey brick-and-timber, western-style house built in 1916 as the pastor's residence of a church, in the centre of Ningdu. On 14 December 1931 the Nationalist 26th Route Army, stationed in Ningdu, announced an uprising and joined the Red Army, which formed it into the Fifth Army Corps. The building now houses the Ningdu Uprising Memorial Hall, whose displays cover the uprising and the Fifth Army Corps.

rows.name: Pingshan Scenic Area, Yudu
rows.summary: Pingshan is a mountain in the far south of Yudu county whose summit, at 1,314 m the highest in the county, is covered by about 50,000 mu (roughly 3,300 hectares) of natural grassland. Its slopes have forest, a waterfall and rock formations such as the Immortals Playing Chess stone, and the county describes the area as a summer retreat with lodging and dining. An evening live-action show in the grounds tells of the Red Army's departure from Yudu in the 1930s and shows Hakka wedding customs.

rows.name: Qianxin Town, Longnan
rows.time_needed: Half a day, or an overnight stay
rows.summary: A hill resort town in Dongkeng village, Lintang township, developed as a wellness and holiday destination with tea growing and forest-based activities; about 100,000 mu (roughly 6,700 hectares) of forest land has been leased to it for that use. The provincial culture and tourism department counts it as a provincial 5A rural tourism site, and it is also a national 4A scenic area. It is a modern resort rather than a historic village, so it suits a few days' stay in the hills more than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qinglongyan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Danxia sandstone cliffs in Nanqiao town, south of Xunwu county town, developed as a hot-spring tourist resort. Its landmark is the Lingshi Wall, a red rock face 200 m high and 800 m long, with the Lingshi hot springs at its foot; the water is a mineral spring rich in lithium, radon, metasilicic acid and fluorine. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism's rural-tourism routes feature the springs as a winter trip, best between November and February.

rows.name: Ruijin Cradle of the Republic Scenic Area
rows.summary: Ruijin was the seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic's central government from late 1931 until the Long March began in 1934, and this scenic area gathers four sets of sites from that period. They are Yeping, where the first national congress of soviets met in 1931 and offices and residences survive in former village buildings; the Red Well area at Shazhouba, to which the government moved in 1933; the Great Hall of the Second National Congress; and a memorial park with a history museum and a martyrs' memorial hall. Xinhua counts 26 nationally protected sites within the area.

rows.name: Sanbaishan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in south-eastern Anyuan, on the Jiangxi–Guangdong border, where the Dongjiang (East River), a main water source for Hong Kong and Guangdong, rises. The range also divides the Yangtze and Pearl river basins, and its main peak, Dongyuan Peak, reaches 1,164.5 m. Walkways lead to the East River First Waterfall, a single drop of more than 120 m, and a glass bridge, a plank walkway and a cableway have been added for views over the forest.

rows.name: Shangbao Terraces
rows.summary: Rice terraces of about 51,000 mu (some 3,400 ha) climbing the mountains of north-western Chongyi across Shangbao, Fengzhou and Sishun townships, with a history of more than 2,200 years. The slopes drop nearly 1,000 m and hold up to 62 tiers, watered by old gravity-fed channels. The terraces were inscribed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in October 2022.

rows.name: Site of the Soviet Area Central Bureau, Xiaobu
rows.summary: A former Gong clan ancestral hall, known locally as Xinwu ('new house'), in Chikan village beside Xiaobu town: a south-facing brick-and-timber building restored in 2008. On 15 January 1931 the Soviet-area Central Bureau of the Communist Party and a central revolutionary military commission were set up here, and Mao Zedong lived in the building. It is the centrepiece of the Xiaobu scenic area, which has a visitor centre and some 18 sites of the early 1930s, among them Zhu De's former residence, the First Front Army headquarters and hundreds of wall slogans.

rows.name: Taiping Bridge, Longnan
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty covered bridge over the Taiping River in Chetian village, Yangcun town, 50 m long, 4 m wide and 17.2 m high overall. The lower level has three piers and two arches, with the middle pier projecting about 5 m like a ship's prow. The upper level is a brick-and-timber pavilion open on four sides, flanked by a dry arch of 8.4 m span at each end.

rows.name: Taoyuan Lejing Park, Dingnan
rows.summary: Taoyuan Lejing is a landscaped hill park on the edge of Dingnan town, themed on the 'Peach Blossom Spring' story by the poet Tao Yuanming. It is laid out around lakes in wooded hills and suits families looking for an easy outing from town.

rows.name: Tianlong Mountain, Quannan
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area in Jinlong town, Quannan county, with trails through pine woodland. The county counts it among its four core scenic areas, alongside the Dinglong Taojiang resort, the Climbing Town and Yaxi village, and parts of it have been built as settings from the martial-arts novels of Jin Yong, such as Mantuo Villa. Hotels and guesthouses have been added around the scenic area.

rows.name: Tongtian Rock
rows.summary: A red-sandstone (Danxia) hill in Shuixi town, north-west of Ganzhou, whose caves and niches hold hundreds of Buddhist statues and well over a hundred inscriptions from the Song dynasty to the Republic, among them Wang Yangming's. Most of the carvings are Song, apart from a few standing Buddhas at Cuiwei Rock that date from the Tang. It is described as the southernmost grotto complex in mainland China and as the largest cave temple in the Jiangnan region.

rows.name: Tongtianzhai, Shicheng
rows.summary: A Danxia (red-sandstone) scenic area in Qinjiang town, south-east of Shicheng, rising to a summit of about 600 m. It lies within the Shicheng geopark and is a provincial-level forest park, and the sights the county lists include an old stone wall and the site of Yuyu Temple.

rows.name: Wulong Hakka Folk Park
rows.summary: A large leisure park of more than 2,000 mu (about 130 ha), with some 300 mu of water, on the south-eastern edge of Ganzhou's urban area. It is laid out around an ecology theme with Hakka and dragon-culture motifs, combining lakeside gardens and farm sightseeing with sports and outdoor-training grounds and conference and resort facilities. It suits families and groups wanting a half-day outing within the city.

rows.name: Wushi Wei, Longnan
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty Hakka walled house in Yangcun town, built in the Wanli reign (1573–1620) and one of the 376 walled houses of Longnan. It joined the national list in 2019, in the eighth batch, and Longnan's walled houses as a group are on China's tentative list for World Heritage.

rows.name: Xingguo Generals' Park
rows.name_zh: 苏区干部好作风纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park of about 508 mu (34 hectares) on the south-western edge of Xingguo town, built around the Soviet-Area Cadres' Work Style exhibition hall, which shows 213 relics, 18 oil paintings and 12 large reconstructed scenes from the Soviet period, including a survey Mao Zedong made in Changgang township. The park, also called Generals' Park, has a generals' hall and a plaza with statues of Mao Zedong, Chen Yi and the 56 generals born in Xingguo, laid out along a Long March route.

rows.name: Xingguo Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: Five sites in and around Xingguo county town record the county's part in the Jiangxi Soviet of 1929–33. They are the Lianjiang Academy of 1718, where a land-revolution cadre training class was run in 1929; the former Jiangxi Military District headquarters with its reviewing stand; the Central Arsenal site group at Guantian; the hall where the first Jiangxi workers', peasants' and soldiers' congress met in May 1932; and Changgang village, where a survey of the township was made in 1933.

rows.name: Xunwu Investigation Site
rows.summary: A two-storey house of timber and earth with cobble-and-lime walls and a wooden arcade on its south front, built in 1917 as the home of an American missionary at the Matigang Catholic church in the county town. In May 1930 Mao Zedong and Zhu De brought the Fourth Red Army to Xunwu, and the army's front committee and Mao lodged here while he carried out a survey of the county's economy and society. It stands in an experience park in the same neighbourhood with a memorial hall on the survey, the county martyrs' memorial hall and a red-culture street opened in 2024.

rows.name: Yangjiao Water Fort
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty rural military fort begun in 1544 in Yangjiao village, Junmenling town, and listed as a national heritage unit in 2013. About 861 m of the Ming wall survives with three gates, the east gate being the best preserved, and only the northern stretch has been lost. Watchtowers and the remains of Hakka ancestral halls can still be seen, restoration work began in September 2015, and the walled village is still home to about 1,000 people.

rows.name: Yangming Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir of about 31 sq km on the border of Shangyou and Chongyi counties, formed by damming the Shangyou River and formerly known as Doushui Lake. Forested hills surround its many bays and islands, 427 bays and 42 islands by the county's count. It is a national forest park and wetland park as well as a 4A scenic area, and Shangyou County took over its operation in September 2022.

rows.name: Yangming Xingu Scenic Area
rows.summary: A landscaped park of about 113 ha on the east bank of the Tao River north of Longnan town, built on reclaimed mining land around the Yushi Xianyan cliff and opened on trial in June 2023. Halfway up the cliff, the Yuxu Cave holds inscriptions, including five poems by the Ming official and philosopher Wang Yangming, written in 1518 after he put down the Sanli uprising, and the cave inscriptions are protected at provincial level. The park's walkways and halls are themed around Wang Yangming's time in Longnan.

rows.name: Yangmingshan Forest Park, Chongyi
rows.summary: A forest park of about 69 sq km on the Hunan–Guangdong–Jiangxi border, rising to 1,259.5 m beside the county town of Chongyi. It was once called Guanyin Mountain, then Yangling in memory of the Ming official Wang Yangming, who put down a rebellion here and set up Chongyi county, and it took its present name in 2017. Its sights include the Lanxi gorge and falls, a small lake called Xiaoyangming Lake, Yunyin Temple and a large bamboo forest.

rows.name: Yangxi Sites: Central Military Commission and Marxism-Communism School
rows.name_zh: 中革军委旧址与马克思共产主义学校旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggé Jūnwěi Jiùzhǐ Yǔ Mǎkèsī Gòngchǎnzhǔyì Xuéxiào Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Two former clan halls of the Liu family in Yangxi, a hamlet of Yeping township just north-west of the Yeping memorial area, were used by the Chinese Soviet Republic. One housed the Central Revolutionary Military Commission, set up there on 25 November 1931 with Zhu De as chairman, and the other the Marxism-Communism School, a central party school opened in 1933. The State Council listed them separately, in 2013 and 2019.

rows.name: Yanyi Wei, Longnan
rows.summary: A Hakka walled house in Yangcun town, begun by Lai Fuzhi in 1650 and finished in 1677, rectangular in plan at 41.5 m by 31.8 m with outer walls 14.3 m high. Families still live in it, and visitors can eat Hakka dishes and buy local produce from residents inside; Yangcun village was in the first batch of Chinese traditional villages in 2012. It shares its national listing, from 2001, with Guanxi Xinwei about 39 km to the north-east.

rows.name: Yashan, Dayu
rows.summary: A mountain resort area of more than 30,000 mu in Huanglong town, inside Meiguan National Forest Park and named after its highest peak, Shuangxiu, whose Y-shaped summit gives the place its name (ya means a fork). A 13 km elevated forest boardwalk, a glass walkway and Wolong gorge cross the forest, while the foot of the mountain has the A Duo leisure village and water-play areas and lodging is spread up the slopes. It was designated a national tourism resort in 2023 and suits families wanting a stay in the hills.

rows.name: Yaxi Ancient Village
rows.summary: A Hakka village in Longyuanba town, north of Quannan, notable for two walled houses: Fuxing Wei, built of rammed earth, and Yafeng Wei, built of stone. Visitors walk through courtyards, lanes and ancestral halls, and on festival nights a long fire dragon made of thousands of incense sticks is paraded through the village.

rows.name: Yongzhen Bridge
rows.summary: A covered timber bridge on granite piers over a river in Yongzhen village, Xinlong township, built in 1653 in the early Qing by a monk, Ao Liu, who raised the funds, and listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.
