It is 38.5 m long and 4.3 m wide, with three spans on two piers and two abutments, and a gallery of nine bays on top. Its beams are stacked fir logs laid in a cantilever pattern, with a different layout on the north and south halves.

rows.name: Yudai Bridge
rows.summary: A covered arch bridge over the Hushan river in Hushan township, built in 1740 under the Qianlong emperor and listed as a national heritage unit in 2013. It has three stone arches on two piers and curves in plan, with an arc 88.15 m long, a cobbled deck 3.8 m wide and a timber gallery in 32 sections, with a small pavilion that doubles as a shrine at the middle. A local wealthy man, Yu Fengqi, paid for it, which is why it is also called Fengqi Bridge.

rows.name: Yuxue Ruijing Scenic Area
rows.summary: A red-tourism park in Jieyuan village, west of Ruijin, built around the live outdoor show Yuxue Ruijing, which the provincial tourism department presented in 2020 as the province's first real-scene performance project that visitors can take part in. 'Ruijing' was the name by which Ruijin was known as the capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic in the early 1930s. The park has been rated 4A since 2020.

rows.name: Anfu Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple and former county school, founded in 1081 under the Northern Song and moved to its present site in 1142; the buildings are mostly Qing, restored in 1863. A pool with a stone "top graduate" bridge, the Dacheng Gate and the Dacheng Hall stand on the main axis, and the hall has a glazed-tile hip roof and statues of Confucius, Mencius, Xunzi and twenty natives of Anfu. Part of the complex is used for displays on the history of Anfu County.

rows.name: Baikou City Site, Taihe
rows.summary: The earthen walls and moat of a walled town of the Han to Jin periods on the south bank of the Gan River at Taihe, covering about 25 hectares in an inverted-trapezoid plan with a smaller inner town in the north. Archaeologists excavated part of it in 2001 and 2004–05 and found about ten gates. Some archaeologists identify it as the seat of the Han county of Luling.

rows.name: Bailuzhou Academy
rows.summary: An academy founded in 1241 by the prefect Jiang Wanli on Bailuzhou, an island in the Gan River in the middle of Ji'an, where Wen Tianxiang studied. It was rebuilt many times after floods and wars; the surviving halls, including Fengyue Tower and Yunzhang Pavilion, date from 1863, and a full restoration ran from 2013 to 2015. It later became a school and is now used for public lectures and study programmes.

rows.name: Baishuixian, Suichuan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area at Baishui village in Bizhou town, known for waterfalls, bamboo and rocks and listed as a provincial scenic area in 1995. The three-tier falls near the Baishuixian temple drop about 86 m, 50 m and 30 m, and the area also has the Seven Star Falls, a narrow cleft about 200 m deep called One-Line Sky, and rock features such as Eagle Beak Cliff. The name comes from the temple, built to honour three sisters recorded in a Qing gazetteer as having become immortals.

rows.name: Baiyun Lake Jiangxin Valley, Qingyuan
rows.summary: A lakeside wellness-resort area on the Baiyunshan Reservoir (Baiyun Lake) in Qingyuan District, under development since 2024 as a forest ecology-tourism and recuperation area. It combines accommodation, restaurants, exhibition space and water sports including a surfing facility, and has a tourist-boat landing on the shore, with others at Baiyun Bay and Shazhou Island. The first-phase visitor centre was completed in May 2026, so the area is new and still being built out.

rows.name: Bixia Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village of the Hu clan on the Fushui River in Futian town, founded in the Tang dynasty, with 36 ancestral halls, 18 old wells, three memorial archways, an old academy and polygonal halls rarely seen elsewhere. It was also a base of the 1930s Communist regional government: the first Party congress of south-west Jiangxi met from 22 to 29 March 1930 in the Hu clan's general ancestral hall (Dunren Hall), a nationally listed brick-and-timber building, and the Gonglüe county government moved to the village in 1932. A company now runs the village for visitors, with festival events and a riverside eco-park nearby.

rows.name: Caolin Red Market Town
rows.summary: A restored market town in the centre of Caolin, built around an old market street, a lower street, a floating bridge and a shopping street, with a red-poetry hall and a former residence of Mao Zedong; the county describes it as combining market culture, revolutionary history, tea and folk customs. In January 1928 Mao Zedong's force occupied Suichuan and held a mass meeting in the market's Wanshou Temple to announce its policy towards traders, and the market then supplied the Jinggang Mountains base with goods such as salt, cotton and medicine. His 1928 report on the Jinggang Mountains records market days drawing about 20,000 people.

rows.name: Chatan Weir
rows.summary: A weir on the Niuhou River that splits the flow into irrigation canals, begun in the 10th century under the Southern Tang by Zhou Ju, a Southern Tang official, and still irrigating more than 50,000 mu (about 3,300 ha) of farmland. It is listed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure and is a national water-conservancy scenic area, in a wooded gorge with a village beside the weir and a path along the bank. It is a quiet stop for anyone interested in historic engineering.

rows.name: Chengjing Hall, Futian
rows.summary: A large ancestral hall in Futian village, begun in the mid-Ming and now mostly of the late Qing, laid out in a T shape with a gatehouse, forecourt, porch pavilion, main hall and ancestor hall. Red Army slogans remain on its inner and outer walls. The national listing groups 23 historic buildings around Futian and Donggu, including residences used by Mao Zedong, Zhu De and Peng Dehuai, army hospital sites and former headquarters of the Red Army.

rows.name: China Jinshi Culture Park, Jishui
rows.summary: A classical-style garden park of about 30 hectares on Nanmen Zhou, a peninsula in the Gan River at the southern edge of Jishui town, built around the China Jinshi Museum on the holders of the highest imperial examination degree. Other parts of the park are a library tower, a pavilion for the top scorer, a Confucian temple, an opera stage, a street of scholars' mansions and replica examination cells, with more than 1,100 old books, portraits, calligraphy and paintings on display. Building began in October 2017.

rows.name: Dafeng Tianyuan, Ji'an County
rows.summary: A countryside leisure park in Dunhou town, listed as a provincial 4A rural tourism point in 2021 and a national 4A scenic area in 2022. It is aimed at family day trips from Ji'an and runs events such as evening light shows.

rows.name: Diaoyuan Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village in Xingqiao town founded at the end of the Tang as the home of descendants of the Song writer Ouyang Xiu, with more than 150 ancestral halls, academies and houses in the Gan regional style. It is on the national list of traditional villages and is a Historic and Cultural Village of China. In recent years restored houses have been given over to guesthouses, exhibition spaces and creative workshops, and a cherry-blossom avenue leads to the entrance.

rows.name: Donggu Revolutionary Base Area, Qingyuan
rows.summary: A She ethnic township in the hills of Qingyuan District that became a Communist-held base area after the Donggu uprising of November 1927 and was a main battleground of the first three Nationalist encirclement campaigns of 1930–31. On its main street stands the nationally listed site of the Donggu Civilian Bank, set up in 1928 and merged into the Chinese Soviet state bank in 1932, and the Donggu Revolutionary Base Museum, in a former forestry-station building, shows more than 200 documents and objects on the base and the second campaign of spring 1931. The Donggu martyrs' cemetery joined the national list of martyrs' memorial facilities in February 2025.

rows.name: Enjiang Old Town, Yongfeng
rows.summary: The restored old quarter of Enjiang, Yongfeng's county town on the Enjiang River, which the county says holds the largest and best-preserved Ming county-town site in Jiangxi: stretches of Ming city wall, an east gate facing the river bridge, and the sites of a county assistant's office and a minister's mansion. More than 160 old buildings have been repaired and the grid of lanes kept, and people still live and shop in the quarter. It is themed on Ouyang Xiu, the Song writer whose family came from Yongfeng, with museums, a Song-style night street and evening light shows.

rows.name: Haimuyuan
rows.summary: A valley resort at Muyuan and Haiyuan villages in the hills of Tanqiu township, known for rafting through a bamboo forest in the warmer months. It also has a jungle-crossing course, suspension bridges, a children's play area, the old Xinxia path, a small folk village and a guesthouse complex rated a four-star homestay in 2025. Rhododendrons colour the slopes in spring, and Qipan Mountain, close to 1,000 m, is the high point.

rows.name: Jinggangshan
rows.summary: The mountain base where Mao Zedong's forces settled from October 1927 and where Zhu De's troops joined them in April 1928, now a scenic area of eight zones around the town of Ciping, including Huangyangjie, Longtan and the main peak. The farmhouses used as headquarters, residences and a hospital were burned after the Red Army left in January 1929 and were rebuilt to their original form after 1949; they can be visited at Ciping, Dajing, Xiaojing and elsewhere, among forested ridges that are in flower with rhododendrons in April and May. The national heritage listing of 1961, made under the old Ninggang county, also includes sites outside the scenic area: Maoping, Longshi and Gucheng in Jinggangshan City, Sanwan, Longyuankou and the county town in Yongxin county, and the county town of Suichuan.

rows.name: Jinmeihua Scenic Area, Xiajiang
rows.summary: A tourism area in Jinping ethnic township, which the county calls the only multi-ethnic township in Jiangxi and where it lists nine groups: Jing, Zhuang, Dai, Yao, Miao, Dong, Yi, She and Han. It combines fruit orchards with a market of stalls in minority style, a pomegranate-orchard guesthouse and restaurant, a study base, and crafts such as wax-resist dyeing and traditional papermaking, and holds festivals such as the Third Day of the Third Month in spring. It suits families and groups for a half-day out.

rows.name: Jishui Eastern Wu Tomb
rows.summary: A large Three Kingdoms brick tomb with a pyramid-shaped domed chamber and a surrounding corridor, found in 1991 during railway construction and dating from the late Eastern Wu period. It was moved about 200 m and rebuilt brick by brick at its present spot, with Jishui County Museum built around it, and more than 120 grave goods in bronze, iron, pottery, porcelain and stone were recovered.

rows.name: Jizhou Kiln
rows.summary: The site of a pottery town at Yonghe that made wares from the late Tang to the early Ming, best known for black-glazed tea bowls with leaf and paper-cut decoration. The national archaeological site park keeps 24 kiln mounds, and the Jizhou Kiln Museum shows white, green, qingbai and black-glazed wares, tea bowls, pillows, toys and figurines. A dragon kiln rebuilt in the 1980s is used for wood-firing events, and Yonghe is itself a listed historic town.

rows.name: Junbu Former Headquarters of the First Front Army, Yongfeng
rows.name_zh: 君埠红一方面军总司令部旧址
rows.pinyin: Jūnbù Hóng Yī Fāngmiànjūn Zǒngsīlìngbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A former Wanshou Palace temple hall in Laoxu village, Junbu township, rebuilt in the Republican period in brick and timber, 17 m wide and 39 m deep, which served as a headquarters of the Red First Front Army. The national listing also covers dozens of related sites across the township, mainly ancestral halls and houses used as army offices, field hospitals and billets, together with former residences of Zhu De, Zhou Enlai and Wang Jiaxiang at Zuofang.

rows.name: Longgang Qianbiao Stele and Xiyang Palace
rows.summary: A stone stele 2.12 m high, set up by the Song writer Ouyang Xiu on the path to his parents' tomb: the front carries his essay 'Longgang Qianbiao' (1,116 characters in 27 lines) in his own regular script, the back a genealogy of the Ouyang family. It stands in a two-storey pavilion in Xiyang Palace at Shaxi, a former Daoist temple at the Ouyang family home that also holds the Wenzhong ancestral hall, study halls and the joint tomb of Ouyang's parents. The stone is dark-green Qingzhou stone from Shandong.

rows.name: Luling Culture and Ecology Park, Ji'an
rows.summary: A large park on the northern side of Ji'an, laid out in recent years as one of the city's ecological parks and named for Luling, the old name of the Ji'an region. Its lotus ponds draw local visitors in summer, and it makes an easy outdoor stop in the city.

rows.name: Luling Renwengu, Ji'an
rows.summary: A district of shops, restaurants and cultural spaces in Ji'an's Luling New Area, laid out along the revived Gu Houhe river and its green corridor. Its centre is Luling Old Street, where a food night market opened in August 2026, and the Luling Renwengu commercial street, which the province listed among its first demonstration commercial streets (reported in January 2023) and which was named in the first batch of national night-time culture and tourism consumption clusters. It is a modern urban development rather than a historic quarter, and suits an evening visit.

rows.name: Majiazhou Concentration Camp Site, Taihe
rows.summary: A camp run by the Nationalist provincial government in Taihe from 1940 to 1945, officially the Jiangxi Youth Training Institute, where almost 500 prisoners, among them senior Communist Party members, were held before the camp moved away in January 1945. The surviving site covers about 5,000 square metres, with the Wang clan ancestral hall, a row of three village houses that includes the main confinement room, 18 smaller houses and an old camphor tree. A memorial park, rated a national 4A scenic area as the Majiazhou Revolutionary History Memorial Park, has been built beside it.

rows.name: Meibei Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village of more than a thousand years on the Fushui River in Wenpi town, promoted as a water-town "generals' village" and developed for visitors with a visitor centre, a trading street, a Wanshou Palace and water activities. Two national heritage sites stand here: the Liang clan's Yongmu Hall, which served as the Red Fourth Army's headquarters in 1930, and the site of the Beitou conference of 7 to 9 February 1930, at which Mao Zedong chaired a joint meeting of Party and army committees that adopted a land law. The listing also covers the home of Liang Xingchu and the Fourth Army's health-corps site at Mingde Hall.

rows.name: Motan Peach Blossom Island, Jishui
rows.summary: A flower and orchard island in the middle of the Gan River south of Jishui town, planted with peach and cherry trees, rape fields and mugwort, and forming the core of the Jihu National Wetland Park. It is laid out for family days out, with children's play areas, a glass footbridge across the river and a craft market. Spring blossom in March is the main draw.

rows.name: Peng Family Stone Carvings, Dazhi
rows.summary: Fifteen natural granite boulders in four clusters along about 1 km of path through Dazhi village carry inscriptions cut between 1447 and 1497 by the Peng family, which produced five jinshi (imperial examination graduates) in four generations. The texts, in regular script, are poems exchanged with friends, epitaphs, tomb markers and records of visits, about 5,300 legible characters in all. Together they record the country life of a Ming official family.

rows.name: Qingyuan Mountain and Jingju Temple
rows.summary: A wooded hill on the south-eastern edge of Ji'an with Jingju Temple, a national key Buddhist temple of the Han areas, founded in the Tang as Anyin Temple and renamed in the Song. It is the temple of the Chan master Xingsi, who taught here until his death in 740 and whose line led to the Caodong school, and the hill has the Qizu Pagoda, the Feilai Pagoda, a mountain pass gate, bridges, a pool and a spring.

rows.name: Sanwan Reorganisation Site, Yongxin
rows.summary: On 29 September 1927 the remnant of the Autumn Harvest Uprising force, fewer than 1,000 men, reached Sanwan, and its front committee under Mao Zedong decided at a meeting in the village to reorganise the 700 or so who stayed into a single regiment, with Party branches at company level and soldiers' committees. On 3 October the regiment assembled at the maple slope and set out for the Jinggang Mountains. The scenic area holds four national-level protected sites (Mao Zedong's former residence, the regimental headquarters, the soldiers' committee site and the maple slope), plus a memorial museum, the old village street and a red-maple lake.

rows.name: Shukou Eco-island, Taihe
rows.summary: An island village in the Gan River at Mashi town, presented by the county as an ecological island. The old village of Shukou was founded in the Southern Song and still has ancestral halls, tombs, steles, plaques and old houses, and the county credits it with 21 jinshi. Paths round the island suit walking, cycling or a boat trip, and the village is known for its local tea and for carp-lantern performances.

rows.name: Site of the Xiajiang Conference
rows.summary: A late-Qing brick-and-timber house of two halls, with a floor area of 598 square metres, on Hengjie street in the old town of Baqiu. In October 1930, after the Red First Front Army had failed to take Changsha and had captured Ji'an, its general front committee and the Jiangxi provincial action committee held a joint meeting here from 17 to 19 October, chaired by Mao Zedong. The county has funded work on the site's surroundings and its exhibition, and the building is used for on-site lessons.

rows.name: Site of the Xiang-Gan Provincial Committee, Yongxin
rows.summary: The Xiao clan's ancestral hall in the centre of Yongxin, built in 1914 of brick and timber, with a church-like front and three halls around two courtyards. The Xiang-Gan provisional provincial Party committee set up its office here on 1 August 1931 and left when the Red Army withdrew from the county town in February 1934. The listing also covers the former headquarters of the Xiang-Gan military district in the grounds of Ren Bishi Middle School.

rows.name: Taoyuan Terraces, Suichuan
rows.summary: Rice terraces climbing the mountainsides around Taoyuan village in Zuo'an town, in a scenic area of 10 km² made up of six zones: Jiaozi Ding, Wangtian Qiu, Panlong Hui, Yunding Xingsu, Taoyuan Huajie and Yunxiao Xianju. The county describes the terraces as small as saucers and as long as ribbons, changing shape with the seasons, and the area adds mountain walks, farm activities, Hakka customs and an evening light show on the terraces. It makes a day trip for photography and country walking.

rows.name: Tianbei Farmers' Painting Village, Wan'an
rows.summary: A village near Gaopi town built up as a showcase for Wan'an farmers' painting, the county's folk art, which the county promotes as a cultural-tourism product. The village has been rated a national 4A scenic area and a provincial 5A rural tourism point, and it hosts family activities such as catching loaches and butterflies in the fields. It suits a short stop for anyone curious about rural folk art.

rows.name: Tomb of Wen Tianxiang
rows.summary: The tomb of Wen Tianxiang, the Southern Song chancellor executed in Dadu (now Beijing) in 1283 under the Yuan, who was reburied in his home district the next year. The earth mound is 2.6 m high and 5 m across, with a sacrificial platform, a spirit path and a stone archway in front; the tomb was restored in the Ming and Qing dynasties and rebuilt with provincial funds in 1983 and 1993.

rows.name: Wan'an City Wall
rows.summary: About 1 km of Ming-period brick-and-stone town wall survives along the Gan River in Furong, the county town of Wan'an, with two of its gates, Guanlan and Wuyun, still standing. Building began in 1078 under the Northern Song and the wall was rebuilt in brick and stone in 1512, but most of it was pulled down after 1949. The 1927 Wan'an uprising entered the town through Wuyun Gate and set up the first county-level soviet government in Jiangxi.

rows.name: Yanfang Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village in Jintan town with a well-preserved Ming and Qing core of lineage halls, academies, memorial archways, houses, ponds and wells linked by lanes paved in stone, set among old camphor trees. The provincial tourism department's description records about 160 historic buildings, including 13 archways; the village was named a provincial historic and cultural village in 2003 and a national one in 2007. Spring Festival customs and markets are held here.

rows.name: Yang Wanli's Hometown, Bantang
rows.summary: Bantang village in Huangqiao town was the home of the Southern Song poet Yang Wanli (1127–1206), and the county presents it as the Yang Wanli Poetry and Painting Town. The village keeps his tomb, a provincial protected site, the Yang clan's ancestral hall and the Nanxi bridge among old blue-brick houses, and the site of his former residence has been restored to show how he lived. Scenes from his poems have been recreated, and the village has a study base for school groups.

rows.name: Yangshimu Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area of 37.5 km² on the Ji'an side of the Wugong Shan range, next to the Wugong Shan 5A area on the Pingxiang side, centred on a granite peak forest whose highest summit, Shisun Peak, is 1,764 m. The name comes from cloud formations that look like sheep and lions chasing each other, and the Song poet Yang Wanli wrote verse on the rock spires rising through the cloud. A high-level walkway gives views of the peaks and the sea of cloud, and walkers can climb to it from below through the Yeniu Waterfall Canyon.

rows.name: Yeniu Waterfall Canyon
rows.summary: A gorge about 13 km long on the Wugong Shan range in Anfu, cut by the Gexian River, with waterfalls, pools, odd rock formations and old pines; it is the walking approach to the Yangshimu peaks. A walkway along the river in the lower gorge passes the Qinglong Falls, about 70 m high, and the Yeniu Falls, about 30 m, and reaches the wide Baiyun Falls. Beyond the end of the walkway the gorge continues as a hiking route.

rows.name: Yew Wellness Valley, Wan'an
rows.summary: A countryside leisure area near Lutian town, named for its yew trees (more than 300,000, according to a 2023 provincial tourism department article), which the area promotes as a natural oxygen bar. Visitors can walk among the trees and try yew products such as yew wine and yew pillows, and there is a restaurant and guesthouses, with flower-viewing events in spring. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Yuanxia Village, Qubai
rows.summary: A tourist village in Qubai township laid out in Jiangxi-style old-village architecture, with grey brick and tile, horse-head gables and flagstone lanes. It has a food street and food court, a playground, a guesthouse hotel, a large stage in period style, riverside stilt houses, bars and cafes, so it is more a place for an evening meal and a stay than for historic sights. The province lists it as a 3A rural tourism demonstration site.

rows.name: Yuntian Lugu, Ji'an County
rows.summary: A rural leisure area in Tongping town, north of Ji'an, built around a large fishing centre, landscaped gardens and orchards of Jinggang mandarins and pomelos. Visitors can fish, pick fruit in season and walk the grounds, which suit families on a day trip from Ji'an. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2022.

rows.name: Yuzhi Wellness Valley, Xiajiang
rows.summary: A wellness park at the foot of Yuzhi Mountain, built around Xiajiang's traditional Chinese medicine industry and opened to visitors in early 2019. It was planned in three zones for wellness experiences, cultural displays and forest recuperation, with exhibits and hands-on spaces on Chinese medicine, set among ancient-style buildings, small bridges and lanterns. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2022 and suits a relaxed half-day outing from the county seat.

rows.name: Ancient Kiln Folk Customs Museum, Jingdezhen
rows.summary: An open-air museum complex built around the Zhen Kiln, a Qing-dynasty porcelain kiln that can fire dozens of kinds of ware at high and low temperatures and was lit again in June 2014. The grounds also hold workshops where craftspeople demonstrate hand-made porcelain and kiln firing, a Qing temple to Tong Bin, the kiln master worshipped as the kiln god, and two groups of historic buildings moved here: the Ming Garden, seven Ming buildings from villages in Fuliang, and the Qing Garden of four Qing buildings. It suits visitors who want to see traditional porcelain-making and old kilns in one place.

rows.name: Fuliang Ancient County Yamen
rows.summary: The government compound of Fuliang, the county town that long administered the Jingdezhen porcelain area, built in the Daoguang reign (1821–50). The surviving buildings are the gate, a courtyard, the main hall, a second hall, the inner residence and the kitchen, which together make up a Qing magistrate's office and residence. Demonstrations of intangible-heritage crafts for visitors are held on the site.

rows.name: Gaoling Kaolin Mine Site
rows.summary: Gaoling ("High Ridge") is the hill village whose name gave the world the word kaolin: its white clay, mixed with local porcelain stone, made the thin white porcelain of Jingdezhen possible. The mining area covers about 10 square kilometres of old pits and white spoil slopes, crossed by a mountain trail of about 7 km that miners used to carry washed clay down to the river wharf. Mining has stopped, and the site is one of the five parts of the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites, inscribed on the World Heritage List in July 2026.

rows.name: Guaishilin Stone Forest, Leping
rows.summary: A scenic area of strangely shaped rock formations on the Wenshan hills where Leping meets Wannian county. It is made up of the stone forest itself, the Water Curtain Cave, a field of boulders and a peak viewpoint, with rocks that look like animals and figures as the main sight.

rows.name: Hongyan Xianjing Cave, Leping
rows.summary: A limestone cave in the foothills of Mao Mountain in north-eastern Leping, about 1.6 km long, with stalactites, an underground waterfall and more than 120 named rock formations. Outside the cave is a stone-forest area of about 9 hectares (140 mu) with a pavilion, and the scenic area also keeps the site of a Song-dynasty study hall of the statesman Hong Hao. The cave stays cool in summer and is promoted as a retreat from the heat.

rows.name: Huangyao Ceramics Park
rows.summary: A ceramics culture park of about 14 hectares (210 mu) in Xianghu town, laid out in grey-brick, dark-tiled buildings with workshop scenes of the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing periods. Visitors can follow the 72 stages of hand-made porcelain from clay to kiln and try some of them, and the park receives school study groups. It is a national demonstration base for hand-made porcelain production and research, so it suits visitors who want a hands-on introduction.

rows.name: Hutian Kiln Site and Folk Kiln Museum
rows.summary: Hutian was a large folk (non-imperial) kiln complex that fired from the Five Dynasties period into the Ming, best known for the pale blue-white qingbai porcelain of the Song dynasty. The Jingdezhen Folk Kiln Museum shows pieces found here, and the excavated site across the road keeps kiln foundations, workshop pits, a Yuan-dynasty brick road and a Ming gourd-shaped kiln, with a Song-Yuan dragon kiln and a Ming kiln under cover on the hillside behind. It is one of the five parts of the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites, inscribed on the World Heritage List in July 2026.

rows.name: Jiangxi Helicopter Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: A science museum of about 10,000 square metres inside the grounds of a helicopter maker in Jingdezhen's high-tech zone; the city is one of China's helicopter-building centres and the Z-8 first flew here in 1985. It displays dozens of real helicopters, models and parts, some of which visitors can climb into, and offers virtual-reality flying and engine-assembly experiences and a view of the helicopter production line. It suits families and anyone interested in aviation.

rows.name: Mingfangyuan Ceramics Park
rows.summary: A ceramics-craft park built in traditional style in the Changnan New District on the north-western edge of Jingdezhen, with a planned area of 1.3 square kilometres. It houses studios of porcelain makers recognised as intangible-heritage practitioners, creation bases of art colleges, the Guoci Pavilion showroom of the Jingdezhen Ceramics Group, and a leisure complex called Jingdezhen Memory with restaurants, bars and performance space. It is a modern development for meeting porcelain makers and shopping for ceramics, not a historic quarter.

rows.name: Mingfentang Opera Stage, Hu'an
rows.summary: The Mingfentang is the ancestral hall of the Cheng family of Hu'an village, begun in 1817, and its stage was added later and took three years to build. It is a double-sided "mandarin-duck" stage, 25 m wide, 12 m deep and 14 m high, with a fair-weather side facing the village square and a rainy-day side facing the main hall, the two backing onto each other. Leping is known as the home of Gan opera and has more than 400 old stages.

rows.name: Red Pagoda, Fuliang
rows.summary: A nine-storey hexagonal brick pagoda, 40.47 m high, on the river road south of the old county yamen in Fuliang, also known as the Dasheng Pagoda. It was first built in 961 under the Northern Song and rebuilt in 1575 in the Ming; the city government restored it over two years from 1984 and reopened it to visitors. It is the landmark of the old county town and a short walk from the yamen.

rows.name: Shuangfeng Pagoda, Fuliang
rows.summary: A six-sided, five-storey brick pagoda 19 metres high, built in the Tiansheng era (1023–32) of the Northern Song by the Huang family of Legong village on the site of the vanished Shuangfeng Temple. It stands in a gap between two peaks of Baolian Hill, with carved stone Buddha figures in its niches, and two old steles beside it, one Southern Song and one Ming, record the temple's history. It became a national heritage unit in 2019.

rows.name: Taoxichuan Creative Quarter
rows.summary: A former state porcelain-factory district east of the old centre, redeveloped from the mid-2010s as a creative quarter. It has artists' studios and ceramic shops, the Central Academy of Fine Arts Taoxichuan Art Museum, a theatre, and markets for ceramics and street food. It shows present-day Jingdezhen, where young potters from across China and abroad work and sell.

rows.name: Xiangjilong Ming Houses
rows.summary: Two timber-framed Ming houses, Numbers 3 and 11 in Xiangjishang lane, built in the Chenghua reign (1465–87) in the old quarter around the Imperial Kiln site. Both face west and share one plan, with high end walls, fire-gables to the north and south, timber frames and a veranda; Number 11 is the larger, with about 455 square metres of floor space. They are part of the town-centre porcelain production centre, one of the five components of the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites, inscribed on the World Heritage List in July 2026.

rows.name: Yaoli Ancient Town
rows.summary: A mountain town in northern Fuliang that made porcelain before the Ming and later supplied porcelain clay and tea to Jingdezhen; its old name was written with the character for "kiln". Its Ming and Qing streets of Jiangxi-style houses stand along the river, with remains of kilns, workshops, wharves and old pack roads around them. In January 1938 Chen Yi presided here over the reorganisation of Red Army guerrilla units in south China before they moved to Anhui to form the New Fourth Army; the three buildings used, the Hongyi Temple, the Jingyi Hall that was his residence and the Cheng ancestral hall, are a national heritage unit.

rows.name: Autumn Harvest Uprising Headquarters Sites, Xiushui
rows.name_zh: 工农革命军第一军第一师师部及第一团团部旧址
rows.pinyin: Gōngnóng Gémìngjūn Dìyī Jūn Dìyī Shī Shībù Jí Dìyī Tuán Tuánbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Two neighbouring sites in the old town of Xiushui, at the foot of Fenghuang Hill: the former headquarters of the 1st Division of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army, and the former Fengyan Academy, built in 1864, which housed its 1st Regiment. The division was assembled here in early September 1927, and a flag-presentation ceremony was held on 9 September, the day the Autumn Harvest Uprising began. The Xiushui Autumn Harvest Uprising Memorial Hall, opened close by in 1977, exhibits the background to the uprising and the formation of the division.

rows.name: Balihu Lake Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area in Jiujiang's Balihu New District, rated 4A in 2015, with Haiyun Beach, Balihu Park and Wenbo Park around the shore of Balihu Lake. The new district also has a poetry gallery, a museum and a city exhibition hall near the water. It suits an easy walk or picnic rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Boyang River Scenic Area, De'an
rows.summary: A river-valley leisure area on the Boyang River at Niejiao town, in wooded hills with farmland along the banks. The main activity is rafting, on a 3.5 km course through woods and fields that suits the warm months, and the valley has also hosted a local folk-culture festival. It was rated 4A in 2020.

rows.name: Changshui Scenic Area, Wuning
rows.summary: A mountain-village scenic area around Changshui village, in the foothills of the Jiuling range in south-eastern Wuning, with yew trees, forest cover and a countryside guesthouse. It was rated 4A in 2021 and is paired with Luxi Cave and the Meeting Wuning night show on a one-day cool-summer route listed by the provincial tourism department in 2025. It suits a quiet rural stop rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Chen Family Hometown, Xiushui
rows.summary: A village scenic area built around Fengzhutang, the Chen family's old house at Zhuduan, listed nationally as the former residence of Chen Baozhen and Chen Sanli. The family produced five well-known figures: the reforming official Chen Baozhen, the poet Chen Sanli, the painter Chen Hengke, the scholar Chen Yinke and the botanist Chen Fenghuai. The older block of the house dates from 1793 and has a central courtyard, the newer block from the Guangxu reign, with flagpole stones in front, and the village has a folk-experience area on Hakka farming customs.

rows.name: Dasheng Pagoda
rows.summary: A six-sided brick pagoda 42.38 m high, standing in the grounds of Nengren Temple in central Jiujiang and so also called the Nengren Temple Pagoda. It has a hollow core, and above the second storey the stairs cut diagonally through the walls from one balcony level to the next, a layout that dates it no earlier than the Song dynasty; the Ming gazetteer records large repairs under the Hongwu and Yongle emperors. It was listed as a provincial site in 1957 and as a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Donghuzhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Zhengcun township, Xiushui county, where Jiangxi meets Hunan and Hubei, with red sandstone cliffs, a valley lake and a waterfall of over 30 m in a rock cave. It is named after two nearby hills shaped like a bell and a drum, which gave it the older name Bell-and-Drum Stockade. Its main draws are via ferrata climbing routes totalling about 3 km, a glass-floored bridge over Yinzi Stream and other adventure rides, so it suits active visitors.

rows.name: Former Mobil Oil Company Site, Jiujiang
rows.summary: A three-storey brick-and-concrete office building on the Yangtze waterfront in Xunyang District, built for the Standard Oil (Mobil) company, which opened a branch in Jiujiang's British concession in 1910. The southern two thirds dates from 1910 and a smaller northern part from 1918, when the Asiatic Petroleum Company added to it. It recalls Jiujiang's years as a Yangtze treaty port and was listed as a national site in 2006.

rows.name: Fuhua Mountain Tourist Area, Gongqingcheng
rows.summary: A 4.76 sq km tourist area on the Poyang Lake shore in Gongqingcheng, opened to visitors in November 2023, that gathers a park, a wetland and several museums in one place. It includes the Gongqingcheng Museum, the Jiangxi Ecological Civilisation Exhibition Hall, an aerospace museum named after Qian Xuesen and a Poyang Lake model test base, along with the cemetery of Hu Yaobang, the party leader who named the settlement Gongqing. A newly built commercial street, Shanghai Memory 1955, adds shops and restaurants in the style of old Shanghai, and the area suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Gongqing Reclamation Culture Park
rows.summary: A museum-style park on the site of the former Gongqing reclamation farm, where young volunteers from Shanghai began clearing land beside Poyang Lake in 1955; the farm later grew into Gongqingcheng. The old farm buildings have been repaired to look as they did in the 1950s and 1960s, and the park has reclamation tools on display, the site of the original Gongqing collective, a bonfire square, a VR hall and about 17 visiting sections. It suits school groups and anyone interested in how the city began.

rows.name: Guanyin Bridge
rows.summary: A single-span granite arch bridge over the Sanxia Stream at the southern foot of Mount Lushan, built in 1014 under the Northern Song and one of the oldest surviving stone arch bridges in China. It is made of 107 granite blocks joined by tongue-and-groove joints without mortar, and the date is carved on the arch. Poets from Su Shi and Huang Tingjian to Zhu Xi wrote about it, and it stands beside Qixian Temple.

rows.name: Gutang Customs House
rows.summary: A group of three Western-style brick-and-timber buildings (a tax office, an administration office and staff quarters) at Gutang, near where Poyang Lake meets the Yangtze. A customs post was set up here in 1723 under the Qing; the surviving buildings date from 1902, and the Lianxi district government describes them as the only fairly complete modern customs station left in Jiangxi. The site is promoted as the first pass on the Ten-Thousand-Mile Tea Road, with displays on its history in the buildings.

rows.name: Huang Tingjian's Hometown, Shuangjing
rows.summary: The village of Shuangjing on the Xiu River, birthplace of the Northern Song poet and calligrapher Huang Tingjian, laid out as a scenic area since 2017 so that the whole village forms the attraction. It has a newly built commercial old street, the Shuangjing Jinshi Garden recalling the village's many successful examination candidates, and the Gaofeng Academy, and the village is also known for Shuangjing tea. It is popular with school study groups.

rows.name: Kairui Countryside Complex, Pengze
rows.summary: A farm-tourism complex of about 7,500 mu (500 hectares) in the Taibo Lake agricultural zone, where rice and crayfish are raised in the same fields. It has a farming museum, a hall on shrimp and crab farming, a village built around that theme, glasshouses, and walkways through orchards and bamboo. It suits families and anyone curious about modern Chinese agriculture, and has been rated 4A since 2022.

rows.name: Longgong Cave (Dragon Palace Cave), Pengze
rows.summary: A karst cave group at the foot of Wulong Mountain in Tianhong town, south-west of Pengze town. The main cave, found in 1978, runs about 1.6 km underground at a steady 18°C all year, and the group also includes the Yuhu and Yuxian caves, a mountain temple and a forest park. A flower garden with a miniature train and other rides has been added on the surface.

rows.name: Longyuan Gorge, Yongxiu
rows.summary: A river gorge in the hills of the Yunshan area, deep inside the Yunju Mountain national scenic zone, with clear streams, cliffs and woods. A family-friendly rafting run through the gorge is its main activity in the warm months. It was rated 4A in February 2026.

rows.name: Luminggu Resort (Deer Valley)
rows.summary: A family resort of about 2,000 mu (roughly 133 ha) on the edge of Xiushui town, built around a deer theme; its second phase, the former Xiushui hot-spring town, opened in January 2025. It combines hot-spring pools with a petting zoo where visitors can feed sika deer, plus evening shows and light displays. It suits families with children rather than anyone looking for heritage or scenery.

rows.name: Lushan Xihai (Lushan West Sea)
rows.summary: A large reservoir lake west of Mount Lushan, created between 1958 and 1972 by damming the Xiu River at Zhelin. Its 308 sq km of water spread mainly across Yongxiu and Wuning counties and are dotted with wooded islands, with boat trips and lakeside walks on offer. The scenic area has three sections, Zhelin, Jinkou and the Buddhist mountain of Yunju, and has been rated 5A since 2020.

rows.name: Lushan Xihai International Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 庐山西海国际温泉度假村
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Yijiahe village on the south shore of the Xihai reservoir, listed by the province as Lushan Xihai Hot Spring Resort, with a large hotel, villas and a spa park of pools grouped by bathing style, among them Chinese, Japanese, Roman and Finnish sections and a herbal-bath cave. It also has a water-play area, and the hot water comes from a spring well. It makes a comfortable base for Lushan Xihai, the 5A lake scenic area, and for Yunju Mountain, and suits an overnight stay.

rows.name: Luxi Cave, Wuning
rows.summary: A cave in the Mufu Mountains near Luxi town, at the source of the Luxi River, with stalactites throughout and an underground stream running through it. The cool interior makes it a summer stop, and the provincial tourism department's 2025 cool-summer route pairs it with Changshui and the Meeting Wuning night show. It was rated 4A in February 2024.

rows.name: Mangu Countryside Complex, Pengze
rows.summary: A countryside leisure complex of about 7,900 mu (530 hectares) south-east of Pengze's national modern agriculture park, styled after the Wei and Jin dynasties. It has flower beds, rice-and-crayfish fields, a fruit-picking area, a fishing area, a children's play area, a small animal park, camping lawns, a hotel and guesthouses. It was rated 4A in February 2026.

rows.name: Nanshan Forest Park, Duchang
rows.summary: A wooded hill on the southern side of Duchang town, laid out as a forest park, with views over the wide waters of Poyang Lake and old temples. Local tradition ties the Song poet Su Shi's verse on Duchang to a visit to Nanshan. It makes an easy stop for lake views and a short walk.

rows.name: Nanshan Park, Jiujiang
rows.summary: A wooded city park in Lianxi district, in the southern part of Jiujiang's built-up area, where residents relax and gather for events. It was the main venue of Jiangxi's 2022 intangible-heritage shopping festival, which brought together stalls for crafts, food and traditional medicine from across the province. It suits a short stop for green space in the city rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Pipa Pavilion and Xunyang River Park
rows.summary: A riverside park on the Yangtze bank in eastern Jiujiang, built around the rebuilt Pipa Pavilion, which takes its name from the Tang poet Bai Juyi's poem Song of the Pipa. Bai Juyi wrote it in 816 after hearing a pipa player on a boat on this stretch of river, then called the Xunyang River, while he was in exile in Jiujiang. The pavilion was rebuilt in 1988, and the park around it, with a pond, scenes from the poem and a digital show in which visitors talk with Bai Juyi, opened in April 2017.

rows.name: Saicheng Lake Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lakeside park and greenway on Saicheng Lake, in the Balihu New District on the western side of Jiujiang. Its shore path is used for walking, cycling and angling, and the park suits a short outdoor stop rather than a full outing.

rows.name: Shizhongshan (Stone Bell Mountain)
rows.summary: A small hill on the Yangtze where Poyang Lake flows into the river, named for the bell-like booming of waves in the caves under its cliffs, a sound the Song poet Su Shi investigated by boat and described in his essay on the mountain. The hill commands the river-lake junction and was fought over by Taiping and Xiang Army fleets in the 1850s; the buildings on it, completed by 1860 and centred on a shrine hall, include Buddhist halls and a guest villa, and the rock is carved with inscriptions by Su Shi, Huang Tingjian, Guo Moruo and others. The buildings and inscriptions are on the national list of protected sites, added in 2013.

rows.name: Sunshine 29 Resort (Huayuan Valley), Wuning
rows.summary: A lakeside resort on more than a hundred islands and peninsulas of the Xihai reservoir in Yangzhou township, named for lying near latitude 29°N. Many of the islands are planted with a single flower, such as peach, magnolia, begonia or verbena, a flower festival is held each spring, and there is a sandy beach with water sports and wooden cabins. Boat routes link it with Wuning town and the main Lushan Xihai scenic area.

rows.name: Suojianglou Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey, six-sided brick-and-stone pagoda about 25 m tall, standing on a rocky point on the south bank of the Yangtze, begun in the 1580s and completed in 1604 to guard Jiujiang against floods and fire and to favour success in the examinations. Also known as Huilong Pagoda, it leans slightly to the north-east after being hit by gunfire in the 1938 fighting for Jiujiang. Beside it stand the Suojianglou pavilion, rebuilt in 2004, and a digital museum about Jiujiang and the river.

rows.name: Taishan Park, Hukou
rows.summary: A town park in the centre of Hukou, on Taishan Avenue, rated 4A as part of the county's Taishan scenic area, which also takes in Shizhong Park, the Hukou County Museum and a planning exhibition hall. The museum and Shizhong Park stand close by, so it fits into a walk around the town centre before or after a visit to Shizhongshan on the Yangtze.

rows.name: Tangtaizong Hot Spring Resort, Lushan
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Wenquan town, on the southern side of Mount Lushan, built in Han and Tang style with bathing pools set into the hillside and a hotel on site. Wenquan is known for its mineral springs, and this resort draws on water that rises from deep wells at about 70°C. It suits a relaxed half-day soak or an overnight stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Tianmu Hot Spring Resort, Lushan
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Wenquan town, at the foot of Mount Lushan, combining spa pools with a hotel, restaurants and meeting and entertainment facilities. Wenquan's mineral springs are used by several resorts, of which this is one, and it suits a relaxed half-day soak or overnight stay more than sightseeing.

rows.name: Tongling Copper Mine Site
rows.summary: The site of an ancient copper mine near Tongling village, worked from the middle Shang dynasty, about 3,300 years ago, until the Warring States period, and named one of China's ten major archaeological discoveries of 1991. Excavations uncovered more than a hundred mine shafts, galleries and open pits, many with timber supports. A museum opened in October 2024 in the new archaeological site park, with three sections on the site's place in bronze-age civilisation, the excavation and its techniques, and conservation, alongside a covered excavation area.

rows.name: Tongwen Academy, Jiujiang
rows.summary: Three listed buildings in the grounds of Jiujiang Tongwen Middle School, in the old part of Jiujiang: the Tongwen Academy building and the office and classroom buildings of the former Ruli Girls' School. The academy was founded in 1867 and the girls' school, set up by the Methodist Episcopal mission, in 1873; the two schools merged after 1949, and the school took back the Tongwen name in 2002. The buildings were listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2013.

rows.name: Tongyuan Paper-Cutting Culture Park, Ruichang
rows.summary: A culture park at Xiafan town, on both banks of the Nanyang River beside the Tongling mine site, built around Ruichang paper-cutting, a craft on China's national intangible heritage list. It is planned in five sections, among them a paper-cutting town with a museum of the craft, a street of craft studios and an opera stage, together with farmland, a mine park and an artists' quarter. The museum has a hands-on area where visitors can try the stages of paper-cutting.

rows.name: Virtuous Mothers Park, Jiujiang
rows.summary: A themed park on the western side of Jiujiang devoted to the figure of the exemplary mother in Chinese tradition. It has display halls and sculptures, and it includes the Jiangxi Virtuous Mothers Culture Museum.

rows.name: Wanjialing Victory Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park on the northern edge of De'an town commemorating the Battle of Wanjialing, fought in the hills of this county in autumn 1938 during the Second Sino-Japanese War between Chinese forces and the Japanese 106th Division. The exhibition hall shows relics and extracts from Japanese soldiers' diaries, and the park was added to China's national list of anti-war memorial facilities in 2015. The battlefield remains, including trenches and bunkers, lie in the hills at Moxi township and are a separate trip.

rows.name: White Deer Grotto Academy
rows.summary: A former Confucian academy in a wooded valley at the foot of Wulao Peak on the southern side of Mount Lushan, counted among the Four Great Academies of China. A school was founded here in the 10th century, and the academy was rebuilt in 1179–80 by the neo-Confucian scholar Zhu Xi, whose rules for students influenced later academies. The grounds include a gate, courtyards and halls, a gallery of stone inscriptions, the Zhu Xi shrine and a man-made stone grotto with a carved deer.

rows.name: Wucheng Migratory Bird Town
rows.summary: A historic trading town on the western shore of Poyang Lake that has become a centre for watching wintering waterbirds, which gather on the lake's wetlands in large flocks. Bird-watching points with hides and towers are set around the nearby lakes, and Wanghu Pavilion in the town looks out over the water. In the high-water season from April to September, a 5 km section of the Yongwu Road at Dahuchi can be covered by shallow water and is promoted as a "water road".

rows.name: Xihai Bay (Xihaiwan), Wuning
rows.summary: A lakeside park that makes up much of the centre of Wuning town, joining Chaoyang Lake, the Shatian River wetland park and several smaller parks with bridges, pavilions and waterside walks. Boats for cruises on the Xihai reservoir leave from the pier here, and in the evening a staged water show, Meeting Wuning, is performed with the shoreline lit up. It is an easy stop for a stroll or a boat trip.

rows.name: Xiufeng Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area at the southern foot of Mount Lushan, centred on Longtan pool and the site of Xiufeng Temple, which was founded under the Southern Tang. The rock faces and steles carry inscriptions from the Tang dynasty to the Republic, among them the Tang Zhongxing Stele by Yan Zhenqing, of which three of the four original stones survive, and a stele by Wang Yangming. Its waterfalls and peaks are linked with Li Bai's poem on viewing a waterfall on Mount Lushan.

rows.name: Yunju Mountain and Zhenru Temple
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A Buddhist mountain in western Yongxiu, one of the three sections of the Lushan Xihai 5A scenic area, rising to about 970 m, with cool summers and wooded valleys that hold waterfalls, among them a 120 m drop at Five Dragon Pool. At its centre is Zhenru Chan Temple, founded in the early 9th century in the Tang dynasty and the ancestral temple of the Caodong school of Chan Buddhism, with halls rebuilt from 1953. A short walk east of the temple, the pagoda court holds memorial pagodas of Chan masters from the Tang to the Yuan dynasties, which form the nationally listed Zhenru Temple Pagoda Forest.

rows.name: Ziyang Embankment
rows.summary: A curved stone embankment about a kilometre long on the western shore of Poyang Lake, at the southern end of Ziyang South Road in Nankang, the seat of Lushan City. It was extended in 1179 by the neo-Confucian scholar Zhu Xi while he was prefect of Nankang, and is named after his pen name Ziyang. Built of stacked stone blocks 7–8 m wide, it has stone bridges to the shore and arched openings that let fishing boats pass through.

rows.name: Anyi Ancient Villages
rows.summary: Anyi Ancient Villages is a group of three villages, Luotian, Shuinan and Jingtai, arranged in a triangle in Shibi town, Anyi county, at the foot of the Meiling hills. The villages date from the Tang dynasty and are listed as Chinese traditional villages; Luotian grew into an old market town on the pilgrim route to Meiling and the Wanshou Palace at Xishan. The lanes have been developed for visitors with homestays, a regional snack street, teahouses and cafés.

rows.name: August 1st Nanchang Uprising Memorial Hall
rows.summary: On 1 August 1927 the Chinese Communist Party launched the Nanchang Uprising, with its general headquarters in this building, the former Jiangxi Grand Hotel, a five-storey brick-and-timber block of 1923 with 96 rooms around a courtyard. The memorial hall, founded in 1956 and open since 1959, displays the events of the uprising, and the second-floor offices and bedrooms of Zhou Enlai and Lin Boqu are part of the building. The 1961 national heritage listing, 'Headquarters of the August 1 Uprising', also covers four other sites in the city, among them the headquarters of He Long and Ye Ting and Zhu De's former residence.

rows.name: Bamboo Sea Pearl, Meiling
rows.summary: Bamboo Sea Pearl, once known as the main peak of Meiling, is a bamboo-covered valley in the heart of the Meiling hills whose slopes climb to the Hualaoji peak, more than 800 m high. A series of coloured cascades drops over rocks at the entrance, and odd-shaped boulders, among them a tortoise-shaped one, stand among the bamboo.

rows.name: Chen Family Memorial Archways, Luoyuan
rows.summary: Two memorial archways of the Ming period stand one behind the other in Luoyuan Chen village, Qili township. The older, the Zhoujin ('Brocade by Day') Archway of 1410, is a four-pillar brick archway about 5 m high that honours Chen Mo, a scholar who took part in compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia; the Lixue Mingxian (Neo-Confucian Worthies) Archway of 1637, about 12 m to its south, is a timber archway of about 6 m with stone lions at its pillars.

rows.name: Fangda Special Steel Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: An operating steel works in Qingshanhu district opened to visitors as an industrial tourism area, rated 4A in June 2022 as the first steelmaker in Jiangxi and the third in China to receive the rating. The plant, which makes spring flat steel and leaf springs for vehicles, has a visitor centre and a gift shop, and a tour can take in a rolling-mill line, a steelmaking plant, a control centre, a wetland landscape at the coking plant and a company exhibition hall. Leisure and study-tour programmes are also offered.

rows.name: Fenghuanggou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Fenghuanggou is a tea-growing and leisure estate of about 6 sq km in red-soil hills in Huangma township, Nanchang County, run as a modern agriculture demonstration park. Terraced tea gardens covering more than 2,100 mu (about 140 hectares) surround a cherry-blossom valley that flowers from late February to April, and the ginkgoes turn gold in December. Lakes, wetland, fruit and vegetable picking and a silk-and-mulberry theme add to a visit, which suits families and photographers in the flowering seasons.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the New Fourth Army, Nanchang
rows.summary: A two-storey French-style house built in 1915 for the warlord Zhang Xun served as the headquarters of the New Fourth Army from 6 January to 4 April 1938, and afterwards housed the CPC Southeast Bureau and the army's Jiangxi liaison office until March 1939. The house and two other buildings stand in a compound beside an exhibition building opened in 2011, which holds a permanent display, 'The Iron New Fourth Army', on the army's formation and wartime service.

rows.name: Former Site of the CPC Southeast Bureau
rows.name_zh: 中共中央东南分局旧址
rows.summary: This is a courtyard of six brick-and-timber houses built in 1917 as a salt merchant's home, on Dongshuyuan Street in Nanchang's Xihu district. The CPC Central Committee's Southeast Bureau, formed in January 1938 and known outwardly as the New Fourth Army's Jiangxi liaison office, first worked here before moving into the army's headquarters building nearby. The houses were restored in 2017 and opened with an exhibition on the bureau.

rows.name: Greenland Central 303 Observation Hall
rows.summary: This is an observation hall high up in one of the twin Greenland Central Plaza towers, supertall skyscrapers of 303 m and 59 floors built between 2011 and 2015. The towers stand in the Honggutan business district on the west bank of the Gan River, and the hall appears on the provincial tourism department's city leisure routes.

rows.name: Guaishiling Ecological Park
rows.summary: Guaishiling Ecological Park is a hill-and-lake leisure area of about 4,200 mu (some 280 hectares) at Xixia town, north-west of Nanchang. Its crags include a natural climbing wall, and a 4.38 km agricultural viewing corridor is built in the form of a Great Wall, with trails, fishing and campsites in the grounds. It is a farm-and-leisure park rather than a wild landscape, and suits families and day trippers.

rows.name: Haihun Marquisate Archaeological Park
rows.summary: Haihun was a Western Han marquisate whose first marquis, Liu He, had been king of Changyi and briefly emperor in 74 BC; the park protects its capital, Zijincheng, its cemeteries and his tomb garden, which a rescue excavation uncovered in 2011. In the tomb garden of about 46,000 sq m the main tomb and a chariot-and-horse pit are displayed under cover, along with the foundations of sacrificial halls, and the garden yielded more than 10,000 sets of gold, jade, bronze, lacquer and bamboo-slip finds. The Haihun Marquisate Museum on the same site shows the finds; the park opened in 2020 and the tomb garden itself to visitors in December 2023.

rows.name: Hongya Danjing
rows.summary: Hongya Danjing is a wooded gorge at the entrance to the Meiling hills, with a waterfall and cliffs carved with old inscriptions, the clearest dated 1185. A legend tells of Hongya, a music master of the Yellow Emperor, who dug five wells here to make elixirs and devised the twelve-tone scale, and the place is one of the Ten Views of Yuzhang, the old name for Nanchang. It has been a provincial heritage site since 1985, and Nanchang's old names Hongzhou and Hongdu are traced to it.

rows.name: Lidu Distillery Site
rows.summary: This is a distillery site of the Yuan to Qing dynasties, found in 2002 when an old workshop of the Lidu liquor works was being rebuilt, and named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of that year. The excavation turned up 22 cellars, 13 of the Yuan and 9 of the Ming, six of which are still in use, together with wells, hearths and two distillation bases. Visitors can see the old cellars and demonstrations of traditional brewing, and the site is also on China's list of national industrial heritage.

rows.name: Lion Peak, Meiling
rows.summary: Lion Peak is a peak on the north-western side of the Meiling hills in Wanli district, named for its resemblance to a crouching lion, with a stream valley, bamboo woods, boulders, a suspension bridge and a summit viewpoint. The scenic area has also added adventure and water activities, and the district promotes it as a cool retreat for the city in summer.

rows.name: OCT Happy Xianghu
rows.summary: OCT Happy Xianghu is a leisure district developed by the OCT (Overseas Chinese Town) group on the west shore of Xianghu lake, rated 4A in 2022. It includes the Maya Beach water park, which the provincial tourism department lists on its summer city route.

rows.name: Pavilion of Prince Teng
rows.summary: The Pavilion of Prince Teng is a nine-storey, 57.5 m tower on the east bank of the Gan River, counted with Yueyang Tower and the Yellow Crane Tower as one of the three great towers of south China. The first pavilion was built in 653 and became famous through Wang Bo's preface of 675; it was destroyed and rebuilt many times, and the present Song-style concrete building, based on Liang Sicheng's sketches, was completed in 1989. Inside are murals of historical figures from Jiangxi and a bronze scale model of the pavilion, and the grounds were extended northwards in 2024.

rows.name: Qingyunpu (Bada Shanren Memorial Hall)
rows.summary: Qingyunpu is a Taoist retreat of long standing on the southern edge of Nanchang where the painter Bada Shanren (Zhu Da, about 1626 to about 1705), a descendant of the Ming imperial house, lived after the fall of the Ming; since 1959 it has been a memorial hall to him. Courtyards among old camphor trees hold his paintings and life story, a garden corridor of stone slabs shows more than 120 of his works, and a newer hall built in 2009–10 displays original paintings. Outside the gate lies Meihu Lake, whose shore is the Bada Shanren Meihu scenic area, with newer arts and culture venues.

rows.name: Shengjin Pagoda
rows.summary: Shengjin Pagoda is a seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda, 50.86 m high, outside the old Jinxian Gate of Nanchang; the first pagoda dates from 904–907 and the present one was rebuilt in 1713–14. A temple, the Qianfo or Taxia Temple, stands at its foot, a temple fair is held on the site each autumn, and the surrounding old street is known for evening food stalls.

rows.name: Sunac Theme Park, Nanchang
rows.summary: Sunac Theme Park is an amusement park in the Jiulonghu area of Honggutan district, part of the Sunac cultural-tourism complex on the south-western side of Nanchang. It runs amusement rides and staged shows, and Sunac's separate ocean park, Sunac Sea World, stands in the same area.

rows.name: Tianxiang Garden
rows.summary: Tianxiang Garden is a 1,150 mu (about 77 hectares) former horticultural farm turned wetland park in Qingshanhu district, on the eastern side of Nanchang, where lakes and marsh draw large flocks of wild birds. Birdwatching is the main draw, and in spring the garden holds a peony festival.

rows.name: Tongyuan Gorge
rows.summary: Tongyuan Gorge is a scenic area in the wooded hills of Xinjian district on the Meiling side of Nanchang, rated 4A in 2024. The city promotes it for spring flowers, with rapeseed fields of about 100 mu and a thousand peach trees, and the provincial tourism department lists it first on a one-day summer route of mountain and stream scenery that goes on to the Meiling hills and Guaishiling.

rows.name: Wanshou Palace Historic Quarter
rows.summary: A quarter of lanes and shops rebuilt in old style around the Tiezhu Wanshou Palace, the Taoist temple of the Xu Xun cult, which stood in Nanchang's old city from the fourth century until it was burned down in the Cultural Revolution; the quarter opened in February 2021. Streets of grey brick and tile hold restaurants and shops selling local snacks and gifts, and an open-air stage is used for evening performances. It is lively after dark, and the city promotes a walking route linking it with the Pavilion of Prince Teng.

rows.name: Xiaoping Path, Nanchang
rows.summary: Deng Xiaoping and his wife Zhuo Lin were sent to Xinjian county, Jiangxi, in October 1969, during the Cultural Revolution, and stayed until February 1973; he worked at the county tractor repair factory and walked each day between it and his residence, a route later called the Xiaoping Path. The site keeps the workshop where he worked, with his bench and tools, the path with a visitors' walkway, an exhibition hall opened in 2013 with six display sections, and the former residence, which stands in the grounds of what is now the Nanchang Army Academy.

rows.name: Yuanchengji Nanchang Urban Culture Quarter
rows.name_zh: 原城纪·南昌城市文化街区
rows.summary: Yuanchengji is a street quarter of about 250 mu (roughly 17 hectares) built in the Yinsanjiao area south-east of central Nanchang and opened in September 2020, designed to recall the city in the Republican era. Its two- to six-storey buildings are new, made in old-street style, and hold an arcade food street, a tea house staging Gan-region opera, craft and intangible-heritage workshops, shops and a boutique hotel. It is a place for a food-and-shopping stroll, not a historic district.

rows.name: Yuling Shanguan and Yunting Villa
rows.summary: Yuling Shanguan and Yunting Villa are two walled garden-residences of the Chen family, the west and east estates of a group of Qing-period houses in Aixi Chen village, Jiaqiao town. Yuling Shanguan covers about 4,500 sq m and has study rooms, a library tower and the Lianchun Pavilion beside a pond; Yunting Villa was begun in 1863 and belonged to Chen Kuicai, a provincial graduate of the Xianfeng reign, and his son Chen Yingchen, a Guangxu-reign jinshi. The estates stand in a working village among brick courtyards and ponds.

rows.name: Zuojiazhai Eco-Park
rows.summary: Zuojiazhai is a countryside leisure park of about 2,200 mu (150 hectares) on the Maogang farm in Qianfang town, Jinxian county, laid out around orchards, flower fields and the Yanming lake. Spring brings cherry blossom and flowering ground-cover phlox, with fruit picking, a long kiwi-fruit corridor, a tropical plant garden and family play areas, and the park stages a live-action show about the 1927 Nanchang Uprising. It was added to the national 4A list in February 2026.

rows.name: Anyuan Miners' Strike Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 安源路矿工人运动纪念馆
rows.summary: A museum on the slope of Niuxingling in Anyuan, the old coal-mining quarter of Pingxiang, housed in a building opened in 1969 that replaced a first exhibition set up in the former workers' club in 1956. Its displays follow the labour movement at the Anyuan collieries and on the Zhuzhou–Pingxiang railway between 1921 and 1930, centred on the miners' and railway workers' strike of September 1922, with large sculpture groups in the halls. The museum also runs the original sites nearby, among them the club, the former colliery office and the mine portal, which have their own entries on this map.

rows.name: Anyuan Railway and Mine Workers' Club Site
rows.name_zh: 安源路矿工人俱乐部旧址
rows.summary: The club of the Anyuan railway and mine workers, founded in May 1922, moved in 1923–24 into a new two-part building on Banbian Street square, designed and paid for by its members: a two-storey office block at the front and a lecture hall behind. The national listing, made in 1982 and extended in 2006, also covers the club's earlier premises at Niujiaopo, which served as the headquarters of the September 1922 strike, the former colliery office where negotiations took place, and the site of a military meeting held in September 1927 before the Autumn Harvest Uprising. The memorial hall on the slope above looks after the site.

rows.name: Anyuan Workers' Night School Site
rows.name_zh: 安源路矿工人补习夜校旧址
rows.pinyin: Ānyuán Lùkuàng Gōngrén Bǔxí Yèxiào Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A small building dating from 1922 on the slope of Niuxingling in Anyuan, listed nationally in 2019 as the site of the night school for railway and mine workers that was run alongside the Anyuan workers' club. It stands next to the club's earlier premises, which served as the strike headquarters in September 1922, and about 200 m south-west of the memorial hall.

rows.name: Huajianli, Wugong Shan
rows.summary: Huajianli is a leisure and culture-tourism complex at the foot of Wugong Shan, built as a lowland attraction to go with the mountain. It stages shows, camp-site parties and food markets at holiday times, and hosted an outdoor electronic-music festival in 2022. It is a modern development in a village setting rather than a historic site, and has since been rated a national 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Mashan Happiness Village
rows.summary: A rural-tourism village on the edge of Mashan town in the south-west of Pingxiang's Xiangdong District, set among farmland and rated a national 4A scenic area. Mashan town has been named one of China's key rural-tourism towns and a provincial 'scenery unrivalled' tourism town. It is a countryside destination for day visits rather than a single sight.

rows.name: Shenggong Hall (Former Pingxiang Colliery Head Office)
rows.summary: A three-storey, German-style brick-and-timber building at the top of a slope, put up in 1898 when the Pingxiang colliery opened as its head office and later used as quarters for the German engineers the colliery employed. After the death in 1916 of Sheng Xuanhuai, general manager of the Hanyeping company that owned the colliery, the building was renamed Shenggong Hall in his memory. Traces of a gun platform built for the colliery's guards survive in front, and the hall was listed nationally in 2013.

rows.name: Wugong Shan Scenic Area (Luxi side)
rows.summary: The Pingxiang (Luxi county) side of the Wugong Shan range is a national 5A area on a granite ridge that rises to Baihe Peak (Jinding), the range's highest point at 1,918 m. The upper slopes are covered by wide alpine meadows, and walkers come for the sunrise and sea of cloud at the top, with cable cars and shuttle buses easing the climb and a sacrificial site beside the summit protected as a provincial relic. A small geology museum in the basement of the visitor centre explains the range, which became a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2024.

rows.name: Xianfeng Sanbao Leisure Park
rows.summary: A countryside leisure park at Zhuyuan village, Xuanfeng town, rated a national 4A scenic area as an agricultural leisure and sightseeing park. Pingxiang's tourism authorities promote it as a place for family outings and farmland leisure within reach of the city. It is a modern commercial park built on farmland, not a historic place.

rows.name: Yangqi Shan and Putong Temple Pagodas
rows.summary: Yangqi Shan is a wooded karst mountain north of Pingxiang, regarded as the ancestral home of the Yangqi school of Chan (Zen) Buddhism. Putong Temple, founded in 713 and renamed in the 1040s when the monk Fanghui began the school there, has two small Tang pagodas in its grounds, one octagonal (2.35 m) and one shaped like a square pavilion, which are a national heritage unit. The scenic area also includes the Nielong Cave, a lit karst cave used as a summer retreat, and a small geology museum.

rows.name: Yueshang Guanghan, Guanghanzhai
rows.summary: A countryside scenic area in Guanghanzhai township, in the forested hills in the south of Pingxiang's Xiangdong District, rated a national 4A scenic area in 2025. People's Daily Jiangxi describes the township's Dashajiang river valley, its village tofu and bamboo-shoot workshops and its village guesthouses. It is a rural leisure area rather than a single sight.

rows.name: Yunding Area, Wugong Shan
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Yunding is a separately rated part of the Luxi side of Wugong Shan, listed as a national 4A scenic area in its own right in 2022 rather than as part of the 5A core. Local tourism authorities join it with the Jinding area around the summit as a 'Yunding–Jinding' circuit. Its start point is the car park at Dongjiang village on the northern side of the range, from which paths climb towards the ridge.

rows.name: Zongpingxiang Mine Portal, Anyuan
rows.summary: The main entrance to the Anyuan colliery, built in 1898: a red-brick gateway about 6 m high set against the hillside and facing north, with a central arch leading down to the workings, guard rooms on both sides and, above the arch, a hammer-and-pick motif with the three characters of its name. The miners' and railway workers' strike of September 1922 began here on 14 September, when workers came up out of the pit on a signal and blocked the entrance until the strike ended a few days later. Mao Zedong went down the mine through it in the autumn of 1921, and the portal has been a provincial heritage site since 1957 and a national one since 2013.

rows.name: Daming Flower Sea, Yugan
rows.summary: Daming Flower Sea is a flower-themed leisure park on the shore of Daming Lake, one of the lakes inside the Kangshan dyke on the south-east side of Poyang Lake. Work began in 2016, and the park has planted gardens of roses, crape myrtle and cherry trees, a landscaped waterfall and areas for wedding photography. It is a commercial attraction, and what is in bloom depends on the season.

rows.name: Dieshan Culture Park, Yiyang
rows.summary: Dieshan Culture Park is centred on Dieshan Academy, a provincial protected site on the Xin River bank, first built in 1318 in memory of Xie Fangde (sobriquet Dieshan), a Southern Song loyalist who refused to serve the Yuan dynasty and died in 1289. The academy was rebuilt in the Ming dynasty and keeps its lecture hall, river-view tower, Wenchang pavilion and osmanthus garden; Fang Zhimin and Shao Shiping studied here between 1916 and 1919. The park became a national 4A scenic area in 2024 and is a stop on a Fang Zhimin heritage route launched in Yiyang in 2025.

rows.name: Ehu Academy
rows.summary: Ehu Academy stands at the foot of Mount Ehu on the spot where, in 1175, the philosophers Zhu Xi, Lu Zuqian, Lu Jiuyuan and Lu Jiuling held the debate known as the Ehu Meeting. The academy took its present name in the Ming dynasty, and its layout dates largely from a Qing rebuilding of 1717 that added a gatehouse, stone archway, hall, ceremonial pool, arched bridge, stele pavilion and imperial-book tower, with rows of student cells beside them. It has been a national heritage site since 2006 and is also a national 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Fairy Valley (Sanqingshan)
rows.summary: Fairy Valley is a stream valley at the foot of Mount Sanqing, one of several smaller scenic areas around the mountain that are separate from the summit circuits. Streams and small waterfalls run through wooded hills, and the valley is set up for outdoor activities such as stream-tracing and forest crossing, with a caravan campsite among its experience bases.

rows.name: Gong Ancestral Halls, Ankeng
rows.summary: Two Qing-dynasty ancestral halls of the Gong clan stand 80 m apart in Ankeng village: Daigong Hall, built between 1743 and 1751, and Xuqian Hall, built between 1747 and 1772. Two large stone slabs on either side of Daigong Hall's rear hall are carved with scenes from the play Huansha Ji, 44 scenes with 240 figures between them. The listing, made in 2013, also names two memorial archways.

rows.name: Guangfeng Redwood Culture and Creative Industry Park
rows.name_zh: 广丰红木文化创意产业园
rows.summary: This is an industrial-tourism park for the redwood furniture and wood-carving trade in Yangkou town, run by a local redwood company and named a provincial industrial-tourism demonstration base in 2022. It is a modern commercial park rather than a historic site, aimed at visitors interested in redwood furniture and carving.

rows.name: Guifeng, Yiyang
rows.summary: Guifeng, in Yiyang County, is a cluster of 36 Danxia peaks of red rock rising above forest on the southern edge of the Xin River basin, with stone pillars, isolated crags, natural arches and caves. It is the Guifeng section of the China Danxia World Heritage property, inscribed in 2010, and its cliff inscriptions are a provincial-level protected site. The Ming-dynasty traveller Xu Xiake praised it as a rarity under heaven, and it became a national 5A scenic area in 2017.

rows.name: Hu Ancestral Hall, Guanxi
rows.summary: The Hu clan's ancestral hall in Guanxi, built in 1614 and restored in 1884, is a two-storey brick-and-timber complex of about 2,020 square metres with a gate, main hall, opera stage and side rooms. A plaque inside reads Qinghua Yimai, tracing the clan to Qinghua in Wuyuan, and a couplet plays on the form of the character Hu. Guanxi belonged to Jiangshan in Zhejiang until 1952, when it was transferred to Yushan, and repairs to the hall began in 2010.

rows.name: Huaiyu Mountains, Yushan
rows.summary: The Huaiyu hills in north-west Yushan County, next to Mount Sanqing, rise to Yungai Peak (1,538 m) and Yuya Peak (1,380 m) and have been a place of learning since the Southern Song, when Zhu Xi lectured here. In January 1935 the Red Army's 10th Army Corps was defeated in the Huaiyushan campaign in these hills, and Fang Zhimin, a leader of the Min-Zhe-Gan base area, was captured. The Qingpin Garden has a statue of Fang Zhimin and a stele carved with his essay 'Qingpin', and is a stop on a Fang Zhimin heritage route launched in 2025.

rows.name: Huangling Village
rows.summary: Huangling is a hillside village of Ming and Qing Huizhou-style houses; its residents were moved to a new village at the foot of the hill, and the old houses were restored for visitors, with cable cars linking the two. It is known for terraces of rapeseed flowers in March and April and for the autumn custom of drying chillies, pumpkins and flowers on large bamboo trays set out on roofs and window ledges. The UN World Tourism Organization named it one of its Best Tourism Villages in 2023, and it became a national 5A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Jiangwan, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Jiangwan is a lived-in Huizhou-style old town in the east of Wuyuan County, with ancestral halls, memorial archways, old houses, theatres and waterways. Its large Xiao-Jiang ancestral hall was rebuilt in 2003, and a folk-custom museum and local crafts such as She inkstone carving show the town's traditions. It has been a national 5A scenic area since 2013.

rows.name: Likeng Residences, Tuochuan
rows.summary: Likeng in Tuochuan township, not the Li-clan Likeng (李坑) at Qiukou, is a Yu-clan village founded in the late Yuan or early Ming dynasty, whose families produced Ming ministers of works and of personnel. More than fifty Ming and Qing buildings survive, and five of them, the Tianguan Shangqing Mansion, Sima Mansion, Yunxi Villa, Yousong Hall and Fushou Hall, are the nationally listed Likeng residences (2006). The village lies in a mountain valley and is a China Historic and Cultural Village.

rows.name: Likeng Village
rows.summary: Likeng, in Qiukou town, is a Li-clan village where lanes follow a winding stream crossed by dozens of stone, timber and brick bridges, with Ming and Qing houses on both banks. Four Ming houses and dozens from the Qing survive, and the village's families produced nine jinshi in the Song dynasty; named views such as the Twin Bridges and the Jiao Spring are marked along the stream. Do not confuse it with Likeng (理坑) in Tuochuan township, a different village listed separately.

rows.name: Lingshan Craftsman Town
rows.summary: A craft-themed tourist district on the road from Shangrao towards Lingshan, listed by local government among the cultural-industry projects of the former Shangrao County.
