Its second phase opened in 2020, and it was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2019. It is a modern development rather than a historic quarter, and suits a short stop on the way to Lingshan.

rows.name: Lingyan Cave, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Lingyan Cave is a group of 36 limestone caves in the mountains of northern Wuyuan, whose walls carry more than 2,000 inscriptions left by visitors over the centuries, among them the words 'Wu Hui Zhu Xi' linked to the philosopher Zhu Xi. The inscriptions have been a provincially protected site since 2006, and the surrounding hills became a national forest park in 1993 and a provincial scenic area in 1995.

rows.name: Min-Zhe-Gan Provincial Offices Site, Geyuan
rows.pinyin: Mǐn Zhè Gàn Shěngwěi Jīguān Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: In December 1932 the Chinese Soviet Republic's Gandongbei (north-east Jiangxi) province was renamed Min-Zhe-Gan, and its party committee and government were based in Fenglin village in Geyuan town until the offices left in November 1934. The nationally listed group covers the provincial party and government offices, the military district headquarters, the open ground known as the Red Square and the fifth branch of the Red Army school, part of a wider set of 34 sites in and around Geyuan. The Geyuan scenic area takes in Fenglin, with the low single-storey offices, an exhibition hall and the square, and Geyuan village about 3 km to the south-east, with the Red Army school site, Lenin Park, an old opera stage and a martyrs' memorial hall.

rows.name: Mount Damao, Dexing
rows.summary: Damaoshan is a mountain of the Huaiyu range in the south-east of Dexing, with a main peak of 1,392 m, and has been a national scenic area since 2012. The scenic area has three parts: the mountain itself, Wufengdong, known for rock formations, clear pools and streams and sites from the revolutionary period, and Shuangxi Lake, a reservoir south-west of the main peak. Bamboo groves and mountain streams line the valley, and the area suits a day trip from Dexing.

rows.name: Mount Gexian
rows.summary: Mount Gexian is a 1,096 m peak of the Wuyi range in Yanshan County, a Taoist mountain where legend holds that the Taoist Ge Xuan became an immortal. Its slopes hold the Yuxu temple complex (the Gexian Ancestral Temple, rebuilt many times and last repaired in 1928) and the Buddhist Ciji Temple, first built in 1593, and a cable car opened in 2017 takes about ten minutes to reach the upper area. At the foot, Gexian Village is a resort of hotels, homestays and evening shows built since 2016.

rows.name: Mount Lingshan
rows.summary: Lingshan is a granite mountain in the north of Guangxin District, with 72 peaks and 36 waterfalls, rock formations known as Sleeping Beauty, the Dragon's Spine and the Kissing Fish, and a main summit of 1,496 m. It is counted as the 33rd of Taoism's 72 blessed lands, with old temples such as Shiren Hall and Shicheng Temple nearby. It has been a national-level scenic area since 2009, and spring brings rhododendrons on the high slopes and terraced fields below.

rows.name: Nanyan Grotto
rows.summary: Nanyan Grotto is a Southern Song rock-cut shrine inside a half-moon-shaped hollow in a Danxia cliff, beside Nanyan Temple on the southern edge of Yiyang town. The cave mouth is about 60 m wide and 15 m high, and its walls hold 28 niches with 45 Buddhist figures, including a main Sakyamuni group with attendants, eighteen arhats in round-arched niches, a Water-Moon Guanyin and donor figures. The carving dates from the Jiading era (1208–1224), and the grotto has been a national heritage site since 2013.

rows.name: Pastoral Idyll (Sanqingshan)
rows.summary: Pastoral Idyll is a countryside-style holiday area beside the mountain road near the Jinsha entrance on the eastern side of Mount Sanqing. It is themed on Jiangnan (lower Yangtze) folk culture and is built around farmhouse-style guest rooms, restaurants, a hot spring and evening bonfire entertainment.

rows.name: Phoenix Lake, Dexing
rows.summary: Phoenix Lake is a reservoir in wooded hills on the southern side of Dexing city, laid out as a lakeside park with walking paths; the Dexing Museum stands in the scenic area. A stone-flagged old trail, the Phoenix Ancient Path, runs along the inner end of the lake and over Phoenix Ridge. It became a national 4A scenic area in 2024 and suits a short local outing rather than a long trip.

rows.name: Pipa Lake, Yugan
rows.summary: Pipa Lake is a lakeside wetland park on the south-western edge of Yugan town, laid out around a large urban lake with a peninsula plaza, walkways, a pavilion and a Ferris wheel. It was built as part of the county's three-lake tourism plan with Poyang Lake and Daming Lake, and a night-market arcade and a public reading room have since been set up there. It suits a short stroll by the water rather than a long visit.

rows.name: Poyang Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Poyang Lake National Wetland Park covers channels, islands and shoreline at Wujincha, on the Poyang County side of China's largest freshwater lake. The lake is a winter refuge for migratory waterbirds, including a large share of the world's Siberian cranes, and the park is one of the bird-watching sites Jiangxi promotes to visitors. It suits a day of birdwatching in the winter months.

rows.name: Qili Street, Yushan
rows.summary: Qili Street is an old street in the south-west of Yushan town, beside the Bingxi river, and the scenic area includes a street of inkstone carvers. Their Luowen inkstones are the town's best-known craft, and Yushan holds the title of home of Luowen inkstones. It suits a short walk to look at the inkstones and the old quarter.

rows.name: Qinghua Rainbow Bridge
rows.summary: A covered beam bridge across the Le'an River at Qinghua, about 140 m long on four stone piers with five openings, with a timber gallery along the deck and a shrine to Yu the Great on one pier. Records date it to the Song dynasty or to the Qianlong reign of the Qing, and it takes its name from a line by Li Bai; it was nationally listed in 2006. Floods in July 2020 destroyed part of the deck and gallery between the east approach and the second pier, and in March 2026 the provincial culture and tourism department reported that emergency repairs had been carried out.

rows.name: Raozhou Ancient Town, Poyang
rows.summary: Raozhou Ancient Town is a tourism and leisure quarter in the north of Poyang town, laid out in old-street style around a pond, with shops selling local snacks and sweets such as scallion biscuits (congsu bing) and filled sugar (guanxin tang). It was named one of China's first national tourism and leisure districts in 2022. The name recalls Raozhou, the prefecture whose seat was at Poyang for many centuries.

rows.name: Shangrao Concentration Camp Site
rows.summary: From March 1941 to mid-1942 the Nationalist government held captured New Fourth Army officers and other Communist-aligned prisoners at several sites around Shangrao, and the national listing covers prison sites at Maojialing, Zhoutian, Licun and Qifengyan. At Maojialing, in the south of the city, the original prison site stands beside a memorial cemetery, a monument and a memorial museum that opened in 1978 and has had a new building since 2005. In May 1942 a group of prisoners escaped from Maojialing, and the camp was moved to Fujian the following month.

rows.name: Shennongyuan (Shennong Palace Cave), Wannian
rows.summary: Shennongyuan is a scenic area in the hills of Dayuan town, Wannian County, built around the Shennong Palace karst cave, whose stalactites and underground river are the main sight. The county promotes it, together with the nearby Xianrendong archaeological site, as a base for learning about rice culture and geology. It suits visitors interested in caves, or anyone combining a visit with the prehistoric site.

rows.name: Shidu Wang Family Mansion
rows.summary: A large merchant's house in Shidu village, Songfeng township, built in 1769 by the local paper merchant Wang Zhixian and also called Zhixian Dawu. The brick, timber and stone building covers about 5,200 square metres with 103 rooms, 36 light wells, 3 wells and 4 ponds, and its joints are cut so tightly that no wedge was used anywhere. It was listed as a provincial site in 2018 and a national one in 2019, and is a good example of the big houses of north-east Jiangxi.

rows.name: Shuimo Shanghe, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Shuimo Shanghe is a tourism development around Shanghe village in Qiukou town, themed on Huizhou culture and built as a cultural-industry park that was complete by 2019. It combines the old village with newly built hotels, guesthouses and visitor facilities beside a lake, and Wuyuan's government counts it among the county's large resort-scale scenic areas.

rows.name: Sixi and Yancun Villages, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Sixi and Yancun are neighbouring villages in Sikou town, just over a kilometre apart, both listed as China Historic and Cultural Villages (Yancun in the fourth batch, Sixi in 2014). Yancun was founded in the Northern Song dynasty and keeps 53 well-preserved Ming and Qing houses, among them the Congting and Dujing halls, with a visitor centre, a village history museum, an old opera stage and a bridge. Sixi has its own merchants' houses, bridge and halls, protected at city or county level.

rows.name: Tongbo Mountain, Guangfeng
rows.summary: Tongbo Mountain is the highest part of Guangfeng, a forested ridge of the Wuyi range on the Fujian border whose main peak reaches 1,534.6 m; its northern slopes have been a national forest park since 2002. The visitor area is built around Jiuxian Lake, a large reservoir among the hills, with other areas such as Baihuayan in the surrounding hills. It suits a day of lake and forest scenery in the mountains south of Guangfeng.

rows.name: Wangkou Village
rows.summary: Wangkou is an old trading village of the Yu clan, founded in the early 12th century and surrounded by water on three sides, which lay on the land route from Huizhou through Wuyuan to Raozhou; its shops and merchants flourished in the Ming and Qing dynasties. A county-protected group of more than twenty old houses, halls, bridges and wharves survives, and the Pingdu weir across the river is provincially protected. The Yu clan ancestral hall (Renben Hall, built in 1736) is one of the national-level Wuyuan ancestral halls, and the village is a China Historic and Cultural Village (third batch).

rows.name: Wangxian Valley
rows.summary: Wangxian Valley is a rock-walled gorge in Wangxian township, in the north of Guangxin District, developed as a tourist destination with a cliff-and-immortals fantasy theme and known for its night views. Yanpu Old Street, its shopping and dining street, has been recognised as a national tourism and leisure district. Shangrao's tourism bureau lists it among the city's busiest sights, with more than 3 million visitors in 2025.

rows.name: Wengong Mountain, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Wengong Mountain is a wooded hill in the hills south-west of Wuyuan town, named after the Neo-Confucian philosopher Zhu Xi (posthumous title Wengong), whose family came from Wuyuan. It is where Zhu Xi came to honour his ancestors' tomb and planted 24 fir trees, which makes it one of Wuyuan's Zhu Xi sites alongside Xi Garden and Lingyan Cave. It suits visitors interested in Zhu Xi or a quiet walk in the forest.

rows.name: Wolong Valley, Dazhangshan
rows.summary: Wolong Valley is a wooded mountain gorge in Dazhangshan township, in the high ground of northern Wuyuan, where a stream drops through pools and small waterfalls. Paths follow the valley, with a viewing platform and a covered bridge along the route. Shangrao's 2025-26 tourism plans list a resort town at the valley as a project under construction.

rows.name: Wuyuan Ancestral Halls
rows.summary: Seven clan halls scattered across Wuyuan make up this national-level group, listed in 2006 and built between the early Ming dynasty (Yuqing Hall at Huangcun in Tuochuan township, 1403–1424) and 1864 (Chengyi Hall at Zhifeng). One of them, the Huang clan's Jingyi Hall of 1683, is also called the hundred-pillar hall. The pin marks Jingyi Hall in a different Huangcun, in Dazhangshan township; another of the seven, the Yu clan's Renben Hall of 1736, stands in Wangkou.

rows.name: Xi Garden, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Xi Garden is a Huizhou-style garden complex on the edge of Wuyuan town, on the site of Zhujiazhuang, the village where Zhu Xi's second- and third-generation ancestors lived. It is laid out around Zhufei Pond, with old Huizhou houses on the east side, the Zunjing Pavilion, a ring of ponds in the middle, an exhibition of She inkstones on the west and the Ziyang Academy on the north, with a shrine to three sages in the grounds. It is used for ceremonies for Zhu Xi's descendants, such as a 2019 visit by descendants from Korea.

rows.name: Xianrendong and Diaotonghuan Caves
rows.summary: Xianrendong is a limestone cave in Dayuan basin, and Diaotonghuan a rock shelter on a hillside about 800 m away; together they hold deposits from roughly 35,000 to 9,000 years ago. Excavations between 1962 and 1999 turned up pottery about 20,000 years old, among the earliest known, and rice phytoliths showing that rice was being cultivated some 12,000 years ago. The site has an exhibition hall and a display area with simulated scenes of Stone Age life, such as threshing grain, fishing and making pottery.

rows.name: Yantian Village, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Yantian is a village settled by Li-clan families in Fuchun town, in north-western Wuyuan, strung along the old Huizhou–Raozhou post road, with a Ming-dynasty patrol post among its hamlets. At the village's water-mouth stand ancient camphor trees, beside old stone bridges, a pavilion and a spring, and a camphor folk park built in 2002 with workshops for paper umbrellas, tofu, oil pressing and mushroom growing. Several of its bridges and old houses are protected at county level.

rows.name: Yinju Stone Tribe, Dexing
rows.summary: Yinju Stone Tribe is a hill hamlet in Dexing whose 18 surviving houses were built in the 1960s and 70s from river pebbles and flat stones, bonded with a clay-and-lime mortar mixed with glutinous rice. The local government restored fallen houses and added an old-style timber complex around them with folk-custom displays, shops, a covered bridge and an opera stage, so the site is part vernacular village and part new tourist development. It suits visitors interested in rural building traditions.

rows.name: Yitian Cultural Tourism City, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Yitian Cultural Tourism City is a purpose-built visitor complex on a river bend south of Wuyuan town, run by the Yitian cultural-tourism company, whose core project is Mengli Laojia ('Old Home in Dreams'), a large live outdoor show with a landscape backdrop. The show presents the struggles of Huizhou merchants, a love story, success in the imperial examinations and a life of retirement, and the complex is also marketed as the Mengli Laojia performing-arts tourist resort. It is a modern development, not a historic site.

rows.name: Yongfu Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: The Yongfu Temple Pagoda is a nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda, 49 m high, built in 1024 in the Northern Song dynasty in imitation of a timber tower, with arched doorways on all eight sides and bracket sets under the eaves. It stands in Poyang town with a public culture plaza at its foot, and has been a national heritage site since 2013.

rows.name: Yu Ancestral Hall, Xinyuan
rows.summary: The Yu clan's ancestral hall, called Yiqing Hall, stands in Xinyuan village in Sikou town and was first built in 1565, in the Jiajing reign of the Ming dynasty. It is a national-level site listed in 2013 and suits a short stop when touring Wuyuan's villages.

rows.name: Yuantou Village, Wuyuan
rows.summary: Yuantou is a small village in a mountain valley in Fuchun town, a settlement of the Wu clan founded in the early Ming dynasty, with a stream, small bridges, a traditional water-mouth grove and old Huizhou-style houses. Old red-bean yew trees grow nearby and rapeseed fields colour the valley in spring. It is quieter and smaller than Wuyuan's best-known villages.

rows.name: Yuanyang Lake (Mandarin Duck Lake), Wuyuan
rows.summary: Yuanyang Lake is a reservoir among wooded hills in Fuchun town, both a nature reserve and a tourist scenic area, promoted as a winter roosting ground for wild mandarin ducks, which arrive in autumn and leave in spring. It suits a quiet visit in the cooler months, when the birds are present.

rows.name: Yulian Waterfalls (Sanqingshan)
rows.summary: A separate 4A scenic area in the Sanqingshan area, laid out as a walk up a forested valley below the mountain's north-eastern slopes, past a series of named waterfalls, nine in all. It offers streams, pools and woodland rather than the granite summit scenery of the main mountain, and suits a short visit alongside it.

rows.name: Yungu Tianyuan Eco-Agriculture Town
rows.name_zh: 云谷田园生态农业小镇
rows.summary: A farm-themed leisure park on the southern side of Shangrao, in Guangxin District, built around smart farming: a vertical vegetable factory and a fruit-and-vegetable base were shown to provincial officials in June 2024, and an aerospace science exhibition opened in 2023. Its first phase opened in 2020, and it is one of four national 4A scenic areas in Guangxin District. It suits families and anyone curious about modern farming rather than traditional villages.

rows.name: Yushan Examination Hall (Kaopeng)
rows.summary: Yushan Kaopeng is a Qing-dynasty imperial examination hall of four blue-brick buildings with 100 individual candidate cells in two rows either side of a stone-paved central passage, on more than 2,000 m². It was first built in 1792, rebuilt in 1838 and repaired in 1867, and is described as one of very few such compounds still standing south of the Yangtze. It became a national heritage site in 2019 and draws visitors interested in the imperial examination system.

rows.name: Zha Ancestral Hall, Fengshan
rows.summary: The Zha clan's ancestral hall in Fengshan village was built in 1664 and named Xiaoyi Hall by the prefect of Huizhou; it was damaged in 1854, rebuilt in 1864 and enlarged in 1898. It covers about 2,460 square metres, with a forecourt, a garden, a large pond, a main hall and a rear hall. It was listed as a national site in 2013.

rows.name: Zhongyi Culture Park (Zhongchen Temple), Kangshan
rows.summary: The park is built around Zhongchen Temple, which stands beside Poyang Lake at Kangshan and honours 36 Ming generals, among them Han Cheng and Ding Pulang, killed in the 1363 Battle of Lake Poyang, where Zhu Yuanzhang defeated Chen Youliang. The temple has three halls in a row, the Dingjiang King hall, a Guanyin hall and the main hall of the loyal officers; the present buildings date from the Qing dynasty and have been restored since 1995. Around them the park has added old-style buildings, gardens, a performance hall and a shopping street, and it was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2018.

rows.name: Zhu Ancestral Hall, Longxi
rows.summary: Longxi is a village near the Zhejiang border whose residents are mostly of the Zhu clan and speak the Jiangshan dialect. Its Zhu Ancestral Hall, first built in the Chenghua era of the Ming dynasty, has three halls in sequence with carved and painted decoration, and the village also has the three-tiered Wenchang Pavilion, rebuilt in 1866 and 12.3 m high. The hall's building craft is on Jiangxi's provincial intangible heritage list (2008).

rows.name: China Cave Capital, Dongcun
rows.summary: Dongcun township, in the north-east of Fenyi county, promotes itself as China's cave capital, and the 4A scenic area opens some of its karst caves to visitors. Xinyu's government lists it among the city's scenic sights alongside Fairy Lake.

rows.name: Fairy Lake, Xinyu
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Fairy Lake is the Jiangkou reservoir on the Yuan river, a large artificial lake of about 50 km² south-west of Xinyu, dotted with nearly a hundred wooded islands. It was renamed in 1994 after a legend, recorded in the Jin-dynasty Soushen ji, of feathered fairy maidens who came down to earth, and is now run as a national tourist resort built around that legend and the Qixi (Chinese Valentine's Day) festival. Visitors take boats among the islands, visit the three islands rebuilt in 2024 with staged shows, and can drive the 34 km lakeside road.

rows.name: Hongyang Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave 983 m long with stalactites and stalagmites under coloured lighting, kept at a steady temperature of about 20°C that makes it a summer retreat. Outside the entrance there are a sunken stage, a non-powered play area, a small train and a slide. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in February 2026, and Xinyu's tourism bureau groups it with Fairy Lake and Jieqiao village.

rows.name: Jieqiao Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village just south of Fenyi town with Ming and Qing family halls, promoted as the home village of the Ming grand secretary Yan Song (1480–1567). It has been developed for visitors, with evening shows such as role-play dramas, opera and molten-iron sparks, and a second phase was under construction in 2024. Xinyu's tourism bureau groups it with Hongyang Cave and Fairy Lake.

rows.name: Jinshishan Mine Park
rows.summary: Jinshishan is a century-old mine in Ouli town, restored and turned into a leisure park covering about 1,278 mu (some 85 hectares), with more than 200 mu of new woodland and 360 mu of grass over the old workings. Its attractions include a central cascade, a mine-tunnel exploration hall, a high combined tower and a cliff-top viewing area, with a resort section in old-town style. Jiangxi Daily reported large crowds there in May 2026, and the provincial list names it the Xinyu Jinshishan resort.

rows.name: Luofang Conference and Xingguo Investigation Sites
rows.name_zh: 罗坊会议和兴国调查会旧址
rows.pinyin: Luófāng Huìyì Hé Xīngguó Diàochá Huì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Four preserved houses around Luofang town record the Red First Front Army's stay in October and early November 1930. In Chenjianao village, a brick-and-timber house of the early Republic was the venue of a joint meeting of the army's general front committee and the Jiangxi provincial action committee, known as the Luofang Conference, and Mao Zedong lodged in it; the other listed houses, in nearby villages, are the site of his interviews with eight Xingguo soldiers, the army's headquarters where Zhu De lodged, and the Jiangxi provincial soviet government office. A memorial hall to the conference stands in Luofang town.

rows.name: Shuanglin Ramie Cloth Culture Tourism Area
rows.summary: A culture-tourism area at Shuanglin town, in the heartland of Fenyi's ramie-cloth industry; Fenyi is known as the home of xiabu, 'summer cloth' woven by hand from ramie fibre. The grounds combine exhibition space on weaving and Xiabu embroidery, which is a national intangible heritage item, with an experience village for hands-on workshops. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2021, and the county was upgrading its experience village in 2024.

rows.name: Shuixi Site of the Third Army Corps Command Post
rows.name_zh: 水西红三军团指挥部旧址
rows.pinyin: Shuǐxī Hóng Sān Jūntuán Zhǐhuībù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A late-Qing ancestral hall of the Liao clan in Shapo village, Shuixi town: a south-facing brick-and-timber building of three halls and two courtyards with 561 m² of floor space. At the end of September 1930, after the attack on Changsha, the Red First Front Army moved back into Jiangxi, and while its front committee met at Luofang the Third Army Corps under Peng Dehuai and Teng Daiyuan took up defensive positions, with its command post here. It was listed as a provincial site in 2018 and as a national one in 2019, in the eighth batch.

rows.name: Autumn Harvest Uprising Sites, Tonggu
rows.summary: A group of sites in Yongning, the county town of Tonggu, centred on the Xiao ancestral hall, a two-block timber-and-earth building of the 1870s on Dingjiang East Road. In August 1927 a Liuyang peasant force took up quarters there, and on 10 September Mao Zedong, then secretary of the front committee, announced its reorganisation as the 3rd Regiment of the First Division of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army and briefed officers on the plan for the Autumn Harvest Uprising. A memorial hall beside it, completed in 1977, covers the uprising.

rows.name: Baifengling Horticultural Park, Gao'an
rows.summary: A horticulture-themed scenic area in the countryside of Gao'an. It was rated national 4A in 2020 and was among 20 scenic areas in Yichun reported as drawing the most visitors over the 2023 National Day holiday. It suits a short rural outing from Gao'an.

rows.name: Chandu Culture Expo Park, Yichun
rows.summary: A cultural park on Chan (Zen) Buddhism on the eastern side of Yichun city, in a prefecture that promotes itself as a holy land of Chan. It was rated national 4A in 2015 and hosts seasonal events such as a moon-festival market, a Chinese-style garden fair, a food market and music nights. It suits an easy visit from the city centre.

rows.name: Chinese Traditional Culture Park, Jing'an
rows.summary: An antique-style cultural park of more than 2,000 mu (about 133 ha) in Baofeng town, built as a traditional-culture study base, where a city-gate opening ceremony and a Confucius ceremony were held in 2018. It was rated national 4A in 2019.

rows.name: Conglin Liquor Expo Park, Shanggao
rows.summary: A liquor-culture visitor park (the name means 'liquor expo park') at Wugu village on the northern edge of Shanggao town. It was rated national 4A in 2017. It suits a short stop for visitors interested in Chinese liquor culture.

rows.name: Dongshan, Yifeng
rows.summary: A mountain village in Tong'an township where the Tang monk Liangjie founded Puli Chan Temple, regarded as the ancestral temple of the Caodong school of Chan (Zen) Buddhism. Beside the temple, Fengqu Bridge, a stone arch bridge dated 1098, is the third Northern Song stone arch bridge with a dated inscription found in Jiangxi, after Guanyin Bridge on Lushan and Mingshui Bridge on Gezao Mountain. The village is a provincial rural tourism point promoted as 'Zen-realm Dongshan', and it hosted a rural Zen culture festival in 2018.

rows.name: Former Hunan-Hubei-Jiangxi Revolutionary Base, Xianyuan
rows.name_zh: 湘鄂赣革命根据地旧址
rows.pinyin: Xiāng È Gàn Gémìng Gēnjùdì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: From April 1932 to January 1934 the Hunan-Hubei-Jiangxi provincial Party committee and provincial soviet government were based at Xiaoyuan, now Xianyuan village. The listed buildings are late-Qing houses and ancestral halls that housed the Party committee, the soviet government, the military district and the newspaper Red Flag, among other offices. The village has added exhibition halls on the base's history, on taxation in the period and on the workers' movement.

rows.name: Gezao Mountain, Zhangshu
rows.summary: A Daoist mountain south of Zhangshu, regarded as the ancestral mountain of the Lingbao school of Daoism and counted as the 36th of Daoism's blessed lands. Relics include the Chongzhen Palace, an immortals' bridge, a pool for releasing animals and an alchemy well, and the Song-dynasty Mingshui Bridge, built in 1111 across a gorge. That bridge is a single stone arch 7.3 m long, with a 34-character dedication carved on its sides, and is a national heritage unit.

rows.name: Henghui Art Agriculture Park, Wanzai
rows.summary: A farm-tourism park in the countryside near Sanxing town, run under the name 'art agriculture' (yishu nongye). It was the first scenic area in Wanzai county to be rated national 4A, in 2017. It suits a short rural outing from Wanzai town.

rows.name: Hongzhou Kiln, Fengcheng
rows.summary: Hongzhou celadon was fired around Fengcheng from the late Eastern Han onwards, and the kiln is counted among the six famous celadon kilns of the Tang; 44 kiln sites in 19 villages lie in six townships on both banks of the Gan River. At Wanniling an old dragon kiln survives and is still fired, and a workshop and display hall there make and explain Hongzhou celadon to visitors, including study groups. Wanniling has been a provincial industrial-heritage tourism base since 2022.

rows.name: Hualin Papermaking Workshop Site, Gao'an
rows.summary: Remains of bamboo-paper workshops in the hills of the Hualin Mountain scenic area near Zhouling village, where archaeologists found the foundations of sixteen water-driven stamping mills along the streams and excavated workshops from the Southern Song to the Ming. The remains allow the whole bamboo-paper process described in Song Yingxing's Ming-dynasty Tiangong Kaiwu to be traced.

rows.name: Jimei Stone Archway, Fengxin
rows.summary: A four-sided stone memorial archway, 12.2 m high and 4.15 m wide, carved to imitate timber construction, standing on the north bank of the Liao River. It was built between 1599 and 1601 to honour the Ming official Hu Shiyuan and his Song-dynasty forebears, and the tablets over its gateways carry the title Jimei and the word for an imperial decree. It joined the national list in 2019.

rows.name: Jingxian Jia Ancestral Hall, Gao'an
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty clan ancestral hall in the middle of Jiajia village, with four halls in sequence on a site of about 1,870 m²: the Zhoujin Hall, a front pavilion for bowing, a rear shrine hall and a Guanyin hall. Chinese sources describe the surrounding village as the oldest and largest surviving traditional village in Gao'an, and a fairly complete one. The hall joined the national list in 2013.

rows.name: Lizhou'ao Eastern Zhou Tomb Museum, Jing'an
rows.summary: A museum at the site of a large Eastern Zhou tomb in Shuikou township, excavated in 2007 after looters broke into it, where a mound about 12 m high covered a pit with 47 coffins, a main burial and 46 accompanying ones. The excavation was named one of China's ten major archaeological discoveries of 2007 and produced more than a thousand objects, among them over 300 textile pieces. The museum, opened in 2010, shows finds from the tomb.

rows.name: Love Flower Town, Fengcheng
rows.summary: A flower-themed park of about 4.7 km² at Tancheng village in Meilin town, built from 2018 on former barren hills around a flower and nursery-stock business. Its sights include a bird-and-flower garden, a lake called Love Sea, a rose garden, a southern plant garden, a flower-castle hotel and a water-screen film show, and a small railway runs through the flower beds. It is promoted as a romantic outing for couples.

rows.name: Mazu Pagoda Pavilion, Baofeng Temple
rows.summary: A hexagonal granite pavilion of 1085 inside Baofeng Temple, covering the tomb pagoda of the Tang Chan master Mazu Daoyi, whose pagoda was first built in 791. The square two-storey marble pagoda was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution and rebuilt to its old form in 1993, while the pavilion survived. The temple took the name Baofeng when the pagoda was rebuilt in 850.

rows.name: Mengshan Silver Mine Site
rows.summary: Remains of a silver-mining district on Mount Meng that worked from the Southern Song to the Ming, about 160 years in all, around the Taizi cliff. The site covers main mine adits, open-cast trenches, a smelting area, a stone-slab road with old bridges, mine-ban inscriptions and the site of the Zhengde Academy. It was listed nationally in 2013, and a provincial archaeological park project was approved there in December 2025.

rows.name: Mingyue Mountain
rows.summary: A 136 km² mountain on the border of Yichun's Yuanzhou district and An'fu county, named for its half-moon outline, with its main peak, Taiping, at 1,735.6 m. Sights include the Yungu waterfall, the Qingyun plank walkway, old stone pagodas on the slopes and a summit lake with small-train camps. It has been a national 5A scenic area since 2015, and the hot-spring town of Wentang lies at its foot.

rows.name: Mingyue Qianguqing Theme Park, Yichun
rows.summary: A commercial theme park in Wentang town, developed with the Songcheng Performance Group and opened on 28 December 2018. Its main attraction is a staged song-and-dance show, Mingyue Qianguqing, drawing on Jiangxi history and folk customs, with scenes on porcelain, the moon goddess Chang'e and the legend of Empress Mingyue. It was rated national 4A in 2019 and is usually combined with Mingyue Mountain and Wentang's hot springs.

rows.name: Qixingling Ski Resort, Tonggu
rows.summary: A mountain resort in Paibu town with a ski area whose slopes the county uses for mass-participation ski races. A new slope was added in 2023, and the resort is on the provincial tourism department's 2025 list of summer cool-weather routes, together with Tangli and Tianzhufeng. It was rated national 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Qiyin Valley
rows.summary: A wooded valley on the eastern side of Mingyue Mountain, run as a separate scenic area from the main mountain gate near Wentang and rated national 4A in 2022. Qiyin Temple on Mount Yang, one of Jiangxi's old Chan monasteries, stands nearby.

rows.name: Sanzhualun Forest Park, Jing'an
rows.summary: A forested valley area in northern Jing'an county, run as a national forest park and best known for river rafting and a small forest train. The park is divided into the Kuang Zhong garden, Luojiaping, Baofeng and Panlong Lake zones, and the white cliffs of Baiya Mountain are among its sights. It was rated national 4A in 2007.

rows.name: Shanggao Battle Sites
rows.summary: Four wartime sites of the 1941 Battle of Shanggao, mostly old ancestral halls and village houses, were opened with displays in September 2020: the general headquarters of the Chinese 19th Army Group, its women's battlefield service corps, a wartime prison and the command post of the 58th Division. In March 1941 Japanese forces advanced on Shanggao and were fought by Chinese units for about 25 days; Chinese sources record some 15,000 Japanese casualties. A cemetery on the eastern edge of Shanggao town holds more than 9,000 Chinese soldiers.

rows.name: Tianzhufeng, Tonggu
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area on the shore of Jiulong Lake in Daduan town, in the county with the highest forest cover in Jiangxi. Boat trips on the lake, a glass bridge and night tours are among its newer attractions. It was rated national 4A in 2019 and is on the provincial tourism department's 2025 list of summer cool-weather routes.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhu Shi, Gao'an
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhu Shi (1665-1736), a Gao'an man who served three Qing emperors, as governor of Zhejiang and later as Minister of Personnel and grand secretary. The burial ground, about 160 m long and 60 m wide on a hillside, has a symmetrical line of spirit-way stele, markers, a stone archway, stone deer, horses and figures, a worship platform and the burial mound. Its size and carving are unusual among Qing officials' tombs.

rows.name: Wanzai Ancient Town
rows.summary: A restored historic quarter in the centre of Wanzai (the Tianxia old-town district) with Ming and Qing buildings, including 26 ancestral halls, old houses and granaries, restored over about five years. It was rated national 4A in 2019 and listed in 2022 among China's selected projects combining intangible heritage with tourism, and local operas such as lantern opera and Nuo opera are staged here weekly. Wanzai is a fireworks town, and the old quarter holds firework displays at festivals.

rows.name: Yuanzhou Qiaolou (Drum Tower)
rows.summary: A gate tower built in 944 under the Southern Tang as part of the Yuanzhou prefectural offices, now known as the Yichun Drum Tower. In 1219 it was fitted with water clocks, a gnomon and a south-pointing needle and served as a local observatory; experts in 1994 judged it the oldest surviving local time observatory site in China. A double-eaved timber hall about 23 m wide and 13 m high stands on a platform 5.5 m high.

rows.name: Zhuweicheng Site, Zhangshu
rows.summary: A settlement enclosure on the north slope of Dagu Hill, named for the earth walls that encircle it and measuring about 410 by 360 m. The south-west rampart is recorded at 17 m high, and excavations in 1974 and 1977 found a late Neolithic layer under an Eastern Zhou one. The national listing now also covers the Guozishan tombs, about 300 m to the west, whose large Eastern Zhou tomb was named one of China's six major new archaeological discoveries of 2021; a provincial archaeological park project approved in 2023 has built a visitor service centre here.

rows.name: Baihe Lake Xixili, Guixi
rows.summary: A family leisure park on the shore of Baihe Lake, a reservoir in north-western Guixi; its water park opened on 30 April 2023. It has water-play rides, boat trips on the lake, an artificial sand beach, a children's play area and off-road rides, with more than 30 hands-on attractions in all. It suits families with children in summer.

rows.name: China Schistosomiasis Control Red Flag Exhibition Area, Yujiang
rows.summary: A memorial area in Yujiang about the campaign against schistosomiasis, a snail-borne parasitic disease. Yujiang county was declared to have eliminated the disease in 1958, the first in China, and the area presents that history in three parts: the China Schistosomiasis Control Memorial Hall, built in 1978 with halls on the disease and the campaign; Tongle Park opposite it, where a 1978 stele carries Mao Zedong's poem "Farewell to the God of Plague"; and the village of Lantian Songjia, with its campaign sites and a village history museum.

rows.name: Lingxi Lake Eco-tourism Area, Yujiang
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area around Lingxi Town in Yangxi township, Yujiang district, rated a 4A scenic area in early 2024. The town is used for school study trips and art-sketching groups and stages holiday events such as comic-themed exhibitions.

rows.name: Mount Longhu
rows.summary: Red sandstone peaks, cliffs and caves rise above the Luxi River south of Yingtan, in a landscape that is one of the six parts of the China Danxia World Heritage Site (2010) and an old centre of Daoism. The main visit is a bamboo-raft ride on the river beneath the cliffs of Xianshuiyan, where ancient cliff coffins can be seen, with walks to viewpoints and the Immortal City area. The Tianshi Mansion and Shangqing Palace are in Shangqing town, about 9 km to the south-east.

rows.name: Qingmaojing Forest Scenic Area, Guixi
rows.summary: A forest scenic area in the Shuangzhen forest farm in the mountains of southern Guixi, with bamboo groves, a sea of cloud seen from the main peak after rain, and the Sandie waterfall, which falls in three tiers for a total drop of more than 100 metres. It is promoted as a cool, clean-air retreat in summer.

rows.name: Tianshi Mansion and Shangqing Palace
rows.name_zh: 嗣汉天师府与大上清宫
rows.summary: The Tianshi Mansion in Shangqing town was the home and ritual seat of the Celestial Masters, the hereditary heads of the Zhengyi school of Daoism, and covers 42,000 square metres. Most of what stands is Qing-dynasty or modern rebuilding, with older parts such as the Celestial Masters' residence hall, a Yuan stele with text by Zhao Mengfu and a bronze bell cast in 1351. About 1.2 km east are the ruins of Daishangqing Palace, a vast Daoist temple that burned in 1930 and is now an excavated site with an exhibition hall.

rows.name: Xianshuiyan Cliff Tombs
rows.summary: The cliffs above the Luxi River hold more than seventy natural caves, some 30 to 50 metres above the water, in which people of the ancient Yue culture placed coffins and grave goods about 2,600 years ago, in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods. Excavations in 1978–79 cleared 18 tombs with 37 coffins and more than 220 objects, among them a flat drum, a zither and parts of a primitive loom, all rare finds. Visitors see the cave mouths from the river and from viewpoints along the cliff.

rows.name: Luling Lake Wellness Lodge, Pingxiang
rows.summary: A lakeside country-estate and eco-park in Xiangdong District, Pingxiang, in western Jiangxi, run by a local farm-development company. It offers accommodation and grounds for a short stay. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Xinguang Mountain Resort, Wuning
rows.summary: A holiday resort in Wuning County, in the hills of north-western Jiangxi, run by a local development company. It is a place to stay in a forested setting rather than a sight in itself. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Dayuzhang Forest Park
rows.summary: Dayuzhang Forest Park is a provincial forest park of wetland, woodland and canals on the south bank of the Yellow River in Qiaozhuang town, Boxing County, centred on the headworks of the Dayuzhang Yellow River irrigation scheme. The county says it has over 100 plant species and some 40 bird species, and its sights include the diversion sluice and a hydraulic-engineering museum, the Huazhao flower garden, a crabapple orchard, wetland, a reservoir with a greenway and a camping base. It suits a quiet day of cycling, fishing and watching the river.

rows.name: Du Shoutian Residence
rows.summary: This is the former home of Du Shoutian, a Qing scholar-official who served as an imperial tutor, in Binbei, north of Binzhou city. The courtyard compound dates from the Wanli era of the Ming and once had hundreds of rooms in some 28 courtyards, but only the embroidery tower, a reception hall and parts of the main and side ranges survive, in the plain northern-Shandong style of the Ming and Qing. Plaques over the gate and hall record the family's official ranks, and the house is also a provincial integrity-education base.

rows.name: Mada Lake
rows.summary: Mada Lake is a freshwater lake and reed wetland south of Boxing county town, about 7 km from east to west and up to 3.5 km wide, which became a national wetland park in 2013. Reeds, cattails and lotus cover much of the shallow water, boats run through channels in the reeds, and the lake is known locally for lotus root, salted duck eggs and fish dishes. It suits a quiet half-day of wetland scenery and local food, with summer lotus the main draw.

rows.name: Puhu Scenic Area, Binzhou
rows.summary: Puhu is a large lake park on the southern edge of Binzhou, between the Yellow River's main and secondary embankments, planned at about 543 hectares of which 180 had been developed by 2017. Its landmark is the Yellow River Tower, a modern tower on the lake's east shore that opened in 2021, and the park also has gardens, boats, a martyrs' cemetery and fishing areas. It is a local leisure park for walking and boating rather than a heritage site.

rows.name: Sun Wu Ancient City
rows.summary: Sun Wu Ancient City is the main tourist zone of Huimin County town, which claims the strategist Sun Wu, author of The Art of War, as a native son. It groups the Wuding Prefectural Yamen, which also holds the former Bohai revolutionary base-area offices, the Wusheng Garden park with weapons and folk museums, the Art of War City theme complex and a park along the moat, all set against a surviving stretch of Song-period city wall. Much of the zone is modern construction, so it suits visitors interested in Sun Tzu and Chinese military culture more than architecture.

rows.name: Weiji Ancient Town and Wei's Manor
rows.summary: Weiji Ancient Town is a tourist zone in Weiji town, one of Huimin County's Yellow River towns, that links two groups of Ming-Qing-style buildings, Wei's Manor and the Weiji old village, along a new old-style street. Wei's Manor, a national heritage unit, is a fortified landowner's compound completed in 1893: a walled rectangle of about 84 by 46 m with round corner turrets and some 48 rooms in six courtyards. The old village is a modern imitation of Ming-Qing houses with more than 200 snack shops, workshops and small attractions, and folk performances in the evenings.

rows.name: Wudi Ancient City
rows.summary: Wudi Ancient City is a walled old town of about 11.5 hectares in the centre of Wudi County, partly original and partly rebuilt in old style since 2010, with a moat and a lotus bay. The county says it keeps the Tang-period Dajue Temple and Haifeng Pagoda, a stretch of Song city wall, the Ming county-yamen hall and the Qing residence of the epigraphy scholar Wu Shifen, while its museum, intangible-heritage hall, shops and evening events are newer additions. It suits an easy half-day of strolling and boat rides on the moat.

rows.name: Xincheng Tianyuan Eco-tourism Area
rows.summary: Xincheng Tianyuan is a large commercial farm-leisure park in Madian town, Huimin County, planned at about 15,000 mu and built round greenhouses and orchards. It has Dutch-style smart greenhouses, a flower house, an animal-feeding area, an EU-standard organic orchard, a 'Forest Tribe' zone opened in 2021 and the Sheng Ge Di Bay hot-spring water park, and it offers camping and bonfire evenings. It is a family destination rather than a heritage or nature sight.

rows.name: Zhangbafo Buddha at Xingguo Temple
rows.summary: Zhangbafo is a standing stone Buddha of the Northern Dynasties, 7.1 m high including its pedestal, which stands in Xingguo Temple in Zhangbafo village, Hubin town; the county dates the carving to the first year of the Tianping era (534). The figure wears a robe over both shoulders and stands on a lotus pedestal carved with guardian figures, an incense burner, garudas and groups of donors, 26 figures in all, and the county calls it a large, well-preserved stone statue carved in the round for the north Shandong plain. The temple around it was rebuilt from 1998 with halls, a chanting hall, a dining hall and a visitor centre.

rows.name: Zhanhua Winter Jujube Eco-tourism Area
rows.summary: This is a jujube orchard park of about 500 mu in Xiawa town, the original home of the Zhanhua winter jujube, a crisp, apple-sized variety, about 20 km from Zhanhua town. It is laid out in three zones, including a lake area, with a covered bridge, a landscaped hill, a waterfall, a jujube-culture corridor, a research institute, a picking garden and reed wetland along the Qinkou River. The trees flower in early summer and carry fruit in autumn, which is the main season for a visit.

rows.name: Debai Acrobatics and Cricket Valley, Ningjin
rows.summary: This is a leisure complex of about 1,000 mu (roughly 67 ha) south of Ningjin town, developed by the Debai group and themed on the county's acrobatics and cricket-keeping traditions. It includes the Dezhou Wild Animal Kingdom (a zoo with more than 1,500 animals and a circus theatre), a courtyard-style family-culture park, a jade museum, an acrobatics school with a theatre and museum, an artificial ski slope and a hot-spring garden hotel. It suits a family day out; the animal and acrobatics shows are staged performances.

rows.name: Debai Hot Spring Resort, Xiajin
rows.summary: Debai is a hot-spring hotel complex in Suliuzhuang town, Xiajin County, in the area of the Yellow River Old Course Forest Park. It has indoor and outdoor hot-spring pools, an indoor swimming pool and spa facilities, and Xiajin's government lists it among the county's main leisure attractions. It suits a relaxing half-day or overnight stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Dongzi Garden
rows.summary: Dongzi Garden is a riverside memorial park in Dezhou commemorating the Han-dynasty Confucian scholar Dong Zhongshu. Its centrepiece is the 24.8 m Dongzi Reading Terrace, with a hall and shrine and a Confucian-culture exhibition hall beneath it, a 6 m bronze statue in front, and a lake with bridges, pavilions and a stone boat. Dezhou's tourism bureau dates the original terrace to the Sui dynasty and says it was destroyed in war in the Republican period, so what stands now is a modern rebuilding.

rows.name: Haidao Jinshan Temple, Qingyun
rows.summary: Haidao Jinshan Temple is a large Buddhist temple complex on the northern edge of Qingyun, rebuilt from 2004 after an older temple that Dezhou's tourism bureau dates to the Sui dynasty was destroyed in the Ming. The scenic area has three zones, worship halls, a commercial area and landscaped grounds, and the bureau describes it as the largest group of antique-style buildings in the surrounding area. It suits a short stop for those interested in modern temple building in northern Shandong.

rows.name: Quancheng Ole Fortress Dream World
rows.summary: Dream World is a theme park in Qihe County with zones styled on European and Western themes, such as a Dutch family town, a western town and a castle, dozens of rides including several roller coasters, a horse show, an international circus and fireworks. It is aimed at families and thrill-seekers. The same resort also has an ocean-and-polar aquarium, a water park and an animal park.

rows.name: Quancheng Ole Fortress Ocean and Polar World
rows.name_zh: 泉城欧乐堡海洋极地世界
rows.summary: This is a large indoor aquarium in Qihe County, completed in 2011, with more than ten halls including a tropical rainforest, an undersea tunnel, shark and turtle halls, a polar animal hall, a seal island and a 5D cinema. It has two show theatres, a mermaid underwater performance and a marine-animal show, both staged for audiences. It suits families, and it belongs to the same Ole Fortress resort as the Dream World theme park, less than 1 km to the north.

rows.name: Thousand-Year Jujube Forest, Leling
rows.summary: This rural tourist area in Zhuji town, Leling, is built around old jujube (Chinese date) orchards, with more than a thousand trees that the local government says are over 1,000 years old, a garden of nearly 600 jujube varieties and a 'mother-and-child' tree of more than 700 years. Inside it stands the Jilu Border Region Memorial Park, opened in 2014, with a museum on the Jilu Border Region, a wartime anti-Japanese base area across northern Shandong and neighbouring parts of Hebei, plus a memorial plaza, a martyrs' stele forest and a tunnel exhibit. It suits a half-day in early autumn, when the fruit ripens.

rows.name: Tomb of the Sultan of Sulu
rows.summary: In 1417 the Eastern King of Sulu, from an old Southeast Asian kingdom in what is now the Philippines, led a delegation of about 340 people to the Ming court and died at Dezhou on the way home, where he was buried; his wife and two sons were later laid beside him. The tomb, in Beiying village on the northern edge of Dezhou, is described by the Decheng district government as the only intact tomb of a foreign king in China with descendants still guarding it; they are now in the twenty-second generation. A museum beside it, a national second-class museum since 2024, presents the history.

rows.name: Guangrao Guandi Temple Main Hall
rows.summary: This Southern Song timber hall, first built in 1128 as the main hall of a Guan Yu temple, is described by the city culture bureau as the only surviving Song-period timber hall in Shandong; it now serves as the main hall of the Sun Wu Shrine. Its single-eaved gable-and-hip roof and bracket sets, repaired in the Ming and Qing, are a rare example of Song-period carpentry, and the surrounding shrine is a modern Song-style compound with exhibitions on Sun Wu, inscribed steles and a long porcelain-carved copy of The Art of War. It stands beside the Dongying History Museum in Guangrao town and has been a national protected monument since 1996.

rows.name: Gudao Locust Forest, Hekou
rows.summary: Gudao Locust Forest is a large locust-tree plantation on the Yellow River delta, in Gudao town, Hekou district, made into a 4A scenic area with an entrance gate, a visitor centre, boardwalks, a festival square and a waterside food street. The draws are woodland walks and seasonal events such as the locust-blossom festival, a windmill festival and photography exhibitions that the area has hosted. Official pages also list local geothermal water among its resources, which explains the 'hot spring' in its official name.

rows.name: Hongtan Wetland
rows.summary: Hongtan Wetland is a coastal tourist area in Kenli district, on the Bohai shore behind a seawall at the edge of broad tidal mudflats. Its reed beds and seepweed flats, which turn red in autumn, are a stopover for migratory birds, and visitors can walk the seawall or go out onto the mudflats at low tide to gather shellfish. It suits families wanting an informal day at the coast.

rows.name: Lancuihu Resort, Dongying
rows.summary: Lancuihu is a lakeside leisure area on the south-west edge of Dongying city, rated 4A in 2015, whose lawns and lakeshore are used for camping and a lawn music season. The city culture and tourism bureau describes plans for hot-spring hotels, a golf course, botanical gardens and water sports, and the area lies about a kilometre from the Yellow River Delta Zoo. It suits visitors wanting an outdoor day or a stay near the city rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Mingcuihu Wetland, Hekou
rows.summary: Mingcuihu is a large lake and wetland park on the edge of Hekou's new town, designed around the themes of the Yellow River, oil, the sea and wetlands. The official page gives about 5,000 mu (roughly 330 hectares) of park with 3,500 mu of water and an 8 km shoreline, with themed zones for culture, leisure and wetland ecology. It was rated 4A in 2022 and suits an easy lakeside walk.

rows.name: Red Liuji, Guangrao
rows.summary: Liuji is a village in Dawang town, Guangrao, that was home to one of the earliest rural Communist Party branches in Shandong, which kept and used a first-edition Chinese translation of the Communist Manifesto, as local government pages tell it. The visit centres on a museum on the branch's former site and a Communist Manifesto memorial hall, with an underground tunnel exhibit, a Qi brush craft hall and a hall for local folk opera. It has also been used as a filming location for television dramas on the party's early history.

rows.name: Sunzi Culture Tourism Area, Guangrao
rows.summary: The Sunzi Culture Tourism Area is a themed leisure district on Sunwu Lake in Guangrao's new eastern district, devoted to Sun Wu (Sun Tzu), author of The Art of War, whom Guangrao claims as a native son. Its core is the Sunzi Cultural Park, with a ceremonial entrance plaza of bronze chariot groups and drum-shaped walls, a large hall and exhibits on military thought. It is a modern development rather than a historic site, and Guangrao holds an annual Sunzi Culture Tourism Festival, the eighteenth opening on 11 September 2026.

rows.name: Tianning Temple, Kenli
rows.summary: Tianning Temple is a large modern Buddhist temple complex in the west of Kenli district, built beside the Tianning Lake wetland park; its main hall was consecrated in 2013 and the area was rated 4A in 2014. The temple has a main hall and a relic pagoda surrounded by side halls, and the city culture and tourism bureau lists a folk-culture street, a Buddhist academy and a riverside park among the wider area's facilities. It suits visitors interested in contemporary Chinese Buddhist architecture and a quiet wetland setting.

rows.name: Yellow River Delta Zoo
rows.summary: The Yellow River Delta Zoo is an urban zoo on the south-west side of Dongying, opened in the early 2010s on about 1,000 mu (roughly 65 hectares) of land. In 2019 the city's culture and tourism bureau reported more than 100 species and over a thousand animals, including giraffes, white tigers and white rhinos, and a dinosaur-themed play area and a jellyfish exhibit have been added since. It suits families, and it was rated a 4A area in 2018.

rows.name: Yellow River Estuary Eco-Tourism Area
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: This 5A area is the visitor section of the Yellow River Delta National Nature Reserve, where the Yellow River meets the Bohai Sea on some of China's youngest land. It has natural willow woods, wetlands and reed beds with boardwalks and a bird museum near the entrance, and the autumn carpet of red seepweed is a seasonal draw. The reserve was set up in 1992 and counts more than 360 bird species, including oriental storks; the area opened to visitors in 2005 and was rated 5A in 2020.

rows.name: Baishou and Baishi Memorial Arches
rows.summary: These are two stone memorial arches of the Qianlong era standing about 100 m apart in the old centre of Shan County: the Baishi Arch of 1769, carved with a hundred lions, and the Baishou Arch of 1765, carved with the character for longevity in a hundred scripts. The Baishi Arch is 13.5 m high, a four-pillar, three-bay arch with a hip-and-gable roof, and the Baishou Arch is almost identical, both with fine relief carving of lions, dragons, clouds and peonies. They stand in a public square (Paifang Square) in the town centre.

rows.name: Caozhou Peony Garden
rows.summary: Caozhou Peony Garden is a large peony park on the north side of Heze city, described by the city government as holding 1,237 peony varieties and more than 600 herbaceous peony varieties. It peaks in April during the city's peony festival, when the flower beds are joined by costume events and stage shows, and it also has a national-flower museum and a street of craft stalls.

rows.name: Fulong Lake Resort, Shan County
rows.summary: Fulong Lake is a large reservoir-lake resort of about 21 sq km of water in the south-west of Shan County, on the course of the old Yellow River, with a lakeside plaza, a long jetty, islands, a rose garden and a Taoist temple, the Laojun Temple. Boats, electric carts and a small train link the sights, and a spring-summer culture festival is held there each year. It is a family and leisure destination for a day by the water rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Guanyin Temple Pagoda, Yuncheng
rows.summary: Yuncheng's Guanyin Temple Pagoda, also called the Tang Pagoda, is an octagonal storeyed brick pagoda built in 931 in the Five Dynasties period, when the Later Tang ruled. Seven storeys originally, it now has five and stands about 32 m high; its eaves are made of brick bracket sets and hung with bells, and an interior stair is recorded as leading up through the core chamber. The pagoda stands in the north of the town beside a small park.

rows.name: Jianshan Scenic Area, Shan County
rows.summary: Jianshan is a lakeside park in the development zone on the east side of Shan County town, laid out around a small hill and Jianshan Lake, with a walking path round the water, boats and a glass bridge. It also holds statues of local figures such as Empress Lü and the Four Gentlemen poets, a red-tourism education base, and, nearby, the Mingran Art Museum and the county cultural centre. It suits a short stroll in town rather than a full-day trip.

rows.name: Jinshan Scenic Area, Juye
rows.summary: Jinshan is a low hill in Hetaoyuan town, about 1.5 km from north to south and rising to 133 m, with karst caves, springs and walking paths; part of it lies in a provincial geopark. On its south slope the local gazetteer places the Qin Wang Dong, a large man-cut cave that it identifies as an unfinished Western Han royal tomb, and the Jinshan Han tombs are a national heritage unit. The hill is the main sight of the Jinshan tourism zone, which also takes in nearby Qinglong and Baihu hills and a stone-built hill village.

rows.name: Juye Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Juye Confucian Temple is a Ming-dynasty temple moved to its present site in 1383, of which only the Dacheng Hall survived the temple's closure in 1947. The hall is a five-bay building with a double-eaved gable-and-hip roof, green glazed tiles and carved stone columns, modelled on the Dacheng Hall at Qufu; the gate and side wings were rebuilt in the 1990s and 2000s. A calligraphy corridor of the Analects and old cypresses line the courtyard.

rows.name: Shan County Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: The museum is a modern science centre of about 24,500 square metres in the north of Shan County town. Its permanent hall has 11 zones and over 300 exhibits arranged around the spirit, beauty and dream of science, and there are three cinemas (4D, VR and dome) and eight hands-on science labs. It is a family or school-group stop rather than a sight for heritage or scenery.

rows.name: Sun Bin Tourist City
rows.summary: Sun Bin Tourist City is a large park of about 999 mu (roughly 67 hectares) in Jishan town, Juancheng County, built on the site of the old Yicheng Temple and opened in 2008. It combines a memorial zone for the Warring States strategist Sun Bin with a Buddhist temple area and gardens; sights named by the county include tombs attributed to Sun Bin and Jing Ke and a joint tomb of the legendary friends Yang and Zuo. It is a modern built attraction for people interested in Chinese military culture, with seasonal festivals and stage performances.

rows.name: Water Margin Heroes City
rows.summary: This is a theme park built in the style of a Song-dynasty town, in Yuncheng County, the home area of Song Jiang, Chao Gai and other characters in the novel Water Margin. Walled courtyards, streets, a reconstructed county yamen and regular costumed performances recreate scenes from the story, and the park is lit up for lantern events at the Spring Festival. It is a modern, commercial attraction for families and fans of the novel, not a historic old town.

rows.name: Wohua Pagoda
rows.summary: Wohua Pagoda, also called Tian Pagoda, in Datianji town is a Tang-dynasty pagoda that the county describes as the oldest surviving above-ground building in south-west Shandong. Its stone base was found in 2007, a survey has shown that part of the structure lies underground, and the county has repaired it and built a surrounding wall and visitor routes since 2016. It is a small, quiet monument for those interested in early pagodas.

rows.name: Yellow River Old Course Wetland Scenic Area, Cao County
rows.name_zh: 曹县黄河故道湿地风景区
rows.summary: This wetland scenic area of about 512 hectares lies in Weiwan town on the bed the Yellow River left behind when it changed course in 1855, beside the Taihangdi reservoir. Its attractions include a lotus pond, reed beds, a peach-and-plum grove, a flower field and a flying camp, with rapeseed in spring and lotus in summer. It is a low-key rural outing for the flowers, boating and photography, not a heritage site.

rows.name: Yongfeng Pagoda, Juye
rows.summary: Yongfeng Pagoda is an octagonal brick pavilion-style pagoda in the south-east corner of Juye old town, about 31 m high with five surviving storeys; local records say it was begun in the Tang dynasty and finished in the Song. It stands beside water, with a tortoise-based stele on its south side, and is the old 'Fanta morning glow' view of the town. It is a short stop usually combined with the Confucian temple.

rows.name: Baimai Springs
rows.summary: A public park in the centre of Mingshui, Zhangqiu, built around the Baimai group of artesian karst springs, one of Jinan's 'seventy-two famous springs'. The main spring rises in a rectangular pool about 25 m long in the courtyard of the Dragon Spring Temple, with small lakes fed by the springs around it and a poetry garden for the Song poet Li Qingzhao, who is associated with Zhangqiu. Mingshui Ancient Town, a new town built in old style, opened beside the park in 2023-24.

rows.name: Baimaiquan Liquor Culture Tourist Area
rows.summary: A visitor area built around the Baimaiquan distillery in Mingshui, Zhangqiu, with liquor-culture displays and a visitor centre, a shop and a restaurant. It was rated a 4A scenic area in December 2021, the first in Zhangqiu themed on industrial tourism, and suits visitors interested in how Chinese grain spirit is made.

rows.name: Best Spring Under Heaven Scenic Area (Baotu Spring and Daming Lake)
rows.summary: The five-A scenic area at the heart of Jinan's old town, made up of Baotu Spring Park, the Five Dragon Pool, the old-city moat and its Huancheng Park, and Daming Lake, with Baotu, Black Tiger and Five Dragon Pool as the three spring groups. Baotu Spring, which the Qianlong Emperor named 'First Spring under Heaven', is the best known of the city's 72 named springs, and a boat trip along the moat leads on to Daming Lake. Inside Baotu Spring Park, Wanzhuyuan is a courtyard house of 13 courtyards with spring pools and carved stone, wood and brick, built in the early twentieth century for the Beiyang general Zhang Huaizhi and now part of the park.

rows.name: Chengziya Site
rows.summary: The type site of China's Longshan culture, where the black-pottery culture of some 4,000 years ago was first identified in 1928 and excavated in 1930 and 1931. The rectangular rammed-earth city wall enclosed about 20 hectares, and a hall protects a section of the west wall. The Chengziya Ruins Museum beside the site, opened in 1994, shows the finds, and the site was added to China's list of national archaeological site parks in December 2017.

rows.name: Daxinzhuang Site
rows.summary: A large Shang-period settlement on the north-eastern edge of Jinan that became an urban centre in the early 13th century BCE and grew into one of the biggest Shang sites outside the Central Plains. Oracle bones with inscriptions found here in 2003 were reported as the first of their kind outside Anyang. The remains lie below ground; the site museum nearby, opened on a trial basis in December 2025, shows more than 800 finds.

rows.name: Duofo Pagoda, Cuiping Mountain
rows.summary: A Buddhist pagoda of the Ming and Qing periods standing on the summit of Cuiping Mountain in Pingyin county; its name means 'many-Buddhas pagoda'. It was listed as a provincial protected site in 1977 and as a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Fanggan Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A hill and gorge scenic area at Fanggan village in Xueye subdistrict, Laiwu, which the Jinan tourism bureau describes as combining mountains, water, forest, springs, waterfalls and rock formations. It is promoted for hiking and clean mountain air, and the village has a small rural-memory museum. It suits a half-day outdoor trip in summer.

rows.name: Fantawild Oriental Heritage, Jinan
rows.summary: A theme park in Huaiyin district belonging to the Fantawild group's Oriental Heritage line, which takes Chinese culture and folk stories as its themes. It has rides and show attractions, with parades, stage performances, seasonal festivals and evening openings. It suits families with children and is a full-day visit.

rows.name: Former Cheeloo University Buildings
rows.name_zh: 原齐鲁大学近现代建筑群
rows.summary: The early-twentieth-century campus of Cheeloo University, a mission university run by American, British and Canadian church bodies, was laid out around a central garden. The surviving halls, including Bergen Hall (1917) and the Alumni Gate (1924), combine a Western collegiate layout with Chinese roofs and decorative details. The site is now Shandong University's Baotuquan campus together with Qilu Hospital.

rows.name: Four Gates Pagoda
rows.summary: A single-storey stone pagoda of square plan, about 7 m along each side, with an arched doorway in each face and a roof of stacked stone slabs, standing beside the ruins of Shentong Temple. An inscription found inside the roof in 1972 dates it to 611, in the Sui dynasty, and it is thought to be the oldest surviving pavilion-style stone pagoda in China. Inside, a central pillar carries four seated Buddhas dated to 544, and an old pine and two small Tang-dynasty pagodas stand nearby.

rows.name: Hongjitang Traditional Chinese Medicine Culture Tourist Area
rows.name_zh: 宏济堂中医药文化旅游景区
rows.summary: A tourist area built by the Hongjitang pharmaceutical group in the Linuo Science Park, laid out in late Ming and early Qing style around a lake modelled on a smaller Daming Lake. It has the Shandong Hongjitang Museum of Chinese medicine, a 456 m relief wall on the history of Chinese medicine, workshops where gelatin and other products are made, and a garden of medicinal plants. It suits visitors curious about traditional medicine.

rows.name: Impression Jinan Spring World
rows.summary: A shopping, dining and leisure block in Huaiyin district, newly built to resemble traditional Jinan architecture. Its water features include a large music fountain on the main square, small cascades along the lanes and a shallow stream where children paddle in summer. It has craft shops and a food street and is lit up at night, so it suits an evening stroll or a family outing.

rows.name: Jiaoji Railway Museum (Former Jinan Station)
rows.summary: The 1915 station building of the German-built Jiaoji (Qingdao-Jinan) railway, in European style with an Ionic stone colonnade and a mansard roof, once held a station hotel and later railway offices. It is now the main building of the Jiaoji Railway Museum, with galleries on how the line was built and its effect on Shandong, a reconstructed station-master's room and a steam locomotive on show. It suits railway and architecture enthusiasts.

rows.name: Jinan Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A botanical garden in the hills of Zhangqiu District, east of Jinan, laid out in themed areas that include a colour-plant garden and a rose garden. Spring brings flowering crabapple, cherry and peony, summer daylilies, roses and lotus, and autumn ginkgo and maple colour, while a climate-controlled subtropical hall holds more than 600 kinds of tropical plants. Its open lawns are used for picnics and camping, so it suits a spring or autumn day out.

rows.name: Jinan International Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large lakeside park in Changqing District, built for the 7th China International Garden Expo, held from September 2009 to May 2010. It has show gardens, flower beds, a sandy shore and boat trips on Changqing Lake, with camping lawns, children's rides and seasonal events. It suits a relaxed day out, especially in the spring flower season.

rows.name: Jinan Sunac Cultural Tourism City
rows.summary: A large leisure complex in Licheng district, east of central Jinan, opened in May 2021 and built new rather than historic. It combines an amusement park with rides and shows, a water park, an indoor sea-themed attraction, a shopping mall, hotels and a riverside bar street. In summer the amusement park opens for evening programmes, and the complex suits families.

rows.name: Jinan Wildlife World
rows.summary: A safari-style wildlife park in the hills of Zhangqiu District, with a walking area in the north and a drive-through area in the south. Its attractions include a sea lion hall, a kangaroo park, an elephant house and a crocodile pond, and in summer 2026 it ran a night zoo with a train ride and staged performances. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Jinxiangshan Amusement Park
rows.summary: A mountain amusement park in the wooded southern hills of Licheng district. The operator lists more than 200 attractions, including rides, a water-play area, a rainbow-coloured photo valley and jungle-crossing courses. It suits families and school or company groups.

rows.name: Jiudingta Chinese Ethnic Park
rows.name_zh: 九顶塔中华民族欢乐园
rows.summary: A theme park in the hills of Liubu, south-east of Jinan, built around replica villages that stage the architecture, song, dance and food of China's ethnic groups. It reopened after a refit in March 2025, with staged live-action plays by day and a fire-themed show in the evening. It is an entertainment park rather than a historic site and suits families.

rows.name: Jiuru Mountain Waterfalls
rows.summary: A wooded mountain valley in Jinan's southern hills where streams and waterfalls run through the woodland. It is run as a leisure resort, with a spring-fed swimming pool, timber cabins, a flower valley, craft workshops and summer-evening music events. It suits a day trip or an overnight stay in the warm months.

rows.name: Laiwu Battle Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum on Huangshan hill in Laiwu, now a district of Jinan, opened in 1997 on the site of an earlier martyrs' cemetery. It covers the Laiwu Campaign of 20–23 February 1947 and the wartime resistance in central Shandong, with an exhibition hall, a panorama painting 17 m high showing the fighting north of the town, a martyrs' memorial tower and an open-air weapons display. It suits visitors interested in the history of the Chinese civil war.

rows.name: Laiwu Campaign Command Post Site
rows.summary: A restored village courtyard in Shiwanzi, Gangcheng District, where Chen Yi, commanding the East China Field Army, had his command post during the Laiwu Campaign of February 1947. The main rooms were restored in 1980 and opened as an exhibition room that shows the desk, chairs and bed collected from the time. It became a provincial heritage site in 1977 and a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Laozhuang Great Buddha
rows.summary: A large seated Buddha carved into the rock at the south foot of Qingtong Mountain, more than 9 m high and dated to the late Sui or early Tang, regarded as the largest rock-cut Buddha in Shandong. The temple that stood here has gone, but eight smaller Yuan and Ming figures, inscriptions and a cave about 30 m deep beside the pedestal survive, and the Baihua spring lies below a cliff to the south-west.

rows.name: Lianhua Cave Grotto, Changqing
rows.summary: A small rock-cut Buddhist cave in the hills of Wufeng, near Shiwo village, dated by provincial records to the Northern Qi and Sui periods. The cave has a painted lotus-pattern coffered ceiling, five main statues and more than 300 small figures. A doorway added in 1626 carries the inscription 'Holy Buddha Lotus Cave'.

rows.name: Lingyan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in a valley on the north-western edge of the Mount Tai range, counted among China's four famous temples. Its Hall of a Thousand Buddhas holds 40 painted clay arhat figures, 32 of them of Song date and 8 Ming, and the 11th-century Pizhi Pagoda rises about 55 m. The Stupa Forest of 167 memorial stupas, some from the Tang, completes a visit.

rows.name: Lotus Mountain, Laiwu
rows.summary: A representative scenic area of Laiwu's southern hills, named for its ring of peaks, which resemble a lotus. It has 36 summits and 72 valleys, with gorges, odd rock formations, caves, waterfalls and pools, and its main peak, Lianhuajian, is about 991 m, the highest in Jinan. It was rated a 4A scenic area in 2023.

rows.name: Luokou Yellow River Railway Bridge
rows.summary: A steel truss railway bridge across the Yellow River at Luokou, built in 1909–12 by the German firm MAN for the Tianjin-Pukou line, with the largest spans of any railway bridge in China at the time. It was damaged in the wars of 1928, 1930 and 1937 and repaired each time, and became part of the Handan-Jinan railway in 2000. It is a landmark of the early railway age along the river.

rows.name: May 3rd Incident Site, Jinan
rows.summary: The former office of the Nationalist government's special commissioner in Shandong, on Jingsi Road in Jinan's old Commercial Port district. On 3 May 1928, during a clash between Chinese Nationalist and Japanese forces known as the Jinan incident, the diplomat Cai Gongshi and members of his staff were killed at this building. It now houses a memorial to Cai Gongshi on the upper floor and, on the ground floor, the Commercial Port Museum on the city's opening to foreign trade in 1904.

rows.name: Qi Great Wall at Jinyang Pass
rows.summary: A mountain pass on the Laiwu–Zhangqiu border where the Qi Great Wall, the oldest surviving wall of its kind in China, runs along the ridge of Jinping Mountain. West of the pass a stretch of wall survives with its parapet, battlements and peepholes, and a gate tower stands on the ridge; the Qi Great Wall Culture Museum opened just south of the pass in 2026. Walking and cycling routes link the pass with other passes and old stone villages along the wall.

rows.name: Red Leaf Valley
rows.summary: A hillside park in Jinan's southern hills where more than 4,000 mu (about 270 hectares) of wild smoke-tree scrub turns red each autumn. Stone steps and paths climb the slopes, the seven-storey Wanye Tower looks over the valley, and Xuanqiu Lake reflects the colours. The park also has themed gardens, including roses, plum and azaleas, and a small temple, Xingjiao Temple.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Jinan
rows.summary: The cathedral of the Catholic Archdiocese of Jinan, built in 1901–05 with Boxer indemnity money and extended in 1906, in twin-towered Gothic Revival style on a Latin-cross plan. It was designed by the Franciscan brother Korbinian Paugger and built by local stonemasons, with 48 m stone towers and black Chinese roof tiles over the nave. It was closed in 1966 and reopened on Christmas Day 1985.

rows.name: Shandong Ancient Architecture Museum
rows.summary: This is the Jinan mother institute of the Red Swastika Society, a Republic-era charitable body that began in Jinan. Building started in 1934 and produced a four-courtyard complex of concrete halls in traditional timber style, with a tall glazed-tile screen wall, a main hall under a green-glazed roof and a twelve-sided, two-storey pavilion at the rear. After restoration it opened to the public in February 2026 as the Shandong Ancient Architecture Museum, which shows traditional building components, techniques and models.

rows.name: Thousand Buddha Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded hill on the southern edge of Jinan, counted with Baotu Spring and Daming Lake as one of the city's three famous sights. About 130 Buddha figures carved in the Sui dynasty remain on the Thousand Buddha Cliff, and Xingguochan Temple, a Tang foundation, stands on the slope, with paths and a chairlift leading up. From the ridge there are views north across the city towards the Yellow River.

rows.name: Thousand-Buddha Cliff
rows.summary: A cliff face of Buddhist rock carvings beside the ruins of Shentong Temple in the hills near Liubu, with more than 200 carved figures and dozens of inscriptions. Most were carved in the 7th century, in the Tang dynasty, and they are regarded as the largest group of cliff statues in Shandong, including figures of a Tang princess and her husband. The national listing also covers the Dragon-Tiger Pagoda, a Tang-period pagoda nearby, and the Nine-Summit Pagoda.

rows.name: Wei'er Road Historic Buildings, Jinan
rows.summary: A group of nine buildings dated 1901–32 along Wei'er Road and neighbouring streets in Jinan's old commercial district, among them the former Deutsch-Asiatische Bank of 1901, the Shandong postal administration building of 1919, a Bank of Communications branch, the former German consulate and clinic, and the Xiaoguanghan cinema. They are examples of the banks, offices and cinemas of early-twentieth-century Jinan. The former Xiaoguanghan cinema now holds a small museum.

rows.name: Xiangshan Tourist Area, Laiwu
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain resort area in Dawangzhuang town, in the north-west of Laiwu District, centred on Xiangshan (918.7 m) with two gorges, Jiutian and Shimen, and three highland villages. These are Wangshimen, described as Shandong's highest administrative village, Shiwuzi, kept in its original mountain style, and Zhujiayu; the area also has forest, springs, lakes and old Buddhist and Daoist sites. It is known for its red and yellow autumn leaves and suits a day of walking and sightseeing.

rows.name: Xiaotang Mountain Han Shrine
rows.summary: A small stone offering shrine from the early Eastern Han dynasty, standing on Xiaotang Mountain near the Yellow River.
