It is the only known shrine of its period still standing in its original form, a building about 4 m long whose black stone walls are carved in shallow relief with processions, hunting, entertainments and mythological scenes, plus visitors' inscriptions from the 2nd century and a Northern Qi eulogy on the outer wall. Tradition links it with the filial exemplar Guo Ju, and it is now sheltered by a protective hall within a walled precinct.

rows.name: Yongji Bridge, Pingyin
rows.summary: A single-arch bluestone bridge over the Langxi River at Dong'e, built in the Wanli reign of the Ming dynasty to replace earlier bridges on the site, the first of which dated from 1500. Dragon heads are carved on the arch crown on both the north and south faces, and it is the largest-span old stone arch bridge in Jinan. It stood at the gate of the old walled town of Dong'e and was still carrying local traffic when reported in 2014.

rows.name: Zhujiayu Ancient Village
rows.summary: A hill village in Guanzhuang, Zhangqiu, founded in the early Ming and kept largely intact, with more than 200 Ming and Qing buildings, bluestone lanes and 99 stone bridges, including a Kangxi-era double bridge that separated foot traffic from flood water. The Zhu clan ancestral hall, the Wenchang Pavilion and the old Shanyin school survive, and the village was a filming location for the television drama Chuang Guandong. It was named in the second batch of China Historic and Cultural Villages and among the first China Traditional Villages in 2012.

rows.name: Ancient City of the Zhu State, Zoucheng
rows.summary: Remains of the capital of Zhu (later Zou), a small state of the Zhou period, which moved here in 614 BC and held the city for over three centuries. Stretches of rammed-earth wall, mostly 3–4 m high and up to about 7 m, survive around Jiwangcheng village at the foot of Mount Yi, enclosing a square roughly 2.5 km on a side. The interior is farmland and villages, with a raised mound in the north-centre that is thought to have been the palace area.

rows.name: Baoxiang Temple, Wenshang
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the north-west of Wenshang town, renamed Baoxiang by a Song emperor. Its centrepiece is the Taizi Lingzong Pagoda, a Song-dynasty brick pagoda that is itself a national protected monument; the crypt beneath it was opened in 1994 and yielded Buddhist relics, among them one venerated as a Buddha tooth.

rows.name: Bian Bridge
rows.summary: A three-arch stone bridge over the Si River at Quanlin in Sishui County, 25 m long, 7 m wide and 6.5 m high, rebuilt in 1181 under the Jin dynasty on an older bridge of the late Tang. Its balustrades are carved with figures, flowers, landscapes, birds and animals, a pair of stone lions sits at each end on lotus-flower bases, and the arches have openwork dragon heads. It stands on the old road from Yanzhou and Qufu towards Linyi and was one of the Ten Sights of Sishui.

rows.name: Cemetery of Mencius' Mother
rows.summary: A wooded family cemetery in Fu village, south of Qufu, where the parents of the philosopher Mencius and some of his descendants are buried. A tree-lined approach leads to a memorial hall in front of the tomb of Mencius's mother, and other Meng family tombs lie to the north-west, one of them marked by a Yuan-dynasty stele of 1333. It is counted among the four Mencius sites, with the temple, mansion and cemetery in Zoucheng.

rows.name: Chongxing Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey, octagonal brick pagoda in the pavilion style, built in the early Northern Song dynasty in the old town of Zoucheng. It was listed as a city-level monument in 1985, a provincial one in 2006 and a national one in 2013. It lies about 1 km north of the Mencius Temple, so it fits easily into a visit there.

rows.name: Cixiao Jianwan Memorial Archway, Jining
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty stone memorial archway standing in a street in Jining's old town, listed as a provincial protected site in 2006 and as a national one in 2013. Its name means roughly "kindness and filial piety both fulfilled". It takes only a few minutes to see.

rows.name: Confucius Six Arts City
rows.summary: A modern cultural leisure complex just south of Qufu's old town, built around Confucius's Six Arts: rites, music, archery, charioteering, calligraphy and mathematics. It has a Six Arts experience zone and a folk-customs zone showing local life in Confucius's hometown, along with shops, restaurants and entertainment. It is a purpose-built attraction rather than a historic site, and suits visitors with spare time after the main Confucian sites.

rows.name: East Great Mosque, Jining
rows.summary: A mosque first built in the early Ming dynasty and later enlarged and restored, on the west bank of Jining's old canal. Built in the Chinese timber style along an east–west axis, it runs from a canal-side gate and a stone archway through courtyards and a domed tower to a prayer hall 28 m wide, with a three-storey rear hall and a moon-viewing tower behind. The hall was built to hold more than 2,000 worshippers.

rows.name: Former Qufu Normal School
rows.summary: Three groups of buildings from a former teacher-training school stand beside the Temple of Confucius: an early twentieth-century assembly hall, an H-shaped teaching block, and a Qing-dynasty examination hall of the former Yanzhou prefecture. The school opened in 1905 as a new-style college in the old examination hall, and the teaching block now houses a memorial museum on the school's Communist Party branch. The site was listed nationally in 2019.

rows.name: Fushan Xihuang Temple Site
rows.summary: The ruins of a large temple to Fuxi and Nüwa on the west slope of Fushan in Guoli town, first recorded on a stele of 931. What survives is a group of stone pillars and stelae and the foundations of a hall, now protected by a boundary wall and stele pavilions. A ceremony honouring Fuxi and Nüwa is held at the site each spring on the third day of the third lunar month.

rows.name: Fuxi Temple, Weishan
rows.summary: A temple to the legendary ruler Fuxi at the foot of Phoenix Hill, in Liangcheng town on the shore of Dushan Lake. The main hall stands on a six-metre bluestone terrace, traditionally the mound of Fuxi's tomb; it is a five-bay, single-eaved building with a hip-and-gable roof of glazed tiles and Song-period stone pillars inside, and with twelve stelae recording repairs it is all that remains of a once larger courtyard complex. A cave behind the hall holds Jin-dynasty cliff-carved poems, and springs rise behind the temple.

rows.name: Guangshan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick-and-stone pagoda 49 m high, also called the Wenfeng Pagoda, standing in Xinghu Park in the centre of Jinxiang. The county government dates its foundation to 630 in the Tang, with the present tower rebuilt in 1561 under the Ming and restored in 1914 and 1999; Japanese artillery shelled off one and a half storeys in 1938. Inside are carved stone Buddha groups on the third and fifth floors, and a stair from the north door of the ground floor climbs the tower.

rows.name: Iron Pagoda of Chongjue Temple, Jining
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal pagoda with an iron shell over a brick core, 23.8 m tall, begun in 1105 under the Northern Song and completed in 1581 when the top two storeys and a gilded finial were added. Its cast panels carry inscriptions and relief figures of seated Buddhas. It stands in the grounds of the former Chongjue Temple, now the old site of the Jining Museum, and cannot be climbed.

rows.name: Jiagudui Peasant Village
rows.summary: A rural tourism village opened in 2016 in Jiagudui village, Dalukou town, built around farming culture and village folk customs. Its attractions include a pottery-making park, a folk-custom street, guesthouses, a folk performance hall, a campsite and flower fields. The activities are aimed mainly at families, and seasonal events include harvest festivals and costume garden parties.

rows.name: Jinkou Dam
rows.summary: A stone dam across the Si River on the eastern edge of Yanzhou, still used as a crossing by road traffic and pedestrians. Its first form dates to the Northern Wei in the early 6th century (sources give 514 or 529); the Yuan rebuilt it as an overflow dam and the Ming lengthened and raised it, and it rests on timber piles with dressed stone blocks held together by iron clamps, which earned it the name Gold-Mouth Jade Dam. It has five sluice openings and two carved stone beasts from the Yuan at the ends of the wing walls, and visitors can walk along the top.

rows.name: Kangwang Valley Flower World, Zoucheng
rows.summary: A flower-themed leisure and agri-tourism park in eastern Zoucheng, built in the late 2010s around flower fields and a lake. Indoor halls cover flowers, tropical plants and vegetable growing, and there are areas for picking fruit and vegetables. It is a modern family-oriented attraction rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Lianhua Lake Wetland Park, Wenshang
rows.summary: A provincial-level wetland park of about 290 hectares on the northern edge of Wenshang town, opened in 2011 and laid out around lakes and islands. It has zones for plant viewing, fruit picking, amusement attractions and folk-custom displays, and a folk museum, the Zhongdu Folk Museum, stands at its north-east corner. It suits a relaxed half-day outing.

rows.name: Lu State Ancient City Archaeological Park, Qufu
rows.summary: The capital of the state of Lu for some 870 years from the early Western Zhou, the city covered about 10 sq km and occupied the eastern and northern parts of present-day Qufu. The archaeological park centres on the excavated palace area around the Temple of Duke Zhou, and takes in the Wangfutai burial area, the Wuyu Terrace, an iron-smelting site and a site museum. The city wall can only be faintly traced on the ground, so it is best for visitors with an interest in early Chinese history.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Shaohao
rows.summary: The tomb of Shaohao, one of the legendary Five Emperors, in Jiuxian village east of Qufu, a large earthen mound inside an enclosure of old trees with a sacrificial hall built in 1738. In front of the tomb stands Shou Qiu, a stepped stone pyramid about 8.7 m high, faced in stone in the early 12th century to mark the legendary birthplace of the Yellow Emperor, with a small pavilion on top. To the south stand the two huge Song steles of the vanished Jingling Palace, one of them left blank and known as the Sorrow of Ten Thousand stele.

rows.name: Mencius Temple and Mansion, Zoucheng
rows.summary: The Temple of Mencius, also called the Yasheng Temple, honours the philosopher Mencius, the 'Second Sage' after Confucius, in his hometown of Zoucheng; its present buildings are largely Qing-dynasty work of the Kangxi years, grouped around a main hall with a green glazed-tile roof. Beside it, the Mencius Mansion was the residence of his descendants, who held a hereditary post in the Hanlin Academy, and is one of the best-preserved historic residential complexes in Shandong. Together with the Mencius cemetery north-east of town they are known as the 'Three Meng' sites.

rows.name: Mount Liang (Shuipo Liangshan Scenic Area)
rows.summary: Mount Liang is a low hill, about 198 m high, in Liangshan County that the classic Chinese novel Water Margin made the stronghold of 108 outlaw heroes. The scenic area is built around that story, with structures put up to match the novel's descriptions, and it is also a provincial forest park and geopark. It will mainly interest readers and fans of the novel.

rows.name: Mount Yi, Zoucheng
rows.summary: A granite hill south of Zoucheng, known in ancient times as Dongshan, the "eastern mountain" that the Mencius says Confucius climbed. Its slopes have granite outcrops, caves and Ming and Qing rock inscriptions, along with rebuilt academy buildings and a cave academy traditionally linked with Confucius. It is also a provincial scenic area and a national forest park, and suits a half-day walk.

rows.name: Nanchi Garden, Jining
rows.summary: A garden park in the south of Jining, themed on the city's Grand Canal heritage, the poets Li Bai and Du Fu, and the Queen Mother of the West. The northern half has classical-style pavilions, archways, a gallery of inscribed steles and a shrine to Du Fu called the Shaoling Shrine, while the southern half is planted as an arboretum and flower gardens. It suits a relaxed stroll rather than a long visit.

rows.name: Nanwang Hub of the Grand Canal
rows.summary: Nanwang, in Wenshang County, is the summit of the Grand Canal, about 38.5 m above sea level, where Ming engineers in the Yongle years built a stone-faced diversion at the junction with the Xiaowen River so that its water could be shared between the northward and southward channels. The works are a World Heritage component of the Grand Canal and the core of a national archaeological site park, which includes the excavated Dragon King Temple complex. It suits visitors interested in canal engineering more than scenery.

rows.name: Nanyang Ancient Town
rows.summary: Nanyang is a small town on a long, narrow island in Nanyang Lake, one of the Four Lakes of southern Shandong, with the old Grand Canal running along it. After a lock was built there in 1331 it grew into a busy canal port and was nicknamed 'second Jining' in the Ming and Qing periods. It is promoted as part of the Weishan Lake tourism area.

rows.name: Nishan Confucian Temple and Academy
rows.summary: A temple on Mount Ni, the hill traditionally held to be the birthplace of Confucius, with an academy beside it, set in the hills east of Qufu. It was first built in the 950s, rebuilt in 1417 in the Ming dynasty and repaired several times, reaching its present form in the Qing; repairs in 1925 were funded by Confucius's 77th-generation descendant Kong Decheng. It is a separate visit from the main Temple of Confucius, Kong Family Mansion and Cemetery in Qufu.

rows.name: Qingshan Temple and Scenic Area, Jiaxiang
rows.summary: A hillside temple group on the western slope of Qingshan, south of Jiaxiang, which began as a shrine to the ruler of the Western Zhou state of Jiao and later became a joint Buddhist and Daoist temple. The surviving buildings are mostly Qing and Republican-era, rising up the slope from a Mount Tai palace archway through the Huijigong Hall to a ten-thousand-Buddha pavilion, with 58 stelae dating from the Song onwards. The surrounding hill is run as a 4A scenic area with several more temples and springs.

rows.name: Shangjiushan Stone Village
rows.summary: Shangjiushan is a hill village of stone houses in Shiqiang town, Zoucheng. China Daily describes it as a rare stone village founded in the early Northern Song period and named after the nine hills around it, and media reports count more than 300 residences in Ming and Qing style. It was added to the seventh batch of China's Historic and Cultural Villages in 2019 and suits a slow walk through the old stone courtyards.

rows.name: Shimen Mountain, Qufu
rows.summary: A wooded hill once called Longmen Mountain and renamed for two facing peaks that look like a stone gate; the main peak, Shenghan, is 406 m high. The hill has twenty-four named scenic spots, some of them caves, and a Qing-dynasty temple complex; places on it are traditionally linked with Confucius studying the Book of Changes and with a gathering of the poets Li Bai and Du Fu. It suits a half-day hike for visitors based in Qufu.

rows.name: Sishui Bin Riverside Park
rows.summary: A landscaped riverside park of about 62 hectares on the Si River, laid out in a modern style as the core public space of the new eco-city district of Sishui County town. Its name, "the banks of the Si", echoes a line by the Song philosopher Zhu Xi. The Sishui County Museum stands beside the park's plaza and takes visitors at weekends and on public holidays only by prior booking.

rows.name: Taibai Lake Scenic Area
rows.summary: Taibai Lake is a lake and wetland scenic area of about 22 sq km on the southern side of Jining, laid out between the old canal on the east and the Grand Canal on the west as an eco-tourism area that combines sightseeing with wetland protection and water purification. Its lotus beds flower in midsummer. It suits a relaxed outing within the city rather than a full day trip.

rows.name: Temple of Duke Zhou, Qufu
rows.summary: The temple honours the Duke of Zhou, brother of King Wu of Zhou, and served as the ancestral temple of the state of Lu at the heart of its ancient capital, in the north-east of present-day Qufu. A temple was set up on the site of Lu's ancestral temple in 1008 and repaired several times under the Yuan, Ming and Qing; statues of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Lu now stand in the Yuansheng Hall. It is a separate site from the main Temple of Confucius, Kong Family Mansion and Cemetery.

rows.name: Temple of Yan Hui
rows.summary: A temple to Yan Hui, the favourite disciple of Confucius, in the north of Qufu's old town; the buildings date from the Yuan to the Qing, with the present layout set in the Ming dynasty. The central of its three parallel axes of gates, halls and courtyards leads to the main Fusheng Hall with its carved dragon pillars, and a pavilion over a well marks the humble lane in which, according to the Analects, Yan Hui lived. Stelae from the Jin, Yuan and Ming dynasties stand in the courtyards, and the temple is a separate site from the main Temple of Confucius, Kong Family Mansion and Cemetery.

rows.name: Temple of Zengzi
rows.summary: The temple to Zeng Shen (Zengzi), a disciple of Confucius, at the foot of Nanwu Hill in southern Jiaxiang, whose founding is traditionally dated to 426 BC. The present Ming-dynasty layout, set within red walls on a north-south axis, has more than thirty buildings, among them a gate hall, an imperial stele pavilion and the Zongsheng Hall, in grounds with many old stelae and cypress trees. Zengzi's tomb lies about 500 m to the west.

rows.name: Tieshan and Gangshan Rock Carvings
rows.summary: Buddhist scripture and a dedicatory eulogy are carved in very large characters across a sloping granite face of Tieshan on the north-western edge of Zoucheng, dated by its own text to 579, in the Northern Zhou period. The main panel is about 61 m by 17 m, and about 700 of the original 946 characters of the sutra survive; the carvings are prized for their calligraphy. A scatter of smaller carvings from 580 lies on the rocks of a ravine on neighbouring Gangshan, to the north.

rows.name: Tomb of Prince Huang of Lu, Zoucheng
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhu Tan (1370–1390), tenth son of the Ming founder, the Hongwu Emperor, and the first Prince of Lu, at the southern foot of Jiulong Mountain. The underground chambers were excavated in 1970–71, yielding more than 2,000 objects, and have been open to visitors since 1988; a second excavated tomb, that of a consort, lies about 60 m to the west. Many of the finds are displayed in the Shandong Museum in Jinan.

rows.name: Wanzi Qianhong Eco-Wellness Resort
rows.name_zh: 万紫千红生态养生旅游度假区
rows.pinyin: Wànzǐ Qiānhóng Shēngtài Yǎngshēng Lǚyóu Dùjiàqū
rows.summary: Wanzi Qianhong is a modern leisure resort built around a lake in the hills of Sizhang town, Sishui County, marketed for countryside relaxation and 'eco-wellness'. It has accommodation and outdoor activities, and the setting is rural hill country rather than a historic site. It suits visitors who want a quiet stay or an outdoor day trip from Qufu.

rows.name: Weishan Lake
rows.summary: The 5A scenic area covers about 77 sq km of Weishan Lake and its shore in Weishan County; the lake is described as the largest freshwater lake in northern China. It takes in Weishan Island, a stretch of the Grand Canal and the Weishan Lake National Wetland Park, where egrets gather in a bird forest in the evenings. Lotus beds flower in summer, and fishermen on the island have traditionally kept cormorants for fishing.

rows.name: Wu Family Shrines
rows.summary: The Wu Family Shrines are the remains of a late Eastern Han family cemetery in Jiaxiang County: stone offering shrines and a pair of stone gate towers, begun in 147 CE, whose walls are covered in carved reliefs of myth and history. The carved stones are displayed on the site in a museum that opened in 2015, whose hall for the gate towers was designed by the architect Luo Zhewen. The reliefs have been recorded since the Song dynasty.

rows.name: Xianhe Flower Sea Eco-Park
rows.summary: Xianhe Flower Sea is a leisure park of flower fields beside a large lake in the northern part of Qufu, in the area promoted as the Qufu International Slow City. It offers flower viewing, family activities and water recreation, and was rated a 4A scenic area in 2019. It is a modern, commercial park rather than a historic site, aimed mainly at families and groups.

rows.name: Xinglong Pagoda
rows.summary: A thirteen-storey octagonal brick pagoda 54 m high in the north-east of Yanzhou's old town, standing in the grounds of the Yanzhou Museum. The tower is built in two stages, a thick lower body of seven storeys with internal galleries and steps and six much narrower storeys above, which gives it a pagoda-on-a-pagoda profile; first built in 602 under the Sui, the present tower dates from the Song and was repaired after a 17th-century earthquake. Excavation of its underground chamber in 2008 produced a stone casket, a gilded silver coffin and a gold relic bottle, and the museum shows local archaeology including Neolithic pottery from nearby sites.

rows.name: Yangshan Battle Memorial, Jinxiang
rows.summary: A hill and village site where, in July 1947, forces of the People's Liberation Army under Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping fought the Nationalist 66th Division in the Southwest Shandong Campaign. A martyrs' cemetery and memorial tower were built on the eastern summit in 1950, and the Southwest Shandong Campaign Memorial Museum stands in the grounds. The surrounding tourist area adds military-themed attractions and a street built in old style.

rows.name: Yanzhou Catholic Church
rows.summary: A German-built Catholic compound in the south-west of old Yanzhou, begun in 1897 and from 1946 the China headquarters of the Society of the Divine Word. The large Gothic cathedral finished in 1899 was destroyed in 1966, but the two-storey brick-and-timber bishop's house of 1901 and a monastery building with a cross and red-tiled roof survive. It was the mission centre for south-western Shandong and is listed as evidence of the exchange between Western and Chinese architecture.

rows.name: Dong'e Ejiao Culture Tourism Area
rows.summary: This is a themed tourist complex run by the Dong'e Ejiao company around ejiao, the donkey-hide gelatin used in Chinese medicine that Dong'e is known for. Its parts include Ejiao City, a replica old-street quarter built as a film set for late-Qing and early-Republican Jinan and Dong'e, the China Ejiao Museum, an experience factory, a hill with a temple to the medicine kings, and a donkey museum and breeding centre. It suits visitors interested in Chinese medicine, industrial tourism or period street scenes.

rows.name: Dongchang Lake
rows.summary: Dongchang Lake surrounds the square, walled old town of Liaocheng and began in 1070, in the Northern Song period, as the town moat. Today it covers over five square kilometres with a shoreline of about 16 km, a lakeside park along the west shore and the Grand Canal passing beside it. It suits an easy walk or boat trip, with the old town's main sights (Guangyue Tower, the guildhall, the iron pagoda) around it.

rows.name: Guangyue Tower
rows.summary: Guangyue Tower is a four-storey timber tower on a brick-and-stone base at the centre of Liaocheng's old town, begun in the early Ming dynasty as a lookout and about 33 m tall. Climbing it gives views over the old town and the lake, and its upper floors hold stone tablets and plaques, including one attributed to the Kangxi emperor; both Kangxi and Qianlong climbed it. It has been a national protected monument since 1988 and is the best-known landmark of Liaocheng's 'water city'.

rows.name: Han Family Cemetery, Shen County
rows.summary: This Tang-dynasty cemetery belongs to a family of military officials that included a governor of the Weibo region, and it preserves the stone figures that lined the tomb avenues: a carved horse, a groom, a warrior, a kneeling sheep and tiger, tomb markers and a spirit-way stele over 6 m tall topped with coiled dragons. The carving is bold and simple round sculpture, and the stele carries about 3,800 characters of inscription valued by calligraphy scholars. It lies in farmland north of Liangpiying village and is of interest mainly to specialists in Tang stone sculpture.

rows.name: Iron Pagoda of Longxing Temple, Liaocheng
rows.summary: This twelve-storey octagonal iron pagoda stands on a carved stone base beside the Grand Canal, in the old Longxing Temple precinct. The Liaocheng tourism bureau calls it the city's oldest surviving ancient structure: it was first built in the Song dynasty, collapsed in the Ming and was re-erected in 1466, and its cast-iron body is about 15.5 m tall. The stone base is carved with dragons, phoenixes, musicians and guardian figures.

rows.name: Jingyang Ridge and Lion Tower
rows.summary: This 4A area pairs two Water Margin sites in Yanggu County. Jingyang Ridge, where the novel has the outlaw Wu Song kill a man-eating tiger, is a wooded sand ridge with a Wu Song temple, a mountain-god shrine, a stele garden and a lake, and it stands on a Neolithic Longshan-culture walled town known from excavation rather than visible remains. The Lion Tower district in Yanggu old town, about 18 km west, has a Song-style tavern building and a recreated shopping street from the story.

rows.name: Jingyanggang Liquor Culture Scenic Area, Yanggu
rows.name_zh: 景阳冈酒文化旅游景区
rows.summary: This is a visitor attraction built since 2008 on the grounds of the Jingyanggang distillery in Yanggu, which makes baijiu, China's grain spirit, and it was rated a 4A area in December 2023. It includes a liquor museum, an exhibition on Yanggu's history, a gallery of local industrial heritage, a Ming-and-Qing-style brewing workshop, hands-on craft rooms and a long relief corridor of the Water Margin heroes. It suits visitors curious about baijiu or the Water Margin theme.

rows.name: Jiuzhouwa Rose Park
rows.summary: Jiuzhouwa is a city park in Liaocheng's high-tech zone built around rose gardens, combined with wetland and play areas, and it was rated a 4A scenic area in December 2024. The city tourism bureau describes it as a theme park, city park, wetland park and cultural park in one, planned around rose-themed gardens and a rose display belt. It suits a family outing or an easy stroll close to the city.

rows.name: Kong Fansen Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This memorial hall in Liaocheng commemorates Kong Fansen, a local-born official who worked in Tibet from 1979 and became party secretary of Ali Prefecture, and who died in a road accident in November 1994 on a trip to Xinjiang. Opened in 1995 on a site of about 19,000 square metres, it has a permanent exhibition of photographs, personal objects, reconstructed scenes and multimedia, plus temporary exhibition and lecture halls. It is one of Liaocheng's red-tourism sites and is also rated a national second-level museum.

rows.name: Linqing Canal Customs House
rows.summary: The Linqing Customs House was one of eight Ming and Qing customs posts on the Grand Canal and, by the Wanli era, the one collecting the most duty, about a quarter of the national total; founded in 1429, it is the only canal customs house to survive in China. About 80 buildings remain, including the ceremonial gate, the north and south passage halls, an office hall and a boat-dues room. It is now run as a tourist site with period-style games and cultural demonstrations, and has opened for evening visits since August 2025.

rows.name: Shanxi–Shaanxi Guildhall, Liaocheng
rows.summary: This temple-guildhall was paid for by Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants who traded in Liaocheng; building began in 1743 and the complex reached its present form by 1809. Along its main axis stand a gate, an opera stage, bell and drum towers, a hall to the god of war Guan Yu and the Chunqiu Pavilion, rich in stone, brick and wood carving and inscribed couplets. It shows how the canal trade shaped Liaocheng, and it has been a national protected monument since 1988.

rows.name: Tomb of Cao Zhi, Yushan
rows.summary: This scenic area on Yushan hill beside the Yellow River holds the tomb of Cao Zhi, the poet-prince of the Three Kingdoms period; it was begun in 233 AD, opened by archaeologists in 1951 and has had its chamber sealed since. The visit takes in the burial mound and memorial buildings, a Sui-dynasty stele and several hilltop viewpoints. It was rated a 4A area in December 2024, and the tomb has been a national protected monument since 1996.

rows.name: Tuqiao Lock Remains
rows.summary: Tuqiao Lock is a Ming-dynasty canal lock, first built in 1471 on the Grand Canal and excavated in 2010–11 as the first lock on the canal to be fully uncovered. Built of blue stone with swallowtail joints, it has a lock mouth about 6 m wide and a side channel, and it was repaired in 2013 and listed as a national monument the same year. It is a quiet rural canal relic rather than a developed attraction, of interest to canal-history enthusiasts.

rows.name: Wanyuan Garden, Linqing
rows.summary: Wanyuan is a modern Suzhou-style garden beside the Grand Canal in the north-west of Linqing, with pavilions, rockeries, ponds and brick, wood and clay carving made by craftsmen from Suzhou, according to the city's tourism pages. A second park carrying the Wanyuan name, the Canal Style Park (East Wanyuan), opened in September 2023 with replica Ming and Qing buildings, shows and food stalls. It suits a relaxed visit alongside Linqing's canal sights, and it is a recreated garden rather than a historic one.

rows.name: Xiaocheng City Ruins, Guan County
rows.summary: Xiaocheng is the earthen-walled site of a Song-period military town in Guan County, traditionally attributed to the Liao Empress Dowager Xiao in 1004; county officials call it the best-preserved Song–Liao fortress site south of the Great Wall. The square circuit of walls survives among the fields, with gate barbicans and a raised mustering platform, and the walls have been conserved and turfed in a recent project. It is a quiet open-air site for history enthusiasts, with a village inside the walls.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple Pagoda, Gaotang
rows.summary: This eleven-storey octagonal brick pagoda rises about 39 m above the street of Liangcun town in Gaotang County; the Qing gazetteer called it a Song pagoda, and a Ming stele records repairs in 1478. Its brickwork imitates timber construction, with brick and ceramic brackets under the eaves, and a Tang-dynasty locust tree 20 m to the north gives the local pairing 'Song pagoda, Tang locust'. It has been a national protected monument since 2013 and is seen mainly from outside.

rows.name: Cangma Mountain and Guan Mountain
rows.summary: Cangma Mountain and Guan Mountain are two wooded hill areas north-east of Linshu town, listed together as one 4A scenic area. Cangma Mountain is a municipal-level nature reserve with forest trails on stone steps and a sightseeing bus, while Guan Mountain, about 3 km to the east, has a long-established Taoist temple and views over the surrounding fields and villages. It is a local hiking and leisure area rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Daigu Landform Scenic Area, Mengyin
rows.summary: Daigu is the type locality of the 'gu' landform: flat-topped mesas capped by a 20–30 m layer of Cambrian limestone, with about 30 clustered around Daigu town in Mengyin County. The scenic area gives views of the mesas, a grassland and camping area, and a former Third Front military-industry site, and the surrounding hills are peach orchards that blossom in spring.

rows.name: Dongfang Ruihai International Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 东方瑞海国际温泉度假村
rows.summary: Dongfang Ruihai is a hot-spring resort and hotel complex in the south of Yishui town, on about 250 mu (roughly 17 hectares) that the county government says holds thermal baths, restaurants and conference rooms; the hotel was rated four-star in 2010. It is a modern leisure complex rather than a heritage site, and suits families or groups who want a soak.

rows.name: Firefly Water Cave and Underground Grand Canyon
rows.name_zh: 萤火虫水洞·地下大峡谷
rows.summary: This 5A area has two cave attractions in Yishui County about 8 km apart. The Underground Grand Canyon is a karst cave more than 6 km long where visitors travel by boat along an underground river among stalactites, and the Firefly Water Cave takes visitors by boat across a dark underground lake where fireflies glow on the ceiling. Above ground there is also a butterfly valley and rafting down a cliff waterfall.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wang Xizhi and Xiyanchi Tombs, Linyi
rows.summary: A small classical-style garden in central Linyi commemorating the calligrapher Wang Xizhi, whom the city counts among its natives. The Inkstone-Washing Pool (Xiyanchi), the Book-Airing Terrace, the Goose Pond and a pavilion sit beside newer calligraphy galleries and a stele corridor, and the park is a provincially protected site (Wang Xizhi's Hometown Site, 2006). Two brick tombs of the late Western Jin or early Eastern Jin period, found in the park's north-east corner in 2003 and now on the national list as the Xiyanchi tombs, are shown in an underground museum.

rows.name: Former Shandong Provincial Government and 115th Division HQ, Dadian
rows.name_zh: 山东省政府和八路军115师司令部旧址
rows.pinyin: Shāndōng Shěng Zhèngfǔ Hé Bālùjūn Yīyīwǔ Shī Sīlìngbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A manor of the Zhuang family, built in the Ming and Qing dynasties in Dadian town, which in the 1940s housed the Eighth Route Army's 115th Division headquarters and the Shandong provincial government set up under the Communist Party. The compound has the former provincial government and division headquarters buildings, exhibition halls on the Shandong anti-Japanese base area and the Zhuang family's gardens and former homes. It is a national patriotic-education demonstration base and was included in a national list of 100 red-tourism routes in 2021.

rows.name: Guantang Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Guantang is a hot-spring resort of about 790 mu (roughly 50 hectares) in the Tangtou hot-spring zone in the north of Hedong district. It combines open-air thermal pools, a hotel and a conference centre with Wenshuixiang, a cluster of Ming and Qing buildings brought from Jiangxi, Anhui and elsewhere and set along a waterway. It is a leisure resort rather than a heritage site, and suits travellers who want to relax for an afternoon after sightseeing in the area.

rows.name: Han Que Gate Towers, Pingyi County Museum
rows.summary: Two Eastern Han stone que (free-standing gate towers), the Huangshengqing Que of AD 86 and the Gongcao Que of AD 87, are displayed indoors in the Han Que Room of Pingyi County Museum in Lianhuashan Park. They carry relief carvings, and the museum also holds Han pictorial stones and other local finds; the que were moved into town from their original site on Babuding hill north of the county seat.

rows.name: Hongshizhai Resort
rows.summary: Hongshizhai is a leisure resort on the shore of Xiangshan Lake in Tongjing town, developed by the operator of nearby Zhuquan village. Linyi's official tourism account lists a cliff-edge fast-car ride, a cliffside glass rafting course, coloured slides and a glass bridge among its attractions, and the county also describes a car-camping ground. It is a commercial adventure resort aimed at families and young visitors, and is often combined with Zhuquan village.

rows.name: Huangshan Dongyi Culture Park
rows.summary: Huangshan Dongyi Culture Park is a park at the foot of Huang Hill in Linyi's Economic and Technological Development Zone, built around the Linyi Dongyi Culture Museum. The museum is a state-run museum on the Dongyi, the ancient peoples of eastern China, in a building designed to resemble a phoenix feather, with eight themed halls. It is a modest urban stop of an hour or two.

rows.name: Jiujianpeng Village Scenic Area
rows.summary: Jiujianpeng is a mountain village at about 640 m on Longding Mountain in Difang town, whose people once lived in a natural rock shelter and later built roads, brought in electricity and terraced the slopes. Visitors come for the terraced orchards and honeysuckle fields along a hill road of about 10 km (the 'Nine Bends, Eighteen Gardens'), the village exhibition hall and its story as a rural self-help model known as the 'Jiujianpeng spirit'.

rows.name: Lanling National Agricultural Park
rows.summary: Lanling National Agricultural Park is a large farm-tourism park in Bianzhuang subdistrict, built to show modern vegetable and fruit growing, with greenhouses, soilless-cultivation displays and picking gardens. Its fields carry seasonal flowers such as rape blossom and sunflowers, and there are lotus ponds. It suits families and school groups, and ties in with Lanling's reputation as a vegetable-growing county.

rows.name: Linyi Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: Linyi Science and Technology Museum is the city's municipal science museum, a large modern building in the Beicheng New Area near the meeting of the Yi, Fang and Liuqing rivers. It has more than 300 hands-on exhibits covering physics, chemistry, biology and astronomy, and is rated a 4A scenic area. It suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Linyi Zoological and Botanical Garden
rows.summary: Linyi Zoological and Botanical Garden is a large municipal park in the south-east of Hedong district, combining a zoo, planted botanical areas and landscaped lakes. The animal enclosures are the main attraction, so it is mainly a family day out rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Longyuan (Dragon Garden) Tourist Area
rows.summary: Longyuan is a resort and rural-tourism complex next to the Tangtou hot-spring zone in Hedong district, built in Huizhou and Suzhou-garden style around a dragon-culture theme, so its buildings are modern rather than historic. The Hedong district government lists its main parts as a dragon-culture 'ancient town', a children's park, a dinosaur park and a 'Love Valley', and a group of nine museums is spread through it. It suits families and school groups looking for a day out.

rows.name: Maquan Leisure Park
rows.summary: Maquan Leisure Park is an orchard-and-farm park in the hills of Tongjing town, Yinan County, developed from 2012 as a 'pastoral complex' with agricultural demonstration and elder-care themes. Cherries are the main crop, among more than 150,000 fruit trees that also include sweet persimmon, grape, hawthorn and chestnut, and visitors can pick fruit and stay in forest cabins. It suits families on a countryside day out.

rows.name: Menglianggu Campaign Memorial Area
rows.summary: Menglianggu is a small mountain of about 1.5 sq km in Mengyin County where, in May 1947, People's Liberation Army forces surrounded a Nationalist army unit in the Menglianggu campaign of the Chinese Civil War. A memorial museum stands nearby and a monument on the hill, and a live-action show called 'Heroes of Menglianggu' is staged in the area. The museum became a national defence education demonstration base in 2015.

rows.name: Mount Meng (Yimengshan) Scenic Area
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: Mount Meng is Shandong's second-highest mountain (Guimeng Peak, 1,156 m) and forms the Mengshan park of the Linyi Yimengshan UNESCO Global Geopark. Its 5A rating covers the Guimeng area in Pingyi and the Yunmeng area in Mengyin, with granite peaks, turtle-shaped rocks and waterfalls, together with Mount Yi in Linqu, Weifang, further north. The neighbouring Tianmeng area in Fei County, with a suspension bridge, a cable car and a cliff-side walkway, is run separately, as is each area, so most visitors choose one.

rows.name: New Fourth Army Headquarters Site, Linyi
rows.summary: A memorial park and museum in Linyi's Hedong District marking the site where the New Fourth Army headquarters was last based, in 1946-47, and where the East China Military Region and East China Field Army were set up. The district government names the New Fourth Army Headquarters Memorial as its only state-run museum. The complex also includes the East China Field Army memorial and former residences of commanders including Chen Yi and Su Yu.

rows.name: Old Capital of the Tan State, Tancheng
rows.summary: These are the remains of the capital of the small Zhou-period state of Tan, on the north side of Tancheng, which stayed a county and commandery seat from the Qin and Han to the Northern and Southern Dynasties. The rammed-earth wall enclosed an irregular four-sided area with a perimeter of about 4.7 km, and only parts of the west and north walls survive, with a raised area in the north-east thought to mark a military platform. The nearby Tanguo Ancient City is a modern street, not this site.

rows.name: Old Capital of the Zeng State, Lanling
rows.summary: Remains of the capital of the Zeng state, a small state of the Zhou period, in the villages of Cheng and Chenghou in Lanling County, which was still occupied in the Han. The county government says traces of the city wall, palace foundations and moat survive, and promotes the site as the ancestral home of people with the surname Zeng.

rows.name: Sites of the Daqingshan Breakout Battle
rows.name_zh: 临沂大青山突围战遗址
rows.summary: These sites commemorate the Daqingshan breakout of 30 November 1941, when thousands of people from Eighth Route Army, Shandong Party and government offices and the Anti-Japanese University's First Branch broke out of a Japanese encirclement at heavy cost; the dead included the German journalist Hans Shippe. The national listing covers the Daqingshan Martyrs' Cemetery near Shuanghou town, laid out in 1944 on about 1.7 hectares, and the former school buildings of the University's First Branch at Donggaozhuang village in Sunzu town. A separate memorial hall and square for the battle stands on the Fei County side of Daqing Mountain.

rows.name: Tancheng Ginkgo Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A 9.9 sq km belt of old ginkgo groves along both banks of the Yi River in south-west Tancheng, which the county government calls China's largest ancient-ginkgo area, with about 48,000 fruit-bearing trees over a century old. The main sites are the Ginkgo and Old Plum Garden in Xincun, with a ginkgo the county puts at over 3,000 years old and 41.9 m tall, a Suzhou-style garden and the ruins of the Guangfu Temple, and the Zhonghua Ginkgo Garden in Chongfang town, which grows 103 ginkgo cultivars.

rows.name: Tanguo Ancient City, Tancheng
rows.summary: Tanguo Ancient City is a modern district built in Han–Tang style on Huangting Road in Tancheng, which opened in May 2021 and draws on local stories such as Confucius's visit to the Tan ruler. The completed part has the Tan King's Palace, with live-action performances, and an 'Imperial Street' of food and shopping that includes an academy, a commandery-office hall and an intangible-heritage exhibition hall. It is a recreated old-style street, not the historic Tan capital, and suits an evening visit.

rows.name: Tiangu Natural Underground Gallery
rows.summary: Tiangu is a karst cave in Liuhuyu village, Yuandongtou town, whose stalactites are shaped like birds, animals and landscapes, hence the name 'natural underground gallery'. Above ground the site also runs rafting, grass-sliding and village-style activities.

rows.name: Tianshang Wangcheng (Royal City in the Sky)
rows.summary: Tianshang Wangcheng occupies the flat top of Jiwang Gu, a cliff-edged mesa of about 577 m with a ring of stone walls and old foundations from the Spring and Autumn period. Archaeologists found a large tomb on the summit in 2012, later named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2013, and the site now offers costumed historical performances, views over the surrounding mesas and stalls selling local snacks.

rows.name: Tianyu Natural Museum
rows.summary: Tianyu Natural Museum, opened in 2004, is a large natural-history museum in Pingyi town with 28 exhibition halls and more than 390,000 items, mainly fossils and mineral and gem specimens from different geological periods. The collection includes more than 1,100 dinosaur fossils and over 2,200 bird fossils. It is one of Pingyi's best-known attractions and suits families and anyone interested in palaeontology.

rows.name: Wuji Guigu
rows.summary: Wuji Guigu is a commercial scenic area in the hills and lake country of Zhulu town, themed on Guiguzi, the Warring States-period thinker. The Junan county government lists glass-slide rafting, boat trips on Jixin Lake and waterfalls among its attractions, and the area straddles the Linyi-Rizhao border. It suits families and groups looking for activities more than heritage.

rows.name: Xueshan Rainbow Valley
rows.summary: Xueshan Rainbow Valley is a leisure park in a wooded valley on the eastern side of Yishui town, best known for an artificial rainbow made with sprayed water and light that the park says can be seen in every season. Its other zones include a 'Lovers' Valley', a 'Happy Valley' of rides and a war-games valley, and it is aimed at families and young visitors rather than sightseers.

rows.name: Yayougou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Yayougou is a rural tourism area in the hills of Lanling County, laid out around a Yimeng stone-house village with flagstone lanes, converted guesthouses and folk performances. It also has a small animal-contact area with alpacas, deer and peacocks. It suits families and weekend visitors from Linyi and Zaozhuang.

rows.name: Yimeng Huakai Tourist Area, Yishui
rows.summary: Yimeng Huakai is a family-oriented park with an agricultural theme at Yinjiayu village in Quanzhuang town, Yishui County, which the county government lists as a 4A scenic area. Its children's area, Yaya Fantasy City, has VR games, handicraft workshops and a swing bridge.

rows.name: Yimeng Red Film and TV Base
rows.summary: The Yimeng Red Film and TV Base, also known as Hongsao Hometown Tourist Area, was set up in 2008 in Changshanzhuang village, an old stone village in Mamuchi township, as a location for filming wartime dramas; more than 400 films and series have been shot there. It now doubles as a red-tourism area with museum courtyards and live-action performances about the wartime Yimeng village women known as 'Hongsao', and villagers work there as extras.

rows.name: Yimeng Yunpu Dongtian, Fei County
rows.summary: A scenic area in Fei County laid out in four parts: the Finger-moving Stone (a balancing rock), Tianmeng Lake, the Yunpu Dongtian zone of rock formations and small waterfalls, and a water park. Paths wind through a maze of tall rock formations beside the lake, where visitors can take boats. The county describes it as a core scenic area of the Yimengshan geopark.

rows.name: Yinan Han Tombs (Beizhai)
rows.summary: A museum built over an Eastern Han tomb group at Beizhai village, near Yinan county town, which opened in 1996. The main tomb is a large multi-chamber stone tomb whose 42 carved reliefs show battles, sacrifices, processions, banquets and music-and-acrobatics scenes, and a second tomb excavated in 1994 produced more than 80 objects. The county describes it as the most complete Han tomb of its kind found in China.

rows.name: Zhisheng Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Zhisheng is a large hot-spring resort at the north-eastern edge of Yinan town, themed on Zhuge Liang, the Three Kingdoms strategist whom Yinan counts among its natives, with Han-style buildings set in a Jiangnan-style garden. It combines thermal baths, a water park, a hotel and conference facilities, and Linyi's official tourism account describes pools among flower plantings in spring. It suits visitors who want a soak after sightseeing in the Yimeng hills.

rows.name: Zhujialin Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: Zhujialin is a rural area in the hills of Andi town that Yinan County has redeveloped since 2016 as a 'pastoral complex' of themed guesthouses, a 'field living room' and flats for creative start-ups. The county has also restored hillsides, reservoirs and old irrigation channels, building 32 ponds and a 5.4 km chain of landscape waterways, and the area was named to Shandong's 2023 list of ecological tourism areas. It suits visitors who want a quiet countryside stay.

rows.name: Zhuquan Village, Yinan
rows.summary: Zhuquan ('Bamboo Spring') is an old village of stone houses built around springs and bamboo groves, renamed in the Qianlong era. From 2008 it was redeveloped as a tourist area, with the villagers rehoused in a new settlement, so it now works as a restored village resort that opened in 2009. Visitors walk the stone lanes, springs and bamboo, and can stay in village homestays.

rows.name: Badaguan
rows.summary: A district of villas and tree-lined streets between Huiquan Bay and Taiping Bay, laid out mostly in the 1930s, with some 200 buildings in the styles of more than twenty countries. Its streets are named after ancient mountain passes and are each planted with a different tree, so the area is known for blossom in spring and colour in autumn. The national heritage listing covers 236 individual buildings, including Huashi Lou, a stone mansion on the shore.

rows.name: Blue Tree Valley Youth Expo Park
rows.summary: A park of hands-on experience halls for children and teenagers in Yunshan town. The halls cover subjects such as science, electricity, weather and earthquakes, construction, traffic, fire safety and traditional crafts. It suits families with school-age children.

rows.name: Cangma Mountain Resort
rows.name_zh: 藏马山国际旅游度假区
rows.summary: A leisure resort area on the south slope of Cangma Mountain in the West Coast New Area, laid out along Kaicheng Road. Its ski slope was upgraded in 2024 with night skiing and a snow-ring run, and hosted a provincial skiing challenge in January 2025; the district's autumn 2025 tourism programme also lists a Cangma Mountain sports carnival and a flight camp. It is mainly a family leisure destination for Qingdao residents.

rows.name: Chaoliandao Lighthouse
rows.summary: A German-era lighthouse on Chaolian Island, a small island in the Yellow Sea about 31 km off the Laoshan coast, built in 1902–03 and the oldest surviving lighthouse in Qingdao. The grey sandstone tower is octagonal and joined to a stone keeper's house with a red-tiled roof and stepped gables. It was damaged in 1914 and again in 1945, repaired afterwards, and added to the national heritage list in 2019.

rows.name: Dazeshan Stone Inscriptions and Zhizang Temple Tomb Pagodas
rows.name_zh: 大泽山石刻及智藏寺墓塔林
rows.pinyin: Dàzé Shān Shíkè Jí Zhìzàng Sì Mùtǎlín
rows.summary: Zhizang Temple is a Buddhist temple on the slopes of Dazeshan, a hill area in northern Pingdu better known for its grapes, and it is surrounded by more than 300 stone inscriptions and steles from the Northern Song to the late Qing, most of them Ming and Qing. Three Ming rock carvings stand around the temple, and near the nearby Rizhao Nunnery more than 120 merit steles, mostly Qing and Republican, form a long line known as a merit-stele forest. The heritage unit also includes the temple's forest of tomb pagodas.

rows.name: Dazhu Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 65 km² in the south of the West Coast New Area, whose main peak, Dazhaiding, rises to 486 m. Shimen Temple stands on the summit among many cave shrines with Buddha figures, and the slopes are known for wild azaleas that flower in spring. With neighbouring Xiaozhu Mountain it forms the 'Shuangzhu Qianyun' view, one of the old eight sights of Jiaozhou.

rows.name: Huadong Vineyard
rows.summary: A winery estate in the Laoshan hills east of central Qingdao. The city's English tourism page lists a vineyard, a grape-culture gallery, a sculpture garden, a wine cellar and a cherry orchard among its sights. It suits visitors interested in Chinese wine who want a short trip out of the city.

rows.name: Jimo Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The site of Jimo, a walled city that was a regional centre on the Shandong peninsula from the Eastern Zhou period to the 6th century and is linked to General Tian Dan's 'fire-ox' victory over the state of Yan. About 1.1 km of the rammed-earth east wall still stands above ground, up to about 5 m high, among farmland. The heritage unit also includes the Liuqu Hills tomb group about 10 km to the north, mostly Han-period tombs.

rows.name: Langyatai
rows.summary: A coastal hill in the south of the West Coast New Area where, according to the Records of the Grand Historian, Qin Shi Huang stayed for three months in 219 BC and had a terrace built. Excavations since 2019 have uncovered a T-shaped rammed-earth platform of about 45,000 m² on the 183 m summit, with a stair of hollow bricks decorated with dragon patterns, rooms below the platform and drainage pipes. It was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013 and named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2025.

rows.name: Lingshan Bay City Balcony
rows.summary: A seafront park and bathing beach on Lingshan Bay in the West Coast New Area, laid out over about 72 hectares (1,075 mu) behind a long sandy beach. It was created in the clean-up of the bay's shoreline and is linked to a continuous coastal path for walking and cycling. Lingshan Island, the tallest island in northern China, lies about 10 km offshore.

rows.name: Maogong Mountain
rows.summary: Maogong Mountain is a hill area of about 3.2 sq km in Chengyang district, known for a natural rock about 8.3 m high that locals say resembles a standing figure of Mao Zedong in a tunic suit; villagers came across it in 2008 while building a hiking path. Footpaths lead past other named rock formations, and a corridor and wall displays along the route present Chinese Communist Party history and quotations. It is mainly a walking and local sightseeing spot.

rows.name: Mingyue Seaweed World
rows.summary: Mingyue Seaweed World is an industrial-tourism site run by the Mingyue seaweed company in the West Coast New Area, opened to visitors in June 2021. Its visit route takes in a seaweed science museum, laboratory areas, a seaweed-themed zone called the Seaweed Tribe, a health workshop and an on-site hotel. It suits families and school groups curious about how a seaweed business works.

rows.name: Old Stone Man Garden
rows.summary: A seaside park in eastern Qingdao named after the Old Stone Man, a sea stack once about 18 m high that local legend says is a fisherman turned to stone while calling for his daughter, carried off by the Dragon King's son. The stack's upper part collapsed in October 2022, so what remains is a reduced pillar. The park has sea views, green hills and bamboo, and suits a short stop on the eastern seafront.

rows.name: Qingdao Chashan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill scenic area north of Pingdu, laid out in seven zones, including children's play, eco-tourism, villa stays and a pilgrimage area, under the theme of rocks, springs, flowers and temples. A walking route of about 2.5 km runs from the entrance to Banruo Temple, a Buddhist temple built in Qing timber style, passing a well called Zhuangyuan Well and a hillside Guanyin figure shaped from planted evergreens. It suits a half-day outing from Pingdu.

rows.name: Qingdao Fantawild Dreamland
rows.summary: A theme park of nearly 700,000 m² in the Hongdao area on the north-west shore of Jiaozhou Bay, run by Fantawild. Its rides and shows retell themes from Chinese culture through film projection and interactive technology. It suits families and visitors who want a theme-park day rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qingdao Forest Wildlife World
rows.name_zh: 青岛森林野生动物世界
rows.summary: A wildlife park in the Xiaozhushan hills of the West Coast New Area, which keeps animals such as elephants and runs nature-study programmes on animal care for school groups. It stands beside Zhushan National Forest Park, and in 2025 it hosted the Qingdao launch of the Earth Day and bird-protection-week publicity campaign. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Qingdao Golden Beach Resort Area
rows.summary: A crescent-shaped beach in Huangdao more than 3,500 m long and about 300 m wide, backed by resort buildings and restaurants. Visitors come for sea views, swimming and beach activities such as sand sculpture, kite flying, speedboat rides and ocean rowing. It suits family beach days in summer.

rows.name: Qingdao Horticultural Expo Park
rows.summary: The former site of the 2014 World Horticultural Exposition, on hills around a reservoir in Licang district and covering about 190 hectares. It has themed gardens with more than 1,700 types of plants. It suits garden visitors and families for half a day.

rows.name: Qingdao Olympic Sailing Center
rows.name_zh: 青岛奥林匹克帆船中心
rows.summary: Built for the sailing events of the 2008 Olympics, this harbour and promenade of about 45 hectares on Fushan Bay is now a waterfront leisure area, with marinas, a long breakwater walk known as Lovers' Dam and the Olympic Sailing Museum, whose two-storey building holds material from the 2008 Games. Signs are in Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean, and sightseeing boats have sailed onto the bay from the harbour. The 5A scenic area is run together with Qingdao Underwater World, an aquarium on the old-town seafront.

rows.name: Qingdao Olympic Sculpture & Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 青岛奥林匹克雕塑文化园
rows.summary: A landscaped city park in Chengyang district, formerly Chengyang Century Park, turned into a sculpture park to mark the 2008 Olympic sailing events held at Qingdao. It has a World Olympic Boulevard, a China Olympic Champion Road and ten themed sculpture groups beside its main paths, with planted areas for plant study. It suits a short stop for a walk among the sculptures.

rows.name: Qingdao Polar Ocean Park
rows.summary: An ocean park on the Fushan Bay shore in Laoshan district, built around an aquarium hall of polar and marine animals that includes penguins, polar bears, dolphins and belugas. It stages shows with dolphins and belugas, and a 360-degree dome cinema was added in 2023. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Qingdao TV Tower
rows.summary: A 232 m lattice broadcasting tower completed in the mid-1990s on Taiping Hill, inside Julin Park, with an observation deck. It suits a short stop for views over the city, combined with a walk in the park.

rows.name: Qingdao Wine Museum
rows.summary: An underground museum devoted to wine on Yan'an 1st Road in Shibei district, opened in 2010 and described as the first wine-themed underground museum in mainland China. Texts, pictures, video, objects and sculptures trace the origins, development and production of wine, and there are interactive areas such as a wine bank, a world bar and cellars. It suits visitors with an interest in wine culture.

rows.name: Qingdao Yinhai International Yacht Club
rows.name_zh: 青岛银海国际游艇俱乐部
rows.summary: A yacht marina and club on the eastern stretch of Qingdao's seafront, with docks and berths, dry docks, a sailing training base, launch ramps and a clubhouse. The city's English tourism page names a site marking China's sea-level datum, a sightseeing tower and a sculpture group called Voyager among the nearby sights. It suits visitors interested in boats and the modern waterfront.

rows.name: Rose Town, Jimo
rows.summary: A rose-growing park and visitor area on farmland in Lingshan subdistrict, which opened to visitors in 2015 after rose planting began there in 2012. State media report more than 3,000 mu (about 200 hectares) of roses in over 1,200 varieties, an underground culture corridor of nearly a kilometre, and rose-based foods and cosmetics. The flowers bloom and are harvested around May, when it is busiest.

rows.name: Shaohai Scenic Area, Jiaozhou
rows.summary: A lakeside wetland park on the edge of Jiaozhou. It is listed as a national wetland park and a national water-conservancy scenic area, and takes its name from Shaohai, an old name for Jiaozhou Bay. It suits an easy walk by the water.

rows.name: Tiantai Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Wenquan on the Jimo coast, with hotel accommodation. It is a spa and leisure destination rather than a sightseeing one. It suits visitors who want a soak and a stay outside Qingdao.

rows.name: Tsingtao Beer Museum
rows.summary: A museum in the original red-brick buildings of the Tsingtao brewery, founded here in 1903 by German and British merchants and listed as a national heritage unit. It opened in 2003 as China's first beer museum and covers the history of the brewery and of brewing, with a production area, tasting of fresh beer, and holographic and projection displays. It suits anyone interested in industrial heritage or Qingdao's German past.

rows.name: World Animal Natural Ecology Museum, Qingdao Binhai University
rows.name_zh: 青岛滨海学院世界动物自然生态博物馆
rows.pinyin: Qīngdǎo Bīnhǎi Xuéyuàn Shìjiè Dòngwù Zìrán Shēngtài Bówùguǎn
rows.summary: A natural-history museum on the campus of Qingdao Binhai University, with more than 4,000 animal specimens from Africa, the Americas and elsewhere, including king cheetah, white rhinoceros, giant panda, golden eagle and crested ibis. Animals are displayed in reconstructed habitat scenes, and further sections cover marine life and the evolution of the universe. It is a national second-grade museum and a national science-education base, and suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Zhushan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested granite mountain park on Xiaozhu Mountain, whose main peak, Dading, reaches 724.9 m and which continues the Laoshan range. It became a national forest park in 2000 and, with Dazhu Mountain, forms the 'Shuangzhu Qianyun' view counted among the old eight sights of Jiaozhou. It suits walkers who want a mountain day without leaving the Qingdao area.

rows.name: Daqing Mountain, Wulian
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Daqing Mountain is a forested hill area of about 30 km² south-west of Wulian town, with gorges, caves, waterfalls and a pagoda, plus a hotel and play facilities on the upper slopes. A Taiji culture plaza hosts Taiji tournaments, including a tenth invitational event in 2026. It suits a day of hill walking and sightseeing.

rows.name: Dengshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Dengshan is a forested hill about 3 km from the coast in Hushan town, Lanshan District, with springs, bamboo groves and the Hongyun Temple. Its 'Dengshan spring dawn' is ranked first among the old Eight Views of Haiqu, an old name for the Rizhao area, and magpies are common. A snow-play park and a Spring Festival temple fair were held here in early 2026.

rows.name: Fulai Mountain
rows.summary: Fulai Mountain is a wooded hill about 300 m high west of Ju County town, with a temple complex around Dinglin Temple, traditionally the home of Liu Xie, author of the literary treatise The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons. A ginkgo beside the temple is given by local authorities as more than 4,000 years old, and the hill also has a hall shared by Buddhism, Confucianism and Daoism, a Daoist temple and a Liu Xie exhibition. It suits half a day of temples and walking.

rows.name: Fulaiqing Tea Resort
rows.summary: Fulaiqing is a tea-themed leisure resort in Xiazhuang town, Ju County, built around a large organic tea garden and a tea-culture hall, with a museum on the 'South Tea to the North' project that began in the 1950s. The Rizhao tourism bureau also lists a deer park, an artificial ski slope and summer rafting, as of 2021. It suits families and anyone curious about northern tea growing.

rows.name: Heihushan Hunting Ground
rows.summary: Heihushan is a company-run hunting ground and holiday resort in the hills of Wulian County, on the west shore of Shimuzi Reservoir. The Rizhao tourism bureau describes it as a legally registered hunting ground with game such as pheasant, wild boar and hare, and says hunting is by members' reservation only. The grounds also have lodging, meeting rooms and an agricultural sightseeing area.

rows.name: Liujiawan Tidal Flat Park
rows.summary: Liujiawan is a beach park on the coast of Taoluo town, with about 5.4 km of shoreline backed by a coastal forest belt. At low tide a broad tidal flat is exposed where visitors dig for clams, razor clams and crabs, a local pastime known as ganhai, and there are also sea bathing, sand sports and a golf practice range. It suits families wanting a half day at the seaside.

rows.name: Longmengu Mountain Resort
rows.summary: Longmengu is a 16 km² mountain-and-lake resort in Sanzhuang town, centred on a flat-topped crag, or gu, 416 m high. Rong'an Group developed it from 2003 and it opened in May 2009, with a lake, gorges and caves, and fruit picking in autumn. It suits a relaxed day out in the hills.

rows.name: Rizhao Ocean Park
rows.summary: Rizhao Ocean Park is a modern marine park on Bihai Road in the Shanhaitian resort area, made up of an aquarium and a four-seasons flower-and-bird garden. It was added to the 4A list in late 2021. It suits families looking for an indoor stop on the city's seafront.

rows.name: Rizhao Seaside National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 日照海滨国家森林公园
rows.summary: This is a coastal forest of black pine, metasequoia and locust trees planted on former salt flats from 1960, covering about 8 km² along some 7 km of sandy shoreline north of Rizhao. It was approved as a national forest park in 1992 and has a beach, cycling routes and seaside hotels, although open fires are banned throughout. It suits a day of cycling or a beach walk.

rows.name: Tiantai Mountain Sun Culture Area, Rizhao
rows.summary: Tiantai Mountain is a wooded hill, 258 m high, in Taoluo town, built up as a sun-culture park around five low peaks. According to the Rizhao tourism bureau it has three themed areas, a place of worship, a sunrise platform and a Shangshu (Book of Documents) area, and it also runs tea tastings, craft workshops and festivals such as a New Year sunrise event. A hot-spring inn is attached.

rows.name: Wanpingkou Seaside Scenic Area
rows.summary: Wanpingkou is Rizhao's main seafront leisure area, built around a sandy beach of roughly 4 km, a lagoon, several plazas, a wedding park and an RV camp. It was rebuilt in 2016 and also has attractions such as a water-slide and children's activity parks. It suits a half day by the sea close to the city centre.

rows.name: Wengweng Paradise
rows.summary: Wengweng Paradise is a bee-themed leisure park in the hills of Longshan town, Ju County, which the Rizhao tourism bureau describes as Shandong's first bee-culture experience park. It has a bee-science museum, a bee-hive maze, lavender flower fields, an organic tea garden, a lake and a children's activity camp. It was added to the 4A list in late 2021 and suits families.

rows.name: Wulian Mountain
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Wulian Mountain is a granite mountain area of about 73 km² in Wulian County, made up of Wulian Mountain itself, neighbouring Jiuxian Mountain and the Longtan gorge and lake. The main peak is 515.7 m high, and sights include rock peaks and viewpoints, the Ming-dynasty Guangming Temple, a provincial heritage site, and wild azaleas that flower in May. It suits a day of walking in hill scenery.

rows.name: Yaowangcheng Site
rows.summary: Yaowangcheng is a settlement of the Longshan culture, among the largest known in Shandong, where excavations since 1934 have found triple city walls, house foundations, burials and sacrificial platforms, and more than 10,000 objects. It is a national heritage unit (sixth batch, 2006). An archaeological site park opened on the site at the end of 2023, with an exhibition of the finds and hands-on archaeology and pottery activities.

rows.name: Baifo Mountain and Grottoes
rows.summary: A 370 m hill on the western side of Dongping, the county seat, whose cliff grottoes are centred on a Shakyamuni statue about 6.7 m high, carved in 587 in the Sui dynasty and protected as a national unit. The hill also has the Sanjiao (Three Teachings) Temple, with Buddhist, Confucian and Daoist figures, two caves called Black Cloud and White Cloud, and a landscaped park and lotus-sculpture plaza within a scenic area of about 10 square kilometres. The county rebuilt the scenic area from 2023 with a hotel and seasonal events such as an autumn chrysanthemum show, and locals traditionally climb the hill for a temple fair on the second day of the second lunar month.

rows.name: Chaoyang Cave, Taoshan
rows.summary: A natural limestone cave on the north-west cliff of the main peak of Taoshan in Hutun town, in three chambers whose walls hold Buddhist and Daoist statues and more than 80 carvings and inscriptions from the Song dynasty to the Republic. They include figures of Guan Yu with his attendants and a 1125 inscription of the words 'Kuai Zai Dong' that the national cultural heritage authority has listed among its famous ancient inscriptions. Taoshan is traditionally linked with Fan Li, the Spring and Autumn minister who became a merchant, and the cave, listed in 2019, is the first national protected unit in Feicheng that is a separate site of its own.

rows.name: Chunqiu Ancient Town
rows.summary: A newly built town in classical northern Chinese style in Feicheng's Xincheng area, on more than 400 mu (roughly 27 hectares) with about 150,000 square metres of floor space. Its theme is the Spring and Autumn period, laid out as separate Qi and Lu zones, and it combines shops, restaurants, lodging, performances and an evening street scene rather than historic buildings. It holds an annual culture and tourism festival, the twelfth edition in autumn 2025, and suits an evening stroll or meal.

rows.name: Culai Mountain Forest Hot Spring Wellness Valley
rows.name_zh: 徂徕山森林温泉康养度假谷
rows.pinyin: Cúlái Shān Sēnlín Wēnquán Kāngyǎng Dùjià Gǔ
rows.summary: A hot-spring and wellness resort in the foothills of Culai Mountain, where a Tai'an government article of 2025 says the springs stand on the site of the Tang-dynasty 'Qianfeng bath'. A winter ski ground beside it has four pistes (beginner, intermediate, advanced and snowboard) and snow-tube runs. It is a modern resort rather than a sightseeing stop, and suits a winter weekend.

rows.name: Dai Temple
rows.summary: The principal temple of the god of Mount Tai, in the old town of Tai'an at the southern foot of the mountain, where emperors held sacrifices to the mountain. The compound of about 100,000 square metres is centred on the Song-dynasty Tianzhang Hall (enlarged by imperial order in 1009), which holds a Daoist wall painting 62 m long, and the grounds also hold more than 200 stone tablets, old cypress and locust trees and the surviving fragments of the Qin-dynasty Mount Tai stele. The Tai'an Museum is housed in the temple, and many visitors come here before or after climbing the mountain.

rows.name: Dawenkou Ancient Stone Bridge
rows.summary: A long stone-slab bridge over the Dawen River on the southern edge of Dawenkou town, first built in the Longqing reign (1567–72) of the Ming dynasty. It runs for about 571 m between the town and Ningyang County, on slabs 3.5 m long and 52 cm wide laid five abreast, and the slabs still carry wheelbarrow ruts. It became a national protected unit in 2013 and is an easy stop alongside the Dawenkou Site.

rows.name: Dawenkou Site
rows.summary: The type site of the Neolithic Dawenkou culture, beside the Dawen River in Daiyue District. It was first found in 1959 and excavated three times, covers about 820,000 square metres, and was occupied through the Beixin, Dawenkou and Longshan phases, some 2,500 years in all. It now operates as the Dawenkou Archaeological Site Park, officially listed as a national archaeological site park in 2025, with a site museum, a protected display of house foundations and excavation areas.

rows.name: Dongping Lake
rows.summary: Shandong's second-largest freshwater lake, described as the surviving water of the 'eight hundred li' Liangshan marsh of the novel Water Margin and a key point on the eastern route of the South-to-North Water Transfer Project. The county government gives a total area of 627 square kilometres, of which the permanent old lake is about 209 square kilometres. Lakeside tourism around Laohu includes boat trips, reed wetlands and fish-based local food, a large double-hulled sightseeing boat added in autumn 2026, and the Great Song Never-Night City, a Song-style district with costumed night shows.

rows.name: Fantawild Adventure, Tai'an
rows.summary: A theme park of the Fantawild chain on the north-eastern side of Tai'an, opened in 2010 and built around science-fiction and fantasy themes. Its rides and shows include Dinosaur Crisis, Future Police, the Mysterious Valley and Conch Bay, together with a water-play area. It is a modern amusement park aimed at families and teenagers.

rows.name: Hongding Mountain Cliff Sutras
rows.summary: Buddhist sutra texts carved in large characters on rock faces of Hongding Mountain, covering close to 1,400 square metres and including dedications dated 563–564 in the Northern Qi dynasty, regarded as the earliest cliff sutras in Shandong. The texts include the Wenshu Prajna Sutra and the Renwang Sutra, in a bold script close to that of the Han-dynasty Zhang Qian stele. The mountain stands in Jiuxian township near the north-western shore of Dongping Lake.

rows.name: Jiliang Mountain Rock Carvings
rows.summary: Buddhist rock-cut figures on Sili hill (also called Jiliang Mountain) in Daimiao town. The county government counts more than 1,000 carved figures from the Northern Qi, Tang and Song periods, which has earned the cliff the names 'Thousand Buddha Cliff' and 'the stone-carving museum of western Shandong'. The hill is also linked in local accounts with the Water Margin story, and the carvings became a national protected unit in 2013.

rows.name: Kunlun Mountain Scenic Area, Dongping
rows.summary: A hill-and-lakeshore scenic area at Nantangzi village on the western shore of Dongping Lake, not to be confused with the Kunlun mountain range. The county government says it was developed from 2008 around film-set villages built for the new Water Margin television series (the Zhu and Song family manors), and lists a stone-carving gallery, a seven-star waterfall, the restored Yueyan Temple and later additions including a glass walkway, zip-line, rock climbing and a children's maze. The village beside it offers fishing-family stays, so it suits a relaxed rural and lake day out.

rows.name: Site of the Culai Mountain Armed Uprising
rows.name_zh: 徂徕山抗日武装起义旧址
rows.pinyin: Cúlái Shān Kàngrì Wǔzhuāng Qǐyì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A memorial site in the Culai Mountain area for the armed uprising of the winter of 1937–38. The Shandong provincial committee of the Chinese Communist Party moved to Culai Mountain in December 1937, announced an uprising on New Year's Day 1938 and formed the Shandong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrilla Fourth Detachment of the Eighth Route Army. A memorial monument stands in Culai Mountain National Forest Park, a privately run museum on the old site at Moshanyu village tells the story, and the site became a national protected unit in 2013.

rows.name: Sun Tribe
rows.summary: A theme park in Manzhuang town built around prehistoric life and the Dawenkou culture of the Tai'an area. It has a Dawenkou culture exhibition hall, a replica ancient village, rides and cinema attractions with titles such as Nuwa Mends the Sky and Ancient Battle, a live-action show about a mountain flood, and an animal park. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Taishan Baotailong Tourist Area
rows.summary: A tourist area in Qiujiadian town, east of Tai'an, built around the Tai'an Underground Dragon Palace, a show cave with stalactites, flowstone and stone columns. A Tai'an government article of 2025 says the cave stays at about 18 °C all year and that visitors can also raft about 3,000 m along an underground stream. The steady temperature makes it a comfortable stop in winter.

rows.name: Tianyi Lake
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area in Manzhuang town, south of Tai'an, that operates as the Taishan Flower Sea scenic area and has a Ferris wheel. Activities reported by the city government include nature-study sessions for school groups, seasonal themed events and an aerospace exhibition held over National Day 2024. It suits a family afternoon rather than a sightseeing visit.

rows.name: Tomb of Xiao Daheng
rows.summary: The tomb of Xiao Daheng (1532–1612), a Tai'an man who served as Ming minister of war and minister of justice. It was built on the emperor's order and finished in 1617, and is known for the stone sculpture along its approach, including a memorial archway, ornamental pillars, warriors, tigers, sheep, horses and attendants. It became a national protected unit in 2013, and a Tai'an government report of October 2024 mentions conservation work at the site.

rows.name: Wubu Stone Village (Huodamen)
rows.summary: A hill village of dry-stone houses, with more than 200 courtyards of the Ming, Qing and Republican periods and the nickname 'first stone village of Shandong'. Its 'huodamen' are family compounds in which several households share one gate, with gates inside gates and lanes inside lanes, and a stone-slab lane marks the old boundary between Tai'an and Dongping prefectures. Since 2016 the village has been renovated with craft workshops, a food street and evening events, so it is now part heritage village and part tourist village.

rows.name: Xinfu Mountain (Lotus Mountain)
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area on Xinfu Mountain, also called Lotus Mountain from its nine peaks, which rises to 994 m north-west of Xintai. A Tai'an government account of 2017 says Emperor Wu of Han built a detached palace on the mountain and that the hill's shape earned it the name 'Little Mount Tai'; the area opened to visitors in 2005 and has Guanyin-themed temple buildings, among them the Guanyin Pavilion and Taiping Chan Temple. It suits a mountain-and-temple day trip from Xintai.

rows.name: Yan Hui Temple and Yan Forest, Ningyang
rows.summary: A memorial temple and family burial grove for Yan Hui (Yan Zi), Confucius's favourite disciple, who is venerated as the 'Restored Sage' (Fusheng). The temple at Sigao village keeps Yuan-dynasty building features, described as 'the second beams do not rest on the main beam', and the protected unit also covers the Yan Forest (Yanlin), the family burial ground. It is a different site from the Yan Temple in Qufu, and became a national protected unit in 2013.

rows.name: Bailang Oasis Wetland Park
rows.summary: A long riverside wetland park on the upper Bailang River, running about 6.7 km from the Bailang River reservoir in the south to Baotong Street in the north on the western side of Weifang's urban area. It is laid out in three parts, a leisure area, a wetland science area and a cultural park, and is a national urban wetland park. It suits a walk or cycle beside the river.

rows.name: Changshan Culture Museum Park
rows.summary: This museum park lies on the northern slope of Changshan, the hill south of Zhucheng where the Song poet Su Shi came to pray for rain in 1075 while serving as the local magistrate.
