Opened around 2011 in Ming-and-Qing palace style, it has dozens of halls, a Buddhist temple and a 21.9 m seated bronze Guanyin, and it displays Buddhist statues, terracotta figures and other art from a local family's private collection. It suits visitors interested in Buddhist art who want a gentle hillside walk.

rows.name: China Gem City, Changle
rows.summary: A large gem and jewellery trading centre in Changle, the county known for its sapphires, laid out as a tourist area that includes the China Sapphire Museum. The museum has exhibits on gem types, the volcanic origin of the local sapphires, processing and gem identification, and the market halls sell sapphires, gold, jade and other jewellery. It suits visitors interested in gems or shopping, and it is a commercial centre rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Dongjiazhuang Han Pictorial Stone Tomb, Anqiu
rows.name_zh: 安丘董家庄汉画像石墓
rows.summary: A large Eastern Han tomb built from 224 stone blocks, 103 of them carved, found in 1959 and later re-erected in Anqiu town. A passage, three chambers and two side rooms carry carved scenes in several techniques, from shallow relief to openwork, including chariot processions, music and acrobatics, hunting, mythical beasts, Fuxi and Nüwa and historical stories, with three richly carved central pillars. It is of most interest to visitors with a taste for Han stone carving.

rows.name: Dongzhen Temple
rows.summary: Dongzhen Temple stands at the foot of Mount Yi (Yishan), the 'Eastern Guardian' among China's five guardian mountains, where emperors and officials sent sacrifices; a shrine to the mountain was ordered in 594, in the Sui dynasty, and the temple moved to this site in the Song. The listed site is the main hall of a compound that was rebuilt and repaired many times, nine times in the Ming alone, and a forest of stone tablets, mostly Yuan to Qing, records imperial rites, repairs and visitors' poems. A local memorial ceremony has been held again each spring since 1979.

rows.name: Fangzi German and Japanese Buildings (Fangci Town)
rows.summary: Fangci Town in Weifang's Fangzi district grew from 1898 as a railway and coal-mining town under German and then Japanese control. It keeps 166 German and Japanese buildings in a core area of 1.97 sq km, together with the 1902 railway station, the former German military headquarters, a locomotive turntable and a coal-mine site, now mixed with art spaces, shops and cafés. It suits anyone who likes industrial and early-20th-century architecture on an easy walking visit.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wang Jinmei
rows.summary: This is the former home of Wang Jinmei (1898–1925), a founder of the Chinese Communist Party and an early organiser of its Shandong branch, in the village where he was born. The house is a restored three-room dwelling with earth walls and a thatched roof, rebuilt on its old foundations in 1960 and enclosed by a wall. It has been a national heritage site since 2006 and is a modest red-tourism stop in the countryside south-west of Zhucheng.

rows.name: Happy Sea Beach, Weifang
rows.summary: An artificial sand beach about 1,600 m long on the Bohai Bay coast in Weifang's Binhai district, opened in 2012 as the city's first sea-side beach. It is set up for paddling and swimming with lifeguards, beach games and camping, with fairground-style rides along the shore. It suits families on a summer day trip.

rows.name: Jinbao Paradise, Weifang
rows.summary: A combined zoo, amusement park and botanical garden in the southern part of Weifang's urban area, opened in the 1990s on the site of a former swamp. The zoo is the main attraction, with tigers, lions, leopards, lemurs and red-crowned cranes, and there are also a children's petting area, rides and a poplar grove with hammocks. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Jingzhi Liquor City, Anqiu
rows.summary: A liquor-culture visitor area built around the Jingzhi distillery in Jingzhi town, south-east of Anqiu. The company was formed in 1948 by merging 72 village distilleries and is known for its sesame-aroma baijiu, and its traditional brewing technique is listed as national intangible cultural heritage. It is a company-run attraction for visitors interested in baijiu, not a historic site.

rows.name: Jiulongyu, Qingzhou
rows.summary: A hill resort and amusement area on the southern edge of Qingzhou, with seasonal flower fields (cherry and rape blossom in spring, sunflowers and lavender in summer, chrysanthemums in autumn), rides such as a roller coaster and carousel, a small zoo, a high-level walkway and a winter snow-and-ice park. It is a commercial leisure area aimed mainly at families, with a guesthouse in a converted village inside it. Folk performances and craft sessions are also offered.

rows.name: Judian Lake, Shouguang
rows.summary: A lake and wetland scenic area in north-west Shouguang on the remains of the ancient Judian marsh, now about 12,000 mu (some 800 hectares) of shallow water fed by four rivers and described locally as Weifang's largest natural wetland. Visitors can boat on the lake, walk a wetland corridor to watch birds and use a water-themed play area. The lake is also promoted as a red-tourism site for local revolutionary history.

rows.name: Lancui Lake Hot Spring Resort, Linqu
rows.name_zh: 揽翠湖天沐温泉度假村
rows.summary: A hot-spring and leisure resort on the eastern edge of Linqu, with a hotel, indoor and outdoor hot-spring pools, meeting rooms and restaurants. It is a commercial multi-pool resort rather than a natural hot-spring site. Weifang's tourism bureau pairs it with Mount Yi and the Shanwang fossil site on wellness routes in Linqu.

rows.name: Linhai Ecological Expo Park, Shouguang
rows.summary: A large wetland park built on saline-alkali land near the Bohai coast in north Shouguang, with lotus ponds, a long wetland water channel and lakes. Visitors can take boat rides among the lotus, which flowers in summer when a lotus festival is held, and see displays on the area's salt-making and fishing traditions. It suits a slow half-day outing rather than a sightseeing circuit.

rows.name: Longxing Temple Site, Qingzhou
rows.summary: Longxing Temple was a Buddhist temple in Qingzhou, founded in the Northern and Southern Dynasties period and later lost. In 1996 a pit near its hall base, found under a school sports field, yielded hundreds of stone Buddhist statues from the Northern Wei to the Northern Song, many still with paint and gilding. The find spot is now partly an open park, while the statues are the star exhibits of the Qingzhou Museum, so come here for the context and go to the museum for the sculpture.

rows.name: Qingshan Xiushui, Changyi
rows.summary: A leisure park made from an abandoned quarry in Changyi, developed by the Jinbao group and opened to the public in July 2015, described locally as Weifang's first scenic area built on a reclaimed mine. Its features include a bamboo grove, a swan lake, a bird garden, an animal park with African species, a lavender garden, and camping and RV grounds. It suits family days out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qingyun Mountain Folk Park, Anqiu
rows.summary: A hillside theme park on Qingyun Mountain in south-east Anqiu, billed locally as the first folk-custom park of Shandong. It is divided into a Jiangnan-style garden area, an ethnic-customs area, an animal park and an adventure valley, with attractions such as a glass skywalk, a rainbow slide, horse riding and archery. It is aimed mainly at families.

rows.name: Qingzhou Ancient City
rows.summary: A restored Ming and Qing-style old town in the centre of Qingzhou, on the site of several successive walled cities, with the open section mostly in the old Nanyang city. Its lanes and shop streets include the Ou Garden, the Zhaode ancient street, the Zhenjiao Mosque (founded in 1302, present buildings Qing), a memorial hall to the painter Li Cheng and, on Linglongshan South Road, two carved stone arches built between 1522 and 1566 in front of the site of the mansion of the Ming Prince of Heng. It is the old-town core of Qingzhou's 5A scenic area, which also takes in Yunmen Mountain and the Qingzhou Museum.

rows.name: Red Sorghum Town, Gaomi
rows.summary: Red Sorghum Town is a tourism complex in the Dongbei Township area of Gaomi, the home district of the Nobel laureate Mo Yan, whose novel Red Sorghum Family was adapted as a Zhang Yimou film and as a TV series that began shooting in Gaomi in 2013. Its main attraction is a walled film-set town built in old style, with the Shan family compound and a bandit stronghold from the TV series, and Mo Yan's former residence stands about 500 m away. It suits fans of the book and films, and families looking for a rural day out.

rows.name: Shihu Garden
rows.summary: A small private garden built in 1885 in the old Weicheng district, covering about 2,000 square metres and named 'Ten Tablets' after its modest size. Courtyards, halls, rockeries, a pond and trees are packed into the compound, which was bought by the wealthy Ding family and now houses a museum. It lies inside a restored cultural district, the 4A scenic area, and suits a short stop for a compact Qing-period garden.

rows.name: Shimenfang Scenic Area, Linqu
rows.summary: A hill scenic area west of Linqu county town, known for its autumn colour: more than 3,000 mu (about 200 hectares) of natural woodland of smoke trees and maples turn red among pines and cypresses in October. The county government and local media promote it as Linqu's main red-leaf spot. The foliage is the main reason to go, so time a visit for October.

rows.name: Shouguang Polar Ocean World
rows.summary: A marine-themed aquarium and leisure complex in Shouguang, with displays of sea and polar animals and scenery, an underwater tunnel and a children's play area. A marine theatre stages shows, including a mermaid performance. It is aimed mainly at families with young children.

rows.name: Shouguang Vegetable High-tech Demonstration Park
rows.name_zh: 寿光蔬菜高科技示范园
rows.summary: A national-level agricultural science and technology park on the east side of Shouguang, established in 2000 as the home of the Shouguang International Vegetable Sci-tech Fair, which is held every spring. Visitors walk through modern greenhouses, seedling-raising and plant-propagation demonstrations and variety displays, including a climate-controlled exhibition hall. It suits anyone curious about Shouguang's place in Chinese vegetable growing, and the fair period is the busiest.

rows.name: Taihe Mountain, Qingzhou
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 20 square kilometres in the south-western hills of Qingzhou, combining forest, valley scenery and religious sites. Its two main zones are the Tianyuan Valley, with temple buildings including the Taihe Temple, and the Huanghuaxi (Yellow Flower Stream) valley, with streams and waterfalls. It suits a day out in the hills.

rows.name: Tuoshan Grottoes
rows.summary: Tuoshan, or Camel Mountain, rises south-west of Qingzhou and carries five main grottoes with 638 Buddhist statues, carved from the Northern Zhou to the Tang along the mountain's eastern edge near the summit. The grottoes are protected by cages and the tallest figure, a seated Buddha, is over 7 m high, while the summit has Haotian Temple, a group of old buildings with a theatre, a Yuhuang hall and a Yuan-dynasty stone hall without beams. It is one of the larger groups of cliff-carved Buddhist images in Shandong and pairs well with Yunmen Mountain nearby.

rows.name: Weixian Internment Camp Site Museum
rows.name_zh: 潍县西方侨民集中营旧址博物馆
rows.pinyin: Wéixiàn Xīfāng Qiáomín Jízhōngyíng Jiùzhǐ Bówùguǎn
rows.summary: The site is an American Presbyterian mission compound founded in 1882, which the Japanese turned into an internment camp during the Second World War, holding more than 2,000 foreign civilians, including 327 children. Seven of the original buildings survive and house a museum with displays on the mission compound, the camp and the wider anti-fascist war, beside a peace park on the Yu River. Internees included the Olympic champion Eric Liddell, who died there in 1945.

rows.name: World Kite Park, Anqiu
rows.summary: A kite park in Anqiu, part of the Qilu Jiudi tourist area, which received the title 'World Kite Park' from the international kite federation in March 2024. It has a large kite-flying field, a three-storey kite culture centre with exhibition halls, flower fields and a food street, and it is the main venue of the Weifang International Kite Festival each April. Go in April for the competitions and mass kite-flying.

rows.name: Yangjiabu Folk Art Grand View Garden
rows.name_zh: 杨家埠民间艺术大观园
rows.summary: A folk-art park in Hanting district, built on the site of the old Ming and Qing village of Yangjiabu, whose woodblock New Year prints and kites are both national intangible cultural heritage. It has four zones, heritage culture, old-village culture, a folk-art old street and live-scene performances, and next to the old shop street stands a surviving group of print-workshop houses. It suits visitors interested in how New Year prints and kites are made.

rows.name: Yangtianshan National Forest Park, Qingzhou
rows.summary: A forested mountain park in the hills of south-west Qingzhou, known as a summer retreat and for its spring locust-blossom season. It has karst caves and cliffs and the Buddhist remains of the Wenshu temple, and the park offers log cabins, RV pitches and camping grounds on site. It suits a day of cool air and walking in the hills.

rows.name: Zhucheng Dinosaur Gully and Dinosaur Halls
rows.summary: Dinosaur Gully is the fossil site south-west of Zhucheng where giant hadrosaur bones were recognised in 1964, and it is now protected under shelters; its fossil corridor is about 500 m long and 30 m deep, with nearly 10,000 bones exposed in the slope. Around it the city has built halls devoted to individual dinosaurs, including a Tyrannosaur Hall about 2.5 km to the north, and a national dinosaur fossil museum was under construction on the gully site in 2025. It suits families and fossil enthusiasts who want to see bones in the rock rather than only mounted skeletons.

rows.name: Zhucheng Dinosaur Museum
rows.summary: Zhucheng Dinosaur Museum stands in Dinosaur Park on the north-western side of the city, in a pyramid-like building beside a lake. Its best-known exhibit is the skeleton of Zhuchengosaurus, a hadrosaur about 16.6 m long and 9.1 m high, dug up at Dinosaur Gully in Zhucheng. Other halls cover Cretaceous life, fossil bones and a dome-screen cinema, which makes it a good first stop for families and anyone interested in palaeontology.

rows.name: Zhucheng Zoo
rows.summary: Zhucheng Zoo is a municipal zoo on the south-eastern side of the city, with animals such as giraffes, zebras and ostriches and a petting area where visitors can feed alpacas. By summer 2026 a new intangible-heritage station offering crafts such as paper-cutting and sugar painting had opened beside the animals, and the grounds also have a Ferris wheel. It suits families with children.

rows.name: British Buildings of Weihaiwei
rows.summary: Two surviving buildings from the British lease of Weihai (1898 to 1930), a former Chinese Regiment building and a colonial official's residence dated 1900 and 1901, stand in a compound at 1 Beishan Road in central Weihai. They form one national heritage unit (seventh batch, 2013) among roughly 68 old Western-style house sites in the city, most near the seafront and on Liugong Island. It suits a short stop on a walk through the old town.

rows.name: Chengshantou Cape
rows.summary: Chengshantou is the rocky cape at the eastern tip of the Shandong Peninsula, with the sea on three sides and eroded coastal cliffs. On the headland stand the Qin Shihuang Temple, described as China's only temple to the first Qin emperor, who visited in 219 BC, and Weihai's oldest lighthouse. It suits a half day of coastal walking and sightseeing.

rows.name: Chishan Fahua Temple and Scenic Area
rows.summary: Chishan Fahua Temple is a Tang-style Buddhist temple at the foot of Red Mountain near Shidao, rebuilt in the late 1980s on the site of a temple founded in 823 by the Silla general Jang Bogo, where the Japanese monk Ennin stayed in 839. The scenic area also holds a memorial pagoda to Jang Bogo, put up in 1991, and a large statue of the Red Mountain god. The temple is promoted as a Buddhist site linking China, Korea and Japan.

rows.name: Furudonghai Cultural Park
rows.summary: Furudonghai ('fortune like the Eastern Sea') is a modern cultural-tourism complex of 1,700 mu (about 1.1 km²) inside the Silver Beach resort, themed on fortune culture, the eastward voyages and Dongyi culture. It is laid out in four zones, for a calligraphy and painting institute, a resort hotel, a yacht club and shops, with gardens of more than 200 plant species, and was rated 4A in 2017. It suits a stroll alongside a beach visit.

rows.name: Huancuilou Park
rows.summary: Huancuilou Park is a hill park in the middle of Weihai, named after the Huancui Tower, with wooded paths, viewpoints over the city and sports courts. It suits a short walk in the city centre.

rows.name: Likou Mountain
rows.summary: Likou Mountain is a range of hills with peaks above 400 m on the south-western edge of Weihai, made a provincial scenic area in 2004 and described by the city as an urban mountain park. Its orchards produce the well-known Likou peaches, and since 2024 it has added a camping base and a guesthouse street, with a visitor centre at Guangfu Temple. It was rated 4A in December 2021.

rows.name: Liucun Stone Tombs
rows.summary: Liucun Stone Tombs are a group of Yuan-dynasty tombs faced in granite blocks, in fields west of Liucun village in Rongcheng's Ningjin sub-district, built for the Cheng family who moved here from Luoyang. About ten survive, seven of them well preserved, with their stone casings intact above ground. They were repaired in 2016 and are listed by Shandong as a provincial archaeological site park.

rows.name: Liugong Island
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: Liugong Island is a pine-covered island of 3.15 km² at the mouth of Weihai Bay, the base of China's Beiyang Fleet in the 1890s and the place where the fleet was defeated in 1895, later used by Britain as a naval base. Visitors see the restored Naval Office, a war exhibition hall, the iron pier, gun batteries and museums on the island's history and the British lease. Its war sites form a national heritage unit and the island is a 5A scenic area.

rows.name: Nahaixiang Seaside Resort
rows.summary: Nahaixiang is a coastal leisure area on Huanhai Road in Rongcheng, with a long sandy beach, a pine belt and resort buildings behind it. Attractions include a Ferris wheel, beach water sports and a boat route to Jiming Island, and the Weihai city government names it among the area's places for a seaside outing. It suits a family beach day.

rows.name: Rushan Silver Beach Resort
rows.summary: Silver Beach is a seaside resort district on the south coast of the Shandong Peninsula, named for its pale sandy beaches, which the Rushan government puts at 21.7 km. Development began in 1992, it became a provincial tourist resort in 1994 and a 4A area in 2002, and hotels, apartment blocks and leisure venues now line the shore. It suits a beach holiday rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Shengjingshan Cliff Inscriptions
rows.summary: Shengjingshan is a wooded mountain in Gejia town, Wendeng District, where cliff inscriptions dating from the Jin to Yuan dynasties are protected as a national heritage unit. The mountain is associated with Quanzhen Daoism; a trail passes Daodejing text carved into the rock and reaches a bronze statue of Laozi at the summit. A district-run scenic area manages the site, with a shuttle, a reservoir boardwalk and a plaza dedicated to the seven Quanzhen masters.

rows.name: Weihai Huaxia City
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Huaxia City is a large themed scenic area in Huancui District, built from 2003 over abandoned quarries on Longshan and rated 5A in 2017. Buildings in traditional Chinese style, a Jiaodong folk-customs museum, lakes and reservoirs and a nine-bend 'lovers' street' sit among restored woodland, and a live show has been staged in a former quarry pit. It suits families and a full day out.

rows.name: Weihai International Bathing Beach
rows.summary: The International Bathing Beach is a sandy beach about 2.8 km long on Weihai's north coast, between Majia Mountain and Yandun Mountain and backed by a pine belt. The city marked out six swimming zones in 2021, and the beach has changing rooms, boat rides and amusements. It suits a half day of swimming in summer or a seafront walk at other times.

rows.name: Weihai Seafront Park Belt and Qiaoxiang Cruise
rows.name_zh: 海滨生态公园风景带·侨乡号游轮
rows.pinyin: Hǎibīn Shēngtài Gōngyuán Fēngjǐngdài · Qiáoxiāng Hào Yóulún
rows.summary: This 4A listing combines a waterfront park belt on Weihai's seafront with the Qiaoxiang, a sightseeing ship that sails on Weihai Bay. The ship's pier is on Dengta Road, next to the Liugong Island ferry terminal. It suits a short harbour cruise combined with a visit to Liugong Island.

rows.name: Weihai Tianmu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Tianmu is a hot-spring and conference resort in Zoujiachuang village, Zhangjiachan town, Wendeng District, set in wooded hills. The Wendeng tourism bureau describes a hotel with lake-view rooms, a conference centre and a spa area with 66 pools, including an indoor swimming hall and open-air hot springs. It suits an overnight hot-spring stay or a day trip.

rows.name: Xianguding Hill Park
rows.summary: Xianguding is a Daoist-themed hill park on Huanshan Road, south of central Weihai, with a temple complex, statues and small lakes among the hills. It suits a short outing from the city centre.

rows.name: Aishan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Aishan Hot Spring Resort is a hot-spring complex beside the village of Aishantang, at the foot of Mount Ai north of Qixia town, with open-air pools and resort accommodation. It is set in a rural hill landscape and suits a quiet day out or an overnight stay.

rows.name: Changdao: South and North Changshan Islands
rows.summary: Nanchangshan and Beichangshan, two linked islands in the Bohai Strait, make up the main sightseeing area of the Changdao archipelago. The north island has the tall sea cliffs of Jiuzhangya and the curving beach of Crescent Bay (Yueyawan); the south island has sea-eroded rock formations at Wangfu Reef, the folk-culture park of Xianjingyuan and Changdao town, with its small museum.

rows.name: Changyu International Wine City
rows.summary: Changyu International Wine City is the winery-tourism area of Changyu, which began making wine in Yantai in 1892, in the Yantai Economic-Technological Development Area. Its visitor core is the Changyu Castel Winery, a chateau in European style set among vineyards, with a tasting room; the wider wine city, begun in 2012, adds a large wine-production centre. It suits wine enthusiasts and anyone wanting a half-day out from Yantai.

rows.name: Changyu Wine Culture Museum
rows.summary: The museum stands on the original premises of Changyu, founded in Yantai in 1892 by the overseas Chinese businessman Zhang Bishi and regarded as the start of modern winemaking in China. Its centrepiece is the century-old underground wine cellar, a national heritage unit since 2013, where visitors can see the cellar and taste wine, while interactive displays and galleries cover the company's history, including a commemorative plate from the Panama exposition. It suits anyone interested in wine or in the history of Yantai as a treaty port.

rows.name: Cishan Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: Cishan Hot Spring Town is a hot-spring resort on the lower slopes of Cishan hill in the western part of the Yantai development zone, with hot-spring bathing, accommodation, restaurants and meeting rooms. It is one part of a larger wellness and retirement community developed by a local chemicals group. It suits a relaxing day out or a short stay from Yantai.

rows.name: Daheishan Island
rows.summary: Daheishan is a volcanic island at the western end of the Changshan Islands in the Bohai Strait, about 70 minutes by ferry from Penglai. Its main sights are the quartzite cliffs, sea caves and coastal walkway of Longzhua Shan (Dragon Claw Mountain), a national geopark site, and a long sand beach at Tuowei. At Beizhuang village the national-listed Beizhuang site is a prehistoric settlement about 6,500 years old, and the Beizhuang Prehistoric Site Museum shows finds from its excavations.

rows.name: Daji Mountain, Laizhou
rows.summary: Daji Mountain is a forested valley and peak (478 m) on the south-east edge of Laizhou that has long been a Taoist retreat associated with the Quanzhen master Qiu Chuji, and temple halls around Daji Lake, including the Taiqing Palace, were rebuilt from the early 2000s. Its cliffs carry 24 historic inscriptions, among them calligraphy cut in 512 by the Northern Wei official Zheng Daozhao, and the hills hold a Yueshi-culture site about 4,000 years old. Newer additions include a 1.6 km rafting course and, in summer, a water-jetpack show.

rows.name: Ding Family Residence, Longkou
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty courtyard compound built by the Ding family of Huang County, nicknamed 'Ding Baiwan' (Ding the Millionaire) and once counted among Shandong's richest families. Four courtyard complexes (the Aifu, Lüsu, Baosu and Chongjian halls) and a private garden survive, with 55 buildings of brick and timber. It has housed part of Longkou Museum since 1985, with period room displays and a memorial hall to Ding Foyan.

rows.name: Fujian Guild Hall, Yantai
rows.summary: The Fujian Guild Hall, also called the Tianhou Palace, is a Qing-dynasty guild hall and temple to the sea goddess Mazu (Tianhou) built by merchants from Fujian, in southern Fujian style with a gate hall, main hall, rear hall and opera stage, and richly carved in wood and stone. Unusually, it faces north towards the sea. It now houses the Yantai Folk Museum, a branch of the Yantai Museum, with displays on Mazu worship and local folk customs.

rows.name: Haichang Fisherman's Wharf
rows.summary: Despite its name, Haichang Fisherman's Wharf is a modern waterfront leisure development on a small land-tied island in Laishan district, with the sea on three sides and buildings in Victorian and Georgian-inspired style. Its main attraction is the Haichang Whale Shark Marine Park, an aquarium, and there is also an amusement area, a food court, a beach play area at the Second Bathing Beach and a pier. It suits families and an easy afternoon by the sea.

rows.name: Haiyang Tourist Resort
rows.summary: Haiyang Tourist Resort stretches along the seafront south-east of Haiyang town, centred on a long sandy beach backed by pine woodland, hotels and villas. It also has a sand-sculpture park, a wetland park and the sports venues left from the third Asian Beach Games, held here in 2012. It suits a beach holiday or a stop on a coastal road trip.

rows.name: Houji Island Lighthouse
rows.summary: Built in 1882 under a British engineer on a small uninhabited island in the Bohai Strait, this is the first lighthouse in the Miaodao (Changshan) archipelago and, according to the national heritage administration, the first modern lighthouse around the Bohai Sea. The 14-metre tower stands with an engine house, a fog-signal platform, the remains of a gun battery and former staff quarters that include a dining hall, a dance hall and a chapel, and the station keeps much of its original layout. The island, about a kilometre long, is ringed by steep cliffs.

rows.name: Jinshatan (Golden Sand Beach) Seaside Park
rows.summary: A long seaside park on Bajiao Bay (also called Taozi Bay) in Yantai's Development Zone, with a wide bathing beach of fine pale sand backed by a belt of coastal woodland. About 15 km of shoreline is divided into ten zones with plazas, boardwalks and a salt-marsh wetland park, and the bay hosts sailing regattas, a marathon and beach music festivals. It is mainly a summer swimming and promenade spot for people staying in Yantai.

rows.name: Junding Winery
rows.summary: Junding Winery is a winery estate that settled in Penglai in 2007 and is named by the Shandong tourism department among Yantai's leisure wineries for wine tourism. It lies in the Nanwang area south-east of the town and suits visitors who want to add a winery stop to Penglai's coastal sights.

rows.name: Kunlong Hot Spring
rows.summary: Kunlong Hot Spring is a hot-spring resort in Longquan town, on the northern foot of Mount Kunyu, with indoor and outdoor pools, a spa, a hotel and water-play areas. Longquan belongs to a district of long-established hot springs in the Kunyu foothills. It suits a relaxing day out or an overnight stay, particularly in cooler weather.

rows.name: Laiyang Cretaceous National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 莱阳白垩纪国家地质公园
rows.summary: This national geopark south of Laiyang protects Cretaceous rocks about 140 to 65 million years old that have yielded dinosaurs, dinosaur eggs, pterosaurs and large numbers of insects, which is why Laiyang is known as the home of Chinese dinosaurs. The geological museum, completed in 2015, has galleries on the Laiyang fauna, the dinosaur family and dinosaur eggs, and its restored skeletons include Tsintaosaurus spinorhinus, a horned duck-billed dinosaur found here that is known in China as the first dinosaur of New China.

rows.name: Luoshan Gold Culture Tourist Area, Zhaoyuan
rows.summary: The Luoshan Gold Culture Tourist Area is built around the Zhaoyuan Gold Museum, at the foot of Luoshan in a city whose gold-mining history local media put at about 2,000 years. The museum has 11 exhibition halls on the geology, mining and refining of gold, gold culture in China and abroad, and the Jiaodong gold-supply story of the war years; behind it, a former mine tunnel is set up for visitors to walk through wearing safety helmets. It suits families and anyone curious about mining.

rows.name: Mou's Manor
rows.summary: Mou's Manor is a clan estate of three groups of linked courtyard houses in the Jiaodong style, with more than 480 rooms on over 20,000 m², built by the Mou family from the Yongzheng reign of the early Qing dynasty to the 1930s. The estate's staff stage short costumed skits about the family's life for visitors. It inspired a novel and a television series about the family, and suits anyone interested in rural life in late imperial China.

rows.name: Mount Kunyu
rows.summary: Mount Kunyu is a forested granite range at the eastern end of the Shandong peninsula, rising to 923 m at Taibo Peak and regarded as the birthplace of Quanzhen Daoism in the 12th century. The visitor area is run as Kunyu Mountain National Forest Park, with separate sub-areas that include Shimenli, Jiulongchi, Wuran Temple, Yanxia Cave and Yuegu Hall. It suits hiking and temple visits from Yantai between spring and autumn.

rows.name: Muping Museum (Former Charity Home)
rows.name_zh: 牟平区博物馆（恤养院旧址）
rows.summary: The former Muping Charity Home, a complex dating from 1933 that was listed as a national heritage unit in 2019, is now the main building of Muping District Museum. Its permanent exhibition covers the history of Muping, 'the thousand-year-old county', and the collections are strongest in Neolithic finds and modern revolutionary relics, with calligraphy, paintings and stone carvings. The museum also runs two other sites in the district: the Leishenmiao battle site and a hall on the early anti-Japanese resistance in the Jiaodong peninsula.

rows.name: Nanshan Scenic Area, Longkou
rows.summary: Nanshan is a large scenic area run by the Nanshan Group in the hills south of Longkou, best known for a seated tin-bronze Buddha of about 380 tonnes that stands above a long flight of 360 steps. Beneath the Buddha's lotus base are halls and a Buddhism museum, and the grounds also hold a jade Buddha hall, the rebuilt Nanshan Chan Temple and a history park laid out along the Chinese dynasties, with a seaside resort area on the Bohai coast belonging to the same complex. Most of the buildings are modern or rebuilt, and it suits a full day out from Longkou.

rows.name: Ole Bao Dream World, Penglai
rows.summary: A theme park on the Penglai coast that opened in the mid-2010s, built in a European style and laid out in seven themed zones with more than 40 rides and attractions. It is run by the same tourism group as Sanxian Mountain and Penglai Polar Ocean World, and a separate water park of the same brand, opened in 2017, stands nearby. It suits families and teenagers rather than visitors interested in heritage.

rows.name: Penglai Polar Ocean World
rows.summary: A marine park close to Penglai Pavilion, run by the same tourism group as the Eight Immortals and Sanxian Mountain parks. It has aquarium halls and a marine theatre where dolphins perform in staged shows. It suits families with children and works as an indoor add-on to a visit to Penglai.

rows.name: Qi Jiguang's Hometown and Ancestral Temple, Penglai
rows.summary: Qi Jiguang, the Ming general famed for defending the coast against raiders, came from Dengzhou, now Penglai, and this 19,000 square metre compound in the old city centre preserves his family's quarter: the family residence, a weapons hall and the three-courtyard ancestral temple, built in 1635 as the Biaogong Temple and open to the public since 1985. Two granite memorial arches of 1565, each about 9.5 m high, stand 140 m apart at either end of Paifang Street. Qi's tomb, a restored brick vault of 1589 with stone figures, lies separately on the south slope of Zhi Hill, about 10 km from the temple.

rows.name: Taixu Palace, Qixia
rows.summary: Taixu Palace is a large Daoist temple complex on the shore of Changchun Lake, built on the former home of Qiu Chuji, the Daoist master born in Qixia who founded the Dragon Gate branch of Quanzhen Daoism. It has more than 30 halls, among them a Three Pure Ones hall that the local tourism bureau bills as the largest in China, and it hosts temple fairs around the Lunar New Year. It suits visitors interested in Daoism, and can be combined with nearby Mou's Manor.

rows.name: Wulin Christian Church, Penglai
rows.summary: Built in 1872 by the American Southern Baptist missionary Tarleton Crawford, this brick-and-timber chapel with an attached bell tower is described as the oldest surviving church in Shandong. It is linked with the missionary Lottie Moon, who worked in Dengzhou, and a memorial stele to her stands at the entrance. It is still used by the local Christian congregation.

rows.name: Yangma Island
rows.summary: Yangma Island is a low island of about 14 km² off the north coast of Muping, linked to the mainland by a bridge, with sandy and rocky shores and a long coastal park along its rocky edge. Tianma Square at the entrance is built around Qin-dynasty and horse-culture themes, since tradition says the First Emperor of Qin kept his horses here. It suits a seaside day out from Yantai.

rows.name: Yantai Hill
rows.summary: Yantai Hill is a small hill on the waterfront in the city centre, named after the beacon tower built on it in 1398 to warn of pirate raids, which gave the city its name. After Yantai was opened as a treaty port in 1861, consulates, customs offices, banks and churches were built on and around it, and the surviving group of 38 buildings, listed nationally in 2006, is described as the most complete former consular quarter in China. Some buildings now house small museums, such as the port-opening exhibition and the Bing Xin memorial hall, and the hill also has a lighthouse and a long evergreen walkway.

rows.name: Yantai West Battery
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty coastal fort on the summit of Tongshen Hill, begun in 1876, enlarged in 1887 and fitted with Krupp guns in 1899 under German engineers; the guns were removed after the 1901 Boxer Protocol. About 700 m of walls link the two surviving gun emplacements, with a gate inscribed 'Dongfan', a drill ground and a semi-underground command post, and the guns on show are replacements gathered around 1980. It is now the West Battery Defence Park, with retired military hardware added after it became a park in 1990.

rows.name: Yunfengshan and Tianzhushan Cliff Inscriptions
rows.name_zh: 云峰山、天柱山摩崖石刻
rows.pinyin: Yúnfēng Shān, Tiānzhù Shān Móyá Shíkè
rows.time_needed: Half a day (Yunfeng Mountain); a day for both sites
rows.summary: A group of Northern Wei cliff inscriptions by the calligrapher Zheng Daozhao and his son, which mark the shift of Chinese script from clerical to regular style. On Yunfeng Mountain near Laizhou, the Zheng Wengong Stele (the lower stele, dated 511) stands in a pavilion partway up the hillside, with more carvings near the summit; on Tianzhu Mountain in Pingdu, about 18 km to the south, the matching upper stele is cut into a cliff above a statue of Zheng at the foot of the hill. Both are reached on foot up stone steps, and Yunfeng is also a wooded hill with views from the top.

rows.name: Zhaotuan Landmine Warfare Site
rows.summary: Zhaotuan is a hill village in Haiyang where, during the Second Sino-Japanese War, local militia used home-made stone and iron mines against Japanese and puppet-regime troops stationed nearby, a campaign that the 1962 film Landmine Warfare drew on. Surviving traces include the Crescent Bridge minefield area and Signal Hill, which has a martyrs' monument, tombs and a pavilion. The village also has a small exhibition hall and the former homes of local militia heroes.

rows.name: Baodugu National Forest Park
rows.summary: Baodugu is a flat-topped crag about 584 m high and the centre of a national forest park in Shanting District. A stepped path climbs through woods to the summit, where an archway and a pavilion were built in 2000; in 1923 bandits who had seized a train (the Lincheng Outrage) took their hostages up here. It suits a day of hill walking from Zaozhuang.

rows.name: Biyang Ancient City Site
rows.summary: These are the earthen walls of Biyang, a small Zhou-period state that a coalition of rival states destroyed in 563 BC. The roughly rectangular city had a wall circuit of about 3.4 km and six gates found by survey, and the remains now lie in farmland near Houtang village. The local government has put up a display stele and a viewing platform on the north wall.

rows.name: Guanshi Pomegranate Garden
rows.summary: Guanshi Liuyuan is a large pomegranate orchard in the hills of Yicheng District, which local records trace back to the Western Han. Paths run among old trees, springs and viewing pavilions towards Qingtan Temple, a valley temple that the city gazetteer dates to the Tang, with blossom in May and fruit in autumn. It suits an easy day among the orchards, with markets and festivals at blossom and harvest time.

rows.name: Moon Bay Wetland Park (Yueliangwan)
rows.summary: Moon Bay is a lakeside national wetland park in Chengtou town, Shanting District, where the town has added a water-screen film show and other evening attractions. It has run light-and-fountain shows and family events in holiday seasons, including a snow-play area in winter. It suits an easy half-day outing with children rather than a sightseeing trip.

rows.name: Mozi Science and Technology Culture City
rows.summary: This district in central Tengzhou is organised around the Longquan Pagoda, an octagonal nine-storey brick-and-stone pagoda about 43 m high that the national heritage list dates to the Ming dynasty. Around it are six museums (the Tengzhou Museum and the Han Stone Reliefs Museum, both national first-class museums, plus museums on the philosopher Mozi, the craftsman Lu Ban and ink-stones, and an art museum) and a folk-culture street with a food court. It suits a half-day of Han-dynasty carved stones and local history.

rows.name: Railway Guerrillas Scenic Area
rows.summary: This is a memorial park and film-set complex on a hill in Xuecheng District, dedicated to the Railway Guerrillas, a local armed unit that fought Japanese forces on the railways around Zaozhuang. It has a 33 m memorial monument (1995) with an approach stair and a gallery of inscriptions, plus a street of Republic-era-style buildings put up as a TV-series set, where live-action battle shows are staged at holiday times. It suits visitors interested in the red-tourism theme or a family day out.

rows.name: Taierzhuang Ancient Town
rows.summary: Taierzhuang is a Grand Canal port town that was badly damaged in the 1938 battle and rebuilt in old canal-town style between 2009 and 2013, covering about 2 km². It has lanes and canal waterways with boat rides, dozens of small themed museums and evening shows, and it contains the North Mosque of 1742, one of the buildings in the national battlefield-site listing. It suits a day of wandering on foot, and the memorial hall and old railway station about 1.5 km to the west add the wartime history.

rows.name: Taierzhuang Battle Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This museum opened in 1993 to commemorate the Battle of Taierzhuang of March–April 1938, which Chinese accounts describe as the first major Chinese victory over Japanese forces in the war. Its displays include documents and relics, a film hall and a circular panorama hall that combines a painting with modelled terrain, lighting and sound to stage the street fighting. It stands about 1 km west of the old town, and the Li Zongren Museum in the old railway station is a short walk away.

rows.name: Weishan Lake Red Lotus Wetland
rows.summary: This wetland on the shore of Weishan Lake, in Tengzhou's Binhu town, is known for wild red lotus and reed beds; Tengzhou's government puts the reeds at about 30 km² and calls it a national wetland park. Visitors can take boat trips among the lotus and reeds, and the flowers bloom in summer. It suits a summer day trip, with lake-fish meals and seasonal events.

rows.name: Xiantanshan Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: Xiantanshan Hot Spring Town is a hot-spring resort in the wooded hills of Xiwangzhuang town, on the south-eastern edge of Zaozhuang. Besides the hot-spring baths, its valley park, Xiantan Mangu, has a lawn used for camping, children's activities and evening performances at holiday times. It suits a short leisure break or a relaxed local day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Xiong'er Mountain Geopark
rows.summary: This national geopark in Beizhuang town, Shanting District, centres on a limestone mesa 509 m high, one of the flat-topped crags typical of southern Shandong. Its main sight is the Shuanglong Great Rift, a deep fissure that local press says stays at about 18°C all year, together with karst caves and a geological museum opened in 2004. It suits walkers and families looking for cool shade in hot weather.

rows.name: Xue State Ancient City
rows.summary: The Xue ancient city was the capital of the state of Xue, which local accounts date from the Xia dynasty to the Warring States and where Lord Mengchang of Qi was later enfeoffed. Its rammed-earth walls run about 10.6 km round and enclose 7.4 km² of villages and farmland, and surveys found twelve gates and iron-working workshops inside. Tengzhou has landscaped a demonstration stretch of wall and is building an archaeological park, so the remains are still mostly earthen banks among villages and fields.

rows.name: Yingtai Eco Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Yingtai is a hot-spring resort in Hongxu town, south of Tengzhou city, which the Zaozhuang tourism authorities list among the city's winter hot-spring destinations. It is a leisure complex for bathing and short stays rather than a sightseeing site, and it runs seasonal hot-spring programmes around holidays. It suits a restful half-day or overnight break from Tengzhou.

rows.name: Yiyun Stone Village
rows.summary: Yiyun Stone Village is a hillside village of stone-slab houses in Shancheng subdistrict, Shanting District, restored in the old style after the original Xinglongzhuang village was relocated. The district government calls it the largest and best-preserved group of stone-slab houses in Shandong, and it now has a blacksmith's shop, an old opera stage, a stone-house memory museum and an intangible-heritage museum. It suits a half-day among traditional rural architecture.

rows.name: Zhongchenhao Kiln Site
rows.summary: Zhongchenhao is a village in Zouwu town, Xuecheng District, where a long-running pottery kiln site is protected as a national heritage unit; the list dates the kilns from the Northern and Southern Dynasties to the Qing. The village has a ceramics museum, and local authorities are developing its pottery heritage as a tourism and creative-industry asset. It suits visitors with a particular interest in Chinese ceramics.

rows.name: Zhongxing Coal Mining Company Site
rows.summary: This is the former base of the Zhongxing Coal Mining Company in Shizhong District, which the local government says was founded in 1878 and was China's first national joint-stock company. The surviving buildings include the company office block, which houses the Zhongxing Culture Museum, a steel mine headframe, the Dianguang (Electric Light) Building, a mining engineers' house and a bullet-scarred blockhouse, within a mine park. It suits visitors interested in China's early industrialisation.

rows.name: Ancient Linzi
rows.summary: Linzi was the capital of the state of Qi for centuries, and its ruins in Qidu town cover about 15 sq km, with a large city and a smaller palace city at its south-western corner. Sections of the rammed-earth walls still stand, some 5–6 m high, the remains of the 14 m-high Huangong platform mark the old palace area, and an archaeological site park at one of the drainage outlets shows the culverts that carried water out under the wall. The Qi Culture Museum and the horse pit hall, described on separate cards, show finds from the city and its tombs.

rows.name: Bashan Traditional Chinese Medicine Health Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 岜山中医药健康旅游景区
rows.summary: A traditional Chinese medicine themed visitor area in Bashan village, Yucheng town, on the northern edge of Boshan, named as one of the first demonstration bases for TCM health tourism in Shandong. Provincial tourism material published in 2023 lists a TCM culture hall (with wax figures of famous physicians, a medicinal-diet hall and an ointment-culture hall), a ceramics-and-glass base with a masters' gallery, the Moon Lake park and a cultural and sports centre.

rows.name: Boshan Ceramics and Glass Art Centre
rows.name_zh: 博山陶瓷琉璃艺术中心
rows.summary: An arts complex on Yanshan Park North Road in central Boshan, the district long known for its pottery and glass. It brings together a glass art museum, a ceramics museum, exhibition halls and a hands-on workshop area where visitors can try making pieces, plus an art hotel and a ceramics garden. It suits those who want to see Boshan's craft traditions indoors rather than at working kilns.

rows.name: Chenzhuang–Tangkou Site and Gaoqing Western Zhou Museum
rows.summary: A small site museum at Chenzhuang village in Huagou town, Gaoqing, beside the Chenzhuang–Tangkou archaeological site, which is listed nationally with dates from the Western Zhou to the Warring States. Excavations here in 2008–10 found more than 50 bronze vessels, nearly ten of them inscribed, with texts that scholars link to the founder of the state of Qi, and the museum tells the story of the site and its finds. It suits visitors interested in the early history of Qi.

rows.name: China Ancient Cart Museum
rows.summary: This museum on the east bank of the Zi River stands on the Neolithic Houli site, where a pit of buried Spring and Autumn period chariots and horses was uncovered in 1990 during construction of the Jinan–Qingdao expressway. The pit hall lies under the expressway's bridge approach and shows the remains where they were found, while a separate gallery displays 19 reconstructed vehicles from the Shang dynasty to the Qing and nearly a hundred models. It suits visitors interested in early Chinese transport or the archaeology of the Qi state.

rows.name: German and Japanese Buildings of the Zibo Mining Group
rows.name_zh: 淄博矿业集团德日建筑群
rows.summary: A group of German- and Japanese-style stone and brick buildings in Hongshan, Zichuan, built from 1904, when German interests opened the Zichuan coal mine, and extended after Japan took over the mine in 1914. A Zichuan government account counts about 18 buildings, among them offices, residences, a watchtower, a bell tower and a reinforced-concrete Shinto shrine of 1917. They are listed as a national modern-historical site and are of interest mainly for the industrial history of Shandong's coal mining.

rows.name: Guojing Liquor Culture Expo Park
rows.summary: A visitor park built around the Guojing liquor distillery on the north-eastern edge of Gaoqing town. It takes in the old Bandaojing well site, an underground store of aged baijiu, a winery museum and a traditional brewing workshop, and visitors can see parts of the modern production line. It is aimed at those curious about how Chinese grain spirit is made.

rows.name: Hongye Shiyan Scenic Area, Boshan
rows.summary: A canyon park close to Boshan, with about 95 per cent forest cover, a stone-built Ming–Qing village, a red-leaf forest that colours in autumn and a pool called Wucai Tan. Visitor additions include a suspended walkway, a glass-bottomed water slide about 2 km long, a lit 'time tunnel' and a replica of part of the Qi Great Wall. It is a leisure destination with modern attractions and is best known for its autumn colour.

rows.name: Huicun Ancient Tower
rows.summary: A courtyard complex of stone-based towers in Huicun village, Kunlun town: a four-storey main tower about 20 m high in the north, two two-storey pavilions about 15 m high on either side and a single-storey hall to the south, built of local stone and grey brick. The national heritage list dates it to the Ming dynasty, while a local account attributes it to Sun Tingquan (1613–74), an official from Boshan. It was protected as a provincial monument in 2013 and as a national heritage unit in 2019.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Cave, Boshan
rows.summary: A karst cave in the hills of Yuanquan town, south-east of Boshan, named after Tang-dynasty Kaiyuan-era inscriptions cut into its rock. The main passage is about 745 m long and up to 30 m wide and high, with stalactites, stalagmites, flowstone curtains and other formations. It is promoted as one of the finest caves in Shandong.

rows.name: Linzi Tombs (Eastern Zhou Horse Pit)
rows.summary: The Linzi tombs are more than 150 aristocratic burials from the Zhou to Han dynasties scattered around the Qi capital, many of them marked by earth mounds. The part most easily visited is the Eastern Zhou horse pit at Heyatou village, now the Duke Jing of Qi horse-pit hall, where more than 600 sacrificed horses lie in a pit about 215 m long that runs round three sides of the main tomb attributed to Duke Jing of Qi (reigned 547–490 BC).

rows.name: Mati Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park of reed beds, canals and lotus ponds on a low plain in Qifeng town, north-eastern Huantai, with about 10 sq km of core wetland. Visitors get around by small boat; the park also has a wetland museum with a 5D cinema and a shrine to five sages, and the lake is known for its lotus in summer. Local festivals include a water-wedding and lantern festival on the 15th day of the seventh lunar month.

rows.name: Pu Songling Former Residence and Liaozhai City
rows.summary: Pu Songling (1640–1715), author of the ghost and fox tales 'Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio', was born and lived in Pujiazhuang, now part of Zichuan. The museum there keeps his rebuilt family home, the Liuquan spring where tradition has him gathering stories from passers-by, his family cemetery, and exhibition rooms of manuscripts, editions and portraits. It is part of Liaozhai City, a modern themed garden of pavilions, a rebuilt temple and displays based on his stories.

rows.name: Qi Culture Museum, Linzi
rows.summary: A large museum complex in Linzi, developed from the earlier Qi State History Museum, that tells the story of the state of Qi, whose capital stood here for centuries. Its galleries run from the pre-Qi cultures through the Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods to the Jixia Academy and the Han, with a stone-carving hall and an animal-shaped bronze zun among the showpieces. A separate football museum covers cuju, the ancient ball game that Linzi promotes as the origin of football.

rows.name: Qishan Scenic Area, Zichuan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 36 sq km south of Taihe town, billed as themed on Qi culture, with a 7.5 km walking route past a waterfall, a cliff-top spot called Tangsanzhai, an old plank road and a cave called Qimen Cave. Its own account mentions traces of the Qi Great Wall and army camps, and later ties to the Ming rebel Tang Sai'er and to the Anti-Japanese War. Rafting, a slide and a children's play area have been added, and the highest point is about 868 m.

rows.name: Swan Lake Slow City, Gaoqing
rows.summary: A leisure area of lakes, reed wetland and farmland beside the Yellow River in northern Gaoqing, admitted to the international Cittaslow ('slow city') network in 2019. Facilities include lakeside walkways, bird-watching platforms, a hot-spring district and themed attractions drawing on local legend and history. It is built mainly for weekend leisure and countryside stays rather than heritage.

rows.name: Tanxishan Scenic Area, Zichuan
rows.summary: A mountain resort on the Zibo–Qingzhou border, in the Ezhuang area of Taihe town, with about nine sq km open to visitors, more than a hundred natural sights and a highest peak of 867 m. Local accounts link the hill to a Ming prince who studied in a cave and to the rebel Tang Sai'er, with an old command platform, a temple and ancient steles. The resort, which marked its 16th anniversary in 2026, also has a glass bridge, a glass-bottomed rafting course and a cliff swing.

rows.name: Wang Yuyang's Hometown, Huantai
rows.summary: The hometown of Wang Yuyang (Wang Shizhen, 1634–1711), a Qing-dynasty poet who rose to be Minister of Justice, in the old town of Xincheng, Huantai. The scenic area centres on his family residence of restored Ming–Qing courtyards, and also takes in the Zhongqin Shrine, now a memorial hall with exhibition rooms and a garden of carved stones, and the 1619 brick memorial arch known as Sishi Gongbao. The residence and the arch are both national heritage units.

rows.name: Wenchang Pavilion, Qingcheng
rows.summary: A three-storey Qing-dynasty pavilion, also called Kuixing Lou, standing at a crossroads in the old county town of Qingcheng, Gaoqing. It is about 20 m tall and rises from a 7 m brick-and-stone base pierced by a cross-shaped archway through which the two main streets pass, with green-glazed tiles and bells hanging from its eaves. Built between 1736 and 1756 and repaired in 1841, it became a martyrs' shrine in 1946.

rows.name: Xitian Temple Buddha, Linzi
rows.summary: A Northern Wei stone Buddha about 5.6 m tall, the national heritage unit known as the Xitian Temple statue, which stands north of Xiguan village in Qidu town, Linzi, and which the district government describes as the largest and most complete movable single-stone Buddha in east China. The temple that first housed it was, according to tradition, founded under the Later Zhao ruler Shi Hu, destroyed in the Yuan period and rebuilt in the Ming. The figure has a full face and a topknot of curled hair, wears a full robe and stands on a lotus base.

rows.name: Yan Wenjiang Temple
rows.summary: A temple complex at the foot of Phoenix Mountain in Boshan, dedicated to Yan Wenjiang, a legendary filial daughter-in-law who, in the story, fetched spring water from afar for her husband's parents. It has a Yuan-dynasty main hall among its three courtyards and a square spring pool at the traditional source of the Xiaofu River. The temple is the focus of an annual folk procession at the end of the fifth and sixth lunar months.

rows.name: Yiyuan Rong Cave Group
rows.summary: A cluster of Ordovician limestone caves on the southern slope of Lushan, in Nanlushan town north-west of Yiyuan, several of which are open to visitors. The best known, Jiutian Cave, runs for about 518 m through nine halls and is noted for its unusually varied crystal deposits, especially its 'stone flowers'. Nearby Qianren (Thousand-Men) Cave yielded Palaeolithic remains in 1965 and was used by the Eighth Route Army as an arsenal in 1938–39.

rows.name: Yuanshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A hilly forest park of about 1,700 hectares on the south-western edge of Boshan, approved as a national forest park in 1992. Walking routes pass the Song-dynasty Yuhuang Palace, Ming and Qing temple buildings in the woods, a field of karst boulders known as the 'stone sea' and a stretch of the Warring States Qi Great Wall. It suits an easy half-day walk from Boshan town.

rows.name: Zhoucun Ancient Commercial City
rows.summary: A preserved merchant quarter in Zhoucun District, built around Dajie (Main Street) and the silk-market and silver-market streets, with more than 50,000 sq m of Ming and Qing buildings in a 60-hectare area. Zhoucun grew into an inland trading hub and was opened as a commercial port in 1904. Today the quarter has shops, old workshops and small museums on silk, printing, tobacco and early banking, plus temple compounds and the local shaobing flatbread.

rows.name: Zibo Ceramics and Glass Museum
rows.summary: A large city museum in Zibo's cultural centre devoted to the ceramics and coloured glass (liuli) for which the city is known. Its five floors trace pottery from the Houli culture some 10,000 years ago to the Qing and Republican periods, glassware from the Western Zhou onwards, and modern work by master ceramicists and glass artists from China and abroad, with hands-on workshops. It makes a useful introduction to Zibo's craft traditions before visiting Boshan.

rows.name: Niulang Mountain, Zaozhuang
rows.summary: A hill scenic area in Shizhong District, Zaozhuang, in southern Shandong, developed by a local tourism company. Visitors walk the wooded slopes. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Huolu Valley, Anqiu
rows.summary: A mountain-valley leisure area near Anqiu, in the hills of central Shandong, developed by a local cultural company in the valley of the same name. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Cao Cao Mausoleum
rows.summary: The tomb of Cao Cao (155–220), the statesman, general and poet of the late Eastern Han, at Xigaoxue village, excavated from 2008 and confirmed by archaeologists in 2009. The Cao Cao Gaoling Ruins Museum, opened in April 2023, is a hall built over the whole site: it covers the brick tomb with its sloping entrance passage, front and rear chambers and four side rooms, together with the remains of the spirit road, the enclosure walls, ditches and buildings in front of the tomb. Its exhibition of 488 objects includes stone tablets naming 'King Wu of Wei', Cao Cao's title, and twelve pottery ding vessels of the kind reserved for an emperor.

rows.name: Chinese Ancient Chestnut Park
rows.summary: A forest park at the eastern foot of the Linlü Mountains, west of Sangyuan village in Huanghua town, laid out around a grove of old Chinese chestnut trees. The city government counts more than 3,000 old chestnut trees here, some 1,300 of them over 600 years old, set among hills and village scenery.

rows.name: Daokou Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old canal town on the Wei River, the Hua County stretch of the Grand Canal, which grew up in the Sui and Tang era of grain shipping. Along the canal the Shunhe streets and Yimian Street run for about 3 km, lined with more than 1,000 rooms of old shops and houses, mostly two-storey hard-gable buildings with grey tile roofs, a large group of Ming and Qing northern townhouses. The town is also the home of Daokou braised chicken (shaoji).

rows.name: Daxing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A solid Song-dynasty brick pagoda of seven close-set storeys on an octagonal plan, more than 20 m high, standing alone on the site of Daxing Temple north-west of Peicun village and so locally called the Peicun Pagoda. Corbelled brick eaves rest on brick brackets and lotus petals imitating timber work, and a single arched opening pierces the fourth storey on the south side.

rows.name: Gaoge Temple
rows.summary: Despite its name not a monastery but a pavilion that survives from the Ming Prince of Zhao's palace in Anyang's old town, rebuilt in 1470 and originally called the Dashi Pavilion. The pavilion, with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof of green glazed tiles, rises more than 20 m on a brick platform about 8 m high, reached by 32 stone steps between stone balustrades with carved lions and dragons; it was restored in 2023.

rows.name: Han Wang Temple and Zhoujin Hall
rows.summary: A memorial temple to Han Qi, chief minister under three Northern Song emperors, and the Zhoujin Hall he built while governing Xiangzhou, standing side by side in the south-east of Anyang's old town. The temple was rebuilt in 1298 and keeps its main hall and side rooms, while the hall, moved beside it in 1498, keeps its gates, side rooms and a book tower. The temple holds more than twenty stelae, among them the 'Record of the Zhoujin Hall', composed by Ouyang Xiu and written by the calligrapher Cai Xiang.

rows.name: Honggu Temple Pagoda and Qianfodong Grottoes
rows.name_zh: 洪谷寺塔与千佛洞石窟
rows.pinyin: Hónggǔ Sì Tǎ yǔ Qiānfó Dòng Shíkū
rows.summary: Remains of Honggu Temple on Honggu Mountain in the Linlü range south-west of Linzhou: a pagoda and the Qianfodong (Thousand Buddha Cave), whose carved Buddhas and engraved sutras include dated inscriptions of the early Tang. The mountain is traditionally associated with the landscape painter Jing Hao, whose art name was Hongguzi, 'Master of Honggu'.

rows.name: Lingquan Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: Cliff carvings around Lingquan Temple, founded in 546 as Baoshan Temple, where the slopes of Baoshan and Lanfeng hills hold more than 200 niches and relief stupas from the Eastern Wei to the Song, many of them memorials to monks and nuns, so that the valley is known as the Ten-Thousand-Buddha Gully. The highlight is the Dazhusheng Cave of 589, guarded by two carved divine kings at its door, with Buddhas on three walls and figures of 24 patriarchs of the Dharma transmission. The temple buildings are modern reconstructions.

rows.name: Ma Family Manor
rows.summary: The well-preserved mansion compound of Ma Piyao, a late-Qing governor of Guangxi and Guangdong, built from the Guangxu reign into the early Republic in Xijiang village, its courtyards covering more than 20,000 m². In May and June 1947 Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping made it the headquarters of the Shanxi–Hebei–Shandong–Henan Field Army and held the meetings here that launched the Southwest Shandong campaign; rooms in the west court display maps, lamps and other objects from that time.

rows.name: Mingfu Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda, about 40 m tall, in the Hua County seat and the only survivor of Mingfu Temple. It is listed as a Song-dynasty building; after lightning damage it was repaired in 1929 and rebuilt to seven storeys.

rows.name: National Museum of Chinese Writing
rows.summary: A national museum devoted to writing, opened in 2009 in Anyang, the city where the Shang oracle bones were found. Its main building takes the shape of an ancient character for 'city wall' and is decorated with Shang-style bronze motifs. The permanent exhibition traces the origin and evolution of Chinese characters against the world's writing systems and the scripts of China's minority peoples, with a gallery on the discovery and study of the oracle bones.

rows.name: Red Flag Canal
rows.summary: An irrigation canal cut along the cliffs of the Taihang Mountains by the people of Lin County (now Linzhou) between 1960 and 1969 to bring water from the Zhang River; the trunk canal is 70.6 km long and the whole network of branches about 1,500 km. The work cut 211 tunnels and built 151 aqueducts, and official reports put the death toll at 81. Visitors walk cliff-side stretches of the channel and see the Red Flag Canal Memorial Hall at Fenshuiling, where the trunk canal divides into three main branches; the hall, reopened in its present form in 2014, tells the story of the construction with about 320 photographs and more than 1,100 objects.

rows.name: Sanyangzhuang
rows.summary: A Han-dynasty farming village buried by a Yellow River flood about 2,000 years ago and found in 2003 while a Yellow River diversion channel was being dug at Sanyangzhuang. In a surveyed area of about 1 km², archaeologists have found more than ten farmstead courtyards with roads, ponds and fields and excavated four of them over 9,000 m², a rare intact picture of country life in the late Western and early Eastern Han. The Anyang government lists the Sanyangzhuang Han Site Museum here among the city's sights.

rows.name: Taihang Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A national geopark of sheer cliffs, terraced fields and gorges on the eastern escarpment of the Taihang Mountains west of Linzhou, covering 89 km² and stretching about 50 km from north to south, with peaks up to 1,739 m and more than 1,000 m of relief. Its main areas are the Peach Blossom Valley (Taohuagu) with its pools and waterfalls, the Taihang Tianlu cliff-top road, the Wangxiangyan cliffs and the Xianxia Valley, and activities include river rafting and a zip line.

rows.name: Tanghe National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Anyang's first national wetland park, along the Tang River west of Tangyin, with open water, wetlands and riverside paths. It lies on the central route of birds migrating through China and in winter draws flocks of waterfowl such as spot-billed ducks, teals and falcated ducks.

rows.name: Tangyin Dream Valley
rows.summary: An amusement park in Tangyin's Antang new town, between Tangyin and Anyang, built around modern rides. According to the city government it has nearly 30 large and medium rides, including a Ferris wheel, and more than 50 family attractions such as rainbow slides and a glass-floored bridge, so it suits families with children.

rows.name: Twin Stone Pagodas of Yangtai Temple
rows.summary: A pair of square stone pagodas with close-set eaves, built in 750 under the Tang, standing side by side at the site of Yangtai Temple on the north bank of the Qi River. The better-preserved west pagoda, about 3 m tall with seven tiers, is carved with Buddhas in niches, guardians, musicians, flying apsaras and dragons and bears the donor's dated inscription; the temple's other buildings are modern.

rows.name: Wanquan Lake
rows.summary: A spring-fed lake and wetland in southern Linzhou where the Qi and Xi rivers meet, named for the many springs that feed it. Paths, plank walkways over the water, bridges and pavilions link its sights, which include the old Shimen Temple and named rock formations.

rows.name: Wenfeng Pagoda in Anyang
rows.summary: The landmark of Anyang's old town, the brick pagoda of Tianning Temple, first built in 952 under the Later Zhou and 38.65 m tall, whose five storeys widen as they rise to give it an umbrella-like outline. Brick reliefs of Buddhist scenes and columns wrapped by coiled dragons ring the base, and the top carries a Tibetan-style finial added under the Qing; the temple's gate and main halls around it were partly rebuilt in 2001.

rows.name: Xiangyu Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: A factory tour at the Anyang Rehabilitation Science City, run by a maker of rehabilitation and physiotherapy equipment and rated 4A in December 2025. Visitors ride sightseeing carts through the production halls, where welding robots and laser cutters turn out some 600 kinds of rehabilitation products, and visit a rehabilitation medicine museum of nearly 6,000 m², a children's rehabilitation experience centre, a museum on mugwort and a traditional Chinese medicine wellness centre. It suits visitors interested in industry and health care rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Xiaonanhai Grottoes
rows.summary: Three small Buddhist caves cut into the limestone cliff of Guigai Hill above the Xiaonanhai spring in the Northern Qi Tianbao era (550s). The middle cave, sponsored by the eminent monk Sengchou, is the richest, with carved Buddhas and long engraved sutra texts; the east cave was moved beside it in 1999, and the group is close in style to the Xiangtangshan caves in Hebei.

rows.name: Xingyang Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty octagonal brick pagoda of seven close-set storeys, the only survivor of Xingyang Temple, founded under the Tang, at Lijiazhuang village south-west of Anyang. Brick brackets imitating timber carry each eave, and the ground-floor chamber, entered from the south, holds the stone Buddha that gives the tower its local name, the Zhangba (Eighteen-Foot) Buddha Pagoda.

rows.name: Xiuding Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: The only survivor of Xiuding Temple, founded in 494, a single-storey square pagoda of the Tang dynasty at the foot of Qingliang Mountain. Its walls are faced entirely with 3,775 relief bricks in more than 70 designs, showing curtains and tassels, guardian kings, dancers, flying figures, elephants, horses and lions, a cladding regarded as unique in China.

rows.name: Yonghe Bridge
rows.summary: A three-arch bluestone bridge, 39.5 m long, over the old course of the Huan River at Yonghe Ji village east of Anyang, whose lower structure dates from the Song and Jin and whose deck was relaid under the Ming. Dragon heads in high relief project from the piers, the arch stones are carved with clouds and dragons, heavenly horses, sea lions, oxen and sheep, and the balustrades carry historical scenes and flowers, with lions and peaches on the posts.

rows.name: Youli City
rows.summary: The site north of Tangyin held by tradition to be Youli, where the last Shang king imprisoned Ji Chang, later King Wen of Zhou, who is said to have worked out the 64 hexagrams of the Book of Changes (Yijing) here. Excavation has found deposits from the Longshan culture to the Shang and Zhou, and the site keeps Ming buildings including the Yanyi archway, the ceremonial gate, the main gate and the second hall. It holds Yijing-themed festivals and ceremonies honouring King Wen.

rows.name: Yuanlin (Tomb of Yuan Shikai)
rows.summary: The tomb of Yuan Shikai (1859–1916), the first president of the Republic of China, who tried to make himself emperor in 1915–16, built in 1916–1918 on the north bank of the Huan River. Its long axis copies the layout of Ming and Qing imperial tombs on a slightly lesser scale but mixes in Western elements: a large brick screen wall, stone bridges, a memorial archway of reinforced concrete, stone officials and animals in the dress of the time, a stele pavilion, the Jingren Hall and the tomb behind iron gates. It reopened in 2021 after its first major restoration in a century.

rows.name: Yue Fei Temple, Tangyin
rows.summary: A memorial temple in the home county of Yue Fei (1103–1142), the Song general who fought the Jurchen Jin and was put to death under a frame-up, rebuilt on this site in 1450 under the Ming and extended under the Qing. Behind the Jingzhong archway stand the gate, the imperial stele pavilion, the main hall and shrines including one showing his mother tattooing loyalty on his back and others to his sons, with walls set with inscribed stelae, among them copies of his own calligraphy. An eastern extension opened in 2014 adds museum displays on his life.

rows.name: Zhangde Prefecture City God Temple
rows.summary: The city god temple of the old Zhangde prefecture in Anyang's walled town, restored in 1369 and again in 1454 under the Ming, with five courtyards and six main halls on its axis. Restored from 1982 and now used as a museum of local folk art and customs, it gained a north gate onto the old-town streets in 2021.

rows.name: Adouzhai
rows.summary: A cypress-covered hill where, according to local legend, Liu Shan (A Dou), the last ruler of Shu Han and the man behind the saying 'too happy to think of Shu', was secretly held after his surrender to Wei. Remains of an old stockade wall, a grove of ancient cypresses, a tomb attributed to Liu Shan and the clear Jinxian River below make it a quiet walk, with flower gardens in the village at its foot.

rows.name: Bixia Palace, Xun County
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex on top of Fuqiu Hill at the south end of Xun County's old town, founded in 1542 for the goddess Bixia Yuanjun and enlarged through the Ming, Qing and Republican periods. Past the gate, opera stage and lotus pool, the main hall has carved eaves and paintings of the Twenty-four Filial Exemplars, and a triple-eaved sleeping hall closes the rear court, where a Tang stone pagoda and sutra pillar now stand. It is the focus of Xun County's large first-lunar-month temple fair, a national intangible heritage item.

rows.name: Chaoyang Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain area just west of Qi County town, best known for Chaoyang Temple, a 'hanging temple' built against the rock face, and an Eastern Wei cave carved with rows of small Buddha figures. Local tradition makes the mountain a winter retreat of the Shang king Di Xin and a place visited by Confucius, and a hill-climbing festival is held here every year.

rows.name: Dapi Mountain
rows.summary: A small hill on the eastern edge of Xun County town whose Tianning Temple shelters the Great Stone Buddha, a colossal seated Maitreya carved from the cliff, begun by most accounts in the Northern Qi and finished in the early Tang, inside a pavilion rebuilt in 1445. The hill holds hundreds of carvings and inscriptions, among them Northern Wei stone beasts, a Tang inscription in praise of the hill, a poem by the Ming philosopher Wang Yangming and calligraphy by Wang Duo. The national listing also covers the Thousand Buddha Cave on Fuqiu Hill in the old town.

rows.name: Guling Mountain
rows.summary: A Taihang mountain area north-west of Qi County promoted as a setting of the Investiture of the Gods legends and a centre of the cult of the goddess Nüwa, with a Nüwa Palace temple complex, rafting on Taigong Lake, a glass suspension bridge and a cable car towards a bronze-roofed summit shrine. A procession-style outdoor show on the Investiture of the Gods is staged daily with costumed characters around the grounds, and nearby Liangshuiquan village has been turned into guesthouses.

rows.name: Jinshan Qi River Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A riverside tourism area of about 14 km² on the Qi River in Jinshan subdistrict, Qibin district, combining the Qi River national wetland park, a Palaeogene volcanic-geology heritage park and the riverside village of Xugou, which has been developed for rural tourism with a riverbank camping ground and restaurants. It is a place for riverside walks rather than major sights, and stages costumed Book of Songs parades on holidays.

rows.name: Sangyuan Town and Taiji Bend
rows.summary: A rural resort village in the Taihang hills west of Hebi, opened in 2017, with guesthouses, a forest playground, a glass walkway, an eco-trail along the Qi River and summer water rides. Nearby the Qi River doubles back on itself between wooded hills in a bend promoted as a natural taiji, or yin-yang, symbol.

rows.name: Shilin Meeting Site
rows.summary: The village where, in June 1947, Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping held a military conference at Falong Temple while the headquarters of their Shanxi–Hebei–Shandong–Henan Field Army stayed here for 12 days during the Civil War. The temple, the courtyard used as army headquarters, the commanders' quarters and an ancient cypress have been restored with exhibitions, and in 2022 the site became Hebi's first red-tourism 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Wey State Capital Ruins
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of Zhaoge, capital of the Zhou state of Wey and traditionally also the last capital of the Shang, which enclosed a rectangular city around today's Qi County town until it was abandoned in the Western Han. Only four broken stretches of rampart survive among streets and fields, and Wey State Capital Ruins Park in the town has been laid out around the wall remains, linked to the Meishui riverside garden; the Zhaixing Terrace and Zhaoge Old Street are close by.

rows.name: Wuyan Mountain
rows.summary: A Taihang foothill in Jijiashan township, Heshan district, named for its five valleys and five rocky peaks, which tradition makes the retreat of Sun Simiao, the Tang physician revered as the King of Medicine. Paths link spots associated with him, among them his hermitage, an alchemy site, a library pavilion, a herb store, a stone mortar and an apricot grove, making it a destination for those interested in traditional Chinese medicine as much as for walkers.

rows.name: Xuantiandong Stone Pagoda
rows.summary: A square, nine-storey pagoda built entirely of stone on the north bank of the Qi River near Panshitou Reservoir, first raised in the Yuan dynasty and rebuilt in 1512–1514. Each storey is carved with rows of small Buddha niches and with guardian figures at the corners; Jin-dynasty statues of the disciples Ananda and Kasyapa found in its crypt in 1998 are now in Hebi Museum.

rows.name: Xun County Ancient Town
rows.summary: The Ming walled town of Xun County, begun in 1370 on the Wei River section of the Grand Canal and now promoted as the Liyang City cultural tourism area. A surviving stretch of wall runs along the river by the Yunxi Bridge, and inside, streets radiate from the Wenzhi Pavilion to the county yamen, the Confucian Temple, a Hanlin mansion traditionally linked to the Duanmu family and round earthen granaries of the 1950s. Evening light shows, folk performances and clay-whistle crafts keep the streets busy, above all during the great temple fair in the first lunar month.

rows.name: Yunmeng Mountain
rows.summary: A Taihang mountain valley west of Qi County, also called Qingyan Mountain, where tradition places the retreat of Guiguzi, the Warring States master of strategy said to have taught Sun Bin, Pang Juan, Su Qin and Zhang Yi. The valley's caves, waterfall and 'Five-li Ghost Valley' are promoted as China's first military academy, and its cliffs carry nationally listed inscriptions from the Song dynasty to the Republican era. Paths also climb to the Nantianmen gate, the Bagua City temple complex and a hilltop grassland.

rows.name: Zhaoge Culture Park
rows.summary: A Shang-themed cultural park on the Qi River, inspired by the Lutai site that local tradition links with the Deer Terrace where Di Xin, the last Shang king, hoarded his treasure and burned himself to death. Its centrepiece is a modern five-storey Lutai Pavilion, 38 metres high, built in Shang high-terrace style, in a park of about 25 hectares with riverside paths, a small tourist train and boat rides. It is a park for strolling rather than an archaeological display.

rows.name: Ancient City of the Yu State
rows.summary: The site of Yu, a walled town of the Western Zhou state granted to a son of King Wu, later a Han marquisate, south-east of Yutai village north of Qinyang.
