The north wall and part of the east wall of its eastern enclosure still stand 2–7 m high and up to 22 m thick, with traces of a moat outside; next to it, work on a park about the Yu clan, which traces its surname to this state, began in 2020.

rows.name: Arabic Stele at Shuinanguan Mosque
rows.summary: A bluestone stele of the Yuan dynasty or earlier, 1.8 m tall, carved with the Islamic declaration of faith in archaic Arabic script inside a circle, with lotus and peony borders on the back; it was found more than 3 m underground when the Shuinanguan Mosque in Qinyang was rebuilt. Kept at the mosque with Ming and Qing steles recording its history, it is early evidence of Muslim settlement in the area, and in 2023 it was named on the national list of famous ancient steles.

rows.name: Baijiayan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A brick pagoda of the Jin dynasty (1115–1234) that belonged to the Baijiayan temple, at Baijiayan in the Yuntai Mountain area. The level ground below the Baijiayan cliffs is said to have been one of the meeting places of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, the 3rd-century poets and recluses who lived around Shanyang.

rows.name: Beida Mosque
rows.summary: One of the largest and best-preserved historic mosque complexes in Henan, rebuilt in 1580 and enlarged under the Qing in Chinese palace style, facing east in three courtyards. Behind a gate hall roofed in peacock-blue tiles, a reception hall, two prayer halls and a vaulted rear chamber are joined under linked roofs crowded with more than 70 glazed ridge beasts, and over ten Ming and Qing steles survive.

rows.name: Chenjiagou
rows.summary: The village in Wen County where Chen Wangting created taijiquan in the late Ming, recognised by China's national martial-arts authorities in 2007 as the birthplace of the art, which UNESCO inscribed as intangible heritage in 2020. The scenic area takes in the Taijiquan Ancestral Hall, the taijiquan museum, the East Gully where the art is said to have been created, the place where Yang Luchan learned it and the Chen Zhaopi memorial garden. Taijiquan enthusiasts from around the world come to train at its many martial-arts schools.

rows.name: Cisheng Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Dawu village in the west of Wen County, first founded in the Tang, destroyed in the wars at the end of the Northern Song and rebuilt under the Yuan, from which most of its surviving buildings date. It is a rural stop for those interested in early timber architecture.

rows.name: Dangyangyu Kiln Site
rows.summary: The site of a large Song-period folk kiln at the southern edge of Dangyangyu village, known for its varied wares, especially white-slipped carved stoneware and marbled 'jiaotai' porcelain; examples are in the Palace Museum in Beijing. Part of the kiln remains is shown under a glass protective hall, and the village keeps the marbled-porcelain craft alive, now a national intangible heritage item, with a museum and working potteries beside the old kiln site.

rows.name: Dasha River Ecological Park
rows.summary: A long riverside park along the Dasha River as it runs through urban Jiaozuo, with a wide water surface that draws egrets and other wild birds, waterside paths and lawns. On the south bank, the Taihang bonsai garden, opened in 2023, is laid out as a Chinese-style garden of rockeries, a lake, pavilions and covered walkways. It suits an easy stroll rather than a full day out.

rows.name: Fucheng Shang City Site
rows.summary: An early Shang walled town of about 3,600 years ago, a square of roughly 300 m a side on a terrace at Fucheng village on the western side of Jiaozuo. Low rammed-earth walls 2–3 m high still stand on the west and north sides, and excavations inside found large rammed-earth palace foundations. It is for visitors with a keen interest in early Chinese archaeology; a site park has been planned.

rows.name: Jiaozuo Film and Television City
rows.summary: A film studio and theme park built from 1995 by the Jiaozuo government and China Central Television, with about 2.5 km² of sets in the style of Spring and Autumn, Warring States, Qin, Han and Three Kingdoms architecture. Many historical dramas were shot here; visitors walk the sets, watch staged performances and try period games such as archery and pitch-pot.

rows.name: Jiaozuo Forest Zoo
rows.summary: A zoo laid out in woodland in Jiefang district, Jiaozuo, with more than 100 species, including Siberian tigers, red pandas and meerkats. Children can feed some tame animals, and staged animal shows are held; it suits families with young children.

rows.name: Jiaying Temple (Jiayingguan)
rows.summary: A temple complex founded in 1723 on the orders of the Yongzheng Emperor as the temple of the dragon kings of the Huai, Yellow and other rivers, close to the north bank of the Yellow River. About 50 Qing buildings survive in two courtyards, among them the imperial stele pavilion, the Great King Hall and the Pavilion of Yu the Great, and it once housed the Yellow River control headquarters of Fu Zuoyi and Soviet advisers. It is a good stop for anyone interested in the long history of taming the Yellow River.

rows.name: Laojia Mogou Village
rows.summary: Mogou, a village in Xiguo town ringed by gullies on three sides, which since 2015 has been renovated in place for rural tourism under the name 'Laojia Mogou' ('Old Home Mogou'). Restored cave dwellings, many now guesthouses, line the Wenshui stream, and attractions added since 2019 include a glass footbridge and a sightseeing train round the village. It suits a relaxed rural day out with local snacks.

rows.name: Miaole Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 13-storey square brick pagoda of the dense-eave type, 34 m tall and hollow inside, first built in the Tang and rebuilt in 955 under the Later Zhou. It stands at Dongzhang village, the temple it belonged to having long disappeared.

rows.name: Mixue Daka International Tea-Drink Dream Factory
rows.name_zh: 蜜雪集团·大咖国际茶饮梦工厂
rows.pinyin: Mìxuě Jítuán Dàkā Guójì Cháyǐn Mènggōngchǎng
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism site at the central factory of Daka International, which supplies the Mixue Bingcheng chain of freshly made drinks, in Wen County. Visitors see exhibits on the history of milk tea and canned food, holographic and Hainan-themed halls and a fruit-cutting game, and can make their own drinks; it opened to visitors in early 2023 and is popular with school study tours. A 3 km 'sweet avenue' links it with Chenjiagou, the birthplace of taijiquan.

rows.name: Qinglong Palace
rows.summary: A temple to the Azure Dragon rain god at Wanhuazhuang village on the north-western edge of Wuzhi county town, founded in the Ming and rebuilt by imperial order in 1813. Its opera stage, worship hall, Jade Emperor pavilion and rear halls keep Ming and Qing steles and plaques, and a large temple fair with rain-praying rites, a provincial intangible heritage item, is held on the second day of the second lunar month; a 9.99 m bronze dragon stands on the square in front.

rows.name: Qingtianhe Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Buddhist carvings on the riverside cliffs of the Dan River north of Bo'ai, in two groups. Deep in the gorge of the Qingtianhe scenic area are a line-engraved Guanyin with sutra text and a record of road building dated 509, under the Northern Wei. Downstream at Shifotan, about 9 km north of Bo'ai town, 59 niches of Sui and Tang Buddhas line about 60 m of cliff, and some of the lowest emerge only when the water is low.

rows.name: Sansheng Pagoda of Tianning Temple
rows.summary: A 13-storey brick pagoda 32.76 m tall, built in 1171 under the Jin dynasty for the Tianning Temple, whose dense eaves taper in a smooth parabolic outline. The temple has gone, and the pagoda now stands in the grounds of the Qinyang Museum in the south-east of the old city.

rows.name: Shanling Mausoleum of Emperor Xian of Han
rows.summary: The tomb of Liu Xie, Emperor Xian, the last emperor of the Han dynasty, who abdicated in favour of Cao Pi in 220 and died in 234 as Duke of Shanyang; his empress Cao Jie, a daughter of Cao Cao, was buried with him in 260. A round earthen mound about 7 m high stands south of Guhan village, with three Qing-dynasty memorial steles and two smaller mounds nearby. It makes a short stop for those following the Three Kingdoms story.

rows.name: Shanyang Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The site of Shanyang, a walled town from the Eastern Zhou to the Northern Qi whose county became the fief of the deposed Emperor Xian of Han in 220. Sections of its rammed-earth wall still rise above ground, about 1,850 m along the north side and 1,350 m along the east, round an enclosure of some 3 km² now swallowed by the eastern part of Jiaozuo. Finds from the Han tombs around it, including a jar inscribed 'Shanyang', are in the Jiaozuo Museum.

rows.name: Shengguo Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda about 27 m tall in Xiuwu county town, first built in the Tang and rebuilt in 1097 under the Northern Song. Unusually for the region, its stairway runs partly inside the pagoda and partly along the outer wall between storeys, and its iron finial carries a 1617 inscription; the temple halls beside it were rebuilt in the 1990s.

rows.name: South–North Water Diversion Tianhe Park
rows.summary: A park running for about 10 km along both banks of the South–North Water Diversion central-route canal where it crosses urban Jiaozuo. Along it are the South–North Water Diversion branch of the National Gazetteer Museum, opened in 2021, which displays project records and machinery such as a tunnel-boring machine, as well as Jiaozuo's Fire God Temple and the Enzhou Post Station street. It suits a walk or bike ride and a close look at one of China's largest water-transfer schemes.

rows.name: Taiping Temple Grottoes, Zhaijian Valley
rows.summary: Buddhist caves and niches cut along about 160 m of limestone cliff in Zhaijian Valley, west of the main peak of Shennong Mountain, begun in the Northern Wei and added to until the Qing, though mostly Sui and Tang. The Thousand Buddha Cave is lined with small niches labelled with Buddha names, and six larger niches include a 3.4 m standing Medicine Buddha with an inscription of 861; three Buddha heads have been stolen since 1994.

rows.name: Thousand Buddha Pavilion, Wuzhi
rows.summary: A temple group at the north end of South Street in Wuzhi county town, founded in 1557 under the Ming and repaired in 1856, of which the gate hall, the middle Buddha hall and the pavilion itself survive. The pavilion, about 18 m high with three tiers of green-glazed eaves, rests on load-bearing brick walls, and the three buildings are not set on a single axis.

rows.name: Tomb of Han Yu
rows.summary: The tomb of Han Yu (768–824), the Tang essayist, poet and Confucian thinker counted first of the Eight Great Prose Masters of the Tang and Song, on a hillside at Hanzhuang village west of Mengzhou. A mound more than 10 m high stands behind an ancestral hall and offering hall that hold 13 steles on his life, within a memorial park with a gateway, spirit way and exhibition hall.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhu Zaiyu
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhu Zaiyu (1536–1611), the Ming prince, mathematician and music theorist who in 1584 set out twelve-tone equal temperament by precise calculation, below Jiufeng Mountain north-east of Qinyang. A low mound about 2.5 m high stands at the end of a 126 m spirit way, beside a corridor of more than 50 m of inscriptions by modern musicologists, dancers, poets and calligraphers; fragments of his 1624 spirit-way stele are kept in the Zhu Zaiyu Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Xianshengwang Temple
rows.summary: A village temple on the southern edge of Mengzhou whose three-bay main hall dates from the Yuan dynasty, with Qing-dynasty dance and opera stages in front. The temple was moved here in 1759 after Yellow River floods, and the hall keeps early timber techniques such as an interior without inner columns and differing brackets on its front and rear eaves.

rows.name: Xidajing 1919 Cultural Tourism Park
rows.summary: A culture and leisure park on the site of the Wangfeng coal mine, known locally as Xidajing ('West Big Shaft'), which the British-owned Pekin Syndicate began building in 1919. The English-built pithead frame still stands beside a square on the site of the 1925 coal miners' strike, close to the former office of the Jiaozuo mining district people's committee, with a themed street and a mine archive hall nearby. It doubles as a red-education base, with exhibitions and short dramas on the history of the Jiaozuo coal miners.

rows.name: Xiguan Mosque, Bo'ai
rows.summary: A mosque in Chinese palace style in the western quarter of Bo'ai county town, enlarged in 1405, whose surviving buildings date from the Qing. Its two-storey gate tower, prayer hall and main hall are roofed in blue glazed tiles, and the brick screen wall and woodwork are carved with peonies, lotuses and chrysanthemums.

rows.name: Yaowang Temple, Jiaozuo
rows.summary: A temple to Sun Simiao, the Tang physician revered as the King of Medicine, at Liguizuo village on the north-eastern edge of Jiaozuo; inscriptions record its founding in the early 12th century, and its main hall dates from the Yuan dynasty. The old hall, restored in 2021, stands among halls rebuilt in 2005–2008, and the courtyard keeps an old cypress, a well and a stele pierced with round and square holes; the temple long served the local trade in Huaiqing medicinal herbs.

rows.name: Yuanrong Temple
rows.summary: An active Buddhist temple in the foothills of the Taihang Mountains at Dangyangyu village, Xiuwu County, just north of Jiaozuo. It is run as a scenic area rather than as a listed monument, and it lies about 1 km from the Dangyangyu kiln site, so the two can be visited together.

rows.name: Yuntai Mountain
rows.summary: A 190 km² scenic area of red-rock gorges, sheer cliff walls, waterfalls and pools in the southern Taihang Mountains, part of the Yuntai Mountain UNESCO Global Geopark, rising to 1,308 m at Zhuyu Peak. Besides gorges such as Red Stone Gorge it takes in the Fenglin Gorge reservoir behind a 100 m stone arch dam, the 4 km Zifang Lake and a valley of wild Taihang macaques. The same 5A listing covers Shennong Mountain in Qinyang and the Qingtianhe gorges in Bo'ai, which make further day trips.

rows.name: Yuxian Temple, Wen County
rows.summary: A Taoist temple of two courtyards below the Qin River dyke at Xubu village, about 12 km from Wen county town, founded under the Yuan as a river-god shrine and rebuilt in the Ming and Qing. On its axis stand the gate, the Jade Emperor Hall of 1527 and the Hall of the Three Pure Ones under green glazed tiles, flanked by smaller side shrines and a bell tower.

rows.name: Zhaibuchang Village
rows.summary: A fortified village of Ming and Qing courtyard houses, most built in the 18th and 19th centuries, with the Wang clan ancestral hall, about 2 km of the village wall of 1868, a moat and three stone bridges. The houses are decorated with carved brick, stone and wood, and the courtyard that served as headquarters of the Ninth Column of the Shanxi–Hebei–Shandong–Henan Field Army, founded here in 1947, holds a military history display.

rows.name: Ancient City of Zhi
rows.summary: The walled town of Zhi, founded in the Spring and Autumn period and later the seat of Han and Northern dynasties lords, whose rammed-earth ramparts enclose the modern town of Zhicheng south of Jiyuan. The walls, roughly 2 km on each side, survive best on the east and south, where stretches still stand 1–9 m high among the fields; Daming Temple and the Guandi Temple are in the same town.

rows.name: Daming Temple, Jiyuan
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Zhicheng, south of Jiyuan, on the site of an ancestral shrine of the Western Han lords of Zhi; it became a monastery in 1040 and was rebuilt over thirty years from 1276. Thirteen Yuan, Ming and Qing buildings stand on a three-courtyard axis, and the Yuan middle Buddha hall is one of only four Yuan wooden halls left in Henan, with an ancient tree spreading in front of it.

rows.name: Erxian Temple, Jiyuan
rows.summary: A Ming and Qing temple at Daxu village in Lilin, north-east of Jiyuan, dedicated to Wei Huacun, a Western Jin Taoist woman venerated as the Lady of the Purple Void. Four halls, among them the Zixu Yuanjun Hall and the Jingying Hall, stand on one axis in a compound about 111 m long with a dozen old steles.

rows.name: Fengxian Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple in central Jiyuan founded in 685, whose Sanqing Hall, rebuilt in 1184 under the Jin dynasty, is one of the three oldest wooden buildings in Henan. The hall is a classic example of 'reduced-column' framing, with only two of its eight interior columns kept, and its huge beams of thorn-wood root gave the temple its popular name, Jingliang Guan; a Tang stele with an image of Laozi stands in front.

rows.name: Guandi Temple, Zhicheng
rows.summary: A temple to Guan Yu, the deified Three Kingdoms general, in Zhicheng town south of Jiyuan. Its buildings date from the Jin dynasty (12th–13th century) and the Qing, and it is counted among Jiyuan's group of early wooden buildings, alongside the Jidu Temple and Daming Temple.

rows.name: Jidu Temple
rows.summary: The temple of the god of the Ji, one of the four great rivers of ancient China, founded in 582 at the river's eastern spring and the largest and most complete of the temples to the Four Rivers. Twenty-three buildings from the Song to the Qing stand on three axes, including a rear hall of 973 that is the oldest wooden building in Henan, a Ming wooden archway gate and the spring-fed pools of the Beihai Shrine with a Song stone balustrade. It is the core of the Jishui Source cultural tourism area, which also takes in Longquan Lake and a peony garden.

rows.name: Mount Wangwu
rows.summary: A Taoist mountain north-west of Jiyuan, ranked first of the Ten Grotto-Heavens of Taoism and the setting of the fable of the Foolish Old Man who moved the mountains. A stepped pilgrim path and a cableway climb to Tiantan Peak (1,715 m), where the Yellow Emperor is said to have sacrificed to Heaven. Near the entrance stands Yangtai Palace, built in 724–727 for the Taoist master Sima Chengzhen, whose Ming Sanqing Hall and three-storey Yuhuang Pavilion have stone columns carved with Taoist figures and stories.

rows.name: Wulongkou Scenic Area
rows.summary: The gorge where the Qin River breaks out of the Taihang Mountains north-east of Jiyuan, home to a national nature reserve for Taihang macaques and to some of China's oldest irrigation works. Water has been drawn off here since the Qin dynasty, and the Ming tunnel intakes of the Yongli and Guangji canals survive, topped by shrines with stone statues of the officials who built them. Monkeys roam the slopes, and the scenic area also has hot springs and a gallery for the landscape painter Jing Hao.

rows.name: Xiaogoubei–Yinhe Gorge Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley at Shaoyuan in the far west of Jiyuan, known for volcanic-rock scenery: a streambed full of multicoloured boulders, a long ridge said to look like a giant turtle and a cliff of pale rock shapes nicknamed 'baby cliff'. Local legend makes it the place where the goddess Nüwa melted coloured stones to mend the sky, and walkways follow the stream past pools and falls; the scenic area runs a water-splashing festival in summer and an ice-fall festival in winter.

rows.name: Yanqing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song brick pagoda on the north-western edge of Jiyuan, built in 1034–1036 on the site of Yanqing Temple beside the Longtan spring, the western source of the ancient Ji River. Six-sided, seven storeys and about 28 m tall, it is decorated with more than a thousand bricks carved with Buddha figures, and an internal stair winds up to the sixth storey; a Song stele inside records its building.

rows.name: Yellow River Three Gorges
rows.summary: A stretch of the Yellow River at Xiaye in south-western Jiyuan, where the reservoir upstream of the Xiaolangdi Dam fills three gorges, Gushan, Longfeng and Bali, between steep peaks. Boat trips run through the gorges, a cableway climbs to the Xuantian karst cave and Taohua Island gives views over the water, and a 6 km rafting run operates in summer.

rows.name: Aisijia Agricultural Carnival
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park in the countryside south-west of Kaifeng, built around six themed exhibition halls on modern farming. Outdoors it has a children's farm, flower fields and play areas, including an adventure playground without powered rides. It suits families with young children.

rows.name: China Hanyuan Stele Forest
rows.summary: A garden of modern stone inscriptions just west of Dragon Pavilion Park, founded in 1985 by the retired Kaifeng official Li Gongtao and built up largely with his own family's money. Long covered corridors display calligraphy, paintings and seal carving cut in stone, arranged in sections for Song-dynasty texts, emperors and statesmen, ethnic-minority scripts and international friendship, set among classical garden buildings. It appeals mainly to visitors interested in Chinese calligraphy.

rows.name: Daxiangguo Temple
rows.summary: A large Buddhist temple in the centre of Kaifeng, with roots in the 6th century, refounded in 706 and renamed Daxiangguo Temple in 712, which under the Northern Song was the capital's leading monastery and a major trading market. Flooded in 1642 and rebuilt under the Qing, it keeps an octagonal Glazed Hall with a four-faced, thousand-armed Guanyin, the only image to survive when the temple was turned into a market in 1927. The temple's Buddhist music is listed as national intangible heritage, and a statue recalls the Water Margin hero Lu Zhishen uprooting a willow here.

rows.name: Dayun Temple Pagoda, Qi County
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda of the Ming dynasty at Wagang village, south of Qi County town, the surviving landmark of the former Dayun Temple. Each storey is marked by brick eaves, and the pagoda stands on its own in a fenced enclosure. It was listed as a national monument in 2019 and is a quick stop for pagoda enthusiasts touring the countryside of eastern Henan.

rows.name: Dongda Mosque, Kaifeng
rows.summary: The principal mosque of Kaifeng's Hui Muslim community, first of the city's 'thirteen mosques' and historically called the leading mosque of Henan. The present buildings date from a rebuilding of 1655 and a restoration of 1846, arranged in three courtyards with a screen wall, gates, side halls, a prayer hall with a rolled roof and a lecture hall, and a women's mosque stands across the street. It is an active place of worship in the old Hui quarter east of the centre.

rows.name: Dragon Pavilion
rows.summary: A Qing palace-style hall raised on a brick platform of 72 steps on the site of the Northern Song imperial palace in the north of Kaifeng's old city. The platform began as an artificial hill in the garden of the Ming princes of Zhou, and the hall, built in the 18th century and rebuilt to the old design in 1856, faces an avenue between Panjia and Yangjia lakes, in a park whose gates have been rebuilt since 1985. The park also marks the sites of the Song palace walls and of its Daqing Hall.

rows.name: Former Residence of Liu Qingxia
rows.summary: The Kaifeng home of Liu Qingxia (1877–1922), a wealthy supporter of the Tongmenghui and of education, who funded revolutionaries and the Henan magazine published in Tokyo, founded Henan's first girls' school and in 1922 gave her family fortune to education. Built in 1880, the house is two parallel three-courtyard compounds with carved doorways, now a memorial museum with displays on her life and on the 1911 Revolution in Henan. The national listing also covers two of her family's courtyard houses in Weishi county town.

rows.name: Henan University Historic Buildings
rows.name_zh: 河南留学欧美预备学校旧址
rows.pinyin: Hénán Liúxué Ōu-Měi Yùbèi Xuéxiào Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The early buildings of Henan University, founded in 1912 as the Henan Preparatory School for Study in Europe and America, on its old Minglun campus beside the Iron Pagoda. Some sixteen buildings of the 1910s to 1930s combine Chinese roofs and bracket sets with Western columns and detailing, among them Building No. 6 of 1919, the Boya Building of 1925 and the archway-style south gate of 1936, and the campus also keeps steles of the old Henan examination hall. The great auditorium of 1934 was gutted by fire in May 2024 during restoration works, and a repair contract was let in late 2025.

rows.name: Jiao Yulu Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park on the old Yellow River dyke at the northern edge of Lankao town for Jiao Yulu, the county's Communist Party secretary from 1962 until his death in 1964, who led local campaigns against drifting sand, waterlogging and salinised soil. It holds his white-marble tomb, where he was reburied in 1966 at his own request, a memorial hall opened in 1994 with exhibits on his life, a monument to revolutionary martyrs and a grove of paulownia trees. It is a national patriotic-education base and receives many Communist Party delegations.

rows.name: Kaifeng City Wall
rows.summary: Kaifeng's Qing-dynasty city wall, rebuilt in grey brick in 1842 after a Yellow River flood, still runs for 14.4 km around the old city and is among the longest surviving city walls in China. Its circuit goes back to the Tang city of Bianzhou, rebuilt in 781, and roughly matches the inner city of the Northern Song capital. Its gate towers are modern reconstructions, the best known being the Daliang Gate on the west side, rebuilt in 1998.

rows.name: Kaifeng Parachute Tower
rows.summary: A reinforced-concrete tower about 85 m tall, built in 1955–56 to train airborne troops and sport parachutists, who were hoisted beneath open canopies and released from three cantilevered platforms near the top. It ends in a lotus-shaped crown with a star-shaped lightning rod and fell out of use as jumps from aircraft took over. Since 2021 it has been the centre of a national-defence education base with an exhibition hall and a display of military equipment.

rows.name: Kaifeng Prefecture Office (Kaifeng Fu)
rows.summary: A modern reconstruction of the government office of Kaifeng Prefecture, which ran the Northern Song capital and where Bao Zheng, the 'Judge Bao' of later legend, served as prefect. It was built following the Song building manual Yingzao Fashi as a large complex of halls and courtyards on the north shore of Baogong Lake. It suits visitors interested in Song government and the Judge Bao stories, and pairs with the Lord Bao Memorial Temple across the lake.

rows.name: Lord Bao Memorial Temple, Kaifeng
rows.summary: A memorial temple to Bao Zheng (999–1062), the Northern Song official who became China's byword for incorruptible justice as 'Judge Bao' of opera and television. Rebuilt in 1984 on the west shore of Baogong Lake on the site of a temple first raised under the Jin and Yuan, it has gates, a screen wall, a stele pavilion and halls that tell his life with a bronze statue, wax figures, models, rubbings and inscriptions. It pairs naturally with the rebuilt Kaifeng Prefecture office across the lake.

rows.name: Po Pagoda
rows.summary: The oldest standing building in Kaifeng, a Northern Song brick pagoda begun in the 970s for Tianqing Temple on the Fan Terrace beside Yuwangtai and finished around 990 after some twenty years of work. Only three massive storeys remain below a small seven-tier pagoda added on top in the early Qing, giving it a squat, bell-like outline; its outer walls are set with dozens of kinds of moulded Buddha bricks, and sutras and donors' names are carved inside. Tradition says the upper storeys were pulled down in the early Ming, though one recent study argues the present shape is close to the original.

rows.name: Qifeng Old Garden, Zhuxian
rows.summary: A modern scenic area in old-town style at Zhuxian, one of the four great trading towns of Qing China, with a lake, bridges, a gate tower, a teahouse and shops built in traditional style. It is a place for a stroll and for Zhuxian's woodblock New Year prints, a national intangible-heritage craft. The historic Yue Fei Temple and Zhuxian Mosque are nearby in the town.

rows.name: Qingming Shanghe Park
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty theme park opened in 1998 on the west shore of Longting Lake, built after Zhang Zeduan's 12th-century scroll Along the River During the Qingming Festival and the Song building manual Yingzao Fashi. The southern part recreates the scroll's street life around a copy of its Rainbow Bridge, with craft workshops, food stalls and costumed performances such as Kaifeng drum troupes, while the northern part is laid out as an imperial garden round a lake. It is a staged, crowd-pleasing picture of Song city life rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Shanshangan Guild Hall
rows.summary: A guild hall built in 1776 by merchants from Shanxi, Shaanxi and Gansu living in Kaifeng, on the site of a Ming mansion of the descendants of the general Xu Da. It is famous for its carving in wood, stone and brick, best seen on the screen wall, the only old opera stage left in Kaifeng, a six-pillared green-tiled archway and the main hall to Guan Yu with seven tiers of wooden carving under its eaves. On the main hall's gables the merchants inscribed their mottos, 'fair trade' and 'profit through righteousness'.

rows.name: Site of Dongjing, the Northern Song Capital
rows.summary: The remains of Dongjing, capital of the Northern Song from 960 to 1127, lie buried under modern Kaifeng beneath the silt of later Yellow River floods. In the city centre the excavated Zhouqiao bridge and Bian River site, with a Ming arch bridge on Song foundations and Northern Song stone river walls carved with sea horses, cranes and clouds, is open as a public archaeology site. The pits reach the Song river banks about 10 m below today's streets, showing how deep the old capital lies.

rows.name: Tianbo Yang Mansion
rows.summary: A Song-style complex built in the 1990s beside the lakes of the Dragon Pavilion area, recreating the mansion of the Yang family generals, whose wars against the Liao are retold in the popular Generals of the Yang Family stories. It has a mock government office with a tower and halls of sculpted scenes from the stories, a family temple, a garden and a drill ground used for costumed shows. It suits visitors who know the Yang family tales from opera or television.

rows.name: Wansui Mountain Wuxia City
rows.summary: A martial-arts-themed park on the northern edge of Kaifeng's old city, run as a scenic area since 2003 and renamed Wansui Mountain Wuxia City in December 2023. Costumed performers stage shows across its old-style streets and arenas throughout the day, and one street skit, a matchmaking scene starring the character Wang Po, went viral on Douyin in 2024 and made the park famous across China. It suits families and anyone after lively entertainment rather than history.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple Pagoda, Weishi
rows.summary: A hexagonal brick pagoda of eight storeys, about 30 m tall, first built in the Taiping Xingguo era of the early Northern Song as the relic pagoda of Xingguo Temple, known locally as the Dongguan (East Suburb) Pagoda. Its upper three storeys were rebuilt in 1546, and its walls inside and out hold some 410 Buddha niches, with a spiral stair round a central column. Flood silt has buried the base, so the entrance now lies slightly below ground level.

rows.name: Yanqing Temple (Jade Emperor Pavilion)
rows.summary: A Taoist temple of the Quanzhen school founded in 1233 where its founder Wang Chongyang died in 1170, renamed Yanqing Guan in 1373 and repeatedly destroyed by floods and war. Its one old building is the Jade Emperor Pavilion, an 18 m brick tower imitating timber in Yuan style, square below with a domed, yurt-like chamber holding a bronze statue of Zhenwu, and an eight-sided pavilion on top sheltering a white-marble Jade Emperor. Sunk in a waterlogged pit after it was dug out of flood silt in 1984, the pavilion was jacked up by more than 3 m in 2010, and an exhibition hall beneath it explains the temple's history and the lifting.

rows.name: Yellow River Bend Scenic Area, Lankao
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area at Dongbatou, where the Yellow River makes the last great bend of its course before turning north-east to the sea, and where in 1855 it burst its dyke and abandoned its old course to the south. Laid out along the levees and the Dongbatou river-training works, it has riverside walking paths, a tourist train on the old Lankao–Dongbatou railway line, an exhibition hall, a camper-van site and wetland where water birds gather. A memorial pavilion marks Mao Zedong's inspections of the river here in the 1950s, and the area is linked with Jiao Yulu's campaign against the county's drifting sand.

rows.name: Yue Fei Temple, Zhuxian
rows.summary: A temple to the Southern Song general Yue Fei, founded in 1478 at Zhuxian, the town his army reached after defeating the Jin at Yancheng, and regarded as one of China's principal Yue Fei temples. Behind the gate are a worship pavilion facing iron kneeling figures of Qin Hui and the others blamed for his death, a main hall with a seated statue of Yue Fei, stele pavilions carved with poems attributed to him including Man Jiang Hong, and a rear hall with bronze figures of Yue Fei and his wife. The listed site also includes a temple to Guan Yu.

rows.name: Zhuxian Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque founded in the Ming and rebuilt in 1738, a reminder that Zhuxian's Ming and Qing trade drew Hui merchants who built several mosques in the town. Its east-facing gate stands on stone columns carved with landscapes and couplets beneath dense wood carving of dragons, phoenixes, lions and leaping carp, and the prayer hall is formed by two linked buildings under green glazed tiles. Two stele pavilions keep Qing inscriptions, one of them in Arabic dated 1805.

rows.name: Bi'an Temple Stele
rows.summary: A Northern Song stone pillar from the vanished Bi'an Temple, known locally as the 'Dragon Pagoda', made up of a carved image section, a panel of seal-script text and a base carried on eight openwork columns carved with coiling dragons. It stands under a pavilion on a brick platform in the grounds of a middle school on Haihe Road.

rows.name: Jiahu Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The baijiu distillery and visitor park of the Jiahu liquor company in Wuyang county town, named after the Neolithic Jiahu site in the same county, where residues of one of the earliest known fermented drinks were found. Among Huizhou-style buildings, visitors see traditional and mechanised distilling workshops, cellar pits and workshops listed as provincial industrial heritage in 2023, rows of old wooden storage vats, a temperature-controlled cellar and an old well called Wuquan.

rows.name: Jiahu Site and Museum
rows.summary: The Neolithic settlement of Jiahu, lived in from about 9,000 to 7,500 years ago, yielded bone flutes made from the wing bones of red-crowned cranes that can still be played, along with signs carved on tortoise shells, early rice and traces of fermented drink. The site museum, opened in 2023 beside Jiahu village, shows the flutes and other finds, and walkways in the archaeological park next to it lead through four timber shelters with displays of a soil profile, house foundations and the origins of farming.

rows.name: Nanjie Village
rows.summary: A village on the southern edge of Linying town, widely described as China's last Maoist village, which collectivised its farming and industry in 1986; a statue of Mao Zedong flanked by portraits of Engels and Lenin stands on its main square, and images of Marx and Stalin appear around the village. Its village-run food factories, best known for instant noodles, have paid for housing and welfare, and the model has drawn both praise and scepticism in the Chinese press. It receives many domestic red-tourism visitors.

rows.name: Sha–Li Rivers Scenic Area
rows.summary: A belt of riverside parks along both banks of the Sha and Li rivers through central Luohe, centred on their confluence and built from 2007 on top of the city's flood-control works. Paths link themed gardens, beaches and promenades with rubber dams, sluices and historic spots such as an iron ox cast to guard the river, an old ferry landing and a Guanyin pavilion, and the rivers have hosted dragon-boat races.

rows.name: Shenzhou Bird Park
rows.summary: A bird-themed park in Yuanhui district on the south side of Luohe, developed from the former Kaiyuan Forest Park and once called the Golden Phoenix Bird Culture Park. It suits families looking for an easy outing in the city.

rows.name: Shoushan Platform and Steles
rows.summary: The earthen platform at Fancheng where in 220 Emperor Xian, the last ruler of the Han, abdicated in favour of Cao Pi, son of Cao Cao, who founded the Wei dynasty of the Three Kingdoms. Two steles carved that year survive in a small temple just north of the platform, one recording the officials' petition urging Cao Pi to take the throne and the other the abdication itself; the halls that once stood on the platform are long gone.

rows.name: Xiaoshang Bridge
rows.summary: A red-sandstone arch bridge over the Xiaoshang River, traditionally dated to 584 under the Sui and rebuilt in early Song style, with one main arch and a small open arch at each end. The arch stones carry reliefs of heavenly horses, lions and lotus flowers, and small carved strongmen at the corners seem to hold the arch up on their shoulders. The scenic area also has a memorial park to Yang Zaixing, a general under Yue Fei who was killed fighting the Jin near the river in 1140.

rows.name: Xu Shen Cultural Park and Tomb
rows.summary: A culture park of about 10 hectares built around the tomb of Xu Shen, the Eastern Han scholar who compiled the Shuowen Jiezi, regarded as the first comprehensive dictionary of Chinese characters. A Han-style hall named for Xu Shen's honorific 'sage of characters', an 80 m avenue of characters carved with famous calligraphy, a dictionary museum, an exhibition hall on the Shuowen Jiezi and a stele forest of more than a thousand stones line the axis leading to the tomb. The earth mound stands on a low rise with steles put up by local magistrates in 1656, 1707 and 1876.

rows.name: Baiyun Mountain
rows.summary: A high forested part of the Funiu range in southern Song County, on the watershed of the Yangtze, Yellow and Huai rivers, protected as a national forest park and nature reserve. Its summit, Yuhuang Peak (2,216 m), is a sunrise and sea-of-clouds viewpoint, and the area has the Jiulong Falls, about 100 m high, pools, a granite 'little Huangshan' ridge and primeval forest. It became a 5A scenic area in 2011.

rows.name: Baoduzhai Old Stockade Village
rows.summary: An old fortified mountain village (zhai) at Dahong in Sanchuan town, western Luanchuan, run as a scenic area around the stockade and its old village houses. In 2026 the county was repairing the old village and its infrastructure and building a Party clean-government education base there.

rows.name: China National Flower Garden
rows.summary: A large peony garden, laid out from 2001 in the riverside Luopu Park on the south bank of the Luo River, over part of the Sui–Tang city site. It grows peonies of more than a thousand varieties in nine colour groups, and two climate-controlled halls opened in 2022 and 2024 hold rare and late-flowering kinds so that the show lasts into early May, followed by herbaceous peonies. It is at its best during the Luoyang Peony Festival in April.

rows.name: Chongdugou
rows.summary: A mountain valley in north-eastern Luanchuan, in the core area of the Funiu Mountain Global Geopark, known for its springs and waterfalls and its extensive bamboo groves. The valley villages have turned to tourism: the wider Chongdugou zone has more than 500 boutique guesthouses and farm inns, evening markets and shows, and it was named a provincial night-economy cluster in 2026.

rows.name: Dahehui, Luoyang
rows.summary: A cultural leisure complex in Luolong District that opened in autumn 2023, built around immersive digital entertainment. Its centrepiece is the walk-through multimedia show Tracing the Ode to the Luo River Goddess, alongside a digital museum, shops, a Sui–Tang themed designer hotel and a cluster of role-play mystery game venues; it suits younger visitors and an evening out.

rows.name: Daimei Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the far north of Xin'an County, on the south bank of the Yellow River upstream of the Xiaolangdi Dam. It is one of the scenic areas of the Daimeishan part of the Wangwushan–Daimeishan geopark, which also takes in Longtan Grand Canyon and Qingyao Mountain nearby and was named a global geopark in 2006.

rows.name: Dinosaur Valley Rafting
rows.summary: A commercial river-rafting attraction on a mountain stream at Chunshu village in Jincun township, in the hills of southern Ruyang County. Rafting on the stream is the main activity, and the scenic area was operating in 2026.

rows.name: Dongzhen Temple, Xin'an
rows.summary: A Taoist temple on Lanke hill south of Tiemen town, next to the Wangqiao Cave, centred on a Hall of the Three Pure Ones with bracketed eaves. It was already established by about 1300: Yuan inscriptions of 1301 and 1309, recorded in the county gazetteer, show its priests praying for the emperor's long life and the authorities protecting its lands, and it later housed the county's Taoist office.

rows.name: Eastern Zhou Royal Horse and Chariot Museum
rows.summary: A museum opened in 2003 over excavated burials of the Eastern Zhou royal city, from which the Zhou kings ruled for some five centuries after 770 BC and whose remains lie under central Luoyang on both banks of the Jian River. It is named after its chariot pit with the remains of a six-horse team, the 'Son of Heaven drives six' of the ancient texts, shown where it was found alongside other horse-and-chariot burials, tombs and bronzes from the royal city and its cemetery.

rows.name: Eighth Route Army Luoyang Office Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 八路军驻洛办事处纪念馆
rows.summary: The liaison office that the Communist Eighth Route Army kept in Luoyang from 1938 to 1942, during the war against Japan, when the city was the headquarters of the Nationalist First War Zone; it was closed in early 1942 on that command's orders. The memorial hall, first opened in 1987, occupies three adjoining Qing-dynasty brick-and-timber courtyard houses with about 150 rooms.

rows.name: Erlitou Site Museum of the Xia Capital
rows.name_zh: 二里头夏都遗址博物馆
rows.summary: A large museum opened in 2019 next to the Erlitou site, the Bronze Age settlement that many Chinese archaeologists identify as a capital of the Xia dynasty, a link the museum's own name asserts but which remains unproven. Five permanent galleries show the finds from six decades of digging, including turquoise-inlaid bronze plaques with animal masks, early bronze ding and jue vessels and large jade blades. The building, clad in rammed earth and aged copper, was designed by a team from Tongji University; the excavated site beside it is laid out as a national archaeological site park.

rows.name: Fuchang Pavilion
rows.summary: A three-storey Taoist pavilion on a cliff top above the site of the old town of Fuchang, in an area where Emperor Yang of Sui once built a palace; the present building goes back to the Ming and was thoroughly repaired in 1819. A long flight of stone steps climbs the slope to it, its roofs are covered in yellow and green glazed tiles, and caves and small shrines cut into the cliff around it honour Taoist, Buddhist and Confucian figures together.

rows.name: Funiu Mountain Ski Resort
rows.summary: A mountain ski resort at Yangshuping village in the Funiu range west of Luanchuan, shortlisted in 2023 as a national-level ski tourism resort, the only one in Henan. Besides outdoor winter pistes served by lifts it has year-round indoor skiing, night skiing in season, camping and family activities.

rows.name: Gongling Mausoleum of the Tang
rows.summary: The imperial-style tomb of Li Hong, fifth son of Emperor Gaozong and eldest son of Wu Zetian, on Hutuo ridge north-east of Goushi town. A broad spirit way lined with stone sculptures leads to a truncated-pyramid earth mound inside a square enclosure, pairs of stone lions stand at its gates, and the smaller mound of his consort, Lady Pei, rises just to the north-east.

rows.name: Guanlin Temple
rows.summary: The traditional burial place of the head of Guan Yu, the Three Kingdoms general later worshipped as a god, which Cao Cao is said to have buried here with princely honours in 220. Behind the temple, rebuilt from 1592 with Ming and Qing halls along a long axis, rises the tomb mound; it is traditionally regarded as the only Guan Yu temple entitled to the rank of 'lin', a term otherwise used for the Confucius cemetery in Qufu. Guan Yu's cult and its temple fair are a listed national intangible heritage, and the complex is one of the 'Guan Yu Cultural Sites' put forward for World Heritage.

rows.name: Han Hangu Pass, Xin'an
rows.summary: The Han-dynasty Hangu Pass on the road between Luoyang and Chang'an, distinct from the older Qin pass of the same name at Lingbao, and since 2014 a component of the Silk Roads World Heritage site. Excavations in 2012–2013 uncovered roads, gate platforms and walls, which are shown in an archaeological site park with a museum.

rows.name: Haoze International Tulip Park
rows.name_zh: 豪泽国际郁金香花海欢乐城
rows.summary: A flower park in Yibin District, south-east of central Luoyang, planted with tulip fields that flower in spring, with fairground rides and children's play areas. It suits a family outing in tulip season.

rows.name: Henan Prefecture Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The Confucian temple and prefectural school of old Henan Prefecture, in the south-east of Luoyang's Old Town, probably founded in the Jin or Yuan period and enlarged in the 1650s. The Ming-dynasty Halberd Gate and the five-bay Dacheng Hall with its glazed hip-and-gable roof survive, with the Minglun Hall behind; a primary school that occupied the buildings was moved out after 2006 and the temple restored.

rows.name: Hometown of the Two Chengs
rows.summary: The village where the Northern Song Neo-Confucian philosopher Cheng Yi lived in later life, named the 'Hometown of the Two Chengs' by the Ming court in 1455 in honour of him and his brother Cheng Hao. Their memorial temple has a ceremonial gate, a hall with statues of the brothers and commemorative plaques, steles and old cypresses, beside a courtyard of Ming–Qing two-storey houses, and a stone arch of 1462 stands at the east end of the village. The complex is now also used for exhibitions on family traditions and integrity for official study visits.

rows.name: Huaguo Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain in south-western Yiyang County that shares its name with the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, home of the Monkey King in Journey to the West, and plays on the story with a Water Curtain Cave square and Monkey King themes. Other scenic areas in China, among them Huaguo Mountain in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, also draw on the Monkey King story.

rows.name: Huiluo and Hanjia Granaries (Grand Canal)
rows.summary: Two walled state granaries founded in 605 under Emperor Yang of Sui to hold grain shipped to Luoyang along the Grand Canal, inscribed in 2014 as part of the Grand Canal World Heritage Site. The Luoyang Granary Museum, set up in 2015, looks after both: at Huiluo, north of the old city, excavated storage pits, a simulated stretch of the granary-city wall and the granary road are shown where they were found. At Hanjia, nearer the Old Town, a hall covers Pit 160, which still held grain when it was excavated in 1972.

rows.name: Jiulong Temple, Yanshi
rows.summary: A riverside temple built by the boatmen of the Yiluo River to honour Huang Shoucai, a folk hero of flood control, and to pray for safe passage; its main hall was finished in 1811 and the rear hall in 1817. The brick-and-timber main hall, rear hall and two-storey bell and drum towers keep painted beams and carvings that show Huang's work on the rivers.

rows.name: Lingshan Temple, Yiyang
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple founded in 1163 under the Jin dynasty at the northern foot of Lingshan hill, facing north across the Luo River, and rebuilt several times under the Ming and Qing; its Great Compassion Hall and main hall still keep Jin-period beams and columns. The main hall holds Ming statues of the Buddhas of the Three Ages, a small pagoda is pieced together from carved stones of six periods from the Northern Wei to the Qing, and an old ginkgo stands in the courtyard; a temple fair is held here each spring.

rows.name: Longfengshan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A large leisure town in Song-dynasty style built on former gullies and slopes north-west of Yichuan county town, with new walls open for walking, lanes, courtyards, food stalls, shops and guesthouses. It is busiest in the evening, when the buildings are lit up, and also runs a study camp on the Neo-Confucianism of the Cheng brothers, whose tombs are nearby.

rows.name: Longmen Fengxiang Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the southern edge of Luoyang, near the Longmen Grottoes, with thermal pools and an on-site hotel. It suits a relaxed half day after sightseeing at Longmen.

rows.name: Longtan Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A 12 km U-shaped gorge cut by the Qing River into purple-red quartz sandstone in northern Xin'an County, the core of the Wangwushan–Daimeishan UNESCO Global Geopark. The trail runs through narrow slot sections, past a chain of deep pools and waterfalls and rippled rock surfaces. It became a 5A scenic area in 2013.

rows.name: Longyuwan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Funiu Mountains of Luanchuan County, which the city government describes as a core ecological scenic area of the range. Wooded valleys and streams lie below high ridges, among them Jijiaojian, at about 2,210 m the highest point in Luanchuan County.

rows.name: Luanchuan Huilan Orchid Culture Park
rows.summary: A park in Heyu town devoted to the huilan orchid (Cymbidium faberi), which opened in April 2023 with the first Luanchuan Huilan festival and which the city describes as the largest orchid park of its kind in northern China. It combines orchid nurseries and research with display halls, an orchid market, study programmes and leisure areas, and suits visitors interested in Chinese orchids.

rows.name: Luanchuan Zhuhai Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A wildlife park in the Chongdugou valley area of north-eastern Luanchuan, best known for its Siberian tigers: more than 200 live here, and in 2026 an agriculture-ministry laboratory named it a Siberian tiger breeding base. A primeval-forest section with a hill-climbing trail opened in 2023, and a cableway serves the park.

rows.name: Luoyang Ancient Tombs Museum
rows.summary: The most accessible part of the Mangshan Tombs, the imperial and noble cemeteries of six dynasties spread over the loess hills north of Luoyang: a museum opened in 1987 and upgraded in 2022, where 25 excavated tombs from the Western Han to the Song and Jin have been moved and rebuilt underground. Visitors can walk down into the Jingling, the tomb of the Northern Wei emperor Xuanwu, and a separate hall shows painted murals taken from tombs of eight dynasties. Another visitable part of the unit is the walled, cypress-shaded Han Guangwu Emperor's Tomb near the Yellow River in Mengjin, long held to be Liu Xiu's tomb, though that identification is disputed.

rows.name: Luoyang Lavender Manor
rows.summary: A lavender-themed flower farm in Yibin District near the Longmen Grottoes, begun in 2013 as an agri-tourism project on the Yi River ecological corridor. It suits a short family visit when the lavender is in flower.

rows.name: Luoyi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A tourist quarter in the east of Luoyang's old city, largely built in recent years in traditional style around surviving monuments: the Wenfeng Pagoda, a stretch of the Jin–Yuan city wall, the Xintan pond and the Henan Prefecture Confucian Temple. It is best known for Hanfu costume hire and photography, and has craft workshops, guesthouses, food stalls, evening lights and costumed street events at festivals.

rows.name: Luze Guild Hall (Luoyang Folk Customs Museum)
rows.summary: A guild hall and temple to Guan Yu built in 1744–1759 by merchants from Lu'an and Zezhou prefectures in Shanxi, beside the Chan River east of the old city; it is described as the largest and best-preserved group of old buildings in central Luoyang. Behind the gate tower, its two-storey opera stage, one of the widest in Henan, faces a double-eaved main hall with elaborate wood carving and carved column bases. Since 1987 it has housed the Luoyang Folk Customs Museum.

rows.name: Main Hall of Xingfu Temple, Yanshi
rows.summary: The one surviving hall of Xingfu Temple, founded in 1509 and repaired under the Kangxi emperor and again in the Republican era; the courtyard around it later served as the Gaoya village school. The hall has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof of green glazed tiles, and inside its timber frame is built differently on each side, with long beams on the east and full-height columns on the west, a layout known locally as 'east beams, west columns'.

rows.name: Mount Laojun and Jiguan Cave
rows.summary: One of the main peaks of the Funiu range, renamed in the Tang after the legend that Laozi retired here to cultivate the Way; Taoist temples have stood on it since the Northern Wei, and three cable-car lines and a long ridge walkway lead up towards the Golden Summit, a cluster of Taoist halls on the crest. The joint 5A area also includes Jiguan Cave a few kilometres west of Luanchuan town, a limestone cave 5.6 km long, of which about 1.8 km of stalactite halls is open, at an even 18 °C year-round.

rows.name: Muzhaling Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain area at Checun in south-eastern Song County, on the northern side of the Funiu range and within the Funiu Mountain nature reserve. One of its sights is Guanmao ('Official's Hat') Peak, and a small ski field lies just to the west of the scenic area.

rows.name: Old City of Luoyang (Han–Wei Luoyang)
rows.summary: The ruins of the capital of the Eastern Han, Cao Wei, Western Jin and Northern Wei, about 15 km east of modern Luoyang, abandoned after the Sui built a new city to the west in 605; it is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage Site. In the national archaeological park, stretches of rammed-earth city wall survive, and the foundations of the Changhe palace gate and the base of the Yongning Temple pagoda are laid out for visitors. The site museum, opened in July 2025, explains the city in three themed halls.

rows.name: Peony Pavilion and Luoyang Peony Museum
rows.summary: A large pavilion-style building at the southern end of Luoyang's modern city axis, opened on trial during the 2022 peony festival, which houses the Luoyang Peony Museum, showing the history of peony growing, peony varieties, peony-themed relics and the modern peony industry with documents, objects, film and live plants. The outdoor garden around it is planted with named peony varieties, including several plants about a century old, and a roving costumed show is staged inside during the April peony festival.

rows.name: Qiantang Zhizhai Museum
rows.summary: A collection of carved tomb epitaphs described as China's largest, gathered in the 1930s by Zhang Fang from tombs looted around Luoyang and set into the walls of 15 brick-vaulted rooms beside his house in Tiemen. The name means 'Studio of a Thousand Tang Epitaphs': most of the more than 1,400 stones date from the Tang dynasty, with smaller numbers from the Western Jin, Northern Wei, Sui and Song, and they are a major source for the study of Tang history.

rows.name: Qicai Fairy Tale Animal Kingdom
rows.summary: A zoo and amusement park in Lianzhuang town, Yiyang County, combining animal and plant collections with funfair rides, pick-your-own farm areas and school study programmes. It reopened in January 2025 after an upgrade that added a tiger free-roaming area, a hippo house and a large circus arena, with staged sea-lion and parrot shows; it suits families with children.

rows.name: Qingyao Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain area in north-western Xin'an County, linked in legend with the Yellow Emperor. Its Lianzhu and Shuanglong gorges hold strings of pools and waterfalls, reached in places by boardwalks and suspension bridges; Shuanglong Gorge is cut into purple-red quartz sandstone, and a restored Ming-dynasty Shuanglong (Twin Dragon) Temple stands by the Black and White Dragon pools. The streams are a protected habitat for the Chinese giant salamander.

rows.name: Shanxi–Shaanxi Guild Hall (Wanli Tea Road Museum)
rows.summary: A guild hall and Guan Yu temple built from about 1711 to 1721 by merchants from Shanxi and Shaanxi near the old river port south of the city wall. Its glazed screen wall, opera stage, worship hall and main hall frame two courtyards with Qing carving and painted beams. Since April 2023 it houses the Luoyang Wanli Tea Road Museum, on the caravan tea trade between southern China and Russia in which Luoyang was a staging post.

rows.name: Shengxian Taizi Stele
rows.summary: A stele set up in 699 on Goushan hill by Empress Wu Zetian, who stayed here on her way to the sacrifices at Mount Song; its text retells the legend of Prince Jin of Zhou, said to have risen to heaven from this hill, and links it to her own reign. Wu Zetian wrote both the heading, in the 'flying white' brush style with bird-like flourishes, and the cursive main text, her only surviving calligraphy, while the back carries a poem and lists of names written by Xue Yao, Xue Ji and Zhong Shaojing.

rows.name: Shenlingzhai National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 53 km² in the mountains south-east of Luoning town, rising to 1,859 m. It is known for its great rock slabs, called the 'stone waterfalls', for natural stands of lacebark pine and a bamboo grove unusually far north, and for its gorge and the Yuhuang Hall of a former Taoist temple.

rows.name: Shuiquan Grottoes
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave on the cliffs of Wan'an Mountain, enlarged from a natural cavern in the Northern Wei, with two large standing Buddhas on either side of a natural fissure in the back wall and walls crowded with small carved niches. Outside, a damaged Northern Wei inscription records the monk Tanfu who led the work, and a Tang niche of Amitabha dated 713 is cut into the cliff.

rows.name: Song Mausoleums Quarry
rows.summary: The valley on the east side of Niuxin hill where stone was cut and roughed out for the Northern Song imperial tombs at Gongyi, about 25 km away. The valley walls show quarry faces, wedge holes and cutting lines, half-finished column bases and animal figures lie on the valley floor, cart ruts are worn into the rock of the old haul road, and carved inscriptions record quarrying for the tomb of Emperor Zhezong in 1100.

rows.name: Soviet-style Buildings of Jianxi
rows.summary: The factory halls and workers' housing built from 1954 in Luoyang's Jianxi District for the industrial projects China undertook with Soviet aid in the 1950s, including the First Tractor Works and the Luoyang copper works. The housing quarters, such as blocks 2 and 10, are in Soviet neoclassical style with Chinese cloud-pattern ornament and are seen from the street on a walk along Wuhan Road and Jianshe Road.

rows.name: Stele of Huisheng Palace
rows.summary: A large Northern Song stele with a dragon crest and a tortoise base, erected in 1034 at Huisheng Palace, a hall built for rites at the Song imperial tombs where portraits of the first three Song emperors were enshrined. The palace has gone, but the stele still stands where it was set up, on Fenghuang hill above Sigou village, its sides carved with clouds and cranes and its base with waves.

rows.name: Sui–Tang City Site Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A botanical garden and peony park laid out over part of the Sui–Tang city site south of the Luo River. In April, during the Peony Festival, its peony gardens are the setting for Tang-costume parades, lion dances and fire performances, and later-flowering varieties extend the season.

rows.name: Sui–Tang Luoyang City Site (Yingtian Gate and Mingtang)
rows.summary: The site of Luoyang as rebuilt by Emperor Yang of Sui from 605, the eastern capital of the Sui and Tang and, under Empress Wu Zetian, the capital of her Zhou dynasty. Its palace heart is a national archaeological park: the Yingtian Gate, the palace's main gate, rebuilt in 2016–2019 over its excavated base, which is shown inside, and Wu Zetian's Mingtang (Hall of Light) and Tiantang, whose foundations are protected and shown under modern halls, together with the Jiuzhou Pond. Dingding Gate, the outer city's south gate 5 km away, has its own museum over the excavated remains.

rows.name: Tianchi Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in north-western Song County, made up of the Tianchi ('Heavenly Lake'), Feilaishi ('Flying Rock'), Yunü Stream and Erlang Gully sections. Feilaishi is known for its steep crags and Yunü Stream for its quiet wooded gorge.

rows.name: Tianhe Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A mountain canyon scenic area at Jiaohe in western Luanchuan, with a cableway up to Wusheng Peak. In March the cornelian cherries grown around Jiaohe for traditional medicine come into flower, and the scenic area has held a blossom festival at that time.

rows.name: Tomb of Fan Zhongyan
rows.summary: The family cemetery of Fan Zhongyan (989–1052), the Northern Song statesman and writer, known locally as the Fan Garden; it is laid out in front and rear sections planted with cypresses, with the tombs of his mother and his sons near his own. A spirit way lined with stone officials, rams, lions and gate pillars leads to a memorial hall with a gilded seated statue of Fan, and the steles include the Song spirit-way stele whose heading was written by Emperor Renzong and whose text was composed by Ouyang Xiu.

rows.name: Tombs of the Cheng Brothers (Cheng Brothers Culture Park)
rows.summary: The cemetery of Cheng Hao (1032–1085) and Cheng Yi (1033–1107), the Northern Song brothers who founded the Neo-Confucian 'study of principle', and of their father Cheng Xiang, at the foot of Jing Hill on the west side of Yichuan town. Three earth mounds stand in a triangle behind a memorial shrine with statues of the three men, with Qing-dynasty stelae before the graves and Ming stone figures, rams and tigers along the spirit way. A culture park built around the old cemetery opened in 2017.

rows.name: Wan'an Mountain Summit Park
rows.summary: A park along the crest of Wan'an Mountain, the 937 m ridge on the south-eastern edge of the Luoyang basin, facing the Song Mountains. A ridge road links a string of viewpoints and rock outcrops, and the summit has small temples to the White Dragon King and the Patriarch as well as the Yuquan Temple; fields of coreopsis flower on the top in early summer.

rows.name: Wanfoshan Grottoes
rows.summary: A group of Northern Wei Buddhist caves cut into a hillside on the north bank of the Yellow River, in the part of Mengjin that was Jili District until 2021. The upper and lower temple areas hold more than 300 figures, among them a cliff-carved standing Buddha about 5 m tall flanked by bodhisattvas, groups of the Buddhas of the Three Ages and reliefs of donors in procession that show the influence of Yungang. After rainwater flooded some statues in 2022, shelters were built and the enclosure walls and gatehouse repaired.

rows.name: Wangfu Bamboo Sea
rows.summary: A valley at Wangfugou in northern Luanchuan with large bamboo groves, rare this far north in China, along with waterfalls and springs. It was named in a 2024 national list of summer-retreat destinations compiled with weather services, and again in the National Climate Center's 2026 summer-climate map.

rows.name: Weipo Xinxu
rows.summary: A leisure and shopping quarter opened in 2024 in and around the old village of Weipo at Chaoyang, Mengjin, where grey-brick lanes and courtyards have been fitted out with cafés, shops, restaurants, a courtyard hotel and event spaces. It is a modern commercial district in an old-village setting rather than a historic site, suited to an afternoon or evening stroll.

rows.name: Wuhua Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda of the Song dynasty, the only survivor of the long-vanished Wuhua Temple, on the west bank of the Lianchang River north of Sanxiang town. It is hollow and built in the pavilion style, with real doorways on the south face of several storeys and blind doors on the other faces.

rows.name: Xiaolangdi Dam Scenic Area
rows.summary: The visitor area at the south end of the Xiaolangdi Dam, the 154 m dam built across the Yellow River in 1994–2001 at the exit of its last gorge, mainly to control silt and floods. The main sight is the water-and-sediment flushing, usually run in early summer, when the outlet tunnels release jets of muddy water; in 2026 a viewing season ran from mid-June to early July.

rows.name: Xigong Barracks
rows.summary: A modern-style barracks begun in 1914 under Yuan Shikai and greatly enlarged by the warlord Wu Peifu after 1920, which in the war against Japan served as headquarters of the First War Zone. The surviving core includes the headquarters courtyard, the two-storey house Wu Peifu built as his office, a study built in 1939 in the style of Yan'an cave dwellings and the remains of an old bridge over the Luo River. Since 2021 it has housed the Luoyang War of Resistance Memorial Hall, whose exhibition presents the Communist-led resistance in western Henan with photographs, documents and objects.

rows.name: Xitai Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain scenic area at Fudian in southern Ruyang County, with Lovers' Valley and the Shengshui Lake. It is best known for its rhododendrons, celebrated each spring with a rhododendron festival that reached its 21st edition in 2023.

rows.name: Yangzigou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A wooded valley on the slopes a few kilometres east of Mount Laojun, south-east of Luanchuan town. It is known for its damp, cool air and dense vegetation, and in 2026 the National Climate Center listed it among the country's forest summer retreats.

rows.name: Yanshi Shang City Site
rows.summary: The walled city at Yanshi, found in 1983 and identified by many archaeologists as Xibo, an early capital of the Shang dynasty, was enclosed by three rings of rammed-earth walls around a palace city. In the palace area the foundation of the palace's pool garden and its drainage channel have been exposed and can be seen on the ground. It pairs with the Erlitou site museum, about 8 km to the west.

rows.name: Yiyang Ancient City of the State of Han
rows.summary: The walled city of Yiyang, a western stronghold of the Warring States kingdom of Han, unrelated to the later Han dynasty, which Qin troops captured in 307 BC; the city stayed in use into the early Han dynasty. Its rammed-earth walls survive best on the east and north sides, still standing several metres high with traces of the moat outside, and a palace enclosure lay in the north-west corner.

rows.name: Zhougong Temple Museum
rows.summary: A temple to the Duke of Zhou, the Western Zhou statesman, said to have been founded by the Sui general Wang Shichong and rebuilt many times; in 1932, when the Nationalist government briefly moved to Luoyang, it housed the Examination Yuan. Its Ming and Qing halls now form a museum, also called the Luoyang Capital Cities Museum, which also takes in the excavated eastern tower of the Yingtian Gate of the Sui–Tang palace next door.

rows.name: Zushi Temple
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty temple hall on North Street (Beidajie) in Luoyang's Old Town, listed as a national monument in 2006. Its surviving main hall stands under a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof, in a street quarter that was being redeveloped for tourism in 2024.

rows.name: Baihetan Park
rows.summary: A riverside park stretching for nearly 10 km along the Bai River at Xinye, landscaped over some 8 km² with footpaths, waterside platforms and themed gardens of tulips, peach, cherry and roses. It holds seasonal flower shows and works Three Kingdoms themes into its landscaping, and was raised from 3A to 4A in 2025.

rows.name: Baotianman Gorge Rafting
rows.summary: A whitewater rafting trip on the Tuan River through the gorges on the southern side of the Baotianman nature reserve in the Funiu Mountains. The run drops about 239 m and takes around three and a half hours past rapids, bends, pools and rocks standing in the riverbed; it suits active visitors rather than a quiet sightseeing day.

rows.name: Baotianman Scenic Area (Nanzhao)
rows.summary: The Nanzhao County side of the Baotianman forests, near Qiaoduan in the Funiu Mountains, where the nature reserve's main peak reaches about 1,830 m. Sights include Baotian Cave, a limestone cave with stalactites, and Baotian Gorge, where a walkway of about 4.5 km follows a chain of pools and waterfalls through the forest.

rows.name: Baotianman Scenic Area (Neixiang)
rows.summary: The visitor area of the Baotianman National Nature Reserve in the Funiu Mountains, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2001 that protects an unusually complete forest on the transition between China's subtropical and warm-temperate zones. Trails lead through old-growth woodland, gorges, streams and waterfalls in a reserve with more than 3,000 plant species, and in spring the slopes are bright with flowering azaleas.

rows.name: Danjiang Daguanyuan
rows.summary: A lakeside resort park built by a private company on peninsulas and islets on the north shore of the Danjiangkou Reservoir, the source of the middle route of the South–North Water Transfer Project. Besides lake views and boats it has modern buildings on Chu and Buddhist themes, including the Fanli Pavilion, the Chufeng Tower, a large Guanyin statue, a recreation of Xiangyan Temple's flooded lower temple and a memorial hall for the water-transfer project.

rows.name: Danxia Temple Pagoda Forest
rows.summary: Monks' funerary pagodas of the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties, in three groups lying 200–760 m from Danxia Temple, a Buddhist monastery at Liushan in Nanzhao County. Fourteen brick and stone pagodas survive among old pines and cypresses, ranging from single-storey stupas to multi-eaved and lama-style towers, several carved in relief.

rows.name: Deyunshan Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A commercial flower park laid out since 2015 on the hills at Erlangmiao, south-east of Fangcheng town, below a wind farm. Large plantings of tree peonies and cherry trees bloom in spring, and the site also has a hillside wildlife park and a children's amusement area.

rows.name: Echeng Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A small temple at Shiqiao north of Nanyang, named after the Han county of Xi'e, with a six-sided brick pagoda founded in 617 under the Sui and rebuilt in the Song. The pagoda stands about 19 m high with seven storeys, the top four restored in recent decades, and has Buddha figures set into its second storey. The courtyard keeps a Qing gate and halls, a pair of Song stone lions dated 1099 and Ming and Qing steles.

rows.name: Erlong Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the north of Neixiang County, inside the Funiu Mountain Global Geopark, named for a ridge of ten linked peaks said to look like two dragons playing with a pearl. The area rises to about 1,380 m and is promoted for its scenery and as a place of pilgrimage and meditation, with Han, Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist cultural themes.

rows.name: Fogou Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Song-dynasty Buddhist figures carved in niches on the slope of Xiangshan hill in eastern Fangcheng County, at a spot known locally as Foyegou ('Buddha gully'). Some 32 niches hold 138 figures, the largest about 1.4 m tall, and the carvings became a national heritage unit in 2013. The township was building a tourism project at the site in 2024.

rows.name: Fusheng Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A brick pagoda in the centre of Dengzhou, built in 1032 under the Northern Song with thirteen storeys, cut to seven by war damage at the end of the Yuan and repaired in the early Ming. About 38 m tall and octagonal, it is faced with more than 2,000 carved bricks of Buddhas, guardians and musicians; the gold coffin and silver casket found in its crypt in 1988 are now in the Henan Museum.

rows.name: Guanhe River Rafting
rows.summary: A whitewater rafting run of about 12 km on the upper Laoguan (Guan) River in the mountains of Xixia County, through some eighteen rapids. It was among the first commercial rafting trips developed in central China and suits active visitors.

rows.name: Huazhou Academy
rows.summary: An academy founded in the 1040s by the statesman Fan Zhongyan while he was governor of Dengzhou, where he wrote his famous essay 'On Yueyang Tower'. The present buildings, in Qing style, form five courtyards with a semicircular pool and bridge and a shrine to Fan, beside the Baihuazhou garden of pools and rockeries and a stretch of Ming earthen city wall.

rows.name: Jingziguan Old Town
rows.summary: A Ming and Qing trading town on the Dan River where Henan, Hubei and Shaanxi meet, whose long old street keeps more than 2,000 rooms of old houses and some 700 shopfronts. Along it stand the old pass gate, a Shan-Shaan guild hall, the Yuwang, Pinglang and Wanshou halls, a mosque, a Buddhist temple and a stele pavilion at the spot where one can stand in three provinces at once.

rows.name: Laojun Cave Scenic Area
rows.summary: A large forested mountain area at Erlangping in northern Xixia County, in the core of the Funiu Mountain Global Geopark, with more than a dozen peaks over 1,000 m, rivers and springs. Legend says Laozi lived here in retreat, and the cave that gives the area its name is promoted as a Taoist grotto-heaven.

rows.name: Longtan Gully Scenic Area
rows.summary: A narrow gorge in the mountains north of Xixia town where a stream drops through a chain of about nineteen waterfalls and deep pools, the highest fall about 35 m. The walk up the valley passes cliffs and huge boulders in thick forest, making it a good half-day outing.

rows.name: Main Hall of Yang'an Temple
rows.summary: A small Ming-dynasty Buddhist hall in Yantai village, about 20 km north-west of Zhenping town, on a temple site founded in 656. The square, three-bay hall with a hip-and-gable roof keeps mid-Ming brackets and beams in local Henan style, and inside stands a marble statue of Bodhidharma dated 1525.

rows.name: Nanyang Prefectural Yamen
rows.summary: The office of the prefects of Nanyang from 1271, under the Yuan, to the end of the Qing, described as the only prefecture-level yamen in China to survive complete. More than 150 rooms of mostly Qing date stand on an axis about 240 m long, with courts, offices and the prefect's residence laid out as a museum of local government.

rows.name: Neixiang County Yamen
rows.summary: Regarded as the best-preserved Qing county government office in China, it was rebuilt in 1894 on a site that had been the seat of Neixiang County since 1304, served as the county government until 1968 and became a museum in 1984. Gates and three main halls line the central axis, leading from the magistrate's courtroom back to his offices and living quarters, with the county jail in the south-west corner and rooms furnished to show how a county was run.

rows.name: Puti Temple, Zhenping
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on Xinghua Mountain at Laozhuang in north-eastern Zhenping County, founded in the 650s under the Tang; the buildings on its main axis are Ming and Qing. It keeps palm-leaf sutras and Burmese Buddha images, and stands among old ginkgo and magnolia trees in a forest park with a lake.

rows.name: Qifeng Mountain Ecotourism Area
rows.summary: The eastern end of the Funiu Mountains in northern Fangcheng County, a ridge of seven peaks topping out at 768 m with cliffs, caves, ravines and forest. Remains of the Chu Great Wall, the chain of defences the state of Chu built around the Nanyang Basin from the Spring and Autumn period, run along the ridge, which is why the area is promoted as home of the 'oldest Great Wall'. Walking trails, including one past stretches of the wall, make it a day out from Nanyang.

rows.name: Seventy-Two Pools Scenic Area
rows.summary: A river valley in the hills north of Fangcheng where the stream runs over broad sheets of bare rock, forming a long chain of pools and small falls that visitors can wade through. The scenic area adds commercial attractions such as a glass bridge, a glass slide and other rides, so it suits families looking for water play rather than a quiet walk.

rows.name: Sheqi Shan-Shaan Guild Hall
rows.summary: A guild hall and temple to Guan Yu built over 136 years, from 1756 to 1892, by merchants from Shanxi and Shaanxi trading in the town of Shedian. Its glazed-tile screen wall, the Xuanjian opera tower, a stone archway and the great worship hall are covered in fine wood, brick and stone carving. The scenic area also takes in other sights of Shedian old town, among them a fire-god temple, an old escort agency and a Qing tax office.

rows.name: Shrine of the Medical Sage (Zhang Zhongjing Tomb)
rows.summary: The tomb and memorial shrine of Zhang Zhongjing, the Eastern Han physician revered in China as the 'Medical Sage' and author of the Treatise on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Diseases. Most of what stands today was rebuilt after the shrine was wrecked in the Cultural Revolution: a Han-style gate with paired towers, the tomb, halls with statues of famous Chinese doctors and the Zhang Zhongjing Museum of traditional medicine.

rows.name: Sishan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested hill park across the Guan River from Xixia town, covering about 7.5 km² of woodland, pools and viewpoints. Paths lead to Matou Hill, the Heilong Pool, the ruins of an academy linked with the Jin-dynasty poet Yuan Haowen and the rebuilt Randeng Temple, a modern group of Buddhist halls with a large nine-dragon screen wall.

rows.name: Sizhou Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty brick pagoda in Tanghe town, founded in 1095 as part of the Puti Temple of Tangzhou and rebuilt in 1377 under the Ming, with its top repaired after lightning strikes in the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. Octagonal and modelled on a wooden tower, it has a stair spiralling round a central column inside and Buddha figures set into its walls.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhang Heng
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhang Heng (78–139), the Eastern Han astronomer, mathematician and poet who presented the first known seismoscope to the court in 132, at Shiqiao in his home district of Xi'e. The mound, about 79 m round, stands in a Han-style memorial park with the Zhang Heng Museum, which has an exhibition on his life and working replicas of his seismoscope, water-powered armillary sphere, south-pointing carriage and distance-measuring cart.

rows.name: Tongbai Mountain Huaiyuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: The forested country around the source of the Huai River in the Tongbai Mountains on the Henan–Hubei border, beginning just outside Tongbai town.
