Its four sections take in the Huai source, Taibai Peak (about 1,140 m, the highest point in southern Henan), Taohua Cave and the Shuilian (Water Curtain) Cave, a Taoist grotto-heaven; the Yuntai Chan Temple, ancestral temple of the Baiyun branch of Chan Buddhism, is also in the area.

rows.name: Tongbai Revolutionary Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall in Tongbai founded in 1984 to commemorate those who died in and around the county during the Long March period, the War of Resistance against Japan and the civil war. The county saw heavy fighting, including the Red 25th Army's breakout from an encirclement at Xiemaling in November 1934 during the Long March.

rows.name: Wolong Gang
rows.summary: The shrine to the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang on Wolong Gang, the low ridge south-west of central Nanyang where he is said, in a disputed tradition, to have lived and farmed for about ten years before joining Liu Bei. Worship here goes back to the Jin dynasty and the present halls are Yuan to Qing, with a thatched pavilion on the site of his supposed cottage and some 400 steles, among them the 'Chu Shi Biao' memorials in the hand of Yue Fei. The Nanyang Han Stone Carving Museum stands at the foot of the same ridge.

rows.name: Wuduo Mountain
rows.summary: A Taoist mountain on the border of Nanzhao and Zhenping counties whose five rocky summits rise to 1,665 m; tradition links it with Yin Xi, some 2,500 years ago, and the Tang Taoist Wu Yun. The scenic area combines the climb to the peaks and the Wanfu Palace temple with a lakeside resort area at Jiulong Lake and a gorge with water play.

rows.name: Xiangyan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in the hills at Cangfang, founded in the Tang dynasty as the seat of the Chan master Nanyang Huizhong and long counted among the four great temples of the Central Plains. Only the upper temple survives, as the lower temple was submerged by the Danjiangkou Reservoir in 1978; its Ming and Qing halls, library and stone archway are known for their brick, wood and stone carving and for a large mural in the main hall.

rows.name: Xixia Dinosaur Remains Park and Laojieling
rows.name_zh: 西峡恐龙遗迹园—老界岭
rows.summary: Two separate parts of the Funiu Mountain Global Geopark in Xixia County share this 5A listing. The Dinosaur Remains Park at Danshui shows a Cretaceous bed of fossil dinosaur eggs with more than 1,000 eggs exposed, together with an egg-fossil museum and a park of model dinosaurs. Laojieling, about 50 km to the north, is a forested ridge on the divide between the Yangtze and Yellow River basins that rises to over 2,200 m at Jijiaojian.

rows.name: Yunlu Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of bamboo groves, forest and waterfalls at Mashankou in eastern Neixiang County, part of the Funiu Mountain Global Geopark. The developed sections follow the Yunlu River, with places to paddle, and climb to the Yaowang and Baota waterfalls; old stone walls on the ridges are attributed to the Chu Great Wall.

rows.name: Zhenping International Jade City
rows.summary: A large jade-trading complex of shops and workshops at Shifosi, the town at the heart of Zhenping County's jade-carving industry, built with private investment in the 2010s. Visitors can browse carved jade and see carving and processing at work, and the town's older jade markets, such as Yudiaowan, are close by.

rows.name: Baiguihu National Urban Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park on the north shore of Baiguishan Reservoir, a lake built in 1958–66 on the south-western edge of Pingdingshan, designated a national urban wetland park in 2009. Boardwalks, lawns and squares run along the shore, making it a place for lakeside walks next to the city museum.

rows.name: Dengtaijia Scenic Area, Wugang
rows.summary: A hill area in southern Wugang named after its 808 m main peak, said to resemble an old lamp stand. Trails and a cliff-side walkway of about 2 km lead past pools and waterfalls such as the Tianchi plunge pool, and through gorges in layered sandstone, conglomerate and shale that preserve fossil mud cracks and other traces of ancient climates; a glass bridge and a water slide are extras.

rows.name: Erlang Mountain, Wugang
rows.summary: A forested hill on the south shore of Shimantan Reservoir, part of the Shimantan National Forest Park and named after the legend of the god Erlang carrying mountains to chase the suns. Visitors climb to a Jade Emperor hall, rebuilt in 2000 after the old one was destroyed by Japanese bombing in 1941, cross a 286 m glass suspension bridge and a footbridge over the water, and can take bamboo-raft or boat trips on the reservoir.

rows.name: Faxing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A brick multi-eaved pagoda about 30 m tall on Tasi Street in Ruzhou, standing on the site of the former Faxing Temple. Its square lower storey keeps the look of its Tang origins, though the upper part was altered in the Song, and the top two storeys and the bronze finial are an early Qing repair; the finial is inscribed with the year 1653.

rows.name: Fengxue Temple
rows.summary: A hillside temple north-east of Ruzhou that keeps about 140 bays of buildings dating from the Tang to the Qing, laid out like a garden among streams and cliffs. Its oldest structure is the nine-storey Qizu Pagoda of 738, built for the remains of the monk Zhen; other highlights are a bell tower holding an iron bell cast in 1125, a Jin-dynasty middle hall and two pagoda forests with more than 80 monks' stupas from the Yuan to the Qing.

rows.name: Huamei Valley
rows.summary: A wooded valley beside national road G311 near Mount Yao, named after the hwamei songbirds that nest there and opened to visitors in 2004. Paths follow a stream past a chain of pools and waterfalls, including a six-tier fall, to a cliff-side walkway, a glass bridge and viewpoints in the forest, with water-play attractions near the entrance.

rows.name: Jia County Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple and county school founded in 1206 under the Jin dynasty and rebuilt many times, with 22 surviving buildings laid out with the school on the left and the temple on the right. The main Dacheng Hall has green-glazed tiles and front columns carved with coiling dragons, and the octagonal two-storey Wenkui Tower, first built in 1579, stands on a red-stone platform. It is run as the Jia County Confucian Temple Museum.

rows.name: Jia County Shanxi–Shaanxi Guild Hall
rows.summary: A guild hall founded in 1693 by merchants from Shanxi and Shaanxi in the western suburb of Jia County town, used for lodging, trade, gatherings and worship. A stage tower sits above the entrance gate between bell and drum towers, facing a hall to Guan Yu and a rear hall, and the screen wall carries a brick-carved dragon.

rows.name: Jiufeng Mountain, Ruzhou
rows.summary: A range of low forested peaks in south-western Ruzhou, named for nine summits that legend links to the Jade Emperor's daughters; the highest, Dazhai, reaches 895 m. Designated a national forest park in 2011 and developed by a private company since the mid-2010s, it has gorges, colourful rock strata and walking trails.

rows.name: Linfengzhai
rows.summary: A village enclosed by walls of red sandstone, built in 1862 by the Zhu family, local salt merchants, to replace an earlier earth wall. The walls, over 6 m high and about 1.1 km round with three gates and a moat, enclose Ming and Qing courtyard houses decorated with wood, brick and stone carving, and the gates still have slots for flood boards.

rows.name: Longquan Li River Stone Bridge
rows.summary: A flat stone-slab bridge of 33 spans across the Li River, also called Cuihua Bridge, recorded in the Ming dynasty and long the main crossing on the north–south road here. It is about 65 m long, with iron cramps binding its slabs, dragon heads carved on the upstream ends of the piers and wheel ruts worn into the granite carriageway; traffic moved to a concrete bridge 150 m upstream in 1981.

rows.name: Majie Storytelling Fair Site
rows.summary: The home of the Majie Storytelling Fair, at which folk storytellers and ballad singers from across China gather every year on the 13th day of the first lunar month, a custom said to date back to 1315 and listed as national intangible heritage in 2006. The scenic area has an exhibition hall of Chinese quyi (storytelling and ballad arts), a hall devoted to the storyteller Liu Lanfang, a Fire God temple and a sculpture square, but the fair day is by far the liveliest time to come.

rows.name: Mount Yao and Spring Temple Buddha
rows.summary: This 5A area joins two separate sights in western Lushan County. Mount Yao (formerly Shirenshan), at the eastern end of the Funiu Mountains, is a granite mountain area of about 268 km² rising to about 2,150 m, known for human-shaped rock pinnacles, waterfalls, forest and autumn colour, with a cable car and a cliff walkway up towards the summit. About 15 km to the east, Foquan Temple is home to the Spring Temple Buddha, a copper statue completed in 2008 that stands 128 m tall including its lotus throne.

rows.name: Mozi Culture Tourism Area
rows.summary: A themed visitor area opened in 2016 at the foot of Mount Yao, built around the Warring States philosopher Mozi, whom Lushan claims as a native. Its core is a new street built in old-street style with food stalls, shops, craft workshops and an inn, served by a narrow-gauge sightseeing train, and paths continue up a side valley to waterfalls, a glass bridge and a dry slide. It suits families who combine it with Mount Yao.

rows.name: Pingdingshan Museum
rows.summary: Pingdingshan's main history museum, opened in 2012 in a building designed by Tsinghua University's architectural design institute, with walls modelled on bundles of bamboo slips. Its permanent displays cover the history and culture of the Pingdingshan area, and its collection includes bronzes from the noble cemetery of the Western Zhou state of Ying, excavated in the city.

rows.name: Qingliangsi Ru Kiln Site
rows.summary: The village site where archaeologists in 2000 confirmed the kilns of Ru ware, the rare duck-egg blue stoneware made for the Northern Song court around 1100, after surveys and excavations that began in 1987. The excavated kilns, glazing workshops and clay-settling pits are preserved inside an exhibition hall built over them, which opened in January 2017, and a separate Ru kiln museum with more than 1,000 exhibits opened in the village later that year.

rows.name: Ruzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The Confucian temple and prefectural school of Ruzhou, converted in 1370 from a Yuan shrine and enlarged in 1811. Its Qing buildings include gateways, shrines to local worthies and a five-bay Dacheng Hall under a green-glazed hipped roof, and the northern half of the complex has housed the city's Ru porcelain museum.

rows.name: Taishan Temple, Houwan
rows.summary: A village temple to the god of Mount Tai at Houwan in eastern Ruzhou, with Ming and Qing buildings around a courtyard. It is still used for local worship and was listed as a national monument in 2019.

rows.name: Three Su Tombs, Jia County
rows.summary: The burial ground of the Song dynasty writer Su Shi (Su Dongpo) and his brother Su Zhe, with a cenotaph for their father Su Xun added in the Yuan dynasty, at the foot of Xiao Emei hill. Beside the three mounds stand a shrine founded in 1350 with Yuan-period painted clay statues of the three Su, the Guangqing Temple, and a stele forest of Su Shi's poems carved around 2000 in modern calligraphy, with a lake laid out in 2002.

rows.name: Western Henan Revolution Memorial Hall, Lushan
rows.summary: The former base of the Communist Party's Henan–Shaanxi–Hubei front and rear committees, which made Lushan their seat in 1947–48, in the town's former county Party committee compound. Deng Xiaoping lived in its two-storey Western-style house, known locally as the Pastor's House, in 1948 and on 25 April that year addressed a joint meeting of the committees at the town's gospel hall. The Western Henan Revolution Memorial Hall, opened here in 2004, shows photographs and objects from the period.

rows.name: Xianglong Valley, Wugang
rows.summary: A canyon scenic area in the hills of southern Wugang with waterfalls, cliffs, forest and a small lake, rising to Longwangzhuang (866 m), which the city's tourism bureau gives as the highest point in Wugang. Local legends tie spots along the trail to the Han emperor Guangwu (Liu Xiu), the Yang family generals and other figures.

rows.name: Xiangshan Temple, Pingdingshan
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on Daxiang Shan north-west of Pingdingshan, revered as the place where, in a legend recorded here in the Song dynasty, the bodhisattva Guanyin attained enlightenment. Its treasures are the nine-storey Guanyin Dashi Pagoda, about 33 m tall and rebuilt in 1068 by order of Emperor Shenzong, and a stele of 1100 carrying the biography of the Great Compassionate Bodhisattva in the calligraphy of Cai Jing, one of 15 Song-to-Qing steles kept in the temple. Most of the halls have been rebuilt since 2008.

rows.name: Yaoshan Grand Canyon Rafting
rows.summary: A commercial rafting run on a mountain river in the Mount Yao area, where visitors paddle inflatable boats down a winding channel with drops, rapids and calmer stretches. It is a summer outing for families and groups rather than a sight in itself.

rows.name: Yaozhuang Tourism Area
rows.summary: A rural tourism area covering six villages of Yaozhuang Hui Township in southern Jia County, where just over half of the roughly 10,000 residents are Hui Muslims. It mixes orchards, a tea garden and eco-farms offering fruit picking with small culture venues such as a hall devoted to Xinyi Liuhe boxing and an old well, and suits a half-day country outing.

rows.name: Ye County Yamen
rows.summary: The county government compound of Ye, founded in 1396 under the Ming and often described as the only Ming county yamen surviving in China; it is now run as a museum. Only the five-bay main hall survives from the Ming, the other halls being Qing rebuilds, laid out along a central axis flanked by two side courtyards.

rows.name: Yeyi Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: The remains of a walled town of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods at Jiuxian village, once a capital of the small state of Xu and the fief of Shen Zhuliang, Lord of She under the state of Chu. Stretches of rammed-earth wall up to about 5.5 m high survive along a circuit of about 9 km, the north wall was consolidated in 2024, and dozens of large tomb mounds lie in the surrounding fields.

rows.name: Cangjie Mausoleum, Nanle
rows.summary: A round earth mound 3 m high at Shiguan village, honoured as the grave of Cangjie, the legendary inventor of Chinese writing, with Ming-dynasty stone figures, lions, columns and a stone gateway in front and a Cangjie temple beside it. The ground beneath is the Shiguan site, a moated Neolithic village of the Yangshao and Longshan cultures, and a Cangjie culture museum stands nearby; the county holds a Cangjie culture week at the site each spring.

rows.name: Dongbeizhuang Acrobatics Culture Park
rows.summary: A park in Dongbeizhuang, a village whose acrobatic tradition the national intangible-heritage list dates to the late Yuan or early Ming dynasty, more than 500 years ago, with troupes of the Liu, Qiao and Li families. At its centre is the Central Plains Acrobatics Museum, described by state media as China's first stand-alone museum on acrobatics, with a 360-degree cinema. Traditional acrobatics are performed for visitors, especially at festivals, and the village puts on its own show at Spring Festival.

rows.name: Former Hebei–Shandong–Henan Border Region Base, Danguai
rows.summary: Danguai, a village in Qingfeng County where the Communist Party's Hebei–Shandong–Henan sub-bureau and military region headquarters moved in September 1944; Deng Xiaoping, then acting head of the North China Bureau, worked here for three months in 1945. The leaders' former quarters and the Chen ancestral hall, used as the military region's first arsenal, are preserved among the village houses, and a memorial museum founded in 2004 and expanded in 2016 has exhibition halls on the wartime base and its arms production.

rows.name: Huiluan Stele
rows.summary: A Northern Song stele carved in 1055 by order of Emperor Renzong with the poem 'The Khitans Leave the Border', written in his own hand by Emperor Zhenzong after the Chanyuan peace with the Liao. The broken original stands in a pavilion on Yujing Street beside a replica made in 1978 from rubbings and a poem stele of the Republican period.

rows.name: Nanle Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The Confucian temple of Nanle County town on South Street, a provincially protected monument whose surviving Qing buildings are the main Dacheng Hall and the Chongsheng Shrine to Confucius's ancestors. It became a 4A scenic area in 2025 and hosts cultural events and summer activities for families.

rows.name: Pushang Park
rows.summary: A large park and leisure resort around a lake on the west side of Puyang city, used for strolls, seasonal lantern fairs and family outings. In February 2026 a family area called Longqi Island opened on an island in the lake, with a sandy beach, water play, children's rides, camping and evening shows.

rows.name: Pushui Town
rows.summary: A recently built leisure quarter in Puyang County town with pavilions and towers in traditional style, food stalls, shops and evening entertainment. It is busiest at night and on holidays, with events such as a summer water-splashing festival, costume parades and sparks of molten iron thrown in the traditional da tiehua performance.

rows.name: Qicheng Ruins Park
rows.summary: A heritage park in Puyang city on the site of Qi, a Spring and Autumn town of the state of Wey where, according to the Chunqiu and Zuozhuan, the feudal lords met seven times; some place the death of Confucius's disciple Zilu here in 480 BC. About 1.5 km of the town's rammed-earth wall still stands in the park, built up over the Longshan, Spring and Autumn and Han periods. The park, laid out from 1991, has displays of the site and its finds alongside memorial sights, and now also hosts intangible-heritage workshops and a traditional-style academy.

rows.name: Shanxi–Hebei–Shandong–Henan Field Army Headquarters Site
rows.name_zh: 晋冀鲁豫野战军指挥部旧址
rows.summary: Baiyige village, just south of Fan County's new town, is where the Shanxi–Hebei–Shandong–Henan Field Army under Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping rested during the Civil War and, in late 1946, held a week-long meeting of its regiment-level and senior officers. Liu and Deng lodged in a villager's house and the meeting was held in a farm courtyard and threshing ground on the edge of the village; the site became a national heritage unit in 2019. Fan County lists it among its heritage sites for visitors and planned further repair and display work there in 2025.

rows.name: Tangwu Gong Stele
rows.summary: A Yuan-dynasty stele of 1356 shaped like a small roofed building: a square pillar inscribed on all four sides in clerical script under a carved stone roof with a lotus finial. Its text tells how a Tangut family came from the Helan Mountains with the Mongol armies and settled here; villagers named Yang nearby regard themselves as their descendants and built the protective pavilion in 1985.

rows.name: Anguo Temple, Shanzhou
rows.summary: A hillside Buddhist temple founded in the Sui dynasty, nicknamed the Glazed-Tile Temple for the glazed tiles on its halls, with buildings mostly of the Ming and Qing. Gates and front, middle and rear halls climb the slope in two courtyards divided by a brick 'fire wall' with a central gate tower in imitation of timber, and the halls keep brick and wood carving.

rows.name: Baolun Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A square brick pagoda with closely set eaves, built in 1176–77 under the Jin dynasty, standing in Shanzhou Park on the site of the old Shanzhou city in western Sanmenxia. It is nicknamed the Toad Pagoda because clapping near its base produces an echo like a croaking toad.

rows.name: Ganshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the mountains about 20 km south of Sanmenxia, rising to Ganlu Peak at about 1,885 m, with forest walks, autumn red-leaf areas, a water play area and a butterfly valley. It also has an outdoor activity base, mountain-bike facilities and a ski centre for winter.

rows.name: Guo State Museum
rows.summary: A museum built over the cemetery of the Western Zhou state of Guo on Shangcunling in northern Sanmenxia, where hundreds of burials, chariot pits and sacrificial pits were excavated from 1956 onwards. Its galleries show bronzes and jades from the tombs of the Guo rulers Guo Ji and Guo Zhong, among them a jade-handled iron sword, and visitors can walk into the excavated pits where real chariots and horses were buried some 2,800 years ago.

rows.name: Hangu Pass
rows.summary: The site of the ancient pass that guarded the narrow corridor between the Central Plain and the Wei valley, fortified by the state of Qin in the Warring States period and fought over for centuries afterwards. Legend says that Laozi wrote the Tao Te Ching here at the request of the pass keeper Yinxi before heading west, and since 1992 the site has been rebuilt with a new east gate tower and Taoist halls such as the Taichu Palace.

rows.name: Hanshan Mountain, Lingbao
rows.summary: A high, thickly wooded mountain in Guxian town, Lingbao, next to the Xiaoqinling nature reserve, whose Jinding summit rises to about 2,200 m. Old Buddhist and Taoist sites survive on the mountain, among them the Sanhuang and Sanguan caves and the Yuhuang Pavilion, along with rock formations tied to local legends. A passenger ropeway climbs the mountain.

rows.name: Hongqingsi Grottoes
rows.summary: A small group of Buddhist cave shrines cut in the Northern Wei into an east-facing hillside at Shifo ('Stone Buddha') village, east of Yima: five caves hold 46 niches and more than 120 carved figures. It is of interest to visitors who follow early cave sculpture on the route between Luoyang and Sanmenxia.

rows.name: Lushi City God Temple
rows.summary: A temple to the city god, the town's protective deity, in the county town of Lushi. The county government calls it one of the larger and best-preserved ancient building complexes in western Henan, with a gate, a performance stage, an offering hall and a main hall flanked by side corridors; it was founded at the end of the Yuan, rebuilt in the early Ming, again in 1464–66 and after a fire in 1550, and repaired several times since 1949 with heritage funds.

rows.name: Miaodigou Archaeological Site Park and Museum
rows.summary: The site of a Neolithic village of the Yangshao culture's Miaodigou phase (about 4000–3500 BC), with a later Miaodigou II layer, excavated in 1956–57 ahead of the Sanmenxia Dam and again in 2002. An archaeological park covers part of the site, and the Miaodigou Museum beside it, designed by Tsinghua University and opened in October 2021, displays painted pottery and other finds from recent excavations.

rows.name: Miaoshang Village Sunken Courtyards
rows.summary: A farming village on the loess tableland south of Sanmenxia whose homes are dug into the ground: each courtyard is a square pit with cave rooms cut into its walls, so the village stays hidden from view until the pit edges. It is on the national list of Chinese traditional villages, its Qing to Republican-era courtyards are a national heritage unit, and some are used for a courtyard holiday village.

rows.name: Niangniang Mountain, Lingbao
rows.summary: A granite mountain and national geopark about 13 km west-south-west of Lingbao, known for its 'stone waterfalls', dark streaks running down bare granite slabs that look like ink paintings. Paths lead past the Baichi Waterfall, a string of pools and a Niangniang temple towards the summit at 1,563 m.

rows.name: Shanzhou Sunken Courtyard Scenic Area
rows.summary: A village of sunken courtyard houses at Beiying, south of Sanmenxia, opened as a scenic area: square pits are dug into the loess and cave rooms cut into their walls, hiding the village below ground level, a building craft listed as national intangible heritage in 2011. Some courtyards are open as folk-culture displays, guesthouses and snack stalls.

rows.name: Shihao Section of the Xiaohan Ancient Road
rows.summary: A surviving stretch of the Xiaohan road, the ancient route between Chang'an and Luoyang through the Xiao Mountains and the Hangu pass, where a limestone road surface and roadside water-storage features can still be seen on the hillside. In 2014 it was inscribed as part of the 'Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an–Tianshan Corridor' World Heritage Site, and Du Fu wrote his 'Three Officers' poems in this area in 759.

rows.name: Shuanglongwan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A river-valley scenic area near the source of the Luo River in western Lushi County, named after the peaks Dalongtou and Xiaolongtou, around which the river winds in an S-shaped loop. It combines riverside walks with caves, side valleys of peach blossom, rafting and evening illuminations.

rows.name: Swan Lake National Urban Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 天鹅湖国家城市湿地公园
rows.pinyin: Tiān'é Hú Guójiā Chéngshì Shīdì Gōngyuán
rows.summary: A large wetland park on the Yellow River flats between the eastern and western halves of Sanmenxia, known for the large flocks of wild swans that winter on its lakes from October. Paths link islands, pavilions and lakes, and the park also has a peony garden that blooms in April and lotus ponds in summer.

rows.name: Wengcheng Waterfall
rows.summary: A small valley in Shiziping township, Lushi County, with five waterfalls in succession, the highest being the 61 m Wengcheng Waterfall, which freezes in winter. Boardwalks follow the stream, and the area also has guesthouses, farm restaurants and children's play areas.

rows.name: Xianmen Mountain, Mianchi
rows.summary: A mountain valley scenic area in Duancun township, about 30 km from Mianchi town, developed by the Yangshao liquor company as part of its tourism estate; it held its opening ceremony and 4A plaque unveiling in April 2023. Walks lead through wooded valleys and flower fields to a lake, the company stores liquor in caves in the hillside, and there is a long drift-rafting run.

rows.name: Yangshao Liquor Estate
rows.summary: The factory tourism area of the Yangshao liquor group in Mianchi, built around its distillery with brewing workshops, a cellar of liquor stored in caves, a museum of world liquor history, company exhibition halls and a pedestrian culture street. It suits visitors interested in Chinese baijiu and how it is made.

rows.name: Yangshao Village Site and Yangshao Culture Museum
rows.summary: The village where the Swedish geologist Johan Gunnar Andersson found Neolithic painted pottery in 1921, giving its name to the Yangshao culture; the site was settled roughly 7,000 to 6,000 years ago and also has Longshan remains. The Yangshao Culture Museum, opened in 2011 and reopened in September 2024 after a refit, presents the finds and the story of the discovery, and a national archaeological site park around the excavation areas has been open since 2021.

rows.name: Yanzishan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills of Chuankou township, Lingbao, with stands of pagoda trees and dawn redwoods, several reservoirs and a cluster of waterfalls. It has restaurants, lodging and walking trails and is run as a forest-wellness destination.

rows.name: Yellow River Danxia Gorges
rows.summary: A scenic area on the south bank of the Yellow River in Potou township, north of Mianchi, where red-rock cliffs and gorges run down to the river above the Xiaolangdi reservoir. It is made up of several gorges with rock formations, streams and pools, and offers rafting.

rows.name: Yellow River Park, Sanmenxia
rows.summary: A riverside park about 5 km long on the terraces above the Yellow River along the northern edge of Sanmenxia, running from the Maojin ferry west to the Yellow River bridge. It keeps the natural banks, gullies and vegetation, with gardens, paths and viewpoints over the river flats, and suits an easy walk from the city.

rows.name: Yuxi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A narrow river gorge more than 30 km long in the mountains of northern Lushi County, with a chain of waterfalls and plunge pools, the best known being the Dacongtan Waterfall. Its main draw is a 6 km drift-rafting route that passes through three rock tunnels and over a series of waterfall drops.

rows.name: Yuxi Herb Garden
rows.summary: A rural tourism park next to the Yuxi Grand Canyon that combines fields of Chinese medicinal herbs and flowers with fruit picking, a recreated western Henan village and local food. It makes an easy stop on a trip to the canyon.

rows.name: Zhongliu Dizhu Scenic Area (Sanmenxia Dam)
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area built around the Sanmenxia Dam, begun in 1957 and brought into use in 1960–61 as the first major dam on the Yellow River, and the Dizhu rock just downstream, the 'pillar in midstream' that has withstood the current for millennia and gave Chinese a proverb for steadfastness. Besides views of the dam and the gorge, the area has a museum, a park on the flood-control legend of Yu the Great, terraced fields, a riverside sightseeing train and a shopping street.

rows.name: Chongfa Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal nine-storey brick pagoda 34.6 m tall, built in 1093–1098 under the Northern Song, standing in the martyrs' cemetery in the north-east corner of Yongcheng's old town; the temple itself has gone. Its interior combines several stair layouts, and 323 yellow- and green-glazed tiles showing the Buddha with two disciples are set into its walls.

rows.name: Fengqi Lake, Sui County
rows.summary: A lakeside park in Sui county town created from 2018 on the site of a disused brickworks. It is best known for evening cultural events, such as the molten-iron 'fire flower' performances, drone shows and folk shows staged at Spring Festival.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Huaihai Campaign General Front Committee
rows.name_zh: 商丘淮海战役总前委旧址
rows.summary: The site at Zhangcaiyuan village, 12 km south-east of Shangqiu's old city, that from 30 December 1948 to 24 March 1949 housed in turn the General Front Committee of the Huaihai Campaign, the Central Plains Field Army headquarters and the front committee for the Yangtze River crossing. Deng Xiaoping, Liu Bocheng and Chen Yi directed the final phase of the campaign from here, and the site has been protected since 1963.

rows.name: Huaihai Campaign Chenguanzhuang Memorial
rows.name_zh: 淮海战役陈官庄纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial park of about 13 ha at Chenguanzhuang, where the Chenguanzhuang encirclement battle of the Huaihai Campaign, in the Chinese Civil War of 1948–49, was fought. Founded in 1963 and enlarged in 1974 and 2007–2012, it has a 24.6 m monument, a memorial hall of about 9,000 m², an exhibition on the fallen, a cemetery with a crypt of remains and a 200 m wall of names, and stone reliefs and bronze statues of the campaign's commanders.

rows.name: Longgang Bay Scenic Area
rows.summary: A farm-tourism and study-tour park at Yinzhuang village, Taiping town, Xiayi County, whose rated scenic area covers about 55 ha of a 340 ha agricultural base. It has strawberries grown on raised racks in greenhouses, an aquaponics hall, a computer-controlled seedling factory, wetland flower fields and a fruit theme park, and also runs farming study courses for school groups.

rows.name: Mount Mangdang
rows.summary: A cluster of low hills in northern Yongcheng, rising to 156.8 m, where Liu Bang, the future founder of the Han dynasty, began his revolt against the Qin by slaying a white serpent, and where the Western Han kings of Liang cut their tombs deep into the rock. Visitors can enter the vast rock-cut tombs of King Xiao of Liang and his queen, whose tomb runs about 210 m, and see Chen Sheng's grave, the memorial to Liu Bang's uprising, the cliff where Confucius is said to have sheltered from rain and the foundations of a Han ritual hall on the main peak. Finds such as a jade burial suit and the 'Four Deities' mural are in the Shangqiu Museum and the Henan Museum.

rows.name: North Lake, Sui County
rows.summary: A lake of about 3.3 km² on the north side of Sui county town, formed when the old walled city of Suizhou was drowned after the Yellow River dykes were breached in 1642. Islands that were the higher parts of the old city now hold gardens such as the Xiang Garden, where the county museum is housed, and the lake is used for canoeing training and triathlon races.

rows.name: Riyue Lake, Shangqiu
rows.summary: An artificial lake of about 1 km² in the business district of Shangqiu's new town, dug as part of the new district's water system to store Yellow River water for irrigation and as a landscaped park. It is an urban park rather than a natural lake, suited to an evening stroll.

rows.name: Riyue Lake, Yongcheng
rows.summary: A large park created from 2009 on land that had subsided over coal workings between Yongcheng's old and new towns, planned to cover 24 km², about a quarter of it water. Lakes, wetlands, islands and gardens with pavilions, towers and bridges make up its 'twenty-four views', and it was named a national water-conservancy scenic area in 2014.

rows.name: Shangqiu Ancient City
rows.summary: The walled city of Guide prefecture, built in 1511 after floods destroyed the earlier town, whose brick inner wall (about 4.4 km round), broad moat-lake and outer earthen rampart give it the 'round outside, square inside' plan of a Chinese coin. Inside the four gates the old grid of lanes survives, much restored since the 2010s, with the prefectural Confucian temple, the Mu family courtyard house and the Zhuang Hui Tang residence of the late-Ming writer Hou Fangyu, while outside lie the Ebo (Fire God) Terrace and the rebuilt Yingtian Academy. Several older cities, including the Zhou-dynasty capital of the Song state, lie buried beneath and around it.

rows.name: Shangqiu Museum
rows.summary: Shangqiu's city museum, which opened in a new building on Huashang Avenue in 2016 and holds about 19,000 objects, mostly from excavations in the region. Highlights include finds from the Western Han royal tombs of Liang at Mount Mangdang, among them a jade suit sewn with gold thread.

rows.name: Shengshou Temple Pagoda, Yanzhuang
rows.summary: A six-sided, nine-storey brick pagoda of the dense-eave type, roughly 20 m tall, built under the Northern Song for the Shengshou Temple, which no longer exists, at Yanzhuang village. Repaired in 1985, it is the only national heritage unit in Sui County.

rows.name: Wanggongzhuang Painting Village
rows.summary: A village about 25 km north-east of Minquan county town known as China's first tiger-painting village, where more than 900 villagers work in painting, mostly tigers in the traditional Chinese style. Visitors walk a street of galleries, see the art exhibition hall and browse paintings for sale, and there is also a fruit-picking garden and a study-tour base.

rows.name: Zhecheng Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The site of Zhecheng's county town from the Warring States period to the Ming, abandoned in the 16th century when Yellow River silt built up outside its walls and left the interior lower than the land around, so that it became a lake. A 230 m stretch of rammed-earth wall, 5–10 m high, survives above ground with the sites of the Xiehe Terrace, linked with the worship of Laozi, and other old landmarks, now part of the Ronghu Lake park on the north side of the present town.

rows.name: Baiquan Gardens, Huixian
rows.summary: A classical garden of Ming and Qing halls and pavilions around a spring-fed lake at the foot of Sumen Hill on the north-west edge of Huixian town; the springs now flow mainly after heavy rain and the lake is topped up from outside. The hill was a retreat for scholars and holds the home and teaching place of the Song philosopher Shao Yong, a Ming Confucian temple, the terrace of the Wei–Jin recluse Sun Deng and many carved steles. The Baiquan herb fair, centuries old and listed as national intangible heritage, takes its name from the place.

rows.name: Baiyun Temple, Huixian
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple founded in the Tang dynasty in the Baiyun Temple National Forest Park on the southern slopes of the Taihang Mountains; its main hall, with glazed dragon and lotus ridge decoration, is Ming, and most other buildings are Qing. Memorial pagodas of monks from the Song to Ming periods stand around the temple and on the wooded slope behind, and the temple keeps a stele of 1008 on its Five Hundred Arhats hall and some very old ginkgo trees; the Qianlong Emperor visited in 1750.

rows.name: Baligou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A canyon scenic area in the Taihang Mountains north-west of Huixian, rated 5A in 2019, where three tiers of red cliffs enclose deep valleys with a string of pools and waterfalls, among them the Tianhe (Heavenly River) Waterfall. Paths link sights such as a 'one-thread-of-sky' cleft and the Black Dragon Pool, and the area now also takes in the Tianjie Mountain and Jiulian Mountain sections on the heights above.

rows.name: Baoquan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area under the red Taihang cliffs west of Huixian, rated 5A in December 2024. It has two linked parts: the Grand Canyon, a gentle valley of streams, pools and waterfalls suited to families, and Ya Tianxia on the cliffs above, which opened in April 2023. A cableway, a lift inside the cliff and the glass-floored Xiangyun platform give views over the lake, the cliff-top zone offers via ferrata, bungee jumping and a cliff roller coaster, and evening light shows are projected on the cliffs and waterfalls.

rows.name: Boyu Village Gentleman Culture Area, Changyuan
rows.summary: A rural tourism area in Boyu village on the edge of Changyuan, the home of Qu Boyu, a statesman of the Spring and Autumn state of Wey whom Confucius praised as a true gentleman. The village, put on Henan's first provincial list of place-name cultural heritage in 2025, is the ancestral seat of the Qu clan and has been developed around the theme of 'gentleman culture'; a clan ancestral ceremony and culture festival took place here in March 2026.

rows.name: Daguan Stele, Xinxiang
rows.name_zh: 新乡文庙大观圣作之碑
rows.pinyin: Xīnxiāng Wénmiào Dàguān Shèngzuò zhī Bēi
rows.summary: A stone stele of 1108 carrying Emperor Huizong's regulations for state schools, written out in his own slender 'thin gold' calligraphy under a six-character heading by the minister Cai Jing. It is one of several surviving copies of this Daguan-era stele in China and stands in a pavilion in the grounds of the former Xinxiang county Confucian temple, in a compound used by local government offices.

rows.name: Dajue Temple and Wanshou Pagoda, Yanjin
rows.summary: A temple in the north-west of Yanjin town whose seven-storey Ming pagoda, the Wanshou Pagoda, gives its name to the square in front. The temple was founded in the Tang dynasty under another name and called Dajue after a mid-Ming rebuilding; besides the main hall it has a shrine to Lu Ban and Ge Hong and steles of the Yuan to Qing periods, including one written by the Yuan calligrapher Zhao Mengfu. A small museum is housed inside the temple.

rows.name: Fenghu Lake Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped lake in the centre of the new Pingyuan district, across the Yellow River from Zhengzhou, built as a reservoir for Yellow River water and opened as a park that was rated 4A in 2019. Paths circle the lake past a history and folk-culture section, lawns and plazas, cherry-tree walks, a wetland area with lotus and a wooded central island.

rows.name: Five Dynasties Dharani Pillar, Weihui
rows.summary: A stone dharani pillar of the Five Dynasties period engraved with Buddhist incantations, rising from a plain shaft through several carved tiers to a jewel-shaped finial. It now stands indoors under a skylight in a building in the north of Weihui town.

rows.name: Former Heshuo Library
rows.summary: A library building completed in 1935 in central Xinxiang, in a Chinese palace style with a raised central bay under curved tiled roofs. The district government describes it as a witness to the 1946 Nationalist–Communist talks in which Zhou Enlai, Zhang Zhizhong and the American envoy George Marshall took part. It faces a public square, and conservation works on the building have been carried out since 2024.

rows.name: Gongcheng City Site
rows.summary: The site of Gong, the Zhou-period city whose ruler Gong Bo He is traditionally said to have governed during the Gonghe Regency that began in 841 BC, the first precisely dated year in Chinese history. A grassy section of its earthen rampart survives in the town of Huixian, lined by a paved walk with a stone balustrade and marked by a large heritage plaque.

rows.name: Guanshan Geopark
rows.summary: A national geopark in the Taihang Mountains north-west of Huixian, named after the ancient Zixia pass on a route through the range. Its scenery comes from cliff collapse and fissuring: forests of rock pillars, a narrow 'one-thread-of-sky' cleft, natural rock bridges and sheer walls, together with waterfalls and pools along the Pangu stream and a cave system known as Baibao Cave.

rows.name: Jiaoding Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Taihang range north of Huixian, rated 4A in 2015, with red cliffs and forested slopes reached by a mountain road that visitors may drive up. It is also a provincial-level holiday area and forest-wellness base, and is a popular spot for snow scenery in winter.

rows.name: Jinghua Garden, Xinxiang
rows.summary: A landscaped leisure park in Xiaoji town, Xinxiang County, run by a local company. The city's culture bureau counts it among the scenic areas that combine sightseeing with a theme park, and it has also been listed as a national agricultural-tourism demonstration site. It is a modern built attraction rather than a historic garden, and suits a short family outing from Xinxiang.

rows.name: Jiuduo Rouduo Braised Meat Culture Park
rows.summary: A factory-tour attraction at the plant of Jiuduo Rouduo, a maker of soy-braised meats and side dishes in the industrial zone of Yuanyang County. A viewing corridor runs past the production workshops, and exhibition halls and a small garden present the company and the tradition of jianglu braised meat. It suits visitors curious about how Chinese packaged food is made.

rows.name: Linglong Pagoda, Yuanyang
rows.summary: A tall hexagonal brick pagoda of 1105, imitating a timber pavilion tower, outside the east gate of Yuanwu town; it belonged to Shanhu Temple, which burnt down in the Qing dynasty. The tower leans noticeably to the north-east, and its lowest storey is buried in Yellow River silt.

rows.name: Longwoyan Forest Park
rows.summary: A provincial-level forest park in the Taihang foothills of northern Weihui, around Longwoyan village, which has turned to village tourism. It is a wooded hill area for walks, and in winter it runs ice-and-snow play areas.

rows.name: Mausoleum of the Prince of Lu
rows.summary: The tombs of Zhu Yiliu, Prince Jian of Lu and a younger brother of the Wanli Emperor, and of his secondary consort Zhao, laid out side by side on the southern slope of Fenghuang Mountain on the model of the emperor's own Dingling tomb near Beijing. A spirit way of stone officials and animals leads past stone archways and a three-arched bridge to gates, a sacrificial hall, a soul tower and walled burial mounds, all within bluestone walls. Many of the sculptures were damaged in the 1960s, while the consort's tomb, used as a prison from 1953 to 2005, came through largely intact.

rows.name: Pagoda of Guangtang Temple
rows.summary: A Song-period brick pagoda, the surviving structure of Guangtang Temple, standing in a village north of Yanjin town. Each of its storeys is marked by a band of brick bracket-work under the eaves, with small arched openings and lattice-patterned panels in the walls.

rows.name: Paomaling Geopark
rows.summary: A provincial-level geopark and forest park in the Taihang foothills of northern Weihui, named after the ridge of the same name. It is an area of wooded hills for walking and scenery, and at the Spring Festival it has staged Ming-themed costume performances.

rows.name: Shamen City Site
rows.summary: The sand-covered remains of a walled town and ferry crossing on an old course of the Yellow River, known locally as Wuqi City, with layers from the Warring States and Han periods beneath Song and Jin–Yuan remains. It was a Song ferry point and, in the late Jin and early Yuan, the seat of Weizhou prefecture until the river moved and floods buried it; stretches of the west and north earthen walls survive among woodland.

rows.name: Shanji Pagoda of Tianwang Temple
rows.summary: A Yuan-dynasty brick pagoda, the surviving structure of the former Tianwang Temple in the town of Huixian. Its tall shaft rises in tiers of brick bracket-work eaves with small arched openings, and it now stands in a small fenced square among new housing.

rows.name: Tang Dharani Pillar of Dingjue Temple
rows.summary: An octagonal Tang-dynasty stone pillar engraved with the Usnisa Vijaya Dharani sutra, which once stood at Dingjue Temple in Xinxiang and is described by the Weibin district government as one of only two surviving Tang dharani pillars in China. It is now kept indoors at the Pingyuan Museum in eastern Xinxiang, the home of Xinxiang Museum, whose displays also cover the Neolithic Mengzhuang site in Huixian.

rows.name: Temple and Tomb of Bi Gan
rows.summary: A temple and tomb complex for Bi Gan, the Shang-dynasty prince who was executed for rebuking the last Shang king, Di Xin, and was later worshipped as a god of wealth. A temple was first founded here in 494, and the present screen wall, gates and sacrificial hall are Ming and Qing rebuilds on an axis that ends at the earthen burial mound, ringed by old cypresses. Among the steles is one whose four characters are traditionally attributed to Confucius, and a Bi Gan culture festival with temple fairs and lantern shows is held each spring.

rows.name: Wangjing Tower, Weihui
rows.summary: A two-storey hall of brick and stone built in 1591 by Zhu Yiliu, Prince of Lu and the only full brother of the Wanli Emperor, who raised it out of longing for his mother in Beijing; its name means 'gazing towards the capital'. It is a vaulted 'beamless' hall with no timber frame, faced with bluestone outside and white stone within. The library hall that once stood on its roof is gone, but a carved four-pillar stone archway still stands up there.

rows.name: Wulongshan Tourist Area
rows.summary: A leisure and amusement complex in Changcun town just north-east of Huixian, with a children's amusement park, a ski slope in winter and staged shows, among them one on the Battle of Muye, in which the Zhou overthrew the Shang. It suits families looking for rides and entertainment rather than scenery.

rows.name: Xiangquan Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A mountain temple on Linluo Mountain whose cliff carvings date from the Northern Qi: a Thousand Buddha Cave with groups of Buddha and bodhisattva figures and, beside it, a carved passage of the Avatamsaka (Huayan) Sutra. Later additions include the stone pagoda of the founding monk Sengchou, a stone pavilion of a thousand Buddhas, and the characters 'Xiangquan' (fragrant spring) carved by the Ming Prince of Lu above the spring that gives the temple its name.

rows.name: Ximing Temple Buddhist Stele
rows.summary: A large Northern Wei Buddhist stele carved with a triad of the Buddha Amitayus between the bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, set against a backscreen decorated with lotus petals, seated Buddhas, flying apsaras and flame patterns. Broken up in the 1960s–70s and buried by villagers, it was dug up, pieced together and re-erected in the early 1990s, and the shelter built over it now forms the Xinxiang County Museum of Stone Carving at Xiaosongfo village.

rows.name: Yuanwu City God Temple
rows.summary: A small temple to the city god on East Street in the old town of Yuanwu, founded in 1369. Its main hall and worship hall date from the founding and keep Yuan-period building features, the front and middle halls were added in the late Ming, and Ming and Qing steles stand in the courtyards. The leaning Linglong Pagoda is a few hundred metres away.

rows.name: Ancient City of the Huang State
rows.summary: The capital of the Zhou-dynasty state of Huang, north-west of Huangchuan town: a rectangular enclosure of rammed-earth walls, still several metres high in places, with a moat outside the east wall. Inside, archaeologists have found wells, bronze-casting workshops and a raised palace platform.

rows.name: Ancient City of the Jiang State
rows.summary: The remains of a walled city at Qisi, linked by ancient texts to the Zhou-dynasty state of Jiang and later the Chu town of Qisi and a Han county seat. Broken stretches of wall survive on three sides of the roughly rectangular enclosure, and the present-day village of Qisi stands within it.

rows.name: Anshan Forest Park
rows.summary: A provincial forest park on Anshan, a wooded hill in Quanhepu township in the east of Gushi County. A Daoist temple, Anshan Nainai Temple, stands near the summit.

rows.name: Chen Yuanguang Ancestral Temple
rows.summary: An ancestral temple in Chenji town honouring Chen Yuanguang (657–711), the Tang general from Gushi who is revered in Zhangzhou, Fujian, and among emigrant communities in Taiwan and South-East Asia as the 'Sacred King who Opened Zhangzhou'. It was founded by his grandson in the Tianbao era of the Tang, and the present halls date from the Jiaqing reign of the Qing.

rows.name: Chengyang City Site Archaeological Park
rows.summary: The site of Chengyang, an Eastern Zhou walled town that was a military stronghold of the state of Chu, surrounded by Chu tombs. Parts of the city wall and the outline of its moat survive, and a tomb excavated here in 1957 yielded a set of bronze bells. The site museum, opened in 2014 inside the archaeological park, is devoted to Chu culture, with bronzes, pottery, lacquered wood and jade, and halls built over two excavated tomb chambers.

rows.name: Dabie Mountains Camping Park
rows.summary: A campground park at the eastern edge of Xin County town, opened in 2017, where self-drive groups can stay overnight, with campfires in the evening. It suits travellers who want to stay out in the Dabie hills while visiting the county's old villages and revolutionary sites.

rows.name: Dasu Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of low wooded hills south-west of Guangshan town, set up in 2015 and taking in Dasu Mountain, Longshou Mountain and the Wangmu Daoist temple area. The monk Huisi taught in the area in the 550s and 560s, and his disciple Zhiyi, later the leading figure of the Tiantai school of Buddhism, studied under him on Dasu Mountain from 560 to 567. Jingju Temple, which honours this tradition, stands in the park, and Su Shi wrote a poem on a visit to it.

rows.name: Deng Yingchao's Ancestral Home
rows.summary: A group of Qing-dynasty courtyard houses in Guangshan town where the grandfather and father of Deng Yingchao, the Communist leader and wife of Premier Zhou Enlai, lived. Restored in 2001 and 2006, its three courtyards hold exhibitions on the lives of Deng and Zhou with personal belongings, a corridor of inscribed tablets and a marble bust of Deng.

rows.name: Dingliwan Village
rows.summary: A hamlet in Balifan town, Xin County, whose old houses were built by families with roots in southern Anhui and northern Jiangxi, in a Hui style of high horse-head gables, grey brick on stone bases, carved brick and stone gatehouses and narrow stone-paved lanes. Five tall gatehouses line the north bank of the village pond, one of them belonging to the house of a Qing prefect, and in 2012 it was named one of the first Chinese Traditional Villages.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Red Army's 1st Army
rows.summary: A three-room brick-and-timber farmhouse with a walled courtyard in Huanggufan village, used in 1930 as headquarters of the Red Army's 1st Army, formed that spring with Xu Jishen as commander and Xu Xiangqian as his deputy. The middle room was the commanders' meeting room, the south room Xu Jishen's bedroom and the north room the mess.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Red Army's 25th Army
rows.name_zh: 红二十五军司令部旧址
rows.summary: The site used in 1933 as headquarters of the Red Army's 25th Army, the force that set out on its own Long March from Hejiachong in neighbouring Luoshan County in November 1934. It stands in Fangwan village, Jianchanghe township, in the hills of southern Xin County near the Hubei border, a few kilometres from the former 1st Army headquarters and the border soviet government site.

rows.name: Former Site of the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Border Special District Soviet Government
rows.name_zh: 鄂豫皖边特区苏维埃政府旧址
rows.pinyin: È-Yù-Wǎn Biān Tèqū Sūwéi'āi Zhèngfǔ Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A former seat, in Yangfan village, of the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Border Special District Soviet Government, which the Communist-led base area proclaimed in June 1930. It is one of a cluster of 1930s Red Army and soviet sites in the hills of southern Xin County, close to the former 1st Army headquarters.

rows.name: General Xu Shiyou's Hometown and Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The birthplace of Xu Shiyou (1906–1985), one of the founding generals of the People's Liberation Army, who as a boy trained at Shaolin Temple, in the hamlet of Xujiawa in Hepu village. The site takes in his family home, a memorial hall on his life and his grave: he asked to be buried beside his mother, and in 1985 Deng Xiaoping approved this exception to the rule that senior leaders be cremated.

rows.name: Guishan Lake Park
rows.summary: A lake park north of Luoshan county town, beside the Youdian township seat, laid out in recent years around a lake with surrounding woodland and walkways. The paths have been themed as an 'intellectual property park', with signboards and illustrations about patents, trademarks and intangible-heritage crafts, and the park makes an easy walk for anyone staying in Luoshan.

rows.name: Hejiachong (Red 25th Army Long March Starting Point)
rows.summary: A village in Tiepu town, Luoshan County, where about 2,900 soldiers of the Red Army's 25th Army assembled by an old ginkgo tree on 16 November 1934 before setting out on their own Long March, which reached northern Shaanxi in September 1935. The He family ancestral hall, a Ming-dynasty building that served as the army's headquarters, is now a memorial hall with period furniture, oil lamps and army shoes on display.

rows.name: Hejiazhai Campsite
rows.summary: A hillside campsite and tent-hotel resort among the tea gardens of Haojiachong village, Shihegang town, opened in 2022, with white tent lodges scattered over the slopes and a shuttle up to the hilltop. When it opened it also had a mirror-glass photo platform and a glass water slide through the woods, plus tea-themed study programmes for school groups.

rows.name: Huangbai Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of forested ridges and valleys in the Dabie Mountains at the southern tip of Shangcheng County, where Henan meets Hubei and Anhui. Fayan Temple, a Buddhist monastery, stands within the park.

rows.name: Jingangtai Maoer Peak Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area on Jingangtai, the highest peak of the Dabie Mountains in Henan, within the Jingangtai National Geopark south-east of Shangcheng town. It takes its name from Maoer ('cat's ear') Peak and suits a day of hill walking on the Henan–Anhui border.

rows.name: Jingangtai Xihe Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Jingangtai National Geopark in the Dabie Mountains of Shangcheng County, made up of a tea-terraced gorge, the Huatuo Valley, a lake ringed by a waterside boardwalk and a river gorge used for rafting. Reports from 2023 and 2024 list canyon trails, a glass suspension bridge, a treetop adventure course and ziplines, and the valley is one of the main sources of Shangcheng's high-mountain green tea.

rows.name: Jinlan Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the wooded Dabie hills on the north-western edge of Xin County town. In 1932 the Red Army fought a blocking action along the line from Fushanzhai to Jinlan Mountain during the Nationalist encirclement campaigns against the base area.

rows.name: Linglong Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake about 5 km long in the tea and bamboo hills of Dongshuanghe township, created in 1965 as the Longwangsi Reservoir, whose waters covered the site of the old Longwang Temple. The scenic area around it combines forest, tea gardens and an old ginkgo tree with lakeside platforms, boating and fishing, and its first phase, finished in 2016, added a folk-culture village and a food street.

rows.name: Lingshan Scenic Area, Luoshan
rows.summary: A granite mountain in Lingshan town, south-west Luoshan County, with forested slopes, streams and waterfalls, forming part of the Dongzhai national bird reserve. Its best-known sight is Lingshan Temple, said to date back to the Northern Wei, where monks and nuns share one temple and a large temple fair is held on the first day of the third lunar month.

rows.name: Longhu Park, Xi County
rows.summary: A long lake park through the middle of Xi County town, created from a former reservoir, with willow-lined embankments, an island and boats on the lake. It was rated 3A until the province raised it to 4A in December 2025, and it makes an easy stroll for anyone staying in town.

rows.name: Mount Jigong
rows.summary: A forested ridge of the Dabie Mountains on the Henan–Hubei border, named after the rooster-shaped crag of Baoxiao Peak and long a summer retreat thanks to its cool climate. From 1898 to 1936 foreign missionaries and diplomats, along with Chinese military figures and businessmen, built hundreds of villas in various styles here, and the surviving early-20th-century buildings are protected as a national heritage site. Paths link the villa quarter with viewpoints and wooded valleys in what is also a national nature reserve.

rows.name: Nanwan Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir in wooded hills just south-west of Xinyang, made by damming the Shi River in 1952–1955, whose dam face carries Mao Zedong's call to harness the Huai River. Three of its islands have been developed for visitors as Tea, Bird and Monkey islands, and Xianyin Temple, first founded in the Southern Dynasties, stands below Xian Mountain at the eastern end. The hills upstream are a main growing area for Xinyang Maojian tea.

rows.name: Pugongshan Mine Park
rows.summary: A mine park on Pugong Hill, across the Huai River from Xi County town, where a former quarry has been landscaped and replanted around a lake among the hills. A natural history museum stands on the site, and the park makes a short outing from Xi County, an ancient county seat on the Huai.

rows.name: Revolutionary Museum of the Capital of the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet Area
rows.name_zh: 鄂豫皖苏区首府革命博物馆
rows.summary: Xin County town, then called Xinji, became the seat of the Communist-led Hubei–Henan–Anhui (Eyuwan) soviet base area in 1931, and former offices of the base survive here, among them those of the Party's Eyuwan Bureau, the soviet government and the Fourth Front Army headquarters. The museum beside them, opened in 1990 and rated a national first-grade museum in 2017, covers the ten years of the base area with weapons, banners, documents, seals, currency and land certificates, plus a gallery on generals from the county.

rows.name: Taohuazhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley about 8 km west of the Jigong Mountain scenic area, named after a local legend of a peach-blossom fairy and known for its streams, pools and waterfalls. Xinyang's official tourism account listed boat trips on its lake, a glass suspension bridge, slides, bungee jumping and jungle rafting among its activities in 2021, so it is aimed at families and groups looking for outdoor fun rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Wenxin Tea Village
rows.summary: A tea-themed tourist village in Shihegang town, in the hills south-west of Xinyang where Xinyang Maojian, one of China's best-known green teas, is grown. Visitors can pick leaves in the tea gardens and watch the tea being fired by hand, a craft listed as national intangible heritage. Nanwan Lake is nearby.

rows.name: West Jiuhua Mountain
rows.summary: A hill scenic area in Chenlinzi town in southern Gushi County, near the Anhui border, built around Miaogao Temple, a Buddhist temple whose monks' stupas are a provincial heritage site. Tea gardens and bamboo groves cover the slopes, and the area is also a provincial geopark.

rows.name: Wuzhanling Eco-tourism Resort
rows.summary: A leisure resort in the wooded valleys of Doushanhe township, Xin County, built around a river-rafting run and also known as Wuzhanling Rafting. It suits a summer day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Xihe and Maopu Old Villages
rows.summary: Two old villages in Zhouhe township: Xihe, a settlement more than 700 years old that sits between green hills and the West River and keeps over 150 old houses of grey brick and dark tile, and Maopu, whose Loushang Louxia hamlet is a listed Chinese Traditional Village. Their Qing houses are listed as heritage buildings, and Xihe has become a busy rural-tourism village with guesthouses and restaurants.

rows.name: Xizhou Shanhai Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the north-western edge of Xi County town, developed from the old state forest farm and named for its "sea" of dawn redwood, pond cypress and bald cypress. It also has large groves of Chinese wingnut and Masson pine, Ma Yuan Square and a cultural hall about Lady Xi, linked with the ancient state of Xi from which the county takes its name, and makes a shady walk close to town.

rows.name: Yongji Bridge, Guangshan
rows.summary: A multi-arch granite bridge, also called Wanjin Bridge, first built in the Ming dynasty, that links the north and south streets of Popihe town across the Popi River. The arches grow larger towards the middle, giving the deck a gentle hump, and the parapets keep carved posts and stone lions.

rows.name: Zhonggulou Family Park
rows.summary: A children's nature park in Popihe town, Guangshan County, laid out on a former forest farm. It has terraced flower beds, playgrounds with slides, climbing nets and sandpits, and cabin lodging, and is aimed at families with young children.

rows.name: Baling Bridge Scenic Area
rows.summary: A park on the western side of Xuchang marking the place where, in Three Kingdoms legend, Guan Yu took his leave of Cao Cao and lifted the parting gift of a robe on the tip of his blade. The original three-arched stone bridge was lost to water works; a modern bridge stands in the park, which also keeps a tablet put up by the late-Ming general Zuo Liangyu. The park's nationally listed Guan Yu Temple, a courtyard complex of halls and a pavilion founded in 1689 and rich in Ming and Qing steles, is unusual in honouring Guan Yu and Cao Cao together in its main hall.

rows.name: China Jun Porcelain Culture Park
rows.summary: A themed park on the north side of Yuzhou devoted to Jun ware, one of the celebrated Song-dynasty ceramics, laid out as a palace-style garden around Tiancheng Pavilion, a building about 50 m tall. The pavilion's halls display the history of Jun porcelain and the work of local kilns, and workshops in the park let visitors try throwing a pot on the wheel. It has hosted several of the city's Jun porcelain festivals.

rows.name: Chunqiu Tower Scenic Area
rows.summary: A walled complex of Ming and Qing-style buildings in the centre of Xuchang's old city, built around the tower where, in Three Kingdoms lore, Guan Yu sat up at night reading the Spring and Autumn Annals while he was held by Cao Cao. The same scenic area takes in the nationally listed Confucian Temple, founded in the Tang and rebuilt several times since, with a screen wall, a semicircular pool and the Dacheng Hall, so that temples to Guan Yu and Confucius stand side by side. A live drama on Guan Yu's story is staged by day and a light show in the evening.

rows.name: City Wall of Xiangcheng
rows.summary: The western side of Xiangcheng's old county wall, the only part left after the south, east and north walls were pulled down between the Republican era and the 1970s. The wall was faced with brick in the late Ming, wrecked by Li Zicheng's rebels and rebuilt in 1651; it now runs along the western edge of the old town, a few hundred metres from the Confucian Temple.

rows.name: Dahongzhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 36 km² in the hills of north-western Yuzhou, named after Dahong, a minister of the legendary Yellow Emperor whom local tradition places here; its highest peak, Wofo Mountain, is 1,156 m. Paths lead past cliffs, caves, streams and pools, and the slopes turn red in the second half of October. Shuttle transport, a glass bridge with a slide and other rides have been added for day-trippers.

rows.name: Huadu Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Chenhuadian town, set among Yanling's flower nurseries, with geothermal bathing pools, a hotel and guesthouses. Camping and seasonal events are held in the grounds, and it makes a base for touring the county's gardens.

rows.name: Huaibang Guild Hall
rows.summary: A guild hall built in 1872 by medicine merchants from Huaiqing prefecture, who traded their 'four Huai herbs' through Yuzhou, one of China's historic medicine markets. Behind a long brick screen wall, its gate-cum-opera stage, side galleries and linked worship and main halls are roofed in peacock-blue glazed tiles and richly carved; the main hall honours Guan Yu flanked by the physicians Zhang Zhongjing and Sun Simiao. It now houses the Yuzhou Museum of Traditional Chinese Medicine Culture.

rows.name: Jianye Green Base
rows.summary: A plant-growing and garden base among the nurseries of Yanling, promoted on the city's 2026 spring flower routes for its anthuriums and crab-apple blossom. The county names it among its main gardens alongside the Flower Expo Garden and Tangyun; expect seasonal planting rather than historic sights.

rows.name: Jinyu Herb Manor
rows.summary: A herb-themed hot-spring resort in Yanling whose bathing pools are infused with fragrant herbs. It is one of several spa resorts the county promotes together with its flower gardens, and suits a relaxing half-day rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Lingjing Xuchang Man Site
rows.summary: The spring-side site where two skull caps of 'Xuchang Man', an archaic human who lived here roughly 100,000 to 130,000 years ago, were dug up in 2007 and 2014, together with stone and bone tools and animal fossils; the finds were published in Science in 2017. A display hall at the excavation area, fitted with a recently completed digital exhibition, presents the dig and its finds.

rows.name: Main Hall of Guanwang Temple, Pojie
rows.summary: The one surviving hall of a village temple to Guan Yu, nationally listed as a Yuan-dynasty timber building and repaired in recent years. It is a modest grey-tiled hall in its own walled yard among village houses, of interest mainly to those looking for early Chinese timber architecture.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Zhu Su, Prince Ding of Zhou
rows.summary: The hillside tomb of Zhu Su (1361–1425), fifth son of the founding Ming emperor, who as Prince of Zhou compiled the Jiuhuang bencao, a pioneering guide to wild plants that can be eaten in times of famine. His tomb and that of a consort were cut into the hills as large brick-vaulted underground palaces, robbed long ago and now empty; the consort's tomb has 18 vaulted chambers off a ring corridor wide enough for a bus. The two tombs and the wooded hills around them are run as a small scenic area.

rows.name: Qianming Temple Pagoda, Yanling
rows.summary: A tall six-sided brick pagoda on Longxing ridge in the north-west of Yanling town, rebuilt in the Song dynasty for a temple first founded in 604; the temple itself has long gone. Its storeys carry brick-carved brackets, blind windows and niches with Buddha figures, and repairs in 1996 found a gilt-bronze Buddha and Ming sutras in its finial.

rows.name: Qianming Temple, Xiangcheng
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the north slope of Shoushan hill south of Xiangcheng, first founded on the summit in 934 and rebuilt several times since; because it faces north it is nicknamed the 'Back-Shadow Temple'. Its finest pieces are a carved-brick screen wall of 1551, showing the Yellow Emperor gathering copper on Shoushan and other legends, and the central Buddha hall with a hip-and-gable roof. A large forest of monks' pagodas west of the temple was destroyed in 1968.

rows.name: Shenhou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A pottery town in the hills south-west of Yuzhou where Jun ware has been made since the Tang and Song, and which is still full of working kilns, studios and showrooms. Its winding old street keeps Ming and Qing houses, the Bolingweng Temple with its opera stage and other shrines, and the town was named a national historic and cultural town in 2005. The town's kiln-site museum is open, and many workshops let visitors watch the firing or try the potter's wheel.

rows.name: Shi'erliancheng Eastern Zhou Walls
rows.summary: Broken stretches of rammed-earth wall winding through the fields north-west of Laocheng in Changge, dated by archaeologists to the Eastern Zhou and thought to be a defensive long wall built by the state of Wei. The name, 'twelve linked walls', comes from the separate sections of earthwork, in which the tamped layers are still clearly visible; bronze weapons have been found along them.

rows.name: Shoushan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hill just south of Xiangcheng town, linked in legend with the Yellow Emperor, who is said to have mined copper here, and ringed by rapeseed fields whose spring flowering has drawn an annual festival since 2018. A walking path circles the hill and leads to a viewing platform on the summit, and Qianming Temple lies at the hill's northern foot.

rows.name: Tangyun Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A garden park among Yanling's plant nurseries that combines a cherry-blossom garden with courtyards, pavilions and colonnades built in Tang-dynasty style among flowering trees. A new Tang-themed section with costume experiences opened in 2026, and the park is a regular stop on the county's spring flower routes.

rows.name: Tianbao Palace
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex north-west of Xuchang, founded in 1240 as an abbey, raised to a 'palace' in 1269, destroyed at the end of the Yuan and rebuilt from the Ming onwards. Along its central axis a triple-arched gate, an offering pavilion on stone columns and halls to Yue Fei, Guan Yu, the Jade Emperor and the Thunder Patriarch lead to the broad Zhenwu Hall, roofed in green glazed tiles and fronted by columns carved with dragons and phoenixes.

rows.name: Tianning Wanshou Temple, Yuzhou
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Yuzhou's old city whose surviving buildings, nationally listed in 2019, date from the Yuan to the Qing dynasties. A tall red-walled hall under a green-glazed roof stands on a street in the old town.

rows.name: Wenfeng Pagoda, Xuchang
rows.summary: A tall octagonal brick pagoda of 13 storeys, built in 1615 on the initiative of the prefect of Xuzhou, Zheng Zhenguang, and also known as the Wenming Pagoda. It stands in a courtyard on Wenfeng Road, now run as the Wenfeng Pagoda Cultural Relics Protection Centre, with three Ming and Qing steles recording its building and repairs in front; it can no longer be climbed.

rows.name: Wucai Dadi Flower Fields
rows.summary: A sightseeing park of flower fields in the core of Yanling County's nursery-growing district, planned in 2015 and laid out from 2016 as part of the county's flower-tourism drive. Expect seasonal flower displays rather than historic sights.

rows.name: Xiangcheng Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A county Confucian temple and school on Limin West Street in Xiangcheng, on this site since the Song and rebuilt many times. Two Ming buildings survive: the Dacheng Hall, rebuilt in the 15th century on Yuan foundations, and the Kuibi, a glazed screen wall of 1585 decorated with panels of coloured brick relief, along with traces of the semicircular pool and the Lingxing Gate.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple Pagoda, Yanling
rows.summary: A brick pagoda, nationally listed as Song-dynasty work, standing in a village south of Yanling town as the only surviving part of Xingguo Temple. The Qianming Temple Pagoda in town is Yanling's other nationally listed pagoda, and the two make a short detour from the county's gardens.

rows.name: Xudu Han–Wei City Site
rows.summary: The site of Xu, where Cao Cao brought the last Han emperor in 196 and where the court stayed until the Wei capital moved to Luoyang in the 220s. Most of the city now lies under farmland, but parts of the inner earthen wall survive and the Yuxiu Terrace, where Emperor Xian is said to have sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, still rises above the fields with temple halls on top. Just to the north, Zhang Gong Shrine is said locally to mark where Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei camped when they were received by Emperor Xian.

rows.name: Yanling National Flower and Plant Expo Garden
rows.summary: A large landscaped garden in Yanling's new town, built in 2002 to show off the county's centuries-old nursery and flower trade, with themed areas for bamboo, wintersweet, bonsai, conifers and tropical plants. It also works as a showground and market for nursery stock and hosted early editions of the Central China Flower and Tree Fair, which is still held in Yanling every autumn. Come for plants and bonsai rather than historic sights.

rows.name: Yuzhou Jun Kiln Site Museum
rows.summary: A museum on the Juntai kiln site in Yuzhou, source of the 'official' Jun wares made for the imperial court, whose date (late Northern Song or early Ming) is still debated; the kilns were found in 1964 and excavated from 1974. The building, designed by the architect Qi Kang and opened in 2011, presents the excavated remains and a chronological exhibition on Yuzhou's history and Jun ware drawn from a collection of about 1,500 objects. The national listing also covers the kiln sites at Shenhou, where a separate kiln-site museum is open.

rows.name: Aoparara Water Park, Xiangdiwan
rows.name_zh: 香堤湾·奥帕拉拉水公园
rows.summary: An outdoor summer water park next to the Xiangdiwan hotel on Zhongyuan West Road in Yulong town, Xingyang, on the western edge of Zhengzhou, built around a large wave pool. It suits families wanting a day in the water close to the city.

rows.name: Central Plains Western Henan Anti-Japanese War Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park in Tianzhongwan village, deep in the Fuxi Mountain area of Xinmi, where General Pi Dingjun set up the Communist-led Western Henan anti-Japanese base area in 1944. It was developed by the local tourism company around Pi Dingjun's former office and keeps the wartime site as a memorial and patriotic-education base.

rows.name: Changshou Mountain, Zhulin
rows.summary: A hill park of about 8.7 km² at Zhulin town in eastern Gongyi, best known for its autumn red leaves and for rocks likened to a dragon and a turtle, which gave it its old name of Longgui Mountain. Trails lead past ponds, a temple hall and three ancient trees, and there are a glass bridge, swing bridges and other thrill rides, along with a food street built in old-town style.

rows.name: Cherry Valley, Zhengzhou
rows.summary: A rural area of loess gullies, woods and cherry orchards about 15 km south-west of central Zhengzhou, crossed by walking trails and dotted with old villages, some of whose houses now hold artists' and makers' studios. Cherries have been grown here for centuries and are a local speciality. It makes an easy half-day walk out of the city.

rows.name: China Greening Expo Garden, Zhengzhou
rows.summary: A landscaped park of about 190 hectares in Zhongmu county east of Zhengzhou, opened in 2010 as the China Greening Expo Garden and laid out around a central lake with themed gardens. It also has a large musical fountain and an exhibition hall, and makes an easy, flat outing.

rows.name: Chongfu Palace
rows.summary: A Taoist temple at the foot of Wansui Peak that grew from a shrine founded under Han Emperor Wu and under the Northern Song became a court-managed temple, whose superintendents included Fan Zhongyan, Sima Guang and the Cheng brothers. After centuries of decline and use as a livestock farm in the 1970s it was restored in 2010. Four Qing halls survive, among them the vaulted brick Jade Emperor and Sanyuan halls, along with some 50 old trees and more than ten steles.

rows.name: Dahecun Site and Museum
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement on the northern edge of Zhengzhou, lived in mainly during the Yangshao period and later in the Longshan, Erlitou and Shang periods, where excavations since 1972 have found house foundations, burials and much painted pottery. Its best-known find is a row of four joined houses whose walls still stand about a metre high, dated to about 5,000 years ago. A new site museum in the Dahecun archaeological park, which opened in 2025, shows more than 1,600 objects on the Yangshao culture.

rows.name: Dahuting Han Tombs
rows.summary: Two large Eastern Han tombs under earth mounds at Dahuting village, Niudian town, west of Xinmi, attributed to Zhang Boya, a commandery governor, and his wife. The western tomb is lined with about 200 m² of carved stone reliefs and the eastern with about 100 m² of painted murals, and between them the scenes include banquets, acrobats, rent collection and a tofu workshop; the tombs are famous for how well they are preserved. Visitors can go down into the western tomb, while the eastern tomb is shown as a replica.

rows.name: Daxiong Mountain Xianren Valley
rows.summary: A mountain-valley scenic area of about 36 km² in Xuzhuang town, Dengfeng, with a lake, streams, waterfalls, caves and red-rock cliffs. Added attractions include a 266 m glass bridge, a dry toboggan run, river rafting and an exhibition hall on the revolutionary history of western Henan. It suits a day of walking and, in summer, water play.

rows.name: Dengfeng City God Temple
rows.summary: A temple to the city god, the protector deity of the county seat, founded in the early Ming and laid out facing south in three courtyards on a site of about 8,200 m² in the old centre of Dengfeng. Its more than 90 Ming and Qing halls and rooms include the main hall and the east and west galleries, which were restored between 2016 and 2018.

rows.name: Dharani Pillar, Xingyang
rows.summary: A Jin-dynasty stone pillar of 1203, about 7 m high, whose octagonal shaft is carved with the Usnisa Vijaya Dharani, a Buddhist protective incantation, and a second sutra on filial piety, above a base with relief figures of guardians. Its top has lotus tiers and four niches holding carved figures. It stands in a modern painted pavilion in Xingyang city, the shaft behind glass, and was listed as a national monument in 2019.

rows.name: Du Fu's Birthplace
