rows.summary: A memorial park below Bijia Hill in Nanyaowan village, Zhanjie town, Gongyi, at the place traditionally held to be where the Tang poet Du Fu (712–770) was born and spent his childhood. Spread over about 25 hectares, its halls, statues and gardens trace his life and the poetry that earned him the title 'Sage of Poetry'.

rows.name: Erqi Memorial Tower
rows.summary: A 63 m twin-towered memorial in Erqi Square in central Zhengzhou, built in 1971 in a Chinese pavilion style at the spot where two Zhengzhou leaders of the Beijing–Hankou railway workers' strike of 7 February 1923 were killed. Visitors can enter the tower, whose floors hold exhibitions, and a clock near the top plays 'The East Is Red' on the hour. The national listing also covers the Erqi Memorial Hall of 1951–53 on Qiantang Road, about 700 m to the south, built on the site of the theatre where the railway workers' union was founded and now holding an exhibition on the strike.

rows.name: Ersha Creative Park (former No. 2 Grinding Wheel Factory)
rows.summary: A major grinding-wheel factory of the 1950s, designed by an East German industrial design institute and built in 1956–64 in Zhongyuan district, western Zhengzhou, with Bauhaus-influenced concrete workshops including the vast sawtooth-roofed ceramic wheel shop. After production ended in the 2010s the listed buildings were converted into the Ersha cultural and creative park, with exhibitions, workshops, shops and cafés.

rows.name: Fanjiamen Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area run by a village tourism company in the hills of Tangzhuang town, north-east of Dengfeng, rated 4A at the end of 2023. Visitors come for Lintai Mountain, a spring said never to run dry, the Lailong limestone cave of about 1.3 km formed along an old underground river, a glass suspension bridge and a small natural lake, with further attractions such as a glass slide and a zip line.

rows.name: Fantawild Adventure Zhengzhou
rows.summary: A technology-themed amusement park opened in 2012 in Zhongmu county east of Zhengzhou, with roller coasters, a flying-theatre ride and dark rides on science-fiction, myth and history themes. It is part of the Fantawild resort, which also has the Fantawild Dreamland park, a water park and a hotel.

rows.name: Fawang Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at the foot of Taishi Mountain that by tradition was founded in AD 71, which would make it one of the earliest in China; its halls are Qing buildings and rebuilds made after 1987. On the slope behind stand six old pagodas, led by a fifteen-tiered square brick pagoda about 35 m tall, dated to the Sui or early Tang, with smaller Tang and Five Dynasties pagodas and a Yuan pagoda of 1316. The notch between two peaks east of the temple frames the rising moon at the Mid-Autumn Festival, one of the traditional sights of Mount Song.

rows.name: Fengle Farm Resort and Malawan Wave Pool
rows.name_zh: 丰乐农庄·马拉湾海浪浴场
rows.summary: A leisure resort opened in 2003 beside the Yellow River levee in Huiji district, north of Zhengzhou, with a large hotel, hot-spring baths, gardens, an animal area, go-karts and a baseball park. Its Malawan water park, built around a large wave pool, opens only in the summer months.

rows.name: Fengquan Lake Scenic Area
rows.summary: The largest scenic area in the Fuxi Mountain tourist zone of north-western Xinmi, covering about 10 km² of red-rock hills, ravines and a lake; it is on the official list as Sanquan Lake. Paths climb to the Xiaoma plateau and run through the Qifeng ravine, and the area has the Phoenix Sky Bridge, a glass suspension bridge, as well as a glass slide and a 2 km mountain coaster. It suits a day of walking with some thrill rides.

rows.name: Fengtai Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: The only survivor of the long-vanished Fengtai Temple: a hollow, nine-tiered hexagonal brick pagoda with closely spaced eaves, 19.1 m high and built before 1081 in the Northern Song. Its tall first storey has a door on the east side, and footholds set into the inner walls rise to the eighth tier; the pagoda was repaired by the local government in 2018.

rows.name: Forts of Liu Bang and Xiang Yu
rows.summary: The remains of two forts built facing each other across the Honggou ravine by Liu Bang and Xiang Yu in the Chu–Han war at the end of the Qin, a stand-off remembered as the origin of the river dividing the board in Chinese chess. Erosion by the Yellow River has carried away most of both forts, leaving chiefly their southern rammed-earth walls, about 460 m of Liu Bang's fort and 260 m of Xiang Yu's as measured in 2009, on the bluff above the river.

rows.name: Fuxi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A red sandstone gorge about 5 km long in the Fuxi Mountain area of north-western Xinmi, with walkways under overhanging cliffs and a series of natural waterfalls. Local legends of Fuxi and Nüwa are attached to many of its features. It is one of several scenic areas in the Fuxi Mountain tourist zone and can be combined with the nearby Red Stone Forest.

rows.name: Gaocheng Astronomical Observatory
rows.summary: A brick-and-stone observatory built in 1276 to designs by the Yuan astronomers Guo Shoujing and Wang Xun: a 9.46 m truncated tower with a 31 m stone 'sky-measuring scale' laid due north, on which the noon shadow of a gnomon was read to fix the length of the year. Nearby stand the Duke of Zhou's shadow-measuring platform, where a stone gnomon was set up in 723 under the Tang, and a Duke of Zhou temple, and the grounds also hold an exhibition hall on the Yangcheng ancient city site. The observatory is part of the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Gongyi Grottoes
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple cut into the foot of Mount Dali on the north bank of the Yiluo River, begun under the Northern Wei around AD 500 and added to until the Song. Its five caves, most with a carved central pillar, hold some 7,700 figures, and three of them have relief processions of an emperor and empress with their courts. A Qing-dynasty hall survives from the temple in front of the caves.

rows.name: Gubaidu Feihuang Tourist Area
rows.summary: An outdoor recreation area on the south bank of the Yellow River at Wangcun, Xingyang, run together with the neighbouring Gubaidu cherry garden. Its main draws are long sand slides down the riverside slopes, a children's sand-slide area, camel rides on the sands and a sightseeing cable car.

rows.name: Gubaidu Fengle Cherry Blossom Garden
rows.summary: A large cherry-blossom park near the Yellow River in Wangcun town, northern Xingyang, planted with more than 80 varieties of cherry tree in four themed sections. It lies where the South–North Water Diversion canal passes under the Yellow River, and a museum of that river crossing, built in 2018, stands inside the park. It is at its best in the spring blossom season.

rows.name: Guchengzhai Walled Site
rows.summary: A walled town of the late Neolithic Longshan culture in Guchengzhai village, Quliang town, east of Xinmi, whose rammed-earth walls still stand 5–16 m high on the south, north and east sides, with gaps marking two gates and traces of the moat. The west wall was washed away by the Zhen River, and excavations inside found the foundations of a large palace hall with surrounding corridors.

rows.name: Hometown of the Yellow Emperor (Xuanyuan Temple)
rows.summary: A memorial complex of about 7 hectares on the northern edge of old Xinzheng, honoured as the birthplace of the legendary Yellow Emperor, Huangdi, where a large ancestor-worship ceremony is held each year on the third day of the third lunar month. At its heart is the Qing-dynasty Xuanyuan Temple on a low mound, with a gate, a main hall holding a seated statue of Huangdi, side halls for his consorts Leizu and Momu and a brick bridge of 1570 in front, set between a worship plaza and a plaza of Chinese surnames. The national listing also covers two small stone halls, a Ming cliff inscription and a long stone stockade wall on Fenghou Ridge in the Juci hills, south-west of Xinzheng.

rows.name: Huayang Ancient City
rows.summary: A walled town of the Zhou period, said to have been the capital of the small state of Hua before it passed to Zheng and then Han; near it Qin defeated the allied Zhao and Wei armies in 273 BC. Its rectangular rammed-earth walls, about 2.3 km round, still rise 10–14 m on the north side with bastions and a silted moat, the west wall stands about 9 m high, and the south wall is largely built over by the houses of Huayangzhai village.

rows.name: Huishan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple below Jicui Peak that began as a Northern Wei detached palace, became a temple in the 6th century and took its present name under the Sui; it counts as one of the four great monasteries of Mount Song. Its main hall is a Yuan-dynasty timber building with large bracket sets, and the compound keeps steles from the Eastern Wei to the Tang. Just to the west stands the brick pagoda of the Tang monk Jingzang, built after his death in 746 and described as the only surviving Tang octagonal brick pagoda imitating timber construction, with several Qing brick pagodas nearby.

rows.name: Jianye Huayi Brothers Film Town
rows.name_zh: 建业·华谊兄弟电影小镇
rows.summary: A film-themed town in Zhongmu county east of Zhengzhou, built in old-street style as a set of film streets: Zhengzhou Street recreates the city's Dehua Street, Datong Road and Fushou Street as they looked about a century ago, and Taiji Street is themed on the film Tai Chi. It has street performances, film-themed shows and rides, craft workshops, restaurants and themed guesthouses, and suits families combining it with the nearby theme parks.

rows.name: Jing Ancient City
rows.summary: The walled town of Jing, the first capital of the state of Zheng after its move east and the fief of Duan, the rebellious brother of Duke Zhuang of Zheng in a famous episode of the Zuo Zhuan chronicle. About eight stretches of its rammed-earth walls, more than 1 km in all and 3–10 m high with clearly visible tamping layers, survive within the Jingxiangcheng Site Ecological Park, opened in 2008.

rows.name: Kang Baiwan Manor
rows.summary: The fortified hillside estate of the Kang family of merchants and landowners, who lived here for some four centuries from the late Ming, at Kangdian beside the Luo River in Gongyi. Built against the loess slope and ringed by walls, it combines street-front houses with cave dwellings: 33 courtyards, 53 multi-storey buildings and 73 cave dwellings in all, with fine brick, wood and stone carving. The rooms keep the family's furniture and inscribed boards, among them the well-known 'Liuyu' plaque of family precepts.

rows.name: Later Zhou Imperial Tombs
rows.summary: The tombs of the rulers of the Later Zhou, the last of the Five Dynasties, near Guodian town: Songling of the founder Guo Wei, Qingling of Emperor Shizong (Chai Rong) and Shunling of the last emperor, Chai Zongxun. Qingling, the largest, is a mound in a walled enclosure of about four hectares with a sacred way and 33 steles dating from 1426 to 1909. Songling is a 10 m mound with a single stele and no stone figures, as Guo Wei asked to be buried simply.

rows.name: Mi County Yamen
rows.summary: The government compound of old Mi County at the centre of Xinmi's old town, seat of the county from 616 until the 1970s; the present buildings date from a rebuilding under the Kangxi Emperor. Its five courtyards hold the main and ceremonial gates, three halls for justice and administration, a two-storey tower and a walled jail used until 2003, with lotus ponds inside the main gate. It is now a museum of local government in imperial China.

rows.name: Nanyue Temple, Dengfeng
rows.summary: A small temple in the middle of Dajindian town, said to have been founded under the Jin dynasty, with courtyards of halls to popular gods that have mostly been rebuilt. The main Fujun Hall is the historic core: a three-bay building with a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof of grey tiles, bracket sets under the eaves and beams painted with dragons, standing on a terrace, with a timber frame that the heritage bureau dates to the Jin dynasty.

rows.name: Northern Song Imperial Tombs
rows.summary: The burial ground of the Northern Song emperors, spread over some 30 km² around Gongyi, where seven emperors and the father of the dynasty's founder lie with their empresses and hundreds of courtiers. More than 900 stone figures survive along the spirit roads, among them elephants, horses with grooms, rams, lions, foreign envoys and officials, many standing in open fields. The Yongzhao Tomb of Emperor Renzong (died 1063), in Gongyi city next to the Gongyi Museum, is the only one whose gate towers and walled enclosure have been rebuilt and is the easiest to visit.

rows.name: Only Henan: Land of Dramas
rows.summary: An immersive theatre park opened in June 2021 in Zhongmu county, directed by Wang Chaoge: a walled 'fantasy city' of rammed loess, 328 m on each side, set among wheat fields. Inside, three main theatres and dozens of smaller courtyard stages run some 700 minutes of performances on Henan's history and culture, from historical figures of the Central Plains to the famine of 1942–43 and the building of the railways. Seeing the three main theatre shows and some of the shorter pieces takes most of a day.

rows.name: Qianchi Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song hexagonal brick pagoda, also called the Empress Cao Pagoda, about 15 m high, on the summit of Dazhou Mountain within the former Shengshou Temple. Legend says Emperor Renzong had it built so that his empress, a local woman, could see her home from the capital. The summit also has the temple ruins, Ming and Qing steles, stone Buddhas and the remains of a stone and brick stockade wall.

rows.name: Qimu Que Gates
rows.summary: A pair of stone gate pillars built in AD 123 in front of a Han shrine to the mother of Qi, son of Yu the Great, who in legend turned into the split boulder that still lies about 190 m to the north. Each pillar, just over 3 m high, is built of stacked stone blocks and capped with a carved imitation of a tiled roof. With the Taishi and Shaoshi gates it is one of the three Han 'que' of Mount Song in the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Qingliang Temple, Dengfeng
rows.summary: A small mountain temple below Qingliang Peak on the southern side of Shaoshi Mountain, whose main hall was rebuilt in 1216 under the Jin dynasty and keeps its hip-and-gable roof of grey tiles trimmed with green glaze, bracket sets and stone column bases. The temple has two courtyards, and a Jin stele of 1216 recording the rebuilding stands beside the hall, with a few later inscriptions.

rows.name: Qinglong Mountain and Ciyun Temple
rows.summary: A forested range of about 51 km² south-east of Gongyi city, a forest park since 1998, with waterfalls, pools and lakes linked by lakeside trails, red leaves in autumn and frozen falls in winter. In its heart stands Ciyun Temple, by tradition founded in AD 64 and counted among China's earliest Buddhist temples; its halls have been rebuilt in recent years, but more than 100 carved stones survive, including 52 Ming and Qing steles and 43 monks' stupa inscriptions.

rows.name: Red Stone Forest, Fuxi Mountain
rows.summary: An area of red sandstone pinnacles and cliffs, about 8 km², around Jianshan and Niuxinshi villages in the Fuxi Mountain area of north-western Xinmi. An outdoor escalator climbs the hillside, a ring-shaped glass walkway runs along the cliffs, and a cliff-top hotel and restaurants serve the wider Fuxi Mountain resort. It can be combined with the Fuxi Grand Canyon nearby.

rows.name: Sanzu Hermitage Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-tiered square brick pagoda of 1223, about 10 m tall, with a curving outline and a carved lotus finial, standing at the site of the Sanzu Hermitage, once called Zhulin Temple, in a mountain valley north of the Songyue Pagoda. The site also keeps Ming and Qing stone carvings, an old ginkgo tree, a cave known as the Luohan Cave and a rebuilt three-bay hall.

rows.name: Shaoshi Que Gates
rows.summary: The stone gate pillars of the Han-dynasty shrine to Shaoshi Mountain, dated by their inscriptions to about AD 118–123 and restored in 1972. Their faces carry more than 70 shallow reliefs, among them a fox chasing a hare, horse racing, cuju football, cockfighting and the animals of the four directions, and the west pillar bears a seal-script title naming the gate. They are part of the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Site of Ancient Xingyang and Guxing Ironworks Museum
rows.summary: The ruins of the Han-dynasty city of Xingyang at Guxing town, north-west of Zhengzhou, a stronghold fought over by Liu Bang and Xiang Yu, whose rammed-earth walls still stand up to 20 m high on three sides. Outside its west gate lay a large state ironworks of the Han commandery of Henan, and a site museum there shows the remains of a Han blast furnace with iron tools and casting moulds from the excavations.

rows.name: Songyang Academy
rows.summary: One of the four great academies of the Northern Song, founded as a Buddhist temple in 484, later a Taoist temple and from 1035 a Confucian academy where the philosophers Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi taught. Its Qing-period courtyards hold a hall to Confucius, a lecture hall, a shrine to the sage-kings Yao and Yu and the Duke of Zhou, and a library, and two ancient cypresses that legend says Han Emperor Wu ennobled as generals. By the gate stands the Tang stele of 744, about 9 m tall and the largest ancient stele in Henan; the academy is part of the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Songyue Pagoda
rows.summary: Built in the Northern Wei in the early 520s, this brick pagoda about 40 m high is the oldest surviving brick pagoda in China and the oldest multi-eaved one, and its twelve-sided plan is unique among Chinese pagodas of its type. Fifteen closely stacked eaves rise above a tall first storey, and the pagoda stands in the grounds of the former Songyue Temple at the foot of Mount Song. It was inscribed in 2010 as part of the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Taishi Que Gates
rows.summary: Twin stone gate pillars built in AD 118 at the head of the sacred way to the Han shrine of Taishi Mountain, standing about 500 m south of Zhongyue Temple and regarded as its symbolic gateway. Each just under 4 m high and capped with a carved stone roof, they are decorated in shallow relief with chariot processions, acrobats, the animals of the four directions and an elephant-like creature. They form one of the three Han 'que' of Mount Song in the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng World Heritage site.

rows.name: Tomb of Ouyang Xiu
rows.summary: The family cemetery of the Northern Song statesman, historian and essayist Ouyang Xiu, who died in 1072 and was buried here in 1075 with his wife, sons and grandsons nearby. The walled compound of about 1.1 hectares has a gate, an offering hall and side halls repaired since 1994, and behind them the burial mounds with stone figures of men, sheep and monkeys and Ming and Qing steles. A tall brick stele tower in front of the memorial shrine holds a Qing re-carving of the spirit-way inscription composed by Su Zhe.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Shousheng Temple
rows.summary: Two hexagonal brick pagodas of the late Northern Song, standing 20 m apart in Ranjia village, Huangdian town, south-east of Zhengzhou; the temple itself has gone. The western pagoda keeps seven storeys, about 30 m high, and the eastern four, both without their tops, and their walls carry rows of small carved brick Buddhas and brick brackets.

rows.name: Yellow Emperor Romance Park
rows.summary: A theme park built by Songcheng Performance with the Xinzheng government around a large stage show, 'Yellow Emperor Romance', a song-and-dance spectacle about the Yellow Emperor and the history of the Central Plains. Around it are a giant statue of the Yellow Emperor, a holographic theatre, an exhibition hall on Yellow Emperor culture, a haunted house, a market street with craft workshops and a large indoor children's play area.

rows.name: Yellow River Fujing Eco World
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park of more than 600 hectares on the Yellow River floodplain at Huayuankou, north of Zhengzhou, set up to hold down wind-blown sand by farming it. Visitors can walk among organic crop fields, try farm activities and use its leisure facilities, and it suits families with children.

rows.name: Yinji International Tourist Resort
rows.summary: A large resort complex in Liuzhai town, Xinmi, south-west of Zhengzhou, combining an indoor ice-and-snow park, a water park, hot-spring baths, an animal park and an ocean-themed park with hotels and a lakeside shopping street. It is built for family stays of a day or two rather than for sightseeing.

rows.name: Yongtai Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist nunnery on the western side of Mount Song, founded in 521 and, by local tradition, named after Princess Yongtai, a sister of the Northern Wei emperor who became a nun here; most of its halls are modern rebuilds. Its chief monument is the Tang-dynasty Yongtai Temple Pagoda, an eleven-tiered square brick pagoda about 24 m tall, joined by a small Jin pagoda of 1209 and a Ming lama-style pagoda of 1638.

rows.name: Yuanling Ancient City
rows.summary: The walls of Yuanling, a fortified town of the Zheng and Han states that became a county seat under the Qin in 230 BC and lost that status in the early Tang. Its rammed-earth ramparts, about 4 km round, are best preserved on the east and north sides, where they stand up to 16 m and 9 m high with bastions. Since 2017 they have formed the Yuanling Ancient City site park, zone C of the Zhengzhou Garden Expo Park.

rows.name: Yuxi Palace
rows.summary: A village Taoist temple in Tuguan, Tangzhuang town, originally called Yuqi Palace, founded in the Ming and repaired in the Qing. Its Ming Jade Emperor Hall has a hip-and-gable roof of glazed tiles with dragon and lotus ridge ornaments and two-tier bracket sets, and the temple also has the Qing Jiuku (Nine Sufferings) and Sanguan (Three Officials) halls, with more than ten steles and stone carvings from the Ming to the Republican era.

rows.name: Zhaixinglou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Daxiong Mountain provincial forest park in Xuzhuang town, south of Dengfeng, opened in the late 2010s beside Yanglin village. Alongside hiking trails it has built attractions such as a tree-top walk, water and dry slides and a zip line, plus a visitor centre, a memorial hall to the wartime Nanshan breakout battle, a hotel and guesthouses. It suits families on a day out from Zhengzhou or Dengfeng; the separate Xianrengu scenic area lies on the same mountain.

rows.name: Zhang Hu Manor
rows.summary: The hillside residence of the Zhang family, owners of a private bank and a coal mine, in Xinzhong village in eastern Gongyi, built mostly in the late Qing and Republican years. Its 13 courtyards combine some 30 cave dwellings cut into the slope with some 80 rooms in street-front buildings, partly in Western style. During the war against Japan it housed the headquarters of the Eighth Route Army's Western Henan detachment, and it is now open to visitors.

rows.name: Zhengzhou City God Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple founded in the early Ming and repaired many times since, dedicated to Ji Xin, the Han general venerated as Zhengzhou's city god. Along its axis stand a gate with elaborate bracketing, a 12 m two-storey opera tower with 19 ridges of glazed ornament, the main hall and a rear sleeping hall, most under green glazed tiles, and a temple fair is held from the 18th day of the third lunar month. The national listing also covers the Dacheng Hall of Zhengzhou's Confucian Temple a few hundred metres to the south.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: The 119-hectare site of the 11th China (Zhengzhou) International Garden Expo, in the Airport Economy Zone south-east of Zhengzhou, laid out as 94 outdoor show gardens. Most were made by mainland Chinese cities in the imperial, Suzhou and Lingnan garden traditions, and 18 by cities in 15 other countries.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Haichang Ocean Park
rows.summary: A marine theme park in Zhongmu county east of Zhengzhou, with aquarium halls for whale sharks, polar animals, penguins and jellyfish, an Ultraman-themed hall and some twenty rides including a Ferris wheel. Staged animal shows are held with dolphins, belugas and other marine mammals, and the resort has three themed hotels.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Mosque
rows.summary: Zhengzhou's oldest and largest mosque, also called the Beida Mosque after nearby North Street, with origins no later than the Ming and traditional Chinese-style buildings dating from the mid-Qing onwards. Facing east, it has a hip-and-gable gate, a two-storey moon-watching tower whose stone columns carry couplets in Chinese and Arabic, and a prayer hall made of several linked roofs; it is still in use for worship.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Shang City
rows.summary: The visitor area on the remains of Zhengzhou's early Shang-dynasty capital, a national heritage site whose rammed-earth inner wall ran for about 7 km round what is now the heart of the city. The 0.21 km² area between Chengdong Road, Chengnan Road, Zijingshan Road and East Street combines the Shang capital national archaeological park, with paths along and over stretches of the ancient city wall, the Zhengzhou Shang Capital Site Museum with about 5,500 m² of galleries, and the museum of the city's archaeology institute showing its major excavated finds.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Xiangshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A leisure area built around Xiang Mountain in Daye town on the eastern side of Mount Song, named after a shrine that, by local tradition, people raised to the Tang poet Bai Juyi after he toured the area as governor in 830. Its core is the Xiangxi Valley of streams, small lakes and waterfalls, with fairy-tale buildings such as 'hobbit houses' and a castle aimed at children. Around it are a Bai Juyi square, guesthouses, old mountain villages and a group of cave dwellings restored by villagers.

rows.name: Zhengzhou Yellow River Cultural Park
rows.summary: The former Zhengzhou Yellow River Scenic Area, a national scenic area and geopark on the hills along the south bank of the Yellow River about 20 km north-west of central Zhengzhou, with wide views where the river leaves the hills for the plain. Its five open sections include the colossal busts of the legendary emperors Yan and Huang, 106 m high including the hill they rise from and finished in 2007, the 'Mother Yellow River' statue, Yueshan Temple hill with its pavilions, and a memorial where Mao Zedong viewed the river in 1952.

rows.name: Zheng–Han Ancient City
rows.summary: The capital of the state of Zheng in the Spring and Autumn period and then of the state of Han, whose irregular rammed-earth walls, about 19 km round, survive in long stretches in and around modern Xinzheng where the Shuangji and Huangshui rivers meet. Its main display is the Zheng State Chariot Pits museum at the Houduanwan noble cemetery, where a great tomb and pits of dismantled chariots and horse skeletons are shown in place. Pit 3, excavated in 2017, held four vehicles, including a richly decorated carriage, and the bones of 122 horses.

rows.name: Zhijidong Cave Site
rows.summary: A cave on the western slope of Dalu Mountain whose deposits, up to 24 m deep in 23 layers, yielded more than 6,500 stone artefacts and many animal fossils in excavations between 1990 and 1995, from the Palaeolithic to the Neolithic. The cave mouth, 13–16 m wide and about 5 m high, can be seen from a railed walkway.

rows.name: Zhongyuan Tower
rows.summary: Henan's radio and television tower in south-eastern Zhengzhou, 388 m to the tip of its mast and built in 2008–09 entirely of steel, on a base shaped like a ritual cauldron. Lifts run to the observation floors, and since 2020 an open-air walkway at 281 m, a tilting viewing platform and a glass slide have been added. The base holds a 175 m-long panorama painting of Henan's scenery.

rows.name: Zhongyue Temple
rows.summary: The temple of the god of Mount Song, the Central Sacred Peak, where emperors had sacrifices offered; it traces its origins to the Qin dynasty, and its present buildings are Qing reconstructions after a fire at the end of the Ming. The walled precinct of about 11 hectares has some 400 bays of gates and halls on a long axis, more than 300 old cypresses and more than 100 steles and cast pieces, including Song-dynasty iron guardian figures and Han-dynasty stone figures. It is still a Taoist temple and is one of the Historic Monuments of Dengfeng inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2010.

rows.name: Dacheng Academy
rows.summary: An academy founded in 1075 by the Neo-Confucian philosopher Cheng Hao while he was magistrate of Fugou, and named after him, the elder of the two Cheng brothers. It moved several times before settling on its present site in 1704, and today's buildings come from a large rebuilding of 1884–85: the gate and Dragon Gate, the lecture hall, east and west examination halls, shrines to Cheng Hao and others, and a Wenchang pavilion. Tucked into the streets of the county town, it is described locally as the best-preserved old academy in northern China.

rows.name: Former Lütan School and Ji Hongchang's Former Residence
rows.summary: The village school founded in 1921 in a former temple at Lütan by Ji Hongchang (1895–1934), a general who fought the Japanese in Chahar in 1933, joined the Communist Party in 1934 and was executed by the Nationalist government that year. The school gate and the Zhongshan lecture hall stand on the axis with classrooms to either side, and about 60 m to the east is his courtyard home with its gatehouse, guard rooms and his own room. School groups visit for guided talks on his life; the larger Ji Hongchang Memorial Hall is in Fugou county town.

rows.name: Guandi Temple, Zhoukou
rows.summary: A temple to Guan Yu that also served as the guild hall of Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants trading at Zhoukou, where three rivers meet; it was begun in 1693 and finished in 1852 after repeated enlargements. Its three courtyards hold more than 140 bays of halls, galleries and an opera stage, with cast-iron flagpoles 22 m tall given by merchants in 1797 and a stone archway of 1765 densely carved with dragons, immortals and scenes from legend. It has been run as a museum since 1986 and is famed for its stone and wood carving.

rows.name: Jianye Canal Town, Zhoukou
rows.summary: A leisure area built from 2017 along Zhoukou's old canal, with a commercial street in old-town style, a large food hall of Central Plains dishes, homestays, camping, boat trips and a farm area. Its own troupe stages short shows on local themes such as Laozi and the canal trade, along with costume parades and wire-flying acts. It is a modern resort-style complex rather than a historic town and suits an evening out.

rows.name: Nandun Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The site of Nandun, capital of the small state of Dun after it was pushed south by Chen, until Chu conquered it in 496 BC, with remains from the Xia and Shang to the end of the Han. A long stretch of the rammed-earth north wall still stands, repaired since 2018, and opposite it rises Guangwu Terrace with a temple to Emperor Guangwu of Han. It is run as a small scenic area with paths and lighting among old trees and tombs.

rows.name: Pingliangtai Ancient City Site
rows.summary: A walled town of the Longshan culture, built more than 4,000 years ago, with square rammed-earth walls about 185 m along each side; it is described as the earliest square-planned town found in China. Excavations found jointed pottery drainage pipes described as the country's earliest urban drainage system, guardrooms beside the south gate, rows of mud-brick houses and the oldest wheel ruts yet found in China, and the site was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2019. A site museum with a model of the town and finds from the excavations is open on the site, and the national archaeological park around the walls is still being developed.

rows.name: Shousheng Temple Pagoda, Gaoxian
rows.summary: A hexagonal seven-storey brick pagoda, 28.5 m tall, first built in the Song and rebuilt in 1518, which leans visibly to the north-east, probably because of soft ground on that side. Set into the south wall of each storey are stone Buddha images, 211 in all, with 14 inscriptions, which record that it was built only in spring and autumn; its bricks are bonded with sticky-rice mortar. It is a quick but unusual stop in the countryside of northern Zhoukou.

rows.name: Shousheng Temple Pagoda, Shangshui
rows.summary: A hexagonal nine-storey brick pagoda, 41.5 m tall, begun in 1033 at the site of the vanished Shousheng Temple on the bank of the Sha River. Each storey has carved brick Buddhas, corner pilasters and bracket sets under the eaves, and a spiral stair inside climbs through the floors. During repairs in 1998 Ming bronze Buddhas and a sutra scroll were found in the iron finial, one image dated 1552.

rows.name: Taihao Fuxi Mausoleum
rows.summary: A vast temple-and-tomb complex to Fuxi (Taihao), the legendary first of China's Three Sovereigns, honoured here since at least the Tang and laid out in its present form by the Ming and Qing along an axis of about 750 m through nine courtyards and a succession of gates. The main Tongtian Hall enshrines Fuxi holding the eight trigrams, the Xianren Hall behind it honours Nüwa, and at the north end rises the earthen burial mound, 13.5 m high, round above and square below. From the second day of the second lunar month to the third of the third, a huge temple fair brings pilgrims, ritual dances and Huaiyang's black clay 'nini gou' toys; the 5A area also includes part of the town's Dragon Lake.

rows.name: Taikang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county Confucian temple of Taikang, founded in 1426, wrecked in the wars at the end of the Ming and repaired under the Qing. Two Qing halls remain: a five-bay worship hall with carved and painted brackets and beams, and the seven-bay, double-eaved Dacheng Hall on a terrace with a dragon-carved stone ramp. The Dacheng Hall mixes northern and southern building traditions, with a combined beam frame, a two-part front roof slope rare in Henan and large upswept corners in a southern style.

rows.name: Taiqing Palace (Laozi's Birthplace), Luyi
rows.summary: The Taoist temple at the traditional birthplace of Laozi, recorded as a Laozi shrine since AD 165 and raised by the Tang emperors, who claimed Laozi as their ancestor, into the imperial Taiqing Palace in 743. Today's Taiji Hall dates from the Qing or the early Republic, but the grounds keep a Tang stele of Emperor Xuanzong's commentary on the Daodejing, a stele of about 8 m composed and written by Emperor Zhenzong of Song after his visit in 1014, an iron pillar and ancient cypresses. In front is a modern square with a 27 m granite statue of Laozi, and the related Mingdao Palace stands in Luyi town.

rows.name: Xiangetai (Confucius Memorial Terrace)
rows.summary: A Confucian shrine on an island in a lake at the south-west corner of Huaiyang old town, built to recall how Confucius and his disciples were trapped without food between the states of Chen and Cai and he went on teaching and playing music. A Confucius temple was moved here in 721 onto an old Han crossbow-training terrace, and the present layout dates from the Ming and Qing, with a gate bearing a 1711 inscription and a seven-bay main hall of 1714 ringed by a gallery of 24 square stone columns, rare in Confucian temples. The academy buildings behind it are modern reconstructions.

rows.name: Ye Family Manor, Dengcheng
rows.summary: The family seat of the Ye merchants, who grew rich from river trade on the Sha River, built in stages over more than a century from the Kangxi to the Xianfeng reigns in the old town of Dengcheng. Three main compounds survive, the Tanglou, Five-Gate and High-Gate courtyards, with tall gatehouses, an open two-storey hall and carved brick, wood and stone throughout, and the city describes it as the largest and best-preserved Qing manor in eastern Henan. It is run as a museum.

rows.name: Yuanzhai Old Residences (Yuan Shikai's Family Home)
rows.summary: The fortified manor of the Yuan family, bought and rebuilt from 1857 by the official Yuan Jiasan, where Yuan Shikai, later President of the Republic of China and briefly self-proclaimed emperor, spent his childhood. Left, central and right groups of courtyards survive with 13 houses and halls, decorated with carved animals and figures on their roof ridges and in brick, stone and wood, beside a garden with rockeries and a pond.

rows.name: Zhoukou Wildlife World
rows.summary: A large safari park and entertainment complex opened around 2020 in Zhoukou Forest Park, with walk-through animal areas, a drive-through enclosure where visitors tour in their own cars or a park train, a bird garden and a ride zone with roller coasters. Its theatres stage acrobatic and circus shows, including staged animal acts, in keeping with Zhoukou's reputation as a home of Chinese acrobatics, and a themed hotel opened in 2026. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Baoyan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song brick pagoda of seven storeys on a hexagonal plan, 28.8 m tall, in Xiping county town and the only remnant of Baoyan Temple. Its brickwork imitates a timber tower, with a niche of carved flying figures on the first storey and a stair that climbs to the sixth floor. Damaged by Japanese shelling during the war, it stands in a small park laid out in 2017 beside a memorial tower to soldiers killed in the War of Resistance against Japan.

rows.name: Cai State Capital Ruins
rows.summary: The capital of the Zhou-dynasty state of Cai, first granted to King Wu's brother Shu Du and the seat of its rulers for about 500 years, around present-day Shangcai county town. Stretches of its rammed-earth walls survive, and on the north wall rises a large rammed-earth beacon platform of the Warring States period, which the county describes as the earliest beacon tower found in China. On the west wall stands the Wanghe Tower, a small complex of Ming-era halls linked with the Double Ninth festival climb.

rows.name: Caihongfang Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: A working baijiu distillery and visitor park on the south bank of the Hong River in Xincai county town, built on the former state-run Xincai distillery and covering more than 600 mu. Visitors see the Cai liquor museum, a recreated hand-made qu (fermentation starter) workshop, the base-liquor warehouses and a tasting centre, plus the Central Plains Liquor Culture Hall on the history of Chinese and local liquor, an exhibition on local party history, a botanical garden and a children's playground.

rows.name: Dongqiao Site (Leizu's Hometown)
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement site of about 48 ha at Dongqiao village, mainly of the Yangshao culture with later Longshan, Erlitou, Zhou and Han layers, which local tradition identifies with the Xiling clan of Leizu, the Yellow Emperor's consort credited with inventing silk-making. The village has built a Leizu temple, a site museum and a village history hall beside it, and holds a large temple fair and Leizu ceremony around the sixth day of the third lunar month.

rows.name: Former Site of the Chayashan Weixing People's Commune
rows.name_zh: 嵖岈山卫星人民公社旧址
rows.summary: The headquarters of China's first people's commune, formed on 20 April 1958 by merging some twenty farming cooperatives west of Suiping, whose reports of record grain yields made the front page of the People's Daily that summer during the Great Leap Forward; Mao Zedong visited it in November 1958. The compound, opened to visitors in 2002 and run as a museum, keeps the 1958 office building with slogans of the time still on its walls.

rows.name: Jinding Mountain
rows.summary: A national forest park in Yifeng town where the Funiu and Tongbai ranges meet, on the climatic border between the subtropical and warm-temperate zones, with six peaks, dense mixed forest and rock formations. Besides hiking paths and an old mountain stockade, the scenic area has a water park and a zoo aimed at day-trippers from Zhumadian.

rows.name: Jiudian Iron Works Site
rows.summary: An ironworking site of the Warring States to Jin periods on both sides of the Tanshan reservoir south of Chushan town, linked in ancient texts with the famous Tangxi and Longquan swords. Its centrepiece is a Warring States smelting furnace excavated in 1987, still 2.25 m high, which the county describes as the oldest and most complete of its kind found in China, kept in a protective building beside a small exhibition hall.

rows.name: Laole Mountain
rows.summary: A forested range of nine linked peaks at the eastern end of the Funiu and Tongbai mountains, the mountain scenery nearest to Zhumadian city, rising to 813 m at Yuhuang Peak. A national forest park with more than 95% forest cover, it is a Taoist mountain whose summit was historically ringed by temples and a worship terrace, and it is promoted as a place for the Double Ninth (Chongyang) festival climb.

rows.name: Mount Chaya
rows.summary: A granite massif on the eastern edge of the Funiu Mountains, a national geopark whose main scenic area of about 50 km² is crowded with weathered rock pinnacles, caves and small lakes carved from granite about 140–120 million years old. It was a filming location for CCTV's Journey to the West television series, and the scenic area has added a dry 'sky rafting' run nearly 2 km long, a moving walkway up the slope and a cliff-side slide.

rows.name: Nanhai Chan Temple
rows.summary: A large working Buddhist monastery on the south-eastern edge of Runan town, enclosed on three sides by the Ru River and rebuilt from 1992 to 2007 under the monk Mingcheng on the site of the old Xiaonanhai temple. Its halls cover some 50,000 m², among them a Mahavira Hall of more than 6,000 m² housing a huge seated Shakyamuni, approached through a 31 m-high gateway and a line of granite archways.

rows.name: Pagoda of Monk Xiugong (Puzhao Temple Pagoda)
rows.summary: A 14 m brick funerary pagoda built in 1194, under the Jin dynasty, by the disciples of Xiugong, abbot of Puzhao Temple, who had died the year before; the temple itself has gone. The hexagonal tower of seven storeys has brick eaves imitating timber brackets, a dated inscription over the doorway on the second storey and empty niches above, and a small garden was laid out around it in 2022.

rows.name: Royal Post Station (Huangjia Yizhan)
rows.summary: A modern culture-and-leisure town in Ming–Qing style in Zhumadian's Yicheng district, themed on the area's long history as a stop on the imperial courier-station network. Its 'seven streets and three lanes', among them an old street and a canal-side water street, are lined with restaurants, shops and inns around Feima Square, the Mawang Pavilion, an opera stage, Confucian and military temples and a post-station museum. It is busiest in the evening, with a night market, light shows and performances.

rows.name: Runing Stone Bridges
rows.summary: Two Ming-dynasty stone bridges over the Ru River at Runan, the old seat of Runing prefecture: the Jimin Bridge at the east gate, first made of stone in 1483, and the Hongji Bridge at the north gate, built in 1505, each with five arches and about 55 m long. Their piers have pointed cutwaters facing the current, and the Jimin Bridge's balustrade carries carved lions and panels of plum, orchid, bamboo, cloud and qilin designs.

rows.name: Tongshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A provincial scenic area in Biyang County made up of Tongshan mountain, the Tongshan Lake reservoir and Yunwu Peak, with forested hills, caves, waterfalls, temples and Taoist halls. The reservoir covers about 16 km² and is dotted with islands reached by boat, and the area is also a national forest park and a national water-conservancy scenic area.

rows.name: Wuying Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey hexagonal brick pagoda in pavilion style, more than 20 m tall, in the south of Runan town, popularly called the Shadowless Pagoda from the saying that it casts no shadow at noon on the winter solstice. Its gently tapering, parabolic outline rises from a sumeru base carved with goats, children and flowers, and imitation-timber brick brackets support every eave.

rows.name: Zhengyang Stone Que
rows.summary: An Eastern Han stone que, the kind of ceremonial gate pillar once set before tombs and shrines, standing in the north-east of Zhengyang county town. Locals call it Wangxiang Tai, the 'terrace for gazing homeward', after a folk tale of a dead merchant who climbed it to look back at his family before returning to life.

rows.name: Zhugou Revolutionary Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The former seat of the CPC Central Plains Bureau and the Henan provincial party committee in 1938–39 in Zhugou town, known at the time as 'Little Yan'an', where Liu Shaoqi and Li Xiannian worked. The memorial hall, founded in 1956 with a name plaque written by Zhou Enlai, keeps 66 rooms of the bureau and its offices, stretches of the village wall and the New Fourth Army drill ground, with an exhibition of more than 1,000 documents, photographs and objects.

rows.name: Great Song TCM Culture Park, Kaifeng
rows.name_zh: 大宋中医药文化主题公园
rows.summary: A TCM-culture theme park in Longting District, Kaifeng, linked to the city's traditional Chinese medicine hospital and themed on the Northern Song capital. Visitors can see exhibits on Chinese medicine history and herb displays. It was listed in 2018 among the first national TCM health-tourism demonstration bases in creation.

rows.name: Baren River Gorge, Badong
rows.summary: A karst river gorge in Chadianzi town, Badong County, also called the Three Gorges Women's Valley, where the scenic area climbs from about 350 to 1,650 metres above sea level. The route passes Qinglang Peak, a three-sided cliff reached along a narrow ridge path, the Longyin Palace limestone cave, a covered bridge and three iron-chain footbridges. The lower valley adds a rafting run, a slide and zip lines, and the shaded gorge is promoted locally as a place to escape the summer heat.

rows.name: Daqingjiang Scenic Area, Enshi
rows.summary: A boat-based scenic area on the Qing River in Enshi, spread across Sancha, Shadi and Xintang townships, where large passenger boats run along about 87 km of river between karst cliffs and villages. On the bank, the Honghua peak-forest area has riverside paths, a 1,056-metre cable car across the river and via ferrata climbing routes. Developed from 2012, it suits visitors who want to see the river's scenery from the water rather than on foot.

rows.name: Dashuijing Old Buildings
rows.summary: A group of buildings in the mountains of Lichuan, mostly Qing-dynasty and Republican-era, that the Li family built up from the former residence of the Huang tusi (local chiefs). The main parts are the Li ancestral hall (built 1846-49), the Li family manor and the 1940s courtyard house of Li Gaiwu, with an old flagstone road and a bridge among the protected elements. Together they have 24 courtyards and more than 200 rooms, and the complex has been a national protected site since 2001.

rows.name: Dixin Valley, Jianshi
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A deep limestone gorge in Gaoping town, Jianshi County, with cliff-hugging plank walkways, a glass bridge more than 200 metres above the valley floor and more than a thousand river-scoured potholes in the stream bed. The scenic area also contains the Jianshi Man site, where Homo erectus remains were found together with fossils of the giant ape Gigantopithecus, roughly two million years old, and a stretch of the old Ba salt road. It opened to visitors in 2014 and has since added rafting, a hillside lift and a hotel built into the cliff.

rows.name: Enshi Tusi City
rows.summary: A replica tusi (hereditary chieftain) manor complex on a hillside in the city of Enshi, opened in 2002, combining Tujia, Miao and Dong architecture, carving and painting. It includes a gate tower, the nine-courtyard Jiujin Hall, a hall to the legendary Ba leader Lin Jun, bell and drum towers and a flower garden, linked by loop paths past more than thirty sights. It is a modern re-creation rather than a surviving site, but it gives a quick introduction to the tusi system that governed Tujia areas from the Yuan dynasty until the 1730s.

rows.name: Fobao Mountain, Lichuan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the hills of Lichuan, with forest cover of more than 95 per cent. Its canyon section has boardwalks, including a glass walkway and a cliff-side plank road, as well as a rafting route and waterfall viewing. It is a day out for visitors based in Lichuan who want to get into the hills.

rows.name: Hefeng Manshanhong Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery on a wooded hillside on the south side of Hefeng town, begun in 1959 and expanded in 1978 as the cemetery of the Hunan-Hubei border soviet area. It holds the graves of Red Army commander Duan Dechang, He Long's sister He Ying and others associated with the revolutionary struggle in the border area. The grounds, about 10 hectares, include a main tomb, a monument, a martyrs' shrine, an exhibition hall of relics and a bronze statue of He Long, and the cemetery is a nationally protected martyrs' memorial and the core of the Manshanhong scenic area.

rows.name: Longchuan Shuixiang
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area on the Qing River in Liangwu township, built as a tourism project by Hubei Communications Investment Group on the theme of the Longchuan Diao, a Lichuan folk song listed as national intangible heritage. Visitors travel by boat into the Shuilian water cave, where the air stays around 18 °C, and the grounds include a wetland park with an open-air stage used for folk shows and water-borne fire-spark displays. It suits a half-day stop for cool air and a staged folk-culture show.

rows.name: Luyuanping
rows.summary: A cliff-ringed hollow in Banqiao town, about 1,700 metres above sea level and more than 500 metres deep, with a farming hamlet, streams, waterfall groups and karst crevices on its floor. Until 2021 the only way in was a steep cliff path; now a 380-metre inclined lift takes about three minutes, a cliff-side slide runs beside the waterfalls and a 158-metre conveyor 'magic carpet' eases the climb back. It is a cool summer retreat.

rows.name: Maodong Cave
rows.summary: A river cave on the Youshui River at Baifusi in Laifeng County, close to where Hubei meets Hunan and Chongqing, where the river flows through an opening about 58 metres wide and 36 metres high and runs underground for some 215 metres. The visit is a boat trip through the cave and down the gorge beyond, between limestone peaks and cliffs, and takes a little over an hour; the boat route opened to visitors in 2021. Local legend says the craftsman-god Lu Ban chiselled the cave in a rabbit year, month and hour, hence the name.

rows.name: Pengjiazhai Stilt-House Village
rows.summary: A Tujia village of Qing-dynasty timber stilt houses (diaojiaolou) on a hillside beside the Longtan River in Lianghekou village, jointed by mortise and tenon with almost no nails. About 30 households still live in the old houses, and the village is promoted as an open-air museum of Tujia life, with rapeseed flowers in spring and rice-planting and harvest activities later in the year. It was listed as a national protected site in 2013.

rows.name: Pingbaying National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 154 km² in the mountains of south-western Xianfeng County, close to the Chongqing border, with forest cover of over 90 per cent. Its features include the Sidong Gorge, a cluster of sinkholes and through-caves in woodland, and extensive azalea woods. It suits a half-day of forest walking.

rows.name: Pingshan Canyon and Rongmei Tusi Site
rows.summary: A village inside a cliff-ringed canyon, the site of the Jue Fu, the main seat of the Rongmei tusi (hereditary chieftains of the Tian family), built from the late Ming dynasty and abandoned after the Qing ended the tusi system in 1735. What survives are stone platforms, an opera-stage ruin carved with the words 'Shan Gao Shui Chang', the Xiaokunlun study terrace and Wanquan Cave across about 50 hectares, and the more visited part today is the canyon, where boats and boardwalks follow a clear green river between the cliffs. A Red Army hospital was also set up in the village in 1930.

rows.name: Shennong Stream
rows.summary: A Yangtze tributary running about 60 km from the Shennongjia mountains through four gorges (Shennong, Mianzhu, Parrot and Longchang) to meet the river opposite Badong town. Visitors travel up the lower stream by tourist boat past cliffs with hanging coffins left by the ancient Ba people, and can try small wooden 'pea-pod' boats hauled by trackers, a practice kept going for tourism after it ended elsewhere on the Yangtze. It suits a half-day boat excursion from Badong.

rows.name: Shizhou Old City Walls, Enshi
rows.summary: The surviving walls and gates of Shizhou, the old walled city of Enshi, in the Liujiaoting area of the present city. The wall, begun in the Song dynasty and extended under the Yuan, Ming and Qing, climbs the hillsides instead of following a plain-city plan, and a stretch of about 1.9 km with Song, Ming and Qing sections is preserved. Visitors can climb the South Gate Tower (Chaoyang Gate), which has a small display hall and a view over the old town, and walk through the passage of the West Gate (Jinhua Gate).

rows.name: Shiziguan Gorge, Xuan'en
rows.summary: A river-gorge scenic area just east of Xuan'en town, about 9.6 km long, with steep rock walls and narrow passes such as the Lion's Mouth. The whole route can be toured by car, and the area also offers paddle-boarding and kayaking and a spot where wild macaques can be seen.

rows.name: Suobuya Stone Forest
rows.summary: A karst stone forest of about 21 square kilometres in the north-west of Enshi, formed in the Ordovician period around 460 million years ago, with limestone pinnacles, narrow slot canyons and visible fossils. The scenic area has four main sections, Qinglong Temple, Lianhuazhai, Mozigou and Jiulonghui, and lies at about 1,000 metres, so it is cool in summer. It sits where Enshi, Jianshi and Fengjie in Chongqing meet.

rows.name: Tangya River Scenic Area, Xianfeng
rows.summary: A scenic area on the upper Tangya River at Huangjindong in the north of Xianfeng County, centred on Huangjin Cave, a large river cave that the Tangya River flows through. A trail runs upstream from the visitor centre to the cave portal, and the area has offered rafting down the river and through the cave. It suits a half-day outing in warm weather.

rows.name: Tangya Tusi Fortress
rows.summary: The remains of the seat of the Qin family, hereditary Tujia chiefs (some scholars say Mongol in origin) of Tangya, who ruled the district under the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties until the Qing replaced hereditary chiefs with appointed officials in 1735. The city, built from 1355, lies between a hill and the Tangya River and was laid out in three tiers, an outer city, an inner city and a palace city, covering about 74 hectares, with carved stone figures among the surviving remains. It is one of three Tusi Sites inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.

rows.name: Tenglong Cave
rows.summary: A cave system on the Qing River with about 59.8 km of passages on five levels, where the river drops more than 30 m at the entrance and flows on underground. Visitors walk a section of the cave, and a theatre inside stages a sung-and-danced show on Tujia history and customs, in air that stays at roughly 12–18 °C all year. Xinhua describes it as one of the largest known caves in Asia, and it is a popular escape from the summer heat.

rows.name: Tujia Daughters' City, Enshi
rows.summary: A shopping and leisure district in Enshi, built in the style of a Tujia old town and opened as a street quarter in 2013, with stilt-house lanes, shops, restaurants, inns, a Tujia folk museum and a theatre. It is themed on the Nü'er Hui, a traditional Tujia folk gathering, which is staged here as a regular event. It is a modern, commercial place rather than a historic quarter, popular in the evening and for photo studios that hire out Tujia and Miao costumes.

rows.name: Wujiatai Tribute Tea Village, Xuan'en
rows.summary: A tea-growing village in Xuan'en County whose tea was presented to the Qianlong emperor in the 1780s, earning it the label 'tribute tea' and an imperial plaque. Boardwalks wind through the tea gardens, with chances to watch or try picking and hand processing, and the village has a tea museum; the tea gardens are a provincial-level protected site, and the tea is on the China-EU geographical indications list. It is a small, rural stop, busiest in spring when the tea is picked.

rows.name: Wuliping Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: A small basin town in Hefeng County that was the centre of the Hunan–Hubei border soviet area in 1929–33, when He Long led the Red Fourth Army and Second Army Corps to build a base in the region. The protected group centres on the old street, which keeps late-Qing and early-Republican houses, and lists 20 former Red Army and soviet sites, among them the border regiment's headquarters, a clothing workshop, soviet government offices and a prison, plus the seat of the Party's border-region committee and a military training class.

rows.name: Wuxiakou (Wu Gorge Mouth), Badong
rows.summary: A scenic area on Damian Mountain above the Yangtze at the eastern mouth of the Wu Gorge, the middle gorge of the Three Gorges, just upriver of Badong county town. A cable car and a tourist road climb the hillside to viewpoints over the sharp bend where the river leaves the gorge. The mouth of Shennong Stream lies only a few kilometres downriver.

rows.name: Xianfo Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A cliff-carving site on the west bank of the Youshui River in Xiangfeng town, facing Hunan's Longshan County across the water. Four main niches hold 13 Buddhist figures, carved between the Tang dynasty and the Five Dynasties period, and a side niche to the south adds sixteen small niches, each holding a small Buddha. It is one of the few surviving cliff-carving groups of this age in the middle Yangtze region, and the temple halls that once stood in front were destroyed in the 1960s.

rows.name: Xuan'en Town and Gongshui River
rows.summary: The county town of Xuan'en, run as a scenic area in its own right and built around the Gongshui River that flows through it. In summer the riverbanks host evening trips by bamboo raft and black-awning boat, with staged performances such as fire-spark (iron-flower) displays and dances. It suits an evening stopover for visitors already in the county.

rows.name: Yangmei Ancient Village, Laifeng
rows.summary: A scenic area made up of two villages, Huangbaiyuan and Shiqiao, in Sanhu township, known for its groves of old Chinese bayberry (yangmei) trees, some of them more than 300 years old. The villages keep Tujia stilt houses, old courtyards, an old theatre stage, a water-powered mill and parts of an old salt road, linked by a tourist road. The fruit ripens around midsummer, the busiest time to visit.

rows.name: Yaotianyan Sinkhole, Xuan'en
rows.summary: A natural sinkhole (tiankeng) more than 290 m deep in Luoquanyan village, Jiaoyuan township, Xuan'en County, set among karst pinnacles and developed as a scenic area. After rain waterfalls pour into the pit, and in summer visitors go down to its cool depths, which Xinhua has reported as one of the county's popular cool-down destinations.

rows.name: Yesanguan Forest Flower Sea
rows.summary: A flower-field attraction in the Tiechanghuang forest park on a plateau above Yesanguan town in Badong County, at more than 1,700 m. It is one of three main sights of the Lüchongpo resort area, with a ski field and a holiday village, where summer temperatures average about 22 °C. It suits a summer day trip to cooler hills.

rows.name: Yesanxia (Wild Three Gorges), Jianshi
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A mountain and river scenic region in Jianshi County, built around the Jingyang stretch of the Qing River and the neighbouring Yesan River. Its main parts are Butterfly Rock cave, the Huanghe peak forest of karst towers, Jingyang Gorge on the Qing River and the Xiaoxihu (Little West Lake) resort area, a cool hill retreat in summer. The old Jingyang pass and old street lie along the river.

rows.name: Yulong Cave, Lichuan
rows.summary: A show cave in Tuanbao township with passages on three levels, found in 1992 when villagers searching for water in a drought came across it. A trail runs along a gorge and over a bridge to the cave mouth, and about 1.6 km of passage is open, lit in colour, with folk dances in traditional costume staged on site. The rock formations are named for what they resemble, such as a swan on its nest and a group of elephants.

rows.name: Yumuzhai
rows.summary: A fortified Tujia village on a hilltop ringed by cliffs, founded in the Hongwu reign (1368–98) by the Ma family of local chiefs and described as the best-preserved Tujia fort. It has four gates, a Qing-dynasty watchtower house and more than 30 old tombs with carved steles and stone sculpture, and over a hundred households, mostly Tujia, still live there. It suits visitors interested in Tujia history and village architecture.

rows.name: Yuxian Valley (Wuyuan Cave), Badong
rows.summary: A scenic area in the hills just outside Badong town, built around Wuyuan Cave, a large cave with a flowing spring and stalactites, and the gorge outside it, where the air stays around 20 °C. The grounds hold Three Gorges stone inscriptions, pavilions and a stele garden recalling the statesman Kou Zhun, as well as the Night Rain Pool, a constant-temperature outdoor pool on the Yangtze bank named after a poem by Li Shangyin. It suits a half-day combining a cave walk and the poetry sites.

rows.name: Ezhou Guanyin Pavilion
rows.summary: A small Buddhist–Daoist temple built on a rock reef in the Yangtze at Longpanji, first built in its present form in 1345 and rebuilt several times since. Its three halls, which include shrines to Guanyin and Laozi, a two-storey pavilion and a lookout pavilion stand on a stone platform in the river, the whole complex being about 30 m long and 24 m high, and at summer high water the river rises around the base. A small park was laid out around it in 2007.

rows.name: Fengqi Oasis Ecological Civilisation Expo Park
rows.name_zh: 凤栖绿洲生态文明博览园
rows.summary: A lakeside expo park in Liangzihu district, close to the Wuhan boundary, whose main building is the Liangzi Lake Ecological Civilisation Exhibition Hall, a two-storey hall of about 18,000 m² on lake protection and water-ecology restoration, described locally as the first of its kind in central China. Displays use interactive screens and 3D projection to cover the lake's history, its wetland ecosystem and local development. Outside are a lakeside camping ground, waterways, a boardwalk and a viewing platform; the park was rated 4A in December 2024.

rows.name: Liangzi Island
rows.summary: A 2.2 km² island in Liangzi Lake, reached by boat from the mainland, with a settlement of grey-tiled stone houses, farmland, small hills and lake views. The lake is the original home of the Wuchang bream, and the island is promoted as a quiet lakeside escape for walks and local fish dishes.

rows.name: Lianhua Mountain Park, Ezhou
rows.summary: A hill park on the south side of Ezhou beside Yanglan Lake, built up with more than 30 man-made sights in dragon and lotus motifs. They include a gate tower, a pagoda called Yuanming Tower, the Jielong dragon terrace and a prayer hall, so it reads as a municipal leisure park rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Wuwang City Ruins, Ezhou
rows.summary: The site of the city that Sun Quan founded in 221 and named Wuchang, capital of the Wu kingdom of the Three Kingdoms period. The walled town was roughly 1,000 m by 500 m, between the Yangtze to the north and the South Lake; today only a stretch of rammed-earth south wall about 60 m long and 4 m high and a section of moat survive within the modern city. Little else is visible, so it is a short stop for readers of Three Kingdoms history.

rows.name: Xingfuyuan Farm Park
rows.summary: A farm-tourism estate beside a lake in Duandian town, developed from 2014 by a Taiwanese-owned company on formerly fallow land. Current attractions listed by the district government include an orchid hall, a lakeside beach and water-play area, a pet park, farming study programmes and outdoor sports, with orchards and flower greenhouses around them. It is a modern leisure development rather than a heritage site, suited to families on a day out from Ezhou or Wuhan.

rows.name: Xishan Scenic Area, Ezhou
rows.summary: A wooded hill park in the west of Ezhou, once called Fanshan, that preserves traces of the Wu state of the Three Kingdoms, whose ruler Sun Quan is said to have built a palace here. Paths lead past Lingquan Temple, the Songfeng Pavilion linked with the Song poet Huang Tingjian, a Wu king's summer palace, a sword-testing stone and an accession altar, and the poet Su Shi often came across the river from Huangzhou to wander here. It has been a 4A area since 2022.

rows.name: Yiting Inscription Rock Carving
rows.summary: A natural rock on the Yangtze bank outside Ezhou's former north gate, carved in AD 765 with a short text in praise of the Yiting pavilion that once stood here, in seal script by Li Yangbing and clerical script by Li Ju, with the text by Pei Qiu. Local authorities describe it as Li Yangbing's only surviving seal-script carving on its original stone, and it was cut out of the river shallows in 2003 and re-set on the bank under a pavilion. The stone is small, about 3.8 m by 3.3 m, so it suits a short stop with the nearby Guanyin Pavilion.

rows.name: Baizi Pagoda, Macheng
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty brick pagoda on Jiulong Hill in Yanjiahe township, built in 783 by the monk Xuying and named after a cypress that once grew from its top. It is a hexagonal multi-storey tower: originally nine storeys, two were destroyed by bombing in the war against Japan, and seven survive to a height of 34.72 m. It is described as the oldest surviving multi-storey brick pagoda in Hubei.

rows.name: Bodaofeng, Luotian
rows.summary: Bodaofeng is a mountain scenic area in Shengli town in the north of Luotian county, in the Dabie Mountains of north-eastern Hubei, and is promoted as a cool summer retreat. It has ridges, pine-covered rock formations and a lake called Yuanmeng ('Dream-Fulfilling') Lake, and the Hubei Daily reported that Huanggang's 2025 summer tourism season was launched on its shore. It is a national forest park and suits visitors who want hill scenery and a cooler climate.

rows.name: Dongpo Chibi
rows.summary: Dongpo Chibi is a complex of pavilions and halls on a reddish-brown rock bluff in the north-west of Huangzhou, which once stood on the north bank of the Yangtze before silt left it several hundred metres from the river. The poet Su Shi (Su Dongpo), exiled to Huangzhou in the Northern Song, wrote his Red Cliff Rhapsody and other famous pieces here, and a prefect renamed the site Dongpo Chibi in the late Kangxi reign. Most of the buildings seen today date from a restoration in 1868, and 139 stone tablets carved from rubbings of Su's handwriting are set into the pavilions.

rows.name: Former Residence of Dong Biwu
rows.summary: Dong Biwu (1886–1975) was one of the delegates at the founding congress of the Chinese Communist Party in 1921 and served as acting Chairman of the People's Republic of China from 1972 to 1975. His former residence in Hong'an is a Qing-period house, listed in 2006 as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit and run as a memorial museum. A memorial hall to him also stands in the county's martyrs' cemetery.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Xiannian
rows.summary: Li Xiannian (1909–1992) was born in Hong'an and served as President of the People's Republic of China from 1983 to 1988. His former residence in Gaoqiao town, a Qing-period house, was listed in 2006 as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit and stands within a memorial park with a memorial hall about his life. The park is one of the red-tourism sites of Hong'an, a county known for the large number of senior army officers it produced.

rows.name: Four Seasons Flower Sea, Yingshan
rows.summary: Four Seasons Flower Sea is a modern leisure and study-tour resort about 1 km south of Yingshan county seat (Wenquan town), beside the upper Bailianhe reservoir and centred on planted flower fields. It also has a hot-spring area, a water-play zone, hotels and guesthouses, and study programmes with a revolutionary-history theme. It is a commercial development rather than a heritage or wilderness site and suits families and weekend visitors from Wuhan.

rows.name: Gaota Temple Pagoda, Huangmei
rows.summary: A Northern Song-dynasty pagoda standing in the built-up area of Huangmei town, beside Guta East Road. It has been protected at provincial level since the first batch of listings and nationally since 2019. As Huangmei is the base town for Wuzu and Sizu temples, it makes a quick stop on the way.

rows.name: Guangji Shiguang Riverside Park, Wuxue
rows.summary: Guangji Shiguang is a riverside park about 2 km long on the north bank of the Yangtze at Wuxue, built from 2013 and opened in January 2016. A central walkway runs between the river embankment and the waterfront, with a main square marked by a large helm sculpture, bronze sculptures on local trades and a terrace for looking out over the river. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2018 and suits a short riverside walk rather than a trip of its own.

rows.name: Guifeng Mountain, Macheng
rows.summary: Guifeng Mountain is a mountain scenic area in Guishan town, Macheng, at the southern foot of the central Dabie Mountains near the Hubei–Henan–Anhui border. Its nine peaks rise to 1,320 m at Daofeng Peak, and about 95 per cent of the area is forested. It is best known for a stand of old azaleas that local sources describe as covering about 100,000 mu and that blooms in spring, and it forms part of the Dabie Mountains geopark.

rows.name: Huangma Uprising and Eyuwan Soviet Area Memorial Park
rows.name_zh: 黄麻起义和鄂豫皖苏区纪念园
rows.pinyin: Huángmá Qǐyì Hé Èyùwǎn Sūqū Jìniànyuán
rows.summary: This memorial park in Hong'an town, the county seat, commemorates the Huangma Uprising of November 1927, when Communist-led peasant forces rose in Huang'an (now Hong'an) and Macheng, and the Hubei–Henan–Anhui revolutionary base area that followed. Set on a wooded hillside, it has a martyrs' monument, memorial halls for Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, an exhibition hall on the history of the base area, and the graves of those who died. The county museum's curator told China Daily that Hong'an lost about 140,000 of its people in the wars of that era.

rows.name: Jinxiu Tongluo Scenic Area, Hong'an
rows.summary: A privately run leisure park of about 4,200 mu (roughly 280 hectares) on the southern edge of Hong'an county seat, beside the Daoshui River. Its landmark is a giant bronze gong, and the park also has a children's play area, a petting-animal park, a military-themed park, a night market, a music fountain, a vintage green train, a riverside campsite and a water-screen light show on Hong'an's revolutionary history. It is aimed at families on a day out and is not a place of historic interest.

rows.name: Lei Ancestral Hall, Macheng
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Lei clan in Leishici village, south-east of Macheng, a building of the Qing to Republican periods. It was protected at provincial level in 2008 and added to the national list in 2019, and the village takes its name from it. The hall is in a village, so check access locally before making a special trip.

rows.name: Li Shizhen Culture Tourism Area, Qichun
rows.summary: A health-tourism area on the shore of Chilong Lake National Wetland Park in the south of Qichun county, built around the legacy of Li Shizhen (1518–1593), the Ming-dynasty physician who compiled the Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica). Its main parts are a culture plaza with a large statue of Li, the Bencao Gangmu Hall, an all-timber exhibition building using mortise-and-tenon joints, a herb garden planted with species from the book, and Qiai Town, a visitor town built in Ming–Qing style with craft workshops, herbal teas and performances. It complements the displays at the Li Shizhen Memorial Hall in Qizhou, and suits families and anyone curious about traditional Chinese medicine.

rows.name: Lishan Eco-tourism Area, Qichun
rows.summary: A village-based tourism area of about 3 sq km in Lishan village, Datong town, in the north-east of Qichun county, developed around tea and the area's revolutionary history. The provincial tourism department lists an artificial lake with a lakeside pavilion, a tea-culture park, a tea street and a 600 mu (about 40 hectares) tea plantation, together with a Red Army cave, a red-culture plaza and gallery, a folk-culture wall and hands-on farming activities. It suits a half-day village outing for visitors already in the area rather than a reason to travel to the region.

rows.name: Long March National Cultural Park, Yingshan Section
rows.name_zh: 长征国家文化公园英山园区
rows.pinyin: Chángzhēng Guójiā Wénhuà Gōngyuán Yīngshān Yuánqū
rows.summary: A Long March-themed park in Taojiahe township on the southern slope of the Dabie Mountains, a key assembly area of the Red 25th Army before its Long March in 1934. The park marks the episode with statues of soldiers, exhibition halls and walking trails, including a 17.3 km history trail, and one trail reaches the surviving trenches of the Niubeiji (Ox-back Ridge) blocking action. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in December 2025.

rows.name: Macheng Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: A martyrs' cemetery and memorial park of about 11 hectares in Macheng, built to commemorate those who died in the Huangma Uprising and the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet area. Its monument carries inscriptions by Ye Jianying and Li Xiannian, and the grounds hold the Macheng Revolutionary Memorial Hall and a memorial hall to General Wang Shusheng. It is on China's list of classic red-tourism areas and fits a red-tourism route through Macheng and neighbouring Hong'an.

rows.name: Nanwudang (Southern Wudang) Scenic Area, Yingshan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Wujiashan National Forest Park in the Dabie Mountains of northern Yingshan, promoted as 'Southern Wudang'. It combines forested mountain and river-gorge scenery with a Daoist temple complex, the Wusheng Palace, and has a ski area in winter. It suits a day in the hills for walking and views.

rows.name: Puyang Temple (Puyang Guan), Qichun
rows.summary: Puyang Guan is a Daoist temple on Fuhu Hill in Caohe, the county seat of Qichun, and the named core of the Li Shizhen Medical-Daoist Culture Tourism Area on the Hubei A-level list. The area's theme is the traditional medicine of Qichun, the home town of Li Shizhen.

rows.name: Qiliping Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: Qiliping is a small town in northern Hong'an county that was a centre of the Communist-led Hubei–Henan–Anhui revolutionary base area between 1927 and 1934, and its surviving sites are listed together as a national heritage unit. They include Changsheng Street, a 600 m stone-paved lane of black-tiled wooden buildings with former Red Army canteens, a pharmacy, post office, union office and bank, where tailors' and blacksmiths' workshops still operate. The Red Army's Fourth Front Army was founded here in November 1931, and a revolutionary memorial hall occupies the former Lenin Primary School.

rows.name: Sanjiaoshan Scenic Area, Xishui
rows.summary: Sanjiaoshan is a mountain scenic area in Lüyang township, Xishui, on the southern slopes of the Dabie Mountains, and is also a national forest park. Activities reported by the Hubei Daily include rafting through the Longtan Gorge, a bungee platform, a camper-van campsite and a ski area. It suits visitors who want outdoor activities and a cooler summer day out from Wuhan or Huanggang.

rows.name: Shuangcheng Pagoda, Hong'an
rows.summary: Shuangcheng Pagoda stands among fields at Zhoujiadun village, in the hills of northern Hong'an county. The national heritage listing dates it to the Song dynasty, although a local account on Chinese Wikipedia credits Zou Pusheng, a general of the late-Yuan rebel leader Xu Shouhui, with building it. It was listed in 2013 in the seventh batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units and fits well with a visit to the Qiliping revolutionary sites nearby.

rows.name: Sizu Temple, Huangmei
rows.summary: The temple of Daoxin, the Fourth Patriarch of Chan Buddhism, founded in 624 and rebuilt several times in the Ming and Qing. Its national listing covers three old pagodas (the brick Pilu Pagoda of 651, 11.34 m high, where Daoxin died; the hexagonal stone Zhongsheng Pagoda of 1099, 8 m high; and the small Song-dynasty Robe-and-Bowl Pagoda) and two old bridges, while the temple also keeps cliff inscriptions. It is an active temple in hill country, usually visited together with Wuzu Temple.

rows.name: Taohuachong Resort, Yingshan
rows.summary: Taohuachong is a mountain resort area in Caopandi town, in the east of Yingshan county in the Dabie Mountains. Its ski resort has seven runs, the longest about 1.2 km, and opens in winter; canyon rafting is a summer attraction. It suits visitors looking for winter sports or a cooler summer break within reach of Wuhan.

rows.name: Tiantai Mountain, Hong'an
rows.summary: Tiantai Mountain is a forested mountain area in the far north of Hong'an county, on the Hubei–Henan border, with a platform-shaped main peak, steep rock faces and named viewpoints along its stone steps. The scenic area also includes the Duitian River, where summer rafting runs down a bed of bluestone slabs. It is a national forest park and suits visitors who want a day of hiking or rafting in the hills north of Wuhan.

rows.name: Tiantangzhai, Luotian
rows.summary: Tiantangzhai is a forested massif in the Dabie Mountains that straddles the Hubei–Anhui border and forms the watershed between the Yangtze and the Huai rivers; this entry is the Hubei side, reached from Jiuzihe town in Luotian county. It is a core part of the Dabie Mountains geopark and is popular in summer for its cooler air, with rafting and a wire-assisted flying ride among the activities near Jiuzihe. The Anhui side, in Jinzhai county, is a separate scenic area with its own rating.

rows.name: Tomb of Bi Sheng
rows.summary: Bi Sheng (died 1051), a Song-dynasty artisan, is credited with inventing the world's first movable type, made of fired clay. A tomb stele identified as his was found in 1990 at Wuguidun village, Caopandi town, Yingshan, which is why Yingshan is regarded as his hometown, and the tomb was listed in 2019 in the eighth batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units. Yingshan's Bi Sheng Memorial Park, opened in 2023, uses modern displays to show clay and wooden movable-type printing.

rows.name: Tomb of Li Shizhen, Qichun
