rows.summary: The burial place of Li Shizhen (1518–1593), the Ming-dynasty physician and naturalist who compiled the Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica). He lies east of his parents' tomb on the shore of Yu Lake, outside the old city of Qizhou; after 1949 the grounds were extended with a stone archway, lotus pond, arched bridge and statue. A memorial hall to the west has a stele gallery, a herb-medicine hall and a herb garden, which makes it a good stop for anyone interested in the history of Chinese medicine.

rows.name: Tongtian River Scenic Area, Wuxue
rows.summary: Tongtian River is a themed tourist area in a hill valley in Yuchuan town, Wuxue, built around the story of Journey to the West. Its attractions follow that novel and include staged shows with scenes such as 'Havoc in Heaven' on weekends and holidays. It is an entertainment-style attraction that suits families and groups rather than a heritage or wilderness site.

rows.name: Wanniantai Stage, Xishui
rows.summary: Wanniantai Stage (the name means 'ten-thousand-year stage') is a Qing-dynasty traditional opera stage in Xishui county. It was listed in 2013 in the seventh batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units, and a stele recording the listing stands beside it.

rows.name: Wu Family Hall in Doushan
rows.summary: The Wu Family Hall is a clan ancestral hall at Doushan village, Baliwan town, built in 1763 by the local Wu lineage and enlarged in 1871 and 1902. It faces north and has three courtyards on a plan about 25 m wide and 56 m deep, with a double-eaved gate tower called Guanle Tower built in the style of a memorial archway. Its main attraction is the carved stone, wood and brick decoration, and it was listed in 2006 as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit.

rows.name: Wunaoshan National Forest Park, Macheng
rows.summary: A national forest park in the wooded hills just north-west of Macheng city, run by its own management office. It is known for a large camellia garden of about 5,000 mu with more than 560 varieties, and also has azalea and chrysanthemum gardens; within it stands Wunaoshan Temple, a Qing-dynasty temple under provincial protection since 1992. It is a green half-day outing from the city.

rows.name: Wuyunshan Ecotourism Area, Qichun
rows.summary: A mountain tea-and-terrace area in the hills of northern Qichun, at an average altitude of about 800 m. The main sights are the Wuyunshan tea gardens and the Leigongyan terraces, about 110 mu of paddy fields split into 310 small plots down a 120 m slope and described as about a thousand years old. The core scenic area covers about 2,000 mu (roughly 130 hectares).

rows.name: Wuzu Temple, Huangmei
rows.summary: A Chan (Zen) Buddhist temple on Dongshan hill, founded in 654, where the Fifth Patriarch Hongren taught. Tradition places here the verse contest between Shenxiu and Huineng that led to Huineng being named his successor. The national heritage listing covers its stone pagodas, old gate, halls and a run of cliff inscriptions, one of them attributed to Su Dongpo.

rows.name: Xiaoganxiang Cultural Park, Macheng
rows.summary: A modern city park in Macheng themed on 'Xiaogan Township', the place that many Sichuan and Chongqing families name as the origin of their ancestors in the Ming and Qing 'Huguang fills Sichuan' migrations. Historians debate how far that family memory matches real origins, and the park is best seen as a heritage-themed memorial space, not a historic site. It is a place for descendants of those migrants to visit when tracing their roots.

rows.name: Yi'ai Lake, Huanggang
rows.summary: An urban lake in the middle of Huanggang's built-up area, made up of an east and a west lake joined by a narrow channel, with about 3.2 sq km of water. It serves as the city's lakeside leisure park and landscape, and the shore park includes a forest of stone stelae and Yunxiang Tower. A pleasant stroll to combine with Dongpo Red Cliff in the west of the city.

rows.name: Zhenggong Pagoda, Wuxue
rows.summary: Zhenggong Pagoda is an ancient pagoda in Wuxue, in south-eastern Hubei. It was listed in 2013 in the seventh batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units, which classes it as an ancient building of the Yuan to Ming period.

rows.name: Dishuiya Waterfalls
rows.summary: A valley scenic area in Paishi town built around a waterfall group that the county government calls the 'three falls and nine pools', the main fall dropping about 68 m. Attractions added in recent years include stream rafting, a glass walkway, a dry slide, a hobbit-themed play area, camping, orchards and flower plantings. A small stalactite cave and a local tale that the Song poet Su Shi visited add colour, and the area was rated 4A in December 2025.

rows.name: Dongfang Mountain
rows.summary: A forested hill of about 475 m with three main peaks, described as the largest forest park in Huangshi's urban area and named for the Han writer Dongfang Shuo, who by local tradition studied and practised Daoism here. Its two main stops are Honghua Chan Temple, an old Buddhist temple described as a thousand years old, and Dongchang Pavilion, a modern nine-storey Tang-style tower run as an immersive entertainment attraction with costume experiences and staged shows. It suits a half-day of walking from the city.

rows.name: Hanyeping Iron and Coal Works Site
rows.summary: Surviving remains of the Hanyeping Coal and Iron Company, formed in 1908 when the Hanyang ironworks founded by the Qing official Zhang Zhidong was combined with the Daye iron mine and the Pingxiang coal mine; Chinese state media call it Asia's earliest combined iron, steel and coal enterprise. In Huangshi the listed remains are a blast-furnace trestle, an ironmaking furnace, a watch tower, an ore unloader and Japanese- and European-style residences along the Yangtze, and a museum has been set up in a former workers' club. It suits visitors interested in industrial history, ideally combined with the Huaxin cement works in the city.

rows.name: Huangshi National Mine Park
rows.summary: A mine park on the site of the Daye iron mine, where records of mining go back to the third century and which was mechanised in the late Qing. Its centrepiece is a vast terraced open pit, more than 2 km long and over 400 m deep, which visitors look down into, set among reclaimed slopes planted with locust trees and tunnel displays. The park opened in 2007 and in 2018 joined China's first list of protected industrial heritage.

rows.name: Huangshi OCT Dinosaur Wonderland
rows.summary: A dinosaur-themed holiday resort on the shore of Daye Lake, opened in 2024. Its main park, the Dinosaur Dream Factory, has more than 30 large outdoor rides, indoor digital attractions and staged shows, with a 99 m illuminated Ferris wheel and go-karts in the neighbouring park and a shopping-and-dining street and hotels alongside. It is a modern theme park rather than a heritage site, and suits families with children.

rows.name: Huaxin Cement Works (Huaxin 1907)
rows.summary: A cement works founded in 1907 and shut down in 2007, which supplied cement for national projects such as the Great Hall of the People and the Wuhan Yangtze Bridge; its brick halls, conveyor galleries, slag store and wet-process rotary kilns, including two large kilns imported from the United States, have been preserved. Since 2022 the site has been reopened as the Huaxin 1907 Cultural Park, with a cement museum, an exhibition hall in the former slag store, cafés, markets and open-air events. It stands in the middle of Huangshi and takes an hour or two.

rows.name: Leishan Scenic Area, Daye
rows.summary: A hill scenic area in Chengui town, about 15 km west of Daye, covering some 55 km² in three zones: Xiaoleishan, with pines and oddly shaped rocks, Daquangou, a stream gorge with cascades and a reservoir, and Tiantaishan. A hot-spring resort stands inside the area, and an old nunnery, Lianhua An, lies in the Daquangou gorge. It suits a half-day outing from Daye.

rows.name: Longfeng Mountain Eco-Park, Daye
rows.summary: A rural-tourism park of nearly 14,000 mu around the twin peaks of Qinglong and Yufeng at Shuanggangkou in Liurenba town, run by one company as a farming-and-tourism enterprise. It has a fruit-and-vegetable picking park, a study and training base with a swimming pool, and a hill park with hiking paths, hydrangea, cherry and azalea plantings, timber cabins and a camping ground. The nearby Red Third Army sites are part of what the park promotes.

rows.name: Longgang Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: A cluster of former Communist offices and residences in Longgang, an old market town on the Hubei–Jiangxi border that served in the late 1920s and early 1930s as a base for the party's east Hubei committee and Soviet government, and was nicknamed 'Little Moscow'. About 70 sites survive, many of them along the old street known as Red Army Street, where nearly a hundred wall slogans and murals remain. Visitors can also see a memorial museum, Red Army cemeteries and the former residence of Peng Dehuai.

rows.name: Red Third Army Group Revolutionary Site
rows.summary: A former landowner's house in Liurenba village, a brick-and-timber complex of two-storey buildings (about 2,400 m²) with a classical Western-style façade, where in June 1930 an enlarged military committee meeting decided to form the Red Third Army Group from the Red Fifth and Eighth Armies. Peng Dehuai was named commander and Teng Daiyuan political commissar. The building is now the Red Third Army Group memorial museum.

rows.name: Shangfeng Ancient Village
rows.summary: A hillside village in Jinhu subdistrict, Daye, nicknamed the village of the 'nine ancients' for its surviving old houses, paths, trees, wells and ancestral halls; local accounts date it to the late Yuan dynasty, some 600 years ago. About forty old houses with grey walls, dark tiles and stepped gables stand among stone paths and wells, a stone forest and a small mountain pond lie in the hills behind, and the village is on China's list of traditional villages. A walk-through scenic show called 'Shangfeng You Xi', a market street and other performances were added for visitors, and the area was rated 4A in December 2025.

rows.name: Site of the Daye Soldiers Revolt
rows.summary: The former Wubei military academy, begun in 1827 and later a school, where on 14 December 1929 a platoon leader named Cheng Zihua, a Communist Party member serving in the Nationalist army, led an armed uprising with Red Army support that is known as the Daye Soldiers' Revolt. Four linked single-storey brick-and-timber buildings of about 2,500 m² survive on the grounds of Daye Foreign Language School, and a memorial exhibition hall opened in them in 2021. It is a short visit for anyone interested in the revolutionary period.

rows.name: Tonglüshan Ancient Copper Mine
rows.summary: An ancient copper-mining and smelting site that was worked from at least the Spring and Autumn period, and probably earlier, until the Han dynasty. It came to light in 1973 when modern miners broke into ancient shafts, galleries and furnaces, and part of it is preserved in a museum built over a surviving shaft in the 1980s, now joined by a new museum that opened in June 2023. Indoor galleries explain how the copper was found, mined and smelted, outdoor areas show the excavated workings, and in 2025 the site became a National Archaeological Site Park.

rows.name: Xiandao Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake in the northern foothills of the Mufu Mountains, once marketed as Qiandao ('Thousand Island') Lake, with about 1,002 wooded islands scattered across roughly 30 km² of water. The hills around it are well wooded, and local sights include relics linked to the Tang poet Luo Binwang, who is said to have retired here, and a Ming-dynasty bell. It is a provincial scenic area and tourist resort, and suits a day trip from Huangshi or Wuhan.

rows.name: Zhaoshan Ancient Village and Peach Country
rows.summary: A rural-tourism area built around Zhaoshan village in Bao'an town, known for its 'gouxue' (blood) peach, with nearly 3,500 mu (about 230 ha) of groves in the village itself that blossom in spring and fruit in summer. Visitors also come for a coffee shop, a plant-dye shop and an immersive water-borne evening show, 'In Peach Blossom Land', staged in the village, and for the rapeseed, plum and chrysanthemum fields of neighbouring villages. It was rated 4A in 2024 and suits a relaxed half day out of Daye or Huangshi.

rows.name: Geek Park, Jingmen
rows.summary: An aviation-themed park inside the iFlyer (Aifeike) Aviation Town in Jingmen's Zhanghe New Area, described as an aircraft museum. The collection of Chinese-built aircraft and models runs from the CJ-6 trainer to the J-20 fighter and includes real airframes such as a Shuihong-5 flying boat and a Y-5 transport. The town around it also offers wind-tunnel flying and light-aircraft flights, and the park is a regular stop for school study tours, so it suits families and aviation fans.

rows.name: Huangxian Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave in Kedian town, on the Dahong Mountain side of Zhongxiang, about 2.6 km long and known for a large hall of rimstone pools and other stalactite formations. The rimstone pools cover about two hectares, and a small traditional village, Shuimeiping, stands on the hill above the cave. It suits visitors who like caves and a day in the hills.

rows.name: Huiyuan Nonggu Experience Park
rows.summary: An agricultural experience park inside Dakou National Forest Park in Zhongxiang, certified as a 4A scenic area in July 2020. Its attractions are a space-agriculture exhibition hall, a creative fruit-and-vegetable farm, a science demonstration centre, small vegetable plots, a livestock and grain experience zone and a traditional games area. It is pitched at families and school groups as an outdoor classroom on nature and farming.

rows.name: Jingmen Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park of about 140 hectares in south-west Jingmen, built on a former coal-mine subsidence area and construction-waste landfill and opened in April 2022 as the main venue of the third Hubei Garden Expo. It was laid out among hills and a lake with 32 show gardens from the expo's participating cities and other bodies, including Jingmen's own garden, a Wuhan garden and a Shennongjia garden, plus a flower valley planted above the mined-out ground. It suits a few hours of easy strolling and garden-viewing rather than a heritage visit.

rows.name: Lulin Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area at Lulin town in northern Jingshan, on the Dahong Mountain side, tied by local tradition to the Lulin peasant uprising of AD 17 against Wang Mang's Xin dynasty, which gave Chinese the phrase for outlaws of the green forest. Sights include Meiren Valley, a rafting run on Yuanyang Creek and the Lulin Ancient Stockade, presented as the rebels' training base. Where the original Lulin Mountain lay is disputed, since ancient and modern sources place it in different areas.

rows.name: Pengdun Rural World
rows.summary: A rural-tourism site in and around Pengdun village in Shipai town, built around modern farming and village life. It includes village scenery, farmers' housing, a farmers' park, six agricultural bases and an old-town-style quarter. It suits a relaxed countryside outing rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qujialing Site and Archaeological Park
rows.summary: The type site of the Qujialing culture, a Neolithic farming culture of the middle Yangtze, where a village some 5,000 years old yielded carbonised rice and painted pottery cups of eggshell thinness. The national archaeological site park, in trial operation since November 2019, has a site museum, open-air areas marking a dozen excavated spots and landscaped areas on the themes of rice and water. Excavations since 2015 uncovered a large ritual building and a prehistoric water-control system, and were named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2023.

rows.name: Shengjingshan Eco-tourism Area
rows.summary: A hill and woodland eco-tourism area on the edge of Jingmen, best known for paragliding, with launch points, a large purpose-built landing ground and a training base that runs multi-day courses. It has hosted international paragliding competitions, and walking routes follow old paths through older woods across just over 5 square kilometres. It opened to visitors in 2019 and suits active day trips and anyone who wants to watch or try paragliding.

rows.name: Site of the CPC Henan-Hubei Border Region Committee
rows.name_zh: 中共豫鄂边区委员会旧址
rows.summary: A preserved former headquarters in Jingshan of the Henan-Hubei Border Region Committee, the Communist Party committee of the Henan-Hubei border base area during the war against Japan. The committee was formed in Jingshan in late December 1939, the New Fourth Army's Henan-Hubei Advance Column was set up there in January 1940 under Li Xiannian, and in 1941 the column was reorganised as the Fifth Division. The site is a nationally protected modern historical site, listed in 2013 for the period 1940–42.

rows.name: Sujialong Tombs and Site Park
rows.summary: A cemetery, settlement and bronze-working site of the Zeng state, a vassal of the Zhou dynasty, excavated in the 2010s, with inscribed bronzes, chariot-and-horse pits and the remains of a bronze-smelting workshop. A site park with a museum and a visitor centre has been built, and the visitor route runs from the museum past the tomb group to the Luoxing smelting site. It suits visitors interested in early Chinese bronzes and the Zeng state.

rows.name: Taizishan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills of south-western Jingshan, with wooded walking trails. It suits a half day of walking in woodland.

rows.name: Wenfeng Pagoda, Zhongxiang
rows.summary: A white-painted Buddhist pagoda of the rare bowl-and-spire (fubo) stupa type, standing in the grounds of Bao'en Temple on Longshan hill in Zhongxiang. A pagoda was first raised here in 880 as a tower of earth, and the present brick-and-mortar tower is a Ming rebuilding of 1389, rising more than 20 metres and topped by a finial of twenty-one stacked rings. It has been a national protected monument since 2006.

rows.name: Xianling Tomb of the Ming Dynasty
rows.summary: The joint tomb of Zhu Youyuan, a Ming prince, and his wife, rebuilt to imperial standard after their son became the Jiajing Emperor and inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2000 with other Ming and Qing imperial tombs. Its plan differs from the other Ming tombs: a vase-shaped outer wall, a nine-bend ceremonial stream crossed by stone bridges, a winding dragon-shaped spirit way lined with stone figures, and two burial mounds joined by a stone causeway. Fire destroyed the timber halls in 1642, so what survives is mostly stonework, gates, stelae and foundations.

rows.name: Zhanghe Reservoir
rows.summary: A large reservoir on the Zhanghe river west of Jingmen, built between 1958 and 1966 mainly for irrigation and water supply, with islands and many inlets across about 100 square kilometres of water. The scenic area around it offers lake views from named viewpoints and islands, and the reservoir was designated a national water-conservancy scenic area in 2002. It suits a relaxed day by the water rather than a sightseeing circuit.

rows.name: Balingshan Tombs
rows.summary: A large field of earth-mounded tombs scattered over the wooded hills of Balingshan National Forest Park north-west of Jingzhou, with nearly 500 mounds recorded and burials ranging from the Eastern Zhou to the Ming dynasty. They include tombs of Ming princes of the Liao line, among them Prince Jian of Liao (Zhu Zhi, who died in 1424 and whose tomb was excavated in 1987), and tombs attributed to rulers of the 10th-century Jingnan state. Expect forest paths and grass-covered mounds; the Liao prince's tomb area is separately rated as a scenic spot by the Hubei list.

rows.name: Chuwang Chariot and Horse Pits (Xiongjiazhong)
rows.summary: Xiongjiazhong is an Eastern Zhou burial ground of the Chu state, with a main earth mound 16 m high, a companion tomb about half its size and 40 chariot-and-horse pits. An exhibition hall about 133 m long covers Pit 1, 132.6 m long, where the 43 chariots and 164 horses excavated so far are laid facing west. The occupant is unconfirmed, with one proposal naming King Zhao or King Hui of Chu, and the site park is also called the Xiongjiazhong National Archaeological Site Park.

rows.name: Honghu Wetland Ecological Tourist Area
rows.summary: This lakeside leisure area of more than 4,400 mu (about 290 ha) on the eastern shore of Hong Lake, at the edge of Honghu city, centres on a 1,500-mu wetland garden of flowers, aquatic plants and reed marsh. The Honghu tourist port, with 102 berths, runs boats onto the lake, and the area also has a lakeside hotel, a greenway, camping and fishing grounds and red-themed walking routes and a water-stage play on the Honghu story. Flowers bloom in spring, lotus in summer and wintering birds can be seen in the cold months.

rows.name: Hunan–West Hubei Soviet Martyrs' Memorial, Honghu
rows.name_zh: 湘鄂西苏区革命烈士陵园
rows.summary: This memorial park on the Yangtze embankment in the south-west of Honghu city is built around the Hunan–West Hubei Soviet martyrs' cemetery and memorial hall, a nationally protected martyrs' memorial site of more than 350 mu (about 23 ha). It records the Communist-led revolutionary base that grew up around Hong Lake around 1930–32 under leaders including He Long, with a monument, a martyrs' shrine, an exhibition hall and a statue of He Long. A memorial park to the 1998 flood-fighting effort and a riverside park lie alongside, between the Yangtze and the lake.

rows.name: Jinan City of Chu
rows.summary: Jinan was a capital of the Chu state in the Warring States period, a walled city of about 16 km², measuring 4.5 km by 3.5 km, just north of Jingzhou. Stretches of earth rampart and moat survive, with 84 rammed-earth building platforms inside (61 in the south-east palace quarter) and more than 400 wells found in excavations; the listing also takes in two Chu cemeteries, Yutaishan and Tianxingguan. Parts of the site, including the south gate of the east wall and the palace area, have been developed as the Chu Jinan Old City Archaeological Site Park.

rows.name: Jingjiang Flood Diversion Sluice, Gong'an
rows.summary: The Jingjiang flood diversion works were built in 1952 in 75 days to protect the Yangtze's Jingjiang reach and the Jianghan plain from flooding, and are a nationally listed water-control project. The north (inflow) sluice at Taipingkou is 1,054 m long with 54 gates, while a second control sluice with 32 gates stands far to the south on the Hu Du river at Huangshantou. The north sluice is run as a waterside scenic area on the Yangtze's south bank, across the river from Jingzhou, and both Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai wrote inscriptions for the project.

rows.name: Jingzhou Ancient City
rows.summary: Jingzhou's old town is enclosed by a brick-faced rampart about 8.8 m high, rebuilt in 1646 on Ming foundations and regarded as one of the best-preserved city walls in southern China. Gate towers such as Binyang Tower on the east side mark the old gates, and the old town also holds the Jingzhou Museum, Taoist temples and shrines to the Three Kingdoms general Guan Yu. The area is tied to Three Kingdoms stories such as Liu Bei 'borrowing' Jingzhou and Guan Yu's defeat here, and the wall is on China's tentative World Heritage list.

rows.name: Jingzhou Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: This park was built for Hubei's second garden expo, held here from 28 September to 28 November 2019, and has stayed open as a public park since. It was laid out with 45 show gardens (17 from Hubei's cities and prefectures, 11 from counties and 17 by garden designers), a main exhibition hall and a water-town landscape of ponds and channels. It lies in the Jinan area close to the site of the ancient Chu capital, and suits an easy half day of garden-walking.

rows.name: Jingzhou Museum
rows.summary: The regional museum of Jingzhou, founded in 1958, holds some 196,000 items, most of them from excavations in and around the city. Its permanent displays cover the prehistoric cultures of the Jianghan plain, bronzes, jades, bamboo-slip documents, ceramics and lacquerware, with the Mashan tomb textiles and the preserved body of a Western Han man from Fenghuangshan tomb 168 among the highlights. Kaiyuan Guan, one of Jingzhou's three nationally listed Taoist temples, stands in the museum grounds.

rows.name: Jingzhou Ocean World
rows.summary: Jingzhou Ocean World is a marine-themed leisure park in Shashi District, open since 2016, with an aquarium (the Undersea Park) and a separate summer water park, both refurbished and reopened on 18 June 2026. The aquarium has polar, Yangtze river and shore-combing play zones, with staged shows including a dolphin meet-and-greet, a mermaid performance and a parade. It suits families with children rather than anyone looking for local heritage.

rows.name: Qujiawan Old Street (Hunan–West Hubei Base Sites)
rows.name_zh: 瞿家湾湘鄂西革命根据地旧址
rows.summary: Qujiawan is a small riverside town whose stone-paved old street of more than 40 brick-and-timber buildings served in the early 1930s as the capital of the Communist-led Hunan–West Hubei revolutionary base. Former offices and quarters line the street, with a martyrs' cemetery and exhibition halls in the town explaining the base's history. It is a designated patriotic-education base, and the listing's era is given as 1930–1932.

rows.name: Taoyuan Town, Shishou
rows.summary: Taoyuan Town is a purpose-built countryside leisure complex at the foot of Lujiao Peak in Taohuashan town, developed by a Hubei provincial culture-and-tourism group on about 325 hectares (4,873 mu). It is laid out as the peak area plus three themed zones, named for flower fields, a peach-blossom village and a rice-field village, with 24 sights in all, and takes its theme from the Chinese 'peach-blossom land' ideal. The surrounding Taohua Mountain range is known locally for its spring blossom, which is the best time to go.

rows.name: Three Taoist Temples of Jingzhou
rows.summary: The nationally listed Three Taoist Temples are Taihui Guan, Xuanmiao Guan and Kaiyuan Guan, all with Ming and Qing halls on older foundations. Taihui Guan, west of the old town, was rebuilt in 1393 by Zhu Bai, Prince of Xiang; Xuanmiao Guan on Jingbei Road has the Jade Emperor Pavilion and a Yuan-dynasty stele recording the founding of its palace; and Kaiyuan Guan, with its Thunder God Hall and Sanqing Hall, stands inside the Jingzhou Museum grounds.

rows.name: Wanshou Pagoda
rows.summary: Wanshou Pagoda is a seven-storey octagonal brick-and-stone tower 40.46 m high, built between 1548 and 1552 for Prince Zhu Xian of Liao to pray for the Jiajing Emperor's long life. It stands on the Jingjiang embankment at Guanyinji, a rocky spur jutting into the Yangtze, and its lowest storey is now buried below the raised dike. Wanshou Park around it also has a 1998 flood memorial pavilion and carved marks of the high-water levels of 1954 and 1998.

rows.name: Weishui Scenic Area, Songzi
rows.summary: Weishui is a large reservoir resort in the hills of south-west Songzi, built round an earth dam about 9 km long whose construction began in 1958, with a lake of roughly 37 km² dotted with hundreds of wooded islands. It also takes in a national forest park of about 53 km² and karst caves such as Yan Jiangjun Cave, 2.2 km long with a flooded section, with boat trips on the lake and a large car-camping base below the dam. A memorial to the 1928 Jiulinggang uprising stands nearby.

rows.name: Xiejiaping Tourist Area, Songzi
rows.summary: Xiejiaping is the only Tujia ethnic township in Jingzhou, set in hills rising to 815 m on the Hunan border at the far south-west of Songzi, with a tourist area planned at about 5,300 mu (some 350 hectares). The sights mix scenery and Tujia culture: the Ming-Qing Huanglin bridge and a cluster of stilt houses, a canyon with waterfalls and karst scenery, a hot-spring area at Quchihe, and a Tujia folk museum and folk-custom street, with local Tujia folk songs and hand-waving dances. According to legend the name, roughly 'Armour-off Flat', comes from the Three Kingdoms general Guan Yu taking off his armour here.

rows.name: Yuexi Peninsula Hot Spring Resort, Honghu
rows.summary: Yuexi Peninsula is a hot-spring resort in Wulin town, Honghu, built around mineral water drawn from about 2,000 m underground at about 76 °C and a large column-free glass-and-steel indoor spring hall. Guests stay in the on-site hotel, some rooms opening straight onto outdoor pools, and the grounds also have a summer water park. It is a leisure resort rather than a sightseeing or heritage stop, suited to an overnight or half-day break from Wuhan.

rows.name: Zoumaling Neolithic City Site
rows.summary: Zoumaling is a late Neolithic walled settlement of the Qujialing culture beside Shangjin Lake, with an earth-banked enclosure about 370 m by 300 m, three gates in its east and west walls and traces of houses inside. The Jingzhou government describes it as among the earliest and largest late-prehistoric walled sites confirmed along the Yangtze. It is being developed as a national archaeological site park; for now visitors mostly see the earth banks and moat in farmland, with a few reconstructed thatched huts.

rows.name: Longwan Archaeological Site Park
rows.name_zh: 龙湾国家考古遗址公园
rows.summary: The park preserves the Longwan site, the remains of a Chu detached palace-and-garden complex of the Eastern Zhou period that archaeologists think may be the Zhanghua Terrace, centred on the Fangyingtai mound. Because earthen remains survive poorly in the damp south, the display hall shows a full-size model of the excavated terrace base above, with real remains such as a shell-paved road, drainage pipes and a side gate exposed below. The Longwan Site Museum, about 2 km from the park gate, shows excavated finds and models of the palace.

rows.name: Dajiuhu Wetland
rows.summary: A high mountain basin at about 1,730 m on the western edge of Shennongjia, covering roughly 20 km², with sub-alpine peat bog, wet meadow, streams and small lakes ringed by hills, a rare habitat in central China that is listed as a wetland of international importance. It is also a water source for the middle route of the South–North Water Transfer scheme, and the area keeps traces of Quaternary glaciation, karst sinkholes and the old Sichuan–Hubei salt road. All visitors switch to a park shuttle bus at the Pingqian transfer centre, and a small train and buses run within the scenic area.

rows.name: Hongping Gallery
rows.summary: A mountain valley area around Hongping town in central Shennongjia, at about 1,600 m, known as Hongping Gallery after a series of paintings by the artist Zhang Bu and popular with painters and photographers. The Gallery Valley section has a 'pearl curtain' waterfall whose flow changes with the seasons and a narrow cleft, the 'line of sky', with 499 stone steps and about 200 m of height difference. Autumn colour and cloud are its main draws, and it combines easily with nearby Tianyan.

rows.name: Shennong Tianchi
rows.summary: A commercially run valley park at Shennongjia's northern entrance, opened in 2014 as Batao Yuan and renamed Shennong Tianchi in 2023. Local legend calls it Emperor Yan's orchard, and the name Batao refers to the wild Ba walnut trees that still grow here; streams, pools and marshy meadows run through Qinling fir forest around a giant fir known as Jiulong Shensha, and the developed area of about 8 km² has an RV and camping ground, a forest adventure park and a winter snow park. It is more a leisure park than wilderness, and suits an easy half day on the way in or out of Shennongjia.

rows.name: Tianyan Scenic Area, Shennongjia
rows.summary: A forest and mountain-pass scenic area in central Shennongjia, named for Yanzi Ya ('Swallow Pass') in the north and Tianmen Ya ('Heaven's Gate Pass') in the south, the latter the highest point of the G209 highway through the area. Highlights are primeval forest, sea-of-cloud and 'Buddha's light' effects at the passes, a high bridge over Yanzi Ya and a cave said to shelter tens of thousands of swiftlets, and the Shennongjia government counts more than 2,400 plant and 200 animal species here. The area is tied to local lore of the 'wild man' (Yeren) and to the Han epic 'Heian Zhuan' (Book of Darkness), and takes about two hours.

rows.name: Bailongtan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A wooded stream valley with a canyon walkway on the western edge of Shiyan, in Zhangwan District. Local tourism pages describe running streams, dense greenery and shaded paths, and it is promoted as a cool place to walk in summer. A short outing for people already in Shiyan rather than a reason to come to the region.

rows.name: Canglanghai, Danjiangkou
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area and boat landing on Danjiangkou Reservoir, in the new district at the edge of Danjiangkou city. Most visitors come for a boat trip on the reservoir; the memorial park for the South-to-North Water Diversion Project stands close by. A low-key stop for people already in Danjiangkou city, best combined with the dam and the memorial park.

rows.name: Cixiaogou Imperial Timber Cliff Inscription
rows.summary: A small Ming-dynasty rock inscription in a gorge in Eping township, carved in 1558 on a cliff to mark the felling of giant nanmu timbers that were sent to Beijing to build the imperial palace. Its nine vertical lines, 73 characters in all, were composed by Liao Xikui, then magistrate of Guanghua county, and describe the search for the timber and its finding; the gorge took the name Cixiao in the same period. The panel measures about 1.7 by 1.8 metres.

rows.name: Dafeng Granary, Yunyang
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty state granary in the old town of Yunyang, on a rise beside the bridgehead of the Yunyang Han River Bridge, rebuilt in 1881 on the site of an earlier prefectural granary. Three black-tiled brick buildings, a main granary with two smaller ones, stand on timber frames with louvred ventilation windows, and old steles and memorial arches gathered from the surrounding countryside are kept in the courtyard. National heritage funding paid for a restoration that began in 2018 and had finished its main structures by late 2019, with a plan to open it as a grain- and farming-culture exhibition.

rows.name: Donggou Red Tourism Area
rows.summary: A red-tourism area in Donggou village, Maota township, in the hills south of Shiyan, centred on a restored Ming–Qing house that holds the Central Plains Breakout (Northwest Hubei) History Memorial Hall. Local sources say the Red Third Army under He Long was active in the area in 1931, and that in 1946 forces that had broken out of the Central Plains under Li Xiannian and Wang Shusheng set up a Communist-led county government here. As of 2020 the hall had about a dozen exhibition rooms and some 120 relics, and the grounds also have an old theatre stage, a village schoolhouse, a martyrs' cemetery, flower gardens and craft workshops.

rows.name: Gan Ancestral Hall, Zhuxi
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty clan ancestral hall in Ganjialing village, Zhongfeng town, built in memory of Gan Jifang, a local garrison officer of the early Qing, and enlarged in the mid-18th and late 19th centuries. It is a brick-and-timber courtyard compound with a main hall, rear hall, side wings and a gate tower under grey-tiled roofs, with a stone-framed gate and some murals and painted decoration, at the heart of a village named in 2012 among China's traditional villages. A Hubei Daily report of February 2026 says the hall has been turned into a cultural display venue, which makes it a short stop for anyone exploring rural north-west Hubei.

rows.name: Gaojia Huawu
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty family residence in Xiejiagou village, Zhuping township, in the hills of north-west Zhushan county near the Hubei–Shaanxi–Sichuan border. Building began in 1797 and took about thirty years, and the house is noted for its horse-head (matou) fire walls and its many carvings. Its name means 'flower house'.

rows.name: Guanyin Cave, Fangxian
rows.summary: A small temple-and-cave site on a hill about 3 km south of Fangxian county town. The county describes its layout as one hall, two caves, three star gods and four views: an ancestral-master hall, side-by-side caves for Guanyin and Guandi (Guan Yu), figures of the star gods Fu, Lu and Shou, and a few viewpoints. Its Qing-dynasty buildings are listed as a provincial heritage site, and it makes a short stop before heading on to Yeren Cave.

rows.name: Hanjiang Green Valley
rows.summary: A leisure area of about 6 km² in Anyang town, Yunyang, with a herb garden of about 330 hectares, a flower field on the water of over 60 hectares, more than 200 hectares of grassland and three themed 'manor' areas. Activities include fishing, barbecue and camping, go-karts, high-level swings and water play, with some twenty rides in all. It is also a national water-conservancy scenic area and a soil-conservation demonstration park.

rows.name: Honggan Ping Orange Orchard, Junxian
rows.summary: A commercial 'smart orchard' beside Danjiangkou Reservoir in Junxian town, run by the Honggan Ping company and rated 4A as an agri-tourism site. Visitors walk a viewing corridor that shows the sensors and data used to manage the citrus groves, pick fruit and join study visits on automated crop protection and harvesting. It suits families and anyone curious about Danjiangkou's citrus industry.

rows.name: Huxiaotan Gorge
rows.summary: A river-gorge scenic area on the Baiquan River in Baiquan village, Daliu township, named 'Tiger Roar Shoal' for the sound of the water pounding the rocks. About thirty natural and cultural sights are strung along the valley, including cliffs, stepped waterfalls, a chain of pools, caves such as the White Tiger Cave and the ruins of an old temple to the Wood Dragon. It is noticeably cooler than Shiyan city in summer, so it is mostly visited then.

rows.name: Jingle Palace, Danjiangkou
rows.summary: A Taoist palace complex on the north shore of Jingle Lake, at the north-eastern edge of Danjiangkou city. It is a reconstruction, built between 2000 and 2006, of the Ming-dynasty Jingle Palace, founded in 1418 in old Junzhou and counted as the first of the Wudang Mountains' great palaces, which went under water when Danjiangkou Reservoir filled in 1967. Some 830 relics, including an archway and a tortoise-borne stele, were moved to higher ground beforehand, so the halls are new; the complex is a working Taoist site that held an ordination programme in 2023.

rows.name: Jiulong Falls, Yunyang
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area in Nanhuatang town, Yunyang district, named 'Nine Dragons Falls' for the series of waterfalls along its stream; the district lists its core area as about 18 km². Walking paths follow the stream between cliffs, pools and woodland. In summer a 2.5 km rafting course runs through the gorge, and a cliff-side sightseeing car and bamboo-raft rides are also on offer.

rows.name: Longtan River, Yunxi
rows.summary: A waterfall and gorge scenic area in Yangwei town, run as a provincial forest park and geopark, with more than sixty sights, over forty of them connected with waterfalls. The route takes in a flight of more than 80 cascades, including the Great Dragon Falls (Dalongpu). A traditional paper-making workshop is also on the route.

rows.name: Nüwa Mountain, Zhushan
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Baofeng town built around the legend of Nüwa, the goddess who in Chinese myth mended the sky and made the first people. Visitors climb to pray for blessings and hear the Nüwa stories, and the summit looks over a sea of cloud, and sometimes the sunrise, when the weather allows. An immersive intangible-heritage hall in the grounds shows more than 200 craft and folk-art items from over ten local categories.

rows.name: Qinglongshan Dinosaur Egg Fossil Geopark
rows.name_zh: 青龙山恐龙蛋化石群国家地质公园
rows.pinyin: Qīnglóngshān Kǒnglóngdàn Huàshíqún Guójiā Dìzhì Gōngyuán
rows.summary: A national geopark in Liupi town protecting a field of Cretaceous dinosaur eggs left where they were laid, with at least 300,000 eggs estimated, which state media describe as the largest known in-situ concentration. Visitors see the fossils and exhibition panels, and the park has added smart-glasses and hologram displays showing dinosaurs hatching. It is popular with family and school groups.

rows.name: Shangjin Ancient City
rows.summary: A compact walled town on the east bank of the Jinqian River, close to the Shaanxi border, roughly 400 by 300 metres with walls about 7 m high, and known locally as the 'Emperor's Ferry' for its river crossing on the way towards Xi'an. The walls were begun in 1368, at the start of the Ming, and fully repaired in 1802, although the national listing dates the town to the Qing; visitors can walk on the wall, see the Shanxi–Shaanxi guildhall and an old street in Ming and Qing style, and take a boat trip on the river. Shangjin was named a national historic and cultural town in 2007.

rows.name: Shiyan Museum
rows.summary: The municipal museum of Shiyan, a national second-grade museum in the city centre close to Beijing North Road. Its displays cover dinosaurs, early humans (including replicas of the Yunxian Man skulls, Homo erectus fossils roughly a million years old found at Xuetangliangzi in Yunyang District), the Wudang Mountains, the Danjiangkou reservoir and Shiyan's car industry, plus finds from the South-to-North Water Diversion reservoir area. Worth an hour for anyone interested in the human and natural history of the Shiyan area.

rows.name: Taiji Gorge
rows.summary: A red-sandstone gorge on the western side of Danjiangkou Reservoir, in Shigu town. It was known as Shuanglong ('Twin Dragons') Gorge before its rename, after the Qinglong and Huanglong ridges that face each other across it. Its Danxia-type landforms led to its listing as a Hubei provincial geopark in 2008.

rows.name: Taohuadao Rammed-Earth Town
rows.summary: A modern rural tourism town in Shuiping town, built in rammed-earth style from about 2018 and called Peach Blossom Island (Taohuadao); its Chinese name, Hangtu Xiaozhen, means 'rammed-earth town'. Its offer is built around health and wellness, including herbal-medicine meals and daoyin exercise sessions, and it has been named one of China's intangible-heritage tourism towns. Local itineraries often pair it with the Longwangya tea gardens.

rows.name: Tianhe Scenic Area, Yunxi
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area on the Tianhe at the southern edge of Yunxi county town, built around the county's Qixi (Double Seventh) culture, which is on China's national list of intangible cultural heritage. Features include Xuanguguan, a temple complex in traditional style laid out with a lake, caves, bridges, pavilions and halls, and Cherry Blossom Valley, planted with cherry trees around small bridges and pavilions. The county has also rebuilt an old street as the Qixi Sky Street, with immersive projection performances.

rows.name: Tianhekou, Yunxi
rows.summary: The place where the Tianhe ('Heavenly River') flows into the Han, in Guanyin town, linked by local tradition to the Qixi (Double Seventh) legend of the cowherd and the weaver girl. The 4A area, about 1.7 km² and rated in December 2025, is a recent development with a wetland park, a riverside loop, a lion-head cliff viewpoint, a visitor centre, farmstays and an RV campsite. Yunxi's Qixi tradition is on China's national list of intangible cultural heritage.

rows.name: Wudang Daming Peak
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Guanshan town, west of the Wudang Mountains' main peak, which Shiyan's tourism commission puts at about 1,316 m in height and roughly 39 sq km in area. It has a cliff-side plank walkway, a narrow 'strip of sky' gorge and the 'South Heavenly Gate' viewpoint, plus a glass skywalk, a cliff swing, zip lines and via ferrata climbing. A newer, activity-led area that gained its 4A rating in 2023, it suits active visitors with a car more than temple-hunters.

rows.name: Wudang Happy Valley
rows.summary: A commercial adventure and amusement park in a wooded river valley in the Wudang Special Zone, about 5 km from the entrance of the Wudang Mountains scenic area and next to Taiji Lake. The special zone's tourism bureau lists a 75 m bungee jump, a rafting course of about 5.8 km, zip lines, a cliff swing and go-karts, plus a children's area with a dozen or so rides. It suits families and groups who want a lively half day alongside a trip to the Wudang temples; it is not a heritage visit.

rows.name: Wudang South Pilgrim Path
rows.summary: A walking-oriented scenic area on the south-western flank of the Wudang Mountains in Guanshan town, on the old pilgrim route by which worshippers from Sichuan, Shaanxi and western Hubei once came to Wudang. Danjiangkou's tourism bureau describes a route of about 20 km along the Jiudao River with plank walkways, streams and rocky peaks, strung with the Lüjiahe folk-song village, the former headquarters of the Red Third Army and rock features such as 'Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl' and 'Dragon-Slaying Cliff'. Known locally as Wudang's 'back garden', it suits visitors who want the countryside and hiking side of Wudang rather than the main temples.

rows.name: Wulong River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested gorge scenic area on the Wulong River, a tributary of the Tianhe that rises in the Qinling foothills on the Hubei–Shaanxi border, nicknamed 'little Jiuzhaigou' locally for its clear water, waterfalls and woods. Sights include the Wangyou Bridge, the Silver Curtain waterfall and a narrow slot called 'Line of Sky', and the Xiangu Gorge has a high glass-floored walkway.

rows.name: Yeren Cave and Valley, Fangxian
rows.summary: A limestone cave and a wooded gorge about 25 km south of Fangxian county town, named after local 'wild man' (yeren) stories; the best known tells of a farmer's encounter at the cave mouth in 1974. The cave has two levels joined by an artificial stairway, with varied stalactite formations lit by coloured lights, and stays cool in summer; the valley beside it has a long gorge with cliff-side walkways and a lake with boats. The wild man is folklore rather than a confirmed species, and the area is promoted mainly as a summer retreat.

rows.name: Yunlong Valley, Sai Wudang
rows.summary: A large mountain-resort development in the Sai Wudang hills south of central Shiyan, in Maojian District, planned over about 24 km² in three phases with wellness, hot-spring, family-study, mountain-sports and folk-culture zones. Sai Wudang, also called Fulong Mountain, takes its name from a main peak that stands about 118 m higher than Wudang's Tianzhu Peak. The district lists the resort as partly open on a trial basis, and a folk-customs museum and a science museum there are stops on a Maojian tourist bus route.

rows.name: Zhushan Turquoise Culture Tourist Area
rows.name_zh: 竹山绿松石文化旅游区
rows.summary: A themed cultural-tourism complex in Zhushan county town, between the Du and Huo rivers, built around turquoise, which is mined in several counties of north-west Hubei including Zhushan, and around local legends and history, from the Nüwa myth to the ancient Yong state and the Peach Blossom Spring story. The county describes it as one core, one street, one district and one waterside corridor, with staged performances, commercial space and river-front walks. It was rated a national 4A area only in December 2025.

rows.name: Baopu Valley Wellness Resort
rows.summary: A wellness resort of about 12 km² in forested hills at the head of the Huai River, on the Hubei–Henan border. It is built around traditional Chinese medicine, with a clinic offering herbal baths, moxibustion and massage, plus forest cabins, guesthouses and walking routes. Local descriptions also mention Xinyi Zhai, a hill stockade dated to the Song dynasty, and a waterfall; it was rated 4A in December 2023.

rows.name: Dahong Mountain
rows.summary: A stand-alone mountain massif of about 305 km² that straddles Suizhou, Jingshan and Zhongxiang, with 127 km² and its highest peak, Baozhu Peak (1,055 m), in Suizhou. Visitors come for the rebuilt Ci'en Buddhist temple on the peak, Bailong Pool (a crater lake high in the hills), two karst caves, a very large ancient ginkgo said to have been planted by Emperor Guangwu of the Han, and a rafting stream. It has been a national scenic area since 1988, and the hills were the base of the Lülin rebels at the end of the Western Han.

rows.name: Former HQ of the New Fourth Army's Fifth Division, Jiukouyan
rows.name_zh: 新四军第五师司令部旧址
rows.summary: In June 1940 the headquarters of the New Fourth Army's Hubei–Henan force moved into the Sun family compound at Jiukouyan, a Qing-dynasty courtyard house built in 1733 with 56 rooms in a three-hall, two-courtyard layout, and the Fifth Division was formally established there on 5 April 1941 under Li Xiannian. The compound is now a memorial museum showing the headquarters' offices and living quarters, and the village has further wartime sites, among them a branch of the Anti-Japanese Military and Political University, a newspaper office and an arsenal, plus a memorial garden opened in 2015. The village is also a listed traditional village.

rows.name: Gaogui Santan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest park and provincial scenic area on the Hubei–Henan border at the foot of the old Pingjing Pass, known for its waterfalls and pools (the 'three pools' of the name), the summit of Dagui Mountain and a grove of qingtan (wingceltis) trees of more than 2,000 mu that local officials bill as the largest in China. It also has the old pass road with a surviving beacon tower, Yang Gong Ridge (named for the Ming official Yang Lian, a native of the area) and Longpa Zhai, a hill fortress protected at provincial level. It became Guangshui's first 4A scenic area in 2023.

rows.name: Journey to the West Park, Sui County
rows.summary: A large leisure resort themed on the novel Journey to the West, covering about 260 hectares in the hills near Dahong Mountain. It combines hot-spring pools, a zoo, a glass bridge, a rose field and themed play areas with more than 800 hotel and cabin rooms on site. It suits families and groups on a leisure break rather than sightseers.

rows.name: Journey to the West Rafting, Huaihe
rows.summary: A rafting run of about 9 km down the Longtan stream in the Tongbai Mountains, with nine bends and more than 30 rapids over about two and a half to three hours, ending close to the expressway exit at Huaihe. Rafting is in four-person boats and runs only in summer, typically from late June to early September.

rows.name: Leigudun Tombs
rows.summary: The cemetery of the rulers of the state of Zeng in the Warring States period, spread over a low rise on the north-western edge of Suizhou as eight burial grounds covering about 116 hectares. The best-known tomb is that of Marquis Yi of Zeng, opened in 1978 and yielding more than 15,000 objects, among them a set of 65 bronze bells whose originals are now in the Hubei Provincial Museum in Wuhan. A protective display building stands over the tomb pit, and the Suizhou Museum next door displays Zeng-state bronzes and gives chime-bell performances.

rows.name: Shennong Tribe
rows.summary: A theme park in the Tongbai Mountains built around rock carvings that county officials present as prehistoric images of the legendary farmer-god Shennong, a sun god and a three-legged sun bird. Visitors walk through sacrificial gardens to the sun and the moon, a stone-carving area and a garden themed on a supposed Shennong script, in a development first rated AAA in 2021. It is best treated as a cultural theme park; the dating and interpretation of the carvings come from the local authorities.

rows.name: Suizhou Cultural Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped park in the eastern part of Suizhou, laid out around the city's cultural themes: the legendary farmer-god Shennong, the Zeng chime bells, the Spring and Autumn minister Ji Liang (whose statue stands partway up the hillside) and the Sui dynasty, which took its name from the city. It is a quiet city park rather than a major sight, and city itineraries pair it with the Suizhou Museum and the Marquis Yi tomb site.

rows.name: Thousand-Year Ginkgo Valley
rows.summary: A valley of ancient ginkgo trees strung along about 12 km of five villages in Luoyang town, with around 300 trees more than a thousand years old. The leaves turn gold from mid-October to late November, which is the main season. After a year-long closure for rebuilding, it reopened in December 2024 and the resort district held its formal opening in July 2025, with new visitor facilities and guesthouses.

rows.name: Tianwangzhai Hill Fortress
rows.summary: A hill fortress of stone walls that follow nine hilltops on Gucheng Mountain in the Tongbai range, with gates and beacon towers; local accounts date it to the end of the Song or the Yuan period. It is a provincially protected relic, billed as the best-preserved stockade of its kind in central China, and part of the Hubei section of the Long March National Cultural Park, with displays on the Red 25th Army's Taibai meeting during the Long March. Cliff walls and a waterfall add a scenic side for those who like hill walking.

rows.name: Yandi Hometown Park, Lishan
rows.summary: A memorial park at Lishan, which Suizhou promotes as the birthplace of Yandi (Shennong), the legendary farmer-god and herbalist. Its core area of about 3.4 km² has more than 60 sights, among them the Shennong Cave said to be his birthplace, a statue of Yandi, an ancestor-worship plaza, the Yandi hall and a herb garden. Ceremonies are held each year around his traditional birthday on the 26th day of the fourth lunar month, and the Suizhou rite is on China's national intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Bailong Temple, Tianmen
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Zaoshi town, north-east of Tianmen, said to have been founded in the Southern Dynasties. The protected buildings are of Ming date and are described as well preserved, and the temple was listed as a national protected monument in 2013.

rows.name: Shijiahe Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic walled settlement of about 8 square kilometres, occupied from about 3900 to 1800 BC and described in state media as the largest, best preserved and longest-lived prehistoric walled settlement found in the middle Yangtze; it is the type site of the Shijiahe culture. Excavations found city walls and moats, large buildings, ritual areas and hundreds of jade pieces. The Shijiahe Site Museum opened to the public on 19 May 2026 and shows finds in six exhibition sections, including jade human-head figures, and the site park also has a performance centre and the excavated Yinxintai area.

rows.name: Tea Sage Hometown Garden
rows.summary: A memorial park in the old town of Tianmen, ancient Jingling, honouring Lu Yu, the Tang-dynasty author of the Classic of Tea, who is revered as the Sage of Tea and was born in the town. It gathers sites linked to his memory, among them a pavilion named for him, Wenxue (Literary) Spring and the ancient Wild Goose Bridge. It suits visitors interested in tea history and a gentle walk through the old town.

rows.name: Dayuwan Ancient Village
rows.summary: A hillside village at the foot of Mulan Mountain, founded in the early Ming dynasty by the Yu family from Wuyuan in Jiangxi, with dozens of Ming and Qing houses in Jiangxi style, horse-head gables and stone-paved lanes; it is a China Historic and Cultural Village. It is run as a scenic area with folk shows such as shadow puppets, puppet plays and bronze-bell music, and each autumn crops are laid out on the roofs for a drying festival.

rows.name: Delin Apartments (Hankou Residence of CPC Leaders)
rows.name_zh: 中共中央领导人汉口住地旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Zhōngyāng Lǐngdǎorén Hànkǒu Zhùdì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Delin Apartments is a three-storey Western-style apartment block built in 1925 in Hankou's former British concession. After the Communist Party was driven underground in July 1927 it housed senior party figures: Zhou Enlai and Deng Yingchao stayed first, then Qu Qiubai, Li Weihan and Deng Xiaoping, and several meetings were held there before the party centre moved back to Shanghai in September 1927. The building was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: Early Buildings of Wuhan University
rows.summary: A group of university buildings put up between 1930 and 1936 on Luojia Hill beside East Lake, combining palace-style Chinese roofs with modern reinforced-concrete frames; 15 sites with 26 buildings are listed as national heritage. They include the old library, the courtyard buildings of the arts and law schools and the hillside men's dormitory, nicknamed the Cherry Blossom Castle for the trees around it. The buildings are still in use on a working campus, so visitors mostly walk between them.

rows.name: Early Modern Buildings of Hankou
rows.summary: A group of European-style banks, consulates and company offices along Yanjiang Avenue and the streets behind it, dating from the decades after Hankou opened as a treaty port in 1861 and five foreign powers took concessions here. The listing covers the former German consulate, the HSBC and Yokohama Specie Bank buildings and the 1909 water tower, with five more buildings added in 2019, among them the former Russo-Chinese Bank. Most are still offices or banks and are best seen from the street, though a few have museums inside.

rows.name: East Lake, Wuhan
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A freshwater lake of about 33 sq km in Wuchang, among the largest urban lakes in China, whose scenic area is divided into six zones including Tingtao, Moshan and Luoyan. Visitors walk or cycle the lakeside greenway, which opened in 2016 and now runs for more than 100 km, and visit Moshan, which has a cherry-blossom park and the Chu City attraction. The Hubei Provincial Museum stands on the western shore.

rows.name: Eighth Route Army Office in Wuhan
rows.name_zh: 八路军武汉办事处旧址
rows.summary: This four-storey building at 57 Changchun Street in Hankou was the Wuhan office of the Eighth Route Army from December 1937 until October 1938, from which the Communist Party liaised with the Nationalist government; the party's Yangtze Bureau also worked here. It was destroyed in a 1944 air raid, rebuilt to the original design in 1978 and opened as a memorial in 1979. Restored offices and bedrooms of Zhou Enlai, Deng Yingchao, Dong Biwu, Ye Jianying and others are shown with a permanent exhibition on Wuhan in the War of Resistance, refreshed in 2025.

rows.name: Fengwa Ancient Village
rows.summary: A cultural-tourism complex in Fenghuang town, Xinzhou District, billed as a cluster of Ming and Qing-style buildings, with antique and folk-custom displays, leisure facilities and local food. In the evenings and at festivals it runs light shows, a fireworks theatre and folk performances, including a staged 'tossing the embroidered ball' wedding-choice show at one of its towers. It is a commercial attraction that suits families and day-trippers wanting a half-day out from Wuhan.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhan Tianyou
rows.summary: A two-storey Western-style brick house that the railway engineer Zhan Tianyou (Jeme Tien Yow) designed for himself in Hankou's former Russian concession and lived in from 1913 until his death in 1919. Zhan, a Yale graduate known as the Father of China's Railroads, was chief engineer of the Beijing–Zhangjiakou line and was in Hankou to direct the Guangdong–Hankou and Sichuan–Hankou railway projects. The house was repaired and opened as an exhibition room in 1993 and is now the Zhan Tianyou Former Residence Museum.

rows.name: Gude Temple
rows.summary: An active Buddhist temple in Hankou, founded in 1877 as a small hermitage and expanded in the early twentieth century into one of Wuhan's four main monasteries. Its halls, built mainly between 1916 and 1934, are an unusual mix of styles, and Jawaharlal Nehru noted its cluster of Indian-style pagodas on a visit in 1954. In 1911 its monks tended wounded soldiers of the Wuchang Uprising, and the remains of more than 3,000 fallen revolutionaries were buried beside it.

rows.name: Hankou Site of the CPC Central Propaganda Department
rows.name_zh: 汉口中共中央宣传部旧址
rows.summary: This building in Hankou's Fuyili lane housing, built in 1917, was the seat of the Chinese Communist Party's Central Propaganda Department from March to September 1927. After restoration it opened as an exhibition hall on the department and on Qu Qiubai, who lived there, and it was listed as a national protected site in 2013. It is a small, single-building stop in old Hankou.

rows.name: Hankow Customs House
rows.summary: Built in 1924 for the Hankou customs office, this four-storey Renaissance-style building has granite Corinthian colonnades and a clock tower, and was Wuhan's tallest building when it opened. The clock still chimes the Westminster tune. Since 2015 the interior has been the Jianghan Customs Museum, with a reconstruction of the 1920s customs hall.

rows.name: Happy Valley Wuhan
rows.summary: Happy Valley Wuhan is an amusement park run by the OCT group, the fifth in its Happy Valley chain, in the eastern suburbs near East Lake; it opened in April 2012. Its rides include a wooden racing coaster and several launched and looping coasters, spread over themed zones. It is a day out for families and thrill-seekers rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Hesheng Bridge Northern Expedition Cemetery
rows.name_zh: 贺胜桥北伐阵亡将士陵园
rows.summary: A memorial garden for National Revolutionary Army soldiers who died in the Battle of Hesheng Bridge, fought on 29–31 August 1926 during the Northern Expedition against Wu Peifu's forces and won by the expedition army. The cemetery dates from 1929 and was added to the national heritage list in 2019; the city also lists it among its municipal-level memorials to fallen soldiers. A flight of stone steps rises through landscaped grounds to a small domed pavilion and monument wall.

rows.name: Huabohui Flower Town
rows.summary: A flower-themed leisure town in Caidian's Sino-French Eco-City, near Houguan Lake national wetland park, with a planned area of 5,300 mu (about 350 hectares). It combines flower fields with rural-experience activities, children's entertainment and holiday stays, and since 2024 has run an immersive evening walk with light projections, live performances and fire shows. It is a commercial, family-oriented attraction.

rows.name: Huaishanji Embankment
rows.summary: A long granite embankment on the Yangtze bank at the foot of Huaishan, begun in the Ming dynasty's Jiajing reign so that boats could be hauled and moored safely past the rocky, fast-flowing stretch at Jinkou. Its three stepped tiers include a towpath, and it is described as the only surviving ancient shipping structure of its kind on the Yangtze. It was restored between 1997 and 2002, and makes a short stop alongside the Zhongshan Warship Museum, about 500 m away.

rows.name: Huaxiang Chagu Tea Valley
rows.summary: A tea-plantation leisure area on Honggang Mountain in Caijiazha subdistrict, Huangpi, which was rated 4A in 2022. The tea hills are planted with plum, cherry and other blossom, drawing most visitors from late winter to spring, and the park holds poetry-and-tea events through the year, including a poetry festival held since 2017. It is a commercial park suited to a relaxed half day.

rows.name: Jinli Tusicheng Tujia Scenic Area
rows.summary: A leisure park themed on Tujia and Miao culture in the hills of northern Huangpi, built in the style of a tusi (hereditary chieftain) fortress town with stilt houses rather than as a historic site. Its main attraction is a rafting course of several kilometres that combines an elevated glass section with a canyon section, and it also has waterfall viewpoints, a splash plaza and folk shows. It is a commercial park, mainly for families and groups.

rows.name: Jinlong Shuizhai Eco-Park
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure park beside Jinlong Lake in Caidian, planted with camellias, lotus, osmanthus and plum so that something is in flower in each season, and known for its lotus ponds, which can be toured by boat in summer. The district lists a waterfall, a long embankment path, a tea garden, an artificial beach, a deer-themed forest play area, a lotus-root museum and an equestrian club among its features. It suits casual family outings.

rows.name: Jiuzhen Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded range of nine linked peaks in Caidian whose main summit, at 276 m, is billed as the highest point on the Jianghan Plain; forest covers more than 90% of the scenic area. Trails pass the site of the Jiuzhen Daoist temple, said to have been founded in the Wei-Jin period and long since vanished, and a valley named for the woodcutter Zhong Ziqi of the Boya and Zhong Ziqi 'high mountains, flowing water' friendship legend. It is mainly a local day-walk and spring-outing spot.

rows.name: Lianghu Manxiang Leisure Park
rows.summary: Lianghu Manxiang is a countryside leisure park in Wulijie, in the south-east of Wuhan's Jiangxia District, run as a large farm resort with guesthouses and meeting rooms, picking and fishing, farm-life activities and bonfire evenings. Provincial media report that it has added a play area with equipment that needs no power, a camping ground and seasonal fruit picking, including mulberries. It is aimed mainly at families and school groups on short stays from the city rather than at sightseers.

rows.name: Mulan Cultural and Ecological Tourist Area
rows.summary: A national 5A area in northern Huangpi District made up of four parts tied to the legend of Mulan, which local tradition places here: Mulan Mountain, a long-standing religious site with an ancient building complex that is also part of a national geopark; Mulan Tianchi (Heavenly Lake), a forest canyon of waterfalls and pools; Mulan Grassland, a steppe-themed park; and Yunwu Mountain, known for its azaleas in spring. Mulan Mountain covers about 30 sq km. Sightseeing buses run within the scenic area.

rows.name: Mulan Huaxiang Flower Village
rows.summary: A former old hamlet in Huangpi, renovated from the mid-2010s and opened as a scenic area in 2017, now a flower and night-tour destination with seasonal flower beds, an animal park, a tropical-plant garden, rides and a children's water park. 'Mulan Night City', a street built in Northern Wei style that opened in 2023, stages shows and light displays in the evening. It is a commercial, family-oriented attraction.

rows.name: Mulan Qingliangzhai
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 10 sq km in the hills of northern Huangpi, known for autumn foliage (a red-maple festival has run since 2015) and as a summer refuge from the city heat. Activities include a glass-bottomed rafting run, a glass walkway and a zip line, and a hillside guesthouse now keeps many visitors overnight. It is a commercial leisure area rather than a wilderness.

rows.name: Mulan Shengtian
rows.summary: A hill-ringed leisure area in Wangjiahe, Huangpi, developed from a former forest farm, with about 90% forest cover, streams, a waterfall and rock formations. Its main draw is the Forest Water Kingdom, a large summer water park with slides, a big pool, a sand beach and a long shaded rafting channel. It is a commercial park aimed at families and young groups.

rows.name: Mulan Water Town
rows.summary: A military-themed leisure park in Wangjiahe, Huangpi, laid out beside a lake and river junction with the look of a Jiangnan water town rather than any historic fabric. Activities listed on the district and city pages include amphibious vehicle rides, off-road buggy rides, live-action CS-style games, jungle courses and field camping. Evening events have included molten-iron sparks and a lit bamboo dragon raft on the lake, so it suits families and groups looking for an activity day.

rows.name: Panlongcheng
rows.summary: The remains of a walled Shang-dynasty city of about 1500-1300 BCE on the north bank of the Yangtze, uncovered by a flood in 1954 and described by the Wuhan government as the highest-ranking and largest early Shang site known in the Yangtze valley. Excavations have found city walls, palace foundations, high-status tombs and a bronze-casting workshop outside the walls, and the site was named one of China's ten major archaeological discoveries of 2024. It is a national archaeological site park, and its museum, opened in 2019, shows bronzes, jades and pottery from the digs while the walls and foundations are laid out in the grounds.

rows.name: Qingchuan Pavilion
rows.summary: Qingchuan Pavilion stands on a rocky point at the foot of Turtle Hill in Hanyang, where the Han River meets the Yangtze, facing Yellow Crane Tower across the water. The scenic area, rebuilt in the 1980s and early 1990s, centres on the Qingchuan tower, first built in the 1540s to honour Yu the Great's flood control, and includes the Iron Gate tower, which houses an exhibition on Wuhan's flood-control history. The nationally listed part is Yuji Palace, a temple to Yu dating back to the Southern Song, whose present buildings were put up in 1863.

rows.name: Site of the 5th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party
rows.summary: This former primary school in Wuchang is where the Chinese Communist Party's Fifth National Congress opened in April 1927, in the school's covered playground, before the delegates moved to another Wuhan venue to continue in secret. The compound was restored to its 1927 layout and opened as a memorial in 2007, with the playground rebuilt and a historical exhibition on the congress. Chen Tanqiu, an early party member, taught and lived at the school from 1922 to 1927.

rows.name: Site of the August 7 Conference
rows.summary: A three-storey brick-and-concrete block in Hankou's former Russian concession, originally part of a foreign-built apartment complex, where leaders of the Chinese Communist Party met in secret on 7 August 1927, after the Kuomintang had turned on its communist allies, to decide the party's course. Mao Zedong's remark that political power grows out of the barrel of a gun is associated with this meeting. The building is now a memorial museum, with an exhibition on the conference on the ground floor and a reconstruction of the meeting room upstairs.

rows.name: Site of the Beijing–Hankou Railway General Union
rows.summary: This small brick-and-timber house in Hankou's Jiang'an District, a former private home, served as headquarters of the Beijing–Hankou Railway General Union after its founding meeting in Zhengzhou was broken up in February 1923. The railway strike organised from here was violently suppressed on 7 February 1923. It has been a memorial since 1981 with an exhibition on the strike, and was shifted slightly when Jiefang Avenue was widened in 1995.

rows.name: Site of the CPC Central Committee Offices in Wuhan
rows.name_zh: 武汉中共中央机关旧址
rows.summary: This three-storey brick-and-timber building in Hankou's old Russian concession district was rented by the Communist Party's Central Committee as offices and a residence in 1927, after it moved from Shanghai to Wuhan, and left the same year. It was repaired from 2014 and, together with two neighbouring historic buildings, opened as a memorial museum on 30 September 2016. Its permanent exhibition on the party centre's months in Wuhan includes 31 restored rooms, among them the Politburo Standing Committee's meeting room and the living quarters of leaders such as Cai Hesen.

rows.name: Site of the New Fourth Army Headquarters, Hankou
rows.summary: This was the first headquarters of the New Fourth Army, set up in Hankou in late 1937 when Communist-led guerrilla forces in southern China were reorganised under the National Revolutionary Army; the headquarters moved to Nanchang in January 1938. Two surviving buildings on Shengli Street were restored by the city in 2005 and now hold a memorial hall, which opened in 2006: one hall carries the history exhibition, the other has the meeting room and staff offices restored along with the commanders' office-bedrooms. The site was listed as a national protected site in 2013.

rows.name: Site of the Wuhan Nationalist Government (Nanyang Building)
rows.summary: A five-storey reinforced-concrete building of 1921 in Hankou, put up by the brothers who ran the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Company, which housed the offices of the Wuhan Nationalist Government from December 1926 to March 1927. The third floor has been restored since 1988 with the hall where the Kuomintang's Second Central Executive Committee held its plenary session in 1927 and some of the government's offices, shown as an exhibition. The building is also known as the Nanyang Building.

rows.name: Surrender Hall of the Sixth War Zone, Wuhan
rows.name_zh: 国民政府第六战区受降堂旧址
rows.pinyin: Guómín Zhèngfǔ Dìliù Zhànqū Shòuxiángtáng Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A white-walled Chinese-style hall of about 400 square metres in Zhongshan Park, built in 1942 as an ancestral hall for the Qing viceroy Zhang Zhidong. On 18 September 1945 General Sun Weiru took the Japanese surrender for the Sixth War Zone here, and it is one of a few surviving surrender venues in mainland China. An exhibition open since 2000 recreates the ceremony at life size with wax figures alongside wartime documents and photographs, and the hall was listed as a national protected site in 2019.

rows.name: Tomb of the Soviet Air Volunteers, Wuhan
rows.name_zh: 苏联空军志愿队烈士墓
rows.summary: A memorial cemetery in Jiefang Park holding the remains of Soviet air volunteers who were based in Wuhan in 1938 and died fighting Japan. The remains were moved here in 1956 from the Hankou International Cemetery, and the grounds have a square-based obelisk and a long granite tomb platform inscribed in Chinese and Russian. It became a national protected site in 2019.

rows.name: Tombs of the Ming Princes of Chu
rows.summary: The burial ground of nine Ming-dynasty princes of Chu on Longquan Mountain in Jiangxia District, a line that began when the Hongwu Emperor's sixth son, Zhu Zhen, was enfeoffed at Wuchang in 1370. Prince Zhao's enclosure, with a gate, halls and stele pavilion rebuilt in 1988 and an excavated underground chamber, is the best preserved and reopened in December 2021 with a new exhibition hall, while archaeologists have been clearing the foundations of other enclosures since 2015. The site was among the first group of Hubei provincial heritage parks named in 2021 and was approved in December 2022 as a national archaeological site park project.

rows.name: Uprising Gate
rows.summary: Formerly called Zhonghe Gate, this is the only one of Wuchang's nine city gates left after the walls were pulled down following the 1926 Northern Expedition siege. The Wuchang Uprising of October 1911 began among soldiers stationed near the gate. The tower was rebuilt in 1981, and the surrounding park was redone for the 1911 centenary with a stele gallery, a covered corridor and a pavilion.

rows.name: Wuhan Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A research botanical garden of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, founded in 1956, whose Moshan campus of about 59 hectares lies on the shore of East Lake. It has 17 specialty gardens, among them a kiwifruit collection and what the garden describes as East Asia's largest aquatic plant garden. It suits plant lovers and families after a half-day walk by the lake.

rows.name: Wuhan Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A public park of about 214 hectares built on a former landfill for the 10th China International Garden Expo in 2015 and kept as a city park afterwards, with its northern part in Dongxihu District and its southern part in Qiaokou District. The Expo laid it out with themed gardens from Chinese cities, and a 2020-23 survey recorded 73 bird species there, up from 26 before the restoration. It suits a half-day stroll or a family outing, and holds a large lantern fair each Chinese New Year.

rows.name: Wuhan Iron and Steel (WISCO) Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.summary: A tourism zone of about 6.1 square kilometres inside the working Wuhan Iron and Steel (WISCO) plant in Qingshan, which opened in February 2023. Its core is Blast Furnace 1, first tapped in September 1958 and retired in October 2019, now an industrial-heritage park with a history exhibition on the ground floor, a recreated casting floor above and a viewing platform, with the plant's rail lines beside it still in use. The furnace was listed as national industrial heritage in 2021, and the zone was named a national industrial-tourism demonstration site in 2023.

rows.name: Wuhan Museum
rows.summary: The city's main local-history museum, in Hankou's Jianghan District; the present building opened in 2001 and the museum was named a first-grade national museum in 2008. Its permanent galleries cover Wuhan's ancient history, including models of the Shang-dynasty city of Panlongcheng, and its modern history from 1848 to 1949, alongside collections of bronzes, jades, ceramics and Ming and Qing paintings and calligraphy. Its prize piece is a Yuan-dynasty blue-and-white plum vase.

rows.name: Wuhan Peasant Movement Institute
rows.name_zh: 武汉农民运动讲习所旧址
rows.summary: A late-Qing courtyard school of four brick-and-timber halls, opened in 1904 as a primary school, which housed the Kuomintang's Central Peasant Movement Training Institute in 1927, with Deng Yanda as director and Mao Zedong as deputy director. About 800 students from 17 provinces trained here between March and June that year. The halls now hold restored offices, classrooms and dormitories, plus exhibitions on the institute and the peasant movement.

rows.name: Wuhan Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: Wuhan Planning Exhibition Hall occupies the east wing of the Citizens' Home civic complex in northern Jiang'an and explains the city's history, growth and development plans over three floors. It has scale models, maps and multimedia displays, with sections on the city's history, the two-river four-bank waterfront, transport and the master plan, and since March 2023 a geology gallery with a relief model of Wuhan. It is an easy, indoor stop for anyone curious about how modern Wuhan is laid out.

rows.name: Wuhan Polar Ocean Resort
rows.summary: An ocean-themed resort in Dongxihu District with aquarium displays, a polar-themed Ice Kingdom that uses animal models, and staged shows such as costumed mermaid performances and a penguin parade. Since July 2025 it has also had a 91 m Ferris wheel and a circus theatre with an ocean-themed big-top show. The complex includes a hotel, restaurants and a spa, and suits families with children looking for a day out.

rows.name: Wuhan Sports Center
rows.summary: A sports complex in Zhuankou, in Wuhan's economic development zone, built in 2002 around a 54,000-seat stadium that staged matches at the 2007 FIFA Women's World Cup and has been home to Wuhan Three Towns football club. It also has an arena, a swimming hall and landscaped plazas that make up the park rated as a 4A scenic area. In 2020 it served as one of the city's temporary Fangcang hospitals for mild COVID-19 cases.

rows.name: Wuhan Wildlife Kingdom
rows.summary: An animal-themed park on Wumei Mountain in Caidian, on a hill that was quarried until around 2000 and has since been replanted; it opened in December 2020.
