Animals include giraffes, zebras, camels and tigers, with animal parades by day and, since July 2026, evening sessions with shows and guided night visits. It is a commercial park aimed mainly at families with children.

rows.name: Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge
rows.summary: The first permanent bridge across the Yangtze, opened in October 1957, links Snake Hill in Wuchang with Turtle Hill in Hanyang; it carries a road on its upper deck, with pedestrian walkways on both sides, and a railway line below. It became a national heritage unit in 2013 and is still in daily use, so the walk across gives views up and down the river. The Wuchang bridgehead tower, closed for years, reopened on a trial basis on 2 October 2026 as the pedestrian stairway up to the deck.

rows.name: Wuying Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey, eight-sided stone pagoda dated to 1270, in the last years of the Southern Song, and built to imitate a timber pagoda; it is often described as the oldest surviving structure in Wuhan. Carved figures of Buddhas, bodhisattvas, arhats and guardians decorate its base and body. After it began to tilt badly it was moved in 1963 from the site of the lost Xingfu Temple to its present spot at the foot of Hongshan, and its name ('Shadowless') comes from a legend that it casts no shadow at noon on the summer solstice.

rows.name: Xinhai Revolution Museum (Wuchang Uprising Memorial)
rows.summary: The Xinhai Revolution Museum is made up of two sites a short walk apart on the south side of Snake Hill, both about the Wuchang Uprising of October 1911. The north district is the Red Building, a 1910 assembly hall where revolutionaries and soldiers declared the Hubei military government on 11 October 1911, with its council chamber and offices restored; Sun Yat-sen spoke there in April 1912. The south district, built for the 1911 centenary, has a historical exhibition on the revolution, and Shouyi Square, with a 1931 bronze of Sun Yat-sen, lies between the two.

rows.name: Yaojiashan Red Village
rows.summary: A mountain village on the Huangpi-Dawu border that served as the base of the New Fourth Army's Fifth Division, whose political and military organs were stationed there from the early 1940s until 1946 under Li Xiannian. Several preserved buildings, including the assembly hall in a clan shrine and former residences, form what the district describes as the only well-preserved group of revolutionary-era buildings in Wuhan, and a museum on the division opened in 2015. The valley also has stream-tracing and camping in summer.

rows.name: Yecun Valley
rows.summary: A family leisure valley in Wangjiahe, Huangpi, with rafting runs, a shallow stream with a stepped weir, and a paddling water park with water-bamboo beds and slides. The grounds also have an earth-art play area, rose beds, go-karts and camping, and an avenue of ginkgo trees that colours in autumn. It is a commercial park aimed at families with young children.

rows.name: Yifu Museum of China University of Geosciences
rows.name_zh: 中国地质大学逸夫博物馆
rows.summary: A natural-science museum on the China University of Geosciences campus beside East Lake, holding about 40,000 geological specimens, several thousand of them rare. Six permanent halls cover the planet and Earth, the origin and evolution of life, minerals and rocks, gems and jade, mineral resources and a donated collection, with dinosaur skeletons among the fossils. The building was completed in 2003 and its design draws on geology, biomimicry and astronomy.

rows.name: Zhiyin Cultural Area (Guqin Terrace and Moon Lake)
rows.summary: The Zhiyin Cultural Area is Wuhan's name for a group of sights in Hanyang built around the legend of Yu Boya and Zhong Ziqi, in which a guqin player found a friend who truly understood his music (a 'zhiyin'). State media describe it as one hill, one lake, one garden and one pavilion: Turtle Hill, Moon Lake, the Guqin Terrace garden and Qingchuan Pavilion. The Guqin Terrace, on the south shore of Moon Lake, is the core: a small garden of halls and courtyards around a white-marble platform said to be where Boya played, first built in the Northern Song and rebuilt in the Jiaqing era of the Qing.

rows.name: Zhongshan Warship Museum
rows.summary: Zhongshan Warship Museum, in the Yangtze-side town of Jinkou, is built around the restored Zhongshan, a gunboat built in Japan in 1913 and renamed in 1925 after Sun Yat-sen. The ship was sunk by Japanese forces in 1938, raised from the river in 1997 and restored, and the museum has shown it with relics from the wreck since 2011. The grounds also hold military vehicles and aircraft in the open air.

rows.name: Ziwei Urban Pastoral Park
rows.summary: A countryside leisure park on Ziwei Ridge in Cangbu, Xinzhou District, opened in 2014 on former scrub slopes and known for plant weaving: sculptures and lettering made from living plants. In March 2024 it opened a wetland cherry garden of islands, bridges and boat rides, and it holds seasonal flower and folk festivals. It is a modern leisure attraction rather than a historic site, and it suits a half-day family outing from Wuhan.

rows.name: Baishui Temple, Zaoyang
rows.summary: A hilltop temple complex at Wudian, south of Zaoyang, commemorating Liu Xiu (Emperor Guangwu), founder of the Eastern Han dynasty, whose ancestral home is placed in this district. The scenic area gathers some twenty sights around Lion Hill and the Gun River, including the temple buildings, a stele gallery, old wells and a memorial pavilion at the source of the Baishui stream. It suits visitors interested in Han-dynasty history who are already in Zaoyang.

rows.name: China Han City, Zaoyang
rows.summary: A Han-dynasty-style capital built in modern times on the eastern side of Zaoyang to honour Liu Xiu (Emperor Guangwu) and present Han culture; it is a themed attraction and film location, not a historic site. Visitors walk among its palace buildings and food and market streets, watch staged shows such as the imperial guard's city-opening welcome, and try craft demonstrations including traditional papermaking, movable-type printing and paper-cutting. It suits families and anyone wanting an easy introduction to Han culture, and in summer it also runs an evening programme.

rows.name: Chuhuangcheng City Ruins
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of a large walled city from the Eastern Zhou to Han periods, covering about 2.2 km² beside Zhengji town, with a smaller inner town in the north-east. Scholars disagree on which Chu city it was, with Yan, Ruo and the capital Ying all proposed. The walls were recorded at 2–4 m high, so expect earthen banks among farmland rather than reconstructed buildings.

rows.name: Cihe Cheng'en Temple
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty Buddhist temple in a valley on the north side of Wuduo Mountain in Cihe town, south-eastern Gucheng. It was founded in the Sui dynasty, enlarged in 1421 under the Yongle Emperor with the Shaolin monk Juecheng in charge, and renamed Cheng'en in 1457. The surviving buildings include the Heavenly Kings Hall and a square main hall, just over 21 m on each side, with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof.

rows.name: Daxie Mountain
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: A forested mountain in south-western Gucheng, run as a national forest park and holiday area, whose main peak, Daughter Peak, reaches about 1,099 m. Forest cover is above 90 per cent and summers average about 22 °C, so it is promoted as a summer retreat. Its best-known feature is a group of more than fifty villas built between 1903 and 1910 by missionaries from eight countries, among them the building where a county soviet government was set up under He Long's Red Army in 1931.

rows.name: Fenghuangzui Site, Xiangyang
rows.summary: A Neolithic walled settlement at Longwang town, north-west of Xiangyang, dated by the provincial culture and tourism department to roughly 5,200 to 3,900 years ago and described as the largest and highest-ranking central settlement found so far in the Nanyang–Xiangyang Basin. Excavations since 2016 have found a wall, a moat, round houses, ash pits and pottery of the Qujialing culture, and in 2019 one excavated round house could be seen under a protective shed beside display boards. An archaeological site park with a museum is being built around it, and the provincial department put the museum's main structure at about 80 per cent complete at the end of 2025.

rows.name: Green Screen Wall, Xiangyang Prince's Palace
rows.summary: The only part of the Ming prince of Xiang's palace in Xiangyang to survive its burning in 1641 is this stone screen wall, about 25 m long and up to 6.6 m high, carved with dragons among clouds and waves and named for its dark green colour. It stands in the old walled city beside the rebuilt Xiang prince's palace, which opened with displays in 2024. A short stop that fits easily with a walk on the city wall.

rows.name: Guangde Temple, Xiangyang
rows.summary: A working Buddhist temple on the western edge of Xiangyang, founded in the Tang dynasty as Yunju Temple and renamed Guangde in the Ming. Its main draw is the Ming-dynasty Duobao ('Many Treasures') Pagoda behind the main hall, begun in 1494: a brick-and-stone base about 7 m high carrying a 10 m Tibetan-style stupa, ringed by smaller pagodas, with 48 stone Buddha figures set in niches. The other surviving buildings were rebuilt in the Qing.

rows.name: Hengchong Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A high-mountain forest area on the main ridge of the Jing Mountains in Houping town, at about 1,700 m on average and rising to just under 1,950 m, so it stays cool in summer. The county lists forest paths, a blueberry-picking garden, log-cabin lodgings and, in winter, a ski field. It lies in the same township as Wudaoxia Gorge, so the two fit into one trip.

rows.name: Huangjiawan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A leisure area of about 9.8 km² on the western outskirts of Xiangyang's Xiangcheng district, which local tradition names as the birthplace of Huang Yueying, the wife of Zhuge Liang. The district government lists fishing, picnic and barbecue spots and active attractions such as grass-sliding and zip-lines. It suits families wanting an outdoor day out in the same western tourism belt as Longzhong rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Jiulu Zhai, Baokang
rows.summary: A karst mountain area in Xiema town, in the south of Baokang County, at about 1,200 m on average. The county lists limestone peaks such as Chuwang Peak, Candle Peak and Elephant Trunk Peak, Huanglong Cave, a glass suspension bridge and a cableway across the gorge.

rows.name: Li Zengbo Victory Inscription
rows.summary: A Southern Song cliff inscription carved in 1254 on a rock face at the east foot of Zhenwu Hill, beside the entrance to the Xianshan greenway south-west of Xiangyang's old city. Its 79-character text, set in a framed panel about 5 m high and 4.5 m wide, records how the Song commander Li Zengbo retook the twin cities of Xiangyang and Fancheng in 1251; the three large title characters have worn away. It is a short stop for anyone interested in Song history or calligraphy, and the traditional site of Liu Bei's horse leaping the Tan stream lies close by.

rows.name: Liuzhuya Mountain Resort, Baokang
rows.summary: A high-mountain leisure area at up to about 1,500 m, built on reclaimed phosphate-mining land in Huanglongguan village, Maqiao town, and rated 4A in 2024. About 90 hillside B&Bs include 72 timber cabins named after the disciples of Confucius and cliff-edge guesthouses, and there are camping, a stream-trekking route in the Suxi canyon and a ski slope in winter. It is mainly a summer retreat for a night or two away from the lowland heat.

rows.name: Longzhong
rows.summary: Longzhong is the wooded hillside west of Xiangyang that tradition names as the place where the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang lived quietly before Liu Bei called on him three times, the origin of the saying about visiting the thatched cottage three times. The grounds mix Ming and Qing buildings with newer additions, and the sights include the Wuhou Temple, the Sangu Hall, a thatched-hut pavilion and the Liujiao well. Nanyang in Henan makes a rival claim to be where Zhuge Liang farmed, so the link is tradition rather than settled fact.

rows.name: Lumen Mountain, Xiangyang
rows.summary: A wooded hill south-east of Xiangyang, once called Suling Mountain, whose present name comes from a shrine said to have been founded in the Eastern Han with a pair of stone deer beside its path. It is known as a retreat for scholars and poets: Pang Degong, who is credited with the nicknames 'Sleeping Dragon' for Zhuge Liang and 'Young Phoenix' for Pang Tong, the Tang poet Meng Haoran, and the late-Tang writer Pi Rixiu. Sights include the entrance archway, the Meng Garden memorial hall to Meng Haoran (opened 2003), a hall commemorating Zhuge Liang's study with Pang Degong, and a slope of weathered rocks.

rows.name: Migong Temple
rows.summary: A shrine on the north bank of the Han River in Fancheng, first built in the Yuan dynasty, enlarged in the Ming and rebuilt in the Qing, and dedicated to the Northern Song calligrapher Mi Fu, who took the sobriquet 'Idle Scholar of Xiangyang'. The four-courtyard compound covers about 16,000 m² and includes a worship hall dating from 1693, the Baojin Hall of 1866, and a collection of stone tablets with 58 steles and 45 carved copies of Mi Fu's calligraphy. It suits calligraphy lovers and anyone strolling the Fancheng riverfront.

rows.name: Nanzhang Mountain Strongholds
rows.summary: Nanzhang County has more than a thousand old stone mountain strongholds, and six built by local communities as refuges in the Ming and Qing dynasties make up the national listing. Chunqiu Stronghold in Donggong town is the one developed as a tourist area: a wall about 1.15 km long encloses more than 150 stone-built rooms on a hill ringed on three sides by the Maoping River. It suits anyone interested in vernacular defensive architecture in a mountain setting.

rows.name: OCT Fantasy Resort, Xiangyang
rows.name_zh: 襄阳华侨城奇幻度假区
rows.summary: A large leisure resort developed by OCT in Xiangyang's Dongjin New Area, opened in stages from 2020. It combines the Fantasy Valley space-exploration theme park, the Dream Beach water park, a children's park, a hot-spring bathing area, a leisure town and several themed hotels. It suits families and groups after an amusement-park day and is a modern entertainment development, not a historic site.

rows.name: Shiziyan Reservoir Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lakeside scenic area in Jinniusi village, Cihe town, built around Shiziyan Reservoir (completed in 1976 on the Mo River, a tributary of the Han) and named for a hill said to resemble a lion. It covers about 6.5 km² and offers a lakeside greenway, a beach, a glass water slide, forest cabins and an off-road vehicle base. It also stages fantasy-themed (xianxia) character shows and night events, so it suits a half-day or overnight outing from Xiangyang.

rows.name: Tang City, Xiangyang
rows.time_needed: Half a day, or an evening
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty-style film set and tourist complex at the foot of Xianshou Hill beside the Han River, built in the 2010s and now marketed as Shengshi Tangcheng ('Prosperous Tang City'); none of it is historic. Its gate towers, palace halls, mansions, temples and market streets follow a Chang'an layout, with canals said to echo the 'eight rivers around Chang'an', and more than a hundred film and television productions have shot here. A walk-through night show, 'Dream of the Great Tang', is the main evening draw, and the operator has been refurbishing the site since 2025.

rows.name: Wudaoxia Gorge
rows.summary: A forested stream gorge inside the Wudaoxia nature reserve, close to the main peak of the Jing Mountains, with a path of about 5 km beside the stream, waterfalls and old trees including a golden-thread nanmu. Its five gorge sections are named after the legend of Bian He, the Chu man said to have found a raw jade here and offered it to the king, and a lit karst cave retells the story. The area closed in 2023 and reopened on 1 October 2025 after a seven-month upgrade that added a new entrance with a lift, a lakeside walk and a family play area; rafting began in June 2026.

rows.name: Xiangfan Wharves, Xiangyang
rows.summary: The surviving river landings on both banks of the Han River at Xiangyang's old city and across the river at Fancheng, 26 of which make up this national heritage unit; they recall the city's old role as a crossing of boat and road routes, summed up as 'southern boats, northern horses', and belong to the Wanli Tea Road World Heritage nomination. Many are now buried or built over, but on the old-city bank the gate towers of the Xiaobeimen, Guanting and Tiezhuang landings still stand by the river below the city wall. The easiest way to see them is on a walk along the north wall, combined with a visit to the old city.

rows.name: Xiangshui River Gorge
rows.summary: A forested river gorge at Putuo'an village in Xueping town, in the south-west of Nanzhang County, known for its chain of waterfalls, with more than fifty named sights including the Seven-Colour Falls and the Three-Tier Falls. A cable car and footpaths run through the gorge, and the cool upland air makes it a summer destination.

rows.name: Xiangyang Ancient City
rows.summary: The walled old city of Xiangyang on the south bank of the Han River, whose mostly Ming-dynasty walls, 7.3 km round, are a national monument and are ringed by a moat up to 250 m wide, the basis of the saying 'iron Xiangyang'. Inside are the Zhaoming Tower, the old city's central landmark, and North Street, lined with tea houses, craft shops and snack stalls, while on the river side the gate towers of the old Xiaobeimen and Guanting wharves still stand. A 2025 city plan covers renovation of the Zhaoming Tower and North Street area, so some buildings may be under works.

rows.name: Yanhe Village
rows.summary: A tea-growing village in Wushan town, Gucheng, developed into a rural-tourism area; the county tourism bureau reports about 1,200 mu (80 ha) of tea gardens and more than fifty family-run farm restaurants and guesthouses in the village. Visitors come for the tea slopes, village lanes and countryside meals rather than any historic sight. It suits a relaxed stop in the Gucheng countryside.

rows.name: Yaozhihe Resort, Baokang
rows.summary: A mountain village in Maqiao town, near the Fang County and Shennongjia borders, that has turned from phosphate mining to tourism. Visitors find waterfalls, a mining museum and an agricultural-culture museum, farmhouse B&Bs, and part of a belt of old mine tunnels about 20 km long that has been opened as the Sanjie Dongtian cave attraction. The village name is tied to a local legend that the ancient ruler Yao stayed here, and the cool upland air makes it a summer destination.

rows.name: Chutian Yaochi Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the bank of the Gan River in Xianning's urban area, at the site of the Feitan ('boiling pool') archway, which local sources call the marker of the 'first spring of central China'. More than 40 pools in ten types are set into the hillside, alongside a constant-temperature swimming pool, herbal baths, spa treatments and a children's pool. It is an easy add-on to a day in Xianning.

rows.name: Hot Spring Valley Resort, Xianning
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort beside the main gate of Qianshan National Forest Park on the edge of Xianning. The bathing area is split into six zones, including indoor halls, a Chu-style area, Japanese-style and South-East Asian-style areas, and Thai-style bath houses, with a water-play area and more than 80 bathing and spa attractions in all. A resort hotel and a tea house on site make it suitable for an overnight stay as well as a day visit.

rows.name: Jiugong Mountains
rows.summary: A forested mountain resort in the Mufu range on the Hubei–Jiangxi border, with a main summit of about 1,650 m and summer temperatures that local authorities put at around 21°C. The scenic area is known for Yunzhong Lake, a high-altitude lake at about 1,230 m, waterfalls and a Song-dynasty Daoist heritage, and it has a ski slope in winter and a wind farm on the ridges. It is a summer escape for visitors from Wuhan, and the tomb of Li Zicheng lies at the western foot.

rows.name: Lingmi Town and Baiya Mountain, Chongyang
rows.summary: A rural resort built and run by a private tourism company at Fanshang village in Jintang town, Chongyang County, in the hills around Baiya Mountain. County media describe timber-cabin lodgings, more than 10,000 peach trees, a rose garden and fruit-growing, with peach blossom in March and April and pick-your-own fruit later in the year. It suits a countryside weekend rather than a particular sight.

rows.name: Longyin Mountain Resort
rows.summary: A mountain leisure park built around 2020 beside Yinshui Cave in Dafan town, on a hill about 519 m above sea level overlooking Fushui Lake. It combines adventure attractions such as a glass bridge, cliff swing, jungle crossing and glass slide with viewpoints, including a stone-forest area, a high meadow and Jiulongding Plaza overlooking the islands of the lake. It suits families and thrill-seekers and pairs easily with the cave next door.

rows.name: Longyou Chibi Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort complex at the foot of Wuhong Mountain beside Lushui Lake, built in Han-Tang style around a hotel, a lakeside spring centre and villas. The city describes more than 40 pools scattered through the wooded hillside, and a 2023 refit added an infinity pool and a children's water park, with a hot-spring bath in every room. It is mainly for soaking and staying rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Lushui Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir of about 57 sq km on the Lu River near Chibi, created in 1958 as a test dam for the Three Gorges and Gezhouba projects, with more than 800 islands among wooded hills and national scenic area status since 2002. Visitors tour the islands by boat, and the park has a dinosaur-themed island with a mine-train ride, an animal petting park, a water-play area and outdoor-activity grounds. It makes an easy half-day trip that combines with the Red Cliff site.

rows.name: Red Cliff Ancient Battlefield, Chibi
rows.summary: A scenic area on the south bank of the Yangtze in Chibi, built around a cliff carved with the two large characters for 'Red Cliff', which tradition credits to the general Zhou Yu after the Battle of Red Cliffs in AD 208, though who wrote them and when is debated. The grounds hold a statue of Zhou Yu, a shrine to Zhuge Liang on the Wind-Worship Platform, the Fengchu Hermitage for Pang Tong (built in 1846), a stele gallery, a battle museum and a large area of newly built Han-style buildings. Scholars disagree about where the battle was fought, with sites near Wuhan and in Jiayu also proposed, so it works best as a Three Kingdoms memorial.

rows.name: Sanjiang Forest Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the eastern foot of Qianshan National Forest Park, beside the Gan River on the edge of Xianning city. More than 70 open-air pools and bath houses are set into the wooded hillside among osmanthus trees and bamboo, and local sources describe the water as a weakly radioactive sulphate-radon spring. It is a place to soak for an afternoon rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Shanhu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the north shore of Bai Lake in the Sanhu–Lianjiang lake area of Jiayu County, opened in 2009 with a four-star hotel, a boat pier and a bathing centre. The county describes about 50 pools in seven themed zones, with water at 47–60°C of an alkaline sulphate-calcium type, plus a salt-flotation hall and spa treatments. It suits an overnight stay beside the lake.

rows.name: Taiyi Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Taiyi village, Fushan, on the southern edge of Xianning city, beside Taiyi Cave, a karst cave, and a lake of more than 200 mu. The original resort opened in 2009 and was rebuilt in 2025–26 as the family-oriented Taiyi Tianmu Hot Spring Resort, which began reopening in February 2026. It now has wooded-hillside pools, a summer water park and a hotel, and the cave stays at about 18°C.

rows.name: Tianye Countryside Park, Guanqiao
rows.summary: A rural leisure park built around Group 8 of Guanqiao village in Jiayu County, with two lakes, a provincial forest park of about 1,800 mu and a 3.3 km lakeside greenway. Other features are a tea house on the highest point, glass greenhouses where visitors pick fruit, a farm museum recording the village's development since the 1978 reforms, and two squares with statues of Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. It is a family day out that shows a modern model village rather than a historic one.

rows.name: Tingsiqiao Battle Site (Northern Expedition)
rows.summary: The site of the battle of Tingsiqiao on 26–27 August 1926, when the National Revolutionary Army's Fourth Army took the town from forces of the warlord Wu Peifu during the Northern Expedition. It has three parts: a martyrs' cemetery laid out in 1929 with tombs, a monument and a pavilion; the low hills of Tanao Mountain, where trenches, bunkers and gun emplacements survive; and a memorial museum in the town that opened in 2009. It suits visitors interested in modern Chinese history, and the museum is officially designated a national patriotic-education base.

rows.name: Tomb of Li Zicheng
rows.summary: A memorial park on the western side of the Jiugong Mountains with a Qing-period tomb mound that has been identified since the 1950s as the grave of Li Zicheng, the rebel leader who set up the short-lived Shun regime and is said to have died near here in 1645. The park has a stone memorial archway, an offering platform, the tomb, an exhibition hall and a slope marking his last battle. Whether he died here is disputed, and graves are also claimed in Tongcheng and in Shimen, Hunan.

rows.name: Wang Mingfan Mansion
rows.summary: A late-Qing family compound in Wutian village, Dalu township, built for Wang Mingfan, who was granted a court title in 1901 that gives the gate plaque its name, 'Dafudi'. An ancestral hall with a wooden opera stage forms the central axis, flanked by symmetrical blocks of houses five courtyards deep, with a school, gardens and craft workshops, all under grey tiles with stone-paved courtyards. Local media describe it as one of the largest surviving Qing-period houses in Hubei, and an old-style pedestrian street has been built beside it.

rows.name: Xiangyang Lake Cultural Figures' Former Sites
rows.summary: A group of former buildings by Xiangyang Lake where, from September 1969, the Ministry of Culture ran a 'May Seventh' cadre school; more than 6,000 staff and writers passed through, among them Bing Xin, Shen Congwen, Feng Xuefeng and Zang Kejia. The protected area has 144 houses of brick-and-tile and mud-brick, a brickworks and three bridges, spread over several sub-sites including the school headquarters, a hospital and Shen Congwen's former dwelling. The plain rural buildings record a 20th-century chapter of Chinese literary life, and interest depends on knowing the writers.

rows.name: Yaogu Mountain and Guyao Village, Tongcheng
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Daping township, Tongcheng County, on Yaogu Mountain (also called Longjiao Mountain, summit about 1,260 m), known for nearly 10,000 mu of wild cherry blossom in March and April, waterfalls and a long reputation as a source of medicinal herbs. At the foot, Guyao village is presented as a base for Yao culture, with a small exhibition hall, a temple to a General Li, a Yao-style street and farm-stay guesthouses. A trail runs from the visitor centre past Yao heritage sites and the Old Dragon Pool to the Sanxian Temple.

rows.name: Yellow Crane Tower Forest Liquor Town
rows.summary: A visitor area inside the working Yellow Crane Tower baijiu distillery in Xianning's high-tech zone, set among wooded hills and a lake. Visitors can see a liquor museum, a field of large ceramic ageing jars and cellars dug into hillside caves. It is a factory tour for anyone curious about baijiu, and it also receives school study groups.

rows.name: Yinshui Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave about 5 km long in Dafan town, Tongshan County, billed as Hubei's first geological park, with an underground stream, stalactite forests and chambers averaging about 30 m high. Visitors can tour it by boat on the underground river, by small train and on foot. The cave stays at about 18–20°C all year, which makes it a popular summer visit.

rows.name: Mengli Shuixiang Water-Town Park, Xiantao
rows.summary: A countryside tourism area beside the Zhaoxiyuan forest farm in Xiantao, laid out as a Jianghan water-village scene with a lotus-pond village (Hetang), wetland paths, painted boats and farm scenes such as ox carts. People's Daily described it in 2023 as a well-known draw, and it appears on Hubei's 2023 spring flower route for Xiantao and Jingmen. It suits a relaxed half day in the countryside, best in the flower season.

rows.name: Mianyang Town, Xiantao
rows.summary: A newly built old-style town on the shore of Pai Lake in Xiantao, with Jingchu-style houses laid out beside the water. Craft workshops let visitors watch or try straw-stalk painting, paper-cutting, shell carving and shadow puppetry. It is a modern recreation rather than a historic town, and suits an easy half-day outing.

rows.name: Baizhao Mountain (Li Bai Cultural Area), Anlu
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Yandian town, Anlu, linked to the Tang poet Li Bai, who local tradition says lived in the Baizhao Mountain area for about ten years and married a local woman. Sights include a Li Bai memorial hall and Peach Blossom Cave, where he is said to have lived as a recluse. Anlu promotes the area as the centre of its Li Bai heritage tourism.

rows.name: Beishan Red Leaf Area, Dawu
rows.summary: An autumn-colour area around Beishan village in Sigu town, in the hills of south-eastern Dawu County, known for stands of Chinese tallow trees whose leaves turn red from late October into November. Dawu promotes the red-leaf season each autumn with a festival that brings markets and evening events to the village. The colour is seasonal, so time a visit for the second half of autumn.

rows.name: Guanyin Lake, Xiaochang
rows.summary: A lake-and-hills leisure district in the north of Xiaochang County, organised around Guanyin Lake, a reservoir, with the nearby hill called Dawu Mountain, which has Buddhist heritage. It is administered as a resort district in its own right, and what it offers is lakeside scenery, countryside walks and spring blossom. It suits a relaxed day out from Xiaogan.

rows.name: Jinhui Manor, Xiaonan
rows.summary: A flower-viewing and picking estate in Pengxing township, just north of Xiaogan city, best known for its spring tulips. It is a seasonal family outing rather than a full-day destination.

rows.name: New Fourth Army Fifth Division Headquarters and Memorial Hall, Baiguoshuwan
rows.name_zh: 新四军五师司令部旧址
rows.summary: The village of Baiguoshuwan was the headquarters of the New Fourth Army's Fifth Division from 1942 to 1945, when the Communist-led force operated behind Japanese lines in central China. The headquarters, political department and staff offices were spread across village houses of grey brick and black tile, which now stand beside a memorial hall with historic photographs, wartime objects and accounts of the division's commanders and base areas. Xinhua describes the village as the command centre for the war in the border area of Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Hunan and Jiangxi.

rows.name: Qianchong Ancient Ginkgo Area, Anlu
rows.summary: A village area in Wangyizhen town, Anlu, noted for its old ginkgo trees, whose leaves turn gold in autumn. Anlu promotes it as one of its three core 4A scenic areas, alongside Baizhao Mountain and the Shengshi Wenying cherry park, and features its golden ginkgo colour on its autumn route. It is a seasonal stop, so time a visit for the ginkgo colour.

rows.name: Shengshi Wenying Cherry Blossom Park, Anlu
rows.summary: A flower park in the countryside of Lidian town, Anlu, best known for its cherry blossom in spring. People's Daily named it among Hubei's cherry-blossom viewing spots in 2023, and Anlu lists it as one of its three core 4A scenic areas. It is a seasonal stop for photography and family outings, so check the bloom before travelling.

rows.name: Shibatan (Eighteen Pools) Gorge, Dawu
rows.summary: A mountain gorge in Sanli town, in the north of Dawu County, with a string of green pools and small waterfalls along a mountain stream. It is also visited in autumn for its red leaves, and a tourist road named after it, the Shibatan Tourist Road, runs up to the area from Dawu. It suits a half-day nature walk, especially in spring and autumn.

rows.name: Shuangfeng Mountain, Xiaochang
rows.summary: A hill resort and national forest park in Xiaochang County, in the foothills of the Dabie Mountains, centred on its twin-summit main peak, Shuangru Peak, which at 888 m is billed as the highest peak in Xiaogan. Forest covers about 89 per cent of the park, and the sights include an old hill stockade (Baiyun), Shuangfeng Academy, Huilong Temple, a spring and a car-camping site. Local tradition ties the area to the Dong Yong and Seventh Fairy legend, and it suits a day of easy walking from Xiaogan.

rows.name: Tangchi Hot Spring, Yingcheng
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort area in Tangchi town, in the west of Yingcheng, a town that takes its name from its springs. The water stays above 72°C all year, and Yingcheng holds the title of 'hometown of hot springs', with hotels and spa resorts built around the springs. It suits an overnight soak or a relaxed weekend stay.

rows.name: Tianyu Lake, Hanchuan
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area on Tianyu Lake beside Makou town in Hanchuan. It has been developed as a leisure district with lakeside walks, bridges, small islands with pavilions, boat trips and a hotel. It suits a light family outing from Hanchuan.

rows.name: Tianzi Lake Eco-Resort, Xiaonan
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure resort on Tianzi Lake in Xiaogang town, north of Xiaogan city, with a hotel, hot-spring pools and water-play areas. The resort promotes the local legend that the Seventh Fairy came down to earth here to meet Dong Yong, the folk tale behind Xiaogan's 'filial piety' name. It is aimed at short family and group stays and day visits from Xiaogan.

rows.name: Xiangyunwan, Yunmeng
rows.summary: A recently built cultural-tourism complex in Yunmeng County in traditional Chinese architectural styles, arranged as Yunmeng Old Street (a dry street and a water street) plus a series of gardens. It is a newly built attraction rather than an original historic district, and suits a half-day outing from Xiaogan.

rows.name: Yingcheng National Mine Park
rows.summary: A former gypsum and rock-salt mining area in Yingcheng, a city known for gypsum, brine and hot springs, now landscaped as a national mine park. It holds the China Gypsum Museum and industrial-heritage displays on the area's geology and mining history, alongside leisure and hot-spring facilities, according to a 2026 state-media report. It suits visitors interested in industrial history who are already in the Yingcheng area.

rows.name: Zhongyuan Military Region Site, Xuanhuadian
rows.summary: A group of historic buildings in the small town of Xuanhuadian where the Communist Party's Central Plains Bureau and the Central Plains Military Region were headquartered from January to June 1946. The protected buildings include the headquarters, an assembly hall, the commanders' residence and the site of talks that Zhou Enlai held with US and Nationalist representatives that year. The Central Plains Breakout, in which the force left the encircled area, began from this district on 26 June 1946, and a renovated memorial hall in the town covers it with multimedia displays.

rows.name: Baibaozhai Rock Dwellings, Dangyang
rows.summary: A group of nearly 200 Qing-dynasty dwellings cut into the cliffs on both banks of the Ju River in Yuquan subdistrict. The caves are built in two storeys linked by passages, with remains of living quarters, defensive features and religious traces inside. They sit within the Baibaozhai riverside scenic area, known locally for its clear water and green hills and used for camping, where a ferry stop at the old rock houses is planned.

rows.name: Bailihuang Alpine Grassland
rows.summary: A highland meadow area of about 40 km² on the ridges of Fenxiang township in northern Yiling district, at an average altitude of about 1,200 m, with open pasture, pine woods, gorges and a row of wind turbines. It is cooler than Yichang city in summer, and activities include horse riding, glass water slides and paragliding. Local promotion presents it as a place for spring flowers, summer coolness, autumn colour and winter snow.

rows.name: Chaibuxi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A band-shaped karst canyon of about 60 km² in the Wuling Mountains in Wufeng county, with rock pillars, sheer cliffs and forested peaks above a stream, often compared with Zhangjiajie, which lies in the same range. The scenic area is split into four zones, Tanzikou, Dawankou, Jiaokou and Duanshankou, plus a protected inner area, with more than 120 named sights and Tujia villages in the valley. It became a national forest park in 1995.

rows.name: Changyang Man Site
rows.summary: A limestone cave known as Longdong, or dragon cave, at Zhongjiawan village, where a fossil upper jaw and teeth of an early modern human were found in 1956. The find, named Changyang Man, is dated to about 195,000 years ago and is among the earliest human remains found south of the Yangtze, though the original fossils were sent to a research institute in Beijing. The cave has an inscribed marker at its entrance, and the surrounding village has been redeveloped around the site.

rows.name: Chaotianhou Rafting, Gaolan
rows.summary: A rafting site on the Gaolan River in Xingshan county, where the main run is 6.5 km long with a 148 m drop through a wooded valley. A newer cave route runs through a lit tunnel and a waterfall cave, and night runs are also offered. The rafting season opens in late April.

rows.name: Chexi Folk Culture Area, Yichang
rows.summary: A folk-culture park in Chexi, a Tujia village in Tucheng township, built around museums and demonstrations of traditional country life. Attractions include a water-wheel museum, a farm-life and Tujia museum, a cluster of old workshops where paper, oil, pottery and liquor are made, and a folk village, along a route of about 10 km. The local government also lists caves, a gorge and a large wild wintersweet grove among its ten sub-areas.

rows.name: Former 066 Missile Base (Third Front), Yuan'an
rows.name_zh: 三线航天066导弹基地旧址
rows.summary: A former inland defence-industry base of the Third Front programme, begun in 1969 in the hills of Yuan'an, where ground-to-ground tactical missiles were developed. It was listed as a national protected site in 2019 and as a national industrial heritage site in 2024, covering the old office district and the Hongfeng factory area. A visitor route now runs through the base's history museum, the former office, communications and archive buildings, a hall of missile models and a bronze statue of Wang Zhenhua, one of the base's leading figures.

rows.name: Guanling (Guan Yu's Tomb), Dangyang
rows.summary: The tomb and temple complex where, by local tradition, the body of the Three Kingdoms general Guan Yu was buried, while his head is traditionally said to lie at Luoyang. It is laid out on a central axis through five courtyards and four halls, from a stone archway to a round earth mound about seven metres high under old trees, and is counted as one of three major Guan Yu temples in China. Its temple fair is on China's national intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Huangling Temple
rows.summary: A temple complex on the south bank of the Yangtze just below the Three Gorges Dam, dedicated to Yu the Great, the legendary tamer of the floods. Its main building, the five-bay Yu Wang Hall with a double-eaved roof, was rebuilt in 1618 and has carved timberwork and painted ceilings, and marks on its nanmu columns record the Yangtze floods of 1860 and 1870. The compound, about 2 hectares on a hillside, also has an opera stage and a shrine to Zhuge Liang.

rows.name: Jiufenggu (Nine Phoenix Valley)
rows.summary: A stream valley about 3 km long in the hills of Wuyanquan town at roughly 800 m altitude, where faulting has cut a narrow U-shaped gorge with cliffs, stalactites, deep pools and waterfalls up to about 20 m high. Visitors walk and wade up the stream, with a zip-line and other adventure activities, and the valley is planted with flowers such as crape myrtle, cherry and azalea. It is mainly a summer cool-off spot, developed as a leisure destination by a private company.

rows.name: Jiuwanxi Scenic Area, Zigui
rows.summary: Jiuwanxi is a tributary of the Yangtze in Zigui whose mouth faces the Cow Liver and Horse Lung Gorge on the Three Gorges reservoir. Its lower reach has been developed as a rafting and gorge-scenery route, and the cliffs hold rock-coffin burials from the Zhou to Han periods. The name recalls a line in Qu Yuan's poem Li Sao about growing orchids, and local legend ties the poet to the stream.

rows.name: Li Laiheng's Anti-Qing Fortress Sites
rows.summary: Remains of the mountain strongholds of Li Laiheng, a commander of the former Shun rebel army who kept resisting the Qing in these hills until 1664. The best-known section, near Baicheng village in Huangliang town, has short stretches of three stone wall lines still standing 3-6 m high, with stone mortars, house foundations and a stone arch bridge. Dozens of other stockade and cave-fort sites are scattered over the hills of Xingshan, so this is a site for history enthusiasts rather than a developed attraction.

rows.name: Mingfeng Mountain, Yuan'an
rows.summary: A red-sandstone hill 408 metres high, circled by water on three sides, with a Taoist temple complex that local tradition dates to the Liang dynasty and links to the Wudang Mountains. The local government lists more than 50 sights, including caves such as Yanxia Cave, a lake, a gorge and the golden-roofed hall at the summit. It is a provincial-level scenic area, and pilgrims come to pray for children and good fortune.

rows.name: Nanbian Old Houses
rows.summary: Two Qing-dynasty courtyard compounds, Laohao and Baohe, about 200 m apart on a mountainside in a small valley village in Huanghua town, listed as a national heritage site in 2019. The family house was first built in 1801 and the surviving buildings date from the Xianfeng reign (1851–61), with finely carved stone, wood and brick showing flowers, animals and folk tales. In 1941 a Nationalist army division set up its headquarters in the village after the fall of Yichang.

rows.name: Nanjinguan Grand Canyon
rows.summary: An 8 km forested canyon on the Xiling Gorge side of Yiling district, with a height difference of about 400 m between its ends, developed for hiking, stream-tracing and canyoning (rope descents down the stream), alongside zip-line and cliff-climbing activities. A boardwalk path of about 6.8 km runs through the woods, and the Xialao stream area is popular with Yichang residents for paddling in hot weather. The canyon was rated 4A in December 2025.

rows.name: Qingjiang Fangshan Scenic Area, Changyang
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of about 60 square kilometres in the core of the Qingjiang National Forest Park, with karst peaks, ravines, streams and waterfalls above Zhengjiabang village. Visitors follow forest paths and a cliff-side plank walkway of just over 6 kilometres, passing old trees and some of the 30 or so caves recorded in the area. Scenery is the main draw, so it suits hikers and photographers.

rows.name: Qingjiang Gallery
rows.summary: A boat-trip scenic area on the Qingjiang River above the Geheyan Dam in Changyang county, where the reservoir winds between steep wooded cliffs and hundreds of small islands. Boats run about 25 km upstream from the Qingjiang Gallery wharf to Wuluozhongli Mountain, which Chinese tradition names as the birthplace of the Ba people, ancestors of today's Tujia. Daoying Gorge ("Reflection Gorge") is another main stop, and the area is also known for local Tujia song and dance.

rows.name: Qingjiang Tianlongwan Resort
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure resort on the Qingjiang River reservoir in Yidu, with a hotel, a sand beach, water sports such as speedboats and pedal boats, and an outdoor team-building ground. Sightseeing boats run from here along the Qingjiang, and the resort is marketed as a short-trip destination from Yichang. It suits families and groups looking for a relaxed waterside break rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qinglin Leisure Tourism Area, Yidu
rows.summary: A leisure area of about 8.5 square kilometres on the Qing River below the Geheyan Dam, spread between Honghuatao and Gaobazhou towns and named after a former temple, Qinglin Temple. It is built around Qinglinsi village, which is known as China's riddle village, and also has a riddle-themed town, an 18-hole golf course, citrus orchards and the shore of the Gaobazhou reservoir. It suits families and anyone wanting an easy countryside day out from Yichang.

rows.name: Qu Yuan's Hometown, Zigui
rows.summary: Qu Yuan's Hometown is a tourist area on Phoenix Hill beside the Yangtze at Maoping, built around the Fenghuangshan Ancient Buildings, a national heritage group of Qing-dynasty buildings moved here because their original sites in Zigui were to be flooded by the Gezhouba and Three Gorges reservoirs. The 24 buildings, four bridges, two city gates, an archway and a well include ancestral halls, river-god temples, a multi-storey pavilion and the Qu Yuan Temple, which honours the poet Qu Yuan, a native of Zigui. The hill lies less than 2 km from the Three Gorges Dam in a straight line and gives views of it; the area is the second part of the joint 5A Three Gorges Dam and Qu Yuan's Hometown tourist area.

rows.name: Shipai Fortress
rows.summary: The site of the Shipai fortress, a Yangtze position between the Three Gorges and Gezhouba dams that Chinese naval gunners fortified in 1938 and that was defended in May 1943 against a Japanese offensive aimed at Chongqing. The scenic area combines a war memorial museum built on the former military ground, a memorial monument and military-themed rafting on Yangjia stream. It overlaps with the Three Gorges Tribe scenic area, which lists the same museum and rafting among its sights.

rows.name: Three Gorges Ancient Stockades
rows.summary: A heritage park in Huanghua town built around the hilltop stone stockades (bingzhai) of northern Yiling, more than 100 of which survive in the town according to local officials. The best preserved, Majia, Lijia and Baima, keep walls, beacon and watch towers, barracks and troop passages, and a small museum that opened in November 2024 explains how local historians date the stockades from the Spring and Autumn period to the Second World War. The Yangjiahe stockade group inside the park is a provincial-level protected site.

rows.name: Three Gorges Citrus Vinegar Estate
rows.summary: A company-run visitor estate of about 1.85 km² in Yidu's citrus-growing country, with orchards, lakes and wetland around a citrus-vinegar brewing estate that opened to visitors in March 2023. Visitors see the brewing and storage halls, a citrus culture centre with exhibits on the history and varieties of citrus, a vinegar-themed walkway and a gallery of dried tangerine peel, and can pick fruit in the harvest season. It is a modern food-and-farm attraction rather than a historic site, suited to families and food-minded travellers.

rows.name: Three Gorges Longyin Valley, Yuan'an
rows.summary: A valley scenic area in Hualinsi town in the Taiping mountains, with waterfalls, a covered bridge, a small lake and riverside platforms in its valley section. The Yichang government also lists the Taiqing Cave, a limestone cave open to visitors, and a children's study-tour base with field classes, outdoor-skills activities and an outdoor combat-game field. It suits families and school groups for a day out.

rows.name: Three Gorges Orange Valley and Zhaxi River Area, Zigui
rows.name_zh: 三峡橙谷·环吒溪河景区
rows.summary: A rural scenic area in Shuitianba township, in the north-west of Zigui county, strung along the Zhaxi River through hillsides of navel-orange orchards; the township has about 4,700 hectares of them. Visitors can paraglide over the orchards, ride a sightseeing mini-train through the orange groves, or take dragon-boat rides on the river, and there is a riverside walkway. It was rated 4A by Hubei's tourism department at the end of 2024.

rows.name: Three Gorges Tribe
rows.summary: A scenic area of about 14 km² around Dengying Gorge, the stretch of Xiling Gorge between the Gezhouba and Three Gorges dams, built around the way of life of Yangtze boatmen and Tujia villagers. Highlights include stilt-house settings beside Longjin Stream, a boat trip round the Mingyue Bend where the river turns about 110 degrees, and Dengying Cave, a cave about 1,500 m long with an underground stream. Folk songs, boatmen's chants and dance shows are staged for visitors, so it is best seen as a cultural-tourism development rather than an old village.

rows.name: Three Gorges Waterfall
rows.summary: A waterfall 102 m high and 80 m wide in a limestone canyon in northern Yiling district, the main one of more than 30 falls along the valley stream. A path lets visitors walk through the curtain of falling water, so expect to get wet; a via ferrata route along the cliff and a cliff-side café have been added in recent summers. The scenic area, rated 5A in July 2022, also includes Golden Lion Cave and the cave spring known as Lovers' Spring.

rows.name: Three Travellers' Cave
rows.summary: A limestone cave in a cliff above the Yangtze at the mouth of Xiling Gorge, named for two literary meetings: the poets Bai Juyi, his brother Bai Xingjian and Yuan Zhen explored it in 819, and Su Xun and his sons Su Shi and Su Zhe followed in 1056. The cave is about 30 m deep, and more than 40 inscriptions and steles survive inside and outside it, among them a Ming-dynasty recut of Bai Juyi's preface. Paths lead up to a hilltop pavilion with a view along the river and down to Lu You Spring, a small pool where the Song poet Lu You drew water to make tea in 1169.

rows.name: Tianran Pagoda
rows.summary: An eight-sided, seven-storey brick-and-stone pagoda 43 m high on the north bank of the Yangtze in Binjiang Park, with guardian figures carved around its base. Tradition says the first pagoda here was built in the Jin dynasty; the present one was rebuilt in 1790–92 with donations from local gentry. A spiral stair of 145 stone steps runs inside, and the pagoda stands beside the Yichang Yangtze River Bridge carrying the Yichang–Wanzhou railway.

rows.name: Wudieshui Grand Canyon (Three Gorges Bamboo Sea), Zigui
rows.summary: A forested stream valley on the south bank of the Yangtze at Sixi, Maoping, known for bamboo groves, caves and waterfalls, and also promoted as the Three Gorges Bamboo Sea. It has a core area of about 9 square kilometres with more than 300 kinds of bamboo, around ten caves and a tiered waterfall; a cave, a bamboo-raft pool and a waterfall are among the open sights. The canyon reopened on 16 July 2026 after upgrades that include a moving walkway up the slope, a waterfall-side platform, a zip-line and a staged folk-wedding show.

rows.name: Wuling Gorge Mouth, Yuan'an
rows.summary: A karst gorge and spa area of about 10 square kilometres in Yangping town, with a five-kilometre gorge path, some thirty viewpoints and four linked caves called Moon, Poplar, Soldiers-and-Horses and Sinkhole. Along the gorge are Qing-dynasty stone inscriptions, a stone tower, a stone stockade and temples, and the resort also has a hot-spring bathing area, rooms and a restaurant. It suits visitors who want a gorge walk and a soak in one day.

rows.name: Xiannü Jiji Theme Park, Zhijiang
rows.summary: A village-based leisure park in Xiangxiang village, Xiannü town, presented as a citrus-themed park and rated 4A in December 2023. Its orange-and-white buildings are styled on Greek island villages, and an orange-cat mascot called Jiji appears across the park. It is aimed at families, with orchard-picking, camping, an animal park opened in July 2026 where visitors feed alpacas, deer and other gentle animals, and a water-play area with citrus-themed slides and evening water games.

rows.name: Xiling Gorge Mouth Scenic Area, Yichang
rows.summary: A scenic area around the eastern mouth of Xiling Gorge, where the Yangtze leaves the Three Gorges on the north-west edge of Yichang. The Yichang government's tourism page lists eight sub-areas, among them Leizu Temple, Baima Cave, Peach Village, a leisure park and the Xialaoxi stream, which is used for rafting and swimming. It is a short trip from the city for gorge and river scenery.

rows.name: Yang Shoujing Academy and Wetland
rows.summary: A modern academy complex, built from 2005, in honour of Yang Shoujing (1839–1915), the Yidu-born historical geographer who completed the 80-volume Shuijing zhu shu, a commentary on the ancient waterways classic. Lecture halls, a library and a shrine stand beside the Gaobazhou reservoir near where the Yangtze, Qingjiang and Yuyang rivers meet, with a wetland education area and a water-sports zone. It is a recreated cultural park; Yang's actual former home and tomb are separate sites in Yidu town.

rows.name: Yangjiawan Old House
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty brick-and-timber mansion in Sandouping, begun in 1787 and enlarged in the Daoguang years (1820–50), two courtyards deep and eleven rooms wide, with seven patios. Its carved doorways and painted decoration show local craftsmanship, and in 1939–45 it served as a river-defence headquarters for the Chinese army. It is the only protected building left in its original place within the Three Gorges Dam works area.

rows.name: Yichang Museum
rows.summary: Yichang's main museum, a large modern building that opened in September 2019 in Wujiagang District next to the city's planning exhibition hall, and rated a first-grade national museum in December 2020. Its galleries, about ten in all, cover local history, natural history, folk customs and traditional architecture, drawn from a collection of some 58,000 items.

rows.name: Yuquan Temple, Dangyang
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the eastern slope of Yuquan Hill, said to have been founded in the 6th century and given its present name in the Sui dynasty; it is counted as an ancestral seat of the Tiantai school and as one of the national key temples of Han Buddhism. Highlights are a cast-iron pagoda from the Song dynasty, a large Sui-period iron cauldron, a Tang-dynasty ginkgo tree over 1,300 years old and a stone carving of Guanyin attributed to the painter Wu Daozi. The temple was rebuilt between 2003 and 2008, and the surrounding forest park also has Three Kingdoms sites linked to Guan Yu.

rows.name: Zhaojun Village
rows.summary: The traditional birthplace of Wang Zhaojun, the Han-dynasty court lady sent to marry a Xiongnu ruler, set beside the Xiangxi River in Xingshan county. The grounds, about 2.7 km², hold a memorial hall with Han and Tang objects excavated locally, a study academy, and landmarks named for her legend such as the Dressing Platform, a zither-playing terrace and Niangniang Spring. The writer Guo Moruo inscribed the names of the hall and the village.

rows.name: Zhuoer Muqiaoxi Eco-tourism Resort, Changyang
rows.name_zh: 卓尔木桥溪生态旅游度假区
rows.summary: A private resort planned over about 15 square kilometres in Muqiaoxi village, developed from 2017 by the Zhuoer group in a river valley of cliffs, waterfalls and forest. It combines scenery with outdoor activities, caravan and tent camping, a Tujia village zone and hotels. It was rated 4A in January 2022 and suits families and outdoor-activity groups.

rows.name: Dakou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the low hills of Zhongxiang, set up as a provincial park in 1992 and raised to national status in 1995. Visitors walk through broad-leaved and mixed woodland and its stream and temple spots. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Yan'er Valley
rows.summary: A privately run eco-agriculture and sightseeing area in the hills of Luotian County, Dabie Mountains. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020; public detail on its attractions is thin.

rows.name: Changde Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: The city's urban planning museum, run by the Changde natural resources and planning bureau and open since 2013, presents Changde's history, culture and planned growth in a series of themed sections. Alongside the displays it runs activities such as child volunteer guides, a photo hunt for 'city memories' and quizzes on local history. It gives a quick indoor overview of the city.

rows.name: Changde Wildlife World
rows.summary: A large zoo and safari-style park of about 2,500 mu (170 ha) in Hanshou County, opened in 2022, which now keeps more than 7,000 animals of over 200 species, among them Asian elephants, Siberian tigers, African lions and pumas. Besides the enclosures there are staged animal shows in a forest theatre and a circus theatre, a small sightseeing train, a petting area and a children's amusement park added in 2024. It is aimed at families on a day out from Changde or Changsha.

rows.name: Chengtoushan Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: Chengtoushan, on the Liyang plain north-west of Li County town, is a round Neolithic town about 325 m across inside a rammed-earth wall and moat that were first built in the Daxi culture more than 6,000 years ago and enlarged several times before the town was abandoned around 4,000 years ago. Excavations from 1991 uncovered house platforms, pottery kilns, cemeteries, an altar, very early fired bricks and rice paddies that are among the oldest known anywhere. Since 2016 the site has been a national archaeological site park, with the walls and moat laid out for visitors and a site museum for the finds.

rows.name: Duo'an Bridge
rows.summary: An eleven-arch stone bridge 211 m long across the Dan River outside the east gate of old Lizhou, first built in 1786 and rebuilt after flood damage in 1820–1821. Its boat-shaped piers stand on timber-pile foundations, and the deck has stone balustrades, a pavilion at mid-span, a stone archway at each end and more than 20 inscribed steles. A restoration begun in late 2023 was finished in December 2024, when the bridge reopened.

rows.name: Fenglin Flower Sea, Taoyuan
rows.summary: A flower-field park of about 2,000 mu (130 ha) in Weihui New Village, in the Fengshu Uyghur and Hui Ethnic Township, with large seasonal flower fields and a vineyard. The township is home to the largest Uyghur community outside Xinjiang, and the area also takes in the former residence of the historian Jian Bozan, the tomb of the early-Ming general Hala Bashi and a mosque more than 600 years old.

rows.name: Former Residence of Lin Boqu
rows.summary: The birthplace of Lin Boqu (1886–1960), a member of the Tongmenghui and of the Chinese Communist Party from 1921, who chaired the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region government, was secretary-general of the Central People's Government and later vice-chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, and is counted among the 'Five Elders' of Yan'an. The house, built in the Tongzhi reign of the late Qing and repaired in 1985, is a southern-style courtyard house of three successive courtyards on a hillside, with about 857 m² of floor space; it opened as a memorial in 1986 under a name board written by Deng Xiaoping. A life exhibition hall completed in 2019 shows documents, photographs and more than 1,200 objects, and the grounds also take in a bronze-statue square, the Lin family graves and a memorial archway; his ashes were brought back to Xiumei in 2013.

rows.name: Huawa Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song brick pagoda in Huawa village in the far north of Li County, octagonal and solid, rising seven storeys and about 22 m from a base about 5.5 m across. Its walls copy brackets and other timber details in brick, and an arched passage on the north side leads to an underground chamber with an eight-sided caisson ceiling. Excavation around the base in 2010 found the foundations of the temple that once stood with it.

rows.name: Huayanxi National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park designated in 1997 at the northern foot of the Jiulong Mountains, an offshoot of the Xuefeng range, where Dingcheng, Taoyuan and Anhua meet, covering about 75 km² of wooded hills and streams. Forest covers about 95 per cent of the land, with Chinese yew, dawn redwood and other rare trees, and large numbers of egrets breed here.

rows.name: Iron Sutra Pillar, Changde
rows.summary: A hollow cast-iron Buddhist sutra pillar of the Northern Song, about 4.3 m tall and weighing some 1.5 tonnes, which stood beside Qianming Temple at Deshan until it was moved to Binhu Park in central Changde in 1979. Its 17 sections, fitted together with tenons, are cast with Buddha figures, guardian strongmen, dragons, tigers and lotus patterns, sutra text and the names and posts of the officials and donors who paid for it. The city's heritage office describes it as the only Song-dynasty iron sutra pillar known in China.

rows.name: Jiashan Temple
rows.summary: A Chan Buddhist monastery in Jiashan National Forest Park, founded in 870 by the monk Shanhui and known from the Song to the Qing as Lingquan Chan Monastery; the Song master Yuanwu Keqin is said to have taught here the koan commentaries collected as the Blue Cliff Record, and the temple is promoted as a cradle of 'tea and Chan' culture. Most of its halls were pulled down after 1949 and rebuilt from 1992 to an 18th-century description, leaving the Qing-repaired old main hall, now the Guanyin Hall, as the chief survivor. On the western slope a mausoleum stands over the grave of the monk Fengtianyu, whom a 1993 conference in Shimen identified as the peasant rebel leader Li Zicheng, a claim that remains disputed and is also made for a tomb at Tongshan in Hubei.

rows.name: Kale Planet Theme Park, Changde
rows.summary: A theme park on Peach Blossom Island in Liuye Lake, opened in January 2020 and built by the culture-tourism technology arm of the OCT (Overseas Chinese Town) group together with Changde's city investment company. Its five themed zones hold more than 20 large indoor and outdoor rides and shows around a fairy-tale castle, and it stages seasonal events such as New Year fireworks and a summer festival. It suits families with children and teenagers.

rows.name: Lingxi Camellia Oil Estate, Jinshi
rows.summary: A camellia-oil estate on the shore of Maoli Lake in Jinshi, run by a local camellia-oil producer, that has been developed into a leisure and wellness area; provincial media describe it as Hunan's first eco-wellness estate built around camellia oil. Visitors can see the camellia plantations and the oil-pressing works as well as lakeside wetland scenery, art and leisure spaces and exhibits on ecology.

rows.name: Liuye Lake Tourist Resort
rows.summary: Liuye Lake, a lake of about 17.6 km² on the north-eastern edge of Changde, is the centre of a tourist resort set up in 1993, rated 4A in 2010 and named a national-level tourist resort in 2020. Its shores have parks and waterfront paths, a Ferris wheel, a statue of the Tang poet Liu Yuxi and lakeside hotels, while Peach Blossom Island in the lake holds a water park and the Kale Planet theme park, which has its own card. The resort combines sightseeing, water recreation and lakeside dining a short trip from the city centre.

rows.name: Lizhou Ancient City Wall
rows.summary: The surviving south-eastern stretch, about 1.9 km long, of the wall of Lizhou, the prefectural city that became Li County town; it was raised in rammed earth in 1372, when the seat moved here, faced with brick in 1404 and repaired many times under the Ming and Qing. The wall stands on dressed bluestone footings, and on the section between the Little South Gate and the East Gate rises the octagonal timber Lipu Tower, also called the Bafang Tower, rebuilt in 1804. Below it lies the octagonal Cangyan pond with the Yuxian Bridge and its pavilion.

rows.name: Lizhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The temple of the former Lizhou prefectural school, founded in 965, moved to this site in the early Ming and rebuilt in 1841–1844, covering about 8,000 m². On its north–south axis are the front gate, the Pan pool with the Zhuangyuan Bridge, the Lingxing Gate, the Dacheng Gate, the Dacheng Hall and the Chongsheng Shrine, flanked by bell and drum towers, stele corridors and shrines to local worthies and loyal officials. In 1925 He Long, then garrison commander of Lizhou, ran a political training school here, and the temple now houses the Li County Museum.

rows.name: Longwang Cave, Shimen
rows.summary: A limestone cave in Baiyun town, Shimen County, beside the waters of the Xianyang Lake national wetland park, opened to visitors in 1988 as the county's first tourist site. Its halls of stalactites, stalagmites and columns are lit with coloured sound-and-light effects, installed in a 2015–2016 upgrade and themed on local dragon legends, and a walkway leads through. It is a different cave from the better-known Longwang Cave at Jiangya in Cili County.

rows.name: Nanchanwan Jin Tombs (Tomb of Liu Hong)
rows.summary: A group of Warring States settlement remains, Jin-to-Tang kilns and tombs in Huangshantou Forest Park, best known for the tomb of Liu Hong, the Western Jin general and governor of Jingzhou, excavated in 1991. His square brick chamber, about 3.8 m across under a domed vault 4.2 m high, yielded 78 objects including tortoise-knob gold seals, a gold belt buckle with dragons and a carved jade cup, and a small museum has been built in front of the tomb. In 2025 it was named one of Hunan's first village museums.

rows.name: Pengshan Scenic Area, Li County
rows.summary: A forested hill area in Linan town, across the Li River from Li County town, rated 4A and listed as a national forest-wellness pilot base. It is laid out for nature and geology study trails, folk-custom activities, a revolutionary-history study section and a Chan meditation and wellness area, and in 2021 it was named a provincial study-tour base. It is set up mainly for school study trips and local day visitors.

rows.name: Shimen Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county Confucian temple of Shimen, founded in 1052 and moved in 1504 to this site near the north bank of the Li River, with most of its present buildings from Qing rebuilding. Three ranges and two courtyards survive on the axis, with the Pan pool and Zhuangyuan Bridge, the Lingxing Gate, the Dacheng Gate and the double-eaved Dacheng Hall of 1779, flanked by stele corridors, bell and drum towers and side halls. In the 1920s and 1930s it housed the county peasant association, a Soviet county government and the headquarters of the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups.

rows.name: Taohuayuan (Peach Blossom Land)
rows.summary: Taohuayuan, facing the Yuan River about 15 km south-west of Taoyuan county town, is the place long identified with Tao Yuanming's fable The Peach Blossom Spring, and temples and Daoist halls have stood here since the Tang. Most of the present shrines, pavilions and bridges, among them the Yuanming Shrine, the Taohua Daoist temple, the Fangzhu Pavilion and the Yuxian Bridge, come from late-Qing rebuilding and restorations of 1979–1988, and together they form a national heritage unit. The 15.8 km² scenic area, rated 5A in 2020, is divided into Taohua Hill, Taoyuan Hill, Qinren Village and Taoxian Ridge, with peach groves along the valleys.

rows.name: Xingzi Palace
rows.summary: A Daoist temple complex on the summit of Xingzi Mountain in Reshi town, founded in 1370 by the Daoist Zhang Daohui as the Sanyuan Palace, renamed after the mountain and enlarged in the late Ming and early Qing and again in 1784, 1807 and 1829. Along its axis stand the Baizi Hall, the Wangye Hall, the South Gate of Heaven, the main Xingzi Palace hall, a sleeping hall and a kitchen hall, all built of stone, carved and roofed with cast-iron tiles.

rows.name: Yu Family Memorial Arch
rows.summary: A white-marble chastity arch about 15 m high and 8 m wide in Pailou village, completed in 1842 by the official Yu Yuechan in honour of his mother, née Luo, who was widowed at 24. The three-tier arch, splayed on plan, carries the words 'by imperial decree' and the provincial governor's request for the honour, and is covered in openwork and relief carving of figures, birds, auspicious animals and flowers.

rows.name: Changsha Ecological Zoo
rows.summary: Changsha's main zoo, opened in 2010 when the old city zoo in Martyrs' Park moved to this 100-hectare site at Muyun in the southern suburbs. It shows more than 300 species in walk-through areas and a drive-through zone, with sections for education, landscaped grounds and leisure, and suits families.

rows.name: Changsha Landscape and Ecology Garden
rows.summary: A landscaped garden park beside the Laodao River at Luohanzhuang village in Kaifu District, on the northern outskirts of Changsha, with about 68 hectares open in its first phase out of a planned 200. It is known for its native Chinese cherry trees, more than ten early-flowering varieties of which the first bloom in February, and lies at the centre of the district's rural leisure area around Shaping and Baixia. It suits a walk or a family outing rather than a special trip.

rows.name: Changsha Riverside Culture Park
rows.summary: A cultural complex on the Beichen Delta where the Liuyang River joins the Xiang, fully opened in 2015 on the site of a former chemical works, grouping the Changsha Museum, the city planning exhibition hall, the Changsha Library, a concert hall and a viewing tower. The Changsha Museum's two permanent galleries cover the city's ancient and modern history, with Shang and Zhou bronzes and Changsha-kiln ceramics as its strengths, and the riverside park makes an easy half-day stop.

rows.name: Changsha Underwater World
rows.summary: An aquarium and marine theme park opened in 2000 in north-eastern Changsha, beside Window of the World, with a 76-metre walk-through tunnel and freshwater and marine galleries. A polar hall keeps belugas, dolphins, walruses, seals and penguins, the park has staged animal shows in a theatre of about 1,800 seats, and there are a water park with slides and a wave pool and a children's playground; it suits families with children.

rows.name: Cheng Qian's Mansion
rows.summary: The two-storey house at Baiguoyuan in central Changsha where Cheng Qian, the Nationalist governor of Hunan, lived in 1949, and where talks with Communist representatives are said to have prepared the province's peaceful handover in August that year. Restored in 2011, it opened in 2015 as a museum of the peaceful handover of Hunan, with the history of the 1949 uprising downstairs and Cheng Qian's life upstairs.

rows.name: Dawei Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 47 km² on the Hunan–Jiangxi border in north-eastern Liuyang, rising to 1,607.8 m at Qixing Ridge, the highest point in the Changsha area, and the source of the Liuyang River. Trails lead through forest past more than 100 waterfalls and landforms attributed to Quaternary glaciers, azaleas cover Wuzishi Peak (1,515 m) in summer, and the mountain also has old temples such as Yuquan Temple and sites of the 1930s Red Army base.

rows.name: Former Residence of He Shuheng
rows.summary: The farmhouse in Shatian township, western Ningxiang, where the Communist revolutionary He Shuheng (1876–1935), who ran the Party's early Hunan committee with Mao Zedong, was born and lived for 26 years; Mao stayed here for three nights in 1917. Built in 1785, it is a single-storey house of 23 rooms behind an earth-brick wall, and its rooms show his glasses, pocket watch and clothes with photographs and copies of his books.

rows.name: Former Residence of Hu Yaobang
rows.summary: Hu Yaobang (1915–1989), who headed the Communist Party as chairman and then general secretary from 1981 to 1987, was born in this Qing brick-and-timber farmhouse of 19 rooms beside the Minxi River in Cangfang village, Zhonghe town, and left it at the age of 15. Restored and opened in 1995, the house is the centre of a 4A scenic area that also has a memorial exhibition hall of 2006 on his life, an ancestral hall, the family graves and a square.

rows.name: Former Residence of Huang Xing
rows.summary: Huang Xing (1874–1916), the revolutionary leader often named with Sun Yat-sen as a founder of the Republic of China, was born in this Qing farmhouse of the 1860s at Liangtang in Huangxing town, south-east of Changsha, and lived here until 1896. Twelve of its original 32 rooms survive, furnished as family rooms and with an exhibition on his life, and a memorial hall to Hunan's figures of the 1911 Revolution opened in the back garden in 2015. His tomb, also part of this national listing, is on Yuelu Mountain.

rows.name: Former Residence of Liu Shaoqi (Huaminglou)
rows.summary: The birthplace of Liu Shaoqi (1898–1969), president of the People's Republic from 1959 until he was purged in the Cultural Revolution, at Huaminglou in south-eastern Ningxiang. The family farmhouse, a brick-and-timber courtyard house of 1871 with about 20 rooms, was restored to its 1961 appearance and reopened in 1980 after Liu's posthumous rehabilitation, and the scenic area around it adds a memorial hall, a bronze statue square and exhibition halls. Mao Zedong's birthplace at Shaoshan is about 20 km away, so the two are often visited together.

rows.name: Former Residence of Tan Sitong
rows.summary: The family home in central Liuyang of Tan Sitong (1865–1898), the reformer and thinker who was executed at 33 with five others when the Hundred Days' Reform failed in 1898. It is a timber-framed courtyard house of 24 rooms behind fire walls, in the Jiangnan style, and since 2013 the national listing has also covered his tomb and memorial shrine elsewhere in Liuyang.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xie Juezai
rows.summary: The birthplace of Xie Juezai (1884–1971), the Communist politician and educator who was president of the Supreme People's Court from 1959 to 1965, in Shatian township, western Ningxiang. The brick-and-timber house of 1850 within a walled yard was a meeting place for local revolutionaries such as He Shuheng, and its rooms show period furniture, an inkstone and his early poems, manuscripts and diaries.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xu Teli
rows.summary: The birthplace of Xu Teli (1877–1968), the educator who taught Mao Zedong, Cai Hesen and Tian Han and later sat on the Communist Party's Central Committee, in Teli village, Jiangbei town, south-east of Changsha. The late-Qing farmhouse, built by his grandfather in the Tongzhi reign (1862–1874), was restored by the county and opened to visitors in 2005.

rows.name: Former Site of Hunan First Normal School
rows.name_zh: 湖南省立第一师范学校旧址
rows.pinyin: Húnán Shěnglì Dìyī Shīfàn Xuéxiào Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Mao Zedong studied at this teacher-training school from 1913 to 1918 and then worked here, and the old campus is now the Mao Zedong and First Normal School Memorial Museum, with his classroom, dormitory, study room and the school hall laid out as they were. The school traces its roots to Chengnan Academy, founded in 1161, and its 1912 buildings, mainly Western in style with courtyards and pavilion roofs and modelled on Tokyo's Aoyama Normal School, were rebuilt to the original design in 1966–68 after the 1938 fire.

rows.name: Former Site of the Xinmin Study Society
rows.summary: This small timber-framed house in Rongwan, below Yuelu Mountain, was the rented home of Cai Hesen's family, and on 14 April 1918 Mao Zedong, Cai Hesen, Xiao Zisheng and ten others founded the Xinmin (New People's) Study Society here, a student society that went on to play a part in the Chinese revolution. The house was destroyed during the war with Japan and rebuilt to its original form in 1984, with plaques inscribed by Deng Xiaoping and Chen Yun over the door.

rows.name: Founding Site of the Red First Front Army, Yonghe
rows.summary: On 23 August 1930 the Red Army's First Army Group under Mao Zedong and Zhu De and Third Army Group under Peng Dehuai and Teng Daiyuan met at the Li family house in Yonghe, northern Liuyang, and merged into the First Front Army, the force also known as the Central Red Army. The house, a Qing residence completed in the Jiaqing reign (1796–1820) in the style of eastern Hunan, is shown with guided tours, and a sculpture of the meeting stands outside.

rows.name: Guanshan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A rural tourism village in Jinzhou town, Ningxiang, built around a Three Kingdoms theme from the local story that Guan Yu camped his troops here during his campaign against Changsha. White-walled houses in Hui style stand beside two lakes, with Three Kingdoms–themed halls and squares, a folk museum, shadow-puppet shows, farm restaurants and guesthouses, and a Three Kingdoms lantern festival has been held here.

rows.name: Han Changsha Kingdom Royal Tombs
rows.summary: The kings and queens of the Western Han vassal kingdom of Changsha were buried in the hills along the west bank of the Xiang, in a belt of some 30 km² from Tianma Hill in the south to Fengpanling in Wangcheng in the north, where more than 20 tombs of kings and members of the royal family have been identified. Part of the cemetery has been laid out as the Han Changsha Kingdom Archaeological Site Park, which offers history talks, Han-style performances and seasonal events in its grounds, and Wangling Park, a city park in Yuelu District, encloses another group of the royal tombs.

rows.name: Heimi Peak National Forest Park
rows.summary: The highest hill in Wangcheng at 590.5 m, on the district's north-eastern border, protected as a national forest park of about 41 km² with forest covering over 80 per cent. Trails for walking and cycling pass a reservoir on the way to a Buddhist temple on the summit, and the mountain is linked by tradition to the Tang monk-calligrapher Huaisu and, through legends and rock carvings, to the Daoist immortal Lü Dongbin.

rows.name: Huayi Brothers Movie Town (Changsha)
rows.summary: A film-themed leisure town carrying the Huayi Brothers name, opened in 2018 in the Dawangshan resort area of south-western Changsha and built around a replica Italian town modelled on Assisi and Venice, with 35 buildings, five squares, a waterfront and 22 bridges, Italian restaurants and craft shops, and film-set experiences. A second area recreates Republican-era Changsha as it looked before the 1938 fire, and the town suits a few hours of strolling and photography.

rows.name: Hunan Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A 120-hectare botanical garden in Yuhua District, southern Changsha, founded in 1985 as the Hunan Forest Botanical Garden and renamed in 2021, which combines research and conservation with public gardens.
