Its ten or so specialist gardens include cherry, magnolia, azalea, camellia, osmanthus, bamboo and shade-plant collections, with rare trees such as Cathaya and the dove tree.

rows.name: Jinggang Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old river port on the west bank of the Xiang where the Wei River once flowed in, a rice market and salt depot busy enough to be called 'Little Hankou' until the river was diverted in 1957; it was here that Zeng Guofan, beaten by the Taiping in 1854, threw himself into the river and was pulled out by his men. Its streets of Ming, Qing and Republican-era houses, shops and guild halls, over 1,000 traditional buildings in all, were restored and opened as a scenic area in 2008, the year it was named a national historic and cultural town.

rows.name: Jinshoutang (Former Hunan Provincial Soviet Government)
rows.summary: Jinshoutang is a manor-like Qing complex of house and ancestral hall with more than 100 rooms, built from 1897 by a widow of the Tu family in memory of her husband, in Chudong village, Daweishan town, near the Jiangxi border. In 1931 the Hunan Provincial Soviet Government was based here for more than nine months, and red slogans of the time survive on its walls, with its mimeograph room in the attic of the north court.

rows.name: Lei Feng Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum in Wangcheng District to Lei Feng (1940–1962), the People's Liberation Army soldier who became the subject of a nationwide campaign from 1963 that held him up as a model of selfless service. Opened in 1968 and enlarged several times, it displays his diaries, books, clothes and work tools, a group of clay figures and inscriptions by national leaders, in grounds of about 11 hectares.

rows.name: Liuyang Confucius Temple
rows.summary: A palace-style Confucian temple modelled on the one at Qufu, moved to this site in 1818 and rebuilt in 1843, with its gates, bell and drum pavilions and Dacheng Hall complete. Tan Sitong and Tang Caichang started a mathematics society in its Kuiwen Pavilion in 1895, and from 1991 the temple housed the Liuyang Museum, which has since moved to a new building elsewhere in the city; its ceremonial music for Confucius has been a national intangible heritage item since 2014.

rows.name: Longping Rice Culture Park
rows.summary: A park in Furong District, eastern Changsha, centred on the Longping Rice Museum, which opened fully in 2019 with three main halls on the history of rice, rice science and Yuan Longping (1930–2021), the agronomist who developed the first hybrid rice varieties in the 1970s. Around the museum in Longping Central Park are a rice-culture square and rice terraces used for hands-on paddy-farming activities, in the district that houses China's national hybrid rice research centre.

rows.name: Mawangdui Han Tombs
rows.summary: The site in eastern Changsha where the tombs of Li Cang, chancellor of the Changsha Kingdom and Marquis of Dai, his wife Xin Zhui and a son were excavated in 1972–74, yielding Xin Zhui's remarkably preserved body, silk paintings, lacquerware and silk manuscripts that include early versions of the Laozi and the Book of Changes. All the finds are in the Hunan Museum's Mawangdui galleries, about 3.5 km to the west, while at the site itself, in the grounds of the Mawangdui campus of Hunan Provincial People's Hospital, the pit of Tomb 3 has been kept under a protective hall.

rows.name: Miyin Temple
rows.summary: A Chan Buddhist monastery on Mount Wei (Weishan) in western Ningxiang, founded in the early 9th century by the monk Lingyou, whose teaching gave rise to the Weiyang (also romanised Guiyang) school of Chan, and named Miyin by imperial grant in 849. It has burned and been rebuilt many times, most recently after a fire in 1918, and its halls, including the Hall of Ten Thousand Buddhas, stand within the Weishan national scenic area of forested hills, also known for Weishan Maojian tea. A giant statue of the thousand-armed Guanyin stands on the hillside in the same scenic area.

rows.name: Qianlong Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park around the former Getang Reservoir of 1956 in Jinggang town, Wangcheng, whose two lakes, Qianlong and Tuantou, lie among the farmland of the Dazhongyuan polder. A resort village opened in 2004 offers a hotel and conference centre, fishing, water sports and farm produce, and the lake hosts dragon-boat races, including a qualifier of Hunan's provincial dragon-boat league in 2026.

rows.name: Qingshuitang (Former Site of the CCP Xiang District Committee)
rows.summary: From late 1921 to April 1923 this small southern-style house at 22 Qingshuitang was the secret office of the Communist Party's Xiang (Hunan) District Committee, with Mao Zedong as secretary, and the home of Mao and Yang Kaihui, whose rooms are furnished as they were. It was the only building linked to the Party's early history in Changsha to survive the great fire of 1938, and it now stands in the grounds of the Changsha Party History Museum beside the ponds that gave Qingshuitang its name, with a statue of Mao put up in 1969.

rows.name: Sanzhen Tiger Park
rows.summary: A captive tiger breeding centre in Jinjing town, northern Changsha County, holding Siberian and Bengal tigers that visitors watch from boardwalks through the woods and from railed viewing points. There is a nursery area with young cubs and visitors can take part in feeding; it suits families with children rather than anyone looking for wildlife in the wild.

rows.name: Shiyan Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake ringed by wooded hills at Tiaoma in Yuhua District, where Changsha, Zhuzhou and Xiangtan meet, run as a 10 km² leisure scenic area. Its features include a glass skywalk across the lake and an island, a glass plank walk, a dragon-boat course and a large outdoor team-building base, and it suits families and groups on a day out from the city.

rows.name: Site of Joining Forces in Wenjiashi of Autumn Harvest Uprising
rows.name_zh: 秋收起义文家市会师旧址
rows.summary: Wenjiashi, a market town on the Jiangxi border, is where the units of the Autumn Harvest Uprising led by Mao Zedong regrouped on 19 September 1927, after their attacks on the cities had failed. They met at the Liren School, which occupies the Wenhua Academy of 1841, whose gate, halls, Dacheng Hall for Confucius and study rooms have been restored, and a memorial museum built beside it in 1977 displays documents, photographs and objects from the uprising.

rows.name: Tanheli Site
rows.summary: A Western Zhou walled town with palace foundations on a terrace where the Duanxi stream meets the Wei River in Huangcai, western Ningxiang, in an area that has yielded hundreds of Shang and Zhou bronzes, among them the Four-Goat Square Zun and the Da He square ding with a human face. The site is now a national archaeological park, and the Tanheli Bronze Museum, opened in 2016, displays finds from the site and the story of bronze-making south of the Yangtze. Beside it is Tanhe Ancient City, a Zhou-themed park built by the Songcheng group and opened in 2017.

rows.name: Taoshuwan Liu Family Mansion
rows.summary: A vast Qing country mansion in Jingang town, southern Liuyang, built in 1849–1853 by the landowner Liu Yunzhuang: four courtyards deep on three parallel axes, it has around 400 rooms within tamped-earth outer walls and covers some 21,000 m², with a stele recording its construction. After 1949 it was divided among village families, and following a full repair in 2014 an exhibition on local worthies opened inside in 2016.

rows.name: Tian Han Culture Park
rows.summary: A culture park in Guoyuan town, Changsha County, built around the birthplace of Tian Han (1898–1968), the playwright and poet who wrote the lyrics of 'March of the Volunteers', now China's national anthem. His earth-brick family house, restored on its original site, stands at the back of the park, with the Tian Han Art Centre and its exhibition, an old-style timber opera stage, a drama arts street and National Anthem Square, and the park holds flag-raising ceremonies and performances about Tian Han and the anthem.

rows.name: Tianxin Pavilion
rows.summary: The three-storey Tianxin Pavilion stands on the only surviving stretch of Changsha's city wall, a brick rampart of Ming origin some 250 m long and 13 m high that escaped the demolition of the walls in 1923–24. A pavilion has stood here since at least the 18th century; the present one, rebuilt in reinforced concrete in 1983–84 after the 1938 fire, has two side pavilions joined by corridors, and the surrounding Tianxin Park has a 1946 memorial pagoda to the dead of the war against Japan.

rows.name: Tomb of Zeng Guofan
rows.summary: The tomb of Zeng Guofan (1811–1872), the Qing statesman who raised the Xiang Army against the Taiping Rebellion, and his wife, on Fulong Hill in Pingtang, south-west Changsha, where he was reburied in 1873. The granite-faced mound with a three-metre stele, stone gate towers and pairs of stone horses, lions and officials was badly damaged in the Cultural Revolution and later looted, and was restored from 1998, the first phase finishing in 2002.

rows.name: Tongguan Kiln Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: The Changsha kilns, strung along the east bank of the Xiang River at Tongguan, made glazed stoneware from the Tang to the Five Dynasties and are seen as the birthplace of underglaze painted decoration, often with poems and proverbs, for markets as far away as Japan, Southeast Asia, West Asia and Africa. The national archaeological site park, opened in 2012, covers the kiln remains and potsherd heaps around Wazhaping, and its Changsha Tongguan Kiln Museum (opened 2018) shows more than 1,000 pieces beside a full-size replica of the Belitung or 'Black Stone', a 9th-century Arab ship wrecked with a cargo of Changsha ware. The Tongguan Kiln Guofeng Park theme resort lies just to the south.

rows.name: Tongguan Kiln Guofeng Park
rows.summary: A large theme park and resort opened in 2018 beside the Tongguan kiln site, with streets in Tang-dynasty style, eight small museums including one on Changsha ware, performance venues, guesthouses and three hotels. Its programme runs from day into evening with a stunt show about the Belitung ('Black Stone') shipwreck, a flying-theatre ride and folk-art performances, and at its southern end is Tongguan Old Street, a historic street of pottery workshops.

rows.name: Window of the World (Changsha)
rows.summary: A 40-hectare theme park opened in 1997 in north-eastern Changsha that combines scaled-down copies of famous buildings from around the world, such as Neuschwanstein Castle and the Pharos of Alexandria, with amusement rides and seasonal festivals. It suits families and groups with children.

rows.name: Xixi Panshi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A boulder-choked ravine on the south-eastern slopes of the Dawei Mountain range at Tianxi village, Zhangfang town, where a stream drops through pools and cascades between great rocks. Villagers developed it from 2015 with plank walks, trails, a glass bridge across the gorge and a grass slide, and the area now also has a children's play park, fruit picking and some 70 village guesthouses.

rows.name: Yang Kaihui Former Residence and Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The birthplace of Yang Kaihui (1901–1930), Mao Zedong's second wife and mother of three of his sons, who was arrested and executed in 1930, in Kaihui town, northern Changsha County. The site groups her family's earth-brick house of 1795 with 36 rooms, her tomb in a memorial garden with a marble statue and a stele of Mao's poem in her memory, the Yangsi temple school where she studied, and a memorial hall opened in 2010 on her life and those of her father Yang Changji and her sons.

rows.name: Yanghu Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park of about 480 hectares at the mouth of the Jin River on the west bank of the Xiang in southern Yuelu District, created on the old Yanghu flood polder from 2010 and opened in stages from 2011. Boardwalks and paths wind through ponds and reed beds with more than 700 plant species and some 130 bird species, with the Egret Pagoda as a landmark and outdoor sculptures from the park's international sculpture festivals.

rows.name: Yingzhu Mountain
rows.summary: A forested ridge of about 509 m in Fulin town, northern Changsha County, with more than 70 linked peaks and spurs, terraced fields, pools, bamboo groves and rock outcrops, and sunrise views over the clouds from the top. It was a battlefield of the Battles of Changsha in the war against Japan, and the Yingzhu Mountain War of Resistance Site Park has an exhibition hall, a former command post and trenches from a 1944 battle.

rows.name: Yuelu Academy
rows.summary: Founded in 976 under the Northern Song at the eastern foot of Yuelu Mountain, Yuelu Academy was one of China's most renowned Confucian academies, where the Neo-Confucian scholars Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi lectured, and its courtyards of lecture halls, library, shrines and a Confucian temple were restored after damage in the Cultural Revolution. It became the Hunan Institute of Higher Learning in 1903 and is part of Hunan University, whose early campus buildings around it, from the Western-style Second Building of 1926 to Liu Shiying's auditorium and old library of 1946–53 with traditional-style roofs, are also protected. Most visitors combine it with a walk up Yuelu Mountain behind.

rows.name: Yuelu Mountain and Orange Isle
rows.summary: Yuelu Mountain, a wooded ridge about 300 m high on the west bank of the Xiang River facing central Changsha, has the Lushan Temple founded in 268, the Ming-dynasty Daoist Yunlu Palace, the Aiwan (Autumn-Admiring) Pavilion of 1792 and, near the summit, a 1212 rock-cut copy of the Yu Stele with 77 archaic characters, as well as the tombs of the 1911 revolutionaries Huang Xing and Cai E. Orange Isle, a sand island some 5 km long in the river, has gardens at its southern tip with a giant sculpture of the young Mao Zedong (2009) and a stele of his 1925 poem 'Changsha'. The two are listed together as one 5A scenic area; Yuelu Academy at the foot of the mountain has its own card.

rows.name: Zhouluo Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area around Shizhu Peak (1,359.7 m) in Shegang town, northern Liuyang, at the source of the Laodao River, with a core of about 14 km² of streams, waterfalls, quartz-veined rock and wild osmanthus groves. Old houses such as the Chen family mansion and a water-mouth pagoda stand in the valley villages, which also have hotels and farm restaurants.

rows.name: Zilongwan Hot Spring Resort, Huitang
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Huitang, the spa town of south-western Ningxiang, set on a hillside below Mount Dongwu and looking over the man-made Zilong Lake. It has open-air thermal pools among trees, water-play facilities and a resort hotel, and suits a relaxing stay rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: 711 Uranium Mine Heritage Site
rows.summary: The site of China's first large uranium mine to be found and worked, at Xujiadong north of Chenzhou: an airborne survey found the deposit in 1956, production began in 1963 (as Mine 711 from 1964), it supplied uranium for China's first atomic bomb, and mining ended in 1994. The old mine settlement has since been reopened to visitors as '711 Time Town', with the miners' housing, club and an air-raid-shelter exhibition hall, sculptures recreating underground work and photo exhibitions, period-style performances on public holidays, and places to eat and stay.

rows.name: Ancient Ancestral Halls of Rucheng
rows.summary: Rucheng County keeps more than 700 clan ancestral halls, the oldest from 1231 and most of them Qing, and nine, from the Ming to the Republic, form this national heritage group. They include the Taibao Di at Waisha (1486), a Zhu clan hall renamed in memory of the Ming minister Zhu Ying; the Li hall (1437) and the timber memorial arch called Bajiao Lou (1489) at Guang'ansuo in Tuqiao; the Lu and Ye halls at Jinshan; and the Zhou halls at Xianfeng.

rows.name: Banliang Ancient Village
rows.summary: A Liu-clan farming village in Gaotingsi town, Yongxing County, first built in 1358, whose lanes of grey-brick houses, ancestral halls and gateways survive largely from the Ming and Qing; 29 old buildings make up the national heritage group, among them the Upper Village Ancestral Hall of 1443 and the early-Ming Lower Village hall. The Middle Village hall (1420) is also a site of the 1928 Xiangnan Uprising, where local peasant forces seized the militia's guns. The village is lived in, with small stalls and guesthouses for visitors.

rows.name: Baoshan National Mine Park
rows.summary: A mine park on Baoshan hill on the western edge of Guiyang county town, set up by the Baoshan non-ferrous metals company on a hill mined since ancient times. A small train takes visitors into the old underground workings, where scenes and tools show ancient mining methods, and there are also a modern open pit and processing works to see; the park became a 4A scenic area in 2014.

rows.name: Dongjiang Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir of about 160 km² among the hills of Zixing, held back by a 157 m double-curvature arch dam on the Lei River that was built in stages between 1958 and 1992. Its best-known sight is the Xiao Dongjiang gorge below the dam, where mist often lies on the water in the early morning and fishermen's boats are photographed from a riverside walkway. Boats run out across the lake to islands such as Doushuai Island, and the dam itself is part of the scenic area.

rows.name: Feitian Mountain
rows.summary: A national geopark of red Danxia sandstone north-east of Chenzhou, where a river winds between cliffs and rock towers weathered into shapes likened to people and animals. Named sights include the Chuantan rock arch, the Heitan cave and the 'Niukou hanging coffins', old coffins placed in a cliff niche whose origin is unknown.

rows.name: Former Residence of Deng Zhongxia
rows.summary: The birthplace of Deng Zhongxia (1894–1933), an early member of the Chinese Communist Party and leader of the labour movement, including the Canton–Hong Kong strike of 1925–26, who was captured and executed by the Nationalist government in 1933. The house in Dengjiawan village is a small two-storey grey-brick farmhouse of the southern Hunan type, about 130 m², kept as a memorial with its family rooms.

rows.name: Fuquan Hot Spring Resort, Rucheng
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Reshui ('hot water') town in eastern Rucheng, near the Jiangxi and Guangdong borders, built over a geothermal field whose springs reach 91–98 °C, among the hottest in southern China. The resort has dozens of outdoor pools, villas and a hotel set among bamboo-covered hills, and in the town people still boil eggs, peanuts and chestnuts directly in the spring water.

rows.name: Gaoyi Ridge
rows.summary: A Danxia landscape of red sandstone cliffs and ridges on the border of Suxian District and Zixing, north-east of Chenzhou, covering about 50.5 km². It lies close to Feitian Mountain, Dongjiang Lake and Banliang village, and guesthouses, cafés and campsites have grown up around its visitor centre.

rows.name: Headquarters of the South Hunan New Year Uprising
rows.name_zh: 湘南年关暴动指挥部旧址
rows.summary: A Qing courtyard compound at 26 Zhongxia Street in Yizhang county town, built under the Shunzhi emperor as the garrison commander's office and later a girls' vocational school, which Zhu De and Chen Yi used as their headquarters for the 'New Year' rising of January 1928 that opened the Xiangnan (South Hunan) Uprising. Its two courtyards of two-storey grey-brick and timber buildings are furnished as in 1928, and a memorial hall beside them tells the story of the uprising.

rows.name: Huilong Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain of about 1,413 m north of Dongjiang Lake in Zixing, rated 4A in December 2024 and visited for sunrise, sunset and sea-of-cloud views from the top and for wild azaleas in May. A hotel, cliff-side guesthouses and a campsite on the mountain let visitors stay overnight, and it is marketed together with the lake ('the lake by day, the mountain by night').

rows.name: Jiulongjiang National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park on the former Daping state forest farm in south-eastern Rucheng County, on the Hunan–Guangdong border, covered mostly in natural broadleaf forest and rising to Fuyin Peak (1,381 m). The Jiulong River rises in the park and flows south into Guangdong, and a trail follows the Qinglong Gorge past a series of waterfalls; a glass walkway was added in 2017.

rows.name: Long March Third Blockade Headquarters Site
rows.name_zh: 中央红军长征突破第三道封锁线指挥部旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngyāng Hóngjūn Chángzhēng Tūpò Dìsān Dào Fēngsuǒxiàn Zhǐhuībù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The Kuang clan ancestral hall (Qingbai Tang) in Baishidu village, a two-storey brick-and-timber hall with fire-gable walls built in 1861. From here Zhou Enlai and Liu Bocheng directed the Central Red Army on 10 November 1934 as it took Baishidu, a town on the Guangdong–Hankou railway, and broke through the Nationalists' third blockade line on the Long March; a stone marker stands outside.

rows.name: Longnü Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort area at Tongkenghu on the north-western edge of Chenzhou, near National Road 106, built around a carbonated spring at about 40 °C used for both bathing and drinking. The site is tied to the Tang tale of Liu Yi, the scholar who carried a letter for the Dragon King's daughter (the 'dragon maiden') herding sheep in exile, and has a Dragon Maiden shrine; its hotel has villas with private hot-spring pools.

rows.name: Mangshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A large mountain forest at the southern tip of Yizhang County on the Hunan–Guangdong border, protected as a national nature reserve and national forest park; its subtropical forest has species named after it, such as the Mangshan pit viper. The main visitor zone is Wuzhi Feng (Five-Finger Peak), where a cableway, a vertical lift and cliff-side walkways run to the summit viewpoints, so that older and less mobile visitors can get up too.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Emperor Yi
rows.summary: The tomb of Xiong Xin, Emperor Yi of Chu (died 206 BC), the figurehead ruler of the rebels against the Qin, whom Xiang Yu sent away to Chen County (today's Chenzhou) and had murdered; the people of Chen buried him here, in what is now the middle of the city. In a small walled park are the round earth mound ringed with granite, a marble tombstone, two stele pavilions with the 'New Stele of Emperor Yi', carved in 1059 with a 1345 record of temple repairs on the back, and its copy, and a memorial shrine with a bronze statue and murals of the Chu–Han wars.

rows.name: Old Kunqu Opera Stages of Guiyang
rows.summary: Three Qing-dynasty theatre stages built into clan ancestral halls in villages of Guiyang County, linked with Xiang Kun, the local Hunan branch of Kunqu opera: the Luo clan hall stage at Daxi (1653, restored 1854), the Ouyang clan hall stage at Xiayang (1718) and the Wei clan hall stage at Zhaojin (1863). The stages stand at the front of their halls, facing the shrines across inner courtyards; those at Daxi and Xiayang have hipped roofs and coffered ceilings, and Daxi and Zhaojin keep painted wooden screens.

rows.name: Shazhou Village (Half a Quilt Story)
rows.summary: A Yao village in western Rucheng County known for the 'half a quilt' story: in November 1934, as the Central Red Army crossed the area on the Long March, three women soldiers who lodged with a villager, Xu Jiexiu, cut their only quilt in two and left her half. Xi Jinping retold the story in his 2016 speech marking the 80th anniversary of the Long March, and since 2017 Shazhou and four neighbouring villages have been developed into a red-tourism area of about 3.2 km², with the 'Warmth of Half a Quilt' exhibition hall, a sculpture and, in Xiushui village, a 1922 house used as the Red Army headquarters.

rows.name: Shilangtan Cliff Inscriptions
rows.summary: A red-sandstone overhang about 12 m high and 150 m long on the north bank of the Bian River, as the Lei River is called in Yongxing, named 'the Vice-Minister's Overhang' after the Tang writer Han Yu, who moored his boat here. Its walls carry about 14 inscriptions from the Southern Dynasties, the Tang and the Qing, including two of Han Yu's own 'Changli passed here', confirmed by experts as his calligraphy in 2009.

rows.name: Site of the Fourth Red Army Front Committee Meeting
rows.name_zh: 红四军前委扩大会议旧址
rows.summary: The Tang family house (Tangjia Dawu) in Guidong county town, with the adjoining City God Temple, where in 1928 the forces of Mao Zedong and Zhu De held an enlarged meeting of the Fourth Red Army's front committee after the setback known as the 'August Defeat'. The meeting reviewed the defeat, put a new action committee under Mao in charge and decided to take the army back to the Jinggangshan base in Jiangxi; listed in 2019 as Guidong's first national heritage site, the house is now a museum of the Red Army's activities in Guidong.

rows.name: Suxian Ridge
rows.summary: A wooded hill on the north-eastern edge of central Chenzhou, named after the legend of a local man who became an immortal ('Su the Immortal'); paths climb past the White Deer Cave, the 'Ascension Stone' and other spots tied to the story. Its cliff inscriptions, carved from the Tang to the Republic, are a national heritage site, the best known being the 'Three Excellences Stele': Qin Guan's poem on his stay at a Chenzhou lodge, with a colophon by Su Shi, in the calligraphy of Mi Fu. It makes an easy half-day walk from the city centre.

rows.name: Tiantang Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Tiantang village in Xujiadong, on the northern edge of Chenzhou, developed in the 2000s around a spring that comes up at about 52 °C. It has Japanese-style open-air pools in landscaped grounds, with a hotel and villas on site, and suits a relaxed half day or an overnight stay.

rows.name: Wangxian Ridge
rows.summary: A forested hill scenic area on the south-eastern edge of Chenzhou city, with walks among streams and small waterfalls under the trees. It lies close to the city centre and has long been paired with Suxian Ridge on a day out from Chenzhou.

rows.name: Wanhuayan Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in the south-western outskirts of Chenzhou, in Beihu District, where lit paths lead past stalactites, stalagmites and flowstone, and the walls carry inscriptions left by visitors from the Song dynasty onwards. An underground river runs through it, and from around the May Day holiday through the summer an 1,800 m rafting route of about 40 minutes follows the river inside the cave, which stays at about 18–20 °C all year. It is managed together with Suxian Ridge as one scenic area.

rows.name: Wanyang Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in Guidong County near the Jiangxi border, part of the Luoxiao range, whose high meadows above 1,500 m, natural tarn and lines of wind turbines are marketed as a 'southern grassland'; azaleas flower on the slopes in spring. Rated 4A in August 2026, it is promoted as a cool summer retreat, with average summer temperatures around 21 °C and forest cover of about 95%.

rows.name: Xiangnan Uprising Memorial Hall and Sites
rows.summary: The Xiangnan (South Hunan) Uprising of January–April 1928, led by Zhu De and Chen Yi, briefly put more than ten counties of southern Hunan under communist control before the troops withdrew to join Mao Zedong at Jinggangshan; the national heritage group covers buildings linked to it in ten counties. In Chenzhou the places to see are the memorial hall on Dongta Ridge, opened in 2010, with about 3,700 m² of exhibitions in five sections, and the late-Qing Chen family house at 35 Xingzhong Street, about 700 m away, which served as the uprising's headquarters and the Chen County soviet government's office and has been restored and open since 2008.

rows.name: Xiuyi Arch
rows.summary: A white stone memorial arch of 1519 at the entrance to the Fan family village of Yidao, on the edge of Rucheng town, raised for the censor Fan Lu ('embroidered robe' was a name for imperial censors), who was jailed after denouncing the Prince of Ning's dealings with eunuchs and cleared when the prince rebelled. Said to be the oldest stone arch in Hunan, it has three openings under three tiers of stone hipped roofs carved with lions and phoenixes. Behind it stand the Fan family temple of 1485, with a plaque presented by Wang Yangming, and the Zhongcheng Hall of 1522, both built for the same family.

rows.name: Xiyao Green Valley National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park, set up in 2010, in the Xishan Yao Township of south-western Linwu County, where forested mountains fall from 1,720 m to about 300 m into deep valleys with streams, waterfalls and caves. Paths follow the valley, a cherry valley planted in 2015 with some 2,000 trees flowers in early April, and the Yao hamlet of Taoyuanping lies deep in the hills.

rows.name: Yangtianhu Grassland
rows.summary: A high grassland of rolling hilltops at around 1,300 m in the mountains south-west of Chenzhou, in Beihu District. Summer temperatures average about 20 °C, so it fills up in July and August with visitors from Chenzhou and the Guangdong cities to the south, who walk the meadows, ride horses and stay on for sunsets and starry skies. A 2022 season of the Hunan TV show 'Chinese Restaurant' was filmed here.

rows.name: Cai Lun Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park in central Leiyang, home town of Cai Lun, the Eastern Han court official credited with improving papermaking around AD 105. At its core is Cai Hou Temple, a brick-and-timber shrine rebuilt in the late Qing on the site said to be his old home, beside Caizi Pond. The park around it was laid out in 2001 and includes a cenotaph tomb and a workshop demonstrating traditional papermaking.

rows.name: Cailun Bamboo Sea
rows.summary: A large area of bamboo forest in Huangshi Town in south-eastern Leiyang, the home district of the papermaking pioneer Cai Lun. Stone paths lead through the bamboo from a visitor centre with a statue of Cai Lun to old hand-papermaking workshops, where craftsmen show the traditional process of soaking, pounding and sheet-forming bamboo pulp. Since December 2024 the old Shangbao crystal mine inside the area, known for its fluorite specimens, has been open as a mine park.

rows.name: China Seal Mountain
rows.summary: A limestone hillside in Miaoqian Town, Changning, known locally as Yanbeiling, on which thousands of designs of historic Chinese seals have been carved into the rocks since 2003. The project was started by the printmaker Wu Guowei, and the carvings reproduce seals from Shang bronze seals to the Qin imperial seal and Tang official seals, in both relief and intaglio; the scenic area, reopened after an upgrade in 2020, also takes in a cave and flower fields.

rows.name: Dongzhou Island
rows.summary: An island about 2 km long in the Xiang River in central Hengyang, whose peach blossom ('Dongzhou peach waves') was one of the city's eight traditional views. Its main sight is Chuanshan Academy, founded in 1878 in honour of the philosopher Wang Fuzhi and moved to the island in 1885 by Peng Yulin, who appointed the scholar Wang Kaiyun as its head; the academy was restored in a renovation of the whole island, which reopened in 2018. Luohan Temple, old camphor trees and a sandy beach at the island's tip, exposed when the river is low, complete a gentle walk.

rows.name: Former Residence of Luo Ronghuan
rows.summary: The birthplace of Luo Ronghuan (1902–1963), a Communist commander who led political work in the Red Army and was made a marshal of the People's Liberation Army in 1955, in Nanwan Village, Ronghuan Town, Hengdong County. The family house was restored and opened to visitors in 1985, and a memorial hall nearby has a full-length bronze statue of him outside.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wang Fuzhi (Xiangxi Caotang)
rows.summary: Xiangxi Caotang is the thatched retreat where the Ming loyalist philosopher Wang Fuzhi (Wang Chuanshan, 1619–1692) spent his final years writing, in Qulan Town, Hengyang County. Built in 1675, the modest brick-and-timber house of about 176 m² is a typical rural home of southern Hunan, and the national listing also covers his tomb in the same area.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xia Minghan
rows.summary: The ancestral home of Xia Minghan (1900–1928), an early Communist organiser executed in Hankou in 1928 and remembered for the poem he wrote before his death, in Lizi Village, Hongshi Town, Hengyang County. The Qing-era compound of 45 rooms, built around 1745, was restored and opened in 2005. It now holds an exhibition on his life, a calligraphy display and restored living rooms.

rows.name: Former Site of the Xiangnan Student Union
rows.summary: The former premises of the Xiangnan (Southern Hunan) Student Union, a student federation active in Hengyang from the May Fourth period of 1919, on the east bank of the Xiang River. The site and its memorial hall hold exhibitions on the union and early revolutionary activity in southern Hunan, including a room associated with Mao Zedong. It hosted the opening of Hunan's Red Tourism Festival in 2022.

rows.name: Goulou Peak
rows.summary: Goulou Peak is one of the main summits of the Hengshan range, rising in the north-east of Hengyang County on the border with Hengshan County, inside a national forest park set up in 1995 that covers about 2,070 ha, takes in five of Mount Heng's 72 peaks and rises to 1,143 m. It gave its name to the Goulou Stele, an inscription in tadpole-like script traditionally attributed to Yu the Great, of which later copies are carved on Yuelu Mountain in Changsha and elsewhere. The forested mountain was rated a 4A scenic area in 2026.

rows.name: Grand Temple of Mount Heng
rows.summary: The largest temple on Mount Heng, at the northern end of Nanyue old town at the foot of the mountain, dedicated to the god of the Southern Peak. First recorded in 725, it was rebuilt in 1882 on the pattern of the imperial palace in Beijing after a fire, earning the nickname 'little Forbidden City of the south'. Nine gates, pavilions and halls stand on its central axis, including the main hall with 72 stone columns, one for each peak, and eight Taoist and eight Buddhist compounds flank them.

rows.name: Hengyang Ornamental Stone Museum
rows.summary: A private museum of ornamental stones in Zhengxiang District, the first private museum approved by Hunan's cultural relics bureau, run by the collector Liu Xuanling. Its two main halls show large and small decorative stones respectively, and galleries on minerals, crystals, fossils and geology serve as a science education base for young people.

rows.name: Huiyan Peak
rows.summary: A 97 m hill in Yanfeng District, traditionally counted as the first of Mount Heng's 72 peaks and the source of Hengyang's nickname 'Wild Goose City', from the old belief that geese flying south turned back here. The hilltop park has the rebuilt Yanfeng Temple, first founded in the Southern and Northern dynasties, the 35 m Huiyan Pavilion, and a small memorial hall at Wang Fuzhi's birthplace on its western slope.

rows.name: Mount Heng
rows.summary: Mount Heng, the Southern Peak among China's Five Great Mountains, is a granite range counted as 72 peaks, whose highest point, Zhurong Peak, stands at about 1,300 m above Nanyue town. Long a centre of both Buddhism and Taoism, its slopes hold temples such as Zhusheng, Fuyan and Shangfeng, and cliff inscriptions from the Southern and Northern dynasties to the Republican era are scattered over some 375 spots. The mountain is also a national nature reserve, with evergreen broadleaf forest giving way to dwarf forest and grassland above about 800 m.

rows.name: Nanhu Park
rows.summary: A wetland park around a former reservoir on the south-western side of central Hengyang, opened in 2014 and the city's largest urban wetland park. Boardwalks, zig-zag bridges and pavilions ring the lake, with restaurants and tea rooms on the shore.

rows.name: Nanyue Martyrs' Shrine
rows.summary: A memorial shrine below Xianglu Peak on the lower slopes of Mount Heng, planned in 1938 and completed in 1943 by the Nationalist government for soldiers killed in the War of Resistance against Japan, and regarded as one of the earliest and largest such memorials in China. Laid out like the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, a 240 m axis climbs from a memorial arch past a tower shaped as five artillery shells and a stele hall to the cross-shaped sacrificial hall. Collective cemeteries of several Nationalist divisions and the tombs of a dozen generals lie on the surrounding hills.

rows.name: Qishan Forest Park
rows.summary: Qishan, formerly called Fenghuang Shan and counted among the 72 peaks of Mount Heng, is a hill in the west of Hengnan County rising to 741 m, protected as a provincial forest park since 1998. Its secondary broadleaf forest is rich in nanmu trees and has 26 ancient ginkgos, ten of them more than 300 years old. Renrui Temple, a provincial heritage site, stands on the mountain.

rows.name: Shigu Academy
rows.summary: Shigu Academy stands on Shigu Hill, where the Zheng and Lei rivers join the Xiang in the north of Hengyang city. Founded around 810 under the Tang and twice given imperial name boards in the Song, it is often counted among the four great academies of the Song, and the Neo-Confucian philosopher Zhu Xi wrote a record of it in 1187. The old buildings were destroyed by Japanese bombing in 1939, and today's complex is a Qing-style reconstruction that opened in 2007.

rows.name: Shuikoushan Lead-Zinc Mining Heritage & Labour Movement Memorial
rows.summary: Mining in the Shuikoushan area of Changning goes back more than a thousand years, and the Qing government set up a mining bureau here in 1896; the listed industrial site has 19 features above and below ground, including old shafts, smelting halls and workers' housing. In 1922 Mao Zedong visited the mine, and later that year the miners' club organised a major strike. Visitors can see a new labour-movement memorial hall, opened in 2021, and the older exhibition hall in a building put up in 1953 for Soviet experts.

rows.name: Siming Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain on the western edge of Qidong County, said to take its name from the four neighbouring counties it looks out over; it became a provincial forest park in 2004 and a national forest park in 2014. Besides woodland walks, the mountain has Siming Temple, said to date from the early Tang, and the late-Ming Tengyun Zushi Hall.

rows.name: Wang Ancestral Hall, Dayu Village
rows.summary: An ancestral hall of the Wang clan in Dayu Village, Lijiang Town, in southern Hengnan County, founded under the Northern Song, restored in the Yongle reign of the Ming and repaired several times under the Qing; it has been a national heritage site since 2013. The Ming-style hall stands on 48 stone columns with more than 300 carved brackets and keeps 32 inscribed couplets attributed to figures from Ouyang Xiu to Zuo Zongtang. The clan still gathers here for an ancestral rite every winter.

rows.name: Zhongtian Village Historic Buildings
rows.summary: A village of the Li clan in Miaoqian Town, Changning, settled in 1404 by descendants of Ming-dynasty soldier households from the Chaling garrison. Its 28 listed buildings date from the Ming dynasty to the Republican era and were made a national heritage site in 2019. China Seal Mountain lies in the same town, so the two can be seen together.

rows.name: Zijin Mountain
rows.summary: A forested hill beside Kaiyun, the county town of Hengshan County, counted in the Mount Heng range as Jinzi Peak. The scenic area covers 4.35 km² with forest cover of about 87%, mixing woodland paths with a few cultural sites, and is promoted as a cool summer retreat.

rows.name: Anjiang Agricultural School Hybrid Rice Memorial Park
rows.name_zh: 安江农校杂交水稻纪念园
rows.summary: The former campus of the Anjiang Agricultural School in Anjiang town, where the rice scientist Yuan Longping taught and did research from 1953 and where his team developed China's three-line hybrid rice system. The memorial park keeps school buildings from 1939 to the 1980s, among them Yuan's former home, the assembly hall, a genetics laboratory, a glasshouse and the experimental rice fields, and the Hybrid Rice Birthplace Museum, opened in 2024, stands about 1 km away. Across the Yuan River lies the Gaomiao Neolithic site, where carbonised rice grains about 7,400 years old have been found.

rows.name: Baiyi Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple of 1759 in Boyang town, western Tongdao, also called the Qianqiu White Pagoda and described as the only Taoist temple in the Dong region. Its centrepiece is a five-storey octagonal timber tower 18.92 m tall with a spiral wooden stair inside and lattice windows on every floor, enclosed by a brick wall.

rows.name: Chongshi Academy, Xupu
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty clan academy in the old village of Yanban, Longtan town, founded in 1834 as the Yanling family school of the Wu clan and renamed Chongshi Academy in 1855. Behind its original archway-style gate the brick-and-timber building has three halls round courtyards, with murals and clay reliefs of landscapes, flowers and birds, carved stones set into a screen wall and a half-moon pond in front; it became a national heritage unit in 2019.

rows.name: Chuanyan Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in Tongxihe town in the Xuefeng Mountains of Xupu County, rated 4A in 2019, with the hilltop Fengxiang Yao village of guesthouses as its main base. An 18 km walking route through it follows the line of march of the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups past an iron-chain bridge over the Shixi River, the old village of Yan'ejie, a stretch of old tea-horse road and Red Army pavilions and bridges.

rows.name: Eryou Mountain
rows.summary: A hill at the meeting of the You River and the Youxi stream north-west of Yuanling town, tied by legend to the scholar Fu Sheng, who is said to have hidden banned books in a cave here during the Qin book burning; the place became a byword for learning in Chinese. Rated 4A in 2025 and promoted as China's Book Mountain, it has a stepped path up to the cave, a visitor centre with exhibition rooms and a floating footbridge across the river.

rows.name: Feishan Mountain
rows.summary: A 720 m mountain north-west of Jingzhou town whose summit temple honours Yang Zaisi (860–954), a local leader of the Five Dynasties period who styled himself Lord of Feishan and is revered across the Hunan–Guizhou–Guangxi borderlands. The summit temple was first built in the Yuanfeng period (1078–1085) of the Song dynasty and rebuilt in 1903 after a fire, and the mountain also has a Qing temple of 1693, a Chan Buddhist temple rebuilt in 2005, the Taoist Fangguang Temple at its foot and old defensive trenches.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xiang Jingyu
rows.summary: An early Qing courtyard house of pine and fir timber in Xupu county town where Xiang Jingyu (1895–1928), an early leader of the Chinese Communist Party and of its women's movement, was born. Together with an exhibition on her life and a square with her bronze statue it forms the Xiang Jingyu Memorial, opened in 1981; she was executed by the Kuomintang in Wuhan in 1928.

rows.name: Gaomiao Archaeological Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic shell-midden site on a terrace of the Yuan River opposite Anjiang town, whose lower layers of about 7,800 to 6,600 years ago define the Gaomiao culture, known for white pottery stamped with phoenix-bird, fanged beast-face and eight-pointed star designs and for large ritual remains. Excavated in 1991, 2004, 2005 and 2024 and named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2005, it now has a site museum, opened in 2024, that shows more than 240 objects and specimens, and is being developed as a national archaeological park.

rows.name: Gaoyi Ancient Village
rows.summary: A Dong village in Gaoyi township, Huitong County, ringed by hills on three sides and a river on the fourth, where 104 houses built between 1380 and 1881 survive. Most villagers are surnamed Yang and trace their descent from the 10th-century local leader Yang Zaisi; it became a China Historical and Cultural Village in 2007 and was rated 4A in 2025.

rows.name: Hongjiang Ancient Commercial Town
rows.summary: An old river port where the Wu River joins the Yuan, which in Ming and Qing times was the main transit point for the produce of south-western Hunan and eastern Guizhou. More than 380 buildings from the Ming dynasty to the Republican era survive, among them temples, money shops, trading houses, foreign firms, workshops, shops and inns, 18 of them protected at national level; named buildings include the likin tax office, the Suzhou and Changde guild halls and an old opium house.

rows.name: Huangdu Dong Culture Village
rows.summary: A Dong village in Pingtan township, Tongdao, run as a cultural scenic area, with timber stilt houses, drum towers and covered bridges. Visitors are met at the village gate with Dong welcome customs, and Dong songs and dances are staged for them at a performance ground; there are village guesthouses for overnight stays.

rows.name: Huangyan Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A karst upland on the slopes of Liangshan south-east of Huaihua city, at an average altitude of about 850 m, that is a provincial tourist resort and forest park and is promoted as a summer retreat. It takes in the Huaihua Grand Canyon and Baima scenic spots and Daping village, where villagers have planted flower fields among the rocks and built cliff walkways and ziplines; grass sledding and rock climbing are also on offer.

rows.name: Jingping Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village of Ming and Qing brick-and-timber houses on the west bank of the Wu River in Zhongfang County, most of whose residents belong to the Pan clan. Its old buildings include the Pan ancestral hall, a Guandi temple and stone memorial archways; it is a China Historical and Cultural Village, was rated 4A in 2025, and keeps up a tradition of qin music linked to a Qing scholar of the clan.

rows.name: Jiufeng Modern Agricultural Expo Park
rows.summary: A modern agricultural park in Hecheng District, Huaihua, that opened in June 2018, built around large climate-controlled show glasshouses growing vegetables, fruit and some 360 unusual varieties. Its zones include farming-technology displays, vegetable and fruit growing areas, leisure areas and an ocean-themed science hall, and it mainly suits families from the city.

rows.name: Longxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old riverside quarter of Longxikou in Xinhuang county town, near the Guizhou border, shaped by Ming and Qing trade on the Wu River, with more than 200 old buildings including a group of historic merchant houses. The Longxi Academy here was revived in 2012 from the Wuyang Academy founded in 1821, and during the war against Japan the architects Liang Sicheng and Lin Huiyin stopped in the town for about ten days on their way south-west.

rows.name: Longxing Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the southern foot of Huxi Hill in Yuanling town, traditionally founded in 628 by order of the Tang emperor Taizong, whose halls preserve building styles from the Song to the Qing and are described as the oldest surviving group of timber buildings in Hunan. The Mahavira Hall of the late Yuan or early Ming, nearly 20 m high on 24 nanmu columns, carries a plaque by the Ming calligrapher Dong Qichang, and the philosopher Wang Yangming is recorded as lecturing here for a month on his way back from exile in Guizhou. From the Guanyin Pavilion at the back there are views over the Yuan River.

rows.name: Matian Drum Tower
rows.summary: A Dong drum tower in Matian village, Pingyang township, in the far south of Tongdao, first built in the Shunzhi reign of the early Qing and restored in 1984. The all-timber tower is 18.72 m high with nine tiers of eaves, the top tier octagonal and the rest four-sided; its eave boards are painted with flowers, birds and insects, and clay tigers, dragons, snakes and phoenixes stand on its corners.

rows.name: Pingtan River Covered Bridges
rows.summary: Nine Dong covered bridges with long timber galleries span the Pingtan River in Pingtan township and Longcheng town; they were built between 1755 and 1853, and most were repaired in the 20th century. The longest, the Huilong Bridge of 1761, is about 63 m long with 22 bays, and the bridges still carry villagers on foot.

rows.name: Qianyang Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old walled town of Qiancheng, former seat of Qianyang County, sits where the Wu River meets the Yuan, with water on three sides, and keeps about 0.8 km² of flagstone lanes lined mainly with Ming and Qing buildings. Survivals include the west Zhongzheng Gate with its gate tower, the bell and drum tower, the Wanshou Palace, the Baoshan Academy, the old county yamen and the Chifeng Pagoda. Furong Tower, a garden pavilion complex built in memory of the Tang poet Wang Changling, has a stele corridor of more than a hundred carved inscriptions in the hands of Yan Zhenqing, Huang Tingjian, Mi Fu and other calligraphers.

rows.name: Simeng Danxia Scenic Area
rows.summary: A stretch of the Xu River at Simeng, west of Xupu county town, where red Danxia sandstone cliffs and peaks rise above the water, a landscape locally nicknamed little Guilin. Downstream the river enters the Quzi Gorge, named after the poet Qu Yuan, whose poem Crossing the River is tied by local tradition to this valley.

rows.name: Site of the Chenzhou Missionary Case
rows.summary: A group of Western-style church and mission buildings on Malu Lane in Yuanling town, where two British missionaries of the China Inland Mission were killed in August 1902 after rumours during an epidemic accused them of poisoning, an affair known as the Chenzhou Missionary Case. With the indemnity, the American Reformed Church mission that took over built a chapel and school in 1907 and several missionaries' houses, and later a hospital and girls' school, beside a Catholic church. In 1938 the buildings housed offices of the Hunan provincial government after it moved temporarily to Yuanling.

rows.name: Su Yu's Hometown
rows.summary: The home village of Su Yu (1907–1984), a leading Communist military commander who later served as Chief of the PLA General Staff and held the rank of Senior General; he was born into a Dong family in Fengmushujiao village, now part of Pingcun town. The scenic area joins his former home to the Su Yu Memorial Hall, devoted to his life and military career, with a memorial square, a bronze statue, a lake and an outdoor display of aircraft, tanks and other heavy weapons.

rows.name: Teng Daiyuan Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall by the Jin River in Mayang county town to Teng Daiyuan (1904–1974), a Miao native of Mayang who was one of the leaders of the Pingjiang Uprising, a senior Red Army political commissar and later the first Minister of Railways of the People's Republic. Opened on 2 November 1986 with its name written by Hu Yaobang, it traces his life in ten sections with more than 300 photographs, more than 60 original documents and objects and two reconstructed scenes. His former home in Yanmen town, with some of his belongings, belongs to the same scenic area.

rows.name: Tongdao Conference Site (Gongcheng Academy)
rows.summary: Gongcheng Academy in Xianxi town was founded in 1105 as the Luomeng Academy and rebuilt by Dong craftsmen in 1792, and is one of the more complete academies surviving in a Dong area. On 12 December 1934 leaders of the Central Red Army on the Long March met here and decided to turn west into Guizhou rather than north into western Hunan, the episode known as the Tongdao Turn. The Tongdao Turn Memorial Hall stands beside the academy.

rows.name: Wanfo Mountain
rows.summary: A Danxia landscape of red sandstone peaks, cliffs and forest in Wanfoshan town, Tongdao, whose main summit rises to 635 m; together with nearby Dong villages it became a national scenic area in 2009. Named sights include the Wanfo summit, Qiansui Peak and Xianrenju, and the summit looks out over hundreds of peaks rising from the forest.

rows.name: West Hunan Bandit Suppression Memorial Park
rows.summary: The national heritage unit for the 1949–1952 campaign in which the PLA's 47th Army fought armed bandit groups across western Hunan has two parts: the 47th Army headquarters building in Yuanling town and the memorial hall in Victory Park on the high ground of old Chenxi town. At the park the memorial hall has steles at its gate listing those killed in the campaign, a museum opened in 2004 shows documents and objects from the campaign in 22 counties, and a victory monument stands in the park.

rows.name: Xuefeng Mountain War of Resistance Sites
rows.summary: A national heritage unit made up of sites from the Battle of West Hunan, fought around the Xuefeng Mountains from April to June 1945 when Japanese forces advanced towards the Zhijiang airfield and were driven back, spread over Xupu and Chenxi counties in Huaihua and Dongkou County in Shaoyang. Its main visitable part is the Wang clan ancestral hall in Wantan village, Huangmaoyuan town, next to Longtan in southern Xupu, which served as a field hospital for more than 2,000 wounded soldiers during the Battle of Longtan and now holds an exhibition of medical equipment, captured Japanese items and other wartime objects. In Chenxi the unit includes the wartime Nanzhuangping arsenal and four bunkers, one of them in Chenxi's Victory Park.

rows.name: Yutou Dong Village
rows.summary: A Dong village in Shuangjiang town founded in the Hongwu reign of the early Ming and rebuilt after a fire in the Shunzhi reign of the Qing, its seven clusters of houses strung along the Yutou stream. Its old buildings include four drum towers, among them the Lusheng Drum Tower, three covered bridges, a gate tower, two Sa altars, two old wells, 78 timber stilt houses and a stretch of old post road.

rows.name: Zhijiang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The former Confucian temple of Yuanzhou prefecture on Xiaobei Street in Zhijiang town, moved to its present site in 1859 and built in 1862–63. Along its axis lie the Pan pool, the Ji Gate, a dance terrace, the 12 m Dacheng Hall with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof and the Chongsheng shrine, and it also holds a 1921 epitaph stone whose heading was written by the novelist Shen Congwen.

rows.name: Zhijiang Surrender Memorial
rows.summary: The site in Qiliqiao village outside Zhijiang town where, on 21 August 1945, a Japanese delegation led by Major General Takeo Imai received the Chinese terms for the surrender of Japan's forces in China, the first step towards the formal surrender ceremony in Nanjing that September. It keeps the 1938 buildings of the Chinese Army headquarters and He Yingqin's office, a memorial museum opened in 1995, and the stone surrender memorial arch first built in 1946–47, destroyed in 1966 and rebuilt from old photographs in 2010.

rows.name: Zhijiang Tianhou Temple
rows.summary: A temple to the sea goddess Mazu on Jiangxi Street in Zhijiang town, first built in the Kangxi reign and enlarged in 1748 by Fujian merchants as their guild hall; it is described as the largest surviving Mazu temple in inland China. Its 10.6 m bluestone gateway, carved in the form of a gate tower, carries 95 relief panels of flowers, animals and legends, and behind it lie a stage, the main hall and a Guanyin hall flanked by halls to the God of Wealth and Guandi.

rows.name: Cai Hesen Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum in Shuangfeng town to Cai Hesen (1895–1931), an early leader of the Chinese Communist Party and friend of Mao Zedong who argued for the Bolshevik approach from France and was executed in 1931, and to his family. It stands on Cai Hesen Square with a statue group of the family and the Cai Chang Library, named after his sister, the first chair of the All-China Women's Federation; the family home is about 22 km to the east.

rows.name: Daxiongshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A mountain forest park in northern Xinhua whose peaks include Jiulong Feng (1,622 m), the highest in central Hunan, and Daxiong Feng (1,602 m), with gorges, waterfalls, old forest and more than 40 summits over 1,000 m. Local tradition makes it the homeland of Chiyou, the legendary rival of the Yellow Emperor, and there are a Chiyou culture park and hall, the rebuilt Xiongshan Temple, a forest of old monks' stupas and Qing rock inscriptions.

rows.name: Former Residence of Cai Hesen and Cai Chang
rows.summary: Guangjia Hall, a late-Qing brick-and-timber farmhouse in Yangqiu village, Jingzi town, where the family of the early Communist leader Cai Hesen (1895–1931) settled in 1899 and where his sister Cai Chang, later first chair of the All-China Women's Federation, was born in 1900. The single-storey house of about 550 m², U-shaped around a main hall, side wings and a courtyard, carries a name board written by Deng Xiaoping in 1985; the family had to sell it in 1908.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zeng Guofan
rows.summary: The family seat of Zeng Guofan (1811–1872), the Qing statesman whose Xiang Army put down the Taiping Rebellion, at Heye in eastern Shuangfeng. Fuhou Hall, a mansion of over 9,000 m² behind a crescent pond, was enlarged for his family from 1865 and finished in 1875, and its four library buildings once held more than 300,000 volumes, one of the largest private libraries of modern China; his birthplace, the Baiyu Hall farmhouse, is also in Heye.

rows.name: Long March HQ of the Red 2nd Army Corps, Fengjia
rows.name_zh: 红二军团长征司令部旧址
rows.summary: A house called Zhuyuan in Shangtuan village, Fengjia town, where the Red 2nd Army Corps under He Long, some 9,000 troops, set up its headquarters after reaching Fengjia on 12 December 1935, a few weeks into the Long March that the 2nd and 6th Corps had begun from Sangzhi. The troops rested here and gathered grain, straw sandals and clothing with help from local people, and the restored house is open as a memorial site.

rows.name: Longshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested range on Lianyuan's southern border, a national forest park since 2007 centred on Yueping Peak (1,513 m), with forest cover of over 90% and seven scenic sections, among them the Feishuiya waterfall valley. Known as a 'mountain of medicinal herbs', it has on its summit the Medicine King Hall honouring Sun Simiao, the Tang physician said to have gathered herbs and written here, first built in the Tang and brought to its present form in 1887.

rows.name: Meijiang Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst national geopark of about 128 km² along the winding Mei River in north-western Lianyuan, opened to visitors from 1992: sheer limestone walls known as the Ten-li Painted Wall, the Three Rock Gates, natural bridges, two lakes, waterfalls and caves such as Xianren Cave, which stays at about 25°C and has a waterfall inside. Its six main areas are Guanyin Cliff, Cangjun Cave, Xianren Fu, Saihai Lake, Longquan Gorge and Dajiangkou, and visitors walk cliff paths or float down the river on rafts.

rows.name: Meishan Longgong Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave system by the Zi River in Youxi township, formed where the Taoxi stream sinks into the hills, with galleries stacked through some 80 m of height: flowstone and stalactites above, helictites and 'frost' crystals on old river sands, a great rubble pile called the Golden Mountain in the Water and stalagmite forests below. About 2,870 m have been explored, and the 1.9 km visitor route includes a 466 m stretch of underground river travelled by boat.

rows.name: Sanliandong Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area of gorges and ridges in Sanliandong village, Weishan township, in Xinhua County. It is laid out around two walking routes, one up a stream gorge called Bingquan Xia (Ice Spring Gorge) with pools and waterfalls, the other along the rocky Longji Feng (Dragon's Spine) ridge.

rows.name: Xinhua North Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal pagoda about 42 m tall, begun in 1834 on Huilong Hill on the west bank of the Zi River at Xinhua town. It stands on a granite base, with a body of grey brick and some stone, iron-tiled eaves and a cast-bronze finial.

rows.name: Ziquejie Rice Terraces
rows.summary: Rice terraces covering tens of thousands of mu on the mountains of Shuiche and Fengjia towns in western Xinhua, farmed for more than 2,000 years and watered entirely by natural seepage and spring flow, with no ponds or dams. They are listed as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System, a World Heritage Irrigation Structure and a national scenic area, and paths and viewpoints look over terraces climbing from the valleys to the ridges.

rows.name: Baishuidong Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national scenic area in Yantang Town, Xinshao County, with two main sections: Bailong Cave, known for its towering 'Southern Sky Pillar', a curtain of flowstone and an 'undersea world' chamber, and a walk through the Baishuidong gorge. The caves and waters here have drawn visitors since the Ming dynasty, and Qing writers left travel accounts of them.

rows.name: Baoqing Prefecture City Wall
rows.summary: The surviving north side of the walls of old Baoqing, today's Shaoyang, with the Qingfeng (north) gate, the Linjin gate and about 1.3 km of wall. The walls were rebuilt in 1372 and repaired in 1852; the other three sides were pulled down in 1939, during the war against Japan, to make it easier for residents to evacuate.

rows.name: Cai E's Former Residence
rows.summary: The farmhouse in Cai'e Township, Daxiang District, where Cai E, the general who led the 1915–16 National Protection War against Yuan Shikai's attempt to restore the monarchy, was born in 1882. The simple three-bay mud-brick house collapsed in 1950 and was rebuilt to its original form in 1991; a neighbouring house holds an exhibition on his life, and the surrounding Cai E hometown scenic area was rated 4A in 2021.

rows.name: Dankou Miao Script Stone Carvings
rows.summary: Stones carved with an old Miao script, other symbols and pictures, found in 2011 during a national heritage survey scattered over the field banks and hillsides around Douchongtou in Xian'e village, Dankou Town, Chengbu. Archaeologists identified the writing as Miao in 2014–16, most of it carved in the Ming and Qing dynasties, and 92 sites with carved stones or building foundations have since been recorded in the village. They are rare evidence of a written form of the Miao language, long thought to have had no script of its own.

rows.name: Dongkou Ancestral Halls
rows.summary: A group of ten clan ancestral halls and the Marshal Zhong Temple scattered across Dongkou County, built between the Ming dynasty and the Republican era, among them the halls of the Yang clans of Jintang and Qutang and of the Tan, Wang, Huang, Liao and Xiao families. They were listed together as a national monument in 2013, and the Qutang Yang hall also housed a section of the Whampoa Military Academy's second branch during the war against Japan.

rows.name: Former Command Post of the Seventh Red Army
rows.name_zh: 中国工农红军第七军指挥所旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngguó Gōng-Nóng Hóngjūn Dì-qī Jūn Zhǐhuīsuǒ Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The Long clan ancestral hall in Zhaishi, then the seat of Suining County, which the Seventh Red Army under Deng Xiaoping, Li Mingrui and Zhang Yunyi used as its headquarters after taking the town on 21 December 1930. Only the gatehouse of the old hall survived later demolition; the rebuilt two-storey courtyard reopened in November 2023 with displays recreating the commanders' rooms and meetings.

rows.name: Former Site of the Whampoa Military Academy Second Branch
rows.name_zh: 黄埔军校第二分校旧址
rows.summary: Buildings used by the second branch of the Whampoa Military Academy after it moved to Wugang in autumn 1938, during the war against Japan. The listed site comprises the Zhongshan Hall, the Faxiang Rock site and the former residence of General Li Minghao, the hall and the house restored by 2021, and a later listing added the Yin clan hall in neighbouring Dongkou County, quarters of the academy's 14th Officers' Corps.

rows.name: Huangsang Ecotourism Area
rows.summary: A forested area in south-western Suining County around the Huangsang National Nature Reserve, where forest covers more than 90% of the land. Its sights include a relict forest of long-bracted hemlock (Tsuga longibracteata), waterfalls, a sea of cloud on the high slopes and Shangbao, a Dong village on China's tentative list for World Heritage since 2012.

rows.name: Huxingshan Huayao Villages
rows.summary: A high mountain township in north-western Longhui, averaging about 1,350 m above sea level, that is home to the Huayao ('Flowery Yao'), a Yao group known for their cross-stitch embroidery and bright costumes. In villages such as Chongmudang, wooden houses stand among groves of ancient trees that the Huayao revere, the Datuo stone waterfall is nearby, and the cool summers draw visitors escaping the heat.

rows.name: Mount Langshan
rows.summary: A 108 km² area of red Danxia sandstone in Xinning County, with flat-topped mesas, free-standing pillars and walls of rock, sheer red cliffs and narrow slot canyons above the clear Fuyi River. It is one of the six areas inscribed together as the China Danxia World Heritage Site in 2010, and its zones include Bajiaozhai, Lajiao (Chilli) Peak, the narrow Tianyi Xiang passage, the Fuyi River, Zixiadong and Tianshengqiao.

rows.name: Shaoyang North Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey brick-and-stone pagoda on the north bank where the Zi and Shao rivers meet, built between 1573 and 1582 to improve the city's fengshui. Lotus patterns decorate its eaves and three stacked iron vases form the finial, one of which was shaken down during a Japanese air raid.

rows.name: Tangtian Wartime Lecture Institute
rows.summary: A late-Qing country villa built in 1877 for the official Xi Baotian at Tangtianshi in Shaoyang County, where in June 1938 the historian Lü Zhenyu, sent by the Communist educator Xu Teli, opened the Tangtian Wartime Lecture Institute; the Nationalist authorities closed it in April 1939. The villa survives as four rows of timber-framed buildings between fire walls, with sixteen blocks and more than sixty rooms.

rows.name: Wei Yuan's Former Residence
rows.summary: The birthplace of Wei Yuan (1794–1857), the late-Qing scholar whose Illustrated Treatise on the Maritime Kingdoms (Haiguo Tuzhi) urged China to learn from Western technology after the First Opium War and influenced reformers in Japan. The two-storey timber courtyard house in Xuetangwan village, Simenqian Town, dates from the early Qianlong era and is enclosed by a rammed-earth wall.

rows.name: Wugang City Wall
rows.summary: Surviving stretches of the old walls of Wugang, about 1.45 km of an original circuit of nearly 5.9 km, unusual for being built of large stone blocks on both faces rather than earth faced with brick. The walls were rebuilt in stone from 1371 under the Ming; four gates survive, and the Xuanfeng tower still stands over the southern Jichuan gate.

rows.name: Xiangjiao Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The distillery and visitor park of Hunan Xiangjiao Liquor, a baijiu maker that grew out of the Shaoyang wine factory founded in 1957. Tours show the traditional process, with grain fermented in old mud pits and the spirit aged in pottery jars, and visitors can blend their own liquor, taste several aroma styles and walk the landscaped grounds; it suits those curious about Chinese spirits.

rows.name: Yinjiatang Mansion
rows.summary: A vast family mansion in Qingshui village, Yangqiao Town, Shaodong, begun in 1823 by the rice-trading Shen brothers and known locally as 'the 108 rooms'. Laid out four halls deep and eleven rows wide around many small courtyards, it has carved beams and window frames, a family opera stage and an ancestral hall at the rear, and was restored from 2017.

rows.name: Yulong Caves
rows.summary: A group of limestone show caves in Chengbu County made up of five connected caves (Yulong, Baiyun, Hongxi, Yangjiao and Biyun) and a natural shaft called Luosi Well, with varied stalactite formations. The caves stay at about 18–23 °C all year, and the area was rated 4A in August 2026.

rows.name: Yunshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A mountain forest park just south of Wugang, an outlier of the Xuefeng range with seventy-one peaks rising to Zixiao Peak at 1,372.5 m, known for drifting cloud and cool summers. The Austrian botanist Heinrich von Handel-Mazzetti collected plants here in 1921, and eleven of the new species found are named after the mountain.

rows.name: Beiwusheng Guild Hall
rows.summary: A guild hall and temple to Guan Yu built around 1665 by merchants from five northern provinces (Shanxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Henan and Shandong) at the Eleventh Wharf on the Xiang River, when Xiangtan was one of the great trading towns of central China. Also called the Guansheng Hall, it is described by the city as the largest intact Guan Yu temple in Hunan, with a front courtyard, carved dragon stone columns and a statue of Guan Yu in the main hall.

rows.name: Dongshan Academy
rows.summary: A late-Qing academy at the foot of Dongtai Hill in Xiangxiang, founded in 1895 and finished in 1900, which in 1905 became a modern-style higher primary school; the young Mao Zedong was admitted in 1909, and the generals Chen Geng and Tan Zheng also studied here. Its buildings, largely as built, follow the Hunan academy plan, with a moat and stone bridge before the gate, three halls on the axis, five study wings on each side and a library, plus some Western touches; the classroom added in 1905, where Mao studied, survives. The academy is part of Dongshan School, still a working secondary school, and the historic area is open as a 4A scenic area.

rows.name: Former Residence of Mao Zedong, Shaoshan
rows.summary: The farmhouse at Shaoshanchong where Mao Zedong was born in 1893 and grew up: an earth-walled, U-shaped house of the central Hunan type, shared with a neighbouring family across the central hall, confiscated by the Nationalist government in 1929 and restored to its original form in 1950, with the family's bedrooms, kitchen and farm tools on show. It is the heart of the Shaoshan 5A scenic area, which also takes in the Mao Zedong Memorial Museum (opened 1964) with his personal belongings, the Mao clan ancestral hall and the Nan'an old village school, a square with a large bronze statue (1993), and Dishui Cave, a secluded villa compound built for Mao in 1960–62 about 4 km away, where he stayed in 1966. Shaoshan is one of the main destinations of Chinese 'red tourism'.

rows.name: Former Residence of Peng Dehuai
rows.summary: The family home of Peng Dehuai (1898–1974), the general who commanded the Chinese People's Volunteers in the Korean War and was defence minister from 1954 until he was purged after clashing with Mao Zedong over the Great Leap Forward at the 1959 Lushan Conference. The mud-brick, tile-roofed house of 17 rooms at Wushi, which Peng paid to rebuild in 1925, stands about 30 m from the site of the thatched cottage where he was born. Around it the Peng Dehuai Memorial Hall, a 4A scenic area of about 30 ha, adds a biographical exhibition and a Korean War hall, a bronze statue, the Dehuai Pavilion and his tomb.

rows.name: Former Residence of Qi Baishi
rows.summary: The birthplace and early home of Qi Baishi (1864–1957), the painter known for his playful shrimps, mice and birds, at Xingdou Pond in Baishi town, Xiangtan County, where he lived for 36 years. It is a modest earth-walled, thatched farmhouse of the 1850s in the central Hunan style, five bays wide, with a wooded hill behind and a lotus pond in front, the scenery of many of his early sketches.

rows.name: Maohu Water Village
rows.summary: A leisure park on Dongshan Island, a sandbar in the Lian River below Dongtai Hill on the eastern edge of Xiangxiang, built around the theme of Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army, whose river navy, by local legend, trained here. Visitors cross the 128 m 'Xiang Army Bridge' hung with plaques of the army's leaders' writings, can take a river trip on a full-size replica of the gunboat Weijing, and see an old ferry boat linked to stories of the young Mao Zedong.

rows.name: Mount Zhao
rows.summary: A 185 m hill on the east bank of the Xiang River at the Xiangtan–Changsha border, whose misty views after rain were painted by Mi Fu as 'Mountain Market in Clearing Mist', one of the classic Eight Views of Xiaoxiang; legend says King Zhao of Zhou drowned in the pool below. Zhaoshan Temple, first built in the Tang, stands on the summit with wide views of the river, Guanyin Temple lies at the foot, and a Qing granite path about 13 km long crosses the front and back hills.

rows.name: Panlong Grand View Garden
rows.summary: A large privately developed flower park in Yuetang District, Xiangtan, in the green belt between Changsha, Zhuzhou and Xiangtan, best known for an azalea garden with about 800 varieties in some 150,000 pots that flowers in March and April. Seasonal displays follow through the year, with a rose garden in late spring, a lotus pond and grape picking in summer, and shows and night events added in 2026.

rows.name: Shuifumiao Reservoir (Shuifu Scenic Area)
rows.summary: A large irrigation reservoir on the Lian River, built in 1958–63, whose main body lies in western Xiangxiang, with the dam at Xikou in Shuangfeng County; its winding arms and dozens of wooded islands form a national wetland park and the Shuifu scenic area. Boats leave from the scenic-area wharf for trips among the islands, where egrets gather, and it is a popular weekend outing for families driving from Xiangtan and Loudi.

rows.name: Yintian Yinhe Scenic Area
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area along the Shao River at Yintian town in eastern Shaoshan, rated 4A in 2026 after about ten years of water-environment works turned an irrigation channel and the old river into a green corridor. It mixes riverside paths, farmland views and water-conservancy works with red-history study visits and rural leisure, and suits a stop on the way between Xiangtan and the Mao sites at Shaoshan.

rows.name: Zhaoshan City Seaside Water Park
rows.name_zh: 昭山城市海景水上乐园
rows.summary: A summer water park of about 18 ha in the Zhaoshan area between Changsha, Xiangtan and Zhuzhou, themed as a tropical beach, with an artificial sand beach and wave pool, large slides, children's water-play areas and an indoor sun-sheltered hall. It suits families on hot days and opens only in the summer season.

rows.name: Aizhai Bridge, Shibadong Village and Dehang Gorge
rows.name_zh: 矮寨·十八洞·德夯大峡谷
rows.summary: A 5A scenic area west of Jishou that joins three places: the Aizhai suspension bridge, opened in 2012, whose 1,176 m main span carries the G65 expressway more than 330 m above the Dehang gorge; the Dehang canyon itself, with cliffs, stone peaks, Miao villages and the 216 m Liusha waterfall; and Shibadong, a Miao village in Huayuan County. Shibadong is known in China as the place where the 'targeted poverty alleviation' policy was first proposed, and UN Tourism named it one of its Best Tourism Villages in 2024.

rows.name: Biancheng (Chadong)
rows.summary: A riverside town on the Qingshui River where Hunan, Guizhou and Chongqing meet; formerly called Chadong, it was renamed Biancheng in 2005 after Shen Congwen's novella Border Town (Biancheng), which is set here. Visitors walk the stone lanes, cross the river on the hand-pulled cable ferry, stand at the three-province boundary marker and visit Cuicui Island, with a 9 m marble statue of the novel's heroine by the artist Huang Yongyu.

rows.name: Bu'ermen
rows.summary: A rocky stretch of the Mengdong River just south of Yongshun county town, listed for an archaeological site of the Shang and Zhou periods and now a national forest park. Its name comes from the Buddhist idea of 'the gate of non-duality', and the park has inscriptions carved into the cliffs, a Guanyin rock shrine, temples and a hot spring.

rows.name: Fenghuang Giant Panda Park
rows.summary: A giant panda park about 7 km west of Fenghuang old town, opened in July 2020 with eight pandas brought from the Dujiangyan Qingchengshan base of the China Conservation and Research Centre for the Giant Panda in Sichuan. The pandas are kept in glass-fronted indoor halls and outdoor enclosures, and the park is mainly visited by families staying in Fenghuang.

rows.name: Former Site of the Hunan–Hubei–Sichuan–Guizhou Revolutionary Base (Tawo)
rows.name_zh: 塔卧湘鄂川黔革命根据地旧址
rows.summary: Seven old courtyard compounds in Tawo Town, Yongshun, that housed the provincial Communist Party committee, revolutionary committee, military district, party school, a branch of the Red Army school, a radio station and an arsenal of the Hunan–Hubei–Sichuan–Guizhou base area, set up by the Second and Sixth Red Army Groups under He Long and Ren Bishi in 1934–35. A memorial hall, a martyrs' monument and a cemetery stand beside the old buildings, which belong to the same national monument as the base's first headquarters in Zhangjiajie and its later sites at Ciyantang and Xinglongjie in Longshan County, which have their own memorial hall.

rows.name: Furong Ancient Town
rows.summary: A Tujia town in Yongshun County built on cliffs above a waterfall that drops into the You River; formerly called Wangcun, it took its present name in 2007 after the film Hibiscus Town was shot here. It also keeps the Xizhou Bronze Pillar of 940, an eight-sided column inscribed with the truce between the Chu ruler Ma Xifan and the local chief Peng Shichou, which was moved here in 1971 when the Fengtan hydropower dam was built and is now displayed in the town's folk-customs museum, a former mission chapel of 1931.

rows.name: Gumiao River Hundred Waterfalls Gorge
rows.summary: A 12.8 km gorge on the Gumiao River in Huayuan County, a river the local Miao regard as their mother river, with more than a hundred waterfalls large and small. About 4.8 km of the gorge, with some twenty waterfalls, is open to visitors along cliff walkways and riverside paths, a walk of about an hour and a half.

rows.name: Hongshilin Red Stone Forest
rows.summary: A national geopark in Guzhang County where columns of red carbonate rock, laid down on an ancient sea floor some 450 million years ago, form a stone forest with a core area of more than 20 km². The rock looks reddish-brown in sunshine and turns dark when wet, so the forest changes colour with the weather.

rows.name: Huangsiqiao Old Fort
rows.summary: A small garrison town about 24 km west of Fenghuang, enclosed by a complete ring of blue-grey stone walls with battlements and gate towers that can be walked round in about ten minutes. It is one of the sites of the national monument 'Fenghuang Old Fortresses', which also covers the Shujiatang and Lahao fortified villages and the Wangpotun outpost, built to control the Miao frontier; local tradition dates the fort to the Tang dynasty, while the listing dates the fortifications to the Qing.

rows.name: Laosicheng
rows.summary: The ruined capital of the Peng clan, the Tujia chieftains (tusi) who ruled the Yongshun area from the 10th century until the Qing ended their rule in the 1720s; the walled city by the Lingxi River was their seat from the Southern Song onwards.
