Excavated palace and office quarters, streets, city walls, chieftains' tombs and temple sites survive, and the city has been one of the three Tusi Sites on the World Heritage List since 2015; a museum nearby explains the finds.

rows.name: Liye Ancient Town
rows.summary: A town on the You River in southern Longshan County, where excavations in 2002 uncovered a walled town of the Warring States period and, in one of its wells, more than 36,000 inscribed Qin-dynasty slips. The Liye Qin Slips Museum, opened in 2010, displays the slips with bronzes and pottery, and the excavated city site lies close by in the old town.

rows.name: Pushi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A former river port on the Yuan River in Luxi County that thrived in the Ming and Qing dynasties, when it was nicknamed 'Little Nanjing'. Its listed old buildings include the Wanshou Palace guild hall, the ancestral halls and family compounds of the Li and Ji clans, a Li family academy, old merchant houses and shops, an escort agency and an embroidery tower, and the town is regarded as the birthplace of Chenhe high-pitched opera (Chenhe Gaoqiang).

rows.name: Qianzhou Old Town
rows.summary: An old walled town on the Wanrong River in southern Jishou, the prefecture capital, with stone-paved lanes, old gates and a riverside street. Its listed monument is the Confucian Temple, founded in 1729, burnt during a Miao uprising in the 1790s and rebuilt from 1801; after losses in the Cultural Revolution only the double-eaved Dacheng Hall, the semicircular pool and its bridge survived, and the temple was restored in 2007, with two side halls now holding exhibitions on the war against Japan and on notable people of Xiangxi.

rows.name: Qiliang Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave at the foot of a cliff in Qiliangqiao village, Tuojiang town, a few kilometres north of Fenghuang old town. Inside are an underground stream and halls of stalactites and other formations, and it is easily combined with a stay in Fenghuang.

rows.name: Rebala Tujia Villages
rows.summary: A cluster of Tujia villages along the Laoche River in Miao'ertan Town, Longshan County, with wooden houses, a large covered bridge and the tall Chongtian tower; Rebala and neighbouring Liuhe were among the first villages named Chinese traditional villages in 2012. The area holds Tujia brocade-weaving events and was rated 4A in 2026.

rows.name: Taiping Mountain, Longshan
rows.summary: A forested mountain park about 4 km from Longshan county town, long a Buddhist site with temple halls on its slopes. Springs from the karst hills gather in a six-tiered waterfall more than 30 m high that falls into a pool ringed by peaks, and after rain the mountain is known for its sea of cloud.

rows.name: Wulong Mountain Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A karst canyon in Guitang Town, Longshan County, covering about 41 km² of the Wulongshan National Geopark and riddled with caves, of which surveys have counted 212. The main sights are Feihu (Flying Tiger) Cave, Remi Cave, Lianyu Cave, Shihua Cave and the Pidu River.

rows.name: Xiangxi Ethnic Culture Park
rows.summary: A cultural complex in the Xiangxi high-tech zone of Jishou, planned from 2015 as a showcase of the prefecture's Tujia and Miao heritage. Its centrepiece is the Xiangxi Prefecture Museum, in a new building opened in 2017, whose five permanent exhibitions cover the region's history, folk customs and revolutionary history and the intangible heritage of the Tujia and Miao, a useful introduction before travelling on to the old towns.

rows.name: Yuanshui Painted Cliffs
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area at Baisha, the county town of Luxi, where cliffs known as the 'ten-li painted wall' line the Yuan River, a stretch of river associated with the writing of Shen Congwen. Visitors come for walks and water-based activities along the cliffs, and the area was rated 4A in July 2025.

rows.name: Anhua Tea-Horse Road Scenic Area
rows.summary: A gorge-and-forest scenic area in Jiangnan town, eastern Anhua, built around stretches of the old mountain trade road on which Anhua's dark tea was carried out by horse caravans; the county presents it as the starting point of the Hunan section of the Ten-Thousand-Li Tea Road. Visitors hike the old road and cliff-side and riverside paths through a deep valley past relics of the caravan trade and Meishan folk culture, a good day for walkers.

rows.name: Baihuazhai Tea Garden
rows.summary: A tea-and-countryside scenic area around Baihuazhai hill above Taoxi town in Anhua, centred on an organic tea plantation and an eco-farm that also grows rice, fruit and vegetables. Since 2021 the area has been developed as a combined tea, culture and wellness project, and it suits a rural outing for those interested in Anhua's tea.

rows.name: Changjiao Massacre Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The memorial site in Changjiao town, Nan County, for the Changjiao massacre of 9–12 May 1943, in which Japanese troops killed some 30,000 Chinese civilians and soldiers trapped between the rivers of the Dongting Lake plain, according to Chinese surveys. A memorial monument of 1986 and a memorial hall of 2008, refitted in 2015, stand in a small lakeside park, close to the 'thousand-person pit' where victims were buried.

rows.name: Chaxiang Huahai Flower Park
rows.summary: A flower park in Anhua County laid out beside the large Chaxiang Huahai resettlement community, built for villagers moved out of the mountains under the poverty-relief programme, and opened to visitors in April 2020. Seasonal flower beds and a viewing platform make it a local leisure spot, and it hosts events such as the county's spring dark-tea picking festival.

rows.name: Covered Bridges of Anhua (Yongxi Bridge)
rows.summary: A group of roofed timber 'wind-and-rain' bridges, 29 of them spread over 17 townships of Anhua County, of which eleven were listed together in 2013. The best known is the Yongxi Bridge in Xitan village, Jiangnan town, built in 1878 and the oldest surviving covered bridge in the county; others in good condition include the Sixian, Madu, Shiyi and Yanzi bridges.

rows.name: Luowen Graffiti Village
rows.summary: A farming village in Wuzui township, Nan County, on a spit of land between the waterways of the Dongting Lake plain, whose houses are painted with large colourful graffiti murals and which is ringed by flower fields, best known for rapeseed blossom in early spring. Once an ordinary village, it has been named a Hunan model 'beautiful village' and a national key rural-tourism village, with a music square and farm restaurants for day visitors.

rows.name: Lutheran Mission Buildings, Yiyang
rows.summary: Four buildings put up by the Lutheran mission in Yiyang between 1904 and 1924 in a mix of Chinese and Western styles: the teaching building and two teachers' houses of the former Xinyi (Lutheran) University on Taohualun, and a pastor's house at Wumafang across the Zi River. The college was one of Hunan's well-known mission schools of its day, and the buildings were restored in 2019–20.

rows.name: Meicheng Confucian and Martial Temples
rows.summary: Anhua's old Confucian temple and its neighbouring Martial Temple in Meicheng town, listed together in 2019. The Confucian temple, founded in 1072 and rebuilt in 1822, keeps a lingxing gate more than 10 m high, a half-moon pool and a double-eaved Dacheng Hall roofed in yellow glazed tiles, and the young Mao Zedong stayed in a side room by its gate in 1917 and 1925.

rows.name: Meishan Culture Park
rows.summary: A privately built culture park in Xianxi town, eastern Anhua, begun in 2007 to present the history, customs and folk art of the old Meishan region of central Hunan. Visitors walk past a village gate, the Wan family compound, an old opera stage, stilt houses and a covered bridge to a Meishan folk museum, and a small exhibition recalls the young Mao Zedong's two study tours through Anhua; tea gardens and orchards surround it.

rows.name: Qingxi Village (Zhou Libo's Home Village)
rows.summary: The village in Xielingang town, Heshan District, on the southern outskirts of Yiyang where the writer Zhou Libo was born in 1908 and later lived while writing about country life, and which is presented as the real-life setting of his 1958 novel Great Changes in a Mountain Village (山乡巨变). His family house, a timber courtyard home of 28 rooms built in 1788, is the centrepiece, with an old-style street built nearby, a digital exhibition, writers' reading rooms and a hall of books signed by contemporary authors among the fields.

rows.name: Qingyun Cave (Yunshang Jiuge)
rows.summary: A natural limestone cave in Maluxi village, Malu town, in western Anhua County, reopened in April 2023 after redevelopment by a private tourism company. Inside, projection mapping, glasses-free 3D screens and a holographic film tell a fantasy story based on Qu Yuan's poem cycle the Nine Songs among the cave's natural formations.

rows.name: Qujiang Tea Garden
rows.summary: A tea garden of more than 500 mu (about 33 ha) in Daan village, Qujiang town, in the hills of western Anhua, one of the historic sources of Anhua dark tea and listed as a national heritage site in 2019. Besides the tea bushes, it keeps timber farmhouses set along the stream and the foot of the hills, old paths, wells and inscribed steles from the tea trade.

rows.name: Taohuajiang Bamboo Forest
rows.summary: A large bamboo forest on the edge of Taojiang county town, which the county presents as one of China's ten great 'bamboo seas', with more than 50,000 mu (about 33 km²) of continuous bamboo. Walking routes and shuttle buses lead through the groves past a bamboo culture museum, the Tianwen Academy and Jinpen Temple, making it an easy green half-day out from Yiyang.

rows.name: Tianyi Muguo Wood Art Park
rows.summary: A wood-art park by Yuxing Lake in the Yuxingshan area of Yiyang's Eastern New District, opened in September 2018 by a Zhuhai company and presented as a 'world wood culture museum'. Its halls display large root and wood carvings, including scenes from classic novels such as Journey to the West and Dream of the Red Chamber, and one hall is given over to wood carvings of the Long March; it suits a couple of hours for anyone interested in carving.

rows.name: Yiyang Olympic Park
rows.summary: A sports park in Heshan District on the south side of Yiyang, built for the 2002 Hunan Provincial Games, with a 30,000-seat stadium, a 5,000-seat arena, a swimming hall, outdoor pools and public fitness grounds. It was the main venue of the 15th Hunan Provincial Games, which opened there in September 2026, and is otherwise a local leisure and sports space rather than a sightseeing attraction.

rows.name: Yuntai Mountain, Anhua
rows.summary: A tea-growing mountain in Malu town, western Anhua, whose top is a basin of about 9 km² rising to 998 m and often wrapped in cloud, known locally as 'the plain on the mountain'. A sightseeing cable car climbs to tea-garden viewpoints, a glass walkway and glass suspension bridge, a rainbow slide, Longquan Cave, Shenxian Rock and a folk-culture village, and the summit is a favourite place to watch sunrise over a sea of cloud.

rows.name: Zhenyan Academy
rows.summary: An academy founded by Hu Linyi, a Qing official and leader of the Xiang Army, and completed in the 1860s, which became a school in 1905 and was rebuilt on its original site in Heshan District, opening to the public on 31 December 2023. The 1.4-hectare complex of rebuilt and new halls includes a Dacheng Hall, a lecture hall, a library, a memorial shrine, a pavilion and a garden, with exhibitions on the academy and the Zhenyan school that grew from it.

rows.name: Zijinwan Happy Kingdom
rows.summary: An amusement park on the east side of the Taohuajiang bamboo forest outside Taojiang county town, with fairground rides and play areas aimed at families with children. It is a local family day out rather than a sight in itself.

rows.name: Chaoyang Rock
rows.summary: A riverside cliff and cave on the west bank of the Xiao River in Lingling, named 'Facing the Morning Sun' in 765 by the Tang poet-official Yuan Jie, who wrote an inscription and a poem for it, and one of the classic Eight Views of Yongzhou. Its walls carry about 150 inscriptions from the Tang onwards, including a record of a visit by Zhou Dunyi in 1066 and a later carving of Liu Zongyuan's poem 'The Old Fisherman', and the site is now a small park.

rows.name: Chen Shuxiang Red Culture Park
rows.summary: A memorial park at Guitou village, Meihua town, Dao County, built to commemorate Chen Shuxiang, commander of the Red Army's 34th Division, and the soldiers of his division. The 34th formed the rearguard of the Central Red Army at the Battle of the Xiang River in late 1934; cut off on the east bank, the survivors fought back into southern Hunan, where Chen was wounded and captured in Dao County on 9 December and took his own life the next day. The memorial hall presents documents, objects and reconstructed scenes, and the grounds hold Chen's tomb, a tomb of 34th Division soldiers and a monument.

rows.name: Danyan Cave Inscriptions
rows.summary: A cave south of Lingling, also called Danshan Rock, whose walls bear some 200 recorded inscriptions, three-quarters of them from the Song dynasty, by visitors including Zhou Dunyi, Huang Tingjian and Yang Wanli. Legend links it with Zhou Zhenshi, a Qin-dynasty recluse said to have lived in the cave, and its 'Autumn Moon at Danyan', when moonlight falls through an opening in the roof at the Mid-Autumn Festival, is one of the Eight Views of Yongzhou.

rows.name: Dongshan Hill & Lingling Confucian and Martial Temples
rows.summary: The wooded hill inside the old city of Lingling, opened as a park in 2018, which gathers several of Yongzhou's oldest buildings: the Confucian Temple, whose double-eaved great hall with yellow glazed tiles and dragon-carved marble columns dates from 1775, and the neighbouring Martial Temple, whose opera stage is used for performances. Also on the hill are Fahua Temple, founded in the Tang and long known as Gaoshan Temple, where Liu Zongyuan once lodged, and the Lütian Hermitage, marking where the monk-calligrapher Huaisu is said to have practised on banana leaves. The old East Gate, Huaisu's inkstone-washing pond and a stele of his 'Thousand Character Classic' were restored when the park was built.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Da
rows.summary: The family home in Caishi town, Lengshuitan, of Li Da (1890–1966), the Marxist philosopher and educator who was one of the founders of the Chinese Communist Party and later president of Wuhan University. Born at Lanjiaoshan in what was then Lingling County, he studied in Japan before returning in 1920; the house is a national heritage site, with an exhibition hall on his life showing photographs, documents and personal belongings.

rows.name: General's Mansion, Xujiaqiao
rows.summary: An official-style residence in Xujiaqiao village, Shuzipu township, south-west of Lingling, begun around the end of the Yuan and the start of the Ming dynasty. Facing west, it consists of two parallel rows of buildings, each four courtyards deep, covering about 2,500 m², and was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Goulan Yao Village
rows.summary: A walled Yao village in Lanxi township, Jiangyong, founded in the Ming dynasty and spread over about 6 km², defended by stone walls, watch houses and gate towers. Within them stand some 30 listed structures, including ancestral halls, temples, an academy, shops, covered bridges, pavilions and an old paved road, among more than 300 Ming and Qing houses. The village keeps its own customs, notably the 'Xini' (mud-washing) festival.

rows.name: Guangli Bridge
rows.summary: A Qing covered bridge, also called the Flower Bridge, over the Dongxi River at Zixishi town in Dong'an County, built in 1773 and repaired in 1876. Three stone arches carry a 36.8 m timber gallery of 17 bays with benches for travellers, crowned by a triple-eaved pavilion in the middle and archway-style pavilions at each end, their ridges decorated with figures, qilin, dragons and fish.

rows.name: Guizailing Ritual Site
rows.summary: A low hill in the south of Dao County scattered with thousands of small carved stone figures, mostly between about 30 cm and 1 m tall and including officials, soldiers and pregnant women, at a site usually described as a place of ritual. The local name means 'Hill of the Ghost Children', and the State Council listing dates the site to between the Song and Qing dynasties.

rows.name: Hanlin Ancestral Hall, Dong'antou
rows.summary: An ancestral hall in Dong'antou village, Wanjing town, begun in 1736 to honour Li Fu, a Ming-dynasty metropolitan graduate, and covering about 6,700 m² with its forecourt. Behind a crescent pond stand a memorial archway of three bays and eight columns under double eaves, carved and painted with birds, flowers, figures and paired dragons, then a gate hall, opera stage, side wings, upper and lower halls and a sedan-chair pavilion shaped like an eight-bearer palanquin.

rows.name: Hanlin Ancestral Hall, Jiu'anbei
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Li clan in Jiu'anbei, a village at the foot of the Jiuyi Mountains whose families all share the surname, named after the clan's Song-dynasty scholars who reached the Hanlin Academy. Behind a half-moon terrace by a pond, a wooden memorial gateway of four columns and three roofs, its main roof carried on seven tiers of bracket sets and flanked by a pair of stone lions, leads to the gate, an eight-column wooden opera stage and five halls in sequence around five courtyards, with carved animals and flowers on the beams. Tradition dates the lower halls to the Song and the gateway to the Ming, with the upper halls added under the Qing, and villagers still use it for banquets, meetings and festival performances.

rows.name: He Family Mansion, Baojing
rows.summary: A Qing-to-Republican mansion complex in Baojing village, Dayu town, in the south of Jianghua, begun in the early Qing by the He clan ancestor He Yingqi. Its gate towers, halls, a galleried 'running-horse' building, the Mingyuan Tower and other houses cover about 11,000 m², with the 500 m² He clan ancestral hall on the north side, and many carved plaques from the Qing survive.

rows.name: Hu Family Mansion, Shanmuqiao
rows.summary: A clan compound in Shanmuqiao village, Youtingxu town, in the east of Lingling, begun in the early Qing. Its mainly brick-and-timber buildings consist of a central public hall flanked by 40 side houses, with a total floor area of about 4,800 m², and it was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Huang Ancestral Hall, Huxi Village
rows.summary: The Qing-dynasty clan hall of the Huangs at the centre of Huxi, a village of about a thousand people, most of them Huangs who settled here at the end of the Ming beside an old market that straddles the Lanshan–Ningyuan county line. Entered through three gateways, the hall has an opera stage just inside the door facing the ancestral shrine across its lower and upper halls, and more than 50 old houses with painted eaves, carved windows and inscribed lintels spread out around it. Red Army units camped in the village twice during the Long March in the autumn of 1934.

rows.name: Huaqiangu Flower Valley & Moon Lake, Shuangpai
rows.summary: A modern flower-valley and lakeside leisure area at Xiadeng village on the edge of Longbo, Shuangpai's county town, created as part of the county's 'Longbo International Slow City' rural-tourism scheme. It was rated 3A in 2019 and raised to 4A at the end of 2023; expect landscaped flower gardens and a lake for a stroll rather than a natural or historic sight.

rows.name: Huilong Pagoda
rows.summary: A brick-and-stone pagoda on a rock outcrop on the east bank of the Xiao River at the northern edge of Lingling's old town, built in 1584 by the local official Lü Huo to protect the city from floods. About 38 m tall and octagonal, it has a ground storey of bluestone blocks, green-glazed eaves and seven storeys inside, where the stairs change direction at every level between its double walls. It has been a national heritage site since 2013, and its reflection in the river at sunset is a well-known local view.

rows.name: Li Ancestral Hall, Shenxia
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Li clan in Shenxia village, Lengshui town, east of Ningyuan county town, begun in 1753 and finished the following year. The hall covers about 1,250 m² and is one of two Ningyuan clan halls added to the national heritage list in 2019.

rows.name: Lianxi, Hometown of Zhou Dunyi
rows.summary: Loutian village in Qingtang town, Dao County, birthplace of the Northern Song philosopher Zhou Dunyi (1017–1073), a founder of Neo-Confucianism whose sobriquet Lianxi is the name of the stream at his home. Its cluster of Ming and Qing buildings is protected, and the village has a memorial hall, the Lianxi Academy and a square, with lotus fields that recall his essay 'On the Love of the Lotus' and flower in summer. The Moon Cave (Yueyan), another sight linked with Zhou, lies about 13 km to the west.

rows.name: Liuzi Temple & Liu Zongyuan Cultural Area
rows.name_zh: 柳子庙·柳宗元文化旅游区
rows.pinyin: Liǔzǐ Miào · Liǔ Zōngyuán Wénhuà Lǚyóuqū
rows.summary: A riverside quarter on the west bank of the Xiao River in Lingling, the old town of Yongzhou, built around the places where the Tang writer Liu Zongyuan lived for ten years in exile from 805. At its centre is Liuzi Temple, founded in 1056 and moved in 1144 to its present site where the Yu Stream meets the Xiao; the three-courtyard hall with its opera stage dates from an 1877 rebuilding and holds the 'Lizi Stele', a text by Han Yu written out by Su Shi. The old Liuzi Street, the Yu Stream and the pools and hills Liu described in his 'Eight Records of Yongzhou' make up the rest of the area.

rows.name: Long Family Compound
rows.summary: A village of the Long clan at Jiantou town in Xintian County, set against hills on three sides, whose Ming-to-Republican houses follow a plan described as 'three halls, nine light wells, 24 lanes and 48 houses'. The grey-brick buildings, with stepped fire walls, carved woodwork and painted eaves, carry 128 couplets on doorways and walls, each in a different calligraphic hand, on themes of farming, study and a quiet life away from office. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and the village is now a scenic area with flower fields round it.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Emperor Shun, Jiuyi Mountain
rows.summary: The temple-mausoleum of Shun, the legendary sage-king whom the Records of the Grand Historian say died on a tour of the south and was buried at Jiuyi, set below Shunyuan Peak in the Jiuyi Mountains. Moved here in 1371 and rebuilt several times, it was restored between 1985 and 1998 with a gate, sacrificial halls, a spirit way of stone figures and some thirty Qing stelae recording imperial sacrifices, and the ceremony to Shun held here is national intangible heritage. About 3 km south, at Yuguan Rock, the excavated foundations of the earlier Tang and Song temple form an archaeological park beside cliff carvings, among them a large 'Jiuyi Shan' inscription by the Southern Song writer Fang Xinru.

rows.name: Ningyuan Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county Confucian temple and school of Ningyuan, founded in the Tang and moved to this site in the south-west of the county town in 965, with the present buildings dating from a rebuilding of 1873–1882. Laid out on a north–south axis over about 10,000 m², it runs from a screen wall and crescent pond through the Lingxing and Dacheng gates to the Dacheng Hall and the Chongsheng shrine, flanked by memorial archways, side halls, a scripture pavilion and the Minglun lecture hall.

rows.name: Qianjiadong, Yao Ancestral Homeland
rows.summary: A group of three mountain basins north of Jiangyong county town, covering about 200 km², which Yao communities in southern China, South-East Asia and beyond know from their manuscript histories as the homeland their twelve clans were forced to leave in 1305. Scholars meeting in Jiangyong in 2002 identified this valley as that homeland, and it now has a Pan Wang (ancestor king) temple and square, old Yao temples and tombs, and forest scenery including the Dabo waterfall.

rows.name: Sangonglei Waterfalls
rows.summary: A chain of waterfalls on a forest stream in the core of Jindong National Forest Park, in the Jindong district that holds Hunan's largest state forest farm. A boardwalk of about 3.2 km follows the stream past more than 20 falls and pools, and a streamside café and paddling area opened in 2026; the district is also known for river rafting and forest homestays.

rows.name: Shanggantang Village
rows.summary: A Zhou-clan village in Xiacengpu town, Jiangyong, on the site of the Han-dynasty county seat of Xiemu, where the family has lived since 828 and around 200 Ming and Qing houses survive. At the village entrance the three-arched Buying Bridge, first built in 1126, stands beside the four-storey Wenchang Pavilion of 1620, and the Yuebei Pavilion cliff nearby is covered with inscriptions, among them the characters for loyalty, filial piety, integrity and honour, each nearly 2 m tall, attributed to Wen Tianxiang.

rows.name: Shidongyuan: Tao Zhu's Birthplace & Longxi Li Family Compound
rows.summary: A scenic area in Panshi town, eastern Qiyang, centred on Shidongyuan, the village where the senior Communist Party leader Tao Zhu (1908–1969) was born, with his former residence, the Shidongyuan reservoir and the nearby Longxi Li Family Compound. The Li compound, a large group of Ming and Qing courtyard houses listed as a national heritage site in 2013, is admired for its carved and painted beams.

rows.name: Shude Villa (Former Residence of Tang Shengzhi)
rows.summary: A country estate at Zhaojiajing village, Luhongshi town, built in 1927 by Tang Shengzhi, the Hunan general who commanded the defence of Nanjing in 1937 and later joined the 1949 Hunan peace uprising. Its brick, stone and timber buildings combine a symmetrical southern-Hunan layout with Western details and include a gatehouse, living and reception blocks, a watchtower, guard rooms, a library and an octagonal pavilion, set in gardens with ponds.

rows.name: Shunhuang Mountain
rows.summary: A forested range on Dong'an County's western border with Xinning County, protected as a national forest park, whose main peak rises to 1,882 m. Its name comes from the legend that the sage-king Shun hunted and lived on the mountain during his tour of the south. At Damiaokou on its eastern foot is Shunhuang Cave, found in 1984 by a villager gathering firewood: more than 700 m of passages and chambers hung with stalactites and lit with coloured lights.

rows.name: Suiyuan Lou Complex, Tantian Village
rows.summary: A group of Qing-dynasty courtyard houses built in the late 1830s in Tantian, a village whose families are all surnamed He and, by their genealogy, descend from a settlement founded in the early 11th century. Three parallel compounds of three courtyards each, with wooden gate towers and stepped 'horse-head' fire walls, are divided by narrow flagstone lanes shut by heavy wooden doors; the gateways carry painted fret patterns and opera scenes, painted murals and clay figures survive inside, and a four-courtyard guest house stands in front. Around them the village keeps a flagstone post road, two old stone arch bridges, wells and the He clan hall.

rows.name: Wuxi Cliff Inscriptions (Wuxi Stele Forest)
rows.summary: Cliffs on the west bank of the Xiang River where the Wuxi stream flows in, about 2 km west of Qiyang, carved since the Tang dynasty with around 500 poems, records and pieces of calligraphy by figures including Yan Zhenqing, Huang Tingjian and Mi Fu. The best known is the 'Ode to the Restoration of the Great Tang', composed by Yuan Jie and written by Yan Zhenqing, prized as the 'three wonders' cliff for its text, calligraphy and stone. A digital museum of the carvings opened in the visitor centre in December 2024.

rows.name: Xiaguan Ancient Village
rows.summary: A large old farming village in Wanjing town, Ningyuan, which clan records say was founded in 499 and which now spans four administrative villages along streams below the Jiuyi Mountains. It is known as the home of Li He (808–873), remembered as the first top-ranked graduate of the imperial examinations from Hunan, and its stone-flagged lanes, small bridges and old houses are presented as a scenic area. Villagers link the place with 'yezi xi', an old leaf-card game, and card and mahjong tables are a common sight along its street.

rows.name: Xianggui Ancient Road, Yongzhou Section
rows.summary: Part of the old overland route between the Xiang River basin and Lingnan, also called the Xiao–He road, which leaves Dao County on two branches, through Jianghua and through Jiangyong, to Fuchuan and Hezhou in Guangxi. Widened under the Qin and in use until the early 1950s, it is protected as some 30 relics along the way: old town and barracks sites, bridges, roadside pavilions, a shop street, villages and stretches of paving. Among the restored points are the Hailong Temple in Dao County, the Lingshan Hermitage and a memorial rest pavilion in Jiangyong, and a pavilion-and-bridge pair and the Huifeng and Yuquan pavilions in Jianghua, so a visit means driving between scattered sites rather than one walk.

rows.name: Yanghua Rock Inscriptions
rows.summary: A south-facing limestone cliff and cave below Huishan hill at Zhuyuanzhai village, just east of Jianghua county town, carved with some 40 inscriptions from the Tang to the Qing, 38 of them still legible. The best known is the 'Inscription on Yanghua Rock' composed in 766 by Yuan Jie, prefect of Daozhou, and cut on the rock by the county magistrate Qu Lingwen in three scripts side by side (clerical, seal and the older zhou script). The cliff was consolidated and the carvings repaired in 2017.

rows.name: Yangmingshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A mountain forest park in north-eastern Shuangpai County, a national forest park since 1992, rising to about 1,625 m. Its upper slopes carry more than 100,000 mu (some 6,700 ha) of wild azaleas that flower in spring, among forest with rare conifers such as Chinese Douglas fir and southern yew. The developed areas take in the azalea slopes, Wanshou Temple, Wanhe Lake and the source of the Xiaohuang River, and the park also has sites linked to the Red Army's Sixth Army Group on the Long March.

rows.name: Yaoshan Water Town (China Love Town), Shuikou
rows.summary: A tourism district in Shuikou, Jianghua, a new town built from 2016 for about 15,000 people moved from the Cengtianhe reservoir area and from poor mountain villages, which the county promotes as a Yao-themed 'China Love Town'. Its water street (Yaodu Shuijie), opened in 2019, mixes new Yao-style stilt houses with Huizhou-style courtyards, shops and food stalls and is lit up in the evenings, with the legend of the Yao ancestor Pan Wang and the third princess as its theme. The town also stages events such as group weddings in Yao dress and part of the county's Pan Wang Festival.

rows.name: Yongzhou Forest Botanical Garden
rows.summary: Yongzhou's forest botanical garden, laid out since 2013 on the grounds of the city's forestry research institute in Yitang town, on the eastern edge of Lengshuitan district, and covering about 520 ha (7,800 mu) of mostly wooded hills. More than 2,000 kinds of trees, bamboos, flowers and climbers grow in themed gardens such as the cherry, osmanthus, camellia and bamboo gardens, alongside a forestry park with a garden for each of Yongzhou's counties and a wetland park round a reservoir. It is a local weekend park for walks and plant-spotting rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Yuchanyan
rows.summary: A small limestone cave at Baishizhai in Shouyan town, Dao County, known locally as Toad Cave, where excavations in 1993–1995 and 2004–2005 found pottery dated to about 18,000 years ago, among the oldest known anywhere, and rice grains that Chinese archaeologists regard as some of the earliest cultivated rice. The cave mouth faces south-east about 5 m above the surrounding ground, and the site is protected as a national heritage site.

rows.name: Yunbing Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area at Nanfeng'ao on the Hunan–Guangdong border south of Lanshan, where a flight of 520 steps climbs to a 1,388 m pass and a viewing platform that straddles the two provinces. It is visited for sunrises and seas of cloud in summer and for rime and ice on the trees in winter, with mossy forest, bamboo valleys and azaleas on the way up.

rows.name: Zhou Family Compound, Ganyantou
rows.summary: A village of Zhou-clan mansions at Ganyantou (also written Jianyantou) in Fujiaqiao town, Lingling, where six well-preserved Ming and Qing courtyard compounds stand together; the largest dates from the Tongzhi reign (1862–1874). Billed locally as the 'finest old mansion of Xiaoxiang', the village is a nationally listed historic village and heritage site.

rows.name: 6501 Underground Tunnels
rows.summary: An unfinished man-made tunnel complex in the hills of Zhongfang, south-east of Linxiang, whose purpose has never been officially disclosed: three levels of passages, halls and shafts run for more than 10 km and cover over 80,000 m². Since an upgrade in 2019 the caverns hold an aerospace science exhibition with Long March rocket and satellite models, while outside there are military vehicle rides, archery, CS-style combat games and weapon models, aimed mainly at school study tours.

rows.name: Cishi Pagoda
rows.summary: A solid seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda 39 m tall on Taqian Street near the lakeshore, one of the oldest surviving pagodas in Hunan, with Buddha niches on four sides of each upper storey. Repairs in 2015 found an inscription dated 1066 and more than 1,000 Tang and Song coins in the spire, pushing its accepted date back from 1242, and it now stands in the restored historic district along Dongting South Road.

rows.name: Dajitou Jetty
rows.summary: A man-made jetty of 1879 on the south bank of the Yangtze at Lucheng, built out from a hill and natural reefs as three stepped granite platforms covering some 1,500 m², where boats on the river were towed and navigation markers set up. It was reported in 2010 as the only intact man-made jetty of its kind left on the middle and lower Yangtze, and the three centipedes carved in relief on its walls were meant to tame the river's dragons.

rows.name: Dayunshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain of 911 m on the border of Yueyang County and Linxiang, a national forest park since 1996 and an old Daoist and Buddhist pilgrimage hill whose restored temples draw worshippers from Hunan, Hubei and Jiangxi, above all at the fairs on the third day of the third lunar month and the ninth day of the ninth. On a cliff beside Longxing Palace is the 'Three Battles, Three Victories' inscription of December 1942, four characters each over 2 m tall with a commentary signed by the Nationalist general Yang Sen, marking the defence of Changsha against three Japanese offensives.

rows.name: Former New Fourth Army Liaison Office, Jiayi
rows.name_zh: 新四军平江通讯处旧址
rows.summary: A pair of two-storey timber shop-houses on Upper Street in the old market town of Jiayi, once the Tianhe general store and the Yichang pharmacy, which from 1938 housed the New Fourth Army's Pingjiang liaison office together with the Communist special committee for the Hunan–Hubei–Jiangxi border. On 12 June 1939, during the wartime alliance between the two parties, troops of the Nationalist general Yang Sen surrounded the office and killed six of its staff, including Tu Zhengkun; the Communist side calls this the Pingjiang Massacre, and the site is listed under that name.

rows.name: Former Pingjiang County CPC Committee (Mao Jianqing's House)
rows.summary: The 1919 country house of Mao Jianqing (1891–1932), a graduate of Tokyo Imperial University who became Pingjiang's Communist Party secretary in 1927 and moved the county committee into his family home. From here the committee directed the 1927 Autumn Harvest risings and the 'March assault on the city' of 1928, in which more than 200,000 people took part; of the original courtyard compound only the two-storey rear block and side rooms survive, with Mao's tomb nearby.

rows.name: Former Residence of Ren Bishi
rows.summary: The birthplace of Ren Bishi (1904–1950), a senior Communist military and political leader who was political commissar of He Long's Second Front Army on the Long March, in Bishi town in southern Miluo. The timber farmhouse of 31 rooms, with a name board written by Deng Xiaoping in 1980, stands beside a memorial hall showing close to 200 objects and more than 400 photographs, and a square with a 7.1 m bronze statue.

rows.name: Hunan–Hubei–Jiangxi Soviet Sites, Changshou
rows.summary: Three sites in and near Changshou, an old market town on the upper Miluo River in eastern Pingjiang, added in 2019 to the national listing of the Hunan–Hubei–Jiangxi revolutionary base, whose main sites are at Wanzai in Jiangxi. On Xinan Street stand the Romanesque Catholic church of 1929, where the region's first congress of workers', peasants' and soldiers' delegates met in September 1931 and set up the provincial soviet government, and the neighbouring Protestant chapel where Peng Dehuai and Teng Daiyuan's Fifth Red Army held an enlarged meeting in October 1929; the provincial party, soviet and military headquarters were in a rammed-earth Qing farmhouse at Gaibandong in Shiyan village.

rows.name: Jiangtun Bay (Finless Porpoise Bay)
rows.summary: A reach of the Yangtze bank at Qigongling in Junshan District, about 107 ha, where the Hualong sand and gravel wharf was demolished in 2017 and the shore cleared and replanted. Yangtze finless porpoises are now often seen in the bend of the river here; on the bank are a monitoring post of the East Dongting Lake National Nature Reserve, an eco-trail and viewing platforms, and behind the embankment an exhibition hall on the protection of the Yangtze presents the area's finless porpoises, Père David's deer and migratory birds.

rows.name: Junshan Island
rows.summary: A hilly island of 0.96 km² with 72 small peaks in Dongting Lake, about 9 km west of Yueyang Tower, tied to the legend of Emperor Shun's two consorts Ehuang and Nüying, whose tears are said to have spotted the bamboo that grows around their tomb here. Paths wind through the tea gardens that produce Junshan Silver Needle tea to the consorts' tomb and temple, the Liu Yi Well from a Tang tale, old rock inscriptions and other sites, with wide views over the lake.

rows.name: Junshan Wild Lotus World
rows.summary: A lake of wild lotus at Tuanhu in Junshan District, where more than 10,000 mu (about 670 ha) of lotus grows in continuous beds and over 300 cultivated varieties have been added. Visitors go by boat through the lotus beds and walk shaded paths to a lotus-viewing tower, an old well, stepping-stone and lotus-viewing bridges and pavilions; it is at its best in summer, when the flowers open from about late June.

rows.name: Longjiao Mountain Yao Relics
rows.summary: In the Longjiao Mountains of north-eastern Linxiang, on the Hunan–Hubei border, lie the remains of a highland settlement area that the Yao people regard as Qianjiadong, their ancestral homeland, occupied from the Western Jin to the Northern Song until its people moved away after about 1010. Spread over some 78 km² are more than 40 groups of relics, among them stone-cairn tombs, stone houses and wells, stilt-house foundations and the 'three passes and nine locks' defensive works, and the mountain has been a provincial scenic area since 2006.

rows.name: Mufu Mountain (Tianyue Mufushan)
rows.summary: The main peak of the Mufu range, about 1,600 m high, on Hunan's border with Hubei and Jiangxi in northern Pingjiang, a national forest park since 2005 that stays cool even in midsummer. The mountain has cliffs, waterfalls and pools, over 1,000 ha of natural Huangshan pine, more than a hundred rock inscriptions and the sites of old Daoist retreats, for Daoists counted it the 25th of their 36 grotto-heavens; shuttle buses run within the scenic area.

rows.name: Pingjiang Uprising Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The former Tianyue Academy, founded in 1720 and moved to this site in 1867, a complex of white gable walls and grey tiles now within the grounds of Pingjiang No. 1 Middle School, where Peng Dehuai, Teng Daiyuan and Huang Gonglüe launched the Pingjiang Uprising on 22 July 1928 and formed the Fifth Red Army. The academy has been a memorial since the 1980s; the present complex, opened in 2008 and refreshed in 2018, adds an exhibition hall on the uprising and on Peng's career to the restored rooms, with an equestrian bronze of Peng Dehuai (1990) on the square in front.

rows.name: Quzi Cultural Park and Qu Yuan Temple
rows.summary: The memorial temple of Qu Yuan, the Warring States poet whose drowning in the Miluo River is remembered at the Dragon Boat Festival, stands at the foot of Yusi Hill by the river: its brick-and-timber halls around three courtyards were moved here in 1754 after floods, the triple gate carries 13 reliefs of his life, and a stele forest of 356 carved inscriptions was added in 1995. Since 2017 the temple has been the core of the Quzi Cultural Park, some 6 km² with a new Quzi Academy, Dragon Boat Festival folk-culture areas and riverside wetland, which also takes in the eleven grave mounds on Miluo Hill, about 6 km to the south-east, that tradition since the Tang has held to be Qu Yuan's tombs.

rows.name: Sheng'an Temple
rows.summary: A large Buddhist temple on the northern spur of Lengjia Hill above South Lake, rebuilt from 1997 by monks from Nanyue on the site of a Tang-dynasty monastery whose abbot Wuxing was commemorated in inscriptions by the writer Liu Zongyuan. Five courtyards climb the slope past a five-arched gateway, the Hall of Heavenly Kings and the main hall to a Guanyin hall with a 5 m gilded camphor-wood thousand-armed Guanyin, and on the summit a nine-storey pagoda 53 m tall looks over South Lake, the city and Dongting Lake.

rows.name: Shiniuzhai National Geopark
rows.summary: A Danxia sandstone landscape of about 62 km² in north-eastern Pingjiang, a national geopark of long red cliff walls, rock 'waterfalls', natural bridges and narrow slot gorges, named after an old stone stronghold whose walls survive for some 2 km; the main source of the Miluo River rises here. It is also run as an adventure park, with a 300 m cliff-face stairway dropping 260 m, a glass viewing platform cantilevered 58.5 m out from a peak, a shop hung on the cliff and a cliffside inn.

rows.name: Wujianshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill of five peaks, the highest 588 m, rising just south-west of Linxiang city, a national forest park since 2008 that covers about 2,880 ha with forest cover of 98%. A mountain road and stone paths lead to old secondary forest, a large stele-forest museum of carved calligraphy, an open-air Guanyin statue, a Qu Yuan academy and farm restaurants, and it works largely as Linxiang's city park.

rows.name: Xiangyin Confucius Temple
rows.summary: Founded in the Northern Song and moved to this site in the early 1100s, Xiangyin's temple of Confucius lost many of its halls to Japanese bombing during the war against Japan, and a road cut through it in 1954 now separates the front court from the main buildings. The surviving Lingxing Gate, memorial archways, crescent pool and Zhuangyuan bridge lead to the Dacheng Gate and the double-eaved Dacheng Hall rebuilt in 1744, and the temple now houses the Xiangyin County Museum.

rows.name: Yangsha Lake Resort
rows.summary: A resort district built around the 4.3 km² Yangsha Lake on the southern edge of Xiangyin town, opened in 2017 and themed on the area's old fishing-village culture. After an upgrade it reopened in May 2026 with a fishing-village water town, a farmers' market, a waterside flower street, children's play areas and animal-contact attractions alongside its lakeside hotels and walks, and it is aimed at families from Changsha and nearby cities.

rows.name: Yueyang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Founded in 1046 by Teng Zijing, the prefect who rebuilt Yueyang Tower, the city's Confucian temple and school keeps its double-eaved Dacheng Hall, 16 m high, whose nanmu columns, lotus-carved column bases and beams are Song-dynasty work beneath a roof rebuilt in 1872. The Dacheng Gate, shrines to local worthies and officials, the crescent pool, the Zhuangyuan bridge and the Lingxing Gate also survive, and the buildings were restored from 2016.

rows.name: Yuezhou Customs House
rows.summary: Hunan's first customs house, opened at Chenglingji in 1899 when Yuezhou, where the Yangtze meets Dongting Lake, became the first port the Qing government opened to foreign trade on its own initiative. Of three British-style buildings finished in 1901 only the hilltop assistant's residence survives, a two-storey arcaded house of brick, timber and stone with fireplaces and tall windows, listed as 20th-century architectural heritage in 2020 and set in landscaped grounds above the port.

rows.name: Yuezhou Kiln Site Museum
rows.summary: Yuezhou ware, the celadon made along the lower Xiang River from the Han to the Tang, was ranked among the six best wares for tea bowls in Lu Yu's 8th-century Classic of Tea, and 26 kiln sites have been found on both banks around Xiangyin. The museum was built in 2003 over the Mawangkan kiln site in Xiangyin town, where a Sui-dynasty dragon kiln was excavated in 1997; it shows celadon and kiln furniture, including Southern Dynasties bowl fragments marked 'Taiguan' that point to supply for the court, and opened an underground gallery in 2010.

rows.name: Zhangguying Village
rows.summary: A clan village of the Zhang family below Bijia Hill in south-eastern Yueyang County, where connected houses built from the Ming and extended through the Qing form three great blocks, Dangdamen, Wangjiaduan and Shangxinwu, with 1,732 rooms, 206 skylit courtyards and 62 lanes over more than 50,000 m². Each hall is built around its courtyards and opens into the next, so much of the village can be crossed under cover, and its drains, light wells and fire-water pools still work; descendants of the founder Zhang Guying still live here.

rows.name: Zuo Zongtang Cultural Park and Memorial Temple
rows.summary: A memorial park of about 18 ha in Xiangyin, the home county of Zuo Zongtang (1812–1885), the Qing general and statesman who fought the Taiping and other rebellions and led the reconquest of Xinjiang, and whose name was borrowed for the dish General Tso's chicken. Its core is the Zuo Wenxiang Temple, built on imperial order by the Hunan governor Wu Dacheng after Zuo's death and completed in 1892, around which a 2012 extension added a memorial museum of eight galleries, an 11.1 m granite statue on a square, a gallery of poems and couplets on steles and a 'chronology avenue'.

rows.name: Baofeng Lake
rows.summary: An artificial lake in a gorge at Suoxiyu in the Wulingyuan scenic area, formed when villagers dammed the valley for hydropower in the 1970s and named after Baofeng Mountain behind it. Ringed by forested sandstone peaks, it is seen by boat, and it was a filming location for the TV series Journey to the West.

rows.name: Former Residence of He Long
rows.summary: The birthplace of He Long (1896–1969), a founder of the Red Army and later a marshal of the People's Liberation Army, at Hongjiaguan in Sangzhi County. The family house has been restored to its original appearance, and the He Long Memorial Hall and a bronze statue of him stand beside it.

rows.name: Former Site of the Hunan–Hubei–Sichuan–Guizhou Revolutionary Base (Dayong)
rows.name_zh: 湘鄂川黔革命根据地旧址
rows.summary: A former Catholic church on Jiefang Road in old Dayong, now central Zhangjiajie, where the Communist provincial committee, revolutionary committee and military district of the Hunan–Hubei–Sichuan–Guizhou base area were set up in November 1934, with Ren Bishi and He Long at their head. The brick-and-timber building covers about 810 m² and is one of several sites of the base listed together; the others are in Yongshun and Longshan counties in Xiangxi.

rows.name: Huanglong Cave
rows.summary: A large karst cave in the Suoxiyu area of Wulingyuan, east of the town, with two dry and two water-filled levels, underground rivers, waterfalls and an underground lake. The guided route of about two hours includes a boat ride on an underground river, and a 20 m stone pillar known as the Sea-Calming Needle is its best-known formation.

rows.name: Jiangya Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Jiangya Town, Cili County, where nine streams, all tributaries of the Lishui, meet. The spring was struck during construction of the Jiangya hydropower dam in the 1990s and rises from a depth of about 350 m at 52–54°C; its bicarbonate water now feeds the resort's pools.

rows.name: Jiutian Cave & Fenglian Creek
rows.summary: A large karst cave in Shuidong Village, Lifuta Town, about 10 km from Sangzhi county town, named for the nine skylights that open from its roof to the surface. Discovered in 1987, it has three levels with underground rivers, pools and natural bridges, and more than 3,300 columns and pinnacles over 3 m tall. Its exit leads into the forested peaks of Fenglian Creek, the other half of the scenic area.

rows.name: Long March Starting Point of the Red Second Front Army
rows.name_zh: 红二方面军长征出发地
rows.summary: Liujiaping in Sangzhi County is where the Red Army's Second and Sixth Corps, led by He Long, Ren Bishi and others, set out on their Long March on 19 November 1935, after a military meeting here decided on a strategic withdrawal. The site has the memorial hall of the Second Front Army's Long March starting point, with group statues of its leaders, a monument and an equestrian statue of He Long.

rows.name: Longwang Cave
rows.summary: A large limestone cave in Jiangya Town, Cili County, about 17 km east of the Wulingyuan scenic area, named after the legend of a dragon king living in the deep pool outside it. Found by local people in 1979 and run by the Huanglong Cave company since 2013, it has dozens of halls and corridors with underground rivers and lakes. It reopened on a trial basis in March 2026 after an upgrade.

rows.name: Puguang Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on Jiefang Road in central Zhangjiajie, founded in 1413 under the Ming by the military commander Yong Jian and renovated in 1733. Along its axis stand the gate, bell and drum towers, the Mahavira Hall, a Hall of Arhats with 18 arhat statues, a Guanyin Hall and the three-storey Yuhuang Pavilion. It is listed together with neighbouring old buildings, among them the Taoist Gaozhen Temple and a Wenchang pavilion.

rows.name: Shiyanping Village
rows.summary: A Tujia village in Wangjiaping Town, in the hills of eastern Yongding District, with 182 timber stilt houses, most built in the Qing dynasty; 85 in the core area are well preserved. Built on the slopes without levelling the ground, the mortise-and-tenon houses sit among terraced fields, old weirs and forest. It was among the first villages named Chinese Traditional Villages in 2012.

rows.name: Tian Family Compound
rows.summary: A Tujia family compound, also known as the Old Courtyard (Lao Yuanzi), in Pengjia Lane off Yongding Avenue, built in the Yongzheng era of the Qing (1723–35) by Tian Qiyuan. Of its original 160 rooms only about 30 survive, covering some 2,000 m², and the house was restored after the provincial heritage bureau approved a repair plan in 2021.

rows.name: Tujia Folk Custom Park (Tusi City)
rows.summary: A commercial park of Tujia-style timber buildings on the western side of Zhangjiajie city, including a chieftain's compound known as Tusi City, with displays of Tujia architecture and customs and staged song-and-dance shows. It is an easy stop within the city for an introduction to the Tujia people, whose homeland takes in Zhangjiajie.

rows.name: Wanfu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on a hillside by the Cili East exit of the Changde–Zhangjiajie expressway, opened in 2016. Naturally flowing water at about 53°C feeds pools in nine zones, alongside a water park with slides, a hilltop hotel and a shopping street. It suits travellers wanting a soak between Zhangjiajie and Changde.

rows.name: Xibu Street
rows.summary: A pedestrian street in Wulingyuan town, built in old-street style and lined with shops, snack stalls and restaurants, which the district counts among its cultural-tourism brands. It is listed as an intangible-heritage experience base, presenting crafts and folk culture of western Hunan.

rows.name: Zhangjiajie Difeng Gorge
rows.summary: A narrow karst slot gorge in Jinlong Village, Lingxi Town, in eastern Cili County, also called the Chaoyang Difeng ('earth crack'). The gorge averages nearly 200 m deep yet narrows to about 3 m across at the top, an unusual crack-like landform of the karst.

rows.name: Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A forested gorge at Sanguansi in Cili County, east of the Wulingyuan scenic area, best known for the glass-bottomed bridge, officially named Yuntiandu, strung across it. Opened in August 2016, the bridge is 430 m long and about 300 m above the canyon floor, and was the world's longest and highest glass-bottomed bridge at the time. It was designed by the Israeli architect Haim Dotan and can hold up to 800 people at once.

rows.name: Zhangjiajie Snow World
rows.summary: An indoor ski and ice centre in Yanghe Township, Cili County, opened in December 2019, with a snow-hall building of over 63,000 m² that takes up to 1,000 people at a time for skiing, skating and snow play. It offers families visiting Zhangjiajie a winter-sports option in any season.

rows.name: Chaling Ancient City Wall
rows.summary: The Southern Song city wall of Chaling, built of stone in 1231–32 along the Mi River, of which about 1.5 km survives with two gates and their barbicans (Yingxiang and Yingxun), a ramp and more than 700 m of riverside embankment. It is described as the only well-preserved Song-dynasty stone city wall in Hunan; an iron rhinoceros set up to guard the embankment also survives, and restored stretches and the Yingxiang Gate tower stand by the river in the old town.

rows.name: Fantawild Adventure Zhuzhou
rows.summary: A large theme park of the Chinese Fantawild chain in Shifeng District, northern Zhuzhou, opened in 2011, with themed indoor attractions, outdoor rides and shows. Its sister park Fantawild Dreamland, opened in 2016, stands next door, and both have staged holiday night events with drone shows; it suits families and ride fans.

rows.name: Former Qunli Porcelain Factory
rows.summary: The former Qunli Porcelain Factory in north-western Liling, founded in 1958 as the Liling Art Porcelain Factory with state funds to make fine underglaze-painted porcelain, which produced tableware for national leaders, the Great Hall of the People and the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse and so earned the nickname 'Red Official Kiln'. Production stopped in 2011; the brick workshops and old machinery have been kept, and after repairs prompted by a 2024 inspection the core workshop reopened as a cultural space for exhibitions and hands-on activities.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Lisan
rows.summary: The childhood home of Li Lisan (1899–1967), a Chinese Communist politician and Politburo member, on the eastern side of Liling, known as Yuyuan ('Taro Garden') from the name over its gate. It is a single-storey courtyard farmhouse in eastern-Hunan style with 32 rooms behind yellow walls, built in the 1880s and bought by his grandfather in 1891.

rows.name: Huahu Valley
rows.summary: A privately developed rural resort in Yantang town east of Chaling, built by the Hunan Wanzhang Group round flower fields, a lake and a gorge; its crape-myrtle garden opened in 2018. Family activities include a high rafting chute down the gorge, coloured slides, horse riding, animal petting and camping, and the resort hosts a grassland music festival, held for the third time in October 2026.

rows.name: Jiuxian Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir in the hills of north-eastern You County, held back by a 50 m earth dam on the You River built in 1958–60 and renamed from Jiubujiang Reservoir in 2004, with about 11 km² of clear water among forested hills. It is now a lake resort and national wetland park with a 22 km lakeside trail, paddleboarding, camping and family events.

rows.name: Liling Kilns at Weishan
rows.summary: The national listing for the Liling kilns, which fired ceramics from the Song to the Republican era, centres on Weishan village in the hills north of Liling, long the heart of the local porcelain industry and known mainly for blue-and-white bowls. Its best-preserved works, the Yuexingwan old kiln factory, founded in the Guangxu era and fired until the 1980s, keeps its clay-refining and shaping workshops, a painting shop and a stepped climbing kiln, restored in 2010–11.

rows.name: Lujiang Academy
rows.summary: A traditional academy in western Liling, founded in 1175 and moved to its present site in the Qing dynasty, with whose teaching the scholars Zhu Xi, Wang Yangming and Zuo Zongtang are all associated. Its halls and courtyards were restored and reopened to the public in 2016, and Liling's old stone Lujiang Bridge is a short walk away.

rows.name: Lujiang Bridge
rows.summary: A ten-arch stone bridge over the Lu River in central Liling, built in 1925 just upstream of a crossing recorded since the Song and destroyed many times by floods and war. About 187 m long and 8 m wide, it is described as the longest old stone arch bridge in Hunan, and it reaches Zhuangyuan islet in mid-river by a side approach; the name plaque was written by Kang Youwei.

rows.name: Mausoleum of the Yan Emperor
rows.summary: One of four places in China honoured as the tomb of the Yan Emperor (Shennong), the legendary ancestor credited with farming and herbal medicine, at Luyuanpo in Luyuan town, Yanling County, beside the Mi River. A temple was first built here in 967 under the Song; its halls burnt in 1954 and were razed in the Cultural Revolution, then rebuilt in 1986–88, and the complex now spreads over a sacrificial hall, the mausoleum hall, a memorial garden and a stele forest on the hill. The memorial rites held here are on China's national intangible heritage list.

rows.name: Red Army Slogan Museum
rows.summary: A museum in Yanling county town devoted to the slogans that Red Army units painted on village walls in this area in the late 1920s and early 1930s, opened in 2011 and described as the only museum of its kind in China. Wall panels removed from old buildings are shown in its halls, most written in lime or charcoal, one in purple dye from a local dye works and one on a wooden board; the county counts 339 surviving slogans at 115 sites, many still in place in the villages.

rows.name: Shennong City Park
rows.summary: A large modern park in Tianyuan District, central Zhuzhou, themed on the Yan Emperor Shennong and laid out round Yandi Square with its statue of Shennong carrying a herb basket, Shennong Lake, the tall Shennong Tower and the Shennong Grand Theatre. It is a modern civic landmark rather than a historic site, good for an evening stroll, and holds a Shennong temple fair at the Spring Festival; the Yan Emperor's actual mausoleum is in Yanling County.

rows.name: Shennong Valley National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the mountains of eastern Yanling County, covered in primary forest and threaded by streams and waterfalls such as the Zhulian (Pearl Curtain) Falls. Six areas with some 40 named sights, among them Jiashui, Taohuaxi and Jiuqushui, are reached by trails from the Nanmuba visitor centre, and its cool summers draw visitors escaping the heat.

rows.name: Shuikou Site of Mao Zedong's First Company Party Branch
rows.summary: The Ye family ancestral hall in Shuikou town, southern Yanling County, where on 15 October 1927 Mao Zedong admitted six soldiers of his Autumn Harvest Uprising force to the Communist Party in the upstairs room, founding the first party branch at company level. The preserved hall is fronted by a memorial square laid out in 2011, and nearby stand the Zhu family hall, used as the regiment's headquarters, and the Jiang family house where Mao lodged.

rows.name: Site of the Chaling Workers', Peasants' and Soldiers' Government
rows.name_zh: 茶陵县工农兵政府旧址
rows.summary: The old prefectural and county yamen of Chaling, an official compound in use from the Southern Song to the Qing, where the Communists set up China's first county-level 'workers', peasants' and soldiers' government' during the Jinggangshan base period. The restored compound of about 1.8 ha, with grey-brick halls and tall stepped gable walls, keeps the layout of an imperial county office and houses exhibitions on that government.

rows.name: Yunyang Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain rising straight behind Chaling county town, protected as a national forest park of about 89 km², which local tradition links with the Yan Emperor Shennong and with tea, and which was briefly honoured as the Southern Peak in the early Tang. Paths lead to the Nanyue Palace and the Ziyun and Baiyun temples, caves, gorges and viewpoints, and pilgrims crowd the Nanyue Palace for its temple fair in the sixth and seventh lunar months.

rows.name: Huitang Hot Spring Sanatorium
rows.summary: A hot-spring sanatorium and resort run by the Hunan Federation of Trade Unions in Huitang, the spa town of south-western Ningxiang. It is a large complex of bathing pools, accommodation and gardens that takes day visitors and overnight guests. It was named one of the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020 and is also on the 2016 list of China wellness-tourism demonstration bases.

rows.name: Tiantang Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park on Tiantang Mountain in Changning, in southern Hengyang prefecture, managed by its own park office. Its Fangjiaqiao area was named one of the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020.

rows.name: Jiuguan Lake
rows.summary: A lake-and-hill scenic area in Hengshan County, run by a private company, with lakeside walks in wooded country. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Yongzhou Strange Snake World
rows.summary: A themed park beside the old town of Lingling about Yongzhou's snake lore, which goes back to the Tang writer Liu Zongyuan's essay on snake-catchers. It is run by a local snake-products company and was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism base.

rows.name: Congxi Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: An ancestral hall in Jinsha village, Caitang town, built between 1870 and 1883 with money from Tan Hiok Nee (Chen Xunian), the Chaozhou-born merchant who became the leading kangchu, or plantation chief, of Johor in Malaya; it is named after his courtesy name, Congxi. It is known for intricate Chaozhou stone carving, including double-sided openwork panels of plum, bamboo, chrysanthemum, birds and animals, alongside gilded woodcarving and porcelain-shard mosaics. Two carved panels stolen in 2006 were recovered and returned the following year.

rows.name: Danfu Yuan
rows.summary: A private collection museum and garden on the eastern side of Chaozhou, also known as Yanfeng Academy, built on the initiative of the Thai Chinese businessman Guo Fengyuan to promote Chinese culture and exchange between China and Thailand. Its halls and corridors show antiques, calligraphy and carved stone qilin and lions in landscaped grounds, and a memorial hall honours notable Chaoshan merchants.

rows.name: Daoyun Lou
rows.summary: An octagonal fortified earthen house of the Huang family in Nanlian village, Sanrao town, northern Raoping, begun in 1477 and finished in 1587 after three generations of building; its eight-sided plan gives it the nickname Bagua Lou. Its rammed-earth wall, with water channels along the top against fire attack, encloses rings of houses, lanes and wells arranged in multiples of eight around a large central yard, and some families still live inside.

rows.name: Dongshan Lake Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort by Dongshan Lake on the northern side of Sangpu Mountain in southern Chao'an District, near where Chaozhou, Shantou and Jieyang meet. Its pools are set at different levels across a landscaped hillside above the lake, with a hotel and other leisure facilities.

rows.name: Green Island Tourist Resort
rows.summary: An eco-tourism resort on the former Wanshanhong farm in Qiandong town, Raoping County, laid out around lakes, bamboo groves and orchards with a hotel, play areas and farming activities, and also used as a study-tour base for school groups. Its 'kiln chicken', baked in a stone oven, is a local speciality.

rows.name: Guangji Bridge
rows.summary: Also called Xiangzi Bridge, this crossing of the Han River below Chaozhou's east gate was begun in the 1170s as a pontoon bridge and built up over centuries into stone-pier spans from each bank joined by a central section of moored boats that could be opened to let ships through. Restored in 2003–07 to its Ming appearance, with its pontoon boats and the pavilions and tower houses on its piers rebuilt, it is now a pedestrian bridge and is traditionally counted among China's four great ancient bridges.

rows.name: Han Wengong Temple
rows.summary: A memorial temple to the Tang writer and statesman Han Yu, who served as prefect of Chaozhou after being demoted, set on the western slope of Bijia Hill on the east bank of the Han River, facing the old town. First founded in 999 and moved to this site in 1189, its present halls date mainly from the Ming and Qing, and steles inside include a Qing recutting of Su Shi's inscription for Han Yu's temple.

rows.name: Historic Residences of Chaozhou Old Town
rows.name_zh: 潮州老城古民居建筑群
rows.summary: A group of Ming, Qing and Republican-era houses in three historic quarters of Chaozhou's walled town, the Ten Lanes by the South Gate, the Xu Fuma Mansion quarter and the old West Gate street, listed together as a national heritage site in 2013. They include scholar-officials' mansions such as the Dafu Di houses in Jiadi Lane and Xingning Lane, the Zhuo residence of the Tongzhi era and the late-Ming mansion of Minister Huang. Walking the lanes off Taiping Road, where several of them stand, gives a good picture of the old town's courtyard houses.

rows.name: Jilüe Huang Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: A private ancestral hall completed in 1887 for Huang Jilüe in Tiexiang Lane, old Chaozhou, known for its Chaozhou gilded woodcarving and stone carving. Instead of the usual auspicious motifs, the gold-lacquered carvings on its beams show historical tales and legends such as the Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage and the Goddess of the Luo River. It is laid out in two sections, with four halls facing one another around the courtyard.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple, Chaozhou
rows.summary: Founded in 738 under the Tang emperor Xuanzong and known since the Ming as Kaiyuan Zhenguo Chan Temple, this is the main Buddhist monastery of Chaozhou's old town and a nationally designated key temple. Along its central axis stand the gate hall, the Hall of Heavenly Kings, the Mahavira Hall and the sutra library, many of them keeping their early form, while side halls include a Dabei Hall of 2005 lined with statues of Guanyin and a Thai-style hall with a bronze Buddha.

rows.name: Xu Fuma Mansion
rows.summary: The residence of Xu Jue, a Northern Song official married to a great-granddaughter of Emperor Taizong, hence the popular title fuma ('imperial son-in-law'); it was first built in the 1060s at Dongfucheng in the north of old Chaozhou. Repaired many times since, it keeps its original plan of three halls five bays wide with side quarters, and one of its four wells still holds clear water; it opened to visitors in 2009.

rows.name: Dongguan Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: A city exhibition hall in Nancheng that tells the story of Dongguan's growth into a manufacturing city. The permanent display, renewed in 2023, shows products made by Dongguan firms and models of the city-centre plan and of the China Spallation Neutron Source, a large physics facility in the city, with films and multimedia screens throughout.

rows.name: Dongguan Science and Technology Museum
rows.name_zh: 东莞市科学技术博物馆
rows.summary: Dongguan's municipal science museum, opened in December 2005 in Nancheng district, with hands-on galleries built around two main themes: manufacturing technology and information technology. Exhibits are interactive, and the building also has a dome cinema. It suits families with children and anyone curious about the industries that turned Dongguan into a manufacturing city.

rows.name: East River Column Memorial Hall and Dalingshan Base Sites
rows.summary: A memorial museum in Dalingshan town on the East River Column, the Communist-led guerrilla force that fought the Japanese in the Dongguan, Huiyang, Bao'an and Hong Kong area during the Second World War. Around it are nine preserved sites of the force's Dalingshan base of 1940–1943, including its headquarters, a meeting room, a newspaper office, a clinic and a former academy.

rows.name: Former Residence of Jiang Guangnai
rows.summary: The family house in Nanzha village, Humen, where Jiang Guangnai was born in 1888; he commanded the 19th Route Army when it fought the Japanese landing at Shanghai in 1932, and later held posts in the government of the People's Republic. Known as Liyin Yuan, it was built by his grandfather in the Daoguang reign of the Qing, and the house is now a small museum.

rows.name: Guanyin Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested hill park in Zhangmutou town, south-east Dongguan, with a Buddhist temple and a large Guanyin square near the summit. A road of about 7 km climbs from the gate to the top, with sightseeing buses for part of the way, and footpaths lead through secondary forest to a lake and viewpoints.

rows.name: Haogang Midden Site Museum
rows.summary: A Neolithic shell-midden site in Nancheng, where an early settlement left heaps of oyster shells along with pottery and stone tools. The site museum, opened in 2007, shows part of the excavated site with two human skeletons more than 5,000 years old, finds from the dig and painted pottery from the West, North and East river basins, with models of prehistoric life by the estuary such as canoe building and oyster gathering.

rows.name: Huayang Lake Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park around Huayang Lake and the creeks of Mayong town, on the Pearl River delta in north-west Dongguan. The waterways were badly polluted until a clean-up begun in 2013 closed electroplating, dyeing and paper works, and the area was approved as a national wetland park in 2015. Paths, cycle tracks and boat trips now run through the restored wetland.

rows.name: Keyuan
rows.summary: A compact Lingnan-style garden in Guancheng, built in the 1850s by the retired Qing official Zhang Jingxiu and counted among the four celebrated gardens of Guangdong. Halls, verandas, pools and rockeries are packed into a small plot, overlooked by the four-storey Ke Tower, the garden's tallest building. The painters Ju Chao and Ju Lian lived here for some ten years, and their work is seen as a forerunner of the Lingnan school of painting.

rows.name: Longfeng Villa Film and TV Resort
rows.summary: A themed park in Fenggang town, opened in 2005 with Hong Kong investment and built around wedding photography, with mock European castles, a fairy-tale town and street sets that also serve as film backdrops. It has since added rides, family attractions and evening shows.

rows.name: Nanshe and Tangwei Ancient Villages
rows.summary: Two walled Ming and Qing clan villages in eastern Dongguan, listed together as a national heritage site in 2006. Nanshe, in Chashan town, is a Xie clan village laid out along a chain of four ponds, with a late-Ming wall and 16 ancestral halls lining the water. Tangwei, about 3 km away in Shipai town, keeps more than 260 Ming and Qing houses with 21 ancestral halls, study halls and watchtowers built of red sandstone and grey brick.

rows.name: Opium War Museum and Humen Forts
rows.summary: The museum in Humen town stands where the imperial commissioner Lin Zexu publicly destroyed confiscated opium in 1839, the event that led to the First Opium War, and its grounds keep the two destruction pools, rebuilt in 1957. Its Sea Battle Museum branch, opened in 1999 near the Weiyuan forts on Nanshan hill, holds the main exhibition on the Opium Wars, and the museum also looks after the Shajiao forts to the south. The Humen forts were begun in 1717, wrecked in both Opium Wars and rebuilt each time.

rows.name: Quejin Pavilion Stele
rows.summary: A Ming stone stele of 1542 in the old centre of Dongguan, recording how the Panyu magistrate Li Kai, sent to regulate foreign trade, refused a gift of money from Siamese merchants. The merchants used the money for a memorial arch, pavilion and this stele instead; the pavilion was lost by the 1960s and rebuilt in 1997 around the surviving stone.

rows.name: Shilong South Bridge of the Kowloon–Canton Railway
rows.summary: A single-track railway bridge of 1907–1911 that carried the old Kowloon–Canton Railway over the southern branch of the East River at Shilong, and is regarded as the oldest surviving railway bridge in Guangdong. Built of steel, stone, timber and concrete, it was retired in 2007 when a new bridge opened a short way downstream, and it can be seen from the riverbanks of Shilong town.

rows.name: Songshan Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir lake at the heart of Dongguan's Songshan Lake high-tech park, with lakeside parkland laid out from 2002. Roads, footpaths and cycle tracks follow the wooded shore, and it is mainly visited for cycling and lakeside walks.

rows.name: Xiangshi Zoo
rows.summary: A privately run zoo in Liaobu town with more than 100 species, among them giant pandas, Asian elephants and Siberian tigers, many kept in open enclosures rather than cages. Staged shows, including a marine-animal show, are put on in its show halls, and it suits a family day out.

rows.name: Yinping Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park across the hills of Xiegang, Qingxi and Zhangmutou towns in south-east Dongguan, the largest in the city, rising to Yinpingzui (898 m), Dongguan's highest peak. Waymarked trails with rest pavilions climb through hill forest towards the summit, and it is mainly a hiking destination.

rows.name: Yinxian Villa Resort
rows.summary: A leisure resort on a wooded hillside in Changping town, with landscaped grounds, hotels and family attractions such as a small zoo, amusement rides, a water park and a glass bridge. It suits a family day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Yiyi Art House Museum
rows.summary: A private museum in Hengli town built on a local family's collection of Chinese art, gathered since the 1970s. Galleries set around courtyards in white-walled, dark-tiled buildings show paintings and calligraphy, ceramics, bronzes, carvings and Ming and Qing furniture.

rows.name: CCTV Nanhai Studio
rows.summary: A film and television base of China Media Group (CCTV) in Shishan, Nanhai, begun in 1996 with street sets of old Hong Kong and Macau built for dramas about the two cities. Its largest set, built in 1997–98 for a series on the Taiping Rebellion, recreates the Taiping court palaces of Nanjing behind a gate tower 300 m wide, beside a moated quarter of Jiangnan-style streets, mansions and teahouses. Visitors walk through the replica sets, which are still used for filming and broadcasts.

rows.name: Changlu Tourism and Leisure Park
rows.summary: A privately built leisure park of about 600 mu (40 hectares) in Lunjiao, Shunde, which grew out of the Changlu farm resort opened in the early 2000s and was rated a 5A scenic area in 2014. It is divided into ten themed areas, among them an amusement-ride park, a fairy-tale animal kingdom, a mine-tunnel aquarium, a snow world, a science hall, a Jurassic zone, a farm-restaurant area and a military-themed area, with a staged show at its Global Village theatre. Themed hotels and dozens of restaurants make it a full-day outing for families.

rows.name: Chencun Flower World
rows.summary: The heart of the flower and ornamental-plant trade in Chencun, a Shunde town promoted as 'China's first flower town', where nurseries, plant markets and display gardens spread across the area. It became a 4A scenic area in 2012, and visitors come to wander among greenhouses and market halls of potted plants and flowers.

rows.name: Donghuali Historic Lane
rows.summary: A historic residential lane in central Foshan, first called Yangwu Street after the Yang and Wu families who lived here in the early Qing and renamed Donghuali in the Qianlong period. Later owners, the Luo family in the early 19th century and the Zhao family in the late Qing, rebuilt and extended the houses, which now line a main lane about 112 m long across some 6,700 m². It is described as the most completely preserved group of Pearl River Delta-style houses in Guangdong.

rows.name: Foshan Ancestral Temple
rows.summary: A Daoist temple to the Northern Emperor (Beidi), the water god revered as Foshan's protector, founded in the Northern Song (1078–1085), rebuilt in 1372 and restored throughout in 1899. Its Ming and Qing buildings include the Wanfu Stage of 1658, regarded as the largest old opera stage in the Lingnan region, the Lingying archway and the main hall with bronze and cast-iron ritual objects, all richly decorated with carving and ceramic ridge figures. The complex is now a national first-grade museum that also takes in a Confucian temple and halls devoted to the martial artists Wong Fei-hung and Ip Man.

rows.name: Kang Youwei's Former Residence
rows.summary: The birthplace and childhood home of Kang Youwei (1858–1927), the leading figure of the 1898 Hundred Days' Reform, in Su village, Danzao town, known locally as the Yanxiang Old House. The 81 m² Pearl River Delta-style house dates from the mid-Qing, was partly destroyed during the war against Japan and restored in 1983, and a memorial hall was built beside it in 1987.

rows.name: Lecong International Furniture Exhibition Centre
rows.name_zh: 乐从国际家居汇展中心
rows.summary: A furniture trade complex of two showroom towers at the head of the furniture strip on Lecong Avenue, in a Shunde town that its government describes as home to the world's largest furniture market. Listed as a 4A scenic area since 2014, it is essentially a furniture mall that suits visitors who want to browse showrooms rather than sightsee.

rows.name: Louvre International Furniture Expo Centre
rows.name_zh: 罗浮宫国际家具艺术博览中心
rows.pinyin: Luófúgōng Guójì Jiājù Yìshù Bólǎn Zhōngxīn
rows.summary: A large furniture showroom complex in Lecong, Shunde, run by the Louvre (Luofugong) home-furnishings group, whose Chinese name is that of the Paris museum. Lecong's government describes the town as having the world's largest furniture market, and this centre, a 4A scenic area since 2012, is essentially a vast furniture mall that suits buyers and design-minded browsers rather than sightseers.

rows.name: Menglishuixiang Scenic Area, Lishui
