rows.summary: A scenic area of flower parks and waterside villages in Lishui town, northern Nanhai, rated a 4A scenic area in 2018. Its centrepiece is the Menglishuixiang Flower Garden, opened in 2017, with flower fields, waterways and a large glasshouse, plus small trains and duck boats for children. Nearby stops on the town's 'water-town garden' route include the cycle path around Xianlu Island and the old village of Chishan.

rows.name: Mount Xiqiao
rows.summary: An extinct volcano of 72 peaks rising from the Pearl River Delta plain in Nanhai District, covering 14 km² and topped by the 346 m Dacheng Peak, with waterfalls, springs and wooded paths. It was a major Neolithic stone-tool workshop and later a centre of Daoism and Ming–Qing Confucian scholarship; today its sights include a 61.9 m seated Guanyin statue on Daxian Peak, Baiyun Cave and a lion-dance and martial-arts hall named after Wong Fei-hung. At Shiyanyan on the mountain, a nationally protected quarry worked from the Song to the Qing dynasty has left huge man-made caverns, some flooded, with stone pillars and tool marks.

rows.name: Nanfeng Kiln
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty dragon kiln in Shiwan, built on a slope in 1506–1521 and fired continuously for about 500 years, a record recognised by Guinness World Records. The sloping brick kiln is 37.8 m long with 34 rows of stoking holes, and it forms the centre of a ceramics quarter with the Gaozao kiln, the Guangdong Shiwan Ceramics Museum, a street of ceramic-figure shops and workshops where visitors can try making pottery.

rows.name: Nanhai Bay Forest Eco-park
rows.summary: A forested hill park on the western side of Xiqiao in Nanhai district, laid out along the Yinxi stream with an easy streamside trail and shallow spots where children paddle. A longer path follows the stream uphill to Qingyun Dong, a Taoist temple complex on the hillside for which the area was long known. It is a gentle family day out from Foshan or Guangzhou rather than a serious hike.

rows.name: Pingzhou Jade Street
rows.summary: A district of jade workshops, trading halls and shops in Pingzhou, Guicheng subdistrict of Nanhai, which grew into one of China's main markets for jadeite (feicui), much of it rough stone from Myanmar, and a centre of bangle making. Listed as a 4A scenic area since 2014, it suits visitors interested in jade carving and jewellery rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Qinghui Garden
rows.summary: One of the four great classical gardens of Guangdong, created in Daliang by five generations of the Long family on the site of a Ming-dynasty garden and given its name in 1806. Its compact 0.34-hectare plot is divided into a southern water garden around a square pond, a central area of pavilions, a boat hall and studies, and a northern residential quarter of bamboo courts. The airy layout, open at the front and denser at the back, suits the hot southern climate, and the buildings are rich in fretwork wood carving and brick carving.

rows.name: Sanshui Forest Park
rows.summary: A large forest park on the northern outskirts of Xinan in Sanshui District, covering more than 120,000 mu (about 80 km²) of wooded hills, reservoirs and lakes. Besides walks in the forest, its sights include a large gilded reclining Buddha, a hall of Han and Tibetan Buddhist art, the Kongsheng Garden Confucian temple, Wuqing Valley and Yuanyang Lake, and there are outdoor sports for groups.

rows.name: Sanshui Lotus World
rows.summary: A lotus park of nearly 1,000 mu (about 65 hectares) in Sanshui District, opened in 2000 and rated a 4A scenic area in 2005, with about 200 mu of lotus ponds among its gardens and an amusement-ride area. It is best visited in the summer flowering season.

rows.name: Shunde Sugar Factory Early Buildings
rows.summary: The surviving early buildings of a sugar refinery founded in 1934 on the north bank of the Desheng River under Chen Jitang's Guangdong administration, built by the Czech firm Škoda and in production from November 1935. It was long regarded as China's largest sugar mill by output and closed in 1993, leaving four early buildings, the boiling and pressing halls and two sugar warehouses, together with crystallisers and molasses tanks.

rows.name: Yingxiang Eco-Park
rows.summary: A large rural tourism park in Hecheng, Gaoming, organised around the seasons: flower fields in spring, water play in summer, hill walks in autumn and farm food in winter. It mixes farm sightseeing with displays of growing methods such as heated greenhouses, hydroponics and the traditional mulberry-dyke fish ponds, and visitors can try making Gaoming lai fen rice noodles, a listed intangible-heritage craft; it suits families.

rows.name: Zaomu Mountain
rows.summary: The highest mountain in Foshan, in the south of Gaoming District, named 'black curtain' for the dense dark forest that covers its slopes. The first 4A scenic area in Gaoming keeps much of its natural forest, with 781 native plant species recorded, and walkers climb to the summit for wide views; 'Zaomu above the clouds' is one of the Ten Sights of Foshan.

rows.name: Zinan Village
rows.summary: A village in Nanzhuang town, Chancheng District, that has made its Lingnan water-village setting into a cultural tourism area and is listed as a national key village for rural tourism and a national study-tour base. Visitors can take the 'Zinan boat' trip along its waterways, watch a staged water, light and dance show titled 'This is Zinan', and visit an art garden and a hall on Cantonese family precepts.

rows.name: Baishuizhai Scenic Area
rows.summary: Baishuizhai is a mountain scenic area in Paitan, northern Zengcheng, crossed by the Tropic of Cancer and best known for the Baishui Fairy Waterfall, which drops from a reservoir high on the slope. A long stone stairway climbs past several waterfall viewing platforms, with a boardwalk along the lower stream, to the reservoir and the hills above.

rows.name: Baiyun Mountain
rows.summary: Baiyun Mountain is a forested range of many peaks on the northern edge of central Guangzhou, a scenic area since ancient times and a popular place for walks, climbs and views over the city. Paths and roads lead to Moxing Ling, the highest peak, the Mingzhu Tower area, Nengren Temple, a stele forest and the Yuntai Garden near the main south gate, and a cable car rises from the visitor centre to the summit area.

rows.name: Baomo Garden
rows.summary: Baomo Garden in Zini village, Shawan, began as a Qing shrine to the Song official Bao Zheng, was destroyed in the 1950s and has been rebuilt since 1995 into a large garden in Lingnan style. Its ponds, bridges and halls are decorated with carved brick, stone and wood, and it holds a long porcelain relief copying the scroll 'Along the River during the Qingming Festival' and the collection hall of the donor Zhao Tailai. The neighbouring Nanyue Yuan is a sister garden.

rows.name: Beijing Road Pedestrian Street
rows.summary: Beijing Road has been a main street of central Guangzhou for centuries: the city's double gate tower stood here from 1244, and in the Qing the street was known for bookshops, antiques and its flower market. Fully pedestrianised since 2002, it is lined with department stores, bookshops and long-established Cantonese restaurants. The scenic area also counts the Nanyue Palace site museum, and the City God Temple and Dafo Temple are close by.

rows.name: Bishuiwan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring hotel resort on the banks of the Liuxi River in Conghua's hot-spring area, opened in 2002 by the civil aviation air traffic bureau for central and southern China. It combines hot-spring bathing pools with rooms, restaurants and meeting facilities, and suits a relaxing overnight stay.

rows.name: Chen Clan Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: Built in 1888–94 with funds from Chen clans across Guangdong's 72 counties, this combined ancestral hall and academy gave lodging to clan members sitting the imperial examinations in Guangzhou. Its symmetrical complex of halls and courtyards is famous for the density of its decoration, with carvings in wood, stone and brick, ceramic roof ridges, plaster mouldings and cast ironwork. It now houses the Guangdong Folk Art Museum.

rows.name: Former Residence of Hong Xiuquan
rows.summary: Hong Xiuquan, leader of the Taiping Rebellion, grew up in the Hakka village of Guanlubu in Huadu, where his mud-brick family home, the village school where he studied and taught, and the Hong ancestral hall stand side by side. Qing troops burnt them in 1854; the house was rebuilt on its old foundations in 1959 and the school was also reconstructed. A memorial hall beside the village square, opened in 2014, tells the story of Hong and the Taiping movement.

rows.name: Former Site of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions
rows.summary: Built in the late Qing or early Republican years as the Huizhou Guild Hall, this building housed the All-China Federation of Trade Unions from 1925 to 1927, when union leaders including Liu Shaoqi, Deng Zhongxia and Su Zhaozheng worked here. The Kuomintang leader Liao Zhongkai was assassinated here in August 1925, and a memorial stele stands in front. Restored as a memorial museum and reopened in 1985, it is a branch of the Guangdong Museum of Revolutionary History.

rows.name: Former Site of the CPC Guangdong District Committee
rows.summary: This three-storey arcaded (qilou) building at 194–200 Wenming Road housed the Guangdong District Executive Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, which directed the party's work in Guangdong, Guangxi and neighbouring regions in the 1920s. It is now a memorial with exhibitions on the committee's history, renewed in 2021.

rows.name: Former Site of the Guangdong Provincial Peasants' Association
rows.summary: This brick villa, built for a deputy leader of the Canton Merchants' Corps and confiscated after the corps' revolt of 1924, housed the third to fifth sessions of the Peasant Movement Training Institute and, from 1925, the Guangdong Provincial Peasants' Association. Mao Zedong lived and worked in a small upstairs room in 1925 while teaching here, and the building, which keeps most of its original form, is now used as an exhibition hall.

rows.name: Grandview Mall
rows.summary: Opened in 2005 at the junction of Tianhe Road and Tiyu East Road, Grandview is one of the largest shopping centres in southern China and in 2011 became one of the few malls in the country rated as a 4A scenic area. Alongside its shops and restaurants it houses the Grandview Polar Ocean World aquarium, a natural-science museum and an indoor rainforest garden, so it suits families on a rainy day.

rows.name: Greater Bay Area Central Wetland Park (Nansha Wetland)
rows.summary: Created on reclaimed mudflats at the mouth of the Pearl River in Wanqingsha, this wetland was planted with mangroves from the 1990s and opened to visitors in 2008, and it is the largest coastal wetland in Guangzhou. It draws large numbers of migratory birds and its ponds fill with lotus in summer, explored on boardwalks and by boat. Long known as Nansha Wetland Park, it was renamed the Greater Bay Area Central Wetland Park in November 2025.

rows.name: Guangdong Customs House
rows.summary: Finished in 1916 for the Chinese Maritime Customs, this granite-faced Neoclassical building on the riverfront was designed by British architects of the customs service and is known locally as the Big Clock Tower for the English mechanical clock of 1915 in its tower. After the Guangzhou customs moved out in 2006 it was restored as a museum on the history of the Guangdong customs.

rows.name: Guangdong Science Center
rows.summary: Opened in 2008 at the western tip of Xiaoguwei Island, the Guangdong Science Center is a large hands-on science museum whose ship-shaped building was certified by Guinness World Records in 2018 as the largest science centre by indoor floor area. Its permanent galleries cover physics experiments, transport, materials, digital technology, flight and space, and green living, with a children's area, several special-format cinemas including an IMAX and a dome theatre, and an outdoor science park beside a lake.

rows.name: Guangxiao Temple
rows.summary: Guangxiao Temple is one of the oldest Buddhist temples in Guangzhou, traditionally founded on the estate of the scholar Yu Fan after his death in 233, and is now the seat of the Guangdong Buddhist Association. Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of Chan Buddhism, was tonsured here under a bodhi tree in 676, and a small brick pagoda said to hold his hair still stands. The grounds also keep two iron pagodas cast for the Southern Han court in the 960s, of which the eastern one survives intact.

rows.name: Guangyu Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Lu clan of Qiangang village was built in 1406 by descendants of Lu Xiufu, the last chancellor of the Southern Song, and its three halls combine northern and Lingnan building methods in a way unusual in the region. Dated records of each major repair since 1553 have made it a reference for Ming and Qing architecture, and its restoration received the top Award of Excellence in UNESCO's Asia-Pacific Heritage Awards in 2003. A long carved eave board found in 2000 shows a panorama of the Guangzhou waterfront in the Qing.

rows.name: Guangzhou Chimelong Tourist Resort
rows.summary: Chimelong is a large privately run resort in Panyu that grew from a safari park opened in 1997 and now combines the Chimelong Paradise amusement park, Chimelong Safari Park, a water park, a bird park and the indoor Chimelong International Circus with several hotels. The safari park is toured partly by open-sided train or car and partly on foot, and keeps giant pandas, including triplets born there in 2014, while Chimelong Paradise has more than 60 attractions, including several large roller coasters. It suits families, and seeing the main parks takes two days or more.

rows.name: Guangzhou Martyrs' Memorial Garden
rows.summary: Laid out in 1954–57 as a memorial park for those killed in the Communist-led Guangzhou Uprising of December 1927, the garden holds the communal tomb of the uprising dead, pavilions commemorating Chinese–Korean and Chinese–Soviet solidarity, and the Tomb of the Four Martyrs of Honghuagang from the 1911 revolution. Within its grounds stands the former Guangdong Provincial Assembly building of the late Qing, where Guangdong declared independence from the Qing in November 1911 and Sun Yat-sen was sworn in as Extraordinary President in 1921. That building now houses the Guangdong Museum of Revolutionary History, also called the Guangzhou Museum of Modern History.

rows.name: Guangzhou Sunac Land
rows.summary: Opened in 2019 in northern Huadu, Sunac Land is a large leisure complex begun by Wanda and completed by Sunac, combining a theme park, an indoor snow park, an indoor water park, a sports centre and a shopping mall. The theme park has six zones themed on Lingnan history and legend, a flight-simulation ride over Guangdong's landmarks and a large show on Lingnan culture, while the snow park, now branded Hot Snow Miracle, has indoor ski slopes.

rows.name: Guangzhou Uprising Memorial Museum (Guangzhou Commune Site)
rows.summary: The former Guangdong provincial capital police headquarters on Qiyi Road was stormed on 11 December 1927 in the Communist-led Guangzhou Uprising, and the next day the Guangzhou Soviet, or Guangzhou Commune, was proclaimed here before being suppressed within three days. The city police handed the gatehouse and office blocks over to the heritage authorities between 1987 and 2005, and after restoration they reopened in 2007 as a memorial museum, part of the Guangdong Museum of Revolutionary History.

rows.name: Guangzhou Urban Planning Exhibition Center
rows.name_zh: 广州市城市规划展览中心
rows.pinyin: Guǎngzhōu Shì Chéngshì Guīhuà Zhǎnlǎn Zhōngxīn
rows.summary: Designed by the architect He Jingtang and set at the western foot of Baiyun Mountain in the new Baiyun district, this exhibition centre tells the story of Guangzhou's history and planning. Displays include a large scale model of the whole city, galleries on urban history, transport and future master plans, and short films in a 4D cinema, and the building also houses the city's local gazetteer library.

rows.name: Guangzhou Zoo
rows.summary: Opened on its present site in 1958, Guangzhou Zoo is counted with those of Beijing and Shanghai among China's three major city zoos, with animals grouped into areas for insects, reptiles and amphibians, birds, primates, big cats and herbivores. Residents include giant pandas, golden snub-nosed monkeys, South China tigers and Père David's deer as well as giraffes, elephants, hippos and rhinos, and the grounds also hold an aquarium opened in 1998.

rows.name: Haizhu National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Haizhu Wetland is a semi-natural wetland of orchards, canals and lakes in south-eastern Haizhu District, long known locally as the 'ten-thousand-mu orchard' and now a national wetland park surrounded by the city. Paths and bridges wind through fruit groves and waterways, making it a green escape close to the Pazhou exhibition area.

rows.name: Huaisheng Mosque and Guangta Minaret
rows.summary: Traditionally said to have been founded in 627 by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, a companion of the Prophet, the Huaisheng Mosque is the main mosque of Guangzhou and one of the oldest in China, although historians place its origins later in the Tang or Song period. Its plain round brick minaret, the Guangta or 'light tower', is said to have carried a lamp to guide ships when the river ran close by, and the present prayer hall and courtyards follow a rebuilding of 1695.

rows.name: Huanghuagang Mausoleum of the 72 Martyrs
rows.summary: This memorial park holds the tomb of the revolutionaries killed in the failed Huanghuagang uprising of April 1911 against the Qing, organised by Sun Yat-sen's Tongmenghui, whose remains were gathered and buried here by Pan Dawei. The cemetery was laid out from 1918 with funds from overseas Chinese, with a tomb pavilion and the Jigong Fang monument topped by a figure of Liberty, which was smashed in 1966 and re-created in the early 1980s. Tombs of other revolutionaries and of the aviation pioneer Feng Ru stand among the trees.

rows.name: Jiulong Lake Resort
rows.summary: Jiulong Lake is a resort area in the hills of Huadong, Huadu, set around a large lake and wooded hills, whose golf club hosted the golf events of the 2010 Asian Games. Since 2021 it has been redeveloped by China Travel Service with the resort brand Aranya into a holiday community with hotels, restaurants, lakeside walks and arts events. It suits a weekend break or a lakeside stroll rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Lingnan Impression Park
rows.summary: When Lianxi village was cleared in 2003 to build the Higher Education Mega Center, several of its old buildings, including ancestral halls and oyster-shell walls, were kept and restored, and some houses were moved here from elsewhere on the island, alongside new buildings in traditional Lingnan style. Opened as a folk-culture village in 2008 and reopened in 2021 after renovation, it has themed halls on Cantonese opera and music, puppetry, wedding customs, crafts and martial arts along a canal-side main street.

rows.name: Lotus Hill (Lianhuashan)
rows.summary: Lotus Hill is a low hill on the Shiziyang channel of the Pearl River that was quarried for stone from the Western Han to the mid-19th century, leaving sheer cliffs, stone pillars, caves and pools now protected as an ancient quarry site. Paths lead up to the Lotus Pagoda, a nine-storey brick tower of 1612 that once guided ships into the river, and to a large gilded bronze statue of Guanyin erected in 1994 facing the water.

rows.name: Maofeng Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: Maofeng Mountain is a forested range in Taihe, northern Baiyun District, whose main peak is the highest in Guangzhou's old urban districts. A hiking route climbs past the old Maofeng Temple, said to date back to around the 10th century, a maple garden that turns red in November and Tianhu Lake to the summit, while Jiulongjian on the northern slope is a lake fed by mountain springs.

rows.name: Memorial Museum of Generalissimo Sun Yat-sen's Mansion
rows.name_zh: 孙中山大元帅府纪念馆
rows.summary: These two three-storey buildings with arched verandas were built in 1907–09 as the offices of the Guangdong cement works, and Sun Yat-sen twice made them his seat of government, for the military government of 1917–18 and for the Generalissimo's headquarters set up in 1923. Restored after residents were moved out from 1998, they opened as a memorial museum in 2006, with Sun's office, bedroom and staff rooms recreated in the south block and exhibitions on his three governments in Guangzhou in the north block. The granite gateway of the cement works, dated 1907, still stands.

rows.name: Nanhai God Temple (Temple of the South Sea God)
rows.summary: Founded in 594 under the Sui dynasty, this is the only one of China's four imperial temples to the gods of the seas to survive, and officials came here to sacrifice for safe voyages, making it a landmark of Guangzhou's maritime trade. Its five courtyards hold many inscribed steles, including one with a text by Han Yu of 820 and imperial steles of the Ming founder and the Kangxi emperor, though the main hall was rebuilt in 1989 after being destroyed in the Cultural Revolution. On a hillock beside it stands the Yuri Pavilion, a classic spot for watching the sunrise over the river.

rows.name: Nansha Tianhou Temple
rows.summary: Rebuilt in 1996 with funds from the Hong Kong businessman Henry Fok on the site of a Ming-dynasty shrine, this large temple to Mazu, the sea goddess Tianhou, climbs the south-east slope of Dajiao Hill above the Pearl River estuary. A granite statue of the goddess faces the sea from the front square, and Qing-style halls rise in tiers to the eight-storey Nanling Pagoda at the top.

rows.name: Nanyue King Museum (Mausoleum of the Nanyue King)
rows.summary: The museum is built over the stone tomb of Zhao Mo, second king of Nanyue, who ruled from Guangzhou in the second century BC; it was found in 1983 when a hill was cut down for building work, and visitors can go down into the burial chambers. Its galleries show the finds, among them the king's jade burial suit sewn with silk thread and his gold seal, together with bronzes, jades and a large donated collection of ceramic pillows from the Tang to the Yuan. A second exhibition area, the Nanyue Palace site on Zhongshan 4th Road, displays the excavated palace garden with its stone pool and winding stone watercourse, along with remains of later palaces and government offices.

rows.name: Peasant Movement Training Institute
rows.name_zh: 广州农民运动讲习所旧址
rows.summary: The institute occupies the former Panyu Confucian school, founded in 1370 and given its present layout in 1747, whose Lingxing Gate, semicircular pond with arched bridge, Dacheng Hall and side corridors survive. From May to September 1926 it housed the sixth and largest session of the Peasant Movement Training Institute, a school of the first Kuomintang–Communist alliance for training rural organisers, directed by Mao Zedong. Since 1953 it has been a memorial museum on the institute and the peasant movement.

rows.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral
rows.summary: Built between 1863 and 1888 by the Paris Foreign Missions Society on the site of the former Liangguang viceroy's office, the cathedral is a Gothic Revival church made entirely of granite, which is why locals call it the 'Stone House'. Its twin-spired façade was modelled on the Basilica of Sainte-Clotilde in Paris, and the stone was quarried in Kowloon and shipped up the Pearl River. It is the seat of the Catholic Archdiocese of Guangzhou and holds regular Masses.

rows.name: Sanyuanli Anti-British Struggle Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This small brick-and-timber temple to the god Beidi, built in the early Qing dynasty, was where the villagers of Sanyuanli gathered in 1841, during the First Opium War, to form a militia against British troops. Since 1961 it has been the Sanyuanli People's Anti-British Struggle Memorial Hall, displaying swords, spears, the militia's three-star banner, a British army uniform and four old cannon.

rows.name: Shamian Island
rows.summary: Shamian is a small sandbank island on the Pearl River in Liwan District that Britain and France held as concessions from 1859 until the 1940s, cut off from the city by a canal dug in 1859. Its quiet tree-lined avenues are lined with banks, consulates, churches and houses in a range of European styles, now used as hotels, restaurants, shops and offices.

rows.name: Shawan Ancient Town
rows.summary: Shawan is a Pearl River Delta town founded in the Song dynasty, whose old lanes and ancestral halls form a historic quarter known as a birthplace of Guangdong music and of ginger milk curd, a local dessert. Its centrepiece is Liugeng Hall, the ancestral hall of the He clan, founded in 1335 and rebuilt on a grand scale from 1698, with five courtyards of fine Lingnan stone, wood and brick carving.

rows.name: Shennong Caotang Museum of Traditional Chinese Medicine
rows.name_zh: 神农草堂中医药博物馆
rows.summary: Opened in 2006 by the Baiyunshan Hutchison Whampoa traditional-medicine company beside its works in Baiyun District, this museum of traditional Chinese medicine is laid out as a garden, with exhibition halls set among beds of growing medicinal herbs. Its two themed areas cover Chinese and Lingnan (southern Chinese) medicine, with displays on health traditions, herbal tea and artemisinin, the antimalarial drug derived from sweet wormwood.

rows.name: Shimen National Forest Park
rows.summary: Shimen is a national forest park in the hills of north-eastern Conghua, based on the Daling Mountain forest farm and covered with some of the best-preserved subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest in the region. Its north-western corner takes in Tiantang Ding, the highest peak in Guangzhou, and other sights include the rock gateway (shimen) that gives the park its name, mountain pools, and stands of wild Mucuna vines and red-flowered Rhodoleia trees.

rows.name: Shitouji Mineral Park
rows.summary: Opened in 2009 by the Shitouji jewellery company in Huadu's jewellery town, this mineral park has an outdoor garden of rocks and petrified tree trunks above an underground exhibition of crystals, meteorites, gemstones and ornamental stones. It also has a shop selling the company's jewellery and a restaurant, and suits visitors interested in rocks and gems.

rows.name: Site of the First National Congress of the Kuomintang
rows.summary: The Clock Tower on Wenming Road, built in 1904 for a teachers' college on the site of the Qing provincial examination hall, hosted the First National Congress of the Kuomintang from 20 to 30 January 1924. The auditorium has been restored to its 1924 appearance, with delegates' names on the seats, and the building later served as the main office of Sun Yat-sen University. It also houses the Guangzhou Lu Xun Memorial, recreating the rooms the writer lived in while teaching here in 1927.

rows.name: Site of the Third National Congress of the Communist Party of China
rows.summary: The Chinese Communist Party held its Third National Congress here in Dongshan from 12 to 20 June 1923, in a rented two-storey house that was destroyed by Japanese bombing in 1938. Its exact position was confirmed by excavation in 2006, when the brick floor was found; the foundations are marked by a small square beside a history exhibition hall opened the same year. The memorial also takes in Chunyuan, a villa next door that housed the party's central offices at the time.

rows.name: South China National Botanical Garden
rows.summary: Founded in 1929 as a botanical institute of Sun Yat-sen University and run by the Chinese Academy of Sciences since 1954, the garden was designated the South China National Botanical Garden in 2022. Its Guangzhou section, open to the public since 1959, has dozens of themed collections such as the magnolia, palm and ginger gardens, a cluster of display glasshouses by a lake, and the Longdong Qilin lakeside landscape, chosen as one of the city's 'Eight Sights' in 1986.

rows.name: Southern Han Mausoleums Museum
rows.summary: The tombs of two rulers of the Southern Han, a tenth-century kingdom based in Guangzhou, were found in 2003 while the Higher Education Mega Center was being built on Xiaoguwei Island: the Kangling of Liu Yan, buried in 942, and the Deling attributed to Liu Yin. A site museum opened beside them in 2019, with permanent galleries on Guangzhou's archaeology and on Southern Han history and culture. Finds include the complete text of an imperial funerary eulogy carved in stone, the earliest of its kind yet excavated, and large groups of tenth-century ceramics.

rows.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
rows.summary: Built in 1929–31 with funds raised from local and overseas Chinese in memory of Sun Yat-sen, this octagonal hall by the architect Lü Yanzhi stands at the foot of Yuexiu Hill on the old city's north–south axis. Its blue-tiled roof covers a 71-metre auditorium without internal pillars, still used for concerts and meetings, and the Japanese surrender in Guangdong was signed here in 1945. A bronze statue of Sun stands in front, and the gardens include a kapok tree about 300 years old.

rows.name: Temple of the Five Immortals
rows.summary: This former Taoist temple honours the five immortals who, in the legend behind Guangzhou's nickname 'City of Rams', rode in on rams bearing ears of rice; it has stood on this site since 1377. Survivors include the Ming rear hall, one of the few intact Ming buildings in the city, and the Lingnan First Tower, a gate tower of red sandstone and timber housing a great bronze bell cast in 1378. A hollow in the rock by the gate is known as the immortals' footprint, and the Nanyue Ancestral Worthies Hall next door, opened in 2017, presents historical figures of Guangdong.

rows.name: Temple of the Six Banyan Trees
rows.summary: Founded in 537 to house Buddhist relics brought from Cambodia, the temple takes its name from the characters 'Six Banyans' that Su Dongpo wrote for it in 1100, still hung over the gate. Its landmark is the octagonal Flower Pagoda, first raised in 1097 and rebuilt in 1373, crowned by a Yuan-dynasty bronze spire pillar cast with more than a thousand small Buddha figures. It remains an active temple, one of the four great Buddhist monasteries of old Guangzhou.

rows.name: Tianren Shanshui Land Art Park
rows.summary: Tianren Shanshui is a landscaped resort of about 10 square kilometres in the hills of Taiping, Conghua, laid out from 2013 around the Shaxi Reservoir. Its gardens, such as Jingjie Garden and Xinyuan Ju, are themed on the poems of Tao Yuanming and modelled on a Song-dynasty painting of the poet's retreat by Li Gonglin, and the resort adds lodging, campsites, outdoor sports and nature-education activities. It suits a day out or a weekend stay in the countryside.

rows.name: Wanmu Caotang (Kang Youwei's School)
rows.summary: This grey-brick hall of three courtyards, built in 1804 as the Qiu clan's lodging for examination candidates, is where the reformer Kang Youwei opened his private school in 1891. Among his students were Liang Qichao and others who later led the Hundred Days' Reform of 1898, after which the school, by then at another site, was closed and its books destroyed. Restored after the residents living in it were moved out from 2004, it is now open to visitors as a small museum.

rows.name: Whampoa Military Academy Site
rows.summary: Sun Yat-sen founded the Army Officer Academy, known as the Whampoa Military Academy, here on Changzhou Island in 1924, in the buildings of a Qing army school, to train officers during the first Kuomintang–Communist alliance. The main school building, bombed in 1938 and rebuilt to its original form in 1996, holds exhibitions on the academy's history and recreated offices, classrooms and dormitories. The site also includes the house where Sun stayed on visits, the academy club hall of 1926 and a memorial to Sun on a nearby hill.

rows.name: Xianxian Mosque and Tomb of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
rows.summary: Chinese Muslim tradition holds that this walled cemetery contains the tomb of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, a companion of the Prophet said to have come to China to spread Islam in the seventh century, and it has long been a place of pilgrimage. His domed tomb chamber, known for its echo, stands among the graves of missionaries and foreign pilgrims, among them a Korean of the 14th century and a Turk of the 18th, with old steles, arches and pavilions around them. A large prayer hall added on the west side in 2010 has made it Guangzhou's largest mosque.

rows.name: Yongqingfang
rows.summary: Yongqingfang is a block of old Xiguan lanes off Enning Road that was renovated by the district government and Vanke and opened in 2016 as a pedestrian quarter of shops, cafés and studios among old houses. The area was a centre of Cantonese opera in the 1920s and 1930s, and it includes the ancestral house of Bruce Lee's family and the Cantonese Opera Art Museum, a new garden complex in traditional style with a stage for regular performances.

rows.name: Yuexiu Park and Zhenhai Tower
rows.summary: Yuexiu Park covers Yuexiu Hill, the low hill that formed the northern end of the walled city, and was made a public park on Sun Yat-sen's orders in the 1920s. Its landmark is Zhenhai Tower, a five-storey tower with red sandstone lower walls built in 1380 on the Ming city wall, a stretch of which survives along the hill; it holds the Guangzhou Museum's display on the city's history, with old cannon and steles outside. Around the park's lakes and hills are the Five Rams statue and the Sun Yat-sen memorial obelisk.

rows.name: Yuyin Shanfang (Yuyin Garden)
rows.summary: Yuyin Shanfang is a private garden built in 1867–71 for the Qing scholar-official Wu Bin in Nancun, Panyu, and is counted among the four famous gardens of Guangdong. Within a small walled plot it fits a rectangular lotus pond, an octagonal waterside pavilion, an arched bridge and halls with carved wooden screens and coloured 'Manchu' windows. The adjoining Yu Garden, added by a descendant in 1922, has a boat-shaped hall and a glass-walled upper room looking over the garden.

rows.name: Bavaria Manor, Heyuan
rows.summary: A large resort estate on the southern edge of Heyuan city, laid out in German Bavarian style, with hotels, holiday housing, a hot-spring spa, a water park and the Black Forest amusement park. Heyuan's government lists it as the city's only national-level tourist resort, and it is aimed mainly at families on short breaks.

rows.name: Former Hong Kong Cultural Figures Rescue Headquarters (Fujian Guild Hall)
rows.name_zh: 香港文化名人大营救指挥部旧址
rows.pinyin: Xiānggǎng Wénhuà Míngrén Dàyíngjiù Zhǐhuībù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty guild hall built by merchants from Fujian in Laolong, which in early 1942 served as a command post for the Communist-organised operation that brought cultural figures and democrats out of Japanese-occupied Hong Kong. Hundreds passed through Laolong on their way inland, among them He Xiangning, Mao Dun, Zou Taofen and Liu Yazi, and the restored three-courtyard hall now holds an exhibition on the rescue.

rows.name: Heping Hot Spring Capital (Relong Hot Spring)
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort area in Reshui town, Heping County, in the hills of northern Heyuan, centred on the Relong Hot Spring resort and rated a 4A scenic area in 2010. Resort hotels with thermal pools lie in the valley, and the Reshui river-rafting run is close by.

rows.name: Heyuan Dinosaur Culture Park and Guifeng Pagoda
rows.summary: A riverside park below Guifeng Hill in Heyuan that groups the Heyuan Dinosaur Museum, the city museum and the Song-dynasty Guifeng Pagoda. The dinosaur museum holds more than 20,000 fossil dinosaur eggs, a collection recognised by Guinness World Records as the largest. On the hilltop, the 42.6 m six-sided brick pagoda, begun in 1132, is the only early Southern Song pagoda in Guangdong with an exactly dated inscription, and its seven outer storeys hide fourteen floors inside.

rows.name: Huanglongyan She Ethnic Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area of wooded hills and landscaped grounds in Zhangxi She Ethnic Township, northern Dongyuan County, themed on the customs of the She people, an ethnic minority of the uplands of south-eastern China. It became a 4A scenic area in 2024, and its grounds include ponds and an open-air performance stage.

rows.name: Huoshan Mountain, Longchuan
rows.summary: A mountain of red Danxia rock cliffs and crags in Tianxin town, northern Longchuan County, counted among the seven famous mountains of Guangdong and protected as a provincial forest park. Poets from Su Dongpo to Qu Dajun wrote about it, and it became a 4A scenic area in 2021.

rows.name: Sujiawei Hakka Village
rows.summary: A Hakka village in Yihe town, Dongyuan County, whose families trace their descent from the Song poet Su Dongpo, made up of 18 mansion-style houses, the oldest dating from the 15th century. It stands by the Dong River, and the scenic area also takes in the riverside scenery promoted as the Dongjiang Gallery.

rows.name: Tuocheng Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old seat of Longchuan County, founded in 214 BC by Zhao Tuo, Longchuan's first magistrate under the Qin and later ruler of the Nanyue kingdom, and the county's centre until 1949. The town keeps a cluster of historic sites, among them the Longchuan Confucian school with its Dacheng Hall, the Zhengxiang Pagoda, the Yuewang Well and a temple to the King of Nanyue.

rows.name: Wanlü Lake
rows.summary: Guangdong's largest man-made lake, a reservoir of about 370 km² formed by damming the Xinfeng River just north-west of Heyuan, scattered with more than 360 green islands and known for its very clear water. Boat tours run from the visitor area to developed zones such as Longfeng Island, Shuiyue Bay and Jinghuayuan, and the Wanlü Valley resort lies on the southern shore. It became a 5A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Yulinmen Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort with villa accommodation near Reshui village in Zijin County, which Heyuan's tourism plan names as the county's leading attraction and one of the city's 4A scenic areas. Its thermal pools and villas suit an overnight stay.

rows.name: Daya Bay Mangrove City Wetland Park
rows.name_zh: 大亚湾红树林城市湿地公园
rows.summary: An urban wetland park at the mouth of the Dan'ao River on Daya Bay, protecting a dense stand of mangroves beside the district's new town, with boardwalks through the trees; egrets nest here in spring. It was rated a 4A scenic area in 2018 and suits an hour or two of walking by the water.

rows.name: Hehu Walled Village
rows.summary: A Hakka fortified house in Hehu village, Yonghan town, completed in 1863 by the Wang clan, measuring 79 by 77 m with 108 rooms off its galleries. Three halls and the ancestral temple line the central axis, enclosed by two-storey outer ranges with four three-storey corner towers and a five-storey lookout tower. A pond and moats guard the front, with an old stone bridge before the gate.

rows.name: Huizhou West Lake
rows.summary: A chain of five shallow lakes on the west side of old Huizhou, linked by causeways and bridges, which Su Dongpo named West Lake during his exile here in 1094–1097. He helped pay for the Su Causeway and the Xixin Bridge, and Gushan islet holds the tomb of his companion Wang Chaoyun and a Dongpo memorial hall; other sights include the Sizhou Pagoda, first built in the Tang, and the old Fenghu Academy. The 5A scenic area also takes in Honghua Lake in the hills to the south-west, and the West Lake shore paths make an easy walk from the city centre.

rows.name: Longmen Iron Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Longtian town, Longmen County, covering about 50 hectares with mountains on three sides, whose iron-rich water emerges at up to 78°C. It has spring-fed pools set in landscaped grounds and villa accommodation, some with private pools.

rows.name: Mount Luofu
rows.summary: A sacred Daoist mountain in north-western Boluo County, revered as the seventh grotto-heaven and 34th blessed land of Daoism, with 432 peaks rising to 1,296 m at Feiyun Peak and hundreds of waterfalls, springs and caves. Its best-known temple, Chongxu Guan, grew from a hermitage of the Eastern Jin alchemist Ge Hong and keeps halls rebuilt in the Tongzhi reign (1862–1874), with his alchemy furnace and herb-washing pool beside it; Huanglong Temple and a Ge Hong museum are among the other sights. Su Dongpo's verses on the lychees he ate below the mountain made it famous from Song times.

rows.name: Nankun Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain area on the Tropic of Cancer in south-western Longmen County, a provincial nature reserve since 1984 and a national forest park since 1993, whose highest peak, Tiantangding, reaches 1,228 m. Streams, waterfalls such as Chuanlong Falls, old trees and bamboo groves make it a summer retreat from the Pearl River Delta, and the small resort centre is full of guesthouses.

rows.name: Nankunshan Yunding Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring hotel resort near the foot of the Nankun Mountains in southern Longmen County, rated a 4A scenic area in 2018. Its thermal pools suit an overnight stay combined with a visit to the Nankunshan forest area, in a county known for its hot springs.

rows.name: Xunliao Bay
rows.summary: A beach resort district on the west coast of the Renping Peninsula, facing Daya Bay in Huidong County, with about 27 km of coastline, eight small bays and dozens of islets. Its white-sand beaches shelve gently, staying under 2 m deep for about 100 m from shore, and the shore is lined with hotels and holiday flats.

rows.name: Ye Ting's Former Residence
rows.summary: The house in Zhoutian village, Qiuchang, where Ye Ting (1896–1946) was born, the general who was front-line commander of the 1927 Nanchang Uprising and commanded the Communist-led New Fourth Army from 1937 to 1941. The house, listed provincially in 1989 and nationally in 2006, is the core of the General Ye Ting Memorial Park, rated a 4A scenic area in 2013, whose memorial hall has an exhibition on his life.

rows.name: Birds' Paradise and Liang Qichao's Former Residence
rows.summary: Birds' Paradise is a river islet in Tianma village covered by a banyan grove that has grown from a single tree over more than 380 years, home to colonies of egrets and night herons that fly out and return at dawn and dusk; boats circle the island, and Ba Jin's 1933 essay about it made it famous across China. About 2 km to the east in Chakeng village is the family home of the late-Qing reformer and writer Liang Qichao, a brick-and-timber house with his study and a covered walkway, with a memorial hall on his life beside it.

rows.name: Dayan Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A wooded hill just north of Shaping, the centre of Heshan, named for its supposed likeness to a wild goose; it was opened as a scenic area in 1989, a park in 1991 and a forest park in 2006. Paths climb past viewing pavilions and the Jiyuan Pagoda to Guiren Peak, and the hill is visited in spring for its 'bird-flower' (Mucuna) vines.

rows.name: Former Residence of Situ Meitang
rows.summary: Situ Meitang (1868–1955), a leader of the Hongmen (Chee Kung Tong) society among Chinese in the United States who organised overseas fundraising during the war against Japan, founded the China Hongmen Zhigong Party and in 1949 joined the Central People's Government Council, was born in this late-Qing village house in Chikan. The small brick house of a hall, two rooms and side corridors now holds a photo exhibition on his life, with a bust in the square in front.

rows.name: Gudou Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort at the foot of Gudou Mountain in Yamen town, southern Xinhui, between the hills and the sea, with both saline and fresh spring pools, a water park, villas and hotels. It is a weekend leisure complex rather than a sightseeing destination.

rows.name: Guifeng Mountain
rows.summary: A forested range of hills on the north-western edge of Xinhui's Huicheng, protected as Guifeng Mountain National Forest Park, with a hill lake, waterfalls and views over the delta plain. Historic sites on its slopes include Yutai Temple and the Zhenshan Pagoda, and it is a favourite local spot for evening walks, Mid-Autumn moon-viewing and Double Ninth hill-climbing.

rows.name: Gulao Water Village
rows.summary: A landscape of villages, fish ponds and waterways inside the Gulao dyke on the Xijiang River, first built in 1394 against floods, developed since 2019 by the OCT Group into a tourism area. Visitors take boats through the channels and walk the waterfront market street and lotus ponds, and the site has added children's play areas and, in 2025, an indoor snow park.

rows.name: Jinjiang Hot Spring Resort, Enping
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort in Datian town, Enping, built around an activity theme, with a hot-spring surf pool, a circular rafting channel and about 50 themed spring pools. It was among the Jiangmen resorts certified in 2018 as using genuine natural hot-spring water.

rows.name: Kangqiao Hot Spring, Taishan
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort in Southeast Asian style in Baisha town, Taishan, with more than a hundred spring pools in activity, leisure, wellness and couples' zones, a water park popular with families and a resort hotel. It was among the Jiangmen resorts certified in 2018 as using genuine natural hot-spring water.

rows.name: Naqin Peninsula Geological and Marine Park
rows.name_zh: 那琴半岛地质海洋公园
rows.summary: A coastal park on a granite peninsula at Beidou town, at the south-western tip of Taishan, where wind- and sea-worn granite boulders crowd the headlands and small bays above the South China Sea. A boardwalk of about 3 km runs round the shore, and the beaches suit families.

rows.name: Quanlin Golden Town
rows.summary: A modern resort town in Dongcheng, east of central Enping, built around a hot-spring park with hotels and holiday housing. Its other attractions are an aviation-themed exhibition hall, a water park and the Dahema go-kart circuit. It suits a weekend of soaking and family activities rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Shangchuan and Xiachuan Islands
rows.summary: The Chuandao resort covers Shangchuan and Xiachuan, the two main islands of the Chuanshan archipelago off Taishan, with granite hills and long sandy beaches such as Feisha Beach on Shangchuan's east coast and Wangfuzhou on Xiachuan. Shangchuan was an early Portuguese trading base in the 16th century, and a memorial chapel and tomb garden mark where the Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier died in 1552; the Taishan Maritime Silk Road Museum opened on the island in 2019.

rows.name: Shanquanwan Hot Spring, Enping
rows.summary: A hot-spring hotel resort in the hills of Datian town, Enping, with themed spring-fed pools, water slides, a children's splash area and a large swimming pool. Enping promotes itself as a hot-spring town, and this is one of several resorts clustered around Datian.

rows.name: Former Residence of Ding Richang
rows.summary: The mansion and ancestral hall built in 1878 by Ding Richang, a late-Qing official and early advocate of the Self-Strengthening reforms, who died here in 1882. Laid out in the shape of the character 興 with 99 rooms, it combines Chaoshan wood carving with Western motifs in its painted beams and plasterwork, and now serves as the Ding Richang Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Gurong Martial Temple
rows.summary: A temple to the war god Guan Yu on Tianfu Road in Rongcheng, founded in 1558 and known for its fine wood carving. A stage, gate hall and main hall survive around its compact courtyard.

rows.name: Huangmanzhai Waterfalls
rows.summary: A forested gorge in the hills of northern Jiexi County with a chain of waterfalls, linked by footpaths and steps up the valley. It is one of Jiexi's main scenic areas and is often visited together with the Jingming hot-spring resort.

rows.name: Jieyang City God Temple
rows.summary: A City God temple in the old centre of Jieyang, founded in 1140 and rebuilt in 1369, with a main hall to the city god and a separate hall to his wife. Boards over the side gates warn wrongdoers with 'So you have come' and 'Your day has come', and the deities are carried through the streets each year on the 23rd day of the first lunar month. A Thunder God temple of 1663 and a Buddhist hall stand next door.

rows.name: Jieyang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The county school and Confucian temple of Jieyang, founded in 1140 and given its present layout in a rebuilding of 1876–1881. Regarded as one of the largest Confucian temples in southern China, it has three parallel ranges: the temple with its Lingxing gate, crescent pool and Dacheng Hall in the centre, and school buildings on either side.

rows.name: Yangmei Jade Village
rows.summary: Yangmei village in Pandong, on the eastern edge of Jieyang city, is where the region's jadeite trade began and is still the core of a large carving and trading district, although no jade is mined locally. Its workshops, showrooms and markets deal in carved jadeite, and Yangmei jadeite carving has been a national intangible heritage item since 2008.

rows.name: Baoguang Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal nine-storey brick pagoda on the west bank of the Jian River in Gaozhou, built in 1576 under the Ming to guard the city's waterway, and one of the city's landmarks. Granite reliefs around its base show auspicious scenes and even local bananas; visitors can no longer climb inside, and the tower is lit at night.

rows.name: China's First Beach
rows.summary: A 12 km sweep of sand about 300 m wide on the Dianbai coast, opened as Maoming's seaside resort in 1993 and named by local officials. It has bathing beaches, water sports, a resort zone and a central plaza, behind a long belt of coastal shelter forest, and it has hosted national and international beach volleyball events. The coast on either side forms the open-access Maoming Seaside Park.

rows.name: Datang Lychee Country, Genzi
rows.summary: A lychee-culture park of about 500 mu at Baiqiao in Genzi town, now officially named Baiqiao Lychee Park, in an area where lychees have been grown for more than 2,000 years. Its heart is the Genzi Tribute Garden, an old orchard said to date from the Sui and Tang with 95 trees over a century old, nine of them more than a thousand years old; the park also takes in the China Lychee Museum, with seven halls on the fruit's history, and a national lychee germplasm nursery.

rows.name: Douzhou Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old walled seat of Xinyi county at Zhenlong, founded in 621 and the county town until 1952, which also served as the seat of Douzhou prefecture from 634 to 1071. The walls were pulled down in 1939, but the red Wenming Gate survives along with the old county school, which rebels of the short-lived Dahong kingdom used as a palace, and a dense quarter of Qing and Republican clan academies, ancestral halls and merchants' houses. It is one of the better-preserved old towns of western Guangdong, worth a slow walk.

rows.name: Fangji Island (Chicken Island)
rows.summary: An island of about 1.9 km² off the Dianbai coast, Maoming's largest, with a sandy beach on its north side, cliffs on the east and a hilltop lighthouse. Long without permanent residents, it was leased to a private developer in 2004 and is now run as a resort island with hotels and villas, a Tianhou temple, snorkelling and diving. Its name, 'release-the-chicken island', comes from sailors who stopped here to pray for safe passage and set a chicken free on the hill.

rows.name: Guangken National Tropical Agriculture Park
rows.name_zh: 广垦国家热带农业公园
rows.summary: A large agricultural theme park of about 5,000 mu on the edge of Huazhou, built by the state-owned Guangdong agricultural reclamation group and approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. Eight themed gardens show tropical crops and fruit growing, with science and hands-on areas and a hotel, and it suits families and school groups.

rows.name: Lady Xian's Hometown and Tomb
rows.summary: The home district of Lady Xian, the sixth-century chieftain of the Li people of Gaoliang who served the Liang, Chen and Sui courts and is honoured as the 'Saintly Mother of Lingnan'. At Shandou village are her tomb, a walled burial ground first built under the Sui and repaired under the Song, Ming and Qing, with half of a Sui stone tortoise stele base and a stele re-erected in 1819, next to her temple and the site of her family home. Newer additions include a giant statue and a memorial square, and the local cult of Lady Xian is a national intangible heritage item.

rows.name: Lotus Lake Manor, Xinyi
rows.summary: A lakeside resort of about 600 mu in Chidong town north of Xinyi, near the Guangdong–Guangxi border, built around Lotus Lake. It combines a lakeside greenway and culture corridors, a glass bridge, a Ferris wheel and a small amusement area with a food street themed on the ancient Baiyue peoples and a Wyndham hotel.

rows.name: Maoming Forest Park
rows.summary: A provincial forest park of about 4,500 mu on the south-western edge of Maoming city, opened in 2002 on the site of an old state forestry farm. Besides wooded hills and walking paths it has botanical gardens, a zoo with an animal-show arena, a water park, an adventure course, a plant maze and a science museum, which make it a family outing.

rows.name: Romantic Coast Resort
rows.summary: A seaside resort on 5.3 km of natural coastline in Maoming's Binhai New Area, built in South-East Asian style around a 'love and romance' theme. Coconut groves, lawns, rocky islets and a fishing harbour frame the beach, and the resort has hotels, restaurants, shops and conference facilities.

rows.name: Xianrendong Scenic Area, Gaozhou
rows.summary: A forested mountain area around Xianrendong village on the southern slopes of Datianding, the high range in north-east Gaozhou, known locally as an 'air-conditioned village' for its cool summers. Besides forest walks and a series of waterfalls, it has wild Mucuna vines whose bird-shaped flowers bloom in spring, a glass suspension bridge, a bamboo slide and guesthouses, and it is promoted as a summer retreat from the lowland heat.

rows.name: Yushui Ancient Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort of about 500 mu at the foot of Reshui (Hot Water) Mountain in Magang town, Dianbai, on what was once an old post road. Hot-spring pools and gardens spread through a valley of rocks and lychee orchards, old poem steles and cliff inscriptions survive in the grounds, and a large resort hotel stands on site.

rows.name: Baihou Historic Town
rows.summary: An old Hakka town in Dabu County whose villages of Hounan and Houbei keep more than 120 houses from the Ming and Qing dynasties, many built in the grand 'official-hall' style of scholar-official families. The town also has Zhaoqing Tang, a hall completed in 1917 and listed as a national heritage site in 2019. The old quarter is divided into five themed areas covering scholar-farmer family life, the old alleys and the former market, and Hounan is a listed Chinese Traditional Village.

rows.name: Changtan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A reservoir on the Shiku River in the hills of Changtan town, northern Jiaoling County, set among wooded slopes in an area protected as a provincial nature reserve. Boat trips on the broad, calm lake have been its main draw, and the area is also promoted for the Hakka village life along its banks.

rows.name: Father-and-Son Jinshi Archway, Chayang
rows.summary: A granite memorial archway built in 1610 in Chayang town to honour Rao Xiang and his son Rao Yuling, who both passed the highest imperial examination and became jinshi. It has four main columns, three bays and three tiers of eaves, and is carved with dragons, lions and the inscriptions 'Father and Son Jinshi' and 'Silun Shimei'; two more stone archways stand beside it to the west.

rows.name: Former Residence of Huang Zunxian
rows.summary: The home of Huang Zunxian (1848–1905), the late-Qing poet and diplomat whose Treatise on Japan argued for reform, beside the Zhouxi stream on the eastern side of Meizhou city. It comprises Renjinglu, his study of the 1880s with Western-influenced details, and Ronglu Di, a traditional Hakka family house; with the Enyuan Di between them they now form the Huang Zunxian Memorial Museum, with an exhibition on his life.

rows.name: Former Residence of Qiu Fengjia
rows.summary: The house that Qiu Fengjia (1864–1912), the Taiwan-born scholar who led local resistance to the Japanese takeover of Taiwan in 1895, built in 1896–97 in his ancestral district after leaving the island; it is also called Peiyuan Tang. Laid out in the Hakka style with two halls and four side wings inside a semicircular rear enclosure, it holds an exhibition of his manuscripts, documents and belongings covering his years in Taiwan, his teaching in Meizhou, Chaozhou and Shantou and his part in early Republican politics. A memorial garden added in front in 2014 has a bronze statue of Qiu shaking hands with Sun Yat-sen.

rows.name: Former Residence of Xie Jinyuan
rows.summary: The birthplace of Xie Jinyuan (1905–1941), the Nationalist army officer who commanded the defence of the Sihang Warehouse in Shanghai in 1937, a Qing-dynasty Hakka house built by his great-grandfather in Jiankeng village, Xinpu town. Its two gateways, inscribed Rulin Di and Jingshu Ju, open onto pebble-paved courtyards, one laid out in a bagua pattern. A three-storey memorial hall beside it presents his life, and both reopened after restoration in 2015 with a statue of Xie in front.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhang Bishi (Guanglu Di)
rows.summary: The family home that Zhang Bishi (Cheong Fatt Tze, c. 1840–1916) built in 1908 in his native village of Chelong; he left Dabu at 16, made his fortune in the Dutch East Indies and Malaya, served as the Qing vice-consul in Penang and founded the Changyu winery in Yantai. Known as Guanglu Di, it is a large Hakka enclosed house laid out with three halls and four side wings inside a rear enclosure, and it was listed as a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Hakka World (Ketianxia)
rows.summary: A large Hakka-themed tourism and residential development in Sanjiao town on the southern edge of Meizhou, built up since the mid-2000s and planned to cover some 637 hectares. Its visitor areas include a Hakka-style town, a main plaza, the hillside Shengren Zhai ('Sage's Village'), a wedding hall and large flower gardens, with sculptures, murals and folk performances on Hakka customs, while housing estates and hotels share the site. It is a modern creation rather than a historic village, and suits visitors wanting an easy introduction to Hakka culture close to the city.

rows.name: Hanshan Historical and Cultural Scenic Area
rows.summary: A tea-growing upland on Hanshan in Fengliang town, northern Fengshun County, developed as a scenic area around the Hanshan tea plantation and rated 4A in 2023. Visitors walk among the tea terraces and the azalea slopes, try tea picking and see the Hanshan Tea Museum, and it makes a half-day outing from Fengshun or Meizhou.

rows.name: Hua'e Lou
rows.summary: A circular earthen fortress house of the Lin family in Lianfeng village, Dadong town, begun in 1608 and regarded as one of the best-preserved round houses (tulou) in Guangdong. Its rammed-earth outer wall, with no windows on the ground floor and gun slits above, encloses three concentric rings of rooms around a pebble-paved courtyard with an old well. The name, 'calyx', comes from a line in the Book of Songs about harmony between brothers.

rows.name: Lee Wai Tong's Hometown Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A football-themed tourism area in Wuhua County honouring Lee Wai Tong (Li Huitang, 1905–1979), the Hong Kong-born footballer of Wuhua descent who captained China at the 1936 Berlin Olympics and later became a vice-president of FIFA. It links his family home, Lianqing Lou, a Hakka house in Laolou village, Hengpi town, with the Huitang Stadium, a statue and square in his honour and the Wuhua Football Science and Technology Museum in the county town of Shuizhai.

rows.name: Lingguang Temple, Meizhou
rows.summary: A Chan Buddhist monastery on Yinna Mountain, founded in the Xiantong era of the Tang dynasty (860–874) by the monk Pan Liaoquan as Shengshou Temple and renamed Lingguang Temple in 1385. Two ancient cypresses before the gate, one living and one long dead, are known as the 'trees of life and death', and the bell tower keeps a bronze bell cast in 1485. The forested mountain around it makes a cool walk in summer.

rows.name: Sanheba Battle Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park on Bizhiwei Hill at Sanhe, the town where the Ting, Mei and Meitan rivers join to form the Han River, marking the battle fought here in early October 1927 between part of the Nanchang Uprising army under Zhu De and the Nationalist 32nd Army. A granite monument with an inscription by Zhu De was raised on the battlefield in 1963 and a martyrs' cemetery added in 1974; a memorial museum on the site presents the battle.

rows.name: Shenguang Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill park in Fuxing subdistrict on the edge of Xingning, a national forest park since 2005, named after the legend that the Song scholar Luo Mengjiao studied here by a divine light before passing the imperial examinations. Temples on and around the hill include the Zushi Hall, Mochi Temple and the shrine of the folk deities Shigu Dawang, and a modern tower, Qichang Lou, designed after a Hakka enclosed house, stands on the summit square.

rows.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall, Sanhe
rows.summary: A memorial hall to Sun Yat-sen completed in 1929 in Zhongshan Park at the foot of Fengxiang Hill, Huicheng village, in Sanhe, the old river-junction town that Sun had visited in 1918 to thank the troops stationed there. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2019, and the Sanheba Battle Memorial Park lies about 1 km away.

rows.name: Tai'an Lou
rows.summary: A square fortified house of the Lan family on Tai'an Road in Huliao, Dabu's county town, built in 1763. Its outer walls combine earth, stone and brick around ranges of rooms, and it was listed as a national heritage site in 2019; the area around it has been developed as a Hakka culture tourism park.

rows.name: Wuzhishi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A Danxia landscape of reddish sandstone cliffs in Chagan town, close to where Guangdong, Fujian and Jiangxi meet, named after five sheer peaks that stand side by side like the fingers of a hand. Trails pass narrow rock clefts, a spring, the rebuilt Shilin Temple (first founded in the Ming dynasty) and the ruins of a pagoda, and a cliffside walkway about 2.9 km long, with glass sections, runs high along the rock faces.

rows.name: Xihewan Hakka Culture Park
rows.summary: A modern theme park at Lanpai village, Yonghe town, on the edge of Xingning, built around Hakka culture, the area's lantern-making tradition and Chinese family names. Its landmark is a 36-metre tower in the shape of a lantern, recognised by Guinness World Records in 2017 as the largest lantern-shaped building, and the park also has a glass suspension bridge, an elevated rafting ride, a water park and sculpture galleries of Hakka folk life.

rows.name: Yannanfei Tea Field
rows.summary: A tea estate and resort in the hills of Changjiao village, Yanyang town, whose terraced tea gardens produce the local Yannanfei tea; it was rated a 5A scenic area in 2011. Paths and walkways run through the tea fields, and the estate hotel is built in the form of a Hakka weilongwu, an enclosed house with a rounded rear range. Visitors can try tea picking and tea making, eat Hakka food and watch Hakka song-and-dance performances.

rows.name: Yanshan Lake International Garden Resort
rows.summary: A flower-themed holiday resort at Nanfu village in Yanyang town, combining seasonal flower gardens with a lake of about 800 mu (some 53 hectares) and the wooded hills of a national forest park. It has children's play areas, Hakka restaurants and pod-style 'Earth capsule' cabins among its lodgings, and suits families on a weekend break.

rows.name: Ye Jianying Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park in Yanyang town built around the birthplace of Ye Jianying (1897–1986), one of the Ten Marshals of the People's Liberation Army, who was born here into a Hakka merchant family. His family house was listed as a national heritage site in 2001, and the neighbouring memorial hall presents his life and career with multimedia and interactive displays. The park also takes in a forest area and visitor facilities.

rows.name: Baojing Palace Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in the Yanziyan hills south-west of Yingde, found in 1981 by a provincial hydrogeology team searching for water. Lit walkways lead through several levels of chambers hung with stalactites, stalagmites, columns and curtains of flowstone. In 1996 archaeologists found chipped stone tools in an old river channel inside the cave, provisionally dated to the Palaeolithic.

rows.name: Dongtian Xianjing (Yingxi Tiankeng)
rows.summary: A karst scenic area in the Yingxi Peak Forest Corridor of western Yingde, billed as South China's first tiankeng: a large collapsed sinkhole among the limestone peaks. It was developed by the same company as the Jiulong farm resort nearby, and the official Yingxi rural tourism route links the two.

rows.name: Guangdong First Peak (Shikengkong)
rows.summary: The scenic area around Shikengkong, at 1,902 m the highest point in Guangdong, on the Nanling range where Yangshan meets Ruyuan County and Hunan. Covering about 138 km² in Chengjia Yao Township, it takes in old-growth forest, high gorges, waterfalls, karst and hot springs, and is a core area of the Yangshan National Geopark. Hikers climb to the summit for sunrise over the clouds, often camping overnight, and winter frost and ice draw visitors on the coldest days.

rows.name: Guangdong Yao Museum
rows.summary: A museum in Liannan's county town devoted to the Yao people, covering the history and culture of the Yao branches across China and abroad. Displays include costume, Yao embroidery and the story of Yao migrations, and the province's Liannan ethnic-culture route pairs it with the Yao villages in the hills to the south.

rows.name: Gulong Gorge
rows.summary: A forested canyon in Qingxin District developed for adventure tourism, best known for white-water rafting on a 6.1 km course that drops 378 m through tight bends and chutes. Above the gorge are a glass sky-walk and viewing platform, aerial adventure rides and a chain of waterfalls with nine tiers. The rafting course was laid out to racing standards and has hosted international events and Guangdong's provincial rafting competition.

rows.name: Hezhong Hot Spring (Qingxin Hot Spring)
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Sankeng town, Qingxin District, with open-air pools beside a tree-lined river embankment; the name means 'hot spring in the river'. Until 2024 the scenic area was officially called the Qingxin Warm Mineral Spring resort, and it has its own hotel and guesthouse rooms for an overnight soak.

rows.name: Huangchuan Three Gorges & Longtan
rows.summary: A river scenic area south of Lianzhou where the Huangchuan, a headwater of the North River, winds through three steep gorges of cliffs and dripping limestone, praised by the 17th-century writer Qu Dajun. The Qingtian glass bridge spans the top of a group of waterfalls on the cliffs, and the Longtan area adds folk performances by local ethnic minorities. The river is also a national water-conservancy scenic area.

rows.name: Huangteng Gorge
rows.summary: A forested gorge in the hills just north of Qingyuan city, nicknamed 'little Jiuzhaigou', where a long, narrow mountain stream has been turned into a white-water rafting run. The course drops past steep canyon walls and waterfalls, and rafting is the main reason to come.

rows.name: Huiguang Pagoda
rows.summary: A six-sided, nine-storey brick pagoda in pavilion style in Lianzhou, first built in 468 under the Liu Song dynasty and rebuilt in the Song. The tower leans noticeably, by about a metre, which has earned it the nickname 'Leaning Tower of the East'.

rows.name: Jinzi Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the uplands of Lianshan Zhuang and Yao Autonomous County, promoted as a place to see snow in southern China, with rare rime ice on the trees in winter. Trails lead past the rock formation known as Yin-Yang Mountain and Queen Peak, with spring flowers, summer sunrises over a sea of cloud and, in autumn, views over three provinces.

rows.name: Jiqingli Xianhu (Jiqingli Black Tea Valley)
rows.summary: A tea and hot-spring resort area north-west of Yingde, the city known as China's home of black tea, built around the hillside plantations of the Jiqingli Black Tea Valley. It combines tea gardens among karst hills and forest lakes with a hot-spring town and a resort community, and the tea valley has been named one of Guangdong's ten most beautiful tea gardens.

rows.name: Jiulong Peak Forest Town (Fenglin Xiaozhen)
rows.summary: A large farm park and rural resort in Jiulong town, set among the limestone pinnacles of the Yingxi Peak Forest, Guangdong's densest belt of karst peaks. It mixes farmland, flower and lotus fields, village guesthouses and hotels, with a small sightseeing train through the lotus ponds and, in the evening, a water-screen light show and night market. A lotus festival is held each summer.

rows.name: Julongwan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Tangtang, the hot-spring town of Fogang County, with bathing pools and hotel accommodation, built by a Hong Kong-invested company. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2008, the first in Fogang County, and is one of several spa resorts around Tangtang.

rows.name: Lianzhou Underground River
rows.summary: A three-level limestone cave in the hills north of Lianzhou, where two dry upper levels lead down to an underground river that visitors travel by boat. The chambers are full of stalactites, stalagmites, columns and flowstone, and the air stays at about 18 °C all year. The writer Qin Mu described it in a 1988 travel essay, and it is one of the best-known sights of north-west Guangdong.

rows.name: Nangang Ancient Yao Village
rows.summary: A hillside village of the Pai Yao, a Yao group whose homeland is Liannan, with houses rising in tiers up a steep mountain slope above Sanpai town. It is listed as a China Historical and Cultural Village, and visitors climb its stepped lanes past the village gate, old defensive walls, the Yao king's house, a hilltop temple and the square used for song and dance gatherings. Provincial tourism routes suggest staying a night in the village.

rows.name: New Yinzhan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Yinzhan in southern Qingcheng District, built around large open-air thermal pools. Besides the pools it has a hotel, private hot-spring villas, sports grounds and a team-building centre, and it has been named one of Guangdong's ten best hot springs.

rows.name: Senbola Holiday Forest
rows.summary: A theme resort in the forested hills of Yangjiao Mountain in Fogang County, opened in 2007 by a Hong Kong developer. It has three main parts: a 'volcano' hot-spring park with a staged eruption show, a glacier-themed water park, and Senbola Wonder World, a forest theme park built around an invented tribal culture. It suits families on a resort break from Guangzhou or Shenzhen.

rows.name: Wanshan Chaowang Stony Desert Park
rows.summary: A viewpoint and national stony-desertification park in the karst hills south of Liannan's county town, named 'ten thousand hills paying homage to the king' after the ranks of rocky peaks facing it across the valley. Its viewing platforms are popular with photographers, and the park also has a ginkgo grove of about 1,000 mu and Guangdong's first exhibition hall on rocky desertification and its control.

rows.name: Xilegu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A large hot-spring resort complex in Tangtang, the hot-spring town of Fogang County, set in the hills around Huanghua Lake. Alongside the Phoenix hot-spring pools it has several hotels and guesthouses, a water park, a playground, a campsite, go-karts, a folk-culture village and staged cultural performances. It is aimed at families on short breaks from the Pearl River Delta, in summer for the water park and in winter for the springs.

rows.name: Xuanzhen Rafting
rows.summary: A resort area on the northern edge of Taihe, Qingxin District's main town, centred on rafting down a mountain stream through a wooded gorge. Around the Xuanzhen Ancient Cave it also has hill scenery and rock formations, a hotel and restaurants.

rows.name: Dadian Stupa, Lingshan Temple
rows.summary: A granite stupa of 824 behind Lingshan Temple in Tongyu town, the tomb of the Chan monk Dadian, who founded the temple in 791 and befriended the exiled Tang writer Han Yu. The bowl-shaped stone tomb rests on an octagonal base carved with dragons, beasts and flowers, and the temple around it is still an active monastery.

rows.name: Fantawild Adventure Shantou (Blue Water Planet)
rows.summary: A science-fiction themed amusement park in Longhu district near the Shantou Bay Bridge, built with ride and show systems from the Fantawild group; official tourism lists now call it Blue Water Planet (Lanshuixing). It has themed indoor and outdoor rides and a children's area, and suits a family day out.

rows.name: Former Chaozhou Customs House
rows.summary: The two-storey customs house of 1919–1921 on Waima Road, wrapped in verandas and topped by a clock, which served the Chaozhou Maritime Customs and its successor until 1988. Restored as the Shantou Customs History Museum, opened in 2008, it tells the story of the treaty port from the customs' founding on Mayu Island in 1860.

rows.name: Former Headquarters of the Eastern Expedition
rows.name_zh: 东征军总指挥部、政治部旧址
rows.summary: Two matching two-storey buildings of 1924 on Waima Road, first a British-run hotel, which served as the command post and political department of the National Revolutionary Army after it entered Shantou in November 1925 during its Eastern Expedition against the warlord Chen Jiongming. Chiang Kai-shek and the Soviet adviser Galen (Blyukher) worked in the west building and Zhou Enlai, head of the political department, in the east one, which now holds a museum on the two expeditions of 1925.

rows.name: Lianhua Peak, Chaoyang
rows.summary: A granite headland in Haimen town, Chaoyang, named for boulders split like lotus petals and tied by legend to the Song loyalist Wen Tianxiang, who is said to have watched here in vain for the fleeing Song emperor's ships in 1278. Lianfeng Academy, built in 1594 in his memory, stands below the peak, and the area also has cliff inscriptions, odd rock formations and a beach.

rows.name: Lianhua Rural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A rural tourism area in Lianhua town, north-east Chenghai, centred on Lianhua Mountain. Paths lead up the mountain, and orchid nurseries, leisure farms and a hot-spring resort lie around its foot; it suits a country day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Longhutan Beach Resort
rows.summary: A sandy beach on Longhutan (Dragon and Tiger Beach) in Haojiang district, south of central Shantou; the scenic area, known until 2023 as the CITIC Golf Seaside Resort, now covers only the beachfront. The beach is used for swimming and water sports, including a national surfing contest in 2025, and a resort hotel and the Zhonghai water park are nearby.

rows.name: Mayu Island
rows.summary: A small island at the mouth of Shantou harbour, known in the treaty-port era as Double Island, where the American and British consulates and the port's first foreign-run customs house opened in 1860 before moving across the harbour during the 1860s. Visitors come for its two Mazu (Tianhou) temples, one founded in the Yuan dynasty, a Qing Dragon King temple and a small swimming beach beneath the Shantou Bay Bridge.

rows.name: Nan'ao Island
rows.summary: Shantou's largest island and the seat of Nan'ao County, crossed by the Tropic of Cancer and linked to the mainland by the Nan'ao Bridge since 2015. It draws visitors to sandy bays such as Qing'ao Bay at its east end and to coastal-defence history, including the Zongbing Fu at Shen'ao, headquarters of the Ming and Qing regional commanders, begun in 1576.

rows.name: Qianmei Village and Chen Cihong's Former Residence
rows.summary: An old village of overseas Chinese families in Longdu town, Chenghai, best known for the mansion compound the Chen family of overseas merchants built between 1910 and 1939. Chen Cihong's former residence has 506 rooms in four linked compounds that join the traditional Chaoshan courtyard plan with Western-style villas, decorated with wood and stone carving, plasterwork and imported tiles and glass.

rows.name: Qilu Fort
rows.summary: A circular Qing coastal fort of 1874–1879 on the Shantou waterfront, its thick walls built of granite and a mortar of shell lime, sand and glutinous rice, and ringed by a moat. It is the centrepiece of Shipaotai (Stone Fort) Park on Haibin Road.

rows.name: Queshi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A cluster of granite hills on the south shore of Shantou harbour, facing the old city across the water, with weathered boulders, caves, cliff inscriptions and harbour views from peaks such as Tashan and Yanfeng. Treaty-port buildings survive among the trees, among them the former British consulate of 1862 and Queshi Church, which mixes Chinese and Western styles.

rows.name: Shantou Station of the Central Red Traffic Line
rows.name_zh: 中央红色交通线汕头交通站旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōngyāng Hóngsè Jiāotōngxiàn Shàntóu Jiāotōngzhàn Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A three-storey arcaded shophouse on Haiping Road in Shantou's old town, which in the early 1930s housed the Huafu electrical shop, a front for a station on the Communist Party's secret courier line between its leadership and the Soviet areas. It now holds a small exhibition on the line, whose other listed stations are in western Fujian.

rows.name: Wenguang Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda in the old centre of Chaoyang, first built in 1131 under the Southern Song and rebuilt several times, most fully in 1635 and 1815. Spiral stone stairs run up inside, stone balustrades ring the middle floors, and it remains the landmark of the old town.

rows.name: Honghai Bay (Zhelang)
rows.summary: A coastal scenic area on the Zhelang peninsula at the eastern end of Honghai Bay, south-east of Shanwei city, where sandy beaches alternate with rocky headlands and a lighthouse stands on the offshore Zhelang Rock. Its steady winds and swell have made it a venue for sailing, windsurfing and surfing since the 1990s, and the scenic area offers sailing, jet-ski and parasailing trips.

rows.name: Luodong Plum Garden
rows.summary: A hillside plum orchard around Luodong village in Shuichun town, Luhe, a Hakka county known for its green plums, rated a 4A scenic area in 2023. Around the Minor and Major Cold solar terms in January, the blossom on more than 10,000 mu (about 670 hectares) of trees covers the slopes white, and boardwalks, a streamside park, old woodland and named rocks can be visited all year.
