rows.name: Red Palace and Red Square, Haifeng
rows.summary: Haifeng's former Confucian school, with its Lingxing gate, crescent pond and Dacheng Hall, where Peng Pai convened the county congress of workers, peasants and soldiers on 18–21 November 1927 that proclaimed the Haifeng Soviet government; the buildings were painted red and renamed the Red Palace. The open ground to the east, where a mass rally was held on 1 December 1927, became the Red Square. The scenic area also takes in the nearby former residence of Peng Pai (1896–1929), the Dequ study hall and the former Chishanyue farmers' association.

rows.name: Shuidishan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort of about 85 hectares in forested hills at the heart of the Shenzhen-Shanwei Special Cooperation Zone, where a river valley forms a chain of pools and waterfalls. Its spring water emerges at about 73°C, and the resort has bathing pools, a long infinity pool and a hotel; a paragliding base operates on the slopes of Shuidi Mountain nearby.

rows.name: Xinshan Red Tourism Village
rows.summary: A village in Fucheng town on the edge of Haifeng that was an early base of the peasant movement led by Peng Pai: its farmers' association was founded in 1923 in the village hall Yipingshe, and its peasant guards drilled on an open ground known as Laohuiding. The village has restored these sites and the former homes of local revolutionaries, and built a red-culture museum, square and street. It is one stop on a national rural-tourism route linking Haifeng's revolutionary sites.

rows.name: Xuanwu Mountain and Yuanshan Temple
rows.summary: A hill in the coastal town of Jieshi, Lufeng, crowned by Yuanshan Temple, dedicated to the Daoist god Xuantian Shangdi and founded in 1127. Enlarged into its present layout in 1577 and renamed in the Kangxi reign to avoid the emperor's personal name, the south-facing temple has a gate hall, middle and main halls and side halls, with plaques inscribed by Lin Zexu and Liu Yongfu.

rows.name: Caoxi Hot Spring Holiday Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Mabao town, Qujiang district, about 2 km from Nanhua Temple, the monastery of the Chan patriarch Huineng, so the two are easily combined. It has outdoor hot-spring pools, a summer water-play pool with slides, sweat-bath and salt-bath rooms, and hotel accommodation. It is a place for an overnight soak rather than a sight in itself.

rows.name: Changwei Village Hakka Enclosure
rows.summary: A four-storey Hakka fortified house in Changwei village, Luoba town, built in 1855, combining an enclosing tower block, an ancestral hall and family dwellings on a rectangular, south-facing plan. It was named one of the hundred major new finds of China's Third National Cultural Heritage Survey in 2011 and listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Donghua Mountain and Donghua Temple
rows.summary: A hill scenic area on the eastern edge of Wengyuan town, centred on Donghua Temple, a Chan Buddhist monastery whose main hall houses a large gilded Buddha. Paths climb from the temple to a hilltop viewing platform over the surrounding hills, and cherry trees around the temple flower in early spring.

rows.name: Guangdong Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A deep, forested gorge in Dabu town in the far south-west of Ruyuan county, cut through quartz sandstone by the Dabu River, which drops from the rim to the valley floor in a large waterfall. A stone stairway of more than 1,300 steps descends into the canyon past rock pillars and falls such as Tenglong Falls and Huanglong Pool, and the scenic area stages high-wire acrobatic shows across the gorge.

rows.name: Gufo Dongtian Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave on the south-western outskirts of Lechang, also called Gufo Yan ('Ancient Buddha Rock') because Buddha images were once placed inside and a temple was built at its mouth. A lit walkway leads through stacked chambers of stalactites, stalagmites and flowstone, which stay cool all year at under 20 °C.

rows.name: Jinglülun Culture Tourism Town
rows.summary: A Chan (Zen) Buddhist-themed hot-spring resort inside Xiaokeng National Forest Park in Qujiang district, opened in 2014, with a forest hot-spring area, a hotel, a suspension bridge across a wooded valley and a jade statue of Guanyin. It is a modern leisure resort, best for an overnight soak combined with a visit to Nanhua Temple.

rows.name: Maba Man and Shixia Site
rows.summary: Shizi Yan, a pair of limestone hills near Maba, is where in 1958 farmers found in a cave the skull of 'Maba Man', an archaic human intermediate between Homo erectus and Homo sapiens, and where a Neolithic settlement and cemetery, the type site of the Shixia culture, was excavated from 1973. A site park with the Maba Man Museum now surrounds the hills.

rows.name: Mantang Wei Hakka Enclosure
rows.summary: Begun in 1833 by the Guan family, Mantang Wei in Aizi town is a fortified Hakka communal house made up of three linked enclosures, the upper, middle and lower wei. Listed as a national heritage site in 1996, it is open to visitors as the Mantang Hakka Enclosure scenic area.

rows.name: Mei Pass and Zhuji Lane
rows.summary: On the Meiling ridge at the Guangdong–Jiangxi border, Zhang Jiuling, later a Tang chancellor, cut a paved road through the pass in 716, opening the main overland route between the Yangtze valley and Guangzhou; the stone road and a gate tower, first built in the Song and inscribed in the Ming 'Nanyue Xiongguan' and 'First Pass of Lingnan', survive. About 15 km south, the old village street of Zhuji Lane was the staging post where many Cantonese clans of the Pearl River Delta place their ancestors before the migration south, and it is lined with rebuilt clan halls and an old stone pagoda.

rows.name: Nanhua Temple
rows.summary: Founded in the early 6th century as Baolin Temple, Nanhua Temple on the Caoxi stream is where Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of Chan (Zen) Buddhism, taught from 677, making it the ancestral seat of Southern Chan. Its halls were largely rebuilt from 1934 under the monk Xuyun, and the Sixth Patriarch Hall enshrines a seated figure of Huineng made over his body; the temple also keeps Song-dynasty wooden arhat carvings.

rows.name: Sanying Pagoda
rows.summary: Completed in 1009 under the Northern Song, this hexagonal brick pagoda in central Nanxiong rises nine storeys outside, with hidden levels between them inside, and is crowned by an iron finial. Its name, 'Three Shadows', comes from a legend that it cast three shadows, two of them upside down; it is also called Yanxiang Temple Pagoda after the vanished temple beside it.

rows.name: Shuangfeng Fort
rows.summary: A large rectangular fortified compound in Shitang village, built from 1899 over twelve years by the local gentleman Li Zisheng to shelter villagers from bandits, with a main tower and four gun towers joined by high brick walls and surrounded by a moat. After 1927 the Communist-led Shitang peasant association held out inside it for nine months against Kuomintang forces; the fort had partly collapsed before 1949 and was later restored.

rows.name: Xijing Ancient Road, Ruyuan
rows.summary: The Xijing Ancient Road was an overland route across the mountains of northern Guangdong towards the Central Plains, first opened in the Eastern Han and kept in use until the Qing. Its best-preserved stone-paved stretches climb through the hills of Daqiao town in Ruyuan county and can be followed on foot.

rows.name: Yunlong Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A square, five-storey solid brick pagoda with a platform at each level, built in the late Tang dynasty between 894 and 901 and repaired in the Ming. It stands in Angang village, Dongtang town, at the site of Xishan Temple, renamed Yunlong Temple in the Qing.

rows.name: Yunmen Temple
rows.summary: Founded in 923 by the Chan master Wenyan, Yunmen Temple is the birthplace of the Yunmen school, one of the five houses of Chan (Zen) Buddhism. Most of its present halls were rebuilt under the monk Xuyun between 1943 and 1951 in traditional Qing style, and the temple keeps a Southern Han stele of the 10th century honouring its founder. Around it, the Yunmen Mountain eco-cultural tourism area adds a water park, go-karts and a Guoshan Yao village.

rows.name: Yuntianhai Forest Hot Spring Resort
rows.name_zh: 云天海原始森林度假村
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in forested hills beside the G105 road in Xinfeng county, with spring-fed outdoor pools, a mountain-water play park and hotel accommodation. It is a leisure resort for a weekend soak rather than a sightseeing destination.

rows.name: Chung Ying Street Boundary Stones
rows.summary: Chung Ying Street in Shatoujiao is a short street whose centre line forms the land boundary between Shenzhen and Hong Kong, marked by stone boundary markers of 1905 carved in Chinese on the side facing Shenzhen and in English on the side facing Hong Kong. The listed stones are those under Shenzhen's care, and the nearby Chung Ying Street History Museum tells the story of the border and the shopping street that grew up along it.

rows.name: Dapeng Fortress
rows.summary: Built in 1394 as a Ming garrison town against coastal pirates, Dapeng Fortress withstood a siege of more than forty days by Japanese pirates in 1571 and in the Qing was the base of the Dapeng naval command during the Opium War years. Its walls and gates enclose lanes of old houses, temples and the mansions of Qing commanders such as Lai Enjue, and a museum has run the site since 1996.

rows.name: Evergreen Resort (Qingqing World)
rows.summary: An eco-tourism farm park opened in 1995 at the foot of Dananshan hill, with a simulated rainforest of artificial mist and rain, a butterfly garden and a petting area with small animals. It now suits young families more than sightseers.

rows.name: Fairy Lake Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A large botanical garden at the foot of Wutong Mountain beside Shenzhen Reservoir, founded in 1983, open since 1988 and now linked with the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Lakes and pavilions frame themed collections including a national cycad conservation centre, desert-plant and shade-plant areas and a fossil forest, and the grounds also hold Hongfa Temple, which draws huge crowds at Chinese New Year.

rows.name: Former East River Column Headquarters, Tuyang
rows.name_zh: 土洋村东江纵队司令部旧址
rows.pinyin: Tǔyáng Cūn Dōngjiāng Zòngduì Sīlìngbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A former Italian Catholic mission in Tuyang village, built in 1912 in a mixed Chinese and Western style, with a two-storey main house, a chapel and a former stable. From December 1943 to May 1945 it was the headquarters of the Communist-led East River Column guerrilla force and of the Guangdong provincial party committee, which held the Tuyang Conference here in August 1944; it has been open as an exhibition hall on the column's history since 1998.

rows.name: Guangming Farm Grand View Garden
rows.summary: A family farm park on land of the old Guangming state farm, founded in the late 1950s and long known for its dairy, with fields, flower beds, animal enclosures and hands-on farming activities such as crop picking. Seasonal festivals add staged shows and evening lantern displays.

rows.name: Guanlan Shanshui Tianyuan Farm Resort
rows.summary: A farm-style leisure park of about 27 hectares in Guanlan, laid out in Lingnan and Hakka water-village style, with a resort hotel, village hot springs, a water park with a wave pool and a children's amusement area. Its country restaurant serves Hakka food, and the park is aimed at families from the city.

rows.name: Mission Hills Shenzhen
rows.summary: Founded in 1992 in Guanlan, Mission Hills Golf Club was recognised by Guinness World Records in 2004 as the world's largest golf facility, with twelve 18-hole courses designed by players such as Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, Ernie Els and Annika Sörenstam. The surrounding 5A leisure area also has a resort hotel, and is mainly of interest to golfers and resort guests.

rows.name: OCT East
rows.summary: A resort and theme-park complex opened in 2007 by the OCT Group in the Sanzhoutian hills above Dameisha beach. Knight Valley is an adventure park with rides and a man-made waterfall, while Tea Stream Valley has tea terraces, wetland gardens, a Chinese-style tea town and a copy of the Swiss resort of Interlaken; a forest train links the areas, and the complex also has hotels, a golf course and Huaxing Temple.

rows.name: OH Bay and Bay Glory Ferris Wheel
rows.summary: A waterfront leisure and shopping district on Qianhai Bay in Bao'an's new city centre, developed by the OCT Group, with seaside promenades, shops and restaurants. Its centrepiece is Bay Glory, a 128 m cantilevered Ferris wheel opened in April 2021, whose cabins look out over Qianhai Bay and the Pearl River estuary.

rows.name: Overseas Chinese Town (OCT) Theme Parks
rows.summary: Nanshan's Overseas Chinese Town groups Shenzhen's best-known theme parks: Splendid China Folk Village, founded in 1988, with small-scale models of Chinese landmarks and full-size replica villages of China's ethnic groups where staged shows are held; Window of the World, opened in 1994, with miniature copies of world landmarks; and Happy Valley, an amusement park with roller coasters opened in 1998. The district around them also has the OCT Contemporary Art Terminal and the OCT Harbour waterfront.

rows.name: Shenzhen Safari Park
rows.summary: Opened in 1993 beside Xili Lake, this safari-style zoo is described by Shenzhen's tourism bureau as the first in China to keep its animals uncaged. Sightseeing vehicles tour the large-mammal areas, and the walking zones include giant pandas and South China tigers.

rows.name: Waterlands Resort (Haishang Tianyuan)
rows.summary: An eco-park opened in 2001 in the coastal wetlands at Shajing, beside the Pearl River estuary, with lakes, streams, woods and lawns, birdlife and seasonal flowers. It combines sightseeing with family entertainment and nature education.

rows.name: Chunwan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst area beside Chunwan town in northern Yangchun, ringed by craggy limestone peaks that have been used as a film location. Its sights include the Longgong Yan ('Dragon Palace') cave, a stone forest of limestone pinnacles, the Tongzhen and Ciyun caves, a tall rock pillar called the 'Sky Candle' and the old Nawu bridge.

rows.name: Da'ao Fishing Village
rows.summary: An old fishing village in the south-east of Dongping town on the Yangdong coast, once a port of call on the Maritime Silk Road, that keeps the look of a Ming and Qing fishing settlement beside its harbour. Its old street faces the moored boats, the village's folk-customs hall now serves as the Yangdong District Museum with displays on the Tanka boat people, and when the fishing season reopens in mid-August the harbour fills with visitors buying fresh seafood.

rows.name: Dajiao Bay, Hailing Island
rows.summary: A curving, horn-shaped sandy bay at Zhapo on the south coast of Hailing Island, the island's earliest-developed and best-known beach, which with its surroundings was rated a 5A scenic area in 2015 as the Dajiao Bay Maritime Silk Road Tourist Area. Over the hill to the west lies the long beach of Shili Yintan, beside which the Maritime Silk Road Museum of Guangdong (opened 2009) displays the hull and cargo of the Southern Song shipwreck Nanhai I.

rows.name: Lingxiao Cave
rows.summary: A large karst cave at Helang town in north-western Yangchun, part of a national geopark, whose chambers rise in three levels above an underground river. Visitors take a boat along about 400 m of the river past lit rock formations, then climb into the halls, where tall stalactite pillars and cliff inscriptions from the Ming and Qing dynasties can be seen.

rows.name: Changgangpo Aqueduct
rows.summary: An irrigation aqueduct striding across the farmland of the Luoping basin, built from 1976 to 1981 by more than 10,000 volunteer labourers from across Luoding county to end the frequent droughts around the county town. A memorial hall in nearby Shuanglian village uses film and interactive displays to tell the story of its construction.

rows.name: Dawan Historic Buildings
rows.summary: A group of late-Qing and early-Republican clan halls, family schools and large courtyard houses of the Li lineage spread through the villages of Dawan town, fourteen of which were listed together as a national heritage site in 2013. They include the Li Clan Ancestral Hall of 1856 and the Qichangzhan mansion of 1920, built in the Lingnan manner with three-bay fronts and successive halls and courtyards.

rows.name: Guo'en Temple, the Sixth Patriarch's Hometown
rows.summary: Founded in 683 on Longshan hill in Liuzu town, Guo'en Temple is where Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch of Chan (Zen) Buddhism, died in 713; it is counted with Guangxiao and Nanhua temples as one of his three ancestral seats, and the Platform Sutra is said to have been compiled here. The present halls date from the Ming to the Republican era, and the surrounding Sixth Patriarch's Hometown resort area also takes in his former home, a lychee tree said to have been planted by him and the Longshan hot spring.

rows.name: Jinshuitai Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: A modern hot-spring resort town in Shuitai, Xinxing county, run by the Xiangshun group and known for having three different types of natural hot spring in one area, with outdoor bathing pools, hotels and conference facilities. Xinxing county is known for its hot springs, and Guo'en Temple at Liuzu town is about 25 km to the west.

rows.name: Longkan Cave Inscriptions
rows.summary: A limestone cave beneath an isolated karst hill near Tanli village, where a text recording the religious retreat founded here in 621 by the Yongning county magistrate Chen Puguang was carved on the wall in 699. Regarded as the oldest surviving cliff inscription in Guangdong, it uses several of the new characters created under Empress Wu Zetian, which makes it valuable for the history of Chinese writing.

rows.name: Tianlu Mountain Resort
rows.summary: A mountain resort in Lidong town on the slopes of Tianlu Mountain, which at about 1,250 m is the highest peak in south-central Guangdong. It offers a 3.8 km rafting run down the Chanlong Gorge, a forest boardwalk through Wuyou Valley, a small mountain train and amusement rides, with a lake-view hotel, hot-spring cabins and hillside villas. It is mainly a weekend outdoor-activity destination for visitors from the Pearl River Delta.

rows.name: Dinglong Bay Marine Tourism Area
rows.summary: A large beach resort on the coast of Qinba town, Wuchuan, opened in 2017, with hotels and holiday flats along a long sandy beach and a water park. At holidays it stages lion dances, folk parades, light shows and fireworks, and it is built for beach holidays and family breaks.

rows.name: Former French Legation and Army Headquarters, Guangzhouwan
rows.name_zh: 广州湾法国公使署旧址
rows.summary: Two colonial buildings facing each other across Yan'an Road in Xiashan, the administrative centre of Guangzhouwan, the territory France occupied in 1898 and held under a lease from 1899 until 1945: the legation of 1903 and the army headquarters of 1905, known locally as the Green Building. After the Japanese occupation and the territory's return in 1945 they housed the new Zhanjiang city government and police, and the legation is now one of Zhanjiang Museum's three sites, with a permanent exhibition.

rows.name: Haibin Volcanic Hot Spring (Blue Moon Bay)
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at the Haibin Hotel in Xiashan district, central Zhanjiang, now listed as Blue Moon Bay; its earlier name, Haibin Volcanic Hot Spring, comes from the geothermal water drawn from volcanic rock. Its outdoor pools make a relaxing spa stop in town rather than a sight.

rows.name: Huguangyan Maar Lake
rows.summary: A volcanic crater lake (maar) in Mazhang district, formed by steam explosions some 140,000 to 200,000 years ago and now the core of the Huguangyan area of the Leiqiong Global Geopark. Footpaths circle the steep, wooded crater above the clear lake, with viewpoints along the rim.

rows.name: Jinsha Bay Seafront
rows.summary: An urban seafront in Chikan district, north of central Zhanjiang, with a sandy bathing beach, a seaside promenade park and open squares backed by the towers of the Jinsha Bay new town. It is a place for a stroll and a swim by the bay rather than a destination in itself.

rows.name: Leizu Temple
rows.summary: A shrine on Yingbang Hill west of Leizhou to Chen Wenyu, the first Tang prefect of Leizhou, worshipped locally as the Thunder Ancestor. Founded in 642, it keeps Ming and Qing halls in three courtyards, four stone figures from the Five Dynasties and more than 40 inscribed steles from the Song to the Qing.

rows.name: Maodegong Drum City
rows.summary: A resort and culture park in Leizhou opened in 2015, themed on drums and built in the style of the region's Ming and Qing architecture. Its food street, named a provincial Cantonese food street in 2022, and its squares host lion dances, Lei opera and other folk performances, with staged shows built around the Leizhou drum.

rows.name: Naozhou Lighthouse
rows.summary: A stone lighthouse on Ma'an Hill, the highest point of Naozhou Island, built from 1899 by the French administration of the leased territory of Guangzhouwan and lit in 1904. The tower of local volcanic stone still turns its original optic of crystal prisms and has been unmanned since 2004, with a small exhibition on navigation marks beside it.

rows.name: Sanlingshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 22,700 mu on the south-western edge of Zhanjiang, known locally as the city's lungs, with low wooded hills around the Chixi Reservoir. A greenway about 17 km long loops through the park, and grey herons and other waterbirds feed in the wetlands by the reservoir.

rows.name: Suixi Confucius Culture City
rows.summary: A Confucian-themed park on Bangtang Ridge in Suixi county town, opened in 2016; its new Confucius temple, completed in 2017, replaces the county's old one, demolished in 1978. The temple is modelled on the one at Qufu, with a seven-bay Dacheng Hall, and is joined by a Wenchang pavilion, a shopping street built in Spring and Autumn style, lotus lakes and natural basalt columns left by ancient eruptions.

rows.name: Deqing Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Deqing's school-temple of Confucius, founded in 1011 and moved to this site in 1081; after a flood its main Dacheng Hall was rebuilt in 1297 and still stands. The hall is known for its unusual timber frame, which leaves out four interior columns and carries very long bracket arms, and the Lingxing Gate, semicircular pond, Dacheng Gate and side halls survive around it. Ceremonies for Confucius and children's first-writing rites are held here twice a year.

rows.name: He River Greenway Gallery
rows.summary: A riverside greenway along the He River in Fengkai County, running from Jiangkou, the county town, upstream to Dazhou town near the Guangxi border, on the old Xiaohe road between Guangdong and Guangxi. Cycle paths, a 121 km 'Hejiang 100 li' cycling route and riverside parks follow the bamboo-lined banks, and sightseeing boats run between Guangxin pier and Longhuang Island with its old-pier park. Villages, guesthouses and a forest wellness base along the way make it a slow, scenic day out.

rows.name: Longmu Ancestral Temple, Yuecheng
rows.summary: The principal temple of the Dragon Mother (Longmu), a river goddess worshipped all along the West River, standing where the Yuecheng River joins the West River in Yuecheng town. The present stone archway, gate, incense pavilion, main hall and side halls date mostly from the late Qing Guangxu reign and are finely worked in brick, wood and stone, and the compound also holds the Dragon Mother's tomb. Her birthday fair in the fifth lunar month is a national intangible heritage item.

rows.name: Longshan Scenic Area, Fengkai Geopark
rows.summary: A karst scenic area in Heerkou town, part of the Fengkai National Geopark, where limestone hills rise from the valley floor in a landscape locals compare to Guilin. Paths lead around the hills and into caves, one of which has been fitted out as a themed show cave.

rows.name: Maozhua Valley (Cat's Paw Valley)
rows.summary: A cat-themed leisure park of about 600 mu in Huilong town, Gaoyao District, built for family day trips. It mixes cat-themed art and interactive attractions with animal and plant displays, fruit and vegetable picking, flower fields, water play and 'starry-sky' tents for overnight stays.

rows.name: Mei'an Temple
rows.summary: A small Buddhist temple on Mei'an hill in western Zhaoqing, founded in 996 by the monk Zhiyuan where, by tradition, the Chan patriarch Huineng had planted a plum tree. Its main hall keeps the beam and bracket structure of the Song period, and the gate and patriarch hall stand on the same axis. The temple is now part of Zhaoqing Museum and holds an exhibition on Huineng's life.

rows.name: Panlong Gorge
rows.summary: A wooded mountain valley in northern Deqing County known for its chain of waterfalls. Visitors climb paths beside the stream past the falls, and the gorge has been used for rafting in the warm season.

rows.name: Qishi River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested river valley in Weizheng town in the hills of northern Sihui, where Sihui meets Guangning and Qingyuan. As its name, 'strange-rock river', suggests, it is visited for a boulder-strewn mountain stream crossed by a broad curtain-like waterfall, with natural pools for swimming in summer.

rows.name: Seven Star Crags & Dinghu Mountain (Star Lake)
rows.summary: Zhaoqing's 5A Star Lake scenic area has two parts: the Seven Star Crags, seven limestone peaks rising from the lakes beside the city centre, and Dinghu Mountain, a forested range about 15 km to the north-east. Paths and boats link the crags, their caves and lakeside walks, and the cliffs carry 531 inscriptions from the Tang dynasty onwards, most of them in Stone Chamber Cave, including Li Yong's record of 727. Dinghu Mountain became China's first nature reserve in 1956 and has subtropical forest, waterfalls, mountain streams and the Buddhist Qingyun Temple.

rows.name: Suijiang Bamboo Sea
rows.summary: An eco-tourism area of bamboo-covered hills along the Sui River on the edge of Guangning, a county known as the home of bamboo. Covering about 8 km², it links an old river pier, a Taoist shrine, a bamboo ecology art museum, plank walkways through the bamboo and a campsite, and is used for walks, camping and stays in bamboo-country guesthouses.

rows.name: Yuejiang Tower (Former HQ of Ye Ting's Independent Regiment)
rows.summary: A quadrangle of two-storey halls around a Lingnan courtyard on a low hill above the West River in Zhaoqing, given its name in 1641 when it was rebuilt on the model of Tengwang Pavilion and rebuilt several times since. In November 1925 it became the headquarters of the newly formed 34th Regiment of the National Revolutionary Army's 4th Army, the 'Independent Regiment' commanded by Ye Ting, which went on to fight in the Northern Expedition. Since 1959 it has housed a memorial hall to the regiment, whose exhibition was renewed for the regiment's centenary in 2025.

rows.name: Zhaoqing City Wall
rows.summary: The brick city wall of the old town of Zhaoqing, built in 1113 when the earth ramparts of the newly promoted prefecture were enlarged and faced with brick, and repaired many times under the Ming and Qing. Most of the circuit survives, although the gate towers were pulled down and much of the wall lowered in the 1920s; the north-west stretch has been restored with battlements and a paved walk on top, crowned by the rebuilt Piyun Tower.

rows.name: Chadong Chen Ancestral Halls
rows.summary: A group of four Qing-dynasty ancestral halls of the Chen clan in Chadong village, Langbian, one of the larger and better-preserved ancestral-hall groups in the Pearl River Delta. The four are the Chen Ancestral Hall, the Liren Ancestral Temple and the Gongsan and Jingxi memorial halls, listed together as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: China (Dachong) Redwood Culture Expo City
rows.summary: A large complex of new buildings in mixed old styles in Dachong, a town whose hardwood ('redwood' or mahogany) furniture industry dates from the late 1970s, combining Lingnan, Jiangnan, Huizhou and imperial palace architecture. It was built as a culture, commerce and tourism complex for the furniture trade, and its old-style halls and streets are as much a shopping centre as a sight.

rows.name: Huayi Plaza, Guzhen
rows.summary: A lighting-industry showcase run by the Huayi lighting group in Guzhen, a town built on the lighting industry. Visitors tour themed, hands-on displays on lighting design and manufacture, and it is mainly aimed at study tours and anyone curious about the town's trade.

rows.name: Sun Yat-sen's Hometown, Cuiheng
rows.summary: The village of Cuiheng, where Sun Yat-sen was born and grew up, centred on the two-storey house that his elder brother Sun Mei paid for and Sun himself oversaw building in 1892, with a Western-style front and a traditional Chinese interior. Beside it the memorial museum, rebuilt in 1999, covers his life and family, and restored village houses and fields show the world of his childhood. The 5A area also takes in the rest of Cuiheng village, the Zhongshan Film and TV City, a Xinhai Revolution memorial park and Litoujian hill with the Sun family graves.

rows.name: Zhan Garden
rows.summary: A private classical garden built from 1998 over five years by the Macau businessman Huang Yuanxin for his mother and named after her family name, Zhan. Laid out by craftsmen brought from Suzhou on a hillside with water through the middle, it blends Suzhou and Lingnan garden styles with some Western touches, and it opened to visitors after his mother moved out.

rows.name: By-Health Transparent Factory
rows.summary: A working factory of the dietary-supplement maker By-Health in Sanzao, Jinwan District, opened to visitors in 2012 so that the public can follow its raw-material stores, production lines and testing laboratories. A nutrition exploration hall added in 2019 offers interactive health displays and simple health checks, and a highly automated fourth-phase plant has been running since 2021; by mid-2026 the site had received more than two million visitors.

rows.name: Chen Fang Family Residence
rows.summary: The home-village complex of Chen Fang (Chun Afong, c. 1825–1906), the Chinese merchant who made a fortune in Hawaii, at Meixi in Xiangzhou District, built from 1891 after his return. It includes his mansion, which mixes Lingnan and Western features, the Chen ancestral hall, the Meixi temple, a watchtower, family tombs and three granite archways granted by the Guangxu Emperor to honour his charity, now the centre of the Meixi Archways park.

rows.name: Dong'ao Island
rows.summary: A small, mostly forested island in the middle of the Wanshan archipelago, south-east of Zhuhai, with one main settlement, Dong'ao village. Its sights include the Dong'ao gun fort, built in 1729 to guard the sea approaches, the ruins of a customs station set up in 1898 and rock formations along the shore.

rows.name: Guishan Island
rows.summary: An island in the Pearl River estuary between Zhuhai and Lantau, seat of Guishan town in the Wanshan archipelago, renamed in 1954 after the warship Guishan, whose crew made a beach landing here in the Wanshan Islands campaign of 1950. Round-island routes lead to the Guishan warship memorial park, a square and poem wall dedicated to Wen Tianxiang, a Mazu temple, rock inscriptions and lighthouses, and the surrounding waters are a base for sea fishing.

rows.name: Imperial Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort opened in 1999 on former paddy fields at Nanmen village, Doumen, in western Zhuhai, where hot water had long welled up from the ground. Built in a Tang-dynasty style, it has outdoor and indoor hot-spring pools, spa treatments, restaurants and a hotel.

rows.name: New Yuanming Palace
rows.summary: A theme park at the foot of Shijing Mountain in Xiangzhou, Zhuhai, opened in 1997 with full-size reconstructions of scenes from Beijing's Old Summer Palace (Yuanmingyuan), which was burnt in 1860. Chinese palace halls and Jiangnan-style garden buildings line a central axis and the shores of a lake modelled on the Fuhai, while the western part recreates the European-style palaces, including the Haiyan Tang and the great fountain.

rows.name: Rossini Watch Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: The factory park of the Zhuhai watchmaker Rossini at Tangjiawan, where a company-funded museum of clocks and watches opened in 2012. Its halls trace timekeeping from ancient instruments to modern wristwatches, with hands-on displays, and a viewing area looks onto the watch production lines.

rows.name: Sites of Japanese Wartime Atrocities on Sanzao Island
rows.name_zh: 三灶岛侵华日军罪行遗迹
rows.pinyin: Sānzào Dǎo Qīnhuá Rìjūn Zuìxíng Yíjì
rows.summary: A group of sites on Sanzao Island recording the Japanese occupation that began in 1938, when Japanese forces built an airbase here and massacred islanders. They include the Wanren Fen ('Ten Thousand Graves') memorial to the massacre victims, first built in 1948 with funds from overseas Chinese and people in Hong Kong and Macau and moved to a hillside at Shengtang village in 1979, the Qianren Fen mass grave at Yunong, a former 'comfort station', a Japanese cliff inscription, bunkers and an ammunition store.

rows.name: Wailingding Island
rows.summary: A hilly island at the north-eastern edge of the Wanshan archipelago, only a short distance south of Hong Kong's outlying islands but administered by Zhuhai as the seat of Dangan town. Most residents live along the west coast around the town and Miaowan, and the clear waters around the island support coral communities.

rows.name: Yequgou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley tourist area in Yuancheng District, Heyuan, run by a local tourism company. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Shuimei Hot Spring Resort (Andun)
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Andun in Huidong County, run by an investment company, with hot-spring pools in a forested valley. Its forest-wellness base was one of the first named nationally in 2020.

rows.name: Baise Happy Town
rows.summary: A leisure complex south-east of Baise built around the Xinghe water park, with other family attractions and a street of restaurants and shops. It is a place for families after water rides and amusements rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Baise Uprising Memorial Park
rows.summary: A memorial park on Yinglong, Panlong and Houlong hills on the east side of Baise, set up in 2008 around the sites of the Baise Uprising of 11 December 1929, in which Communist forces led by Deng Xiaoping, Zhang Yunyi and Wei Baqun founded the Seventh Red Army. Its main sights are the Baise Uprising Memorial Hall, with exhibitions on the uprising and the You River base area, the uprising monument and the Youjiang ethnic history museum. In the old town by the river, the Cantonese guild hall of 1720 that housed the Seventh Red Army's headquarters and the three-storey Qingfeng Building of 1911, its political department, are also part of the park.

rows.name: Cen Family Buildings (Gongbao Mansion), Xilin
rows.summary: The hillside compound of the Cen family above the Tuoniang River at Nalao, home of the Qing official Cen Yuying, Viceroy of Yunnan and Guizhou, and his son Cen Chunxuan. Its centrepiece, the Gongbao Mansion begun in 1876, is a three-courtyard brick-and-timber residence with painted beams and carved wood; around it stand the family's Nanyang Academy, the Rongludi house, a three-storey octagonal pavilion, an ancestral hall and a Ming-dynasty general's temple. The buildings blend Han official architecture with the building traditions of the Zhuang region of western Guangxi.

rows.name: Dashiwei Tiankeng (Leye Sinkholes)
rows.summary: The largest of about 30 collapse sinkholes around Leye: Dashiwei is about 613 m deep, 600 m long and 420 m wide, with an underground river and a primeval forest of about 9.6 hectares growing on its floor. The scenic area at Shuaba village also takes in neighbouring sinkholes such as Baidong and Shenmu, and lies within the Leye–Fengshan UNESCO Global Geopark, listed in 2010.

rows.name: Dawangling Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest scenic area in the heart of the Dawangling nature reserve, known for its well-preserved old-growth forest, groves of tree ferns and river rafting. The rafting run is 5 km long with a drop of 126 m, on a boulder-strewn stream shaded by the forest canopy.

rows.name: Debao Pony Kingdom
rows.summary: A family theme park built around the Debao pony, the county's small local horse breed, opened in 2020 at the exit of Jixingyan Cave. Visitors can ride and watch the ponies, and the park has a pony arena and a theatre for staged shows, a petting area, a play park and wooden-cabin and tent hotels. It suits families with young children.

rows.name: Equan Spring
rows.summary: A large karst spring 6 km south of Jingxi city, welling up from an underground river into a clear pool among rice fields and limestone peaks; its waters flow on towards Detian Waterfall. A 15-arch Qing-dynasty stone bridge crosses the outflow, bamboo rafts pass beneath it, and a stele carved with a huge character for 'goose' recalls the legend behind the spring's name.

rows.name: Fangshan Cultural Park, Debao
rows.summary: A riverside park of about 17 hectares in the centre of Debao town, joining Fangshan hill and the former Jiuqu Bridge park along the Jian River. The Debao Ethnic Culture Centre, completed in 2016, has a 1,200-seat theatre and an exhibition of the county's intangible heritage, such as the Zhuang horse-bone fiddle and wheat-straw flower baskets, and the park hosts Zhuang song gatherings at festivals.

rows.name: Former Site of the Youjiang Workers' and Peasants' Democratic Government
rows.name_zh: 右江工农民主政府旧址
rows.summary: The Jingzheng Academy, a Qing-dynasty school founded by local gentry in Pingma, Tiandong's county town, which became the seat of the Youjiang Workers' and Peasants' Democratic Government set up after the Baise Uprising of 1929. Its brick halls, among the best-preserved old buildings in the town, hold exhibitions on the Youjiang revolutionary base area, and the site is the hub of Tiandong's red-tourism circuit.

rows.name: Ganzhuang Mountain (Buluotuo Site)
rows.summary: A hill near Baiyu revered by the Zhuang as the home of Baeuqloxdoh (Buluotuo), the creator god and first ancestor in Zhuang mythology. Paths lead to a worship hall, an ancestral shrine, Zhuang totem sculptures, a spring and several caves. From the 7th to the 9th of the third lunar month, Zhuang people from across the region gather here for a large song fair, rites honouring Buluotuo and folk sports.

rows.name: Gulongshan Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A 7.8 km chain of four gorges joined by three underground-river caves in Huru town near the Vietnamese border, best known for a rafting run that passes through gorges and caves in turn. The forested gorges hold a dozen waterfalls, among them the 128 m Gulong Falls and a 68 m curtain fall.

rows.name: Haokun Lake
rows.summary: A clear green lake in the karst hills of southern Lingyun County, ringed by limestone peaks, with small islands and lone peaks rising from the water. Zhuang and Yao villages line the shore, and the area has been developed for lakeside leisure and village stays.

rows.name: Jinxiu Ancient Town, Jingxi
rows.summary: A shopping and dining district on the east side of Jingxi city, built in old-town style around Zhuang and border-culture themes, with a commercial street, a night-market food street, themed inns and waterside restaurants. It is a modern development rather than a historic town, and is busiest in the evening when the streets are lit up.

rows.name: Jiuzhou Old Town, Jingxi
rows.summary: A Zhuang town south of Jingxi, once home to the local chieftain family, known for its hand-made embroidered balls (xiuqiu), which hang along the main street; visitors can learn to cut and stitch one in the workshops. Waterside houses, an old bridge and the Jiuzhou Zhuang Ecomuseum, opened in 2005, make it a pleasant stroll, and at Spring Festival the town stages dragon dances and a re-enacted chieftain's wedding parade.

rows.name: Jixingyan Cave
rows.summary: A four-level limestone cave 13 km south of Debao town, of which the second level is open on a route of about 2 km through five halls. Its highlight is a field of rimstone pools covering more than 6,000 m², stepped like rice terraces, with a dark stalagmite known as the 'bell' rising among the white flowstone. A large old Chinese horse chestnut and a mulberry tree stand at the entrance.

rows.name: Longyunshan Tea Town, Leye
rows.summary: A mountain resort built around a 3,000-mu (about 200-hectare) organic tea plantation in Gantian township, about 20 km from Leye town. A 5.6 km trail climbs through the tea fields past three tower pavilions and viewpoints, and the hotel complex has a tea-ceremony hall, a tea-culture exhibition and a workshop where visitors can pick and process their own tea. It suits a quiet stop with tea tasting on the way to or from Leye's sinkholes.

rows.name: Red Leaf Forest Park, Debao
rows.summary: A forest park just north-east of Debao town, planned to cover about 1,000 hectares, whose sweetgum trees turn red, crimson and yellow in autumn around Hongfeng Lake, the Red Leaf Valley and two reservoirs. It is at its best in the autumn leaf season; the rest of the year it is a quiet place for walks among hills and water.

rows.name: Site of the Xilin Incident
rows.summary: A restored old building and stone-paved courtyard on Dongxin Street in Ding'an, which was the seat of Xilin County in the 1850s. Here, in February 1856, the county magistrate had the French Catholic missionary Auguste Chapdelaine tried and executed, together with two Chinese Catholics, on charges that included preaching outside the treaty ports; France cited his death when it joined Britain in the Second Opium War.

rows.name: Tiandong Wetland Park
rows.summary: A town park on the western side of Pingma, Tiandong's county seat, laid out around lakes beside the Baigu River. It makes an easy stroll for travellers stopping in Tiandong, for example after visiting the Youjiang government site nearby.

rows.name: Tianzhou Old Town
rows.summary: A Zhuang-themed town built in traditional style in Tianyang and opened in 2014, covering about 100 hectares with canals, a Buluotuo square, an ancestral pagoda, watchtowers, a Zhuang history museum and streets of shops, restaurants, inns and bars. It is a modern development rather than a historic town, and stages Zhuang song contests, lion-and-dragon parades and Buluotuo processions at festivals.

rows.name: Tongling Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A deep, forest-filled gorge in Huru town near the Vietnamese border, entered by a path that drops through old trees into a cave about 100 m high and on to Tongling Falls, a single 188.6 m drop into a pool fed by an underground river. More than 2,300 plant species, including tree ferns, grow in the gorge, and an underground-river tunnel leads on to the farmed Nianba Gorge. The loop walk takes about 3–4 hours.

rows.name: Tongtian River Cave
rows.summary: A show cave with an underground river in Liming township, formerly called Ganmo Cave: a 1.68 km walk through large chambers with more than twenty columns over 20 m tall is followed by a 1.6 km boat ride on the underground river, about 1.5 hours in all. It is also known as the Red Army Cave, because a Seventh Red Army unit under Wei Baqun held out here under siege for 36 days in 1931, a story told in a small exhibition hall at the site.

rows.name: Zhen'an Park and Gantuo Cave Site, Napo
rows.summary: A town park at the foot of Houlong Hill on the north side of Napo, around Gantuo Cave, where excavations in 1997–2000 found burials and more than a thousand pottery, stone, bone, shell and iron objects from the late Neolithic to the Iron Age, including a ritual zhang blade, the first found in Guangxi. A spring still flows from the cave, whose walls bear inscriptions from different periods, and remains of the Qing-era Zhen'an chieftain's office lie by its southern mouth.

rows.name: Beihai Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped park built as the venue of the fourth Guangxi Garden and Horticulture Expo, with themed display gardens laid out across the grounds. It makes a pleasant walk on the way between the city and Silver Beach.

rows.name: Beihai Ocean Window
rows.summary: A modern marine-themed exhibition centre in the south of Beihai city, with aquarium tanks, themed halls on ocean life and interactive science displays. It is aimed mainly at families with children and suits a rainy day.

rows.name: Beihai Old Town (Zhuhai Road Old Street)
rows.summary: Beihai's old commercial quarter near the northern shore, where Zhuhai Road, Shaji Street and Zhongshan Road form a nationally listed historic block of shophouses with Western-style facades from the treaty-port years. Zhuhai Road is now a pedestrian street lined with shops and cafés.

rows.name: Beihai Silver Beach
rows.summary: Beihai's main beach, a strand of fine white quartz sand running about 24 km along the south shore of the peninsula from Qiaogang to Daguansha, with a very gentle slope into the sea. It was developed as a resort from 1990, became one of China's first national tourism resorts in 1992, and its large 'Tide' sculpture is the city's landmark.

rows.name: Beihai Underwater World
rows.summary: An aquarium on Chating Road in central Beihai, with tanks of marine fish, sharks and other sea life. It is an easy indoor visit for families, especially on a rainy day.

rows.name: Caoxiecun Site Park
rows.summary: The excavated remains of a Han-dynasty town beside the Ximen River on the western edge of Lianzhou, which researchers working on Hepu's Maritime Silk Road heritage bid believe was the seat of the Hepu commandery. Since 2019 the remains have been covered with protective shelters and given a reconstructed wharf and walkways, and the site has been opened as a site park.

rows.name: Dashi Pavilion
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty timber pavilion at the centre of Yong'an, once one of the Ming coastal garrison posts, named after the bodhisattva Guanyin (Dashi) who is worshipped inside. Two double-eaved hip-and-gable pavilions are joined into one building about 16 m deep, with ridges decorated with dragons, phoenixes and other figures and with painted eaves and brackets.

rows.name: Gaode Old Town
rows.summary: The historic core of Gaode, an old market town on the north-eastern edge of Beihai city that belonged to Hepu county until 1951, whose three old streets are protected by Guangxi as the Gaode Three Streets historic block. The city promotes it as one of Beihai's sights alongside the better-known Old Street on Zhuhai Road.

rows.name: Hepu Han Tombs Park & Han Dynasty Culture Museum
rows.name_zh: 合浦汉墓群·汉代文化博物馆
rows.pinyin: Hépǔ Hànmù Qún · Hàndài Wénhuà Bówùguǎn
rows.summary: Hepu was a Han-dynasty starting port of the Maritime Silk Road, and in this heritage park on the edge of Lianzhou the grassy mounds across the lawns are barrows over 476 tombs of the Han to Wei–Jin period, with a visitor centre and an archaeology display area completed in 2021. Across the road, the Hepu Han Dynasty Culture Museum, founded in 1978, holds more than 5,200 objects from the Hepu tombs, many of them brought from South-East Asia, South Asia, West Asia and the Mediterranean; its best-known piece is a green-glazed Persian jar of the late Eastern Han, and the tombs also yielded a Roman glass bowl. Next to the museum is the Hanlü Culture Park, a Han-themed park.

rows.name: Hepu Mooncake Town
rows.summary: A mooncake-themed visitor complex at a baking factory in Lianzhou, built on Hepu's claim to the origin of filled cakes through a poem Su Dongpo wrote when he passed through the town. A culture hall traces the history of mooncakes and moon-worship customs with a large collection of cake moulds, visitors can watch the factory's production lines, and there is an area for trying baking.

rows.name: Hui'ai Bridge
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty bridge just outside the former west gate of Lianzhou, the old walled seat of Hepu, listed by Guangxi in 1994 and as a national heritage site in 2013. It is a short stop that combines well with the Caoxiecun site park and the arcaded shophouses of Fumin Road in the county town.

rows.name: Impression 1876 Historic Quarter (Beihai Treaty-Port Buildings)
rows.summary: Central Beihai's group of Western-style buildings from the treaty-port era that followed the 1876 Chefoo Convention, spread over about 1 km around Beijing Road, Jiefang Road and Zhongshan East Road, among them the British consulate of 1885, the customs building of 1883 and the Qing post office of 1897. Some hold small exhibitions on the treaty-port years, such as the display on foreign trading firms in the 1891 building of the German Sengbao firm on Jiefang Road. The national heritage listing covers these 15 city buildings and two 19th-century churches on Weizhou Island.

rows.name: Jinhaiwan Mangrove Forest
rows.summary: A tract of coastal mangrove forest and tidal flats at Daguansha, east of Silver Beach, visited for its birds and the sea creatures of the mudflats. Sightseeing carts run through the area.

rows.name: Maritime Silk Road First Port (Haisi Shougang)
rows.summary: A newly built Han-style harbour town at Yanlou village south-west of Lianzhou, themed on Hepu's role as a starting port of the Han-dynasty Maritime Silk Road. Its main draw is an open-air evening show in which more than 200 performers re-enact merchant ships arriving and departing, with shops and restaurants in Han-style buildings around it.

rows.name: Qiaogang Town
rows.summary: A small seaside town at the southern tip of Beihai, founded in 1979 as an overseas-Chinese fishing commune to resettle more than 7,700 ethnic Chinese who had left Vietnam. Its residents keep their own Cantonese dialects, and the harbour, market and streets of this returnee community are visited as one of Beihai's distinctive neighbourhoods.

rows.name: Shengtang Catholic Church, Weizhou Island
rows.summary: A Gothic-style Catholic church in Shengtang village in the middle of Weizhou Island, built by missionaries of the Paris Foreign Missions Society and completed around 1880. It is described as the largest Catholic church on the Guangxi coast, and together with the smaller Chengzai church elsewhere on the island it is part of the national heritage listing of Beihai's modern buildings.

rows.name: Weizhou Island (Nanwan & Crocodile Hill)
rows.summary: A volcanic island of about 25 km² in the Beibu Gulf, with lava coasts, sea cliffs and fringing coral, described as China's largest and geologically youngest volcanic island and protected as a national geopark since 2004. The 5A area takes in Nanwan (South Bay), a harbour formed in an ancient crater, and Crocodile Hill on its western side, where a coastal walkway passes a volcanic vent, sea caves, a sea arch, craters and fossil trees. Elsewhere on the island are beaches such as Shiluokou, Hakka fishing villages and two 19th-century Catholic churches.

rows.name: Xingdao Lake (Hongchaojiang Reservoir)
rows.summary: A large reservoir in the hills of northern Hepu, built between 1959 and 1964 on the Hongchao River and named Xingdao ('star islands') Lake for the more than 1,000 islets scattered across its water. It served as an outdoor location for CCTV's 1990s television series of the Water Margin, and besides irrigation and water supply it is now used for tourism.

rows.name: China (Nanning) Leyang City
rows.summary: A wellness and retirement-living resort town in Fusui County, planned from 2010 and opened in stages from 2022, laid out around a lake with landscaped grounds. Visitors can go boating, pick fruit, camp or use its therapy and sports facilities, and it runs a seniors' university and holds folk festivals. It is aimed mainly at older long-stay guests and at families.

rows.name: Daliancheng Fortress
rows.summary: After 1885 the Guangxi military commander Su Yuanchun made this ring of hills just north of Pingxiang his frontier headquarters, linking the peaks with walls, blockhouses and eight hilltop gun batteries and closing the passes with four gates over nearly two decades of building. Inside are the Wusheng Palace, a three-hall temple to Guan Yu used by the garrison, the three-level Baiyu limestone cave that Su used as a retreat and command post, and four old wells. It is a component of the national heritage unit of the Liancheng fortress sites and Friendship Pass.

rows.name: Discover Nonggang Scenic Area
rows.summary: An ecotourism area developed from 2018 at Siqing village, Xiangshui township, beside the Nonggang National Nature Reserve, whose karst hills carry seasonal rainforest and are home to rare langurs and birds. It offers walks through forested limestone country with views over green peaks, and a campsite for cars.

rows.name: Dongna Yuwan (Anping Xianhe)
rows.summary: A stretch of karst river scenery on the Heishui River at Anping village, Leiping, formerly marketed as Anping Xianhe and also a national wetland park. Its named sights include Swallow Cave, river islands and shoals, and a cliffside path named after the Ming traveller Xu Xiake, who described the local Anping native chieftaincy in 1637. The site of the chieftain's seat and Anping's old street survive, and Zhuang customs such as eight-tone music and dragon dances are staged for visitors.

rows.name: Former French Consulate, Longzhou
rows.name_zh: 法国驻龙州领事馆旧址
rows.summary: Two matching two-storey French-style buildings in Longzhou, ringed by verandas behind 20 tall arches, with stone floors and spiral stairs of ironwood. Built as the station for a railway that was never completed, they housed the French consulate from 1898 until 1949, apart from a break after 1930. The buildings are open with an exhibition on Longzhou's links with France.

rows.name: Friendship Pass
rows.summary: Friendship Pass is the historic gateway on the China–Vietnam border south-west of Pingxiang, known as Zhennan Pass until 1953 and given its present name in 1965. The four-storey, 22 m gate tower holds exhibitions on the pass's history, Ming-dynasty walls climb the hills on either side, which carry old gun batteries such as the group on Jinji Shan, and a colonnaded French-style building of 1896, remodelled in 1914, once housed the border affairs office. The pass saw the 1885 Battle of Zhennan Pass in the Sino-French War.

rows.name: Ho Chi Minh Exhibition Hall, Longzhou
rows.summary: A late-Qing house at 99 South Street in Longzhou that served as the secret office of the Communist Party of Vietnam, at a time when the town was a main base abroad for Ho Chi Minh and other Vietnamese revolutionaries. It now houses the Ho Chi Minh Exhibition Hall, with photographs and displays on their activities in Longzhou and on China–Vietnam ties, and is used for youth exchange visits between the two countries. It became a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Lichuan Cultural Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park on the edge of Tiandeng county town, registered as a regional-level forest park and upgraded to a 4A scenic area in 2019. A walking path follows the Lichuan River through its wooded, landscaped grounds, which residents use for exercise and leisure. It suits a short stroll for travellers passing through Tiandeng.

rows.name: Litun Tianmeng Scenic Area
rows.summary: A memorial and study-tour site at Litun, a hamlet in the karst hills of Tuokan township whose villagers spent 24 years cutting a tunnel through the mountain to the outside world. A memorial hall tells the story, the tunnel itself is presented as a museum, and visitors can walk the old mountain path the villagers once used. Its first phase had opened by early 2021, aimed mainly at study tours and political-education visits.

rows.name: Longgong Cave (Longgong Xianjing)
rows.summary: A large natural limestone cave at Naling, near Daxin, with lofty chambers of stalactites, stalagmite columns and pools, lit with coloured lights along the visitor route. Part of the cave system has been fitted out as a refrigerated ice-and-snow attraction kept near freezing, and the scenic area also runs a long cliffside rail ride and rafting on the Na River. It suits families and anyone wanting a cool stop on the Detian circuit.

rows.name: Longguwan Dinosaur Park
rows.summary: A dinosaur-themed amusement park near Fusui that opened in 2017, themed on the 'nest of three dinosaurs' fossil find in Fusui County, with recreated dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals, rides and play areas. It closed at the end of 2021 for a rebuild and has since reopened as part of the Longguwan resort, where a wildlife park was being added in 2025. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Longzhou Red Army Trail and Tianqin Zhuang Village
rows.summary: An old horse-caravan path of about 2 km over the hills between Shuilong and Fucha hamlets, once the main route from Longzhou towards Jingxi and Baise, which, according to the local account, Deng Xiaoping travelled several times in 1929 while organising the Baise and Longzhou uprisings. It is presented as a red-tourism site with a history hall and visitor centre at Fucha. The adjoining Tianqin Zhuang Village is a modern leisure area with a large pool, restaurants, a water market and replica Zhuang wooden houses.

rows.name: Longzhou Uprising Memorial Park
rows.summary: The memorial park centres on the Longzhou Uprising Memorial Hall, opened in 2004 as the new exhibition building of the Eighth Red Army memorial museum, which covers the uprising of February 1930 in which Communist-led troops under Yu Zuoyu, Li Mingrui and Deng Xiaoping formed the Eighth Red Army and a short-lived soviet along the Zuo River. In the old town nearby, the former Eighth Red Army headquarters, where Deng worked and lived in 1929, keeps the two cypress trees he planted at its gate.

rows.name: Mingshi Pastoral Scenery
rows.summary: The valley of the Mingshi River in Kanxu township, where the river winds between rice fields and steep karst peaks dotted with Zhuang villages. Often filmed for television, including the fantasy drama Hua Qian Gu, it is promoted as part of the 'China–Vietnam border landscape gallery', and Mingshi village was named a national key rural-tourism village in 2019. Several resort hotels have been built in the valley.

rows.name: Paiyangshan Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 1,340 hectares on a state forest farm in Ningming County, covered in Tongmian pine and star-anise plantations with clear streams running through the valleys. Wildlife includes the Guangxi warty newt, pangolins and Burmese pythons, and tree ferns grow in the forest. Its dark skies have drawn a Guangxi stargazing gathering, and it is popular for summer walks and stream play.

rows.name: Pingxiang Rosewood Culture Expo City
rows.summary: A large trade and exhibition complex in southern Pingxiang devoted to hongmu (rosewood) furniture, with showroom halls where hundreds of furniture firms display their work, a shopping street and buildings in traditional Chinese style. Its former expo centre was turned into a rosewood culture museum in 2020, showing Ming and Qing furniture, carvings, timber samples and woodworking tools. It suits visitors interested in Chinese furniture and craft, or in shopping.

rows.name: Shijinglin Stone Forest and Chongzuo Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: Two adjoining parks in Chongzuo's southern new district: Shijinglin, a karst 'stone forest' of about 100 hectares opened in 1991, with weathered limestone pinnacles, small caves and pools named after the shapes they suggest, and the landscaped grounds built for the 7th Guangxi Garden and Horticulture Expo. Shijinglin is part of the Huashan national scenic area and hosts a Zhuang song fair each year on the 10th day of the fourth lunar month. Both make an easy outing from the city centre.

rows.name: Taiping Ancient Town
rows.summary: A leisure and shopping district in central Chongzuo built around the site of Taiping prefecture's city wall, first raised in 1372 under the Ming and now partly repaired, with a restored inner waterway. Streets of new buildings in old style hold food stalls, shops, guesthouses and stages for folk performances, and the area is busiest in the evening. Taiping has been an administrative seat since the Song, and the old wall is a regional heritage site.

rows.name: White-headed Langur Ecotourism Area
rows.summary: A visitor area on the edge of the Banli section of the Chongzuo White-headed Langur National Nature Reserve, which protects the critically endangered white-headed langur, a blackish monkey with a white crown, cheeks and neck found only in the karst hills of south-west Guangxi. It has a visitor centre, paths into the limestone hill forest, a white-headed langur museum and a study-tour base next to a long-running primate research station. The reserve also shelters François' langurs, cycads and golden camellias.

rows.name: Xiaoliancheng Fortress (Jiangshan Forts)
rows.summary: A hill fortress near Longzhou, also called the Jiangshan forts, built from 1886 by the Guangxi military commander Su Yuanchun as the command centre of the frontier defences facing French-ruled Vietnam. Fifteen gun batteries, once armed with German Krupp cannon, line the ridges and guard the routes inland from the Zhennan, Shuikou and Ping'er passes. It is a component of the national heritage unit of the Liancheng fortress sites and Friendship Pass.

rows.name: Yuhuashi Scenic Area
rows.summary: An area of about 3 km² on a bend of the Zuo River where countless coloured pebbles are cemented into rounded, many-hued conglomerate outcrops and cliffs, an unusual rock landscape for the region. A cave called Tianyan (Sky Eye) and several groups of ancient Zuojiang cliff paintings lie within the scenic area, and boat trips run on the river. It sits about 10 km downstream of the Zuojiang Leaning Tower, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Zuojiang Leaning Tower
rows.summary: A five-storey octagonal brick pagoda, also called Guilong Pagoda, standing on a rocky islet in the Zuo River just outside central Chongzuo. Begun in 1621 with three storeys and raised to five in the Qing, it is about 17.6 m tall and was built leaning some 1.4 m towards the oncoming current, which the builders are said to have done on purpose. Inside, a brick stair climbs through the hollow core.

rows.name: Bailang Beach
rows.summary: A long sandy beach on the Jiangshan Peninsula south of Fangchenggang, whose name means 'white waves', developed since the 1990s from a fishing village's shore into a beach resort with clean sea and fine sand. The peninsula's 76 km coastline now holds more than 20 scenic areas, making it a good base for a seaside stay.

rows.name: Beilun Estuary & Zhushan (Dongxing Border River Scenic Area)
rows.summary: The mouth of the Beilun River at Zhushan, where the border river between China and Vietnam meets the sea, marked by the Qing boundary stone No. 1 of 1890 and the zero-kilometre monument of the Guangxi border highway. Nearby are the old street of Zhushan, once a trading port, the Sansheng (Mazu) temple of 1876, a grove of ancient banyans and mangroves in the core of the Beilun Estuary national nature reserve.

rows.name: Dongxing Border Gate (Guomen)
rows.summary: The riverside area around the Dongxing port, a first-class national land crossing to Mong Cai in Vietnam over the Beilun River, where the frontier inspection building at the end of the Beilun River Bridge is known locally as the 'national gate'. Around it are the Qing boundary stone No. 5, the China–Vietnam Friendship Park, temples to Guanyin and Guandi, a museum of qiaopi (overseas remittance letters) and the riverside Hedi Road, lined with shops selling Vietnamese goods.

rows.name: Jing Islands & Golden Beach
rows.summary: The 'three Jing islands' of Wanwei, Wutou and Shanxin, now joined to the mainland by land reclamation, are home to most of China's Gin (Jing) people, whose ancestors came from the Hai Phong area of Vietnam about 500 years ago and who speak the Gin language alongside Cantonese. Their village ha pavilions host the Ha song festival, a national intangible heritage item held on Wanwei and Wutou from the 10th day of the sixth lunar month, with singing to the single-string zither and dances. On Wanwei's south shore is Golden Beach, a 13 km strand of golden sand facing the Beibu Gulf.

rows.name: Shiwandashan Bird Park
rows.summary: A bird park inside the Shiwandashan National Forest Park on the Hongqi forest farm, with aviaries holding many species of birds in a setting of subtropical broadleaf forest. The surrounding forest park, the core of the Shiwandashan national nature reserve, has forest walks, an old stone-stepped trail towards the Fulong pass and Yao villages.

rows.name: Shiwandashan Butou Hot Springs
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in a valley about 5 km from Shangsi town at the foot of the Shiwandashan, built around a low-temperature carbonate spring that the old county gazetteer records as used locally since the Ming. It has a large outdoor pool, a children's pool, an indoor swimming pool, smaller feature pools and a terraced cascade of warm pools, with villas for overnight stays.

rows.name: West Bay (Xiwan) Waterfront
rows.summary: The waterfront of West Bay in the centre of Fangchenggang, where a walkway of almost 50 km links a tourist wharf, a city beach and about 15 parks around the bay. Its sandy bathing beach is popular with residents and visitors in summer, and the 1.57 km West Bay sea bridge, opened in 2003, crosses the water.

rows.name: Anlan Riverside Park
rows.summary: A riverside park running about 10 km along the south bank of the Yu River in central Guigang, from the Yujiang No. 2 Bridge downstream to the Anlan Pagoda. A greenway with cycle paths passes flower beds, lotus ponds, old wharf remains and a square of Qin-style replica buildings and terracotta-warrior statues, with views of the river bridges and old factory chimneys. It is a favourite place for locals' evening walks.

rows.name: Beidi Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain area on the southern flank of the Dayao Mountains in Dapeng township, Pingnan, rising to Beidi peak at about 1,300 m and covering some 22 km² of woods, gorges and waterfalls. Developed from the late 2010s, it has canyon rafting, a glass walkway, cliff-hung boardwalks and hiking paths, and temples built around the cult of Beidi, the Taoist Northern Emperor. It suits a day of walking and rafting in summer.

rows.name: Bushan Gujun Culture Town
rows.summary: A culture and leisure quarter of about 0.67 km² opposite the Qintang district government, built in old style around springs at the foot of Longtou Hill. It takes its name from Bushan, the ancient county that served as a commandery seat from Qin to Sui times and is generally placed in today's Guigang. Evening markets and festivals are held in its streets.

rows.name: Dongmei Eco Park
rows.summary: A rural leisure park in the hills of Siwang township, set among rice fields, bamboo groves, streams and two old villages with temples and stone paths. It has barbecue areas in the bamboo, fruit-picking orchards, a windmill and children's activities, and was named a Guigang centre for traditional-medicine health tourism in 2024. It suits families on a country day out.

rows.name: Foziling Wellness Resort
rows.summary: A hillside leisure and wellness resort in wooded country north-east of Pingnan, best known locally for its summer water park fed by mountain spring water, with large pools, slides and a children's splash area. It suits families looking for a summer day out.

rows.name: Gongzhou Park
rows.summary: Pingnan's main town park, named after Gongzhou, the prefecture that had its seat here from the Tang to the Song. It takes in a martyrs' monument, two lakes, one of them planted with lotus, a Zhuangyuan (top-scholar) Pavilion and the Buddhist Zhengjue Temple, and a hillside of peach trees draws crowds when it blossoms around the Spring Festival. It is a pleasant stroll for anyone stopping in Pingnan.

rows.name: Guigang Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped garden-expo park in western Guigang, laid out around waterside wetlands and fields on the theme of Guigang as the 'lotus city'. Its zones include a Guigang garden, a lotus square, wetland walks and a set of display gardens from around Guangxi. It suits a relaxed walk, especially in the lotus season.

rows.name: Guiping Xishan (West Hill)
rows.summary: A wooded Buddhist hill, also called Siling Shan, rising just west of Guiping at the meeting of the Qian and Yu rivers, protected as a national scenic area and national geopark of about 13 km². Paths climb past springs, rock outcrops and tea gardens to temples including the Xishi'an nunnery, founded in 1646 and now one of China's national key Buddhist temples, and the Longhua Temple behind it. Its tea and the Ruquan spring water are local specialities.

rows.name: Hemei Qintang Lotus Park
rows.summary: A lotus-growing park north of Qintang built from 2014 around the district's lotus-root farming, which has a history of more than a thousand years. About 200 hectares of lotus ponds hold over 350 varieties, crossed by boardwalks and cycle paths, with a wind-and-rain bridge, a lotus science exhibition and farm-stay inns. Qintang holds a lotus festival here each summer, the best time to visit.

rows.name: Jintian Uprising Site
rows.summary: The village of Jintian where Hong Xiuquan's God Worshippers declared their revolt on 11 January 1851, the start of the Taiping Rebellion. On Xiniu Ridge the ramparts of their rectangular camp, about 65 by 35 m, survive around the stone where the flag was raised, with the old drill ground and Xiniu Pool nearby, and outlying sites include the site of Wei Changhui's home and the Sanjie Temple front-line post. A modern museum beside the camp tells the story of the movement through themed halls and a 3D cinema.

rows.name: Longtan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the hills north-west of Guiping, within the Dapingshan nature reserve and the Jintian state forest farm. It protects a well-preserved tract of subtropical monsoon evergreen broadleaf forest, rare in south-eastern Guangxi and rich in relict plants, with streams and the Longtan waterfall. It suits a day of forest walking.

rows.name: Nanshan Park and Temple, Guigang
rows.summary: A park on a craggy karst hill on the south side of Guigang, known for its caves and for Nanshan Temple, founded in 989 when a monk set up a shrine in a cave of Lion Head Hill. Song emperors sent it calligraphy and a name plaque, and its relics include an old stone Buddha, Song and Ming iron bells, a stele carved in 1329 from a Yuan emperor's inscription, and centuries of cliff inscriptions. The park also has Lotus Hill and Qilin Lake among some 30 named spots.

rows.name: Pingnan Xiongsen Animal World
rows.summary: A large private zoo and breeding centre of about 87 hectares on the edge of Pingnan, best known for its big numbers of tigers, African lions and black bears, with petting areas and other animals. Its programme has included staged circus and animal-act shows. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Pingtianshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 1,676 hectares in the hills north-west of Guigang, with dense forest, canyons, waterfalls, tree ferns and hillside tea gardens. Its summit, Dapingtian (1,157.8 m), is the highest point in Guigang and is topped by a broad grassy meadow with views over the Yu River plain, popular for sunrise. Trails, a campsite and forest-stay facilities make it a weekend escape for the city.

rows.name: Shanbian Village
rows.summary: A rural tourism village in Xintang township on the southern edge of Guigang, named one of China's 'beautiful leisure villages'. Old red-brick houses along its lanes have been turned into workshops for embroidery, oil painting, tea and pottery, and in spring the fields around it turn yellow with rapeseed flowers. A retired fighter jet and tank are also on display.

rows.name: Site of the First CCP Guangxi Provincial Congress
rows.name_zh: 中共广西省第一次代表大会旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Guǎngxī Shěng Dì-yī Cì Dàibiǎo Dàhuì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: An old house on Rongxing Street in central Guigang, once the home of Communist Party member Zhang Guocai and a secret liaison post, where the first congress of the Party's Guangxi provincial organisation was held in secret on 16 June 1928. It now holds an exhibition on the congress with documents, photographs and objects.

rows.name: Xishanquan RV Campsite
rows.summary: A large car and RV campsite resort in the hills of Xishan town outside Guiping, rated a five-star campsite in Guangxi. Accommodation ranges from motorhomes and motel rooms to valley cabins and glamping tents, and there are rope courses, archery tag, mock combat games, a playground, a cycle track and climbing walls. It suits families and groups looking for outdoor activities.

rows.name: Baishouyan Stone Inscriptions
rows.summary: Inscriptions carved into Baishouyan, a limestone hill with a cave on the edge of Baishou town, added from the Song dynasty to the Republican era. They lie a few hundred metres from the Ming walls of Yongning, so the two national heritage sites are easily seen together.

rows.name: Bajiaozhai
rows.summary: A massif of Danxia red-sandstone peaks in Meixi town on the Guangxi–Hunan border, named after the eight upturned corners of its 818 m main peak; its Hunan side belongs to the Langshan scenic area. Trails and viewpoints look over clustered peaks, rock pillars and deep gorges, often wrapped in cloud.

rows.name: Butterfly Spring
rows.summary: A park built around two steep karst hills beside National Road 321 south of Yangshuo town, on the stretch of countryside known as the Ten-Mile Gallery. A cave runs through one hill, named after a butterfly-shaped formation, and a suspension bridge crosses to the second hill, with butterfly-themed gardens below.

rows.name: Dabitou International Tourist Resort
rows.name_zh: 大碧头国际旅游度假区
rows.summary: A countryside resort at Dabitou, a traditional village of the Bin clan in Miaotou town, north-eastern Quanzhou County, set among karst hills near the Xiang River. It has a hot spring with bathing pools and spa lodges, farmland landscapes, homestays in village houses and activities such as off-road buggy rides, aimed at weekend and wellness breaks.

rows.name: Daxu Ancient Town
rows.summary: A historic market town on the Li River south-east of Guilin, with more than a thousand years of history, whose 2 km main street, paved with bluestone, is lined with old shop-houses. Along it are temples, guild halls and the Wanshou (Longevity) Bridge, and bamboo rafts leave from the waterfront.

rows.name: Dongli Ancient Village
rows.summary: A village resort on the Chaotian River near Daxu, set among houses in the traditional northern-Guangxi style, with craft and intangible-heritage workshops, farmland and guesthouses. It is pitched as a rural escape from Guilin and often combined with the Gudong Waterfall and Daxu old town.

rows.name: Fengyu Cave
rows.summary: A show cave about 16 km south-west of Lipu town that runs for 5.3 km through nine hills, named after the fish that live in its underground river. Visitors walk a 2.2 km dry section of stalactites, stalagmites and large halls, then take a boat along part of the underground river.

rows.name: Former Guangxi Provincial Art Hall
rows.summary: A theatre and arts hall on Jiefang West Road designed during the war against Japan by the playwright Ouyang Yuqian, which opened in February 1944 with the first Southwest Drama Exhibition. Burned when Guilin fell later that year, it was rebuilt to the original plan in 1946 as a red-walled, grey-tiled hall about 40 m long, and is still in use as the Guilin Art Hall.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Zongren
rows.summary: The family compound of Li Zongren (1890–1969), the Guangxi-born Kuomintang general who became Vice-President and then Acting President of the Republic of China, in his home village near Liangjiang. Behind high walls, a gatehouse and blockhouses are dozens of mostly two-storey timber halls, wing rooms and granaries, with ponds and a garden. The protected site also covers his official residence of 1948–49 on the south shore of Shanhu Lake in central Guilin, now a museum on his life.

rows.name: Gongcheng Temples and Guild Halls
rows.summary: A group of Ming and Qing buildings in Gongcheng town. The Confucian Temple, founded in 1410 and rebuilt in 1842, climbs the hillside in terraces from its Lingxing gate and Pan pond to the double-eaved Dacheng Hall, and the Guandi (Wu) Temple of 1603, rebuilt in 1862, stands beside it with its own opera stage. Nearby are the Zhou Wei Shrine to a Song-dynasty official born in Gongcheng and the Qing-era Hunan Guild Hall, promoted together with the temples as the 'three temples and two guild halls'.

rows.name: Guanyan Cave
rows.summary: A cave system with an underground river, about 12 km long, that emerges on the east bank of the Li River at Caoping and is named after the crown-like shape of the hill above. Visitors descend by lift and travel through the open section on foot, by small train and by boat, and can leave by boat towards the Li River. The explorer Xu Xiake described the cave in 1637, and it opened to tourists in 1995.

rows.name: Gudong Waterfall
rows.summary: A spring-fed waterfall in a wooded valley near Daxu on the east side of the Li River. Visitors wade into the stream and climb up the falls through the water, which makes it a popular place to cool off in summer.

rows.name: Guihai Qinglan Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park on the eastern edge of Guilin laid out on a former golf course, with wide lawns, lakes and pine woods ringed by karst peaks. It is a relaxed place for walks, picnics and camping, with family activities such as pedal boats.

rows.name: Guilin Merryland Resort
rows.summary: A large resort on the southern edge of Xing'an town, opened in December 2000 and covering about 4 km², with a theme park of family rides, a 27-hole golf course and a resort hotel beside a lake. It was among the first sites in China rated 5A; the regional list now rates it 4A.

rows.name: Guilin Office of the Eighth Route Army
rows.name_zh: 八路军桂林办事处旧址
rows.summary: The building on Zhongshan North Road that housed the Eighth Route Army's liaison office in Guilin from November 1938 until 1941, during the wartime cooperation between the Communists and the Kuomintang against Japan. The two-storey brick-and-timber shop house was destroyed when Guilin fell in 1944 and rebuilt to its original design in 1967. It opened as a memorial museum in 1977, and a new exhibition hall was added in 2013.

rows.name: Guilin Tourism University Campus
