rows.summary: The main campus of Guilin Tourism University in Yanshan District, a college founded in 1985 to train staff for the tourism industry, whose landscaped grounds, crossed by the Xiangsi River, are run as a scenic area. Visitors can walk the riverside grounds among the teaching buildings.

rows.name: Hongxi Canyon
rows.summary: A forested canyon in the hills of northern Lingui, named after the reddish rocks of its stream bed, with a waterfall as its main sight. Walkways follow the stream through the forest, and the site also offers outdoor activities.

rows.name: Hongyan Village
rows.summary: A village in Lianhua town in southern Gongcheng County, rebuilt by its villagers to a single plan as a model new village and now run as a rural scenic area among persimmon orchards. Visitors walk the orchards, at their most colourful in autumn when the fruit ripens, and stay or eat in the villagers' guesthouses and restaurants.

rows.name: Jiangtou and Changgangling Villages
rows.summary: Two old villages in Lingchuan County protected together as one national heritage site. Jiangtou, on the Gantang River north of Guilin, was settled by descendants of the Song philosopher Zhou Dunyi and keeps more than 180 houses and ancestral halls, mostly Ming and Qing; it is known for the many officials it produced. Changgangling, in the hills near Lingtian east of Guilin, prospered as a stop on the overland trade route between Hunan and Guangxi after the Lingqu Canal declined.

rows.name: Jingjiang Princes' Palace & Solitary Beauty Peak
rows.summary: The walled seat of the Ming-dynasty Princes of Jingjiang, begun in 1372 in the heart of Guilin; its stone walls, gates and hall terraces survive, and the grounds now hold a campus of Guangxi Normal University and an exhibition on the imperial examinations once held here. Inside the walls rises Solitary Beauty Peak, climbed by 306 steps for a view over the city, its cliffs carved with inscriptions including the earliest record of the saying that Guilin's scenery is the finest under heaven. The protected site also takes in the princes' tombs, more than 300 burials at the foot of Yao Mountain east of the city, one of them restored as a museum.

rows.name: Jinzhongshan Resort
rows.summary: A resort area in the karst hills of Luojin town, eastern Yongfu County, built around Yongfu Cave, a show cave with golden-coloured formations, and a large karst sinkhole that can be entered on foot from the bottom, where it meets an underground river. A hot spring and river rafting make it a weekend retreat from Guilin.

rows.name: Kitten Mountain (Mao'er Shan)
rows.summary: At 2,141.5 m, Kitten Mountain is the highest peak in Guangxi and is often called the highest in South China; it rises on the border of Xing'an and Ziyuan counties. A national nature reserve of about 17,000 hectares, reaching into Longsheng County, protects its subtropical evergreen and mixed broadleaf forest and the headwaters of the Li River. In 1996 local herb gatherers found here the wreck of a US B-24 bomber that crashed on the mountain in 1944.

rows.name: Laoshanjie Longtanjiang Canyon
rows.summary: A forested river canyon in the Yuecheng range, known locally as Laoshanjie, in Huajiang Yao township, opened as a scenic area in 2021; it joins the Longtanjiang gorge with sites linked to the Red Army's crossing of Laoshanjie during the Long March in 1934. Visitors can walk a section of the Long March trail, and a Red Army culture park with a restored stretch of the old path and a memorial square is being added.

rows.name: Lewan Village Old Buildings
rows.summary: A group of village houses and ancestral halls from the Qing dynasty to the Republican era in Lewan, a village in the farmland south-west of Gongcheng's county town, listed as a national heritage site in 2019. The listing covers the Lewan Great House, three ancestral halls of the Chen clan and two groups of courtyard houses belonging to Chen and Jiang families.

rows.name: Lijiang (Lipu River) National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park along the Lipu River and its tributaries, spread over several townships around Lipu town. Its ecology and science centre near the town introduces the river's wetlands.

rows.name: Lijiang Bay
rows.summary: A scenic area on the Lipu River in Qingshan town, south-west of Lipu, where visitors take boat trips along the river among karst peaks and walk through Tiangong Cave, a show cave. It lies on the road from Yangshuo to Fengyu Cave and is easily combined with it.

rows.name: Lijiang Houhai, Guilin Sunac Resort
rows.summary: The shopping and leisure quarter of the Guilin Sunac International Tourism Resort, a large resort in Yanshan District that opened in June 2021. Around it are the resort's theme park, Sea World ocean park and Water World, and a performing-arts centre, making it a full day out for families.

rows.name: Lingqu Canal
rows.summary: A canal dug on the First Emperor's orders between 219 and 214 BC to move troops and supplies south, linking the Xiang River, which flows to the Yangtze, with the Li River and the Pearl River system across a low watershed. Its works survive in and around Xing'an town: the Huazui, a ploughshare-shaped stone spur that splits the Xiang, the angled spillway dams called the Big and Small Tianping, the Qin embankment and old lock gates along the 36.4 km of the South and North channels. It was named a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in 2018.

rows.name: Liu Sanjie Grand View Garden
rows.summary: A theme park on the Taohua River at the foot of West Hill, named after Liu Sanjie, the singing heroine of Zhuang folk legend. Visitors can trade folk songs with costumed performers at its singing stage, watch scenes from the classic film about her in the performance hall and see staged ethnic song-and-dance shows among reconstructed buildings.

rows.name: Nanxi Hill Park
rows.summary: A park around Nanxi Hill in southern Guilin, a twin-peaked limestone hill rising about 140 m above the Nanxi stream, which winds along its northern foot to the Li River. Three linked cave systems inside the hill, among them White Dragon Cave, can be walked for about 500 m, and nearly 200 inscriptions from the Tang onwards are carved around the caves. The White Dragon Spring at its foot once sent its water to the court as tribute.

rows.name: Osmanthus Commune
rows.summary: An osmanthus-themed attraction among the fields of the Taohua River valley on the western edge of Guilin, a city whose name means 'forest of sweet osmanthus'. It has an osmanthus culture exhibition hall, a themed garden, a hotel and a study centre for school groups, with activities such as making osmanthus cakes.

rows.name: Qianjiadong Cultural Tourism Resort
rows.summary: A resort opened in June 2023 in the traditional villages of Xiaolong and Sudong between Guanyang and Xinxu towns, built around the Yao tradition that Qianjiadong is the ancestral homeland of the Yao people, a place many Yao visit to trace their roots. Set in the landscape of the Qianjiadong National Nature Reserve, it combines Yao-style buildings, displays of Yao dress and history and a water show with farmland and mountain scenery.

rows.name: Reed Flute Cave
rows.summary: A show cave in Guangming Hill on the north-western edge of Guilin, named after the reeds at its mouth that were used to make flutes, with a path of about 500 m through chambers of stalactites, stalagmites and columns lit in bright colours. More than 70 ink inscriptions left by visitors since the year 792 survive on its walls, and the cave was opened to tourists in 1962.

rows.name: Sanqianli Resort, Xingping
rows.summary: A modern resort and leisure district built on the north-eastern edge of Xingping, with a street of shops and restaurants, holiday housing and hotels set among fields and karst peaks along the Dayuan River. It runs evening boat trips and lantern events on the water and makes a base for the Xingping stretch of the Li River, a short ride from Xingping old town and the view printed on the 20-yuan note.

rows.name: Seven Star Park
rows.summary: Guilin's largest park, about 137 hectares on the east bank of the Li River, named after its seven hills; paths lead past the Flower Bridge to Seven Star Cave, a large show cave with lit formations. At the south-west foot of Crescent Hill the Guihai Forest of Steles museum encloses Longyin Cave and Longyin Rock, whose walls carry 213 inscriptions from the Tang to the Republican era. They are the densest group of the Guilin Stone Inscriptions, a national heritage site of more than 2,000 carvings spread over some twenty hills across the city.

rows.name: Shiwaitaoyuan (Land of Idyllic Beauty)
rows.summary: A landscaped theme park beside the Guilin–Yangshuo road near Baisha, laid out to evoke Tao Yuanming's fable of the Peach Blossom Spring. Boats pass a large water wheel and slip through a narrow channel into a lake, where staged folk dances are performed on the shore among Zhuang-style buildings, a wind-and-rain bridge and totem poles. It was among the first national 4A scenic areas, named in 2001.

rows.name: Silver Cave
rows.summary: A show cave in Maling town, Lipu, that runs through twelve hills on three levels. Its glittering calcite formations, which give the cave its name, include the halls known as Snow Mountain with Waterfall, the Music Stone Screen and the Jade Pool.

rows.name: Sites of the Battle of the Xiang River (Jieshou)
rows.summary: A national heritage site of fourteen places in Xing'an, Quanzhou and Guanyang counties linked to the Battle of the Xiang River, fought from 25 November to 2 December 1934 as the Central Red Army forced its way across the river during the Long March at heavy cost. Its focus is Jieshou town on the Xiang, where the Red Army Hall (Sanguantang), a two-courtyard building used as the crossing headquarters of the central leadership, stands near the ferry crossing. Other parts include battlefields, river crossings, command posts, buildings with Red Army slogans and martyrs' graves.

rows.name: Song City Wall of Guilin (Dongzhen Gate)
rows.summary: The surviving fragments of Guilin's old city wall, much of it from 1258–1272, when the walls of Jingjiang Prefecture were pushed north and west and faced with stone along the river against the advancing Mongol armies. The best-preserved piece is Dongzhen Gate on the Li River below Diecai Hill, a vaulted stone gateway 6.4 m high with a passage 16 m deep and wall sections still running towards Diecai and Tiefeng hills. A Song inscription on the south face of Yingwu Hill records the work and includes a carved plan of the walled city.

rows.name: Two Rivers and Four Lakes & Elephant Trunk Hill
rows.pinyin: Liǎng Jiāng Sì Hú · Xiàng Shān
rows.summary: Central Guilin's ring of waterways, which links the Li and Taohua rivers with Ronghu, Shanhu, Guihu and Mulong lakes and was dredged and joined into one loop around 2001, with lakeside parks, bridges and the Sun and Moon Pagodas on Shanhu Lake. At its southern end Elephant Trunk Hill, the city's emblem, stands where the Taohua River meets the Li, its arch, Water-Moon Cave, making the hill look like an elephant drinking from the river. Boat tours circle the waterways, and the floodlit lakes are a popular evening sight.

rows.name: West Hill Park
rows.summary: Guilin's second-largest park, made up of the West Hill peaks, Yin Hill with its caves, and West Lake. West Hill was a Buddhist centre in the Tang dynasty, and more than 200 Buddha figures in some 90 niches survive on Guanyin Peak and the neighbouring crags, one of them dated 679. Stone steps climb the peaks for views over the western side of the city.

rows.name: Xiang River Battle Memorial Park (Quanzhou)
rows.name_zh: 红军长征湘江战役纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park completed in September 2019 beside the Jiaoshanpu battlefield in Caiwan town, commemorating the Battle of the Xiang River of late 1934, when the Central Red Army fought its way across the river between Xing'an and Quanzhou during the Long March at heavy cost. It consists of the memorial park and a memorial hall with exhibitions on the campaign.

rows.name: Xiang River Breakthrough Martyrs Monument Park
rows.name_zh: 红军长征突破湘江烈士纪念碑园
rows.pinyin: Hóngjūn Chángzhēng Tūpò Xiāngjiāng Lièshì Jìniànbēi Yuán
rows.summary: A memorial park in Xing'an town, built in 1995 in memory of the Red Army soldiers killed in the Battle of the Xiang River in late 1934, during the Long March. A memorial hall on the battle opened in the park in November 2014, and the park is now also called the Xiang River Battle Memorial Park.

rows.name: Xiangshan Temple Pagodas and Inscriptions
rows.summary: The site of Xiangshan Temple on Xiang Hill at the western edge of Quanzhou town, a Buddhist monastery founded in 756 by the monk Quanzhen and burned in 1945. What survives is a group of pagodas, among them the Miaoming Pagoda, and stone inscriptions carved on the hill between the Song and Qing dynasties.

rows.name: Xiaoyao Lake
rows.summary: A lake park in Daxu town on the east side of the Li River, where paths follow the shore against a backdrop of karst hills. It is usually combined with the nearby Gudong Waterfall and Daxu old town on a day out from Guilin.

rows.name: Xinxu Battle Memorial Park (Jiuhaijing)
rows.name_zh: 新圩阻击战酒海井红军纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park completed in 2016 in Xinxu town, Guanyang County, where Red Army units fought a blocking action at Xinxu during the Battle of the Xiang River in late 1934, part of the Long March. It has a memorial and an exhibition hall on the Xinxu fighting, and close by in Hemu village are the Jiuhaijing memorial tower and the battle's field aid station in a Qing ancestral hall, both part of the national heritage site of the battle.

rows.name: Yanwo Lou
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Jiang clan in Shigang village, north-east of Quanzhou town, known as Yanwo Lou, the 'swallow's-nest tower'. Its timber memorial gateway with four pillars and three tiers of roofs dates from the Ming dynasty and leads to a mid-Qing gatehouse, side galleries, a middle hall and a rear hall.

rows.name: Yao Mountain
rows.summary: At 909 m, Yao Mountain on the north-eastern edge of Guilin is the highest peak in the city area and, unlike the limestone towers around it, a soil-covered mountain. A chairlift and footpaths climb to the summit for wide views over the karst peaks, a toboggan run comes down part of the slope, and azaleas cover the mountainside in late spring. The Ming princes' tombs of the Jingjiang line lie at its south-western foot.

rows.name: Yongning Prefecture City Wall
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty walled town at Baishou, first built of earth in 1477 and rebuilt in dressed stone in 1482, which became the seat of Yongning Prefecture in 1571. The rectangular circuit, about 1.2 km round and up to 3.7 m high with four gates, is described as the most complete Ming city wall surviving in Guangxi.

rows.name: Yuzi Paradise
rows.summary: A landscape sculpture park among karst hills south of Guilin, founded in the late 1990s by the Taiwanese entrepreneur Cao Rizhang. More than 200 artists from around the world have left large contemporary works across its lawns, lakeshores and pine woods, many of them made at the international sculpture symposiums held here, and a Club Med resort opened at the park in 2013.

rows.name: Zengpiyan National Archaeological Site Park
rows.summary: A Neolithic cave site at the foot of Dushan hill in southern Guilin, lived in roughly 12,000 to 7,000 years ago, whose excavations in 1973 and 2001 yielded very early pottery, stone, bone and shell tools, and crouched burials. The cave can be visited, and a 9.5-hectare archaeological park around it includes a site museum displaying the finds.

rows.name: Zhuangyuan Nahehai Street District
rows.summary: A redeveloped street district in the centre of Yongfu town, on the former site of the home of Wang Shize, the first person from Guangxi to take first place (zhuangyuan) in the imperial examinations. It combines dining, shopping and entertainment, with zhuangyuan-themed souvenirs and photo spots in scholar's robes, and hosts festival events such as those at the Dragon Boat Festival.

rows.name: Zijiang River & Tianmen Mountain
rows.summary: A scenic area on the upper Zi River north of Ziyuan town, where boat and raft trips run past red-sandstone (Danxia) cliffs to a landing below Tianmen Mountain. Paths on the mountain lead through narrow rock clefts to a glass viewing platform.

rows.name: Bala Monkey Mountain
rows.summary: A forested karst valley at Bala hamlet in Qiaoyin township, where villagers have protected a troop of more than 600 macaques since reforestation began in the 1990s, and the monkeys come to feeding areas and let visitors approach closely. The site also has a children's playground, a petting area with deer, horses and peacocks, and farm restaurants, and is aimed mainly at families; it was rated 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Bama Crystal Palace Cave
rows.summary: A show cave on a hillside at Daluo village, Nashe township, known for dense clusters of snow-white helictites, needle-like crystals and flower-shaped formations. The corridor-shaped cave is over 600 m long and 8–40 m wide with a fairly level path, and it was one of Bama's first 4A sites, in 2009.

rows.name: Bama Longevity Island
rows.summary: An island of about 3 hectares in the Pogui section of Cifu Lake, the reservoir on the Panyang River 8 km from Bama town, ringed by karst hills. By day it is a culture park on Bama's longevity customs; in the evening there are bonfire parties, long-table dinners and the outdoor show 'Dream of Bama', which stages a Yao wedding and bronze-drum dances.

rows.name: Baping Wetland and Forest Area
rows.summary: A wetland and forest area at Baping in Mangchang town, developed since 2020 within the Laxi National Wetland Park, a highland wetland of about 560 hectares where 168 bird species have been recorded. Boardwalks lead past lakes and lotus ponds, and the nearby Baping terraces and flower fields offer farm stays, home cooking and fruit picking.

rows.name: Changle Palace Cave
rows.summary: A show cave on Leishan hill in Bandeng village whose entrance is so low that adults must crouch to get in, opening into tall halls divided by columns of stalactites. Two main sections hold more than 20 smaller chambers, and about 1.5 km of passages with 14 named viewpoints are open to visitors; it was rated a national 4A site in 2022.

rows.name: Chengjiang National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park on the clear blue-green Chengjiang River, which rises at the Jiudun skylights in Daxing town and flows 42 km south through farmland to the Hongshui River. The 4A area of about 3.1 km² at Yili, north of Du'an town, is part of the Chengjiang national water-conservancy scenic area, and snorkelling in the river has become popular in summer.

rows.name: Chenglong Lake
rows.summary: A lake park ringed by hills on the edge of Luocheng town, named after Yu Chenglong, the Qing official famed as an incorruptible magistrate, who served in Luocheng and is said to have written poems beside it. It was rated 3A in 2015 and has since been raised to 4A.

rows.name: Colourful Maonan
rows.summary: A cultural area in Sien, the county town of Huanjiang, the only autonomous county of the Maonan people, built around the Maonan Museum. Opened in 2012, the museum holds more than 1,200 objects and has galleries on the feitao thanksgiving ritual, the Fenlong festival, flower-bamboo hat weaving and bronze-drum casting, plus a revolutionary history gallery added in 2019. Beside it stand the seven-storey Sien Pagoda, climbed for views over the town, and squares themed on Nuo masks and bronze drums.

rows.name: Cotton Tiankeng Resort
rows.summary: A resort around a karst tiankeng (giant sinkhole) at Shendong hamlet in Mianhua village, which also takes in Changsheng Cave, a show cave of stalactites, and the Mulao village of Shendong. Cliff-edge attractions include a hotel, a bookshop lit up at night, a pool, glass and cliff walkways, a via ferrata, a zip line and a small cliff train, alongside a Mulao intangible-heritage hall.

rows.name: Danlu Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded hill scenic area at Danlu hamlet in Wuai town, built around the remains of a Ming-dynasty alchemy site that the county describes as one of the most complete found in China, with karst caves and local Taoist, lantern-dance and tusi (chieftain) traditions. Since opening in 2018 it has added a glass walkway, a glass slide and a glass suspension bridge, a staged show and long-table banquets.

rows.name: Danquan Liquor Cave
rows.summary: A visitor site at the Danquan distillery in Nandan town, founded in 1956 and now Guangxi's largest liquor producer, where visitors can follow baijiu production from grain to blending. Its highlight is Dongtian Jiuhai, a natural karst cave with a constant temperature of about 15 °C and room for some 50,000 tonnes of base liquor, certified by Guinness World Records as the largest liquor-storage cave.

rows.name: Donglan Red Tourism Area
rows.summary: A group of revolutionary sites linked to Wei Baqun, a Zhuang leader of the 1920s peasant movement, rated 4A together in 2011. In the county town, the Donglan Martyrs' Cemetery, founded in 1956, holds Wei Baqun's tomb, a memorial tower and a hall of about 600 documents, photographs and relics, next to the Wei Baqun Memorial Hall. Some 30 km south-west near Wuzhuan are Lenin Cave, the vast natural cave where Wei ran Guangxi's first peasant movement institute in 1925, the 1906 Kuixing Tower used by the Seventh Red Army's front committee under Deng Xiaoping in 1930, and Wei's rebuilt mountainside home.

rows.name: Du'an Underground River Geopark
rows.name_zh: 都安地下河国家地质公园
rows.pinyin: Dū'ān Dìxià Hé Guójiā Dìzhì Gōngyuán
rows.summary: A national geopark of about 210 km² along the Disu underground river system, which with its 12 tributaries runs for some 241 km beneath the karst before joining the Hongshui River. More than 300 skylights, collapse windows down to the river, pock the landscape, and the Tunbang and Jiuling skylights in Dongmiao township are the main visitor spots; peach-blossom freshwater jellyfish appear in some pools between April and October.

rows.name: Fengshan Geopark and Sanmenhai
rows.name_zh: 凤山国家地质公园·三门海
rows.summary: Fengshan's half of the Leye–Fengshan UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2010, a karst landscape of peak clusters, caves, sinkholes and natural bridges. Its best-known sight is Sanmenhai in Poxin village, seven collapsed sinkholes joined by an underground river, three of which visitors enter by boat through cave mouths open to the sky. The geopark museum is at Chuanlong Cave on the edge of Fengshan town.

rows.name: First Bend of the Hongshui River
rows.summary: A viewpoint above a sweeping U-shaped bend where the Hongshui River loops through a gorge at Banwen village in Sanshi town. A glass viewing platform shaped like a bronze drum, a nod to Donglan's bronze-drum tradition, looks down over the meander.

rows.name: Geyasigu Baiku Yao Folk Park
rows.summary: A Baiku Yao (White Trousers Yao) culture resort of about 9.6 km² at Ganhe hamlet in Lihu Yao township, where a river winds past fields into a cave among karst hills. Alongside courtyard hotel buildings and a mud-and-timber hotel in Baiku Yao style, it has restaurants, a cave theatre, farm-experience fields and a workshop showing how Baiku Yao clothing is made, with staged song-and-dance evenings and long-table feasts.

rows.name: Hongshui River Hundred-Li Gallery
rows.summary: A 27.7 km² stretch of the Hongshui River running upstream from Dahua town towards Guhe township, within the Hongshui River–Qibainong scenic area, where tour boats cruise between karst hills and riverside villages. Rated 4A in 2019, it forms the backbone of Dahua's river tourism, linking the county town with the reservoir and peak-cluster scenery upstream.

rows.name: Huixian Mountain
rows.summary: A craggy hill in Bailongshan Park on the northern edge of Yizhou, a sightseeing spot since the Tang dynasty, climbed for views over the town. Its cliffs and caves carry inscriptions from the Song dynasty to the Republican era, protected nationally since 2013, together with carved figures in White Dragon Cave and a Ming inscription on the bird-shaped Qiyun rock at the summit.

rows.name: Liu Sanjie's Hometown
rows.summary: A river scenic area where the Xiajian River meets the Longjiang east of Yizhou, presented as the home of Liu Sanjie (Third Sister Liu), the legendary folk singer whose song tradition, nominated by Yizhou, is on the national intangible heritage list. Boats run up the clear Xiajian past karst peaks, bamboo groves and a 'water stone forest' of rocks in the river, with stops at a house shown as Liu Sanjie's home, folk-song performances and farm restaurants.

rows.name: Longxianggai Maple and Ginkgo Park
rows.summary: A former mining area at Lamo village near Chehe town, between about 700 and 1,200 m, that has been regraded and replanted with 18 introduced maple varieties, ginkgo, peach, azalea and peony, and was rated 4A in 2023. It is best known for autumn colour, when the maples, ginkgo and pink muhly grass turn, and has forest trails, viewing platforms, a rainbow slide, a campsite, guesthouses and displays on the area's mining past.

rows.name: Miluotuo Cultural Park
rows.summary: A riverside park of about 30 hectares in Du'an's Hedong district, opened in 2015 for the county's 60th anniversary and themed on the Bunu Yao, whose creation epic of the goddess Miluotuo became national intangible heritage in 2011. It has wind-and-rain bridges, waterfalls and lakes, a riverside promenade, a culture street, a hotel and the museum of the Du'an Underground River Geopark.

rows.name: Mulun Karst Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A tourism area on the south-eastern edge of the Mulun National Nature Reserve, part of the Huanjiang Karst component of the South China Karst World Heritage Site since 2014, which protects karst forest continuous with Maolan in Guizhou. Visitors come for the Gubin River, with a walk through its butterfly gorge, rafting and riverside camping, and there is a hotel and visitor centre at Xiazhai hamlet.

rows.name: Nandan Mineral Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Tanghan village in Chehe town, fed by water that reaches the surface at about 62 °C. It has a dozen public pools, nine private courtyard pools, a hot-spring swimming pool, a children's water park, a hotel and villas, set among wooded hills.

rows.name: Niujiaozhai Waterfalls
rows.summary: A forested karst gorge of about 10 km² at Bamian village, Minglun town, where a 3 km trail passes more than ten tiers of falls in quick succession, nine of them large. The best known, Seven Fairies Falls, is about 60 m wide and over 50 m high and drops in seven strands; the area borders the core of the Mulun karst World Heritage area.

rows.name: Panyang River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Panyang River valley around Jiazhuan town, rated 4A in 2009 as Bama's main river area: the river re-emerges from underground at Poyue village and flows past Zhuang and Yao villages known for their long-lived residents. Along its course are the large caves of Baimo and Bainiao, the latter entered by boat beneath a skylight, and bamboo rafts drift on the clear green water.

rows.name: Qibainong National Geopark
rows.summary: A national geopark of about 323 km² in northern Dahua, declared in 2009, covering what is regarded as one of the world's densest clusters of karst peaks and enclosed hollows: some 9,000 peaks with summits above 800 m crowd around more than 2,500 depressions. Roads wind through the Bunu Yao villages of Qibainong township past high lakes, the Banlan canyon and viewpoints, and a geopark museum stands at the entrance.

rows.name: Qimei Water Town
rows.summary: A riverside cultural quarter in Dahua's Gujiang community on the Hongshui River, developed by the county around its ornamental-stone culture, local food and Zhuang and Yao customs, with a stone museum, a food hall, an ethnic museum and Mituo Temple. It was rated 4A in 2019 and hosts folk events such as rice-cake pounding at festivals.

rows.name: Red Army Slogans Building, Hechi
rows.summary: A building in Hechi town, the county seat until 1953, whose original walls still carry 55 slogans and six drawings left by the Red Army around 1930, when the Seventh Red Army under Deng Xiaoping and Zhang Yunyi stayed in Hechi three times and reorganised there. The sites where the Seventh and Eighth Red Armies were stationed were restored between January 2010 and December 2011, when a memorial hall on the armies' reorganisation at Hechi also opened in the town.

rows.name: Sandaowan Resort
rows.summary: A resort area of about 830 hectares on the Hongshui River near Xingli village in Disu town, set among karst hills, Bunu Yao villages and farmland. It offers riverside stays and aerial views over the valley, and runs a model-aircraft science camp and study programmes for school groups.

rows.name: Tianlong Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A forested karst gorge about 15 km long and 800–1,000 m deep just outside Tian'e town, formerly promoted as Longtan Grand Canyon National Forest Park and rated 4A in 2014. With forest cover of about 96 per cent it shelters rare plants such as slipper orchids and golden camellia, and trails lead to a viewpoint over the town, primeval forest, an orchid garden and Lion Cave.

rows.name: Tianshang Hegu (Tian'e Riverside)
rows.summary: Tian'e's riverside town scenic area on the Hongshui River, joining Tianfu Hill park with the town's embankment walks, a food street, a fountain square and an elevated skywalk. Visitors climb Tianfu Hill to the Fuwang Pavilion and the Dong Xi Literary Museum, devoted to the Tian'e-born novelist Dong Xi, winner of the Mao Dun and Lu Xun literary prizes, or take a boat on the river within sight of the Longtan dam; paddleboarding has become popular in summer.

rows.name: Yantan Scenic Area
rows.summary: The reservoir area of the Yantan hydropower station on the Hongshui River, whose 110 m dam was built between 1985 and 1995, now developed for lakeside stays. Its landmark is Meinü (Beauty) Peak, a karst ridge said to resemble a sleeping woman, where a campsite opened in 2023 with space-capsule pods, forest cabins, RV pitches, tent lodges, a hotel, hiking paths and viewing platforms over the lake.

rows.name: Yaowang Tianxia
rows.summary: A Baiku Yao cultural tourism complex at Wangshang hamlet in Lihu Yao township, rated 4A in 2023, laid out in areas for intangible-heritage displays on Baiku Yao food, weddings, funerals, bronze drums and top-spinning, with shops, restaurants, hotels and guesthouses and a family park. At major festivals Baiku Yao people gather at its Yaowang village square to play bronze drums, blow ox horns, sing and dance. The complex also takes in Dongtian Shengjing, an underground canyon with waterfalls inside a cave.

rows.name: Yuanyang Cave
rows.summary: A two-level karst cave at over 700 m on Phoenix Hill just east of Fengshan town, about 480 m long, up to 320 m wide and 52 m high at its tallest hall. Dense clusters of stalagmites, one of them 36.4 m tall, form what looks like a stone forest underground, and the visitor route through the first level winds for about 1.2 km. Below it, at the foot of the hill, the twin pools of Yuanyang Spring have long been counted the first of Fengshan's eight views.

rows.name: Yunguantian
rows.summary: An upland pasture and camping area in Mangchang town at around 1,000 m, rated 4A in 2022, with mountain meadows, woodland, karst peaks and farmland. Facilities include a viewing platform above the clouds, a campsite, a coffee house and walking trails, and it draws visitors on the rare winter days when snow falls.

rows.name: Zhenzhuyan (Pearl Cave) Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst scenic area of about 5 km² at Dandong village in Liujia town, built around a stalactite cave lit with coloured lights and marketed since 2022 as the Luming Sengu resort. Outside are natural swimming pools in the river, plank walks and pavilions, and a forest campsite with tents, a forest pasture and family activities.

rows.name: Zhuangxiang Generals Memorial Park
rows.summary: A red-tourism memorial park in Nongying, the home village of General Wei Guoqing (1913–1989), created for his centenary with a restored version of his former home. Its memorial hall, opened in September 2013, has seven galleries: the ground floor covers Wei Guoqing's life, and the upper floor 19 generals who rose through the Seventh and Eighth Red Armies, among them Zhang Yunyi, Li Tianyou and Wei Jie.

rows.name: Daguishan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Dagui Mountains at Butou town, south of Hezhou city, one of the first national forest parks approved in China, with forest covering about 93% of its area. Its 4A scenic area of about 3.5 km² is mainly a place for forest walks.

rows.name: Fuchuan Eco-Agriculture Science Park
rows.name_zh: 富川生态高值农业科技示范园
rows.pinyin: Fùchuān Shēngtài Gāozhí Nóngyè Kējì Shìfànyuán
rows.summary: An agricultural demonstration park of about 58 ha near Fuli town, centred on a 9,600 m² greenhouse that shows soilless and hydroponic vegetable growing and giant vegetable-shaped displays. Around it are fruit orchards for seasonal picking, a farming-culture exhibit, a bamboo grove, flower fields, family allotments and a wetland area planted with lotus and other water crops. It suits families and school groups more than general sightseers.

rows.name: Fuchuan Ming City
rows.summary: The old walled county town of Fuchuan, begun in 1396 under the Ming, through which the Xiaohe Ancient Road, the old road linking the Xiao River in Hunan with the He River, entered by the north gate and left by the south. Much of the wall and part of the moat survive, enclosing a Confucian temple, a martial temple, pebble-paved lanes, old opera stages, a lantern tower, wells and old houses; the county town also keeps the Republican-era arcade street of Xinyong Jie.

rows.name: Fuchuan Yao Wind-and-Rain Bridges
rows.summary: Twenty-seven covered bridges built between the late Ming and the late Qing over streams and fields near old villages along the Xiaohe Ancient Road in Fuchuan Yao Autonomous County, home to Yao and Han communities; they come in stone-arch, stone-beam and timber-beam forms, topped by tiled galleries and pavilions that mix the Chinese covered-bridge tradition with Yao building features. The best known are a pair at Youmu village called the 'yin-yang bridges': the Huilan Bridge of 1602, a three-arch stone bridge with a gallery, pavilion and painted tower and twelve steles on its history, and the 35 m Qinglong Bridge of 1624 with its three-storey tower. Others stand in villages around Chengbei, Mailing and Chaodong towns.

rows.name: Gui River Scenic Area, Zhaoping
rows.summary: A 25 km stretch of the Gui River, the lower course of the Li River, centred on Zhaoping town, from Songlin Gorge upstream to Matan Gorge downstream. Boat trips run between green hills and bamboo-lined banks, combining Li River-style scenery with narrow gorges.

rows.name: Gupo Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested mountain park about 26 km north of central Hezhou, near the Hunan and Guangdong borders, with 25 peaks over 1,000 m and a highest summit of 1,844 m, the tallest in eastern Guangxi; its many cliffs give waterfalls in almost every ravine. Paths lead past streams and falls in the lower valleys, and the surrounding resort area also takes in the Jade Stone Forest, Shibashui, hot springs and a riverside park.

rows.name: Huangyao Ancient Town
rows.summary: A market town ringed by karst hills in Zhaoping County, founded in the Song dynasty, built up in the late Ming and at its most prosperous under the Qing Qianlong emperor, and named after its two main clans, the Huangs and the Yaos. More than 300 Ming and Qing houses of grey brick and dark tile line its flagstone lanes, with ancestral halls, temples, an old opera stage, wells, small bridges with pavilions over the stream, and old banyan trees, and the town has served as a set for many films and TV dramas. In 1945 the Communist Party's Guangxi provincial working committee moved its offices here, and the buildings around Baozhu Temple are now a memorial museum.

rows.name: Jade Stone Forest, Hezhou
rows.summary: A rare stone forest of white marble, the stone known in Chinese as 'Han white jade', in Huangtian town north of Hezhou. The site, about 25 ha, was long an open-cast quarry; after the stone ran out it was restored and opened as a scenic area, with paths winding among white pinnacles and spires.

rows.name: Jiang Family Hakka Walled House, Hezhou
rows.summary: A large Qing-dynasty walled compound of the Hakka Jiang clan in Renchong village, Liantang town: square and symmetrical, enclosed by a wall about 3 m high, with halls, corridors, rooms and light wells interlocking inside, and fine carving of qilin, dragons, phoenixes, birds and flowers on its eaves, windows, screens, beams and pillars. The Jiangs, who came from Wuhua in Guangdong, built eight walled houses around Liantang; the northern Renchong house is open as part of the Hezhou Hakka Ecomuseum, with displays of Hakka dress, daily life and farm tools, and a few Jiang families still live in it.

rows.name: Linhe Old City (Hejie)
rows.summary: The old town of Hejie, on both banks of the Lin River where it joins the He, was the seat of Linhe county and later of Hezhou for some 2,000 years, from the founding of Linhe County in 111 BC until the county offices moved to Babu in 1952. The west-bank city keeps about 1.1 km of earthen walls up to 6 m high, the 27 m Kuixing Tower of 1740 rising from the wall, flagstone streets, old wells and about twenty clan ancestral halls, mostly of the Ming and Qing. Across the river the Hedong quarter has arcaded shops and the Qing-dynasty Yuedong Guild Hall built by merchants from Guangdong.

rows.name: Ma Yin Temple (Hundred-Pillar Temple), Fuxi
rows.summary: Two temples in Fuxi village honouring Ma Yin, the 10th-century King of Chu in the Five Dynasties period: the Ma Chu Great King Temple, founded in 1396 and moved here in 1848, and a temple founded in 1413 whose hall, the Hundred-Pillar Temple, stands on 120 timber columns raised on stone bases, with an opera stage in front. The stream between them is crossed by a wind-and-rain bridge, the Zhongling Bridge, and Fuxi itself is a listed traditional village with a long flagstone street, gate towers with carved plaques, and clan halls.

rows.name: Nanshan Tea Plantation, Zhaoping
rows.summary: Tea gardens covering the hills just south of Zhaoping town, ringed by mountains and often wrapped in mist, known for the county's early spring tea. Spring, from March to June, is the best time to visit, while the new leaves are being picked.

rows.name: Shenxian Lake & Shenjian Stone Forest
rows.summary: Two adjoining scenic spots in Fuli town in the farm country east of Fuchuan: Shenxian Lake, a lake with rural scenery beside the old village of Babailing, and the Shenjian Stone Forest, a small cluster of sword-like limestone pinnacles. Both lie in a farming district of vegetable fields, navel-orange orchards and the Hengtang Reservoir, and make an easy outing from Fuchuan town.

rows.name: Shibashui (Eighteen Waters) Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley on the northern outskirts of Hezhou, below Gupo Mountain, where a stream drops through a long chain of waterfalls and pools, a type of stepped cascade uncommon in southern China. Paths climb beside the falls through the woods.

rows.name: Xixi Forest Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in forested hills at Nanxiang town in eastern Hezhou, where the spring water comes out at up to 86.5°C. More than a hundred outdoor pools are spread through the woods, from plain spring-water pools to a children's water park and a hilltop infinity pool, with hotel rooms, villas and inns on site. Most guests come from neighbouring Guangdong, and it suits an overnight soak rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Yingjia Village & CPC Guangxi Provincial Committee Memorial Park
rows.name_zh: 英家·中共广西省工委纪念园
rows.pinyin: Yīngjiā · Zhōnggòng Guǎngxī Shěng Gōngwěi Jìniànyuán
rows.summary: Yingjia, in Qingtang town in south-western Zhongshan County, is an old market village near the Xiaohe Ancient Road that prospered from the late Ming onward. From 1942 to 1945 it was a base of the Communist Party's Guangxi provincial working committee, and in June 1947 it was the scene of the Yingjia uprising; a museum on the committee's history opened in 2016. The village also keeps the Yuedong Guild Hall, built in 1777 by merchants from Guangdong, a brick, timber and stone hall known for its carving.

rows.name: Ziyun Cave (Ziyun Wonderland)
rows.summary: A limestone cave in a karst hill at Limu village, Etang town, on the south-western edge of Hezhou city, lit with coloured lights. In 2023 its operator, the Guangxi Tourism Development Group, added a 17-scene show in the cave that combines projections, sound and mixed-reality headsets with the formations and with Yao legends.

rows.name: Baiya Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A 10 km red-rock (Danxia-type) canyon in the hills of north-eastern Wuxuan, 5–40 m wide, with 37 bends, ten waterfalls and hundreds of steep side gorges that give it the name 'hundred cliffs'. Paths lead through forest with tree ferns and other protected plants past pools and cascades, among them the Tiannü Sanhua fall with a single drop of 86 m; the site reopened in 2022 after new walkways and a visitor centre were built.

rows.name: Baxian Tianchi (Eight Immortals Lake)
rows.summary: A lake about 150 m long and 100 m wide lying more than 100 m up a hillside south of Wuxuan, ringed by eight small peaks that gave it the name 'Eight Immortals'. The county gazetteer notes that its level hardly changes in flood or drought; it was listed as a Guangxi scenic area in 1988 and opened to visitors in 2018.

rows.name: Dayaoshan Panwangjie (Lianhua Mountain)
rows.summary: Formerly the Lianhua (Lotus) Mountain scenic area, a 23 km² area of quartz-sandstone peaks north-west of Jinxiu whose main summit rises to 1,350 m and whose cluster of pinnacles resembles a lotus bud. Trails climb through old forest past stone pinnacles, cliffs and deep ravines to viewpoints over seas of cloud, and there is a temple to Panhu, the legendary ancestor of the Yao.

rows.name: Guo Songnian Manor
rows.summary: A manor house begun in 1920 by Guo Songnian, a late-Qing scholar-graduate, in Yagang village in southern Wuxuan, covering about 2,800 m² and combining Chinese and Western architectural styles. It became a national heritage site in 2019 and is one of more than 20 early-20th-century manors in the county.

rows.name: Gushagou
rows.summary: A mountain area in north-eastern Jinxiu, largely inside the Dayao Mountains national nature reserve, combining rafting on the Changliu River gorge, the Lingzu canyon with its clear stream and coloured pebbles, the old village of Lingzu, red maple woods on Niulingding and the high Yao village of Bale. A glass walkway along the cliffs at Bale's Shimen pass looks out over the ridges, and the uplands are used for paragliding and hiking.

rows.name: Guxiang Hot Springs (Xiangzhou Hot Springs)
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at Reshui ('hot water') village east of Xiangzhou town, built around the Xiangzhou hot springs, with bathing pools set among green hills, fields and village houses. It makes a relaxing stop on the way between Laibin or Liuzhou and the Dayao Mountains.

rows.name: Heshan National Mine Park
rows.summary: An industrial heritage park on about 27 hectares of the former east mine of the Heshan Mining Bureau, Guangxi's first coal-mining enterprise, beside national road 322. It has a mine-park museum, an underground coal-mining experience, a steam locomotive, a train restaurant, the ruins of the coal-preparation building and a hall of mining machinery, plus karting and other rides.

rows.name: Mo Chieftain's Office (Mo Tusi Yamen)
rows.summary: The administrative seat and residence of the Mo family, hereditary local chieftains (tusi) who governed Xincheng under the Ming and Qing, begun in 1582 and used until the chieftain system was abolished in 1906. Laid out on a north-facing axis at the foot of Cuiping Hill over more than 4 hectares, it has a gate, three halls, a rear garden and ancestral halls, surrounded by officials' mansions, a pavilion, a cave and a drill ground that now houses a chieftain-culture exhibition. It is described as the largest and most complete chieftain's office surviving in south-west China.

rows.name: Shanshui Yaocheng (Jinxiu Town)
rows.summary: Jinxiu county town, at about 775 m in the Jinxiu River valley in the heart of the Dayao Mountains, is described by the county as the highest county town in Guangxi; it has been rebuilt in Yao style and made a 4A scenic area as a whole. Its sights include the Yao Museum, the Gongde and Santing bridges, the Panwang Valley, Yaodu Square and streets of Yao crafts and food. It is the base for exploring the Dayao Mountains, home to five distinct Yao groups.

rows.name: Shengtang Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir and river gorge at the foot of Shengtang Mountain in south-eastern Jinxiu, where the river winds between peaks and cliffs of red sandstone. Visitors come for boat trips on the reservoir, rafting on the river and swimming in spring-fed pools, and the scenic area also presents Yao village customs.

rows.name: Shengtang Mountain
rows.summary: The main peak of the Dayao Mountains and, at 1,979 m, the highest summit in central Guangxi, revered by the Yao as a holy mountain. Its often cloud-wrapped ridges of purple-red sandstone carry pines, rhododendrons that flower in May, stone rivers left by ancient glaciation and a Ming-dynasty stone wall.

rows.name: Time Island Resort, Penglaizhou
rows.summary: A resort on Penglaizhou, an island of about 27 hectares in the Hongshui River east of Laibin, with steep karst banks, rocky outcrops and thick vegetation. Guests stay at the island hotel, take boat trips around the island, barbecue and join local food activities such as making oil tea and glutinous rice cakes. The island also holds the site of the Song-dynasty seat of Xiangzhou, a protected archaeological site.

rows.name: Wenhui Pagoda
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty pagoda in Fuji village near Qianjiang in western Laibin, built in the Wanli reign by the garrison commander Huang Wenhui, after whom it is named. It was listed by Guangxi in 2009 and became a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Xialiantang Village
rows.summary: A village of the Liu family in eastern Wuxuan, set among ponds and old longan groves, with two notable buildings: the General's Mansion, a walled Qing courtyard compound begun in 1801 with 175 rooms where about a hundred people still live, and the Liu Bingyu Manor of 1908. The manor, built by an army general of the Republican era, combines a traditional courtyard plan with Western-style architecture and became a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Xincheng Lavender Manor
rows.summary: A flower farm on the southern edge of Xincheng town, billed as the largest lavender estate in Guangxi, with fields of lavender, verbena and other flowering plants laid out for strolling and photography. Visit in the flowering season, as by late autumn few plants are in bloom.

rows.name: Yinshan (Cathaya) Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the Dayao Mountains national nature reserve north-east of Jinxiu town, named after the Cathaya (yinshan), a rare conifer found only in China, which grows here with southern yew and Bretschneidera. It is the part of the reserve richest in rare species, including macaques and the golden Kaiser-i-Hind butterfly, and also has the site of a 'sent-down youth' camp and the Dayaoshan ecology museum.

rows.name: Bagongtang Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park of about 107 hectares in the new town of Liujiang District, created from a large pond and opened in October 2019. Paths and bridges circle the lake, with a bird island where egrets gather, flower meadows and the Bagong pagoda set against a karst hill, and the park is lit up at night.

rows.name: Bailiandong Cave Science Museum
rows.name_zh: 白莲洞洞穴科学博物馆
rows.summary: A museum at Bailian Cave, a limestone cave about 1,870 m long south of Liuzhou where digs since 1956 have yielded stone tools, human teeth, animal fossils and traces of fire spanning roughly 37,000 to 7,000 years ago. The site museum and a newer exhibition hall display the finds, including river-snail shells that show how long people here have eaten snails.

rows.name: Baipeng Lotus Garden
rows.summary: A lotus-growing area at Baipeng, the centre of Liujiang's double-crop lotus-root farming, with about 45 hectares of lotus fields in a scenic area of about 79 hectares. Boardwalks cross the ponds, a small sightseeing train runs between them, farm restaurants serve lotus-root dishes, and a lotus festival is held each summer.

rows.name: Batuan Bridge
rows.summary: A Dong wind-and-rain bridge over the Mengjiang River at Batuan village in Dudong, built between 1896 and 1910. It is about 50 m long on a single stone pier, with three pavilions over the pier and the two ends, and has separate lanes for people and for livestock.

rows.name: Buyang Xianren Mountain Tea Hills
rows.summary: Tea gardens covering the hillsides of Buyang, a Dong village in Bajiang township, at about 600 to 1,000 m, where tea is the main crop and the early-spring harvest is the local speciality. Paths lead from the entrance through a maple grove and terraced tea gardens to a Dong hamlet, an old tea garden and a stretch of old trading path, and there are campsites and wooden cabins on the hill.

rows.name: Danzhou Old Town
rows.summary: A walled old town on an island in the Rong River that served as the seat of Huaiyuan county (renamed Sanjiang in 1914) through the Ming, Qing and Republican periods. Its surviving sights include the Danzhou Academy, the Fujian-Guangdong guild hall, the east and north gate towers and stretches of the old wall, among about 33 hectares of pomelo orchards. Many villagers now run guesthouses and small restaurants.

rows.name: Dong Tiangong Cultural Area
rows.summary: A complex of new Dong-style timber buildings, including drum towers and covered corridors, around a cultural square in Guyi, Sanjiang's county town, opened in 2021 among 15 old sweetgum trees aged 100 to 200 years. Dong music shows with lusheng reed pipes, leaf-blown songs and pipa ballads are staged for visitors, and evening opening began in 2024 with a music festival.

rows.name: Dule Rock Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst landscape park about 12 km south of central Liuzhou made up of twelve limestone peaks, a clear stream and two man-made lakes. Lit paths link three show caves, Panlong, Tongtian and Shuiyun, about 680 m long in total, and a forest of inscribed steles includes calligraphy by the film actor Zhao Dan.

rows.name: Fenghuang River Eco-Tourism Resort
rows.name_zh: 凤凰河生态旅游度假区
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the upper Liu River at Luoman, west of Liuzhou, developed as part of the Liu River tourism belt and rated 4A in 2015. It draws geothermal water from a deep well for public and private hot-spring pools, alongside a resort hotel, villas and outdoor activity areas.

rows.name: Guangxi Ecological Science Garden
rows.summary: A science-education scenic area on the campus of the Guangxi Eco-Engineering Vocational and Technical College in Shatang, north of Liuzhou, rated 4A in 2023. Visitors walk through its east and west gardens, groves of old and notable trees, the historic buildings of the former forestry school and the woodland around Junwu Lake, and it is used mainly for study tours.

rows.name: Gulinglong Infused-Liquor Factory Park
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism site at the Guangxi Gulinglong group's garden-style factory in Chuanshan town, which makes infused liquors, spirits steeped with herbs and, in some cases, snakes and other animals. Visitors see the brewing and bottling halls, a museum of infused liquor with jars of snakes and other creatures, a tasting hall, a collection of about 600 kinds of Chinese and foreign liquors, and a rooftop rice field.

rows.name: Heli Three Kings Temple
rows.summary: A temple complex in the Dong village of Heli, Liangkou township, built in a mix of Han Chinese and Dong styles and dating from the Ming and Qing dynasties. Four neighbouring villages held a joint rite to the Three Kings here each year on the second day of the second lunar month, and a stele set up in 1794 confirmed the temple as their shared ritual centre. Visitors see it together with the Renhe wind-and-rain bridge in the same village.

rows.name: Ho Chi Minh's Former Residence, Liuzhou
rows.summary: A group of sites linked with the Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh, who was detained in and later lived in Liuzhou between 1942 and 1944 while working with the Vietnamese Revolutionary League. The main site is the former Nanyang Inn on Liushi Road, built in 1930, where he lived from 1943 to 1944 and which now holds an exhibition on his time in Liuzhou. The listing also covers the nearby Lequn Society building, a cave on Panlong Hill where he was held, and the Red Building at the Liuzhou Hotel, where he met Zhou Enlai in July 1954.

rows.name: Keliwan Happy World
rows.summary: An amusement park in the Liudong New Area, opened in 2017 as Kale Planet and rated 4A in 2018, now operating under the Keliwan Happy World name beside the Liuzhou Garden Expo Park. It has outdoor rides and play areas aimed at families with children and teenagers.

rows.name: Keliwan Water Park
rows.summary: An outdoor water park in the Liudong New Area with water rides and pools, mainly a summer outing for families and young people. It shares the Keliwan name with the neighbouring amusement park.

rows.name: Laojun Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave on the south-western edge of Rongshui town, also called Zhenxian Cave, through which the Lingshou stream flows for about 300 m past stalactites and cliff inscriptions. More than 30 inscriptions and 17 Song-dynasty steles survive, among them a passage from the Book of Changes in the hand of Sima Guang, and the Ming traveller Xu Xiake stayed here for 13 days. Two Song stone bridges cross the stream at the mouth, and during the war against Japan the cave housed an arsenal.

rows.name: Liu River Scenic Area (Baili Liujiang)
rows.summary: The scenic stretch of the Liu River as it loops through central Liuzhou, lined with landscaped promenades on both banks. Sightseeing boats leave from the East Embankment pier, and after dark the banks are floodlit and a large musical fountain plays on the river by the north bank.

rows.name: LiuGong Industrial Tourism Site
rows.summary: The main works of LiuGong, the construction-machinery maker founded in Liuzhou in 1958 that built mainland China's first wheel loader in 1966, rated a 4A industrial-tourism site in 2018. The works receive study groups and visiting delegations and suit travellers interested in heavy industry.

rows.name: Liuhou Park and Liu Zongyuan Shrine
rows.summary: A city-centre park laid out from 1906 around the shrine to Liu Zongyuan, the Tang poet and essayist who governed Liuzhou and died here in 819. The shrine, founded in 822 and rebuilt in 1987 to a Qing plan, keeps about fifty steles from the Song dynasty onwards, among them the Lizi Stele of 1217 with a poem by Han Yu in Su Shi's calligraphy. Behind it is a memorial tomb holding Liu's robes and cap, and the park is a popular gathering place for local musicians and dancers.

rows.name: Liuzhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A modern reconstruction of Liuzhou's Confucian temple, first founded in the early Tang dynasty, standing on the east bank of the Liu River below Dengtai Hill. The complex, mainly in Song style with southern Chinese details, comprises the Dacheng Gate, Dacheng Hall, Chongsheng Shrine and Minglun Hall, and hosts traditional-culture events on festivals.

rows.name: Liuzhou Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped park in the Liudong New Area, built for the first Guangxi Garden and Horticulture Expo and opened in October 2011. Its themed show gardens, lakeside promenades, fountain and flower squares and a greenhouse spread over about 42 hectares of planting and 12 hectares of water, with more than 380 plant species.

rows.name: Liuzhou Industrial Museum
rows.summary: A city industrial museum opened in 2012 in the sawtooth-roofed workshops of the former No. 3 Cotton Mill, on a site of about 11 hectares. Its main hall shows more than 6,000 machines and products made or used in Liuzhou since 1902, with steam and diesel locomotives outside, and further halls cover the city's companies and its recovery from acid-rain pollution.

rows.name: Liuzhou Military Museum Park (Old Liuzhou Airfield)
rows.summary: A museum park on the old Liuzhou airfield, built by the Guangxi provincial authorities in 1929 and used during the war against Japan by the Chinese air force, Soviet volunteer airmen and the American Flying Tigers; it was bombed many times and occupied by Japanese forces in 1944. Eighteen barrack buildings, a control tower and pillboxes survive, and the barracks house an exhibition on Liuzhou during the war. Aircraft, tanks, armoured vehicles, a patrol boat and artillery are displayed outdoors.

rows.name: Liuzhou Museum
rows.summary: The city's main museum, founded in the late 1950s and housed since 2003 in a granite building in the style of a city gate on the east side of People's Square. Its permanent galleries cover fossils and prehistoric remains, Liuzhou's history, ethnic costume and silverwork, ancient bronzes, painted fans and calligraphy, carved inkstones and stone steles.

rows.name: Liuzhou Urban Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: A two-floor exhibition on the east bank of the Liu River about the city's history and planning. The ground floor centres on a 1:750 model of the whole city and a virtual tour along the river, and the upper floor covers bridges and other engineering works, ethnic culture and tourism in Liuzhou and its counties.

rows.name: Liuzhou Zoo
rows.summary: The city zoo on the southern edge of Liuzhou, which moved here from Liuhou Park in 2005 and keeps more than a hundred species. It has a big-cat area, an aviary, a small-animal area where children can feed animals and a herbivore enclosure crossed by boardwalks among sika deer and ostriches, and an ice-and-snow play area opened in 2024.

rows.name: Longnü Gully
rows.summary: A valley in Sirong township on the south-western slopes of Yuanbao Mountain, with clear pools, waterfalls and forest beside Miao and Dong villages of wooden houses and drum towers. Sights include the Longnü Pool and waterfall, terraced fields and the Red Army Bridge, first built by the Red Seventh Army when it passed through in 1930 and later rebuilt as a Dong wind-and-rain bridge.

rows.name: Longtan Park
rows.summary: A large karst park in southern Liuzhou, with 24 limestone peaks around two spring-fed pools, Longtan and Leitan, that steam on winter mornings, and a lake crossed by a covered bridge. Near the pools are Ming-dynasty cliff inscriptions on Lei Hill, a stele pavilion recalling Liu Zongyuan's prayer for rain here, reconstructed Zhuang, Yao, Miao and Dong houses and a nine-tier drum tower. At the foot of Longtan Hill a display hall covers the Liyuzui shell-midden site, where human remains about 12,000 to 7,000 years old and Neolithic layers were excavated in 1980.

rows.name: Luosifen Town
rows.summary: A themed town at Taiyangcun, west of Liuzhou, developed since 2018 around luosifen, the city's river-snail rice-noodle soup, and recognised as a national modern agricultural industrial park. It brings together raw-material farms, noodle factories and study-tour facilities, and its hilltop launch site is a paragliding base that hosted the Guangxi championships in 2024.

rows.name: Luowei Luosifen Industrial Park
rows.summary: An industrial park in the Luowei area of southern Liuzhou where packaged luosifen, the city's river-snail rice-noodle soup, is made, rated a 4A industrial-tourism site in 2018. Visitors watch the automated packing lines from viewing corridors and tour a luosifen culture exhibition hall, and it suits food-minded travellers and school groups.

rows.name: Malu Hill Stone Park and Liuzhou Stone Museum
rows.summary: A hillside park in eastern Liuzhou built around ornamental stones, a long-standing local passion. Its centrepiece is the Liuzhou Stone Museum, a stone-shaped building whose three floors show stones from the Hongshui River, from elsewhere in China and abroad, and minerals and fossils, and a large stone market lies across the road.

rows.name: Mapang Drum Tower
rows.summary: The drum tower of Mapang, a Dong village in Bajiang township, first built in the Qing dynasty and rebuilt in 1943. Square in plan with 11.5 m sides and 13 m tall, it rises in nine tiers of eaves on a timber frame with four main pillars, and is counted among the largest historic Dong drum towers.

rows.name: Mengwu Miao Village Folk Culture Park
rows.summary: A Miao culture park inside the Shuanglong Gully resort, set up around 2018 by dismantling stilt houses in remote mountain villages and rebuilding them here, with some of their Miao owners resettled to work in the park. It has reconstructed stilt houses and covered bridges, staged Miao song-and-dance shows, and craft halls where visitors watch lusheng-making, Miao embroidery and silversmithing.

rows.name: Oriental Dream Works – Liukong Creative Park
rows.name_zh: 东方梦工场·柳空文创园
rows.summary: A creative park in the former Liuzhou Air Compressor Works, a state factory founded in 1958 and listed as national industrial heritage in 2021. Its red-brick workshops now hold a cinema, an industrial experience hall, an art gallery, a theatre and studios, and the park was rated 4A in 2020.

rows.name: Que'er Hill Park
rows.summary: A park on a peninsula-shaped hill in Liubei District, surrounded by lakes on three sides, whose summit, about 180 m above sea level, looks out over the northern industrial district. Lakeside paths, flower gardens and a children's amusement area make it a weekend spot for local families.

rows.name: SAIC-GM-Wuling Baojun Base
rows.name_zh: 上汽通用五菱宝骏基地
rows.summary: The Baojun car plant of SAIC-GM-Wuling in the Liudong New Area, rated 4A in 2018 and opened for industrial tours in June 2019. Guided routes lead past production lines, a new-energy vehicle laboratory, a company history hall and an exhibition on electric, connected and self-driving cars, and there is a test-drive area.

rows.name: Sanjiang Great Dong Village (County Town)
rows.summary: The scenic area covering the modern Dong-style landmarks of Guyi, Sanjiang's county town, rated 4A in 2012. Its centrepiece is the Sanjiang Drum Tower, 42.6 m tall with 27 tiers of eaves, built in 2002 under the master carpenter Yang Siyu, with viewing decks inside, and the area also takes in the Sanjiang wind-and-rain bridge, the 'Dong Bird's Nest' bullfighting arena, a stele corridor on Dong history and Moon Street, a street of shops in Dong style.

rows.name: Sanjiangkou Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A riverside area at Laobao, where the Duliu (Rongjiang) and Xun rivers meet and become the Rong River, rated a 4A scenic area in 2023. It combines boat trips along the rivers, an old banyan grove at Chankou village, visits to Dong villages, and farming, camping and leisure activities on Yongxing islet.

rows.name: Shimen Fairy Lake
rows.summary: A karst scenic area of about 470 hectares around the Shimen reservoir in Daliang town, named after a huge natural stone gateway near its entrance. A glass walkway runs along the cliff, boardwalks lead through upper, middle and lower caves linked by an underground river, and boats continue from the lower cave onto the lake. Old cliff inscriptions and the ruins of an academy add some history.

rows.name: Shuanglong Gully Forest Resort
rows.summary: A forested valley north-west of Rongshui town with about 420 hectares of old-growth public-welfare forest, two streams, waterfalls and a small reservoir. Trails lead through the forest, and the resort adds a glass suspension bridge, zip lines and other adventure activities; the Mengwu Miao culture park lies within it.

rows.name: Xiancaotang Reishi Mushroom Factory
rows.name_zh: 仙草堂生态灵芝透明工厂
rows.summary: A see-through factory of the Guangxi Xiancaotang pharmaceutical company in Rong'an's county town, where visitors follow the growing and processing of lingzhi (reishi) mushrooms. It has smart greenhouses that imitate mountain-forest conditions, production halls open to view, a lingzhi science hall and a restaurant serving lingzhi dishes.

rows.name: Xianghe Xiangyun Lotus Fields
rows.summary: A farming and leisure area around Shixiang hamlet near Zhongdu, centred on about 67 hectares of lotus ponds among karst peaks, rated 4A in 2018. The lotus flowers in summer, when boardwalks lead across the ponds past waterwheels, and a cycling route links the fields with Zhongdu Old Town, the Xiangshui waterfall and the Xiangqiao karst geopark.

rows.name: Xiangqiao Karst National Geopark
rows.summary: A national geopark of karst scenery in Zhongdu town, with caves, underground rivers, a natural stone bridge and sinkholes among wooded limestone hills. The Jiulong (Nine Dragons) Cave lies at the end of a cycling route from Zhongdu Old Town past the Xiangshui waterfall and a stone forest.

rows.name: Yueye Dong Village
rows.summary: A purpose-built Dong-style leisure quarter of about 4.8 hectares in the centre of Sanjiang's county town, built and run by the state-owned Guangxi Tourism Development Group and rated 4A in 2020. Its main draw is Zuomei Sanjiang, an evening staged song-and-dance show about Dong courtship customs, alongside a night market, long-table banquets and buffalo fights held on holidays.

rows.name: Yufeng Hill (Liyufeng Scenic Area)
rows.summary: Two limestone hills rising from the city on the south bank of the Liu River: Yufeng Hill, about 156 m above sea level, and the taller Ma'an Hill. Yufeng Park is themed on the folk singer Liu Sanjie, who in legend sang here and rode a carp into the sky from the pool below, and a cave halfway up holds painted figures telling her story. From Ma'an Hill's summit there are views over the loop of the river and the whole city.

rows.name: Zhiqing Town (Educated Youth Town)
rows.summary: A theme village at Luoya on the Rong River, where more than 400 urban 'educated youth' were sent to live and farm during the Down to the Countryside Movement. The lane from the jetty to the village square is lined with houses painted with period slogans and murals and hung with old photographs, and the village has a museum on the movement.

rows.name: Zhongdu Old Town
rows.summary: A market town in north-western Luzhai county with nearly 2,000 years of history, listed as a national historic and cultural town. Its old quarter keeps Ming- and Qing-era houses, the Yuedong (Cantonese) guild hall, a Guandi temple whose restoration was completed in 2023, and a banyan-shaded river wharf. A cycling route leads on past lotus fields, the Xiangshui waterfall and a stone forest to the Xiangqiao karst geopark.

rows.name: Bagui Tianyuan Agricultural Park
rows.summary: A modern agriculture showcase set up in 1999 by the Guangxi Department of Agriculture on the training farm of the provincial agricultural school and now run under Guangxi Agricultural Vocational University. Greenhouses and demonstration plots show fruit, vegetables and flowers grown with modern methods, and it suits families and school groups interested in farming.

rows.name: Baiyi Shanghe City
rows.summary: A creative and leisure district in the red-brick workshops of the former Nanning silk-spinning mill, built in 1966, south of the Yong River in Jiangnan District, converted and opened in 2018. The old factory buildings now hold an industrial-history gallery, exhibition and performance spaces, craft shops of intangible-heritage makers, cafés, bars and restaurants, and the district is liveliest in the evening.

rows.name: China Jasmine Garden, Hengzhou
rows.summary: A jasmine park of variety gardens, a wetland lake and wide flower fields around Shijing village in Xiaoyi town, at the centre of Hengzhou's jasmine industry, which produces more than 80 per cent of China's jasmine flowers and jasmine tea. In the summer picking season visitors can walk the fields, watch growers picking the buds and try picking themselves, and the Shijing jasmine market nearby trades the day's flowers.

rows.name: Dalong Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake in the karst hills of Xiyan town in northern Shanglin County, formed in 1958 by damming underground water, which now covers about 560 hectares with 14 small islands and 16 caves. Boat trips on the lake pass limestone peaks nicknamed Lotus, Penguin and Peacock hills, and visitors can also go into Dalong Cave on the shore.

rows.name: Damiaojiang Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: An outdoor recreation area of about 630 hectares at the foot of the Daming Mountains nature reserve in Shanglin County, built around a forest rafting run on the Damiao River. Besides the rafting it has stream walks to waterfalls, a wetland park, a wisteria walk lined with windmills and a children's play area, and it suits families looking for a summer day in the hills.

rows.name: Daming Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain range in central Guangxi, about 68 km long and spanning Wuming, Shanglin, Mashan and Binyang, whose main peak, Longtou Shan, reaches 1,760 m, the highest in central-southern Guangxi, and which the Tropic of Cancer crosses. Most of it is a national nature reserve of about 17,000 hectares with almost complete forest cover, and the scenic area, entered from Liangjiang town on the Wuming side, lies at an average altitude of about 1,200 m.

rows.name: Dingsishan Neolithic Site
rows.summary: A freshwater shell-midden site on a terrace where the Bachi River meets a stream, lived on from about 10,000 to 6,000 years ago and excavated between 1997 and 2000, when 331 burials, many of them tightly flexed, were found; it gave its name to the Dingsishan culture, the first Neolithic culture defined in Guangxi. A site park and a shell-shaped museum with about 1,300 m² of galleries and more than 200 artefacts opened with the neighbouring Garden Expo Park in 2018, inside a 4A countryside area of farmland, fruit picking and campsites.

rows.name: Dream Town (Mengxiangcheng)
rows.summary: A modern resort area built in imitation of the Austrian lakeside village of Hallstatt, set by a lake among karst peaks near Yiling Cave in Shuangqiao town. Its European-style streets and lakeside buildings serve mainly as a large wedding and wedding-photography base, so it suits photographers and couples rather than visitors looking for history.

rows.name: Fengling Children's Park
rows.summary: A children's park of about 56 hectares laid out over hilly ground in the Fengling district of eastern Nanning, opened on 1 June 2012. It has an amusement park of themed zones with rides, including roller coasters and a Ferris wheel, a summer water park and grassy slopes for play, and suits families with children.

rows.name: Flower World of Nanning
rows.summary: A flower-themed leisure park of about 113 hectares in Shuangqiao town, Wuming, with seasonal flower fields, bougainvillea gardens, a large lawn, lotus ponds crossed by a Zhuang-style covered bridge and a hilltop walkway with a glass section. A European-style chapel on a patch of artificial white sand is used for weddings and photo shoots, and festival events such as Spring Festival fireworks and lion dances are staged for families.

rows.name: Former Nanning Yucai School
rows.summary: The Nanning Yucai School was set up in October 1951 at Ho Chi Minh's request to train Vietnamese cadres, teachers and young people under the Vietnamese name Khu Học Xá Trung Ương; Vietnamese staff ran it and taught mostly in Vietnamese, with Chinese support, and about 7,000 students passed through it in seven years. The listed building is a Qing-dynasty clan ancestral hall in Hede village, Xinxu, where the school began. In 1954 the school moved to a new campus, now Guangxi University's west campus, where a statue of Ho Chi Minh with children and a photo exhibition on the school stand.

rows.name: Fubo Temple, Hengzhou
rows.summary: A temple to Ma Yuan, the Eastern Han general titled the Fubo ('Wave-Subduing') General, on the north bank of the Yu River at the Wuman Rapids, which tradition says his troops cleared for boats during his southern campaign. Founded before the Song dynasty and rebuilt many times, it is the largest temple to Ma Yuan in southern Guangxi, laid out around three courtyards with bell and drum towers, an archway, a covered gallery and front, middle and rear halls. Parts were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and the restoration was completed in 2008.

rows.name: Golden Camellia Park
rows.summary: A city park on the west side of Nanhu Lake devoted to golden camellias, rare yellow-flowered camellias under national protection, with a gene bank that collects and studies many kinds of them alongside other camellias and tea plants. The bushes flower from November to April, at their best in January and February, and a small science hall explains the plants.

rows.name: Guangxi Botanical Garden of Medicinal Plants
rows.summary: A research botanical garden founded in 1959 on 202 hectares of low hills on the north-eastern edge of Nanning, which conserves more than 10,000 species of medicinal plants and was certified by Guinness World Records in 2011 as the largest medicinal botanical garden. Themed areas cover Guangxi's own medicinal plants, trees, climbers, shade plants, the ginger family, tropical plants and medicinal animals, and it serves as a teaching base for traditional Chinese medicine.

rows.name: Guangxi Gaofeng Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park run by the state-owned Gaofeng Forest Farm in the hills on Nanning's northern edge, with a core area of about 1,200 hectares and around 90 per cent forest cover. Its attractions include a glass bridge, forest go-karts, a viewing platform over the city, a water slide and children's play areas, as well as a China–Vietnam Friendship Forest grown from Manglietia seeds that Ho Chi Minh gave to Zhou Enlai in the 1960s.

rows.name: Guangxi Museum of Nationalities
rows.summary: A museum of the cultures of Guangxi's 12 long-established ethnic groups beside the Yong River within the Qingxiu Mountain scenic area, completed in December 2008 and opened to the public in May 2009, in a main building whose shape is taken from a bronze drum. Its four permanent exhibitions cover bronze drums, the ethnic cultures of Guangxi, Zhuang culture and everyday objects of the past century, and an open-air park shows traditional houses of different groups.

rows.name: Guangxi Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: A large exhibition hall in the Wuxiang New Area, opened on 8 November 2011, presenting Guangxi's development and its urban and regional planning in about 46,000 m² of floor space. Its three floors of galleries include a digital display centre, halls on Guangxi's landscapes and on cooperation with ASEAN, and a gallery of gifts of friendship, and it suits visitors curious about modern Guangxi.

rows.name: Guangxi Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: Guangxi's main science museum, founded in 1983 and moved into a new building near Minzu Square in December 2008, with about 9,000 m² of permanent exhibitions on engineering, information technology and bioengineering. There are also temporary exhibitions, a youth science studio and special-format cinemas, and the building's design draws on Elephant Trunk Hill, Yangshuo's Moon Hill, oyster shells and bronze drums.

rows.name: Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Museum
rows.name_zh: 广西壮族自治区博物馆
rows.summary: Guangxi's main history museum, founded in 1934 and a national first-grade museum, which reopened on Minzu Square in November 2022 after more than four years of rebuilding that doubled its floor space and enlarged its galleries to about 10,000 m². Its largest gallery traces Guangxi's history from Palaeolithic hand axes 800,000 years old to the Ming and Qing dynasties, with bronze drums such as the Western Han drum with flying egrets from Luobowan, and other halls show porcelain and a dragon carriage given by the Sultan of Brunei.

rows.name: Gula Daohuaxiangli (Cai Family Mansion)
rows.summary: A rural scenic area of about 72 hectares in Cai village near Gula town, built around the Cai family's old residential compound of more than 180 rooms, whose halls, courtyards and corner watchtowers date from rebuilding after 1859 in the late Qing dynasty. The village is surrounded by water on three sides and by rice fields, and since it opened as a scenic area in October 2019 it has combined the old houses with farmland views and farm-stay restaurants.

rows.name: Gumingzhai Zhuang Village
rows.summary: Guminzhuang, a Zhuang village developed as the Gumingzhai scenic area, lies beside a lake with small islands in a valley ringed by hills and has 158 rammed-earth houses, most of them built in the Qing and Republican periods. The houses have rough-stone bases, yellow-earth walls and grey-tiled roofs, many arranged as a central ancestral hall between two wings around a small courtyard, and the county describes the village as the largest and best-preserved of its kind in Guangxi. It suits a quiet walk among old houses with the lake and hills around them.

rows.name: Jiangnan Park, Nanning
rows.summary: A large city park south of the Yong River in Jiangnan District, opened in June 2018 and laid out around linked lakes with Wenfeng Hill as a backdrop. Lawns, flowering trees, covered walkways and pavilions in old Chinese style surround the water, and a square at the west gate has a sculpture decorated with Zhuang motifs such as bronze drums and brocade.

rows.name: Jiulong Waterfalls National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the state-owned Zhenlong forest farm in the hills of northern Hengzhou, where streams drop through a cluster of waterfalls in tall forest below Jiulong Mountain. Within about 2.5 km² there are more than ten falls, many around 30 m high, spaced 100–300 m apart along forest paths.

rows.name: Jiuquwan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Santang town on the north-eastern edge of Nanning, open since November 2005, with indoor and outdoor thermal pools and décor drawing on Zhuang and other ethnic cultures. It also has a water park with nearly 6,000 m² of pools under a large shade roof, plus a hotel and restaurants, and suits a relaxing half-day out of the city.

rows.name: Kunlun Pass
rows.summary: A mountain pass on the old road between Nanning and Liuzhou, first walled with stone in 816 and best known as the site of the Battle of Kunlun Pass in December 1939, when Chinese troops of the Fifth Army retook the pass from the Japanese army after about two weeks of fighting with heavy casualties on both sides. From the memorial archway 331 steps climb to a 14.74 m memorial tower and the cemetery of the fallen, beside a pavilion carrying an inscribed account of the battle.
