A museum on the site displays weapons, helmets, photographs and film about the battle.

rows.name: Liangfengjiang National Forest Park
rows.summary: One of the earliest national forest parks approved by China's former Ministry of Forestry, on the south-western outskirts of Nanning along the Liangfeng River. It has a large plant garden with a wide collection of trees, a cultural garden containing Tianning Temple of the Guangxi Buddhist Association, and a small amusement area.

rows.name: Longhu Mountain
rows.summary: A nature reserve of forested limestone hills in Pingshan township, Long'an County, known as one of China's 'four great monkey mountains' for its more than 3,000 wild rhesus macaques. Besides watching the monkeys, visitors can walk in forest that shelters more than 1,200 plant species and over 200 kinds of wild animals, and take part in water activities.

rows.name: Longmen Shuidu
rows.summary: A leisure resort in forested hills around Longmen Reservoir on the north-western edge of Nanning, about 15 km from the city centre. It combines hot-spring and herbal-bath pools, a summer water park and a long glass suspension bridge with walking paths and themed gardens, and suits families on a day out from the city.

rows.name: Minge Lake
rows.summary: A landscaped lake park beside the Nanning International Convention and Exhibition Centre in Qingxiu District, with lakeside promenades, bars and restaurants, evening lights and sightseeing boats. It makes an easy evening stroll from the convention centre.

rows.name: Mingshan Eco-Tourism Area
rows.summary: A hill area in Chenping town in southern Binyang County, made up of three peaks whose highest, Mingshan Top, rises to 876 m, the second-highest point in the county, above plum orchards and villages. Promoted as a 'Lingnan plum village', it has a visitor centre and viewing platforms, and visitors come to climb the peak and walk among the plum trees, especially in the blossom season.

rows.name: Nanguo Countryside
rows.summary: A rural tourism area in Nagong hamlet, Sugong village, Shuangqiao town, built around a museum of rural house building that presents the village architecture of different ethnic groups alongside new building methods. Around it are an expo garden of model new farmhouses, a farm and homestays, and it suits a countryside half-day with children or a group.

rows.name: Nanning Culture, Tourism and Art Park
rows.summary: A 4A area created in 2023 by grouping four sites run by the Guangxi Tourism Group in the Wuxiang area south of the Yong River: the 'Guanglü Nanning Night' evening leisure district, the Guangxi Art Museum, Central Park and the 'Yunduoduo' young artists' camp. Together they combine night-time strolling and entertainment with art exhibitions and park space, and suit an evening out more than a sightseeing visit.

rows.name: Nanning Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: The 263-hectare site of the 12th China International Garden Expo, opened in December 2018 beside the Bachi River in Yongning District on the south-eastern edge of Nanning. Gardens built by Chinese cities and ASEAN countries spread around its lakes, among them the China–ASEAN Friendship Pavilion linking ten national pavilions and an ASEAN Garden with Cambodian, Lao and Philippine sections, and seasonal flower and grass fields draw crowds in autumn.

rows.name: Nanning International Convention and Exhibition Centre
rows.summary: The hillside convention centre on Minzu Avenue that is the permanent venue of the annual China–ASEAN Expo and one of Nanning's landmark buildings, whose 41-hectare grounds were rated a 4A scenic area in 2021. Displays and landscaping themed on the expo's history and on the cultures of China and the ten ASEAN countries make it a sightseeing stop between trade fairs, and it looks across to Minge Lake.

rows.name: Nanning Polar Ocean World
rows.summary: A large indoor aquarium in the Rongsheng Tianhe Haiyue City shopping complex in Jiangnan District, laid out in themed halls on ocean legends, the polar regions and marine life, with an animal-petting area for children. Its animals include sea lions, seals, penguins and many kinds of fish, and staged shows such as a sea-lion show and an underwater show are part of the programme, so it is mainly a family outing.

rows.name: Nanning Wanda Mall
rows.summary: A large indoor shopping and entertainment complex opened in June 2017 in the Wuxiang New Area south of the Yong River, rated 4A in 2018 for its indoor attractions. Its former indoor theme park has been converted into an indoor ski centre, opened in July 2026, which is kept at −5 °C all year and has three ski runs, a snow-play area and a training centre, alongside the mall's shops and restaurants.

rows.name: Nanning Zoo
rows.summary: Nanning's city zoo, opened in April 1975 among about 37 hectares of subtropical gardens on University East Road in the north-west of the city. Around 30 exhibit areas house animals such as Asian elephants, gibbons, golden snub-nosed monkeys, tigers and lions, and staged animal shows, including a sea-lion show, are part of the programme, alongside two funfair areas with rides.

rows.name: Nongla Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hamlet in the karst peak-cluster hills of Guling town, Mashan County, whose villagers replanted the limestone hills around it after they were stripped of trees in the 1950s, and which is often cited as a model for reversing rocky desertification. The surrounding Nongla nature reserve protects limestone forest, and the scenic area has an exhibition hall on desertification control, a Buddhist temple and paths past oddly shaped peaks and rocks.

rows.name: People's Park, Nanning
rows.summary: A city park in central Nanning, also called White Dragon Park after its 7-hectare White Dragon Lake, which has a small island reached by two bridges. Stone steps climb Wangxian Hill, the highest point in downtown Nanning, to the Zhenning Fort, built in 1917 by the Guangxi warlord Lu Rongting on the site of an old temple and still holding its German Krupp gun. The park also has a shady botanical garden with an old banyan and a 25 m Monument to Revolutionary Martyrs.

rows.name: Pujin Park
rows.summary: An open park laid out over three limestone hills, Jinzhen, Yinzhen and Gong'e, in the middle of Pumiao, the seat of Yongning District. It serves mainly as a place for residents' walks and exercise, and suits a short stroll for visitors passing through Pumiao.

rows.name: Qingxiu Mountain
rows.summary: A hilly park of 18 low ridges on the north bank of the Yong River in south-eastern Nanning, developed from a former forest farm since 1984, whose highest point rises to 289 m. Its themed gardens include a cycad garden with about a hundred plants more than 1,000 years old, a large orchid garden, a rainforest garden and the China–ASEAN Friendship Garden, linked by a covered Friendship Corridor in the style of Dong wind-and-rain bridges. Paths also lead to the Guanyin Chan Temple, founded in the Northern Song, and the Ming-style Longxiang Pagoda, built in 1986 on the summit.

rows.name: Scenic Yong River and Ancient Yongzhou
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area of about 1.5 km² along the Yong River in central Nanning, from Yangguan Wharf to Lingtie Bridge, rated 4A in 2020, with sculptures on the city's history and legends, the Changyou Pavilion, arcades and remains of old city walls along the bank. Its core is the 'Ancient Yongzhou' evening cruise from Minsheng Wharf past the floodlit bridges and banks, with stories of Nanning's history told on board.

rows.name: Shouchuang Children's Park
rows.summary: A children's play park attached to the Shouchuang (Capital) Outlets mall on Kunlun Avenue in north-eastern Nanning, rated 4A in November 2023. Its main draw is a large playground of non-motorised play equipment, with other play, sports and learning activities for children, so it suits families with young children rather than adult travellers.

rows.name: Shuijin Shunzhuang Scenic Area
rows.summary: A canyon resort area in Leping village, Guling town, ringed by the Daming Mountains, where the Shuijin stream runs through a natural gorge about 10 km long with waterfalls, spring pools and cascades. Walkways lead through the gorge to attractions such as a glass bridge and slides, and the area also has a farming display zone and a themed resort hotel.

rows.name: Wuxiang Lake Park
rows.summary: A 122-hectare park around five linked lakes in the Wuxiang New Area south of the Yong River, opened in August 2013 as the site of the third Guangxi Garden and Horticulture Expo. Paths lead past themed gardens on Guangxi's regions and Zhuang culture, and the park borders the Guangxi Planning Exhibition Hall and the Guangxi Art Museum.

rows.name: Xiangxieli Nanguo Hot Spring Valley
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in the Jiahe City development on Kunlun Avenue in north-eastern Nanning, next to a golf course, also known as the Jiahe City Hot Spring Valley. Its main draw is a large complex of outdoor thermal pools, several themed on bathing traditions of different countries, together with a water park and on-site accommodation, and during the annual China–ASEAN Expo it has served as a reception venue for visiting delegations.

rows.name: Xiaodubai Village
rows.summary: A rural tourism village in Qiaolao village, Guling town, beside the Mashan–Shanglin road, rebuilt with white-walled, grey-tiled houses in local Zhuang style and known as the 'home of waterwheels' for the wheels along its streams. Visitors come for farm-stay meals and lodging, seasonal fruit and vegetable picking, flower fields, cycling and the waterwheel landscape, and it makes a stop on the way to Nongla.

rows.name: Yiling Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave in Yiling village, Shuangqiao town, about 25 km north of central Nanning, whose Zhuang name means 'a cave as beautiful as a palace', with a 1,100 m route through 24,000 m² of chambers full of stalactites, stalagmites, columns and flowstone. Outside, a Zhuang culture garden displays old farm tools, stone implements and handwoven Zhuang clothing, alongside poem tablets by visitors such as Guo Moruo and a children's play area.

rows.name: Yongzhou Old Town (Sanjie Liangxiang)
rows.summary: The old commercial heart of Nanning near the Yong River, centred on the Sanjie Liangxiang historic district of three old streets (Xingning, Minsheng and Jiefang roads) and two Ming–Qing lanes (Jinshi and Yinshi), whose history goes back to the Song dynasty. Restored and reopened as a pedestrian district in 2018, it has more than 20 protected buildings and sites, including the City God Temple, the Deng Yingchao Memorial Hall, the Xinhui and Lianghu guild halls and Republican-era arcaded shophouses, now filled with cafés, bookshops and snack stalls. Since 2025 it has been promoted together with the neighbouring Zhongshan Road food street and Shuijie as Yongzhou Old Town, and it is busiest in the evening.

rows.name: Zhicheng Tang City Site
rows.summary: Remains of Zhicheng, a fortified seat of local chiefs under the Tang dynasty, in a narrow valley in Shanglin County where steep hillsides serve as ramparts and stretches of wall close the valley mouth and divide it into an inner and an outer town. On a cliff in the outer town is the Zhicheng Stele of 697, and in a cave about 4.5 km away is the Liuhe Jiangu Dazhai Song inscription of 682, both composed by the local chief Wei Jingban and among the earliest surviving inscriptions to use Sawndip, the old Zhuang characters.

rows.name: Bazhaigou
rows.summary: A forested valley on the northern flank of the Shiwan Mountains in Guitai town, where a spring-fed gorge of about 16 km runs through subtropical forest with streams, pools and waterfalls. Hiking and wading along the streams are the main draw.

rows.name: Beibu Gulf Flower Park
rows.summary: A flower park in Shabu town east of Qinzhou, with fields of cockscomb in autumn and spring plantings such as snapdragons, cosmos and strawflowers. It also hosts nature-study visits and floral-art activities.

rows.name: Dalu Village
rows.summary: A village of Ming and Qing mansions in Fozi town, nine building groups put up by the Lao family between 1546 and 1826 among ponds and old trees. It is known for its 'three olds' of old houses, old trees and old couplets, with Qing-era name boards and couplets still hanging in the halls, and villagers stage caicha tea-picking opera and tiaolingtou dances in the slack farming season.

rows.name: Former Residences of Liu Yongfu and Feng Zicai
rows.summary: The mansions of two Qing generals from the old Qinzhou region who fought the French in the Sino-French War, protected nationally since 2001 and rated 4A together in 2006. Liu Yongfu's Sanxuan Tang of 1891, in the old town, has 119 rooms behind 4 m walls, halls with gilded murals and woodcarving, and exhibitions on the war and his Black Flag Army. Feng Zicai's Gongbao Di of 1875, about 4 km north at Baishuitang, is a three-row, nine-building compound from which he set out for the 1885 victory at Zhennan Pass.

rows.name: Linhu Forest Park
rows.summary: A provincial-level forest park on the southern edge of Qinbei district, about 3 km from central Qinzhou, laid out for walking among wooded hills and lakes. It is a popular suburban green space with nature-education and outdoor-activity areas, and was rated 4A in 2017.

rows.name: Liufeng Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded hill rising 182 m above the Mingke River in the centre of Lingshan town, named after its six peaks and admired as a beauty spot since the Song dynasty; it was rated 4A in 2017 and was a filming location for the TV series The Bad Kids. Paths climb past temples and Taoist halls such as the Beidi Temple, Guanyin Pavilion and Sanqing Palace, and Sanhai Cave on the west side holds more than 150 inscriptions carved over the centuries.

rows.name: Nawu Mountain Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 230 hectares on Nawu Mountain in Nali town, rated 4A in 2019, within a regional geopark. From the glass walkway and glass bridge near the summit visitors look out over seas of cloud, wind turbines and, on clear days, the Beibu Gulf.

rows.name: Qinzhou Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A park of about 80 hectares in Qinzhou's eastern new town, built for the 9th Guangxi Garden Expo, which opened here on 2 December 2016 on the theme of coastal scenery and Nixing pottery. Fourteen gardens named after Guangxi's cities are spread among hills and water, with the Qinzhou garden at the centre, an ASEAN garden and a Nixing pottery museum, next to the Nixing pottery creative-industry park.

rows.name: Qinzhou Old Street
rows.summary: Qinzhou's historic district of qilou arcade buildings along Zhongshan Road and the neighbouring streets of the old town, a short walk from Liu Yongfu's former residence. Visitors come for snack stalls serving local dishes such as pig's-trotter rice noodles, the Qinzhou Bookstore and street performances of caicha opera, and in September 2026 the three-storey 33 Canal Bookstore opened in an arcade building on Renmin South Road.

rows.name: Sanniang Bay
rows.summary: A curving bay of beaches, rocks, fishing villages and coastal woodland in Xiniujiao town, known as the home of the Chinese white dolphin (Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin), seen offshore in numbers since 2003. Boats take visitors out to look for the dolphins, and the bay also has a bathing beach, a dolphin science museum, seafood restaurants and shores where visitors dig for sandworms and gather shellfish at low tide.

rows.name: Shenfu Liquor Estate
rows.summary: An industrial-tourism site of about 11 hectares at the Shenfu liquor works on the northern edge of Pubei town, home of Shenfu jiu, a liquor made with ants that was already well known in the 1980s and whose making is listed as Qinzhou city-level intangible heritage. Opened in 2020 and rated 4A in 2021, it combines a liquor museum and old brick workshops with a water park, a Ferris wheel, an 'Ant Kingdom' play area and a greenway.

rows.name: Wuhuang Mountain
rows.summary: A granite upland of about 40 km² around Longmen town, with nine main peaks averaging some 700 m and topped by Qingshanding at 778.8 m, known for fields of egg-shaped boulders, high meadows, tea gardens, terraces, streams and waterfalls. It is divided into the Rentoushi, Meizhuizhai and Shizhuling areas, and visitors come for sunrise, seas of cloud and the wind turbines on the ridges.

rows.name: Canghai Lake & Wuzhou Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A large landscaped lake in the new Canghai district on the south bank of the Xi River, built to hold back floodwater and now the centre of Canghai National Wetland Park, with gardens, paths and footbridges around the shore over about 215 ha. Within it the Wuzhou Garden Expo Park shows gardens in the styles of cities across Guangxi. It is a pleasant place for a walk, especially early in the morning or at sunset.

rows.name: Changping Yao Village
rows.summary: Changping village in the Changping Yao Ethnic Township, in forested mountains in the north-east of Mengshan County, where a spring-fed stream runs through a Yao village surrounded by woodland. It has been developed for rural tourism, with a wind-and-rain bridge, a heart-shaped peach-blossom island, wooden cabins and farm restaurants serving Yao dishes, and was named one of Guangxi's key rural-tourism villages in 2022. It suits a quiet countryside stay rather than a heritage visit.

rows.name: Dongshan Culture Park, Cenxi
rows.summary: A hillside park on the edge of Cenxi city, laid out over a whole hill for exercise and recreation, with stone stairways, pavilions, a rock garden, a Confucius temple, a tea house and Dongshan Pavilion at the top. It is divided into themed sections on old customs, honest government, filial piety and Confucian learning. It is mainly a local park, worth a stroll if you are passing through Cenxi.

rows.name: Former Residence of Li Jishen
rows.summary: The fortified family house in Liaoshen village where Li Jishen (1885–1959) was born: a Kuomintang general who later chaired the Revolutionary Committee of the Kuomintang and was a vice-chairman of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic from 1949. The present house, built in 1925, is a brick-and-timber courtyard compound with 53 rooms and gun towers at its four corners, linked by a walkway along the roof. Upstairs, his bedroom, reception room and telegraph room keep their period furnishings, and an old ironwood grove stands behind the house.

rows.name: Former Sites of the CPC Wuzhou and Guangxi Committees
rows.name_zh: 中共梧州地委·广西特委旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Wúzhōu Dìwěi · Guǎngxī Tèwěi Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Two small brick-and-timber houses in Wuzhou's arcade quarter linked to the Communist Party's early years in Guangxi. A three-storey house on Xingren Lane off Jianshe Road held the party's Wuzhou committee, set up in 1925 as its first regional organisation in Guangxi, and a four-storey house of 1925 in Weixinli off Minzhu Road was used by the Guangxi Special Committee after it moved back to Wuzhou in 1928. An exhibition hall beside the first house covers the party's activity in Guangxi in the 1920s.

rows.name: Liang Yusheng Park
rows.summary: A hilltop park in the south-east of Mengshan town, formerly Aoshan Park, turned in 2005 into a park named after Liang Yusheng (Chen Wentong, 1924–2009), born in Mengshan County and, with Jin Yong and Gu Long, one of the best-known wuxia (martial-arts) novelists of the 20th century; Jin Yong wrote the name over the gate. Its landmark is the five-storey hexagonal Aoshan Pagoda, first built in 1762 and rebuilt in 1985, whose door couplet Liang wrote on a visit home in 1987. The small Yong'an Temple stands at the foot of the hill, and the view at sunset from the pagoda is one of Mengshan's traditional eight scenes.

rows.name: Lingnan Culture Park, Wuzhou
rows.summary: A large complex of new Ming-style buildings beside the Dragon Mother Temple, covering about 6 ha and rated 4A in 2024, themed on the office of the Viceroy of Liangguang, which the Ming court set up in Wuzhou in 1469 to govern Guangdong and Guangxi; the philosopher Wang Yangming later served here as viceroy. Inside are exhibition spaces on the culture of the Lingnan region, with bronze drums among the artefacts on show, and stages for folk performances. It is a modern reconstruction rather than a surviving building, and it is easily combined with a walk through the arcade quarter.

rows.name: Liubao Tea Town
rows.summary: A mountain town in Cangwu County that gives its name to Liubao tea, a dark (post-fermented) tea known for its betel-nut aroma, ranked among China's famous teas in the Qing dynasty; its making is a national intangible-heritage item. The scenic area covers the town's memorial arch, tea industrial park, tea gardens and tea street, and the old Hekou wharf with its great camphor tree, start of the 'tea-boat route' by which Liubao tea was shipped downriver and overseas. Visitors can walk the gardens, buy tea at source and, at times, watch or try tea-making.

rows.name: Rose Lake Park, Wuzhou
rows.summary: A lakeside park in Longxin village on the western side of Wuzhou, facing Changzhou Island across the river, built around a lake that was created in 1976 when a levee turned low-lying fields into a fish farm. From 1992 the lake and Changzhou Island were developed together as a countryside recreation area, and it is now a city park crossed by Sanlong Avenue. It is mainly of interest to local walkers and families.

rows.name: Shibiao Mountain
rows.summary: A red-sandstone (danxia) landscape in Xiangqi town in the south of Teng County, about 16 km² of red cliffs and peaks above a river with sandbanks, bamboo groves and the old village of Daojia. The scenic area includes rafting on the Siluo River, the Shibiao mountain stockade, the Shilong Canyon, Daojia village and a beach park.

rows.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall & Zhongshan Park, Wuzhou
rows.summary: Wuzhou's oldest park, laid out on a hill above the old town in 1924 when the city wall was pulled down, and renamed Zhongshan Park in October 1930 when its memorial hall to Sun Yat-sen was completed. Sun stayed in Wuzhou three times in 1921–22 while preparing the Northern Expedition, and the white hall, which combines a Chinese palace-style front with a domed tower and a 1,000-seat auditorium, displays photographs and objects on his life and his visits to the city. The park also has gardens, a bamboo grove on the back slope and a memorial hall to the revolutionary Wei Baqun.

rows.name: Tianlongding Mountain Park
rows.summary: A mountain park in Nandu town in the south of Cenxi, around Tianlongding, at 1,211 m the highest peak in Wuzhou prefecture, known for its grassy summit meadows and for seas of cloud that form at a relatively low altitude. Trails lead past a mountain lake, streams and waterfalls, and the park caters for hiking, camping and mountain biking, with farm restaurants nearby.

rows.name: Tianshu Xiagu (Heavenly Book Gorge)
rows.summary: A wooded gorge about 5 km east of Mengshan town, also called Yumengchong, winding for more than 10 km past clear pools and oddly shaped rocks. It takes its name from a huge character for 'heaven' at the mouth of the valley and a rock in a pool said to look like a book of heavenly scripts. Spots along the trail are themed on Liang Yusheng's martial-arts novels, such as Fairy Pool, Sword-Washing Pool and a 'Golden Sabre' stockade.

rows.name: White Cloud Mountain (Baiyun Shan), Wuzhou
rows.summary: A forested hill park on the north-east edge of Wuzhou's old town, opened in 1981, covering about 355 ha over two summits and rising to 367 m, the highest point in urban Wuzhou. A 3.7 km road climbs from the Bingquan soy-milk house at the foot to the Yunfeng Pavilion on the top, with views over the city and the meeting of its rivers, passing Si'en Temple halfway up. On the eastern slope the Longquan valley has rocks, a waterfall and shaded paths.

rows.name: Wuzhou Arcade Town & Dragon Mother Temple
rows.summary: Wuzhou's old riverside trading quarter: 22 streets, about 7 km in all, lined with some 560 arcaded shophouses (qilou), most built after the city wall was demolished in the 1920s, mixing Chinese carved brick and lattice windows with Western balconies, columns and arched windows, with iron rings on the pillars and upper-floor 'water doors' for mooring boats when the rivers flood. Among them stand the protected treaty-port buildings of the late Qing and Republican years, after Wuzhou was opened to foreign trade in 1897, including the old customs house, the Standard Oil office, the Xinxi Hotel, the post office, the Catholic church and the former British consulate on Zhushan hill. At the quarter's north end, on the east bank of the Gui River, the Dragon Mother Temple, founded in the early Northern Song and rebuilt in the Ming and Qing, honours the river goddess Longmu and draws pilgrims from Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau on her festival days.

rows.name: Yong'an Royal City (Taiping Heavenly Kingdom Sites), Mengshan
rows.summary: Mengshan, then called Yong'an, was captured by the Taiping rebels in the autumn of 1851, and it was here that their leader Hong Xiuquan issued edicts, named his kings and set up the rebel state's first institutions. The protected sites in the town centre are the Wu Temple to Guan Yu, since rebuilt, a stretch of the old town wall and the spot where the edicts were issued, beside a magnolia tree more than 500 years old, with a corridor of edict steles. The scenic area wraps these into a riverside park, an old-banyan park and themed shopping streets along the Meijiang River.

rows.name: Darongshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A 4,825-hectare national forest park on Darong Mountain north of Beiliu, whose 1,275 m summit is the highest point in Yulin prefecture. Trails and stream-trekking routes run through subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest to the Nine Waterfalls Valley and a mountain lake, Tianhu.

rows.name: Duqiao Mountain
rows.summary: A red-sandstone (Danxia) mountain south-east of Rong County town, a Taoist retreat since the Han dynasty and counted as the 20th Taoist grotto-heaven. A cableway climbs to the North Grotto-Heaven and Suopo Rock, where calligraphy by Su Dongpo survives and a statue of him stands, and trails link temples, cliff caves and viewpoints; the Ming traveller Xu Xiake spent several days here and wrote a long account of it.

rows.name: Goulou Cave
rows.summary: Four linked limestone caves, Baogui, Yuque, Baisha and Taoyuan, about 1 km long in all, at the foot of Goulou Hill 3 km north-east of Beiliu; old Taoist texts list the site as the 22nd of the 36 grotto-heavens. The lit caves hold stalactites, columns and flowstone, the rock walls inside and out carry more than 120 inscriptions from the Tang dynasty on, and tradition says the Jin-dynasty alchemist Ge Hong sought the post of Goulou magistrate to practise here.

rows.name: Guiling Valley
rows.summary: A hillside eco-park in Shapo town whose main sight is a wall climbing the crest of Bazi Ridge, promoted as the 'little Great Wall of the south'. A 500 m elevated steel walkway with a bell platform links to the wall and looks over the Xiexian range, and there are zip lines, go-karts and a children's play area.

rows.name: Kelawan Water Park
rows.summary: An outdoor water park on the riverside Jiangbin East Road in Yulin, with a large wave pool, a water fortress and a lazy river. It is aimed at local families on hot summer days.

rows.name: Liuwan Mountains Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the Liuwan Mountains, a range about 70 km long on the borders of Yulin, Bobai and Pubei whose main peak, Kuishanding, reaches 1,118 m. Facilities include a lookout platform on Lianhua Peak, a forest music square and a campsite.

rows.name: Republican-era Villas of Rong County
rows.summary: Eleven buildings from the late Qing and Republican periods spread across Rong County, mostly villas and family homes of Republican-era generals and officials from the county, such as Huang Shaohong and Huang Xuchu, together with the old library and old teaching building of Rong County Middle School. Several stand in the county town, including Huang Shaohong's three-storey villa of 1927 on South Street and Huang Xuchu's two-storey villa of 1933; others are in villages and townships, two of them inside township government compounds.

rows.name: Sanhuan Ceramics Town, Beiliu
rows.summary: An industrial and visitor complex built by Guangxi Sanhuan, one of China's leading makers of everyday porcelain, in Beiliu, a pottery centre since the Song dynasty. Its ceramics museum traces Chinese and local ceramics from early dynasties to the present, and the company's showroom displays the tableware it exports to more than 80 countries. It suits travellers with an interest in ceramics.

rows.name: South-east Guangxi Anti-Japanese Uprising Sites, Xingye
rows.name_zh: 桂东南抗日武装起义旧址
rows.summary: A group of village sites in Chenghuang town linked to the armed uprising against Japanese forces launched here in March 1945. The centrepiece is the Zhensheng Building, a brick-and-timber house in mixed Chinese and Western style built in 1912–14, which served as headquarters of the county's anti-Japanese self-defence army; on nearby Gongyan Ridge some 2,000 fighters and villagers held a rally on 3 March 1945 to launch the uprising.

rows.name: Tongshiling Resort
rows.summary: A hill resort on Tongshiling, east of Beiliu, where karst limestone and red Danxia sandstone cliffs occur side by side and where copper was smelted and bronze drums cast in the Han dynasty. A statue group of Zhao Tuo, the ancient king of Nanyue, stands before the gate tower, and a 10 km route of walkways, a glass skywalk and summit rides such as slides, grass and dry-snow sledging and go-karts climbs the hill. It suits families and active travellers more than heritage seekers.

rows.name: Wucai Tianyuan Agricultural Park
rows.summary: A modern farming demonstration zone on the eastern edge of Yulin, laid out as a rural park with seasonal flower fields, lotus ponds and a cherry garden. Rapeseed blooms in early spring and lotus from mid-May into August draw local visitors for walks, photos and cycling.

rows.name: Xielu Villa
rows.summary: A private garden estate laid out on a hillside at Xielu village from about 1920, often called one of China's four great private manors. Its pavilions, halls, ponds and paths spread over about 26 hectares, following the model of Suzhou and Hangzhou gardens while mixing Hakka and Western architectural details.

rows.name: Yuntian Cultural City
rows.summary: A large palace-style building complex on Jiangbin Road in Yulin, opened as a cultural attraction with halls of sculpture, a folk-culture museum and displays of collected treasures. Many visitors come mainly for the imposing exterior, and the forecourt hosts lion dances and martial-arts shows at festivals such as New Year.

rows.name: Zhenwu Pavilion & Rongzhou Old Town
rows.summary: The three-storey timber Zhenwu Pavilion was built in 1573 on the Jinglüe Terrace by the Xiu River, a platform said to date from the Tang dynasty, when the poet-official Yuan Jie drilled troops here. Its lever-like bracketing joins nearly 3,000 timber pieces without nails, and four inner columns on the second floor hang about 2 cm clear of the floor. Around it the former People's Park was rebuilt in 2014–16 as Rongzhou Old Town, a 25-hectare scenic area with a reconstructed prefectural hall, a museum, Kaiyuan Temple, an old-style shopping street and boat landings on Xiujiang Lake.

rows.name: Hongshui River Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest-park area in the south of Donglan County, in the middle reaches of the Hongshui River, that groups a regional-level forest park, Pohao Lake National Wetland Park and the Donglan River Valley tourist resort. Visitors come for lakeside and forest walks in karst hill country. It was named among the first national forest-wellness bases in 2020.

rows.name: Binglanggu Li and Miao Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.name_zh: 槟榔谷黎苗文化旅游区
rows.summary: A cultural park in Sandao town, set in an areca-palm valley, that presents Li and Miao traditions through demonstrations of Li brocade weaving, nose-flute and bamboo-instrument music, a staged Li wedding and a hands-on area where visitors learn the Li firewood dance. It also has century-old boat-shaped Li houses and stages the open-air show Binglang Guyun. The park displays several items on China's national intangible-heritage list, including Li textile techniques.

rows.name: Qixianling Hot Spring National Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 七仙岭温泉国家森林公园
rows.summary: A national forest park beneath the seven jagged peaks of Qixianling, with a forest zone and a hot-spring zone. A rainforest walk passes trees that flower on their trunks, epiphyte 'sky gardens' and strangler figs on the way to a viewing platform over Baoting, and hot springs rise naturally in the park's streams. Around the Qixi festival, usually in August, Baoting holds the Qixian Hot Spring Water Festival, a water-splashing celebration with Li and Miao song and dance that has run since 2000.

rows.name: Shenyu Island Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.summary: A lakeside leisure area on the Maozhen Reservoir in the hills of Xiangshui town, built around a jade-culture theme and named after an island in the lake. Visitors can take a boat on the lake and see a jade art gallery and a rainforest-ecology exhibition hall, and the lakeside hotel runs forest-wellness sessions for its guests. It suits a short leisure visit.

rows.name: Yanoda Rainforest Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.name_zh: 呀诺达雨林文化旅游区
rows.summary: A rainforest tourism zone in the hills of Sandao town, best known for stream trekking: visitors wade up forest streams in helmets and water shoes, climb the Lian'en waterfall, work through a ten-stage waterfall-wading course and ride a zip-slide above the canopy. A '123 Adventure Park' with canyon stream descents on fixed cables and rafting opened in July 2026. It was rated a 5A area in 2012 and suits active travellers and families.

rows.name: Feng Clan Ancestral Hall, Shique Village
rows.summary: A group of Feng clan halls in Shique village, the first Hainan home of the Feng family, who trace their line to Feng Bao and Lady Xian, the sixth-century leader who asked the Liang court to set up Yazhou prefecture on the island. The group consists of the main ancestral hall, whose first courtyard is the General's Mansion, a temple to the Marquis of Xiayang and the Wenlin Feng Gong hall; the main hall was last restored in 1884 and keeps stone carvings and painted murals. Around them stand more than 230 old houses of volcanic stone along 15 lanes in a comb layout, and most villagers still carry the Feng surname.

rows.name: Fushan Coffee Culture Town
rows.summary: A tourist town built around the coffee of Fushan, where coffee has been grown since the 1930s and whose beans hold national geographical-indication status. Its first phase has a large coffee square and some 19 local and international coffee brands, among them houses presenting the coffees of Vietnam, Turkey and Ethiopia, along with the town's own coffee academy, a lawn market and a snack street. It holds coffee festivals and stage performances through the year and became a 4A scenic area in 2025.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Meilang
rows.summary: Two Buddhist pagodas of volcanic stone that once stood in front of the vanished Jirui Nunnery, dated to the Song or Yuan dynasty. The six-sided larger tower and the four-sided smaller one, known as the elder and younger sister, stand about 20 m apart, each in its own pond, with a small stone bridge over the channel that links the ponds; the larger tower carries carved officials and warriors, and the smaller one Buddhist figures and four coiled-dragon pillars. Two nearby tombs, of Lingzhao and of Chen Daoxu and his wife, were added to the listing in 2006.

rows.name: Ancient City of Danzhou
rows.summary: The old walled seat of Danzhou prefecture, founded in the early Tang dynasty and used through the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing, which now forms the core of Zhonghe town. The wall once ran about 1.6 km around an irregular square with four gates; about 200 m of it still stands complete, 450 m survives in ruins and another 950 m survives as foundations. Inside the old town are the Kuixing tower, the Ningji and Guandi temples, the old West Gate lane and a well, among ordinary houses.

rows.name: Dongpo Academy
rows.summary: The site where the poet and official Su Dongpo (Su Shi), exiled to Hainan in the late 1090s, lived and taught in Danzhou; the academy that grew up around his Zaijiu Hall was rebuilt in the Ming and Qing dynasties, destroyed in the Cultural Revolution and restored in 1982. The Zaijiu Pavilion and Hall, side rooms and corridors now serve as an exhibition hall, and the grounds also have Dongpo Lake, a bridge, a statue, a memorial hall for the Guanglang Hermitage and Dongpo's well. Guides use augmented-reality devices, and a live 'Dongpo micro-theatre' show is staged on site.

rows.name: Shihua Water Cave Geopark
rows.summary: A karst geopark at Yaxing in western Danzhou, built around a limestone cave that visitors tour partly on foot and partly by small boat, with a stone forest above ground. The cave holds stalactites and other limestone formations, and the park also runs study programmes for school groups.

rows.name: Yangpu Ancient Salt Field
rows.summary: A salt field of more than a thousand flat-topped volcanic-rock slabs, each cut with a shallow trough and a thin rim, laid out on the shore at Yantian village on the Yangpu peninsula. Seawater fills the stones at high tide and evaporates at low tide, leaving salt to be gathered by hand, a method in use here since at least the Song dynasty that a few villagers still follow. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and as a national industrial heritage site in 2024.

rows.name: Ding'an Old City
rows.summary: The old county town of Ding'an, whose walls were begun in 1466 and finished in 1519; the west gate, the north gate and more than a kilometre of wall survive, along with several of the main streets inside. The restored old county office and a later arcaded old street are part of the site. It is a quiet place for a walk along the wall and through the old quarter.

rows.name: Murui Mountain Revolutionary Base
rows.summary: A mountain base area of the Communist-led Qiongya forces, which held out on Murui Mountain in 1928 and again in 1932. The memorial park, completed on 1 August 1996 and named a national patriotic education base in 2001, displays historical material and objects from the Hainan revolutionary struggle. About ten sites of the period have been rebuilt, including a Red Army cooperative, a sewing group and a transport office.

rows.name: Wenbifeng Pangu Culture Park
rows.summary: A Taoist and Pangu-legend complex of about 1,200 mu at the foot of Wenbi Peak near Nanli Lake, built in Southern Song style around the Yuchan Palace, a group of Taoist halls and shrines. In local legend the peak is Pangu's nose, and paths lead past lotus ponds and a bell and drum tower to a rock known as the dragon head and tortoise back and to a Pangu cave. The park also serves vegetarian meals and has a wellness-retreat centre.

rows.name: Basuo Labourers' Memorial Site
rows.name_zh: 侵华日军侵琼八所死难劳工纪念地
rows.pinyin: Qīnhuá Rìjūn Qīn Qióng Bāsuǒ Sǐnàn Láogōng Jìniàndì
rows.summary: A site on the shore at Basuo that records the forced labour used by the Japanese army to build Basuo port, a railway and military works between 1939 and 1942, when workers brought from Shanghai, Guangzhou, Hong Kong and Hainan, together with more than a thousand Allied prisoners of war, were put to work. An incomplete count puts the deaths at more than 10,000, and the dead were buried in a pit on the beach known as the ten-thousand-person pit. A memorial monument stands at the site, and two labour-prison buildings of the period were moved 500 metres to its eastern part in 2013.

rows.name: E'xian Ridge
rows.summary: A forested limestone massif in Donghe town on the shore of the Daguangba reservoir, whose main peak, E'niang Jiufeng, rises above 1,200 metres and is covered in rainforest on karst. Boats run on the reservoir among karst hills, and a climb of about an hour leads to E'niang Cave, where roughly 800 metres of route among stalactites and stalagmites are open. The area also includes a Li and Miao village, and it was rated 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Huali Valley (Rosewood Valley)
rows.summary: A leisure park themed on Hainan's huanghuali rosewood, with a plantation of more than a million trees, flower fields, a picking garden, a visitor centre, a rosewood museum, caravan and star-gazing cabins, and a hot-spring resort. It combines forestry and tourism and focuses on forest wellbeing and hot-spring holidays. It became Dongfang's first 4A scenic area in November 2022.

rows.name: Dongzhai Harbor Mangrove Tourist Area
rows.summary: A visitor area on the Dongzhai Harbor mangroves, part of a national nature reserve on Haikou's north-east coast that protects about 26,000 mu of mangrove wetland with 36 mangrove species. A boardwalk of about 1,700 m runs out over the water in three sections, a 33.5 m tower gives a view over the forest, and electric boats go through the channels. At low tide the trunks and roots stand exposed.

rows.name: Former Qionghai Customs House
rows.summary: The former customs house of Haikou, completed in 1937 on Deshengsha Road at the edge of the Qilou district. Qiongzhou Customs had been set up at Haikou in 1876; the customs service used the building until 1991 and its anti-smuggling bureau until 2017. The facade was restored in 2020, and an overseas-Chinese museum is planned for the interior, which had not opened by autumn 2026.

rows.name: Haikou Qilou Old Street
rows.summary: A historic district of more than 600 arcaded shophouses (qilou), largely built between the mid-nineteenth and mid-twentieth centuries by Hainanese who had traded in South-East Asia, combining Chinese plasterwork and murals with European and Asian columns and arches. The core streets (Zhongshan, Bo'ai, Xinhua North, Deshengsha and Jiefang roads) were restored from 2007 and now hold shops, guesthouses, heritage exhibition halls and a Tianhou temple. The old street runs for about 3.9 km in all and was named one of China's first ten historic and cultural streets in 2009.

rows.name: Haikou Volcanic Cluster Global Geopark
rows.summary: The Haikou section of the Leiqiong Global Geopark, a lava plateau south of Haikou with more than 40 Quaternary volcanoes, the youngest of which erupted in the Holocene. The visitor area centres on the Maanling group of four neighbouring cones, where the main cone, Fenglu Ling, can be climbed for views over Haikou and the Qiongzhou Strait. Visitors also see ropy and wood-grained lava surfaces and lava tubes.

rows.name: Hainan Changying Fantasy Park
rows.summary: A film-themed amusement park developed by the Changying film group, which opened as Changying Global 100 Fantasy Park and has since been renamed. Landmarks include the Loulan Tower and a Zheng He treasure-ship building, set around Bayin Lake, and the park stages parades and light-and-water shows on the lake. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Hainan Museum
rows.summary: The provincial museum, in the Hainan Cultural Park on Guoxing Avenue, has occupied its present building since 2008 and was rated a national first-class museum in 2012. Its permanent exhibitions cover the history of Hainan, the island's minority peoples, intangible cultural heritage and a selection of relics, alongside changing exhibitions. It stands beside the Hainan Library and the Hainan Centre for the Performing Arts.

rows.name: Hainan Tropical Wildlife Park and Botanical Garden
rows.name_zh: 海南热带野生动植物园
rows.summary: A zoo set in about 1,500 mu of planted tropical forest in the hills south of Haikou, opened in 1996, with a drive-through area and a walking area. Animals on show have included giant pandas, an Asian elephant, brown bears and takin. It was badly damaged by Typhoon Yagi in September 2024 and reopened within a month.

rows.name: Holiday Beach
rows.summary: A long city beach on Haikou's north-western coast, facing the Qiongzhou Strait and running alongside Binhai Avenue, set up as a visitor beach in 1995. Behind the sand are landscaped paths and areas for dining and water sports, and the sea is used for swimming, sailing and windsurfing.

rows.name: Hou Family Compound, Qiongshan
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty merchant family's compound in Baodao village, built around 1800 by the Hou family, who had moved from Guangdong and prospered as pawnbrokers. Five parallel courtyard ranges of timber-framed halls open off three gateways on the south side, with carved woodwork, plaster ridge decoration and local basalt stonework; the main hall of the third range, locally known as the seventeen-tile-row hall, is tall and richly decorated. The Hou family still use it for ancestral rites and festivals.

rows.name: Mission Hills Haikou
rows.summary: A large resort complex on a black lava plateau south of Haikou, developed since the late 2000s around ten 18-hole golf courses. Besides hotels it has a volcanic hot-spring valley with 168 hot and cold pools, a water park, the Feng Xiaogang Movie Commune (a film-set town recreating streets of twentieth-century China, with stage shows) and a duty-free mall, outlet shops and restaurants. It suits golfers, families and shoppers more than sightseers.

rows.name: Qiongya Red Army Reorganisation Site, Yunlong
rows.name_zh: 琼崖工农红军云龙改编旧址
rows.pinyin: Qióngyá Gōngnóng Hóngjūn Yúnlóng Gǎibiān Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: On 5 December 1938, at the market town of Yunlong, the Communist-led Qiongya Red Army was reorganised as an anti-Japanese independent unit under an agreement with the Nationalist authorities on the island. The memorial park has a bronze soldier, a statue of the Communist and Nationalist commanders shaking hands, corridors carved with inscriptions and battle summaries, and a hall whose photographs and texts trace the Qiongya Red Army from its founding through the Anti-Japanese War and the civil war. The memorial was first built in 1952 on the site of the market-town temple where the ceremony was held, and has since been extended several times.

rows.name: Qiu Jun's Former Residence and Tomb
rows.summary: Qiu Jun (1421–95) was a Ming scholar-statesman from Qiongshan who rose to Grand Secretary. His boyhood home in Jinhua village is a low timber house whose main hall, Kejitang, keeps Song and Yuan-style roof framing and is among the oldest surviving timber dwellings on Hainan. His tomb lies about 6 km away in Qiu Jun Cultural Park, where an exhibition hall of more than 3,000 square metres presents his life and Ming and Qing relics.

rows.name: Site of the First Qiongya Congress of the Communist Party
rows.name_zh: 中共琼崖第一次代表大会旧址
rows.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Qióngyá Dìyī Cì Dàibiǎo Dàhuì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A two-range courtyard house of brick and timber, built around 1920 by the Qiu family, where 11 delegates representing some 240 party members met in secret in June 1926 and elected the Qiongya regional committee of the Communist Party. The first hall holds relics from the meeting, portraits of the delegates hang in the side rooms, and the rear hall and side wings carry a photograph exhibition on the history of the party organisation on Hainan. The small garden courtyard lies in Zhulinli (Bamboo Grove Lane), in the middle of the city.

rows.name: Temple of the Five Lords
rows.summary: A memorial complex in Haikou's old Fucheng quarter honouring five Tang and Song officials who were banished to Hainan, among them the chancellors Li Deyu and Li Gang. The central two-storey timber hall was built in 1889 and stands among shrines to Su Dongpo and to two Han-dynasty Fubo generals, with the Fusu spring, garden pavilions and an exhibition hall of Hainan relics. The complex shows how Hainan served as a place of exile in imperial times.

rows.name: Tomb of Hai Rui
rows.summary: The tomb of Hai Rui (1514–87), the Ming official remembered for his incorruptibility, was completed in 1589 as a granite mound reached along a spirit way of stone archways and carved animals and officials. It was badly damaged during the Cultural Revolution and restored in 1982. The surrounding Hai Rui Cultural Park, expanded from the heritage site, adds an exhibition hall on his life and on integrity in office, an academy hall and a connecting gallery.

rows.name: Xiuying Fort
rows.summary: A Qing coastal fort on a low rise above Haikou's north-western shore, built in the early 1890s on the orders of the viceroy Zhang Zhidong to guard the Qiongzhou Strait against a French threat. Five emplacements for German-made Krupp guns stand in a line facing the sea, with barracks, a magazine and a parade ground behind, and displays of historical photographs. It is counted with the Humen, Wusong and Dagu forts as one of China's four great old coastal forts, and is now hemmed in by apartment blocks.

rows.name: Zhuyaling City Site
rows.summary: The earthen walls of a small walled town survive on a rise beside the Nandu River, enclosing about 2.9 hectares, with a gap in the south wall that marks the gate. The national list dates the site from the Han to the Tang period; excavations in 2022 uncovered building platforms, roof tiles, bricks and pottery that archaeologists associate with a Tang-era county or prefectural seat. What a visitor sees is the line of the walls, the stepped slope at the gate and the village around it.

rows.name: Hainan Liberation Park and Lingao Cape Lighthouse
rows.summary: A memorial park on Lingao Cape, the headland on Hainan's north-west coast where troops of the People's Liberation Army's 40th Army landed in the early hours of 17 April 1950, in the crossing of the Qiongzhou Strait that brought Hainan Island under PRC control. The 86-mu park, opened in 2006 and renamed Hainan Liberation Park at the end of 2020, has a large sculpture group, a memorial to the dead of the 40th and 43rd Armies and a museum on the crossing. Inside the park stands the Lingao Cape lighthouse, a 22 m cast-iron tower built by the French in 1893 and listed nationally in 2013.

rows.name: Boundary Island (Fenjiezhou)
rows.summary: A small uninhabited island in Riyue Bay off Guangpo town, whose name, 'dividing-line island', refers to the climatic divide between northern and southern Hainan. The scenic area offers beaches, snorkelling and diving among corals and a wreck, ray and turtle encounters in the shallows, a sightseeing submarine and an ocean theatre, along with jet skis and other water sports. It has been rated 5A since 2013.

rows.name: Former Lingshui County Soviet Government
rows.name_zh: 陵水县苏维埃政府旧址
rows.summary: A white-walled, tiled building in Yelin, built in 1921 as the Qiongshan Guild Hall. On 16 December 1927 a congress of workers, peasants and soldiers held there proclaimed the Lingshui county Soviet government, the first county-level Soviet government in the Qiongya area, which broke up in June 1928. The building now holds an exhibition on the Soviet's history, using scenes, panels, objects and audiovisual displays.

rows.name: Hainan Ocean Paradise
rows.summary: A marine-life theme park resort at Li'an, opened in December 2021 as R&F Ocean Paradise, covering about 2,000 mu (roughly 130 hectares) in five themed zones. It combines dozens of rides with animal halls and aquariums of South China Sea species, sea-lion and mermaid-themed shows, a polar animal hall with polar bears, belugas and penguins (opened in July 2024) and a separate water park (opened in April 2025). It suits families with children.

rows.name: Nanwan Monkey Island
rows.summary: A macaque reserve on the Nanwan peninsula beside Xincun harbour, established in 1965, where more than a thousand macaques live in the forest. A cable car over the water links Xincun harbour with the reserve, and paths lead to the monkeys. The tourist area has added a dome-screen theatre show, sea sports and horse riding.

rows.name: Qingshui Bay (Clear Water Bay)
rows.summary: A beach-resort district on Lingshui's coast with about 12 km of shoreline, fine sand and clear water. Its sights include the Freedom Lighthouse, a red-and-white landmark tower used as a film location, a sea-viewing platform and a stretch of beach known for its 'singing sand', and it has several resort hotels. It was named a provincial tourist resort in 2021.

rows.name: Baishiling
rows.summary: A hilly area beside the Wanquan River covering 16.24 square kilometres, made up of four linked ridges with peaks, valleys, lakes and forest of about 90 per cent cover, the highest point reaching 328 metres. An aerial cableway opened in 1995, and glass walkways, a via ferrata and a camping area have been added since.

rows.name: Boao Forum for Asia Permanent Venue
rows.name_zh: 博鳌亚洲论坛永久会址
rows.summary: The permanent conference site of the Boao Forum for Asia, on Dongyu Island where the Wanquan River meets the sea. The grounds hold the forum's conference halls and hotels beside the water, with a globe sculpture in front of the main venue and a waterfront promenade. The forum's annual meeting takes place here each spring.

rows.name: Cai Family House, Boao
rows.summary: Four brick-and-concrete courtyard houses built between 1924 and 1934 in Liuke village by four Cai brothers, Chinese merchants in Indonesia, covering about 2,645 square metres in a regular rectangle facing west. A well, a lotus pond, an orchard and service buildings lie around them. Traditional Chinese decoration is mixed with South-East Asian and Western details, and the compound is nicknamed Hainan's first overseas-Chinese house.

rows.name: China (Hainan) Museum of the South China Sea
rows.summary: A large museum beside the fishing harbour at Tanmen, opened in April 2018, with about 70,000 square metres of floor space. Its exhibitions cover the maritime history of the South China Sea, navigation technology, marine life, the ancient Maritime Silk Road and the history of fishing in these waters, and they include finds from underwater archaeology such as cargo recovered from shipwrecks. Tanmen is a long-established fishing port.

rows.name: World Tropical Fruit Window
rows.summary: A tropical-fruit park in Dalu town that grows and displays some 680 fruit varieties introduced from Latin America, Australia and South-East Asia, with science-education displays alongside the orchards. Visitors can also see seasonal shows and themed photo sets, and the park was rated 4A in 2024. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Baihualing Rainforest Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A forested hill area in Hainan's central highlands, opened to visitors in 2019, with a tree-top boardwalk, tree houses, a swinging bridge over water, a glass slide and a 2 km rainforest slide, along with Baihua Waterfall, which drops more than 300 m in all. It lies next to the northern gate of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park, and Li and Miao folk song and dance are among the activities it offers.

rows.name: Atlantis Sanya
rows.summary: An ocean-themed resort complex on Haitang Bay that opened in April 2018, covering about 31 hectares with a 1,314-room hotel, restaurants and a shopping arcade. Day visitors use the Aquaventure water park, the Lost Chambers aquarium, a theatre show and the dolphin and sea-lion encounters. It suits families and groups planning a water-park day.

rows.name: Da Xiao Dongtian
rows.summary: A coastal scenic area at the foot of Nanshan hill in Yazhou district, named Da Xiao Dongtian, or 'Great and Little Cave-Heavens' (a Daoist term for sacred grottoes), in the Song dynasty. The Xiaodongtian rock inscriptions, dating from the Song dynasty to modern times, are protected at provincial level, and the grounds also hold the Sanya Natural History Museum.

rows.name: Luhuitou Park
rows.summary: A hill park on the peninsula just south of central Sanya, covered in evergreen tropical monsoon forest. On the summit a large stone sculpture shows the Li legend of a hunter and a deer that turns into a girl, the story behind Sanya's nickname 'Deer City'. Viewpoints look north over the city and east to Dadonghai bay.

rows.name: Luobi Cave
rows.summary: A limestone cave under Luobi Peak, the southernmost prehistoric cave site found in China so far. Excavations in 1992–93 recovered human teeth, stone and bone tools and the bones of 45 mammal species from about 10,000 years ago. A new round of excavation begun in 2025 has uncovered a burial 13,000 to 12,000 years old, the oldest found on the island, and the site is on the national list of archaeological site parks under creation, with a site museum planned.

rows.name: Nanshan Cultural Tourism Zone
rows.summary: A large modern Buddhist-themed park on the coast west of Sanya, built around Nanshan Temple, founded in 1998, and the Guanyin of Nanshan, a 108 m statue (including its base) on an artificial islet that was consecrated in 2005. The statue has three faces, one looking inland and two out to sea, and the grounds also hold gardens, further statues and a longevity theme taken from the saying 'long life like the Southern Mountain'. A longevity festival has been held here since 1999.

rows.name: Sanya International Duty Free Shopping Complex
rows.summary: A large duty-free shopping mall run by China Duty Free Group on Haitang Bay, which moved here in 2014 from a smaller shop in Dadonghai that opened in 2009. Its halls sell perfume, cosmetics, jewellery, watches, leather goods and fashion brands, and a third phase was topped out in January 2026.

rows.name: Sanya Red Detachment of Women Performing Arts Park
rows.name_zh: 三亚红色娘子军演艺公园
rows.summary: A show-centred theme park in Tianya district, laid out in three zones named Red Memory, Red Sanya and Sea of Stars. Its main production is the open-air show Red Detachment of Women, which uses dance, martial arts and Li and Miao elements to retell the 1930s story of the women's company of the Communist-led Red Army on Hainan. The park also has a musical-fountain plaza, a Silk Road crafts centre and a children's playground.

rows.name: Tianya Haijiao
rows.summary: A beach west of Sanya scattered with large boulders, several carved with the characters that made the place famous: Tianya (edge of the sky), cut in 1733 by the Yazhou prefect; Nantian Yizhu (pillar of the southern sky), added in 1909; and Haijiao (corner of the sea), added in 1939. The inscribed rocks are a provincial heritage site, and because Chinese poetry uses the name for the farthest reaches of the world, couples often come here. On clear days islets can be seen offshore.

rows.name: West Island
rows.summary: A small island off Sanya's western coast, the offshore island nearest to the city, with a working fishing village of old coral-stone houses whose history goes back more than 400 years. Visitors can walk the lanes, where nets are hung out to dry, and stay overnight in homestays once the day-trippers have left.

rows.name: Wuzhizhou Island
rows.summary: A small island of about 1.5 square kilometres in Haitang Bay, with sandy beaches, rocky shores and tropical forest, and water sports on offer around its coast. Visitors cross by boat and tour the island by electric buggy, which is required to see the hillside and sea views in parts of the back of the island.

rows.name: Yacheng Academy
rows.summary: The former Confucian school of Yazhou prefecture, founded in 1044 in the Northern Song dynasty, moved to this site in 1823 and repaired in 1872. It is laid out in three courtyards, from a gate wall and Lingxing Gate through a crescent pool and the Dacheng Gate to the Dacheng Hall and a rear shrine; the Dacheng Hall, gate, side halls, two shrines and the pool are Qing buildings and the rest has been rebuilt. It opened to the public in 2007 and stands in Yazhou ancient town.

rows.name: Yalong Bay Tropical Paradise Forest Park
rows.name_zh: 亚龙湾热带天堂森林公园
rows.summary: A forest park on the hills behind Yalong Bay, set in dense tropical forest. Its best-known feature is the Guojianglong suspension bridge, 168 m long and hung nearly 40 m above the valley, which appeared in the film If You Are the One 2 and in later television dramas. It suits visitors who want a forest walk close to the Yalong Bay beach resorts.

rows.name: Menghuan Xiangshan Fragrance Park
rows.summary: A fragrance-themed garden park of more than 600 mu (about 40 hectares) in the hills beside the central expressway, with over a hundred kinds of scented flowers and herbs, about 400 mu of lemon orchard and some 10,000 agarwood trees, more than half of them nearly 30 years old. It also has a fragrance museum and a hotel, and runs seasonal flower displays and sachet-making and fruit-picking activities. It suits families and photographers.

rows.name: Xinglong Tropical Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A botanical garden founded in 1957 and open to visitors since 1997, run by the Spice and Beverage Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences. It holds more than 3,200 tropical and subtropical plant species, with collections of coffee, pepper, vanilla and cocoa, and rainforest features such as buttress roots and flowers borne directly on trunks. It sits in Xinglong, an overseas-Chinese settlement known for its coffee.

rows.name: Coconut Grand View Garden
rows.summary: A coconut-themed park of 443 mu (about 30 hectares) that grew out of a palm germplasm collection of the Coconut Research Institute and has been open to visitors since 1980. It grows 217 palm species and 130 rare tree species among coconut groves, and has a coconut science museum, a coconut-grove maze, a petting area and an adventure camp. It suits families with children and school groups.

rows.name: Doubing Pagoda
rows.summary: An eight-sided, seven-storey brick pagoda about 20 metres high on the main peak of Qixing Ridge above Puqian, built in the Ming dynasty as a feng shui tower that also served as a navigation mark. A stone plaque over the doorway dates its construction to 1625, and a spiral staircase of 104 steps climbs inside to the top. Damaged eaves and walls were repaired, with the work finished in July 2023.

rows.name: Fu Family House, Wenchang
rows.summary: A compound of three two-storey blocks in a village in Wencheng town, built in the 1910s by brothers who had made their money in Singapore, using local fired brick and imported Thai hardwood. The layout, side wings and painted decoration along the wall tops follow the village houses of northern Hainan, while the gate, the upper-floor cooling pavilion, the verandas and the plaster relief borrow the arcaded Nanyang style of South-East Asia. It has served as a guerrilla base and as a primary school, and parts of its roof and walls had collapsed by 2013.

rows.name: Han Family House, Wenchang
rows.summary: A four-courtyard family house built in 1936–38 in Fuzhai village by Han Qinzhun, a Wenchang merchant based in Thailand. The compound covers about 1,335 square metres on a single axis, with 16 side rooms, high surrounding walls and two square pavilions on the roof of the east wing, and it mixes Hainan, South-East Asian and Western styles. Murals inside and outside the walls show the family's sawmill in Thailand and scenes of the village.

rows.name: Song Family Ancestral Home
rows.summary: A courtyard house in Changsa town linked to the family of Charlie Soong (Song Jiashu), the father of Song Qingling and Song Meiling, who married Sun Yat-sen and Chiang Kai-shek. The original dwelling no longer stands, and the present courtyard house is a rebuild of the 1980s. An exhibition hall beside it displays photographs and objects connected with the Song family.

rows.name: Tonggu Ridge
rows.summary: A coastal ridge at the north-eastern tip of Hainan, surrounded by sea on three sides, with 18 linked peaks and a main summit of 338 metres. Its slopes carry a coastal tropical evergreen monsoon forest with 1,019 recorded plant species, 12 of them rare or endangered, as well as boulders, beaches, a river and a lake within the area. A path climbs to the summit, which is a popular place to watch the sunrise.

rows.name: Wenchang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The former county Confucian temple and school of Wenchang, founded in the Northern Song dynasty and moved to its present site in 1375, early in the Ming. The main compound faces east and has about 3,300 square metres of floor space, with a crescent pool and bridge, the double-eaved Dacheng Hall and side halls, most of them built in the Ming and Qing, while the grounds also hold the Wenchang Palace, Minglun Hall and the Weiwen Academy.

rows.name: Xibei Academy
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty academy begun in 1893 in Puqian town on the initiative of the calligrapher and scholar Pan Cun, with funding from the governor-general Zhang Zhidong, though Pan died just before it was finished. A crescent-shaped pond lies in front of the gate, whose plaque was written by the calligrapher Yang Shoujing. The buildings have more than 3,000 square metres of floor space and stand in the grounds of Wenbei Middle School.

rows.name: Wuzhishan Red Canyon
rows.summary: A rainforest gorge in Nansheng town developed for visitors from 2015, with a 3.8 km rafting run through the canyon and a 3.8 km boardwalk along its banks. Other attractions include a double suspension bridge (one deck glass, one timber) about 40 m above the water, a glass slide and a Li and Miao restaurant.

rows.name: Wuzhishan Revolutionary Base Memorial Park
rows.name_zh: 五指山革命根据地纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park built from 2001 on the site of the Qiongya Column's headquarters in Maogui village, the last base of the Communist-led armed struggle on Hainan before 1950. A 23 m monument stands above the plaza, with a martyrs' cemetery nearby, and a history hall of 2,558 square metres covers 1939–50 in seven sections: the Baisha uprising, the creation of the Wuzhishan central base, the three offensives of 1948–49 and the changes in the Li and Miao autonomous areas after 1950.

rows.name: Rendi Mountain Rainforest
rows.summary: A rainforest-edge hotel and resort area near Wuzhishan City in central Hainan, run by a local company, with forest walks from the hotel. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Bawangling
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in the Li highlands of Changjiang County, managed by the Bawangling Forestry Bureau and best known as a habitat of the Hainan gibbon. It offers forest-park trails and tropical rainforest scenery. It is one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: 816 Nuclear Military Plant
rows.summary: An unfinished underground nuclear plant dug into a mountain beside the Wu River from 1966 as part of the Third Front programme, meant to produce plutonium for weapons and to survive a nuclear attack. Work was halted in 1984 with about 85 per cent of the construction done; the tunnels run for more than 20 km and the largest chamber, built for the reactor, is 79.6 m high. Declassified in 2002, it opened to tourists in 2010.

rows.name: Anju Ancient Town
rows.summary: Anju sits where the Qiong River joins the Fu River, 17 km north of Tongliang, and was once an important distribution centre for goods on the upper Yangtze. Its hillside old town of stone-flagged lanes is run as a scenic area with a recently rebuilt Confucian temple and county yamen, and in 2022 it was named a national intangible-cultural-heritage tourism area; dragon-boat races are held on the river.

rows.name: Antao Pottery Town
rows.summary: A pottery-themed tourist area in Anfu Subdistrict built around Rongchang pottery, a craft listed as national intangible cultural heritage, linking the Rongchang Pottery Museum, the old Taobao post road and craft-experience sites. Holiday events have included markets, street performances and hands-on crafts such as sugar-figure making and opera-mask painting.

rows.name: Ayi River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The valley of the Ayi River, a tributary that rises in Guizhou and flows through Pengshui into the Wu River, home to protected animals such as François' langur. The scenic area follows the river south of Pengshui town, and rafting on it is the best-known summer activity.

rows.name: Baigong Temple & the Han Que Pillar-Gates
rows.summary: A memorial temple to the Tang poet Bai Juyi, who served as prefect of Zhongzhou, first built in 1630 and rebuilt in 1986, now a museum park in the Zhong County town. Since 2003 its grounds have held two Eastern Han stone pillar-gates (que), the Dingfang Que and the Uninscribed Que, moved from sites flooded by the Three Gorges reservoir; the taller tower of the Dingfang pair stands 6.26 m high. Holograms and multimedia displays present the county's relics in the halls.

rows.name: Baiheliang Underwater Museum
rows.summary: A museum built around White Crane Ridge, a rock ledge in the Yangtze off Fuling that showed above water only in the dry season and bears some 170 inscriptions and carved fish recording the river's low levels in 72 years since 764. When the Three Gorges reservoir submerged the ridge, it was enclosed in a shell of filtered water about 40 m down; visitors ride a 91 m escalator to a gallery and look at the carvings through 23 portholes. The museum opened in 2009, with exhibition halls on the riverbank explaining the inscriptions.

rows.name: Baili Bamboo Sea (Guanyin Cave area)
rows.summary: Part of the Baili Bamboo Sea, about 230 km² of continuous bamboo forest in the valleys between a dozen peaks over 1,000 m on Mingyue Mountain, on Liangping's border with Sichuan. The rated area is the Guanyin Cave section at Zhengzhi village in Zhushan town, and nearby villages such as Lieshen have turned former gypsum-mining land into guesthouses for summer stays.

rows.name: Beidi Yiyuan Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort with bathing pools in landscaped grounds at Baishiyi, in Chongqing's western suburbs. It is a place for a relaxing soak rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Changshou Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir formed by the Shizitan dam on the Longxi River, completed in 1956 for hydropower, with about 65 km² of water dotted with more than 200 islands. The scenic area around it includes island and lakeshore viewpoints, the Donglin Temple, founded in the Song dynasty, and stepped waterfalls on the Longxi River below the dam.

rows.name: Chashan Zhuhai (Tea Hills and Bamboo Sea)
rows.summary: A national forest park on the hills just north of Yongchuan town, where tea plantations give way to large stands of bamboo crossed by walking trails. Baodaoling ridge, the highest point in western Chongqing, is the place for sunrise and seas of cloud, Baoji Temple stands in the forest, and an activity area offers a summer toboggan and slides, with a campsite added in 2024.

rows.name: Chen Duxiu's Former Residence
rows.summary: Shiqiangyuan, a walled Qing-dynasty courtyard house on Heshanping where Chen Duxiu, a founder and the first general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, lived from 1939 until his death in 1942. The east-wing rooms he shared with his wife Pan Lanzhen, a bedroom, parlour and study, are shown as they were, beside an exhibition in seven parts that follows his life from the New Culture and May Fourth movements to his last years in Jiangjin. The museum took its present form in 2012, and the house is a Chongqing municipal heritage site.

rows.name: Chen Tuan's Hometown (Chongkan Rapeseed Fields)
rows.summary: Farmland around Chongkan town, one of the places claimed as the birthplace of the 10th-century Daoist sage Chen Tuan, where the rapeseed fields along the Qiong River turn yellow every March and a taiji (yin-yang) pattern about 236 m across has been planted in the core area. Visitors tour the flowers on foot, by boat, by small sightseeing train and by sightseeing cable car, and a Taiji town built in traditional style has a statue of Chen Tuan, an exhibition hall and temple buildings.

rows.name: Chiyou Jiuli City
rows.summary: A large hillside complex of Miao-style buildings on the edge of Pengshui town, rated 4A in 2016, with stilt houses, the Jiuli Palace and a ceremonial square, built around the Miao legends of Chiyou and the ancient Jiuli people. By day visitors climb through the complex for the views, and in the evenings it opens for night visits with light shows on Miao themes.

rows.name: Chongqing Bonded Goods Experience Zone
rows.name_zh: 重庆保税体验旅游景区
rows.summary: A shopping and exhibition zone inside the Lianglu–Cuntan bonded port area of Liangjiang New Area, run by the port's operating company, where imported goods are displayed and sold at a bonded commodity trading centre. It is of interest mainly to shoppers looking for imported products.

rows.name: Chongqing City Walls (Tongyuanmen and Dongshuimen)
rows.summary: Surviving stretches of the walls of old Chongqing, rebuilt in 1373 under the Ming on earlier foundations and set along the cliffs above the Yangtze and Jialing rivers; of the 17 gates only three open gates and one closed gate remain, as much of the circuit was pulled down from the 1920s. The protected sections are at Tongyuanmen, where a city-wall park with rebuilt towers opened in 2005, and at Dongshuimen above the Yangtze beside the Huguang Guild Hall. A 15 km walking route around the Yuzhong peninsula follows the old wall line.

rows.name: Chongqing Garden Expo Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park of about 220 ha around Longjing Lake in Chongqing's northern suburbs, opened in November 2011, with 127 show gardens in the styles of Chinese regions and cities and of several foreign partner cities, set among hills, arched bridges and wetland. Electric carts and boats link the gardens across the site.

rows.name: Chongqing Industrial Culture Park (Chongqing Industrial Museum)
rows.summary: An industrial heritage park on the old Chongqing Iron and Steel works at Dadukou, opened in 2019 after the steelworks moved out to Changshou. Its museum tells the story of Chongqing industry from the opening of the port in 1891 to the present, centred on a British-built 8,000-horsepower twin-cylinder steam engine of 1905, with locally made machinery, vehicles and motorcycles. Old chimneys and other relics of the plant are kept in the grounds as landscape features.

rows.name: Chongqing Jianchuan Museum
rows.summary: A cluster of themed museums opened in 2018 by the collector Fan Jianchuan in the wartime air-raid tunnels of the former Hanyang Arsenal, which moved here from Hanyang in Wuhan and became the Nationalist Ordnance Department's First Arsenal. Some 51 tunnels survive in the hillside by the Egongyan Bridge: three linked ones form the arsenal site museum with recreated wartime production, and others hold museums of weapons history, wartime relics, ration coupons, traditional Chinese medicine, wedding customs and Chongqing life.

rows.name: Chongqing Jihua Park
rows.summary: A large sports and leisure complex in Longxing, announced in 2016 as an extreme-sports centre, whose facilities include an indoor ski slope. It runs family activities on public holidays and lies next to the Liangjiang film set, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Chongqing Natural History Museum
rows.summary: Chongqing's natural history museum, open in its present building at the foot of Jinyun Mountain in Beibei since 2015, with a design based on the spreading roots of the huangge fig, the city tree. Its collection of more than 110,000 objects covers fossils, minerals, animals and plants, and the dinosaur galleries show Sichuan Basin skeletons such as Omeisaurus and Tuojiangosaurus. The museum grew out of the Western China Academy of Sciences, founded in 1930, and the wartime Western China Museum, and it still runs the academy's old campus in central Beibei as a second site.

rows.name: Chongqing Negotiations Sites (Yiyuan)
rows.summary: Five wartime residences and offices linked with the 1945 Chongqing negotiations between the Nationalists and the Communists: Chiang Kai-shek's residence, two buildings of his aides' office, the residence of the Nationalist politician Song Ziwen (T. V. Soong), known as Yiyuan, and the residence of Wu Tiecheng. Yiyuan, a Gothic-style villa of 1937 on Sixin Road where the US envoy George Marshall stayed from December 1945 and where the first Nationalist–Communist ceasefire agreement was signed in January 1946, opened as an exhibition hall in 2018; the 1940 Wu Tiecheng residence stands on Jialing New Road beside the Stilwell Museum. The other three buildings are inside the compound of the municipal Communist Party committee.

rows.name: Chongqing People's Auditorium & People's Square
rows.summary: A vast assembly hall built in 1951–54 for the Southwest regional government, with a domed central hall modelled on Beijing's Temple of Heaven, colonnaded wings, blue-green glazed roofs and red columns. The round auditorium under its 46 m steel-framed dome seats about 4,200 people and is still used for the city's major meetings. It faces the Three Gorges Museum across People's Square, a popular gathering place in the evenings.

rows.name: Chongqing Planning Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: Chongqing's urban-planning museum moved in 2022 from Chaotianmen to a new building on the Nanbin Road riverfront at Danzishi, looking across the Yangtze to the Yuzhong peninsula. Its exhibitions trace how the mountain city has grown and how it is planned to develop.

rows.name: Chongqing Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: Chongqing's main science museum opened in 2009 in the Jiangbeizui business district beside the Grand Theatre, close to where the Jialing River joins the Yangtze. Its themed halls cover everyday science, transport, defence technology, disaster prevention with simulated hazards, basic science and space flight, and there is a children's science playground and giant-screen and 4D cinemas.

rows.name: Chongqing Three Gorges Immigration Memorial (Wanzhou Museum)
rows.summary: Wanzhou's main museum, designed by the architect Cui Kai and opened in 2018, which also serves as the Wanzhou District Museum. Its lower gallery traces Wanzhou's history from its earliest settlements some 7,000 years ago to its days as a Yangtze trading port, and the two levels above document the building of the Three Gorges Dam and the resettlement of about 1.3 million people from the reservoir area.

rows.name: Chongqing Zoo
rows.summary: Chongqing's main zoo, opened in 1955 on 45 hectares of hillside at Yangjiaping, about 8 km south-west of the city centre. It keeps one of the largest groups of giant pandas in any Chinese zoo and breeds pandas and South China tigers, alongside red pandas, white tigers and African elephants.

rows.name: Ciqikou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A former river port on the Jialing River whose name, 'porcelain mouth', recalls the pottery trade of the Ming and Qing dynasties, now a busy pedestrian quarter of 12 flagstone lanes lined with old-style shops and snack stalls. Among its timber houses are Baolun Temple, a Wenchang Palace and several listed Qing-era homes, and near the old wharf stands the 'Little Chongqing' stone inscribed by Lin Sen, the wartime head of the Nationalist government.

rows.name: Da Eling Scenic Area (Eling Park)
