rows.summary: A hilltop scenic area on the narrow ridge of the Yuzhong peninsula, rated 4A in 2022 and centred on Eling Park, laid out in 1909 as the villa garden of the merchant Li Yaoting at the highest point of the peninsula. The Liangjiang Pavilion looks over both the Yangtze and the Jialing, and the park also has a Japanese-style garden presented by the twin city of Hiroshima. Since November 2025 a 460 m walkway built against the cliff has linked it with Fotuguan Park to the west.

rows.name: Dafengbao Forest, Huangshui
rows.summary: The core forest area of Huangshui National Forest Park, which reaches 1,934 m, with dense old woodland and more than 20 marked sights along its trails. Summer temperatures far below those of Chongqing make it a popular hiking and summer-escape spot, often combined with Sun Lake next door.

rows.name: Damu Flower Valley
rows.summary: A flower park on the slopes above Damu, a mountain town at about 1,000 m in south-eastern Fuling that fills with visitors escaping the summer heat. Seasonal flowers are planted on terraces, around a lake and along forest paths, and in summer 2026 the park held its first lantern festival with large light displays among the flower beds.

rows.name: Daning Saltworks Site, Ningchang
rows.summary: Ningchang, a narrow valley town north of Wuxi county town, was a major salt-producing centre of south-west China, and this national heritage site at the foot of Baoyuan Mountain covers the remains of its saltworks from the Song dynasty to the Republican era. Along the old town are the Qianlong-era salt commissioner's office, the saltworks administration office, production and workers' buildings, and old salt roads leading into the mountains. Ningchang is a listed Chinese Historical and Cultural Town, and the first phase of conservation work on the saltworks has been completed.

rows.name: Danzishi Cliff Buddha
rows.summary: A large seated Buddha carved into the Yangtze riverbank cliff below the former Dafo Temple, completed in 1365 for Ming Yuzhen, who founded the short-lived Xia state with its capital at Chongqing at the end of the Yuan dynasty. Five more Buddhas were cut into the rock behind it in 1421 and are sheltered by the Five Buddha Hall, rebuilt in 1844; most of the rest of the temple was lost from the Cultural Revolution onwards.

rows.name: Danzishi Old Street
rows.summary: Danzishi grew from the early 19th century around one of the ferry landings on the Yangtze's south bank, opposite the Chaotianmen confluence, and keeps older buildings such as the French Naval Barracks of 1902 and the Wang family compound. The hillside has since been redeveloped as a stepped quarter of shops, bars and restaurants in old-street style that looks across the river to the Yuzhong peninsula. The restored barracks belong to a national heritage group of former Allied diplomatic and military premises from Chongqing's years as wartime capital.

rows.name: Diaoyu Fortress
rows.summary: A Southern Song mountain fortress on Diaoyu Hill, a peninsula where the Jialing, Qu and Fu rivers meet east of Hechuan, which held out against Mongol armies for 36 years from 1243. The Mongol Great Khan Möngke died during his siege of it in 1259; its stone walls and gates, naval wharf and other remains form one of the best-preserved Song battlefield sites in China and a national archaeological park.

rows.name: Dieshi Flower Valley
rows.summary: A landscaped valley south of Youyang county town beside the G65 expressway, where the scenic area doubles as an open motorway service area. It is built around outcrops of stromatolite, layered rock dating from the Cambrian period about half a billion years ago, with named rock features themed on local Nuo masked-ritual culture, such as a circle of pillars for the twelve month-gods. Seasonal flower fields, including pink muhly grass in autumn, and a zip line complete the visit.

rows.name: Dongwenquan (East Hot Springs)
rows.summary: A hot-spring area along the Wubu River in eastern Ba'nan, where springs supply a string of bathing resorts and hotels and a warm, steamy cave, Redong, is used as a natural sauna. Around the springs, karst peaks have cliff walkways and small caves, and the area also has Baisha Temple with its ancient trees and the tomb of Yang Cangbai, secretary-general of Sun Yat-sen's government in Guangzhou.

rows.name: Early Buildings of Chongqing University
rows.summary: A group of early buildings on Campus A of Chongqing University in Shapingba: the Science Building, Engineering Building and Wenzi Hall, built in the early 1930s as the university settled here, the Yinchu Pavilion named after the economist Ma Yinchu, and the 'July 7th' wartime auditorium of National Central University, built after that university moved to Chongqing in 1937. The buildings combine Western forms with Chinese-style details such as dormer windows, and the stone-walled Engineering Building was damaged by Japanese bombing during the war.

rows.name: Fengdu Ghost City
rows.summary: A hill of temples and shrines on Ming Mountain above the Yangtze at Fengdu, linked since the Song dynasty with the underworld court of Chinese folk religion and Taoism. Halls, bridges and gates named after the stages of the afterlife, such as Naihe Bridge, Ghost Gate Pass and the Tianzi Hall, the oldest building at about 300 years, are filled with statues of demons and judges, and some of the tests of the dead are re-enacted for visitors. It is a regular stop for Yangtze cruise ships.

rows.name: Fenghuang Mountain Lantern Folk Culture Area, Xiushan
rows.summary: A hill park at about 600 m on the eastern edge of the Xiushan county town, developed as a showcase for the Xiushan flower-lantern song and dance, a national intangible-heritage tradition. It joins the Fenghuang Mountain forest park and its old temples, a Lingguan hall built in the early Yuan and Chuandeng Temple of 1575, with a lantern gallery, a lantern food street and evening light shows.

rows.name: Fengsheng Ancient Town
rows.summary: Fengsheng, in the hills of eastern Ba'nan, grew as an overland trading post, is nicknamed the 'first dry port on the Yangtze' and is listed among China's historic and cultural towns. Its old quarter keeps fortified watchtowers in the local Sichuan–Chongqing style, streets laid out in a nested-square plan and Ziyun 'ringing stones' that chime when struck, and the town is being developed as a showcase of old commercial culture.

rows.name: Former Legislative Yuan, Judicial Yuan and Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission
rows.name_zh: 国民政府立法院、司法院及蒙藏委员会旧址
rows.pinyin: Guómín Zhèngfǔ Lìfǎyuàn, Sīfǎyuàn jí Méng-Zàng Wěiyuánhuì Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A building at Guanyinyan put up in 1935 as the private Yilin Hospital and taken over from 1937 by the wartime Legislative Yuan, Judicial Yuan, Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission and other government offices. It went back to the hospital after the war and is now the outpatient building of Chongqing Zhongshan Hospital, so it is seen from Zhongshan 1st Road.

rows.name: Former Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Nationalist Government
rows.summary: A two-storey brick-and-timber building mixing Chinese and Western styles, with an upper veranda, inside People's Park in central Yuzhong. Built as the left wing of the Ba County council, it housed Chongqing High School from 1929 and the Foreign Ministry's offices during the war; it was taken down and rebuilt in 1996 and is used by the district's heritage office, and the Yuzhong District Museum lists its main site at the same address.

rows.name: Former Residences of Yang Angong and Yang Shangkun
rows.summary: The family houses in Shuangjiang of Yang Angong (1898–1927), an early Communist Party organiser in Sichuan who was executed in 1927, and of his younger brother Yang Shangkun, President of China from 1988 to 1993. Yang Angong's Qing courtyard house on the main street has exhibitions on his life and on the family, and Yang Shangkun's birthplace, the Changtanzi compound of 1862 at Jinlong village on the edge of town, holds an exhibition of photographs, objects and documents on his career. The scenic area also takes in the Tianba compound, a large Yang family courtyard house of 1878, and the brothers' cemeteries, Yang Angong's being in Tongnan town about 10 km away.

rows.name: Former Roosevelt Library
rows.summary: A library built of local stone and timber in 1938–41 for the wartime Chongqing branch of the National Central Library, which became the National Roosevelt Library in 1947 in memory of US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, the only library in China named after a foreign president. Later part of the Chongqing Library and then the city's children's library, it was restored and opened to the public in May 2026 with an exhibition on its history from 1945 to 1949 and reading rooms for United Nations and Stilwell documents.

rows.name: Former Site of the National Political Council
rows.summary: A three-storey brick-and-timber building in mixed Chinese and Western style on Zhonghua Road in the Jiefangbei shopping district, listed as the wartime site of the National Political Council (1938–1946), the advisory assembly in which the Nationalists, the Communists, smaller parties and independents sat together during the war against Japan. The council was set up in Wuhan in July 1938 and moved to Chongqing that November.

rows.name: Former Western China Academy of Sciences
rows.summary: The 1930s campus of the Western China Academy of Sciences, a private research institute founded in Beibei in 1930 by the shipping entrepreneur Lu Zuofu, which during the war with Japan gave a home to scientific bodies moved from eastern China. Its main building, the grey-walled, two-storey Huiyu Building of 1934, holds an exhibition on the academy's history that includes a relief map of China's terrain made in 1944; the geology building, Lu Zuofu's former residence and a geomagnetic survey marker stand nearby. The campus is now the historic site of the Chongqing Natural History Museum, with displays on early science in western China and the wartime move of research bodies inland.

rows.name: Furong River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The lower gorge of the Furong River, the largest tributary of the Wu River, a national scenic area since 2002 that runs for 35 km from Haokou to Jiangkou through a V-shaped karst canyon with largely untouched forest on both sides. Part of the river is a buffer zone of the Wulong Karst World Heritage site, and Furong Cave opens on its bank near Jiangkou.

rows.name: Geleshan Martyrs' Cemetery (Baigongguan and Zhazidong)
rows.summary: A memorial park at the foot of Gele Mountain on ground that in the 1940s held a base of the Nationalist intelligence service (Juntong), where the wartime Sino-American Special Technical Cooperative Organization (SACO) was also set up, and its two prisons for political detainees: Baigongguan, a former villa, and Zhazidong, a former coal pit. Days before the People's Liberation Army took Chongqing at the end of November 1949, most of the prisoners, many of them underground Communist Party members, were executed, an event known in China as the '27 November massacre'. The site has the restored prisons, an exhibition hall, a cemetery and monuments; the Chinese official name of the heritage unit is the 'SACO concentration camp site'.

rows.name: Geleshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded ridge on the western edge of central Chongqing, made a national forest park in 2004, whose highest point, 693 m, is at Yunding Temple. Six marked hiking trails climb through the forest, the rocks around Yunding Temple carry inscriptions by the calligrapher Ke Huang and his friends, and a cable car also runs up the hill.

rows.name: Gongtan Ancient Town
rows.summary: Gongtan stands where the Apeng River flows into the Wu River, facing Guizhou across the water, and was known for its long flagstone street and timber stilt houses propped on the rocky bank. When the Pengshui hydropower dam flooded the original town, its buildings were dismantled and rebuilt about 1 km downstream between 2007 and 2009, so what visitors see today is a relocated reconstruction.

rows.name: Guanyinqiao Shopping District
rows.summary: One of central Chongqing's main shopping districts, centred on a pedestrian street and plaza in Jiangbei north of the Jialing River. Department stores, malls and restaurants surround it, making it one of the city's busiest places for shopping and eating out.

rows.name: Guanyintang Wetland Park
rows.summary: An urban wetland park in central Bishan, built in the 2010s as one of the district's main city parks during a programme of river clean-up and new green spaces. Its waterside paths make it a quiet place for a stroll.

rows.name: Guiyuan
rows.summary: The house of the Nationalist general Zhang Zhizhong on Zhongshan 4th Road, lent to Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai as their working base during the Chongqing negotiations of August–October 1945; the 'Double Tenth Agreement' between the Communists and the Nationalist government was signed here on 10 October 1945. The two-storey brick-and-timber villa, named after the two osmanthus trees in its courtyard, has been open as an exhibition since 1977 and is run by the Hongyan Revolutionary Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Guiyuan Town (Jingzhu Village), Fairy Mountain
rows.summary: A rural tourism project in Jingzhu village on the Fairy Mountain plateau, where old farmhouses have been restored and joined by new buildings of rammed earth, glass and steel, among them a village library with a café and a cluster of boutique guesthouses. The village, at 800–1,300 m among karst hills, was named one of UN Tourism's Best Tourism Villages in 2022 and also has fruit-picking farms.

rows.name: Gujian Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain near Qijiang town, counted among the 'New Twelve Views of Bayu', where visitors climb for sunrise and seas of cloud from the summit. Jingyin Temple, a working Buddhist temple, stands near the top, and campsites and holiday lodgings at the foot make it a weekend retreat.

rows.name: Guo Moruo's Former Residences (Third Department and Cultural Work Committee Sites)
rows.summary: The two wartime offices of the Third Department of the Military Affairs Commission's Political Department, which ran anti-Japanese propaganda under the writer and historian Guo Moruo from 1938, and of the Cultural Work Committee he led from 1940 until it was disbanded in 1945. The country office, Quanjia Yuanzi, a late-Qing courtyard house in Xiyong where Guo wrote historical plays such as Qu Yuan, has been the Guo Moruo Memorial Hall since 2005. The city office at 8 Tianguanfu in Yuzhong, a 1930s house later used as homes, was restored and opened with an exhibition in 2021.

rows.name: Haichang Caribbean Water World
rows.summary: An outdoor water park on Nanshan, the ridge above the south bank of the Yangtze, run by the Haichang group, with water slides, a children's splash area and a wave pool. It opens only in the summer season, usually from mid-May, and suits families looking for a break from Chongqing's summer heat.

rows.name: Hailan Yuntian Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort around Hailan Lake in Chongqing's western suburbs, combining outdoor and indoor spring pools with a lakeside hotel, boating and hillside walks over roughly 100 hectares. It is a family weekend retreat rather than a sightseeing destination.

rows.name: Hanfeng Lake
rows.summary: A lake created in the heart of Kaizhou by a regulating dam that since 2017 has held the water at 170–175 m, so that the falling Three Gorges reservoir no longer leaves bare mudflats around the town. It covers about 15 km² with more than 30 bays and 41 islands; lakeside parks and wetlands, a covered bridge, the Juziyuan garden with the Wenfeng Pagoda and the newly built Kaizhou Old Town line its shores. Boat trips and water sports such as kayaking and paddleboarding run from the lakeside.

rows.name: Hanhai Ocean Park
rows.summary: A large aquarium and marine park at Longzhouwan in Ba'nan, with a 360-degree coral-reef tank, a shark hall, an underwater tunnel, a penguin house and the Aegean Theatre for staged shows. It suits families, and a Hanhai-branded whale-and-dolphin water park lies nearby.

rows.name: Happy Valley Chongqing
rows.summary: A large theme park opened in July 2017 as the seventh in the Happy Valley chain of the Overseas Chinese Town group, with roller coasters including a wooden coaster and a wing coaster, family rides and stage shows. In summer its Maya Beach water park adds a wave pool and water slides, and it suits families and thrill-ride fans looking for a full day out.

rows.name: Heishan Valley and Wansheng Stone Forest
rows.summary: A 13 km gorge walk through dense forest in Heishan town near the Guizhou border, past waterfalls, pools, floating walkways and a great rift canyon, in a valley where François' langurs and dove trees are among the rare species recorded. The 5A listing also covers the Wansheng Stone Forest, or 'Dragon-Scale Stone Sea', a national geopark of karst pinnacles and caves whose rock surfaces are covered in scale-like ridges.

rows.name: Hong'an Ancient Town (Biancheng)
rows.summary: An old river town where Chongqing, Guizhou and Hunan meet, about 47 km south-east of the Xiushan county town, said to be the model for the setting of Shen Congwen's novella Border Town (Biancheng). Its sights include a pavilion where 'a cock's crow is heard in three provinces' and a monument to the Second Field Army's 1949 advance into the south-west, and a long-running immersive show, Meeting Biancheng, stages Tujia wedding customs around the town; a newer resort quarter nearby adds evening shows.

rows.name: Hongensi Forest Park
rows.summary: An urban forest park opened in 2009 on Longji Ridge in Jiangbei, north of the Jialing River, planted with many varieties of osmanthus along themed walks. On the summit stands Hong'en Pavilion, a seven-storey tower in Ming–Qing style whose viewing deck looks over the Yuzhong peninsula, Liangjiang New Area and Shapingba.

rows.name: Huanghuacheng Island City
rows.summary: An island in the Yangtze that held a walled city of the late Southern Song, the seat of Xianchun Prefecture, and one of the best-preserved Song and Yuan town sites in the reservoir area. Excavations since 2016 have traced its gates, walls, government offices, an academy and workshops, now shown on site and in a display centre opened in May 2026, while the rest of the island is a national wetland park.

rows.name: Huangshan Wartime Capital Sites
rows.summary: From 1938 to 1946, when Chongqing was China's wartime capital, Chiang Kai-shek and the Military Affairs Commission used a group of villas hidden in the pine woods of Huangshan, a hill in the Nanshan range, as residences and offices. The 15 listed sites include Yunxiu Lou, Chiang's three-storey residence, Songting, the aides' and guards' quarters, a small school and the air-raid shelter below the house, and the complex is now run as the Chongqing Anti-Japanese War Sites Museum.

rows.name: Huashi Ancient Fort
rows.summary: A fortified hamlet on top of a steep, isolated peak in Huashi village, near Shuanggui Temple, used as a military stronghold in the Ming and Qing periods, which keeps old watchtowers, gateways and a stone hall. It is now run as a scenic area with viewing terraces and a gallery of local crafts, alongside added attractions such as a long two-stage dry slide and a glass bridge.

rows.name: Huatian Rice Terraces
rows.summary: Rice terraces step down the hillsides around Hejiayan village in Huatian township, at an average altitude of about 800 m, and have been farmed for more than 400 years. Restored from 2012, the roughly 8,000 mu (about 530 ha) of terraces now grow organic 'Huatian tribute rice' and turn gold before the autumn harvest.

rows.name: Huayan Temple
rows.summary: A large working Buddhist monastery beside Huayan Lake on the south-western edge of central Chongqing, whose older buildings are protected as a Chongqing municipal heritage site. The temple has been much extended since the early 2000s and houses the Chongqing Buddhist College, and the surrounding scenic area adds lakeside gardens, a cave, a large outdoor Buddha statue and the Huayan Buddhist Museum.

rows.name: Huguang Guild Hall
rows.summary: A complex of Qing-dynasty guild halls on the Yangtze at Dongshuimen, built by merchants and settlers from Hubei, Hunan and Guangdong who came with the early-Qing migration known as 'Huguang fills Sichuan'. Its Yuwang Temple, Qi'an Hall and Guangdong Hall, largely rebuilt in 1846, have courtyards, halls and opera stages, and together with newer buildings in the same style they house a museum of that migration.

rows.name: Huilong Manor
rows.summary: A large fortified manor at Shuangfeng village on the northern edge of the Simian Mountain area, regarded as one of the finest historic estates in south-west China. Its stone-and-timber courtyard buildings cover more than 2 ha and stand on 328 stone pillars beside a 38 m watchtower; who built it and when has not been established. It is usually combined with a visit to Simian Mountain or Zhongshan Ancient Town.

rows.name: Jialing River Rural Reconstruction Sites (Lu Zuofu Memorial Hall)
rows.name_zh: 嘉陵江三峡乡村建设旧址群
rows.pinyin: Jiālíng Jiāng Sānxiá Xiāngcūn Jiànshè Jiùzhǐqún
rows.summary: Ten buildings across Beibei left by the rural reconstruction movement that Lu Zuofu led from 1927 as head of the local defence bureau, when he set out to turn the Jialing gorges area into a planned, modern district. The former bureau office, an old Wenchang temple at Wenxingwan, is now the Lu Zuofu Memorial Hall; other parts include the Red House, now the Beibei art gallery, and Qingliang Pavilion in Beibei Park, a group of villas in North Hot Spring Park, and the former Rural Reconstruction College at Xiema, now a memorial hall to the educator James Yen.

rows.name: Jiefangbei (People's Liberation Monument)
rows.summary: The clock tower at the heart of Chongqing's main shopping district, built in 1946–47 as the Monument to the Victory in the War of Resistance on the site of a wartime wooden 'Spiritual Fortress', and renamed the People's Liberation Monument in 1950. The octagonal tower, with clock faces and relief panels near the top, stands where Minzu, Minquan and Zourong roads meet, in a pedestrian square ringed by malls and office towers. It is the usual starting point for exploring central Yuzhong, with Hongyadong a short walk to the north.

rows.name: Jin'ao Rural Park (Jin'ao Mountain)
rows.summary: A rural leisure area on Jin'ao Mountain in Tiaodeng town, at the southern tip of Dadukou facing the Yangtze, among the nearest countryside to central Chongqing. Coloured terraced fields, farm restaurants and guesthouses spread over the hill, which rises to 495 m, and the area was rated 4A in 2024.

rows.name: Jindao Gorge
rows.summary: A limestone gorge about 10 km long on the south-western slopes of the Huaying Mountains in north-eastern Beibei, where a stream has cut along a fault into a deep, narrow canyon of potholes and clear pools. Sights along the route include waterfalls, caves and a slot section called the 'thread of sky', and the steep fall of the stream has made the gorge a place for canyoning.

rows.name: Jingzhuba Cliff Coffins
rows.summary: Coffins placed in natural recesses high in a cliff at Jingzhuba, in the valley north of Wuxi county town, dated to the Han dynasty or earlier. Wuxi promotes them as the earliest and most complete group of Western Han cliff coffins in the Three Gorges region.

rows.name: Jinyun Mountain
rows.summary: A forested ridge above the Jialing River on the north-western edge of Beibei, protected as a national nature reserve and long a centre of Buddhism in the Chongqing area. Its main temple, Jinyun Temple, was founded in 423 and rebuilt in 1683; in 1932 the monk Taixu set up the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute here, and the temple, its Ming-dynasty gateway and stone carvings are protected as the national heritage site of that institute. Paths lead through the woods from the temple to viewpoints on the peaks.

rows.name: Jiuchongtian Scenic Area
rows.summary: A clifftop attraction at over 1,000 m in Lianhuadong village in the hills of Shuanglu, built from 2015 and opened in 2017. Its main features are a glass-floored bridge about 280 m long over a sheer drop, a glass cliff walkway of about 3.5 km and thrill rides such as cliff swings, and it draws summer visitors to the cool mountain air.

rows.name: Kaizhifeng Peony Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hillside peony park at Mudan village in Taiping town, on the Mingyue Mountains, the centre of Dianjiang's long tradition of peony growing, where many varieties bloom in April and May. It is named after the 4th-century painter Gu Kaizhi, who according to local legend saw Dianjiang's peonies, and has a petal-shaped glass viewing platform.

rows.name: Kaizhou Museum
rows.summary: The district museum of Kaizhou, opened in 2013 on the Civic Square beside Hanfeng Lake, with seven galleries and more than 10,000 objects on the history and culture of the old Kai County. It stands on the lakeside promenade, so it combines easily with a walk around Hanfeng Lake.

rows.name: Kuizhou Museum
rows.summary: The museum of Fengjie County, long known as Kuizhou, opened in 2017 on the eastern edge of the county town and holds more than 20,000 objects, from carvings the museum attributes to 'Fengjie Man' some 130,000 years ago to a large Chu-style bronze ding, an Eastern Han pottery horse and Song-dynasty porcelain. Its grounds take in the Yaokui Pagoda on its original site, the rebuilt Yidou and Kaiji city gates with a stretch of the old prefectural wall, and the Dacheng Hall of the former Confucian temple.

rows.name: Laitan Ancient Town & Erfo Temple
rows.summary: A walled old town on a hill above the Qu River, dating from the Song dynasty, with Ming- and Qing-era houses, flagstone lanes and a Qing barbican gate, and one of the first ten towns named a Chinese Historic Town in 2003. Beside it, Erfo Temple shelters Song-dynasty cliff carvings, among them a large seated Buddha and rare groups of figures from the Chan (Zen) school.

rows.name: Lanying Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A deep canyon near Lanying township in eastern Wuxi, promoted locally as one of the deepest gorges in Asia. Its best-known sight is the Lanying 'sky road', a narrow road cut into the cliffs high above the gorge, which has become a popular drive and photo stop.

rows.name: Lehe Ledu Theme Park
rows.summary: An animal-themed park on the edge of Yongchuan with a large zoo where giant and red pandas, chimpanzees, elephants, giraffes, lions and tigers can be seen. It adds a children's play area, evening events and staged animal shows, is aimed at families and gets very busy on public holidays.

rows.name: Lesser Three Gorges & Mini Three Gorges
rows.summary: Boat trips from Wushan town up the Daning River, which joins the Yangtze there, pass through its three gorges, Longmen, Bawu and Dicui, about 50 km in all, before visitors change at the Madu River to smaller boats for the narrower Mini Three Gorges. Macaques live on the cliffs, especially in Bawu Gorge, and in late autumn the slopes are among Wushan's main red-leaf areas. A combined boat-and-road loop goes on to Dachang, a small walled town that was a seat of local government from the Jin dynasty and was taken down and rebuilt on a new site downstream for the reservoir, keeping three of its gates.

rows.name: Liangjiang International Film City
rows.summary: A film and television set built from 2012, first for the film Back to 1942, that recreates wartime Chongqing of the 1930s and 1940s, when the city was China's provisional capital. Its 'Republic of China Street' has more than 200 replica buildings, among them the Victory Monument, the Nationalist government building, banks, a theatre and the Xinhua Daily office, and it was enlarged between 2015 and 2017.

rows.name: Liu Bocheng Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum to Marshal Liu Bocheng in Shengshan Park in central Kaizhou, opened in December 1992 for the centenary of his birth, with its name written by Deng Xiaoping. Six halls hold an exhibition on his life and military career drawn from a collection of more than 4,500 items, and it is one of China's officially listed 'red tourism' classic sites.

rows.name: Liu Bocheng's Former Residence
rows.summary: The family home in Zhoudu village, south of the Kaizhou town, where Liu Bocheng, the one-eyed marshal of the People's Liberation Army, was born in 1892. The house is protected as a national heritage site and has displays on his early life, and the surrounding village is run as the 'Marshal Liu's Hometown, Red Zhoudu' scenic area.

rows.name: Liujia Wharf
rows.summary: A riverside leisure complex on the Beibin Road waterfront in Jiangbei, with restaurants, bars and riverside entertainment by the Jialing River. Jiangbei District promoted it in 2021 as its second municipal-level night-market street after the Jiujie bar district, and it is mainly a place for dinner and drinks by the river.

rows.name: Longgang National Geopark
rows.summary: A karst area of about 17 km² in Qingshui Tujia Township whose centrepiece, Longgang, is a sheer-walled tiankeng (giant sinkhole), with the caves of Da'an Cave and the canyon of the Shisun River nearby. The Cloud Corridor, a glass walkway cantilevered out from the cliff top, is the best-known viewpoint.

rows.name: Longqiao River
rows.summary: A karst river valley in Longqiao Tujia Township where a stream fed by an underground river system about 50 km long flows for some 3.7 km at the surface, passing beneath a large natural rock bridge that spans the canyon. The valley lies at about 1,500 m among densely forested mountains.

rows.name: Longshuixia Fissure Gorge
rows.summary: A deep, narrow slot canyon cut into the limestone south of the Three Natural Bridges, inside the same Wulong Karst World Heritage area. A lift takes visitors down into the fissure.

rows.name: Longtan Ancient Town
rows.summary: Longtan, the main town of eastern Youyang, is a listed Chinese Historical and Cultural Town whose old streets are run as a scenic area. Its best-known building is the childhood home of Zhao Shiyan (1901–1927), an early Chinese Communist leader who co-founded the Chinese Youth Communist Party in France with Zhou Enlai and was executed in Shanghai in 1927; the house is a national heritage site kept as a memorial.

rows.name: Longtouzui Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the hills of Zishui township in northern Kaizhou, promoted by the district as a forest sports park, with woodland walks and open lawns. It is mainly a cool summer retreat for people from the Kaizhou area.

rows.name: Marshal Nie Rongzhen Exhibition Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum to Nie Rongzhen, the Jiangjin-born marshal who directed China's nuclear-weapons and satellite programmes, opened in 1999 at the foot of Aiping Mountain on the edge of Jiangjin's urban area. Its main building centres on a 36 m tower shaped like a rocket carrying a satellite, and the exhibition follows his life in five sections, from work-study in France and the Jin-Cha-Ji base area of the war against Japan to the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' programme. In front, a bronze statue stands above a square displaying a retired fighter aircraft, artillery and missiles.

rows.name: Meixin Red Wine Town
rows.summary: A leisure town beside the Yangtze at Linshi, with Chinese- and European-style buildings, an amusement park, a ferris wheel, riverside guesthouses and the 'Foreigners' Street' that moved here from central Chongqing. Since 2022 a network of cable-car lines has linked it to vineyards, a winery and a second, larger ferris wheel on the hills above, and it is mainly a weekend outing for families.

rows.name: Mount Jinfo
rows.summary: A flat-topped limestone massif in the Dalou Mountains, ringed by cliffs up to 300 m high and rising to over 2,200 m at Fengchuiling, which joined the South China Karst World Heritage Site in 2014. The plateau has forests, caves and karst landforms and an exceptional range of plants, with more than 4,700 seed-plant species, and it is a refuge for the rare François' langur. Cable cars from the north and west slopes reach the top, where there are ski slopes in winter.

rows.name: Mount Puti
rows.summary: A 598 m hill above Changshou's Puti Ancient Town, named after Bodhidharma according to the county annals, with the Buddhist Puti Temple on its summit. The temple, first built in the Northern Song dynasty and destroyed several times, was rebuilt in 2014 as a large timber complex of gate, bell and drum towers and halls, reached by a long stone stairway decorated with the character shou, 'longevity'.

rows.name: Mowei Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain near Pengshui town, at around 1,400 m above sea level, with forest cover of about 91 per cent, listed as one of China's 'forest oxygen bars'. In 2021 it became one of the first national youth nature-education camps, and the county is developing it as a mountain holiday resort.

rows.name: Nanmuwan Golden Nanmu Grove
rows.summary: Nanmuwan, in Jinsinan ('golden-thread nanmu') village of Liangzeng township in western Youyang, is known for a large grove of golden-thread nanmu (Phoebe zhennan), a prized hardwood, including several trees more than 1,000 years old. Stone-flagged paths run between the trees and the village's traditional houses.

rows.name: Nanshan Rock Carvings, Dazu
rows.summary: A small group of Daoist carvings at the Yuhuang Temple on the hilltop about 2 km south of Dazu town, cut mainly in the Southern Song (1131–1162) and one of the five Dazu groups on the World Heritage list. The Sanqing Cave has a square central pillar and rows of small standing deities around its walls, and a dragon carved as the main figure of its own cave is rare in Chinese cave art; Song and Qing steles stand alongside. The site opened formally to visitors in July 2024.

rows.name: Nantian Lake
rows.summary: A mountain resort area at 1,400–2,000 m about 45 km south of the Fengdu county town, built around a lake in forest that covers nearly nine-tenths of the land. It is a summer retreat from the Chongqing heat and in winter runs a ski area, with lakeside walks, camping and hotels, and it was named a national tourist resort in 2020.

rows.name: Nanwenquan (South Hot Springs)
rows.summary: Developed as a park from 1927 around hot springs known since the Ming dynasty, Nanwenquan in Ba'nan combines spring baths, boat trips on the Huaxi River, a cliff waterfall and gardens. During the war years Lin Sen, Kong Xiangxi and Chiang Kai-shek built retreats beside the springs, and their villas, with the former research department of the Central Political Institute, form the Nanquan wartime sites, a national heritage group.

rows.name: Nanyaojie Red Army Base Sites
rows.name_zh: 南腰界红三军司令部旧址
rows.pinyin: Nányāojiè Hóng Sān Jūn Sīlìngbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: In 1934 the Red Third Army, led by He Long and Guan Xiangying, made the small town of Nanyaojie, in the hills of southern Youyang, the centre of its Sichuan–Guizhou revolutionary base area, with headquarters in a Qing-dynasty courtyard house, the Yu family compound. The scenic area takes in the preserved headquarters, with the rooms He Long and Guan Xiangying used, and some 34 other relics of that period, among them the meeting ground where the Second and Sixth Red Army Groups joined forces, the Daba ancestral hall, the army's political department and Red Army graves.

rows.name: Nie Rongzhen's Former Residence
rows.summary: The family home at Langjia village near Wutan where Nie Rongzhen, later a marshal of the People's Liberation Army who led China's nuclear-weapons and satellite programmes, was born in 1899. Known locally as Shiyuanzi, it is a Qing-dynasty timber compound of three halls; most of it burnt down in 1923 and it was rebuilt on the old plan in 1988. Rooms show furniture and objects from his childhood and schooling in Jiangjin, and the surrounding village is run as the Marshal Nie's Hometown scenic area.

rows.name: North Hot Spring Park (Beiwenquan)
rows.summary: A riverside park at the foot of Jinyun Mountain, on the south bank of the Jialing River's Wentang Gorge, laid out around Wenquan Temple, founded in 423 and rebuilt in 1432. In 1927 Lu Zuofu turned the temple grounds into the Jialing River Hot Spring Park, adding swimming pools, baths and a restaurant, and the springs, which stay above 40°C all year, are still used for bathing. Several 1930s villas in the park belong to the national heritage group of Beibei's rural reconstruction sites.

rows.name: Peng Ancestral Hall
rows.summary: A fortress-like clan hall of the Peng family in Liming Village, completed in 1864 after some 20 years of building, whose nine-storey tower rises above the surrounding woods. The walled compound of about 3,500 m² holds a theatre stage, schoolrooms, side halls and watch and gun towers, with carved beams, lattice windows and stepped gable walls. The restored hall and the Peng family houses around it form a listed traditional village that receives study groups and day visitors.

rows.name: Puti Ancient Town (Changshou Ancient Town)
rows.summary: A new town built in traditional Ba-Yu style at the foot of Puti Mountain on the edge of Changshou's urban area, rated 4A in 2014, with canals, a main street and old-style buildings including a yamen, an opera stage, a City God temple, a Confucian temple and gate towers. Its theme is longevity, a play on the district's name, and it holds festivals such as a hotpot festival.

rows.name: Qianjiang City Grand Canyon (Balahu)
rows.summary: A gorge about 10 km long and some 200 m deep that runs through the middle of Qianjiang city, separating the old town from the new district, developed as a scenic area under the Tujia name Balahu, meaning 'gorge'. Its cliffs, woods and caves hold temples, pavilions and rock carvings, including a 123 m figure of Guanyin carved into the cliff face. It is the easiest of Qianjiang's sights to reach from the city centre.

rows.name: Qianye Grassland
rows.summary: An upland grassland in Yuchi town in northern Shizhu, high enough to stay cool in summer, with open pasture, woods and rocks grazed by cattle and sheep. Visitors come to camp and watch the stars in summer and to see the red firethorn berries that cover the slopes in autumn, and a zip line and cliff swing have been added.

rows.name: Qicai Dream Garden
rows.summary: A rural leisure park in Huangjuemen village on the south side of Tongliang, next to Xuantian Lake, with flower fields planted for each season, fruit and vegetable picking, a woodland area and a small Bayu-style village street with shops and guesthouses. Families come for the water play area, children's rides, mini-train and grass sledding, and Tongliang's fire-dragon dance is staged here at festivals.

rows.name: Red Rock Village (Hongyan) Revolutionary Memorial
rows.summary: The hillside compound by the Jialing River where the Chinese Communist Party's Southern Bureau and the Eighth Route Army's Chongqing liaison office worked from 1939 until early 1947, during the wartime alliance with the Nationalist government. Zhou Enlai lived and worked here, and Mao Zedong stayed for 41 days during the 1945 Chongqing negotiations; the office building, which looks two-storeyed from outside but has three floors, keeps their offices, bedrooms and the secret radio room. A memorial hall completed beside it in 2000 covers the bureau's history, and the protected site also includes the Zengjiayan 50 residence and the former Xinhua Daily sales office in central Yuzhong.

rows.name: Rongchang Xiabu Town
rows.summary: A shopping and leisure quarter of 24 courtyard buildings in Ming and Qing style, completed in 2015 and named after xiabu, the ramie cloth whose weaving is one of Rongchang's national intangible heritage crafts. Besides xiabu shops it has restaurants, bars and night markets, and it hosts many of the district's festivals and evening events.

rows.name: Ronghui Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort complex at Lishuwan in urban Shapingba, with outdoor and indoor spa pools, a water-play area and hotels. Its small restaurant-and-shop street, Quanli Xiaozhen, has hosted summer evening markets, and the resort suits a relaxing half-day rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Sanhe Lake Wetland Park
rows.summary: An urban wetland park of about 140 hectares around the Sanhe Lake reservoir in the eastern new district of Dianjiang town, opened in July 2022 with a ring path linking eight zones, wetland planting and an island. Billed as Dianjiang's first 'smart park', it has digital guides and a running track whose roadside screens show runners their distance and laps; it is mainly a local recreation space, best combined with Dianjiang's spring peony season.

rows.name: Sanxia Yuanxiang (Three Gorges Homeland)
rows.summary: A rural scenic area in the karst uplands of Xinglong Town, opened around 2020, built around a pair of cliffs that locals call Dry Kuimen for their likeness to the gate of Qutang Gorge, and a cave known as Shenxian Cave. Flower fields, winding flower terraces and a children's farm fill the valley, part of the Xinglong resort area that Fengjie promotes as a cool summer retreat.

rows.name: Shenlong Gorge
rows.summary: A forested gorge near Nanping on the western side of the Jinfo Mountain range, with a walking trail past waterfalls and pools and a rafting run down its stream in summer. It was rated 5A jointly with Mount Jinfo in 2013, lost that status in 2016 and has been a 4A in its own right since 2022.

rows.name: Shibaozhai
rows.summary: A sheer rock outcrop on the north bank of the Yangtze in Shibao Town, climbed by a red timber pavilion built against the cliff in the early 19th century and raised from nine to twelve storeys in 1956, with a Buddhist hall on the summit. Since the reservoir filled, the rock stands as an island protected by a large ring dyke, and many Yangtze cruise ships stop here.

rows.name: Shimen Great Buddha Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Song- to Yuan-dynasty Buddhist carvings in the cliff at Shimen, beside the Yangtze in western Jiangjin, listed as a national heritage site in 2013. The main figure is a standing Guanyin about 13.5 m tall with her feet on lotus flowers, sheltered by a seven-eaved timber hall built against the rock.

rows.name: Shimenshan Rock Carvings, Dazu
rows.summary: A 72 m cliff of Buddhist and Daoist carvings at Shimen village, about 20 km east of Dazu town, cut between 1094 and 1151 and one of the five Dazu groups on the World Heritage list. The Daoist figures stand out, among them the Jade Emperor flanked by the guardians Thousand-Li Eye and Wind-Following Ear, the Three Sovereigns cave and a tableau of the God of the Eastern Peak, while the cave of the Western Three Saints and Ten Guanyin holds ten tall, crowned bodhisattvas. The site opened formally to visitors in July 2024.

rows.name: Shisun Mountain (Yunwuping)
rows.summary: A pair of forested hills on the border of Jiangjin and Yongchuan, known locally as the 'male' and 'female' Shisun peaks, with a small lake, several Buddhist and Taoist shrines and the old walls of the Yunwuping hill fort. It is a place for hill walks, cloud views and temple visits rather than major sights.

rows.name: Shuanggui Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A lake of about 120 hectares on the south-western side of the Liangping district town, a reservoir of 1951 that was cleaned up from around 2010 and turned into a wetland park of reed beds, channels and small wetlands crossed by boardwalks. More than 200 bird species have been recorded there, and it is the best-known wetland of Liangping, which has been named an International Wetland City.

rows.name: Shuanggui Temple
rows.summary: A Chan Buddhist monastery founded in 1653 by the master Poshan Haiming and named after its two osmanthus trees, known as an ancestral seat of Chan in south-west China and listed among the country's key Buddhist temples since 1983. Seven buildings stand on its main axis, among them the Mahavira Hall on 72 stone columns, Poshan's stupa, the Hall of Great Compassion and the sutra library, which keeps a Buddhist canon presented by the Yongzheng Emperor; a hall of 500 arhats was added in 1998. The fields, lotus ponds and wetlands around the temple are being developed as the Shuanggui Tianyuan scenic area, which so far adds a vegetarian food centre and visitor centre.

rows.name: Shuangjiang Ancient Town
rows.summary: A market town near the south bank of the Fu River, founded in the early Qing and named after the two streams that wind around it, which keeps more than 20 Qing-dynasty courtyard houses along flagstone lanes and small bridges. Among them are the Yuwang Palace, a Huguang guild hall with an opera stage, and the family houses of Yang Angong and Yang Shangkun, which are kept as memorial museums; it was named one of China's first historic and cultural towns in 2003.

rows.name: Simian Mountain
rows.summary: A forested upland on a spur of the Dalou Mountains in southern Jiangjin, where red sandstone cliffs, lakes and more than a hundred waterfalls are spread over a scenic area of about 213 km². The best-known sight is the Wangxiangtai Waterfall, about 150 m high, whose cliff outline is likened to a heart; other areas include Longtan Lake, the Honghai lake and Pearl Lake. It is a cool summer retreat for people from Chongqing and suits one or two days of walking between the falls and lakes.

rows.name: Snowy Jade Cave
rows.summary: A limestone show cave in Fengdu known for the unusually white, jade-like colour of its formations, which are still growing. It runs for 1,644 m on three levels, and its highlights include a stone 'flag' about 8 m long, a stone shield about 4 m high and dense clusters of coral-like growths and soda-straw stalactites.

rows.name: Songgai Ancient Town
rows.summary: A river port on the north bank of the Yangtze in southern Yongchuan, listed among China's historic and cultural towns, whose flagstone streets lead past riverside teahouses with storytellers, the old county yamen and the site of a wartime cotton-spinning mill. Nearby are the Ming-dynasty Chen Gong weir and the tomb of the Southern Song classicist Chen Shaonan, and the town became a 4A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Soong Ching-ling's Former Residence (China Defence League Headquarters)
rows.summary: A German-style brick-and-timber house of 1937 at Lianglukou where Soong Ching-ling, widow of Sun Yat-sen, lived from 1942 to 1945 and ran the China Defence League, the organisation she founded to support China's resistance against Japan. Her office and bedroom and the league's office and meeting room are shown as an exhibition, now a branch of the Three Gorges Museum; it first opened in 1993 and reopened in 2013 after repairs.

rows.name: South Mountain Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A large botanical garden on the wooded crest of Nanshan above the south bank of the Yangtze, with themed gardens for roses, camellias, plum blossom and orchids and a garden of rare and endangered plants; its camellia collection is recognised as an International Camellia Garden of Excellence. Within the camellia garden stand villas that housed the French embassy, the Indian commissioner's office and part of the Soviet embassy when Chongqing was China's wartime capital. A giant golden eagle statue on the ridge is a local landmark.

rows.name: Stilwell Museum
rows.summary: The 1930s house on Jialing New Road that was the home and headquarters of the US general Joseph Stilwell from 1942 to 1944, when he was Allied chief of staff in the China theatre and commanded US forces in China, Burma and India. His office, bedroom, adjutant's room, meeting rooms and air-raid basement are furnished as they were, with displays of his manuscripts, uniforms and belongings. The museum was refurbished and reopened in August 2023.

rows.name: Sun Lake (Taiyang Lake), Huangshui
rows.summary: A reservoir lake in the highlands of Huangshui, in the south-east of Huangshui National Forest Park next to the Dafengbao forest, used for angling and water sports and as the venue of an open-water swimming race and the Huangshui triathlon. Like the rest of the Huangshui area it stays cool in summer, when it fills with visitors escaping the heat of Chongqing.

rows.name: Teyuan (Museum of the History of China's Democratic Parties)
rows.summary: The mansion of Xian Ying, a wartime supporter of the democratic movement, built in 1929–31 at Shangqingsi; the China Democratic League began here in 1941 as the League of Chinese Democratic Political Groups. Since 2008 its two three-storey villas have held a museum of China's non-Communist 'democratic parties', enlarged in 2011 and renamed the Museum of the History of China's Democratic Parties.

rows.name: Three Gorges Ladder City
rows.summary: A hillside park in the centre of Yunyang's new county town, which was built here from 1999 after the Three Gorges reservoir flooded the old town. It takes in the Three Gorges Cultural Relics Park and Panshi Fortress, a hilltop stronghold used from the Tang to the Qing dynasties, where stretches of stone wall and two gateways survive.

rows.name: Three Gorges Light Night Cruise
rows.summary: An evening show cruise launched at Wushan in 2021, on which visitors watch light projections across 152 buildings on both banks, the Goddess Temple and its hills and the Wushan Yangtze bridge, followed by a staged night show in Longmen Gorge. The show draws on local themes such as the Goddess of Wushan, the red autumn leaves and the resettlement of the reservoir towns.

rows.name: Three Gorges Museum
rows.summary: Chongqing's main history museum, opened in 2005 on People's Square opposite the People's Auditorium and one of China's national first-grade museums. Its four core galleries cover the Three Gorges, the ancient Ba people of the region, the growth of Chongqing as a city and its wartime years, and much of the collection comes from excavations in the area flooded by the Three Gorges Dam. Further galleries show paintings, ceramics, coins and Han-dynasty sculpture.

rows.name: Three Gorges Summit (Sanxia Zhidian)
rows.summary: A mountain-top scenic area opened in 2020 along more than 10 km of the ridge of Chijia Mountain above Kuimen, whose highest point, at 1,388 m, looks down on the Yangtze entering Qutang Gorge. Terraces and monuments along the ridge celebrate Kui, the legendary music master of ancient China, and a glass walkway runs along the cliff edge; a ridge-top hiking trail of about 10 km, the Taibai Bird Path, links the area with White Emperor City along the cliffs on the north side of the gorge.

rows.name: Tiankeng Difeng (Xiaozhai Tiankeng & Tianjing Gorge)
rows.summary: A karst area in Xinglong Town made up of Xiaozhai Tiankeng, a vertical-walled sinkhole more than 500 m deep whose name gave geologists the term tiankeng, and Tianjing Gorge, a narrow slot canyon some 37 km long. A long staircase descends into the sinkhole, beneath which an underground river runs, and the area lies at around 1,200 m with cool summers.

rows.name: Tianshengcheng Fortress Ruins
rows.summary: A natural rock mesa above Wanzhou with sheer cliffs on every side, fortified in the 13th century as one of the Southern Song mountain strongholds against the Mongols; the Song general Shangguan Kui held it through a siege of more than a month, and local tradition says Liu Bei of Shu Han once camped here. The ruins on the summit look out over the city.

rows.name: Tianxin Temple (Zhongtai Tianxin Buddhist Culture Area)
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple among old trees in the hills of Tianxingsi town in eastern Ba'nan, at the centre of a Buddhist culture area that the district promotes for tea drinking and meditation classes. Guesthouses, one of them in a restored old courtyard house, lie in the surrounding villages.

rows.name: Tieshanping Forest Park
rows.summary: A forested upland on the Tongluo Mountain ridge in the east of Liangjiang New Area, facing Nanshan across the Yangtze. Walking trails link its 'ten views', among them the old Sengguan Temple, the remains of an old battlefield and of works that once guarded the river, flower fields and lookouts over the Yangtze.

rows.name: Tomb of General Zhang Zizhong
rows.summary: The grave of Zhang Zizhong, the Nationalist army-group commander killed in Hubei in May 1940 during the Zaoyang–Yichang campaign, the highest-ranking Chinese officer to die in the war with Japan. After a state funeral he was buried here on Meihua Hill in November 1940; the large carved characters of the hill's name and the inscription on the tomb are by General Feng Yuxiang. The cemetery rises in three levels, with the round tomb at the top, a garden in the middle and a memorial hall by the square below.

rows.name: Tongjing Hot Spring Scenic Area
rows.summary: A hot-spring and gorge scenic area where the Wentang River leaves its gorge at Tongjing, in the far east of Beibei District (until 2025 part of Yubei). Springs here rise at up to 61°C and feed bathing pools, and the scenic area also takes in river gorges, caves and waterfalls.

rows.name: Tongnan Great Buddha Temple
rows.summary: A temple at the foot of Dingming Hill on the Fu River just west of Tongnan town, built against a cliff carved from the Sui to the Republican era with about 126 niches and more than 900 Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian figures. Its centrepiece is a gilded seated Buddha 18.43 m high, begun in the Tang and finished in the Song, sheltered by the seven-eaved Great Buddha Pavilion; the temple also keeps Guanyin and Jade Emperor halls and an 1843 couplet by Zeng Guofan.

rows.name: Tucheng Old Street (Red Army Street)
rows.summary: An old street of flagstones, timber eaves and remains of the town wall in the Chengkou county town, laid out in the Jiaqing era of the Qing dynasty about 200 years ago. It carries the Red Army name because Chengkou was part of the Sichuan–Shaanxi revolutionary base area, which the Fourth Front Army of the Red Army entered in October 1933, and the county's Soviet government and Red Army memorial parks are also in town.

rows.name: Tujia Thirteen Villages (Tujia Shisanzhai)
rows.summary: A group of 13 Tujia hamlets of wooden stilt houses spread along the Banjia stream in the north of Xiaonanhai town, where around 200 households still live. Flagstone paths and covered bridges link the hamlets, and visitors can hear Tujia folk songs and see the baishou hand-waving dance, while embroidery, weaving and batik are still practised; Hejiazhai is the largest and best preserved of the villages.

rows.name: Wanling Ancient Town
rows.summary: A historic riverside market town in north-eastern Rongchang, called Lukong until 2013 and listed among China's historic and cultural towns. Its old quarter takes in the Darong Bridge and the Niushiba wharf, a Huguang guild hall, the Zhao clan shrine and a memorial hall to the Ming official Yu Maojian, and opera and folk performances are staged there on holidays.

rows.name: Wansheng Old Street
rows.summary: This old street in central Wansheng recreates Wanshengchang, the market from which the town grew: first called Wanshouchang, it was renamed in the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, when sales of local coal and coke drew merchants and guild halls from Jiangxi, Zhejiang and Huguang. The stone Sanyuan Bridge over the river, paid for by a merchant in the Xianfeng reign, still stands, and the street is now a shopping and dining district.

rows.name: Wanshou Mountain, Shizhu
rows.summary: A craggy forested mountain at 1,200–1,500 m east of Shizhu county town, topped by the two rock pillars that, in local legend, gave the county its name ('stone pillars'). The scenic area, opened in 2019, is built around the old battlefield where Qin Liangyu, the Ming-dynasty woman general who commanded Shizhu's troops, built a stockade against attackers, and the nearby Wanshou Old Village shows Tujia stilt houses and customs.

rows.name: Wanzhou Grand Falls (Qinglong Falls)
rows.summary: A broad curtain waterfall on the Qinglong River in Ganning Town, 64.5 m high and about 150 m wide, which Wanzhou promotes as the largest waterfall in Asia. It is billed as one of the few falls that can be seen from every side, and paths lead behind the curtain of water.

rows.name: Wanzhou Riverfront (Three Gorges Pinghu) & Xishan Clock Tower
rows.summary: Wanzhou's riverside parks and promenades along the wide reservoir lake created by the Three Gorges Dam, with the old city wall, Cengong Cave, walks under huangge fig trees, a light show in Yinghuadu Park and evening boat trips on the lit-up river. Walks usually start at the Xishan Clock Tower in Xishan Park, a 50 m, 12-storey tower completed in 1932 that is counted with the customs-house clock towers of Shanghai and Wuhan among the three great clock towers of the Yangtze and still chimes the hour.

rows.name: Wartime Bank Buildings of Chongqing
rows.name_zh: 重庆抗战金融机构旧址群
rows.summary: Six former bank buildings in the old financial quarter around Datong Street, Xinhua Road and Jiefang East Road, left by the banks that operated here while Chongqing was China's wartime capital. They are the former Central Bank, Bank of China, Bank of Communications, Meifeng Bank, Chuankang Pingmin Commercial Bank and Juxingcheng Bank; most are seen from the street on a short walk between Jiefangbei and Xiaoshizi, and the Meifeng Bank building on Xinhua Road now houses the Chongqing Financial History Museum.

rows.name: Wenfeng Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain-top Taoist temple on the north bank at the western mouth of Wu Gorge, first built in the Ming dynasty as Lingyun Temple and rebuilt in 1786 for the Quanzhen Longmen school. The site looks over the river on one side and wooded ridges on the other, and the hillsides are one of Wushan's main red-leaf areas in late autumn.

rows.name: Western Mushroom Valley
rows.summary: A mushroom-themed family park in Lüshui village, Conglin town, north-east of Wansheng, combining fairy-tale play areas for children with a picking area where visitors can gather enoki, shiitake, straw mushrooms and lingzhi. It is one of Wansheng's farm-tourism projects and suits families with young children.

rows.name: White Emperor City (Baidicheng) & Qutang Gorge
rows.summary: A hilltop temple complex at the western mouth of Qutang Gorge, named after the warlord Gongsun Shu, who proclaimed himself the White Emperor in AD 25; since 1533 its halls have honoured Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang of the Three Kingdoms, and Tang poets including Li Bai and Du Fu wrote famous verses here. Since the Three Gorges reservoir filled, the hill has become an island joined to the north bank by a bridge, with Southern Song walls and the beacon tower of the Qutang Pass among its ruins and a direct view of Kuimen, the gate of the gorge pictured on the 10-yuan note. Boats run into the 8 km gorge, whose south-bank cliffs carry inscriptions from the Song dynasty to the Republican era, part of them now under water and part cut out and moved.

rows.name: Wu Gorge – Goddess Peak Scenic Area
rows.summary: The land side of Wu Gorge, about 15 km east of Wushan town. Its main sights are the Goddess Sky Road, a 12 km mountain road at around 1,200 m with five viewing platforms facing Goddess Peak and others of the Twelve Peaks across the river; Jingtan Peak; and Shennü Stream, a narrow side gorge on the south bank. Sightseeing buses, the Huangyan cableway, a 200 m cliff-side lift and boats link the viewpoints, and the slopes turn red with autumn leaves from November to January.

rows.name: Wu River Gallery (Pengshui)
rows.summary: The steep-walled gorge of the Wu River south of Pengshui, part of the roughly 100 km stretch from Pengshui past Gongtan to Yanhe in Guizhou that is known as the 'hundred-li gallery' for its cliffs and dark green water. The 4A scenic area is based at Wanzu town, and sightseeing boats run through the gorge.

rows.name: Wulingshan Great Rift Valley
rows.summary: A karst landscape of gorges, cliffs, caves and streams in the mountains of south-eastern Fuling, rated 5A in 2024 and covering about 30 km² with a height range of some 1,380 m. Its headline sights are the narrow Qingtian slot canyon, the deep Wanzhang vertical shaft, a waterfall where an underground river pours out of Laojun Cave, and the 'Copper and Iron Walls' of steeply folded rock strata.

rows.name: Wulingshan National Forest Park, Fuling
rows.summary: A forest park on the Wuling Mountains in south-eastern Fuling, centred on the old Damu state forest farm, with dense forest and upland grassland. Forest cover is about 95 per cent and July and August average under 20°C, so it is used mainly as a summer retreat for walking and forest stays.

rows.name: Wushan Museum
rows.summary: The county museum of Wushan, which grew out of the county's cultural relics office, opened in December 2012 and holds more than 50,000 objects; it was rated a national second-grade museum in 2018. Its main exhibition follows the area from the Longgupo site, whose simple stone tools the museum dates to about two million years ago, through the Neolithic Daxi culture to the local Wu culture, and smaller galleries show highlights such as a Han gilt-bronze plaque with the Queen Mother of the West.

rows.name: Xiangguo Park, Dazu
rows.summary: Dazu's largest city park, covering about 87 ha around two lakes, Miaoshan and Xiangquan, laid out on the theme of Dazu's old name, the 'land of begonia fragrance'. Covered bridges, pavilions, cascades, a public stage, children's play areas and an evening light-and-water show are spread through it, and the Song-style Changzhou Ancient Town street lies alongside. It makes an easy evening stroll after a day at the carvings.

rows.name: Xiaonanhai Lake
rows.summary: A mountain lake formed in 1856, when an earthquake brought down a hillside and dammed the Laojiao stream, leaving a natural rubble dam over 1 km long and a lake of about 2.9 km² with three small islands. It is one of the best-preserved historic earthquake sites in China and is now a national geopark; Chaoyang Temple island was the meeting place of an anti-Qing uprising society shortly before the 1911 revolution.

rows.name: Xiazhuang Village and its Cliff Road
rows.summary: A village at the bottom of a deep, cliff-ringed basin in Zhuxian Township that was cut off from the outside until its residents, led by the village Party secretary Mao Xianglin, spent seven years carving an 8 km road along the cliffs. The road, the citrus orchards planted since and a small exhibition room on the village's story now draw visitors, and state media present Xiazhuang as a model of the national poverty-alleviation campaign.

rows.name: Xiliutuo Riverside Town
rows.summary: A modern riverside leisure quarter on the Yangtze at Lijiatuo in Ba'nan, developed by the Ronghui property group around Xiliutuo Town, a newly built pedestrian district whose streets, courtyards and terraces are laid out on different levels with a Ba-culture theme. People come mainly for the local food and for walks or rides along the Babin riverside road.

rows.name: Xituo Ancient Town
rows.summary: A Yangtze river port facing the Shibaozhai pavilion across the water, which grew rich on the salt and river trade from the Qing dynasty and was named one of China's first historic and cultural towns in 2003. Its main street, the Yunti Jie or 'ladder to the clouds', climbs the hillside from the river in long flights of stone steps between tiers of Tujia stilt houses, past old halls such as the Yuwang Palace and the Ziyun Palace.

rows.name: Xiuhu Park
rows.summary: A large lake park in Bishan, created in the 2010s as one of more than 30 public parks the district built while cleaning up its rivers. Lakeside paths, lawns and gardens make it a pleasant place for a walk, and a car-camping park lies alongside.

rows.name: Xiushan West Street
rows.summary: The old western quarter of the Xiushan county town on both banks of the Meijiang River, the heart of the town since it was founded in 1736, restored as a folk-culture area of about 1 km². Old streets and lanes lead to the Tianhou Temple, the Bagua Well, a stretch of the old town wall, courtyard houses, an old opera stage and covered bridges, and the streets are hung with flower lanterns at festivals.

rows.name: Xuantian Lake
rows.summary: A lake of about 1,500 mu (100 ha) at the foot of Bayue Mountain on the southern edge of Tongliang, landscaped with lakeside running paths and designated, with the mountain, a municipal-level tourist resort in 2022. On its Dragon Dance Plaza an outdoor show, 'Chasing the Dream: Tongliang Dragon', staged on selected dates since 2022, presents the town's dragon and fire-dragon dances with lighting and stage effects.

rows.name: Yangtze River Cableway
rows.summary: An aerial tramway that has carried passengers across the Yangtze since 1987, spanning 1,166 m between Xinhua Road in Yuzhong and Shangxin Street at Longmenhao on the south bank. The cabins hold about 80 people and take a few minutes to cross, giving a high view of the river, its bridges and the Yuzhong skyline; the line itself has been a listed municipal heritage site since 2009.

rows.name: Youshui River Bend (Hewan Village)
rows.summary: Hewan is a Tujia village on the Youshui River in Youshuihe town, eastern Youyang, in the valley the county treats as the heartland of its Tujia culture. Its old hillside hamlet, Hewan Shanzhai, is rated one of the county's leading tourism resources, and village households run guesthouses under the county's 'Taoyuan Renjia' homestay scheme.

rows.name: Youyang Taohuayuan (Peach Blossom Spring)
rows.summary: A 50 km² scenic area on the edge of Youyang's county town that presents itself as the real-world model for Tao Yuanming's fable of the Peach Blossom Spring, with a secluded karst valley of streams, fields and peach trees, Taigu Cave and the large Fuxi Cave with its wide variety of dripstone formations. Other sections include a national forest park, Youzhou Ancient Town (a 1.3 km street of Tujia-style stilt buildings) and the 2,800-seat Taoyuan Grand Stage for the live show 'Dreamlike Peach Blossom Spring'. On the central square visitors can join Tujia hand-waving dances or listen to wood-leaf songs.

rows.name: Yunyang Lakeside Greenway
rows.summary: A greenway of riverside parks around the reservoir lake at Yunyang's county town, which was rebuilt here after the Three Gorges reservoir flooded the old town. Its eight themed parks, among them the Moonlight Lawn, were all open by 2022.

rows.name: Zhang Fei Temple
rows.summary: A temple to Zhang Fei, the Three Kingdoms general whose head, by tradition, was buried here; founded in the late Shu Han period, it stood for centuries on the south bank of the Yangtze opposite the old Yunyang town. Ahead of the Three Gorges reservoir it was dismantled and rebuilt, largely from its original materials, in a similar setting on the south bank facing the new county town, and reopened in July 2003. Its halls and pavilions honour Zhang Fei and the poet Du Fu, who stayed here for two years.

rows.name: Zhang Zhizhong Memorial Hall (Former Political Department of the Military Affairs Commission)
rows.summary: A rural compound at Sanshenggong village in Tuzhu, western Shapingba, used from 1938 to 1945 by the Political Department of the Nationalist government's Military Affairs Commission. It is also known as the former residence of the Nationalist general Zhang Zhizhong, and it is now open as the Chongqing Zhang Zhizhong Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Zhongshan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A riverside market town on the Shunxi River in southern Jiangjin, on the northern approach to Simian Mountain, listed as a National Historic and Cultural Town. Its long, narrow old street grew from three market sections joined together and once held more than 300 workshops and shops; bamboo-craft and sauce shops, grocers, small restaurants and old tea houses still trade there. A fire in 2021 damaged over 200 m of the street, which was repaired and reopened in early 2023.

rows.name: Zhoujunji Hotpot Seasoning Factory Tour
rows.name_zh: 周君记火锅食品工业旅游体验园
rows.pinyin: Zhōujūnjì Huǒguō Shípǐn Gōngyè Lǚyóu Tǐyànyuán
rows.summary: The hotpot-seasoning factory of the Zhoujunji company in Zhongliangshan, which has run factory tours since 2006. Visitors see the chillies, ginger and other raw materials, watch the production lines and the traditional frying of hotpot base, can fry a batch themselves and finish with a hotpot meal. A museum of Sichuan and Chongqing seasonings and hotpot culture opened beside the factory in 2025.

rows.name: Zhuoshui Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old trading town on the Apeng River that grew up from the late Tang and flourished in the Ming and Qing, with about a kilometre of flagstone lanes lined by Tujia stilt houses and Hui-style buildings. A 658 m covered 'wind-and-rain' bridge spans the river, and the 5A scenic area also takes in the nearby Puhua underground river, with three natural bridges and a large sinkhole.

rows.name: Zhuxi Eco Park
rows.summary: A rural leisure park in Zhuxi town, opened in 2021 with Kaizhou's Zhuxi rural-revitalisation zone and themed on the bamboo (zhu) and streams (xi) of its name. It offers countryside walks and farm landscapes and is mainly a weekend outing for families from the Kaizhou area.

rows.name: Colourful Forest, Fengsheng
rows.summary: A privately developed woodland park in Fengsheng town, planted with trees and shrubs chosen for their coloured foliage and run by Chongqing Bangtian Agriculture. It sits beside the historic town of Fengsheng and is mainly a place for autumn colour and short walks. It is listed as one of the first national forest-wellness bases (2020).

rows.name: Chongqing Medicinal Plant Garden
rows.summary: A medicinal-plant garden run by the Chongqing Institute of Medicinal Plant Cultivation at the foot of Jinfo Mountain in Nanchuan District, one of the oldest such gardens in China. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism base.

rows.name: Ancient Qiang City and Pingtou Village, Maoxian
rows.summary: A large complex on the edge of Mao County town, built after the 2008 earthquake to present the culture of the Qiang people. It houses the China Qiang Museum, a reconstructed Qiang king's residence and halls for crafts and performances. Pingtou, a Qiang village on the slope just above, has become a summer retreat with many family guesthouses.

rows.name: Bangtuo Monastery
rows.summary: A Nyingma monastery in northern Zamtang County, founded in the Yuan period and known for its 39 stupas built between the Ming dynasty and the Republic. In the middle of the stupa group are stacked more than 100,000 stone slabs carved with Tibetan scriptures, most cut in 1438 and the rest, a Kangyur, between 1910 and 1920.

rows.name: Bipenggou
rows.summary: A high valley in Li County, within the Miyaluo nature area, climbing from about 2,400 to 4,500 metres past forest, streams and waterfalls towards snow peaks. It is best known for its autumn colours, and sightseeing buses run up the valley from the visitor centre.

rows.name: Choubian Tower, Xuecheng
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty tower in the old street of Xuecheng, a small town on the Zagunao River in Li County. Its name means 'tower for planning frontier affairs', and it was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Cuo'erji (Chöje) Monastery and Rangbala
rows.summary: Zamtang is a leading centre of the Jonang school of Tibetan Buddhism, and Cuo'erji (Chöje) Monastery at Zhongrangtang, whose national listing dates its buildings from the Yuan to the Qing, is one of its historic monasteries. Nearby, the Rangbala heritage park gathers workshops where Jonang thangka painting and other local crafts are taught and shown.

rows.name: Dagu Glacier
rows.summary: A group of mountain glaciers in Heishui County, spread between about 3,800 and 5,100 metres within a protected scenic area of high peaks and forest. A cable car lifts visitors to viewpoints near the ice, which was only identified by scientists in 1992. Go in clear weather and allow for the altitude.

rows.name: Dazha Monastery
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery founded in 1663 by the first Dazha Living Buddha, which gives its name to Dazhasi, the county town of Zoige. Its assembly halls are a short walk from the town centre and make an easy stop when crossing the Zoige grasslands.

rows.name: Dhe-Tsang Monastery
rows.summary: Founded in 1414, Dhe-Tsang (Dazang) Monastery is the head monastery of the Gelug school in northern Sichuan, set in a remote valley of Dazang township north of Barkam. Its buildings were destroyed in the late 1950s and rebuilt in 1993–1997, and it was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Diexi Lake and Songpinggou
rows.summary: In 1933 an earthquake destroyed the old town of Diexi on the upper Min River and dammed the river, creating a lake that now covers the site of the old town. Viewpoints look out over Diexi Lake, and the side valley of Songpinggou to the west holds a chain of further lakes among forest.

rows.name: Emutang Flower Meadows, Hongyuan
rows.summary: Natural grassland in southern Hongyuan County where more than 30,000 mu (about 20 km²) of meadow turns into a sheet of wildflowers from early June to early August. Yellow, purple, white and blue flowers spread towards snow peaks, and in the hills above lie the sacred lake Cuoqiong and about 20 other mountain lakes reached on horseback or on foot. It is a summer stop on the G248 south of Hongyuan town.

rows.name: Flower Lake, Zoige
rows.summary: A shallow lake in the Zoige marshes beside the G213, seen from wooden boardwalks that were rebuilt outside the reserve's buffer zone to protect the wetland. In summer it is ringed by flowering meadows and is a good place to watch waterbirds; the wider Zoige wetland is a breeding ground for black-necked cranes.

rows.name: Guanyinqiao, Jinchuan
rows.summary: Guanyinqiao, in north-western Jinchuan County, is a Tibetan Buddhist pilgrimage centre built around its Guanyin (Avalokiteshvara) temple. The rated scenic area also takes in the river valley and high meadows around the town. It is a living religious site: dress modestly and walk clockwise around the shrines.

rows.name: Jiangweicheng Site, Weizhou
rows.summary: On a ridge above the Min River at Weizhou, Wenchuan's county town, are the remains of a walled hilltop fortress traditionally linked to the Three Kingdoms general Jiang Wei, though historians doubt he built it. More than 100 metres of wall survive, from Han rammed earth to Ming stonework, with an earthen mound said to be a generals' review platform, on a site settled since Neolithic times. The national listing also covers the Neolithic Yingpanshan site near Mao County town.

rows.name: Jiawuhai Lake and Panda Park
rows.summary: A mountain lake near Wujiao in Jiuzhaigou County, set among forest and snow peaks in an area of Baima Tibetan villages. A giant panda park beside the lake opened in November 2019 with pandas on loan from the China Conservation and Research Center for the Giant Panda, among them Xiao Liwu, who was born at San Diego Zoo in 2012.

rows.name: Kepan Tianjie and Zhibo Watchtowers
rows.summary: Kepan Tianjie ('sky street') is a ridge-top Jiarong Tibetan village above the Suomo River at Songgang, with the ruins of the Songgang chieftains' residence, two stone towers and some three dozen traditional houses, now restored with guesthouses and shops. Close by stand the Zhibo watchtowers, two stone towers of the Qianlong period, octagonal outside and round inside, 29 and 24.7 metres high.

rows.name: Lianbao Yeze (Stone Mountain)
rows.summary: A granite massif on the border between Aba County and Qinghai, a southern spur of the Bayan Har range whose highest peak reaches 5,369 metres. Jagged grey peaks rise above more than a hundred lakes, and the range forms the divide between the Yellow River and Yangtze systems. Valleys such as Longke, Zhumu and Zhagar are explored from the visitor centre.

rows.name: Lianghekou Meeting Site
rows.summary: At Lianghekou in Xiaojin County the Communist Party Politburo met on 26 June 1935, after the Red Army's First and Fourth Front Armies had joined forces at Dawei earlier that month. The meeting adopted the strategy of moving north to set up a base in the Sichuan–Shaanxi–Gansu region. The meeting site is protected as part of a national heritage listing of Long March sites in Aba.

rows.name: Long March Memorial Monument, Songpan
rows.summary: A memorial park on Yuanbao Hill above Chuanzhusi, completed in 1990 to commemorate the Red Army's Long March across the Songpan grasslands in 1935. The main monument, topped by a bronze statue of a Red Army soldier, is 41.3 metres high, and the park also has a granite sculpture group and a Long March museum.

rows.name: Moon Bay, Hongyuan
rows.summary: A crescent-shaped meander of a grassland river just outside Hongyuan town, part of the upper Yellow River wetlands. In summer the green pasture and the looping, shining river make a classic view of the Aba grasslands, best seen from the slopes above.

rows.name: Riganqiao Marsh
rows.summary: A large highland marsh near Waqie on the Hongyuan grasslands, part of the wider Zoige wetlands, where streams and pools spread across the peatland of the upper Yellow River basin. It is greenest in summer, and the stupas and prayer flags of Waqie are close by.

rows.name: Risimanba Tower House
rows.summary: A stone tower house (diaofang) in Zongke township, southern Zamtang County, dated by its national heritage listing to the Yuan and Ming periods. Buildings of this kind combined a family home with a defensive tower.

rows.name: Sanao Snow Mountain
rows.summary: Three snow peaks, Aotaiji, Aotaimei and Aotaina, rising above Luhua, the county town of Heishui. Their valleys, lakes and meadows attract trekkers, and the peaks have become popular with novice mountaineers; the nearby village of Deshiwo has trained more than 200 licensed mountain guides.

rows.name: Shenzuo Village
rows.summary: A Tibetan village in Chali township in eastern Aba County, with high pastures behind it and old forest facing it across the river. Its stone houses, small prayer halls and the surrounding grassland and woods make it a quiet stop on the grassland routes.

rows.name: Shiwai Liyuan Pear Orchards, Jinchuan
rows.summary: A 14.4 km² stretch of the Dajin River valley in Jinchuan County where Gyalrong Tibetan villages sit among snow-pear orchards; the county grows more than 40,000 mu (about 2,700 hectares) of the pears, and over a million trees line the valley. The orchards blossom white in March and April against snow peaks and turn red in autumn, and the scenic area spans Qingning, Ka'er and Sha'er townships. Come for the spring blossom or the autumn colour.

rows.name: Wenchuan Earthquake Memorial Area, Yingxiu
rows.summary: Yingxiu, in Wenchuan County, lay at the epicentre of the magnitude-8.0 earthquake of 12 May 2008, and this 5A-rated zone brings together the places that commemorate it. The collapsed buildings of Xuankou Middle School have been left as they fell as a memorial, surrounded by the rebuilt town. The zone also takes in the rebuilt town of Shuimo nearby and the forested valleys of Sanjiang.

rows.name: Wori Chieftain's Residence
