rows.summary: Built around 1750, after the family sided with the Qing court, this was the seat of the Wori chieftains, a Jiarong Tibetan line of 23 generations. The surviving south scripture hall, rebuilt in the mid-1940s, is a five-storey stone-and-timber tower with three tiers of eaves and a pyramidal roof, and beside it stands a square stone watchtower.

rows.name: Yu the Great Cultural Area, Wenchuan
rows.summary: Mianchi, on the Min River south of Wenchuan county town, is traditionally held to be the birthplace of Yu the Great, the legendary tamer of China's floods. The cultural area links an altar to Yu with other places in the area tied to the legend, and local celebrations of Yu's birthday are traditionally held on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month.

rows.name: Zengda Watchtower
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty stone watchtower at Zengda in southern Jinchuan County, guarding the Dajin River valley. Towers like this protected the passes of the Jiarong Tibetan chiefdoms, whose fortifications featured in the Qianlong Emperor's 18th-century Jinchuan campaigns.

rows.name: Zhegu Mountain Nature Park
rows.summary: A nature park on Zhegu Mountain, the high pass on the G317 between Miyaluo and Barkam, with conifer forest, alpine meadows and wide mountain views. In winter part of the park runs as a ski area.

rows.name: Zhuokeji Chieftain's Residence
rows.summary: The fortified residence of the Zhuokeji chieftains, rulers of one of the eighteen Jiarong Tibetan chiefdoms of western Sichuan until 1955, faces the old stone village of Xisuo across the Xisuo River. The present stone-and-timber building, of up to five storeys and rebuilt in 1938–1940 after a fire, blends Tibetan and Han Chinese styles and is open as a museum. Mao Zedong and other Red Army leaders stayed in the earlier building during the Long March in 1935, and exhibitions cover both Jiarong culture and that period.

rows.name: Bairuxi Grottoes
rows.summary: Bairuxi is a group of Tang-dynasty Buddhist niches carved into the rock in southern Tongjiang county. It became a national heritage site in 2013 and is one of several Tang carving sites in the county.

rows.name: Baiyi Ancient Town
rows.summary: Baiyi is an old trading town on the Ba River in southern Pingchang county that grew along the Micang trade road between Sichuan and Shaanxi. Its historic quarter, a provincial heritage site, keeps temples, memorial arches, pavilions and old merchant mansions.

rows.name: Enyang Ancient Town
rows.summary: Enyang is an old market and river town on the Enyang River, about 15 km south-west of central Bazhong. Its stone-paved lanes keep timber-fronted shops, courtyard houses and temples, and the riverside makes a pleasant stroll.

rows.name: Guangwu Mountain
rows.summary: Guangwushan covers more than 400 km² of the Micang range on the Sichuan–Shaanxi border, with limestone peaks, deep valleys, caves and large tracts of beech forest rising to 2,507 m. It is best known for its autumn colour, when the forests turn red and gold, and the Micangshan National Forest Park, around Daba, is part of the same area. With the Nuoshui River it forms the Guangwushan–Nuoshuihe UNESCO Global Geopark.

rows.name: Huahu Lake, Bazhou
rows.summary: A lake area around Huacheng Reservoir in Huacheng town, about 20 km north-east of central Bazhong, listed as a National Water Conservancy Scenic Area. The town around it is being developed as a lakeside eco-town with farm-based sightseeing and leisure. It is a quiet lakeside outing for those staying in Bazhong.

rows.name: Huangjia Mountain, Pingchang
rows.summary: A tea-growing hill area of about 12.6 km² spanning Xixing and Tuya towns, where more than 400 hectares of tea bushes follow the slopes and low clouds often settle in the valleys. It is a home of the local folk dance Fanshan Jiaozi, listed as national intangible cultural heritage in 2008. It suits a rural outing in spring.

rows.name: Jiuzhaishan Park, Bazhong
rows.summary: A landscaped hill park on the eastern side of Bazhong, in the city's economic development zone near Bazhong East railway station. It is used mainly by local residents for walks and family outings rather than as a destination for visitors from afar.

rows.name: Kongshan Basin
rows.summary: Kongshan is a high upland basin of meadows, farmland and forest ringed by mountains in northern Tongjiang county; 'Tianpen' means 'sky basin'. A memorial park recalls the Battle of Kongshanba, fought here by the Red Fourth Front Army in the 1930s, and the battlefield is a provincial heritage site.

rows.name: Nankan Grottoes
rows.summary: On Nankan Mountain, on the southern edge of central Bazhong, more than 170 niches holding about 2,700 painted Buddhist figures were cut into the cliffs, most of them in the Tang dynasty. It is the largest and best preserved of the Bazhong Grottoes, a protected group that also includes the smaller North Niches, West Niches and Shuining Temple carvings around the city.

rows.name: Nantianmen, Pingchang
rows.summary: A forested hill area of about 18.5 km² in Wumu town, once a stage on the Micang ancient road and a military strongpoint of the Sichuan–Shaanxi revolutionary base area. It has been developed for outdoor sport, with a forest sports park, a mountain-bike trail, a self-drive campsite and the Shuanghe eco-garden. It suits hikers, cyclists and campers more than sightseers.

rows.name: Nuoshui River Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Nuoshui (Xiaotong) River cuts through the limestone of the Micang range in northern Tongjiang county, and its scenic area is known for karst caves, gorges and forested valleys. Together with Guangwushan it makes up the Guangwushan–Nuoshuihe UNESCO Global Geopark.

rows.name: Qianfoyan Grottoes, Tongjiang
rows.summary: This cliff in Qianfo village, just west of Tongjiang town, holds 54 niches with more than 3,000 Buddhist figures, carved mainly in the Tang dynasty. It is a compact, easily reached example of the Buddhist rock carving found across the Bazhong area.

rows.name: Red Fourth Front Army Headquarters Site
rows.name_zh: 红四方面军总指挥部旧址
rows.summary: From the winter of 1932 to the spring of 1935 the Red Fourth Front Army used Tongjiang's Confucian temple as its headquarters while it held the Sichuan–Shaanxi revolutionary base. The temple, first built in 1062 and rebuilt in the Ming, keeps a Qing main hall and side halls on terraces above a square with sculptures, and houses a memorial museum on the period.

rows.name: Shimen Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A group of Tang-dynasty Buddhist niches cut into the rock at the Shimen Temple site in Bazhou District, east of central Bazhong, and listed as a national heritage site in 2019. Art historians count it among the better-preserved of the many Tang carving sites around Bazhong and date the start of work here to around 740, the same years in which niche-cutting at the city's Nankan Grottoes increased sharply.

rows.name: Sima Water Town, Pingchang
rows.summary: A leisure area around Sima town, on the border of Pingchang County and Bazhou District, built around an artificial lake and wetlands. It includes the Sima National Wetland Park, a filial-piety culture garden, a water park and a modern agricultural demonstration park. It suits families and weekend visitors from Bazhong rather than travellers looking for historic sights.

rows.name: Wangping Red Army Martyrs' Cemetery
rows.summary: This hillside cemetery at Wangping in Tongjiang county was begun by the Red Fourth Front Army in 1934 and, after scattered graves from across the county were moved here in 2012, holds about 25,000 Red Army dead. The scenic area also includes Red Cloud Cliff, where the slogan 'Chihua Quanchuan' ('Turn all Sichuan Red') is carved in giant characters, one of the best known of the Red Army stone inscriptions that survive around Bazhong.

rows.name: Anren Ancient Town
rows.summary: Anren is a market town on the western edge of the Chengdu Plain, listed among China's historic towns in 2005, with well-preserved streets of traditional western Sichuan architecture. Its main sights are the Liu Family Manor, a sprawling landlord estate built by the Liu Wencai family from the late Qing onwards and now a national heritage site, and the Jianchuan Museum Cluster, a large private group of museums on 20th-century Chinese history. Between them they easily fill a full day.

rows.name: Baihetan National Wetland Park, Xinjin
rows.summary: A wetland park on the Min River at Xinjin, where river deposits have built up sandbars, gravel shoals and grassy meadows. It was approved as a national wetland park in 2013, and more than 180 bird species had been recorded there by 2022. Riverside paths make it a quiet spot for walking and birdwatching on the southern edge of Chengdu.

rows.name: Bailu Music Town & Annunciation Seminary
rows.name_zh: 白鹿音乐小镇与领报修院
rows.pinyin: Báilù Yīnyuè Xiǎozhèn yǔ Lǐngbào Xiūyuàn
rows.summary: Bailu is a small mountain town in Pengzhou, marketed as a 'music town'. Its main historic sight is the Annunciation Seminary, regarded as one of the largest French-style church complexes in Sichuan, run by French missionaries from 1908 to 1949. Badly damaged in the 2008 earthquake, the seminary was restored in 2016 and is a national heritage site.

rows.name: Baodun Site
rows.summary: Earthen ramparts of a walled town of the Baodun culture, some 4,500 years old, the largest of six prehistoric walled towns on the Chengdu Plain protected under one listing. The culture is the earliest known on the plain and is linked to the first phase of Sanxingdui. An exhibition hall opposite the walls, opened in 2022, displays finds and explains how the town was built, and the site became a national archaeological park in 2025.

rows.name: Baoguang Temple & Gui Lake
rows.summary: Two neighbouring sights in Xindu, north of Chengdu. Baoguang Temple, a working Buddhist monastery founded in the Tang dynasty, has a 13-tiered Tang pagoda with a visible lean and a Hall of Arhats with more than 500 sculpted figures. About a kilometre to the south, Gui Lake is a classical western Sichuan garden beside the old town wall, associated with the Ming scholar Yang Shen and known for osmanthus in autumn and lotus in summer.

rows.name: Baoshan Scenic Area, Pengzhou
rows.summary: A tourist area around Baoshan village in the Longmen Mountains of Pengzhou, combining two forested valleys, Taiyangwan and Huilonggou, with a hot-spring resort and village tourism. Taiyangwan lies within a nature reserve and geopark and has walking routes rising from low to high mountain zones. Baoshan itself has a national reputation as a model mountain village.

rows.name: Chengdu International Intangible Cultural Heritage Park
rows.summary: A large event park of about 1,780 mu (119 hectares) in western Chengdu, built as the permanent home of the Chengdu International Intangible Cultural Heritage Festival, whose ninth edition opened here in May 2025. Between festivals it hosts music festivals, markets, sports events, film shoots and a few exhibition and immersive-experience venues, so what is on varies widely. It is worth a visit mainly when the festival or another event is running.

rows.name: Chengdu Polar Ocean Park
rows.summary: A marine park of about 7 hectares in Huayang, Tianfu New Area, on the southern side of Chengdu, opened in 2010 as Haichang Polar Ocean World and since renamed. It keeps polar bears, beluga whales, walruses and sea lions among other marine animals, and stages dolphin and sea-lion shows. It is a family attraction, and most visitors spend around four hours.

rows.name: Chengjia Tea Country, Pujiang
rows.summary: Rolling tea country around Chengjia town in Pujiang county, south-west of Chengdu, with some 22,000 mu (about 1,500 hectares) of tea gardens, more than half of them organic. Visitors walk among the plantations, try picking and processing tea and stay in tea-garden guesthouses. It is at its best in spring, when the Chengdu tea-picking festival is held in Pujiang.

rows.name: Chuanwang Palace, Xinchang
rows.summary: A temple to the 'King of Sichuan', Li Bing, the engineer of the Dujiangyan irrigation system, beside the Hutiao River at Xinchang in western Dayi. First founded in the Ming, its present wooden buildings date from 1926. They use the local chuandou timber-frame technique and are a valuable example of early twentieth-century temple building in western Sichuan.

rows.name: Danjing Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded mountain in Pengzhou known for tree peonies since at least the Song dynasty, when the poet Lu You wrote that Tianpeng (Pengzhou) peonies were the finest in Sichuan. A peony festival, held since 1985, fills its hillside gardens each spring, usually from late March. Paths also lead to a shrine to Lu You, Jinhua Temple and old cliff carvings.

rows.name: Danjingtai, Longquan Mountain Urban Forest Park
rows.summary: A hilltop viewing park on the ridge of the Longquan Mountains, opened on New Year's Day 2020 as the first showcase project of the Longquan Mountain Urban Forest Park. From 702 metres above sea level it looks over the island-studded Sancha Lake and the new Eastern New Area, and on clear days to distant snow peaks; the main building has an exhibition on the forest park and an ecology display. It suits a half-day drive for the views.

rows.name: Daoming Bamboo Village
rows.summary: A rural hamlet in Daoming, Chongzhou, known for Daoming bamboo weaving, a local craft added to China's national intangible cultural heritage list in 2014. Its landmark is Zhuli, a contemporary building whose roofline forms an infinity sign when seen from above and whose name comes from a poem by Lu You. Workshops and shops around the village show woven bamboo work being made and sold.

rows.name: Dongjiao Memory
rows.summary: A cultural and creative district in Chenghua, east Chengdu, converted from the Hongguang Electron Tube Factory, a state electronics plant founded in 1958. Its old workshops, chimneys and pipework now house live-music venues, galleries, studios, cafés and shops; it opened in 2011 as the Eastern Suburb Music Park and took its present name in 2012. It suits an afternoon or evening for anyone interested in industrial heritage or Chengdu's music scene.

rows.name: Early Buildings of Sichuan University (Huaxiba)
rows.summary: Campus buildings from 1913 to 1954, mainly the old West China Union University campus at Huaxiba plus the administration building on the main Wangjiang campus. The Huaxiba group, including the clock tower and the old library, combines Western brick construction with Chinese-style tiled roofs, a blend chosen by the missionary societies that founded the university.

rows.name: Feixiange Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: One of the two protected groups of the Pujiang Grottoes, near Chaoyang Lake, with Buddhist and Taoist niches carved from the Tang to the Qing, the earliest dated 689. Surveys count 64 Tang niches with 491 figures, plus Five Dynasties and Qing work. The largest figure is a 6-metre seated Tang Maitreya, and one Wu Zhou-period niche shows the Three Sages of the Western Paradise.

rows.name: Fenghuang Lake, Qingbaijiang
rows.summary: A wetland park around a lake in Qingbaijiang district, north-east of Chengdu, rated a 4A scenic area in 2022. It is best known for its cherry blossom, with more than 16,000 trees of dozens of varieties that flower in March and April, when a cherry-blossom festival is held, and has footpaths and boardwalks around the water. Visit in spring for the blossom.

rows.name: Guanxian Old Town, Dujiangyan
rows.summary: The historic core of Dujiangyan, a city known as Guan County until 1988, lying beside the ancient irrigation scheme. Much of it was rebuilt after the 2008 earthquake, but its lanes include West Street, the starting point of the old road into the mountains towards Songpan, a restored stretch of the old city wall, the Confucian temple and the City God Temple, a nationally protected group of halls climbing the slope of Yulei Mountain. It is easily combined with a visit to the Dujiangyan Irrigation System.

rows.name: Guanyin Temple, Xinjin
rows.summary: A temple in Yongshang, south of Xinjin, founded in 1181 and rebuilt many times; two Ming halls survive alongside a Qing gate and halls. The Vairocana Hall, built in 1462, holds seven finely drawn, richly coloured murals painted in 1468. The Guanyin Hall has sculpted groups of the bodhisattva and arhats.

rows.name: Guose Tianxiang Amusement Park
rows.summary: A large theme-park and resort development in Wanchun, Wenjiang, on Chengdu's western edge, built in a foreign-themed style beside a big housing estate. It has three parks: the Fairy-Tale World; a land park with roller coasters, drop towers and other rides; and a water park open in the warmer months. It is aimed at families with children.

rows.name: Haibin City, Shuangliu
rows.summary: A large indoor shopping and entertainment complex in the Jiaolonggang area of Shuangliu, south-west Chengdu, listed as a scenic area for its leisure attractions. Alongside shops and food halls it contains an aquarium with fish displays and mermaid shows, an ice rink and flight-simulator experiences. It is a rainy-day option for families rather than a sightseeing destination.

rows.name: Happy Valley Chengdu
rows.summary: An amusement park in Jinniu district, north-west Chengdu, opened in January 2009 as the third park in the Happy Valley chain. Its rides include several roller coasters, among them a Bolliger & Mabillard dive coaster added in 2017. It suits families and ride enthusiasts looking for a day off from sightseeing.

rows.name: Hongkou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley along the Baisha River in the mountains north of Dujiangyan, bordering the Longxi–Hongkou National Nature Reserve, a habitat of giant pandas and golden monkeys. In summer it is popular for white-water rafting and for cooling off beside the river, and side gorges such as Shenxigou lead further into the hills.

rows.name: Huanglongxi
rows.summary: A historic river town where the Luxi River joins the Jin River south of Chengdu, a stop on the river trade since the Han dynasty and one of China's listed historic towns. Cobbled lanes of mostly Qing-era timber houses lead to old wharves and temples such as Zhenjiang Temple and Gulong Temple, and the town is often used as a set for period films. Many houses are now souvenir shops, and it is very busy at weekends and holidays.

rows.name: Huashuiwan Hot Spring Town
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort town in the mountains of Dayi county, on the road up to Xiling Snow Mountain, with a river running through it between the hills. Its hotels and bathhouses use a spring marketed as 'ancient seawater', and since 2024 the town and Xiling Snow Mountain have together formed a national-level tourist resort. It suits a soak and an overnight stop before or after the mountain.

rows.name: Huawu Renjian Flower Park, Xinjin
rows.summary: A flower park of more than 3,000 mu (about 200 hectares) in Xinjin district, on the southern fringe of Chengdu. It runs a sequence of flower festivals through the year, among them tulips, rhododendrons, lupins, sunflowers and lilies, with water-based amusements alongside. It is best in spring for a half-day stroll.

rows.name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral, Chengdu
rows.summary: The cathedral of the Catholic Diocese of Chengdu, completed in 1904 on what was then Ping'anqiao Street in the city centre. The complex includes a large and a small chapel and the bishop's residence. It remains an active place of worship.

rows.name: Jiezi Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town on the Weijiang River at the foot of Fengqi Mountain, on the back side of Mount Qingcheng. Lanes of timber houses run beside clear streams, and a Qing-dynasty paper-burning pagoda stands at the head of the old street. Guangyan Temple lies in the forest on the mountain above.

rows.name: Jinmen Silk Quarter, Xindu
rows.summary: A recently developed cultural and commercial quarter in Sanhe, Xindu district, north of Chengdu, themed on Shu brocade and promoted as the starting point of the Southern Silk Road. It houses the Sichuan Silk Museum, which traces silk-making from sericulture to drawloom weaving, and has brought in more than 100 intangible-heritage crafts such as Shu brocade, Shu embroidery and lacquerware, alongside shops and restaurants. It suits visitors interested in textiles and traditional crafts.

rows.name: Jinsha Site Museum
rows.summary: The museum stands on the Jinsha site in western Chengdu, a centre of the ancient Shu culture discovered in 2001 and dated to roughly 1250–650 BC. A large hall covers part of the excavations, and the exhibition halls show gold, jade, bronze and stone finds, among them the Golden Sun Bird gold foil, now the emblem of China's cultural heritage, and kneeling stone figures. It continues the story told at Sanxingdui, whose culture Jinsha succeeded.

rows.name: Kuiguang Pagoda
rows.summary: A hexagonal brick pagoda in Dujiangyan city, rebuilt in 1831 on a Ming predecessor by a county magistrate to promote local scholarship. At 52.67 metres with 17 tiers of eaves, it is described as the old pagoda with the most storeys surviving in China. Spiral stone stairs run through the lower five storeys, and a small shrine to the magistrate stands beside it.

rows.name: Lingyan Temple and Thousand Buddha Pagoda
rows.summary: A temple on the southern slope of Lingyan Mountain just north of Dujiangyan city, rebuilt in the Ming and Qing; only its Qing main hall and bell tower survive. Beside it stands the Thousand Buddha Pagoda, a 3-metre solid stone stupa from the Tang Kaiyuan era (713–741) whose thirteen tiers are covered with seated Buddhas. It pairs well with a visit to the Dujiangyan irrigation works.

rows.name: Luxelake Water City
rows.summary: A planned lakeside district in Tianfu New Area, south of central Chengdu, built from 2010 around an artificial lake of about 2,100 mu (140 hectares) fed with water from the Dujiangyan irrigation system. Its 1.92 km² visitor area mixes waterfront paths, islands and parks with housing, cafés and shops. It suits an afternoon walk and an interest in new urban development.

rows.name: Ming Tombs of the Princes of Shu
rows.summary: A group of more than ten tombs of Ming-dynasty Princes of Shu and their consorts, spread over the low hills of Shiling in eastern Chengdu. The tomb of Prince Xi lies at the centre of the group, and a museum there lets visitors walk into the stone burial chambers. The group was listed as a national heritage site in 1996.

rows.name: Nongke Village, Pidu
rows.summary: A flower- and bonsai-growing village in Youai town, Pidu, north-west of Chengdu, promoted as the birthplace of nongjiale, the farmhouse restaurants and guesthouses now found across rural China. Visitors walk among some 300 mu (20 hectares) of nursery gardens and potted landscapes and eat in farmhouse courtyards. The village also presents itself as the home area of the Han-dynasty scholar Yang Xiong.

rows.name: Northern Zhou Stele of King Wen
rows.summary: A stele carved in 557 on a great boulder in the Longquan Mountains, recording the deeds of Yuwen Tai, honoured as King Wen of Northern Zhou, and dedicating a Buddhist and a Taoist image. Sheltered by a roofed gallery, its 40 lines and more than 1,400 characters remain clear. Carved niches from the Northern Zhou to the Qing share the same rock, behind Dafo Temple beside the old Chengdu–Chongqing post road.

rows.name: Peach Blossom Homeland, Longquanyi
rows.summary: A hillside orchard area at Shanquan in the Longquan Mountains, on Chengdu's eastern edge, centred on the peach groves for which Longquanyi is known. It has more than 30 viewpoints linked by themed footpaths, including a long stepped trail, and a small museum of peach culture. Come in March for the blossom, when the district's peach-blossom festival (held since 1987) takes place, or in summer for the fruit.

rows.name: Pingle Ancient Town
rows.summary: A market town on the Baimo River at the foot of the Qionglai Mountains, a settlement since the Western Han and traditionally counted as a stop on the Southern Silk Road. Old banyan trees line the riverbanks, two-storey timber shophouses face stone-paved lanes, and the Leshan Bridge, a multi-arched Qing-dynasty stone bridge, crosses the river. It is one of China's listed historic towns.

rows.name: Qinggangshu Village, Pidu
rows.summary: A model village in Sandaoyan town, Pidu, on the north-western edge of Chengdu, where streams and irrigation channels run among western-Sichuan farmhouses and tree-shaded linpan homesteads. It is popular for spring rapeseed blossom, cycling and farmhouse meals, and has hosted outdoor music festivals. It combines easily with Sandaoyan's rebuilt riverside quarter a few kilometres away.

rows.name: Qiong Kiln Site, Shifangtang
rows.summary: The remains of a large folk pottery works at Shifangtang that fired ceramics from the Sui to the Song dynasties, the biggest known site of the Qiong ware tradition. More than a dozen kiln mounds survive, among them long sloping 'dragon' kilns, and excavations recovered more than 10,000 objects. Now a national archaeological park, it shows excavated kiln remains under cover, with an exhibition hall and a pottery-making area.

rows.name: Qionglai Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Three groups of Tang-to-Song Buddhist cliff carvings around Qionglai are protected together: Pantuo Temple, Shisun Mountain and Huazhi Temple. At Pantuo Temple, on the outskirts of the city, carving began in 820 and four niches hold 1,099 figures, including the Three Sages of the West, a thousand-Buddha niche and a Pure Land scene. The Shisun Mountain group lies further north-west in the hills.

rows.name: Ruiguang Pagoda, Huaikou
rows.summary: A 33-metre square brick pagoda of 13 storeys in the grounds of Ruiguang Temple, on the east bank of the Tuo River at Huaikou; its recorded founding date is 1148, in the Southern Song. Backed by Snake Hill and facing the river, it has an inner stairway of 133 steps reaching the tenth storey and an iron finial. Locals call it the White Pagoda.

rows.name: Sandaoyan Water Town, Pidu
rows.summary: A riverside town in northern Pidu, named after a legend that an early Shu ruler built three weirs of bamboo baskets here to divert water for the fields, and once a busy river port and trading post. Its waterfront has been rebuilt as Huili Street, a lane of restaurants, snack stalls, teahouses and shops recreating the look of the late Qing and early Republic, beside canals and small bridges. Small museums in the town cover birdcages, Sichuan cuisine, jade and Han pottery.

rows.name: Sansheng Flower Villages
rows.summary: A belt of flower-growing villages in Sansheng subdistrict on Chengdu's south-eastern edge, developed as five themed areas known as the 'Five Golden Flowers': Flower Village Farmhouses, Happy Plum Grove, Jiang Family Vegetable Plots, East Hedge Chrysanthemum Garden and Lotus Pond Moonlight. Among the gardens stands the Xu Liaoyuan Museum of Modern Design Art, which holds art and design exhibitions. It is an easy half-day escape from the city centre.

rows.name: Shengde Temple White Pagoda
rows.summary: A multi-storey Song-dynasty pagoda in the south of Jianyang, known locally as the White Pagoda and listed as a national heritage site in 2006. It is a short stop for travellers passing through Jianyang, east of Chengdu.

rows.name: Shixiang Lake, Pujiang
rows.summary: A lake park in Pujiang county, south-west of Chengdu, combining about 800 mu (53 hectares) of water with a large area of secondary forest, planted lawns and extensive flower fields. It is best known for its tulip festival in spring and lily displays in autumn, with more than 20 viewpoints around the grounds. It makes a day trip for flower lovers in March–May or September–November.

rows.name: Shuijingfang Distillery Site
rows.summary: The remains of a baijiu distillery worked from the Ming and Qing dynasties, found in 1998 when a Chengdu liquor plant was rebuilding, with drying floors from three periods, eight fermentation pits and stoves. It was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 1999 and is on the country's World Heritage tentative list with other old baijiu workshops. The site is shown in the Shuijingfang Museum, which is still a working distilling workshop.

rows.name: Stone Pagoda Temple
rows.summary: A temple in Gaohe, western Qionglai, centred on a 17.8-metre square pagoda of red sandstone carved between 1169 and 1172, with a double plinth, a colonnade and twelve tiers of close-set eaves. The main hall is a Ming rebuilding. In 1935 the temple housed a local Red Army soviet government, and a Long March memorial hall now stands on the site.

rows.name: Tianfu Hibiscus Garden
rows.summary: A themed park in the Jiang'an River green belt of Wuhou district, south-west Chengdu, opened in 2018 and developed with Joy City Holdings around the hibiscus, Chengdu's city flower. It mixes flower meadows, a eucalyptus grove and seasonal flower islands with a bookshop, restaurants and art spaces, and runs festivals, lantern shows and camping events. It suits a relaxed half-day rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Tianfu International Slow City, Chongzhou
rows.summary: A rural leisure area around Baitou town, west of Chongzhou on the Chengdu Plain, made up of the Qimu River wetland park, the Wuxing village folk-culture area and open rice and rapeseed fields. Visitors cycle or walk along the river past white-walled western-Sichuan houses, linpan homesteads and farm restaurants, and the rapeseed fields flower yellow from late February into March. It suits a slow day of cycling in spring.

rows.name: Tiantai Mountain (Qionglai)
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in western Qionglai, protected as a national scenic area and forest park and included in the Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries World Heritage Site. Trails follow the Jinlong River past shoals, cascades and waterfalls towards Yuxiao Peak, the main summit at 1,812 m. On warm evenings between late spring and autumn the valleys are known for large displays of fireflies.

rows.name: Tianyi Nongyuan Art Park
rows.summary: An art park in Wuhou district, south-west Chengdu, founded in 2005 and now grouped into three sections that combine artists' studios, galleries and teaching spaces. Old-style courtyards and modern outdoor sculpture surround galleries such as the Yue Art Museum, and the park hosts exhibitions and craft markets. It suits visitors interested in contemporary Chinese art.

rows.name: Tomb of Wang Jian
rows.summary: The burial mound of Wang Jian (847–918), founding emperor of the Former Shu kingdom, excavated in the 1940s and now the Yongling Museum. Unusually, its three chambers lie at ground level inside the mound rather than underground. The middle chamber holds the coffin platform carved with a band of female musicians, and the rear chamber a seated stone figure taken to be the emperor.

rows.name: Wangcong Temple
rows.summary: A memorial temple in Pidu to Wangdi (Du Yu) and Congdi (Bieling), two legendary kings of ancient Shu, traditionally credited with teaching farming and taming floods. Their burial mounds stand within the grounds, and it is described as the only shrine in south-west China honouring two kings together at their tombs. The surviving halls date mainly from the Qing dynasty, and the site is protected at provincial level.

rows.name: Wangjianglou Park
rows.summary: A riverside park on the Jin River honouring the Tang poet Xue Tao, who is said to have drawn water from a well here to make her coloured letter paper. Buildings added in the Ming and Qing include the tall Chongli Pavilion, a Chengdu landmark, along with smaller halls and the Xue Tao Well. The park grows more than 100 kinds of bamboo, a plant she loved.

rows.name: Weiran Flower Sea, Longquanyi
rows.summary: A large commercial flower park in Tong'an, Longquanyi, on the eastern edge of Chengdu, planted mainly with seasonal flowers such as tulips, poppies, zinnias and coneflowers, including some grown from space-bred seed. Beyond the flower beds it runs a sightseeing train, children's rides, camping and evening shows, and it has hosted the Cactus music festival. It is a family day out, best in spring.

rows.name: Wufengxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A riverside town on the Tuo River in the Longquan Mountains of Jintang County, which prospered as a busy river port in the Qing dynasty. Its old lanes of timber houses lead to halls built by migrant merchant communities, notably the Guansheng Palace and the Nanhua Palace, the Guangdong guild hall.

rows.name: Xiling Snow Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in the Qionglai range in Dayi County, crowned by Daxuetang, at 5,364 m the highest peak in Chengdu municipality. Visitors come for forest and high-mountain views in summer and for the ski area in winter. The snow peak is often identified with the western ridge whose snows Du Fu described framed in his window in Chengdu.

rows.name: Xinchang Ancient Town
rows.summary: A long-established foothill market town in western Dayi County, laid out on a grid of old streets and lanes. A large number of Qing and Republican-era buildings in the western Sichuan vernacular style survive. It is quieter than nearby Anren and the two can be combined in a day.

rows.name: Xingfu Tianyuan Rural Park, Wenjiang
rows.summary: A showcase rural area of about 1,400 mu (93 hectares) at Xingfu village in Wanchun, Wenjiang, on the western edge of Chengdu, presenting farm life on the Chengdu Plain. A greenway through the fields links western-Sichuan courtyard houses, flower nurseries, a wetland park, a crape-myrtle garden and a small farming-culture museum. It suits an easy half-day out of the city and can be combined with the Guose Tianxiang amusement park, also in Wanchun.

rows.name: Yanhua Pond
rows.summary: A garden in the centre of Chongzhou that began as a Tang-dynasty official's garden and took its form in the Song, when the magistrate Zhao Bian dug the pond and the poet Lu You, who held office here, wrote about it. The buildings are mostly Qing rebuildings. The 3.5-hectare site combines the pond garden, a shrine to Lu You and the town's former Confucian temple.

rows.name: Yuantong Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old river-port town on the Wenjing River in Chongzhou, once one of the busier wharves of the western Chengdu Plain. Grey-tiled houses from the late Qing and early Republican years line the river, alongside the Huang family ancestral hall, a Guangdong guild hall and a late-Qing Catholic church.

rows.name: Zhanqi Village, Pidu
rows.summary: A model village in Tangchang, Pidu, noted for its collective land reforms and visited by Xi Jinping in February 2018; an exhibition hall presents the village's development and that visit. The Eighteen Village Workshops, opened in 2018, show crafts such as Tangchang cloth-shoe making, soy-sauce brewing and grain-liquor distilling, and there is also a farming-culture museum and an old-style street. It suits visitors curious about rural development in China and traditional crafts.

rows.name: Zhenguo Temple White Pagoda and Pengzhou Pagodas
rows.summary: Three Northern Song brick pagodas around Pengzhou are protected together: the Zhenguo Temple White Pagoda at Danjingshan, the Yunju Yuan pagoda and the Zhengjue Temple pagoda. The White Pagoda, built between 1054 and 1060, is a square 13-tier tower with close-set eaves, 28 metres high, with reliefs of Buddhas, bodhisattvas and peacocks under its eaves. All three were damaged in the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake and have since been repaired.

rows.name: Bashan Grand Canyon
rows.summary: The Bashan Grand Canyon scenic area covers river gorges, cliffs and forested mountains in the Daba range of north-eastern Xuanhan county, around the Tujia ethnic township of Dukou. Viewpoints and routes along the gorges are the main draw, and Tujia villages set it apart culturally from the rest of Dazhou.

rows.name: Batai Mountain
rows.summary: Batai Mountain, south-east of Wanyuan city in the Daba range, is a national geopark of isolated peaks and sheer cliffs, known for sunrise views, seas of cloud and 'Buddha's light' halos. Glass walkways and a glass bridge, camping and winter snow sports are part of a visit, and the slopes turn red in autumn.

rows.name: Congren Valley
rows.summary: Congren Valley is a 41 km² karst landscape of gorges, caves, springs, waterfalls and forest in the hills east of Qu County town, protected as a national forest park and provincial geopark. It is named after the Cong, a branch of the ancient Ba people, and a cave-dwelling site and small exhibition hall on their history sit alongside natural sights such as the Longqiu Waterfall.

rows.name: Han Que of Qu County
rows.summary: Qu County has six sites with seven stone que, the pillar-gates that stood before tombs of the Eastern Han to Western Jin, carved in stone to imitate timber buildings; they amount to about a quarter of all surviving Han que in China. Most stand in the fields around Tuxi town under glass shelters added in 2019, and the China Han Que Culture Museum, opened in 2015, explains them.

rows.name: Jinshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: Jinshan is a wooded hill in Pu'an town, a few kilometres west of Kaijiang county town, centred on Jinshan Temple, a Buddhist monastery. It is a local destination for temple visits and walks in the surrounding woods.

rows.name: Kaijiang Memorial Arches
rows.summary: Two Qing-dynasty stone memorial arches in Kaijiang county honour widows for chastity and filial devotion: the Tao Arch at the entrance to Renshi town, raised for the wife and concubine of the official Zhang Jiufeng, and the Hu Family Arch near Gantang town. They were listed together as a national heritage site in 2006.

rows.name: Lenin Street Stone Arches and Red Army Slogans
rows.summary: Four Qing-dynasty memorial arches, built between 1817 and 1901 to honour virtuous widows, stand along the old street of Shiqiao town in Dachuan District; their tiers of eaves are carved with dragons and phoenixes, scenes such as the Eight Immortals and the Peach Garden Oath, and some 480 human figures. In 1933 the political department of the Red Army's 30th Army carved slogans onto the arches and nearby rock faces, and the street is now known as Lenin Street.

rows.name: Qu County Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Qu County's Confucian temple is a Qing-dynasty complex of three courtyards on a hillside above the Qu River, built in stages between 1663 and 1821 and fronted by a carved stone Lingxing Gate of 1794. It now houses the Qu County History Museum and became a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Shenjianyuan (Zhang Aiping Former Residence)
rows.summary: Shenjianyuan, in Luojiang town north-east of Dazhou city, is built around the childhood home of Zhang Aiping (1910–2003), a Red Army veteran who later directed China's early nuclear tests and served as defence minister. Exhibition halls on Zhang, on other Dazhou-born commanders and on the Red Army in the region hold about 1,200 items.

rows.name: Wanyuan Red Army Park
rows.summary: On Tuoshan hill above Wanyuan city, this memorial park commemorates the 1934 Defence of Wanyuan, when the Red Fourth Front Army held the area against Sichuan warlord forces. At its centre, the Defence of Wanyuan war-history exhibition hall presents the campaign.

rows.name: Wenfeng Mountain, Qu County
rows.summary: An open hillside park in Qu County town themed on local history and Confucian scholarship. Its landmark is a modern octagonal nine-storey Wenfeng Pagoda, 68.7 m tall, on the site of a pagoda that fell and was rebuilt several times in the Qing dynasty, together with the 56.5 m Wenfeng Pavilion recalling a Song-era lookout and a garden of sculptures and relief walls on the county's imperial-exam graduates. It is a short visit if you are in Qu County for the Han-dynasty stone towers.

rows.name: Wufeng Mountain
rows.summary: Wufeng Mountain in eastern Dazhu county is a national forest park; its ridges, between 600 and 1,080 m, are covered by a bamboo forest of many species that stretches for tens of kilometres. Paths lead through the bamboo past streams, small lakes, karst caves and pavilions.

rows.name: Wumei Mountain, Dachuan
rows.summary: A 17.75 km² rural area around Baijie, south of Dazhou, centred on orchards of mume trees grown for wumei, the smoked dried fruit, which blossom in January–February and ripen in May–June. Besides orchards and flower fields it takes in Baijie old street, founded in 1614, with a fig tree over 200 years old, the character 'Kui' carved into a cliff in 1835, the Wumei Lake reservoir and the walls of the hilltop Pingding fort. Most visitors come for the winter blossom and local plum products.

rows.name: Yanglie Water Village, Xuanhan
rows.summary: An open rural leisure area of about 6.8 km² along the Zhou River near Xuanhan, developed since 2013. It strings together the Yanglie village centre with displays of Ba culture, a riverside promenade, the Yuzixi wetland park, a cycle path, flower fields used as a wedding-photo base and a play area called Ba People's Happy Valley. It is a suburban outing spot, best in spring and autumn.

rows.name: Zhenfo Mountain Temples
rows.summary: Zhenfo Mountain, in Fushan town about 35 km from Dazhou city, is topped by a Qing-dynasty complex of temples, among them Dehua Temple and the Jade Emperor and Tianzi halls, where Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist worship share one hillside. The wider scenic area adds forested ridges, karst caves and Yanzhi Lake.

rows.name: Deyang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Deyang's Confucian temple, one of the largest in Sichuan, covers about 28,000 m² in the city centre. First built in the Southern Song, it moved here in 1368 and was rebuilt between 1848 and 1855; along its axis stand a great screen wall, the Lingxing Gate, a semicircular pool, the Dacheng Gate and the double-eaved, seven-bay Dacheng Hall.

rows.name: Golden Qingping, Mianzhu
rows.summary: A mountain leisure area around Qingping, a small town in the Longmen Mountains north-west of Mianzhu, where a former mining district has been turned into a tourist area. Old mine tracks now carry a vintage-style steam sightseeing train, and the town promotes forest walks, a pleasant mountain climate and a mix of Qiang and Han folk culture. It suits a day or an overnight stay in the mountains rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Huijian Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Huijian village in Huilan, just east of Shifang city, traditionally said to date back to the Tang. Its present halls, among them the Great Buddha Hall, the Juehuang Hall and a sutra library, are of the Ming and Qing periods and keep early painted decoration on their beams, ceilings and brackets; it was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Jiannanchun Distillery Site (Tianyi Laohao)
rows.summary: The Tianyi Laohao workshops in central Mianzhu are the Qing-dynasty distillery of the Jiannanchun baijiu company, with old fermentation pits still in use. Also listed as national industrial heritage, the site lies on Jiannan Old Street, where visitors can watch traditional distilling, and the Jiannanchun liquor history museum is nearby.

rows.name: Jiulong Mountain–Lutang Mountain Tourist Area, Mianzhu
rows.summary: A rural tourism belt along the foot of the Longmen Mountains west of Mianzhu, spread over several townships. It combines the Jiulong village tourism area with farm restaurants and hill walks, the China Rose Valley, a large Damask rose plantation, and the Lutang hot-spring resort, fed by a natural thermal spring. It suits a relaxed day of countryside, flowers and bathing rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Longju Temple
rows.summary: Founded in the Tang and rebuilt under the Ming and Qing, Longju Temple keeps a Middle Hall built in 1447. Its ten mural panels, about 86 m² painted in 1466 with the Twelve Bodhisattvas of Perfect Enlightenment, are regarded as among the finest Ming temple murals in Sichuan; the gate and sutra library were rebuilt after 1986.

rows.name: Luocheng Ruins and Fanghu Park
rows.summary: Guanghan stands on the site of Luo, the Han-dynasty county town that Liu Bei besieged in 214, the campaign in which his adviser Pang Tong was killed. The protected ruins of the old city lie within Fanghu Park, a lakeside public park in the centre of Guanghan.

rows.name: Mianzhu New Year Print Village
rows.summary: Mianzhu woodblock New Year prints, printed from carved blocks and then coloured by hand, are one of China's four great New Year print traditions and have been national intangible cultural heritage since 2006. This village area in Xiaode, south of Mianzhu, is one of the city's three centres of print-making, where door gods and auspicious scenes are produced and displayed.

rows.name: Pang Tong Shrine and Tomb
rows.summary: The shrine and tomb of Pang Tong (179–214), the adviser to Liu Bei who was killed by an arrow during the campaign for Sichuan, an episode retold in Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The shrine, restored in 1691, has a gate, main and side halls with statues of Pang Tong and Zhuge Liang, and the tomb beside it under old cypresses. It lies at Baima Pass, on the old road north from Chengdu.

rows.name: Xiaoquan Old Town
rows.summary: An old market town on the Chengdu Plain known as the home of Jiang Shi, a model of filial devotion in the classic Twenty-Four Filial Exemplars, who is honoured at the Jiang Xiao Shrine. Its sights include old streets and the Yanzuo Temple, whose Longhu Sarira Pagoda is listed as a Yuan-dynasty structure.

rows.name: Yijiaheba Rural Tourism Area, Guanghan
rows.summary: A village-run leisure area at Youyi village in Sanshui town, where the Yazi, Shiting and Mianyuan rivers meet east of Guanghan, built up around fish ponds, orchards and farmland. Weekend visitors come for angling, fruit picking, farm meals and a water park, and the village is a national leisure-fishery demonstration base. It is a local family outing rather than a sight in its own right.

rows.name: Zhongjiang North Pagoda
rows.summary: A slender, square brick pagoda with many tiers of eaves, dating from the Song dynasty and standing on a hilltop on the north side of Zhongjiang's county town. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: 18th Army Cave Dwellings, Ganzi
rows.summary: In 1951, soldiers of the People's Liberation Army's 18th Army dug cave dwellings into a hillside about 4 km from Ganzi town while building Ganzi airfield, in support of the army's march into Tibet. More than a thousand caves survive across the slope, and a small cave museum at the site explains how they were built.

rows.name: Bage Mani Wall
rows.summary: The Bage Mani Wall is a long wall built entirely of stones carved with Buddhist mantras and images, running across the grassland of Shiqu County. Together with the Songge (Gsumge) Mani Stone Castle it is protected as a national heritage site dating from the Ming and Qing dynasties, and local Tibetans still add carved stones and walk around it as an act of devotion.

rows.name: Beri Monastery
rows.summary: Beri Monastery stands on a hillside above the north bank of the Yalong River about 10 km west of Ganzi town, and its present buildings date from the Qing dynasty. In 1936 its lama, the 5th Gedar Rinpoche, assisted the Red Army as it passed through Ganzi on the Long March, and the national heritage listing commemorates the monastery's role from then until his death in 1950.

rows.name: Bori Bridge
rows.summary: Bori Bridge is a wooden cantilever bridge across the Yalong River in Xinlong County, 125 metres long with a 60-metre span, the longest-spanning bridge of its kind surviving in the Tibetan areas. A bridge was first built here at the end of the Yuan or start of the Ming dynasty, and the present structure dates from the Qing.

rows.name: Chachenggou Hot Springs, Xiangcheng
rows.summary: A valley at Kemai village in Ranwu township, Xiangcheng County, where the county counts 108 hot springs between 17°C and 85°C within half a square kilometre. Bathing outdoors in the springs is an old local custom, which gives them the name Tianyu ('sky bath'), and the 4A area, rated in 2022, also takes in canyon pastures, alpine lakes and traces of the old tea-horse road. It lies on the Greater Shangri-La loop road between Daocheng and Shangri-La.

rows.name: Dadu River Suspension Bridge, Luding
rows.summary: A steel suspension bridge 132 metres long across the Dadu River, about 900 metres upstream of the old Luding chain bridge, built between November 1950 and the end of May 1951 by highway engineers, army engineering troops and local labourers to carry the new Sichuan–Tibet Highway over the river. Its gate-shaped towers carry the name 'Dadu River Bridge' in Liu Bocheng's calligraphy and a couplet by Zhu De, and screen walls at the west end bear an account of the construction and Mao Zedong's poem 'The Long March'. It has been closed to traffic since around 1970, when a new arch bridge was built upstream, and its fenced-off span is best seen in full from the opposite bank.

rows.name: Dengma Wetland Park
rows.summary: Dengma Wetland Park takes in riverside wetland around Zhengke and Luoxu in the Jinsha River valley of southern Shiqu County, on the border with Tibet. At about 3,300 metres the Luoxu area lies well below the rest of Shiqu, a county whose plateau averages more than 4,000 metres and which is among the most remote parts of Sichuan.

rows.name: Derge Parkhang
rows.summary: The Derge Parkhang is a working Tibetan printing house founded in 1729 by Tenpa Tsering, king of Derge, and attached to the Sakya-school Gonchen Monastery. It holds what is described as the world's largest collection of carved Tibetan woodblocks, from which scriptures, commentaries and works on history and medicine are still printed by hand, with printers working in pairs to ink the blocks and roll the paper.

rows.name: Duoraogamu Cultural Park, Tagong
rows.summary: A cultural park below Mount Zhara (Yala) near Tagong, rated 4A in February 2025 and built around the Minyak Tibetan culture of the area. It has a Minyak culture and arts centre, a tea-horse road trading hall and areas for Tibetan medicine, folk customs, nomad life, handicrafts and farming, while hot-spring and guesthouse facilities are being developed. It works as an introduction to local culture on the road between Kangding and Tagong.

rows.name: Fudi Serthar Cultural Area (former Waxu Tribe area), Luoruo
rows.summary: A 4A cultural area listed at Luoruo, the township in the Larung valley of Serthar County, which until recently went by the name Waxu Tribe Cultural Tourism Area. Xinhua describes it as a living showcase of Tibetan culture, where local communities are still organised along traditional clan lines and customs from the Gesar epic era survive. Luoruo is also home to the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, founded in 1980 and one of the largest Tibetan Buddhist academies, whose students' small red-painted dwellings cover the valley slopes.

rows.name: Gesar King City, Garzê
rows.summary: A newly built cultural complex on the south-eastern edge of Garzê county town, begun in 2017, opened in 2019 and themed on King Gesar, hero of the Tibetan epic, with zones for Gesar culture, the epic, grassland and wetland. It forms one scenic area with the Yalong Bay wetland park along the Yalong River, which also offers farming and herding experiences. It suits travellers on the G317 interested in the Gesar epic tradition.

rows.name: Gsumge Mani Stone Castle
rows.summary: The Gsumge (Songge) Mani Stone Castle is a rectangular mass of stacked mani stones, carved with mantras and Buddhist images, about 73 by 47 metres and 9 metres high, rising to 15 metres, on the Zachuka grassland of Shiqu County. Built without any frame or mortar, it hides a maze of narrow corridors around a central shrine to King Gesar and his generals. Local tradition links it to the Gesar epic, and carved stones from the 11th–12th centuries have been found within it.

rows.name: Huiyuan Temple (Gata)
rows.summary: Huiyuan Temple was founded in 1728 on the orders of the Qing Yongzheng Emperor in the Gata valley north of Bamei, and the 7th Dalai Lama lived here for seven years before returning to Tibet; the 11th Dalai Lama was born in a nearby village in 1838. Red walls set with 108 white stupas enclose a large courtyard and a multi-storey main hall with three bronze Buddha statues.

rows.name: Kangba Hanzi Village, Yajiang
rows.summary: A Tibetan village on the G318 at Xi'eluo, formerly called Jiezhu, which registered the name 'Kangba Hanzi' (men of Kham) as a trademark in 2005 and turned to tourism; it became a 4A area in 2022. Solid timber Tibetan houses line the valley, many now run as family guesthouses, alongside a Kham-style shopping street, with old ruins on Guogang summit and small lakes in the surrounding hills. It suits travellers on the Sichuan–Tibet road looking for a village overnight stop.

rows.name: Kangba Wendu Cultural Park
rows.summary: Kangba Wendu is a large, newly built culture park beside Dêgê town presenting the crafts and traditions for which Dêgê is known across Kham. Its many exhibition halls cover Kham culture, the Gesar epic, the southern school of Tibetan medicine and the region's traditional crafts.

rows.name: Kasa Lake (Liangquhe Scenic Area)
rows.summary: Kasa Lake is a freshwater plateau lake at roughly 3,510 metres, set among grassland and hills just off the G317, the northern Sichuan–Tibet highway, in western Luhuo County. It is the centre of the Liangquhe Scenic Area and a haunt of waterbirds, and makes an easy stop on the drive between Luhuo and Ganzi towns. Chonggu, the township around the lake, also has a site of the ancient stone-cist tombs for which Luhuo is known.

rows.name: Kathok Monastery
rows.summary: Kathok, founded in 1159, is one of the six great 'mother monasteries' of the Nyingma school of Tibetan Buddhism, perched at about 4,000 metres some 700 metres above the valley floor in Baiyu County. It was rebuilt in 1656 and again after its destruction in the 1960s, and a new temple and assembly hall were completed in 2016.

rows.name: Lalong Tso Wetland
rows.summary: Lalong Tso is a national wetland park high on the plateau of eastern Baiyu County, where moraine-dammed lakes lie among glacier-polished rocks and boulders left by ancient glaciers. Its marshes and lakes are said to be a breeding ground for black-necked cranes.

rows.name: Lharima Stone-Slab Village
rows.summary: Lharima, in Zhazong village in southern Xinlong County, is a Tibetan settlement of some 370 households whose two- and three-storey houses are roofed with stone slabs and linked by lanes paved with blue-grey stone. The village forms one ensemble with Zhazong Monastery, a painted stone scripture stupa and a group of chortens, and its houses keep the traditional layout of livestock on the ground floor and living quarters above.

rows.name: Litang Monastery
rows.summary: Litang Monastery, begun in 1581 in the time of the Third Dalai Lama, is regarded as the largest Gelug monastery in Kham. Its halls climb the slope on the northern edge of Litang town at about 4,000 metres, and much of the complex has been rebuilt since the 1980s.

rows.name: Litang Old Town
rows.summary: Litang's old quarter, on the north side of this high-plateau town at about 4,000 metres, covers roughly 1.5 square kilometres: some 4,000 Tibetan houses in 13 old villages, many still lived in by local families. At its heart is Renkang Street, where a traditional house is honoured as the birthplace of the 7th Dalai Lama, Kelsang Gyatso, and Litang Monastery stands on the hillside just above.

rows.name: Luding Bridge
rows.summary: Luding Bridge is an iron-chain suspension bridge spanning about 100 metres across the Dadu River in Luding town, built in 1705–1706 on the orders of the Kangxi Emperor as a key crossing on the road between Sichuan and Tibet. In May 1935, during the Long March, Red Army troops captured the bridge, an episode known in China as the 'Seizing of Luding Bridge'. Visitors can walk across its swaying plank deck, and a memorial hall nearby presents the history of the crossing.

rows.name: Minyak Holy Land, Kangding
rows.summary: A tourist area west of Zheduo Pass in Kangding, presented as the first themed area devoted to the culture of the Minyak (Muya) Tibetans, in an area that was once a checkpoint on the tea-horse road. It takes in grassland and flower meadows, traditional herding pastures, viewpoints such as the 'Princess's Dressing Table' lake, and Ranti Monastery, a Tibetan Buddhist monastery said to be more than 600 years old. It is an easy stop on the Sichuan–Tibet road between Kangding and Xinduqiao.

rows.name: Moshi Park
rows.summary: Moshi ('ink stone') Park is a forest of dark grey rock pinnacles near Bamei in Daofu County, standing out against the surrounding grassland. The stones are described as mylonite, rock crushed and sheared along the Xianshui River fault, which runs past Bamei, and then weathered into spires.

rows.name: Mugecuo Lake
rows.summary: Mugecuo is an alpine lake at about 3,780 metres in the mountains north-west of Kangding, nearly 3 km long and fringed by forest, grassland and snow peaks. The scenic area also takes in smaller alpine lakes and hot springs nearby, and is part of the Mount Gongga national scenic area. Its official name, 'Kangding Love Song', borrows the town's famous folk tune.

rows.name: Muri Mani Wall
rows.summary: The Muri Mani Wall is a long wall of stones carved with Buddhist mantras and images on the grasslands of Sêrxü (Shiqu) county in north-western Sichuan, built up by pilgrims over many centuries. The national listing dates it from the Tang to the Qing dynasties, and pilgrims still walk circuits around it.

rows.name: Palpung Monastery
rows.summary: Palpung, at Babang in Dêgê County, is the historic seat of the Tai Situ lamas and the mother monastery of the Karma Kagyu school in Kham; the present monastery was founded in 1727 by the 8th Tai Situ with the support of the king of Derge. It is known for its large library and thangka collection and its link with the Karma Gadri painting style, and has been restored since the 1980s.

rows.name: Qingde White Tibetan Villages
rows.summary: Around Qingde, just south of Xiangcheng town, villages of whitewashed rammed-earth Tibetan houses stand among terraced barley fields in the valley. These white houses are a signature of the Xiangcheng area, on the road between Shangri-La and Daocheng.

rows.name: Sampeling Monastery
rows.summary: Sampeling, in full Ganden Sampel Norbu Ling, is the main Gelug monastery of Xiangcheng, first built in 1669. It was destroyed in 1906, rebuilt in 1919 and destroyed again during the Cultural Revolution, and the present complex on the hill above the town dates from its rebuilding in 1995.

rows.name: Sangdui Red Grass Wetland
rows.summary: In the river valley at Sangdui, north of Daocheng, shallow pools are filled with an aquatic grass that turns deep red in autumn. It is a popular photo stop beside the highway between Litang and Daocheng.

rows.name: Tsopu Valley
rows.summary: Tsopu is a high valley in northern Batang County whose sacred lake, Tsopu Lake, lies backed by snow peaks and forest. Smaller lakes and the small Tsopu Monastery lie nearby.

rows.name: Wuxu Lake
rows.summary: Wuxu Lake is a clear green barrier lake set among mountains about 25 km from Jiulong town, within the Mount Gongga national scenic area. It lies higher than the county town, itself at about 2,900 metres, so the air is thin and nights are cold even in summer.

rows.name: Xiangcheng Rammed-Earth Towers
rows.summary: Xiangcheng's rammed-earth watchtowers are tall defensive towers of packed earth, dated to the Ming dynasty, standing near the county town. They share the valley with Xiangcheng's whitewashed earthen houses and are under 2 km from Sampeling Monastery, so the two make an easy combined visit.

rows.name: Xinlong Red Mountains
rows.summary: The Red Mountains lie in Yinduo township in the north-west of Xinlong County. They are a high-altitude Danxia landscape of red rock ridges and cliffs strung out along a valley.

rows.name: Xinluhai (Yilhun Lha Tso)
rows.summary: Xinluhai, Yilhun Lha Tso in Tibetan and officially Yulong Latso, is a glacial lake at about 4,020 metres at the foot of Chola Mountain, about 3 km long and dammed by glacial moraine; it is described as the largest lake of its kind in China. It lies just off the G317 highway about 10 km west of Manigange, an easy stop on the road between Ganzi and Dêgê.

rows.name: Yala Snow Mountain, Daofu
rows.summary: Yala (Zhara Lhatse), the 5,820-metre sacred peak that dominates the Tagong grassland, also rises above Daofu County to the north, and this scenic area covers that northern side. It takes in forest, meadows and alpine lakes beneath the snowfields.

rows.name: Zangbala Flower Fields, Litang
rows.summary: A flower-field and farm area at Hange village in Zhuosang township, south of Litang, beside the G227 road and next to the Haizishan nature reserve. Summer flower fields, starry night skies and farm sightseeing are the draw, with camping, horse riding, archery and fruit and vegetable picking, and guesthouses and restaurants are being added. It suits a stop on the drive south from Litang rather than a special trip.

rows.name: Baozhen Fortress
rows.summary: Baozhen Fortress is a walled clan stronghold that the Duan family began building in 1910 on a ridge in rural Wusheng county, enclosing courtyards, halls and storerooms behind stone walls about 2 km long and on average 6.5 m high, with a continuous gallery of gun ports. The old Duan family compound stands just outside, and the fortress survived later decades because it was used as a grain store.

rows.name: Chongxiang Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: At Chongxiang Temple, in the hills north-east of Guang'an city, Buddhist figures and inscriptions were carved into the cliff over more than a thousand years, from the Sui dynasty to the Qing. The carvings became a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Former residence of Deng Xiaoping
rows.summary: The late-Qing farmhouse in Paifang village where Deng Xiaoping was born in 1904 now stands in a large landscaped memorial park about 6 km north of central Guang'an. Visitors see the family's rooms, the neighbouring Hanlin and silkworm-house courtyards, a statue of Deng and an exhibition hall of relics from his life. His old primary-school buildings in the city belong to the same protected site.

rows.name: Huaying Mountain
rows.summary: Huaying Mountain is a long ridge on the eastern side of the Sichuan Basin, dividing the central Sichuan hills from the parallel ridges further east, and the scenic area above Huaying city is promoted for its stone forest, caves and forest walks. Baoding peak (1,586 m) on the same range has been a Buddhist pilgrimage site since the Tang dynasty. In the late 1940s the mountains sheltered the eastern Sichuan Communist guerrillas whose uprising lies behind characters in the novel Red Crag.

rows.name: Shenlong Mountain Ba Stone City
rows.summary: A hill park on the southern edge of Guang'an's new town, rising about 81 metres above the city as its highest point. Its centrepiece is a fortress-like complex built from tens of thousands of massive dressed stone blocks, presented as a stronghold of the ancient Ba people on the old route between the Ba, Shu and Qin lands. The summit gives wide views over the city.

rows.name: White Pagoda, Guang'an
rows.summary: Guang'an's White Pagoda is a multi-storey Song-dynasty masonry pagoda on the edge of the city. A national heritage site since 2013, it is an easy stop to combine with Deng Xiaoping's former residence north of town.

rows.name: Bailin Ancient Town
rows.summary: A small town in the south of Zhaohua District that grew up around the Bailin post station on the southern branch of the old Shu Road. A stretch of flagstone street survives, lined with timber-framed houses in the northern Sichuan vernacular style; local accounts also mention a Kuixing Pavilion, Guangshan Temple and Bailin Lake beside the town.

rows.name: Donghekou Earthquake Relics Park
rows.summary: A memorial park where the Wenchuan earthquake of 12 May 2008 brought down whole mountainsides around the village of Donghekou in Qingchuan County, burying more than 780 people. The collapsed slopes, rubble fields and lakes dammed by landslides have been preserved across an area of about 50 km², and geologists study it for the variety of landslide forms it shows.

rows.name: Heming Mountain Taoist Carvings, Jiange
rows.summary: A hill about 1 km east of Pu'an, the old county town of Jiange, with 21 niches and 88 carved figures, mainly Taoist, made between the Northern Wei and the Republican era. Its best-known pieces are a figure of the deity Changsheng Baoming Tianzun, described as unique among Taoist carvings in China, a stele reproducing Yan Zhenqing's calligraphy of the 'Hymn to the Restoration of the Tang', and an inscription with a text by the Tang poet Li Shangyin.

rows.name: Huangze Temple
rows.summary: Huangze Temple, at the foot of Wulong Mountain on the west bank of the Jialing River, is described as the only temple in China dedicated to Wu Zetian, the Tang empress who by tradition was born in Guangyuan. Its cliff holds about 1,200 Buddhist sculptures in six caves and dozens of niches, begun in the sixth century and mostly carved in the Tang, while the halls display a stone figure traditionally said to show the empress herself. The temple now also serves as a museum.

rows.name: Jueyuan Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the west side of Wulian, a town on the old Shu Road in southern Jiange County, founded in the Tang and rebuilt in 1457 under the Ming. Its main hall, a single-eaved building with a hip-and-gable roof, keeps about 140 m² of Ming wall paintings on its walls and more behind the altar.

rows.name: Longmen Pavilion Scenic Area
rows.summary: Longmen Pavilion is one of the best-known cliff-side plank-road sections of the ancient Jinniu Road near Chaotian, where the route between Qin and Shu was carried along the cliffs. The scenic area also takes in the Longmen stone forest and a group of caves.

rows.name: Micang Mountain Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A canyon landscape in the Micang Mountains of northern Wangcang County, on the Sichuan–Shaanxi border, part of the natural divide between northern and southern China and rich in plant and animal life. Its forests are known for their autumn colour, with ridge trails, viewing platforms and lookout towers.

rows.name: Mingyue Gorge
rows.summary: A narrow gorge of the Jialing River near Chaotian where six generations of routes squeeze through side by side: an ancient plank road, the Jinniu post road, a boat-haulers' towpath, the river itself, the Sichuan–Shaanxi highway and the Baoji–Chengdu railway. About 2 km of plank walkway has been rebuilt on the original beam holes cut into the cliff, among the best preserved in China, so visitors can walk the cliff face above the river. The gorge forms part of the Jianmen Shu Road heritage site.

rows.name: Mumen Conference Site
rows.summary: Mumen Temple, built in the Kangxi reign of the Qing on a hillside above Mumen town in south-eastern Wangcang County, hosted a six-day conference of the Red Fourth Front Army's leaders in late June 1933, after which the army expanded rapidly in the Sichuan–Shaanxi base area. The temple now displays relics from the Red Army period.

rows.name: Pingle Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural scenic area at Yuanba, south-east of Guangyuan city, built around Pingle Temple and said to take in the wooded Qifeng Gorge and Ziyun Lake. It is mainly a local weekend escape for walks in the gorge, with the temple adding some interest.

rows.name: Qingxi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A small walled town on the upper Qingzhu River at the foot of Motian Ridge, close to where Guangyuan, Mianyang and Gansu meet, with surviving stretches of Ming city wall and lanes of timber houses in the northern Sichuan style. It is the base for the Tangjiahe reserve and for walks on the Yinping Road, the mountain route by which the Wei general Deng Ai's army entered Shu in 263.

rows.name: Red Army City, Wangcang
rows.summary: The old streets of Donghe, the Wangcang county town, which from November 1934 housed the Red Fourth Front Army's headquarters and more than 40 party, government and military bodies, making it the centre of the Sichuan–Shaanxi base in its final phase and the army's assembly point for the Long March. Three main streets and two lanes of Qing-era timber houses survive, and small memorial halls occupy former headquarters buildings.

rows.name: Tangjiahe National Nature Reserve
rows.summary: A forested mountain reserve of about 400 km² in the far west of Qingchuan County, established in 1978 and now part of the Giant Panda National Park, ranging from about 1,100 m to almost 3,900 m. Its forests shelter giant pandas, Sichuan takin and golden snub-nosed monkeys, and visitors explore by road and trail along the Tangjia River valley. Qingxi ancient town, just to the south, is the gateway.

rows.name: Thousand-Buddha Cliff (Guangyuan)
rows.summary: A cliff on the east bank of the Jialing River north of Guangyuan, honeycombed with Buddhist niches carved from the late Northern Wei to the Ming, most of them in the Tang. Some 848 niches with more than 7,000 figures survive along a face about 400 m long and over 40 m high, although more than half of the original carvings were destroyed when the Sichuan–Shaanxi highway was cut along its foot in 1935–1936. The main caves include the Great Buddha Cave and the Lotus Cave.

rows.name: Zengjiashan
rows.summary: A karst upland in Chaotian District, mostly 1,300–1,400 m above sea level, where stone forests, sinkholes, gorges and caves are scattered among farmland and forest. Its cool summers have made it one of northern Sichuan's main summer retreats, with a great many guesthouses and farm stays, and it often sees snow in winter.

rows.name: Zhaohua Ancient Town
rows.summary: A small walled town where the Bailong River meets the Jialing, known in antiquity as Jiameng; after the Qin conquered Shu and Ba in 316 BC they set up a county here, and the town calls itself the first county seat in Sichuan. Inside the gates are flagstone lanes of old houses and the Longmen Academy, and nearby is the tomb of Fei Yi, one of the leading ministers of the Three Kingdoms state of Shu Han. The town lies on the old Jinniu Road and is an easy stop between Guangyuan and Jianmen Pass.

rows.name: Zhongzipu Microlith Archaeology Museum
rows.name_zh: 中子铺细石器考古博物馆
rows.summary: A museum opened in October 2024 in Zhongzi town for the Zhongzipu site, where excavations in 1990 and 1991 recovered about 20,000 finds, among them microliths (tiny flaked stone tools) from a layer dated to roughly 7,000 to 6,000 years ago. Archaeologists count the site among the earliest Neolithic remains in the Sichuan Basin. Its 3,000 square metres of galleries show more than 1,000 finds, including microblade cores, scrapers and polished stone tools, with reconstructions of how they were made and used.

rows.name: China Nuclear Fusion Museum
rows.summary: The former experiment hall of the Southwestern Institute of Physics, a Third Front nuclear research institute, where the HL-1 tokamak (China Circulator One) was completed in 1984; it is listed nationally as the site of China's first controlled nuclear fusion experimental device. Since 2012 the hall has housed the China Nuclear Fusion Museum, with the HL-1 device itself as the centrepiece of displays on the history of the country's fusion research.

rows.name: Dafo Chan Monastery, Emeishan
rows.summary: An active Buddhist monastery in Emeishan city, about 5 km east of Baoguo Temple at the foot of Mount Emei, run as a Buddhist cultural tourism area. Its halls and courtyards can be visited on the way to or from the mountain without entering the Mount Emei scenic area.

rows.name: Feilai Hall, Emeishan
rows.summary: A temple complex about 2 km north of Emeishan city whose main Feilai Hall, rebuilt in 1279 and repaired in 1298, is the largest surviving Yuan-dynasty timber building in Sichuan. Originally a Song temple to the god of Mount Tai, it gradually became a Buddhist temple from the late Ming, and its halls climb the hillside along a single axis. It is a worthwhile stop for anyone interested in early Chinese timber architecture on the way to or from Mount Emei.

rows.name: Heizhugou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Xiaoliangshan mountains of Ebian Yi Autonomous County, whose scenic area covers about 575 square kilometres at altitudes from roughly 1,500 to 4,288 metres. Its old-growth forest, gorges and streams are rich in wildlife and plants. Unconfirmed stories of people and animals going missing here in the 20th century led the media to call it the 'Bermuda Triangle of the East', and its original Yi name, Sihuo, is said to mean 'valley of death'.

rows.name: Jiajiang Thousand Buddha Cliff & Dongfeng Weir
rows.summary: A sandstone cliff on the bank of the Qingyi River just outside Jiajiang town, carved with some 270 Buddhist niches; most date from the Tang dynasty, with later additions into the Qing. Alongside runs the Dongfeng Weir, a working irrigation canal that was among the first World Heritage Irrigation Structures named in 2014.

rows.name: Jinkou Grand Canyon of the Dadu River
rows.summary: A deep gorge of the Dadu River in mountainous Jinkouhe District, listed both as a 4A scenic area and as a National Water Conservancy Scenic Area. The Chengdu–Kunming railway threads along the canyon through tunnels, and Guancunba station, built in 1966 in the canyon, sits partly inside a tunnel. Jinkouhe District is almost entirely mountain, with nearly 2,800 m between its lowest and highest points.

rows.name: Lei Family Residence, Jingyan
rows.summary: A large Qing manor built in 1773 for the family of Lei Chang, a Qianlong-era court official, on the edge of Qianfo town in Jingyan County. Inside a stone enclosure wall about 4 metres high, four successive courtyards along the main axis and their side wings hold 121 rooms around 12 light wells, with carved timber and stone details. Some rooms now hold displays on the Lei family, old workshops and farming life.

rows.name: Leshan Wumu Culture Museum
rows.summary: A large museum in Suji town devoted to wumu, the dark timber formed when ancient trees were buried in old riverbeds by earthquakes, floods or landslides. Its halls show raw buried trunks alongside wumu carvings, and one hall lets you watch carvers at work. Suji lies on the road between Leshan and Mount Emei, so the museum is an easy stop between the two.

rows.name: Luocheng Ancient Town
rows.summary: A market town in Qianwei county whose main street is wide in the middle and narrows at each end, giving it the outline of a boat; the street is traditionally dated to the late Ming dynasty. Broad eaves resting on rows of wooden columns form covered arcades along both sides, shading the shopfronts from sun and rain. Luocheng was named a Sichuan provincial historic town in 1992.

rows.name: Mahao Cliff Tombs
rows.summary: A cemetery of rock-cut tombs dug into the sandstone of Lingyun Hill beside the Leshan Giant Buddha; a 1985 survey counted 330 tombs along more than 300 metres of cliff, most from the Eastern Han dynasty. Above one tomb entrance is a small seated Buddha in Gandharan style, considered one of the earliest Buddhist images in China. A site museum displays the tombs and their carvings.

rows.name: Muchuan Bamboo Sea
rows.summary: Muchuan county in the hills of southern Leshan is thickly covered in bamboo, and this scenic area beside National Road 213 near Yongfu town showcases it. Roads and paths lead through bamboo-covered ridges, valleys and streams.

rows.name: Nongfu Spring Emeishan Factory Tour
rows.name_zh: 农夫山泉峨眉山工业旅游区
rows.summary: A working bottled-water plant of the Nongfu Spring company in Gaoqiao town, at the foot of Mount Emei, opened to visitors as an industrial tourism site. Tours show the production line for natural drinking water and spring-water testing, along with displays on the company and its water source, and the site is used for school study trips. It suits families and anyone curious about modern manufacturing more than scenery seekers.

rows.name: Oriental Buddha Park
rows.summary: A privately run theme park beside the Leshan Giant Buddha, filled with reproductions of Buddhist statues and carvings in stone and other materials. It holds around 3,000 statues, including a reclining Buddha about 170 m long. It is a modern park, run separately from the Giant Buddha site, for visitors who want more Buddhist imagery after the main sight.

rows.name: Qianwei Confucius Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple in Yujin, the county town of Qianwei, founded in the Northern Song and rebuilt several times, with buildings mainly of the Ming and Qing; it is one of the largest Confucian temples in Sichuan. Its gates, halls and courtyards follow the formal axis typical of temples to Confucius, and it is noted for its wood and stone carving.

rows.name: Sanjiang White Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty pagoda in Sanjiang town, Jingyan county, built of brick and timber on a square plan. Its 13 storeys rise to about 28 metres in the dense-eave style, each marked by a closely spaced projecting roof.

rows.name: Sichuan Tourism Expo Park, Emeishan
rows.summary: A modern complex of about 87 hectares in the eastern new district of Emeishan city that combines exhibition, culture and tourism venues with city shopping. It is of most use to travellers already staying in Emeishan, rather than a destination in its own right.

rows.name: World Jasmine Expo Park, Qianwei
rows.summary: A jasmine-themed agricultural park in Qingxi town that opened in 2020, with a core area of about 87 hectares planted with more than 120 jasmine varieties. Qianwei is a major jasmine-growing county, with about 5,700 hectares of jasmine supplying the scented-tea trade. It is a rural flower park rather than a historic site, best for those interested in tea and gardens.

rows.name: Wuyou Temple & Lidui
rows.summary: A Buddhist monastery more than a thousand years old on the summit of Wuyou Hill, next to the Leshan Giant Buddha; it is the oldest temple in the area and one of China's officially designated key Buddhist temples. The hill itself, known as Lidui ('the detached mound') because a channel separates it from neighbouring Lingyun Hill, is protected as a national heritage site.

rows.name: Yanggong Que, Jiajiang
rows.summary: A pair of carved stone pillar-gates (que) in the countryside south-east of Jiajiang town, dated by the heritage authorities to between the Han and Song dynasties. Que of this kind marked the approach to tombs and shrines, and Sichuan holds a large share of those that survive in China.

rows.name: Boshiwahei Rock Carvings
rows.summary: Boshiwahei is a group of large boulders in the hills of Wanchang township, Zhaojue County, incised with Buddhist figures and dated to the Tang and Song periods, when this region lay within the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms. It is a rare early Buddhist site in the Yi heartland of Liangshan and is protected as a national heritage site.

rows.name: Huili Ancient Town
