rows.summary: Huili, in the far south of Liangshan near the Yunnan border, has been a county seat since the Western Han dynasty and was named a national historic and cultural city in 2011. Its old quarter keeps lanes of traditional shopfronts and courtyard houses, entered through the north gate tower, Gongji Lou.

rows.name: Huili Conference Site
rows.summary: In May 1935, after crossing the Jinsha River on the Long March, the Red Army spent about two weeks around Huili, and the Communist Party's Politburo held an enlarged meeting at Tiechang on the outskirts of the town. The meeting site is now a memorial area presenting this stage of the Long March.

rows.name: Jianchang Old Town, Xichang
rows.summary: Jianchang is the old name of Xichang, and its old town on the north side of the modern city keeps stretches of the former city wall and the Datong Gate, with lanes of older houses, teahouses and snack stalls inside. It makes an easy evening stroll after a day at Qionghai Lake.

rows.name: Kaidilila Hot Springs, Ningnan
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Pisha town, Ningnan County, in southern Liangshan. The Liangshan government describes a naturally flowing spring of about 70°C rich in fluoride and other minerals, feeding dozens of linked outdoor pools, and the resort also has private spring courtyards and a self-drive camp. It draws visitors from Yunnan and Panzhihua and suits a rest stop on a road trip through the region.

rows.name: Lingshan Temple, Mianning
rows.summary: Lingshan ('Spirit Mountain') is a forested mountain scenic area about 17 km east of Mianning town, centred on Lingshan Temple, a Buddhist temple whose halls are built up the hillside. The temple is an active place of worship, and local tradition dates its founding to the Qianlong reign of the Qing dynasty.

rows.name: Luoji Mountain
rows.summary: Luoji Mountain is a range running south from Qionghai Lake near Xichang, with summits above 4,300 metres. Its upper slopes keep well-preserved landforms carved by Ice Age glaciers, while primeval forest with rhododendrons and rare trees covers the lower ground. A cable car from the Puge side lifts visitors into the high country.

rows.name: Mahu Lake
rows.summary: Mahu is a deep mountain lake in Leibo County, in the far east of Liangshan, formed where glaciers dammed an old river valley and measured in 1982 at 134 metres at its deepest point. Forest covers the surrounding hills, and the Menghuo Hall by the lake is a provincial heritage site. It is a quiet stop well away from the main tourist routes.

rows.name: Yihai Lake (Yihai Alliance Site)
rows.summary: Yihai is a small mountain lake in northern Mianning County where, on 22 May 1935, during the Long March, the Red Army commander Liu Bocheng and Xiaoyedan, a leader of the local Yi Guoji clan, swore brotherhood in a blood oath, allowing the army to pass through Yi territory. The meeting place on the grassy slope above the lake is a protected heritage site, and the episode is known in China as the Yihai Alliance.

rows.name: Bao'en Pagoda, Luzhou
rows.summary: A seven-storey brick pagoda of the Southern Song dynasty in the old centre of Luzhou, known locally as the White Pagoda. It has been repaired several times since the Ming but keeps its Song outline, and it is a short walk from the Laojiao old cellars.

rows.name: Chunqiu Temple, Xuyong
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty temple to Guan Yu on Shaanxi Street in Xuyong county town, enlarged around 1900. Its name refers to the Spring and Autumn Annals, the classic Guan Yu is traditionally shown reading, and it is known for late-Qing woodcarving on its windows, lintels and other fittings, depicting historical scenes and legends.

rows.name: Dongwo Hydropower Station
rows.summary: A small hydropower station on the Longxi River that Shui Xiheng, a Luzhou engineer who had studied in Germany, began building in 1921 to use a 44-metre natural drop in the Dongwo gorge; it was completed in 1925 as the Jihe power plant with a 140-kilowatt Siemens generator and is still generating today. In 2018 the Chinese Hydraulic Engineering Society recognised it as the first hydropower station in China designed and built by Chinese engineers, and it is also listed as national industrial heritage. A statue of Shui stands at the entrance, two old turbine generators still run in the machine hall, and the gorge around it is laid out as Dongwo Park, popular with local families and school study groups.

rows.name: Dongyunba Umbrella Village, Jiangyang
rows.summary: A rural scenic area at Fenshuiling town, Jiangyang district, combining the Dongyunba national modern-agriculture demonstration park with Sanli ('umbrella village'), a new rural-community street of about 1.1 km built in old-street style and hung with oil-paper umbrellas. Fenshui oil-paper umbrella making, a craft with some 400 years of history, is on China's national intangible heritage list, and the street has an umbrella museum, umbrella-making experiences and hanfu costume shops. It suits craft enthusiasts and photographers.

rows.name: Fenghuang Lake, Naxi
rows.summary: A winding reservoir lake with more than ten islands in Naxi district, south-west of Luzhou, set within some 30 km² of forested hills. The surrounding area takes in gorges, rock formations, waterfalls and caves among forest and bamboo, along with waterside villages and a liquor-making estate. It suits a quiet day in the countryside from Luzhou.

rows.name: Fubao Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town in south-eastern Hejiang County, built on a ridge where streams meet, whose Ming and Qing buildings make up a nationally protected group and one of China's listed historic towns. Its main street, Huilong Street, climbs up and down the crest past timber houses with small grey-tiled roofs, stilted rooms and overhanging galleries above the water, and among them stand temples and guild halls built by settlers from Hubei and Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian and Jiangxi who moved in from the early Qing, such as the Wanshou and Tianhou palaces. Fobao National Forest Park lies in the hills to the south-east.

rows.name: Hejiang Han Stone Coffin Museum
rows.name_zh: 合江汉代画像石棺博物馆
rows.summary: A county museum devoted to the relief-carved stone coffins of the Eastern Han dynasty (25–220 CE) found in cliff tombs around Hejiang, where the Chishui River joins the Yangtze. Such coffins are the most common find from the nationally listed Hejiang cliff tombs, whose 13 groups are cut into riverside cliffs scattered across the county, so the museum is the practical place to see their carving.

rows.name: Huangjing Laolin Forest
rows.summary: A large forested upland in northern Gulin county, protected as a national forest park and a provincial nature reserve, with extensive subtropical evergreen broadleaf forest. Its best-known sight is Bajiedong, a chain of eight waterfalls and rapids along a gorge, and trails lead past streams, deep pools and old trees.

rows.name: Longnao Bridge
rows.summary: A stone beam bridge built in the late 14th century, early in the Ming dynasty, that crosses the Jiuqu River on 12 piers; the middle eight are carved into large dragons, qilin, lions and elephants, heads facing upstream. It is the best known of Luxian's carved 'dragon bridges', a wider group of Ming and Qing bridges across the county that is also nationally listed, and it now stands within the Longqiao Culture Eco-park.

rows.name: Luxian Song Stone Carving Museum
rows.summary: A museum in Luxian county town that displays carved stone panels from the Song-dynasty tombs found across the county, of which more than a hundred are known. The reliefs of guardian warriors, musicians, servants, the four directional animals, furniture and household objects give a detailed picture of daily life in 12th- and 13th-century Sichuan. The tombs themselves, including the nationally listed Puqiao, Changlinggeng and Luopanzui groups, lie on hillsides in the countryside, so the museum is the place to see their carvings.

rows.name: Luzhou Laojiao Old Cellars
rows.summary: The historic core of the Luzhou Laojiao distillery, one of the best-known makers of strong-aroma baijiu, where earthen fermentation pits dating from the Ming dynasty are still in use. The old cellar groups and workshops were listed as a national heritage site in 1996, and the visitor area around Guojiao Square lets you see the working pits and learn how the liquor is made.

rows.name: Qifeng Aqueduct
rows.summary: Two stone arched aqueducts built between 1973 and 1978 to carry irrigation water across the valleys around Qifeng town as part of the Sanxikou reservoir scheme. The larger Huafeng Aqueduct runs for 1,122 metres on 47 main arches and stands up to 43 metres high, while the 1-km Shengli Aqueduct carries a footway beneath its water channel. Both are still used for irrigation and by people crossing on foot.

rows.name: Qingliang Cave Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Ming-dynasty Buddhist cliff carvings at Qingliang Cave in Maling town, in the hills of Xuyong County. The site was listed as a national heritage site in 2013, but little has been published about it, so check access locally before making the trip.

rows.name: Qu Family Manor
rows.summary: A large rural estate built by the Qu family during the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns of the Qing dynasty (roughly 1796–1850) and used into the Republican era. Its more than 80 rooms are arranged around 48 courtyards and guarded by four watchtowers, making it a nationally listed example of a fortified family compound in southern Sichuan.

rows.name: Red Army Long March Site, Shixiangzi
rows.name_zh: 红军长征过石厢子旧址
rows.summary: Shixiangzi, a small Yi township in the hills where Sichuan, Yunnan and Guizhou meet, is where the Central Red Army camped in early February 1935 after its first crossing of the Chishui River, spending the Spring Festival there during the Long March. Sichuan historians place here the 'Jiming Sansheng' meeting ('a rooster crows in three provinces') at which Zhang Wentian replaced Bo Gu at the head of the Communist Party, although sites in Yunnan and Guizhou are also claimed for it. Preserved sites in the township include the meeting site, a Red Army mint and an exchange office of the Chinese Soviet Republic's bank, and a Red Army Long March memorial park holds an exhibition hall on the meeting.

rows.name: Shenbicheng Fortress
rows.summary: The ruins of a Southern Song mountain fortress on a cliff-bound promontory above the Yangtze, built in 1243 when Luzhou's government moved here to resist the Mongols. It held out until 1277, changing hands five times along the way. The east and west gates and much of the wall survive, along with traces of the drill ground, beacon tower and offices and several rock inscriptions recalling the siege.

rows.name: Taiping Ancient Town
rows.summary: A hillside market town on the Chishui River, on the Guizhou border, where the Red Army crossed during the Long March in 1935: the second and fourth of the 'Four Crossings of the Chishui' were made at Taiping Ferry. Its lanes of old houses include the former quarters of the Red Army headquarters, hospital and bank, and a memorial hall up the town's stone steps sets out the history of the campaign.

rows.name: Tianxiandong Scenic Area
rows.summary: A densely forested danxia landscape of red sandstone cliffs, valleys, streams and stepped waterfalls in Naxi district, south of Luzhou. Local legend says the goddess Jiutian Xuannü once lived here, giving the area its name, and the scenic area also takes in the small old town of Ledao on the Yongning River, with streets of Ming and Qing houses.

rows.name: Xianshi Soy Sauce Workshops
rows.summary: A working soy-sauce brewery beside the Chishui river whose old timber workshop courtyard, sloping drying ground and small Sanguan temple go back to a sauce house of the late Qing. Hundreds of glazed earthenware vats stand in rows on the drying ground, where the sauce ferments for three years or more in sun by day and river dew by night, a method listed as national intangible heritage. The old workshop and drying ground have been fully open to visitors since 2025, with hands-on sessions and products such as soy-sauce ice cream.

rows.name: Yaoba Ancient Town
rows.summary: A well-preserved market town on the old road from Luzhou to Chishui in Guizhou, said to have begun as a post station in the Northern Song and to have flourished in the Ming and Qing. Its old streets of Ming and Qing shops, houses and halls are protected together as a national heritage site, and the town has often been used as a film location.

rows.name: Yuantong Temple, Luxian
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Leiba village in Yusi town, in the countryside of northern Luxian, also known as Yuantong Chanlin; it was founded in 1506 and rebuilt in 1608 under the Ming dynasty. Behind an archway gate inscribed with the temple's name stand a front hall and a middle hall, both with double-eaved hip-and-gable roofs, the middle hall resting on four stone columns over 6 metres tall; the Luzhou government describes it as the county's only surviving Ming temple building. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 2002 and as a national one in 2019, and can be paired with the Ming-dynasty Longnao Bridge, about 5 km to the south.

rows.name: Yuchan Mountain Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A wooded hill beside Luxian county town holding more than 400 Ming-dynasty cliff carvings, begun in the Yongle reign. The best-known niche is a Thousand-Armed Guanyin more than 5 metres tall above a small relief of nine dragons bathing the infant Buddha, and another shows the Eighteen Arhats crossing the sea.

rows.name: Zhangba Longan Grove
rows.summary: A large grove of old longan trees in the Qiancao area of Jiangyang district, Luzhou, planted in the Qing dynasty and listed as a Sichuan provincial protected cultural relic in 2007. Now a 4A scenic area on the edge of the city, it hosts an annual longan festival and makes an easy stroll from the centre.

rows.name: Bao'en Temple, Meishan
rows.summary: A village temple south of Meishan founded in the Tang, of which only the main hall survives, built in 1327 under the Yuan and extensively repaired in 1761. Its beam-frame timber structure and single-eaved hip-and-gable roof preserve Song-style building methods, making it a rare survivor for architecture enthusiasts.

rows.name: China Pickle City, Meishan
rows.summary: An industrial zone in Chongli, Dongpo District, where about a hundred companies in the Sichuan pickle (paocai) industry are clustered, run as a 4A industrial-tourism area. Visitors can see the China Paocai Museum, opened in 2012, upgraded in 2018 and described as the country's only museum devoted to pickles, walk a pickle-themed shopping street and view some factory production lines. It suits food-minded travellers already visiting Meishan.

rows.name: Danling White Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty pagoda in Danling town, known locally as the White Pagoda and protected as a national heritage site since 2013. It is a quick stop when visiting the Tang cliff carvings at Zhengshan and Liuzui to the west of town.

rows.name: Ganquan Temple, Renshou
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty temple in the countryside of south-eastern Renshou County, protected as a national heritage site since 2013. It lies only a few kilometres from the Shuangbao memorial arches, and the two can be visited together.

rows.name: Heilongtan Reservoir
rows.summary: A large reservoir in the hills of Renshou County, completed in 1972 and fed by the Dongfeng Canal, which carries water from the Dujiangyan irrigation system. The lake and its hilly shoreline were made a provincial scenic area in 1986 and make an easy rural outing from Chengdu.

rows.name: Jiangkou Cliff Tombs
rows.summary: More than 4,500 Han-dynasty tombs cut into the cliffs and hillsides around Jiangkou, spread over some 30 km² beside the Min River. The site museum, the Jiangkou Han Cliff Tomb Museum, presents the tombs and what was found in them, a good introduction to Han burial customs in Sichuan.

rows.name: Liujiang Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town in the hills of western Hongya County, with timber stilt houses along its river and lanes of older shops and homes. Its best-known building is Zengjiayuan, a family mansion completed in 1937 and now a national heritage site. The town lies on the way to Mount Wawu and is often combined with it.

rows.name: Maoshui Village Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Six niches with 22 figures carved between the Song and Qing dynasties in a gully called Dafogou near Yucheng, Renshou County. Most are Buddhist, but Confucian figures and Li Bing, the builder of Dujiangyan revered as a local deity, also appear. The best-known niche shows the Buddha preaching and is nicknamed the 'flower-holding Buddha'.

rows.name: Mount Wawu
rows.summary: A flat-topped mountain in south-western Hongya County whose long, roof-like summit plateau gives it its name, 'Tiled House Mountain'. Its slopes are protected as a national forest park and rise to 2,830 m above sea level, making it a cool, forested escape from the Sichuan Basin in summer.

rows.name: Nengren Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Buddhist cliff carvings from the Tang and Song dynasties at Nengren Temple in eastern Renshou County, protected as a national heritage site since 2013. They belong to the network of rock-carved shrines found across this part of central Sichuan.

rows.name: Pengzu Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded hill in Pengshan District linked to Pengzu, a figure of Chinese legend said to have lived for about 800 years and revered as a symbol of long life. The scenic area includes a tomb and shrine attributed to him, a grove and the neighbouring Xiannü (Fairy) Mountain.

rows.name: Renshou City Wetland Park
rows.summary: A public wetland park in Renshou county town, one link in a chain of waterways and parks the county has laid out through the town. It has open water and wetland planting with shaded footpaths, and a musical fountain plays on weekend and holiday evenings. It is a local leisure park, worth a stroll if you are staying in Renshou.

rows.name: Renshou Giant Buddha
rows.summary: A large Tang-dynasty Buddha carved into the hillside at Niujiaozhai in northern Renshou County, surrounded by more than a hundred smaller niches. The carvings are spread over two areas, Niujiaozhai and Tanshenyan, and include Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian figures. It sees far fewer visitors than the Leshan Giant Buddha.

rows.name: Sansu Shrine
rows.summary: The former family home of the Song-dynasty writers Su Xun and his sons Su Shi (Su Dongpo) and Su Zhe, turned into a memorial shrine in the early Yuan and now run as a museum. Red walls enclose ponds, bamboo and old trees, with halls holding statues of the Su family, an old well, an inkstone-washing pond and a collection of calligraphy and paintings. It was badly damaged in the 2013 Lushan earthquake and reopened after repairs in 2016.

rows.name: Shuangbao Memorial Arches
rows.summary: Two stone memorial arches standing 44.5 m apart in the countryside of south-eastern Renshou County, erected in 1881 to honour two widowed women of the local Xu family for their chastity and filial devotion. Their faces are carved with 339 niches showing opera scenes, folk tales, animals, birds and flowers, a fine example of late-Qing stone carving.

rows.name: Zhengshan and Liuzui Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Tang-dynasty Buddhist niches carved into large boulders at two neighbouring spots, Zhengshan and Liuzui, in the hills west of Danling town. Locals call them the 'big boulder' carvings, and the two groups are close enough to see in one visit.

rows.name: Zhongyan Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: Buddhist cliff carvings dating from the Tang to the Qing, some 48 niches spread among the upper, middle and lower temples of Zhongyan, a wooded hill on the east bank of the Min River south of Qingshen town. Zhongyan is associated with Su Dongpo, who studied here as a young man, and rock inscriptions attributed to him and to Huang Tingjian survive on the site.

rows.name: Baishui Lake, Anzhou
rows.summary: A hill reservoir at Jushui in western Anzhou District, where 23 islands break up some 3,000 mu (about 2 km²) of water into inlets and channels. Several episodes of the sequel to the television series Journey to the West were filmed here in 1999. It is a national water-conservancy scenic area and 4A site, usually visited together with nearby Mount Luofu.

rows.name: Bao'en Temple, Pingwu
rows.summary: Built between 1440 and 1446 by the local chieftain Wang Xi, this Buddhist monastery in Pingwu town is a remarkably well-preserved Ming complex whose timber frames are all of nanmu wood. Highlights are a nine-metre wooden statue of the thousand-armed Guanyin and a great octagonal revolving sutra cabinet that still turns, along with Ming murals and sculpture.

rows.name: Beichuan Qiang City and Earthquake Ruins
rows.summary: Beichuan, China's only Qiang autonomous county, was devastated by the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, and this area links the rebuilt county town at Yongchang with the memorial sites of the disaster. The new town has the Qiang Folk Museum, devoted to the culture of the Qiang people, while about 25 km to the north the ruins of the old county town are preserved as a memorial beside the 5·12 Wenchuan Earthquake Memorial museum.

rows.name: Bishui Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: About 25 Tang-dynasty Buddhist niches carved into the rock at Bishui Temple, on the east bank of the Fu River in central Mianyang. A 2007 survey found that some show the early-Tang style of the capital Chang'an, and one depicts Amitabha with fifty-two bodhisattvas.

rows.name: Foye Cave
rows.summary: A karst cave in Dakang town, north-west of Jiangyou, with chambers of stalactites, stalagmites and rimstone pools and an underground river toured by boat. Its name refers to a Buddha-like stalagmite said to have been found in the underground river in the Republican era, and it is promoted as a filming location for the 1986 television series Journey to the West.

rows.name: Hualin Temple, Yanting
rows.summary: The main hall of a former temple in Huoxing village, Fuyi town, in north-eastern Yanting County, originally called Doushuai Temple; ink inscriptions on its beams, read with infrared photography in 2015, date it to 1311 under the Yuan dynasty. Despite Ming and Qing repairs it keeps its Yuan timber frame, rare in Sichuan, in which a single beam more than 11 metres long spans the whole front. The hall stands on a raised platform under a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof and is the only old building left of the temple.

rows.name: Kaixi Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Tashui, in Anzhou district west of Mianyang, whose surviving buildings date mainly from the Ming dynasty. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and suits travellers with a special interest in old temple architecture.

rows.name: Li Bai Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A museum and Tang-style garden beside the Changming River in Jiangyou, dedicated to the Tang poet Li Bai, who grew up nearby. Halls and pavilions around a lotus pool present his life and work, and the main Taibai Hall holds a statue of the poet; Taibai Park adjoins the site.

rows.name: Li Bai's Former Residence, Qinglian
rows.summary: Qinglian is traditionally held to be the boyhood home of Li Bai, whose family is said to have settled here around 705, when he was about five. The site groups the Longxi Yuan, where he is said to have studied as a child, with the Taibai Shrine, the Fenzhu Lou and other places tied to his family. The Longxi Yuan was founded in the Northern Song, rebuilt under the Qing and badly damaged in the 2008 earthquake.

rows.name: Li Ye Que
rows.summary: The single surviving pillar of the funerary que of Li Ye, an official who lived at the turn of the Western and Eastern Han, is thought to date from the start of the Eastern Han and is regarded as the earliest of China's surviving Han que. Only the base and the 2.45-metre shaft remain, inscribed in clerical script, and it stands under a protective pavilion in the Li Jieshi Shrine, where it was moved in 1845, at the foot of Changqing Mountain.

rows.name: Ma'an Temple
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty temple in Liujia town, in rural eastern Youxian district, Mianyang, whose buildings line up along a single axis: a two-storey opera tower of 1867, the Hall of the Heavenly Kings of 1702, the main hall of 1750, and Guanyin and Jade Emperor halls behind. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and lies a few kilometres from Yuquan Temple.

rows.name: Mianyang Science and Technology Museum
rows.summary: Mianyang's science museum reflects the city's role as China's 'Science City', home to the national nuclear weapons research academy, and is themed on the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' programme. Its three floors cover missiles, aviation and spaceflight, satellites, nuclear weapons and nuclear technology, and science in Mianyang, and there is a digital dome cinema.

rows.name: Mount Douchuan and Yunyan Temple
rows.summary: Mount Douchuan rises above the east bank of the Fu River north of Jiangyou, its bare rock summit peaks linked by suspended iron chains. Yunyan Temple, where Buddhist and Taoist worship have long been combined, spreads over the slopes; its Feitian Zang hall, described as the only surviving Song-dynasty building in south-west China, houses a revolving Taoist sutra cabinet built in 1181.

rows.name: Mount Jiuhuang
rows.summary: A limestone mountain area in eastern Beichuan County known for the Ape King Cave and other karst caves. A cable car serves the slopes, and the scenic area adds walkways and Qiang-style buildings.

rows.name: Mount Luofu, Anzhou
rows.summary: An isolated, steep and wooded hill in western Anzhou District, raised from an ancient seabed by tectonic movement, which in mist seems to float in the clouds. Close by are the Luofushan hot-spring resort and the Feiming Chan Monastery, a Buddhist site founded in the Tang dynasty. It is mainly a hot-spring and walking weekend destination for people from Mianyang.

rows.name: Mount Xunlong
rows.summary: A small scenic area of eroded conglomerate rock beside the new Beichuan county town, with rock forests, a waterfall and a cave explored by boat. It also has Longyin Town, a film-set street built in the style of a Republican-era Sichuan town.

rows.name: Pingyang Fujun Que
rows.summary: A rare surviving pair of Eastern Han stone que, ceremonial pillar-gates, standing about 27 m apart beside the Furong Stream in front of the new Mianyang Museum. Each que has a main and a subsidiary tower carved to imitate timber architecture, and the pair was among the first sites placed under national protection in 1961.

rows.name: Qijiang Cliff Tombs
rows.summary: The hills around Qijiang, an old town in southern Santai County on the site of the ancient state of Qi, hold a large group of Han-dynasty tombs cut into the cliffs, with more than 1,600 recorded. Part of the Jinzhongshan group, on the hillside at the western end of the old town, is open to visitors, and the town's old streets are worth a stroll.

rows.name: Qinglinkou Old Town
rows.summary: A small Qing-dynasty market town in the hills north-east of Jiangyou, on the Qingyun Creek near the Tong River. Its centrepiece is the Heyi or Red Army Bridge, a three-arched stone bridge topped by a timber gallery; the town also keeps a Wenchang temple, a Guangdong–Fujian guild hall, an old opera stage and slogans carved by the Red Army's Fourth Front Army in 1935.

rows.name: Qiqushan Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex on Qiqu Mountain just north of Zitong, founded as a shrine to the local deity Zhang Yazi and rebuilt as a Wenchang Palace after he was honoured as Wenchang, god of literature, in the early Yuan dynasty. Its 23 halls and pavilions date mainly from the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties and climb the hillside in an informal layout, surrounded by more than 20,000 ancient cypresses.

rows.name: Tongchuan City Wall
rows.summary: Santai was the seat of Tongchuan prefecture, and more than 2 km of its city wall survive. First built in the Ming Jiajing era and rebuilt from 1767 under the Qianlong emperor, the wall is about 6 m high and 9.8 m thick and had gates on all four sides.

rows.name: Two Bombs City
rows.summary: From 1969 to 1992 this compound at the foot of Changqing Mountain was the headquarters of the Ninth Academy, now the China Academy of Engineering Physics, the institute that developed China's nuclear weapons. Its preserved buildings include the auditorium, the headquarters offices, the archive and the house where the physicist Deng Jiaxian lived, and the Sichuan Two Bombs City Museum, opened to the public in 2024, presents the history of the nuclear weapons programme.

rows.name: Weiste Agricultural Park, Beichuan
rows.summary: A modern-farming showcase on the edge of Yongchang, the new Beichuan county town built after the 2008 earthquake. Smart greenhouses form a miniature eco-farm displaying mountain crops and farming technology, and hot-spring and hotel facilities are attached. It suits families and school groups more than general sightseers.

rows.name: Wenxing Temple, Yanting
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty temple in Exi village, in what is now Exi town in rural Yanting County, whose main hall carries beam inscriptions dated to the first year of the Longqing reign (1567). The single-eaved hip-and-gable hall, about 12 metres square, keeps its bracket sets in their original form, with the tips of the slanting cantilever arms curled up like elephant trunks, and inside is a wall painting dated 1726. It is one of several early timber halls in Yanting County, along with the Yuan-dynasty main hall of Hualin Temple.

rows.name: Wolongshan Thousand Buddha Cliff
rows.summary: A single boulder of white quartz sandstone carved on all four sides with Buddhist niches: rows of small 'thousand Buddha' niches on the south face and Buddha triads on the east and west faces. An inscription beside the west niche is dated 634, early in the Tang dynasty, so the site serves as a yardstick for dating Tang carving in Sichuan, and it was among the first sites chosen for Sichuan's rural grotto culture parks.

rows.name: Xianhai Lake, Mianyang
rows.summary: A reservoir lake about 15 km east of central Mianyang, formed by the Chenkang Reservoir of the Wudu irrigation scheme and run as a national water-conservancy scenic area and 4A resort. The lake covers about 7 km² within a 75 km² scenic zone, with a lakeside boardwalk, cycle paths, water-sports facilities and lakeside hotels, and its water is kept clean enough to meet China's Grade II standard. It is a weekend retreat for Mianyang residents and an easy half-day out from the city.

rows.name: Yaowang Valley, Beichuan
rows.summary: A forested mountain valley in Beichuan run as a 4A wellness area themed on traditional Chinese medicine. It covers about 15 km² at an average altitude of around 1,400 m, with more than 160 kinds of medicinal herbs grown on its slopes and about 1,800 century-old magnolia (xinyi) trees that flower white to purple each April. It suits a cool-weather walk or a spring blossom trip from Mianyang.

rows.name: Yuewang Tower
rows.summary: The first Yuewang Tower was built on Gui Hill in 656 by Li Zhen, Prince of Yue and a son of Emperor Taizong, and was praised by poets including Du Fu before being destroyed and rebuilt several times. The present 99-metre tower, completed in 2010, is a modern reconstruction in Tang style and a landmark above the Fu River; the riverside parks of the Three Rivers Peninsula belong to the same scenic area.

rows.name: Yuntai Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A large Taoist temple complex on Yuntai Mountain in southern Santai County, founded by a Taoist hermit early in the 13th century under the Southern Song. Its Ming and Qing buildings, including the Xuantian Palace (Zhenwu Hall), a sutra library and bell and drum towers, stretch for about a kilometre from the gate to the main hall. It combines well with the Qijiang cliff tombs and old town nearby.

rows.name: Yuquan Temple
rows.summary: A rural temple in Dongxuan, in eastern Youxian district, Mianyang, whose main hall dates from the Ming dynasty and whose gate and other buildings, with carved timber bracket sets, are Qing. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and lies a few kilometres from Ma'an Temple.

rows.name: Zunsheng Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple north-west of Santai town whose surviving buildings, centred on a timber main hall, date from the Ming and Qing dynasties. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Baba Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque and Sufi shrine of the Qadiriyya order on Panlong Mountain, just north of Langzhong old town. It grew from the tomb pavilion that disciples built for the Sufi teacher Khoja Abd Allah, who came to preach in Langzhong in 1684 and died in 1689; the present buildings are Qing, and it was listed as a national monument in 2013.

rows.name: Daxiangshan Giant Buddha, Langzhong
rows.summary: A Buddha almost 10 m tall, carved in the Tang dynasty into Daxiang ('Great Image') Mountain across the Jialing River from Langzhong old town, at the site of the Dafo Si (Great Buddha Temple). The cliffs around it carry further carvings dating from the Tang to the Qing, and below the summit is the cave where, by tradition, the three Chen brothers of the Northern Song, two of whom became top examination graduates, studied as boys.

rows.name: Former Residence of Zhu De
rows.summary: The birthplace and childhood home of Zhu De, commander-in-chief of the Red Army and later one of the ten marshals of the People's Republic, in Linlang village, Ma'an town, Yilong County. The scenic area takes in the site where he was born in 1886, the farmhouse where the family later lived, a memorial hall on his life opened in 1982, and the Ding family manor, a large landlord's estate in the same village built between about 1906 and 1925.

rows.name: Guanyin Temple Main Hall, Nanbu
rows.summary: The listed main hall of Guanyin'an, a Buddhist temple in the countryside south of Nanbu county town, is a timber building of the Ming dynasty. It is valued for its bracket sets, more elaborate than those of other Sichuan halls of the same period and carved with floral decoration under the front eaves, and for building methods that follow those of the area's Yuan-period halls.

rows.name: Lifeng Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple on Datongluo Mountain in Daping town, western Nanbu County, whose main hall was built in 1307 under the Yuan dynasty and is the oldest building in Sichuan with a dated inscription. The complex also keeps its gate, east and west ranges, a worship hall and the Huangniang (Empress) Hall, with later buildings dating up to the Republican era.

rows.name: Qibao Temple
rows.summary: A hilltop complex above the Xixi river in western Jialing district, rebuilt as a Buddhist temple in 1518 and turned into the Nanchi Academy in 1742 by a local scholar. Its courtyards climb a south–north axis through a stone gateway and temple halls to the Wenchang and Kuixing towers and the academy buildings at the back, which housed a school from 1912 until a new one was built elsewhere. The district heritage office describes it as the largest old academy complex in north-east Sichuan.

rows.name: Shengzhong Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir among the hills of Nanbu County, created by a dam begun in the 1970s, with a long, branching shoreline of wooded peninsulas and islands. It is best known in China for angling and hosts an annual international fishing competition. Boat trips on the lake suit those who do not fish.

rows.name: Tiangong Yuan
rows.summary: A temple in the countryside south-west of Langzhong dedicated to Yuan Tiangang and Li Chunfeng, two Tang-dynasty astrologers revered as masters of feng shui, who according to local legend chose their burial places here. The present buildings date from a Ming rebuilding of 1459, and Li Chunfeng's tomb lies on Wulongtai hill to the south. The scenic area adds a feng shui compass plaza and an old street.

rows.name: Wenchang Pavilion of Wulong Temple
rows.summary: The Wenchang Pavilion of the Wulong (Five Dragons) Temple stands at the foot of Wulong Mountain in Helou township, in the countryside north-west of Langzhong; the temple was founded in the Tang and rebuilt under the Yuan. Despite repairs in the Ming and Qing, the timber pavilion keeps its Yuan structural frame and is one of the few Yuan wooden buildings left in Sichuan.

rows.name: Wuliang Pagoda
rows.summary: Nanchong's White Pagoda, a brick pagoda modelled on timber construction, stands on Heming Mountain in Gaoping District, looking across the Jialing River to the city centre. Its date is disputed, with proposals ranging from the late Tang to the Southern Song, but it is regarded as the earliest of Sichuan's Song-era pagodas and a record of the shift from Tang to Song design. The hill around it is laid out as the Heming Mountain park, with walks and river views.

rows.name: Xichong Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The former county Confucian temple of Xichong, built for the official cult of Confucius and the local state school, in the county town north-west of Nanchong. Its surviving buildings date from the Ming and Qing dynasties, and it was listed as a national monument in 2013.

rows.name: Xishan Scenic Area, Nanchong
rows.summary: A chain of wooded hills on the western edge of Nanchong's Shunqing district, laid out as a large park with paths, temples and views over the city. Its best-known building is the Wanjuan Lou, a library tower honouring Chen Shou, the Nanchong-born historian who wrote the Records of the Three Kingdoms; other sights include Qile Temple, a cluster of Eastern Han cliff tombs and the former headquarters of the Shunlu Uprising of the 1920s.

rows.name: Yong'an Temple Main Hall, Nanbu
rows.summary: A small timber hall standing in fields in north-western Nanbu County, the one old building left of a temple founded in the Tang that later became the ancestral temple of the local Du family. The hip-and-gable hall, three bays wide, is dated to the Yuan or the very start of the Ming and is one of the few buildings of that age surviving in Sichuan, notable for its massive timbers and elaborate bracket sets. The gate and side rooms around it are modern.

rows.name: Yong'an Temple, Langzhong
rows.summary: A rural temple in the hills east of Langzhong, founded in the Tang, whose main hall was built in 1333 under the Yuan and is one of Sichuan's rare Yuan-era timber buildings. Interior columns were omitted to open up the hall, whose Yuan mural of the Eight Classes of Divine Beings was destroyed in the Cultural Revolution and later recreated from surviving photographs; the gate, Guanyin tower and side halls are Qing.

rows.name: Yujishan Giant Buddha
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty standing Buddha about 17.5 m tall, carved almost entirely in the round from the rock of Yuji Mountain at Beiyuan, in eastern Nanbu County, and described as the largest round-carved standing stone Buddha in China. It is also known as the Beiyuan Buddha, after the town below the mountain.

rows.name: Yutai Mountain Stone Pagoda
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty stone pagoda on Yutai Mountain just north of Langzhong, also known as the Tengwang Pavilion pagoda after the pavilion built on the hill by the Tang prince Li Yuanying, Prince of Teng. The hilltop is laid out as the Tengwang Pavilion park, looking south over the old town and the Jialing, and Du Fu wrote poems about the prince's pavilion during his stay in Langzhong.

rows.name: Zhouzi Ancient Town, Peng'an
rows.summary: A riverside town on the Jialing in Peng'an County, named in honour of the Song Neo-Confucian thinker Zhou Dunyi, who is said to have taught here; a shrine to him, a former Jiangxi guild hall and an old wharf survive among its lanes. The wider scenic area covers the river's wetland islands, where in the warmer months hundreds of water buffalo swim out to graze each morning, a sight promoted as the 'hundred oxen crossing the river'.

rows.name: Chonglong Mountain, Zizhong
rows.summary: A hill on the north-eastern edge of Zizhong's old town whose cliffs, known as the North Cliff, carry 172 niches with more than 1,700 Buddhist figures carved from 783 through the late Tang, the Five Dynasties and the Song. Guardian kings, Guanyin and Pure Land scenes are common, and the rock faces also bear centuries of inscriptions, including calligraphy credited to Huang Tingjian and Su Dongpo's characters for the Huanyu Pool, re-carved here in 1928 from his original at Qingshen. Since an upgrade finished in 2025 the carvings can be seen without railings and two pavilions on the hill hold exhibitions; the scenic area also takes in Yongqing Temple near the summit and the Confucian and Guandi temples on Zhuangyuan Street below.

rows.name: Guyu Lake, Longchang
rows.summary: A large reservoir west of Longchang, officially Guyumiao Reservoir, listed as a National Water Conservancy Scenic Area. Its open water draws migratory birds in autumn and winter, including the rare Baer's pochard and black-headed gulls, and visitors can cycle around the lake. It makes an easy add-on to Longchang's stone memorial archways.

rows.name: Lexian Peninsula, Neijiang
rows.summary: A peninsula in a loop of the Tuo River on the edge of Neijiang city, laid out as a riverside leisure area. Its Tashan Park has greenway paths with the river on two sides, and the Sanyuan Pagoda on its hill was first built in the Tang dynasty and rebuilt in the Jiaqing reign of the Qing. It suits an easy walk for anyone staying in Neijiang.

rows.name: Longchang Stone Arches
rows.summary: Longchang is known for its stone memorial arches (paifang): 17 survive, built between 1496 and the late 19th century to honour upright officials, chaste widows, filial sons and long-lived elders. Most are four-pillar, three-gate bluestone gateways carved in imitation of timber, about 11 metres high, and the main groups stand along the old roads at the town's South and North Gates.

rows.name: Luoquan Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old salt-making town strung along one long street in the gorge of the Zhuxi River, a tributary of the Tuo, where brine wells were worked for centuries. Its nationally listed Yanshen (Salt God) Temple, a Qing building, honours Guan Zhong as patron of the salt trade alongside Guan Yu and the god of fire, and in August 1911 the town hosted the secret Luoquan meeting that pushed Sichuan's Railway Protection Movement towards armed revolt.

rows.name: Shengshui Temple, Neijiang
rows.summary: An active Buddhist monastery on the western side of Neijiang, founded in the 860s–870s under the Tang and named after the spring that flows from the cliff behind it. Its courtyard halls were rebuilt in the Kangxi and Yongzheng reigns of the Qing, and the grounds also hold Han cliff tombs, two Ming memorial arches and about 80 niches of Tang and Song rock carvings with more than 500 figures.

rows.name: Shibanhe Stone River
rows.summary: A shallow river that runs for around 7 km over a bed of solid rock, in the hills of the Weiyuan dome north-west of Weiyuan county. The water is mostly well below knee height, so the open stretch, with rapids and small waterfalls, is popular for wading and stream walks in summer; adventure activities have also been added.

rows.name: World Fig Expo Park, Weiyuan
rows.summary: An agricultural park in Sifang village, Xiangyi town, built around fig growing, one of Weiyuan County's farm industries. It is described as China's first expo park themed on the fig industry, with dozens of fig varieties planted and a visitor centre, and the village has a small exhibition room on local history and fig growing. It suits families and those interested in farming rather than travellers looking for scenery.

rows.name: Xianglongshan Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A cliff of Buddhist carvings on a small hill in central Neijiang, begun in the Tang dynasty and added to as late as the Republican era. Some 131 niches with 815 figures and 24 inscriptions survive, led by a Tang Thousand-Armed Guanyin over 7 metres tall and a seated Amitabha in a niche 4.5 metres high.

rows.name: Zhang Daqian Park
rows.summary: A hilltop park in Neijiang, the home town of the painter Zhang Daqian (Chang Dai-chien, 1899–1983), one of the best-known Chinese artists of the 20th century. It brings together a memorial hall to his life and the Zhang Daqian Museum, designed by the Barcelona architects EMBT and opened in 2019, beside the old Xilin Temple on the same hill.

rows.name: Zizhong Confucian and Guandi Temples
rows.summary: Zizhong's Confucian temple and its temple to Guan Yu (Wumiao), both mainly Qing buildings, stand about 100 metres apart on Zhuangyuan Street in the old county town, an unusual pairing. The Confucian temple is entered past a screen wall and the Zhuangyuan Bridge to the Dacheng Hall, which keeps a large Ming spirit tablet to Confucius dated 1530, while the Wumiao's green-and-yellow glazed roofs contrast with the Confucian temple's red-brown tiles.

rows.name: Ashuda Four Seasons Flower Sea
rows.summary: A flower park opened in January 2025 on the capped Majiatian tailings reservoir, where the Panzhihua steelworks piled ore waste for about 50 years until it was closed in 2022. More than 400 mu (about 27 hectares) of flower beds ring a central pool, laid out so that from above they form a kapok flower, the tree the city is named after, and there are also a small animal area, a garden restaurant, an open-air music plaza and a shopping street. It suits families and anyone curious to see how an old industrial site has been reused.

rows.name: Ertan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of steep wooded hills around the reservoir of the Ertan hydropower station on the lower Yalong River. Its 240-metre double-curvature arch dam belongs to what was the largest power station China completed in the 20th century, and the lake shore, forests and viewpoints around it make an easy outing from Panzhihua.

rows.name: Gesala
rows.summary: A high plateau of meadows, forest and limestone country in north-western Yanbian County, on the border with Yunnan, where karst sinkholes, a stone forest and caves are the main sights. It lies around Gesala Yi Ethnic Township, and the culture of the Yi communities who live here is part of the draw.

rows.name: Lisu Terraced Fields, Xinshan
rows.summary: Terraced fields climbing the hillsides around Xinshan, a Lisu ethnic township in the hills of Miyi County, worked by the Lisu for generations. They are most photogenic in late spring and early summer, when the flooded terraces reflect the sky, and the township also promotes stargazing and Lisu customs.

rows.name: Yishala Village
rows.summary: A Yi village in the dry, hot valley of the Jinsha River near the Yunnan border, listed as a Historical and Cultural Village of China in 2005. Its red-walled, grey-tiled houses with carved eaves show the influence of settlers from Jiangsu and Anhui on the local Lipo Yi, and the village keeps up its own ritual music and sheepskin-drum dance. It was once a staging post on old trade routes into Yunnan.

rows.name: Baofan Temple
rows.summary: A small temple in Baofan village, Pengxi County, whose Ming and Qing buildings are a national heritage site. Its main hall holds wall paintings of arhats dated 1466, under the Ming, admired for their flowing brushwork and described as among the finest temple murals in Sichuan; they are the main reason to visit.

rows.name: China Dead Sea Resort, Daying
rows.summary: A salt-water resort in Daying County built over an ancient underground salt lake around 3,000 m below the surface, whose brine is pumped up to fill its pools. The water is over 22% salt, so bathers float easily as in the Dead Sea, and it comes out of the ground hot enough to be used for thermal pools. It is a family water park; the Zhuotong salt wells nearby show how brine here was once drilled by hand.

rows.name: Gaofeng Mountain
rows.summary: A hilltop Taoist complex 25 km north of Pengxi, first built in the Tang dynasty and by the late Ming and early Qing regarded as the largest Taoist centre in central, eastern and northern Sichuan, where Confucian and Buddhist worship were also practised. Its surviving temples date mostly from the late Qing and early Republican era, and on the mid-slope a group of buildings is laid out as an eight-trigram (bagua) maze with four gates. A fire in May 2017 destroyed the Sanqing Hall and damaged neighbouring halls, but the maze was not affected.

rows.name: Guangde Temple, Suining
rows.summary: Guangde Temple is a working Buddhist monastery on Wolong Hill at the western edge of Suining, founded in the Tang dynasty and renamed several times by imperial order before receiving its present name in the Ming. Its protected buildings span the Song to Qing periods. Suining promotes itself as the legendary home of Guanyin, and the same scenic area includes Lingquan Temple on a hill across the Fu River.

rows.name: Guanyin Lake and World Lotus Expo Garden, Suining
rows.name_zh: 观音湖·世界荷花博览园
rows.summary: Guanyin Lake is the stretch of the Fu River held back by the Guojundu dam in Suining, now a national wetland park of about 600 ha with three islands. On Shenglian Island, the park's core, the World Lotus Expo Garden grows more than 800 varieties of lotus and water lily from 23 countries and regions, which flower in summer. Visitors walk the island's boardwalks and the lakeshore, mostly in June–August for the lotus.

rows.name: Huiyan Temple Main Hall
rows.summary: The Ming-dynasty main hall of Huiyan Temple, a rural temple in the southern part of Pengxi County south-east of Suining, protected as a national heritage site since 2013. It is mainly of interest to those following Sichuan's surviving Ming timber architecture.

rows.name: Jinhua Mountain & Chen Zi'ang Reading Terrace
rows.summary: Jinhua Mountain rises above the Fu River north of Shehong, with a Taoist temple first built in the Southern Liang dynasty and the reading terrace of Chen Zi'ang, an early Tang poet who studied here as a young man. The present terrace buildings were moved to the rear of the hill in the Qing dynasty, and a memorial hall to the poet stands nearby. It makes a quiet visit of temple halls and river views.

rows.name: Jinxian Temple, Pengxi
rows.summary: A village temple at Zhoujiadian, just north of Pengxi county town, whose main hall is dated by inscriptions on its beams to 1327, under the Yuan dynasty. The three-bay, single-eaved hip-and-gable hall, about 9 by 16 metres with eight bracket sets under its eaves, keeps its original form and an unusually full set of dated inscriptions, making it a valuable example of Yuan timber building. It can be combined with Pengxi's Baofan Temple, known for its Ming murals, about 11 km to the south-west.

rows.name: Longfeng Ancient Town, Suining
rows.summary: A tourist town of about 148 ha beside the Fu River south of central Suining, rated 4A in 2012. Its streets of traditional-style buildings hold shops, workshops and small venues, including a storytelling hall, an archery range, an apothecary, a wine shop and a square dedicated to the Guanyin legend, presenting themes from Guanyin worship to old market-town life. It is best for an evening stroll and snacks.

rows.name: Pengxi Kui Pagoda
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty pagoda in Pengxi's county town, named after Kui, the star traditionally linked with literary and examination success. It stands a few hundred metres from the Song-dynasty White Pagoda of Jiufeng Temple, so the two are easily seen together.

rows.name: Pengxi White Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty pagoda that once belonged to Jiufeng Temple, standing in Chicheng, the county town of Pengxi, where it is known as the White Pagoda. The Qing-dynasty Kui Pagoda stands only a few hundred metres away, so the two are easily seen together.

rows.name: Qicai Mingzhu Rural Park, Anju
rows.summary: A large rural leisure area of about 9,400 mu (some 630 ha) in Yufeng town, Anju District, strung along the G318 road. It is divided into seven clusters, among them flower fields, peach and fruit orchards, farm villages, an egret island and a 'Huang E ancient town' themed on the Ming poet couple Huang E and Yang Shen, and it has a large outdoor training camp. It is a weekend spot for Suining families, with fruit picking in season.

rows.name: Raoyi Temple
rows.summary: A Ming and Qing temple in Tuopai, the Shehong town best known for its liquor distillery, protected as a national heritage site since 2013. Its old halls make a short detour for travellers in the Shehong area.

rows.name: Shede Liquor Culture Area (Tuopai Distillery), Shehong
rows.summary: The distillery of Shede Spirits at Tuopai town in Shehong, maker of the Tuopai and Shede brands of baijiu, opened to visitors as a 4A liquor-culture area. The company traces its roots to the Tai'an workshop of the late Qing dynasty and a distillery founded in 1940, and visitor routes take in brewing and starter-making workshops and the jar cellars where the liquor is aged. It suits travellers curious about how Chinese liquor is made.

rows.name: Shehong Petrified Wood Geopark
rows.name_zh: 射洪硅化木国家地质公园
rows.summary: A national geopark in the hills south of Shehong where fossilised tree trunks from the Jurassic period are exposed and protected where they lie. Footpaths lead past the fossil beds, and an on-site museum explains the geology; the scenic area is promoted under a Jurassic theme.

rows.name: Songjing Taoyuan (Song Well Peach Garden), Daying
rows.summary: A 4A area (2025) in Zhuotong Well town that pairs the Zhuotong salt-well site, where narrow-bore percussion drilling was developed in the Northern Song (1041–48), with a new Song-dynasty-themed village among peach orchards. The village has inns, craft and food stalls, campsites and well derricks set up in the fields to show the old technique, hosts a peach-blossom food festival and Song-style art events, and a small tourist train links the parts. It suits a half-day combined with the well site itself.

rows.name: Zhuotong Salt Wells
rows.summary: Daying is where the zhuotong well, a small-bore salt well drilled by percussion with an iron bit on a wooden frame and lined with large bamboo tubes, was developed in the Qingli era of the Northern Song dynasty (1041–1048). It is often described as the forerunner of modern deep drilling for brine, oil and gas. An exhibition hall in Zhuotongjing town shows the tools used to drill the wells and make salt.

rows.name: Anshunchang Red Army Crossing Site
rows.summary: A ferry crossing on the Dadu River where, in May 1935, a small Red Army vanguard crossed by boat under fire during the Long March, opening the way for the advance on Luding Bridge. A memorial hall presents the crossing, and a riverside monument completed in 1983 marks the landing. In 1863 the Taiping general Shi Dakai's army was trapped and destroyed at the same place.

rows.name: Bifengxia Gorge & Panda Base
rows.summary: A wooded valley in the hills north of Ya'an that pairs a gorge walk with the Bifengxia base of the China Conservation and Research Center for the Giant Panda. Walkways lead through two V-shaped gorges past dozens of waterfalls, while the panda base has received several pandas born in zoos abroad. The scenic area also includes a wildlife park.

rows.name: Dengchigou Church & Panda Discovery Site
rows.summary: The valley where the French missionary-naturalist Armand David was based in 1869, when he obtained a giant panda; the specimen he sent to the natural history museum in Paris was the first scientific specimen of the animal. The church he worked from, begun in 1839, survives, its Sichuan-style timber exterior enclosing a Gothic-style interior. It lies in Fengtongzhai township, whose nature reserve is part of the Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries World Heritage Site.

rows.name: Fan Min Que
rows.summary: A stone pillar-gate (que) from the tomb of Fan Min, dated to 205 AD in the Eastern Han dynasty, standing about 3 km south of Lushan county town with his memorial stele and other carvings. The que was broken up in the late Qing and reassembled in 1957, partly from original Han stones, using Gao Yi Que as its model. The stele beside it stands on a carved stone tortoise and records Fan Min's career in clerical script.

rows.name: Feixianguan Pass
rows.summary: A riverside pass in the mountains west of Ya'an that was a gateway on the Tea Horse Road, the old trade route that carried tea from Sichuan to Tibet. The pass and its Nanjie archway are protected as part of the national Tea Horse Road heritage listing, and the old Feixianguan bridge over the river is a provincial heritage site.

rows.name: Former Mingde Middle School (Xikang Museum)
rows.summary: A three-storey brick and stone building in a mix of Chinese and Western Republican-era styles on Zhangjiashan hill in Ya'an, built for the Mingde junior middle school, a mission school funded by the American Baptists and founded by the missionary Frederick N. Smith; the facade still bears the school's name. Since 2017 it has housed the Xikang Museum, which reopened in July 2025 after renovation: the ground-floor galleries follow the former Xikang province, whose capital moved to Ya'an in 1950, and the upper floor covers the history of Yucheng district, including a recreated Republican-era classroom.

rows.name: Gao Yi Que
rows.summary: A pair of carved stone pillar-gates (que) built in the Jian'an era (196–220) of the Eastern Han dynasty at the tomb of Gao Yi, a governor of Yizhou. The right-hand que survives largely intact, covered in relief carvings and inscriptions, with a pair of winged stone beasts (bixie) in front and the tomb mound behind. The site, now in a small heritage park, was badly damaged in the 2013 Lushan earthquake, after which a conservation plan was approved.

rows.name: Huahai Guoxiang Orchards, Hanyuan
rows.summary: An orchard district around Jiuxiang in Hanyuan County, where pear, peach, cherry and apricot trees flower each spring. It takes in the pear-blossom slopes around Jiuxiang, the peach orchards of Shuangxi and Shengou and the Confucian temple at Qingxi. It is mainly a spring blossom destination and can be combined with the Jiuxiang stone archway.

rows.name: Jinfeng Mountain & Jinfeng Temple
rows.summary: A wooded hill park on the edge of Ya'an city whose slopes hold Jinfeng Temple, a Buddhist temple protected as a Sichuan provincial heritage site. It is an easy short outing from the city centre for a walk among the trees and a look at the temple halls.

rows.name: Jiuxiang Stone Archway
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty stone memorial archway (paifang) in Jiuxiang town, Hanyuan county, protected as a national heritage site since 2013. Archways of this kind were raised to honour individuals or families recognised by the state, and their stone frames were often richly carved.

rows.name: Kaishan Temple, Yingjing
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Yingjing county town, now home to the county museum, whose main hall, built in the Chenghua reign of the Ming in the late 15th century, is one of the few Ming timber buildings left in Sichuan. Some of the hall's bracket timbers are carved as elephants and dragons, and traces of Ming painted decoration survive on its beams. It can be combined with the Yandao ancient city site on the western edge of town.

rows.name: Labahe & Mount Erlang
rows.summary: A forested river valley on the eastern side of Mount Erlang in Tianquan county, with trails and a cable car into the higher forest; the Labahe nature reserve here is part of the Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries World Heritage Site. Mount Erlang (3,437 m) is the divide between the Qingyi and Dadu rivers; the Sichuan–Tibet highway (G318) crosses it, today through a tunnel.

rows.name: Lingguan Stone City, Baoxing
rows.summary: A tourism district around Lingguan town in Baoxing County built on the local white-marble industry. It combines a stone-carving park where visitors can watch marble being worked, a stone-products street at a village rebuilt after the 2013 Lushan earthquake, a re-created Qingyi street and museum on the ancient Qingyi Qiang state, a wetland park laid out in the shape of a panda's head and the Lingjiu gorge with a natural Buddha-head rock and a seven-storey pagoda. It is a stop on the road to Baoxing and the panda country beyond.

rows.name: Longcanggou Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in Yingjing county, about 196 km from Chengdu, valued for the diversity of its forest plants and its streams and waterfalls. The Diecuixi trail follows a creek through dense, often misty forest past cascades and viewing platforms, and the park is a popular summer escape from the heat.

rows.name: Longmen Ancient Town & Qinglong Temple
rows.summary: Longmen, in a valley north-east of Lushan county town, was the epicentre of the magnitude 6.6 earthquake of 20 April 2013, and the rebuilt township is now run as a scenic area, Longmen Ancient Town. Its historic centrepiece is the main hall of Qinglong Temple, a timber hall dated by its beam inscription to 1323, in the Yuan dynasty, and protected as a national heritage site.

rows.name: Mingshan Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty Confucian temple on top of Yuehua Hill in the town of Mingshan, moved to this site in 1841 and protected as a national heritage site since 2013. Its Lingxing Gate, semicircular pool, Dacheng Gate, side ranges, Dacheng Hall and Chongsheng Shrine follow the formal layout of a county Confucian temple. It stands within the grounds of Mingshan Middle School, so access may be limited.

rows.name: Moon Lake, Mingshan
rows.summary: A small lake and tea-garden leisure area at Jiefang village, Baizhang town, on Mingshan's tea-garden greenway. It has a wetland, fishing platforms, viewing decks, a crescent-moon landmark, walking paths, a square themed on the 'educated youth' sent to the countryside and a wedding-photo base. It is a local leisure stop, pleasant if you are travelling the tea greenway.

rows.name: Panda Ancient Town, Baoxing
rows.summary: A quarter of Muping, Baoxing's county town, developed from 2012 in traditional western Sichuan style and themed on the giant panda, which was first described to Western science from Baoxing in 1869. It contains a memorial hall to the Red Army's crossing of Jiajin Mountain on the Long March and a riverside walk with displays on panda evolution. It makes a convenient base for Dengchigou and the road north over Jiajin Mountain.

rows.name: Pingxiang Tower & Hanjiang Old Town
rows.summary: A rebuilt old quarter of Lushan county town, laid out after the 2013 Lushan earthquake and themed on Jiang Wei, the Three Kingdoms general who held the title Marquis of Pingxiang. Its centrepiece is Pingxiang Tower, a Yuan-dynasty building dedicated to him and protected as a national heritage site, and the quarter also has a memorial hall to the earthquake.

rows.name: Qiaoqi Tibetan Village & Shenmulei
rows.summary: Qiaoqi, Baoxing county's only ethnic township, lies in a high valley above 2,000 metres at the head of the eastern branch of the Qingyi River, and most of its people are Tibetan. The scenic area pairs the village and its reservoir with Shenmulei, an area of ancient trees and forest trails higher up. The road continues north over Jiajin Mountain, crossed by the Red Army on the Long March in 1935.

rows.name: Shangli Ancient Town
rows.summary: A historic market town in the hills north of Ya'an, with lanes of old timber-framed houses beside its streams, now run as a tourist village. Its sights include carved stone memorial archways and the Han family mansion, built in 1824 and protected as a Sichuan provincial heritage site, and Wujia village within the town was among the first places named Chinese Traditional Villages in 2012.

rows.name: Wanggangping
rows.summary: A mountain area east of the Dadu River in Shimian county, climbed by a cable car about 3.5 km long. Its upper viewpoints face Gongga Shan, about 30 km away in a straight line, and are visited for sunrise on the snow peaks, seas of cloud and old rhododendron forest; there is also a small ski area.

rows.name: Yandao Ancient City, Yingjing
rows.summary: The site of Yandao, a county seat founded by the Qin state in 312 BC and later a staging post on the Southern Silk Road, in Gucheng village on the western edge of Yingjing town. Stretches of the old city walls remain, and the national listing also covers the He Jun inscription, a Han-dynasty rock carving recording road-building. The village is known for its black sand pottery, still made in workshops where visitors can watch and try.

rows.name: Yunfeng Mountain & Yunfeng Temple
rows.summary: A forested mountainside about 4 km from Yingjing county town, spanning roughly 1,000 to 2,600 metres and centred on Yunfeng Temple, also known as Taihu Temple. Founded in the Tang dynasty, burned in the early Yuan and rebuilt from the mid-Ming onwards, the temple has mostly Qing-style halls. Its grounds are known for ancient Phoebe zhennan (nanmu) trees, including one promoted as about 1,700 years old.

rows.name: Zhougong Mountain
rows.summary: A forested outlier of the Qionglai range just south of Ya'an city, rising to about 1,743 metres and encircled by the Zhougong and Qingyi rivers. Much of it is a provincial forest park, and hot springs at its foot are a popular local retreat.

rows.name: Aikou Stone Archway
rows.summary: A 17-metre carved stone archway (paifang) in Aikou village, Yuhe, in the hills of southern Gong County, raised in 1848 by a local scholar in honour of his widowed mother and listed as a national heritage site in 2006. Its three tiers of eaves and its crossbeams are carved with scenes from the Twenty-Four Exemplars of Filial Piety and from operas. It is a single monument rather than a full attraction, best seen on the way to the hanging coffins further south.

rows.name: Bowang Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in Xingwen County named after the ancient Bo people, whose stone gateway and wall remains survive on the mountain; it is a provincial scenic area and part of the Xingwen UNESCO Global Geopark. Paths lead through large groves of moso bamboo, gorges and waterfalls to Feiwu Cave, two deep shafts linked by an underground stream, with a waterfall inside.

rows.name: Cuiping and Zhenwu Mountains
rows.summary: Two linked wooded hills on the west side of central Yibin, south of the Min River, laid out as a large city forest park. On Zhenwu Mountain stands a complex of Taoist temples begun in 1574 and much extended in the Qing, centred on the Ming-dynasty Xuanzu Hall, with Buddhist and Confucian halls alongside; Cuiping Mountain has the Nezha Temple, the Zhao Yiman Memorial Hall in the former Cuiping Academy, and the Qianfo Rock carvings.

rows.name: Daguan Tower, Yibin
rows.summary: A gate tower in the centre of Yibin's old town, first built in the Jiajing reign of the Ming as the city's drum tower. Destroyed at the end of the Ming, it was rebuilt under Kangxi, burned again in 1764 and rebuilt the following year, when it took the name Daguan Lou; it remains a landmark at the Xijiekou junction.

rows.name: Folai Mountain, Changning
rows.summary: A pear-growing hill area near Changning town, centred on Foli village, part of a belt of some 12,000 mu of pear orchards. The trees flower white in March, and pears can be picked in summer, roughly from July to September. It makes a half-day outing from Changning or the nearby Shunan Bamboo Sea.

rows.name: Hanging Coffins of the Bo, Gong County
rows.summary: Wooden coffins lodged in niches and on wooden stakes driven into sheer limestone cliffs at Matangba, near Luobiao, and Sumawan, near Caoying, in southern Gong County, placed there over several centuries from around the Song dynasty. Tradition attributes them to the Bo people, against whom the Ming launched a major campaign in 1573, although historians debate who made them.

rows.name: Hengjiang Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old river town at the southern tip of Yibin's Xuzhou District, on the Hengjiang River near the Yunnan border, long known as a gateway between Sichuan and Yunnan. Its old quarter, which took shape in the Ming, keeps some 30 Ming and Qing courtyard houses, among them the provincially protected Zhu family residence, and the Shicheng Mountain forest park lies just south of the town.

rows.name: Jiuzhou Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty pagoda, repaired in the Ming, standing on the Jiuzhou flats on the north-western side of Yibin near the Wuliangye distillery grounds. It has been protected since 1956 and was listed as a national heritage site in 2013.

rows.name: Lengyan Temple, Pingshan
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple at Zhongdu, in the mountains of western Pingshan County, with buildings dating from the Ming dynasty. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 2007 and a national one in 2013, and lies well off the usual tourist routes.

rows.name: Liubeichi Park
rows.summary: A small park on the north bank of the Min River in Yibin, built around the rock channel where the Song poet and calligrapher Huang Tingjian, exiled here from 1098 to 1100, is said to have floated wine cups during poetry gatherings. The cliffs around the 'flowing cup pool' are covered with inscriptions carved from the Song to the Republican era, protected as a national heritage site since 2019.

rows.name: Lizhuang Ancient Town
rows.summary: A riverside town on the south bank of the Yangtze east of Yibin, with stone-paved lanes, Qing-dynasty guild halls and temples, and the Zhang family ancestral hall with its windows carved with a hundred cranes. From 1940, during the war against Japan, it sheltered Tongji University, institutes of Academia Sinica and the Society for the Study of Chinese Architecture, whose former premises, where Liang Sicheng finished his history of Chinese architecture, are now a protected site. On the edge of town stands the Ming-dynasty Xuanluo Hall, which Liang counted among Lizhuang's 'four wonders'.

rows.name: Long Family Manor, Pingshan
rows.summary: A late-Qing manor of six courtyards stepped up a tea hill at Yanmen village, begun in the early 19th century for an official family named Long, rebuilt in the 1850s and enlarged in 1870. A tall gateway, stepped firewalls in the Huizhou style and a surviving watchtower give it the look of a small fortress. Inside are carved doors and windows and two stone reliefs of the Twenty-four Filial Exemplars set into the walls of the front courtyard.

rows.name: Longhua Old Town and Baxian Mountain
rows.summary: Longhua is an old town in Pingshan County with stone-paved lanes and the Liang Bridge over the clear Xiaolong stream, shaded by old huangjue fig trees. Above it rises Baxian Mountain, a scenic area with hiking paths, a tea garden and a large modern standing Buddha that overlooks the town.

rows.name: Nanguang River Cliff Tombs, Kejiu
rows.summary: Rows of rock-cut tomb chambers in the red cliffs of Hongyan Mountain near Kejiu in Gao County, part of a group of cliff tombs and carvings along the Nanguang River that is listed as a national heritage site. A path climbs past more than 40 tombs, including one incised inside with a pair of fish holding a pearl, to the cliff-hugging Banbian ('half-sided') Temple and its Qing rock carvings.

rows.name: Nanxi Old Town and City Wall
rows.summary: The riverside heart of Nanxi, a former county town on the Yangtze downstream of Yibin, where more than a kilometre of city wall survives with three gates, among them the Wenming Gate facing the river. The wall was rebuilt in stone in the Ming dynasty and repaired many times since, and the gate towers date from the Qing; the streets behind it are largely rebuilt in traditional style.

rows.name: Qidonggou Gorge
rows.summary: A wooded gorge of the Mianxi River in Changning County, hemmed in by red sandstone cliffs with waterfalls and springs, and popular in summer for its 3 km rafting run. Within the scenic area are the Qigedong ('Seven Caves') Eastern Han cliff tombs, a national heritage site, and a glass footbridge.

rows.name: Wuliangye Distillery and Old Cellars
rows.summary: Yibin is the home of Wuliangye, one of China's best-known baijiu spirits, and the company's tourism area presents the history and making of the liquor through its Liquor Culture Museum and distillery grounds. In the old town, the Changfasheng and Lichuanyong workshops keep fermentation pits and brick-and-timber buildings from the Ming and Qing dynasties, protected as a national heritage site.

rows.name: Xijiashan Manor
rows.summary: A large country manor in Jiang'an County, begun in 1612 under the Ming and extended and repaired over the following centuries. Its 123 rooms of timber-framed buildings are set around three successive courtyards with a garden alongside, a well-preserved example of a southern Sichuan gentry residence.

rows.name: Xingwen Stone Sea
rows.summary: A karst landscape on the southern rim of the Sichuan Basin, where fields of limestone pinnacles (the 'stone sea'), large caves such as Tianquan Cave and giant collapsed sinkholes, or tiankeng, form the core of the Xingwen UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2005. It was one of the first places in China where tiankeng were studied, and the surrounding county is home to Miao communities and traces of the ancient Bo people.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wu Yuzhang
rows.summary: The birthplace of Wu Yuzhang (1878–1966), who in 1911 helped lead Rong County's declaration of independence from Qing rule, later joined the Communist Party and became president of Renmin University of China. The rural site in Shuangshi keeps his family's old house and the grave he shares with his wife, beside which a rebuilt residence and an exhibition hall on his life opened in 1988.

rows.name: Former Rong County Military Government
rows.summary: On 25 September 1911, in the old county yamen of Rong County, Wu Yuzhang, Wang Tianjie and other members of the Tongmenghui declared the county independent of Qing rule and set up a military government, 15 days before the Wuchang Uprising. The surviving late-Qing courtyard of the yamen, with its main and rear halls, gate and side wings, has been open as an exhibition since 1988, and its ten galleries cover the Tongmenghui's revolutionary activity in Rong County. A monument to the uprising, unveiled for its centenary in 2011, stands in Shouyi Square in front.

rows.name: Fushun Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple in the centre of Fushun, founded in the Northern Song and rebuilt under later dynasties, laid out along a 160-metre axis from the semicircular pool and Lingxing Gate to the Dacheng Hall. The double-eaved main hall, 25 metres tall, was first built in 1291, and the scenic area also takes in the town's West Lake nearby.

rows.name: Huanhou Palace, Zigong
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty guild hall built by Zigong's butchers and meat traders and dedicated to Zhang Fei, the Three Kingdoms general whose posthumous title gives it its name. It has an opera stage, a main hall and bell and drum towers, richly decorated with plaster relief, wood and stone carving. After a restoration completed in 2023 it has reopened to visitors.

rows.name: Jianshan Scenic Area, Zigong
rows.summary: A rural hill area of 2.86 km² in Rongbian town outside Zigong, more than 70% wooded, best known for its peach orchards and the peach-blossom fair that opens each March. A 2020 revamp added lakes, flower beds for every season, a fishing ground, a poetry gallery, a suspended boardwalk, zip lines and other outdoor activities, alongside farmhouse restaurants. It is a local day-out spot that suits families more than sightseers.

rows.name: Rongxian Giant Buddha
rows.summary: A 36.7-metre seated Buddha carved from a sandstone hill on the edge of Rong County town in the Tang dynasty, usually ranked second in size among China's ancient stone Buddhas after Leshan. It sits within the Dafo Temple, rebuilt in the Qing, whose halls climb the hillside around it alongside Tang and Song cliff carvings and a garden of inscribed steles.

rows.name: Xianshi Ancient Town
rows.summary: A salt-trade town on the Fuxi River south-east of central Zigong, founded in the Sui dynasty and for centuries a wharf and staging post on the route that carried Zigong's salt downriver. Its lanes keep late-Qing and early Republican houses, temples and guild halls, and it is listed as one of China's historical and cultural towns.

rows.name: Yuchuan Ancestral Hall, Zigong
rows.summary: The ancestral hall of the Wang Sanweitang, one of Zigong's great salt-merchant families, built in 1873 by the family head, Wang Langyun, in what is now Bancang subdistrict. Two linked courtyard compounds, the Yuchuan Hall and the Chengde Hall, are enclosed by high fire walls and decorated with carved stone column bases and woodcarving on the brackets and beams; the hall later housed Zigong's first new-style school. Restoration began in 2024, with plans to make it a museum of Zigong's salt merchants.

rows.name: Zhaohua Ancient Town
rows.summary: A riverside old town on the Tuo River in Fushun County, south-east of Zigong. It was the birthplace of Liu Guangdi, one of the 'Six Gentlemen' executed in 1898 after the failure of the Hundred Days' Reform.

rows.name: Zhennan Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty brick pagoda in Rong County town, known locally as the White Pagoda: square in plan, with eleven storeys in the pavilion style above a plain base. It stands less than a kilometre west of the Rongxian Giant Buddha, from whose hillside it can be seen, and is easily combined with a visit there.

rows.name: Banyueshan Giant Buddha
rows.summary: A Maitreya Buddha about 20 metres tall carved into the hillside of Banyue Mountain south of Ziyang, the largest of six niches at the site. An inscription of 793 survives in the niche, though when carving began is debated, and the figure was finished only in 1131, under the Southern Song. The temple that once stood in front was pulled down during the Cultural Revolution, when the statue was also damaged.

rows.name: Baosen Lemon Town, Anyue
rows.summary: A lemon-themed farm park in Yanqiao village, Wenhua town, in Anyue, the county named China's home of lemons, rated 4A in 2023. Across about 3.2 km² it combines lemon orchards and a lemon exhibition hall with leisure facilities and accommodation, and it is promoted for spring outings and family breaks. It can be paired with the Anyue rock carvings, the main reason most visitors come to the county.

rows.name: Former Residence of Chen Yi
rows.summary: The rural family home in Laodong town where Chen Yi (1901–1972) was born and grew up. He became a Communist military commander, one of the ten marshals of the People's Republic, mayor of Shanghai from 1949 and foreign minister from 1958 until his death; the house is preserved as a memorial site and forms the core of a scenic area named after him.

rows.name: Kunfo Temple Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: A group of Buddhist cliff carvings at Kunfo ('Sleeping Buddha') Temple in the countryside of Lezhi County, begun in the Sui dynasty and added to up to the Song. It was listed as a national heritage site in 2013 and lies well off the usual tourist routes.

rows.name: Mumen Temple
