rows.summary: A small Ming temple in the hills north of Anyue, built around the stupa of the Chan master Wuji (1380–1446). Its centrepiece is the stone pavilion that the Zhengtong emperor ordered to shelter his stupa, carved to look like a timber building down to its brackets, rafters and roof tiles; only its two doors were made of wood, which gave the 'Wooden Door Temple' its name. The main hall and patriarch hall also survive.

rows.name: Yuping Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain of about 1,200 m beside Liujiang ancient town in Hongya county, developed as a leisure area with hiking trails, a forest adventure park, a forest-themed hotel and a campsite. It also has a paragliding take-off point and a forest-ecology museum. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Micang Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Micang Mountains of Nanjiang county, in northern Sichuan near the Shaanxi border, with visitor car parks and a shuttle-bus route into the forest. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020, run by the park's management bureau.

rows.name: Haizi Mountain Forest Resort
rows.summary: A mountain resort area around Wangyu town in Yucheng district, Ya'an, run by a rural-tourism company under the name Shiwai Xiangcun. Facilities reported include a mountain hotel and a peacock park. It was one of the first national forest-wellness bases named in 2020.

rows.name: Anshun Confucius Temple
rows.summary: A Confucian temple in the old centre of Anshun, founded in 1394 as the prefectural school temple and rebuilt many times since; only the stone carvings survive from the Ming, with most of the rest Qing or later. Five successive courtyards lead from an entrance screen wall through a ceremonial pool and a gateway to the Dacheng Hall, whose front columns are carved with openwork coiled dragons. Listed nationally in 2001, it is a short walk from other old-town sights such as the Wumiao and Wang Ruofei's former home.

rows.name: Anshun Wumiao (Temple of Guan Yu and Yue Fei)
rows.summary: Founded in 1382 as a shrine to the Three Kingdoms general Guan Yu, this temple in central Anshun was rebuilt in 1666 as a martial temple and since 1919 has honoured Guan Yu together with the Song-dynasty general Yue Fei. The main hall has 36 monolithic stone pillars, the tallest 14 m, and the compound includes the three-storey timber Guanyin Pavilion added in 1792. It was added to the national heritage list in 2013.

rows.name: Baojiatun Irrigation System
rows.summary: Baojiatun is a garrison-farming village founded in the Ming dynasty, and its irrigation works, begun in the Hongwu reign (1368–98) and still in use, are a national heritage unit. A fish-mouth diversion splits the upstream river in two, and weirs, main channels, two mill-houses and stone bridges, including a seven-arch bridge, carry the water to the fields around the village. The weirs and channels run through the village's farmland, and the village, a China Historic and Cultural Village, also has old mansions and a fortified tower.

rows.name: Duocai Wanxiang Tourism Complex
rows.summary: A modern resort-style leisure complex on Xihang Avenue in Anshun's economic development zone, combining entertainment, holiday accommodation, business conferencing and wellness-themed attractions. It is a purpose-built leisure development rather than a historic or natural site.

rows.name: Former Guizhou Aero Engine Factory (Third Front)
rows.name_zh: 三线贵州航空发动机厂旧址
rows.pinyin: Sānxiàn Guìzhōu Hángkōng Fādòngjī Chǎng Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A Third Front industrial site in Pingba district: from 1964 the Third Front programme moved defence industry into the mountains of south-west China, and an aero-engine works here, now AECC Guizhou Liyang Aviation Power, built the WP-7 and WP-13 turbojet series. A workshop set inside a natural cave, with old machine tools, can be seen, and an exhibition hall has sections on aviation science, Third Front construction and the factory's later development.

rows.name: Former Residence of Wang Ruofei
rows.summary: The house in central Anshun where Wang Ruofei (1896–1946), an early leader of the Chinese Communist Party, was born and grew up. A timber courtyard house of Qing date, built by his great-grandfather, it opened to visitors in 1982 and displays furniture, material on his activities while studying in Japan and France, and clothing he wore at the 1945 Chongqing negotiations. It was added to the national heritage list in 2013.

rows.name: Gaodang Buyei Ancient Village
rows.summary: A Buyei village near the Huangguoshu waterfalls where more than 120 houses are built of stone, with flagstone lanes and stone-slab roofs; experts date the settlement to the Ming dynasty. It has a Buyei folk museum with over 3,000 everyday objects, a central square used for festivals such as the sixth day of the sixth lunar month, and some restored houses run as homestays. Its historic buildings are protected at provincial level.

rows.name: Getu River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst river-and-cave scenic area in Ziyun county, with limestone hills, large cave arches and a river running through. It is divided into the Dachuandong (Big Through-cave), Xiaochuandong (Small Through-cave), Dahe (river) and Yaoyan sections plus several separate sights, with Miao villages along the river. It is also a well-known rock-climbing area.

rows.name: Guanling Fossil Park
rows.summary: A fossil park in Guanling county that protects the Guanling biota, a Late Triassic marine fauna more than 200 million years old, with ichthyosaurs, placodonts, turtles, sea lilies and ammonites among its fossils. Its main visitor area is under 1 sq km, within a much larger planned park area. The park is used for school study trips.

rows.name: Hongshan Reservoir
rows.summary: A small reservoir on the north-east side of central Anshun, begun in 1958 and filled in 1959, now ringed by a landscaped park. A 2017 makeover added art installations, boardwalks, walking paths, pedestrian bridges and picnic areas, and it became a 4A scenic area that year. It suits an easy walk by the water close to the old town.

rows.name: Jiuxian Scenic Area, Guanling
rows.summary: A cave-themed leisure area in Yongning town, Guanling county, with a show-cave route and a separate water-recreation zone. It is a modern leisure attraction rather than a heritage site.

rows.name: Jiuzhou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A historic town in Xixiu district that was once the seat of the old Anshun prefecture and is a China Historic and Cultural Town, home to tunbao people descended from Ming-era soldiers. Its four main streets keep many Ming and Qing courtyard houses of stone walls, timber frames and stone-slab roofs, restored in recent years in the original style, and local women wear Fengyang-style Han costume. Festivals such as the tunbao New Year, dixi processions and the City God procession are held through the year, and the old streets now hold more than 400 shops and other businesses.

rows.name: Longgong (Dragon Palace) Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst scenic area south of Anshun built around the Dragon Palace, a cave with an underground river that visitors tour by boat, with the Longmen waterfall at the cave entrance. Around it are gorges, waterfalls, peak forest, cliffs and a stone forest, and routes combine the cave boat ride with the Qunfang Valley and a second boat trip at Xuantang. It neighbours the Huangguoshu scenic area and is often visited with it.

rows.name: Qianshan Xiushui Scenic Area, Puding
rows.summary: A countryside leisure park near Puding county town, built around a lake, with a camping base at the 'Twenty-four Pools', go-karts, a coloured slide and river drifting. Holiday events have included 'tieshui chonglong', a molten-iron dragon display listed as provincial intangible heritage. It is a suburban leisure base for family outings.

rows.name: Tangyue Village
rows.summary: Tangyue is a village in Leping town, Pingba district, promoted since about 2017 as a model of rural reform and poverty reduction. After a flood it registered land, forest, housing and water-works rights and pooled its farmland in a village cooperative, an approach known as the "Tangyue road". A visitor area opened in October 2017, and the village was named in the first list of national key villages for rural tourism in 2019.

rows.name: Tianlong Tunbao
rows.summary: A stone-built town in Pingba district, on the old route west to Yunnan, settled by Ming-era garrison soldiers from the lower Yangtze region; their descendants are known as Tunbao people. Its stone lanes and shops are open to visitors, local women wear the traditional Fengyang-style Han dress, and a performance ground stages dixi, a masked 'ground opera' of martial episodes from the Three Kingdoms and other heroic romances. Tiantaishan Wulong Temple stands on the hill about 2 km to the east.

rows.name: Tiantaishan Wulong Temple
rows.summary: A temple-fortress on top of the 70 m Tiantai hill, begun in 1590 and combining a Buddhist temple, a Daoist hall and a military stronghold; its outer walls are built hard against the cliff, which drops away on three sides. The halls include the Great Buddha Hall, with relief carvings of the 24 filial exemplars, the Jade Emperor Pavilion and a Guansheng Hall, and a sword, robe and plaque attributed to the general Wu Sangui are kept here alongside a display of local dixi opera costumes. Listed nationally in 2001, it stands on the hill beside the Tianlong Tunbao old town.

rows.name: Xiaohewan Village
rows.summary: A waterside village in Xiayun town, Pingba district, billed by the provincial culture and tourism department as one of the prettiest villages in central Guizhou, with rapeseed and pear blossom in spring. It is run as a countryside leisure area with farmhouse restaurants, homestays and room for visitors to park RVs.

rows.name: Yelang Cave
rows.summary: A karst scenic area in Biandanshan town, Zhenning county, upstream of the Huangguoshu waterfalls. It combines caves, a sinkhole, a canyon, a waterfall and primary forest with Buyei village culture, and festivals are held here each year on the third day of the third lunar month and the sixth day of the sixth.

rows.name: Yunfeng Tunbao (Yunshantun)
rows.summary: Yunshantun and the neighbouring Benzhai are the core of Yunfeng Tunbao, a group of eight fortified villages in Xixiu district settled in the early Ming dynasty by soldiers posted to Guizhou. Yunshantun is enclosed by stone walls and has a main street of roughly 600 m with houses from the Ming, Qing and Republican periods, while Benzhai is a maze of lanes, loopholed walls and stone watchtowers. Both are on the national heritage list, Yunshantun is also a China Historic and Cultural Village, and the scenic area adds a culture exhibition centre and craft workshops.

rows.name: Axilixi Grassland (Ertaipo)
rows.summary: Axilixi Grassland, also called Ertaipo, is a plateau of pasture in southern Hezhang at an average height of about 2,300 m, where cattle and horses graze beneath wide views and, in fair weather, seas of cloud. It opened to visitors in September 2019 and is best known for the 'Wave Road', a road that undulates over the hills and has made the area a self-drive destination; a small sightseeing train and campsites are among the other features. It is promoted together with Jiucaiping, about 15 km away, and the two are usually visited together.

rows.name: Baili Dujuan Rhododendron Forest
rows.summary: Baili Dujuan is a mountain forest of wild rhododendrons on the Bijie plateau, with more than 60 species recorded and, according to the Bijie government, a thousand-year-old azalea 'king' among the trees. The 5A scenic area, about 126 sq km in all, has two main parts, Pudi and Jinpo, linked by shuttle buses in the flowering season, which runs from about March to late April, and summer temperatures average about 19 degrees Celsius. Yi, Miao, Bai and other peoples live around the area, and the cool summers make it a retreat from the heat as well.

rows.name: Dajiucaiping (Hezhang side)
rows.summary: Dajiucaiping ('big chive plateau') is a high plateau in south-western Hezhang between about 2,300 and 2,777 m, covered in wild chive plants whose purple flowers open from July and peak in August and September. Wind turbines, seas of cloud and karst rock walls add to the views, and the cool summers have made it a popular escape from the heat; the scenic area covers about 80 sq km. A second, higher summit, Xiaojiucaiping (2,900.6 m, the highest point in Guizhou), lies nearby on the Liupanshui side and has its own entrance.

rows.name: Datun Tusi Manor
rows.summary: Datun Tusi Manor is a walled hillside residence and administrative seat of a Yi tusi family, a hereditary local chieftain under imperial rule, built up from the Qing dynasty to the early Republic. Three parallel ranges of halls and gardens climb the slope along the main axis, with a pond garden crossed by a covered bridge, and four of the six blockhouses that once ringed the walls survive. It became a national heritage unit in 1988, and Bijie's culture bureau describes it as the best-preserved Yi tusi manor in north-west Guizhou.

rows.name: Fangjiaping Scenic Area
rows.summary: Fangjiaping is a mountain park in the Baili Dujuan district built around outdoor activities rather than flowers. The district's 2024 announcement lists more than 20 activities, including night-time programmes, RV camping, a rail-guided slide car and a cliff swing. It suits families and active visitors more than those looking for rhododendron blooms.

rows.name: Gonglongping National Forest Park
rows.summary: Gonglongping is a forest park of more than 1,700 hectares in the hills near Bijie, with forest cover that Bijie's government puts at 95 per cent. Its main sights are Tuntianjing, a deep karst sinkhole, and a round stone 'echo platform' about 10 metres across. There is also a forest campsite among the trees, and the cool summer air is part of the draw.

rows.name: Guanyindong Palaeolithic Site
rows.summary: Guanyindong is a cave in Guanyindong village, Qianxi, where excavations from the 1960s uncovered more than 3,000 stone tools and the bones of 23 mammal species, among them giant panda and rhinoceros. Bijie's culture bureau dates it to about 240,000 years ago and calls it the largest early Palaeolithic cave site south of the Yangtze. It is a protected excavation site and visitor facilities there are thinly documented, so check locally before travelling.

rows.name: Jiming Sansheng
rows.summary: Jiming Sansheng ('cockcrow in three provinces') is a border village where Guizhou, Yunnan and Sichuan meet, named for the saying that a cock's crow here is heard in all three. It is linked to a meeting of the Communist Party's leaders held in February 1935 during the Long March, and the scenic area pairs that history with views over a deep gorge. The Sichuan and Yunnan villages along the border use the same name and each presents its own claim to the meeting, so travellers should check which side they are heading for.

rows.name: Jinhai Lake
rows.summary: Jinhai Lake is a lakeside and wetland park on the edge of the Jinhaihu New Area, between Bijie's Qixingguan District and Dafang, with more than 1,200 mu (about 80 hectares) of water. It has lakeshore paths, boats and camping lawns, and a gorge section with an old plank road and caves. It is a city-edge place for a short break rather than a long excursion.

rows.name: Jiudongtian
rows.summary: Jiudongtian is a stretch of the upper Wu River system, known here as the Zongxi River, that runs through a chain of karst caves open to the sky through collapsed roofs, on the boundary of Dafang and Nayong counties. Boats run between several of the caves and under natural stone bridges. It was approved as a national scenic area in 2004 and is called a 'karst encyclopaedia' locally.

rows.name: Mu'ege Ancient City and Shexiang Tomb
rows.summary: Mu'ege is a Yi name meaning the place where a ruler lives, and it was the seat of the Yi rulers of the Shuixi region, now Dafang; the 'ancient city' here is a reconstruction begun in 2008 on the old site. Its centrepiece is a rebuilt Guizhou Xuanweifu, the Ming-era Guizhou pacification commissioner's office, completed in 2011, beside the Shexiang Museum and other buildings. Less than a kilometre away is the tomb of Shexiang (1358–1396), the Yi woman who acted as Guizhou's pacification commissioner in the early Ming; the tomb was restored in the 1980s and sits in a landscaped park with a bronze statue, a pond and a stele gallery.

rows.name: Old Buildings of Zhijin
rows.summary: Zhijin's old town, founded in 1666 and named among Guizhou's four early historic cities, holds a group of 25 listed heritage points, among them the Caishen and Heishen temples and seven old bridges, dating from the Yuan to the Qing dynasty. The best known is the Caishen (God of Wealth) Temple, a wooden hall of stacked eaves that rises like a pagoda and was rebuilt in 1783. The lanes beside the Guancheng River can be walked in a couple of hours, and the site pairs easily with Zhijin Cave about 23 km away.

rows.name: Shexiang Ancient Town
rows.summary: Shexiang Ancient Town is a newly built district in the north of Dafang, developed mainly as a poverty-relocation project for about 12,000 residents. Its tourist streets are built in Ming and Qing style with elements of local Yi manor houses, and include three themed shopping quarters, eight squares, ten art towers and a terraced flower garden. It is a place for an evening stroll, shops, food and performances rather than a historic old town.

rows.name: Sichuan–Yunnan–Guizhou Revolutionary Committee Site
rows.name_zh: 川滇黔省革命委员会旧址
rows.summary: This former church compound in central Bijie served as the office of the Sichuan–Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Revolutionary Committee, set up by the Red Army's 2nd and 6th Army Groups in February 1936. The committee was formed in Dafang on 8 February and moved to Bijie on 17 February, and Bijie's government records that commanders including He Long, Xiao Ke, Ren Bishi and Wang Zhen worked there. The compound is now a museum holding several hundred items and is part of a national heritage listing that also covers related sites in Dafang County.

rows.name: Yishan Flower Valley
rows.summary: Yishan Flower Valley is a planted flower garden beside Pengcheng, the main town of the Baili Dujuan district, made to give visitors something to see after the rhododendron season ends. Bijie's 2026 visitor itineraries list a boardwalk through the flower beds, a small sightseeing train, a pet park and a bookshop among its attractions. It is a compact, family-oriented stop that works best combined with the main Baili Dujuan rhododendron areas.

rows.name: Youshanhe
rows.summary: Youshanhe is a karst gorge and forest scenic area of about 67 sq km in north-eastern Dafang, one mountain range away from Baili Dujuan. Its best-known sight is Xianyu Peak, a rock tower rising from the river valley with water on three sides and an old temple on top; a glass walkway runs along the gorge, and the high meadow of Cuisuba, at about 1,700 metres, has a campsite and grassland walks. It is described as part of a national forest park and is promoted for cool summers and hiking.

rows.name: Zhijin Cave
rows.summary: Zhijin Cave is a large karst show cave in the hills north-east of Zhijin town, known locally as Daji Cave until a county tourism survey team explored it in 1980. Formations along the visitor route are named for what they resemble, among them the 'Upside-down Pipa', the 'Overlord's Helmet', the 'Silver Rain Tree' and 'Lingzhi Mountain'. It is a 5A scenic area and is easily combined with the old town of Zhijin.

rows.name: Zhongguohe Rafting Resort
rows.summary: Zhongguohe is a rafting resort on the Zhongguohe river in Zhongjian township, Qianxi, whose rafting course and themed viewpoints follow the 1990s film A Chinese Odyssey (Dahua Xiyou), with spots named after scenes in it such as the Moonlight Box and Dinosaur Valley. It was developed by a private company and, after being upgraded from 3A, became Qianxi's first 4A scenic area in 2021. Rafting is the main summer activity, and the township has guesthouses and hotels for an overnight stay.

rows.name: Baimayu Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring and wellness resort in a mountain valley at about 1,340 m in Kaiyang county, where the climate is cool and often misty. Its courtyard-style buildings hold about 70 guest rooms, and the spring water runs at around 40 °C; the Guiyang government says it adds traditional Miao, Dong and Yao healing methods and Chinese-medicine health checks. It suits a quiet overnight stay away from the city.

rows.name: Changpoling Ancient Road (Tea Horse Road)
rows.summary: One listed section of the Tea Horse Road, the network of old caravan routes across south-west China, whose Guizhou part has 35 listed points spread across Qianxinan, Anshun, Guiyang, Liupanshui and Bijie. This stretch lies inside Changpoling National Forest Park: about 3 km of blue-grey stone paving roughly 1.5 m wide, begun in the Yuan period and rebuilt in the Ming, running through pine woods to a large forest lawn. The city forestry bureau calls it the only well-preserved old post road around Guiyang, and the park also has a cherry-blossom lake.

rows.name: Colourful Guizhou City
rows.summary: A modern shopping, dining and entertainment district near Longdongbao airport, begun in 2011 and opened in 2014. It brings together a multi-ethnic culture display centre, a city air terminal, a creative park, an aquarium and many food and souvenir outlets, and the Guiyang government pitches it as the first or last stop on a trip to Guizhou. It suits a short visit before or after a flight.

rows.name: Colourful Guizhou Fengjingyan Cultural Park
rows.name_zh: 多彩贵州风景眼文创园
rows.summary: A cultural park beside Guiyang's Longdongbao airport that showcases Guizhou's intangible cultural heritage, open since July 2015. It combines exhibition spaces, shops, restaurants, a theatre and study programmes, and sits next to the Shuanglong ecological wetland park; the Guiyang government nicknames it the airport's park and a playground for intangible heritage. It suits a short stop before or after a flight.

rows.name: Former Dade School
rows.summary: A temple compound in old Guiyang that became a school: it began as a Yuan-period temple to Nan Jiyun, was rebuilt in the Ming and Qing as the Zhonglie Palace, and in 1901 became the site of a school that took the name Dade in 1912. The courtyard buildings now hold a museum on the school's history and on the development of modern education in Guiyang and Guizhou. It became a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Geological Museum of Guizhou
rows.summary: A natural-science museum in Guanshanhu district, opened in August 2021. Its four permanent exhibitions cover Guizhou's fossils, including ichthyosaurs, the Guizhou dragon and sea lilies, its karst landscapes, its mineral resources and the history of geological work in the province. It was rated a national first-class museum in 2024.

rows.name: Guiyang Forest Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A forest wildlife park of about 5,000 mu (some 330 hectares) at the Zhazuo forest farm in Xiuwen county, home to more than 200 species and some 2,000 animals according to the Guiyang government. It is built around viewing and breeding wild animals, with a conventional funfair and a glass-sided water slide as extras. It suits family outings.

rows.name: Guiyu Hot Spring
rows.summary: A garden-style hot-spring resort in Wudang district that the Guiyang government presents as Guizhou's first open-air garden hot spring. Its pools include a children's area, herbal pools, a whirlpool, fish-therapy pools and a standard-size swimming pool, with water drawn from about 1,900 m underground at around 53 °C. It suits an easy soak close to Guiyang.

rows.name: Jiaxiu Tower and Wenchang Pavilion
rows.summary: Two Ming-founded towers from old Guiyang that share one national listing. Jiaxiu Tower, first built in 1598 and last rebuilt in 1909, stands on a rock in the Nanming River and is treated as the city's emblem; a famous long couplet hangs inside. About 800 m to the north, Wenchang Pavilion (1596) is a three-storey pavilion on the barbican of the old east gate, whose upper two storeys have a nine-sided plan that is rare in China.

rows.name: Kongxuetang (Guiyang Confucius Academy)
rows.summary: A Confucian academy and cultural complex in Han–Tang style, opened to the public in 2013 in the middle of the Huaxi National Urban Wetland Park. A ritual axis runs from a statue of Confucius up to the Dacheng Hall and the Apricot Altar, and halls include an underground Confucius exhibition and a hall on Wang Yangming's years in Guizhou. The 4A area also takes in the Huaxi National Urban Wetland Park, a karst river-valley park of about 941 hectares.

rows.name: Lewan International Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in the Lewan International development in eastern Wudang district. The Guiyang government describes its water as a silicic-acid spring drawn from nearly 3,000 m underground, with indoor pools that include herbal, rose, milk and sulphur baths, and a Chinese-medicine wellness hall. It is aimed at family outings and short wellness breaks.

rows.name: Matouzhai Old Village
rows.summary: A hillside village in the Diwo basin of Hefeng township that grew up around the Yuan-dynasty seat of a regional governor, set up in 1283, and later a Ming-period headquarters of the Song family, the hereditary local chiefs of the Shuidong area. About 90 Ming and Qing courtyard houses survive, blending Han timber-frame construction with Buyei details such as carved lattice windows and side gates, along with the foundations of the governor's office and Red Army slogans written in 1935. It lies on the Ten-Mile Gallery countryside route and was named a National Historic and Cultural Village in 2008.

rows.name: Nanjiang Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A river canyon in Kaiyang county noted for karst cliffs, cascades and tufa formations, with some 40 waterfalls along its length. Provincial tourism authorities have counted more than 80 natural sights, and the canyon has long been promoted as a rafting destination with cliff-side walkways. It sits beside the Ten-Mile Gallery countryside, so it can be combined with Matouzhai village.

rows.name: Nanshan Tianmu Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in traditional Chinese architectural style on a wooded hillside beside the Nanshan state forest farm in Yongjing town, Xifeng county, with pools laid out in cascading terraces. The Guiyang government counts 79 indoor and outdoor pools, 245 guest rooms and an indoor children's play area; the spring water, at about 48 °C, comes from around 2,500 m underground. In 2025 it was one of three Guiyang hot springs rated 'golden grade' under the provincial standard.

rows.name: Penglai Xianjie Mushroom Town
rows.summary: An agri-tourism site in Niuchang township, Baiyun district, built around the district's edible-mushroom industry. The mushroom-themed 'Moli Town' project adds recreation, restaurants, shopping, folk-culture experiences and accommodation, and the site is designated a city-level study base for school pupils. It suits family and school outings.

rows.name: Poly International Hot Spring
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort on the wooded edge of Wudang district, beside a five-star hotel and a small lake where visitors can feed black swans. The Guiyang government lists more than 40 indoor and outdoor pools, among them herbal, red-wine and vinegar pools, a starlit hydrotherapy hall, fish-therapy pools and water slides for children, fed by water at about 67 °C. It suits a family soak or half-day break near the city.

rows.name: Qiangui Liuguang Hot Spring
rows.summary: A riverside hot-spring resort at Yangming Wharf on the Liuguang River canyon in Xiuwen county, built in terraces up the slope above the water. It combines hot-spring bathing with a hotel, restaurants, canyon boat trips and outdoor activities, and opened on a trial basis in January 2015. The Guiyang government says the spring water comes from about 1,800 m underground at 56–60 °C.

rows.name: Qianling Mountain Park
rows.summary: A forested hill park with a lake and woodland paths in the north-west of Guiyang's urban area, built from 1957. Its best-known sights are Hongfu Temple, reached by a winding path, the Qilin Cave where Zhang Xueliang was held, and the troop of wild macaques that live in the park; the macaques can bite, and visitors are asked not to feed them. It is one of Guiyang's main sights and a popular place for a half-day walk.

rows.name: Qingyan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A walled stone town founded in 1378 as a Ming military post and later a market town, with walls, gates, lanes and houses built of the local blue-grey stone that earned it the name 'stone city'. Its sights include temples, a Catholic church, memorial archways and the former residence of Zhao Yijiong, Guizhou's first civil-service top scholar, and part of its old streets is also a listed section of the Tea Horse Road. Local snacks include fried tofu balls and braised pig's trotters.

rows.name: Quanhu Park
rows.summary: A lake park of about 1,080 mu (72 hectares) in the south of Baiyun district, with some 205 mu of water and about 750 mu of planting. Its named sights include the Quanhu Secret Realm, the Jade Water Long Bridge and Cloud Tower, and the park serves as a green corridor between Baiyun and Guanshanhu districts. It suits an easy walk in the city.

rows.name: Shiguang Guizhou Themed Town
rows.summary: A modern themed town of about 140,000 square metres in Qingzhen, between Red Maple Lake and Baihua Lake, built in the style of 1940s Shanghai and old Guiyang architecture, with shops, restaurants and entertainment. The Guiyang government says four lanes (military, merchants, officials and townspeople) tell Guizhou's story, from the Triassic fossils shown on the town walls to the Ming-era Tunpu garrison-settler culture. It is a purpose-built attraction rather than a historic town.

rows.name: Siji Guizhou Resort
rows.summary: A holiday resort complex in Qingzhen built around a water park and hot springs under a four-seasons theme. The Guiyang government describes a summer water park and winter bathing in natural hot springs, aimed at leisure and wellness stays.

rows.name: Taoyuan River Gorge
rows.summary: A river gorge resort of about 15.7 sq km in Liutun town, Xiuwen county, with lakes, caves, springs, waterfalls and canyon scenery along the Taoyuan River. The Guiyang government calls it one of Guizhou's best-known rafting spots, and it also offers water play, forest walks, a hot-spring hotel and study programmes for school groups. It suits an active day trip from Guiyang.

rows.name: Tianhetan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A karst scenic area in Shiban town, Huaxi district, named for a natural stone bridge that spans a pool where a river runs through its caves. Features include a dry cave and a water cave, the Beauty Pool waterfall and the Shibang cascade. It is a nature outing south-west of the city.

rows.name: Wanxiang Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort and hotel in Wudang district, north-east of central Guiyang. Indoor baths and a garden of nearly 50 outdoor pools are fed by spring water drawn from about 2,200 m underground at around 57 °C, according to the Guiyang government. It also has a spa centre, a children's water-play area and a hotel, so it works as a soak close to the city.

rows.name: Xiangchou Guizhou Rural Culture Park
rows.summary: A themed park on the Xiangchou campus of Qingzhen's vocational education city, in Zhanjie town, built around rural life and traditional farming culture. The Guiyang government says it draws on three strands: agrarian civilisation, the philosophy of Wang Yangming and the local reading-and-farming tradition. It is a purpose-built culture park rather than a historic village.

rows.name: Xifeng Concentration Camp Site
rows.summary: The site of a prison that the Kuomintang's military intelligence bureau ran near Xifeng from 1938 to 1946; the memorial hall counts more than 1,200 prisoners, among them communists, patriots and democrats, and Yang Hucheng, a leader of the Xi'an Incident. Nine prison blocks with 52 rooms survive in the compound, now the Xifeng Concentration Camp Revolutionary History Memorial Hall, opened in 1997, with an exhibition on the camp and its prisoners. The Xuantian Cave, a second place of confinement, forms part of the protected site.

rows.name: Yangchang Flower-Painting Town
rows.summary: A flower-themed leisure park of about 789 mu (some 53 hectares) in Yangchang town, Wudang district. Its 20-odd attractions include a flower-art walking street, a flower hill, a lawn, an RV camp, a culture square about the Shuidong region and a garden recalling the 'educated youth' era. It also serves as a city-level labour-education base for school pupils, and suits family and school visits.

rows.name: Yangming Cave and Yangming Cultural Park
rows.summary: The cave on Qixia Hill where the Ming philosopher Wang Yangming lived for about three years from 1508, after being exiled to the Longchang post station, and where tradition places the 'Longchang enlightenment' that shaped his later teaching, including 'unity of knowing and acting'. The cave carries inscriptions from the Ming, Qing and Republican periods, and the cultural park around it adds a memorial hall, a plaza and the Longgang Academy where he taught. The national listing also covers the Yangming Shrine in Guiyang city, a separate site.

rows.name: Yunmanhu Eco-Resort Park
rows.summary: A family-oriented leisure park built around an artificial lake in the Gui'an New Area, formed by linking two reservoirs and opened in 2016. The main section, an eco-resort park of about 2,200 mu (some 150 hectares), is laid out in Swiss-style buildings with themed zones such as Wonder Island, Rainbow Garden, Adventure Forest, Valley of Wind and Roaming Hills, and by 2024 had added an artificial pink-sand beach and summer-evening events. It suits families wanting a lakeside day out from Guiyang.

rows.name: Baichehe Hot Spring Resort Area
rows.summary: Baichehe is a river-valley resort area in Panlong town, Shuicheng, built around hot springs and promoted as a summer retreat. It has hot-spring baths, more than 90 homestays with about 1,500 rooms, a wetland park, riverside paths and family attractions such as slides and children's boats. It suits long stays and families rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Dadong Site
rows.summary: Dadong is a karst cave in Panzhou where excavations in 1992 and 1993 found Palaeolithic stone tools and large numbers of animal fossils; the city tourism page counts more than 2,000 stone artefacts and nearly 10,000 fossils to date, and published age estimates range from about 100,000 to 300,000 years. It lies inside the Dadong Bamboo Sea scenic area in Zhuhai town, which also has bamboo-forest walks and a zip line. The site is protected as a national heritage unit.

rows.name: Dala Xiangu
rows.summary: Dala Xiangu is a leisure-farming and rural-tourism area in Panzhou with a wetland park, a lake, about 300 mu (20 hectares) of coloured flower fields laid out in circular patterns, a cartoon-themed play area and a lakeside hotel. The name 'Dala' is given as a Buyei word meaning mutual help, and the agronomist Yuan Longping, known as the father of hybrid rice, visited and inscribed the name. It is a family leisure stop rather than a wild landscape.

rows.name: Guizhou Third Front Construction Museum
rows.summary: This museum in Liupanshui's Shuicheng old town is about the 'Third Front', the programme from the mid-1960s to relocate defence and heavy industry to the interior, in which Liupanshui became a coal and steel centre. The main building has seven exhibition halls, a separate hall uses sound and light to recreate factory floors, a workers' canteen and a supply cooperative, and large objects such as a steam locomotive stand outdoors. It opened in 2013 and holds more than 20,000 items.

rows.name: Huilongxi Spa Resort
rows.name_zh: 回龙溪康养休闲度假旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Huílóngxī Kāngyǎng Xiūxián Dùjià Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: Huilongxi is a spa and leisure resort beside Yanjiao old town, with hot-spring baths, a rafting course, a hotel and conference facilities, and ethnic-culture and entertainment attractions. The spring water is piped from the Mugong springs, a village known locally for longevity, and the area has a provincially protected group of late-Qing and Republican-era trading buildings.

rows.name: Luobie Longjing Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Luobie Longjing is a hot-spring resort in the Luobie Buyei-Yi ethnic township, south-east of Liuzhi, with more than 60 soaking pools of different kinds, an indoor and outdoor water park, restaurants, rooms and meeting facilities. It is built for relaxing stays and family outings rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Meihuashan Scenic Area and Ski Resort
rows.summary: Meihuashan is a mountain scenic area of about 40 sq km on the edge of Liupanshui, rising to about 2,499 m, with a resort park laid out in the shape of a plum blossom, a ski area first built in 2015 and a mountain cable car of nearly 10 km. Viewpoints look over karst peaks, cloud seas and forest, and the city promotes it for flowers in spring, cool summers, autumn colour and winter skiing. It is a short ride from the city centre.

rows.name: Shengjing Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: Shengjing Hot Spring is a hot-spring resort of about 6.3 sq km in Liuguan subdistrict, Panzhou, combining indoor and outdoor pools with a waterfall, a wave pool, a cave-style soaking pool and a children's water park. The grounds also hold a lakeside park, a forest park, a sports park, a wetland park and a hotel with conference rooms. It suits families and groups wanting a spa stop.

rows.name: Tuole Ancient Ginkgo Village
rows.summary: Tuole is a village of about 1,400 old ginkgo trees in Shiqiao town, Panzhou, where wooden walkways, viewing platforms and a path through the old village have been built among the trees. The leaves turn gold in autumn, which is the busiest season, and stalls sell roasted ginkgo nuts and dried chestnut-rose fruit. It is a short, scenic stop that is easy to combine with Wumeng Grassland.

rows.name: Wumeng Grassland
rows.summary: Wumeng Grassland is a plateau of pasture and dwarf rhododendron at about 2,000 to 2,857 m in Panzhou, with a high lake called Tianchi, a natural-bridge canyon on the Qingshui river and a ski area. It is promoted for rhododendron bloom in spring, cool summers, 'Buddha's light' halos in autumn and winter snow, and was one of Guizhou's first provincial-level tourist resorts. Horse riding, camping and a coloured slide track at the ski area are among the activities.

rows.name: Xiaochong Tombs, Panzhou
rows.summary: Xiaochong is a hillside burial ground of the Zhang and Deng families behind Huatun in Hanlin Subdistrict, Panzhou, with more than 130 graves dating from the Qing dynasty onwards. Most are built as carved stone arches, among them a three-tier hexagonal pavilion-style gravestone 5.1 metres high, and pairs of stone flagpoles that the city government says could be raised only once a family member had earned an examination degree. It covers more than two hectares and was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013; it suits visitors interested in local stone carving and Qing funerary customs.

rows.name: Xiaojiucaiping (Zhongshan side)
rows.summary: Xiaojiucaiping ('small chive plateau') is the Liupanshui-side approach to the Jiucaiping range and its summit, at 2,900.6 m the highest point in Guizhou, on the border with Hezhang County. Wild chives cover the ridges, and the area has karst stone-forest rocks, caves and sinkholes, rhododendrons in spring and a well-known camping ground; the city also describes it as a provincial-level tourist resort. Hezhang's Dajiucaiping, with its own entrance, covers the neighbouring plateau.

rows.name: Yushe Forest Park and Snow Mountain
rows.summary: Yushe National Forest Park, in the hills of Shuicheng District south of central Liupanshui, is best known for Yushe Snow Mountain, which the city describes as Guizhou's first alpine ski resort. It has beginner, intermediate and advanced slopes, a snow-play area, snowmobile and cable-car rides, and has hosted youth alpine ski races; frost on the trees and frozen lakes are noted in winter. Outside the snow season the forest park is a cool place for walks.

rows.name: Zangke River Scenic Area
rows.summary: Zangke River is a broad stretch of river water in southern Liuzhi, about 51 sq km of water surface at around 724 m above sea level, with an outdoor-sports base at Laowang Mountain. The scenic area has a hotel and a Yelang culture exhibition centre, and has hosted international paragliding and kayaking events since 2012. The city also lists it as a provincial-level tourist resort.

rows.name: Basha Miao Village
rows.summary: Basha is a Miao village a few kilometres from Congjiang county town, home to nearly 2,800 people, whose residents have kept customs such as haircuts with sickles, tree worship and carrying muskets with special permission from the police. The scenic area has a visitor service centre, and visitors can watch staged performances including musket firing, sickle haircutting, dances and wedding customs. It was rated 4A in 2018.

rows.name: Chong'an River Watermills
rows.summary: A row of traditional water-powered grain mills stands on a sandbar in the Chong'an River just south-east of Chong'an town in Huangping County, built from the Ming dynasty by local people influenced by the garrison settlers who brought new production methods from central China. At their late-Ming peak there were more than 40 mills; 19 mill houses survive in a line along the 343 m sandbar, and a 2015 heritage survey recorded 13 still in use, grinding tung seeds for oil, bamboo for paper and incense powder. The sandbar splits the river into two channels about 1.1 m apart in height, which drives the hidden water wheels, and the mills have been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Dali Dong Village, Rongjiang
rows.summary: Dali is a Dong village of about 300 households in Zaima township, Rongjiang County, whose old timber houses, five wind-and-rain bridges, stone-paved lanes, wells and drum tower are protected together as a national heritage group. Two- and three-storey timber houses sit on either side of a stream, with granaries and drying racks at the village edge, and a paved path laid in 1793 still leads out of the village; the drum tower was rebuilt in 2005 on its old site. Dali was added to China's World Heritage tentative list in 2006 and became a national protected site in 2013.

rows.name: Danzhai Wanda Village
rows.summary: Danzhai Wanda Village is a purpose-built tourism town beside Donghu lake in the middle of Danzhai county, built by the Wanda Group under a 2014 poverty-alleviation agreement with the county and opened in July 2017. It is a modern development in Miao architectural style, with themed streets and squares, craft shops (a large share devoted to heritage crafts such as batik and traditional papermaking), lake boating, a glass bridge and hot-spring hotels. It suits visitors who want an easy introduction to local crafts rather than a historic village.

rows.name: Diping Wind and Rain Bridge
rows.summary: Diping Bridge crosses the Nanjiang River between the upper and lower Dong hamlets of Diping in the far south-east of Liping County, and was first built in 1882. Close to 60 m long, it has a stone pier mid-stream that divides it into two cantilevered timber spans, with a five-tier tower on the pier and a three-tier tower at each end, and its interior walls are painted with scenes of Dong life such as weaving and singing. Floods swept the bridge away in 2004 and it was rebuilt to its original design in 2006; it has been a national protected site since 2001.

rows.name: Feishan Temple, Jinping
rows.summary: Feishan Temple is a temple complex on the north bank of the Qingshui River in the old part of Jinping county town, built in 1769 in memory of Yang Zaisi, a local chief of the late Tang and Five Dynasties period. It has two parts: Feishan Palace, a walled courtyard with a gate, main hall and opera stage, and Feishan Pavilion, a four-storey timber tower about 25 m high. The buildings were repaired or rebuilt in 1813, 1872, 1881 and 1893, and the complex has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Feiyunya Ancient Buildings, Huangping
rows.summary: Feiyunya is a temple-and-garden complex on a wooded hillside north-east of Huangping, centred on Yuetan Temple, which was founded in 1443 under the Ming. It is entered through a five-bay memorial-arch gate and includes a covered gallery, a pavilion built against the cliff beside a natural cave, and Yangyun Pavilion, whose arched roof heritage records call unique among Guizhou's old buildings; most of what stands today dates from the Guangxu reign (1875–1908), and the main hall is a Confucian temple hall moved from Jiuzhou town in 1986. Ming and Qing stone tablets and some twenty cliff inscriptions survive, and the complex has been a national protected site since 2006.

rows.name: Former Heping Village, Zhenyuan
rows.summary: The former Heping Village is a walled compound on Heping Street in Zhenyuan's old town, once a Qing garrison office and then a prison, that served as a camp for Japanese prisoners of war held by the Nationalist government from 1938 to 1944. Chinese records say 600 to 700 prisoners passed through and that some formed an anti-war league there, the name Heping (peace) coming from the Japanese writer Kaji Wataru, who worked with them. Parts of the compound were rebuilt in the 1980s and 2000s and now hold an exhibition; it is a national protected site (2006) and is described in official records as the only well-preserved Japanese prisoner-of-war camp in China.

rows.name: Gaoguo River, Zhenyuan
rows.summary: Gaoguo River is a forested gorge river in Yangchang town, north-west of Zhenyuan, best known for summer rafting: a course of about 5 km that drops some 200 m past rapids, pools and waterfalls and takes three to four hours. The rafting ends near Sanzhai village, a cluster of Dong, Miao and Tujia hamlets with a Dong drum tower, a wind-and-rain bridge and stilt houses, where evening cultural shows are staged. The river area has been a provincial scenic area since 2000.

rows.name: Gaoqian Drum Tower
rows.summary: Gaoqian Drum Tower stands in the Zaiyang hamlet of Gaoqian village, Xiajiang town, Congjiang County, and was built in the Yongzheng reign (1723–35), with repairs between the Jiaqing and Guangxu reigns and again in 1983. A timber tower of fifteen tiers of eaves on a hexagonal plan, about 23 m high, it has a double-roofed crown, painted eave boards, a fire pit and ox-hide drums on its second and top floors. Chinese heritage records call it the tallest surviving old drum tower of the Dong, and it has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Guidong Scenic Area, Sansui
rows.summary: Guidong is a rural scenic area in Jieping village, Bagong town, centred on a karst cave that local sources describe as about 4 km long, with stalactites, grooves and an underground stream. Only a first phase of the cave has been opened to visitors, lit in colour; around it are bamboo forest, a workshop showing traditional bamboo-pulp papermaking, farmland, a glass maze and an evening light show. The area was rated 3A in 2017 and upgraded to 4A in 2023.

rows.name: Jiabang Terraces
rows.summary: The Jiabang terraces climb the steep slopes of Jiabang township in southern Congjiang, covering more than 10,000 mu (about 667 ha) along some 25 km, with Miao villages scattered among the fields. Plots are small, many holding only a row or two of rice, so the paddies follow the contours closely; rice is planted in spring and the terraces turn gold in early autumn. Each spring a Kaiyang festival, held on 19 April in 2026, marks the start of planting with a ritual led by village elders, farming demonstrations and a field-climbing race.

rows.name: Jianhe Hot Spring Resort
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort in Wenquan village, Cengsong town, north-east of Jianhe county town, fed by six springs; the water comes out at about 38–53 °C and is a radon-and-sulphur type. It has more than 80 indoor and outdoor pools, a seasonal water park, a theatre with Miao-themed water shows, hotels and a shopping street in Miao and Dong style. It is a developed leisure resort aimed at holiday-makers rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Jingou Wind and Rain Bridge
rows.summary: Jingou Wind and Rain Bridge is a covered timber bridge over a small stream at Jingou hamlet, Zengying village, in Wangdong town, Congjiang County. First built in 1884, it collapsed, was rebuilt in 1992 and repaired in 2007; it is about 34 m long with ten bays, a five-tier pavilion roof over its middle and timber cantilevers carrying the bridge house across a single stone-and-concrete pier. Chinese heritage records name it as the representative pavilion-style wind-and-rain bridge, and it has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Jiuzhou Ancient Town, Huangping
rows.summary: Jiuzhou is an old market town on the upper Wuyang River in Huangping county, long a trading and grain centre of eastern Guizhou. Its Ming and Qing buildings, a national heritage unit, include old houses on West Upper Street, the Renshou Palace, a Jiangxi guildhall built in 1786 with an opera stage, a Tianhou (Mazu) temple and a Catholic church. The Fuzhong Bridge, first built under the Ming, is a stone arch bridge of about 68 m and the largest ancient stone arch bridge in the county.

rows.name: Lanmenggu Blueberry Valley
rows.summary: Lanmenggu is a blueberry-growing park in Longshan town, Majiang, one of two blueberry parks (with the nearby Wukaping park) in the county's blueberry tourism area. Majiang began planting blueberries in 1999 and is now one of China's largest blueberry-growing counties. Visitors walk among the plantations and, in the picking season from about June to August, can pick berries; the park also offers jam-making and wine-making.

rows.name: Long'ao River Scenic Area
rows.summary: Long'ao River is a river valley in the north-west of Cengong county whose tourist stretch runs about 16.5 km, with gorges, waterfalls, caves and farmland. Boat trips run along the gorge from Aimenguan, a Ming-dynasty stone mountain gateway. Nearby are Majiazhai, a village of courtyard houses with carved stone flag-bases and old lanes, where people still live and farm, and the former command post of a Red Army corps.

rows.name: Longli Ancient Town
rows.summary: Longli is a walled garrison town founded under the Ming in the late 14th century, when soldiers and their families from Jiangnan and Jiangxi were settled here. It keeps its city gates, sections of wall, cobbled lanes and dozens of old houses and clan halls, and many residents are descended from the garrison and still perform customs such as the painted-face dragon dance and Han opera at the New Year. Its Ming and Qing buildings are a national protected group, and the village is a National Famous Historic and Cultural Village.

rows.name: Lower Wuyang River, Zhenyuan
rows.summary: The lower Wuyang River runs from Gaobei Lake near Shibing down to Zhenyuan, within the Wuyang River national scenic area. This section is known for its gorges, notably Zhuge Gorge and Longwang Gorge and the Peacock Screen rock.

rows.name: Qiaojie Old Street, Liping
rows.summary: Qiaojie, literally 'upturned street', is an old street about 1 km long in the centre of Liping, named because its middle dips and both ends rise like a carrying pole. It is lined with Ming and Qing brick houses with fire-break walls and old guildhalls, and today holds craft and snack shops. The Liping Conference site, a Qing-dynasty merchant's courtyard house where the Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party met in December 1934 during the Long March, stands in the street area beside a memorial hall; on 18 December the meeting decided to change the planned route towards the interior of Guizhou.

rows.name: Qinglongdong Ancient Architectural Complex
rows.summary: Qinglongdong (Qinglong Cave) is a group of Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian buildings built into a cliff of Zhonghe Mountain above the Wuyang River at the eastern end of Zhenyuan's old town, begun in 1388 and taking its present form by the early Qing. Its roughly 40 buildings include the cave temple itself, the former Ziyang academy, the Zhongyuan Buddhist hall high on the cliff, Wanshou Palace, a three-courtyard hall with an opera stage, and the seven-arch Zhusheng Bridge, topped by a three-storey pavilion, which carries the old post road across the river. Heritage records describe it as a blend of south-western minority and central Chinese Han building traditions, and it has been a national protected site since 1988.

rows.name: Sanmentang Village
rows.summary: Sanmentang is a Dong village on the Qingshui River, close to the Hunan border, that was long a timber-trading port. Its protected buildings, listed as Qing to Republican in date, include two ancestral halls, the Wang clan's Taiyuan Hall (rebuilt in 1908) and the Liu clan hall, with courtyard houses, wells, stone bridges, stone tablets and old trees around them. The group has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Shanmu River, Shibing
rows.summary: Shanmu River is a clear mountain river in the Shibing karst World Heritage area, inside the Wuyang River national scenic area, and one of the three main scenic areas of Shibing Karst. It is best known for rafting: a course of about 9 km through a forested gorge with a mix of rapids and calm stretches, plus a section of about 2 km lit for evening drifts in summer. The water is described as meeting mineral-water standards.

rows.name: Shidong Miao Town
rows.summary: Shidong is a Miao market town on the middle Qingshui River, long a meeting place for the villages around it and a main venue for two festivals on China's national intangible-heritage list. The Sisters' Festival, on the 15th day of the third lunar month, centres on young women in silver headdresses and embroidered costume; the dragon-canoe festival, on the 24th to 27th of the fifth lunar month, features races between canoes made of three joined fir trunks with paddlers standing. The dates follow the lunar calendar, so check them before going.

rows.name: Shudong Single-Pillar Drum Tower
rows.summary: The Shudong drum tower stands in the middle of the lower hamlet of Shudong village, Yandong town, Liping County, and is known as the single-pillar drum tower (it is also called the fir-tree tower) because its frame is built around one pillar running the full height of the tower. The present square, seven-tier tower, about 15.6 m high, was rebuilt in 1922 on an older design, local tradition dating the original to 1636, and heritage records say it is the only Dong drum tower built with this central-pillar structure. Records also praise it as the ancestor of drum towers, and it has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Upper Langde Miao Village
rows.summary: Upper Langde (Langde Shangzhai) is a Miao village of more than 100 households in Langde town, Leishan, set against a hillside and facing a stream, with the first houses dating from the late Yuan or early Ming. Its two- and three-storey timber stilt houses stand around a bronze-drum plaza used for gatherings and dances, and a 40 m wind-and-rain bridge crosses the stream in front. The buildings are a national protected group (2001); a village museum was set up here in 1986, and it was among the first Miao villages opened to visitors.

rows.name: Xiasi Ancient Town
rows.summary: Xiasi is an old river town on the Qingshui River in Kaili, once a post station on a Tea-Horse trade route, and it still has a waterfront of old landing stages. The streets are lined with whitewashed walls and grey-tiled houses, and visitors can try craft workshops such as batik, tie-dye, lacquered fans and sachet-making.

rows.name: Yanmen Zhangguansi Walled Town
rows.summary: Yanmen is a small walled stone town on the north bank of the Qingshui River in Gulong town, Huangping County, built as the seat of a hereditary native chieftain (zhangguansi) under the Ming and Qing. The office was set up in 1470 and raised to zhangguansi rank in 1658, held by the He family, and the stone wall, completed in 1741, ran about 1.6 km round and 3.3 m high, with gates on three sides, three gun platforms on the hill side and two river gates. The timber buildings inside have long since collapsed, the south gate is gone and 107 m of wall was taken down for stone in 1972, but most of the circuit survives, and it has been a national protected site since 2013.

rows.name: Yuntai Mountain, Shibing
rows.summary: Yuntai Mountain, about 13 km north of Shibing, is the best-known part of Shibing Karst, inscribed in 2014 as part of the South China Karst World Heritage property. The landscape is dolomite karst of peaks and gorges, often wrapped in cloud, with walking routes between a number of viewpoints. The mountain was a Buddhist site some 600 years ago, and old temple buildings and cliff inscriptions survive.

rows.name: Zai'e Drum Tower
rows.summary: Zai'e Drum Tower stands in the Dong hamlet of Zai'e, part of Gaoqian village in Xiajiang town, Congjiang County. Its origins are uncertain and local tradition places it in the Yongzheng reign (1723–35); the present octagonal tower of thirteen tiers of eaves was rebuilt in 1986 and repaired in 2004, and has a stone-paved floor, a fire pit and a wooden oil press kept inside. It is a national protected site (seventh batch, 2013) and lies a few hundred metres from Gaoqian Drum Tower.

rows.name: Zengchong Drum Tower
rows.summary: Zengchong Drum Tower stands at the centre of the Dong village of Zengchong in Wangdong town, Congjiang County, and dates from the early Qing dynasty, with stone tablets beside it, the earliest dated 1672. It is a timber tower of thirteen tiers of eaves under an octagonal pyramid roof, about 21 m high including its finial, with a fire pit in the middle of the ground floor and a long hide drum hung on the fifth floor. A 2008 article on China's intangible-heritage website describes it as the earliest and largest of Guizhou's more than 400 Dong drum towers, and it has been a national protected site since 1988.

rows.name: Zhenyuan Ancient Town
rows.summary: Zhenyuan sits on an S-shaped bend of the Wuyang River, which divides the old prefectural city on the north bank from the old garrison city on the south bank, both built under the Ming. Once a major staging post on the route from central China to Yunnan and Guizhou, the town keeps Ming and Qing houses, guildhalls, temples, stone-paved lanes and riverside docks, sections of the Ming city walls and the Tianhou (Mazu) Palace, a Qing temple rebuilt in the 1870s with funds from Fujian merchants; boats run on the river, including in the evening. The best-known sight is the Qinglong Cave complex, a group of Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian buildings begun in 1388 and built against a cliff above the river.

rows.name: Caotang Old Town and Houchang Conference Site
rows.name_zh: 草塘千年古邑（猴场会议旧址）
rows.summary: Houchang, also called Caotang, is an old town in Weng'an developed as a tourism area; the prefecture lists some thirty sights there, including an opera tower, the former Qishan Academy and a jinshi (scholar) tower. It is best known for the Houchang Conference, a Communist Party Politburo meeting held here on 31 December 1934 and 1 January 1935 during the Long March. The courtyard where it met is preserved, with a memorial hall beside it, and the site has been a national protected site since 2019.

rows.name: Duyun Tea Culture and Film Town
rows.summary: A tea-themed and film-set area in Duyun's eastern development zone which the city's tourism list describes as made up of the Qin-Han Film City, the China Tea Culture Expo Park and a Republic-era themed town. The Expo Park's gate hall, pagodas and pavilions are modelled on the Chinese pavilion at the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition and house tea trading, a tea culture centre and a display of objects. The film sets are modern constructions, not historic buildings, and have hosted many television productions.

rows.name: Fuquan Ancient City and City Wall
rows.summary: The old walled town of Fuquan, whose Ming-dynasty city wall, begun in 1391 as an earth wall and rebuilt in stone about ten years later, ran for roughly 4.8 km with four gates. Where the wall crossed a river it was built as a stone arch bridge with an iron sluice, so the town could keep its water supply under siege. The scenic area, planned at 3.88 sq km, also lists the Confucian temple, the Xiongzhen gate tower, a wetland park and a Zhang Sanfeng-themed museum.

rows.name: Gejing Bridge, Fuquan
rows.summary: A three-arch stone bridge across the Maha river, begun in 1618 and finished after about thirty years, paid for with donations raised by a local man, Ge Jing. It is 52.7 m long and 23 m high, with pointed arches, and a Qing-dynasty pavilion, the Sanyuan Pavilion of 1670, stands at the north end.

rows.name: Haohuahong Village, Huishui
rows.summary: A rural tourism area of about 5 sq km beside the Lianjiang river in Huishui, where Buyei people make up about 96% of residents. The prefecture presents it as a showcase for rural tourism combining Buyei culture, farming experiences and agricultural sightseeing, and the county's 2026 holiday report describes a flower garden, a sand-beach area and water-play attractions. Haohuahong is also the name of a Buyei mountain-song style popular around Huishui.

rows.name: Hongshui River Scenic Area, Luodian
rows.summary: A purpose-built riverside leisure area on a reservoir of the Hongshui River at Hongshuihe town, on Guizhou's southern border with Guangxi, with a floating walkway of about 5 km as its centrepiece. Around it are a floating swimming pool and water park, tropical and palm plant gardens, a night-lit flower park on a peninsula and a seven-storey viewing tower; the prefecture's page puts a full visit at about two hours. It is aimed at families and water-sports visitors and promoted as a place for a warm-winter break.

rows.name: Jinhai Xueshan, Guiding
rows.summary: A rural tourism area of about 19 sq km in Panjiang town, made up of 14 villages where about 95% of residents are Buyei. Its name, 'golden sea, snow mountain', describes the spring sight of white plum blossom on the hillsides against yellow rapeseed fields beside the Wengcheng river. Attractions include a flower valley and, according to the county's 2026 reports, an early-cherry garden and a family area with a rice-field mini train and a Ferris wheel.

rows.name: Oil-Painting Grassland, Longli
rows.summary: A leisure park on a high mountain plateau in Longli, with grassland of around a thousand mu (about 67 hectares) and, in season, flower fields that include white azaleas. A cable car links the foot of the hill with the plateau, where attractions include a glass bridge, a zip line, grass-skiing, a camping area and a run of nearly 4 km on non-powered scooters back down; the lower area has a commercial street in Miao and Buyei architectural styles. It suits families on a day out from Guiyang.

rows.name: Pingtang Sky Bridge
rows.summary: A highway service area turned destination beside Pingtang Bridge, a three-pylon cable-stayed bridge 2,135 m long whose tallest pylon is 332 m high, opened on 30 December 2019 across the Caodu river gorge. The service area, open to visitors since October 2020, has viewing platforms for the bridge and gorge, a bridge museum, an astronomy area, a cliff-top hotel and a campsite.

rows.name: Shanmu Lake Park, Duyun
rows.summary: The central park at Shanmu Lake, a municipal park of about 80 hectares in Duyun's eastern new town, in the core of the Duyun Economic Development Zone. The prefecture describes it as a general public park combining green space, culture, recreation and fitness facilities. It is a local recreation space, so it suits a short walk rather than a full visit.

rows.name: Shenquan Valley, Changshun
rows.summary: Shenquan Valley is a riverside leisure area of about 8.8 km along the Wuma river in Changshun, running from the Weiyuan tidal spring to the Qinglong pool. Its signature sight is the 'tidal well' (chaojing), a spring whose water surges out and falls back irregularly, from two or three to seven or eight times a day according to the prefecture, each surge lasting five to ten minutes. The county reports that a hotel, campsites, off-road go-karts and children's attractions have been added in recent years.

rows.name: Tiandong Scenic Area, Dushan
rows.summary: A themed leisure park in Jichang town, Dushan, built around Tiandong, a limestone cave where coloured lights pick out the stalactites, and Duxiu peak, which visitors can climb for views over the surrounding area. The grounds also hold gardens, lakes and a Buyei-style village under a 'heavenly court' theme, and the park has hosted music festivals. It suits a short family stop rather than a long visit.

rows.name: Wushan Gorge, Shuanglong Town
rows.summary: A gorge leisure area at Shuanglong in Longli, between two reservoirs, with rock paintings on its cliffs and a newly built courtyard-style town beside it. Attractions listed by the county include a cliff-side glass walkway, a suspension bridge, a via ferrata route and a water park. It is aimed at families and active day-trippers from Guiyang.

rows.name: Yaoshan Ancient Village, Libo
rows.summary: A village area of about 3.6 sq km in Yaoshan Yao township, described by the prefecture as a main settlement of the Baiku ('white-trousers') Yao, a name from the knee-length white trousers men traditionally wear. Many houses are mud-walled with thatched roofs, a cluster of granaries stands among them, and visitors can see a village-history museum and craft workshops and watch staged performances in the evenings. The Libo Yao monkey-drum dance, a funeral and ancestral-rite dance of the Baiku Yao, has been on China's national intangible-heritage list since 2008 and is also performed for visitors.

rows.name: 24-Switchback Road
rows.summary: A winding mountain road built in 1936 on the old Guizhou–Yunnan highway, climbing about 250 m in 24 hairpin bends over four kilometres. It became a symbol of US support for China in the Second World War after American army engineers reworked it in 1943, is part of what is called the Stilwell Road, and is a national-level protected monument; English-language sources also call it the 24-zig or the 24-bend road. The scenic area around it also has a viewing platform and exhibition hall, built in 2016 and run separately from the road itself.

rows.name: Amei Qituo Town
rows.summary: A hillside town built to rehouse the whole of Sanbao Yi township on the edge of Qinglong county town, named after Amei Qituo, a Yi bridal dance on China's national intangible cultural heritage list that is often called the Eastern tap dance. It has a dance culture hall, a craft street with embroidery and batik shops, Miao and Yi culture squares, a pagoda and guesthouses in Yi-style buildings, and in the evening visitors are invited to join the dancing on Jinmen Square. It is a modern resettlement town rather than a historic village, and Yi and Miao culture is presented there for visitors.

rows.name: Beipan River Canyon, Zhenfeng
rows.summary: A U-shaped canyon of the Beipan River in Zhenfeng, about 94 km long within the county, with karst peaks, caves and waterfalls along a reservoir created by the Dongqing dam; the area is part of the Beipan River National Wetland Park. The main way to see it is a boat trip upstream from the dam area, about two hours there and back to the Xiaohuajiang iron-chain bridge, and the county also points to rock paintings, cliff inscriptions and old Tea-Horse Road paths along the gorge. It is billed locally as Guizhou's little Three Gorges.

rows.name: Fangmaping Grassland
rows.summary: A highland grassland of about 21,000 mu at an average height of 1,630 m on the northern edge of Xingren, nicknamed Gaoyuan Saiwai, the plateau frontier. Besides the open pasture there are karst sinkholes, cliffs and a plateau lake, with flower fields in season and activities such as grass-sliding, kite flying, camping and horse riding. It suits families and outdoor-minded visitors, and hosts camping and kite-flying events.

rows.name: Guizhou Chun Leisure Park
rows.summary: A leisure park of about 2,400 mu in the urban area of Xingyi, named after the Guizhou Chun baijiu brand and described in provincial tourism promotion as one of 14 liquor-and-tourism scenic areas in Guizhou. It has cherry and plum woods, flower fields, a covered wind-and-rain bridge beside a waterfall, a children's amusement area, an adventure playground, ziplines, boating, a mushroom-themed lodge hotel and an open-air beer garden. It is aimed at families and short visits, and a riverside path of about 21 km, with electric shuttles, now links it to Wanfenglin.

rows.name: Liu Family Manor, Xingyi
rows.summary: A walled family compound of about 13 courtyard houses on roughly 70 mu at Xiawutun, added to over four generations of the Liu family in a mix of Chinese and Western styles. It was the home of Liu Xianshi, a leading figure in Guizhou politics and military governor in the early Republic, and of his brother Liu Xianqian. The surviving buildings include a loyalty shrine, a flower hall, a study, a family temple and a parade ground, together with part of the wall, a blockhouse and a French-style building.

rows.name: Lutun Archways and Old Town
rows.summary: Lutun is a Ming-era military settlement in the Yilong New Area east of Xingyi, where three Qing stone memorial archways dated 1839 to 1846 still stand in the old streets, two honouring people who reached 100 and one a woman praised for chastity and filial devotion; the group is a national-level protected monument. The old town lies inside the Yilong Mountain Tourism, Sport and Leisure Expo Park, the 4A scenic area of about 1,000 mu that also has a convention centre and a baseball and softball park. It is a short stop, mainly for those curious about the fortified-settlement towns of Guizhou.

rows.name: Maling River Canyon
rows.summary: A fissure gorge cut by the Maling River just north-east of Xingyi, more than 70 km long and up to a few hundred metres deep, with waterfalls pouring from its walls and lime-rich deposits hanging from the cliffs. The core section, the Tianxing Gallery, is the part most visitors see, and UNESCO notes more than 100 cascades after heavy rain. It is a national-level scenic area and part of the Xingyi UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2024.

rows.name: Pu'an Tea Culture Scenic Area
rows.name_zh: 普安茶文化生态旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Pǔ'ān Chá Wénhuà Shēngtài Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: A tea-tourism area at Chayuan, east of Pu'an town, built around local claims that the region is an origin of tea: the county dates a fossilised tea seed found nearby in 1980 to more than two million years ago, and says more than 20,000 ancient wild tea trees survive in Pu'an. The Buyei Tea Source Town at its centre has a tea-culture park, a Shennong shrine, a pavilion for Funiang, whom local tradition names as the Buyei tea ancestor, and a tea-bowl-shaped exhibition hall, while the surrounding hills have tea plantations, a mountain-bike course and guesthouses. It suits visitors who want to see tea country and try picking or brewing.

rows.name: Sanchahe Lake, Zhenfeng
rows.summary: A reservoir lake in Zhexiang town, north of Zhenfeng, named for the three rivers that meet here and developed as a lakeside leisure area of roughly 2,100 mu. It has a camping ground and RV park, lakeside hotels, a bridge, cliff inscriptions of the character for tiger, a former manor house and the Buyei village of Nakong. It suits families and camping weekends.

rows.name: Shuangyufeng Twin Peaks
rows.summary: Two rounded karst peaks rising about 260 m above their surroundings, which the local Buyei call the Holy Mother Peaks, on the road from Zhenfeng towards Guiyang; many local pages still use the older name Shuangrufeng. The scenic area adds a small stone forest, a lake, a Buyei village and a heritage showcase for local costume, blacksmithing and traditional pottery. It is a short visit for the views and the crafts, close to Sanchahe Lake.

rows.name: Tomb of the Eighteen Scholars, Anlong
rows.summary: The tombs and memorial shrine of eighteen Southern Ming court officials killed in 1654, after they objected to the domination of the court at Anlong by Sun Kewang, leader of the Daxi army. The Yongli Emperor, the last Ming claimant, had based his court at Anlong from 1652. The site lies at the foot of Tianbang Hill and has many cliff inscriptions left by later visitors; nearby, a rebuilt Southern Ming palace houses a museum on the period.

rows.name: Wanfeng Lake
rows.summary: A large reservoir on the Nanpan River where Guizhou, Yunnan and Guangxi meet, formed by the Tianshengqiao-I dam and named for the many karst peaks around it. The prefecture describes a surface of about 176 square kilometres with dozens of islands, peninsulas and bays, and visitors come for boat trips, lakeside fishing and views. The 4A scenic area covers nine lakeside spots on the Xingyi shore, with a visitor centre, a fishing service centre and boat services.

rows.name: Wanfenglin Peak Forest
rows.summary: Wanfenglin is a plain of cone-shaped karst peaks south of Xingyi; UNESCO's geopark profile counts more than 20,000 of them. Roads and footpaths wind between the peaks past farmland and Buyei villages, and the area has one of Guizhou's larger clusters of homestays. It lies within the Xingyi UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2024, and was rated a 5A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Xingyi Geopark Museum
rows.name_zh: 兴义国家地质公园博物馆
rows.summary: A geopark museum in Wusha, west of Xingyi, devoted to the Middle Triassic marine reptiles and fishes of the Xingyi fauna, above all the small reptile Keichousaurus, known as the Guizhou dragon. It has two buildings, the museum itself with six exhibition halls and a hall that preserves fossil beds in place, and offers hands-on activities such as fossil preparation, aimed at school-age visitors. UNESCO dates the fauna to roughly 242 to 237 million years ago, and it is one of the features of the Xingyi UNESCO Global Geopark, designated in 2024.

rows.name: Zhaoti Embankment and Lotus Wetland
rows.summary: A lotus-filled wetland on the north-eastern edge of the old town of Anlong, built around a stone embankment, a provincial-level protected monument, that a local garrison officer raised in 1694 to hold back floodwater. More than 5,000 mu of lotus are grown here, and in midsummer the flowers, a curving viewing bridge and pavilions draw visitors to what the prefecture describes as the largest lotus-viewing spot on the Guizhou plateau. Egrets, herons and moorhens are among the waterbirds recorded in the wetland.

rows.name: Zhenfeng Ancient Town
rows.summary: A restored old quarter at the foot of Feng Hill on the east side of Zhenfeng, once the Buyei market settlement of Mingu, with Ming and Qing streets, courtyard houses, the Wenchang Palace and the former guild halls of merchants from Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong and Guangxi. The county says repair and opening to visitors began in 2015, while the scenic area as a whole was built from 2017 and opened in 2018, so part of what visitors see is new construction in old style. It is best for an evening stroll when the streets are lit.

rows.name: Daming Border City
rows.summary: A riverside attraction on the Jinjiang river in Tongren, built in the style of a Ming-dynasty frontier town and themed on the Ming court bringing the local Sizhou and Sinan chiefdoms under its rule. It is a modern, artificial landscape rather than a historic site, and a scenic-area upgrade project was listed among Tongren investment projects in 2023.

rows.name: East Guizhou Special District Revolutionary Committee Site
rows.name_zh: 黔东特区革命委员会旧址
rows.summary: A brick-and-timber meeting hall of about 400 square metres at Tudiwan in Qiaojia town, Yanhe county, where delegates from Yanhe, Yinjiang and Dejiang counties and Red Army representatives founded the East Guizhou Special District Revolutionary Committee on 21–22 July 1934. It was listed as a national heritage unit in 2006, together with related sites in Dejiang and Yinjiang counties. The building faces east and carries a name plaque written by Liao Hansheng, who served as political commissar of the Ninth Division of the Red Army's Third Army.

rows.name: Jiufeng Agricultural Expo Park
rows.summary: A farm-tourism park in Wanshan district that opened in 2015, built around large greenhouses where more than a hundred kinds of unusual fruit and vegetables are grown and visitors can pick seasonal produce. It also has flower and marine-science exhibition halls, holiday villas and a hotel, and it takes school study groups. It suits families and anyone curious about modern farming.

rows.name: Lizhi Gorge
rows.summary: Lizhi Gorge is part of the Wujiang Gorge scenic area in Yanhe Tujia Autonomous County, where the Wujiang river runs between steep cliffs. Visitors see it from a boat, passing cliff formations that have been given names such as Beauty Peak, Tianmen Stone and Straw Hat Rock.

rows.name: Loushang Village Ancient Buildings
rows.summary: A hillside village in Guorong township, beside the Fodingshan nature reserve, whose buildings include the Zitong Palace temple, an opera stage, the Tianfu well and lanes of courtyard houses, most of them late Qing. Building began in the Wanli reign of the Ming; the temple's main hall was rebuilt in 1867 and its rear hall in 1882 after damage in 1861, and the opera stage dates from 1916 and the well from 1938.

rows.name: Miaowangcheng (Miao King's City)
rows.summary: A Miao fortified village in Songtao Miao Autonomous County, said to date from the early Ming dynasty, when it was the seat of a local Miao chiefdom. Stone-walled lanes with eleven gateways, stilted timber houses and a stream run through a steep-sided valley, and local authorities put its history at more than 600 years.

rows.name: Shiqian Prefectural Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Shiqian's prefectural Confucian temple was founded in 1413, the year Guizhou was made a province and Shiqian a prefecture, and was repaired in the 18th and 19th centuries. The compound rises in three courtyards from the gate and pond to the Dacheng Hall, whose column bases and terrace are carved with dragons and carp-leaping-the-dragon-gate reliefs. In January 1936 the Red Army ran a school here after taking the town.

rows.name: Sinan Stone Forest
rows.summary: A field of karst limestone pinnacles beside the Silin reservoir on the Wujiang river in Changba town, covering roughly 5 square kilometres. The rock forms range from needles and swords to towers, pillars and castle-like masses, and some are named after animals, such as the twelve zodiac stones.
