It has been a national geopark since 2009, with a geology museum and walking trails, and the 4A listing also covers a hot-spring site in Sinan town.

rows.name: Sitang Ancient Buildings, Sinan
rows.summary: A group of Ming and Qing buildings along Anhua Street in Sinan county town, listed as a national heritage unit in 2006. It includes the prefectural Confucian temple (first built in 1486), Wanshou Palace with its opera stage, Chuanzhu Palace, the Wangye temple and a Qing salt merchant's house with its salt store, alongside old houses and lanes.

rows.name: Wanshou Palace, Shiqian
rows.summary: A temple compound in Shiqian old town whose core, Wanshou Palace, was built in 1588 under the Ming and repeatedly repaired in the Qing; four neighbouring temples (Yu the Great, Zhonglie, the Jade Emperor and Heishen) complete the five groups. Its brick-built memorial-arch gateway, bell and drum towers and opera stage are decorated with brick carvings and patterned tiles.

rows.name: Wucai Yangshanhe Gorge
rows.summary: A karst gorge about 2.5 km long and 100–400 m deep in Dejiang county, opened to visitors in 2020, with a sinkhole, natural bridge, caves, stone forest and underground river. Its centrepiece is Nuoxian Cave, where the underground stream shows several colours and a fried-egg-shaped mineral formation is the best-known curiosity. A glass suspension bridge, a viewing platform and an inclined cable car take visitors across and down into the gorge.

rows.name: Yamugou Valley
rows.summary: A forested stream valley fed from Fanjingshan in Zhaibao village, Taiping town, with small waterfalls and clear rock pools. Xinhua reports forest cover above 97 per cent and an average temperature of about 17°C. It is a low-key add-on for visitors staying near the Jiangkou entrance to Fanjingshan.

rows.name: Yelang Ancient Spring Hot Springs
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort at the edge of Shiqian county town, in a county known as a hot-spring homeland: about twenty spring sites with 36 outlets have been surveyed there. The springs have been used for more than 400 years, and the resort has more than 130 bathing pools of different kinds as well as a water park with a wave pool. A cable car links it with the cliff-top Xianren Street attractions, so a visit can combine a mountain outing with a soak.

rows.name: Yunshe Village
rows.summary: A Tujia village at the foot of Fanjingshan on the Taiping River, with stone-paved lanes and old timber houses, most of them dating from the Ming and Qing periods. Visitors can see hand-papermaking and Tujia weaving demonstrations, a small museum on Tujia wedding customs and the clear Shenlong Pool. It makes an easy stop before or after climbing Fanjingshan.

rows.name: Yuping Dong Folk Village Park
rows.summary: A purpose-built tourist complex in Tianping town that presents Dong culture in newly built timber architecture, including a drum tower and some thirty Dong-style houses. Inside are small museums of Dong embroidery and bamboo flutes, a mock 1960s-70s village market street, a lotus-pond wetland park, and an outlet shopping street across the road. It was built from the late 2010s, so the buildings are modern, but it gives an easy introduction to Dong music, crafts and food.

rows.name: Zhaiying Ancient Town, Songtao
rows.summary: Zhaiying was a busy river-trading town in the Ming and Qing periods, nicknamed 'Little Nanjing', and its old core survives as a national heritage group of houses, shops, guildhalls, town walls and a wharf. Partition walls, hidden passages and loopholes show that the buildings were also designed for defence, and the architecture mixes Han and Miao features, with ox-horn door lintels and fish-bone pebble patterns on guildhall walls.

rows.name: Zhongnanmen Old Town, Tongren
rows.summary: Tongren's old quarter lies on a peninsula with the Jinjiang river on three sides, and its restored courtyard houses, lanes and wharf from the Ming to Republican periods now host evening events such as street concerts and open-air films. Several monuments in and around the old city make up the national heritage unit known as the Dongshan ancient buildings, including Dongshan Temple on its hill (first built in 1516), Chuanzhu Palace (founded in 1375, with an opera stage) and the courtyard home of Zhou Yiqun, an early Communist Party figure. The lanes are most lively in the evening.

rows.name: Zhusha Ancient Town (Wanshan Mercury Mine)
rows.summary: Wanshan was China's largest cinnabar and mercury producer, mined for more than 2,000 years until the mines closed in 2001, and the remains are a national heritage unit and a national mine park. Zhusha Ancient Town is the converted mining settlement, with restored workers' streets, shops and canteen from the mining days, old tunnels where cinnabar can still be seen in the rock, and a glass walkway along a gorge. It suits anyone interested in industrial heritage and how it is reused.

rows.name: Bing'an Ancient Town
rows.summary: Bing'an is an old river-trading town on the Chishui River, once a staging post for the boats that carried Sichuan salt into Guizhou, with timber stilt houses built along the steep riverbank, a stone town gate, a Qing-era towpath and an old bridge. In January 1935 units of the Red Army's First Army Corps camped here during the Long March, ahead of the first crossing of the Chishui, and the town has a First Army Corps exhibition hall and a memorial hall for General Geng Biao. It was named a Chinese Traditional Village in 2012 and suits visitors who enjoy historic riverside architecture.

rows.name: China Danxia Valley, Xishui
rows.summary: A forested river valley with red Danxia sandstone walls in Sancha River town, Xishui County. Its best-known sight is the Wangxiantai grotto, a rock-cut complex carved into the cliff for the Qing-dynasty businessman Yuan Jindao and described in local media as Guizhou's finest grotto. Streams and forest against the red rock make up the rest of the scenery.

rows.name: China Liquor Culture City, Maotai
rows.summary: The visitor complex of the Moutai distillery in Maotai town, the home of Moutai baijiu on the Chishui River. It includes a museum of famous Chinese liquors and displays introducing Moutai's history and culture.

rows.name: Chishui Danxia
rows.summary: Chishui is one of the six components of the "China Danxia" World Heritage site (inscribed 2010), a landscape of red sandstone cliffs, forested gorges and waterfalls around Chishui city. The main stop is the Great Waterfall (Shizhangdong), about 76 m high and 80 m wide and described as the largest waterfall on danxia terrain in China; the area is also known for dense bamboo forest and for tree ferns, a plant group that survives from the Jurassic. Plan about a day for the main sights, with the bamboo forest and the Sidonggou falls nearby.

rows.name: Feilongzhai, Yuqing
rows.summary: A scenic area on the shore of Feilong Lake, a reservoir on the Wujiang River in Yuqing County, presented as a Miao village with local folk culture. Its best-known feature is the Feilong Corridor, a 999 m promenade whose dragon motifs give the place its name. Nearby Langshuiwan, another part of the Feilong Lake area, offers boat trips and water sports.

rows.name: Former Site of Zhejiang University in Meitan
rows.summary: In 1940 Zhejiang University, evacuated during the war with Japan, moved to Meitan under its president Zhu Kezhen, with more than 700 staff and students, and taught here until 1946. Nine sites used by the university survive in Meitan town and nearby Yongxing town, including the former Confucian temple that served as its office and library, a Catholic church where professors lived, and a guild hall used as the graduate school. The temple, in the town centre, is close to the Giant Teapot park.

rows.name: Former Tianmenhe Hydropower Plant
rows.summary: A wartime hydropower station in Tongzi county, begun in 1941 and generating from April 1945, built to power the Nationalist-run 41st Arsenal, which had moved here from several provinces during the war with Japan. Its generator hall, control room and tailrace tunnel were cut into karst caves for concealment, two American-made generators from the 1940s remain in the hall, and a 1944 stone memorial tower to its builders and a set of inscribed tablets survive. It lies about 1 km from the dam that formed Xiaoxihu, the small lake where Zhang Xueliang was held, and suits visitors interested in industrial or wartime history.

rows.name: Four Crossings of the Chishui River Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial museum opened in 2007 in Tucheng town, telling the story of the Red Army's four crossings of the Chishui River between January and March 1935 during the Long March. Several of the crossings were made in what is now Xishui County, and the Red Army fought a heavy battle at Tucheng on 28 January 1935 before the first crossing. The hall is the main venue of a group of smaller museums in the old town, covering topics such as the women soldiers of the Red Army, the Red Army hospital and shipping on the Chishui River.

rows.name: Gouba Conference Site
rows.summary: Gouba is a village in Fengxiang town where the Red Army's headquarters stopped in March 1935 during the Long March. At a farm compound called Xinfangzi, Politburo meetings on 10-12 March debated whether to attack the town of Daguxinchang, and a three-man military command group of Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Wang Jiaxiang was set up. The meeting site is preserved, with an exhibition hall on the conference, and it suits visitors tracing the Long March around Zunyi.

rows.name: Hailongtun
rows.summary: The ruins of a mountain stronghold of the Yang family, the hereditary tusi (chiefs) of Bozhou, begun in 1257 under the Southern Song and destroyed when Ming forces took it in 1600. Cliffs guard it on every side, and stone gates such as the Feihu and Feilong passes and several kilometres of walls survive on Longyan mountain, enclosing about 1.6 sq km. It is one of the three Tusi Sites inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.

rows.name: Heart of the Tea Sea, Fenggang
rows.summary: A large tea-growing landscape in Tianba village, Yong'an town, Fenggang County, at about 1,000 m, where tea bushes grow in bands among pine and other trees. A cableway of about 780 m and a glass walkway give views over the plantations, which are the core of Fenggang's zinc- and selenium-rich tea. Spring tea-picking, farmstays and camping among the tea gardens are the other draws.

rows.name: Hongguoshu Scenic Area
rows.summary: Hongguoshu is a scenic area in Dalucao township, Suiyang county, that combines caves, a waterfall about 35 m high, forest and limestone rock formations, and is nicknamed the "geological museum of Guizhou" locally. Visitors can walk to the caves and falls, cross a glass suspension bridge and eat cave-style hot pot in a cave restaurant. It is one of ten A-level scenic areas in Suiyang county.

rows.name: Jiangxi Guild Hall, Fuxing
rows.summary: Built in 1831 by Jiangxi salt merchants in the old river port of Fuxing, this guild hall (also called Wanshou Palace) has a front hall, main hall, rear hall and side wings, and local authorities describe it as one of the largest and best-preserved guild halls in south-west China. It now houses the Chishui Danxia Stone Carving Art Museum, with danxia stone carvings, Han-dynasty stone coffins and sculptures, and Song-dynasty carvings and reliefs. Fuxing was a landing point on the trade that carried Sichuan salt into Guizhou, and the hall stands on the town's old street.

rows.name: Little West Lake, Tongzi
rows.summary: A reservoir lake beside Tongzi town, formed in the 1940s together with the Tianmenhe hydropower station, with wooded hills around it. General Zhang Xueliang, held under house arrest after the 1936 Xi'an Incident, was confined at Tianmen Cave by the lake from December 1944 until his transfer to Chongqing in 1946. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Loushan Pass
rows.summary: A steep gateway pass through the Daloushan range between Zunyi and Tongzi, long a strategic crossing between Guizhou and Sichuan. Red Army forces fought a battle here in late February 1935 on the way to retaking Zunyi, and Mao Zedong's poem 'Loushan Pass', written the same month, made the name widely known. The site has the pass gateway, battle remains on the surrounding peaks, a monument and a memorial exhibition hall.

rows.name: Manaoshan Fortified Camp
rows.summary: Manaoshan is a hill stronghold in Fenggang county, built between 1857 and 1860 by a local militia leader, Qian Qingyun, as a refuge for his community during the uprisings and unrest that swept northern Guizhou in the mid-19th century. Stone walls more than 5 m high wrap around seven hilltops, with 48 stone gates, gun platforms and loopholes, and a network of caves runs beneath them; the walls total more than 10 km. It is a surviving example of the region's defensive mountain camps and suits visitors interested in vernacular military architecture.

rows.name: Maotai Liquor Town
rows.summary: Maotai is the town on the Chishui River where Moutai baijiu is made: distilleries there date back to the early 19th century, and it became a river port in 1745 when Qing officials opened the Chishui to shipping. The tourist district is the renovated riverside old town, where visitors can walk the streets, taste local baijiu and see the town lit up at night. A memorial tower on the riverbank recalls the Red Army's crossing of the Chishui at Maotai in 1935.

rows.name: Meitan Giant Teapot Tea Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 天下第一壶茶文化博览园
rows.pinyin: Tiānxià Dìyī Hú Chá Wénhuà Bólǎnyuán
rows.summary: A tea-culture park in Meitan whose centrepiece is a teapot-shaped building 73.8 m high, certified in 2006 by a Shanghai record-keeping body as the world's largest teapot-shaped structure. Inside, the China Tea Ceremony Hall has galleries on tea in the Tang, Song, Ming and Qing dynasties, on minority tea customs, and on Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese tea traditions. It suits visitors interested in tea culture, and lies close to Meitan's wartime Zhejiang University site.

rows.name: Meitan Tea Sea Eco-Park
rows.summary: A rural tea-tourism area around Hetaoba village, about 10 km from Meitan county town, where tea plantations surround a village of Qianbei-style houses whose carved window lattices bear small teapot motifs, echoing the Giant Teapot in the county town. The county government describes a leisure area combining village houses, tea-culture experiences, local restaurants and water recreation. It is a different place from the large 'China Tea Sea' viewing area at Yongxing town, further north-east.

rows.name: Peach Blossom Spring Scenic Area, Zheng'an
rows.summary: A scenic area in Shiping township, Zheng'an County, themed on Tao Yuanming's classical essay about a hidden peach-blossom valley. Visitors pass through a natural karst cave into an open valley of fields and streams, billed as 'one mountain, two worlds', with boat trips on the water.

rows.name: Qingxi Gorge
rows.summary: Qingxi Gorge is a river gorge in Suiyang county, nicknamed a "jade belt" for the green of its water, and is sold as part of the Shierbeihou ("Twelve Behind") tourism area alongside Shuanghedong cave. Boats run on the water, where a 120-seat vessel was built in 2023, and a camping base has been added. It suits travellers who want a day on the water, combined with the cave in the same county.

rows.name: Shanping, Tongzi
rows.summary: A rural tourism area in Shanping village, Loushanguan subdistrict, south of Tongzi county town, developed as a farming-and-tourism demonstration project during China's poverty-alleviation campaign. Its flower fields were reported in 2016 as a sea of purple blooms, and the county lists Shanping among its main tourism sites.

rows.name: Shuanghedong Cave Network
rows.summary: Shuanghedong is a cave system in the dolomite hills of Suiyang county, explored to about 440 km, which Chinese sources describe as the longest cave in Asia and the third longest in the world. Part of it is open to visitors, with underground rivers and waterfalls, curled stone and gypsum flowers among its features and activities such as a cave via ferrata and cave concerts; the remains of more than 40 giant pandas have been found in the cave. It was added to China's World Heritage tentative list in 2025.

rows.name: Shuangmen Gorge
rows.summary: Shuangmen Gorge is a river-gorge scenic area in Fenghua town, Suiyang county, promoted as "China's Poetry Valley" and officially recognised as a national water-conservancy scenic area. Its theme is poetry culture, tied to Suiyang's long-standing image as a "poetry town". It suits travellers who want to combine it with other Suiyang sights such as Shuanghedong cave.

rows.name: Shuiyin River Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A river canyon in Mugua town in northern Tongzi County, where the Shuiyin River runs through a gorge with more than ten large waterfalls and dozens of smaller ones. Rafting down about 4 km of the river is the main activity and runs in the warmer months.

rows.name: Sidonggou Waterfalls
rows.summary: Sidonggou is a valley of stepped waterfalls in the red-sandstone hills near Chishui, with four main falls strung along a route of about 5 km. The falls are known as Water Curtain Cave, Moon Pool, Flying Frog Cliff and White Dragon Pool, each with a different shape. It suits walkers who want a waterfall day trip from Chishui city.

rows.name: Taiyangping Azalea Hills, Hongguan
rows.summary: A hilltop scenic area at about 1,500 m in Hongguan Miao ethnic township, in the west of Bozhou district, known for slopes of wild azaleas that bloom in spring; the township holds an azalea festival in May. A glass viewing platform looks out over Bozhou, Jinsha and Renhuai, and the area also has bungee and aerial-swing rides and guesthouses.

rows.name: Tomb of Deng Ping
rows.summary: Deng Ping, chief of staff of the Red Army's Third Army Corps, was killed in February 1935 during the second capture of Zunyi; his tomb, built in 1958–59 and moved in 1984, stands in the Red Army martyrs' cemetery on Red Army Hill. The cemetery also has a 30 m martyrs' monument, a wall of names of more than 3,000 soldiers who died in the Sichuan–Guizhou–Yunnan border area, and a small exhibition on those killed in the Zunyi fighting. It suits visitors combining the Zunyi Conference site with other Long March memorials in the city.

rows.name: Tucheng Old Town
rows.summary: A former trading port on the Chishui River, where the Red Army fought a heavy battle in January 1935 and made its first crossing of the river. Its old streets and ferry crossing hold a series of Long March sites, including former residences of Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Liu Bocheng, a Red Army salt store and several small museums, among them those of the women soldiers of the Red Army and of Chishui River shipping. The national heritage listing, the battle sites of the Four Crossings of the Chishui, also covers the Erlangtan and Maotai ferries and Loushan Pass; twelve of its sites are at Tucheng.

rows.name: Yang Family Tusi Tombs (Yang Can Tomb)
rows.summary: Tombs of the Yang family, the hereditary tusi (local chiefs) who ruled the Bozhou region around Zunyi for centuries. The best known is the tomb of Yang Can, a Southern Song official: a two-chambered stone tomb of the mid-13th century built from 496 sandstone slabs and carved with about 190 reliefs, said to be the richest in carving of the Song tombs known in south-west China. The national listing, widened in 2019, also covers the tomb of Yang Hui, a Ming-dynasty chief, which lies elsewhere in the Zunyi area.

rows.name: Yelang Liquor Valley
rows.summary: Yelang Liquor Valley is a baijiu-themed tourist area in Renhuai's famous-liquor industrial park, in the Maotai area of Zunyi. The Renhuai government describes hills and water around the site, village houses several hundred years old, and a blend of Yelang-culture themes with visitor experiences of traditional sauce-aroma baijiu making. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in December 2024.

rows.name: Yunmentun (Water Gate to Heaven), Sandu
rows.summary: A riverside scenic area at Sandu town in Zunyi's Xinpu New Area, covering about 8 sq km at the meeting point of three rivers. Its best-known sight is the Water Gate to Heaven, a natural karst gateway over the river described as about 80 m wide and 100 m high; visitors also tour the river gallery by boat and can see a rock fissure about 200 m long, the Great Rift.

rows.name: Zheng'an Guitar Culture Park
rows.summary: A guitar-making and visitor park in Zheng'an County, where local figures cited in People's Daily say about one in seven of the world's guitars is made. In the south area, a guitar plaza hosts band performances and there is a guitar-themed street and a guitar museum; in the north, visitors can watch guitars being made in the factories. The county also runs a summer music season and guitar festivals.

rows.name: Zunyi Conference Site
rows.summary: The former residence of a Guizhou army commander, a two-storey house of the early 1930s, where the Chinese Communist Party's Politburo held an enlarged meeting on 15–17 January 1935 during the Long March. The meeting reviewed the failure of the fifth encirclement campaign and is regarded in party history as the point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was established. It forms the core of the Zunyi Conference Memorial Museum, whose protected buildings also include the nearby house where Mao Zedong, Zhang Wentian and Wang Jiaxiang stayed and the former Red Army political department at the Yangliu Street Catholic church.

rows.name: Niangniangshan National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park in the highlands of Panzhou, managed by its own park office. It was named in 2020 as one of the first national forest-wellness bases, and visitors come for its wetland and upland scenery.

rows.name: Shuidong Xiangshe
rows.summary: A rural tourism complex in Kaiyang County run by a local tourism company, set among villages and hills north of Guiyang. It was named in 2020 as one of the first national forest-wellness bases.

rows.name: Cuiya 27 Degrees Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area in Meitan County, one of Guizhou's best-known tea districts, run by a local scenic-area operating company. It was named in 2020 as one of the first national forest-wellness bases.

rows.name: Taohuajiang, Meitan
rows.summary: A rural tourism area along the Taohuajiang river in Yuquan subdistrict of Meitan county, known for its spring peach blossom and a festival held there in March. Villages such as Xinshi serve as its visitor hubs. It was listed in 2017 among the first 13 national health-tourism demonstration bases.

rows.name: Beihai Wetland
rows.summary: Beihai is a protected wetland in a volcanic basin north of Tengchong. Much of its water is covered by floating mats of matted grass and roots, said to be up to about 2 m thick, which grew on volcanic ash and organic matter. Boardwalks lead across the marsh, and visitors can step out onto the springy grass rafts.

rows.name: Dongshan Grassland
rows.summary: Dongshan is an upland meadow on the hills east of Tengchong, a state pasture from 1983 that was badly overgrazed and has been restored since 2012. Its open grassy slopes give wide views west over the Tengchong basin.

rows.name: Gaoligong International Coffee Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 高黎贡国际精品咖啡文化园
rows.summary: A coffee-themed park in the Lujiang valley, Baoshan's main coffee-growing area below the eastern flank of the Gaoligong range, rated 4A in 2022. It combines coffee plantings with a coffee-culture exhibition centre, a visitor processing workshop where you can follow coffee from bean to cup, a café, guesthouses, tents and an RV campsite.

rows.name: Gaoligong Mountain Tea Expo Park
rows.summary: A tea-themed park in Qingshui township next to Tengchong airport, operating since 2013, with tea gardens holding a collection of more than 500 Chinese tea varieties and a tea-culture museum by the entrance. Visitors can pick, process and taste tea, and there is a tea-themed restaurant, a hotel and an RV camp.

rows.name: Guangzun Temple
rows.summary: Guangzun Temple, north-east of Baoshan, is a temple complex where Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian worship share one site. Its surviving halls, among them a Jade Emperor Pavilion and a Holy Mother Hall, date from the Qing dynasty and the Republican era. Local tradition holds that the temple began as the family temple of a Nanzhao king.

rows.name: Guoshang Cemetery
rows.summary: Guoshang Cemetery was completed in 1945 for soldiers of the Chinese Expeditionary Force's 20th Army Group who were killed retaking Tengchong from Japanese forces in 1944. On the small hill of Xiaotuanpo, 3,346 small headstones fan out around a memorial tower in sectors for each division, below a memorial shrine whose walls carry 9,618 names and a monument to Allied servicemen. The adjoining Western Yunnan Anti-Japanese War Museum, in a new building opened in 2013, covers the wider war in western Yunnan.

rows.name: Hanzhuang City Site
rows.summary: These are the rammed-earth walls of a town of the Eastern Han dynasty, linked to Yongchang commandery, which the Han set up in this area in AD 69. The rectangular enclosure measures about 370 by 315 m, with walls up to about 5 m high, and it is regarded as the best-preserved Han-era town site found in Yunnan. Once known as Zhugeying ('Zhuge's camp'), it lies beside Zhugeying village and is of most interest to those keen on early frontier history.

rows.name: Huitong Bridge
rows.summary: Huitong Bridge is a steel-cable suspension bridge over the Nu (Salween) River, finished in 1935 with funds raised by the overseas Chinese businessman Liang Jinshan and Chinese communities in Burma, and later the Burma Road's only crossing of the river. Chinese troops blew it up on 5 May 1942 to stop the Japanese advance, and it was repaired in August 1944 during the counter-offensive. Replaced in 1974 by a newer bridge 400 m downstream, it was restored to its original form in 2015.

rows.name: Jade Emperor Pavilion, Baoshan
rows.summary: The Yuhuang Ge is a Ming-dynasty pavilion dedicated to the Jade Emperor, the supreme deity of Chinese folk religion and Taoism. It stands on Baoxiu Road on the western side of central Baoshan, close to the foot of Taibao Mountain, whose forest park makes a natural pairing.

rows.name: Jiangdong Ginkgo Village
rows.summary: Jiangdong, in Gudong town north of Tengchong, is a cluster of four farming hamlets set among tens of thousands of ginkgo trees growing on fertile volcanic soil, more than a thousand of them over a century old. From mid-November to early December the leaves turn gold. The village was listed as a Chinese traditional village in 2013.

rows.name: Qihualing Flower Park
rows.summary: A flower and family leisure park at the foot of the Gaoligong range in Qushi township, developed by a property company as part of a holiday-housing project and rated 4A in 2020. Flower fields and a rose garden set around a chain of small lakes are mixed with rides such as a long slide, a zip line and swing bridges, a water play area and a small farm.

rows.name: Qinghua Lake Wetland Park
rows.summary: Qinghua Lake National Wetland Park spreads across the floor of the Baoshan basin on the east side of the city, taking in an East Lake and a West Lake, the Beimiao reservoir and the banks of the East River. The lakes are described as the last remnant of an ancient lake that once filled the basin, and the park makes an easy walk on the edge of the new town.

rows.name: Rhododendron King Ancient Wood Park
rows.summary: An exhibition park of about 5 ha in Tengchong's economic development zone that displays more than 300 pieces of ancient timber and tree roots, including yew, left uncarved and unpainted to show their natural colour, grain and shape. A second hall shows wooden furniture, tea tables and smaller crafts, with a workshop where visitors can try woodworking, and there is a wood-themed restaurant.

rows.name: Shanzhou Forest Farm
rows.summary: This forest farm on Daliangshan in Shidian county was planted from 1988 by Yang Shanzhou, a former Communist Party secretary of Baoshan prefecture, who after retiring led local people in reforesting the mountain. By the time he handed the farm to the state free of charge in 2009 it covered about 3,700 hectares. Visitors see the original shed headquarters, an exhibition room on his life, a stele garden and a memorial cemetery, set among the plantations he started.

rows.name: Simola Wa Village
rows.summary: Simola is the middle hamlet of Sanjia village in Qingshui township, a Wa settlement with a history of more than 500 years. Visitors walk through the village to its folk-culture square and a small museum of Wa culture, and in recent years villagers have opened farmhouse restaurants.

rows.name: Songshan Battlefield
rows.summary: Songshan, a mountain above the Nu (Salween) River, was held and heavily fortified by Japanese forces from 1942, cutting the Burma Road, until the Chinese Expeditionary Force took it in September 1944 after months of fighting. The battlefield park preserves bunkers, trenches, shell craters and the tunnel dug to blow up the main Japanese strongpoint, plus a cemetery for Chinese soldiers of the 103rd Division. The listed site also takes in Japanese wartime sites in Longling town, such as the former headquarters and the Dongjiagou 'comfort station', some now exhibition halls.

rows.name: Wenchang Palace, Qiluo
rows.summary: This temple complex in Xia Qiluo village honours Wenchang, the god of literature and examinations, and blends the layout of a Confucian temple with a Taoist shrine. Its main axis runs from the gate past a semicircular pool and the Lingxing gate to the Wenchang Hall, with further halls on parallel axes. First founded in the Ming Wanli reign, it lies a few kilometres south-east of Heshun and makes an easy addition to a visit there.

rows.name: Youdian River Park
rows.summary: A riverside park along the Youdian River through the centre of Changning county town, built as a river clean-up and wetland-restoration scheme and opened in 2017. It links a tea-themed park with a tea museum and teahouse, farmland and farming-experience plots, and restored wetlands around a lake, and is used for walking and cycling.

rows.name: Chuxiong Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Chuxiong's Confucian temple was founded in the Ming dynasty, and in the Qing the county and prefecture temples were combined on one site. The main Dacheng Hall, built in 1469, is a five-bay hall with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof whose beam frame still follows Ming practice. The Dacheng Gate, the Pan pool with its Sanyuan Bridge and the Zunjing library pavilion also survive.

rows.name: Chuxiong Prefecture Museum
rows.name_zh: 楚雄彝族自治州博物馆
rows.summary: Opened in July 1995, the prefecture museum in Chuxiong covers the archaeology, history and Yi culture of central Yunnan in eight main galleries, with fossils, bronzes and Yi costume among its strongest collections. Its best-known exhibits are the bronze drums excavated in 1975 from the Wanjiaba tombs on the edge of the city, some still blackened with soot from use as cooking vessels.

rows.name: Dayao White Pagoda
rows.summary: This solid brick pagoda on top of Baofa Hill, above Dayao county town, was first built in the Nanzhao period and has an unusual outline: a large oval crown swells above a narrow waist and an octagonal base, like the hammer used to strike a stone chime, which gives it its other name, Qingchui Pagoda. It stands 15.45 metres tall, and its bricks are moulded with incantations in Chinese and Sanskrit.

rows.name: Defeng Temple, Yao'an
rows.summary: Defeng Temple, beside Meige Square in Yao'an county town, is a Buddhist temple whose Ming-dynasty buildings are protected as a national monument. It is easily combined with a visit to Longhua Temple at nearby Guanglu.

rows.name: Guanglu Old Town and Longhua Temple
rows.summary: This scenic area covers the old centre of Guanglu, a small town north-west of Yao'an county seat, and Longhua Temple at the town's western edge. First a hermitage housing a reclining Buddha and enlarged in the Yuan dynasty, the temple was destroyed and rebuilt several times; the present buildings date from 1907. Its five-bay main hall contains a large Buddhist shrine canopy, one of the bigger surviving examples.

rows.name: Heijing Old Town
rows.summary: Heijing, on the Longchuan River, grew rich on its salt wells and was at its most prosperous in the Ming and Qing dynasties. The town keeps much of its Ming–Qing layout, with the Dalong Shrine, a Confucian temple, an old opera stage, the Wu family mansion, the Wuma Bridge across the river and a salt-mining museum. It is listed as a national historic and cultural town.

rows.name: Jinshan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A Ming–Qing-style commercial and residential quarter in Lufeng city, built from 2017 as part of a shantytown-redevelopment scheme and opened in 2019. Its stream, bridges, opera stage, courtyard inns, shops and restaurants are all new. The genuine stone Xingxiu Bridge, completed in 1832 and a nationally protected monument, stands next to it.

rows.name: Lion Mountain, Wuding
rows.summary: Lion Mountain, just west of Wuding town, has long been called the 'first mountain of the south-west'. Its Zhengxu Temple, founded in the Yuan dynasty, is linked by legend to the Ming Jianwen Emperor, who is said to have hidden here as a monk after losing his throne. A large peony garden, with over 120 varieties, has been planted in the scenic area.

rows.name: Lufeng World Dinosaur Valley
rows.summary: Lufeng has been known for Jurassic dinosaur fossils since 1938, when the first skeletons, including Lufengosaurus, were dug up in the area. In the Chuanjie basin south of the city, World Dinosaur Valley has a large fossil site hall displaying finds from the surrounding beds, among them the skull of Lishulong, an early Jurassic sauropodomorph described in 2024. The rest of the valley is given over to a dinosaur theme park and a hot-spring hotel.

rows.name: Shiyang Old Town
rows.summary: Shiyang, north-west of Dayao, is an old salt town, once the seat of the Baiyanjing salt administration, and has a salt-culture museum. Its Confucian temple, founded in 1368, moved to its present site in 1609 and rebuilt in 1879, keeps its Dacheng Gate, main hall and side halls, while most other buildings, including the Lingxing Gate, are modern reconstructions. The main hall holds a 2.3-metre bronze statue of Confucius cast in 1708, described as one of only two large bronze Confucius statues known to survive.

rows.name: Xingxiu and Fengyu Bridges
rows.summary: Xingxiu Bridge, in Xingxiu Park on the old course of the Xingxiu River in Lufeng city, is a seven-arch stone bridge 118.8 metres long, completed in 1832 after earlier bridges on the site had been washed away several times. Built of red sandstone bonded with lime and sticky-rice mortar, it carried the main caravan road to western Yunnan and has a memorial archway at its east end and a ten-pillar stone gateway at its west end. Fengyu Bridge, listed with it, stands about 1 km to the north.

rows.name: Yi People's Ancient Town
rows.summary: A Yi-style 'ancient town' newly built in Chuxiong city as a commercial, hotel and residential district, with an opera stage, squares, shops and restaurants. In the evenings locals and visitors join bonfire dancing in the squares; there is no old fabric, but it is a lively place to eat and see Yi music and dance.

rows.name: Yi Ten-Month Solar Calendar Park
rows.summary: A modern cultural park in Chuxiong's high-tech zone that presents the Yi people's traditional ten-month solar calendar. Its centrepiece is a three-tiered circular platform, used as an altar and observation terrace, topped by ten totem pillars and faced with about 40 relief panels of Yi myths and folk tales, and an exhibition hall explains the calendar.

rows.name: Yuanmou Man Site
rows.summary: Two fossil human incisors found here on 1 May 1965 belong to Yuanmou Man, an early Homo erectus usually dated to about 1.7 million years ago, though the dating has been disputed. The find spot, on a hillside near Danawu village south-east of Yuanmou town, opened as an archaeological site park in May 2025, with a monument at the discovery site, the protected core of the excavations and renewed exhibition facilities. The Yuanmou Man Museum in town covers the finds in more detail.

rows.name: Yuanmou Man World Park
rows.summary: A leisure park on Fenghuang hill in Yuanma town, themed on the 'Yuanmou Man' hominin fossils found in the county, combining cultural displays with water-park rides and a hot-spring pool complex. It is a commercial leisure site; the fossil site and the Yuanmou Man Museum are separate.

rows.name: Yunnan–Burma Railway Bridges and Tunnels at Lianxiangguan
rows.name_zh: 滇缅铁路炼象关桥隧群
rows.summary: This 6.3 km stretch of abandoned line near the old Lianxiangguan pass, south-east of Lufeng, keeps a roadbed, five bridges and four tunnels of the Yunnan–Burma Railway, begun in 1938 to bring in foreign aid during the war against Japan. Work stopped in 1942 when Japanese forces invaded Burma; from 1958 the eastern section was completed on the old roadbed as the Kunming–Yipinglang railway, which was dismantled after the Chengdu–Kunming Railway opened in 1970.

rows.name: Zixi Mountain
rows.summary: Zixi Mountain, west of Chuxiong city, was one of Yunnan's Buddhist holy mountains in the Ming and Qing dynasties and is now a forest park and summer retreat. Ziding Temple stands on the mountain, and a camellia species garden, forest roads and walking trails spread across its slopes.

rows.name: Ancient Bridges of the Bi River
rows.summary: A group of 37 historic bridges over the Bi River and its tributaries in Yunlong County, mostly built between the Ming dynasty and the early Republic and listed together as a national monument in 2013. They cover the four basic types of traditional Chinese bridge, beam, floating, arch and suspension, which has earned the county the nickname of a 'museum of bridges'. They are scattered along the valleys rather than in one place, so a car is needed to see more than one or two.

rows.name: Butterfly Spring
rows.summary: A clear, square spring pool edged with marble at the foot of the Cangshan range, about 27 km north of Dali Old Town. It is famous for accounts of butterflies gathering over the water in spring, recorded by the Ming traveller Xu Xiake, although such swarms are now rarely seen. The spring is the centrepiece of a landscaped park and a common stop on trips around Erhai Lake.

rows.name: Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture Museum
rows.name_zh: 大理白族自治州博物馆
rows.summary: The prefecture's main museum, opened in 1986 beside the Xi'er River in Xiaguan, in a building that blends Tang-style architecture with Bai house forms. Its displays focus on the history of the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms and on Bai culture, with further galleries on bronze-age cultures, ceramics, Buddhist art, Dali marble, local historical figures and painting and calligraphy, drawn from a collection of about 16,800 items.

rows.name: Dali Geothermal Kingdom
rows.summary: A hot-spring resort beside Cibi Lake on the edge of Eryuan town, where mainly sulphurous springs at about 70–90 °C feed more than 30 open-air pools of different styles. Guest rooms are set in Bai-style courtyards, and it is a convenient stop on the road between Dali and Shaxi or Jianchuan.

rows.name: Dali Ocean World
rows.summary: An aquarium and marine theme park in the new hillside district of Haidong on the east side of Erhai Lake, with twelve themed halls including an underwater tunnel, a jellyfish hall, a polar section and displays of fish native to south-west China. A dolphin show, a 5D cinema and an indoor snow play area are aimed at families with children.

rows.name: Deyuan City Ruins
rows.summary: A hilltop fortress above Dengchuan, at the northern end of the Erhai plain, that was the seat of Dengdan, one of the six chiefdoms the Nanzhao kingdom absorbed in 738, and then guarded Nanzhao's northern approaches. Rammed-earth walls about 900 m round, best preserved on the west side and still up to 3.8 m high, enclose four terraces, and the site is described as the best-preserved Nanzhao-era walled town known. On the top terrace a temple rebuilt in 1988 honours Lady Baijie, the chief's widow of local legend.

rows.name: Fotu Pagoda (Snake Bone Pagoda)
rows.summary: A 13-tier square brick pagoda about 30 m tall, built under the Nanzhao kingdom and close in date and form to Qianxun Pagoda, the tallest of Dali's Three Pagodas. It stands on the lower slopes of the Cangshan range north of Xiaguan, in front of Fotu Temple, which was rebuilt in 1998 after the original temple was lost. Its popular name, Snake Bone Pagoda, comes from the legend of Duan Chicheng, a local hero who killed a giant serpent, although the pagoda built for his remains was a different one nearby that had collapsed by the late Ming.

rows.name: Hongsheng Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 16-tier square brick pagoda about 44 m tall at the south-western corner of Dali Old Town, built during the Dali kingdom; because it stands alone, its temple is known locally as the 'One Pagoda Temple'. Like the main pagoda of the Three Pagodas it has the hollow, multi-eaved form typical of the Tang era, and repairs in 1982 recovered more than 500 relics stored inside. A group of Qing-dynasty halls dedicated to Laozi stands in front of it.

rows.name: Jianchuan Old Town
rows.summary: The old quarter of Jianchuan, a Bai county town between Dali and Lijiang renowned for woodcarving, a craft listed as national intangible heritage in 2011. Ximen Street keeps a run of Ming courtyard houses and a memorial shrine built between 1392 and 1641, and a short walk west, at the foot of Jinhua Mountain, the Jingfeng Pavilion complex groups an octagonal triple-eaved pavilion, a pagoda, a Confucian hall and other mostly Qing buildings decorated with local carving and painting.

rows.name: Jianchuan Woodcarving Art Town
rows.summary: A woodcarving-themed town at Shihe village beside Jianhu Lake, built from 2017 and devoted to Jianchuan woodcarving, a Bai craft on China's national intangible cultural heritage list. It has a woodcarving square, master carvers' workshops and showrooms where you can watch artisans at work, alongside the older Bai houses of Shihe village. Most of the complex is new, so pair it with Jianchuan Old Town for historic architecture.

rows.name: Kublai Khan Stele, Dali
rows.summary: A stone stele erected in 1304 at the Sanyuejie fairground just west of Dali Old Town, recording Kublai Khan's campaign that brought the Dali kingdom under Mongol rule. Its text, composed by the Hanlin scholar Cheng Wenhai, originally ran to some 1,300 characters, of which more than 1,000 survive.

rows.name: Mount Jizu
rows.summary: A Buddhist holy mountain north-east of Erhai Lake, venerated as the place where the Buddha's disciple Mahakashyapa waits for the coming of the future Buddha, and a meeting point of Chinese, Tibetan and Theravada Buddhist traditions. Under the Ming dynasty it held hundreds of temples; many were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution and only some have been rebuilt, chief among them Zhusheng Temple in the heart of the mountain and Jinding Temple on the 3,248 m Tianzhu Peak, topped by the 42 m Lengyan Pagoda completed in 1934. The Ming traveller Xu Xiake climbed it twice and compiled the mountain's gazetteer.

rows.name: Nanzhao Iron Pillar
rows.summary: A cast-iron column 3.3 m tall and weighing about two tonnes, erected in 872 under the Nanzhao kingdom according to the 22-character inscription on its west face. It stands inside the main hall of Tiezhu (Iron Pillar) Temple, whose gate and courtyards were rebuilt in the Qing dynasty.

rows.name: Nuodeng Village
rows.summary: A Bai village built up a steep hillside above an old salt well near Yunlong, said to have kept its name since the Nanzhao period and long made prosperous by salt. More than a hundred courtyard houses climb the slope among Ming and Qing temples, including a Confucian temple, a martial temple and the three-storey Yuhuang Pavilion, first built in the Ming, whose ceiling is painted with the 28 lunar mansions. Brine still rises from the old well, and some villagers still make salt by traditional methods.

rows.name: Qianshi Mountain (Thousand Lions Mountain)
rows.summary: A wooded hill at Manxianlin on the western edge of Jianchuan, where local stonemasons have carved more than 3,000 lion figures into the rocks and boulders along its trails since the late 1990s. Seeing them means walking narrow paths through the forest.

rows.name: Shibaoshan Grottoes
rows.summary: Buddhist cave carvings on forested Shibao Mountain above the Shaxi valley, cut during the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms. Seventeen grottoes in three groups, at Shizhong Temple, Shiziguan and Shadengqing, hold 233 figures: Buddhas, bodhisattvas, guardian kings and monks, but also, unusually, Nanzhao kings with their courtiers and families. The carving shows Tang and Song influence, similar to cave art in Sichuan, combined with a strongly local style.

rows.name: Shimen Pass Gorge
rows.summary: A gorge on the western flank of the Cangshan range, where a stream from the Cangshan peaks drops through a chain of pools and waterfalls between sheer cliffs, with walkways following the water. A cliffside skywalk with a glass-floored section has also been built along the gorge wall.

rows.name: Shuimu Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded mountain near Yunnanyi with the Shuimu Temple complex, one of the earliest Buddhist sites in Yunnan, a centre of Chan (Zen) Buddhism in the west of the province and a royal temple under the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms. In the temple's front courtyard stands a 15-tier square brick pagoda about 18 m tall, first built in the Dali kingdom and restored in 1605, and about a kilometre to the north lies a forest of 72 monks' tomb stupas, said to be the largest such group in south-west China. Xu Xiake, the Ming travel writer, was among its visitors.

rows.name: Taihe City Ruins and Nanzhao Dehua Stele
rows.name_zh: 太和城遗址与南诏德化碑
rows.pinyin: Tàihé Chéng Yízhǐ yǔ Nánzhào Déhuà Bēi
rows.summary: The site of Taihe, capital of the Nanzhao kingdom from 739 to 779, on the slope between the Cangshan range and Erhai Lake. Little survives above ground except stretches of its rammed-earth north and south walls, but the Nanzhao Dehua Stele, erected in 766, still stands in Taihe village: its text of some 3,800 characters on Nanzhao's relations with Tang China and Tibet is now mostly worn away, yet it remains a key source for the kingdom's history.

rows.name: Tianfeng Mountain Taoist Temples
rows.summary: A large group of Taoist halls on the summit of Tianfeng Mountain in Pupeng, eastern Xiangyun County, and an important centre of the Zhengyi school of Taoism in western Yunnan. First built in the late Ming and rebuilt and extended many times since, the halls step up the mountainside and are decorated with stone and wood carving and painting in a distinctive local Yi style.

rows.name: Tianlong Babu Film City
rows.summary: A film set built in 2002 below the Cangshan mountains for a CCTV television adaptation of Jin Yong's martial-arts novel Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils, and used since for other productions. Its streets, palaces and gate towers recreate the Song-era Dali kingdom alongside the Liao and Western Xia courts, and since 2023 a martial-arts-themed street has staged performances for visitors.

rows.name: Tianshengqiao Natural Bridge, Midu
rows.summary: A karst scenic area a few kilometres east of Midu town, centred on Tianshengqiao, a natural rock bridge, with walking trails through a wooded valley. It is marketed under the name of 'Xiaohe Tangshui' ('The Flowing Stream'), a love song adapted in the 1940s from a folk tune of Midu County.

rows.name: West Lake (Eryuan)
rows.summary: A small highland lake at the northern foot of the Cangshan range, about 2 km² at 1,968 m, whose water drains south into Erhai Lake. Six villages and seven islets are scattered across it, and the lake and its reed beds are protected as a national wetland park, home to birds such as the purple swamphen. The Ming traveller Xu Xiake rated its scenery above that of Hangzhou's West Lake.

rows.name: Wuliang Mountain Cherry Blossom Valley
rows.summary: A tea plantation on the slopes of Wuliang Mountain in Nanjian county where winter-flowering cherry trees were planted among the tea terraces. For a few weeks around December the pink blossom against the green tea rows draws crowds of photographers, with paths and viewpoints across the hillside. Outside the flowering season it is simply a working tea plantation.

rows.name: Wutai Temple, Midu
rows.summary: A temple complex in Dasi village, Juli, in south-eastern Midu County, founded in the Ming dynasty and repaired and extended under the Qing and in the early Republic. Its 'three pavilions and five halls', among them a Guanyin pavilion, a Buddha hall, a hall for Laozi and a Confucius hall, show Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism worshipped side by side, and most of the main buildings keep their original structure. Each year on the 15th day of the second lunar month it hosts the Wutaishan antiphonal singing fair.

rows.name: Xinhua Village, Heqing
rows.summary: A Bai village on the edge of the Heqing plain whose families have long made silverware by hand, a craft that the county gazetteer traces back more than 500 years and that is on China's national intangible cultural heritage list. Its lanes are lined with family workshops where smiths hammer and engrave bowls, jewellery and teapots. It is a busy commercial centre for the trade, so compare prices before buying.

rows.name: Yunnanyi
rows.summary: A village on the old caravan road south-east of Xiangyun, named after the Han-dynasty Yunnan County seated here and the post station ('yi') kept on the route from the Yuan to the Qing dynasties. About 1.7 km of the old stone road survives, lined with shopfronts, caravan inns, family compounds, ancestral halls and temples mostly of the mid-to-late Qing, and the Qian family's former caravan inn now houses the Yunnan Horse Caravan Culture Museum. Both the village buildings and its stretch of the Tea Horse Road are national heritage sites.

rows.name: Zhoucheng Confucian and Martial Temples
rows.summary: The Confucian temple of the old Binchuan prefectural school, founded in 1494 in Zhoucheng, Binchuan's former seat, with the town's Martial Temple beside it. Laid out in four courtyards facing west, it keeps its screen wall, Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Gate, side galleries, the main Dacheng Hall and the double-eaved Chongsheng Shrine, most of them dating from the mid-to-late Qing dynasty.

rows.name: Mangshi Dai Ancient Town
rows.summary: A Dai-style quarter built from 2019 on a hillside on the east side of central Mangshi and opened in 2020, with the Menghuan Palace, a hall styled on Dai Buddhist temple architecture, and lanes of restaurants, craft and costume shops and a hotel. It is busiest in the evening, when the night-market street fills with food stalls and street performers. It is a modern development rather than a historic town.

rows.name: Mengbanaxi Rare Plant Garden
rows.summary: A garden park on the south-east side of central Mangshi, formerly the Mangshi Nationalities Cultural Palace, whose Dai name means 'a beautiful place'. It is planted with hundreds of century-old trees and displays petrified wood, rare stones and large root carvings, and peacocks roam the grounds.

rows.name: Menghuan Silver & Golden Pagodas
rows.summary: A white Theravada Buddhist pagoda on Leiyarang hill above Peacock Lake in Mangshi, built as a counterpart to the Menghuan Golden Pagoda a few hundred metres away. The golden pagoda, completed in 2007 to replace one destroyed during the Second World War, is more than 70 metres tall and is described as the tallest Theravada pagoda in China.

rows.name: Moli Tropical Rainforest
rows.summary: A forested valley north-east of Ruili whose Dai name is said to mean 'beautiful waterfall'. The scenic area covers about 7 square kilometres of dense forest with streams and a waterfall of about 60 metres. Local legend holds that the Buddha preached here and left a footprint in the rock, and a gilded stupa has been built beside it.

rows.name: Nandian Chieftain's Yamen
rows.summary: The headquarters of the Gong family, hereditary chieftains (tusi) of Nandian who ruled the area for about five centuries, in Zhedao, the county town of Lianghe. Begun in 1851 and enlarged until 1935, it is laid out like a Han Chinese government office, with 47 buildings around four main and ten side courtyards, and is often called the 'Dai Forbidden City'. It houses the Western Yunnan Tusi Culture Museum, opened in 2015.

rows.name: One Village, Two Countries
rows.summary: A Dai village south-west of Ruili where the China–Myanmar boundary runs through the settlement, so that the Chinese part is called Yinjing and the Myanmar part Mangxiu. Boundary marker No. 71 stands beside the village, villagers from both sides share a well, and a swing hangs across the line.

rows.name: Peacock Valley, Mangshi
rows.summary: A forest park in the hills north-east of Mangshi where peacocks are bred and roam the grounds in large numbers, and flocks are released from the hillside in staged flights down into the valley. A glass viewing tower, flower fields, tea gardens, ethnic song-and-dance shows and rides such as a dragon-shaped slide fill out a family day out.

rows.name: Wanding Bridge
rows.summary: A short bridge over the Wanding River on the China–Myanmar border, first built in 1938 for the Burma Road; the present steel truss span was put up by Chinese and American forces in January 1945 after Japanese troops blew up its predecessor. During the Second World War Allied supplies entered China here and Chinese Expeditionary Force troops crossed into Burma. A new road bridge replaced it in 1993, and the old span is now kept as a monument; the heritage listing also covers the former hall of the 1956 China–Burma border people's rally.

rows.name: Yunyan Pagoda
rows.summary: A Dai Buddhist stupa complex on Yunyan hill at the edge of Yingjiang county town, commissioned in 1946 by the local chieftain Si Hongsheng and finished only in 1955–56 after delays caused by epidemic and war. A white, gold-tipped central stupa about 20 metres tall rises from a five-tiered square base about 19 metres wide, ringed by 44 smaller stupas.

rows.name: Balagezong (Shangri-La Grand Canyon)
rows.summary: A deep canyon area in the north-west of Shangri-La, near the borders with Sichuan and Tibet, within the Hongshan section of the Three Parallel Rivers World Heritage Site. The land drops from Gezong Snow Mountain, at 5,545 metres the highest peak in Shangri-La, to about 2,000 metres in the valley; plank walkways and viewpoints line the canyon, and the Tibetan village of Bala sits on a mountainside at about 2,900 metres.

rows.name: Cizhong Catholic Church
rows.summary: A Catholic church in the village of Cizhong in southern Deqin County, rebuilt here by French missionaries of the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1909–1911 after their earlier church, about 15 km to the south, was burnt in 1905. Its design mixes a Romanesque Revival plan with Tibetan, Han and Bai building traditions. Used as a primary school during the Cultural Revolution, it survived largely intact, and the church, side buildings, gate, cellar and vineyard are all preserved.

rows.name: Potatso National Park
rows.summary: A protected area of lakes, wetlands, forest and alpine meadow east of Shangri-La, inaugurated in 2007 as the first reserve in mainland China to be named a national park, within the Three Parallel Rivers World Heritage area. Park buses carry visitors from the entrance to forest-ringed Shudu Lake, which is circled by boardwalks. Bita Lake and the Militang meadow were closed to visitors after a central environmental inspection in 2017, and a park notice for 2026 still keeps the main part of Bita Lake and its lakeside boardwalk closed for conservation.

rows.name: Shika Snow Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain rising to around 4,500 metres just south-west of Shangri-La town; its Tibetan name is said to refer to a place where red deer roam. A cableway of about 4.2 km climbs from a meadow at about 3,270 metres to viewing points above 4,000 metres that look out over the surrounding ranges on clear days.

rows.name: Shouguo Temple, Kangpu
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Qing dynasty in Kangpu township, in the Lancang (upper Mekong) valley of north-western Yunnan, usually described as belonging to the Karma Kagyu school. Its main hall is the core of the protected site and is known for its wall paintings.

rows.name: Tongle Lisu Village
rows.summary: A Lisu village of about 130 households on a slope above the east bank of the Lancang (upper Mekong) at about 2,200 metres, founded more than 200 years ago. Its 137 houses are mostly log cabins of crossed round timbers with wooden-shingle roofs weighted with stones, living quarters upstairs and space for livestock below, and field huts, fire houses and water mills stand on the opposite slope and in the valley below.

rows.name: Yezhi Tusi Residence
rows.summary: The seat of the Wang family, hereditary Naxi chieftains (tusi) of the Yezhi area, begun under the Kangxi emperor and enlarged until it reached its present size in the Guangxu era. Built round connected courtyards in the local 'three wings and a screen wall' plan, it mixes Han, Tibetan, Naxi and Bai styles and includes the chieftain's quarters, guard rooms, stables, watchtowers and a Black God Hall.

rows.name: Alu Ancient Cave
rows.summary: A group of karst caves in Luxi County, billed as the 'First Cave of Yunnan', made up of the Luyuan, Yuzhu and Biyu caves and the underground Yusun River, together more than 3 km long. The Ming geographer Xu Xiake explored the caves and described them in his travel diaries. The name comes from the Yi language, and the caves are part of the Luxi Alu national geopark.

rows.name: Baofenglong Trading House
rows.summary: A tin-smelting works and residence built between 1916 and 1926 for a leading Gejiu tin merchant surnamed Li, described as the city's only surviving tin-smelting site of the Republican era. Its Chinese-Western buildings include an east gate tower with an opera stage, a four-storey French-style main block, a three-storey embroidery tower, a corner blockhouse and the remains of the smelting furnaces.

rows.name: Bisezhai Railway Station
rows.summary: A station on the French-built Yunnan–Vietnam railway, opened in 1909, where goods were transferred to the narrow-gauge Gejiu–Bisezhai–Shiping line, turning a small village into a busy trading post nicknamed 'Little Paris of the East'. Passenger trains stopped in 1992, and the yellow-walled, red-tiled French station buildings, the Greek-run Gelusi hotel, merchants' warehouses and a branch customs house are now a railway heritage park. Feng Xiaogang filmed scenes of his 2017 film Youth here.

rows.name: Dishui Miao Town
rows.summary: A newly built Miao-style district and tourist hub on the Muyang River at the north-western edge of Pingbian county town, with stilt-style houses, covered bridges and a waterfall on the river. A Miao culture centre and the Yunnan Miao Medicine Museum present local history and Miao herbal medicine.

rows.name: Dongfengyun Art Town
rows.summary: An art and leisure town begun in 2014 on the former Dongfeng state farm south of Mile, a grape-growing area since the farm was founded in 1958. Its landmark is a cluster of domed, flame-like buildings in local red brick designed by the artist Luo Xu, with halls for exhibitions and events. Vineyards, hot-spring resorts and hotels surround the core.

rows.name: Faux Namti Bridge
rows.summary: A steel arch railway bridge built in 1907–08 by the French Batignolles company to carry the Yunnan–Vietnam railway across the Sicha River gorge, 102 m above the riverbed, between tunnels cut into sheer cliffs. Its parts were made in France and carried into the gorge by mules and porters, and it was the only bridge between Hekou and Bisezhai not blown up in 1940. The shape of its supports gives it the Chinese nickname Renzi Qiao, after the character 人.

rows.name: Fenghuang Eco-Park
rows.summary: A large city park in Kaiyuan's southern new district, opened in 2017, made up of Phoenix Hill, Phoenix Lake with a small beach and lakeside walks, and a wetland along the Nandong River. The clock-tower-style Phoenix Tower on the hill houses an exhibition on Kaiyuan's history, and 1909 Square beside the Yunnan–Vietnam railway displays old locomotives and track of three gauges. It is a local leisure park, convenient if you are breaking a journey through Kaiyuan.

rows.name: Former Mengzi Customs House and Southwest Associated University Memorial
rows.summary: Mengzi was opened as a treaty port after the Sino-French War, and its customs house, set up in 1889, was the first in Yunnan. Around South Lake survive the customs office, the French consulate of 1888, a French prison, the 'French Garden' and the French-style building of the Gelusi trading house, a firm set up by a Greek merchant in 1906. In 1938 the arts and law faculties of the wartime National Southwest Associated University taught here for several months, recalled by a memorial hall.

rows.name: Huquan Eco-Park
rows.summary: A large lakeside park on the western side of Mile city, set around a broad lake with a sand beach, islands, lakeside paths and birds such as egrets and black swans. A hotel, restaurants and hot-spring pools stand within the grounds, and the park doubles as a public park for local residents.

rows.name: Jinping Mountain and Mile Maitreya Buddha
rows.summary: A hillside temple park north of Mile whose centrepiece is a seated, laughing Maitreya Buddha 19.99 m tall, installed in 1999 at the top of a flight of 1,999 steps. Below it, Mile Temple, said to have been founded in the Song and rebuilt in the Ming, was restored in the Qianlong era and enlarged in 1999. The city shares its Chinese name with Maitreya (Mílè), which makes the statue a local emblem.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Changhong Bridge
rows.summary: An open-spandrel stone arch bridge over the Nanpan River, completed in 1961, with a main span of 113 m, a total length of 171 m and a height of 30 m. The arch centring collapsed in a storm during construction in 1960, killing 18 people, and slogans of the period are carved on the parapet posts. Since a new bridge opened in 1996 it has carried only a county road.

rows.name: Keyi Village
rows.summary: A village of the Axi, a branch of the Yi people, north of Mile, regarded as one of the birthplaces of the Axi tiaoyue, a moonlight dance to the three-stringed guitar listed as national intangible heritage in 2008. Now run as a tourist 'ethnic town' with a Yi museum, it is still home to some 700 villagers, whose earth-yellow house walls are painted with figures of the dance. Visitors come for the village itself and its song and dance performances.

rows.name: Laihe Pavilion
rows.summary: A small hillside complex at the top of Xiaoruicheng village on the shore of Yilong Lake, made up of a pavilion with upswept eaves and the Wenchang and Kuixing halls behind it. First built in the late Ming as the Haishan Pavilion, it was renamed after a legend of the immortal Lü Dongbin flying away on a crane, shown in a painted statue inside. The terrace looks out across the lake.

rows.name: Laoyin Mountain
rows.summary: The forested mountain that rises steeply above the east side of Gejiu, the old tin-mining city, to a summit of about 2,160 m. The Baohua cable car, running since 1997, climbs some 400 m up the slope, and a glass walkway about 350 m long, opened in 2019, wraps around the mountainside high above the city and Jinhu Lake.

rows.name: Mabang Ancient Town (Yisa), Honghe County
rows.summary: Yisa, the county town of Honghe County, is built along a narrow ridge south of the Red River; it grew rich on mule-caravan trade and is known as a home town of overseas Chinese. Its East Gate tower and 18 houses on East Gate Street, built from the late Qing to the Republican era, blend Chinese courtyard plans with Western-style features. Among them are the mansions of the Yao and Qian families.

rows.name: Nalou Chieftain's Office
rows.summary: The headquarters of a Yi hereditary chieftain (tusi) of the Nalou line, built in 1907 high on a mountainside above the north bank of the Red River, nearly 1,000 m above the water. Three courtyards with more than 70 rooms climb the slope, with offices at the front and living quarters behind, inside walls with defensive corner towers.

rows.name: Nandong Cave, Kaiyuan
rows.summary: A scenic area on the southern outskirts of Kaiyuan where underground streams emerge from the limestone hills to form the Nandong River; long counted first among the area's traditional eight views, it opened to visitors in 1988. It takes in eight karst caves, among them Taoyuan Cave with a dry section and a water section, and the century-old metre-gauge Yunnan–Vietnam railway runs through it. The Phoenix Valley section adds a glass skywalk and a glass slide.

rows.name: Samaba Rice Terraces
rows.summary: Samaba is a sweep of Hani rice terraces on a single mountainside in Baohua town, Honghe County, which the prefecture's publicity department puts at more than 14,000 mu (over 9 sq km) in over 4,300 levels. A viewing platform looks across the whole terraced slope at once, and a walkway leads down among the paddies. It lies in a different county from the World Heritage terraces of Yuanyang, about 45 km to the south-east.

rows.name: Shiping Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Shiping's Confucian temple, founded in the Yuan dynasty and rebuilt in 1389, stands in the old town of a county long known for its scholars, among them Yuan Jiagu, the only Yunnanese to come first in an imperial examination (1903). Its axis runs from the Lingxing Gate past the Pan pond and the Dacheng Gate, with side halls, to the main Hall of the Former Teacher and the Zunjing library pavilion.

rows.name: Shuanglong Bridge
rows.summary: A 17-arch stone bridge about 148 m long where the Lu and Tachong rivers meet west of Jianshui, described as the largest and finest old stone bridge in Yunnan. It began as a three-arch bridge in the Qianlong era and was lengthened from 1839 after floods widened the river. A three-storey pavilion with yellow glazed tiles stands at its centre and a smaller octagonal pavilion at its southern end.

rows.name: Swallow Cave (Yanzidong), Jianshui
rows.summary: A large karst cave in the hills east of Jianshui, divided into a dry cave and a water cave through which an underground river flows. It is named after the swifts that nest under its roof in great numbers, arriving in spring and leaving in summer. Together with Jianshui's old town it forms part of the Jianshui national scenic area.

rows.name: Taiping Lake Forest Resort
rows.summary: A forest and lake resort on the outskirts of Mile city, built on once-barren karst hills that have been replanted, with forest cabins to stay in, flower fields and a lakeside wetland. It is set up for family days out and short breaks, with resort hotels in the wider development.

rows.name: Tuanshan Village
rows.summary: A village of courtyard mansions about 13 km west of Jianshui, settled by the Zhang clan from Jiangxi in the early Ming and rebuilt on a grand scale in the late Qing with fortunes made in the Gejiu tin mines. Twenty-one historic gates, temples and ancestral halls and 38 old houses survive, laid out around the Zhang ancestral hall. The listed buildings include the Zhang Family Garden, several mansions, the Dacheng Temple and three of the old village gates.

rows.name: Xin'ansuo Old Buildings
rows.summary: Xin'ansuo, south-east of Mengzi, was a Ming military garrison town, walled in 1517, and is now a national historic town, although its walls were pulled down in 1951. Its listed temples are Zhutian Temple, the City God Temple, Guanyin Temple, the Wenchang Palace (Zhongshan Hall), a Guandi temple and a Yuhuang Pavilion. The surrounding area is Mengzi's main pomegranate-growing district.

rows.name: Yilong Lake
rows.summary: A shallow plateau lake beginning just east of Shiping town, known for the lotus flowers that cover parts of its surface. Its area has shrunk considerably since the 1980s, and a wetland park now lines part of the shore. Laihe Pavilion on its north-western shore gives a view across the water.

rows.name: Yuhuang Pavilion, Mengzi
rows.summary: A temple group in central Mengzi whose main building, the triple-eaved Tongming Pavilion founded in 1578, stands about 20 m tall between matching east and west pavilions added in 1734. Behind it are the carved hall of the Jianyang guild, built by Jianshui merchants in 1770, and a Kangxi-era hall of the old county yamen. Run as a Buddhist temple since 2000, it still keeps the Jade Emperor on its top floor.

rows.name: Zhengying Village
rows.summary: An old village in Baoxiu, west of Shiping, with lanes of traditional courtyard houses; it was named a Chinese historic and cultural village in 2008. Its two nationally listed buildings are the Chen ancestral hall, founded in 1925 by the late-Qing scholar-official Chen Hetang (Chen Jun) behind an archway-style gate, and the Zheng ancestral hall of the 1880s, noted for its wood, stone and brick carving.

rows.name: Zhou Family Mansion (Wangyun Museum)
rows.summary: A Chinese-Western merchant's mansion of four courtyards and about 90 rooms, built from 1916 by Zhou Ziyin, a banker and railway promoter, reportedly with money the Guangdong governor Long Jiguang had given him to build a residence for Long. In 1938 one of its buildings was the women's dormitory of the National Southwest Associated University, and since 2014 the house has held the Wangyun Museum.

rows.name: Anning Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Also called the Lianran Confucian Temple, it was founded in 1302 under the Yuan dynasty in what is now the old centre of Anning, and after Ming and Qing rebuilding it grew to 22 buildings arranged in seven successive sections. Only the main Dacheng Hall and the Chongsheng Shrine survive from the old complex, and the Anning City Museum has been built around them.

rows.name: Anti-Japanese War Victory Memorial Hall, Kunming
rows.summary: A palace-style hall blending Chinese and Western elements, completed in January 1946 on the site of the Qing Yunnan–Guizhou governor's office to mark victory in the war against Japan; from 1950 it was called the People's Victory Hall. Its central hall is planned in the shape of a warplane, and with the curved buildings around it the layout evokes a raised cup, a reference to the wartime 'Hump' airlift. A 27-metre monument to the people's heroes, completed in 1995, stands at the south end, with a memorial exhibition room in the space beneath its base.

rows.name: Caoxi Temple, Anning
rows.summary: A Chan Buddhist temple at the foot of Cong Hill, 1.5 km south of Anning's hot-spring town of Wenquan, probably founded in the Dali Kingdom period by monks devoted to the patriarch Huineng. Its main hall, the double-eaved Baohua Pavilion, was restored in 1694 and houses a wooden Buddhist trinity that scholars have dated variously from the Southern Song to the early Ming. Local legend holds that once every 60 years the Mid-Autumn moon shines through a small round window onto the face of the main Buddha.

rows.name: Daguan Lou and Daguan Park
rows.summary: A lakeside park in south-western Kunming whose focal point is Daguan Lou, a three-storey Qing-dynasty pavilion facing south over Dian Lake towards the Western Hills. The pavilion is known for the long couplet by the Qing scholar Sun Ran on its gateposts, reputed to be the longest in China, and the willow-lined park around it is a local favourite for tea, kite-flying and boating.

rows.name: Dizang Temple Sutra Pillar
rows.summary: A seven-tier octagonal pillar of red sandstone, about 6.5 metres tall, carved in the Dali Kingdom period with Esoteric Buddhist imagery: Heavenly Kings, Buddhas and bodhisattvas fill tiers of niches, with texts in Chinese and Sanskrit. Rediscovered in 1919 on the site of the old Dizang Temple, it now stands under a glass roof in the central hall of the Kunming Museum, whose collections also include bronzes, Ming blue-and-white porcelain and relics of the wartime Flying Tigers.

rows.name: Eastern and Western Pagodas
rows.summary: Two 13-storey brick pagodas in the dense-eave style, about 400 metres apart in central Kunming, first built under the Nanzhao kingdom in the 9th century. The Western Pagoda, about 35 metres tall, was rebuilt after an earthquake in 1499, and the taller Eastern Pagoda, about 40 metres, was rebuilt on a new site in the 1880s after an earthquake brought it down in 1833; each is crowned with four bronze 'golden cockerels'. A pedestrian street laid out in 2002 links the two.

rows.name: Fenglongwan Resort
rows.summary: A resort built around the Fenglongwan Reservoir, dammed on the Malong River in 1956, at Tangzi in Xundian county. Its centrepiece is a newly built fairy-tale town on an Aladdin theme beside the water, with a sightseeing train and boat trips around the lake; it is aimed at families and photographers.

rows.name: Former Site of National Southwest Associated University
rows.name_zh: 国立西南联合大学旧址
rows.summary: From 1938 to 1946 Peking, Tsinghua and Nankai universities shared a wartime campus in Kunming as National Southwest Associated University, and what remained after they returned north grew into today's Yunnan Normal University. On its campus survive an original tin-roofed classroom, the university's memorial stele engraved with the names of 834 students who joined the armed forces, and the tomb of four people killed in the December 1st Movement protests of 1945. The Southwest Associated University Museum on the site, first set up in 2011, reopened with new displays in 2018, the 80th anniversary of the university's arrival in Kunming.

rows.name: Fulintang Pharmacy
rows.summary: A traditional Chinese medicine shop at 31 Guanghua Street, founded in 1857 and regarded as the oldest surviving pharmacy in Yunnan. The protected building is a three-storey timber and earth corner house at the junction with Wenming Street, with finely carved eaves, and the shop's name comes from a phrase wishing good fortune on the 'apricot grove', a classical term for the medical profession.

rows.name: Golden Temple (Taihe Palace)
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex on Mingfeng Hill whose centrepiece is a hall cast entirely of copper, 6.7 metres high, rebuilt here in 1671 by the general Wu Sangui with more than 250 tonnes of copper after the original of 1602–1604 had been moved to Jizu Mountain. It is regarded as the largest and best-preserved all-copper hall in China. Walled courtyards with other Taoist halls surround it, and the wooded park holds a camellia garden of more than 1,200 varieties with an annual camellia show.

rows.name: Guandu Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old ferry settlement near the northern shore of Dian Lake, about 10 km south-east of central Kunming, whose temples, pavilions and lanes were restored and partly rebuilt in 2001–2003. Its finest monument is the stone Diamond Pagoda in front of Miaozhan Temple, completed in 1458: a 16-metre central tower and four smaller corner towers on a square base pierced by arched passages. Several other temples survive in the town, among them Fading Temple and the Tuzhu Temple.

rows.name: Haikou Chuanzi Sluice
rows.summary: A combined sluice and multi-arched stone bridge built in 1836 at the outlet of Dian Lake, at Zhongtan village in Haikou. Its northern, central and southern sections span three parallel channels, a layout that recalls the three strokes of the Chinese character chuan and gives the sluice its name; it once served to hold back water, release floods, irrigate fields and carry traffic.

rows.name: Historic Buildings of Yunnan Observatory, Fenghuang Hill
rows.name_zh: 凤凰山天文台近代建筑
rows.summary: Three historic buildings on Fenghuang Hill in eastern Kunming, within what is now the Yunnan Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Two blue-brick blocks, with a variable-star dome and a solar spectrograph darkroom, date from 1939, when the astronomy institute of the Academia Sinica moved west during the war and set up an observing station here; a red-brick sunspot observatory with a metal dome followed in 1957. The observatory is still a working research centre.

rows.name: Huize Hall, Yunnan University
rows.summary: The landmark building of Yunnan University, built in 1923–1924 to a design by the engineer Zhang Banghan as the main building of the university's predecessor, Donglu University, on the site of the old Yunnan provincial examination hall. The Western-style building has Baroque touches and some Chinese detailing, and since 2020 its ground floor has housed the Yunnan University History Museum.

rows.name: Jiaozi Snow Mountain
rows.summary: A high massif on the border of Luquan County and Dongchuan District in northern Kunming, rising to more than 4,000 metres as the highest point of the eastern Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. It has been a national nature reserve since 2011, and in winter it is the main place near Kunming to see snow, with a cableway serving the upper slopes.

rows.name: Jiuxiang Scenic Region
rows.summary: A karst area in Yiliang County where more than 20 caves have formed in layers along the Maitian River, a tributary of the Nanpan; where cave roofs have collapsed, the river runs through gorges and under natural bridges. Parts of the cave system opened to visitors in 1989, and the area became a national geopark in 2009. The visitor route links the shady Yincui gorge with caverns such as the White Elephant and Bat caves and the rock formations known as the Fairy Fields.

rows.name: Kedu Red Army Long March Memorial
rows.summary: A memorial museum, opened in 1977, in Dangui, a Hui village in Kedu town, Xundian County, set around two courtyard houses where the headquarters of the Central Red Army stayed on 30 April 1935 during the Long March. That night the Central Military Commission met here to plan the crossing of the Jinsha River; Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Liu Bocheng lodged in one house and Mao Zedong, Wang Jiaxiang and Zhang Wentian in the other. The national listing also covers Jiaoping Ferry in Luquan County, where the army crossed the Jinsha into Sichuan on 3–9 May 1935 and where a museum now marks the crossing.

rows.name: Kunming Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A research garden in the northern suburbs of Kunming, founded in 1938 and run by the Kunming Institute of Botany of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. It holds about 5,000 species of vascular plants, with collections of camellias, magnolias, begonias, ferns, medicinal herbs and rare and endangered species.

rows.name: Kunming Sunac Ocean World
rows.summary: An indoor aquarium in the Sunac cultural-tourism complex by the Caohai part of Dian Lake in Xishan district, which also holds an indoor ski and snow park.
