Its surviving two-storey main hall has an assembly hall painted with protector deities, Tsongkhapa and the life of the Buddha, and an early mural of the Buddha leaving his palace in the Maitreya chapel.

rows.name: Aiwang (Iwang) Temple
rows.summary: Aiwang Temple, in Samada township south of Kangmar, was founded in the 11th century, early in the revival of Buddhism in Tibet, and later passed to the Gelug school. Its small red-walled chapels keep clay sculptures from the 11th and 12th centuries: the figures in the main hall recall Chinese cave-temple sculpture of the Northern Wei to Tang periods, while those in the east chapel resemble Central Asian work. Many statues were damaged in 1966, but eleven bodhisattvas and two guardian figures survive in the east chapel.

rows.name: Chongba Yumtso
rows.summary: Chongba Yumtso is a glacial lake at about 4,570 m on the north side of the Himalaya in southern Kangmar County, and the source of the Nyang River that flows down past Gyantse to Shigatse. Snow peaks ring the water, and in mid to late June rhododendrons flower pink and white along the shore; the scenic area also has dome-shaped 'bubble' rooms for stargazing.

rows.name: Chöde Temple, Drolma Lhakhang and Tang Envoy Inscription
rows.name_zh: 曲德寺、卓玛拉康、大唐天竺使出铭
rows.pinyin: Qūdé Sì, Zhuómǎ Lākāng, Dà Táng Tiānzhú Shǐ Chū Míng
rows.summary: Three listed relics stand in and near Zongga, the county town of Gyirong: Chöde Temple, a Gelug monastery destroyed in the 1960s with a small chapel rebuilt on its ruins, and next to it Drolma Lhakhang, a Nyingma hall with finely carved wooden pillars and lion brackets that probably belonged to the royal city of the Gungthang kings. About 4.5 km north of town, a Chinese inscription carved on a cliff in 658 records the passage of the Tang envoy Wang Xuance on his mission to India; it is the only Tang-dynasty inscription so far found in Tibet. A pavilion now shelters the inscription, and a small exhibition hall about it opened in 2025.

rows.name: Gyantse Dzong
rows.summary: Gyantse Dzong is a fortress on a steep rock above Gyantse that was the seat of one of Tibet's major districts; the castle dates mainly from the late 14th century. In July 1904 British troops of the Younghusband expedition stormed it after months of fighting with Tibetan defenders around the town, and the site is now presented as a memorial to that resistance, with old gun positions, a monument and a museum. On the way up are restored rooms of the old district government, and the top looks over the old town and Palcho Monastery.

rows.name: Gyirong Valley
rows.summary: The Gyirong Valley cuts deep into the central Himalaya, falling to about 2,800 m around Gyirong town, where dense forest and farming villages lie beneath snow peaks. For centuries it was one of the main routes between Tibet and Nepal. Besides walks in the valley, visitors see the town's Phagpa Temple and nearby villages such as Nai.

rows.name: Langdong Manor and Langba Village
rows.summary: Langba, a listed traditional village on the upper Nyang River in Kangmar County, was renovated and opened as a scenic area in 2023 around Langdong Manor, an aristocratic estate house more than 500 years old. Visitors can tour the manor, stay in village homestays and watch villagers perform the local folk song-and-dance.

rows.name: Lin'en Cliff Carvings
rows.summary: On a cliff at Sangga village in Ngamring County, 15th-century carvers cut Buddhist images and Tibetan inscriptions into the rock, among them the six-syllable mantra and a eulogy of a Shakyamuni image. Both inscriptions were added to the national list of famous ancient inscriptions in 2023, and a conservation project for the site was being prepared in 2026.

rows.name: Nenying Monastery
rows.summary: Nenying Monastery, in the upper Nyang valley south of Gyantse, traces its founding to the Tibetan Empire and became a Gelug monastery in the 15th century; it is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of the Tibetan opera Nangsa Öbum. In 1904 it was the scene of fighting between Tibetan defenders and the British expedition advancing on Gyantse. Rebuilt afterwards and again after damage in the 1960s, it has been restored since 2010; an old door still shows bullet holes, and a memorial stone outside commemorates the defenders.

rows.name: Pala Manor
rows.summary: Pala Manor, the seat of the Pala family, who held high office in the old Tibetan government, is regarded as the only Tibetan aristocratic manor to survive largely intact. It was rebuilt here after the family's earlier house near Gyantse was burned in 1904, and its three-storey main building keeps the chapel, reception rooms and furnishings, including the family's imported goods. Facing it, the cramped quarters of the estate's household servants (nangzan) are preserved and used as an exhibit.

rows.name: Palcho Monastery
rows.summary: Palcho (Pelkor Chöde) Monastery, below the hills on the north-western edge of Gyantse, was built from 1418 by the local ruler Rabten Kunzang Phag with the scholar Khedrup Je, and is unusual in housing Gelug, Sakya and Shalu communities side by side. Beside its assembly hall rises the Gyantse Kumbum, a many-tiered stupa whose dozens of small chapels are lined with 15th-century murals and statues in the local Gyantse style. Together with the fortress it is the main sight of Gyantse.

rows.name: Phagpa Temple, Gyirong
rows.summary: Phagpa Temple in the centre of Gyirong town is a four-storey tower temple of stone and timber with tiered eaves, flame-shaped copper corner fittings and a copper roof, built in a style that shows strong Nepalese influence. Tradition dates its founding to the reign of Songtsen Gampo; the building has been repaired many times, was restored in the 1980s and belongs to the Gelug school. In 1789, during the wars between Tibet and the Gorkha kingdom, Qing and Gorkha representatives held peace talks near the temple.

rows.name: Phuntsokling Monastery
rows.summary: Phuntsokling Monastery, near the Yarlung Tsangpo in Lhatse County, was founded in 1614 by the scholar Tāranātha as a centre of the Jonang school, with the support of the Tsang rulers. In the mid-17th century it was converted to the Gelug school under the Fifth Dalai Lama and renamed Ganden Phuntsokling. Its buildings are laid out like a mandala around a large assembly hall, with smaller chapels, many of them ruined and partly restored, the ruins of the printing house and the old district fort, and further halls up the hillside.

rows.name: Qilin Gorge Earth Forest
rows.summary: Qilin Gorge, also known as the Mu Village earth forest, is a valley in Qiongzi township on the north side of the Himalaya where meltwater has eroded the soft sediments into crowded ranks of earth pillars and fins. Viewpoints look over the formations towards snow peaks on the horizon, and villagers of Mu run the site through a tourism cooperative.

rows.name: Sakya Monastery
rows.summary: Sakya Monastery, founded in 1073 by Khön Könchok Gyalpo, is the seat of the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism, whose leaders governed Tibet under Yuan-dynasty overlordship in the 13th and 14th centuries. Its walls are painted in the school's dark grey with red and white bands; the massive walled South Monastery, founded in 1268, holds a great assembly hall lined with a wall of scriptures, while the older North Monastery on the hillside across the river was largely destroyed in the 1960s and is partly rebuilt. The old town around the monastery is a separate scenic area, Sakya Old Town.

rows.name: Shalu Monastery
rows.summary: Shalu Monastery, founded in the 11th century in a side valley south-east of Shigatse, is the mother monastery of the small Shalu (or Butön) school, founded by its 14th-century abbot Butön Rinchen Drub, the scholar who edited the Tibetan Buddhist canon. After an earthquake in 1329 it was rebuilt with craftsmen sent from the Yuan court, so its main hall has Tibetan walls under green glazed-tile roofs in Chinese style. Most of its murals and sculptures date from that rebuilding, and the old wall paintings in its chapels and corridors are the main reason to visit.

rows.name: Site of the Yadong Customs House
rows.summary: The Qing government opened a customs house here in 1894, at the meeting of two mountain streams south of present-day Yadong, after treaties with Britain made Yadong a trade mart on the route between Tibet and British India. Customs duties were never actually levied, and the Tibetan government closed the post in 1913. Only sections of its walls survive.

rows.name: Baimaqumi Garden Hotel (Lhasa)
rows.name_zh: 奇正白玛曲秘花园酒店
rows.summary: A hotel in Lhasa's Chengguan District run under the Baimaqumi brand of the Tibetan medicine company Qizheng, offering Tibetan-medicine external therapies as part of a stay. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base under the name Baimaqumi Tibetan medicine external-therapy resort.

rows.name: Feidu Gorge and Huang'anba
rows.summary: A scenic area on the northern slopes of the Daba Mountains in Shuping town, at the southern tip of Ankang where Shaanxi borders Chongqing, combining the Feidu River gorge with the Huang'anba upland pastures. The gorge is known for its unusual trees, oddly shaped rocks, waterfalls and deep pools, with red leaves in autumn, while Huang'anba is open grassland and meadow.

rows.name: Fengyan Ancient Terraces
rows.summary: Hillside rice terraces in Xuanwo town, Hanyin County, made up of the Fengjiang and Yanping terrace systems and described as the largest and best-preserved Qing-dynasty terraces found in the Qinling–Daba region. They were begun in the Qianlong era by the Wu clan, migrants from Changsha prefecture in Hunan, built up on a large scale in the mid-19th century and are still farmed; Ming–Qing farmhouses such as the Wu family's 'flowered house' stand among some 12,000 mu (about 800 ha) of fields, golden with rice in autumn. The terraces became a national heritage site in 2019.

rows.name: Guiguling (Yunwu Mountain)
rows.summary: The highest mountain in Shiquan County, also called Yunwu Mountain and protected as a national forest park, where the Warring States strategist Guiguzi is said to have taught his disciples. Its main peak is ringed by five ridges, and visitors come for old-growth forest, oddly shaped peaks, rocks and trees, caves, and seas of cloud in autumn; it is also regarded as a Daoist mountain.

rows.name: Nangong Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of 7,648 ha in eastern Langao County, described by the provincial government as the first in Shaanxi, whose three-peaked summit, Jinding, reaches 2,267 m. It is known for stone forests left by ancient volcanic eruptions, well-preserved Quaternary glacial landforms on its southern slope, dove trees and other rare plants, and temples that began as a Daoist temple in 1126 and later became Buddhist; a glass skywalk looks out over the sea of clouds.

rows.name: Qianceng River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested river valley in Hengxi town in the far south of Langao County, in the Daba Mountains. A path follows the clear stream upstream past a string of green pools through dense woodland, and the valley is often combined with Nangong Mountain and the Bashan grassland on trips through southern Ankang.

rows.name: Qinba Culture and Ecology Park, Ankang High-tech Zone
rows.summary: A belt of public parks of about 67 ha in the core of Ankang's High-tech Zone, west of the city centre, made up of a sports park, Beichen Park and a culture park. It has a large musical fountain, cycle tracks and outdoor courts, a landscaped water channel modelled on the Yue River with gold-panning motifs, and features that recreate landmarks from Ankang's counties such as Nangong Mountain and Houliu old town.

rows.name: Shaanxi–Gansu Tea-Horse Road and Wafangdian Guild Halls
rows.summary: A scenic area at Wafangdian in Xiangyang town, where the Zhu and Ren rivers meet west of Ziyang town, built around the Qing guild halls of the merchants of the old tea trade, together with a tea-hill trail and a small tea garden. Its centrepiece, the Beiwusheng Guild Hall ('Hall of the Five Northern Provinces'), was begun at the end of the Qianlong era and finished in the Tongzhi era; its two halls, once dedicated to Guan Yu, carry about 100 m² of murals of the Twenty-four Exemplars of Filial Piety and the Three Kingdoms. The murals, hidden behind panelling when the hall became a granary in 1952 and rediscovered in 2006, were conserved in a Sino-German project, and performances are now staged in the guild halls.

rows.name: Shiquan Old Town
rows.summary: The historic core of Shiquan town on the Han River, with the Yuwang Palace, a temple to Yu the Great first built in the Tang, and a cluster of Ming and Qing buildings including the old county yamen, the Jiangxi guild hall and the east and west gates. In the evening its old streets turn into a night market of food stalls serving local dishes.

rows.name: Shuanghekou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A small market town in the hills of northern Hanyin County, founded in the early Ming about 600 years ago where the Loufang and Lishu rivers meet, and long the trading and transport centre of the area. Its old street keeps old shopfronts and a guild hall, and it is often visited together with the Fengyan terraces and the memorial hall of Hanyin's scholarly Shen brothers.

rows.name: Shuanglong Scenic Area
rows.summary: A dragon-themed scenic area in Shuanglong town, southern Hanbin District, where a 5.6 km loop links Longtan Gorge, Xianglong Valley, the Youlong waterfall, the Qinglong stockade and the Yulong Palace. Built around the theme of the origins of the Chinese dragon, it combines gorge walking, limestone caves and a hilltop stockade with dragon legends and staged performances.

rows.name: Shuhe Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old Han River port 53 km east of Xunyang town, where the Shu River joins the Han, nicknamed 'Little Hankou' for its river trade. It keeps stone-paved lanes, Ming and Qing guild halls and old wooden houses with plank fronts, lattice windows and fine carving, and is listed as a national historic and cultural town.

rows.name: Taohuaxi (Peach Blossom Creek)
rows.summary: A wooded creek valley in Tielu village, Guangfo town, about 15 km from Pingli town. The stream drops through a series of clear pools and stepped cascades, which the local tourism bureau likens to a small Jiuzhaigou.

rows.name: Tianbao Terraced Farm Park
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park in Tianbao village, Cangshang town, in western Baihe County, built around hillsides of stone-walled terraced fields presented as 'land art'. It combines working farm and livestock areas with sightseeing, melons and fruit grow on the terraces in season, and it lies about 12 km south of Shuhe Ancient Town, with which it is often paired.

rows.name: Tianshu Gorge
rows.summary: A gorge in Baxian town at the southern end of Pingli County, on the Chongqing border and within the Qianjiaping national forest park, with old forest, waterfalls and mid-mountain meadows. Its name, 'Heavenly Books Gorge', comes from the layered, vertically jointed slabs of slate strewn along the stream, which local legend says are books left behind by the Eight Immortals.

rows.name: Tongchewan Leisure Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 12 km² river-and-forest leisure area on the Wenshui River in Tongchewan town, on the southern slopes of the Qinling in Ningshan County, with streams, falls, springs and pools under more than 90% forest cover. It bundles five attractions: a 5.6 km rafting run on the Wenshui that passes through a 200 m tunnel, a riverside water park, the Canglong Gorge forest park with plank walkways past its pools, the Huangliang Gully wellness garden, and an unusually designed City God temple.

rows.name: Yanshan Waterfalls
rows.summary: A wooded valley in Xihe town, southern Shiquan County, where a stream drops more than 300 m in 13 steps, forming 47 waterfalls and 36 pools. Footpaths climb beside the falls, cliffs and flower plantings, and the valley stays mild in winter and cool in summer.

rows.name: Yanxiang Cave
rows.summary: A natural limestone cave system in Yundou town on the Han River in southern Shiquan County, of which about 1.6 km has been opened to visitors. Inside are stalactites, flowstone 'waterfalls', stone curtains, rimstone dams, stalagmites and many other formations, and the cave keeps a mild, even temperature all year.

rows.name: Yinghu Lake
rows.summary: The reservoir behind the Ankang Dam on the Han River, about 15 km south-west of central Ankang, with some 77 km² of water and nearly a hundred islands and peninsulas; it is an important source area for the central route of the South–North Water Diversion. Boat trips visit islands such as Jinluo and Yuxing, and the shores have temples, villages and lakeside guesthouses.

rows.name: Zhongba Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A 21 km² canyon scenic area in Houliu town, Shiquan County, of cliffs, stacked boulders, mountain springs and thick bamboo and woodland. Plank walkways fixed to the cliffs pass high waterfalls and clear pools, and the trip is often combined with the riverside old town of Houliu and the Zhongba craft village nearby.

rows.name: Beishouling Neolithic Site
rows.summary: A Neolithic village site of about 6 ha on a terrace on the west bank of the Jinling River in northern Baoji, occupied from about 5100 to 3790 BC. Excavated between 1958 and 1978, it has a lower layer of the late Dadiwan culture and upper layers of the Yangshao (Banpo type) culture and yielded painted pottery such as a boat-shaped jar and a pot showing a waterbird pecking a fish; a museum now protects and displays part of the site.

rows.name: Changleyuan Wartime Industrial Site (Shenxin Cotton Mill)
rows.summary: Remains of the Shenxin cotton mill that the Rong family's textile firm moved from Hankou to Baoji in 1938, during the war against Japan. Workers dug 24 linked cave workshops into the Changle loess terrace, about 1.75 km long in all, which went into production in April 1941, and the site also keeps the mill's office building and a thin-shell concrete workshop.

rows.name: Cishan Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple about 5 km east of Linyou town, begun in the Renshou era of the Sui (early 600s), when the court summered at the nearby palace, and extended under the Tang. Twelve caves, six niches and 47 statues are cut into a 28 m cliff, and the main Buddha of Cave 1, said to have been paid for by the Sui imperial house, is 5.5 m tall.

rows.name: East Lake, Fengxiang
rows.summary: A lake garden on the south-east edge of Fengxiang town that grew from an old pond called Yinfeng Chi ('Phoenix Drinking Pool'). In 1062 the poet Su Shi, then an assistant judge of Fengxiang prefecture, had it dredged and enlarged, fed with spring water and planted with lotus and willows, and named it East Lake; pavilions, bridges and halls in classical garden style surround the water.

rows.name: Feng County Revolutionary Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall in Fengzhou opened in 2016 on the county's twentieth-century political history. Its exhibitions cover the Communist organising in the local garrison that led to the Liangdang Mutiny of April 1932, which Xi Zhongxun helped to organise, the Red Army's passage through the county, the wartime Industrial Cooperatives (Gung Ho) movement and the end of Nationalist rule in the county.

rows.name: Fufeng City God Temple (Fufeng County Museum)
rows.summary: A City God temple in the centre of Fufeng town, founded in 1370 and enlarged and restored through the Ming and Qing, which now houses the Fufeng County Museum. More than ten buildings climb a rammed-earth terrace that rises 13 m from south to north, from the opera stage, gate, wooden archway and bell and drum towers to the offering hall, the five-bay main hall and the rear halls.

rows.name: Fumei Campaign Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall and martyrs' cemetery at Changxing in Mei County for the Fumei Campaign of 10–14 July 1949, in which the People's Liberation Army defeated Hu Zongnan's Nationalist forces in the Wei valley between Fufeng and Mei County. Begun in the 1950s, when the remains of fallen soldiers were gathered here, and opened to the public in 1972, it has a 19.49 m monument and exhibitions on the campaign with relics and a sand-table model.

rows.name: Guanshan Grassland
rows.summary: An upland of alpine meadow and forest in the Guanshan mountains on the Shaanxi–Gansu border, at Guanshan village in Tiancheng town, south-west Long County. The grassland, a provincial scenic area and tourist resort, is at its best in summer, when it is a popular cool-weather retreat.

rows.name: Jintai Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex founded in the late Yuan or early Ming dynasty on the loess terrace above central Baoji, known through the tradition that Zhang Sanfeng, legendary founder of the Wudang school and of taijiquan, practised here. Its buildings rise up the slope along a central axis, among them the two-storey Jade Emperor Pavilion, an octagonal pavilion and Sanfeng Cave, and the temple is the core of the Taiji Source Cultural Area.

rows.name: Jiulong Mountain, Chencang
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in western Chencang District whose nine converging peaks are said to resemble nine dragons, with red-sandstone Danxia cliffs rising to 1,910 m and forest. A hot-spring hotel named after the mountain has been built for visitors.

rows.name: Longmen Cave (Longmendong)
rows.summary: A Taoist mountain sanctuary in Xinjichuan town north-west of Long County, where the Quanzhen master Qiu Chuji spent seven years in retreat in the late 12th century; the Longmen (Dragon Gate) school of Taoism, which honours him as its patriarch, takes its name from the place. Temple halls are built against cliffs and in caves above a gorge, within a forest park.

rows.name: Palace of Nine Perfections (Jiucheng Palace)
rows.summary: Remains of a Sui and Tang summer palace in Linyou town: Emperor Wen of Sui built the Renshou Palace here in 593–595, Tang Taizong rebuilt it as the Jiucheng (Nine Perfections) Palace in 631, and a flood destroyed it in 836. Excavations from the late 1980s traced a precinct about 1 km long, including a Sui hall that filled a gap in the record of Chinese palace architecture. The original Liquan Spring stele of 632, composed by Wei Zheng and written by Ouyang Xun and long admired as a model of standard-script calligraphy, is kept in the Linyou County Museum.

rows.name: Qingfeng Gorge National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in a Qinling gorge near Taochuan in Taibai County, with dense forest, streams and the Qingfeng Waterfall. The area keeps traces of Quaternary glaciation.

rows.name: Red River Valley Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in Yingtou town, Mei County, on the north slopes of the Qinling below the main peak of Mount Taibai. Paths lead up a wooded valley past streams, small temples and waterfalls, among them the Doumu Falls.

rows.name: Shuicheng Three Kingdoms Town
rows.summary: A modern tourist town at Caijiapo in southern Qishan County, built in old style around canals and ponds on a Three Kingdoms theme. Its period-style streets hold shops and food stalls, so it suits a relaxed stroll rather than heritage sightseeing.

rows.name: Taiping Temple Pagoda, Qishan
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda built in 1088 under the Northern Song, about 28 m tall, the sole survivor of Taiping Temple in Qishan town. It stands at the centre of the Taiping Pagoda street block, a leisure street of local crafts and food such as Qishan saozi noodles and shadow-puppet carving.

rows.name: Temple of the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Culture Scenic Area)
rows.summary: A temple to the Duke of Zhou, the royal regent who helped consolidate the early Zhou kingdom, at the foot of Fenghuang Hill north-west of Qishan town; its present halls date from the Ming and Qing dynasties. The hill's southern slope is the Zhougong Temple archaeological site, where excavations in the 2000s found large Western Zhou tombs thought to belong to the Duke of Zhou's family and more than 11,000 fragments of oracle bones. The temple is now part of the Zhou Culture Scenic Area, marketed as China·Zhouyuan, which adds a modern Zhou-themed town where staged shows recreate Zhou rites and scenes from the Investiture of the Gods legend.

rows.name: Tomb of Li Maozhen, Prince of Qin
rows.summary: The tombs of Li Maozhen (856–924), a late-Tang warlord who ruled the state of Qi from Fengxiang and was made Prince of Qin in the year he died, and of his wife Lady Liu: two separate tombs in one precinct, excavated in 1999 and 2001. A spirit way lined with stone figures leads to the mounds, and both burial chambers can be entered; the wife's tomb ends in a gateway of carved brick imitating timber architecture. A small exhibition covers Li's life.

rows.name: Tongtianhe National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of wooded mountains and streams in the Qinling range of northern Feng County, in Tangzang town. It is promoted for a high-mountain 'stone forest' of rock pillars.

rows.name: Xiaozai Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple complex on Douji Hill at Fengzhou, facing the old town of Fengzhou across the river. Its name, 'temple of dispelling disaster', comes from a local tradition that Emperor Xuanzong of Tang prayed here while fleeing the An Lushan rebellion.

rows.name: Yongcheng Site and Tomb of Duke Jing of Qin
rows.summary: Yongcheng, in present-day Fengxiang, was the capital of the state of Qin for more than two centuries from 677 BC; its walled city, palace and temple sites and the cemetery of the Qin dukes lie mostly beneath farmland. The visitable part is the Baoji Museum of Pre-Qin Mausoleums at Nanzhihui, built over Tomb 1, the tomb of Duke Jing of Qin (died 537 BC). Excavated between 1977 and 1986, the tomb is a pit about 300 m long and 24 m deep, described as the largest pre-Qin tomb yet excavated, and contained 186 human sacrifices.

rows.name: Zhouyuan Site and Baoji Zhouyuan Museum
rows.summary: The Zhouyuan plain at the foot of Mount Qi was the homeland and early capital of the Zhou people and remained a political and ritual centre through the Western Zhou; the site covers about 30 km² across Fufeng and Qishan counties. Excavations since the 1970s have uncovered palace foundations at Fengchu and Zhaochen, hoards of inscribed bronzes, oracle bones and, in 2024, three rings of Western Zhou city walls. The Baoji Zhouyuan Museum in the core area at Zhaochen village displays bronzes, jades, pottery and building materials from the site.

rows.name: Changqing Huayang Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area around Huayang, an old post town on the Tangluo road across the Qinling that keeps Ming- and Qing-era buildings, beside the Changqing National Nature Reserve at an average altitude of about 1,700 m. The crested ibis, giant panda, golden snub-nosed monkey and takin all live wild in these mountains, and the Qinling Four Treasures Park and its exhibition hall introduce them. The town also has the former headquarters of the Red Army's 25th Army.

rows.name: Crested Ibis Pear Garden
rows.summary: A scenic area on the edge of Yang County town that combines pear orchards with the Crested Ibis Ecological Park, a rescue and breeding centre for the endangered crested ibis. Visitors can watch the birds in a rewilding aviary of nearly 10,000 m²; it was in this county that the last seven known wild crested ibises were found in 1981.

rows.name: Foping Panda Valley
rows.summary: A wildlife park in a forested valley north of Foping town, on a corridor used by the Qinling giant panda population and close to the Foping National Nature Reserve. It contains a training base where more than ten giant pandas, among them the brown panda Qizai, have been prepared for life in the wild, a canyon where troops of golden snub-nosed monkeys roam, and an enclosure of golden pheasants and other pheasants.

rows.name: Former Site of National Northwest Associated University
rows.name_zh: 国立西北联合大学旧址
rows.summary: Three wartime sites of the National Northwest Associated University, which was formed in 1938 from universities that had moved west from Beiping and Tianjin and whose colleges taught in Chenggu County until 1946. They are the law and commerce college's two-storey brick building in Chenggu No. 1 Middle School, the Confucian Temple hall, now inside a school, and two courtyards of the former Catholic cathedral at Guluba, where the engineering college was housed. The Chenggu County Museum opened an exhibition hall on the university in 2019, with the Guluba church bell.

rows.name: Hanjiang Source Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested valley in Ningqiang County where the Yudai River, regarded as the source of the Han River, rises among wooded hills and streams, with mist and ice in winter. Ningqiang keeps a strong Qiang cultural tradition, and Qiang song-and-dance and nuo troupes regularly perform here, including ritual feats such as climbing a ladder of blades.

rows.name: Hanzhong Museum (Gu Hantai)
rows.summary: Hanzhong's city museum occupies Gu Hantai, the raised terrace where Liu Bang is said to have lived as King of Han before founding the Han dynasty, crowned by the Wangjiang Tower. Its prize exhibit is the Shimen Thirteen Inscriptions, Han and Northern Wei carvings such as the Ode to Shimen that were cut from the cliffs in and around the Baoxie road's Stone Gate tunnel before a reservoir flooded it in the early 1970s, and are treasured as masterpieces of Chinese calligraphy. Other galleries cover the plank roads across the Qinling, Han-era Hanzhong and finds from Song tombs.

rows.name: Juehuang Hall, Liangma Temple
rows.summary: The Juehuang Hall of Liangma Temple, a five-bay brick-and-timber hall with a hip-and-gable roof and double tiers of bracket sets, built in 1261 under the Yuan dynasty. It is the only Yuan-era building surviving in Hanzhong's counties and is of interest mainly to lovers of early Chinese timber architecture.

rows.name: Kaiming Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 13-storey brick pagoda about 27 m tall in Yang County town, built in the Tang dynasty in the early 8th century and repaired under the Southern Song, and regarded as the oldest brick pagoda in southern Shaanxi. Each face of every storey has a Buddha niche flanked by two small carved pagodas, 52 niches and 104 pagodas in all, and bells hang from the corners.

rows.name: Lingyan Temple, Lueyang
rows.summary: A temple of Tang origin on Yuwen Hill above the east bank of the Jialing River just south of Lueyang town, with halls built into two natural caves, now a museum of more than 140 inscribed steles and cliff carvings. Its treasure is the Fuge Song, a cliff inscription of 172 AD in Han clerical script celebrating the rebuilding of a plank road and one of the 'three Han odes', which was cut from its original site on the west bank of the Jialing and moved here in 1979. A 1.5 km cliff walkway with glass sections opened behind the temple in 2024.

rows.name: Liping National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Daba and Micang mountains near the Sichuan border south of Hanzhong, with primeval forest, gorges and waterfalls along the Yudai and Xiliu rivers and extensive stands of Bashan pine. Its best-known sight is Longlin ('Dragon Scale') Mountain, a reddish ridge whose rock is packed with fossil nautiloids (Sinoceras) more than 400 million years old.

rows.name: Longtou Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain resort in the Micang range on the Sichuan border south of Hanzhong, on limestone riddled with caves and sinkholes, with viewpoints and sights such as Hanwang Terrace, Fairy Cave and the Longtou waterfall. A cableway climbs to the ridge, where there are cliff walkways and a glass skywalk, and there is a ski area in winter.

rows.name: Luojiaba Old Town
rows.summary: A small market town at the head of the Muma River, at the northern foot of the Micang Mountains, whose old riverside street has been rebuilt in traditional style. The scenic area also takes in the Huilong Gorge and the restored venue of the Zhongjiagou meeting, a site from the revolutionary period, and the town stages folk performances and food fairs on holidays.

rows.name: Shimen Plank Road Scenic Area
rows.summary: A scenic area at the mouth of the Bao valley, where the Baoxie road, the oldest of the plank roads across the Qinling to Sichuan, came out onto the Hanzhong plain and where the Eastern Han cut the Shimen ('Stone Gate') tunnel through the cliff. The original tunnel was flooded by the Shimen reservoir in the early 1970s and its famous inscriptions moved to the Hanzhong Museum, so visitors see a reconstructed cliff-side plank road, a replica tunnel, the dam and the reservoir, which can be toured by boat.

rows.name: Tomb and Temple of Cai Lun
rows.summary: The burial place of Cai Lun, the Eastern Han court official who presented an improved method of papermaking to the emperor in 105 and was later made Marquis of Longting, the town where his tomb lies. A memorial temple stands in front of the mound, and a paper culture museum beside it shows papermaking by traditional methods.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhang Qian
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhang Qian, the Han envoy whose journeys to Central Asia in the 2nd century BC opened the routes later called the Silk Road, and since 2014 part of the UNESCO World Heritage site 'Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor'. A Han-style memorial hall with exhibitions on his missions leads to the cypress-shaded mound, fronted by a stele put up by the Qing governor Bi Yuan in 1776 and a pair of stone beasts, smashed in 1967 and later pieced together. Scholars of the wartime Northwest Associated University excavated it in 1938 and confirmed it as his tomb.

rows.name: Tomb of Zhuge Liang
rows.summary: The tomb of Zhuge Liang, chancellor of the Shu Han kingdom in the Three Kingdoms period, who asked to be buried below Mount Dingjun after he died on campaign in 234. A walled precinct of Ming and Qing halls, with an opera stage, Ming-dynasty statues of Zhuge Liang flanked by Guan Xing and Zhang Bao, and dozens of inscribed boards and steles, leads to the mound, which is ringed by a white marble balustrade carved with 35 scenes from his life. Ancient cypresses surround it, and a temple fair is held at the Qingming festival.

rows.name: Wuhou Temple, Mian County
rows.summary: The oldest of China's many temples to Zhuge Liang, founded in 263 on the order of the last Shu Han emperor, Liu Shan, near the strategist's burial place below Mount Dingjun. Its Ming and Qing buildings line a long axis from an old opera stage and bell and drum towers to the worship and main halls, where a statue of Zhuge Liang sits among steles carved with poems by writers such as Li Shangyin and Lu You. A centuries-old magnolia in a side courtyard draws visitors when it flowers in March.

rows.name: Wulongdong National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of forested mountains and valleys in Wulongdong town, northern Lueyang County, made up of the Wulong Valley, the Qinglong and Bailong gullies, the Sanfo Temple area and a Di-Qiang folk village. The village has houses built in the style of the Di and Qiang peoples who once lived here, and Qiang dances, bonfire evenings, embroidery and paper-cutting are offered to visitors in the town.

rows.name: Wumen Weir
rows.summary: A working irrigation weir on the Xu River north of Chenggu, said to date back to the Han and named after the five gated intakes at its head; its rock-cut channel through Doushan hill was made under the Yuan and widened under the Ming by heating the stone with fire and cracking it with water. The low weir, 374 m long, still feeds an 8.9 km canal that waters about 7,300 mu (490 ha) of fields, and it is listed, with other historic Hanzhong weirs, as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure.

rows.name: Wuzi Mountain
rows.summary: A wooded hill a little over 10 km south-east of Xixiang town, covered by some 200 hectares of lacebark pine, a rare tree with mottled pale bark. Cliff inscriptions and carved images are scattered over the mountain, among them the characters 'Feifeng Shan' that local legend attributes to the Three Kingdoms general Zhang Fei, and the summit looks out over Xixiang and its valley.

rows.name: Xinghan Shengjing
rows.summary: A modern culture park built in Han-dynasty style around Hanyuan Lake in Hanzhong's Xinghan New Area, with a large Han Culture Museum, the Han Yuefu hall of Han-style music and banquets, a city planning exhibition hall and two streets of shops and restaurants. In the evening a water show, Tian Han Chuanqi, is staged on the lake, and holiday events include Hanfu costume parades.

rows.name: Zhandao Water World
rows.summary: A hillside water park at Daoshuiwan in Wuguanyi town, in the Qinling valleys of Liuba County, with a wave pool, large water slides, a lazy river and children's water play areas, themed on the ancient plank roads of the area. A river-rafting run starts from the same site, and it is a summer outing for families rather than a historic site.

rows.name: Zhang Liang Temple and Zibai Mountain
rows.summary: A large Ming and Qing temple complex at the south-eastern foot of Zibai Mountain in the Qinling, dedicated to Zhang Liang, the strategist who helped Liu Bang found the Han dynasty and who, by tradition, retired here as a recluse. Its twelve parts climb from a memorial archway and bridge through gate halls, a Hall of the Three Pure Ones and garden courtyards to a pavilion reached by a steep stairway, and it is one of the largest and best-preserved temples to Zhang Liang in China. The scenic area also takes in Zibai Mountain behind it, a national forest park whose karst summit, reached by cableway, has grassy sinkhole meadows at up to about 2,600 m.

rows.name: Zhiguo Temple
rows.summary: A temple west of Yang County town whose surviving building is a two-storey Ming sutra library roofed in yellow and green glazed tiles. It was built after a local monk, Zhiguo, cured the eye disease of the Wanli emperor's mother in 1584, in return for which the emperor sent a Buddhist canon of 6,780 scrolls and funds for a library to house it.

rows.name: Danjiang River Rafting
rows.summary: A commercial rafting trip on the Dan River (Danjiang) at Danfeng, in which visitors drift in rafts down a stretch of the river valley between the Qinling hills. It is a warm-season activity that suits families and groups wanting a few hours on the water, and it can be combined with Dihua Ancient Town upstream.

rows.name: Dihua Ancient Town
rows.summary: A scenic area opened in 2014 at Dihua, an old post station on the Shangyu road about 15 km west of Danfeng and the home village of the novelist Jia Pingwa. Its two streets are Song–Jin Street, whose paving marks the 12th-century border between the Song and Jin, and Qingfeng Street, the old village street restyled after his novel The Shaanxi Opera; the restored Erlang Temple is described as Shaanxi's only surviving Jin-dynasty building. There is also a museum of Jia's work near his old family home, and wide lotus ponds that are lit up for night visits.

rows.name: Jinsi Gorge (Jinsixia)
rows.summary: A system of narrow, steep-walled limestone gorges on the southern side of the Qinling in Shangnan County, made up of the White Dragon, Black Dragon and Green Dragon gorges, Shiyan Stockade and the Danjiang source area, with a combined gorge length of 20.5 km. Streams run through dense forest between the cliffs, and the area is rich in plants and wildlife. It was rated a national 5A scenic area in 2015 and is also a national geopark, national forest park and national water park.

rows.name: Manchuan Ancient Town (Manchuanguan)
rows.summary: An old trading town at the south-eastern tip of Shaanxi on the border with Hubei, which grew from the Eastern Jin onwards as a river-and-road transfer point between the Qin lands to the north and Chu to the south. Its core is a row of three Qing guild halls begun in 1881 – the Mule Caravan Guild Hall, the Northern Guild Hall and the Wuchang Guild Hall – covering more than 12,000 m², and the mule guild's paired opera stages are finely built and carved; the Mule Caravan Guild Hall is a national heritage site.

rows.name: Moon Cave (Yueliang Dong)
rows.summary: A limestone show cave halfway up a hillside above the Jinqian River in Yangdi town, south-western Shanyang County, at the heart of a scenic area that also takes in the Jiashi Gorge. Local legend gives the cave nine levels, of which four, with more than 1.5 km of passages, have been opened, winding like a maze past stalactites and other formations; the Tianpeng Shanzhai scenic area lies about 15 km to the west.

rows.name: Muwang National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of 3,616 ha in the far west of Zhen'an County, designated in 2003, with old-growth forest, high-mountain wetland, rhododendron groves, peaks and rock formations. It has four areas – Sihaiping with gorges, waterfalls and alpine meadow, Shuangtouma with a long bare-rock 'stone waterfall' and rhododendrons, Cigou with its rhododendron belt, and Yingzuifeng (Eagle-Beak Peak) – and is home to protected animals such as takin, golden eagle, black bear and giant salamander; the rhododendrons flower in spring.

rows.name: Niubeiliang National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park on the main ridge of the Qinling in Zhashui County, named after its ox-back-shaped summit and rising from about 1,000 m to 2,802 m. Its zones run from Lingniu (Takin) Valley, with streams, pools and waterfalls, up through Qinling fir and rhododendron belts to alpine meadow and Quaternary glacial landforms; the rhododendrons flower in May and the woods turn red in autumn. The park lies within the Niubeiliang UNESCO biosphere reserve and was rated 4A in 2013.

rows.name: Qinling Jiangshan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forest scenic area of about 2,400 ha in Yaoshi town in the north of Shangzhou District, near the source of the Dan River, with more than 90% forest cover. Its sights include a glass suspension bridge, the Doucao waterfall, a patch of karst 'stone teeth' rare in the Qinling, and the reputed retreat of the Four Hoary Recluses of Mount Shang from the early Han.

rows.name: Taohua Valley, Zhulinguan
rows.summary: A valley at Zhulinguan near where Shaanxi, Henan and Hubei meet, developed around soil-and-water-conservation works and described by the city government as Shangluo's largest peach-blossom viewing area. It is a national soil-and-water-conservation demonstration park and national water park, and was rated 4A in early 2026; spring, when the peach trees flower, is the time to go.

rows.name: Tayun Mountain
rows.summary: A pagoda-shaped peak in Chaiping town, south-west of Zhen'an town, crowned by a group of Daoist temple buildings more than 500 years old. The Guanyin hall on the Golden Summit stands on a rock pinnacle with sheer drops on three sides; a cableway, a glass bridge and swings have been added, and the peak is a noted spot for seas of cloud.

rows.name: Tianpeng Mountain Stronghold (Tianpeng Shanzhai)
rows.summary: A mountain scenic area in south-western Shanyang County, named after a 6 km gorge between the Yintai and Dingjia ridges and a stone stronghold (shanzhai) about 300 m long, from the Ming–Qing period, on the Yintai ridge above it. Paths follow the gorge past pools, waterfalls and features such as a water-curtain cave and a narrow 'one-line sky' cleft, and climb to the old stronghold walls; the area has been developed for tourism since the early 2010s.

rows.name: Tianzhu Mountain (Shanyang)
rows.summary: A national forest park of steep crags and pinnacles about 30 km south-east of Shanyang town, rising to 2,074 m; its best-known sights are the free-standing rock pillar called Tianzhu Moxiao, the knife-edge Daobeiliang ridge and seas of cloud after rain. The mountain has long been a centre of Daoism, and of the dozen or so temples built over the centuries the Shuangfeng Daoist temple and Yungai Temple survive in good condition.

rows.name: Yangchengyi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A themed scenic area in Fushui town, just east of Shangnan town, built around Yangcheng post station on the old Shangyu road and the late-Ming rebel leader Li Zicheng, who is said to have camped in the nearby hills. It has three parts: a post-station complex rebuilt on the old site; the Chuangwang Zhai hilltop stronghold themed on Li Zicheng, where a staged horseback battle show is performed; and a large tea-garden park where visitors can try picking tea.

rows.name: Yungaisi Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old market town on the river 18 km west of Zhen'an town, named after Yungai Temple, a once-large monastery rebuilt in the Ming and Qing dynasties. Its front, back and 'half' streets run for more than 1.2 km between some 40 courtyard houses in a mix of Huizhou and Sichuan styles, mostly from the Ming–Qing period or later and restored since 2013. The temple, the old streets and a set of carved cliff inscriptions on the hill nearby are provincial protected sites.

rows.name: Zhashui Karst Caves
rows.summary: A cluster of more than a hundred limestone caves in Xialiang town, Zhashui County, set among gorges and waterfalls. The main show caves are Foye Cave, whose Zhuanjinglou section is crowded with stalactites, stalagmites and formations likened to figures and animals, and the corridor-shaped Tiandong (Heaven Cave) next to it, where the formations are within arm's reach.

rows.name: Chenlu Ancient Town
rows.summary: A hillside pottery town south-east of central Tongchuan, the one Yaozhou-ware kiln centre that kept making ceramics after the Song and Yuan dynasties, where by local tradition the kiln fires have never gone out. Houses and cave dwellings are stacked in tiers up the slopes, with walls built of old pottery jars and lanes paved with potsherds, and workshops let visitors try making pots.

rows.name: Chongxing Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey hexagonal brick pagoda about 16 m high, built in the Northern Song and the only surviving part of Chongxing Temple, known locally as the Tongchuan Pagoda. It stands in the grounds of the Yintai District cultural centre at the foot of Yintai hill in the old centre of Tongchuan.

rows.name: Huaxi Valley, Yijun
rows.summary: A flower-garden park on the edge of Yijun town, planted with herbaceous peonies, a medicinal-herb valley and bamboo, with windmills, a play castle and other attractions for children, a 100 m slide and a toboggan run of about 1 km. It holds peony-season and beer and food festivals, and suits families.

rows.name: Jinsuoguan Stone Forest
rows.summary: A sandstone landscape in the hills of Jinsuoguan, north of central Tongchuan, where rockfalls and weathering have left a maze of pillars, cliffs and boulders, unusual on the plateau north of the Wei River. Paths wind through the rocks, and a cableway, a glass suspension bridge, a cliff swing and a zip line add thrill rides.

rows.name: Shende Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal brick pagoda about 35 m tall below the Bushou plateau on the northern edge of Yaozhou town, built in the Song dynasty and repaired under the Ming and Qing. It is the main survivor of a site that held a Northern Wei monastery, the Tang Shende Temple and later a Ming academy, and its eaves rest on brick imitations of timber bracket sets.

rows.name: Xishan Shengjing
rows.summary: A wooded valley of red Danxia sandstone cliffs at Zhaojin, said to be the landscape behind Travellers among Mountains and Streams, the famous painting by the Northern Song artist Fan Kuan. A former coal-mining area that has been replanted, it has mountain paths, a cableway to a viewing platform named after the painter, a campsite and a hotel, and is known for red autumn leaves and frozen waterfalls in winter.

rows.name: Yanchang Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A hexagonal Song-dynasty brick pagoda with close-set eaves, the only building left standing at Yanchang Temple, which by legend was founded by a Northern Wei princess who modelled ten thousand Buddha figures here, hence its other name, Wanfo (Ten Thousand Buddhas) Temple. The temple halls were pulled down by troops in 1940, and its Northern Wei stone pagoda and two carved steles were moved to Yaowang Mountain. It is mainly for those already visiting Yaozhou's other pagodas and temples.

rows.name: Yaowang Mountain
rows.summary: A temple-covered hill just east of Yaozhou town where the Tang physician Sun Simiao, revered as the 'King of Medicine', is said to have lived in retreat, with Jin- and Yuan-era halls, Yuan murals and a memorial hall on his life and on Chinese medicine. Its stone carvings are regarded as China's largest collection of Buddhist statue steles from the Northern Dynasties, Sui and Tang, with more than 100 steles and about 45 cliff-carved figures, beside steles of Sun Simiao's prescriptions carved in 1572. A temple fair listed as national intangible heritage runs for about ten days around the second day of the second lunar month.

rows.name: Yaozhou Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Yaozhou's Confucian temple, founded in the Northern Song and rebuilt and repaired under the Yuan, Ming and Qing, keeps its Lingxing Gate, Ji Gate, side halls and a seven-bay Dacheng Hall whose roof frame preserves Jin and Yuan building features. It houses the Yaozhou District Museum, with excavated finds from the district shown in the side halls, and stands beside Wenmiao Street, a shopping and food street rebuilt in Tang–Song style.

rows.name: Yaozhou Kiln Museum
rows.summary: The site museum of the Yaozhou kilns at Huangbao, which from the Tang to the Yuan made what is generally regarded as the finest northern celadon, prized in the Northern Song for its olive-green glaze over carved and later moulded decoration. Besides galleries of excavated ceramics, two halls shelter excavated kiln and workshop remains, including a Tang site where sancai three-colour wares were made, and there are demonstrations of traditional pottery-making.

rows.name: Yijun Grottoes
rows.summary: A group of small Buddhist cave temples and cliff carvings from the Northern Dynasties to the Tang scattered across Yijun County, among them Huashiya, whose earliest caves were cut in the early 6th century, and the Fudi Grotto. Fudi, cut in 535 under the Western Wei in a cliff on an island in Fudi Lake east of Yijun town, is known for carvings that place Buddhist and Taoist figures in the same niche.

rows.name: Yuhua Palace
rows.summary: A forested valley in the north of Tongchuan where Emperor Taizong of Tang completed the Yuhua summer palace in 647; it was turned into a monastery in 651, and the pilgrim-monk Xuanzang spent his last years here translating Buddhist scriptures. Little of the palace survives above ground, but the scenic area, also a national forest park, has the site of the Sucheng Court, a Xuanzang memorial hall, lakes and woodland walks, and a ski slope in winter.

rows.name: Zhaojin and Xiangshan
rows.summary: Zhaojin, in the red Danxia sandstone hills west of Tongchuan, was the centre of the Shaanxi–Gansu Border revolutionary base set up in the early 1930s by Communist leaders including Liu Zhidan and Xie Zichang; its sites include the cliff caves of Xuejiazhai, used as Red Army strongholds, a memorial hall on the base's history first opened in 2004 and rebuilt in 2013, and an immersive light show on the Xuejiazhai battle. The scenic area also takes in Daxiangshan, a Buddhist mountain about 12 km to the north-east with a temple said to date from the 4th century and linked by legend to Princess Miaoshan, who became the bodhisattva Guanyin.

rows.name: Chongshou Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 13-storey square brick pagoda with close-set eaves, 45 m tall, built in 1096 and known in Pucheng as the North Pagoda. Chongshou Temple itself has long gone, and the pagoda stands on its own in the middle of the county town.

rows.name: Daxiang Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A solid Song-dynasty brick pagoda with 13 close-set eaves, 28 m tall, at Yangjiawa village south-east of Heyang town; locals also call it the Longwang Temple Pagoda. The temple was destroyed during the war against Japan, and the square tower now leans more than 5 degrees to the north-east.

rows.name: Fawang Temple, Hancheng
rows.summary: A temple in Xizhuang town founded in 1022 for Fang Yin, a local healer who by legend used acupuncture to bring about the birth of the future emperor Renzong, treated Emperor Zhenzong and was given the title Fawang. Three Yuan-period halls line its axis, ending in the raised rear hall with glazed ridge beasts, and a small hexagonal brick pagoda in front of the first hall is said to be Fang's tomb. Temple fairs are held at Qingming and twice more in the lunar year.

rows.name: Fengtu Charity Granary
rows.summary: A walled charity granary at Chaoyi, begun in 1882 at the urging of the Qing minister Yan Jingming, a native of the town, after the Guanzhong famine of 1877, and still used to store state grain. Built as a fort within a fort, it has an outer rammed-earth wall and an inner rectangle of about 133 by 83 m whose 58 vaulted storage chambers form the inner wall; Empress Dowager Cixi is said to have called it the 'first granary under heaven'. Twelve small exhibition halls cover grain storage and local history.

rows.name: Former Residence of Yang Hucheng
rows.summary: The house that General Yang Hucheng, commander of the Northwestern Army, built in his home county in 1934, two years before he and Zhang Xueliang detained Chiang Kai-shek in the Xi'an Incident. The traditional south-facing courtyard house has a main east courtyard and a garden in the west courtyard, and it has been open as a memorial hall since 1983.

rows.name: Fuping Ceramic Art Village (FLICAM)
rows.summary: A ceramics-themed village on the northern edge of Fuping town, built around the FuLe International Ceramic Art Museums (FLICAM). Each pavilion is devoted to ceramic artists from one country or region and shows work they made during residencies here: the French and Scandinavian pavilions opened first in 2005, followed by Australasia, North America and, in 2016, Ukraine.

rows.name: Great Wall of Wei (Huayin section)
rows.summary: Remains of the rammed-earth wall that the Warring States kingdom of Wei built from the 350s BC along its western border with Qin, running from the foot of Mount Hua north through Dali, Chengcheng and Heyang to the Yellow River in Hancheng. More than 50 stretches survive, and in Huayin the best preserved, east of Chengnan village, is about 365 m long and still about 7 m high, with traces of a fort and a beacon tower.

rows.name: Guandi Temple, Liuzhi
rows.summary: A temple to Guan Yu, the deified Three Kingdoms general, in Liuzhi village, founded in 1535 and rebuilt in 1619, 1699 and 1787. An offering hall with glazed ridge ornaments and elaborate bracket sets stands before the main hall, flanked by small halls to the goddess Niangniang and the physician Hua Tuo. The village school used the temple after 1949, and it was repaired in 2015 and 2018.

rows.name: Heyang Confucian Temple
rows.summary: The Confucian temple of Heyang county town, of which three main buildings survive: the five-bay Dacheng Hall, rebuilt in 1369, the Minglun Hall and the Zunjing Pavilion of 1610. The pavilion, a three-storey Ming timber building under double hip-and-gable eaves, reopened in 2026 after a year-long restoration, and the temple grounds house the Heyang County Museum.

rows.name: Huayan Temple, Mazhuang
rows.summary: A small Buddhist temple in Mazhuang village, Longmen town, rebuilt in the Ming and Qing and later used as a primary school. An offering hall and a main hall, both under overhanging gable roofs with elaborate bracket sets, stand between east and west side halls, and a conservation project for the buildings was approved in 2019.

rows.name: Jingjin Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey square brick pagoda, 33 m tall, in the courtyard of the county cultural centre on East Street in Chengcheng town. It was built with Jingjin Temple under the Tang emperor Suzong in the mid-8th century and repaired in 1047. The temple was destroyed during the war against Japan, leaving the hollow pagoda with its imitation-timber brick brackets and arched openings on every storey.

rows.name: Liangdai Village Rui State Site Museum
rows.name_zh: 梁带村芮国遗址博物馆
rows.summary: The site museum of the cemetery of Rui, a small Zhou-dynasty state on the Yellow River conquered by Qin in the 7th century BC, where excavations from 2004 found more than 1,300 tombs and 64 chariot-and-horse pits. Opened in 2018, its four galleries show about 800 bronzes, gold ornaments and jades from the 26,000 objects recovered, arranged to follow the order of excavation.

rows.name: Lingao Lake
rows.summary: A reservoir lake of about 2,200 mu (150 ha) in the loess uplands of northern Weinan, designated a national wetland park and promoted by Baishui county as the 'Lingao Lake International Slow City'. A road and lakeside paths ring the water, with viewing platforms and a sandy beach, and the scenic area extends to the planted forests of Fangshan.

rows.name: Longmen Iron and Steel Works
rows.summary: The working plant of Shaanxi Longmen Iron and Steel at Longmen, opened to visitors as an industrial tourism site on the theme of how steel is made. Guided visits in hard hats take in the company exhibition hall, the ore yard, the ironworks, the converter steel plant, the rolling mill where red-hot billets are drawn out into strip, and the production control centre, and they suit older children and anyone curious about heavy industry.

rows.name: Luoshan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A square brick pagoda on the eastern peak of Ruluo Hill above Dongma village, which its style places in the Tang dynasty. Seven and a half of its original nine storeys survive, about 30 m high, while only traces of the temple around it remain. The wooden stairs inside were destroyed in the 1860s.

rows.name: Pucheng Examination Hall
rows.summary: A Qing-dynasty examination hall in the Huaiyuanli old-lanes district of Pucheng, where candidates from the county sat the imperial civil-service examinations. It is now the Pucheng Qing Dynasty Examination Hall Museum, on the same lane as the former residence of General Yang Hucheng.

rows.name: Puzhao Temple, Hancheng
rows.summary: A village Buddhist temple at the south corner of the old Wucun fort, founded in 1316 under the Yuan and restored in 1823. Its main hall is an original Yuan building, five bays wide under a single hip-and-gable roof of glazed tiles, surrounded by smaller shrines, a Guanyin cave and old steles. Since the late 1990s endangered Yuan buildings from elsewhere in Hancheng have been moved into its grounds for safekeeping, among them the Sanqing Hall of Ziyun Temple.

rows.name: Qiachuan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A national scenic area of reed beds, lotus ponds and warm springs on the Yellow River floodplain east of Heyang. Black storks, swans and dozens of other bird species use the wetland, and among its seven warm springs the Chunü ('Maiden') Spring is known for the sand that boils up from its bed beneath floating bathers. The area is linked to 'Guanju', a poem in the Book of Songs that is said to have been set here.

rows.name: Qiaoling Mausoleum
rows.summary: The mausoleum of the Tang emperor Ruizong (Li Dan), whose burial chamber was cut into Feng Mountain north-west of Pucheng, with a walled precinct built around the hill. Its long spirit way is lined with sculpture regarded, with that of Qianling, as among the finest of any Tang tomb: carved pillars, a pair of winged xiezhi beasts, ostriches in relief, horses, officials and, at the south gate, a pair of lions.

rows.name: Qiaoshangqiao (Bridge on a Bridge)
rows.summary: A two-tier stone arch bridge over the Chishui River at Chishui town. The lower bridge was built in 1667, and when silt had raised the riverbed a second bridge was laid on top of it in 1832; the lower one stayed buried until sand dredging in the 1980s exposed it again. The bridge is 70 m long with nine arches, and four arches of the lower bridge are now visible.

rows.name: Qing'an Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey square brick pagoda, 30 m tall, in Jiaoxie town north-east of Weinan, also called the Laihua Pagoda. First built under the Tang and repaired in the Northern Song, it was brought down by the great Jiajing earthquake of the 1550s and rebuilt to the old design in 1558. Brick brackets imitating timber survive under the eaves of the lowest two storeys.

rows.name: Sanqing Hall of Ziyun Temple
rows.summary: The main hall of Ziyun Temple, a Taoist temple founded in 1270, which was moved in 2001–03 from a middle-school campus in Hancheng into the compound of Puzhao Temple in the old fortified village of Wucun. The three-bay hall stands on a raised brick base with a terrace in front and a hip-and-gable roof with glazed ridges. Of the temple's surviving halls it is the only one that keeps its Yuan-dynasty form.

rows.name: Shaohua Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park on the northern slopes of the Qinling Mountains south-east of Huazhou, named Shaohua ('Lesser Hua') as the smaller neighbour of Mount Hua further east. Paths climb wooded gorges such as Shimen Gorge to the hillside Qianlong Temple, near which a glass-floored walkway runs along a cliff.

rows.name: Shenlou of Chengcheng City God Temple
rows.summary: The only surviving building of Chengcheng's City God Temple: a Ming tower, also called the music tower, rebuilt in 1582 on a high terrace. A three-bay central tower under triple eaves is flanked by two smaller one-bay towers with cross-shaped hip-and-gable roofs.

rows.name: Sites of the Weihua Uprising
rows.summary: Sites of the Weihua Uprising, an armed rising led by the Chinese Communist Party in Weinan and Hua counties in 1928 and put down by Nationalist forces that June. The main site is the former primary school at Gaotang, once a Taoist temple and academy, where the rebels' military committee and headquarters were based; a memorial hall opened there in 1988, with a martyrs' cemetery to its south. The listing also covers a Qing-era temple at Dongyang used by the party's East Shaanxi committee and a village shrine where Liu Zhidan's guerrillas were active.

rows.name: Tailing Mausoleum
rows.summary: The mausoleum of the Tang emperor Xuanzong (Li Longji), who chose the site himself and was buried here in 763 with Empress Yuanxian, its burial chamber cut into Jinsu Mountain north-east of Pucheng. More than 30 of the stone officials, envoys, horses, ostriches and pillars that once lined its spirit way survive, beside a Qing stele that calls him 'Yuanzong' to avoid the Kangxi Emperor's personal name. The tomb of the court eunuch Gao Lishi, its only satellite burial, lies nearby.

rows.name: Temple and Tomb of Cangjie
rows.summary: A temple and tomb honouring Cangjie, the legendary inventor of Chinese writing, laid out with the temple in front and his walled tomb mound behind. Along the axis stand a screen wall, gate, offering hall, main hall and a Yuan-style rear hall, flanked by an opera stage and bell and drum towers among dozens of ancient cypresses, and a stele carved with 28 'bird-track' characters attributed to Cangjie stands inside. A ceremony for Cangjie is held here every year at the Guyu solar term in April.

rows.name: Temple and Tomb of Sima Qian
rows.summary: The shrine and tomb of Sima Qian, the Western Han historian who wrote the Records of the Grand Historian, on a ridge above the old Xiayang ferry on the west bank of the Yellow River at Zhichuan. A stone path climbs to an offering hall and a rear hall rebuilt in 1126 under the Northern Song, behind which stands his round brick tomb, crowned by an old cypress and fronted by a stele of 1776 by the Shaanxi governor Bi Yuan.

rows.name: Temple of Yu the Great, Hancheng
rows.summary: A small village temple to Yu the Great, the legendary tamer of floods, at Zhouyuan on the eastern edge of Hancheng, founded in 1301 according to an inscription on its offering-hall pillars and rebuilt in 1579. Two halls survive, an offering hall and a three-bay main hall, which keeps Qing murals, wooden plaques and painted clay statues of Yu and the Tang general Guo Ziyi.

rows.name: Tong Pass
rows.summary: Tongguan, the fortified pass first built in 196 AD where the Wei River flows into the Yellow River, guarded the eastern approach to the Guanzhong plain and its capitals. Its walled town was demolished for the Sanmenxia Dam reservoir around 1960, but remains of the Han and Ming walled towns, the Ming Lower South Gate and the old Shuipo Lane survive. Since 2011 a tourism development on the hill to the east has added squares, old-style shopping streets and a rebuilt Shanhe Yilan gate tower, which since 2018 has housed the Tongguan County Museum.

rows.name: Weinan Grape Industrial Park
rows.summary: A large table-grape estate at Xiagui in northern Linwei district, run as a farm park with a 10,000 m vine-covered arcade, rain-shelter vineyards, big greenhouses, a winery and a European-style garden. It is busiest in summer, when the arcade is in leaf and visitors come to pick grapes, and it holds a grape music season each July.

rows.name: Weinan Museum
rows.summary: The city museum of Weinan, rated a national second-grade museum, on Letian Street in the west of the city. Its permanent exhibition, 'Yu Hua Xiang Yi: the Story of Weinan', follows the eastern Guanzhong region from prehistory to modern times through finds from across the prefecture.

rows.name: Weinan Taohuayuan Folk Culture Park
rows.summary: A folk-culture park built in the Linghe river valley south of Weinan, laid out in Ming–Qing Guanzhong style with timber courtyard houses, a gate tower, pavilions, a pagoda and a group of temples. It has a food street, traditional craft workshops and guesthouses, and suits a half-day outing from the city.

rows.name: Xiyue Temple
rows.summary: The temple where emperors sacrificed to the god of Mount Hua, the Western Sacred Peak, founded under the Western Han in 134 BC near the mountain and moved to this site in the Eastern Han. Its Ming and Qing buildings stand in a walled compound almost 500 m long with corner towers, where a series of gates and courtyards with a stone archway and stele pavilions lead to the nine-bay Haoling Hall, and it is often called the 'Forbidden City of Shaanxi'.

rows.name: Yaotou Kilns
rows.summary: An old pottery village in Yaotou town whose folk kilns, traced by the Ming county gazetteer to the Tang dynasty and at their height under the Ming and Qing, made everyday black-glazed stoneware such as bowls, jars and basins, a craft potters still practise here. The site of about 4 km² keeps 129 kilns from the Ming, Qing and Republican periods, 78 workshops and 75 old houses, and the local firing technique has been national intangible cultural heritage since 2006.

rows.name: Yuhuang Houtu Temple, Hancheng
rows.summary: A village temple at Xiyuan in Longmen town dedicated to the Jade Emperor and the earth goddess Houtu, founded in the Yuan dynasty and rebuilt in 1463 and 1820. Laid out on three parallel axes, it has an opera stage facing the central offering and main halls, with halls to the god Xuanwu and to the three sworn brothers of the Three Kingdoms on either side. The open-sided offering hall keeps clear Yuan-period features.

rows.name: Zhonghuajun Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A culture-themed leisure park on the Jingshan plateau on the Fuping–Yanliang border, built around the legend that the Yellow Emperor cast his bronze tripods at Jingshan. It has a food street, a 'guochao' quarter of cafés and craft-experience shops, a hanfu shop, an inn, night markets and a recreated village of an ancient tribe, with iron-flower fire displays, Han–Tang dance shows and themed holiday programmes, and it suits families and evening visits.

rows.name: Bailucang
rows.summary: A themed leisure town on the White Deer Plain (Bailuyuan) south-east of Xi'an, opened in April 2017 and built around the life and folk customs of the plain in the early Republican era of the 1910s. It is a modern development rather than a historic village, with Republican-style streets, a waterside lane and some 300 snack and food stalls, and suits an easy half-day close to the city.

rows.name: Banpo Museum
rows.summary: The excavated site of a Neolithic village of the Yangshao culture, lived in roughly 6,800 to 5,300 years ago, on the east bank of the Chan River in eastern Xi'an. Discovered in 1953 and excavated in five seasons from 1954 to 1957, it is covered by China's first museum built on a Neolithic site, opened in 1958, where a large hall shelters the foundations of round and square houses, storage pits, kilns and the village's defensive ditch, and galleries show painted pottery and stone tools.

rows.name: Bayun Pagoda
rows.summary: Bayun Pagoda, also called Ruiguang Pagoda, was begun in 708 under the Tang and stands in the south-west of Zhouzhi county town. It is a square brick pagoda of close-set eaves that once had 13 storeys, of which 11 survive. It makes a short stop on the way to Louguantai or the Heihe valley.

rows.name: Caotang Temple
rows.summary: Caotang Temple, at the north foot of Guifeng Peak, grew from the garden where the Later Qin ruler housed the Kuchean monk Kumārajīva from 401, and where he led the translation of Buddhist scriptures that laid the foundations of East Asian Madhyamaka thought. His relics rest in a small Tang-dynasty stupa, carved in imitation of a timber pavilion from marble and stone of eight colours and known as the Eight-Treasure Jade Stupa. Restored from 1952 and an active monastery again since 1984, the temple is laid out in five courtyards with a memorial hall to Kumārajīva.

rows.name: Chanba National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park on the floodplain of the Wei River at the northern edge of Xi'an, close to Weiyang Lake. It offers an easy walk among lakes and wetland planting rather than a sight in its own right.

rows.name: Chongyang Palace
rows.summary: Chongyang Palace in Zu'an town is one of the three ancestral temples of the Quanzhen school of Taoism, on the spot where its 12th-century founder Wang Chongyang practised and was buried. The vast medieval complex was almost entirely lost and today's halls were largely rebuilt from the 1980s, but the Zu'an stele forest preserves dozens of inscribed steles, most of them large Yuan-dynasty tablets on the school's patriarchs and imperial edicts carved in Chinese and the Phags-pa script. Among them are inscriptions in the hand of the calligrapher Zhao Mengfu and portrait steles of Wang Chongyang and his seven disciples.

rows.name: Cuihua Mountain
rows.summary: A national geopark in the Zhongnan range of the Qinling Mountains, south of Xi'an, known for the huge rock blocks and boulder fields left by ancient landslides. Its centrepiece is Tianchi, a lake about 600 m long formed where fallen rock dammed the Taiyi valley, and paths climb from the lake through the landslide debris towards the higher peaks.

rows.name: Daqin Pagoda
rows.summary: This seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda in the Qinling foothills was first recorded in 1065, when the poet Su Dongpo visited it and wrote a poem about the Daqin temple. Daqin was an old Chinese name for the Roman world, and since 2001 some writers have claimed the site as a Tang-dynasty church of the Church of the East, a claim for which there is still no conclusive archaeological evidence. An earthquake in 1556 badly damaged the pagoda and the temple was abandoned; its exterior was repaired in 1999.

rows.name: Duling, Tomb of Emperor Xuan of Han
rows.summary: The mausoleum of the Western Han emperor Xuan, begun in 65 BC on the plateau south-east of Xi'an and used for his burial in 48 BC: a flat-topped pyramid of rammed earth about 29 m high, with the smaller mound of Empress Wang some 575 m to the south-east. The mounds stand in a planted forest park, the Shanglinyuan (Duling) eco-scenic area, where a tree-lined avenue leads to stelae, including the national heritage marker, in a railed enclosure at the foot of the emperor's mound.

rows.name: Eighth Route Army Xi'an Office Memorial Hall
rows.name_zh: 八路军西安办事处纪念馆
rows.summary: This row of brick courtyard houses at Qixianzhuang on Beixin Street served the Chinese Communist Party as a covert liaison post from 1936, first in a rented dental clinic, and from 1937 to 1946 as the Eighth Route Army's open office in Xi'an during the wartime united front with the Nationalists. Its staff sent young volunteers on to Yan'an and bought and shipped supplies to the Communist base area; Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and Deng Xiaoping were among those who worked or stayed here, as did the Canadian doctor Norman Bethune and the American journalist Agnes Smedley. A memorial hall since 1959, it shows the restored offices, radio and cipher rooms and living quarters across four courtyards.

rows.name: Epang Palace
rows.summary: The site of the palace that Qin Shi Huang began in 212 BC and never finished: what survives is the rammed-earth platform of its front hall, more than 1 km long, about 400 m deep and 7–9 m high. Excavations since 2002 have found no trace of the fire said to have destroyed it, and a 2025 dig showed that it was raised over the bed of a former lake. The tree-covered terrace stands in an archaeological site park with lawns, paths and display boards, but there is no museum; the replica palace theme park built beside it in 2000 was demolished in 2013.

rows.name: Erlong Pagoda
rows.summary: On a ridge east of Taiyi town at the foot of the Zhongnan Mountains stands the lower part of an early Tang brick pagoda, square in plan, of which seven storeys of close-set eaves survive. No temple is recorded for it, so villagers call it the Erlong or fengshui pagoda; its top storeys were pulled down for their bricks in the 1960s until the authorities stopped the work, and the remains were strengthened in 2006. Its carved stone finial is kept in Wujiagou village to the north.

rows.name: Fenghao Site and Western Zhou Chariot Pits
rows.summary: The remains of Feng and Hao, the twin capitals of the Western Zhou dynasty on either bank of the Feng River until 771 BC, which now lie under farmland and villages south-west of Xi'an. The part visitors can see is the Fenghao Site Chariot Pit Exhibition Hall at Zhangjiapo in Mawang, on the west bank, where an excavated burial pit holds two wooden chariots with the skeletons of their six horses and of a driver.

rows.name: Gongshu Hall
rows.summary: From outside, Gongshu Hall in Qi village looks like an ordinary Ming–Qing farmhouse hall, but inside is a rare survival of fine carpentry said to date from the Yongle era (1403–1424). Miniature multi-storey pavilions and towers, made at about one-thirtieth of real size, sit above coffered ceilings while carved shrine cabinets line the walls, and the hall is considered the only surviving built example of the 'heavenly palace pavilions' described in the Song building manual Yingzao Fashi. Only the main hall, of about 100 m², remains; a small woodwork museum was set up here in 2014, and a Chinese–French team has studied and conserved the painted woodwork since 2017.

rows.name: Guangren Temple
rows.summary: The only Tibetan Buddhist temple in Shaanxi, built on the Kangxi Emperor's orders in 1703–1705 just inside the north-west corner of Xi'an's city wall to lodge lamas travelling to and from the Qing court. It is an active Gelug monastery, largely rebuilt and enlarged since the 1950s, whose halls line one axis behind a gate bearing a plaque in the Kangxi Emperor's calligraphy, with a Thousand-Armed Guanyin among its images.

rows.name: Guanzhong Folk Art Museum
rows.summary: A privately funded museum at the foot of South Wutai Mountain, built by the collector Wang Yongchao, to which some 40 Ming and Qing courtyard houses from across the Guanzhong plain were moved and re-erected. Besides the houses it shows stone, wood and brick carving, folk crafts and customs, and more than 8,600 carved stone hitching posts set out in rows.

rows.name: Han Chang'an City and Weiyang Palace Site
rows.pinyin: Hàn Cháng'ān Chéng Wèiyāng Gōng Yízhǐ
rows.summary: The site of Chang'an, capital of the Western Han dynasty, whose walled city of about 36 km² lies on the north-western edge of modern Xi'an. Its main palace, Weiyang Palace, first built in 200 BC, is now an open archaeological park where visitors walk over the great rammed-earth platform of the Front Hall and see the foundations of the empress's hall, archives and offices marked out on the ground. The palace site was inscribed in 2014 as part of the Silk Roads World Heritage site.

rows.name: Hancheng Lake Park
rows.summary: A long lakeside park in north-western Xi'an, created from 2006 out of the Tuanjie Reservoir, which had been dug in the 1950s along the old moat of the Han-dynasty capital. Paths run past Han-themed sculpture, a 21.5 m statue of Emperor Wu and the 64 m Dafeng Pavilion, which has small exhibitions inside and views over the lake from the top, and the remains of the Han city's south-east corner are marked in the park.

rows.name: Heihe National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park at the headwaters of the Heihe River on the northern slopes of the Qinling in Zhouzhi County, opened in 2000 and made a national forest park in 2006, covering 7,462 hectares with forest over more than 90 per cent of it. Trails follow clear streams past pools, waterfalls and stretches of old pine, oak and birch forest in an area that forms a corridor for giant pandas, and holes cut for the ancient Tangluo plank road survive on the cliffs.

rows.name: Huayan Temple Pagodas
rows.summary: Two brick pagodas stand on the edge of the Shaoling plateau above the Fanchuan valley, all that survived when Huayan Temple, birthplace of the Huayan school of Buddhism, was destroyed by a landslide in the 18th century. The larger, a seven-storey square pagoda of 642, is the tomb pagoda of the school's founder Dushun; the smaller, hexagonal one honours the fourth patriarch Chengguan, was recorded as rebuilt in 1272 and was moved a short distance in 1986 after another landslide. During that move relics, early Qing sutras and Buddhist images were found inside it.

rows.name: Jingde Pagoda (Baolin Temple Pagoda)
rows.summary: This solid, square brick pagoda of seven storeys is all that remains of Baolin Temple, founded in the early Tang in the Zige valley of the Qinling foothills and destroyed in 1862. An inscribed stone found on its fifth storey in 1988 dates the present pagoda to 1092, in the Northern Song. It suits walkers exploring the valleys south of Huyi.

rows.name: Jinlong Gorge
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area on the northern edge of the Qinling Mountains in Huyi District, west of General Mountain (Jiangjun Shan). A walking route follows the wooded valley upstream past a chain of waterfalls and pools.

rows.name: Kunming Pool Qixi Park
rows.summary: A large lakeside park opened in 2017 on part of the Kunming Pool, the artificial lake that Emperor Wu of Han had dug in his Shanglin hunting park to train a navy, now refilled as part of a water project in Fengdong New City.
