The park is named after the Qixi festival and its legend of the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl, and has lakeside promenades, wetland planting and children's play areas.

rows.name: Lantian Man Site, Gongwangling
rows.summary: At Gongwangling in Lantian County a partial skull of Homo erectus was recovered from the loess in 1964; known as Lantian Man, it was dated in 2015 to about 1.6 million years ago, which would make it the oldest firmly dated Homo erectus fossil in East Asia. Animal bones from the same beds include giant panda, tapir and the elephant-like Stegodon, species now typical of southern China. A small state-run site museum stands at the find spot.

rows.name: Qinglong Temple
rows.summary: In Tang Chang'an, Qinglong Temple was where the master Huiguo taught esoteric Buddhism to the Japanese monk Kūkai, who took the teaching back to Japan in 806, so the temple is revered as a cradle of both Chinese and Japanese esoteric Buddhism. The temple was destroyed in 1086 and forgotten until archaeologists located its site in 1963; halls in Tang style were rebuilt from the 1980s, with memorial halls to Huiguo and Kūkai and a Kūkai monument raised in 1982 together with the four prefectures of Shikoku. Cherry trees brought from Japan in 1986 draw crowds when they flower in spring.

rows.name: Qinling National Botanical Garden
rows.summary: A botanical garden opened in 2017 on the northern slopes of the Qinling Mountains in Zhouzhi County, with a planning area of 639 km² that rises more than 2,000 m from the plain into the mountains. The visitor area holds themed gardens for peonies, ginkgos, orchids and water plants, a large greenhouse and a palaeobotany hall, while the mountain zones protect native forest.

rows.name: Qinling Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A large zoo at the foot of the Qinling Mountains in Chang'an District, with more than 300 animal species. Visitors walk round one section to see animals such as golden monkeys, flamingos, hippos and Asian elephants, and ride through drive-through enclosures of African and Asian herbivores and of big cats; giant pandas are also kept. It suits families and makes an easy day out from the city.

rows.name: Qujiang Polar Ocean Park
rows.summary: An aquarium complex in the Qujiang district of southern Xi'an, made up of the Qujiang Ocean World aquarium, opened in 2005, and a polar hall added in 2013, on a site of about 4.7 hectares. The aquarium has an underwater tunnel and a tropical rainforest hall, and the polar hall keeps animals such as polar bears, Magellanic penguins, Arctic wolves and seals. It suits families with children.

rows.name: Red 25th Army Headquarters Site, Gepai
rows.pinyin: Gěpái Zhèn Hóng Èrshíwǔ Jūn Jūnbù Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: In February 1935 the Red Army's 25th Army, then building a base area on the Hubei–Henan–Shaanxi borders, set up a township soviet government at Gepai in the Qinling Mountains, described as the first Communist-led local government in the Xi'an area; it ran until the army moved on in July 1935. The army's headquarters building and the site of an enlarged meeting of the party's provincial committee for the base area, held here in April 1935, still stand on the town's old street. A memorial hall in traditional courtyard style, built on the site of the soviet government, displays photographs and objects from the period.

rows.name: Revolution Park
rows.summary: Laid out in 1927 in the north-east of the walled city, Revolution Park commemorates the soldiers and civilians who died during the siege of Xi'an in 1926, and a mass public funeral for them was held here in March 1927. Its Revolution Pavilion is the Mingyuan Tower moved from the Qing provincial examination hall, and the grounds keep a group of old memorial steles and statues of Yang Hucheng, Liu Zhidan and Xie Zichang. Today it is also a neighbourhood park with a lotus pond and pavilions.

rows.name: Shaanxi Natural History Museum
rows.summary: A natural history museum opened in January 2008 beside the Shaanxi TV Tower, with a crescent-shaped nature building and a glass-sphere science building. Its galleries cover geology, fossils and insects and recreate the habitats of Qinling wildlife such as the giant panda, golden snub-nosed monkey, takin and crested ibis, while a separate Kenneth Behring hall shows African and North American animal specimens donated in 2014. A dome cinema and an outdoor science area make it popular with families.

rows.name: Shengshou Temple Pagoda, Nanwutai
rows.summary: Shengshou Temple stands on Nanwutai in the Zhongnan Mountains, and its square brick pagoda of seven storeys is said to date from the Sui and on stylistic grounds is no later than the early Tang. The temple was rebuilt in the Northern Song after being destroyed at the end of the Tang, and keeps its gate and halls along with the pagoda, whose iron finial is thought to be Song work. North of the pagoda is a small stone memorial stupa to the 20th-century Pure Land master Yinguang.

rows.name: Shijingli Town
rows.summary: A new themed town on the Feng River in Fengdong New City, opened in September 2017 and themed on the Book of Songs (Shijing), the ancient poetry anthology, close to where the Western Zhou capitals of Feng and Hao once stood. It combines a landscaped riverside with shops, restaurants and creative businesses, and suits an easy stroll and a meal.

rows.name: Shuilu'an Temple
rows.summary: Shuilu'an began as the Water and Land Hall of the old Wuzhen Temple, the only building to outlast it, and in the Ming dynasty a Prince of Qin made it his family's Buddhist chapel and enlarged it into a small temple. Its main hall is crowded with thousands of painted clay figures, many of them modelled in relief across the walls. The east-facing complex of gate, front, middle and main halls is run as a museum of wall sculpture.

rows.name: South Wutai Mountain
rows.summary: A peak of the Zhongnan range south of Xi'an, named for its five summit terraces and long a centre of Buddhist retreat. A forested path of about 12 km climbs from a bamboo valley past a small waterfall and oddly shaped rocks to a string of small temples near the 1,688 m summit, and Shengshou Temple, founded under the Sui dynasty, keeps an old brick pagoda in the valley below.

rows.name: Taiping National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the Taiping valley of the Qinling Mountains in Huyi District, named after a Sui-dynasty palace and rising from about 880 m to 3,000 m between steep cliffs, rapids and pools. Its best-known sight is a cluster of waterfalls, among them the Rainbow Waterfall, with larch and birch woods higher up and wild redbud flowering on the slopes in April.

rows.name: Tang Altar of Heaven (Tiantan Heritage Park)
rows.summary: This round earthen altar of four tiers, finished in white lime plaster and climbed by twelve evenly spaced stairways on each tier, is where the emperors of the Sui and Tang dynasties made sacrifices to Heaven south of their capital, Chang'an. Excavated in 1999, it lay beside a university sports ground until a small heritage park was laid out around it and opened in 2018.

rows.name: Tang West Market
rows.summary: A Tang-style shopping and cultural quarter built in the 2000s on the site of the West Market, the international market of Tang-dynasty Chang'an. Its Tang West Market Museum, opened in 2010, shows excavated remains of the market's crossroads, cart ruts, a stone bridge, shop foundations and drains where they were found, with galleries on Silk Road trade drawn from a collection of more than 20,000 objects.

rows.name: Wangshun Mountain
rows.summary: A national forest park in Lantian County, part of the Zhongnan range of the Qinling, covering about 36 km² and topped by Jade Emperor Peak at 2,239 m, with sheer rock faces that have earned it the nickname of Shaanxi's little Huangshan. It is named after Wang Shun, a son of local legend who carried earth up the mountain to bury his mother, and a temple to him, oddly shaped rocks, a narrow gorge and an old azalea tree line the climb.

rows.name: White Deer Plain Film and TV City
rows.summary: A film and television theme park built by the Shaanxi Tourism Group on the White Deer Plain, the loess tableland that gave its name to Chen Zhongshi's novel, and opened in July 2016. It mixes filming sets of old Guanzhong streets and villages with a long outdoor hillside stairway, parades of costumed film characters, daytime shows and an evening light show in the valley, and suits families on a half-day trip.

rows.name: Xi'an City God Temple
rows.summary: Founded in 1387 and moved to this site off West Street in 1433, this Taoist temple is the seat of the chief city god, held to rule over the city gods of the north-western provinces. Its main hall, with a single-eaved hipped roof, was rebuilt in 1723 with timber from the demolished palace of the Ming princes of Qin, and an opera stage of 1887 stands in front of it. For decades the courtyards were filled by a wholesale market, which was moved out in 2003 when the temple was returned to the Taoist association.

rows.name: Xi'an Expo Park
rows.summary: The grounds of the 2011 Xi'an International Horticultural Expo, laid out on the delta between the Chan and Ba rivers in north-eastern Xi'an and covering 418 hectares, of which 188 hectares are water. Kept as a public park after the expo, it has lakes, themed gardens and the Chang'an Tower, built as the expo's landmark.

rows.name: Xi'an Incident Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The memorial hall occupies the mansion of the Nationalist general Zhang Xueliang, where on the night of 11 December 1936 he briefed his commanders for the Xi'an Incident: the detention of Chiang Kai-shek the next morning to press for an end to the civil war and a united front against Japan. Its three three-storey houses of the mid-1930s, set in a row, hold period rooms and exhibitions on the incident, including the east building where the Communist delegation led by Zhou Enlai stayed during the negotiations that followed. The memorial hall also runs Yang Hucheng's Zhiyuan villa on Qingnian Road, while the Wujianting lodge and the pavilion marking where Chiang was caught are inside Huaqing Palace in Lintong.

rows.name: Xiangji Temple
rows.summary: Xiangji Temple is regarded as the cradle of Pure Land Buddhism, founded by a disciple of the Tang master Shandao in his memory after his death in 681. The Shandao Pagoda, a square Tang brick pagoda that has lost its upper storeys, stands at the north end of the temple's axis behind halls rebuilt many times after damage in the An Lushan rebellion and the persecution of Buddhism in the 840s. It is an active monastery, and Chinese and Japanese monks have held joint ceremonies here in Shandao's memory.

rows.name: Xianyou Temple and Fawang Pagoda
rows.summary: Fawang Pagoda was raised in 601, when Emperor Wen of Sui sent Buddhist relics to be enshrined at Xianyou Temple at the mouth of the Heihe valley, and it is regarded as China's only surviving Sui-dynasty brick pagoda. Square in plan with seven tiers of close-set eaves, it resembles the Small Wild Goose Pagoda in Xi'an, though its finial is lost. To make way for the Heihe reservoir the pagoda and temple were dismantled and rebuilt on the ridge north of the water between 1999 and 2003, and a small temple museum stands beside them.

rows.name: Xingjiao Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the Shaoling plateau south of Xi'an, founded in 669 to house the remains of Xuanzang, the monk whose pilgrimage to India inspired Journey to the West. Its west courtyard holds his five-storey brick pagoda, about 21 m tall, flanked by the smaller pagodas of his disciples Kuiji and Yuance, and the three were inscribed in 2014 as part of the Silk Roads World Heritage site. The temple halls themselves were burnt in the 19th century and rebuilt during the Republican period, and it remains an active monastery.

rows.name: Yisushe Theatre
rows.summary: Yisushe, a company founded in 1912 to reform Shaanxi's Qinqiang opera, has performed since 1917 in this theatre, built in 1916 as the Yichunyuan and one of the earliest modern-style theatres surviving in China. The theatre is now the heart of the Yisushe Cultural Block just north-east of the Bell Tower, which also has a museum on the company's century of history and an open-air stage where Qinqiang excerpts have been performed regularly since spring 2023.

rows.name: Zhaohui Pagoda
rows.summary: Also called Gaoling Pagoda, this octagonal brick pagoda of 13 storeys with close-set eaves stands in Zhaohui Square in Gaoling and takes its name from the vanished Tang monastery of Zhaohui. Its building date is not recorded, but the written sources and its structure point to the middle Tang. The pagoda is hollow, with a brick stair inside and arched openings in each storey.

rows.name: Zhouzhi Water Street
rows.summary: A riverside leisure quarter laid out from 2012 along the Sha River, an old river that skirts Zhouzhi county town, with the Qinling Mountains as a backdrop. Its centre is Yanhuo Xiangzi, a lane district built in Han and Tang style and opened in 2022, where outdoor shows, small indoor theatres, open-air stages for folk performances and costumed characters accompany food stalls and inns. It is busiest in the evening and suits a night out from Xi'an or a stop on the way to Louguantai or the Qinling parks.

rows.name: Zhuque National Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the Lao valley of the Qinling Mountains in Huyi District, set up in 1992 and made a national forest park in 1999, covering about 26 km² from around 500 m to over 3,000 m. Trails pass waterfalls, one of them more than 100 m high, rock formations and pine woods, and the highest section climbs to rocky peaks near the main Qinling ridge.

rows.name: Anwu Wartime Youth Training Class Site
rows.summary: The Wu family manor at Anwu village where, from 1938 to 1940, the Communist Party ran its Wartime Youth Training Class, a school that prepared young people for work in the war against Japan. The surviving east courtyard of the manor held the class's offices, the two-storey Wangyue Tower housed its directors, the opera stage of the Yingxiang Palace was used for training and performances, and the cypress-shaded Wu family cemetery served as an open-air classroom. The site is now a memorial museum.

rows.name: Baoben Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda on the north side of Wugong town, on the site of the Baoben Temple that Emperor Taizong of Tang made out of a villa used by his mother, near the house where he was born. The temple has gone, and the pagoda, listed as Song-dynasty work, was taken down and rebuilt in 1994 because it was leaning badly.

rows.name: Beidu Iron Pagoda
rows.summary: A nine-storey octagonal pagoda cast in iron between 1605 and 1610 on a brick base, the only survivor of Fuchang Temple at Beidu, first built under the Jin dynasty. A spiral brick stair runs inside, and an iron plaque over the south arch names it the Thousand Buddha Pagoda.

rows.name: Changyu Reina Castle Winery
rows.summary: A winery of the Changyu wine group, opened in October 2013 in Qinhan New City between Xi'an and Xianyang and run with Italy's Reina winemaking family. Its castle-style building stands beside vineyards and a wine-themed garden, and visits take in the underground cellar of about 15,800 m², built to hold 15,000 oak barrels.

rows.name: Chongwen Pagoda
rows.summary: A thirteen-storey octagonal brick pagoda built between 1591 and 1605 in Chongwen town, standing on a Sumeru-style base. Its temple, known as Tiefo Temple, was destroyed in 1862, leaving only the pagoda and the gate, which now stand in a small park.

rows.name: Dafo Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A cave temple cut into the cliff on the south bank of the Jing River west of Binzhou, listed in 2014 as part of the Silk Roads: Chang'an–Tianshan Corridor World Heritage Site. Carving began in the late Northern dynasties, and its centrepiece, the Great Buddha Cave of 628, holds a huge seated Amitabha flanked by the bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, counted as the largest Buddha figure in Shaanxi. Smaller caves of the Tang to Ming periods with hundreds of figures and inscriptions spread along the cliff on either side, and the Mingjing Terrace pavilion, rebuilt in the Ming, stands before the main cave.

rows.name: Fucha Town
rows.summary: A tea-themed tourist town in Jinghe New City north of Xi'an, opened in August 2015 on the site of the old village of Shuangzhao and devoted to fu tea, a fermented brick tea. It has a tea street of shops and tea brands, a folk-food street of Guanzhong snacks and the China Fu Tea Culture Museum, and is mainly a place for tea tasting, snacks and an evening stroll.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple Pagoda, Binzhou
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick-and-timber pagoda of 1053, from the Northern Song, in the centre of Binzhou, where it is known as the Bin County Pagoda. Its temple has gone, and the wooden stair inside was rebuilt during repairs in 1985.

rows.name: Lewa Adventure
rows.summary: An amusement park in Jinghe New City north of Xi'an, opened as Lewa Hengye Happy World around a cluster of roller coasters and some 30 rides. After an upgrade it reopened on 1 May 2026 as Jinghuayuan · Darenguo, themed on the classic novel Flowers in the Mirror, adding lantern walks and costumed characters to the rides, with lantern displays and shows in the evening. It suits families and teenagers.

rows.name: Malan Revolutionary Site
rows.summary: Malan, in the hills of northern Xunyi County, was the seat of the Communist Party's Guanzhong sub-region of the Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia Border Region in the 1940s, on an important route from Xi'an to Yan'an. The site keeps a hillside of 375 cave dwellings dug by soldiers and local people after the sub-region's offices moved here at the end of 1941, a memorial monument and the Malan Revolutionary Memorial Hall, which shows photographs and office objects of the period and has a digital exhibition. It was named one of China's 100 classic red-tourism sites in 2005.

rows.name: Maoling
rows.summary: Maoling is the tomb of Emperor Wu of Han (157–87 BC), the largest of the Western Han imperial mausoleums, whose great flat-topped mound rises on the loess plateau between Xianyang and Xingping. The Maoling Museum lies about 1 km to its east in the grounds of the tomb of his general Huo Qubing, where galleries hold the Western Han stone sculptures from Huo's tomb, among them the 'Horse Trampling a Xiongnu', together with finds from the tombs around Maoling. A path climbs Huo Qubing's mound to a pavilion on its top.

rows.name: Mawei Station Folk Culture Park
rows.summary: A folk-culture park built from 2012 in a gully left empty when Lijiapo village was moved, named after the Mawei post station where Yang Guifei, consort of Emperor Xuanzong, was put to death during a mutiny of his guards in 756. Behind rammed-earth walls and a gate tower are new buildings in traditional style, restored loess cave dwellings with a collection of more than 23,000 old farm tools and household objects, and a snack street of Guanzhong dishes, with workshops pressing oil, making tofu and grinding chilli in stone mills. Yang Guifei's tomb is close by.

rows.name: Northwest A&F University Museums
rows.name_zh: 西北农林科技大学博览园
rows.summary: A group of six museums on the campus of Northwest A&F University in Yangling, opened to the public in 2005 and described by the university as China's largest group of agriculture-themed museums. They cover insects, animals, soils, plants, the history of Chinese agriculture and water conservancy, drawing on collections that include more than 1.5 million insect specimens, and are set among a butterfly garden, an arboretum and herb and grain gardens. It suits families and anyone curious about natural history and farming.

rows.name: Qin Straight Road at Shimen Pass
rows.summary: The Qin Straight Road was the military highway that the First Emperor ordered in 212 BC, running north from Yunyang near today's Chunhua along the Ziwu Mountains to Jiuyuan beyond the Yellow River. In Xunyi County it follows the main ridge of the Ziwu range, where long stretches of its broad roadbed survive under forest cover; at Shimen Pass a small museum presents the road, and remains of Qin–Han buildings and beacon towers lie along the route.

rows.name: Qingfan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Tang-dynasty brick pagoda, locally called the North Pagoda, on Beisi Lane in the old centre of Xingping. The temple, founded in 627 and renamed Baoning Temple in 978, has gone, leaving the hollow seven-storey octagonal tower.

rows.name: Sanyuan City God Temple
rows.summary: A walled temple complex in Sanyuan town founded in 1375, whose mostly Ming-dynasty buildings line one axis of gates, carved timber and stone memorial archways, a Qing opera stage of 1757, twin bell and drum towers and a main hall with a large City God statue. A rear palace of 1486 decorated with glazed-tile dragons and phoenixes, and a set of Ming–Qing paintings of the Ten Kings of Hell in the worship hall, are among the highlights. The temple also houses the Sanyuan County Museum, with halls of Tang finds and calligraphy by Yu Youren.

rows.name: Shahe Ancient Bridge Site
rows.summary: Remains of ancient bridges of the Qin and Han periods across the Sha River in Fengxi New City, which carried one of the main routes linking the capital Chang'an with the outside world. The site is protected within a heritage park, and the nearby Silk Road Bridge Culture Theme Hall uses digital displays to tell the history of the Silk Road and of ancient Chinese bridges.

rows.name: Shilang Lake
rows.summary: A lake among the loess hills south-west of Binzhou, developed as an eco-tourism area. A walkway runs around the shore past fishing platforms and a glass suspension bridge, with campsites, guesthouses and restaurants by the lake.

rows.name: Shunling Mausoleum
rows.summary: The tomb of Lady Yang (died 670), mother of Wu Zetian, which Wu raised to an imperial mausoleum and named Shunling in 690 after she proclaimed herself emperor. The walled precinct has gone, but Tang stone figures of men, horses, rams, lions and unicorns still stand around the mound, now laid out as a heritage park on the plateau east of Xi'an Xianyang airport.

rows.name: Silk Road Happy World
rows.summary: A Silk Road-themed park in Fengxi New City on the western edge of Xi'an, opened in April 2023 by the Shaanxi Tourism Group, laid out as seven themed streets that recreate places along the old trade routes, such as Rome, Persia and India, as stage-set architecture. Street performances, costumed characters, shops and restaurants fill the streets, and it is aimed at families and evening visitors.

rows.name: Site of Qin Xianyang
rows.summary: Remains of the palace district of Xianyang, capital of the state of Qin from 350 BC and of the First Emperor's empire until it was burned in 206 BC, on the terrace north of the Wei River. A site museum beside the excavated foundations of Palace No. 1, opened in 1995 and since renovated, shows models of the palace and finds such as hollow bricks with dragon and phoenix designs, drainage pipes and coins. Since 2025 the area has been a national archaeological site park, which also takes in the Qin-Han Hall of the Shaanxi History Museum, opened in 2024.

rows.name: Tai Pagoda, Xunyi
rows.summary: A brick pagoda built in 1059 under the Northern Song, imitating a timber pavilion-style tower in its octagonal plan and seven storeys. It stands in Taita Cultural Square in the centre of Xunyi town.

rows.name: Wugong City God Temple
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty City God temple on East Street in Wugong town, the former county seat, repaired in the Qing and in modern times. Along its axis stand the gate, side halls, an opera stage, an offering hall under a rolled-ridge roof, and main and rear halls under single-eaved hip-and-gable roofs.

rows.name: Wuling Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A five-storey octagonal brick pagoda on the site of the vanished Wuling Temple, founded under the Northern Wei, south-west of Yongping, the old county town of Yongshou. Long thought to be Tang, it was dated to the Northern Song after Xining-era coins and a brick inscribed with the year 1107 were found at its top during repairs in 1983; two stone Buddhas and a Qing stele also survive.

rows.name: Xianyang Confucian Temple (Xianyang Museum)
rows.summary: Xianyang's Confucian Temple, founded in 1371, has housed the city museum, now the Xianyang Museum, since 1962; its four courtyards combine the original Dacheng Hall and side galleries with Ming buildings moved here from other temples in 1963. The galleries focus on Qin and Han Xianyang, with finds from the Qin palace sites and a hall of the painted Western Han soldier and horse figurines excavated from a satellite tomb of the Changling mausoleum at Yangjiawan.

rows.name: Xianyang Lake
rows.summary: An artificial lake by the Wei River in central Xianyang, lined with riverside parks and promenades. Weibin Park runs along its north bank and the Gudu Langqiao, a covered footbridge, crosses the water; it makes an easy evening walk after the Xianyang Museum in the Confucian Temple, a few hundred metres to the north.

rows.name: Yangling Modern Agriculture Innovation Park
rows.summary: A showcase of modern farming of about 87 hectares in the Yangling agricultural high-tech zone, and Shaanxi's first 4A-rated agricultural tourism site. Eight exhibition halls cover factory seedling production, soilless cultivation, flowers, bonsai, a 'super vegetable garden', southern fruit trees and crops of western China, set among seed nurseries and an artificial lake planted with aquatic plants. It suits families and visitors interested in how farming technology works.

rows.name: Yuanjia Village
rows.summary: A Guanzhong farming village near Liquan that turned to rural tourism in 2007 and is now lined with brick-and-timber houses in Ming–Qing style. Its snack streets serve Guanzhong dishes made on the spot from the village's cooperative oil, vinegar, tofu and chilli workshops, and an old street holds craft shops for weaving, shadow puppets and woodblock New Year prints, along with cafés, bars and guesthouses. It drew about 9.5 million visitors in 2024, so weekends and holidays are very crowded.

rows.name: Yunji Eco-Park
rows.summary: An eco-park and rural resort among locust-tree woodland in the hills of Yongshou County, with guesthouse courtyards, woodland walks and farm-style restaurants. Yongshou is known for its locust-tree forests and locust-blossom honey, and the trees flower in late spring.

rows.name: Zhao Mausoleum
rows.summary: Zhaoling, on Jiuzong Mountain in Liquan County, is the mausoleum of Emperor Taizong of Tang (died 649) and the largest of the Tang imperial tombs; begun in 636, it was the first Tang imperial tomb cut into a mountain, and its many satellite tombs hold princes, princesses and ministers such as Wei Zheng and Li Jing. The Zhaoling Museum, set up at the satellite tomb of the general Li Ji, shows steles and epitaphs gathered from these tombs in its 'Zhaoling Forest of Steles' halls, together with Tang tomb murals and other finds. The Six Steeds reliefs that once stood at the mausoleum are now in Xi'an's Beilin Museum and in the United States.

rows.name: Zhaoren Temple
rows.summary: A temple in Changwu town founded on the order of Emperor Taizong of Tang in 629 for the soldiers killed at the battle of Qianshuiyuan, where his army had defeated the warlord Xue Rengao. Its surviving Main Hall is an all-timber building with a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof and no columns inside: beams laid across the corners of a nested-square ceiling frame carry the roof onto twelve posts hidden in the walls, which gives it the local name 'hall without pillars'.

rows.name: Zhengguo Canal Headworks
rows.summary: Where the Jing River leaves the Zhongshan hills north-west of Jingyang lie the headworks of the Zhengguo Canal, the irrigation canal begun by the state of Qin in 246 BC that turned the salty northern Guanzhong plain into farmland. As the river cut its bed deeper, later dynasties moved the intake upstream, so the site keeps remains of successive intakes from the Qin canal to the Jinghui Canal completed in 1932, with steles recording the works; the canal system was listed as a World Heritage Irrigation Structure in 2016. The scenic area around the headworks also takes in a stretch of the Jing River gorge.

rows.name: Baishan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal brick pagoda of the early Northern Song dynasty on Bai Shan at Zhiluo, locally called the Zhiluo Pagoda; it is all that remains of Baishan Temple. Its eleven closely stacked eaves rise to 43.3 m.

rows.name: Bao'an Revolutionary Site
rows.summary: Zhidan's county town, then called Bao'an, was the seat of the Communist Party Central Committee from July 1936 to January 1937, between its stays at Wayaobao and Yan'an, and the American journalist Edgar Snow visited the leaders here in 1936 for his book Red Star Over China. The site keeps a row of five stone cave dwellings used by Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai's residence and the cave used for Politburo meetings, and the Anti-Japanese Red Army University site stands on a hillside south of town.

rows.name: Former Border Region High Court
rows.name_zh: 陕甘宁边区高等法院旧址
rows.summary: The hillside compound on Longwan Shan, just south of Pagoda Hill, that was the seat of the High Court of the Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia Border Region, the Communist-led administration based in Yan'an, from 1941 until the court moved to Xi'an in 1949, apart from a year away during the fighting of 1947–48. Its offices, guard quarters and prison have been restored, 57 cave dwellings in all, and an exhibition hall on the Border Region's courts displays more than 1,000 documents and objects.

rows.name: Fuyan Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty brick pagoda at Dongcun village in Fu County, locally called the Dongcun Pagoda and the only survivor of Fuyan Temple. The hollow, octagonal tower has thirteen storeys and stands 30.2 m tall.

rows.name: Ganquan Canyon
rows.summary: A group of narrow Danxia slot canyons in Ganquan County, also called the Yucha Canyon, made up of side gorges such as Huashugou, Longbagou and Yueyagu where curving red rock walls close in overhead. The sculpted walls have earned it the nickname 'China's Antelope Canyon', and its landforms were the subject of a 2019 CCTV documentary.

rows.name: Huangling National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park of about 44 km² in the Qiaoshan forest on the upper Ju River, south-west of Huangling town, opened to visitors in 2015. Its northern Xuanyuan Valley, which local legend makes the birthplace of the Yellow Emperor, has lakes, meadows and forest trails, and a ridge road leads south to Zi'e Temple with its cliffside shrines and walkways; it makes a green half-day outing for people visiting the Huangdi Mausoleum.

rows.name: Huanglong Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 13 km² forest scenic area in the wooded Huanglong Mountains on the south-western edge of Huanglong town, with its visitor centre at Dianzihe village. It takes in Wuliang Shan, whose hilltop Lianyun Temple grew from an earlier Taoist shrine and keeps steles going back to the Ming dynasty and centuries-old pines and cypresses, a 6.2 km forest trail to Muke Zhai hill, a stone-carving gallery on local culture and a lake with water activities.

rows.name: Hukou Waterfalls (Shaanxi side)
rows.summary: The largest waterfall on the Yellow River, where the river is squeezed from a bed several hundred metres wide into a narrow rock trough and plunges into it in a roar of brown water and spray; the 'teapot spout' (hukou) shape gives the falls their name. This card covers the west-bank viewing area in Yichuan County, Shaanxi; the opposite bank belongs to Jixian in Shanxi, and the falls and their 5A rating are shared between the two provinces. The falls are widest in the summer flood season, and the Qilangwo Bridge below them links the two banks.

rows.name: Kaiyuan Temple Pagoda, Fu County
rows.summary: A square Tang-dynasty brick pagoda, built in 740–741, standing halfway up the west hill above Fu County town, where it is known as the Xishan Pagoda; the temple around it has long gone. The hollow pagoda has eleven storeys and still stands 41.8 m tall, although its top storey is broken.

rows.name: Laoshan National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Lao Shan hills of south-western Ganquan County, south of Yan'an, where secondary forest covers the loess hills; the provincial forestry bureau puts its forest cover at 92%. It is a place for forest walks and picnics on a day trip from Yan'an.

rows.name: Long March Victory Memorial Park, Wuqi
rows.name_zh: 中央红军长征胜利纪念园
rows.summary: A memorial park on Shengli ('Victory') Hill above Wuqi town, approved in 2005, marking the end of the Central Red Army's Long March, which reached Wuqi on 19 October 1935. Steps lead up past bronze sculptures, including a bugler, to the Long March Victory Monument and the hilltop command post of the 21 October 'cut the tail' battle, in which the Red Army ambushed the cavalry pursuing it.

rows.name: Luochuan Conference Site
rows.summary: The village school at Fengjia, about 10 km north of Luochuan town, where the Communist Party Politburo held an enlarged meeting from 22 to 25 August 1937. The meeting adopted the Ten-Point Programme for Resisting Japan and Saving the Nation, the Red Army was reorganised as the Eighth Route Army, and the site now has the Luochuan Conference Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Nanniwan
rows.summary: A valley about 45 km south-east of Yan'an where the Eighth Route Army's 359th Brigade was sent in 1941 to clear land and farm, as the Communist base area sought self-sufficiency under an economic blockade; the campaign is the subject of the 1943 song 'Nanniwan'. The scenic area has the Great Production Movement exhibition hall, rice paddies on the valley floor and restored sites such as the Yan'an artillery school and the brigade's former headquarters at Jinpenwan, about 10 km to the east.

rows.name: Qiankun Bay
rows.summary: A great looping meander of the Yellow River in the Shanxi–Shaanxi canyon at Yanchuan, promoted as the 'first bend of the Yellow River' and part of the Yellow River Meanders national geopark. Viewpoints on the Shaanxi rim look down on the river curling around a spur of loess hills, with Shanxi on the far bank; the scenic area was raised to the national 5A rating in 2024.

rows.name: Qingliang Mountain and Wanfo Caves
rows.summary: Qingliang Mountain, in central Yan'an across the Yan River from Fenghuang Hill and Pagoda Hill, holds the Wanfo Caves, four Buddhist grottoes with carvings from the Song, Yuan and Ming dynasties, and a glazed-tile pagoda. The largest cave, about 17 m wide and 13 m deep, has stone screens covered in reliefs of Buddhas, bodhisattvas and arhats, though the statues on its central altar were remade in 1985. During the war years Xinhua News Agency, the Liberation Daily, the central printing works and Xinhua Bookstore were based on the hill, and the Yan'an News Memorial Hall there tells that story.

rows.name: Qiulin Anti-Japanese War Memorial Site
rows.summary: Qiulin, a small town in Yichuan County, was the headquarters of the Nationalist army's Second War Zone under Yan Xishan after the Japanese advance drove it out of Shanxi in 1938. The memorial site presents the former headquarters and other wartime sites in and around the town, with an exhibition hall on the period.

rows.name: Shihong Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple on the north bank of the Chuanzi River at Han village in Zhiluo town, west of Fu County town, also called the Chuanzihe Grottoes. Its seven caves were begun in the Sui dynasty's Daye era (605–617), and carving went on through the Tang, Song and Yuan into the Ming.

rows.name: Tiebiancheng Ruins
rows.summary: The remains of a walled frontier town of the Northern Song period at Tiebiancheng in the far west of Wuqi County, listed as a national heritage site in 2013. Stretches of the old wall and a watch platform survive and are presented as a small local scenic area.

rows.name: Wan'an Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A Northern Song Buddhist cave temple on a hillside at Yu village in Shuanglong town, west of Huangling, carved between 1095 and 1115. Its carved Buddhas and other figures are presented as a small scenic area.

rows.name: Wanfeng Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty brick pagoda, repaired in the Ming dynasty, standing on the site of the vanished Xingguo Temple at Fucheng village in Luochuan County. The hollow, octagonal tower has thirteen storeys and is more than 40 m tall.

rows.name: Wayaobao Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: Wayaobao, now the centre of Zichang, was where the Communist Party Politburo held an enlarged meeting from 17 to 25 December 1935, chaired by Zhang Wentian, which set out the party's policy of an anti-Japanese national united front. The memorial covers the meeting site, a row of brick cave dwellings in the Tian family courtyard at Xiahetan, together with the sites of the Northwest Revolutionary Military Commission and the Anti-Japanese Red Army University and the former residences of Mao Zedong, Zhang Wentian and Zhou Enlai.

rows.name: Wuqi Revolutionary Site
rows.summary: The cave-dwelling compound in Wuqi town where the Communist Party leadership stayed after the Central Red Army arrived on 19 October 1935 at the end of the Long March; the Politburo met here on 22 October to set its next tasks. The north and south courtyards, linked by a stone passage, keep the former quarters of Mao Zedong and Zhang Wentian and now form the Wuqi Revolutionary Memorial Hall.

rows.name: Yan'an Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: The compounds where the Chinese Communist Party Central Committee lived and worked while it was based in Yan'an from January 1937 to March 1947 are spread across the city: the cave dwellings, offices and assembly halls of Yangjialing, where the party's Seventh National Congress met in 1945, Zaoyuan (Date Garden), Wangjiaping, Fenghuang Hill and the former Northwest Bureau. The Yan'an Revolutionary Memorial Hall at Wangjiaping, founded in 1950 and reopened in a new building in 2009, displays documents, photographs and relics from those years. On Pagoda Hill (Baota Shan) above the city stands a nine-storey Ming-dynasty brick pagoda, about 44 m tall, which became a symbol of Yan'an and of the Communist revolution.

rows.name: Yanyi Oil Well
rows.summary: The oil well completed in 1907 by the Yanchang Oil Factory, which the Qing government had authorised in 1905, known in China as the country's first onshore oil well; the factory also built China's first refinery here. The well-head is preserved in a small square in Yanchang town with a monument bearing a 1985 inscription naming it 'China's first onshore oil well', and the derrick and boiler beside it are replicas made in 2005.

rows.name: Zhang Side Memorial Site
rows.summary: The place in Ansai where Zhang Side, a soldier of the Communist Party's central guard regiment, was killed on 5 September 1944 when a charcoal kiln he was digging collapsed. Mao Zedong's speech at his funeral, 'Serve the People', became widely known in China, and the memorial site has an exhibition hall on his life, the remains of the kiln and a memorial square.

rows.name: Zhongshan Grottoes
rows.summary: A Northern Song Buddhist cave temple at the foot of Zhong Shan west of Zichang, begun in 1067. Its main hall, Cave 4, holds 16 free-standing statues 2–3 m tall among carved pillars, and its walls and pillars are covered with more than 10,000 small relief Buddhas; four smaller caves are badly weathered.

rows.name: Baiyun Mountain Temples, Jiaxian
rows.summary: A large Taoist temple complex on Baiyun Mountain above the west bank of the Yellow River just south of Jia County town, founded in 1605 and rebuilt and enlarged in 1724. Fifty-six old buildings survive, among them the Zhenwu Hall, the Five Dragons Palace, the Jade Emperor Tower and the Hall of the Three Pure Ones, with more than 1,900 Ming and Qing murals and over 120 inscribed steles. Its temple fair early in the fourth lunar month draws worshippers from neighbouring parts of Shaanxi, Shanxi and Inner Mongolia.

rows.name: Bilinwan Resort
rows.summary: A modern four-season resort south of Shenmu city, with a water park and amusement rides for the summer season. In winter it runs a ski area with eight runs, three of them built to FIS standard, which was chosen to host alpine skiing and snowboard events of Shaanxi's first Winter Games in February 2026.

rows.name: Boluo Fortress
rows.summary: A walled hilltop garrison town on Huangyun Hill above the south bank of the Wuding River, one of the forts of the Ming-dynasty Great Wall frontier in the Yulin region, with stone walls and four gates around an old main street; it is protected as a provincial heritage site. In October 1946 the Nationalist garrison stationed here under Hu Jingduo went over to the Communist side, an event known as the Hengshan Uprising.

rows.name: Bulanghe Women's Militia Sand-Control Company
rows.name_zh: 补浪河女子民兵治沙连
rows.summary: In 1974, 54 young women with an average age of 18 formed a militia company at Bulanghe to plant trees and fix the dunes of the Mu Us sands near the Inner Mongolia border, and the unit became known across China. The site has an exhibition hall on nearly fifty years of local sand control, the company's barracks and military-themed activities including a live-firing range and clay-pigeon shooting.

rows.name: Chiniuwa Folk Culture Village
rows.summary: A hill village of old stone cave dwellings among jujube groves near the Yellow River, which its residents have turned into a folk-culture tourist village. Villagers perform their own open-air show, 'An Ox on the High Hill', recreating northern Shaanxi farm life, and the village has a northern Shaanxi folk-custom museum of old everyday objects in 68 exhibition rooms as well as cave dwellings converted into guest rooms. It suits visitors curious about rural life on the loess plateau.

rows.name: Dang Family Manor, Suide
rows.summary: A hillside manor of cave-dwelling courtyards at Hejiashi village, begun in 1814 and enlarged by six generations of the Dang family until the Republican period, stepped up the slope and decorated with stone, brick and wood carving. The county describes it as the most completely preserved Qing-era complex in Suide, and restoration of five of its courtyards was signed off by the provincial heritage bureau in January 2026.

rows.name: Erlang Mountain, Shenmu
rows.summary: A temple-covered ridge on the west bank of the Kuye River facing central Shenmu, also called Bijia ('brush-rest') Mountain because the Ming emperor Wuzong is said to have likened its outline to one in 1518. More than a hundred halls, pavilions and shrines of Ming, Qing and later date line about 1 km of the crest around the temple of the god Erlang, and together they form a provincial heritage site. Crowds climb it for the temple fair on the evening of the seventh day of the lunar new year.

rows.name: Erlintu Grassland
rows.summary: A grassland scenic area in Erlintu township on the sandy steppe at the edge of the Mu Us Desert, run as a farm-and-grassland leisure park with open pasture, flower fields and a children's play park. Visitors come in summer for camping, farm activities, a folk-food street and bonfire evenings, and it lies close to Hongjiannao Lake, so the two are easily combined.

rows.name: Fuzhou Ancient City, Fugu
rows.summary: A walled hill town above the Yellow River at Fugu, the seat of Fuzhou prefecture from 911, whose stone walls date from the Five Dynasties and Song. The walls, about 2.3 km round and roughly boot-shaped, have four main and two small gates, with barbicans outside the south and small west gates, and enclose Ming and Qing buildings including a Confucian temple, a City God temple, the Wenchang pavilion, the Ronghe Academy and a Thousand Buddha cave.

rows.name: Haojiaqiao Village
rows.summary: A loess-hill village south-west of Suide that the Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia Border Region government named a 'model village' in 1944, when the labour hero Liu Yuhou led its farmers' labour-exchange teams in the wartime production drive. It now presents that history as one of Suide's red-history education sites, and has turned 26 empty cave dwellings into guesthouses alongside a northern Shaanxi-themed shopping street and a village cinema.

rows.name: Heilongtan (Black Dragon Pool), Zhenchuan
rows.summary: A hillside temple to the Black Dragon King above a group of spring-fed pools beside the Wuding River at Zhenchuan, founded in the Ming Zhengde period (1506–1521) and long visited by farmers praying for rain. Visitors pass a carved stone archway of 1931 and climb 48 steps to a courtyard with bell and drum towers and a main hall with painted murals, while nine springs run into small stone pools around the temple. The temple fair on the 13th day of the sixth lunar month draws tens of thousands of people.

rows.name: Hongjiannao Lake
rows.summary: Regarded as China's largest desert freshwater lake, Hongjiannao now covers about 37 km² where the loess plateau meets the Mu Us Desert on the border with Inner Mongolia. It is a national nature reserve, described by the local government as the world's largest breeding ground of the relict gull, with 195 bird species recorded, and its shores mix sandy beaches, grassland and wetland. The scenic area offers kayaking and other boat trips, sand buggies, and camel and horse rides.

rows.name: Hongmen Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: An eleven-storey octagonal brick pagoda about 27 m tall, built in the Taiding era of the Yuan dynasty (1324–1328) at the Hongmen Temple south-west of Tawan town; the temple itself has long gone. The hollow pagoda has closely spaced eaves and is known locally as the Bell Pagoda, after the wind bells that once hung from every corner of its eaves.

rows.name: Jiang Family Manor
rows.summary: A fortified cave-dwelling manor built for the Jiang family in the late Qing, with lower, middle and upper courtyards climbing a hillside behind crenellated stockade walls and gun platforms. A stone-paved ramp with a right-angle turn leads up to the gate past stables and a deep well, and the courtyards show how a wealthy northern Shaanxi household lived.

rows.name: Li Zicheng's Palace, Mizhi
rows.summary: A hillside group of Ming and Qing buildings on the southern slope of Panlong Mountain at the north end of Mizhi town, which local tradition links to Li Zicheng, the Mizhi rebel leader who overthrew the Ming dynasty in 1644, as his palace, and which also served as a temple of the Taoist god Zhenwu. A path climbs from the opera stage past the Plum Blossom Pavilion, the Pengsheng Tower, a stone archway and the Jade Emperor Pavilion, with displays on Li's rebellion and his short-lived Shun dynasty.

rows.name: Linzhou Ancient City (Yangjiacheng)
rows.summary: The earthen ruins of Linzhou, a frontier prefectural city of the Tang to Ming dynasties on Yangcheng Hill north of Shenmu, known locally as Yangjiacheng ('Yang family city') because the family of the Northern Song general Yang Ye held it. About 2.8 km of rammed-earth wall survives, up to 18 m high, around a site of about 1.1 km² made up of an east city, a barbican, an inner citadel and a western quarter. An exhibition hall, a military-culture park at the east gate and landscaped western ruins have been laid out for visitors, and the hill is known for apricot blossom in spring.

rows.name: Mahuangliang Loess Geopark
rows.summary: A 37 km² geopark on the loess plateau east of Yulin, where deep gullies have cut the thick loess into a 'peak forest' of pillars and ridges and exposed sections of Quaternary sediment, with desert landforms and fossil finds nearby. A two-storey visitor building holds a loess geology museum and an art gallery of paintings and photographs made here, and the area is a favourite of painters and photographers, especially after snow.

rows.name: Mingzhou Old Town, Suide
rows.summary: The historic core of Suide town, run as a cultural tourism district that links the Mingzhou historic street with the Suide Revolutionary Memorial Hall, a museum of Han-dynasty carved stone reliefs and the Fusu Culture Garden around the tomb on Shushu Hill traditionally attributed to Fusu, eldest son of the First Emperor of Qin. On the hill stands the Xundi Tower, first built in the early Ming and recently rebuilt in Ming style on its old site.

rows.name: Northern Scenery (Beiguo Fengguang) Scenic Area
rows.summary: A red-tourism scenic area on the Gaojiawa plateau above the Yellow River, named after the opening words of Mao Zedong's poem 'Snow' (Qinyuanchun · Xue). In February 1936, as the Red Army prepared to cross the river east into Shanxi, Mao came up to this plateau from his quarters in nearby Yuanjiagou village to survey the crossing in deep snow, and wrote the poem back in Yuanjiagou that night. The modern scenic area has the Cangxue Tower, a museum of Mao's poetry and a visitor centre.

rows.name: Northern Shaanxi Folk Song Museum
rows.summary: A museum devoted to the folk songs of northern Shaanxi, with about 5,700 m² of displays on traditional songs, the revolutionary songs of the Yan'an years such as 'The East Is Red', newer compositions and the region's folk music. The complex also has a 500-seat theatre, part of a youth activity centre, that doubles as a stage for folk-song performances.

rows.name: Qixing Temple, Fugu
rows.summary: A small Ming-dynasty temple, also called the Haotian Palace, on a hilltop about 1 km north of the old Gushan fort town in Fugu county. Built entirely of brick, it has a front hall and a beamless main hall roofed with a brick vault under a hip-and-gable roof, and local legend makes it the wedding place of the Song general Yang Ye and his wife She Saihua.

rows.name: Shengdu Amusement Park
rows.summary: An open-plan amusement park inside the Yuxi riverside park in central Yulin, opened in October 2014. It opened with more than 20 large outdoor rides and over ten indoor ones, among them an 89 m Ferris wheel, a six-loop roller coaster and a water flume ride, and it suits families and thrill-ride fans.

rows.name: Shimao
rows.summary: The ruins of a stone-walled city built around 2300 BC and abandoned around 1800 BC, the largest known walled settlement of China's late Neolithic, with inner and outer stone walls enclosing more than 400 ha around a terraced palace platform called Huangchengtai. It is now a national archaeological site park and on China's tentative list for World Heritage. The Shimao Museum, opened in November 2023, shows 688 jades, stone carvings, pottery, bone objects and painted mural fragments from the site.

rows.name: Site of the Xiaohe Meeting
rows.summary: The village where the CPC Central Committee under Mao Zedong and the PLA headquarters stayed for 48 days in summer 1947 while moving around northern Shaanxi during the civil war, and where an enlarged Central Committee meeting on 21–23 July 1947, held under a shelter in a villager's courtyard, decided the PLA's shift from strategic defence to the offensive. The site preserves the meeting courtyard and the cave dwellings used by Mao, Zhou Enlai and other leaders, the Galagou meeting site and a memorial hall, and has been fully open to visitors since 2012.

rows.name: Wave Valley, Jingbian
rows.summary: A Danxia landscape of eroded red sandstone in the gullies at Longzhou, south-east of Jingbian town, named for the wave-like layering of its rock. On holidays the scenic area stages local folk performances such as yangge and waist-drum dancing, the 'running donkey' dance and northern Shaanxi folk songs, and it drew 88,000 visitors over the 2026 National Day week.

rows.name: Wubu Stone City
rows.summary: The former county town of Wubu, a stone-walled town on a hilltop above the west bank of the Yellow River, first built in the Northern Han period of the tenth century and still holding Ming and Qing buildings. Its walls, yamen and temples were badly damaged by fighting and dismantling between 1936 and the 1950s, and most residents moved down to the new town by the river, but the walled hilltop and its old courtyards can still be explored.

rows.name: Yangjiagou Revolutionary Site
rows.summary: From November 1947 the CPC Central Committee's front committee under Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and Ren Bishi, together with the PLA headquarters, spent 120 days in this loess-valley village during the civil war, and held an enlarged Central Committee meeting here on 25–28 December 1947, known as the December Meeting. The memorial site preserves the leaders' cave-dwelling residences and the meeting hall within the hillside manor of the local Ma family, with displays in a memorial hall.

rows.name: Yellow River Eastward Crossing Site, Wubu
rows.summary: A Yellow River scenic area north of Wubu town that links three sites: the Erqi rapids, opposite Qikou in Shanxi, where the narrowed river pours over rock ledges; the old Guaishang ferry, with rafting on the river; and the memorial park at the Chuankou ferry, where Mao Zedong crossed into Shanxi on 23 March 1948, leaving northern Shaanxi after 13 years. The park has a monument, a memorial hall, sculptures and a landing stage.

rows.name: Daping Fengyuan Flower Park
rows.summary: A flower park in the Daping agricultural park at Shuichuan, south-east of Baiyin city, opened in 2018, where beds of verbena, Iceland poppies, petunias and other flowers are laid out in the shape of a phoenix. A coloured slide, high swings and a small tourist train run beside the flowers, and there are a fruit-picking garden and tents for overnight stays, so it is mainly a family outing from early summer to autumn.

rows.name: Huining Red Army Reunion Site
rows.summary: In October 1936 the Red Army's First and Fourth Front Armies met at Huining during the closing stage of the Long March, and the protected site in the centre of the town preserves the Huishi gate tower, the venue of the joint celebration meeting and the former headquarters of several Red Army commands. Also on the site are the Reunion Tower, a forest of steles with commanders' inscriptions and the Long March Victory Memorial Hall, which presents the march and the meeting.

rows.name: Shuian Sanhe Scenic Area
rows.summary: A riverside leisure park of about 47 ha on the Yellow River at Sanhe village, Dongwan, that combines farm and flower displays with a summer water-play area where water obstacle-course contests are held. It suits families looking for a summer day out from Jingyuan or Baiyin.

rows.name: Shuichuan Yellow River Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park of about 3,000 mu (roughly 200 ha) on the Yellow River at Shuichuan, south of Baiyin city, with lotus ponds that flower in summer, reedbeds, an artificial lake, zigzag bridges and a small tourist train. Waterbirds such as black swans and great crested grebes live here, and the park is often visited together with the nearby Daping flower park.

rows.name: Yellow River Stone Forest
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A national geopark on a bend of the Yellow River in Jingtai, where conglomerate beds about 2.1 million years old have been eroded into pillars and spires mostly 80–100 m tall, packed into some 10 km² of gullies. Visitors explore the Yinma Gorge and riverside viewpoints and can ride the river on traditional sheepskin rafts, and the cliffs have served as a backdrop for many Chinese films and TV dramas.

rows.name: Yongtai Fortress
rows.summary: A Ming garrison town built in 1606–08 on the plain of western Jingtai, still enclosed by rammed-earth walls 8–12 m high and about 1.7 km round, whose outline earned it the nickname 'Turtle City'. Once home to 2,000 infantry and 500 cavalry, it is now a near-empty village of a few dozen households, and a flower farm beside it is visited together with the fortress.

rows.name: Baling Bridge, Weiyuan
rows.summary: Baling Bridge spans the Qingyuan River in Weiyuan county town, close to the source of the Wei River: a covered timber cantilever-arch bridge 40 m long, with a gallery of 13 bays. A bridge is recorded here since the early Ming, but the present arch was first built in 1919–21 on the model of the Wo Bridge at Xinglong Mountain near Lanzhou and rebuilt in the early 1930s; plaques at its ends were written by Zuo Zongtang, Chiang Kai-shek, Yu Youren and other public figures.

rows.name: Bangluo Conference Site
rows.summary: On 27 September 1935 the Communist Party's Politburo Standing Committee, then on the Long March, met in the principal's office of the Bangluo central school and decided to make the Shaan-Gan base area in northern Shaanxi the destination of the march; the next day Mao Zedong spoke to the Shaanxi–Gansu Detachment's company-level and higher officers at a threshing ground beside the school. The protected site includes the meeting room, 17 former quarters of Party and Red Army leaders and a memorial hall with exhibitions on the meeting and on the Red Army's passage through Tongwei, and it is on the national list of red-tourism classic scenic areas.

rows.name: Changjiahe Hawthorn Town
rows.summary: A farm-tourism area in Changjiahe town built around hawthorn orchards planted by a local cooperative from 2018, with blossom in spring and fruit in autumn. Around the orchards are a Daoist-style temple complex used as a study base, an old fortified village, the Longzhu viewing terrace, a small pet and bird park and traditional villages used as bases for sketching and photography, so it suits a countryside day out from Tongwei.

rows.name: Langdutan Grassland
rows.summary: Langdutan is a broad upland of wetland meadows and grassland at an average height of about 2,600 m around Lüjing town in eastern Min County, threaded by winding streams and grazed by yaks, cattle and sheep. The G316 runs through it, which makes it an easy summer stop for wildflowers and cool weather, and a summer horse-racing festival has been held on the grassland.

rows.name: Lijia Longgong (Li Clan Ancestral Temple)
rows.summary: The Lijia Longgong is the ancestral temple of the Li clan in Longxi, the clan's ancestral seat, said to have been founded in the early Tang and named from an inscription by Emperor Taizong. The surviving buildings come from rebuildings of 1577, 1648 and later, with new buildings in the old style added in recent years, and people surnamed Li visit it to trace their roots. It is usually visited together with the Longxi Museum beside it, whose collection includes Neolithic pottery and Song–Yuan tomb brick carvings.

rows.name: Minzhou Conference Site
rows.summary: A memorial at Sanshilipu outside Min County town to the Minzhou Conference of 16–18 September 1936, at which the Communist Party's Northwest Bureau, meeting while the Red Army's Second and Fourth Front Armies were in Min County, rejected Zhang Guotao's plan to take the Fourth Front Army west and decided that the forces should go north to join the First Front Army. The Red Army passed through Min County in 1935 and stayed in 1936, when a Gansu provincial Soviet government was set up here, and the memorial hall presents that history.

rows.name: Nanping Mountain, Lintao
rows.summary: Nanping Mountain rises south of Lintao to an average height of about 2,800 m, and its snow-capped summit is the setting of 'Snow on the Southern Hills', one of the old Eight Views of Taoyang. The eco-tourism area in Nanping town has peony and herbaceous-peony fields, with Lintao's purple-spotted peonies flowering here in late spring, as well as farm-stay guesthouses, farming activities and, in winter, snow paths and sledging.

rows.name: Shouyang Mountain, Weiyuan
rows.summary: Shouyang Mountain in Lianfeng town south of Weiyuan is one of several places claimed as the mountain where the brothers Bo Yi and Shu Qi, refusing to eat the grain of the Zhou, starved to death; its nine lotus-like peaks have had Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian cave temples and halls since the Han and Wei. Nearby, the Yiqi tomb has a stele in the hand of Zuo Zongtang and the Qingsheng Shrine, first built in the Tang and last restored in 1874, with modern statues of the brothers by He E.

rows.name: Weihe Source Scenic Area
rows.summary: The Wei River is traditionally said to rise here in the Niaoshu ('Bird and Rat') Mountains south-west of Weiyuan, where the Book of Documents records Yu the Great guiding its waters, and the springs that feed it emerge in the wooded headwater valley. The scenic area has a hall to Yu the Great, a temple to the Wei River Dragon King and an exhibition hall on the river's history, and it is the core of Weiyuan's tourism.

rows.name: Weiyuan Tower, Longxi
rows.summary: The Weiyuan Tower stands in the centre of Longxi: a three-storey timber drum tower 26 m tall on a brick base, first built under the Northern Song in the 11th century, moved to its present site in 1261 and rebuilt in 1368. A water clock was added in 1341, a drum in 1464, and a bell cast in 1102 was hung here in 1836, which is why it is also called the Bell and Drum Tower; its present form dates from an enlargement of 1716.

rows.name: Yuangudui Village
rows.summary: Yuangudui is a hill village in Tianjiahe township, Weiyuan County, at about 2,440 m, which Xi Jinping visited in February 2013 and which has since developed rural tourism. Visitors see the rebuilt village with its farm stays, among them a deer-themed one, and fields of lilies and of medicinal herbs such as codonopsis and astragalus grown for sale.

rows.name: Yuelu Mountain, Lintao
rows.summary: Yuelu Mountain is the wooded hill on the eastern edge of Lintao town, long a Daoist site and a meeting place for scholars. Paths lead up past temple halls to the Chaoran Terrace and the Jiaoshan Academy, linked with the Ming official Yang Jisheng, who set up a school while exiled to Lintao, then called Didao; at the foot is the Yuquan spring by Longquan Temple, one of the old Eight Views of Taoyang, and in late spring the hill has displays of purple-spotted peonies.

rows.name: Yuexin International Calligraphy and Painting Village
rows.summary: A cultural tourism complex in Tongwei county town, in a county known for its calligraphy and painting culture, made up of a long calligraphy and painting gallery with more than 100 commercial galleries, the Yuexin Art Museum, a hot-spring pool complex, a hotel and an organic fruit-picking farm outside the town. It suits visitors interested in Chinese brush art, and the spa pools use spring water piped from the Tangchi valley south-west of the town.

rows.name: Zheyang and Guiqing Mountains
rows.summary: Two forested mountain areas in the south of Zhang County that together make up a national forest park. Zheyang Mountain, south-west of the county town, is a deep gorge of streams, pools and waterfalls between cliffs that serve as a training base for China's national rock-climbing team, with Song and Ming inscriptions along the path; Guiqing Mountain, further south, has steep peaks, old-growth woods, a bridge across a chasm and a temple first built in the Ming Longqing era.

rows.name: Awancang Wetland
rows.summary: A broad wetland grassland around Awancang town in Maqu county, inside the great loop of the upper Yellow River known as its First Bend, where the river's side channels meander through pasture, pools and marsh. It is grazing land for the Tibetan herders' yaks, sheep and Hequ horses, a breed famous across China, and the wide open views are the attraction.

rows.name: Ciri'na and Mao Zedong's Former Residence
rows.summary: A Tibetan village on the Bailong River in Wangzang town, Têwo county, where the Central Red Army stayed in September 1935 on the first stage of its Long March through Gansu; Mao Zedong lodged in a two-storey Tibetan house of rammed-earth walls and log beams. The house, looked after by the third generation of the family who hosted the soldiers, is kept as Mao Zedong's former residence, and the village is a stop on the Long March sites route through Têwo with the Ejie meeting site and Lazikou.

rows.name: Dangzhou Grassland
rows.summary: A grassland scenic area on the edge of Hezuo, the capital of Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, made up of the Dangzhou grassland park and the forested South Mountain, with natural pasture and summer wildflowers. It is the main venue of the prefecture's Shambhala tourism and arts festival and a gathering place for Tibetan and other local community festivals and celebrations.

rows.name: Dayu Valley
rows.summary: A valley system in the Dieshan range south of Jonê county town, inside the Tao River National Nature Reserve, where a tributary of the Tao River runs for about 70 km through forest, alpine meadow and wetland below Zhayikega, the 4,920 m main peak of the Dieshan. Its developed side valleys, such as Qibu and Ajiao, have rock features including One-Line Sky, Triangle Stone, Yangzhuo Lake and Moon Gate, and the valley also holds Tibetan villages and Qibu Monastery.

rows.name: Ejie Meeting Site
rows.summary: A Tibetan village house in Gaoji village, Dala township, where the Politburo of the Communist Party of China held an enlarged meeting on 12 September 1935, the day after the Central Red Army's Long March column crossed into Gansu from Sichuan; 'Ejie' is a Chinese rendering of the Tibetan name Gaoji. The meeting adopted a decision on the errors of Zhang Guotao, confirmed the plan to continue north and renamed the northbound force the Shaanxi–Gansu Detachment; the village around the site is now a 4A scenic area with guesthouses run by its residents.

rows.name: Ganjia Grassland and Bajiaocheng
rows.summary: A high grassland basin in the north of Xiahe county with pastures, rivers and gorges below the long Baishiya cliff, at whose foot stand Baishiya Monastery and the Baishiya Karst Cave, a Tibetan Buddhist pilgrimage cave where a Denisovan jawbone about 160,000 years old was found. The scenic area also includes Bajiaocheng, the 'eight-corner town', a walled town of the Tang to Ming periods laid out as a hollow cross, whose 2.2 km of walls still enclose a village.

rows.name: Laga Mountain
rows.summary: A mountain area 33 km west of Zhouqu county town, between Jiuzhaigou and Lazikou, whose Tibetan name means 'a place the immortals love'. It combines Tibetan hill villages, grassy slopes, streams and forest, and it was named among the '100 wonders of north-west China' at a regional tourism fair in 2018.

rows.name: Lazikou Pass
rows.summary: A narrow gorge in the Min Mountains of Têwo county where the Lazi River runs between sheer cliffs, for centuries the main way between northern Sichuan and southern Gansu. On 16–17 September 1935 Red Army troops under Yang Chengwu took the pass, held by Nationalist forces in blockhouses, by climbing the cliffs to attack from the flank, which opened the Long March route north; the site has a memorial monument, a memorial hall, reconstructed blockhouses and bullet marks on the rock.

rows.name: Taozhou Garrison Town
rows.summary: The walls of a Ming garrison town, rebuilt from 1379 as the seat of the Taozhou Guard on the old Tang–Tibet road, which still enclose the small town of Xincheng in Lintan county; it is regarded as the largest surviving garrison town (weicheng) in China. The walls run 5.43 km and stand up to 9.9 m high, climbing from the riverside plain to a ridge almost 300 m above it, with beacon platforms on the western ridge; they were badly damaged in an earthquake in 2013.

rows.name: Yeliguan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain and forest scenic area around Yeliguan town in Lintan county, on the north-eastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau, rated a national 5A area in 2024. It takes in the Yeliguan National Forest Park along the Yemu River, with pasture and the narrow, cliff-walled Lianzhu Gorge upstream and forested ravines downstream, and Tianchi Yehai, a mountain lake 7 km north of the town, known locally as Changye Pool after the Ming general Chang Yuchun, whose temple stands on its shore.

rows.name: Zecha Stone Forest
rows.summary: A gorge in Larenguan township, Luqu county, where sheer rock walls and pinnacles rise above grassland and dense forest, shaped over a long time by wind, rain and running water; fossils of ancient sea creatures are found on the peaks and in the caves. It lies inside the Gahai–Zecha National Nature Reserve, set up with State Council approval in 1998.

rows.name: Zhagana
rows.summary: A cluster of Tibetan villages inside a natural 'stone city' of limestone peaks north of Têwo county town; the name is Tibetan for 'stone box'. Below the 3,970 m Guanggai Shan, wooden houses, barley-drying racks and terraced fields sit under cliffs and spruce forest, a scene the botanist Joseph Rock praised after visiting in 1925, and UN Tourism named Zhagana a Best Tourism Village in 2023.

rows.name: East Lake Ecological Park, Jiayuguan
rows.summary: A large park in Jiayuguan's southern district, built from 2002 to 2006 as the centrepiece of the new part of the city, covering 165 ha with a 56 ha artificial lake, a 640 m ribbon stream, a central square, waterfall walks, pavilions, bridges and about 90 ha of planted woodland and lawns. Its landmark is the Western Pearl weather tower, and the lake hosts the Jiayuguan International Triathlon, whose 17th edition was held here in July 2026.

rows.name: Fantawild Adventure Jiayuguan
rows.summary: A theme park of the Chinese Fantawild chain, opened in 2015 on Fangte Avenue in Jiayuguan's southern district, with twenty-odd rides, dark rides and shows built around Chinese stories and 4D and interactive effects, among them a flying-theatre ride, a snow-mountain adventure, a magic-castle show, a log flume and Boonie Bears attractions. The same company's second park in the city, Fantawild Silk Road Myth, has rides and shows on Silk Road, legend and folk-culture themes; both suit families and groups of young people.

rows.name: Wei–Jin Tombs, Jiayuguan
rows.summary: A large cemetery of brick tombs from the Wei and Jin periods (3rd–5th centuries) in the Gobi between Jiayuguan and Jiuquan, known as the 'underground gallery' for its painted bricks. Each brick in the tomb walls carries a small, freely drawn scene of daily life in the Hexi Corridor, such as farming, herding, butchering and feasting, and an excavated tomb near Xincheng is open so visitors can see the paintings in place.

rows.name: Zixuan Winery Estate
rows.summary: The winery estate of Gansu Zixuan Wine, part of the JISCO (Jiuquan Iron and Steel) group, on the airport road north-east of Jiayuguan, covering about 65 ha. Visitors tour the winery and its 13,700 m² underground barrel cellar, which the city presents as the largest single wine cellar in Asia, taste the wines and pick grapes in season; wine and grape-seed products are sold on site.

rows.name: Beihaizi Pagoda
rows.summary: A Ming–Qing brick Buddhist pagoda in Beihaizi Park, also called North Lake, the old temple grounds on the northern edge of Yongchang that grew from the Tang-founded Jinchuan Temple into the town's leading Chan Buddhist complex by the Qing. The park keeps the pagoda, the Five Buddhas Temple, a lake pavilion and old trees, and hosts Yongchang's temple fair on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month.

rows.name: Jinshui Lake
rows.summary: A man-made lake park east of central Jinchang, built between 2005 and 2008 as a water-storage and landscape project in this water-short city: five lakes linked by ribbon wetlands, with islands, bridges and jetties, cover about 236 hectares, 60 of them water. It is an open suburban green space with themed scenic corners, exercise and older people's activity areas and an outdoor nature-education zone.

rows.name: Mars Base 1
rows.summary: A Mars-themed experience park on the red-rock Gobi south of Jinchang, built from 2022 because the terrain resembles the Martian surface, with simulated survival bases and science-fiction sets that have also served as film and television locations. Visitors can try more than 30 activities such as a weightlessness experience, live role-play games and 'Mars sleeping pods'; it is aimed at families and school study trips.

rows.name: Shengrong Temple Pagodas
rows.summary: Two square Tang brick pagodas face each other across the Yushan gorge north of Yongchang, regarded as the oldest surviving pagodas in Gansu: the larger, 16.2 m tall and shaped like Xi'an's Small Wild Goose Pagoda, has murals inside with inscriptions naming the temple, and the smaller solid one is 4.9 m. They belonged to Shengrong Temple, which local records date to 561 and which the Sui emperor Yang renamed Gantong Temple when he visited in 609; a Northern Wei stone Buddha, the temple's famous 'auspicious image', still stands against the cliff, and its legend is painted in several of the Mogao caves at Dunhuang.

rows.name: Yongchang Bell and Drum Tower
rows.summary: The landmark of Yongchang's town centre, completed in 1587: a square platform of rammed earth faced with brick, 7.2 m high and pierced by four arched passages, carries a two-storey timber tower with three tiers of eaves, 24.5 m tall in all, with a great iron bell on the platform and a large drum inside. Damaged in the 1927 Gulang earthquake, it was dismantled and rebuilt to its original form in 1984–86, and inscribed boards on every side carry phrases such as 'Embracing the Western Regions'.

rows.name: Zijin Flower City
rows.summary: A flower park of about 38 hectares on the northern outskirts of Jinchang, planted with some 40 kinds of herbs and flowers, among them lavender, verbena and cosmos, that colour the fields purple in the flowering season. It is the core of a wider planned green belt on the city's northern side and is visited for walks and photographs among the flowers.

rows.name: Boluozhuanjing Film Base (Old Aksay Town)
rows.summary: The abandoned former seat of Aksay Kazakh Autonomous County, on the northern slopes of the Altyn-Tagh, left empty when the county town moved down to the plain in 1998 and since used as a film set. Most of its buildings date from around 1980, and films shot among its empty streets since 2002 include Hero, Wind Blast and Dragon Blade.

rows.name: Changma Grottoes
rows.summary: Buddhist cave temples in the Changma basin south-west of Yumen, dated by their national listing (2019) to the Northern Wei through the Qing. The Jiuquan tourism bureau counts the caves, with the Luzigou and Qingshigou rock art nearby, among the sights of the Changma valley, an upland area of snow peaks, gorges, grassland and wetland.

rows.name: Chijin Gorge Reservoir
rows.summary: A scenic area built around the Chijin Gorge reservoir on the Shiyou River in Chijin town, between Yumen's old and new towns, run as a water-conservancy scenic area in the Gobi. The earth dam, built in 1968 and given a wave wall in 1978, holds a reservoir of up to about 11 km² that irrigates the surrounding oasis farmland, and the grounds hold a replica of the Han dynasty Yumen Pass, a Dragon King Pavilion and other newly built shrines, a Han beacon tower, a Qing stele and the remains of an old post station.

rows.name: Guazhou Gobi Sculpture Corridor
rows.name_zh: 瓜州戈壁雕塑艺术长廊
rows.summary: A group of large outdoor artworks in the Gobi on the road from Guazhou towards the Yulin Caves. The best known is Son of the Earth, a sleeping baby 15 m long carved in red sandstone by Tsinghua University sculptor Dong Shubing, and close by stands his Boundless, a 60 m-long, 21 m-high white steel frame of palace pavilions drawn from Dunhuang murals; other works include Han Wu Xiong Feng and Gobi Ark.

rows.name: Jianshui Jinguan and Diwan Fort (Juyan Han Frontier Sites)
rows.summary: The Gansu part of the Juyan frontier sites: Han dynasty forts and a checkpoint on the east bank of the Ejin (Hei) River in northern Jinta county, part of the Han defences that run on into Inner Mongolia. Diwan fort, built of rammed earth around 121 BC as the seat of the Jianshui frontier command, stands 500 m south of the Jianshui Jinguan checkpoint and 9 km north of the Dawan forts, and thousands of Han wooden slips have been excavated here since 1930; the county has made the three sites into a military-history scenic area.

rows.name: Jinta Desert Poplar Forest
rows.summary: A planted forest of Euphrates poplars on the desert edge north-west of Jinta town, grown through volunteer tree-planting campaigns since the 1960s to stop the sand at what had been the county's worst wind gap; the poplar scenic area covers nearly 10,000 mu (about 6.7 km²). Local media call it the largest planted forest in the Hexi Corridor, and it is at its best in late September and October, when the leaves turn gold.

rows.name: Jiuquan Drum Tower
rows.summary: The landmark tower at the central crossroads of Jiuquan: its rammed-earth base was the east gate tower of the city rebuilt under the Former Liang in the 4th century, found itself at the centre of town when the walls were extended east in the Ming, and was faced with brick in 1725. The three-storey wooden tower on top dates from 1905, after a fire in 1865, and the four arched gateways carry inscriptions naming where each road leads: Mount Hua to the east, Yiwu (Hami) to the west, the Qilian Mountains to the south and the desert to the north.

rows.name: Jiuquan Park (Western Han Jiuquan Scenic Spot)
rows.summary: A lake park on the east side of central Jiuquan around the spring that gave the city its name: legend says the Han general Huo Qubing poured wine from the emperor into it to share with his troops. Soldiers and residents organised by the Qing general Zuo Zongtang are said to have dug out the lake and planted the trees, the Nationalist government named it Quanhu Park in 1942, and today, as the Western Han Jiuquan Scenic Spot, it has the old spring, pools, pavilions and willows more than 130 years old from Zuo's time.

rows.name: Jiuquan Tianbao Ornamental Stone Exhibition
rows.summary: An indoor exhibition of ornamental stones in a shopping complex in Jiuquan's Suzhou district, presented by its operators as China's largest stone-appreciation attraction. Its halls show the 'four famous stones' of ancient China and modern collectors' stones, with large holdings of yardang stones, 'cartoon' stones and the locally named Jiuquan black eagle stone, and it runs study courses for school groups.

rows.name: Qilian Reed Sea
rows.summary: A reed, cattail and marsh wetland in Yinda town on the northern edge of the Jiuquan oasis, at the edge of the Badain Jaran desert, with the Ming Great Wall along its south side. Reed beds turn golden under white plumes in autumn and water birds live among them; it suits a short outing from the city rather than a special trip.

rows.name: Suoyang City
rows.summary: The ruins of a walled Silk Road city in the Gobi south-east of Guazhou, seat of Guazhou prefecture under the Tang and abandoned in the 16th century; the rammed-earth walls of the inner city still stand 9–12.5 m high. The archaeological park also takes in the Ta'er Temple ruins, ancient irrigation canals and more than 2,000 tombs, and the site is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing (2014).

rows.name: Xuanquan Post Station Site
