rows.summary: A Han dynasty relay station on the Silk Road between Dunhuang and Guazhou, in use from about 111 BC until the Wei–Jin period to lodge envoys, officials and foreign guests. Excavations in the early 1990s recovered some 70,000 objects, including about 35,000 inscribed wooden and bamboo slips, after which the ruins were backfilled for protection, and the site is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing. A visitor area opened in 2025 beside the motorway with a full-size reconstruction of the station, and a display centre with 3D and interactive exhibits on the excavations was completed the same year.

rows.name: Xueyu Ziting Eco-Cultural Park
rows.summary: An open park in Dangchengwan, the county town of Subei Mongol Autonomous County, made up of a flower field of about 1,000 mu, Ziting Lake and a fruit and vegetable picking garden. In late summer and early autumn the beds of cosmos, calendula, cleome and other annuals are in full flower, with boardwalks, pavilions and windmills among them; it is mainly a leisure spot for residents and passing travellers.

rows.name: Yang Pass
rows.summary: The site of Yangguan, the southern of the two Han dynasty frontier passes west of Dunhuang, fortified around 120 BC to guard the southern Silk Road route to the Western Regions; the fort had fallen into ruin by about AD 900. The scenic area has the Yangguan Museum next to the site, and the pass is remembered through Wang Wei's Tang poem of parting, which made 'west of Yang Pass' a byword for leaving old friends behind.

rows.name: Yulin Caves
rows.summary: Buddhist cave temples cut into both cliffs of the Yulin River gorge south of Guazhou, regarded as a sister site of the Mogao Caves and managed by the Dunhuang Academy. About 43 caves hold some 270 painted statues and more than 5,200 m² of wall paintings from the Tang to the Yuan, with secular scenes such as farming, wine-making, a smelting furnace and a wedding among the Buddhist subjects. The Eastern Thousand Buddha Caves, about 45 km to the east, belong to the same protected unit and have eight decorated caves of the Western Xia and Yuan.

rows.name: Yumen Oilfield Old No. 1 Well
rows.summary: The old oil town of Yumen, regarded as the cradle of China's oil industry, is where in 1939 geologist Sun Jianchu's team drilled the first well beside the small Laojunmiao temple; until the Daqing field was found, the Yumen field was the country's largest. The red-tourism area keeps the Old No. 1 Well with a pumping unit, the Qing-dynasty temple, a monument to Sun Jianchu, a statue and memorial hall for the oil worker Wang Jinxi and an oil-city park.

rows.name: Yumen Pass
rows.summary: The Jade Gate, the Han dynasty frontier pass at the western end of the Hexi defence line beyond Dunhuang, through which the northern Silk Road left for the Western Regions; it is traditionally said to be named after the jade brought in from the west. Visitors see the square rammed-earth fort known as Xiaofangpan, the larger Dafangpan ruins, a Han granary, and stretches of Han wall and beacon towers in the Gobi, and the site is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing (2014).

rows.name: Yuze Lake Park
rows.summary: A city park in Yumen's new town, begun in 2000 when the city government moved here from the old oil town, laid out around an inner lake, an outer lake and a newer extension. Paths link a cultural promenade, squares, a lake island, wetland and a children's play area, with landmarks such as the Yanyu Pavilion, a memorial archway, a zigzag bridge, an old-style water tower and a Ferris wheel.

rows.name: Zhang Zhi Calligraphy Culture Park (Caosheng Guli)
rows.summary: A calligraphy-themed culture park in Guazhou county town honouring Zhang Zhi, the Eastern Han calligrapher from this region who is revered in China as the 'sage of cursive script'. Its 681 mu of grounds hold water features, pavilions, halls, sculpture and steles, including a memorial square with his statue and a memorial hall, and it suits visitors with a strong interest in Chinese calligraphy.

rows.name: Five Springs Park (Wuquan Mountain)
rows.summary: A hillside park on the northern slopes of Gaolan Mountain in southern Lanzhou, named after five springs that legend says appeared when the Han general Huo Qubing struck the ground with his whip. Temples climb the slope in 25 building groups first built in the Yuan and extended through the Ming, Qing and Republican periods, among them Junyuan Temple, a Wenchang Palace, a Wuhou Shrine to Zhuge Liang and a Thousand Buddha Pavilion. It became a public park in 1955 and holds a temple fair on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month.

rows.name: Former Lanzhou Office of the Eighth Route Army
rows.name_zh: 八路军兰州办事处旧址
rows.summary: The Eighth Route Army's office in Lanzhou from August 1937 to November 1943, during the wartime cooperation between the Communists and the Nationalists against Japan. Its two compounds, on Jiuquan Road and Gannan Road about 220 m apart, form a memorial museum that reopened after restoration in 2011, on the office's work and on its leaders and visitors, among them Xie Juezai, Zhou Enlai and Ren Bishi.

rows.name: Gan'en Temple, Hongcheng
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist temple built in Chinese style in Hongcheng town, founded in 1492–1494 by the fifth Lu chieftain of Liancheng and named Gan'en ('Gratitude') by the Hongzhi Emperor in 1495. Its Ming buildings survive around a main Buddha hall; the statues and wall paintings inside today, including scenes from Journey to the West, are later work.

rows.name: Hekou Ancient Town
rows.summary: A former Yellow River ferry and trading town on the western edge of Lanzhou, where the Zhuanglang River joins the Yellow River, restored since 2014 as a historic district around Hekou village. Its 'four streets and seventeen lanes' radiate from a two-storey bell and drum tower, lined with 37 Ming and Qing courtyard houses, the site of Gansu's first customs house and shops selling local snacks. Local traditions such as the military Nuo dance and Hekou gauze lanterns are kept up here.

rows.name: Jincheng Pass Cultural Park
rows.summary: A riverside cultural park on the north bank of the Yellow River at the foot of Baita Mountain, centred on a reconstruction of Jincheng Pass, the fortified gate that guarded the old river crossing. It houses small museums on Yellow River bridges, Qinqiang opera and painted pottery. The 4A scenic area, rated in December 2023, also takes in Zhongshan Bridge and Baita Mountain Park, which rises directly behind the pass.

rows.name: Jintian Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex founded in 1400 outside the old west gate of Lanzhou, whose surviving halls, mostly of Qing date, stand on three parallel axes. Most of its grounds became the Lanzhou Workers' Cultural Palace, and its entrance was moved from the south to the north side when the Lanzhou–Xinjiang railway was built. Halls on the central axis are dedicated to Zhenwu, the Jade Emperor, the Three Pure Ones and Laozi, among others.

rows.name: Lanzhou Prefecture City God Temple
rows.summary: Lanzhou's City God temple, dedicated like Tianshui's to the Han general Ji Xin, dates back at least to the Song and took its present layout after a rebuilding in 1837. Along its axis stand a memorial archway moved here in 1956 from a Ming princely garden, an opera stage rebuilt in 2003, an offering hall with gilded Qing boards and a double-eaved main hall; the compound is used as the city's No. 1 Workers' Club.

rows.name: Lanzhou Shuimo Danxia
rows.summary: A badlands landscape of banded red and grey hills in Shuping town in the north-west of Lanzhou municipality, opened on a trial basis in 2020 after the brickworks that once dug its red clay were closed. In the core visiting area, roads and walkways link a series of viewing platforms over the eroded ridges and gullies.

rows.name: Lanzhou Waterwheel Expo Park
rows.summary: A riverside culture park on the south bank of the Yellow River, opened in 2005 to recall the giant wooden waterwheels that once lined the river at Lanzhou, lifting water to irrigate the fields along its banks. Replica Yellow River waterwheels turn alongside other types of waterwheel from around the world, in a waterwheel garden, a waterwheel square and a culture square on the riverside promenade.

rows.name: Lu Tusi Yamen and Miaoyin Temple
rows.summary: The seat of the Lu chieftains, descendants of a Mongol Yuan prince who submitted to the Ming and ruled Liancheng for nineteen generations until 1931, with a residence first built in 1378. Beside it stands Miaoyin Temple, a Tibetan Buddhist monastery founded in 1427 whose Wansui Hall and Duojiqiang Hall keep Ming and Qing ceiling paintings of mandalas, and the Xianjiao Temple hall across the street is also part of the site.

rows.name: Qingcheng Ancient Town
rows.summary: An old river town on the Yellow River at the northern tip of Yuzhong County, listed as a national historic and cultural town, whose Ming-to-Republican courtyard houses are protected as a national heritage site. Its sights include the Gao family ancestral hall, the Luo family courtyard, the Qingcheng Academy and a City God temple.

rows.name: Qiyun Pastoral Town, Yuzhong
rows.summary: A rural leisure complex built around Lijiazhuang village on the edge of Yuzhong county town, with flower fields, farm restaurants, guesthouses, play attractions for children and craft workshops. It was rated a national 4A scenic area in 2024.

rows.name: Renshou Mountain, Anning
rows.summary: A hill park on the north side of Anning District in western Lanzhou, set among peach orchards. It is the main venue of Lanzhou's annual Peach Blossom Festival, held when the trees flower in mid-April, with photography exhibitions, food markets and performances.

rows.name: Shichuan Ancient Pear Orchard
rows.summary: An orchard of centuries-old pear trees on the Yellow River flats around Shichuan town in Gaolan County, where the Ming set up a garrison fort in 1495. The trees flower in mid-April, when the town holds blossom-season events, and in summer their broad canopies shade picnics and walks between the villages.

rows.name: Shifogou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the wooded hills of Agan town on the southern edge of Lanzhou, the closest of the city's forest parks. Gentle trails and boardwalks follow the valleys, where summer temperatures stay several degrees below the city's, and farmhouse restaurants along the way serve local dishes such as jiangshui noodles.

rows.name: Tulugou National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in Liancheng town in the north-west of Yongdeng County, where gorges, streams, waterfalls and dense forest make it one of Lanzhou's main summer retreats. It can be combined with the Lu Tusi Yamen and Miaoyin Temple in Liancheng.

rows.name: Western Dinosaur Water Park, Lanzhou New Area
rows.summary: A large water park in Lanzhou New Area, about 7 km south of Zhongchuan Airport, built in 2017 as part of a resort district developed with the company behind Changzhou's China Dinosaurs Park. An indoor water hall under a glass dome shaped like a dinosaur egg is paired with outdoor slides, pools and a lazy river, aimed at families.

rows.name: Xinglong Mountain
rows.summary: A forested mountain range in Yuzhong County south-east of Lanzhou, protected as a national nature reserve since 1988, whose seven peaks rise to 3,021 m. The scenic area is divided into an eastern and a western mountain, with wooded trails and temples, and its summer temperatures average around 18°C, well below the city's.

rows.name: Zhongshan Bridge
rows.summary: Lanzhou's best-known landmark, a steel truss bridge across the Yellow River completed in 1909 by a German firm as the first permanent bridge over the river at Lanzhou, replacing a pontoon bridge on the same crossing. Renamed in 1928 in honour of Sun Yat-sen, it gained its arched upper trusses when it was strengthened in 1954 and has been open only to pedestrians since 2004. From the deck there are views along the river and up to Baita Mountain on the north bank.

rows.name: Bafang Thirteen Lanes
rows.summary: The old Hui Muslim quarter of Linxia, the historic Hezhou, where eight mosque communities (fang) grew up around their mosques and thirteen lanes took shape from the early Qing; some 2,000 households still live here, more than 98 per cent of them Hui. Renovated without moving its residents out, it is now a culture and leisure district of grey-brick courtyard houses, mosques, craft workshops and food stalls, where Hui brick carving, wood carving and painted decoration can be seen and listed buildings include the dragon screen wall of the North Mosque and the courtyard at 80 Daga Lane.

rows.name: Bingling Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: Buddhist caves and niches carved over some 1,600 years into the red sandstone cliffs of the Dasi gully on the north bank of the Yellow River, in the Xiaojishi Mountains 35 km south-west of Yongjing county town; Cave 169, with an inscription of 420 under the Western Qin, is described by the site's conservation institute as the earliest dated cave in China. About 216 caves and niches survive with more than 800 statues and some 1,000 m² of murals in both Chinese and Tibetan Buddhist styles, the largest figure being a seated Tang Maitreya 27 m high, and the site is part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing of 2014. The 5A tourism area also takes in the Liujiaxia Dam and reservoir and the Bingling Stone Forest of red sandstone pinnacles, part of the Linxia UNESCO Global Geopark since 2024.

rows.name: Dadun Gorge
rows.summary: A system of four gorges about 13 km long, forming a Y shape below Heida Mountain (3,300 m), 6 km west of Dahejia town in Jishishan, the autonomous county of the Bonan (Bao'an), Dongxiang and Salar peoples. Cliffs, five streams, more than twenty waterfalls and many springs fill the gorges, and the plant life is rich, with rhododendrons and lilac in flower in early summer and frozen waterfalls in winter; parking areas, restaurants and visitor facilities are at the entrance.

rows.name: East Mansion and Butterfly Building, Linxia
rows.summary: Two Republican-era mansions in Linxia city: the East Mansion (Donggongguan), completed in 1947 as the residence of Ma Buqing, a north-western warlord general, and the smaller Butterfly Building in the Bafang quarter about 1 km to the west-south-west. The East Mansion, now a museum and a 3A scenic area, is visited above all for the Linxia brick carving on its courtyard walls and screens.

rows.name: Fataishan Resort
rows.summary: A year-round resort in Songming town next to the Songmingyan scenic area, with the Songmingyan International Ski Resort for winter sport and, in summer, a glass walkway, mountain rafting, grass-sliding and children's play areas such as go-karts. It also hosts events such as hua'er folk-song contests and bonfire evenings, so it suits families and groups looking for an active day out rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Hezheng Paleozoological Museum
rows.name_zh: 和政古动物化石博物馆
rows.summary: A museum of fossil animals in Hezheng county town, founded in 2003 and now a national first-grade museum, holding more than 40,000 fossils from the late Cenozoic beds of the Linxia Basin. Its collections include giant rhinoceroses, shovel-tusked elephants, the three-toed horse Hipparion, the giant horse Equus eisenmannae, the giant hyena and the Hezheng sheep, which the museum describes as unique to Hezheng, and it is a core site of the Linxia UNESCO Global Geopark.

rows.name: Hualin Fossil Site (Wanshou Valley)
rows.summary: A fossil site in a farming valley at Hualin, south-east of Hezheng county town, whose in-situ fossil hall (opened 2013) shows about 3,200 m² of Hipparion-fauna bones, some 11 to 5 million years old, as they lay when buried. The valley's rocks record four successive mammal faunas of the Linxia Basin, from giant rhinoceroses of about 27 million years ago to Equus horses of about 2 million years ago, and the site also has a geological section and the geopark's main monument square.

rows.name: Kangle Birch Forest
rows.summary: A scenic area of natural forest at Liewa village in Basong township, on the Taizi Mountains tourist highway in southern Kangle County, where some 3,000 mu (200 ha) of birch woods cover the hillsides and forest cover reaches about 95 per cent. It has a visitor centre, nature trails and a woodland play area, and draws visitors for summer shade, golden autumn leaves and winter ice-and-snow events.

rows.name: Linjia Neolithic Site and Painted Pottery Centre
rows.summary: A Neolithic settlement of the Majiayao culture on the loess tableland at Linjia village in Dongyuan township, excavated in 1978, where a small bronze knife of about 3000 BC, promoted locally as the earliest in China, came to light. Beside the site the Linjia Painted Pottery Heritage Base, a study centre, has a 400 m² hall showing about 300 craft reproductions of pottery from the Dadiwan, Yangshao, Majiayao and Qijia cultures, reconstructed burial and site scenes, and workshops where visitors can shape, paint and fire pots in the old way.

rows.name: Liujiaxia Dinosaur National Geopark
rows.name_zh: 刘家峡恐龙国家地质公园
rows.summary: A geopark in Yanguoxia town protecting Early Cretaceous dinosaur trackways found in 1999 in the rocks above the Yellow River, with footprints of sauropods, theropods, ornithopods and pterosaurs as well as resting traces, tail drags, ripple marks and plant fossils. Its core is the hall over the first trackway site, covering about 1,400 m² of rock with 276 prints in 23 trackways on five levels, including a sauropod hind print 1.5 m long billed as the largest known; at the entrance a wall of full-size casts shows the main kinds.

rows.name: Liujiaxia International Paragliding Camp
rows.summary: A paragliding base on the north shore of the Liujiaxia Reservoir (Bingling Lake) in Yangta township, with its launch on Huangjia Mountain at about 2,300 m and a height difference of some 580 m to the landing ground. It hosts rounds of the national paragliding league and pilots' meets with powered and smoke-trail flying displays, and the county is promoting it for low-altitude tourism.

rows.name: Qijiaping Site (Qijia Culture)
rows.summary: The type site of the Qijia culture (about 2300–1500 BC), one of China's earliest Bronze Age cultures, found in 1924 by the Swedish geologist Johan Gunnar Andersson on a terrace of the Tao River at Yuanziping village in Qijia town; it is described locally as the only site to have yielded all five kinds of early artefact, in stone, bone, pottery, jade and bronze. A Qijia Culture archaeological site park is being laid out here, its visitor centre completed in 2025, and the finds are shown at the Qijia Culture Museum in Guanghe county town, which holds more than 4,000 objects including a bronze mirror billed as China's earliest.

rows.name: Songmingyan
rows.summary: A national forest park and provincial scenic area in the foothills of the Taizi Mountains in Songming town, named for the roar of the wind in its pines echoing off the cliffs. Temples first built in the Ming, among them the Yuhuang Pavilion, the Bodhisattva Hall, the Shengmu Palace and the Dugang Temple, cling to the cliffs among the forest, and from the 26th to the 29th day of the fourth lunar month it holds a large hua'er folk-song fair.

rows.name: Yanzhi Lake Park
rows.summary: A town park in Kangle county town at the meeting of the Yanzhi, Zhongdi and Suji rivers, laid out around Yanzhi Lake with three stone arch bridges and a three-storey pavilion standing in the middle of the lake. It also has a children's park, a fun park and a sports park, flower beds from spring to autumn and light displays at night.

rows.name: Zhuzigou Valley
rows.summary: A valley inside the Taizishan nature reserve at Bazigou village, Minglu township, in southern Kangle County, with alpine meadows, forest and streams, which joined the 4A list in January 2026. Summer visitors come for the meadows and for folk-song and music events, and in winter the valley offers horse-drawn sleighs, a ski slope, a rime-coated "ice cave" and hotpot in heated tents; a small amusement park with a rainbow slide and fairground rides opened beside it in April 2026.

rows.name: Bikou Old Town
rows.summary: Bikou is an old trading town on the Bailong River near the Sichuan border, long a landing where goods such as medicinal herbs were loaded for shipment downriver, and most of its merchants came from Sichuan, which gave it a Sichuan-flavoured dialect and a taste for Sichuan opera. Its old lanes and merchants' shopfronts recall that trade, tea gardens climb the hills around it and the Bikou Reservoir lies just upstream; it was named a provincial historic town in 2006.

rows.name: Chenyuan Eco-Park
rows.summary: An 8.7 km² rural leisure park in Chenyuan town, just west of Chengxian, laid out with orchards, woods and flower-lined roads. It combines countryside sightseeing with farming-culture activities, children's cartoon-themed amusements and stalls selling local produce, and suits families on a day out.

rows.name: Dabuzishan Qin Royal Cemetery
rows.summary: On the hills above the Western Han River east of Li County town lies the Dabuzishan cemetery of the early Qin lords at Xichui, the Qin people's first centre, with the earliest tombs of Qin rulers yet excavated. The tombs were heavily looted in the late 1980s and early 1990s and many objects went abroad; rescue excavations began in 1994, and the finds are shown in the Gansu Qin Culture Museum in Li County town. The site is on China's list of national archaeological park projects, and the county includes the Xichui cemetery in its visitor routes.

rows.name: Du Fu Thatched Cottage, Chengxian
rows.summary: The Du Gong Shrine at the mouth of Feilong Gorge, south-east of Chengxian, commemorates the poet Du Fu, who stayed briefly at Tonggu, as the town was then called, in 759 before moving on to Chengdu; it is promoted as the earliest of China's many Du Fu 'thatched cottages'. Its courtyard of old cypresses holds more than ten steles from the Song to the Republican era, and paths lead on into the gorge to the Phoenix Terrace, Wanzhang Pool and an old plank road.

rows.name: Fujin Guangyan Temple
rows.summary: Fujin Guangyan Temple in Sanhe town, Wudu, is a Buddhist temple founded in the Song whose timber hall dates from the Southern Song, with Qing repairs. It was listed as a provincial heritage unit in 1993 and as a national one in 2019, and it is of interest mainly to those who follow early Chinese timber architecture.

rows.name: Gansu Qin Culture Museum
rows.summary: The Gansu Qin Culture Museum on Qinren Square in Li County town has a collection of several thousand objects, many recovered from the early Qin cemetery at Dabuzishan and the Xichui area. Highlights include a small four-wheeled cart, ding and gui vessels of the Qin lords and a set of Qin bells, which together show the archaeology of the Qin homeland before the state moved east.

rows.name: Guan'egou Scenic Area
rows.summary: Guan'egou is a set of forested gorges on the edge of Tanchang county town, where Guanzhu Gully, Eman Gully and Leigu Mountain are linked into one U-shaped circuit of about 66 km². Paths follow the streams past waterfalls, the valleys turn red and gold in autumn, and since May 2025 a 2.5 km cable car has linked Guanzhu Gully with the upper areas towards Leigu Mountain. It became a national geopark in 2014 and a 5A scenic area in 2022.

rows.name: Hadapu Long March Sites
rows.summary: Hadapu, a town on the old route between Sichuan and the north-west, is where Red Army columns on the Long March halted and reorganised in 1935, and where the Party leadership decided to head for the Communist base in northern Shaanxi. Its Red Army Street keeps buildings used at the time, including the Guandi Temple where a cadres' meeting was held and the old post office, and a Long March memorial hall tells the story. The town is a national historic town and one of China's red-tourism classic scenic areas.

rows.name: Huaqiao Village, Kang County
rows.summary: Huaqiao is a village in Changba town, in the hills of western Kang County, that has been developed as a rural tourism area with countryside walks, holiday and retirement stays, folk-culture experiences including traditional liquor-making, and a centre where local farm produce is processed and sold. It has been named a model rural-tourism village and serves as a rural tourism training base for Gansu, so it suits visitors curious about village life in the hills of southern Gansu.

rows.name: Jialing River Gorges, Hui County
rows.summary: A large scenic area of 217.6 km² along the gorges of the upper Jialing River in south-eastern Hui County, with cliffs, forest, caves and waterfalls, among them the Meiya Falls, which drop more than 400 m. Visitors can hike Moon Gorge, see the formations of Swallow Cave, walk through the Ming–Qing houses of Daoping old village, raft a 13 km stretch of the river in summer and, in autumn, see the 153 ancient ginkgo trees of Tianhe village; remains of old plank roads on the Shu roads survive along the cliffs.

rows.name: Jinhui Liquor Culture Park
rows.summary: The landscaped brewery park of Jinhui, a strong-aroma baijiu maker whose roots go back to a state distillery formed from local workshops in 1951, in Fujia town north-west of Hui County town. Visitors see the liquor-culture exhibition hall, the brewing workshops, the pottery-jar and stainless-steel storage halls and the bottling line, with gardens, a cherry-tree avenue and a spring-fed lake around them; it suits those curious about how Chinese liquor is made.

rows.name: Jinhui Mining Industrial Tourism Area
rows.summary: An industrial tourism site at Jinhui Mining's lead–zinc mine north of Hui County town, on the Xicheng lead–zinc belt. The company presents it as a green, digitised mine with its works underground and landscaped gardens on the surface, and it offers sightseeing and popular-science visits for those interested in modern mining.

rows.name: Liangdang Mutiny Memorial Hall
rows.summary: This memorial hall in Liangdang county town commemorates the Liangdang Mutiny of 2 April 1932, when Xi Zhongxun and other Communist organisers led about 200 soldiers of a Nationalist battalion stationed in the area into revolt and reformed them as a Red Army guerrilla detachment, which was later broken up. The red-tourism scenic area links the hall with the battalion's former command post, the site of the mutiny, the camp at Yangdian and Taiyang Temple, where the detachment was reorganised, and it is used for patriotic and Party education.

rows.name: Lichuan Brick Pagoda
rows.summary: A Northern Song brick pagoda, also called the Lichuan White Pagoda, in Xunzhuang village west of Hui County town, the surviving part of the White Pagoda Temple built in the Chunhua era (990–994). Repaired in the Daoguang era as an octagonal tower of twelve storeys, it lost its upper storeys in the earthquake of 1879 and now stands nine storeys high.

rows.name: New Baishui Road Cliff Inscription
rows.summary: A Northern Song cliff inscription at Wangjiahe village south of Hui County town, recording in 883 characters of regular script, set out in 26 columns, how the Baishui road through these mountains was built and later rerouted. The text was written out by the Song official Lei Jianfu, and the carving is listed among China's notable ancient steles and inscriptions.

rows.name: Qishan Fort and Wuhou Shrine
rows.summary: The Qishan scenic area east of Li County town is built around Qishan Fort and its Wuhou Shrine to Zhuge Liang, one of the earliest shrines to him, rebuilt in the Ming and Qing dynasties, on the ground where Shu Han armies campaigned against Wei in the Three Kingdoms period. Around it are some ten sites linked by tradition to those campaigns, such as the terrace where Zhuge Liang is said to have reviewed his troops, a hollow where troops were hidden and an old cypress named after him.

rows.name: Shanwan Menggu Valley
rows.summary: A valley resort of about 240 ha in Lianghekou town, Tanchang, built around the Qiang and Tibetan culture of the area, with flower fields and farmland on the valley floor and forest above. About 6.5 km up from the gate, a homestay village mixes surviving village houses with new buildings in Qiang–Tibetan style, and visitors come for local food, Qiang folk-culture activities and walks; it suits families and visitors wanting a quiet countryside stay.

rows.name: Wangba Rural Scenic Area, Kang County
rows.summary: A rural scenic area of villages and wooded valleys around Wangba town, 10 km from Kang county town, centred on Dashuigou village, with a village-life exhibition hall, log-cabin lodgings and the cliffs of Qinglin Gully. The township's folk arts, among them the bangbang whip performance, ballad singing and sheepskin-drum music, were listed as Longnan intangible heritage in 2006, and the area suits visitors looking for a short countryside stay.

rows.name: Wanxia Lake
rows.summary: Wanxia Lake is a reservoir lake of about 120 ha just west of Xihe county town, with reed beds, water birds and boat trips on the water. Its Qiqiao culture garden has a statue of the Weaving Maid by the sculptor He E and a museum of Xihe's Qiqiao (Double Seventh) festival, which draws crowds to the lake at festival time.

rows.name: Wanxiang Cave
rows.summary: A large karst cave on the south side of the Bailong River east of Wudu, filled with stalactites and other formations along the visitor route, whose walls carry inscriptions and poems left by visitors since the Northern Zhou. Its name was written by Zhao Puchu, and a second, sister cave was found nearby in 2007. It is a provincial heritage unit, scenic area and geopark.

rows.name: Wenxian Tianchi Lake
rows.summary: Wenxian Tianchi, also called Yangtang Tianchi, is a long, winding mountain lake formed where faulting dammed the Yangtang River in the mountains north of Wen County, its shoreline broken by headlands and ringed by forested peaks. Together with the smaller Penjing Pool, where trees grow out of the shallow water, the Yinma Pool and Huanglin Gully, it forms one scenic area that is at its best in autumn colour.

rows.name: Xixia Ode and Ancient Plank Road
rows.summary: In the Tianjing Mountain gorge west of Chengxian, the Xixia Ode was cut into the cliff in AD 171 to praise Li Xi, governor of Wudu, for building a plank road through the gorge; its 385 characters of clerical script under a seal-script heading, beside a carved panel of five auspicious omens, make it one of the 'Three Odes of Han' prized by calligraphers. A walkway leads through the steep, wooded gorge past traces of the old plank road, later inscriptions and pools such as Huanglong Pool.

rows.name: Yangba Scenic Area
rows.summary: Yangba, in the far south of Kang County, is a humid, forested valley area of bamboo groves, streams, tea gardens and palms, promoted as the 'Xishuangbanna of Gansu' for its almost subtropical feel. Its best-known parts are Meiyuan Gully, Hongdou Valley and the old-growth forest along the Qing River, where paths follow clear streams and pools.

rows.name: Yunhua Mountain
rows.summary: Yunhua Mountain, north-east of Xihe, is a steep danxia-type peak shaped like a jade tablet, which gave it the old name Guishan, with more than ten small Daoist temple halls, including one to the Xuanwu emperor, packed onto its narrow summit. It is known locally as a long-standing Daoist mountain and as the birthplace of Xihe's Qiqiao (Double Seventh) festival, and in autumn the summit often looks out over a sea of cloud.

rows.name: Yunping Three Gorges
rows.summary: The Yunping Three Gorges, Tudi, Guanyin and Xigou, cut through forested mountains south-east of Liangdang and form a provincial scenic area of cliffs, overhanging pines, waterfalls and caves with more than 60 named sights, among them a temple and two rock 'gates'. Lacebark pines and red leaves make autumn a good time for the walks, and the area lies over the ridge from the Santan scenic area in Hui County.

rows.name: Zhang Guolao Scenic Area, Liangdang
rows.summary: A rural scenic area of about 320 ha in the hills of Yangdian town, north-east of Liangdang, built around the Guolao Dengzhen Cave, which legend links with the Daoist immortal Zhang Guolao. Around it are a farm park, the traditional village of Chengou, an eco-sightseeing garden and pine woods with a large natural stand of lacebark pines, and three of Liangdang's traditional Eight Views lie within it. It suits walkers and visitors after a quiet countryside stay.

rows.name: Zhujiagou Old Village, Anmenkou
rows.summary: Zhujiagou is an old village on the Yanzi River near Anmenkou town, listed as a Chinese traditional village in 2016, whose main sights are the Qing-style Zhu family compound, a covered 'wind-and-rain' bridge and an ancient Chinese wingnut tree said to be a thousand years old. The wider Anmenkou scenic area adds a valley of old ginkgo trees and an eco-farm, and the town has some fifteen homestays and twenty farm stays, so it is easy to stay overnight.

rows.name: Ancient Lingtai and Jingshan Forest Park
rows.summary: A wooded hill park on Zhongtai Hill in the middle of Lingtai town, around the 'Ancient Lingtai', the terrace that legend says King Wen of Zhou raised for offerings to Heaven after his campaign against the state of Mixu. Modern Han-style gateways, pavilions and a hall to three local worthies, among them the physician Huangfu Mi, line the paths to a hilltop viewpoint, and the park also holds the Lingtai County Museum, strong in Western Zhou bronzes, and a memorial hall on the county's revolutionary history.

rows.name: Chengji Ancient City Site
rows.summary: Remains of Chengji, a county town founded under the Western Han on a terrace where the Nan and Lidian rivers meet; after an earthquake in 734 the county moved to present-day Qin'an, and a fort was rebuilt here in 1067. About 490 m of rammed-earth wall, mostly of Song date and 1.5–3 m high, survives in the fields, and tradition names Chengji as the birthplace of the mythical sage-king Fuxi.

rows.name: Guanshan Lianhuatai Scenic Area
rows.summary: A forested mountain area in the Guanshan, the old Long Mountains on Huating's western border, rising to 2,748 m at Wutai Shan, with birch and pine forest over more than 90 per cent of the land, meadows, rock pinnacles, waterfalls and old Buddhist and Taoist temples. It is visited mainly for cool summer walking and autumn colour along its two main trails, Xuanfeng Shan and Lianhuatai.

rows.name: Haizhaigou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A rural valley at Dazhai, south-east of Pingliang, developed as an activity resort. In the warmer months it offers glass-slide rafting, a long glass-floored walkway across the valley, zip lines, high-ropes courses and a water park, and in winter there is a ski slope; it suits families looking for activities rather than scenery or history.

rows.name: Huangfu Mi Culture Park
rows.summary: A traditional-medicine themed scenic area at Zhang'aopo village, the home district of Huangfu Mi (c. 215–282), the scholar-physician who compiled the Canon of Acupuncture and Moxibustion, one of the earliest systematic works on acupuncture. Around his tomb and memorial hall are a culture park, a herb garden, mugwort fields and an acupuncture centre offering moxibustion sessions, plus a small petting zoo, and an acupuncture forum is held here.

rows.name: Jieshipu Long March Memorial and Mao Zedong's Former Residence
rows.name_zh: 界石铺红军长征毛泽东旧居纪念馆
rows.pinyin: Jièshípù Hóngjūn Chángzhēng Máo Zédōng Jiùjū Jìniànguǎn
rows.summary: A memorial in Jieshipu town marking the Red Army's passage on the Long March: in October 1935 Mao Zedong and other leaders camped here with the Shaanxi–Gansu column, and in October 1936 Red Army units again passed through while the three main forces gathered in the Huining–Jingning area. The house where Mao stayed is preserved with its furnishings, and exhibition halls display some 235 items from the period.

rows.name: Jingning Confucian Temple
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty state Confucian temple, rebuilt on its present site in the Jiajing reign, whose Lingxing Gate, semicircular pool, Dacheng Gate and seven-bay Dacheng Hall stand on a north–south axis, with the Minglun Hall of the old school to the west. It lies within the grounds of Jingning No. 1 Middle School, which used the buildings as classrooms and offices until 2002; they have since been restored.

rows.name: Kongtong Mountains
rows.summary: Kongtong Shan, a forested spur of the Liupan range just west of Pingliang, is one of the sacred mountains of Taoism: legend says the Yellow Emperor came here to ask the immortal Guangchengzi about the Dao, and it is also known as the cradle of the Kongtong school of martial arts. Taoist, Buddhist and Confucian halls are scattered over its crags, among them the Huangcheng ('Imperial City') temple complex on the summit ridge and the cliff-edge halls of Leisheng Peak, both founded in the Northern Song, and the brick Lingkong Pagoda of 1029 at the Middle Terrace, with a pine growing from its top.

rows.name: Longquan Temple, Chongxin
rows.summary: A wooded valley just north of Chongxin town, a provincial scenic area and geopark named after the temple at its heart, where the Guanzhu Spring feeds a waterfall and an ancient cypress coils along the cliff, a scene called the 'coiling dragon cypress'. The valley is a cool summer retreat with festival markets and fairs, and the Chongxin County Museum stands on the west side of the scenic area.

rows.name: Mijiagou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A wooded valley and provincial forest park on the edge of Huating, run as a family leisure area with streams, peach and flower fields, a climbing wall, adventure courses, a children's playground and live-action combat games, plus cave-dwelling restaurants and yurts. Summer temperatures under the trees stay around 20 °C, and local families come for blossom in spring, shade in summer and colour in autumn.

rows.name: Niujiaogou Palaeolithic Site
rows.summary: The gully at Baijia village in eastern Jingchuan where a human fossil about 50,000 years old, known as 'Jingchuan Man', was found in 1974, the first early human fossil from Gansu. A small site exhibition hall is part of the Baijia folk-culture village, a rural tourism spot with a farming museum, water features and orchards.

rows.name: Shigong Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A small group of Buddhist cave shrines cut into a hillside near Shangguan in southern Huating, begun under the Northern Wei and carved on into the Sui; 14 caves and niches survive, known for their finely carved flying apsaras. It is listed as one of the outlying parts of the Guanshan Lianhuatai scenic area.

rows.name: South Grotto Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple on the north bank of the Jing River, begun in 510 by Xi Kangsheng, prefect of Jingzhou, and often paired in local accounts with the North Grotto Temple near Qingyang as the 'twin pearls' of eastern Gansu's cave art. Its main cave, 11 m high and 18 m wide, holds seven standing Buddhas about 7 m tall with paired bodhisattvas, under ceiling reliefs of the life of the Buddha.

rows.name: Temple of the Prince of Wukang
rows.summary: A temple on Chongxin's East Street to Li Yuanliang, the Tang general and Prince of Wukang who built Chongxin's walls and garrisoned them against Tibetan Empire raids; it existed before 797 and was moved to this site in 1370. Its five-bay sleeping hall under a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof keeps a timber frame of Song–Yuan character, one of the older wooden buildings in Gansu, and is fronted by a Qing worship hall.

rows.name: Tianjiagou Soil and Water Conservation Scenic Area
rows.summary: A loess gully system just north of Jingchuan that decades of soil-conservation work have turned green, now a national water-conservancy scenic area and soil-conservation demonstration park. Paths lead past the 'thousand-year earth arrows', ranks of sheer loess pillars left by erosion, to a water play area, fishing ponds, pavilions and cave-dwelling style lodgings; it suits a half-day family outing.

rows.name: Wangmu Palace and Dayun Temple, Jingchuan
rows.summary: Jingchuan's Queen Mother of the West culture area joins two sites in the town. At the foot of Huizhong Hill, linked in legend with the Queen Mother of the West, the Wangmu Palace Grotto is a Northern Wei central-pillar cave about 11 m high with more than 200 carved figures in three tiers, among them a white elephant carrying a pagoda, behind a four-storey timber facade added in the late Qing. About a kilometre to the north, a museum stands on the site of Dayun Temple, where Buddhist relics in nested gold, silver, bronze and stone caskets were unearthed in 1964.

rows.name: Yan'en Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda some 33 m tall on Baota Ridge in eastern Pingliang, built between 1535 and 1546 and long called the Daming Pagoda after the stone plaque reading 'Da Ming' over its arched south door. It was raised by Consort Wen of the Ming princely house of Han, which held Pingliang as its fief, to pray for her late husband; the rest of Yan'en Temple has gone, and the pagoda is now the centrepiece of Baota Park.

rows.name: Yunya Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A forested gorge in the Guanshan mountains of Zhuanglang where red sandstone cliffs hold Buddhist caves begun in the late Northern Wei and restored up to the Qing: on the main cliff, about 300 m long and 80 m high, 19 caves in three tiers keep stone and clay statues and fragments of murals, with well-preserved Ming clay figures in Caves 6 and 7. The scenic area is also a national forest park, and the Chenjiadong caves in a nearby valley, part of the same heritage listing, add weathered rock-cut Buddhas and a small seven-storey Tang stone pagoda.

rows.name: Dong Laoye Shan (Xinglong Shan) Temples
rows.summary: A Daoist mountain, 1,774 m high, in north-eastern Huan County near the meeting point of Gansu, Shaanxi and Ningxia, also called Xinglong Shan and known for the saying that a cock's crow here carries into three provinces. Temples stood on it by the mid-Ming dynasty and numbered 72 by the Qing; the surviving halls date from the Ming and Qing periods and stand among newer buildings. In mid-October 1935 part of the Red Army camped on the mountain during the Long March, and a memorial park laid out in 2007 has a statue of Mao Zedong and a forest of steles inscribed with his poem 'Snow'.

rows.name: Donghuachi Pagoda
rows.summary: An octagonal brick pagoda of seven storeys on Baota Hill above Donghuachi village in Linzhen township, built in 1099 under the Northern Song and repaired under the Jin and the Ming. It rises 26 m with no base, entered by an arched door on the north-east side, and its upper storeys have real and blind doors, brick brackets under the eaves and balconies with carved balustrades of clouds, phoenixes, deer and tigers on the lowest three levels; the floors and stairs inside have gone. The tower was fully restored in 2012–13.

rows.name: Former Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia Provincial Soviet Government, Helianwan
rows.name_zh: 河连湾陕甘宁省苏维埃政府旧址
rows.pinyin: Héliánwān Shǎn-Gān-Níng Shěng Sūwéi'āi Zhèngfǔ Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: Helianwan village in Hongde town was the seat of the Communist Party's Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia Provincial Committee and Provincial Soviet Government from July 1936 to September 1937, after they moved here from Wuqi in northern Shaanxi, with Li Fuchun as party secretary and Ma Xiwu as chairman. On 18 November 1936 Zhou Enlai, Peng Dehuai, Xiao Jinguang and Chen Geng planned the Battle of Shanchengbao here, and local accounts add that the American journalist Edgar Snow visited the village in 1936 and described it in Red Star Over China.

rows.name: Huanzhou Old Town and Huanxian Pagoda
rows.summary: A scenic area of 518 mu (about 35 ha) at the north gate of Huan county town, opened in September 2021 and laid out in Song style around the Huanxian Pagoda and the remains of the walled Song-era town of Huanzhou, a frontier post against the Western Xia in the time of Fan Zhongyan. The pagoda is an octagonal brick tower of five storeys, 22 m high, with bracketed eaves, balconies with carved balustrades and an iron finial recording a repair of 1264; a brick found at the top in 2014 bears a date of 1043. The new terraces around it, rising in five zones from the pagoda, hold old-style buildings, water cascades and courtyards.

rows.name: Longqi Valley (Heilaoguo)
rows.summary: A narrow rocky gorge more than 1 km long at Maosi village in the Pu River valley south of Xifeng, whose winding course is said to look from above like a coiled dragon; it is also called Heilaoguo, the "black pot", because the stream sinks underground and has scoured the dark rock into a pot shape. In winter ice pillars, icicles and frozen falls hang from the gorge walls, and in spring the valley floor is yellow with rapeseed; the scenic area also takes in the old village of Maosi and a camping ground at Yueliangwan.

rows.name: Luochuan Old Town: Zhao Stone Archways and Confucian Temple Hall
rows.summary: Luochuan, now a village on the Silang River in Yonghe town, was a county seat for many centuries, and three red-sandstone memorial archways of the late Ming stand on the axis of its main street, carved with scenes from the career of the official Zhao Bangqing, auspicious motifs and inscribed boards, one board a gift of the Wanli Emperor. The Qingguan and Tianguan archways (1614–15), each 8.4 m high, were raised by the prefecture and county in his honour, and the Enchong archway (1617), 9.7 m high, he built to honour his two mothers. Nearby, in the grounds of the former Zhengning No. 2 Middle School, stands the five-bay Dacheng Hall of the old county Confucian temple, first built in the Yuan, rebuilt in 1369 and repaired several times under the Qing.

rows.name: Nanliang Revolutionary Sites
rows.summary: In 1934 Communist organisers led by Liu Zhidan, Xie Zichang and Xi Zhongxun made Nanliang, in the Ziwuling hills of eastern Huachi County, the base of a Soviet government for the Shaanxi–Gansu border area; it took the name Shaanxi–Gansu Border Region Soviet Government in November 1934 and moved to Xiasiwan in Shaanxi in April 1935. The red-tourism area around Liyuanbao has the Nanliang Revolutionary Memorial Hall, with a general exhibition and halls on Liu, Xie and Xi, the Lenin Primary School, now a nine-year school, and the former offices of the border region military committee and Soviet government at Zhaiziwan.

rows.name: Ningshou Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A square brick pagoda of five storeys in the pavilion style, 21.2 m high and 6 m wide at the base, built in the Five Dynasties to Northern Song period at Zhengping village on the north bank of the Jing River. It is the only survivor of the Ningshou Temple, swept away by floods in the Qing; local tradition credits Li Shimin, the future Tang emperor Taizong, with founding the temple to pray for his mother's long life, and the pagoda is also known as the Zhengping Tang Pagoda.

rows.name: North Grotto Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist cave temple cut into a sandstone cliff about 20 m high and 120 m long on the east bank of the Pu River where it meets the Ru, south-west of Xifeng, begun in 509 under the Northern Wei and extended under later dynasties into the Qing. Nearly 300 caves and niches with about 2,100 stone figures survive, many worn by weathering, with traces of painted murals; the centrepiece, Cave 165, is 14 m high, 21.7 m wide and 15.7 m deep and holds seven standing Buddhas. The Beishikuyi scenic area beside the grottoes adds parking and visitor facilities, and 1.5 km to the south-west a 323 m stretch of old road cut into the red rock at Shidaopo still shows deep cart ruts.

rows.name: Qin Straight Road (Qingyang Section)
rows.summary: A military road that the First Emperor of Qin ordered General Meng Tian to build from 212 BC; its Qingyang section, a national heritage unit of roughly 300 km, follows the forested Ziwuling ridge through Zhengning, Ning, Heshui and Huachi counties, and scholars still debate whether the Gansu line was the main road or a branch. The Qingyang tourism bureau directs visitors to the Diaolingguan Forest Park on the Shaanxi border in Zhengning County, where the old roadbed runs through the woods together with the Diaoling Pass, beacon-tower remains and a temple to Meng Tian.

rows.name: Shanchengbao Battle Site
rows.summary: The site of the Battle of Shanchengbao in November 1936, the first major engagement fought by the Red Army after its three main forces had joined up at the end of the Long March, in which troops under Peng Dehuai defeated part of Hu Zongnan's Nationalist First Army around Shancheng. The Shanchengbao Battle Memorial Park, begun in 2009 and opened in 2014 on the north side of Shancheng beside National Road 211, has a memorial hall on the campaign, a monument and the battlefield sites.

rows.name: Shuangta Temple Sculpted Pagodas
rows.summary: Two red-sandstone pagodas carved all over with Buddhist figures, the only standing remains of a temple founded in 1156–89 under the Jin in Linzhen township and destroyed by an earthquake in the Qianlong era. They were later moved from that valley site to a hillside on the east side of Huachi county town, now the Dongshan Shuangta forest park. The larger tower, 12.6 m high in thirteen tiers each set in a lotus bowl, carries about 3,500 figures of Buddhas, bodhisattvas, disciples, donors and celestial musicians, with scenes of the Buddha's nirvana and earlier lives; the second, badly damaged by thieves, keeps eleven tiers and 615 figures.

rows.name: Ta'erwan Sculpted Pagoda
rows.summary: A slender octagonal stone pagoda of thirteen tiers of close-set eaves, 10.93 m high, carved from local red sandstone in 1102–06 under the Northern Song and moved from Ta'erwan village in Taibai to the courtyard of the Heshui County Museum, also called the Longdong Ancient Stone Carving Art Museum. Its ground storey is covered with more than 600 carved figures, and the hollow shaft narrows from 1.29 m across at the base to 59 cm at the top, which has earned it a place among China's fifty noted pagodas as the most slender. The museum around it shows Buddhist stone sculpture of the Northern Wei to Qing periods and has a hall devoted to a Yellow River stegodont fossil.

rows.name: Xiangle Brick Pagoda
rows.summary: A hexagonal brick pagoda in the pavilion style in Xiangle town, begun under the Song and described as seven storeys, now about 22 m high with its top collapsed. The tall ground storey opens on the south into a hexagonal chamber, the upper storeys alternate real and blind doors flanked by lattice windows, the second to fourth levels have balconies, and the eaves of every storey are carried on five imitation-timber brick brackets to a face.

rows.name: Xiaojin Pagoda
rows.summary: A Song-dynasty brick pagoda, also called the Jincheng Temple Pagoda, on the south street of Xiaojin town; the temple around it has gone and only the tower survives, patched up in the Qing. It is octagonal and in the pavilion style, now seven storeys and about 20 m high with a broken top, with real or carved doors and lattice windows on its faces and bracketed eaves and balconies on every storey.

rows.name: Yaowangdong Wellness Town
rows.summary: A modern tourist town in old-street style on the east bank of the Rouyuan River at Qingcheng, about 3.2 km long and below the Zhouzu Mausoleum; it takes its name from a cave associated with the legendary physician Qibo. It has restaurants and snack streets, folk performances, traditional Chinese medicine and wellness services, courtyard guesthouses and leisure rides such as a glass bridge, slides and go-karts, and is lit up in the evenings. A hot-spring resort between the town and the mausoleum area opened at the end of 2025.

rows.name: Zhoujiubang Wooden Archway
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty timber memorial archway, built in 1505 on South Street in Qingcheng, the old county town, by the Qingyang prefect to honour Buzhu, the ancestor of the Zhou royal house who tradition says brought his people to this valley. It has four columns and three bays under a hipped tiled roof about 12 m high, and hangs a board reading "Zhou Jiu Bang" ("old land of Zhou") in the calligraphy of the painter Qi Baishi. It is the only survivor of more than a hundred archways the town had before the 1970s, and it stands within the Qingzhou old-town tourist area.

rows.name: Zhouzu Mausoleum
rows.summary: A forest park on the East Hill above Qingcheng, named after the tomb traditionally held to be that of Buzhu, the Xia-period ancestor of the Zhou royal house, who is said to have brought his people here and taught them farming. Since the 1980s the county has rebuilt temples, halls, pavilions and steles on the hill: 822 stone steps lead up to the Zhaozhou Shengzu archway and the Zhouzu Hall with statues of Buzhu and his son and grandson, and another area honours Qibo, the legendary physician of the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, with a large forest of inscribed steles. The Bagua Pavilion on the summit looks over the old town and the Rouyuan River.

rows.name: Ziwu Huaxi Valley
rows.summary: A flower-valley leisure area at Lianjiabian in Taibai town, on the edge of the Ziwuling forest in eastern Heshui County, laid out around a visitor centre and car park. Its named areas include the Ziyunhai flower fields, a streamside path with a small waterfall and a stalactite cave, a garden of mixed flowers, a children's play area and a rose garden, and it also has a zip line, a glass bridge and wooden cabins among the flowers.

rows.name: Dadiwan Site
rows.summary: One of the key Neolithic sites of the Yellow River basin, occupied from about 7,800 to 4,800 years ago, where excavations from 1978 uncovered more than 700 features, among them house foundations, hearths, kilns and graves, and nearly ten thousand artefacts. It is on China's list of national archaeological park projects and has a museum of the finds; its best-known feature is F901, the burnt-clay floor of a large building that archaeologists interpret as a communal meeting hall.

rows.name: Daxiangshan (Big Buddha Mountain)
rows.summary: A hillside of temples and grottoes on Wenqi Mountain just west of Gangu town, named after the large Buddha carved into the cliff near its summit. Stepped paths about 1.5 km long lead past halls such as a Taihao Palace to Fuxi, a Wenchang Pavilion and a Guandi Hall up to the Big Buddha Hall, with wide views over the Wei River valley. Together with the Shuiliandong grottoes about 35 km to the west it forms one national heritage site.

rows.name: Fengshan Hill, Qin'an
rows.summary: A hill on the eastern edge of Qin'an town covered by the Taishan Temple complex, 41 Ming and Qing halls, pavilions and cave shrines built on nine terraces, with Confucian, Buddhist and Taoist figures side by side. Its landmark is the Penglai Pavilion of 1749, and the slopes around the temples are planted as a forest park among old cypresses.

rows.name: Fuxi Temple, Tianshui
rows.summary: A Ming-dynasty temple to Fuxi, the legendary forefather of Chinese civilisation, laid out as a series of courtyards along one axis on Fuxi Road in the old part of Tianshui. An opera stage across the road, a memorial archway, a gate and a ceremonial gate lead to the double-eaved Xiantian Hall, which holds a painted statue of Fuxi, and the Taiji Hall behind it. A large public memorial ceremony for Fuxi is held here every year, and the historic Fuxi City streets lie just outside.

rows.name: Gupo Grassland
rows.summary: Upland meadows, forest and rocky peaks around the headwaters of the Ji River in southern Gangu County, between about 1,760 and 2,700 m above sea level. Visitors come in summer for horse riding and walks across the grassland, and sights within the area include Shigu Mountain, mentioned in the 6th-century Commentary on the Water Classic, and Heitan Temple, first built in the Yuan dynasty.

rows.name: Heyu Cliff Inscription
rows.summary: An Eastern Han inscription carved into a rock face at Heyu in eastern Zhangjiachuan County, listed as a national heritage site in 2019. It is one of the surviving traces of the old Guanlong road, which crossed the Guan Mountains between Gansu and the Guanzhong plain of Shaanxi.

rows.name: Houjie Mosque
rows.summary: A working mosque of Tianshui's Hui community in Qinzhou District, whose buildings date from the Ming and Qing dynasties. Its prayer hall is a Chinese-style timber building with a grey tiled roof and a porch of carved lattice doors, entered through a grey-brick gate with an arched doorway on the street. Visitors should dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

rows.name: Hu Family Residences (Tianshui Folk Museum)
rows.summary: Two Ming-dynasty courtyard mansions facing each other across a street in Tianshui's old city, built in the Jiajing era (1522–1566) by the scholar Hu Laijin and lived in by his descendants for generations. The South House is now the Tianshui Folk Museum, with timber halls, a hanging-flower gate and screen walls around its courtyards.

rows.name: Ji Xin Temple, Tianshui
rows.summary: Tianshui's City God temple, dedicated to Ji Xin, a general of the founder of the Han dynasty who is worshipped as the city god in Tianshui and Lanzhou. A county office in the Yuan dynasty and converted into a City God temple in the early Ming, it keeps 21 halls along one axis, and its main hall holds a Ming mural of the city god's procession dated 1625.

rows.name: Majiayuan Site and Chariot Museum
rows.summary: Majiayuan, in the hills north of Zhangjiachuan town, is a Warring States cemetery of Western Rong chieftains, a people drawn into the state of Qin, whose tombs held richly decorated chariots and gold and silver ornaments in a style linked to the steppe cultures further west. The finds are displayed at the Majiayuan Chariot Museum in Zhangjiachuan town, which opened in 2023 and shows more than 500 sets of objects alongside full-size and scaled reconstructions of the chariots.

rows.name: Mutisi Grottoes
rows.summary: A cave temple high on the slopes of Bailin Mountain in Mali town, west of Wushan, named, legend says, after a wooden ladder that was once the only way up the cliff to it. About 18 caves and niches and four halls hold more than 80 statues and wall paintings, the finest from the Song dynasty, and renovated paths climb through woods that turn red and gold in autumn.

rows.name: Nanguo Temple (Nanshan Scenic Area)
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in a fold of the hills about 2 km south of central Tianshui, already a sizeable monastery in the Tang dynasty and visited by the poet Du Fu in 759, who wrote verses about it. Its courtyards hold ancient cypresses estimated at more than 2,000 years old, celebrated as one of the Eight Views of Qinzhou, old pagoda trees at the west gate and a shrine to Du Fu set up in 1904. From the hillside there are views over the whole city.

rows.name: Ping'an Grassland
rows.summary: An expanse of high mountain meadows, valleys and streams in the Guan Mountains of Zhangjiachuan Hui Autonomous County, where the early Qin state is said to have pastured its horses. Boardwalks link viewpoints across the grassland, and in summer visitors come for horse riding, camping, star-view cabins and evening bonfires.

rows.name: Qin'an Confucian Temple
rows.summary: Qin'an's Confucian temple, founded before 1297, keeps a Ming-dynasty Dacheng Hall under a single-eaved hip-and-gable roof of glazed tiles, one of the better-preserved Ming timber buildings in Gansu. Glazed panels of coiled dragons flank its doorway, and the courtyard has nine old cypresses, one of them planted in the early Ming.

rows.name: Qingjuanshan Resort
rows.summary: A countryside resort around Sunji village in Pingnan town, south of Tianshui, laid out around a lake lined with themed wooden cabins where visitors can fish, go boating and cook their catch in the cabins' kitchens. Outdoor activities include a rock-climbing wall and a treetop adventure course, and there are restaurants serving local dishes.

rows.name: Shengshou Temple, Wushan
rows.summary: A temple in Wushan County whose surviving buildings date from the Yuan dynasty to the Republican era, listed as a national heritage site in 2019. Wushan County includes it on a suggested sightseeing route with the county museum and the Mutisi Grottoes.

rows.name: Shuiliandong Grottoes and Lashao Temple
rows.summary: A group of cave temples in a narrow gorge north-east of Wushan town, named after a natural cave about 50 m high whose overhang turns into a curtain of water when it rains. Its best-known work is the giant Buddha carved in relief on the cliff at Lashao Temple, dating from the Northern Zhou, while the Thousand Buddha Cave and other shrines keep statues, murals and inscriptions added from the Later Qin to the Yuan. The area is now run as the Tianshui Cliff Grottoes Cultural Tourism Area.

rows.name: Suwan Folk Manor
rows.summary: A rural folk-culture park in Sujiawan village, Pingnan town, in the hills south of Tianshui, which became a 4A scenic area in 2025. Visitors can explore displays of local folk customs and pick seasonal produce, and on public holidays there are performances such as molten-iron 'fireworks' and face-changing. It lies near the Qingjuanshan resort, and the two are promoted together.

rows.name: Xingguo Temple, Qin'an
rows.summary: A Yuan-dynasty Buddhist temple in the centre of Qin'an town whose main building, the Prajna Hall, is dated by an inscribed board of the Zhishun era (1330–1333) found inside its wall in 1974. The west-facing temple keeps a gate, a Hall of the Heavenly Kings and bell and drum towers on its axis, and the Qin'an County Museum stands next to it.

rows.name: Yuquan Taoist Temple
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex climbing the foot of Tianjing Mountain on the north side of Tianshui's old city, founded in the Tang dynasty and rebuilt by Quanzhen Taoists from the Yuan onwards. Its Ming and Qing halls rise in terraces up the slope, among them a Ming Jade Emperor Hall, and it keeps more than fifty inscribed steles, including a four-sided Yuan stele. A temple fair, known locally as chaoguan, is held on the ninth day of the first lunar month.

rows.name: Baita Temple Site and Liangzhou Assembly Memorial Hall
rows.summary: The site of a Yuan-period Buddhist monastery at Wunan, south-east of Wuwei, where in 1247 Sakya Pandita, head of the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism, met the Mongol prince Köden (Godan), a grandson of Genghis Khan who held Liangzhou as his appanage. Remains of the old stupas stand among a field of white stupas with gilded tops, and the Liangzhou Assembly Memorial Hall on the site displays finds and the history of the meeting.

rows.name: Binggou River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A mountain valley at the eastern end of the Qilian range in the Tianzhu Tibetan Autonomous County, named after its glacier-fed river, with alpine meadows grazed by white yaks, conifer forest and wild iris grassland. Sightseeing buses run up the valley, and a long trail and boardwalk climb to Chaierlonghai, a clear tarn below snow peaks; going there and back is a strenuous high-altitude day walk of around 20 km.

rows.name: Dongda Monastery, Tianzhu
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist monastery at Saishisi in southern Tianzhu, nearly 400 years old, whose Tibetan name means 'great monastery of the Datong'; its buildings blend Han Chinese and Tibetan styles and it was once a leading monastery of the Tibetan Huarui area. The side walls of its assembly hall carry a complete mural cycle of the novel Journey to the West, about 200 years old and believed to be the only one of its kind in Tibetan areas, showing the monk Tang Seng and his disciples Monkey, Pigsy and Sandy on their pilgrimage.

rows.name: Gulang Battle Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial park in the south-west of Gulang town on the battlefield of November 1936, when the Western Route Army of the Chinese Red Army fought the forces of the Ma clique around Gulang during its advance west along the Hexi Corridor. A three-storey exhibition hall follows the Western Route Army's campaign with 926 artefacts, documents and battle dioramas, and the grounds include a memorial square and a martyrs' cemetery.

rows.name: Haizang Temple
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple on the north-western edge of Wuwei whose surviving halls and painted beams date from the Ming to the Republican era, set among pines and cypresses several centuries old, many of them protected trees. It stands inside Haizang Park beside the Haizang wetland, a quiet stop after the city's museums.

rows.name: Leitai Han Tomb
rows.summary: A brick tomb of the late Eastern Han with front, middle and rear chambers, found in 1969 under Leitai, an earthen terrace topped by a Ming Taoist temple in northern Wuwei; it yielded more than 230 objects, among them a procession of bronze horses, chariots and figures and the Bronze Galloping Horse (Flying Horse of Gansu), later chosen as China's tourism emblem. The originals are in the Gansu Provincial Museum in Lanzhou; the site is now the Leitai Han Culture Museum, a 12.7-hectare park with the tomb, the temple and a large replica array of the bronze procession.

rows.name: Ruian Fort
rows.summary: A fortified manor begun in 1938 at Santao village south-west of Minqin, where a landowner's family compound sits inside high rammed-earth walls with honeycomb battlements; it is one of the best-preserved fortified farmsteads in north-west China, nicknamed the 'Palace Museum beyond the frontier'. Its courtyards follow a symmetrical 'front hall, rear chambers' plan with carved brick and timber detail, and the fort is managed together with the Minqin County Museum.

rows.name: Shajing Culture Folk Museum and Village
rows.summary: A village folk-culture centre in a former school at Xintao, Sanlei, built around a museum set up by local villagers, said to be the largest privately run folk museum in Gansu, with thousands of objects of rural life and several hundred pottery, stone and bone finds of the Shajing culture, the early first-millennium BC culture named after a site in Minqin. It also offers farming-life activities and evening village shows, including a staged play of the Su Wu sheep-herding story.

rows.name: Shengrong Temple, Minqin
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple in Minqin whose surviving buildings date from the Ming dynasty to the Republican period, listed as a national heritage site in 2013. Minqin's tourism promotion calls it the 'Thousand Buddha Summit' temple and presents its old buildings and relics as a record of the oasis's history since the Ming.

rows.name: Shenzhou Desert Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A wildlife park on the desert edge east of Wuwei that specialises in desert animals of north-west China, notably Przewalski's horses, Tibetan wild asses and wild Bactrian camels, alongside zoo species such as golden snub-nosed monkeys, African lions, brown bears and Amur tigers. There is a hall of desert wildlife specimens and a petting area with marmots and alpacas, and it is mainly a family and school-trip destination.

rows.name: Suwu Desert Scenic Area
rows.summary: A desert leisure area on the southern edge of the Tengger Desert near Minqin, named after Su Wu, the Han envoy of the famous sheep-herding exile story, whom local tradition links with Minqin. It groups the International Desert Sculpture Creation Base, with more than a hundred works by artists from around the world set among the dunes, a 'Star-Picking Town' with an astronomy hall and stargazing cabins, a Su Wu culture town, and dune buggies and off-road rides, with evening shows in the autumn season.

rows.name: Tiantishan Caves
rows.summary: Among the earliest Buddhist cave temples in China, cut into cliffs above the Huangyang River in the Qilian foothills from the time of the Northern Liang ruler Juqu Mengxun in the early fifth century and reworked up to the Qing; 19 caves survive in three tiers. When a reservoir was built at the foot of the cliff in 1959–60, most sculptures and some murals were moved to the Gansu Provincial Museum, but the largest group, a monumental seated Buddha with attendants, stayed in place and has been shielded from the reservoir water by a cofferdam since 1992; a site exhibition hall tells the caves' story.

rows.name: Wuwei Confucius Temple
rows.summary: Built in 1437–1439 and enlarged up to the Republican era, this is one of the largest Confucian temples in north-west China, laid out in three courts side by side: the Wenchang Palace to the east, the temple proper with its semicircular pool, Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Hall and Zunjing Library in the middle, and the old Confucian school to the west, with more than 30 steles from the Tang to the Qing. The city's Western Xia Museum across the road displays the Western Xia Stele of 1094, the only known stele with matching texts in Tangut and Chinese, whose rediscovery in the early 19th century reopened the study of the Tangut script.

rows.name: Wuwei Desert Park
rows.summary: A desert-themed park on the desert edge east of Wuwei, billed as the first in China built around desert scenery, that mixes sand dunes with planted woodland, grassland and landscaped gardens across more than 530 hectares. It holds a spring pear-blossom and kite festival and an autumn fun run.

rows.name: Biandukou
rows.summary: Biandukou, called Dadoubagu in the Sui, is a pass of over 3,500 m on the old route across the Qilian Mountains between Minle and Qinghai, linked by Chinese sources with Huo Qubing's army, the monk Faxian and Emperor Yang of Sui. The scenic area on the northern approach, at about 2,800 m, is known for summer rapeseed fields and highland pasture, Buddhist rock carvings, and campsites, cabins and riding trails for self-drive visitors.

rows.name: Binggou Danxia
rows.summary: The second major scenic area of the Zhangye Danxia geopark, opened in 2014 on the north bank of the Liyuan River in Sunan: in contrast to the striped hills of Qicai Danxia, it is a landscape of red sandstone cliffs, walls, pillars and spires. Its sandstone 'window-lattice' formations, weathered into rows of upright ribs like the windows of a palace, are the type locality for that landform.

rows.name: Binhe Jiuliangye Distillery
rows.summary: The Binhe distillery in the Minle eco-industrial park, maker of Jiuliangye baijiu, is open to visitors as a liquor-culture scenic area covering its starter-making, distilling and bottling halls, blending cellars and a large storage cellar. Outside, the grounds on the edge of the Gobi have a lake, rose and marigold fields, organic sorghum and maize plots, viewing platforms and barbecue and self-drive campsites.

rows.name: Dafo Temple, Zhangye
rows.summary: The temple was founded in 1098 under the Western Xia, and its two-storey Great Buddha Hall shelters a painted clay reclining Buddha about 35 m long, often described as the largest indoor reclining Buddha in China, with his ten disciples standing behind him. The temple houses the Ganzhou District Museum, and the scenic area also takes in the earthen Mituo Qianfo stupa of the Ming (about 33 m tall) and the Shanxi Guild Hall next door, built by Shanxi merchants in 1730 with a gateway stage and a timber memorial arch.

rows.name: Dahuwan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A lake and wetland leisure area in the Heihe valley near Gaotai, centred on the Chongwen Tower, a 41.7 m five-storey timber tower in southern Ming–Qing style built in 2011–12, with a lakeside plaza, boardwalks and bridges. It hosts local festivals, concerts and dragon-boat races on the lake, and its visitor centre, car parks and paths were renovated in 2024.

rows.name: Danxiakou Tourist Town
rows.summary: A modern tourist town built in old style near the north entrance of the Qicai Danxia scenic area, mixing grey-tiled Huizhou-style houses with the walls and gate towers of the north-west. Its lanes hold restaurants, guesthouses, craft workshops and small exhibition rooms, and staged entertainment includes a gate-opening welcome, a camel-caravan parade, costumed street actors and the stage show Huidao Zhangye.

rows.name: Ganquan Red History and Culture Area
rows.name_zh: 甘泉红色历史文化旅游区
rows.summary: A 50 ha district in central Zhangye that joins red-history sites, including the Gao Jincheng Martyr Memorial Hall and an exhibition on the Western Route Army's 1936–37 campaign in the Hexi Corridor, with the Ganquan spring, rebuilt traditional gardens, the Sanyuan Museum and two lakes. There is also a children's playground, a water-screen film show and performances of local intangible heritage.

rows.name: Han and Ming Great Wall at Xiakou, Shandan
rows.summary: In Shandan county two Great Walls run side by side along the narrow 'waist' of the Hexi Corridor, often only 10–80 m apart: the Han wall to the north, mostly trenches and beacon towers, and the Ming wall of rammed earth to the south. At Xiakou, an old walled post on the Silk Road, the brick-arched gate and a gate tower over the main street survive below stretches of the walls, with patrol trails, signboards and a visitor centre added since 2022 as a demonstration section of the Great Wall National Cultural Park.

rows.name: Heishuiguo Ruins
rows.summary: The 'Black Water Kingdom' is a 16 km² spread of ruins in the sands north-west of Zhangye, where the eroded rammed-earth walls of a southern and a northern town still stand among dunes, with Han bricks, Han–Jin tombs and prehistoric finds scattered around them. The standing walls are Ming, but local historians link the site with the Han seat of Zhangye commandery and later post stations, abandoned each time sand overran the oasis.

rows.name: Liushahe Scenic Area, Linze
rows.summary: A riverside park of about 230 ha on the south side of Linze town, with lakes including Swan Lake, a Danxia-style hill and square, a Journey to the West garden and a 'hundred stones' garden carved with poems. It serves as the town's main park, with walking and fitness trails, a visitor centre and an ice playground in winter, and black storks have been recorded along the river.

rows.name: Luotuocheng Ruins
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of one of the largest Han–Tang town sites in the Hexi Corridor stand in farmland west of Gaotai: built here after an earthquake destroyed the earlier county town in AD 180, it became the seat of Jiankang commandery under the Former Liang and, in 397, the first capital of the Northern Liang. It was abandoned after Tibetan forces took the corridor in 766, and painted bricks and other finds from the surrounding cemeteries, which hold some 3,000 tombs, are displayed at the Gaotai County Museum.

rows.name: Lushuiwan Scenic Area
rows.summary: A chain of man-made lakes with lakeside parkland on the north-western edge of Zhangye, with bridges, promenades and the Shuitian Yise square, and sightseeing carts running between them. It suits an evening walk or bike ride, and its paved promenades host events such as roller-skating races.

rows.name: Mati Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A group of Buddhist cave temples in the Qilian foothills of Sunan, begun in the Northern Liang in the early 5th century and used into the Qing, spread over seven sites including the Mati North and South temples, the Thousand Buddha Caves and Jinta Temple. The best-known is the 'Thirty-three Heavens', five tiers of chambers cut into the cliff of Mati North Temple and linked by internal passages, and the scenic area adds forested valleys and Yugur and Tibetan culture.

rows.name: Minle Silk Road Pastoral Park
rows.name_zh: 民乐现代丝路田园综合体
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park in northern Minle built around fruit-picking orchards, flower fields, a folk-culture village and street and a farming-culture study area. Other features include cherry and pear orchards, peony and orchid gardens, food workshops, a children's playground and a hot-spring resort, and it suits families on a day out from Zhangye.

rows.name: Pingshanhu Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A canyon of red sandstone and conglomerate cut into the desert hills north-east of Zhangye, opened to visitors in 2014, where trails and viewpoints lead along the ridges and down into narrow gorges of a 95 km² scenic area. It lies in Pingshanhu Mongolian Township, and the scenic area adds Mongolian food, music and yurts to hiking and geology.

rows.name: Qilian Mountain Deer Park
rows.name_zh: 祁连山鹿文化生态旅游区
rows.summary: An alpine valley on the Jinchang River at 2,700–3,500 m in Sunan where more than 600 farmed Qilian red deer (white-rumped deer) graze on high grassland below snow peaks, and visitors can see them at close quarters. Hot-air balloon rides and grass-sledging are offered, and it makes a stop on National Road 213 between the Danxia areas and Sunan town.

rows.name: Tongzi Temple Grottoes
rows.summary: A small cave-temple site on two cliff faces east of Minle, first cut in the Northern Wei: the southern caves have murals of Journey to the West stories, and the northern ones Bodhisattvas and a thousand-armed Guanyin. Most surviving paintings are Ming and Qing and mix Buddhist, Taoist and folk deities, and the Tongzi Temple at the foot of the cliff is an active place of worship.

rows.name: Wenshushan Grottoes
rows.summary: A cave-temple complex in the Wenshu Mountains south-west of Jiuquan, spread over a front and a back hill, with over 130 caves recorded, including about 30 from the Wei and Jin to the Qing that keep more than 500 statues and some 1,200 m² of murals. The early central-pillar caves were cited by the archaeologist Su Bai as examples of the 'Liangzhou model' of early Hexi cave art, and the Wenshu Temple at the foot, a Gelug Tibetan Buddhist monastery, shares the valley with Chinese Buddhist and Taoist shrines.

rows.name: Western Route Army Memorial Hall, Gaotai
rows.name_zh: 中国工农红军西路军纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial to the Western Route Army, the Red Army force of about 21,800 that crossed the Yellow River in October 1936 and was defeated by Ma clique forces in the Hexi Corridor over the following months; its Fifth Army was destroyed at Gaotai in January 1937. Built on the 1957 martyrs' cemetery, where Fifth Army commander Dong Zhentang and more than 3,000 soldiers are buried, it has a monument, sculpture groups and a museum building modelled on a beacon tower, with eight galleries on the campaign.

rows.name: Wulan Ancient Town
rows.summary: A modern tourist town built in old style at Gucheng village in Jiantan, east of Zhangye, whose centrepiece is the Jiuqu Huanghe lantern maze: a 2.4 km labyrinth laid out on the nine palaces and eight trigrams, with 365 lanterns, nine halls and more than 700 walls decorated with themes from traditional cosmology and Hexi history. A branch of the Zhangye gazetteer museum opened in the town in 2023.

rows.name: Xilai Temple
rows.summary: A working Chan (Zen) Buddhist temple in the lanes of Zhangye's old town, said to date back to the Tang and rebuilt under the Ming, which took the name Xilai Si after a Qing restoration in the Kangxi reign. Its gate, Guanyin Hall, scripture library and Ming-period Jingang Hall stand round a courtyard that is now the seat of the Ganzhou District Buddhist Association.

rows.name: Xusanwan Ancient Fort and Tombs
