rows.summary: A small rammed-earth fort standing alone on the gravel plain west of Gaotai, with corner towers and a square barbican outside its south gate; the area belonged to the Han county of Biaoshi, and the fort was reused as a Ming–Qing outpost before being abandoned. Thousands of tomb mounds of the Han to Five Liang periods are scattered over the plain around it.

rows.name: Yanzhi Mountains
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a full day
rows.summary: A forested outlier of the Qilian range south of Shandan, rising to 3,978 m, which the Han general Huo Qubing won from the Xiongnu and where Emperor Yang of Sui is said to have received envoys from 27 states in 609. The forest park has dense forest, gorges lined with rock formations and the Zhongshan Temple on the heights, and is a cool summer retreat above the Hexi Corridor.

rows.name: Yuantong Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A Tibetan-style stupa of brick and earth about 23 m tall at Liuba in Minle, said to have been founded in the Northern Song and restored several times under the Ming and Qing, when a Qianlong-era rebuilding raised it by more than 3 m. Its two-tier square base carries eight small corner stupas, twenty niches round the upper base hold Buddhist images, and the temple that once stood in front was destroyed in the mid-20th century.

rows.name: Yueya Lake Park, Gaotai
rows.summary: A town park on the western edge of Gaotai, built since 1992 around a natural reed-marsh lake that was long counted among the county's ten sights as 'the lake reflecting the crescent moon'. Its 37 ha hold four lakes, five islands, nine bridges and sixteen pavilions, an old-style courtyard, a folk-collection museum and a fishing park, making it a pleasant stop for a stroll.

rows.name: Yugur Culture Corridor
rows.summary: A 27 km scenic road through the Qilian foothills around Kangle in Sunan Yugur Autonomous County, home of the Yugur, a people of about 15,000 who speak Turkic and Mongolic languages and mostly follow Tibetan Buddhism. Along the Yu–Kang road it links a yurt camp, the Wanfo gorge, a Western Route Army monument, Yugur heritage and song-and-dance venues and the Saihan Tala alpine grassland, combining Danxia scenery, meadows and Yugur culture.

rows.name: Yugur Folk Culture Resort, Sunan
rows.summary: Sunan's county town, Hongwansi, and its surroundings form this scenic area, which includes the Yugur Fengqing Yuan cultural park, ethnic villages, a red-history theme park, the Xiliugou folk-culture street and the Solangge racecourse. Traditional horse races, song-and-dance shows and festivals present Yugur, Tibetan and Mongolian culture, and there are campsites and RV pitches for self-drive travellers.

rows.name: Zhangye Drum Tower
rows.summary: Zhangye's Drum Tower, also called Zhenyuan Tower, rises 28 m at the crossroads in the middle of the old city: a brick-faced platform pierced by four arched passages carries a two-storey timber pavilion under a pyramidal tiled roof. It was first built in 1507, burned in 1648 and rebuilt in 1668, and a Tang-dynasty bronze bell hangs on its platform.

rows.name: Zhangye East Granary
rows.summary: A Ming state granary founded in 1392 in Zhangye's old town, whose nine surviving storehouses, with ventilation and rat-proof holes at the foot of their walls, make it one of the more complete old granaries in China. After restoration it reopened in September 2025 with an exhibition on farming and grain storage and the Ganzhou intangible heritage centre, where local crafts such as paper-cutting, embroidery and clay modelling are shown and taught.

rows.name: Zhangye National Desert Sports Park
rows.name_zh: 张掖国家沙漠体育公园
rows.summary: An 18 km² park in the desert dunes 13 km south of Zhangye, laid out for outdoor sport, sightseeing and children's play, with a motorsport circuit that has staged a round of the China Rally Championship nine years running. In winter part of it becomes a snow playground, and it suits families and anyone wanting desert scenery close to the city.

rows.name: Zhangye National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park on the northern edge of Zhangye, where boardwalks wind through reedbeds, ponds and stands of tamarisk and oleaster, and lotus ponds bloom in midsummer. Protected birds such as the lesser kestrel and the Eurasian hobby have been recorded here, and it is popular with residents for summer lotus-viewing and autumn colour.

rows.name: Qihuang TCM Culture Museum (Qingyang)
rows.name_zh: 庆阳岐黄中医药文化博物馆
rows.summary: A museum of traditional Chinese medicine culture in Qingcheng County, the Qingyang area that local tradition links with the legendary physician Qi Bo and the Zhou ancestor Buzhu. Travel features place it on a route with the old town of Qingzhou and the Zhouzu Mausoleum. It was listed in 2018 as a TCM health-tourism demonstration base (creation unit).

rows.name: Golog Peaceful Liberation Memorial, Dari
rows.summary: A memorial site near Zhalang Temple in Dari County, marking the arrival in August 1952 of a Northwest Military and Political Commission work team, whose meeting with tribal and religious leaders at the temple on 24 August is described in official accounts as the peaceful liberation of Golog. The site has an 8.4 m monument with an inscription in Tibetan and Chinese, raised in 2008, and the unit was added to the national heritage list in 2019. It is a remote stop for visitors interested in the modern history of the Golog grasslands.

rows.name: Rakya Monastery
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery in Lajia town, Maqên (Maqin) County, built in the Qing period and also known in Chinese as Jiachan Temple. It stands in the Yellow River country of northern Golog, where the provincial tourism route lists Lajia town as the Yellow River Bend stop, and it has been a national heritage unit since 2013.

rows.name: Red Army Valley, Banma
rows.summary: A forested valley in Yartang township, Banma County, where Red Army units spent about three weeks in July 1936 on the Long March, and which local people renamed Red Army Valley. The national heritage unit is a slogan the soldiers wrote on a rock face at the valley mouth, now sheltered by a pavilion, and the scenic area adds a memorial hall opened in 2017 with Long March relics, plus a bridge, spring and stockade named for the Red Army.

rows.name: Amidongsuo (Niuxin Mountain)
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Amidongsuo is the mountain also called Niuxin ('Ox Heart') Mountain, a peak that local Tibetans hold sacred, rising south of Qilian town in the middle Qilian Mountains. The scenic area covers about 120 km² and takes in a long east–west valley, grassland and shrub forest below slopes where the snow lies all year; spring brings wheat and rapeseed fields at the foot of the mountain and summer brings green pasture. It is the 5A area of Qilian County, and Zhuoer Mountain, across the Bayi River to the north, looks straight at it.

rows.name: Atomic City (Plant 221 Site), Haiyan
rows.summary: Atomic City is the former site of Plant 221, China's first nuclear weapons research and production base, set up from 1958 on the Jinyintan grassland north-east of Qinghai Lake, where state accounts say the country's first atomic and hydrogen bombs were developed. The plant was dissolved in 1987 and the site handed to the local government in 1995; preserved parts include the detonation test ground, an assembly plant, the Shangxing station where, in the Qinghai Daily's account, the first atomic bomb was loaded on a train for Lop Nur, and an underground command centre. The Atomic City memorial museum, opened in 2009 and reopened in June 2021 after refurbishment, presents the history with photographs, documents and objects, and Jinyintan is also summer grazing land for local Tibetan and Mongol herders.

rows.name: Dayu Folk Village, Haiyan
rows.summary: Dayu Folk Village is a privately run Tibetan folk-culture park at Jinyintan near Xihai town, named after the Dayu tribe of the Qinghai Lake area. Its grounds hold a folk museum, an experience area and a performance centre, and the village also serves as a campsite for recreational vehicles on the lake circuit.

rows.name: Gangcha Tibetan Lakeside Town
rows.summary: Gangcha is the county town north of Qinghai Lake, rebuilt in Tibetan style and promoted as the 'Plateau Seaside Tibetan City'. The county government's description lists Tibetan-style building groups, an ethnic history museum called Tancheng (the mandala), a song-and-dance performance centre and the Shaliu River, up which the lake's naked carp (huangyu) migrate in summer. The county also lists an old site for offerings to the lake, Matou Lazetan.

rows.name: Gangshika Peak
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Gangshika is the highest peak of the eastern Qilian Mountains, a glaciated mountain of 5,254.5 m in Menyuan County that climbers often treat as a first snow mountain, because the approach is gradual and it lies under 160 km from Xining. The scenic area, a managed development that opened in 2024–25, has a visitor service centre at the foot of the mountain, horse rides and walks in summer, snow and ice activities in winter, a guided climbing route from a base camp at about 4,350 m, and a 47 km backpacking route along the Lenglongling range added in 2025. It was named a national ski-mountaineering training base in 2016, and the film The Climbers was partly shot here.

rows.name: Menyuan Rapeseed Flower Fields
rows.summary: The valley floor at Menyuan is farmed with rapeseed, which turns it yellow against the surrounding mountains in July. The scenic area is built around the Yuanshan flower-viewing platform at Qingshizui, about 3,000 m above sea level and the county's first commercial tourist site (built in 2006), with a boardwalk, viewing decks and a second flower area, Fenfangyu, nearby. Peak bloom is usually from mid-July, so a visit is strongly seasonal.

rows.name: Qilian Mountain Eco-Ranch, Menyuan
rows.summary: The Qilian Mountain Eco-Ranch is a commercial grassland park in the Menyuan valley, developed from 2016 by a private tourism company, with its first phase opened in June 2017. Its zones cover pasture sightseeing, livestock-product displays, folk-custom experiences, song and dance shows, walking areas and grassland lodging, and it lies next to the Menyuan rapeseed flower area.

rows.name: Wenjia Ranch, Haiyan
rows.summary: Wenjia Ranch is a privately run grassland resort near the east shore of Qinghai Lake in Haiyan County, begun in 2017 by a team of university graduates with a few rented tents and set up as a company in 2019. It has a Tibetan-style 'starry sky' hotel and guesthouses, a restaurant, a craft centre, a bookshop, an incense-making workshop, a nomad-life experience area, a viewing platform and an evening bonfire with group dancing. It suits visitors who want a night near the lake with organised Tibetan-style activities rather than a historic or protected site.

rows.name: Xihai Commandery City Site, Haiyan
rows.summary: These are the remains of the commandery city that the regent Wang Mang set up in about 4 CE at the end of the Western Han, with trapezoid earth walls about 600 m across that still stand 4–12 m high. Finds here include a stone tiger-tally casket inscribed with the first year of the Xin dynasty (9 CE), and coins and coin moulds from the Western Han and Xin periods. The county has added replica walls, gates and tourist buildings around the site, and Haiyan's Xihai Commandery Museum displays finds.

rows.name: Zhuoer Mountain, Qilian
rows.summary: Zhuoer Mountain is a ridge of red sandstone and conglomerate (Danxia landform) on the north bank of the Bayi River, with a summit at about 2,930 m that serves as a viewing platform over the town, the river and Amidongsuo to the south. Its viewpoints include the Ethnic Unity pagoda, a Western Xia-era beacon tower, Lovers' Cliff and the 'Eye of Heaven' lookout, and in summer rapeseed flowers add yellow to the view. The Haibei government counts it as part of the county-wide 'Qilian Scenery' tourist area; its Tibetan name is given locally as Zongmu Mayouma.

rows.name: Ahetan Mosque
rows.summary: A Qing-period mosque in the Salar village of Ahetan in Ganduo town, Hualong, listed nationally in 2013 after provincial protection from 1988. The tourism ministry's rural routes pair it with the village's Salar folk-culture experiences, food and views of the Yellow River. It is an active place of worship, so visit quietly and ask before entering.

rows.name: Beishan National Forest Park, Huzhu
rows.name_zh: 互助北山国家森林公园
rows.summary: A large forest park in the mountains north-east of Huzhu, rising from about 2,100 m to over 4,300 m and also a national geopark. Its central zone, Langshidang, is the best developed, with red and white birch woods, waterfalls, two high-altitude lakes and a Tibetan stupa. It is a day trip for walking and mountain scenery rather than a single sight.

rows.name: Chuzang Monastery
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery in the hills north of Huzhu, founded in 1649 and one of four well-known monasteries of north-eastern Qinghai. Its buildings were damaged in the 1720s, rebuilt from 1732 and restored again after the Cultural Revolution; Qing records mention a Shakyamuni hall built in 1830 and a brick-carved nine-dragon screen approved for its front. It is a working monastery, set among steep hills beside the Nanmenxia reservoir.

rows.name: Dandou Monastery
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Jinyuan Tibetan township, Hualong, regarded as one of the main cradles of the later diffusion of Buddhism on the Tibetan plateau. The complex has more than 200 rooms and halls, among them the Great Prayer Hall, a Maitreya hall, meditation halls and a stupa. It dates from the Ming and Qing periods and was listed nationally in 2013.

rows.name: Gönlung Monastery (Youning Temple)
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery in the hills east of Huzhu, founded in 1604 and long called the mother of the monasteries north of the Huangshui river. It housed the first Gelug seminary in north-eastern Tibetan areas and was the seat of the Changkya and Thuken incarnation lineages. It was burned in the 1720s during the Qing suppression of a Mongol-led revolt and rebuilt from 1732 under the name Youning, meaning 'protecting Xining'.

rows.name: Hehuang Culture Museum
rows.summary: A regional museum in Ledu District that opened in July 2023 and is described in Chinese state media as the only comprehensive museum devoted to Hehuang culture, the cultures of the Huangshui valley in eastern Qinghai. It shows about 1,180 objects in 17 categories, from stone, jade and bone objects to pottery, porcelain, gold and textiles. The walls of its entrance hall display 374 painted pots from the Liuwan cemetery.

rows.name: Hongshuiquan Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque in Hongshuiquan village, Ping'an District, listed nationally in 2013 as a Ming-to-Qing building. The tourism ministry's rural routes highlight its fine brick and wood carving and an exhibition hall on ethnic unity. It is an active place of worship in a hill village, so visit quietly.

rows.name: Jiezi Gongbei
rows.summary: A Muslim tomb shrine (gongbei) in Jiezi town, Xunhua, listed nationally in 2013 as a Qing-period tomb. It stands near Jiezi Mosque, regarded as the Salar people's ancestral mosque, and within walking distance of the Camel Spring, where Salar tradition places their ancestors' arrival. It is an active place of worship, so visits should be respectful and may be limited.

rows.name: Lajia Archaeological Site
rows.summary: Lajia is a Qijia-culture settlement about 4,000 years old on a Yellow River terrace, where excavations found houses destroyed in a sudden disaster, with victims' remains still inside. The cause is still debated, with earthquakes and floods the main explanations. A bowl of noodles from the site, identified as millet in a 2005 paper in Nature, is described by its authors as the oldest noodles yet found; a site museum and archaeological park show the finds to visitors.

rows.name: Liuwan Cemetery and Painted Pottery Museum
rows.summary: Liuwan is a Neolithic to Bronze Age cemetery found in 1974, where about 1,700 graves of the Majiayao, Qijia and Xindian cultures, dating from roughly 4,600 to 3,600 years ago, were excavated. The Liuwan Museum of Ancient Painted Pottery in the village, opened in 2004, holds almost 38,000 objects, including more than 17,000 pottery pieces, many painted with saw-tooth, frog and circle designs. It is the place to see the painted pottery of the Majiayao and Qijia cultures.

rows.name: Ping'an Yi (Hehuang Folk Culture Quarter)
rows.summary: A newly built cultural quarter in Ping'an District, laid out in the style of an old post-station village and themed on Hehuang, the Huangshui valley of eastern Qinghai, whose food, architecture and crafts reflect its many ethnic groups. Its lanes hold regional restaurants, a courtyard inn with hot-spring baths, cafés and craft shops, with staged folk performances. It is a place to eat, stay and browse in newly built old-street style, not a historic town.

rows.name: Qili Flower Sea
rows.summary: A rural-tourism park at the foot of Mount Kangeda in Shanzhuang village, Gushan town, Minhe County, developed from 2017 on stony wasteland. It covers about 60 hectares, of which roughly 20 hectares are flower beds that bloom from spring to autumn, with boardwalks and viewing pavilions. Besides the flowers it has slides, a glass water slide, a children's play area, village guesthouses and, in winter, a small ski and snow-tube slope, so it suits families and day trips more than hikers.

rows.name: Qutan Temple
rows.summary: A Gelug-school Tibetan Buddhist monastery in a side valley south of Ledu, begun in 1392 in the early Ming dynasty and laid out like a small palace with a gatehouse, three courtyards and a long axis of halls, and nicknamed the 'little Forbidden City' in tourism material. Its covered corridors carry about 400 square metres of Buddhist wall paintings, and two Ming imperial stele pavilions stand in the front court. It is described as the best-preserved large Ming temple complex in north-west China.

rows.name: Salar Homeland Folk Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 撒拉尔故里民俗文化园
rows.summary: A folk-culture park in Majia village, Jiezi town, set up to present the life of the Salar, a Muslim people whose ancestors, by tradition, migrated here from Central Asia and who live mainly in Xunhua. It has a visitor centre, a marriage-customs hall, a folk museum, a display of traditional Salar timber-and-wattle houses and an exhibition on Qinghai hand-pulled noodles, with Salar-style meals and guesthouses. It makes a good introduction to Salar culture alongside the nearby Camel Spring.

rows.name: Salar Mosques of Xunhua
rows.name_zh: 撒拉族清真寺古建筑群
rows.summary: A national heritage group of five Qing-period mosques of the Salar community in Xunhua County, at Mengda, Qingshui (Hedong), Tashapo, Zhang'ga and Kewa, listed together in 2013. They are active places of worship, so go outside prayer times and ask before entering.

rows.name: Tianyoude Liquor Workshop
rows.summary: The historic workshop of the Tianyoude brand of highland-barley (qingke) liquor in Weiyuan, listed nationally in 2013 as a Qing-period industrial site. The company offers an industrial-tourism visit that the tourism ministry's route listing presents as the source of Chinese highland-barley liquor. Highland-barley liquor is Huzhu's signature drink and a protected geographical-indication product.

rows.name: Tu Native Land Park, Huzhu
rows.summary: A folk-culture complex around Weiyuan, the county town of Huzhu Tu Autonomous County, presenting Tu (Monguor) culture through traditional-style courtyard houses, an old oil mill, liquor workshops and a chieftain's mansion, with live song, dance and wedding performances. Its linked sites include the Rainbow Tribe village, the Western Tu folk village and Naton Manor. It was rated a national 5A scenic area in 2017 and suits travellers who want an introduction to Tu life; the Tianyoude liquor workshop is a short distance away.

rows.name: Wendu Monastery and the 10th Panchen Lama's Birthplace
rows.name_zh: 文都寺及班禅大师故居
rows.pinyin: Wéndū Sì jí Bānchán Dàshī Gùjū
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery, also written Bimdo or Biandu, in Wendu Tibetan township, Xunhua, together with the house where the 10th Panchen Lama was born in 1938. The house is a Tibetan-style courtyard building of three yards. The monastery and the house were listed together as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: Western Route Red Army Sites, Xunhua
rows.name_zh: 循化西路红军革命旧址
rows.summary: According to official accounts, over 400 captured soldiers of the Red Army's Western Route Army were held in Hongguang village, then called Zanbuhu, by Ma Bufang's forces from 1939 to 1946 and set to forced labour clearing land and building houses, a school and a mosque. The mosque has red-star, sickle and other motifs worked into its roof brickwork, and Qinghai media describe it as the only mosque in China built by Red Army soldiers. The village also has a Western Route Red Army memorial hall and the soldiers' former houses, and was renamed Hongguang in 1987.

rows.name: Xiaqiong Monastery
rows.summary: A Gelug monastery in remote hills in Chapu Tibetan township, Hualong, named for the roc-shaped mountain it stands on ('Xiaqiong' means roc in Tibetan). Founded in 1349 by a teacher of the Gelug founder Tsongkhapa, it is one of the oldest monasteries in Qinghai. It is counted among four noted monasteries north of the Huangshui river, and Chinese sources record that a Qing emperor granted it a four-language plaque.

rows.name: Fusi City Site (Tuyuhun Capital)
rows.summary: Fusi (also written Fuqi) was the capital of the Tuyuhun kingdom, a Xianbei-founded realm that held the Qinghai Lake region and the Qaidam Basin until it fell to the Tibetan Empire in 663. The ruins lie on grassland on the south bank of the Buha River, with an inner walled enclosure and a much larger outer one; a 2018–2020 survey confirmed that the city dates from the Northern Dynasties to the early Tang and was reused in the Song. What remains are earthen walls and mounds in open pasture, so it mainly suits those interested in the history of the Qinghai Lake region.

rows.name: Guide Confucian Temple and Yuhuang Pavilion
rows.summary: This is a cluster of temples in Guide's old town, begun in 1592 under the Ming and mostly rebuilt in the late 19th century under the Qing, with a Confucian temple, a literary courtyard, the Yuhuang (Jade Emperor) Pavilion, a Guan–Yue (war god) temple and a City God temple side by side. Some Ming and Qing inscriptions and murals survive, and the Yuhuang Pavilion gives views over the town and the Yellow River. The county government describes it as one of Qinghai's best-known ancient building complexes.

rows.name: Guide National Geopark
rows.summary: The geopark is a Danxia landscape of red sandstone and conglomerate cliffs near Ashigong village in Garang township, where earth-pillar formations sit on the upper layers and seven differently coloured gorges cut through the lower ones. It was approved as a national geopark in 2009 and is laid out with viewing platforms and thirteen 'earth culture' plazas; the colour of the rock changes with the weather.

rows.name: Longyangxia Scenic Area
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: Longyangxia is a Yellow River gorge scenic area built around the reservoir behind the Longyangxia hydropower dam (completed in 1992). Visitors take boats on the reservoir and walk gorge-edge walkways where blue sheep and golden eagles can sometimes be seen, and the old dam-builders' town of Longyangxia keeps many 1970s and 1980s buildings. A Danxia 'earth forest' park with a wooden boardwalk of about 2 km lies nearby.

rows.name: Qingqing Yellow River Scenic Area, Guide
rows.summary: Along its stretch at Guide the Yellow River runs unusually clear, which gave rise to the local saying that 'the Yellow River is clear at Guide'. The riverside scenic area on the south bank at Heyin town has a waterwheel plaza, walkways and boat trips on the river past red Danxia cliffs.

rows.name: Saizong Monastery
rows.summary: Saizong is a Gelug monastery of Tibetan Buddhism below Saizong ('Monkey Fortress') mountain, founded in 1923 by the third Aro Tsang lama of Rongwo Monastery. Its main building is a hundred-pillar prayer hall, and pilgrims walk a circuit of the mountain past caves, springs and rocks that local tradition links to Padmasambhava, Tsongkhapa and King Gesar. The county government calls it the largest Gelug monastery in Hainan Prefecture.

rows.name: Shizang Monastery
rows.summary: Shizang is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Hebei township in the far south of Tongde County, near the Yellow River. The county government says it holds scriptures printed by the sixth Panchen Lama, robes of the fourth Panchen Lama, a large collection of Kangyur and Tengyur volumes and a hall of thousands of Buddha images, with painted murals; the national list dates its buildings to the Qing dynasty.

rows.name: Wenchang Temple, Guide
rows.summary: Wenchang Temple is a Qing-dynasty temple of Wenchang, the god of literature and examinations, in Xiapai village, Hexi, on the Yellow River plain west of Guide town. It is one of four national heritage units in Guide County and a stop on the county's 'Ancient Charm of Guide' heritage route, with the Pearl Temple and the Confucian Temple.

rows.name: Zhenzhu (Pearl) Temple, Guide
rows.summary: Zhenzhu ('Pearl') Temple is a Gelug monastery on the edge of Guide's old town; local tradition says a senior monk founded it in the 1240s with a donation of a load of pearls, hence the name. Its gate and side halls date from 1817, and the Qinghai Tibetan Buddhist institute stands opposite.

rows.name: Zongri Site
rows.summary: Zongri is a Neolithic settlement and cemetery on a Yellow River terrace at Tuanjie village, which gave its name to the Zongri culture of about 5,000 years ago, known for painted pottery with dancing-figure and two-people-carrying designs. A site park, opened as a scenic area in May 2025, has an archaeological display area where some excavated tombs and the 'first hearth' are covered by glass so that visitors can look in, a painted-pottery experience hall and a Yellow River viewing platform, while the famous pots themselves are held in museums.

rows.name: Chaka Yihao Salt Lake
rows.summary: Chaka Yihao, formerly Tiankong Yihao ('Sky Number One') until its renaming in July 2022, is the second tourist area of Chaka Salt Lake, on the eastern part of the lake; it opened in July 2019 after nearly a year of trial operation. It was planned at about 14 km² with five zones, including salt culture, wetland sightseeing and creative-culture areas, and it runs separately from the main Chaka Salt Lake scenic area, which has its own entrance.

rows.name: Emerald Lake, Da Qaidam
rows.summary: Emerald Lake is a group of former mining pools in the Da Qaidam salt lake, an industrial legacy of the area's mineral extraction, where brine of differing mineral content shows colours from pale blue to deep green. The local government gives the area as about 15 km², and the water is still tied to industrial salt extraction, so it is a working landscape as much as a scenic one. The scenic area has a visitor centre, viewing platforms and a car park.

rows.name: General's Building (Qinghai–Tibet Highway Headquarters), Golmud
rows.summary: The General's Building is a two-storey brick building from 1956 that served as the office and home of Mu Shengzhong, who commanded construction of the Qinghai–Tibet Highway (completed to Lhasa in December 1954); it was the first two-storey building in Golmud. It is now the centre of a 9.8-hectare memorial park, opened in 2009, with a Qinghai–Tibet Highway museum and the Heaven Road memorial tower, whose 39.16 m height echoes the roughly 3,916 km combined length of the highway and the railway. The displays cover how the highway was built and how Golmud grew around it.

rows.name: Kunlun Mountain Tourist Area, Golmud
rows.time_needed: Half a day to a day
rows.summary: The Kunlun tourist area is Golmud's name for a string of Kunlun Mountains sights south of the city along the Qinghai–Tibet road rather than a single gated park; Golmud's promotion lists Kunlun Spring and Wuji Longfeng Palace among them. Kunlun Spring does not freeze at about 3,540 m, and the Kunlun Mountains National Geopark (opened in 2008) along the same road takes in the glaciers around Yuzhu Peak (6,178 m) and the surface rupture left by the magnitude 8.1 earthquake of 2001 near Kunlun Pass. It is a high-altitude drive.

rows.name: Qarhan Salt Lake
rows.summary: Qarhan is a vast salt flat in the southern Qaidam Basin, much of it worked for potash and other salts; the Golmud government gives its area as 5,856 km². The visitor area is built around a central wharf (really an industrial brine-pumping station), the 32 km 'Wanzhang Salt Bridge' where the Golmud–Dunhuang road and the Qinghai–Tibet railway run over the salt crust, and fields of 'thousand-island' salt flowers.

rows.name: Reshui Tombs
rows.summary: Reshui is a large cemetery of the Tuyuhun kingdom under Tibetan Empire rule (7th–8th centuries) on both banks of the Chahanwusu River, with hundreds of earth-covered mounds on the grassland. The best known is the Xuewei Tomb (M1), a mound about 11 m high that locals nickname the 'Nine-Storey Demon Tower'. Finds such as silks, including one woven with Middle Persian script, and gold and silver ornaments with Central and West Asian designs show Silk Road trade through Qinghai; excavation is still under way and the finds are displayed in Dulan County Museum.

rows.name: Wusute Water Yadan
rows.time_needed: Half a day on site, plus a very long drive
rows.summary: Wusute is a shallow saline lake in the Taijinar basin of the western Qaidam Basin, where eroded clay ridges (yardangs) rise out of the water among salt flats and desert. The Da Qaidam authorities say thousands of wild ducks gather on the lake, most visibly in autumn, which is why it is also called Duck Lake. The tourist park opened in 2018 at about 2,700 m, inside a yardang field that the local government puts at roughly 100 km².

rows.name: Bao'an Fort Villages
rows.summary: A national heritage group of four Ming and Qing military-farming (tuntian) forts on the terraces of the middle Longwu river in Tongren: Bao'an old town and the fort villages of Nianduhu, Guomaru and Wutun. The forts date from the Ming dynasty, were enlarged in 1574 and served as a garrison base for the Ming and Qing governments in the Longwu valley. Bao'an's Chengnei village was among China's first listed traditional villages in 2012.

rows.name: Heri Temple and Mani Stone Wall
rows.summary: A Nyingma temple in Heri town, Zêkog (Zeku) County, known for its stone-sutra wall of more than 100,000 engraved slabs, which the county government gives as over 200 m long. The slabs carry mainly the Kangyur and Tengyur, with images of Buddhas, Padmasambhava and stupas; by local tradition the carving began in the early 19th century and was completed in the 1950s, and Heri stone carving is listed as national intangible heritage. The county's Heri scenic area, about 2.5 sq km, centres on the temple and the wall.

rows.name: Nangla Qianhu Manor
rows.summary: The manor of the seventh Nangla (Ang'la) qianhu, a hereditary Tibetan local chief of the Jainca area, built in the late 1940s in Jianbaang village. It is a wooden courtyard complex of two-storey halls around two courtyards, with a brick-carved screen wall and more than 200 rooms, and the provincial government press office calls it one of the best-preserved Tibetan aristocratic estates in Qinghai and the Amdo region. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 1998 and nationally in 2019.

rows.name: Rongwo Monastery and Rebgong Old Town
rows.summary: Rongwo (Longwu) Monastery in Tongren, called Rebgong in Tibetan, is a large Gelug monastery of the Amdo region with origins in the 14th century, and the centre of a valley of Tibetan and Tu (Monguor) villages famed for thangka painting. The 4A-rated Rebgong historic area strings together the monastery, the old street, painting academies, Wutun's lower monastery and Guomaru, a mud-walled fort village a short drive from town. China News (2023) counts 23 halls and prayer halls and 27 lama residences at the monastery.

rows.name: Bianmagou Flower Sea
rows.summary: A flower garden of about 800 mu (roughly 53 hectares) in Bianmagou village, Shuobei Tibetan township, Datong County, at an average height of about 2,800 m. The village began planting it around 2015 with plateau flowers such as lupins, gaillardias and irises and with spruce and crab-apple trees, and has since added a glass water slide, farmhouse restaurants and guesthouses. Xinhua found the flowers in bloom in late July, and it suits a half-day trip from Xining.

rows.name: Dan'gar Ancient Town
rows.summary: The old town of Huangyuan County, called Tongkor in Tibetan, founded in the Hongwu era of the early Ming (1368–98) and made the seat of a Qing sub-prefecture, the Dan'gar Ting, in 1829. It has two gates, the Gonghai Gate to the west and the Yingchun Gate to the east, and its lanes hold a City God temple, a Guandi temple, a Fire God pavilion, a Golden Buddha temple and other shrines. It makes an easy stop on the road from Xining to Riyue Mountain and Qinghai Lake.

rows.name: Dongguan Mosque
rows.summary: A mosque in the Dongguan quarter on the east side of Xining, a focus of the city's Hui Muslim community, founded in the Hongwu era of the early Ming (1368–98). The compound covers about 11,940 square metres, with a prayer hall of 1,102 square metres. It was listed as a provincial heritage site in 1986 and as a national one in 2013.

rows.name: Huangyuan City God Temple
rows.summary: A palace-style temple built into the hillside in the heart of Dan'gar old town, begun in 1776, rebuilt in 1801 and repaired in 1911 and 1926. It faces south and covers about 6,000 square metres, and is counted among the best-preserved palace-style buildings of the old town. It was listed as a national heritage unit in 2013.

rows.name: Kunlun Jade Culture Museum
rows.summary: A museum in the Biological Science and Technology Park in Xining's Chengbei district, in the same museum cluster as the Tibetan Medicine Culture Museum and the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau Natural Museum. Its three floors are arranged in ten sections on the history of jade culture in China and on the culture of Qinghai's Kunlun jade. It was upgraded in 2017 and opened to visitors in March 2019.

rows.name: Laoye Mountain
rows.summary: A 2,928 m mountain above Qiaotou town, the seat of Datong Hui and Tu Autonomous County north of Xining, taking its name by tradition from a Guandi temple on its slopes, with other small temples along the ascent. It is the home of the Laoyeshan huaer gathering, a folk-song festival held each summer, traditionally around the sixth day of the sixth lunar month; huaer folk song is on China's list of intangible cultural heritage.

rows.name: Limeng Pedestrian Street
rows.summary: A modern shopping and dining quarter in central Xining, built in an old-street style of Qin-brick and Han-tile design and laid out as 'two streets, four gates and eight lanes'. It mixes local snack restaurants with national chains, cafes, bars and a cinema, and a 2019 state-media guide describes it as a gathering place for young locals. It is a modern commercial development, not historic Xining, and stands a few minutes' walk from the Qinghai Provincial Museum.

rows.name: Nanliang Hutai Site
rows.summary: A rammed-earth mound of the Sixteen Kingdoms period, said to be what remains of a nine-tier reviewing platform built by Tufa Hutai, crown prince of Southern Liang, with room below for 100,000 troops according to the records. Only the mound survives, known locally as the commander's terrace, and it stands in a small heritage park in Xining's Chengxi district. It was listed as provincial heritage in 1957 and as a national site in 2013.

rows.name: Qinghai Provincial Museum
rows.summary: Qinghai's provincial museum, open to the public since 1986 and housed since 2001 in a large building on West Gate Street in central Xining. Its collections, strongest in pottery and including paintings and calligraphy, coins, textiles, ethnic costume and religious objects, are shown mainly in a 'Qinghai Historical Relics' exhibition, with smaller displays on archaeology, intangible cultural heritage and revolutionary relics, arranged since an upgrade in 2021. It was ranked a national first-grade museum in 2017.

rows.name: Qinghai Tibetan Culture Hall
rows.summary: A privately run museum of Tibetan history and culture in Lusar, Huangzhong District, opened in 2010 and housed in two exhibition halls. The first covers the history of the Tibetan people, Buddhist figures and deities, masks, thangka, script and epics, costume, song and dance, the 'three arts' of Kumbum and Tibetan opera, and the second presents Tibetan Buddhist views of the cosmos and of life and death. It makes a useful companion to a visit to Kumbum Monastery nearby.

rows.name: Qinghai Tibetan Medicine Culture Museum
rows.name_zh: 青海藏医药文化博物馆
rows.summary: A national first-grade museum devoted to Tibetan medicine and plateau civilisation, in Xining's Biological Science and Technology Park, with nearly 60,000 objects including fossils, stone tools, pottery, gold and silver, silks, old manuscripts, medical instruments and thangka. It is best known for a thangka scroll 618 m long, 'Grand View of Tibetan Cultural Art', painted by artists from five provinces and regions; a second 410 m volume was installed in April 2025. Other highlights include a Tubo-period gold headdress inlaid with turquoise and a manuscript of the Four Medical Tantras (Subsequent Tantra).

rows.name: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau Natural Museum
rows.summary: A natural-history museum in Xining's Biological Science and Technology Park, opened in 2011 and a few minutes' walk from the Tibetan Medicine Culture Museum. Its displays introduce the landscapes of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and its animal and plant life.

rows.name: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau Wildlife Park
rows.summary: A zoo and wildlife rescue centre at the foot of Fenghuang Mountain on the western edge of Xining, opened in 2009 and best known for its snow leopards, most of them rescued from the wild; Xinhua reported in 2025 that it kept 12 of the roughly 20 snow leopards on public display in China. According to Xinhua, its small-cat house is the only place in China where visitors can see the Chinese mountain cat, also called the desert cat.

rows.name: Riyue Mountain
rows.summary: A pass at 3,399 m on the road west from Xining to Qinghai Lake, dividing the Huangshui river basin and the farming zone to the east from the Qinghai Lake basin and the herding zone to the west. By tradition Princess Wencheng of the Tang passed this way in 641 on her journey to marry the Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo, and legend says she smashed a magic mirror here that showed only her own reflection, and that the Daotang River, which unusually flows west, rose from her tears. Two small modern temples on the pass carry murals of the royal couple and nomad life, and a folk-song gathering is held around the sixth day of the sixth lunar month.

rows.name: Western Route Army Memorial Hall, Xining
rows.name_zh: 中国工农红军西路军纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial museum in Xining on the Red Army's Western Route Army, the force that crossed the Yellow River westwards in October 1936 and was defeated by Ma family armies in Gansu's Hexi Corridor by March 1937, when more than 9,000 of its soldiers were captured. Its permanent exhibition, 'The Power of Faith: Soldiers of the Western Route Army in Qinghai', has six units and seven reconstructed scenes and shows more than 130 relics, among them a worn pair of knitted trousers found with a soldier's remains in 1956. A multimedia online exhibition hall accompanies the galleries.

rows.name: Xiangqu Kayang Outdoor Resort
rows.summary: An outdoor resort in the high forest and pasture hills of Lanlongkou town, Huangzhong District; an official 2020 case study calls it the nearest primeval forest to Xining, with 81.1% tree cover, and gives its Tibetan name Kayang as 'pure place'. Facilities listed there include an 18 km boardwalk trail, an 800 m water slide, mountain-bike and motorbike tracks, a caravan camp, a winter ski area and a climbing area. It suits families and groups who want a day of outdoor activity near Xining rather than sightseeing.

rows.name: Xinhualian Tongmeng Park
rows.summary: A children's theme park and resort complex at Duoba in Huangzhong District, built around a Silk Road theme and open since 2019 on a site of about 24 hectares. It combines a land amusement park with rides, an indoor water park, an aquarium, a 'Silk Road Town', an ethnic food street, an ocean-themed hotel and a large Ferris wheel. It suits families with young children.

rows.name: Xining Sports Park
rows.summary: A municipal sports-themed park on Haihu Avenue in Xining's Chengbei district, opened in 2016 as one of the main areas of the city's ring-road ecological park. Local reports describe walking paths, a lake, open woodland and grass, a tai chi plaza, a dance plaza, fitness equipment, ball courts, a children's play area and a self-drive and RV campsite. It is mainly a place for local exercise and leisure, and suits a short stop rather than a sightseeing visit.

rows.name: Zongjiagou Scenic Area
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area in Riyue Tibetan township, Huangyuan County, with rock formations, natural caves and a hall to the Queen Mother of the West, a figure of Kunlun mythology. In winter a display of ice falls and icicles lit with coloured lights covering 40,000 square metres drew visitors in 2021, according to China News Service. It is a short outing on the road between Xining and Qinghai Lake rather than a major sight.

rows.name: Dana Temple and the Stupas of Gesar's Thirty Generals
rows.time_needed: A day, with the long drive
rows.summary: A Yelpa Kagyu monastery on the slopes of Dana (Horse-Ear) Mountain in the far north-west of Nangqian County, near the border with the Tibet Autonomous Region, said to be the only surviving monastery of its school and to have begun as a Bon temple. It is closely tied to the epic of King Gesar, and in two cliff caves above it stand 37 small stone-and-mud stupas known as the Thirty Generals of Gesar, whose relics were radiocarbon-dated to the Song dynasty, about 1115. The monastery reopened in 1981 and was listed with the stupas as a national heritage unit in 2006.

rows.name: Princess Wencheng Temple and Lebagou Rock Carvings
rows.summary: A small Buddhist temple built against a cliff in the Beinagou valley near Gyêgu (Jiegu), Yushu's main town, where Vairocana and eight attendant bodhisattvas are carved in relief on the rock above the hall, with more carvings and Tibetan inscriptions elsewhere in the valley and in neighbouring Lebagou. Locals call it the Princess Wencheng Temple after the Tang princess who by tradition passed this way to Tibet, though an inscription naming the reign of Tride Songtsen and the dog year of 806 points to the Tibetan imperial period. The hall was renovated in 1938 and 1989, and a memorial hall to the princess stands beside it.

rows.name: Xinzhai Jiana Mani Stone Pile
rows.summary: A huge pile of carved mani stones on a hillside at Xinzhai, on the edge of Gyêgu (Jiegu), Yushu's main town, begun, by tradition, in the late 18th century by the first Jiana lama of Jiegu Monastery and added to by pilgrims ever since. It now covers about 20,000 square metres, roughly 270 m long, 80 m wide and three to four metres high, carved with mantras, sutras and images of Buddhist figures, with prayer-wheel corridors and chapels added since the 1980s. It was damaged in the 2010 Yushu earthquake and repaired afterwards.

rows.name: Zangniang Stupa and Sangzhou Temple
rows.summary: A large stupa dating from the Northern Song period (960–1127), standing beside Sangzhou monastery on the south bank of the Tongtian River in Yushu. The two were listed together as a national heritage unit in 2001, and the buildings were damaged in the 2010 Yushu earthquake, after which emergency repairs began in 2011.

rows.name: Daying Ancient City
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of a frontier town built in the Song dynasty, when it was known as Yangmacheng ('horse-rearing town'), and used under the Ming from 1406 as a state horse-breeding station. The rectangular circuit, about 400 by 500 m with walls 5–12 m high, keeps half-moon barbicans at its south and north gates and bastions along its walls, and is counted among the best-preserved old towns around Guyuan.

rows.name: Guyuan Ancient City Walls
rows.summary: Surviving sections of the walls of Guyuan, founded in 114 BC as the seat of Anding commandery and rebuilt many times as a frontier stronghold; under the Ming it was one of the Nine Border Garrisons and seat of the governor-general of the three Shaanxi frontiers, and its outer wall was faced with brick in 1575. The walls were badly damaged in the 1920 Haiyuan earthquake and mostly pulled down in 1971–72; the surviving earthen stretches, in the north-west of the old city between the Heping and Jingshuo gates, were consolidated in 2014–15.

rows.name: Guyuan Museum
rows.summary: A national first-grade museum, opened in 1988, with about 20,000 objects and best known for Silk Road finds from the Northern Dynasties, Sui and Tang tombs excavated around Guyuan. Highlights include a painted Northern Wei lacquer coffin and, from the tomb of the Northern Zhou general Li Xian, a gilt silver ewer and a glass bowl with raised bosses from Sasanian Persia, alongside northern-style bronzes of the Warring States period. The two permanent galleries cover Guyuan's history and the Silk Road in Guyuan.

rows.name: Jiangtaibu Long March Meeting Site
rows.name_zh: 将台堡红军长征会师纪念园
rows.summary: The earthen fort where the Red Army's Second Front Army met the First Front Army on 22 October 1936, after the First and Fourth had met at Huining on 9 October; the meeting completed the union of the three main Red armies and is taken as the end of the Long March. A 1996 monument stands beside the fort, whose walls, about 70 by 68 m and some 10 m high, enclose a memorial hall to the meeting, an exhibition on the Long March route and a stele garden; the memorial park was enlarged in 2006 and 2016.

rows.name: Kaicheng Site (Palace of the Prince of Anxi)
rows.summary: Remains of the palace of Manggala, Prince of Anxi and third son of Kublai Khan, built from 1272 at Kaicheng in the northern Liupan Mountains and used as a Yuan imperial summer retreat until an earthquake wrecked it in 1306. The rammed-earth walls of the palace city, standing 1–9 m high, and the platforms of its halls survive among other Yuan-period remains, though farming has damaged much of the site.

rows.name: Liupan Mountain Long March Memorial
rows.name_zh: 六盘山红军长征纪念馆
rows.summary: A memorial complex on the pass over the Liupan Mountains, the last high range the Red Army crossed on the Long March in October 1935, a crossing Mao Zedong marked in his poem 'Mount Liupan'. A memorial pavilion was put up on the summit in 1985 and a memorial hall with displays on the march opened in 2005, and a 2.5 km 'Red Army trail' built in 2013 has more than 200 sculptures in 18 scenes. Newer additions include an intangible-heritage hall and a themed post office, and the area was rated 5A at the end of 2024.

rows.name: Liupan Mountain National Forest Park
rows.summary: A national forest park in the Liupan Mountains of southern Ningxia, whose main peak, Migang Shan, reaches 2,942 m; the damp slopes carry birch, poplar, oak and bamboo thickets that stand out from the dry Loess Plateau around them. Its main visitor areas are Xiaonanchuan, a wooded stream valley at one of the sources of the Jing River, and the 8 km Liangdian Gorge, along with an ecology museum and a botanical garden. It is separate from the Long March memorial on the Liupan pass further north.

rows.name: Xumishan Grottoes
rows.summary: More than 130 Buddhist cave temples cut into the red sandstone hills of Mount Xumi from the late Northern Wei to the Tang dynasty, spread over about 1.5 km in groups such as Dafolou, Zisungong, Yuanguangsi, Xiangguosi and Taohuadong. The best-known figure is the seated Tang Maitreya Buddha of Cave 5, about 20.6 m high, while the Yuanguangsi group, mostly Northern Zhou, holds the richest carving. Many caves were damaged by the 1920 Haiyuan earthquake, erosion and the Cultural Revolution, and the scenic area has a museum on the Silk Road and Buddhist cave art.

rows.name: Huaxia Qishishan Park
rows.summary: A landscaped park of about 1.1 km² beside Xinghai Lake in Dawukou, created by grading, covering and planting a former power-station ash dump that stood 13 m above the surrounding land. It displays ornamental stones and stone carvings in themed areas, with a spring garden, a children's science play area and a winter snow park, and suits a short walk.

rows.name: Sand Lake (Shahu)
rows.summary: A freshwater lake fringed with reed beds and backed by sand dunes, developed for tourism since 1990 from a fish lake on a state farm; the scenic area covers about 80 km², including some 45 km² of water and 22 km² of semi-mobile dunes. Migratory birds gather on a bird island in the eastern wetlands, and visitors can cross the lake by boat, ride camels and slide on the dunes, or visit the Ningxia Wetland Museum and an international sand-sculpture park.

rows.name: Shengwei Ancient City
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of a city founded in 1024 by the Tangut ruler Li Deming, a square of about 590 m a side that is described as the only Western Xia town site in Ningxia with a complete circuit of walls. The west, north and south walls still stand 2–6 m high with traces of a moat, while the east wall is largely lost under a village; earthquakes in 1627, 1739 and 1920 caused much of the damage.

rows.name: Tianzhou Pagoda
rows.summary: A seven-storey hexagonal brick pagoda about 38 m tall in Yaofu town, Pingluo county, once part of a temple; its present structure dates from a Qing rebuilding after the 1739 earthquake. Every storey is lined with arched niches, and brick carvings of mock timber brackets, landscapes and figures decorate the eaves above the lowest level. The surrounding temple halls were destroyed in the Cultural Revolution, and the pagoda was restored from 2013.

rows.name: Yuhuang Pavilion, Pingluo
rows.summary: A Taoist temple complex on North Street in Pingluo county town, on the site of a Ming White Dragon temple that was rebuilt as a Jade Emperor pavilion in the late 19th century and enlarged in 1939. Its halls climb in successive courtyards up an earthen platform as much as 10 m high to a three-storey tower about 27 m above the street, linked by galleries and sky bridges, with 16 halls housing Taoist deities. A newer Buddhist section with jade Buddha statues and a large Guanyin statue has been added alongside.

rows.name: Dong Fuxiang's Mansion (Dong Fu)
rows.summary: The fortified residence of Dong Fuxiang, the late-Qing general whose Gansu troops took part in the 1900 siege of the Beijing legations, built in 1902–1905 after he was dismissed and sent home. Rammed-earth walls 8.5 m high with corner platforms enclose a compound of linked courtyards with more than 100 brick-and-timber rooms and much carved brickwork. The moat and outer enclosure have gone, but the walled core has been restored and is open as a scenic area.

rows.name: Habahu Lake Ecotourism Area
rows.summary: A national nature reserve on the south-western edge of the Mu Us Desert, where small lakes and wetlands lie among sand dunes, dry steppe and planted belts of willow, peashrub and other trees. The tourism area has a museum about the reserve and a self-drive campground with wooden cabins and tent pitches.

rows.name: Kangji Temple Pagoda
rows.summary: A 13-storey octagonal brick pagoda of the dense-eaves type in the old town of Weizhou, about 43 m tall since its 1985 restoration. It was first built with nine storeys, probably in the Western Xia period, raised to 13 under the Ming, and repaired in 1581 after an earthquake in 1561 wrecked the temple around it. Bronze, wooden and silver Buddhist statues and scriptures were found in niches on its top storey during the 1985 repairs.

rows.name: Niujiafang Folk Culture Village
rows.summary: A village on the southern edge of Wuzhong developed as a rural tourism area of about 130 ha, with grey-brick houses, rammed-earth courtyard walls and a village museum of Yellow River farming and folk life. It also has homestays, a food street, craft workshops, a children's play area and fruit picking, and suits a half-day visit for local food and village life.

rows.name: Qingtongxia Yellow River Grand Canyon and 108 Stupas
rows.summary: A scenic area of about 126 km² around the Qingtongxia gorge, officially described as the last gorge on the upper Yellow River, taking in the Qingtongxia dam (begun in 1958), a water-conservancy museum and the Dayu culture park at the heart of the Ningxia Yellow River irrigation system, a World Heritage Irrigation Structure. Its best-known sight is the One Hundred and Eight Stupas, Tibetan-style brick stupas in twelve rows that form a triangle on the hillside above the west bank. First built in the Western Xia period, they have been rebuilt several times and no longer keep their original form.

rows.name: Tongxin Great Mosque
rows.summary: Regarded as Ningxia's oldest and largest mosque, it is built in Chinese style with Islamic decoration on a 7 m brick platform; it probably began as a Yuan-period Buddhist temple, became a mosque in the early Ming and was rebuilt several times, notably in 1791 and 1907. In October 1936 the Red Army's Western Expedition held the founding meeting of the Yuhai County Hui Autonomous Government here, and the mosque is counted as part of the Red Army Western Expedition Memorial Park. The park's memorial hall, opened in 2006, covers the expedition and the 1936 visit of Edgar Snow and George Hatem to the Red Army at Yuwangbao, in today's Tongxin county.

rows.name: Xingwuying Ming Garrison Town
rows.summary: The walls of a Ming garrison town founded in 1444 where two lines of the Ming Great Wall meet, a rough rectangle about 600 by 475 m with barbican gates on its south and west sides. Villagers stripped most of the brick facing in the 1970s, but the rammed-earth walls with their wall towers and the 7 m base of the central bell-and-drum tower still stand.

rows.name: Yanzhou Ancient City Cultural Tourism Area
rows.summary: A cultural tourism district on the north side of Yanchi county town, laid out along the Ming Great Wall that runs past the town and forming the core of Yanchi's part of the Great Wall National Cultural Park. It groups a Great Wall gateway (Changcheng Guan), the Ningxia Great Wall Museum, the Jiuqu folk-culture park, the old walled town of Huamachi and Yinma Lake, and is also an evening leisure and food area.

rows.name: Zhangjiachang Ancient City Site
rows.summary: The site of a walled town used from the late Qin to the early Eastern Han, which archaeologists believe was the seat of Xuyan county; its low rammed-earth walls are now mostly buried under drifting sand. Excavations have yielded tiles, pottery, bronze and iron tools, clay seals and more than a thousand coins, and a small site museum shows finds from the town.

rows.name: Bairuiyuan Goji Museum
rows.summary: A company museum run by the goji (wolfberry) producer Bairuiyuan, tracing what it presents as 4,000 years of goji culture and the modern Ningxia goji industry. Visits can include a see-through processing plant and the company shop, and suit travellers curious about Ningxia's best-known crop.

rows.name: COFCO Great Wall Tianfu Winery
rows.summary: A winery of COFCO's Great Wall Wine brand, completed in 2012 on reclaimed desert land at the foot of the Helan Mountains, just across the road from the Western Xia tombs. It has a 7,000 m² underground cellar and extensive vineyards, and offers winery tours, tastings and family activities.

rows.name: Changyu Longyu Chateau (Moser XV)
rows.summary: Changyu's Ningxia wine estate, opened in 2013 as Chateau Changyu Moser XV, a joint venture with the Austrian winemaker Lenz Moser, and rebranded Longyu in 2021. A European-style château with a moat stands among the estate's own vineyards, and its visitor centre has an exhibition on the history of Changyu, China's oldest wine company, founded in 1892.

rows.name: Haibao Pagoda
rows.summary: Yinchuan's 'North Pagoda', a square brick tower on a high platform, about 54 m tall in total, whose stepped projections give it a twelve-cornered plan; it stands in Haibao Temple, the seat of the Ningxia Buddhist Association. Excavation suggests the pagoda was first built between the Northern Dynasties and the Tang, but repeated earthquakes mean the present tower largely dates from Qing rebuilding in the 18th century.

rows.name: Helan Mountain National Forest Park (Suyukou)
rows.summary: A forest park in the Suyukou valley of the Helan Mountains, inside the Helan Mountains national nature reserve north-west of Yinchuan. Shuttle buses run up the valley from the Songtao Shanzhuang stop, and plank walkways and trails climb through wooded slopes to viewpoints over the range.

rows.name: Hengcheng Yellow River Resort
rows.summary: A Yellow River-themed resort on the east bank opposite Yinchuan, built around Hengcheng, a Ming-dynasty fort on the riverbank where the Great Wall east of the river began, beside an old ferry crossing used by the Kangxi Emperor in 1697. Besides the fort, it has newly built halls, an old-style street, a ferry pier, riverside restaurants and a self-drive campsite.

rows.name: Hongfo Pagoda
rows.summary: A late Western Xia brick pagoda (about 1190–1227) standing alone in the countryside of Helan County, with an unusual two-part form: a three-storey octagonal tower topped by a Tibetan-style stupa. When it was restored in 1990, silk paintings, clay figures and a tablet inscribed in Tangut were found inside, and the rebuilt pagoda now stands 35 m high.

rows.name: Huangsha Ancient Ferry
rows.summary: A Yellow River leisure area on the east bank north-east of Yinchuan, named after an old ferry crossing and combining sand dunes, reed wetland and riverside farmland. The usual activities are camel rides on the dunes and boat or raft trips on the river, and it suits families and anyone wanting desert scenery close to the city.

rows.name: Huaxia Hetu Yinchuan Art Town
rows.name_zh: 华夏河图银川艺术小镇
rows.summary: An arts district on the west bank of the Yellow River south-east of Yinchuan, developed around the Museum of Contemporary Art Yinchuan (MOCA Yinchuan). Besides the museum it has an artists' village, a sculpture park and wetland and canal-side parks, and suits visitors interested in contemporary art.

rows.name: Seeing Helan Performance Town (Manpu Town)
rows.summary: A modern leisure town opened in 2016 across National Road 110 from the Zhenbeibu film studio, first built around a Helan Mountains wine theme and later relaunched as the 'Seeing Helan' immersive performance town. Staged plays and street shows recreate a Tang-dynasty frontier town, with costumed actors mixing with visitors, and the town also has a hot-spring complex, a wine exhibition hall and food streets. It was named a national tourism and leisure district in 2025.

rows.name: Mingcui Lake National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A national wetland park, approved in 2006 and covering 6.67 km², around a 2.88 km² freshwater lake that survives from an old chain of lakes east of Yinchuan and was restored from farmland from 2000 onwards. Its name refers to green reeds and birdsong, and the reed beds and waterbirds are the main attraction, about 3 km from the Yellow River.

rows.name: Ningxia Agri-Tourism Park
rows.summary: A 2,170-mu (about 145 ha) agricultural park started in 2009 by the state-owned Ningxia Nongken group just outside Helan county town. It combines modern horticulture with fruit picking, children's play areas, sports grounds and study programmes, and is aimed mainly at families.

rows.name: Pagoda of Chengtian Temple
rows.summary: Yinchuan's 'West Pagoda', an eleven-storey octagonal brick pagoda 64.5 m high, the tallest in Ningxia. It was first completed in 1050 under the Western Xia as a reliquary, but the present tower was built in 1820 after an earthquake in 1739 destroyed the original, and it stands in the grounds of the former Chengtian Temple in the old city.

rows.name: Rock Paintings of Helan Mountains (Helankou)
rows.summary: The Helankou gorge is the best-known site of the Helan Mountains petroglyphs, with some 6,000 images carved on boulders and cliff faces along the valley and generally dated to between about 10,000 and 3,000 years ago. They show animals, herding and hunting scenes and, above all, stylised human faces, about two-thirds of the range's face images being found here, along with a few later Tangut (Western Xia) inscriptions. The Yinchuan World Rock Art Museum near the entrance explains the carvings.

rows.name: Shuidonggou
rows.summary: One of the first Palaeolithic sites excavated in China: Pierre Teilhard de Chardin and Émile Licent dug here in 1923, and later excavations recovered stone tools, hearths and ostrich-eggshell beads left by late Palaeolithic people. The scenic area links the excavation localities and a site museum (opened 2011) with a section of the Ming Great Wall, the walled Hongshanbao fort and the Cangbingdong tunnel fortifications.

rows.name: Tianshanhai World (Yellow River Pearl)
rows.summary: An indoor water park in Binhe New Area on the east bank of the Yellow River, with heated pools and water slides kept warm all year. It is a family leisure venue rather than a sightseeing stop.

rows.name: Twin Pagodas of Baisikou
rows.summary: Two Western Xia-period brick pagodas standing 100 m apart on a terrace at the mouth of the Baisikou gorge in the Helan Mountains, where more than a hundred temples once stood. The octagonal towers, about 39 m and 36 m tall, are covered with tiers of painted stucco Buddhas, guardians and animal masks, many from Yuan and Ming repairs, and Tangut and Sanskrit inscriptions were found on their central pillars during restoration in 1986.

rows.name: Western Xia Culture Park
rows.summary: A Western Xia (Tangut) themed park at the foot of the Helan Mountains on Yinchuan's western edge, with new buildings in imitation Western Xia palace style set among lakes and gardens. Live-action shows on Western Xia themes are its main feature, alongside wine tasting and restaurants, and it pairs easily with a visit to the nearby Western Xia tombs.

rows.name: Wofu Bairui Ningxia Goji Hall
rows.summary: A goji (wolfberry) exhibition hall opened in 2022 by the Ningxia producer Wofu Bairui in Yinchuan's Xixia District. It combines displays on goji growing and health-food culture with a see-through factory corridor, a product tasting centre and a restaurant serving goji dishes.

rows.name: Yellow River Military Culture Park
rows.summary: A defence-themed park in Binhe New Area on the east bank of the Yellow River, opened in 2013 around the decommissioned destroyer Yinchuan, one of China's first-generation guided-missile destroyers, which served from 1976 to 2012. The ship is the centrepiece of a park with a lake, a peace plaza and areas for defence-education activities aimed at school groups and families.

rows.name: Yongning Najiahu Mosque
rows.summary: A Hui mosque in Najiahu village, Yongning County, founded in 1524 by members of the Na clan, who trace their descent from the Yuan-dynasty statesman Sayyid Ajall Shams al-Din. Its present buildings date mainly from the Qing dynasty, and it remains the place of worship of the village's Hui community.

rows.name: Yuehai Bay
rows.summary: A large lake and park area in Jinfeng District covering 1,739 ha, 922 ha of it water, made up of Yuehai National Wetland Park, a water park, Lanshan Park and the Flower Expo Garden. The wetland was made a national wetland park in 2006, and the big open-air amphitheatre in Lanshan Park is a popular place to watch the sun set behind the Helan Mountains.

rows.name: Yuhuang Pavilion, Yinchuan
rows.summary: A Taoist pavilion complex on an 8 m brick-faced platform in the old centre of Yinchuan, rebuilt as a Jade Emperor temple after the earthquake of 1739 on the site of a drum tower first built in the Yongle era of the Ming. A two-storey hall flanked by bell and drum towers crowns the platform, which is pierced by an arched gateway, and the halls reopened for exhibitions after refurbishment in 2015.

rows.name: Yuquan International Winery
rows.summary: A winery of the state-owned Ningxia Nongken group in the Yuquan wine village of Yongning County, set among vineyards, with buildings in Song-dynasty style decorated with classical wine poetry; it bills itself as China's first poetry-themed winery. It is a second-growth estate in the Helan Mountains East classification, and visits take in the winery, a wine-poetry exhibition and tastings.

rows.name: Zhenbeibu China West Film Studio
rows.summary: A film studio founded by the writer Zhang Xianliang in the ruins of two old frontier forts at Zhenbeibu, on the plain below the Helan Mountains. Films shot here include Red Sorghum, A Chinese Odyssey and New Dragon Gate Inn, and visitors walk through the Ming fort, the Qing fort and an 'Old Yinchuan' street laid out as film sets.

rows.name: Zhihui Yuanshi Winery
rows.summary: A winery in the Helan Mountains foothills built on an abandoned gravel quarry, restored with vineyards, shelter woods and underground cellars dug into the old pits. Visitors follow the route from vineyard and fermentation hall to barrel cellar and tasting hall, and the estate received more than half a million visitors in 2025.

rows.name: Damaidi Rock Art
rows.summary: A dense field of rock carvings in the Weining Northern Mountains north of Zhongwei, where thousands of panels with roughly 8,000 individual figures have been recorded in a core area of about 6 km², showing hunting, herding, animals and sun and moon symbols. Some researchers see in their recurring signs a forerunner of Chinese writing, but the dating, spanning the Neolithic to the Western Xia according to the heritage listing, remains disputed.

rows.name: Gao Temple, Zhongwei
rows.summary: A temple complex in central Zhongwei that brings Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian halls together on terraces rising from the gate to a three-storey main tower 29 m high. Rebuilt several times after earthquakes and a fire in 1942, it reopened as a Buddhist site in 1982; the main tower has halls for the Jade Emperor, Confucius and other figures, and a tunnel linking two ponds is called the 'cave of hell and reincarnation'.

rows.name: Liuzhou City Ruins (Tiandu Fort)
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of Tiandu, a Northern Song frontier fort later taken by the Western Xia, who are thought to have based their Tiandu military command here; it was abandoned in 1749, when a new town was built a few kilometres to the east on the site of present-day Haiyuan. The rectangular enclosure, about 400 by 380 m, keeps walls 4–7 m high with barbican gates to the north and south and towers at the corners.

rows.name: Mingshazhou Pagoda
rows.summary: An eleven-storey octagonal brick pagoda in Anqing Temple at Mingsha town, on the south bank of the Yellow River in Zhongning County. First built around the Western Xia period, it was rebuilt in 1569–1580 after the 1561 earthquake, lost its upper half in the 1709 earthquake and was restored to its present height of 42 m in 1985.

rows.name: Qiying Beizui City Ruins
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of a frontier town founded in the Sui dynasty, made the seat of Xiaoguan county under the Tang and garrisoned until the late Ming, at Beizui village near Qiying. Inner and outer walls, now 1–5 m high, enclose an area of about 650 by 600 m, with a fortified enclosure and barbican at the north-east corner.

rows.name: Sikouzi Scenic Area
rows.summary: A gorge scenic area of about 18 km² in the hills south of Xuanhe town, known in ancient times as Beihai. Its eastern part is a narrow karst gorge with odd rock formations, while the western part has red sandstone (danxia) cliffs, a natural cave and spots tied to local legends such as that of the Han envoy Su Wu herding sheep.

rows.name: Tengger Desert Wetland – Jinsha Island
rows.name_zh: 腾格里沙漠湿地·金沙岛
rows.summary: A wetland leisure area on the south-eastern edge of the Tengger Desert, where a chain of lakes and reed beds meets the dunes, with an island in the main lake. Visitors walk round the lakes, climb a dune of about 30 m and see seasonal flower fields and a 4 km stretch of earthen Ming Great Wall that runs through the area, and water birds gather on the lakes.

rows.name: Aksu Museum
rows.summary: The prefecture museum of Aksu, also called the Aksu Prefecture Museum and Heritage Institute, opened in its present colourful building in 2009 and holds about 2,000 objects on the history of the Aksu region and the Kucha kingdom. Digital galleries let visitors explore Kizil, Subashi, the Kizilgaha beacon and other sites in VR, and a gallery reproduces Kucha cave murals.

rows.name: Aksu National Wetland Park
rows.summary: A wetland park beside Aksu city covering about 5,000 mu (330 ha), of which some 1,800 mu is water, laid out as 23 linked lakes with paths and five viewing platforms. It draws waterbirds such as ducks, coots and grebes, and protected species recorded here include the black stork and golden eagle.

rows.name: Ancient Kucha City Ruins
rows.summary: These are the remains of the walled capital of the ancient Kucha kingdom, identified as Yancheng of the Han dynasty and Yiluolu of the Tang, within today's Kuqa city. Stretches of the old city wall survive, excavations have yielded Han-dynasty coins, and the wall has been the subject of a recent protection and display project.

rows.name: Daolang Tribe Scenic Area, Awat
rows.summary: A folk-culture scenic area in Awat County themed on Dolan (刀郎) culture, the tradition behind Dolan muqam music, set among old desert-poplar woodland by a river. It stages Dolan song and dance and folk sports such as horse racing at festivals, and about 100 residents live and run shops inside the scenic area.

rows.name: Desert Flower Sea, Xinhe
rows.summary: A desert leisure park of about 3,000 mu (some 200 ha) opened at the end of 2016 on a patch of dunes surrounded by oasis farmland in Qiaolepaibage village, Xinhe County. Flowerbeds are planted among the dunes, and the park offers desert off-road rides and water-based amusements.

rows.name: Duolang River Scenic Area, Aksu
rows.summary: The landscaped banks of the Duolang River through Aksu city, a 4A scenic area since 2018, with promenades, pavilions such as the Gumo Pavilion and a small amusement area. Waterbirds gather on the river and locals come for evening walks, so it is an easy stroll rather than a destination in itself.

rows.name: Jiayi Village
rows.summary: Jiayi is a village in Xinhe County known for making traditional Uyghur musical instruments, a craft it has practised for more than 300 years; nearly half of its roughly 290 households build instruments such as the dutar, ajek and rawap. Visitors can watch instruments being made in family workshops and at the village's instrument-making centre, and one master craftsman is a national-level intangible heritage bearer.

rows.name: Kangqi Wetland, Baicheng
rows.summary: A wetland in Arele village, Kangqi township, where the Karasu and Muzat rivers meet east of Baicheng county town, developed for rural tourism since 2018. Rapeseed and sunflower fields line a stretch called the 'ten-li gallery', visitors can go kayaking, and village families run restaurants along a food street.

rows.name: Kekeya Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall at the core of the Kekeya greening project, which since the 1980s has planted forest across the gravel desert that once sent dust storms into Aksu. Photographs, objects, reconstructions and VR displays tell the story of the tree planters, and the roof, modelled on Tomur Peak, has a viewing platform over the planted shelter belts.

rows.name: Kesiletage Buddhist Temple Ruins
rows.summary: The ruins of a Kucha-style Buddhist monastery of the Northern Dynasties to Tang period, built in terraces up a bare hill near Kalpin, with a main hall, monks' rooms and a stupa base. Walls and hall remains stand 5–7 m high and a passage keeps traces of murals, and the Qiudayitage fort stands on a nearby hill about 800 m to the north-east.

rows.name: Kizil Caves
rows.summary: Kizil is the largest Buddhist cave complex of the ancient Kucha kingdom and among the earliest in China, cut into cliffs above the Muzat River from about the 3rd century until the 8th–9th centuries. It has around 350 caves in four groups, more than 80 of them with murals in the distinctive Kucha style, and has been part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing since 2014. Visitors see a selection of the caves with a guide.

rows.name: Kizilgaha Beacon Tower
rows.summary: A Han-dynasty beacon tower of rammed earth laid in layers with reeds and branches, still about 16 m high, standing on gravel desert north-west of Kuqa. Weathering has split its top so that it looks like a double tower, and remains of buildings lie to its north. Part of the Silk Roads World Heritage site since 2014, it is laid out as a heritage park with a visitor centre.

rows.name: Kizilgaha Caves
rows.summary: Kizilgaha is a group of 54 Buddhist caves, 46 of them numbered, cut into gully cliffs north-west of Kuqa from the 5th century and one of the main cave sites of the ancient Kucha kingdom. Several caves keep murals, including donor figures in Tocharian dress, and the site lies about 600 m north of the Kizilgaha Beacon Tower.

rows.name: Kumtura Caves
rows.summary: Kumtura is the second-largest cave group of ancient Kucha after Kizil: 112 caves cut between the 5th and 11th centuries along about 3 km of cliffs above the Weigan (Muzat) River. Its murals run from early Kuchean work through Tang Chinese to later Uyghur styles, some with inscriptions in Chinese and Old Uyghur, and the southern group holds a rare surviving clay Buddha.

rows.name: Kuqa Grand Mosque
rows.summary: Kuqa's main mosque stands on a mound on the north-western side of the old town; tradition dates its founding to the 16th century, and the present prayer hall, gatehouse and court building come from a rebuilding completed in 1932 after a fire. The domed brick gatehouse rises more than 15 m, and the prayer hall, which holds about 3,000 worshippers, rests on 88 carved wooden columns under painted ceilings. Beside the gate are the rooms of a former religious court.

rows.name: Kuqa Palace
rows.summary: Kuqa Palace is a reconstruction, completed in 2004, of the residence of the Kuqa princes, a hereditary title first granted under the Qianlong Emperor in the 18th century and held by twelve generations. The compound mixes Chinese and Islamic architectural styles and houses exhibitions on the princely family, Kucha history and local folk life, next to a surviving stretch of Qing-dynasty city wall.

rows.name: Liu Pingguo Inscription
rows.summary: An Eastern Han cliff inscription of about 105 characters in clerical script, cut in 158, records how Liu Pingguo, a general of the Kucha kingdom, had men cut the rock and build a pass station at the mouth of the Boziklig gully. The valley leads over the Tian Shan towards Ili on the old route known as the Wusun Road. Found by Qing soldiers in 1879, the characters are now faint, and the spot is fenced, with a memorial stele and a flood wall.

rows.name: Molana Arshidin Mazar
rows.summary: The shrine complex of Arshidin, the 14th-century Sufi teacher credited with bringing the Moghul khan Tughlugh Timur to Islam, lies between Kuqa's old and new towns. Most of the present buildings date from 19th-century rebuilding: a mosque with a tiled brick minaret, and a flat-roofed tomb hall about 16 m square with carved wooden lattices and painted floral panels, surrounded by family graves.

rows.name: Qilan Ancient City, Kalpin
rows.summary: Qilan Ancient City is a Qing-dynasty ruin site in the desert about 7 km east of Qilan village in Kalpin County, listed nationally as the Konaqilan ruins. It was rated a 4A scenic area in 2023, and the county promotes it as one of its main heritage sights.

rows.name: Sea-Buckthorn Forest Wetland Park, Wushi
rows.summary: A wetland park in Wushi County built around a large stand of wild sea-buckthorn, with a boardwalk of about 5 km winding through the thickets beside streams and springs. Local people come here to walk and camp, and Aksu tourism routes usually pair it with Yanquanshan Park in the county town.

rows.name: Simsim Caves
rows.summary: Simsim is the easternmost of the Kucha cave groups: 52 caves spread over about 800 m at the mouth of a gorge in the Qoltag hills, cut from around the 4th century and abandoned by about the 9th. Its murals show Kuchean, Chinese and later Uyghur styles, and some square caves have a distinctive lotus-petal lantern ceiling, though many caves are badly damaged.

rows.name: Subashi Temple Ruins
rows.summary: Subashi ('head of the water' in Uyghur), recorded in Chinese sources as the Zhaohuli monastery, was the largest Buddhist monastery of the Kucha kingdom in the Wei-Jin period, at the foot of the Qoltag hills north-east of Kuqa. Its east and west temple groups keep the earthen remains of stupas, halls and monks' quarters, and a 6th–7th-century reliquary painted with musicians and dancers found here is now in Tokyo. The site has been part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing since 2014.

rows.name: Tang Anxi Protectorate Culture Park, Xinhe
rows.summary: A modern culture park in Xinhe county town named after the Tang dynasty's Anxi Protectorate, rated 4A in 2023. It serves as an evening market and events venue, and was listed in 2022 among the region's first night-time culture and consumption districts.

rows.name: Tarim River Wetland and Poplar Forest, Shaya
rows.summary: A scenic area of wetland and natural desert-poplar (Populus euphratica) forest beside the Tarim River south of Shaya county town. Regional tourism routes promote it for the meeting of desert and river, and the poplars are at their best in autumn.

rows.name: Tianshan Mysterious Grand Canyon
rows.summary: A narrow canyon about 5.5 km long cut into red-brown sedimentary rock on the southern flank of the Tian Shan, part of a national geopark; locals call it Kizilya, 'red cliffs'. Visitors walk along the canyon floor between towering walls, and inside the canyon is the Ah-ai Grotto, a small 8th-century Buddhist cave with Tang-style murals found by a herdsman in 1999.

rows.name: Tianshan Sacred Tree Garden
rows.summary: A grove of ancient trees in a spring-fed oasis at about 1,700 m in the Tian Shan foothills of Wensu County, covering some 600 mu (40 ha). Its 289 old poplars, averaging about 145 years, grow in contorted shapes where groundwater rises along fault lines, earning it the nickname 'museum of old trees'. Fences protect the trunks and props hold up some of the heavier branches.

rows.name: Tianshan Tomur Scenic Area
