rows.summary: Tianshan Tomur is a 752 km² mountain scenic area in Wensu County below Tomur Peak, at 7,443.8 m the highest summit of the Tian Shan, and in December 2024 it became Aksu Prefecture's first 5A area. Its three main parts are a red-rock canyon with salt-dome landforms, Ta Village with guesthouses and play areas, and the Kyrgyz township of Bozidun. The canyon lies in the Tomur section of the Xinjiang Tianshan World Natural Heritage site (inscribed 2013), and Kyrgyz traditions such as the Manas epic and Kyrgyz embroidery are part of local culture.

rows.name: Tonggusibashi City Ruins
rows.summary: The walls of a Tang-dynasty town, about 250 by 230 m and up to 7 m high with bastions and corner towers, stand on the alluvial plain of the Weigan River in southern Xinhe County. It was the centre of a Tang military-farming district under the Anxi Protectorate, surrounded by smaller forts, beacon towers and old canals, and documents of the Dali era (766–779) and Tang coins have been found here.

rows.name: Weigan River Eco-Cultural Scenic Area, Shaya
rows.name_zh: 渭干河生态文化旅游景区
rows.pinyin: Wèigān Hé Shēngtài Wénhuà Lǚyóu Jǐngqū
rows.summary: A park area on the Weigan River in Shaya, rated 4A in 2023, centred on Yanming Lake People's Park and its lakeside wetland. It has an evening market and outdoor stage, sports grounds used for the village basketball league, and a ski slope in winter, so it is a place to see local life rather than a sight in itself.

rows.name: Wushitu'er and Xiahetu'er Ruins
rows.name_zh: 乌什吐尔和夏合吐尔遗址
rows.summary: Two ruined walled sites face each other across the mouth of the Weigan (Muzat) River just south of the Kumtura Caves, with remains mainly of the Wei-Jin to Tang periods. Wushitu'er on the east bank keeps walls 2–4 m high with bastions and a corner tower, while little more than wall fragments and a tower under 10 m tall survive at Xiahetu'er on the west bank. Scholars have identified the pair variously as Buddhist monasteries and as the Tang-dynasty Zhejue Pass, and excavations since 2019 have added finds from the Han period.

rows.name: Yanqi Pastoral Complex, Shaya
rows.summary: An agri-tourism complex built around a modern agricultural science park in Gulebage town, Shaya County, rated 4A in 2024. It offers themed farm sightseeing and leisure, and surrounding villages have opened homestays and pick-your-own orchards along newly upgraded rural roads.

rows.name: Yanquanshan Park, Wushi
rows.summary: Yanquanshan is a landscaped scenic park at the western end of Wushi county town, used mainly by local residents for walks. Aksu tourism routes pair it with the Sea-Buckthorn Forest Wetland Park, and it was named a regional model scenic area for visitor conduct in 2024.

rows.name: Youyi Road Tombs, Kuqa
rows.summary: A cemetery of the Jin and Sixteen Kingdoms period (3rd–5th centuries) found in 2007 during building work on Youyi Road in Kuqa, where Han-style brick-chambered tombs matching those of the central plains and the Hexi Corridor in form were found for the first time in Xinjiang. The tombs have sloping passages, vaulted chambers and carved-brick details, and the finds included more than 700 coins. The Wei-Jin Ancient Tombs Museum, built over the tombs 7–8 m underground, opened to the public in July 2024.

rows.name: Agonggaiti Grassland Stone Figures Park
rows.summary: A Kazakh culture park on the Agonggaiti grassland beside the road from Burqin to Kanas, built around a group of ancient steppe stone figures and rock carvings left by early nomads. Visitors can walk among the carved standing stones and watch horsemanship shows, Dawaz tightrope walking and the 'girl chase' riding game, and try Kazakh customs and food. Surrounded by hills, pine woods and streams, it is often the first stop on the way into Kanas.

rows.name: Altay Birch Park
rows.summary: A park of wooded river islands at the north-western corner of Altay city, where the Kelan River splits into six islands under birch and poplar. A boardwalk of about 5 km loops through the woods, with a woodland cafe, a small animal park and a sightseeing train. The birches turn gold from late September, and in winter hoar frost coats the trees.

rows.name: Baisha Lake
rows.summary: A small freshwater lake ringed by pale sand dunes at the Bingtuan's 185th Regiment in the far north-west of Habahe County, about 2.5 km from the Kazakhstan border. Mixed woodland and dense reeds grow around the shore, lotus flowers open on the water in June, and the neighbouring Singing Sand Hill gives the dunes a rumbling sound. The 5A area also includes the regiment's 'Northwest First Company' site.

rows.name: Chemurchek Stone Figures and Stone-Cist Tombs
rows.name_zh: 切木尔切克石人及石棺墓群
rows.summary: A Bronze Age burial ground of the Chemurchek culture, of about 2700–1800 BC, spread over some 44 km² of steppe around Chemurchek town west of Altay city, with large stone-walled grave enclosures, cairns ringed with stones and stone cists. Carved stone figures stand on the east side of the graves facing the sunrise, and this pairing of stone figure and stone cist is the hallmark of the culture. A representative 113 cm figure from the Kaiyinar No. 2 cemetery was moved in 2002 to the Altay Prefecture Museum, where visitors can see it.

rows.name: Fuyun Riverside Scenic Area
rows.summary: A landscaped riverside promenade along the Irtysh in Fuyun county town, rated 3A in 2016 and 4A in 2019. It links the south-bank embankment walks, a pedestrian suspension bridge, a musical fountain square on Karatunk island, a weir and Nanshan Park, and residents use it daily for walks, dancing and games. It makes an easy stop on the way to Koktokay, and was listed as a regional tourism and leisure street in 2023.

rows.name: Grassland Stone City and Tongtiandong Cave
rows.summary: A 59 km² stretch of the Saur Mountain foothills south-east of Jeminay where weathering has shaped the granite into rounded boulders, stacks, basins, hollows and caves rising out of grassland, with more than 200 kinds of wild flowers in spring and early summer. Within it lies the Tongtiandong cave site, the first Palaeolithic cave site found in Xinjiang, where excavations since 2016 have traced human use back about 45,000 years and found carbonised wheat around 5,200 years old. Display boards at the cave explain the finds, and the area also has a spring in a rock cave and the old pastures of Ailin, a Kazakh prince of the late Qing and Republican era.

rows.name: Habahe Birch Forest
rows.summary: A belt of natural birch forest along the Habahe River valley just west of Habahe town, rated a national forest park in 2010 and linked to the town by the Akqi national wetland. Paths and wooden bridges lead through the white-trunked birches, and the park has a visitor centre built to look like a birch stump, a Kazakh folk-culture area with yurts and a Ferris wheel above the forest. The leaves turn gold in autumn.

rows.name: Kelan River Riverside Scenic Area
rows.summary: An 11.6 km riverside scenic belt of about 720 hectares along the Kelan River through Altay city, from the Birch Park bridge in the north to the Red Stone area in the south. Walking and exercise areas, photo spots and cultural venues follow the river between the mountains that ring the city, and on summer evenings the banks fill with residents and visitors out for a stroll. In winter the long, heavy snow season turns it into a place for snow play close to the centre.

rows.name: Koktokay Rare Metals National Mine Park
rows.name_zh: 可可托海国家矿山公园
rows.summary: A former rare-metal mine in Koktokay town, built around the huge open pit of the Number 3 Vein, a deposit found in 1935 that is known as a natural geological museum for its 84 minerals, including lithium, beryllium, tantalum, niobium and caesium. Around it are the Ayiguozi mine tunnel, Soviet-style wooden bridges and buildings, an exhibition hall of ore specimens and company history, and the old ore-dressing plant and machine works. The park is run as a patriotic-education base on the mine's role in the 'Two Bombs, One Satellite' programme and received its plaque as a national industrial-tourism demonstration base in 2023.

rows.name: Koktokay Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 788 km² 5A scenic area around Koktokay in the Altai, centred on the Irtysh Grand Canyon, where the young Irtysh River runs through forest past waterfalls, striking rock formations and the peak known as Divine Bell Mountain. It also takes in Kekesuli, a reed-fringed lake used by migratory birds as a stopover and breeding ground, Yilemu Lake and the Kalaxianger earthquake fault zone. Rafting, off-road motorbikes and paragliding have been added in the canyon, and in autumn the birch and poplar woods turn yellow and gold.

rows.name: Sandaohaizi Stone Mounds and Deer Stones
rows.summary: A high basin of three lakes, Bianhaizi, Zhonghaizi and Huahaizi, at about 2,700 m on the Altai watershed near the Mongolian border, where summer pastures hold a Bronze Age landscape of giant stone mounds, tombs and deer stones. The largest mound, about 15 m high and 76 m across, is laid out like a wheel, with four paved stone paths running out to an outer ring of sunken stone slabs, and around it lie further large and medium mounds, about a hundred smaller cairns, deer stones carved with animals and weapons, and rock art. Excavations by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in 2013–16 studied the site, which is also a summer camping and wildflower area.

rows.name: Sino-Russian Old Wharf Street
rows.summary: A riverside leisure quarter of about 20 hectares on the Irtysh in Burqin town, built around the old wharf of the Sino-Soviet river shipping that once ran on the Irtysh. It brings together a night market on the river embankment, the Sino-Soviet Shipping Memorial Hall, the sites of the old wharf and pontoon bridge, a Russian-style shopping street and a theatre.

rows.name: Ulungur Lake Golden Coast
rows.summary: A sandy beach resort on the north-eastern shore of Ulungur Lake, with clear water, a shallow stretch about 100 m wide and water of around 20–22°C in summer. Besides swimming and sunbathing there are jet skis, flyboarding, parasailing, cruises around the lake to watch birds and grilled cold-water fish from the lake, and a wetland science museum of eight halls belongs to the Ulungur Lake national wetland park. In winter the resort hosts an ice and snow festival with ice fishing, and an autumn cold-water swimming meet.

rows.name: Wucaitan (Five-Colour Beach)
rows.summary: A stretch of the north bank of the Irtysh 24 km from Burqin, where water and wind have carved the ground into multicoloured ridges, gullies and pinnacles, facing the green riverine woods on the far bank. Boardwalks lead over the eroded formations to viewpoints, a suspension bridge crosses the river and a lighthouse-style tower gives views along it, and the colours are richest at sunset, the favourite time for photographers. It is a usual stop on the road between Burqin and Kanas.

rows.name: Sleeping Poplar Valley
rows.summary: A stand of dead desert poplars on the north-western edge of the Taklamakan in the 14th Regiment's land, where trunks covering more than 3,000 mu (about 2 km²) still stand upright or lie in twisted shapes; local sources link the die-off to the Keriya River ceasing to reach the area in the late Ming or early Qing period. The scenic area has a visitor centre, a sightseeing train, camel rides and buggies, and the bird-rich Swan Lake wetland, with boardwalks and a bird-watching tower, lies close by. October and November, when the living poplars turn gold, are the best months.

rows.name: Taklamakan – 359th Brigade Cultural Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 塔克拉玛干·三五九旅文化旅游区
rows.summary: A tourism area in Aral, the Bingtuan city of the 1st Division, centred on the 359th Brigade Reclamation Memorial Hall, which presents the history of the army units that came to Xinjiang around 1950 and turned to farming and land reclamation on the northern edge of the Taklamakan. It also includes the 'Gate of the Desert' area of the 11th Regiment, with desert sports and farm sightseeing, and was rated 5A in 2021.

rows.name: Tarim River Source Scenic Area
rows.summary: The scenic area at Xiaojiake, west of Aral, where the Aksu, Hotan and Yarkand rivers meet to form the Tarim, China's longest inland river. Paths lead through riverside desert-poplar forest towards the confluence, and the site, open since 2023, has a visitor centre, the 'Eye of the Tarim' observation tower overlooking the meeting of the rivers, small halls on the river and on the desert poplar, a campground and a children's play area.

rows.name: Yuergun Military Reclamation Site
rows.summary: A group of buildings put up in 1971–73 by the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps at Yuergun, kept as a record of the Corps' land-reclamation settlements: a club with an auditorium and open-air cinema, and a clinic. The club walls carry moulded slogans and star motifs and its doors and windows have carving by Uyghur woodworkers, while the clinic is described as the only surviving reclamation-era medical building in southern Xinjiang.

rows.name: Baluntai Yellow Temple
rows.summary: A Gelug (Tibetan Buddhist) monastery founded in 1888 by the Torghut Mongol khans in a Tian Shan valley at Baluntai, given the name Yong'an Temple by the Guangxu emperor and long the chief religious centre of the Torghut and Khoshut Mongols. Its two-storey main hall, with apricot-yellow walls and upturned eaves, stands at the centre of a group of temple buildings and stupas beside the Baluntai river, and a large Maitreya festival is held on the 15th day of the first lunar month.

rows.name: Bayanbulak Grassland
rows.summary: A high grassland basin in the central Tian Shan at about 2,000–2,500 m, home mainly to Mongol herders, where the Kaidu River meanders through marshes and oxbow lakes. Its Swan Lake wetlands form a national swan reserve and part of the Xinjiang Tianshan World Heritage Site, and the best-known view is the river's 'nine bends and eighteen turns' from the viewpoint above it.

rows.name: Bayingolin Prefecture Museum
rows.summary: The prefecture museum of Bayingolin in Korla, founded in 1990 and opened in 2008, and rated a national second-grade museum in 2018. Its collection covers more than ten kinds of objects, among them bronzes, pottery and porcelain, textiles, gold and silver, jade, murals and mummies.

rows.name: Beishan Forest Park, Hejing
rows.summary: A forest park on formerly bare gobi hills at the north-western edge of Hejing town, where gravel quarries were moved out from 2013 and more than 50 kinds of trees and shrubs, among them desert poplar, oleaster, sea buckthorn and walnut, were planted on drip irrigation fed from the Huangshui gully. A path of about 3 km climbs from the entrance past flower gardens to a patriotic and national-defence education base on the hilltop, and the park also has a fruit-picking orchard, a small zoo and Butterfly Spring, where swans gather. Local families come here to walk, camp, fish and barbecue.

rows.name: Bogedaqin Ancient City
rows.summary: The rammed-earth walls of the largest Han-to-Tang city site in Bayingolin, a rectangular enclosure with barbicans at its gates and traces of an outer moat. It is identified as Yuanqu, capital of the Yanqi kingdom in Han times, and it flourished under the Tang as the seat of the Yanqi Area Command, a city recorded in Xuanzang's Great Tang Records on the Western Regions. Finds include a Tang bronze turtle tally and coins, and the Yanqi County Museum shows a scale model of the city with objects from the site.

rows.name: Bosten Lake
rows.summary: Bosten is Xinjiang's largest lake, a freshwater lake of more than 1,000 km² lying at about 1,048 m in the Yanqi Basin on the south side of the Tian Shan. It is fed mainly by the Kaidu River and drained by the Kongque (Peacock) River, and its wetlands make it one of China's main reed-growing areas and Xinjiang's largest fishery. The 5A scenic area has two sections, Dahekou at the mouth of the Kaidu River and Lianhai World.

rows.name: Golden Sand Beach, Bosten Lake
rows.summary: A sand-beach resort on the north-eastern shore of Bosten Lake in Hoxud County, upgraded in 2024–25 with a visitor centre, lakeside promenade, jetty, hotels and guesthouses. In summer visitors swim and paddle, go sailing or boating, and join evening events such as bonfire parties.

rows.name: Gongnaisi Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park in the Gongnaisi (Künes) valleys of the Tian Shan in north-western Hejing County, at an average altitude of about 2,000 m, where the main valley runs for some 40 km. Pure stands of Tian Shan spruce cover the upper valley terraces, giving way to mixed spruce, birch, aspen and willow lower down, with mountain and forest meadows between them.

rows.name: Hongshan Nuclear Test Command Centre Site
rows.name_zh: 红山核武器试爆指挥中心旧址
rows.pinyin: Hóngshān Héwǔqì Shìbào Zhǐhuī Zhōngxīn Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: The former Hongshan headquarters area of Base 21, the Malan nuclear test base, which from 1966 housed the command centre and research institutes for China's nuclear tests at Lop Nur, and where scientists such as Deng Jiaxian lived and worked. After the base's facilities fell out of use in the 1980s, the former research and command centre was developed from 2012 into the Malan military history park, which is open to visitors.

rows.name: Horashan Silk Road Village
rows.summary: A farming village on the southern slope of the Horashan range west of Yanqi, developed as a rural tourism area and rated 4A in 2018, with a horse-culture hall, a market street built in the style of ancient Yanqi, farm restaurants, guesthouses and a visitor centre. The surrounding valleys hold yardang rock formations, rock art, a rafting run and the ruins of a Tang-dynasty Buddhist temple, which is a national heritage site.

rows.name: Kaidu River Scenic Area, Bohu
rows.summary: Riverside parkland along the Kaidu River at Bohu town, rated 4A in 2022, with walks, Tianhuwan Square and the 182 m Qinbo Bridge, whose glass-floored deck is lit with coloured lights and music in the evening. The Bohu County Ecological Museum, opened inside the scenic area in May 2025, covers the nature, history, intangible heritage and herding life of the Bosten Lake area over four floors. It is mainly a place for an evening stroll on the way to or from Bosten Lake.

rows.name: Loplik Village
rows.summary: A tourist village on the banks of the Tarim River in Yuli County that presents the culture of the Lop people (Lopliks) of the lower Tarim, relaunched in 2025 after a major upgrade. Its old-village area shows traditional Loplik houses, palaz weaving, fishing and hunting, and music and dance, a Silk Road bazaar recreates the trade of the ancient Lop Nur region, and camel rides and other desert activities are offered on East Sand Hill.

rows.name: Manhan Khan's Palace
rows.summary: The palace of Manchuk Jab (Manhan), khan of the Old Torghut Mongols, built in 1919 in the centre of Hejing to a design by his uncle, the fifth Shengqin lama. The grey-brick and timber palace has about 60 rooms arranged around a two-storey main hall flanked by east and west wings, and now houses the Hejing County Ethnic Museum.

rows.name: Miran
rows.summary: The ruins of a Silk Road oasis town where the Lop desert meets the Altun Mountains, once part of the Shanshan (Loulan) kingdom, with a large rectangular fort built under Tibetan rule in the 8th–9th centuries, Buddhist temple and stupa ruins and traces of an ancient irrigation system. Aurel Stein excavated murals here in 1907, including winged figures in a Roman-influenced style signed by a painter named Tita, and Tibetan documents found in the fort are among the oldest known in that script.

rows.name: Shikshin Temple
rows.summary: The largest Buddhist site of the ancient kingdom of Karasahr (Yanqi), founded in the Jin period and abandoned only when Islam reached the area around the 15th century. The mud-brick remains of 93 buildings, including temple halls up to about 25 m across, stupas and monks' cells, spread over a ridge beside 11 cave shrines with traces of painting, making it the only site in Xinjiang that keeps stupas, halls, caves and living quarters together. Sculptures and murals removed by early-20th-century expeditions are now in museums in Berlin, London, Paris, Tokyo and elsewhere, and a site museum stands by the ruins.

rows.name: Swan River, Korla
rows.summary: A landscaped river corridor in Korla's newer districts, near Minsheng Bridge, with riverside walks, summer lotus beds and boat rides. It is mainly a place for an evening stroll rather than a sight in itself.

rows.name: Tarim Desert Poplar Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of about 100 km² on the middle Tarim River in Luntai County, set in natural desert-poplar (Populus euphratica) forest on the northern edge of the Taklamakan. A sightseeing train runs along a 17 km route with stops at lakes and viewpoints, and the trees turn gold from mid-October to early November.

rows.name: Adunqiaolu Site
rows.summary: A national heritage site in the upper Bortala valley of Wenquan County, protected for its tombs set in stone enclosures and its groups of rock art, and named among China's top ten new archaeological discoveries. Part of the site is laid out as the Adunqiaolu 'Mother Stone' scenic area, and a site park is under development.

rows.name: Alashankou Border Tourism Area
rows.summary: The border tourism area at Alashankou, the rail and road port on the Kazakhstan border in the Dzungarian Gate, a pass with gales of force 8 or more on more than 180 days a year. Visitors see the national gate facing Kazakhstan's Dostyk, where guides explain the history of the broad- and standard-gauge railways and the China–Europe freight trains, and an import-goods shopping centre stands beside the visitor centre. The border-defence post known as the 'first post in the wind gap' is open by appointment only.

rows.name: Arixiate Stone-Figure Tombs
rows.summary: Tombs of the Sui and Tang period on the Arixiate grasslands of Wenquan County, north-west of Harbuhu town and marked by standing carved stone figures, listed as a national heritage site in 2006. A second national listing, the Arixiate stone circles and cairn tombs of the Spring and Autumn to Warring States period, lies in the same part of the county.

rows.name: Bortala River Scenic Area, Bole
rows.summary: The scenic area strings together three landscaped river belts in the middle of Bole, the Bohe, Kaiping and Qinghe belts, about 4.8 km long in all and linking the old town in the north with the new town in the south. The Bohe belt, centred on Jinshui Bridge, has lakeside parkland including a Swan Lake zone, the Kaiping belt has a lake park with an evening water show, and the Qinghe belt has an ice rink and the Beijing Road night market.

rows.name: Dalete Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: The ruins of a large walled town, probably the medieval city of Bolad (孛罗) on the Silk Road north of the Tian Shan, occupied from the Kara-Khanid period around the 9th century until it was abandoned in the 14th. Rammed-earth inner and outer walls survive, the south wall for about 550 m and up to 3 m high, and excavations since 2016 have uncovered houses, a brick bath-house, kilns and workshops for crystal, iron and coins. A digital exhibition hall in the nearby village of Chagansumu is open to visitors as part of a planned archaeological park.

rows.name: Etuokesai'er Tianquan Hot Spring, Wenquan
rows.summary: Etuokesai'er Tianquan ('heavenly spring'), also known as Xiao Wenquan, is a hot spring high in the Etuokesai'er River valley at about 2,650 m, and one of Wenquan County's three noted hot springs. The scenic area also takes in the river valley, the Narensala waterfall about 12 km west of the spring and the Daban glacier, with meadows where herds of horses graze. A resort complex has been under development at the spring since the early 2020s.

rows.name: Mutetaer Desert, Jinghe
rows.summary: A desert scenic area of sand dunes in Tuotuo town, Jinghe County, which held its first desert culture festival in 2018. Activities include off-road vehicles and sand motorbikes, a big-tyre dune vehicle and a dune-climbing challenge.

rows.name: Shengquan Hot Spring, Wenquan
rows.summary: Shengquan ('holy spring') is Wenquan County's best-known hot spring, used for about a century and the site of a sanatorium from 1954, now a spa complex in the county town with public pools, an outdoor bath, saunas and a hotel. The water is about 48–50 °C in summer and 41–42 °C in winter, and the Wenquan wetland and birch woods lie opposite.

rows.name: Wenquan River Valley Forest
rows.summary: A riverside forest scenic area built in 2019 on the Bortala River just north of Wenquan county town, laid out around a 36 km greenway through marsh, sea-buckthorn scrub and woods of poplar and willow. It has a visitor centre, a tree-house and photo spots, and the greenway has hosted half-marathons. A neighbouring village runs farm restaurants and guesthouses.

rows.name: Beacon Towers of Changji
rows.summary: A protected group of Tang to Qing beacon towers, Qing post stations and a stretch of Tang road along the northern route of the Silk Road through seven counties and county-level cities of Changji, from Manas in the west to Mori in the east. Most towers are rammed-earth, flat-topped pyramids; among the best preserved is the Tang tower at Wugongtai in Hutubi County, about 7 m high, whose rammed layers and timber reinforcing holes are still clearly visible.

rows.name: Beiting Ancient City (Beshbalik)
rows.summary: The earthen ruins of Beiting (Beshbalik), seat of the Tang Beiting Protectorate and later the summer capital of the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho, which was the leading city on the northern side of the Tianshan for some 700 years until its destruction in the 15th century. Its nested outer and inner walls survive and have been part of the Silk Roads World Heritage listing since 2014; west of the city stands the excavated Uyghur Buddhist temple known as Xidasi, a two-tier mud-brick building with niches, statues and murals. A site museum explains the city's history.

rows.name: Century Park, Hutubi
rows.summary: A large landscaped public park in Hutubi county town, used by local people for walks and for festivals such as the Lantern Festival light displays. It suits a short stop on the way to the Kangjiashimenzi rock carvings in the county's southern hills.

rows.name: Dushi Tourism Resort
rows.summary: A leisure resort north-east of Changji city that grew from a farm guesthouse opened in 1997 into a large complex of orchards, amusement rides, a water park and restaurants. It is aimed at families and day-trippers from Ürümqi and Changji, with fruit picking in season.

rows.name: Huaxing Youyou Valley
rows.summary: A leisure park in the Changji National Agricultural Science and Technology Park north of Changji city, combining a winery, a small animal park, flower nurseries and an outdoor activity camp. It holds seasonal events such as Dragon Boat Festival activities and suits families looking for a short outing from Ürümqi or Changji.

rows.name: Jiangbulak Scenic Area
rows.summary: A 48 km² mountain scenic area on the northern slopes of the Tianshan south of Qitai, known for the dry-farmed wheat fields that roll across the hills below forest and snow peaks. Sights include the 'Tianshan wheat sea' viewpoints, Magouliang village, the Jiangbulak gorge, a flower meadow and a 'gravity hill'. Within the area lies Shichengzi, a walled Eastern Han town that some scholars identify with Shule, where the Han officer Geng Gong's garrison held out under siege; excavations from 2014 to 2019 uncovered its walls, gates and corner towers.

rows.name: Kangjiashimenzi Rock Carvings
rows.summary: A Bronze Age rock-carving panel under an overhang of a south-facing red cliff in the danxia hills of south-western Hutubi County, with hundreds of carved human and animal figures. The upper, earlier carvings show a row of dancing women in tall headdresses and pairs of horses, while the lower scenes include tigers and crowds of male figures with explicit fertility imagery. Scholars date most of the work to the second or first millennium BC.

rows.name: Manas Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: The earthen walls of a Tang-dynasty garrison town, locally called Pochengzi, on the plain north-east of Manas town; it is the westernmost Tang city site on the northern foot of the Tianshan and stayed in use until about the Western Liao or Yuan period. Rammed-earth walls survive on three sides of a large rectangle, with traces of gates, barbicans, corner towers and a moat, and a ruined beacon tower stands outside to the south-east. Scholars identify it with the Tang post of Wuzai or the garrison town of the Qinghai army.

rows.name: Manas National Wetland Park (Yanfeitai)
rows.summary: A national wetland park formed by the Manas and Taxi rivers and the reservoirs and canals between them, piloted from 2011 and formally designated in 2016. Large numbers of migrating birds stop here in spring and autumn on the West Asia–East Africa flyway, and Yanfeitai is one of five visitor zones with boardwalks, viewing platforms, bird hides and a wildlife exhibition hall.

rows.name: Qianfodong Temple, Jimsar
rows.summary: A Buddhist temple and cave shrine near Jimsar town, rebuilt in the Qing dynasty and restored since 1993, now set in a temple park with halls to Kshitigarbha and Guanyin and a main Buddha hall. It holds temple fairs on Buddhist festival days, with prayer ceremonies, local opera and food stalls.

rows.name: Tangchaodun Ancient City
rows.summary: The ruins of Pulei, a county town founded under the Tang in 640 and used by the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho, the Western Liao and the Mongols until it was abandoned in the 15th century, now on the north-eastern edge of Qitai town. The north wall still stands with the large earthen mound that gives the site its name, and excavations since 2018 have uncovered a Roman-style bathhouse, a Church of the East monastery with wall paintings and a Buddhist temple.

rows.name: Tingzhou Ecological Green Valley
rows.summary: A riverside park about 13 km long on the Toutun River at the boundary between Changji and Ürümqi, created by a five-year clean-up, completed in 2021, of a valley once scarred by gravel pits and workshops. On the west bank Changji's green valley links five themed parks, from nature-restoration ponds and sports grounds to an industrial-heritage park, while the east bank holds the Bingtuan 12th Division's Toutun valley forest park. Footpaths run along the water, where ruddy shelducks and other water birds can be seen.

rows.name: Xiaolizhuang Military Reclamation Site
rows.summary: The former headquarters of a Bingtuan farming division, built from 1953 by army land-reclamation units on the east bank of the Manas River as a complex of Soviet-style farm buildings, including offices and a large assembly hall. In the 1950s and 1960s it was the administrative, economic and school centre of the area east of the Manas River; it later became an army base and fell into disuse after 1989. Several buildings were stabilised from 2016, and the site has since been used as a film location.

rows.name: Xinjiang Agricultural Expo Park
rows.summary: A large agricultural showground and garden at the core of the Changji National Agricultural Science and Technology Park, with exhibition areas, glasshouses of tropical plants and fruit, and fields for picking fruit and vegetables. It holds flower shows and seasonal festivals and suits families and anyone curious about farming in Xinjiang.

rows.name: Zhonghua Biyu Yuan (Manas Jade Park)
rows.summary: A large commercial complex in Manas town built in the 2010s around the trade in Manas green jade (biyu), with a jade and stone market, shops, restaurants and a sports centre. It hosts the county's jade culture festival and mainly suits visitors interested in looking at or buying nephrite.

rows.name: Baiyanggou Buddhist Temple Ruins
rows.summary: These are the ruins of a large Tang-dynasty Buddhist monastery strung for more than 10 km along both banks of the Baiyang River west of Hami. The main hall once held a clay seated Buddha more than 10 m high modelled onto the cliff, with central-pillar caves, monks' cells, a lecture platform and a stupa nearby.

rows.name: Barkol Lake
rows.summary: Barkol Lake, known in Han times as the Pulei Sea, is a salt lake at about 1,585 m in the western Barkol grassland, ringed by the Barkol and Moqin Ula mountains. Its northern part yields salt and its southern part mirabilite and brine shrimp, and in summer herders pitch felt tents and graze their flocks on the meadows along the shore.

rows.name: Barkol Old City
rows.summary: Barkol was a Qing garrison town on the grassland north of the Tian Shan, one of the four great military cities of northern Xinjiang, with a Han city built in 1731 and a Manchu city in 1772. Its long rammed-earth walls survive, and the scenic area follows them to the gates, a granary, the Xiangu temple, an old academy, an exhibition hall and an old-town culture street. The Kazakh pastures of the Barkol basin surround the town.

rows.name: Dahe Tang City Ruins, Barkol
rows.summary: Dahe is a Tang-dynasty town site of two adjoining walled enclosures on the flat floor of the Barkol basin. The western enclosure's walls still stand with corner platforms and bastions, and finds include Tang lotus-pattern floor bricks and eave tiles; the site is thought to be the Tang garrison of Ganluchuan.

rows.name: East Tianshan Scenic Area, Hami
rows.summary: This mountain scenic area north of Hami links four spots in the eastern Tian Shan: Mingsha Shan, a singing sand dune; the alpine meadows of Baishitou, named after a lone white boulder; Songshutang, cool in summer and snowy in winter; and Tianshan Temple, a viewpoint whose temple is said to date back to the Tang. A scenic road climbs through belts of Tian Shan spruce and Siberian larch, so a single drive passes from desert to snowy peaks.

rows.name: Gaojiahu Wetland, Barkol
rows.summary: Gaojiahu is a spring-fed wetland of ponds, marsh and winding streams on the Barkol grassland, listed among China's important wetlands and home to water birds, with the snowy Tian Shan as a backdrop. Boardwalks cross the meadows and visitors can boat and fish, and the area has a visitor centre, a waterside restaurant, a glass water slide, star-gazing cabins and about thirty farm stays.

rows.name: Hami Dahaidao Yardang Scenic Area
rows.summary: South-west of Hami, wind has carved the Gobi into a vast field of yardangs, ridges and mesas of clay and sandstone in shapes given names such as the Starship and the Horse's Head, along the line of the Dahaidao, an ancient short cut between Turpan and Dunhuang. The area is also where the fossil pterosaur Hamipterus was found, and in September 2026 it was inaugurated as the Hami Pterosaur–Yardang National Geopark, with the new Hami Pterosaur Museum inside. The museum's six oval halls display pterosaur skeletons and fossil eggs and embryos.

rows.name: Hami Kings' Mausoleum
rows.summary: For more than two centuries Hami was ruled under the Qing by a line of nine local Uyghur princes, and their burial ground in the south of the city mixes Islamic, Chinese and Mongol architecture. The largest tomb, of the seventh prince, is a domed brick mausoleum faced with green and blue tiles, beside wooden pavilion-roofed tombs of later princes and the Aitika Mosque, described as Hami's largest, with a flat roof carried on about a hundred red pillars. Next door the princes' palace has been rebuilt, and the two together form the Hami King scenic area.

rows.name: Hami Museum
rows.summary: The Hami Museum, a national first-grade museum, holds the main collection of the Hami region, with stone tools, bronzes, painted pottery, woodwork, woollen textiles and naturally preserved mummies from prehistory to the Ming and Qing. The permanent display on ancient Hami highlights finds from the Yanbulaq cemetery and the Dongheigou site, the mummies from the Wubao cemetery are among its highlights, and a second gallery covers the region's geology. The same complex, the Hami Cultural Heritage Institute, also has an exhibition on the region's music, dance, crafts, food and festivals.

rows.name: Huancaigou Stone Inscriptions
rows.summary: A lone boulder at the mouth of Huancaigou gorge, beside the old road over the Tian Shan from Hami to Barkol, carries inscriptions from three dynasties. On one face an Eastern Han text dated AD 140 is partly legible; another face bears a Tang inscription of AD 640 linked to the general Jiang Xingben, overcut in 1750 with the large Qing characters naming the gorge.

rows.name: Lafuqueke Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: Lafuqueke is a Tang-dynasty walled town on the east bank of the Baiyang River at Wubao, split into northern and southern halves by flood erosion. West of the walls lie the ruins of a large Buddhist temple with a hall, caves, monks' cells and a stupa, and a cemetery to the north yielded Tang coins.

rows.name: Yiwu Desert Poplar Forest
rows.summary: A large forest of desert poplar (Populus euphratica) on the edge of the Naomaohu basin in Yiwu County, run as a national desert park and scenic area since 2004. A route of about 23 km leads past gnarled old trees, an area of ancient root forms and viewpoints such as Bow Mountain. It is also promoted as a base for star-gazing and drone photography.

rows.name: Aitika Mosque, Yutian
rows.summary: A mosque in Yutian (Keriya) town, also known as the Yutian Grand Mosque, whose origins are traced to the 13th century. It was enlarged in 1665 and rebuilt in 1947 with funds raised by the local community, and it is listed as a national heritage site among China's modern historic buildings.

rows.name: Damagou Buddhist Temple Ruins
rows.summary: A group of Buddhist temples of the Khotan kingdom found in 2000 in the scrub desert of Toplukdong, Damagou township, now shown in a heritage park. Temple No. 1, of the 6th–7th century, is a tiny shrine with a seated Buddha in Gandharan and Gupta style and wall paintings, protected by a site museum opened in 2007; the larger temples No. 2 and 3, probably of the 8th century, show features of the Tibetan period. The temples were abandoned when the Karakhanids conquered Khotan around the year 1000.

rows.name: Hotan Museum
rows.summary: The prefecture's main museum, which opened in its present form in May 2020. Its seven halls trace the history of Hotan, an oasis on the southern Silk Road and the seat of the Buddhist kingdom of Khotan, using models, holograms and animation alongside excavated objects, and include a hall devoted to the Niya site. Finds from desert sites that are hard to visit can be seen here.

rows.name: Kurban Tulum Memorial Hall
rows.summary: A memorial hall in the home village of Kurban Tulum, the Uyghur farmer known as 'Uncle Kurban', built in 2003 and enlarged several times since. After receiving land in the early 1950s he set out to thank Mao Zedong in person, and in 1958 he met Mao in Beijing with a Xinjiang farmers' delegation, a story later retold in songs and a film. The hall is on the national list of classic red-tourism sites and tells his life through displays and sculpted scenes.

rows.name: Lalikun National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Lakes and reed beds about 20 km north-west of Moyu town, where the oasis farmland meets the desert, designated a national wetland park in 2012. Visitors take boat trips through the waterways and watch the water birds.

rows.name: Longhu Lake, Yutian
rows.summary: A reed-fringed lake on the edge of the Taklamakan near Xiwule township, reached through a belt of desert poplar woodland west of Yutian town. Developed as a scenic area since 2016, it has a pier, viewing platforms, a small science museum and the former home of Kurban Tulum. Fish were released into the lake in 2024 and 2025 to keep the water clear, and more water birds now winter here.

rows.name: Moyu Old Town (Karakax)
rows.summary: The old quarter of Moyu (Karakax) county town, rated a 4A scenic area in 2020. Its square and streets host festivals and craft displays, including a regional intangible-heritage exhibition in 2025, and an experience hall introduces traditional herbal medicine beside a large riverside mural of a healer.

rows.name: Niya ruins
rows.summary: The ruins of Jingjue (Cadota), an oasis kingdom on the southern Silk Road that flourished from the Western Han to the Western Jin, scattered along the dried lower course of the Niya River deep in the Taklamakan. Remains of timber-framed houses, orchards, a stupa, Buddhist shrines and cemeteries lie among the dunes; they were first excavated by Aurel Stein from 1901 and again by Chinese–Japanese teams from about 1990. Finds include many Kharoshthi documents and the Han brocade armguard inscribed 'Five stars rising in the east benefit China', now in the Xinjiang Museum in Ürümqi.

rows.name: Rawak Stupa
rows.summary: The ruins of a Buddhist temple of the ancient Khotan kingdom on the sandy edge of the Taklamakan north-east of Hotan, centred on a large domed stupa on a cross-shaped base inside a walled courtyard. The courtyard walls were once lined with colossal clay statues and reliefs; Aurel Stein uncovered 91 of the statues in 1901, and by his return in 1906 treasure-hunters had destroyed most of them. Scholars date the temple to roughly the 3rd to 7th centuries, and a boardwalk leads around the remains.

rows.name: Tuancheng Old Quarter, Hotan
rows.summary: A renovated old quarter of Hotan city around Gezi Xiang (Pigeon Lane), where traditional Uyghur courtyard houses with aiwan halls have been kept and the lanes turned into a garden-like district of homes, workshops, cafés and restaurants. It was named a national tourism and leisure block in 2023 and is liveliest in the evening, when music restaurants, book cafés and street performers open up around its public square.

rows.name: Wuluwati Scenic Area
rows.summary: A large mountain reservoir at the point where the Karakax River leaves the Kunlun Mountains, formed by the Wuluwati dam, which was built between 1993 and 2001 for irrigation, flood control and hydropower. The scenic area around the lake is visited mainly for boat trips on the water and for the Kunlun setting.

rows.name: Xaidulla Outpost Ruins
rows.summary: The ruins of a high-altitude garrison post at about 3,800 m, on a river terrace where the Karakax River meets a tributary beside the Xinjiang–Tibet highway. First built in 1877 under the Qing after the reconquest of southern Xinjiang, it remained a garrison post through the Republican period into the mid-20th century. A walled barracks compound of cobble and mud brick and a hexagonal mud-brick watchtower on a small hill still stand, though both are badly eroded.

rows.name: Xinjiang Kunlun Mountain Scenic Area
rows.summary: A large mountain scenic area in the central Kunlun above Ulughsay township, south of Qira, covering more than 596 km² of high grassland, valleys and snow peaks; it grew out of the Banlange summer pasture and was rated 4A in 2021 as 'Kunlun Shengjing'. Herds graze the meadows below the snow line, shuttle buses run up to viewpoints such as Diru Peak, and Kunlun-culture displays add to the scenery. It was named a national adventure-tourism scenic area in 2023 and passed the landscape assessment for 5A status in 2024.

rows.name: Yotkan Ancient City
rows.summary: A walled tourist town opened in 2022 at Bagqi, about 5 km from the buried site of Yotkan, which scholars regard as the probable capital of the ancient kingdom of Khotan. Its design is based on a 10th-century Dunhuang mural of the Khotan capital: red walls enclose white Uyghur-style aiwan houses, a Xuanzang square, food lanes, craft workshops, guesthouses and exhibition halls. The original Yotkan site lies under farmland with nothing to see above ground, and some of its finds are in the Hotan Museum.

rows.name: Yulongwan Desert Park
rows.summary: A desert recreation area in Duolu township on the edge of the Taklamakan, where visitors slide down the dunes and try other sand activities, and school groups learn about the shelter belts planted to hold back the sand. It was rated 4A in 2024 and has been a stop on the Taklimakan Rally.

rows.name: Aktas Girl Peak
rows.summary: Upland grassland on the Aktas pastures north-west of Tekes, a 'sky grassland' of flower meadows in early summer, with primulas and globeflowers, and forest edges below snow peaks. The scenic area has boardwalks, wooden cabins and viewing decks, riding and cycling routes, and in winter snowmobiles, horse-drawn sledges and traditional horseback games.

rows.name: Baitulla Mosque Minaret
rows.summary: The Qing-era minaret of Yining's Baitulla Mosque (now the Jiefang South Road Mosque), completed in 1773 with Qing court funds and built by craftsmen from inner China. Shaped like a Chinese drum tower, it rises about 18 m in three timber storeys with green-glazed roofs above a brick-faced earthen base pierced by an arched passage. The rest of the old mosque was replaced by new buildings in 1995, leaving the minaret as its only Qing structure.

rows.name: Daxigou Fushou Mountain
rows.summary: Hills of wild fruit forest in Daxigou township, Huocheng County, where some 60 kinds of wild fruit tree grow, mainly wild apple, wild cherry plum, apricot and hawthorn; the wild cherry plum here is its only natural population in China. The slopes are white and pink with blossom in April, when a mountain-flower festival is held, and turn red and gold in autumn.

rows.name: Dengta Educated Youth Museum
rows.summary: A museum opened in 2014 at the former Dengta pasture near Zhaosu, where more than 80 educated youths from Beijing and Shanghai were sent to live and work in the 1970s under the 'up to the mountains and down to the countryside' movement. Photographs, documents and everyday objects in and around the old camp buildings show their work and daily life. The camp is a regional protected heritage site and the museum was the first in Xinjiang on this theme.

rows.name: Former Political and Cultural Centre of the Three Districts Revolutionary Government
rows.name_zh: 三区革命政府政治文化活动中心旧址
rows.pinyin: Sānqū Gémìng Zhèngfǔ Zhèngzhì Wénhuà Huódòng Zhōngxīn Jiùzhǐ
rows.summary: A reviewing stand, open-air theatre and stage completed in 1949 as the main gathering place of the Three Districts (Ili, Tacheng and Altay) during the Three Districts Revolution of 1944–49, now in Yining's People's Park. The two-storey Soviet-style reviewing stand faces a sloping auditorium that once seated about a thousand people, with the stage at the far end, and the grounds were used for rallies, sport, films and performances. The stand later housed the Ili prefecture museum until 2004.

rows.name: Gedeng Mountain Stele
rows.summary: A stone stele with an inscription composed by the Qianlong Emperor to mark the Qing army's victory over the Dzungar ruler Dawachi at Gedeng Mountain in 1755, set up on the hilltop in the early 1760s. About 3 m tall, it bears the text in Chinese and Manchu on one face and Mongolian and Tibetan on the other, and stands in a pavilion reached by a stone path. It is the only one of the four steles on the Dzungar campaigns that still stands where it was first erected.

rows.name: Gongliu Wild Walnut Valley
rows.summary: A valley in the hills near Gongliu town that shelters a rare natural stand of wild walnut trees, a relict species from the Tertiary period, within a scenic area of about 12 km². More than 350 rare plant and animal species have been recorded, and an exhibition hall on the wild walnut forest serves school and family groups.

rows.name: Guandi Temple of Nadaqi Niru
rows.summary: A temple to the warrior god Guan Yu built in 1907 by the Xibe garrison of the seventh banner company (niru), whose ancestors were moved from Manchuria to guard Ili in 1764; it is the largest and best-preserved Qing Guandi temple left in Qapqal County. The main hall's side walls carry 24 painted scenes of Guan Yu from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms captioned in the Xibe script, beside a hall to three goddesses and a memorial hall. An iron bell cast in the 1810s–20s, inscribed in Chinese and Manchu, was brought here from a neighbouring company's temple.

rows.name: Guozigou Valley
rows.summary: A winding gorge about 32 km long through the northern Tianshan, named for the wild fruit forests on its slopes and long the main route from Sayram Lake down into the Ili valley, once a branch of the northern Silk Road. The G30 expressway crosses it on the Guozigou Bridge, now a sight in its own right, and the snow peaks, spruce woods and roadside viewpoints make it a regular stop on the drive between Ürümqi and Yining.

rows.name: Huiyuan Ancient City
rows.summary: Huiyuan was founded in 1763 as the seat of the Qing General of Ili, the highest military and civil official in Xinjiang, and remained the region's chief city until Xinjiang became a province; after the old city was ruined in the 1860s and 1870s, a new town was built in 1882–93 about 7.5 km to the north. The new town keeps its bell and drum tower, a three-storey timber pavilion on a brick platform at the central crossroads, and the restored office compound of the Ili General, with exhibition halls on the generals' rule, a Confucian temple and other Qing yamen buildings. Two stretches of the old city's rammed-earth wall, each over 800 m long, survive in fields near the Ili River.

rows.name: Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Museum
rows.summary: The prefecture's main museum, founded in 1993 and now housed in a large new building on Ruyi Street in western Yining. Its collection of about 6,500 objects is shown in permanent galleries on the Ili valley's history from the pre-Qin period, gold and silver work from the Boma tombs, and the region's nature and resources. It is a national second-grade museum and a useful introduction before touring the valley.

rows.name: Ili Old Town (Kazanqi)
rows.summary: The old quarter of Yining, about 3.5 km² of lanes with more than 300 traditional buildings and many courtyard houses in blue and white, where about 120,000 people still live. Visitors tour by horse-drawn cart or electric buggy, with home visits, craft workshops, song-and-dance shows and flocks of pigeons over the rooftops, and the Shaanxi Great Mosque stands inside the area. Long known as the Kazanqi Folk Tourism Area, it was renamed the Ili Old Town Cultural Tourism Area in 2024–25 as part of a bid for 5A status.

rows.name: Ili River Scenic Area
rows.summary: A riverside park along the Ili River on the southern edge of Yining, popular with locals on summer evenings and for watching the sunset over the water. It has riverside paths and viewpoints, a campsite and space for open-air weddings, and has hosted a dragon-boat race at the Dragon Boat Festival.

rows.name: Jinxiu Garden, Kuytun
rows.summary: A landscaped park in the city of Kuytun, developed around the North Xinjiang Botanical Garden and used by local people for walks and open-air performances. The prefecture's 2022 plan lists old-style, Buddhist-culture and amusement areas among its projects there.

rows.name: Kalajun Grassland
rows.summary: A great sweep of alpine meadow on the northern slopes of the Tianshan in Tekes County, ranging from about 1,300 m to nearly 4,000 m and used as summer pasture by herders. With Kurdening it forms part of the Xinjiang Tianshan World Natural Heritage site. Shuttle buses link viewpoints in western Kalajun, known for its wave-like rolling hills, and eastern Kalajun, with flower meadows, the forested Kurdai canyon and views of snow peaks.

rows.name: Khorgos China–Kazakhstan International Cultural Tourism Area
rows.name_zh: 霍尔果斯中哈国际文化旅游区
rows.summary: A tourist zone at the Khorgos land port made up of the Chinese part of the China–Kazakhstan Horgos International Border Cooperation Centre, a cross-border trade zone set up under a 2005 agreement, and the National Gate area with an exhibition hall on the history of the crossing. Inside the cooperation centre visitors can walk through the passage linking the Chinese and Kazakh sectors, shop in duty-free malls on both sides and visit the China Culture Hall, while beside the gate are a Central Asian-style street and a 108 m sightseeing tower.

rows.name: Kurdening Scenic Area
rows.summary: A broad valley on the northern side of the Tianshan in Gongliu County, unusual for running north to south and filled with primeval forest of Schrenk's spruce, part of the Xinjiang Tianshan World Natural Heritage site. Rivers, meadows and snow peaks frame the forest, and after spring rain low cloud often fills the valley. It also opens in winter for snow activities.

rows.name: Liuxing Street
rows.summary: A residential quarter of Yining laid out from 1935 on a six-pointed street plan, with lanes radiating from a central square through six wedge-shaped blocks of blue, green, orange and purple-painted houses and courtyards. Renovated from 2009 and named a historic and cultural district by the regional government in 2010, it is now full of guesthouses, cafés, craft shops and small museums, including an accordion hall, while residents of several ethnic groups still live there. Locals often dance to live music in the square on summer evenings.

rows.name: Mausoleum of Sultan Vais Khan
rows.summary: The tomb of Vais Khan, a 15th-century ruler of the Eastern Chagatai Khanate (Moghulistan), on the north side of the Abrel hills in Yining County. The present building dates from 1876, when local Muslims had it rebuilt by Han craftsmen as a four-storey pavilion of earth brick and timber with upturned eaves and a yellow-glazed roof, topped by a crescent. It is one of the four best-known mazars of the Ili region and has long been a place of pilgrimage.

rows.name: Nalati National Wetland Park
rows.summary: Reed beds, rivers, marshes and lakes in Xiaoerbulake town, Xinyuan County, a national wetland park since 2019 on a migration route for birds. Boardwalks, viewing platforms and boat trips lead through the reeds, and a scientific survey reported in 2024 found here the largest breeding colony of glossy ibis known in China.

rows.name: Nilka Wetland Ancient Poplar Forest
rows.summary: Riverside woodland of old poplars and Tianshan birch along the Kash River just west of Nilka town, part of a belt of poplar forest that follows the river for about 110 km and a national wetland park since 2014. Boardwalks lead through the trees, where squirrels, foxes and pheasants may be seen, and a rafting stretch of about 2 km runs in summer.

rows.name: Nulasai Ancient Copper Mine
rows.summary: Remains of a copper mine and smelting site in the Nulasai ravine of the Abrel hills south of Nilka, dated by radiocarbon from mine timbers to about 2,400 years ago, around the early Warring States period. Four mine entrances survive, one shaft about 20 m deep still shored with logs, and a slag heap in the valley has yielded ore, slag and lumps of roughly smelted copper matte. It is counted among the earliest copper mines and smelting sites found in north-west China.

rows.name: Princess Jieyou Lavender Garden
rows.summary: A lavender park in Qingshuihe town, Huocheng County, set up to show the whole lavender industry, from nurseries and fields to oil distilling and product displays. Huocheng is one of China's main lavender-growing areas, and the fields are in flower in June, the garden's busiest time. It takes its name from Princess Jieyou, a Han-dynasty princess sent to marry into the Wusun, whose lands lay in this region.

rows.name: Qing-dynasty Karun Sites of Ili
rows.summary: Sixteen surviving guard posts (karun, from the Manchu and Xibe word for a watch post) of the late Qing defence system around Ili, once manned by Manchu, Han and Xibe troops. Most are square rammed-earth forts about 30–35 m a side; Wutongzi in Qapqal keeps walls about 10 m high with corner towers, while others survive only as low wall stumps.

rows.name: Shaanxi Great Mosque, Yining
rows.summary: The largest mosque among the nine Qing-era towns of Ili, founded in the mid-18th century by Hui settlers from Shaanxi and Gansu and brought to its present size by 1781. It is built in Chinese style, with a pagoda-like minaret and a prayer hall under tiled roofs, and some of its tiles and carved bricks were carried from Shaanxi. It stands inside the Ili Old Town tourist area.

rows.name: Shengyou Temple, Zhaosu
rows.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist (Gelug) temple built in 1884–98 by the Oirat Mongols of Ili with craftsmen brought from Beijing, described as the largest and best-preserved Tibetan Buddhist temple complex in Xinjiang. Eight of its original eleven halls remain, from the dance hall at the gate and the retreat hall to hexagonal bell and drum pavilions and the main hall, combining Chinese timber building with Tibetan and Mongol decoration. Six Tianshan spruces planted in 1889 still stand between the gate and the main hall.

rows.name: Tangbula Grassland
rows.summary: A chain of grassland, spruce forest and hot springs strung along the upper Kash River valley for more than 50 km in eastern Nilka County, often called the 'hundred-li gallery'. Some 113 side valleys open off the main valley, and the area is a national forest park popular with photographers and summer visitors. The name is explained locally as meaning 'seal' or 'imprint'.

rows.name: Tekes Bagua City
rows.summary: The county town of Tekes, laid out on a radial plan modelled on the eight trigrams (bagua) of the Book of Changes: from the Taiji altar at the centre, streets run outwards across four ring roads, 64 streets in all over about 8 km². The town was listed as a national historical and cultural city in 2007, and its centre is a 4A scenic area with a visitor centre and a night-time leisure district.

rows.name: Tianshan Flower Sea
rows.summary: An agri-tourism park developed since 2017 on former gravel desert in Kashi town, Yining County, covering about 46 km² of lavender, flower fields and orchards. Apricot blossom in spring, lavender in summer (now extended into autumn by late-flowering techniques) and fruit picking in autumn are the main draws, with campervan pitches, cabins and a lavender-oil distillery on site. It suits photographers and families rather than travellers looking for wild landscape.

rows.name: Tughlugh Timur Mausoleum
rows.name_zh: 吐虎鲁克·铁木尔汗麻扎
rows.summary: The tomb of Tughlugh Timur, a descendant of Chinggis Khan's son Chagatai and the first Mongol khan in the region to adopt Islam, built between 1363 and 1369 north-east of Huocheng. The two-storey mausoleum, square with a dome, has a great arched portal framed by Quranic inscriptions and covered in glazed tiles of blue, green, brown, white and other colours in Central Asian Islamic style. A smaller tomb of his son stands beside it.

rows.name: Tukai Desert
rows.summary: An area of mostly fixed and semi-fixed sand dunes beside the Ili River south-west of Huocheng town, described locally as the only desert inside an oasis in Xinjiang. Since 2021 it has been run as an amusement complex, Tukai Desert Happy World, with a desert water park, camel rides, dune buggies, ATVs and go-karts, and a staged song-and-dance show on the Han princess Jieyou.

rows.name: Tuohulasu Grassland
rows.summary: Rolling hill grassland on the southern side of the Keguqin range of the western Tianshan, north of Yining County town, with spruce, streams and summer herds below snow peaks. The Kazakh name is explained locally as 'keep going and you arrive over the mountain', after an old herders' route between Jinghe and Yining that crosses the grassland. Sights include an apricot-blossom valley and Wuxifu Gou, a long forested canyon.

rows.name: Xiaoerbulake Liquor Culture Town
rows.name_zh: 肖尔布拉克酒文化小镇
rows.summary: A distillery town in Xinyuan County built around a large baijiu works, where visitors can see the Western Regions Liquor Culture Museum, a liquor street, a sauce-aroma baijiu workshop and a yard of decorated earthenware storage jars. It is a factory-tour stop on the main road between Yining and Nalati and a regional industrial-tourism site.

rows.name: Xiaohongnahai Stone Figure
rows.summary: A warrior statue of reddish granite, about 1.8 m tall above ground, standing on a low earthen platform and carved for the tomb enclosure of a ruler of the Western Turkic Khaganate around 600 AD, most likely Nili Khagan. The figure wears a crown and braids and holds a cup and a short knife, with a worn Sogdian inscription of 20 lines below the waist. It is the centrepiece of the Grassland Stone Figure scenic area, where more than ten other stone figures stand.

rows.name: Xiata Ancient City Ruins
rows.summary: Ruins of a walled town of the Tang to Yuan periods in Kuositobie village, Xiate township, on the approach to the Xiata ancient road over the Tianshan. Stretches of earthen wall and scattered roof tiles remain, and a flood embankment built in 2019 protects the site from a nearby river.

rows.name: Xiata Scenic Area
rows.summary: The mouth of the Xiata valley on the north side of the Tianshan, with spruce forest, meadows and river valleys below the Muzart glacier and snow peaks. It is the northern end of the Xiata ancient road, a 120 km route across the mountains to Wensu County in the Aksu region that has long drawn experienced trekkers. Roads, parking and a shopping street were upgraded in 2024.

rows.name: Xibe Ancient City and Jingyuan Temple
rows.summary: A modern tourist town in old style in Sunzhaqi Niru, a Xibe village outside Qapqal town, built around Jingyuan Temple, the Tibetan Buddhist (Gelug) temple of the Qing Xibe garrison, whose halls were rebuilt in the late 19th century on a Chinese plan with a Hall of the Heavenly Kings, a main hall and side halls. The town also holds the Xibe Museum, on the move of Xibe soldiers and families from Manchuria to guard Ili in 1764, and an archery museum, since the county is known for Xibe archery. A gate-opening ceremony is staged at the town gate.

rows.name: Zhaosu Celestial Horse Culture Park
rows.summary: An equestrian park at the Zhaosu horse farm, in the heartland of Ili horse breeding, with a national-standard racecourse, grandstands, an indoor equestrian hall and stables. It hosts horse races through the season and the Celestial Horse (Tianma) Festival, held in early summer, with horse shows and performances.

rows.name: Zhaosu Jade Lake
rows.summary: A glacier-fed lake dammed high in the Aheyazi valley of the Tianshan, whose milky blue-green colour, given by fine rock flour from the glaciers, shifts with the light. A one-way road up the valley leads to the Yujing Tianfeng viewpoint above the lake, and the woods around it turn gold from mid-September to early October.

rows.name: Zhaosu Wetland Park
rows.summary: Wetland and meadow along the upper Tekes River and its tributaries south of Zhaosu town, where some 90 bird species have been recorded, including demoiselle and common cranes, whooper swans and great bustards. On summer evenings herds of horses are driven through the river for a staged show, 'Celestial Horses Bathing in the River', watched from a viewing platform.

rows.name: Dushanzi Grand Canyon
rows.summary: The Dushanzi Grand Canyon is a section of the gorge, about 200 m deep, that the meltwater-fed Kuytun River has cut through the gravel foothills of the Tian Shan south of Dushanzi. Walkways along the rim look down on walls scored with grey-black gullies and, from July to September, on meltwater channels braiding across the flat floor; the canyon has also been used as a film location. It lies near the start of the Duku Highway, the mountain road across the Tian Shan to Kuqa.

rows.name: Heiyoushan
rows.summary: Heiyoushan, 'Black Oil Mountain', is a low mound of natural asphalt just outside the city centre, formed over ages as crude oil seeped to the surface and set with the sand; Karamay, Uyghur for 'black oil', is named after it. Some 36 oil springs still bubble on the hill, twelve of them ringed with stone into little pools, and at one, the 'jumping spring', bubbles rise faster when visitors jump beside it.

rows.name: Karamay No. 1 Oil Well
rows.summary: Karamay No. 1 Well struck oil on 29 October 1955, the discovery that opened the Karamay oilfield and gave rise to the city. The wellhead is preserved beside a memorial erected in 1982, at the centre of a sunken commemorative plaza with relief walls and two mirror-steel 'oil bubble' sculptures, completed in 2015. It is listed as a national heritage site, an industrial heritage site and a national red-tourism site.

rows.name: Karamay River
rows.summary: The Karamay River is a canal-fed waterway, opened in 2000, that brings water from the Irtysh diversion scheme right across the oil city to a reservoir on its south-western edge. Riverside parks and promenades run its whole length from Jiulongtan, a pool framed by traditional-style buildings at its head, under a string of footbridges and road bridges, making it the city's main leisure area.

rows.name: World Ghost City, Urho
rows.summary: The World Ghost City, also called the Urho Wind City, is a field of yardangs on the north-western edge of the Junggar Basin, where strong winds have carved layered rock into shapes likened to palaces, towers, people and animals. It became Karamay's first 5A scenic area in 2020.

rows.name: Xinjiang's First Oil Well, Dushanzi
rows.summary: In 1909 the Qing authorities drilled Xinjiang's first machine-drilled oil well at Dushanzi with a cable-tool rig bought from Russia, starting the region's modern oil industry. Today a short length of the drill casing stands inside a small concrete railing on the slope of the Dushanzi mud volcano, and the site of Xinjiang's first oil-refining still lies about 150 m to the east.

rows.name: Afaq Khoja Mausoleum
rows.summary: The family mausoleum of Afaq Khoja, a 17th-century Sufi leader of Kashgar, begun in 1640 for his father, and popularly called the Tomb of the Fragrant Concubine after the legend of the Qianlong Emperor's Uyghur consort. Its square tomb hall, faced with green and yellow glazed tiles under a large dome and framed by four corner towers, stands at the back of the complex with the lecture hall, the Jaman mosque, the high and low prayer halls and the gatehouse. Since the mid-2010s the front part has been built up as the Xiangfei Garden, a themed area with a family history hall, displays on the Fragrant Concubine story, embroidery and craft stalls, performances and a staged welcome ceremony.

rows.name: Bachu Red Sea Scenic Area
rows.summary: A large leisure area 12 km from Bachu county town that links a folk-culture village, a stretch of the old Silk Road route along the Kashgar River, Golden Poplar Island in the desert-poplar woods, the Red Sea Bay water park and wetlands. Developed since 2009, it has a core area of about 80 km² joined up by a 38 km touring loop.

rows.name: Dawakun Desert Scenic Area
rows.summary: A desert scenic area on the western edge of the Taklamakan beside the Yarkand River in Yopurga County, where a lake lies among the sand dunes beneath the distant Kunlun range. Open since 2002, it offers camel rides, dune rides in off-road vehicles, sand sliding and water activities, with staged song-and-dance shows and an avenue of desert poplars at the entrance. It has been named a national water-conservancy scenic area and a national desert park, and lies about 100 km from Kashgar.

rows.name: Dolan Painters' Village
rows.summary: A village of Dolan farmer painters in Kumkusar township just south of Markit, twice named a national folk-art village by the Ministry of Culture, whose painters have exhibited their work in China and abroad. The scenic area has galleries of farmer paintings, a gourd-painting hall, a hall of traditional musical instruments, a memorial hall on Taklamakan exploration and a square for Dolan song and dance, and visitors can often watch painters at work and buy their pictures. Dolan farmer painting was added to the county's intangible heritage list in 2021.

rows.name: Jame Mosque, Yarkand
rows.summary: The oldest and largest mosque in Yarkand, whose founding is dated variously from 1409 to the 17th century, when it was enlarged and named Jame under Abdullah Khan, and which was repaired several times in later centuries. A gateway with a half-domed iwan, a balcony and paired minarets leads into a courtyard with a pool and willow and poplar trees, lined with the small rooms of the lecture halls. Behind a screen wall the broad, flat-roofed prayer hall stands on a platform, with slender painted columns and coffered ceilings whose motifs mix Uyghur, Islamic and Chinese designs.

rows.name: Jiashi Town Poplar Eco-Park
rows.summary: An ecological park on the north-western side of Jiashi county town, opened in 2019 and planned over about 1,050 mu around a stand of desert poplars linked by waterways. Paths lead through the poplar woodland, flower beds and waterside areas, and there are fairground rides such as a pirate ship and a rainbow slide, speedboats, a poplar night market and a camping area. It works mainly as a town park, with local people making up about half its visitors, and makes a short stop on the road between Kashgar and Aksu.

rows.name: Jinhuyang Desert Poplar Forest Park
rows.summary: A forest park of desert poplars on the alluvial fan of the Yarkand River about 35 km south-west of Zepu, covering some 40,000 mu (about 27 km²), much of it natural poplar woodland, with water on three sides and the Kunlun range in the distance. Channels of the river wind through the forest between stretches of open gobi, and a 200-year-old Xinjiang poplar on the park's south-western edge is revered locally as a sacred tree. The leaves turn gold in autumn, and a small tourist train and electric carts run along the routes through the woods.

rows.name: Jirzankal Cemetery
rows.summary: A cemetery of around 500 BC on terraces above the Tashkurgan River, where low round burial mounds lie beside long stripes of alternating black and white pebbles laid across the gravel ground. Excavations in 2013 and 2014 by the Institute of Archaeology of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences found pottery, wooden and bronze objects, iron pieces and glass beads, and the excavators linked the burials to early Zoroastrian practice. The name is a transliteration of the Tajik Jerzankol, 'the place where the eagle stands on the stone'.

rows.name: Khunjerab Pass National Gate
rows.summary: The national gate building at the Khunjerab Pass, where the Karakoram Highway (G314) reaches the border with Pakistan at about 4,700 m, on the only land crossing between the two countries. Rated in 2021 as a red-tourism scenic area, it centres on the gate, the boundary marker and a monument to the opening of the pass in the 1980s. The border port has been open all year round since late 2024, but the altitude makes even a short visit hard work.

rows.name: Mor Buddhist Temple Ruins
rows.summary: The ruins of the largest known Buddhist monastery around Kashgar, where two mud-brick stupas, one round with a domed top and one stepped and square, still stand on a gravel terrace. Excavations since 2019 have uncovered 18 buildings with 62 rooms, among them monks' quarters, halls and a kitchen, and many fragments of Buddha images; the monastery was founded around the 1st century AD and abandoned around the 10th century. It was named one of China's top ten archaeological discoveries of 2024, and its Uyghur name Mor, 'chimney', comes from local people taking the stupas for beacon towers.

rows.name: Princess Castle
rows.summary: The ruins of a fortress dated to the Tang dynasty, listed as the Gongzhubao ancient city site, about 70 km by road south of Tashkurgan near the Kalachigu valley. Its name is linked to a tale told by the monk Xuanzang in his Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, of a Han Chinese princess on her way to marry a Persian king who was placed on a high rock for safety during local unrest.

rows.name: Taklamakan N39° Desert Scenic Area
rows.summary: A desert activity area among the Taklamakan dunes in Markit County, used for a stage of the Taklimakan Rally; its name refers to the 39th parallel north. Modified four-wheel-drive vehicles take visitors along beginner, intermediate and advanced dune routes, and there are camel treks along the sand ridges, sand sliding, study tours on desert plants, stargazing and desert camping. A 2.5 km desert road, a large car park and two viewing platforms have been added in recent years.

rows.name: Tashkurgan Stone City (Pamir Scenic Area)
rows.summary: A 5A scenic area on the edge of Tashkurgan town built around the hilltop Stone City, the ruined walled town that was the seat of the Han-era kingdom of Puli and was greatly enlarged under the later kingdom of Qiepantuo, described by the monk Xuanzang on his way home from India. Its walls rise on stone footings with mud-brick above and enclose remains of the Jin and Tang periods and a Qing government compound, looking down over the meadows and streams of the Alar Golden Grassland wetland below. The area also includes the Caiyun Renjia Tajik folk village of traditional houses and a heritage park with Tajik music, dance and wedding-custom performances, and visits are made by shuttle bus from the visitor centre.

rows.name: Tomb of Mahmud al-Kashgari
rows.summary: The tomb of Mahmud al-Kashgari, the 11th-century scholar who compiled the Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk, a dictionary of the Turkic languages, in Baghdad in the 1070s; local tradition holds that he was born at Opal and returned there to teach. The shrine stands on a hillside of springs and old trees known locally as the Holy Man's Hill, with a gate, the tomb chamber and rooms for prayer, recitation and lodging in plain timber-and-earth construction. After earthquake damage it was rebuilt in 1984–86 in its earlier form, with an exhibition room added.

rows.name: Why Are the Flowers So Red Scenic Area
rows.name_zh: 花儿为什么这样红景区
rows.summary: A long, narrow river valley south-east of Tashkurgan promoted as the home of 'Why Are the Flowers So Red', the song from the 1963 film Visitors on the Icy Mountain that the composer Lei Zhenbang adapted from the Tajik folk song 'Guli Bita'. The 985 km² scenic area takes in the valley's villages and about 5,000 mu of natural woodland, and is known locally as a village of song and dance.

rows.name: Yarkand Khanate Royal Tombs
rows.summary: The burial ground of the khans of the Yarkand Khanate, which ruled from Yarkand in the 16th and 17th centuries, lying behind the Altyn Mosque in the old town. In the mosque's courtyard stands the domed mausoleum of Amannisa Khan, a royal consort and musician honoured for her work in compiling the Uyghur Twelve Muqam, who was given an exceptional burial in the royal cemetery; the present memorial mausoleum was built in 1992. The Altyn Mosque itself is noted for its painted ceilings.

rows.name: Yarkand Old Town
rows.summary: The historic quarter of Yarkand (Shache), once the capital of the Yarkand Khanate, rated as a 4A scenic area in 2022. Its lanes include the Kazanchi old street, where coppersmiths and ironworkers make pots and other wares in open workshops among food stalls and shops selling farm produce, and visitors can try crafts such as Atlas silk tie-dyeing. Festival evenings and performances are staged in the old town, and the royal tombs and the Jame Mosque are close by.

rows.name: Yengisar South Lake Resort
rows.summary: A lakeside resort along the dam of a reservoir 5.5 km south of Yengisar town, inside a national wetland park. Along the shore are the Yengisar Knife Museum, devoted to the town's handmade knives, a bird science hall, a boat pier, a shopping street and a hotel, and it has been a regional study-tour base for school groups since 2021. It suits a stop for families or anyone interested in Yengisar knives on the road between Kashgar and Yarkand.

rows.name: Zhang Qian Silk Road Cultural Park
rows.summary: A park in Shule county town dedicated to Zhang Qian, the Han dynasty envoy to the Western Regions, centred on the Han-style Zhang Qian Memorial Hall and Shule Museum opened in 2010. Its galleries cover Zhang Qian's mission, finds from the ancient kingdom of Shule and local folk customs, using sculpture, reliefs, touch screens and projections. Two new venues opened at the end of 2025: the Kunlun Station Natural Science Museum, with about 1,400 animal specimens and models, and a nature-photography centre run under the Chinese National Geography brand.

rows.name: Zonglang Spring
rows.summary: A spring oasis at the foot of the Kunlun Mountains, where water trickles from cracks in a cliff above the east bank of the Ulukustang River into a round pool about 10 m across, shaded by four ancient willows. The 18 km² scenic area adds wetland meadows and riverside walks, and an upgrade in 2026 brought an evening water show, kart track, water games, open-air dining tents and short helicopter flights over the oasis. The name is a transliteration said to mean 'water with fish', with lingquan ('miraculous spring') added for the spring's reputation.

rows.name: Aibifu Aijiemu Mazar, Upper Artux
rows.summary: A domed shrine-tomb in Upper Artux, rebuilt between 1889 and 1899 by local merchant brothers on a site venerated since the Karakhanid period; local tradition says it honours a merchant from Persia who cancelled the villagers' debts. The tall brick tomb chamber is crowned by a dome faced with blue glazed tiles and decorated with carved brick and plaster, and it survived the great Artux earthquake of 1902. A small mosque and lodgings for caretakers and pilgrims stand in the walled courtyard.

rows.name: Azihan Fig Village
rows.name_zh: 阿孜汗无花果风情小镇
rows.summary: A traditional Uyghur village in Songtak town just outside Artux, protected as a traditional village and opened to visitors around its fig orchards and Artux-style houses. A folk-culture street, four themed lanes and a shaved-ice shop run by the same family for three generations are among the sights, and figs can be picked in season.

rows.name: Oytak Glacier Park
rows.summary: A mountain valley west of Oytak town in Akto County, where glaciers come down from snow peaks to forest, meadows and waterfalls. Viewpoints take in the glacier, avalanche slopes, waterfalls and small lakes such as Feitian Lake, and the park is visited as a cool summer retreat.

rows.name: Kokdala Lavender Culture Park
rows.name_zh: 可克达拉薰衣草文化产业园
rows.summary: A lavender park on the edge of Kokdala, the Bingtuan city of the 4th Division in the Ili valley, with lavender fields, a lavender science museum, a showroom for the park's lavender and fragrance products and a souvenir shop. The fields flower in summer, when the park is a popular photo stop and the lavender campground beside it, with water and charging points, fills with tents and camper vans; it suits a short stop on an Ili valley road trip.

rows.name: Desert Veterans Red Tourism Area (47th Regiment)
rows.summary: A red-tourism area in the 47th Regiment's town, Laobing ('veterans') Town, on the southern edge of the Taklamakan, built around the Memorial Hall of the PLA's March into Hotan. In December 1949 about 1,800 soldiers of a PLA regiment crossed the desert on foot, some 790 km in 18 days, to reach Hotan, and many then stayed to farm here; the hall tells the story with photographs, objects and multimedia, and a monument on the square in front is dated 22 December 1949.
